### UserGroup public vector argument-count/register census (2026-11-08)

Compared the 39 function-list entries in `workbench/libs/usergroup/usergroup.conf` with their direct `AROS_LH` definitions in the selected source set. Entry counts and configured register sequences match except `setlastlog`, recorded as OD11555. This census does not claim generated-header output, target compiler behavior, external call-site compatibility, or full type-equivalence verification; no build was run.

### UserGroup `setlastlog` public vector arity (OD11555 added; 2026-11-08)

Compared the `setlastlog` function-list entry with generated prototype/call behavior and its source LVO body (`workbench/libs/usergroup/usergroup.conf:72-73`; `tools/genmodule/writeincclib.c:39-49`; `tools/genmodule/functionhead.c:287-310`; `compiler/arossupport/include/libcall.h:602-611`; `workbench/libs/usergroup/getutent.c:367-375,419-436,456-462`). The function list emits a three-argument public prototype and an LVO call passing `(D0,A0,A1)`; the implementation at LVO 42 reads `(D0,A0,A1,A2)` as uid/name/console/host. The generated client's `host` is consumed as `con`, and the implementation reads an unprovided A2 as `host`. Rechecked the repository's `setlastlog` references: only its declaration/documentation and definition are present, with no maintained in-tree call. Added OD11555 as a conditional public API ABI candidate. No generated header, build or call was run; source-only.

NetInfo module/vector and target-selection reconciliation (2026-11-08; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): compared `workbench/devs/netinfo/netinfo.conf`, its complete local `mmakefile.src`, `NetInfoReq`, BeginIO/AbortIO definitions, and genmodule's configured-vector mapping (`tools/genmodule/config.c:365-389,1186-1202,1380-1384`; `netinfo.c:260-295`; `include/netinfo.h:15-28`). The configured handlers use LVOs 5/6, request in A1, and void/LONG returns; the request starts with the standard Message/Device/Unit/command prefix. The local common/quick edges are commented, and a repository-wide `mmakefile.src`/`mmakefile` search found no other parent reference to `workbench-devs-netinfo`; its device target is explicit-build only. `usergroup.library` includes NetInfo call sites but has no dependency on the device target. Corrected the prior manifest ledger statement that the common aggregate selects it. OD1909 and OD1901 remain conditional source candidates; their selected in-tree client routes require the NetInfo device to be separately built/installed. No generated files or builds were produced.

speech.device request/renderer ownership follow-up (2026-11-08; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the complete 720-line `speech.c` body and traced BeginIO/AbortIO, worker dequeue/completion, reset/flush counters, audio acquisition rollback, double-buffer playback, cancellation and final audio release (`workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:94-196,210-244,246-378,390-510,611-720`). `GetRequest()` publishes `sb_Current` while holding `sb_Lock`; AbortIO removes only still-queued messages or signals the current request, and reset/flush decrement `sb_ControlsPending` on either worker completion or queued abort. `NarratorSpeak()` drains each in-flight audio slot on finish and aborts/waits any remaining slot before returning; the release command is processed by the same worker only after that request returns. The inspected normal/failure cleanup paths did not establish another independent defect. OD11455 remains the separately recorded ExecSMP open/last-close interleaving. External IO request lifetime and audio.device behavior remain outside this source-only trace.

### speech.device close/open SMP candidate recheck (OD11554 withdrawn; 2026-11-08)

Re-traced final-close and BeginIO ordering after the initial candidate. Close sets `sb_Closing` and queues `SPEECH_RELEASE_AUDIO` while holding `sb_Lock`; BeginIO needs that same lock to queue new requests (`workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:591-597,611-720`). A request from an opener racing with final Close is therefore queued after the release message. The single worker handles release first, clears `sb_Closing`, then dequeues the new request; `NarratorSpeak()` lazily reacquires audio for that request (`:210-244,438-510`). Releasing this internal shared audio session during the overlap establishes no persistent failure or canceled new request. Withdrew OD11554 as unsupported. The generic generated reference-count race remains separately tracked as EK745; this speech-specific state consequence is not retained. No schedule, request, or audio operation was run; source-only.

USB Audio OD3172 `AHIDB_MaxMixFreq` general-query path expansion (2026-11-06; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): traced AHI's `_AHI_GetAudioAttrsA()` `AHIDB_MaxMixFreq` case (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:491-496`) through `AHIsub_GetAttr()` to USB Audio `subLibGetAttr()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3926-3936`). The generic attribute case subtracts one from the zero frequency count and sends `-1` to the getter; the getter's unchecked `nam_FreqArray[arg]` indexes the preceding `nam_NumFrequencies` field in the current struct layout (`usbaudio.h:102-105`), so it returns a bogus zero rate. Expanded OD3172 to make clear this path is available to any AHI client querying `AHIDB_MaxMixFreq`, in addition to the selected requester path. It remains an invalid array index without an established out-of-object access. No mode query, device or build was run; source-only.

Virtual Bluetooth Configure Response result/state trace (OD11454 added; 2026-11-06; no file/LOC credit): followed signaling `case 0x05` (`vbthci_peer.c:603-628`) through both channel completion flags. The peer extracts the source CID but ignores the response flags/result, unconditionally sets `lc_ConfOut`, and can transition to open once `lc_ConfIn` is set. Compared with the selected AROS L2CAP manager, which closes the channel for any result other than `BT_L2CAP_CONFIG_RESULT_SUCCESS` (`channel_manager.c:330-347`) and sends success for the current no-option request path (`:298-320`). Added OD11454 as a conditional optional-device interoperability candidate; selected in-tree negotiation does not currently provide the non-success trigger. No response or session was run; source-only.

Virtual Bluetooth ACL reassembly and signaling boundary recheck (2026-11-06; no new OD or file/LOC credit): traced `BTCMD_WRITEACL` from `vbt_HandleRequest()` to `vbtp_HandleACL()` and its per-link `ln_RxBuf` state (`vbthci_unit.c:503-509`; `vbthci_peer.c:689-729`; `vbthci_intern.h:74-100`). The HCI payload is clamped to the request's supplied length; every fragment append is bounded by `VBT_RXBUFSIZE`; first fragments shorter than the L2CAP header are dropped; and complete PDUs are checked against their declared L2CAP length before dispatch. A declared length that cannot fit the 1,100-byte reassembly buffer is discarded on overflow, without crossing the buffer. Continuation or reserved boundary sequences without a valid first fragment can leave unusable partial state until a later first fragment resets it, but no separate persistent or caller-visible failure was established. L2CAP signaling command-specific minimum-parameter validation remains covered by OD11450; CID wrap remains OD11451. No packet was constructed or processed and no build was run; source-only.

CAMD retry wait VBlank-cadence pass (OD10532 added; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): re-read all 196 physical lines of `workbench/libs/camd/camdwait.c`, traced every local `CamdWait()` call, and followed the worker request through generic `UNIT_VBLANK` insertion/completion plus the PC and m68k timer implementations. Confirmed that the AROS worker submits 10 microseconds but waits for VBlank processing; on PC's 50 Hz emulation, a request queued just after a frame event can wait nearly 20 ms. Selected callers use this helper to retry full MIDI output buffers or poll SysEx completion. Added OD10532 with the explicit-target qualification: `workbench-libs-camd` is buildable but is not connected to the active `workbench-libs-complete` edge in this snapshot. Corrected the row's prior characterization of the interval as a small bounded delay. Existing full-body credit stands. No MIDI operation, timer request, or build was run; source-only.

USB MassStorage unit-number width and Open lookup pass (OD11011; 2026-11-01): traced the shared `mss_staticdata.unitNum` allocator through cache assignment (`storageclass.c:125-128`), the accepted `maxLUN <= 15` range and one-task-per-LUN loop (`:168-174,265-278`), the worker's `uint8_t unitnum = lun + mss->unitNum` narrowing (`storage_task.c:69-74`) and storage into the 32-bit `msu_unitNum` (`:148`; `storage.h:91-94,135-140`). Added OD11011 for duplicate IDs and misrouted/inaccessible opens. The USB MassStorage class is selected by Raspberry Pi ARM and AArch64 package manifests (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:188`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:227`) and its module includes this worker (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/mmakefile.src:9-11`). No device, request, volume, or build was exercised; source-only.

Production callers are limited to `DeleteMidi()` (outgoing and incoming owner lists; `deletemidi.c:53-80`) and `NextMidiLink()` (`nextmidilink.c:56-75`); the latter explicitly documents that `CL_Linkages` must be locked (`:31-33`). `DeleteMidi()` holds `CLSemaphore` across each traversal and removal (`:53-86`), and `UnlinkMidiLink(..., FALSE, ...)` removes the cluster-side node while leaving the owner node in the MidiNode list until that node is freed, with the next node saved before freeing the current one (`unlinkmidilink.c:25-41`; `deletemidi.c:55-65,69-80`). No invalid or unlocked in-tree helper call was found. `developer/debug/test/misc/camdtree.c` contains a separate local copy, not a caller of the library helper. SANA-II successful-wire-error candidate correction (OD3105, OD3114 and OD3289 withdrawn; 2026-10-31): checked the SANA-II Revision 7 contract, which describes `ios2_WireError` as a more specific code that may be set when `io_Error` is nonzero and requires it when an applicable error code exists. It does not require a meaningful `ios2_WireError` on success. The uninitialized-success-output candidates therefore do not establish defects. Earlier dated OD3105/OD3114/OD3289 notes below are superseded; no source-body or LOC credit changed. [Specification](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/SANA-II_Revision_7#Errors). Source-only; no request was sent.

USB-MIDI embedded CAMD bridge loader/build-gate reconciliation (OD4300/OD4301/OD4459 rechecked; 2026-10-31; no new OD or LOC credit): traced the non-m68k embedded driver object from `rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c` through `camd/mmakefile.src`'s relocatable binary object rule and the class's `_binary_poseidonusb_start/_size` write path (`camdusbmidi.class.c:196-206`). The source `MidiDeviceData` initializer ends with `Flags = 0` (`poseidonusb.c:35-51`); `workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:231-245` rejects any AROS driver without bit 0 and closes its loaded segment before reaching `Init()` at `:249-252`. This confirms OD4300 gates that non-m68k generated-image path and the later callback/ring findings. Also decoded the checked-in `CAMDDriver.c` array as big-endian words against the public structure layout: its `MDEV` record starts at byte `0x24`, with `NPorts=0x10` and `Flags=0` at offsets `0x44-0x45`. The `__mc68000__` class branch therefore has the same format flag if that image is packaged, but the local manifest declares CPU aliases only for i386, x86_64, ARM, AArch64 and PPC (`camdmidi/mmakefile.src:3-11`); this pass does not claim m68k class-target selection. `InitCamd()` scans `DEVS:Midi` only in its initialization path (`workbench/libs/camd/init.c:16-55`), consistent with OD4459 for files written after that scan. The class module target is optional from the USB class aggregate in this snapshot (`rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:9-31`), while its declared CPU variants are explicitly buildable. Generated object behavior, external CAMD drivers, and class/runtime operation remain unverified. No binary was loaded, driver initialized, or build/run performed; source-only.

<a id="usb-hid-worker-detach-before-dos-init-od2184"></a>
USB HID worker detach-before-DOS-init pass (OD2184 restored; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): rechecked both worker loops against Exec Wait semantics and the hub's disconnect disposal (kbdclass.c:357-369,241-257; mouseclass.c:265-290,226-235; usbhubclass.c:543-549; rom/exec/wait.c:129-141). Keyboard's first wake while dos_not_ready is set always takes the readiness branch and discards Ctrl-C, even if OpenLibrary succeeds there; mouse can handle Ctrl-C in the same wake only when OpenLibrary succeeds, so it loses the signal if DOS remains unavailable. Wait clears the received bits, and Dispose sends only one Ctrl-C without joining the worker. If no later report signal wakes it, the worker remains waiting with its input.device open and local allocations retained after child disposal. Restored the prior coverage-only OD2184 as a scoped worker/resource-lifetime finding; no body, path or LOC credit. No detach, DOS failure or worker was run; source-only.

<a id="usb-hid-worker-open-failure-event-buffer-leak-od2312"></a>
USB HID worker Open-failure cleanup pass (OD2312 restored and consolidated; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): compared keyboard and mouse worker startup/early-return paths (workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/kbdclass.c:329-352; mouseclass.c:238-260). Each allocates its local InputEvent batch before OpenDevice("input.device", ...), but on Open failure deletes only the request and port, clears the worker-task field, and returns without freeing the batch. Since the pointer is not stored in the object, later Dispose cannot reclaim it. Restored the keyboard's coverage-only OD2312 and consolidated mouse coverage-only OD2806 into one finding for the same cleanup omission, distinct from OD10994's batch-allocation failure and OD10995's keyboard request-allocation failure. Existing file-body credit remains unchanged; no path/LOC totals changed. No worker, device-open failure, or allocation was induced; source-only.

<a id="usb-hid-field-width-and-signedness-review-od3142-od3143-rechecked"></a>
USB HID field-width extraction recheck (OD3142 strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-read all of `hid_get_data()` and followed `loc.size` from the HID Report Size global through `hid_locate()` into the mouse X/Y report path (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid.c:291-303,407-435,438-458`; `mouseclass.c:139-158,63-65`). Confirmed the existing OD3142 full-width mask issue and refined its C-semantics note: after the width-sized mask shift, a 32-bit sample with its high bit set also reaches a left shift of negative `int32_t` with shift count zero, which is undefined; a 31-bit size likewise makes the signed mask shift unrepresentable. Larger sizes still exceed the helper's 32-bit assembly/result model. Kept this within OD3142 rather than splitting overlapping width cases. OD3143 remains the independent omission of descriptor signedness. No descriptor, report or device was used; existing body credit unchanged; source-only.

SD-card MMC frequency candidates withdrawn for unreachable state (OD3314/OD3356; 2026-10-25): re-ran a repository-wide code search for `AF_Card_MMC`, `AB_Card_MMC` and `sdcu_Flags`. `AF_Card_MMC` is only defined and tested; no checked-in code sets it. `CommonInit()` creates the pool with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_init.c:115`), the unit is allocated from it (`sdcard_bus.c:368`), and `AllocVecPooled()` forwards the pool requirements through `AllocPooled()` to `InternalAllocPooled()`/`stdAlloc()` which clears allocations requested with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:74-79`; `allocpooled.c:88-93`; `memory.c:1183-1185,671-673`). The only MMC-frequency callers are guarded by that unset flag (`sdcard_bus.c:88-95,115-125`), so the `MMCSwitch()` return mismatch and 52 MHz flag-mask mismatch have no selected unit trigger. Marked OD3314 and OD3356 withdrawn and removed both from the active master index. Their earlier detailed/report and dated-ledger claims are superseded; the helper code remains selected but dormant. External code that writes this private flag and actual card behavior remain outside this source-only pass.

speechcore mixed-mode renderer candidate correction (OD9544 withdrawn; 2026-10-24): rechecked `Decode()` and the default `S` voicing 0x1c after `Z` 0x96. `Decode()` clears `d3` for non-mixed noise frames; the renderer masks the waveform contribution to 0..31 and all first 32 amplitude entries are zero (`workbench/libs/speechcore/synth_render.c:78-90,263-275`; `workbench/libs/speechcore/speech_voice.c:381-383`). Therefore the alleged extra harmonic sample is zero, and no independent PCM defect was established from the sticky flag. Removed OD9544 from the report and index; the broader renderer audit remains open. Source-only.

Trackdisk worker-creation candidate reconciliation (OD3343 expanded; OD3566 withdrawn; 2026-10-24): rechecked `TD_InitTask()` against `NewAddTask()`, `Exec_InitETask()` and `Exec_CleanupETask()` (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:567-642`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:268-309`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:101-146,238-260`). The later `NewAddTask()` failure leaves the caller's TaskData, stack and MemList allocations in place, launches no worker, and is followed by an unconditional wait for a signal only that worker sends. This overlaps OD3343's existing worker-setup failure root cause and has been merged into OD3343; OD3566 is withdrawn and its master-index link removed. This supersedes the older duplicated wording at the 2026-10-17/18 follow-up and detail-reconciliation entries. The separate early-allocation failure that returns through the init hook and worker-side timer allocation failure (OD3342) remain distinct. No failure or boot was induced; source-only.

BTHID report-capacity boundary recheck (OD3454 strengthened; 2026-10-23): traced descriptor Main-item Report Size/Count through `bParseReport()`'s per-field offsets and final report bit count, then through `bOpenReportChannels()`'s `BTHID_MAXREPORT` clamp and `bHandleReport()`/`bProcessItem()` dispatch. Confirmed the parser has no 256-byte acceptance check and the input decoder receives no actual-length/buffer-capacity argument. A compact variable report with 65 32-bit fields is 260 bytes; its last field begins at byte 256, beyond the allocated buffer. Kept this distinct from OD3469, whose trigger is a short successful transfer for a report otherwise within the class limit. Rechecked Classic output/feature packet truncation against `bSendReport()` and the touched-flag clearing; HOGP output uses a separate path. No descriptor, transfer, or device was used; source-only.

OD3463 signed-report decode C-semantics correction (2026-10-23): rechecked `bProcessItem()`'s byte-aligned 16-bit, byte-aligned 32-bit, and generic signed-field extraction against the applicable signed-left-shift rules. The negative signed `BYTE << 8` and repeated negative `LONG << 1` remain undefined for valid negative fields. The 32-bit path shifts promoted `UBYTE` values by 24; high-byte results fit 32-bit unsigned but not signed, so the conversion is implementation-defined, not an independent UB finding. Narrowed OD3463 and its index summary; no selected compiler result establishing incorrect 32-bit decoding was found. This was a source/correctness correction, not a runtime test or whole-body credit. Source-only.

Review correction (2026-10-23): OD3129, OD3839, OD3846, OD3848 and OD4148 are withdrawn. Their dated notes below overstate positive signed shifts into the sign bit as undefined behavior; under the applicable C rules these conversions are implementation-defined. No selected compiler behavior establishing incorrect parsing, filtering, pilot masks or PTD maps was demonstrated. OD3847 remains active because its negative signed left shifts are undefined independently. Exec EK8800 was also withdrawn: the DevProc, NVMe, and ATA bit-31 mask expressions mentioned below have implementation-defined signed conversion, with no selected compiler defect demonstrated. Do not count these shift cases as active findings.

m68k Amiga mouse button-coordinate candidate review (OD2003 withdrawn as a bug candidate; 2026-10-23): followed the HIDD's consecutive VBlank motion/button callbacks through the selected `gameport.device` event queue and `input.device` forwarding to Intuition (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/mouse/mouseclass.c:50-82`; `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:618-784`; `rom/devs/input/processevents.c:312-375`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:1974-2005,2198-2209`). GamePort copies X/Y into all emitted `InputEvent`s, including button codes, but Intuition processes pointer deltas only in its `IECODE_NOBUTTON` branch; button handling does not apply those coordinates. No selected consumer therefore establishes duplicate pointer motion, and the public GamePort event-coordinate contract does not establish that button-event X/Y must be zero. Withdraw OD2003 from candidate status rather than infer a defect from external consumers. Other external GamePort clients and hardware timing remain outside this caller trace; source-only.

m68k Amiga mouse state-attribute candidate review (OD859 withdrawn; 2026-10-23): the mouse HIDD's `Root::Get` returns without writing `msg->storage` for `aoHidd_Mouse_State` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/mouse/mouseclass.c:211-229`). The selected shared HIDD mouse attribute documentation explicitly says this historical attribute is reserved and must not be used (`rom/hidds/mouse/include/mouse.h:65-82`), so the unwritten storage is not a supported API defect. No in-tree query caller was found. Source-only.

m68k potgo / LowLevel port-ownership pass (OD9424 added; 2026-10-23): read the complete `arch/m68k-amiga/lowlevel/readjoyport.c` body and all three complete potgo resource vectors, then traced the selected LowLevel manifest and Amiga boot HIDD/resource lists. The public read path uses the requested mask after an incomplete `AllocPotBits()` result, continues into autosense because `JP_TYPE_NOTAVAIL` is zero, and unconditionally passes that requested mask to `FreePotBits()` after polling. The selected AmigaMouse constructor holds `0x0f00` for port 0, establishing a checked-in owner for the failed-allocation path. Added OD9424. Full LowLevel-library API/caller coverage, direct potgo clients beyond these callers, and hardware effects remain open. No joy-port call or hardware operation was run; source-only.

m68k LowLevel `SetJoyPortAttrsA()` stub/caller pass (2026-10-23; no new finding): read the complete architecture-specific stub and compared it with the public function documentation, generic implementation, and checked-in call sites. The m68k vector walks tags but implements no operations and returns FALSE; the generic vector also returns FALSE. The debug LowLevel test invokes it for controller type/rumble setup and ignores the result, while the checked HID-class uses are through optional vector hooks (`developer/debug/test/lowlevel/lowlevel.c:140-161`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6850-6936`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:6115-6207`). OD4241 serial/parallel unit-factory cross-implementation recheck (2026-10-24; no new finding): reread all six Unix, m68k-Amiga, and PC serial/parallel `NewUnit` factory paths and their matching `DisposeUnit` slot-release paths. Each factory publishes the `OOP_NewObject()` result and marks the unit bit used without checking for NULL; each disposer requires a non-NULL object pointer matching a stored slot before clearing that bit. The `OOP_NewObject()` contract and implementation return NULL when the public class cannot be found or the root allocation fails (`rom/oop/newobject.c:80-83,104-126`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-131`). The selected serial.device/parallel.device open paths treat that NULL as failure, free their temporary unit records, and do not call `DisposeUnit()` (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:170-195`; `workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_init.c:162-184`), leaving the reservation until the parent HIDD is destroyed. This confirms OD4241's shared root cause and consequence; no separate per-backend finding was added. Both PC BSP package manifests list `serial` and `parallel` in `KHIDDS` (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:68`), while the direct `kernel-pc-i386-parallel` boot dependency edges are commented (`:62` and `:54`); package membership does not by itself establish top-level target selection. No allocation failure or device open was induced; source-only.

Deneb unit-32 in-tree reachability pass (OD4161 strengthened; 2026-10-24): traced the selected `AddUSBHardware` program manifest and its positional `DEVICE,UNIT/N` parser (`rom/usb/poseidon/shellcommands/mmakefile.src:6-17`; `AddUSBHardware.c:25,69-79,108-116`), the `psdAddHardware()` task setup and unit storage, then `pDeviceTask()` into `OpenDevice()` (`poseidon.library.c:4399-4411,9180-9183`). The command has no unit range check, so `AddUSBHardware denebusb.device 32` reaches Deneb `Open_Unit()` with 32 and the confirmed `hd_Units[32]` read occurs before any board enumeration. The subsequent out-of-bounds store still requires 33 matching boards. Updated OD4161’s in-tree trigger; no device was present/opened and no command was run. Source-only.

Setup's lock omission is not covered by the new driver's unpublished status because another public removal can mutate existing list entries. Manifest follow-up: `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:91-94,162-165,226` selects both `pcibcm2712` and `pcirp1` in the Raspberry Pi AArch64 quick/package targets, so the two independent bus-driver backends are present in this configuration; each creates a PCI object and registers its driver (`pcie2712_init.c:1008-1030`; `rp1_pci.c:274-283`). This proves multi-driver build configuration, not that either expunge/removal path runs at runtime. Added OD3636 as a distinct conditional object-lifetime race, not a duplicate of OD3563's overbroad removal filter. No driver operation was run; source-only.

BWFM association-slot concurrency and selected supplicant caller recheck (OD3635 retained, 2026-10-17): confirmed `S2_SETOPTIONS` is handled in the request's BeginIO call and reaches `TermIO` immediately after `queue_associate` publishes the single slot (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1421-1492,1788-1793,1897-1901`). The control task separately snapshots and clears that slot under the same semaphore, then performs the blocking join outside it (`:1502-1532`); two concurrent BeginIO callers can therefore replace the slot before the worker takes its snapshot. The selected WirelessManager callback copies its SSID into a bounded NUL-terminated temporary, performs synchronous `DoIO`, and releases its tag list after return (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:382-405,441-445`), so that single callback path does not itself establish overlapping requests. This keeps OD3635 conditional on concurrent/multiple SANA-II clients, with high confidence in accepted-request overwrite and no evidence of an in-tree overlap. No request concurrency was run; source-only.

USB Audio playback scheduling and AHI start/stop recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed `subLibStart`/`subLibStop` through RTIso start/stop and the timer-fallback path, then traced periodic `nOutReqHook` buffer selection, sample-count accumulation, deferred mixer interrupt, and alternating USB-buffer publication (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2544-2605,2624-2674,3680-3807`; `usbaudio.h:113-131`). AHIRecord FLAC bitreader callback short-read recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed `bitreader_read_from_client_`'s input-capacity and returned-byte accounting (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/FLAC/bitreader.c:208-287`) through the selected decoder's `read_callback_` and public read-status contract (`stream_decoder.c:2790-2857`; `stream_decoder.h:291-306,467-508`). Short positive reads are handled by the reader. A zero-byte `CONTINUE` makes the internal wrapper return success without adding data and can leave bitreader loops retrying, but the public callback contract says zero bytes indicates error/end-of-stream, and the supplied stdio example reports end-of-stream when `fread` returns zero; this is treated as an invalid callback result, not a decoder bug. Default AHIRecord recording does not use the bundled decoder, and no maintained client supplies an alternate callback. No stream or callback was run. Source-only.

GPIOSetFunc RP1 mux-contract cross-check (2026-10-17; no additional OD): compared the RP1 branch's direct `func & 0x1F` write and output-enable changes (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/gpio/gpio_init.c:95-110`) with in-tree callers using BCM `GPIO_FSEL_ALT0/ALT3` constants (`bcm2708.h:395-402`; `pl011bt_init.c:89,115`) and the GUI's generic input/output values (`workbench/c/GPIO.c:107-116`). I did not promote it as a bug without that evidence; hardware mapping verification remains open. Existing OD3480 still covers the independently established BCM2712 base-address width issue, and OD3484 the command's invalid-pin success result. Source-only.

Bluetooth HID output-array parse-error follow-up (OD3475, 2026-10-17): traced malformed array tokens through direct writes in `bParseArrayString` to `bDoAction`'s output/feature touched flags and full-array encoding (`bthid.class.c:3976-4156,3927-3970,5423-5427,5460-5464`). Bluetooth HID input-channel rearm pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): checked completion/error handling in `bHandleReport` through the binding worker loop and Bluetooth `btSendChannel` (`bthid.class.c:823-900,951-970`; `objects.c:1152-1179`). Aborted/disconnected reads wait one second; other errors are logged once per error value and wait 250 ms. Every completion is rearmed unless Ctrl-C is pending. If Bluetooth is offline, `btSendChannel` queues an immediate `BTIOERR_NOTREADY` reply, which the worker consumes and retries after the error delay. This path therefore does not leave the worker permanently waiting with no read request; no new finding established. Channel teardown and device/library lifecycle remain open. No channel or device was used. Source-only.

RP1 synthetic PCI driver client reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new OD): re-read `rp1_pci.c` end to end and traced virtual config-space probing/writes, `MapPCI`, address translation, aligned DMA allocation/free and initialization into the selected `pcixhci` client and `rp1.resource` producer. The local xHCI client pairs DMA allocation with the original returned base; resource publication occurs only after the exported register addresses are initialized. Existing OD929 covers discarded hardware-driver registration failure after RP1 MSI routes are reserved; OD1839/OD922 cover BAR/address-window behavior. SDSC CMD6 busy-retry arithmetic recheck (OD3450 withdrawn, 2026-10-17): evaluated the `while (--timeout > 0)` exit precisely (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_sdscunit.c:102-117`). With three busy responses, the fourth loop-condition evaluation decrements timeout from 1 to 0, so the following `timeout > 0` gate skips switch mode. A non-busy response breaks while timeout remains positive and permits switching. OD3450 was a false positive and has been removed from the detailed report and index. No card command was issued. Source-only.

SD-card timer-rollover type-width recheck (OD3313 expanded, 2026-10-17): compared `sdcb_Private`'s `IPTR` width with `sdcard_CurrentTime()`'s `ULONG` return across ARM32/AArch64 (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_bus.h:109`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43,85`; `sdcard_bcm2708time.c:18-20`). On the AArch64 BCM2711 Arasan fallback, `bus->sdcb_Private + 6` remains a 64-bit deadline when the 32-bit low timer wraps. A write whose timestamp is within six microseconds of rollover can therefore leave `BCM283xWriteLong` polling an unreachable deadline forever; a somewhat earlier pre-wrap timestamp can stall until the same low counter value recurs. AArch32 instead retains the skipped-minimum-delay behavior already recorded. Expanded OD3313 and narrowed this additional hang to the BCM2711 Arasan fallback; no timer or board was exercised. Source-only.

Efika PCI DMA page-attribute lifetime pass (OD3410, 2026-10-17): traced `AllocPCIMem` through the generic aligned allocator and Efika `KrnSetProtection` rounding, then `FreePCIMem` through its fixed 4096-byte restore and generic `FreeVec`. PC i8042 controller-task creation failure follow-up (OD3348, 2026-10-17): confirmed `i8042Kbd__Root__New` ignores the NULL-capable `NewCreateTask` result then waits for SIGF_SINGLE, while only the worker sends that completion signal. USB Audio sample-conversion and AHI recording contract pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): read all eight playback converters and all eight recording converters in `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2778-3132`, then traced hook selection and buffer sizing through `subLibAllocAudio` (`:3328-3538`) and `nInDoneHook` (`:2690-2737`) into AHI's S16-stereo `AHIRecordMessage` contract (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:290-300`; AHI API docs in `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c`). For 8/16/24/32-bit mono/stereo layouts, playback emits the most-significant 8/16/24/32 bits in the endpoint's little-endian sample layout, and recording expands/truncates to the required S16 stereo frame layout; conversion hook count is in frames and output buffers use the corresponding frame-size product. The known 24-bit mono byte-count fallthrough remains OD3163; shared capture-buffer reuse under multiple pending xHCI PTDs remains OD3228. No independent converter defect established. Remaining USB Audio body/caller review remains open, especially descriptor extents, interface/format negotiation and callback interleavings; this pass does not mark the file complete. No audio stream or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio high-speed interval range recheck (OD3173 expanded, 2026-10-17): confirmed Poseidon transforms every valid high-speed isochronous `bInterval` (1–16) to `1 << (bInterval - 1)` microframes (`poseidon.library.c:8483,8525-8553`); audio pacing multiplies/divides using the resulting count as if it were milliseconds (`usbaudio.class.c:3161-3166,3721-3738`). The factor-eight scale error applies even at `bInterval=4` (eight microframes = 1 ms, treated as 8 ms), not only intervals shorter than 1 ms. Expanded OD3173 trigger and example. No stream was run. Source-only.
USB Audio selected-target graph recheck (OD3168–OD3171 scope, 2026-10-17): corrected the earlier classification. `kernel-usb-classes-common` includes `kernel-usb-classes-usbaudio` (`rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:10-12`), and `kernel-usb-nopci` includes the complete class set (`rom/usb/mmakefile.src:17-22`; classes aggregate `:36-43`). ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi and riscv-native boot manifests select `kernel-usb-nopci` (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:148-150`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:157-159`; `arch/riscv-native/boot/mmakefile.src:80-87`). OpenSBI selects a subset that excludes Audio (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:87-95`). The descriptor-bounds findings therefore apply to selected Raspi/riscv-native builds when the class is installed/loaded; they are not claimed for the OpenSBI boot image. The prior commentary that the target was absent from the parent graph was incorrect; no report finding was removed. Source-only.
xHCI RTIso teardown caller recheck (OD3206 retained, 2026-10-17): verified Poseidon sends `UHCMD_REMISOHANDLER` synchronously via `DoIO`; xHCI `devBeginIO` dispatches directly to `cmdRemIsoHandler` in that caller, while a distinct event task walks and completes periodic requests. `cmdRemIsoHandler` uses `Disable()` around removal/free, not an SMP-shared lock, supporting the recorded cross-CPU overlap (`poseidon.library.c:5607-5634`; `pcixhci_dev.c:198-200,258-265`; `xhci_hw.c:523-541`; `uhwcmd.c:1545-1587`). Existing OD3206 retained; no event or teardown was run. Source-only.
USB Audio callback and teardown recheck (OD3163/OD3206 retained, 2026-10-17; no new finding): the input done hook divides a 24-bit mono byte count by three and falls through to the 32-bit four-byte case, corroborating OD3163 (`usbaudio.class.c:2707-2734`). Source-only.
USB Audio mode-allocation error and rate-ordering recheck (OD3208 retained, 2026-10-17): verified the selected AHI `_AHI_AllocAudioA` error path calls `AHI_FreeAudio`, which invokes the subdriver `FreeAudio` hook even when the allocation callback returned `AHISF_ERROR` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:481-512,518-521,656-658,712-735`). `subLibFreeAudio` guards optional endpoints/buffers and `DeleteMsgPort(NULL)` is explicitly a no-op (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3580-3664`; `rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:40-57`), so the inspected early returns do not establish an independent cleanup bug. OD3208 is confirmed: `nSelectAudioMode` sends the current `ahiac_MixFreq` before `subLibAllocAudio` adjusts it to a listed frequency, and duplex sibling setup occurs after that adjustment (`usbaudio.class.c:3134-3189,3328-3331,3375-3404,3489-3503`). Source-only.
USB Audio task-nesting consequence recheck (OD3229 retained, 2026-10-17): verified the selected Poseidon class-scan caller invokes the forced-binding method before its own `Forbid`, and that the failure branch in `usbForceInterfaceBinding` calls unmatched `Permit` before the method’s insertion `Forbid`. Exec task nesting starts at -1, decrements on `Permit`, increments on `Forbid`, and treats negative values as task-switch-enabled; therefore this does not suppress scheduling as the initial draft claimed. The following Poseidon `Forbid` reaches -1 and does not exclude task switches. Corrected OD3229’s consequence and confidence wording in the report/index. Re-read `nLoadClassConfig` and confirmed its constant FALSE return is not used by its checked callers. Remaining audio-class work includes descriptor extents, interface/format negotiation and callback interleavings. Source-only.
USB Audio sublibrary expunge ownership recheck (OD3239 retained, 2026-10-16; no additional finding): verified the successful `libInit` baseline reference is decremented before `RemLibrary`, whose sublibrary expunge vector removes the library node and frees `lib_NegSize + lib_PosSize` (`usbaudio.class.c:88-91,135-140,2491-2520`). The class expunger makes no later access through `nh_SubLibBase`. This rules out a normal successful-expunge allocation leak; the partial-init NULL dereference remains OD3239. No library open/expunge was run.
USB Audio binding predicate/caller recheck (OD3168/OD3171/OD3209/OD3230 cross-check, 2026-10-16; no new OD): `nVerifyAudioStreamDevice` accepts only AudioControl interfaces whose v1.0 header names at least one matching AudioStreaming interface, but reads `bcdADC` and `bInCollection` before checking descriptor length; these header extent issues remain OD3168/OD3171 (`usbaudio.class.c:166-218`). `usbAttemptInterfaceBinding` closes its temporary Poseidon library handle before entering the force-binding method, which opens its own handle (`:224-241`). Poseidon invokes Attempt only when the interface has no binding (`poseidon.library.c:6353-6389`); the force path then publishes its class record before worker startup, matching OD3209, while concurrent list selection/publication remains OD3230. No separate accepted-interface or duplicate-binding consequence was established in this pass. No descriptor, interface binding, device, or hardware was used.
AHCI zero-sector-count cross-check (DISK-121 revalidated; no new OD, 2026-10-16): re-read READ/WRITE(6/10/12/16) decoding, ATA FIS count selection and PRDT construction (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_scsi.c:443-543`; `rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:2108-2128`). READ/WRITE(10/12/16) zero counts remain zero; the LBA28 path explicitly documents ATA count zero as 256 sectors, while NCQ/LBA48 also submit zero in their count fields. `ahci_load_prdt` creates no PRDT for zero `scsi_Length`, so the source supports a SCSI no-op becoming a non-no-op ATA command with a zero-length DMA mapping, but does not establish what hardware does with that mismatch. DISK-121 already covers this exact zero-count semantic mismatch, so no duplicate OD finding was added. No command/device was exercised; source-only.

Gameport trigger predicate caller recheck (OD3215, 2026-10-16; retained, direct-client scope): a repository search found `gpu_trigger` is assigned by `GPD_SETTRIGGER`, returned by `GPD_ASKTRIGGER`, and otherwise read only inside the disabled `#if 0` predicate in `fillrequest` (`rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:371-390,727-736`). The selected input.device sets `GPTF_DOWNKEYS | GPTF_UPKEYS` and zero deltas, so its normal mouse request is permissive and does not establish a selected visible mismatch (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:147-153,230-240`). USB audio terminal-name capacity follow-up (OD3176, 2026-10-16): traced the fallback name collection across every non-streaming terminal against the eight-pointer arrays, then followed the over-count through `nAddAudioModes`, `subLibGetAttr`, and AHI mode-info string copying. The ninth input write overlaps `nam_NumOutputs`; the ninth output write overlaps `nam_Tags`; the published count and unchecked getter can therefore expose invalid names/counts. A valid range containing none of those discrete AHI rates leaves `nam_NumFrequencies` at zero, yet the mode is registered; the selected AHI maximum-rate query then subtracts one and reaches the unchecked array lookup. USB Audio endpoint interval and mode-selection unwind recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced Poseidon's endpoint descriptor parser through the `EA_Interval` value consumed by `nSelectAudioMode` and the selected `psdSetAltInterface`/AHI allocation-failure cleanup. Full-speed and high-speed isochronous endpoint `bInterval == 0` are both normalized to 1 before the audio class reads them (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8520-8553,8590-8610`), so the suspected zero-interval divisor is not supported for those speeds; SuperSpeed isochronous zero interval is likewise normalized (`:8495-8517`). If mode selection or a later allocation step fails after changing the alternate setting, cleanup can leave it selected when the device has no zero-bandwidth alternate; that path is already covered by OD3361 (`usbaudio.class.c:3134-3167,3328-3329`; AHI unwind `audioctrl.c:656-658,712-728`). No descriptor, device, interface switch or allocation was exercised. Source-only.

USB Audio discrete sample-rate filtering recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed the `bSamFreqType` loop when it skips advertised frequencies above 64 kHz (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1220-1253`). Although the loop decrements `nam_NumFrequencies` and `cnt` together, this keeps `cnt` as the destination index among retained rates while `fptr` advances across every descriptor entry; e.g. `[96000, 44100, 48000]` leaves exactly `[44100, 48000]`, with no uninitialized hole. `nam_MinFreq` is also updated before filtering, but a retained in-range rate lowers it below any skipped high rate. The all-filtered/zero-count case remains OD3172; no separate mixed-list omission or bogus zero frequency was found. No descriptor or mode database was used; source-only.

UHCI constructor allocation boundary recheck (OD2963; 2026-10-15): expanded the existing unchecked schedule/TD finding to include `UHCI::Root::New`'s unchecked PCI frame-list allocation and subsequent 1,024-entry write (`uhciclass.c:417-420,484-486`). Also traced OOP_NewObject failure into HIDD_USB_AttachDriver; AttachDriver returns FALSE on a NULL object, so no separate null-object dereference candidate is added. Count unchanged. No allocation failure or controller was run. Source-only.

UHCI completion error-interrupt pass (OD2971, 2026-10-15): traced enabled timeout/CRC interrupt status through uhci_Handler and the synchronous control/bulk wait loops. The handler gates on USBINT, acknowledges status and skips queue/error processing when that bit is absent; non-final TDs lack IOC, while selected MassStorage waiters use a 10-second timer and zero-timeout callers have no timer. Added OD2971, qualified to the hardware's error-only status case. No transfer was run. Source-only.

UHCI DMA alignment and SMP allocator pass (OD2970, 2026-10-15): verified the PCI HIDD allocator contract guarantees page alignment and the checked generic method returns NULL on allocation failure; no page-mask or sentinel mismatch was promoted. Found the actual concurrency issue: UHCI's library-shared descriptor bitmap/list uses only Disable around test/set, insertion, removal and reclamation, while ExecSMP Disable is CPU-local. The x86_64-pc SMP target selects kernel-package-usb and that package includes UHCI. Added OD2970. No controller or SMP race was run. Source-only.

UHCI failed interrupt-registration cleanup pass (OD2969, 2026-10-15): traced AllocVecPooled failure from UHCI AddInterrupt through HID::New and HID::Dispose into RemInterrupt. ForeachNode exits on the non-null tail sentinel, and the truthy check sends it to Exec Remove, which dereferences the null successor. Added OD2969. Rechecked `intr->i_td`: although normal registration never initializes it, the UHCI pool requests MEMF_CLEAR and Exec stdAlloc clears each allocation, so the fresh record field is NULL; no uninitialized-pointer candidate is added. No allocation failure or disposal was run. Source-only.

UHCI descriptor and remaining class-method pass (2026-10-15; no additional finding): read `uhciclass.c:1080-1255`, tracing root-hub power/feature methods, the two-port descriptor and interrupt endpoint, USB device descriptors, UTF-16LE strings, and `UHCI_InitClass`/expunge. The fixed descriptor sizes and selected USBDevice string decoding agree; class init still has the separate OD2961 attachment issue. Full class lifecycle review remains open. Source-only.

UnixIO Wait readiness-registration race restoration (OD115, 2026-10-15): restored the missing detailed entry after tracing the one-shot poll, stack waiter registration, fcntl O_ASYNC setup and unconditional Wait in `UXIO_Wait`, then the selected LinuxInput Wait/ReadFile loop. The missed wake is explicitly conditional on host behavior when arming async notification for an already-readable descriptor; no host behavior was run. Darwin periodic polling is excluded. Source-only.

UnixIO interrupt-list initialization ordering recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): `UXIO_Init` registers SIGIO and, on Darwin, SIGALRM before `NewList(&intList)` (`arch/all-unix/hidd/unixio/unixio_class.c:1173-1195`), which initially suggested an interrupt could traverse an uninitialized list. The selected hosted kickstart includes both `kernel-unixio` and `kernel-timer` (`arch/all-unix/boot/mmakefile.src:31-47`); the residents have priorities 91 and 50 respectively (`unixio.conf:4`; `rom/timer/timer.conf:5`), the selected resident sorter orders higher priorities first (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:104-120`), and InitCode walks that ordered list (`rom/exec/initcode.c:69-95`). UnixIO initialization therefore precedes Timer_Init, whose `setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, ...)` call starts SIGALRM (`arch/all-unix/timer/timer_init.c:143-155`). SIGIO also lacks a selected pre-init UnixIO registration producer. The Darwin callback window is not reachable on the checked startup sequence; no candidate promoted. External host signal state and nonstandard module-load sequences remain unverified. Source-only.

OHCI replacement-tail failure follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2903): rechecked `ohci_AllocTD` allocation failures against `AddInterrupt` publication and the selected HID caller. The replacement-tail failure is distinct from allocation of the interrupt bookkeeping record and from failed `CreatePipe`: this path leaves an invalid queue but returns success. The detailed finding and index are updated; no low-memory condition or controller was exercised. Report count is 263 OD; broader USB/controller coverage remains open. Source-only.

BCM2708 I²C candidate reconciliation (2026-10-14): restored five coverage-only candidates as OD2834–OD2838 after tracing the packaged subclass through generated class startup, inherited `i2c.hidd` transaction dispatch and its byte methods. Both Raspberry Pi package lists include the HIDD, but no in-tree class instantiation was found; runtime use remains conditional. No module or hardware was run.

MassStorage media-sense error-path follow-up (OD2832, 2026-10-14): traced startup and periodic TestUnitReady failure through RequestSense to DirectSCSI. Both callers inspect `sense[2]` regardless of the method result; DirectSCSI can fail before receiving data, leaving the local 18-byte buffer uninitialized and allowing false disk-present transitions. Added OD2832. Source-only; no USB transfer was run. The separate DISK-027 write-chunk defect was rechecked and remains cross-referenced rather than duplicated here.

USB MassStorage teardown/transfer race follow-up (OD2831, 2026-10-14): traced hub disconnect disposal into `Storage::Dispose`, the per-LUN worker's synchronous HandleIO/DirectSCSI path, and both selected controller bulk-transfer implementations. Dispose only signals workers and immediately deletes pipes; OHCI does not take the pipe semaphore in DeletePipe and frees the timeout/ED/pipe, while UHCI bulk has no pipe lock and DeletePipe frees queued TDs/pipe. Hub worker priority 10 exceeds LUN worker priority 1, making preemption during an in-flight worker request a source-supported interleaving. Added OD2831. Source-only; no hardware or timing test was run.

ACPICA OS-glue caller recheck: the checkout pins fetched ACPICA release 20260408 in `arch/all-native/acpica/mmakefile.src:6-25`, but its source archive is not present in this repository. The complete local symbol search finds definitions, not direct in-tree callers, for `AcpiOsExecute`, `AcpiOsWaitEventsComplete`, `AcpiOsSleep` and `AcpiOsStall`; `ACPICA_InitTask` is locally launched by the post-Exec resident and calls `AcpiInitializeSubsystem`, handler installation, and standalone table/object initialization (`acpios_aros.c:979-1034,1138-1164`). Therefore OS-hook behavior that depends on ACPICA’s external callers remains pending; the existing `AcpiOsExecute` stub is not counted as a concrete selected failure without a caller path. Timer availability/order, firmware behavior and asynchronous startup remain pending. No library, firmware, or hardware was run.

OHCI attribute-base caller recheck (no new driver finding): generic `OHCI_Init` ignores `OOP_ObtainAttrBases`'s result for five interfaces, but generated OHCI class startup runs before INITLIB and registers its `Root`, `Hidd_USBDevice`, `Hidd_USBHub` and `Hidd_USBDrv` interfaces (`ohci.conf:18-45`; `tools/genmodule/oopsupport.c:49-59,208-215`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:42-62`). The selected PCI HIDD initialization also obtains `IID_Hidd_PCIDevice` before making the PCI object available (`rom/hidds/pci/pci_init.c:29-49`). Therefore these selected OHCI IDs already have buckets on ordinary startup, and the earlier/final attrbase-allocation failure paths do not supply a demonstrated low-memory trigger through this call; generic OOP helper failures remain GD1214/GD1216. Efika's package selects its separate built-in OHCI initializer and bypasses this generic enumerator (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/boot/mmakefile.src:83-91`). No module or hardware was run.

PC i8042 constructor-handshake recheck (OD2320/OD2321): OD2320 covers both New methods ignoring a NULL NewCreateTask result before waiting; NewCreateTaskA returns NULL on allocation/task setup failure. OD2321 now details the distinct keyboard-worker failure: port/request/timer-open failure reports through the still-NULL CtrlTask field and faults before waking New. The root allocator clears instance storage. These are separate absent-worker and started-worker failure paths. No allocation or device-open failure was induced.

RTL8139 failed-startup rollback recheck (OD2319): followed a failed worker setup through the parent handshake into the common `DeleteUnit` call. The worker can be released to clean up and exit before the parent unconditionally signals its stored task pointer; signal-zero exhaustion also leaves `signal_0 == -1` for `1 << signal_0`. Exec SMP `Signal` dereferences the task before checking terminal state, and the service task can reclaim a self-removed worker. The subsequent name wait separately inherits EK799's transient false-absence window. No startup failure or teardown was run.

OHCI/HID teardown recheck (2026-10-11, OD2443): reread `Cause` and `SoftIntDispatch`, OHCI done-list completion and `DeletePipe`, HID `Root::Dispose`, and USB hub disconnect disposal. Exec SMP's `SoftInts[pri].sh_SpinLock` covers enqueue/dequeue only; dispatch releases it before invoking `is_Code`. OHCI `DeletePipe` sets ED_K, unlinks the ED, frees pending TDs/timer/ED/pipe, but has no callback-node removal or in-flight wait. HID then frees `hid->buffer` and delegates object disposal. The source confirms a queued-or-running callback lifetime gap under cross-CPU ExecSMP overlap, but the package-route recheck found checked-in OHCI/HID routes are Sam440/Efika; no checked-in ExecSMP configuration selecting this package was found. OD2443 remains a conditional source-level configuration concern, not a demonstrated shipped configuration. No USB device, disconnect or scheduler interleaving was run.

Speechcore prosody bounds recheck (2026-10-11): reread `ScanPhrase`, `MarkBoundaries`, `NextPhrase`, all eight 128-byte prosody arrays, and the phrase-level pitch/range/contour consumers. The phrase builder rejects a cumulative count above 128 before later phrase writes; per-phrase descriptor writes are bounded before indexing, and the contour interpolation remains between marked syllables. This pass found no additional prosody-array bounds defect. It does not close frame-side pitch indexing or static table semantics; the earlier custom-voice prefix read was provisionally labeled OD2487; that candidate was withdrawn on 2026-10-26 after checking the public resource/API construction paths. No speech output was generated.

Speechcore frame/pitch index recheck (2026-10-11): traced `SCSpreadStress` primaries through `ScanPhrase`, `MarkContour`, `AssignPitch`, and the frame writer. One prosody entry is produced per primary marker; the phrase accumulator rejects a 128th entry, so AssignPitch's `v` index remains within the 127 populated slots. Frame pitch writes go through `PutPitch`'s byte-length check, and transition writes use `MarkOne`'s range check; the sentinel occupies the extra allocated frame. No additional index or transition-write candidate was established. OD9642's short-stream interpolation overread remains separate. No speech output was generated.

NVMe removal caller recheck (2026-10-15; OD2960 retained): re-read generic `HW_RemoveDriver` registration removal and disposal, then searched all checked-in direct callers. No NVMe controller removal caller was found. NVMe is configured `noexpunge`, which prevents module expunge but does not alter `HW_RemoveDriver`'s object-disposal contract; `NVME__Hidd_StorageController__RemoveBus` separately reports removal unsupported. Its class inherits the generic setup method, which always succeeds, so the failed-setup disposal branch does not supply an ordinary in-tree NVMe trigger. OD2960 remains conditional on a public manager/client removing a registered NVMe controller. No object was removed. Source-only.

Optional iOS UIKit candidate restoration (2026-10-15; OD2639, OD2645, OD2646, OD2785, OD2794, OD2795): restored the detailed startup/task-publication, native-window rollback, startup-result, expunge ordering, viewport, and CopyBox findings from the reviewed source rows. Rechecked the local call paths; the four `#MM` dependency lines are commented, no checked-in parent build/package edge references `kernel-hidd-uikit`, and `arch/all-ios/README.txt` says no UIKit display driver is available. These findings are therefore limited to explicitly building/loading this optional target, not a checked-in default image. No iOS build, display, interrupt, or scheduling test was run. Source-only.

PC SMBIOS IPMI class-lifetime candidate restoration (2026-10-15; OD1687 restored): traced the selected x86-64 PC boot package’s `smbios-ipmi` module through successful `HW_AddDriver` registration and generated OOP class expunge. The initializer retains no child handles, removes no registered drivers, and does not pin the module after success; its config does not set `noexpunge`. No in-tree expunge caller or runtime teardown was found. Source-only.

ATA bus discovery timer-open failure and selected caller pass (OD9425 added; 2026-10-23): traced all `ata_InitBus()` work behind `ata_OpenTimer()` through the cleared OOP instance state and `Hidd_ATABus_Start()`'s empty-device cases (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:2723-2777`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:112-128`; `rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:511-566,972-1011`). If timer setup fails, both device types remain zero/`DEV_NONE`. With `KeepEmpty=TRUE`, the bus still receives a number and start returns TRUE without spawning its discovery task. The selected PCI probe retains non-legacy empty buses and the storage-controller setup reports this success (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/probe.c:630-632`; `rom/devs/ata/ata_controllerclass.c:125-160`); the Amiga Gayle probe sets `KeepEmpty=FALSE` and rejects the empty bus. Added OD9425 for conditional missing-drive detection masked as successful empty-bus registration. No timer failure, controller, or device scan was induced; source-only.

ATA OD9425 failed-start teardown cross-check (2026-10-23; no separate finding): checked both `KeepEmpty` branches through `StorageController__Hidd_StorageController__AddBus()` and `ATABus__Root__Dispose()` (`rom/hidds/base/storage/storage_controllerclass.c:85-126`; `rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:581-604`). With `KeepEmpty=FALSE`, failed empty-bus setup is disposed; the ATA destructor removes the reset callback and frees allocated PIO/DMA interface blocks. This did not establish a separate callback/object leak. With `KeepEmpty=TRUE`, the empty bus is accepted, which remains the specific OD9425 consequence. No HIDD registration, disposal or IRQ was run; source-only.

# other-drivers file-by-file audit tracker

<a id="sam440-direct-serial-unit-root-new-bounds-pass-od2509"></a>
Sam440 direct serial-unit constructor bounds recheck (OD2509 expanded; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit): compared `serial.conf`'s registered `CLID_Hidd_SerialUnit`/Root.New method with `PPC4xxSerUnit__Root__New()`. The constructor consumes `aHidd_SerialUnit_Unit` and indexes `bases[unitnum]` without a range check (`arch/ppc-sam440/serial.hidd/serial.conf:24-36`; `SerialUnitClass.c:90-125`); both `bases[]` and `cs_Unit[]` contain four entries (`SerialUnitClass.c:87-88`; `serial_intern.h:57-66`). Its parent `NewUnit` factory limits ordinary calls to 0–3 (`SerialClass.c:45-72`), so the trigger is direct OOP construction, not serial.device. The base-array access precedes the currently compile-invalid `class_static_data.sd_Unit` store; therefore fixing OD4005's blockers does not itself add a bounds guard. Consolidated this same constructor-boundary defect with PC serial OD2509. The Sam440 target remains optional, absent from the checked default package, and unbuildable as written. No object, build, or UART access was used; source-only.

<a id="sam440-default-baud-preference-recheck-od2536"></a>
Sam440 serial default-baud preference cross-check (OD2536 expanded; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `PPC4xxSerUnit__Root__New()` against the Intuition default preferences, the setter range, and serial.device's first-open path. The constructor copies `prefs.BaudRate` (default 5, defined as `BAUD_9600`) directly into `data->baudrate` (`arch/ppc-sam440/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:127-137`; `rom/intuition/intuition_preferences.h:6-14`; `compiler/include/intuition/preferences.h:143-149`), then calls `set_baudrate()` whose accepted range begins at 50 (`SerialUnitClass.c:588-593`) and ignores its FALSE result (`:173`). `serial.device` creates the HIDD unit only during Open and then initializes callbacks/publishes the unit without applying a baud value (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:170-184`). This is the same OD2536 preference-to-setter mismatch already recorded for PC/OpenSBI, scoped for Sam440 to explicit target use after the compile blockers OD4005 are repaired; the target is not in the checked default board package. The resulting wire rate still depends on the firmware's prior divisor. No HIDD, serial.device, baud change, build or I/O was run; source-only.

<a id="sam440-serial-irq-array-and-handler-context-reconciliation-od4006-od4008"></a>
Sam440 serial OD4006/OD4008 data-flow reconciliation (2026-11-01; report wording corrected; no new ID or LOC credit): checked the full `class_static_data` field order (`serial_intern.h:57-66`) against PPC32 stores in `GetIRQs(int *)` (`serial_init.c:27,40-54,69-72`). Its 16-byte write starts at the four-byte `cs_IRQ` array: the first int occupies the IRQ bytes, and the following three ints overwrite `cs_Unit[0..2]` before registration. The handler loop therefore reads both malformed IRQ-byte values and overwritten context pointers; `cs_Unit[3]` retains its pre-unit state. Separately traced `serial.device` opening the HIDD library before it creates a unit (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:74-91,170-174`): the one-time `ADD2INITLIB` registration is not repeated when a unit is later constructed, so fixing only the array overrun still leaves stale pre-unit handler data. The unit constructor's attempted store is to nonexistent `class_static_data.sd_Unit` (`SerialUnitClass.c:141`; `serial_intern.h:57-66`), already within OD4005's compile-blocker scope. Corrected OD4006 to include malformed IRQ vector values and OD4008 to distinguish stale/corrupt pre-unit context from a blanket NULL claim. Generated `hidd/irq.h` callback-data semantics and runtime handler behavior remain unverified; the explicit target is still unbuildable as checked in and is not in the checked default Sam440 boot package. No IRQ, build, device, or I/O was run; source-only.

PCNet32 reply-publication caller follow-up (OD3130; 2026-10-17): rechecked the worker's `ReplyMsg` then `request->io_Unit` dereference (`pcnet32/handler.c:184-187`) against Exec's reply publication and `WaitIO` contract (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`; `rom/exec/waitio.c:50-80`). The maintained AROSTCP SANA-II shutdown path waits on outstanding requests and immediately deletes each returned request (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:579-589`), confirming that a replied request's storage is client-owned/reusable after completion. Exec `Signal` explicitly handles a signaled waiting task being run on another CPU or rescheduled locally before the caller continues (`rom/exec/signal.c:359-385`). This supports OD3130's post-reply lifetime hazard; the specific concurrent reuse still depends on the reply task's scheduling and was not induced. No request was issued. Source-only.

PCNet32 RX DMA buffer stride cross-file recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): checked `pcnet32_open`'s RX descriptor addresses against the allocator extent and receive-side descriptor lookup (`pcnet32.c:306-320,357-362`; `unit.c:304-310,380-386`; `pcnet32.h:392-409,430-456`). `rx_buffer` is a `struct eth_frame *`, not a byte pointer, so `&rx_buffer[i]` advances by one full frame (1544 bytes); allocation is `RX_RING_SIZE * RXTX_ALLOC_BUFSIZE`, and the same index selects the descriptor and receive frame. The apparent one-byte stride is not a defect. Existing RX descriptor findings OD3078/OD3079 concern FCS and chained-descriptor semantics, respectively. No frame or hardware was used. Source-only.

PCNet32 Open/configure/online ordering follow-up (2026-10-17; no new OD): confirmed the Open vector starts the controller before `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE`; that command updates the init-block MAC bytes, and `S2_ONLINE` calls `start` only while IFF_UP is clear (`pcnet32_init.c:208-245`; `handler.c:328-352,667-684`; `pcnet32.c:286-295,418-438`). The selected AROSTCP client first obtains the station address with `S2_GETSTATIONADDRESS`, saves it as `ss_hwaddr`, then supplies the same saved address to `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:355-382,465-475`), so this ordering does not establish a wrong-address result on that maintained caller. `CmdOnEvent` reports the current IFF_UP state to later listeners (`handler.c:566-605`). Without a checked SANA-II contract establishing that Open must leave the unit offline, no separate protocol violation is promoted; custom-address and external-client behavior remains unverified. No request or device was used. Source-only.

PCNet32 statistics lifecycle recheck (OD3070-OD3072; 2026-10-17): traced `S2_TRACKTYPE`, `S2_UNTRACKTYPE` and `S2_GETTYPESTATS` through the serialized worker and the RX/TX callbacks (`handler.c:366-523`; `unit.c:435-442,564-570,1024-1029`). Confirmed OD3071 covers the NULL global-tracker copy on allocation failure and the early `user_count` increment that remains after duplicate/baseline-allocation errors; OD3070 separately covers callback traversal racing tracker removal on ExecSMP; OD3072 covers baselines and unit tracker nodes lost on Close/DeleteUnit. `CmdGetTypeStats` has no independently reachable missing-tracker state in the serialized non-racing path after a successful TrackType; if callbacks race UntrackType, that lifetime case is already captured by OD3070. No additional finding or duplicate ID added. No tracking request or callback was run. Source-only.

PCNet32 configured-address application follow-up (OD3645; 2026-10-17): traced the selected Open vector into `pcnet32_open`, which writes the init block and issues the controller initialization before setting IFF_UP (`pcnet32_init.c:223-245`; `pcnet32.c:331-374,418-438`). `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` then mutates only the init-block `phys_addr` through `pcnet32_set_mac`; it neither reinitializes nor stops the running controller (`handler.c:328-352`; `pcnet32.c:286-295`). `S2_ONLINE` only calls `start` when IFF_UP is clear (`handler.c:667-684`). Added OD3645 for a configured address differing from the pre-Open address; the maintained AROSTCP path configures the station address it queried, so that caller does not establish the trigger. No device or request was used. Source-only.

OHCI control-transfer size and post-DMA follow-up (OD2906 expanded; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): traced the 8 KiB guard through SETUP/STATUS construction and the unconditional completion cache call. For input buffers at or above 8192, no DATA descriptor is queued, but `CachePostDMA(msg->buffer, &length, 0)` still runs (`ohcidriverclass.c:861-879,964-974`). The selected USB stack can pass the allocated full configuration buffer using the device's 16-bit `wTotalLength` (`usbclass.c:306-311`). USB configuration `wTotalLength` endian candidate recheck (no new OD or coverage credit; 2026-10-27): checked the suspected direct assignment `request.wLength = config.wTotalLength` in `workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbclass.c:306-310` against the packed `USBDevice_Request` layout (`workbench/devs/USB/include/usb_core.h:22-29`) and `AROS_WORD2LE`/`AROS_LE2WORD` definitions (`compiler/arossupport/include/macros.h:257-278`). On big-endian PPC, the descriptor field contains little-endian bytes and the packed request field expects the same wire byte representation; direct field-to-field assignment preserves those bytes. The separate `AROS_LE2WORD` conversion is correctly used to obtain the host allocation length. Therefore the direct assignment is not an endian defect, and no finding is added. No request was sent or target built; source-only.

USB HID signed absolute-axis recheck (2026-10-15; OD2301 restored): USB HID 1.11 §6.2.2.7 defines signed report values when either logical bound is negative. The selected USBMouse code passes that raw value in `IENewTablet` with `range=max-min+1`, and selected Intuition divides the value by the range without subtracting `min`; for a valid -127..127 absolute axis, zero is the midpoint but maps to the screen origin.
