PC serial sibling-unit IRQ lifetime recheck (OD2781, 2026-10-14): followed the non-owner port's final close from `serial.device` unit removal through HIDD Dispose and the shared interrupt callback. The second unit has no `unitsdh`, so it skips `RemIntServer`; local `Disable` only masks the disposing CPU, while `common_serial_int_handler` can already hold its unit pointer on another CPU before the slot is cleared and the object freed. This is distinct from OD2779's server-owner removal and OD1454's post-unlink null device lookup. No port or interrupt was used.

OHCI constructor/failed-init recheck: restored the missed VBlank request issue as finding 208 after tracing `CreateIORequest`'s null return into Exec `OpenDevice`'s direct dereference. Added finding 2102 for failed HCCA/ED allocations (allocator returns null on PCI DMA/page allocation failure) reaching unchecked root-constructor writes; OD2318 now details the failed-init cleanup gap: the USB object and later PCI-side objects/references are not disposed after a subsequent init failure. Existing OD1604 was restored with exact `ohci_CreateTimer`→`ohci_Delay` call and null-return chain; this differs from finding 208's second, embedded VBlank request. OHCI class initialization's ignored class/object/attach failures are now grouped with the same UHCI behavior under finding 218. These are source-only checks; no controller, allocation failure or module load was exercised.

Raspberry Pi battclock SET-result/caller recheck (OD1953): `ResetBattClock` calls `WriteBattClock(0)` (`rom/battclock/resetbattclock.c:40-48`), and selected `SetClock RESET` dispatches to it (`workbench/c/SetClock.c:166-170`). `WriteBattClock` calls `MBoxCall` without checking its returned pointer (`arch/arm-raspi/battclock/writebattclock.c:41-53`), and then independently writes the requested Amiga time to `DEVS:battclock` (`:61-77`). `mbox_call_locked` returns `(volatile unsigned int *)-1` for invalid requests or when its bounded wait expires, and returns the original message pointer only after a reply with the matching channel and physical address (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/mbox/mbox_init.c:34-43,73-108`). Even when a transport reply arrives, the caller does not check the RTC property response status. On a later successful GET, `ReadBattClock` returns a hardware timestamp greater than the Amiga epoch before trying the file fallback (`readbattclock.c:41-64,68-89`). Therefore if SET is rejected or not applied while GET continues to return the previous valid clock value, the newly saved fallback is ignored and callers see stale time. If a rejected reset leaves a prior valid hardware time, the selected `ReadBattClock` returns it before reading the zero fallback, so this caller establishes a direct reset/read inconsistency. The physical RTC's SET/GET behavior remains unverified; OD1834 separately covers loss of an older fallback file on a short/failed DOS write. No mailbox call was made.

AHI-Handler pathname mutation follow-up (OD1951): traced DOS's public `Open(CONST_STRPTR, ...)` through `InternalOpen`'s device-name suffix and `fs_Open` to the selected handler packet (`rom/dos/open.c:31-35,129,211-219`; `fs_driver.c:47-58`). On `AROS_FAST_BSTR`, `C2BSTR` is an identity cast and freeing is a no-op (`rom/dos/dos_intern.h:295-297`); the packet's BSTR address therefore aliases the caller string. The AHI handler's slash-to-space loop mutates that alias before copying (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:313-315,323-345`). The documented `AUDIO:PRIORITY/1` form confirms a slash-bearing valid path (`workbench/devs/AHI/Docs/ahiusr.texinfo:777-785`). Thus string-literal/read-only storage can fault and a writable caller buffer is changed; ordinary BSTR builds copy and do not take this path. A repo search found no checked-in direct `Open("AUDIO:...")` C caller, so this is a public API/configuration trigger rather than an in-tree client reproduction. No open call was run.

CharMap selection and line-shift follow-up (OD2051): `C_INSERT_LINE` and `C_DELETE_LINE` swap/clear backing-line contents without changing the mouse selection's stored line pointers or row coordinates (`rom/devs/console/charmapconclass.c:739-795,893-922,1524-1533,1563-1574`). The standard superclass moves the corresponding pixels with `ScrollRaster` (`stdconclass.c:589-633`). A three-row selection of row-one `AAA` followed by CSI `L` at row zero moves the highlighted pixels to row two, while Copy still reads the now-empty row-one pointer (`charmapconclass.c:1311-1337`). Redraw uses the stale row coordinate (`:1018-1099`) and does not reconcile the selection. The destination row remains the same linked `charmap_line`, but `charmap_resize(..., 0)` frees its text storage and clears its text pointer (`rom/devs/console/charmap.c:61-139`); the stale Copy route therefore observes an empty line and loses the visible selection, not a freed-text use-after-free. The in-tree `C_INSERT_LINE`/`C_DELETE_LINE` dispatch is selected by the CharMap console unit (`charmapconclass.c:905-922`; `consoleclass.c:475-490`). This resolves the earlier open question in the CharMap row below. No console sequence was run.

Build-selection correction (OD2210 withdrawn): the legacy `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/ata/ata_amiga.c` path is not selected. The architecture ATA manifest supplies only `waitnano` (`arch/m68k-amiga/devs/ata/mmakefile.src:7-12`), and the generic `ATA_DEVICEFILES` list does not include `ata_amiga` (`rom/devs/ata/mmakefile.src:21-33`). The disk report independently records the related tuple observation as inactive-source DISK-317. Card-resource review therefore retains only the selected boot RAM-card and Prism2/EtherLink3 caller paths; prior ATA caller traces are not evidence for selected behavior.

Native m68k Amiga device-tree inventory at the pinned snapshot: all 19 checked-in `.c`/`.h` paths under `arch/m68k-amiga/devs` were compared with this ledger. Eleven CD, CD32 MPEG and Paula audio paths have individual rows here. The eight without rows are four ATA sources (`ata_amiga.c`, `bus_pci.c`, `dma_generic.c`, `waitnano.c`) and four trackdisk C/header paths (`trackdisk_{device,hw}.{c,h}`); those are assigned to the separate disk subsystem report, whose complete file coverage has not been independently rechecked by this ongoing other-driver audit. A card-resource caller cross-check found ATA's short-configuration-tuple length mismatch, but the current ATA override selects only `waitnano`; DISK-317 records that inactive-source observation as withdrawn rather than counting it as an active bug. This is an inventory/scope boundary, not a claim that all eleven tracked paths are fully reviewed.

Gameport result-count follow-up (OD1191): reread all `BeginIO` command branches, `fillrequest`, the queued reply walk and selected input.device's request setup/consumption (`rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:302-448,581-785`; `rom/devs/input/processevents.c:216-251,530-575`). OD1191 is detailed in AROS-other-drivers.md: `GPD_READEVENT` can return fewer event records than fit in `io_Length` but neither the immediate nor queued path sets `io_Actual`. The selected input.device reads one event and checks `io_Error`, so stale-count impact remains scoped to direct clients that inspect the result count. `GPD_ASKCTYPE` and `GPD_ASKTRIGGER` also return fixed-size data without updating `io_Actual`, but no checked-in C client of either query was found and no separate query candidate is credited. Device-request runtime and external clients remain open.

Netinfo iterator reset follow-up (OD2879/OD2263/OD1911; no new candidate): reread the legacy password and group `set*ent`/`get*ent` wrappers against netinfo's `ResetCmd`, `ReadCmd`, `InternalSetEnts` and initial per-open cursor (`workbench/libs/usergroup/getpwent.c:199-263`; `getgrent.c:207-271`; `workbench/devs/netinfo/entries.c:161-197,371-463`; `server.c:216-236`). `ResetCmd` always writes a successful `io_Error` after obtaining the list head, even when opening or allocating for the initial parse failed; both wrappers discard the synchronous reset result and mark the shared `setent_done` flag. OD1911 remains only a qualified error-conflation concern: a failed initial open or scratch-buffer allocation leaves the empty map and ResetCmd reports success, but no stronger caller-visible contract violation was established. The shared cross-database flag is OD2879. `ReadCmd` advances before its copy-out error, confirming OD2263; the wrappers neither retry nor reset after that error. No separate reset-failure candidate is counted. Security-library forwarding and external direct-device callers remain outside this selected legacy-client trace; no database access was run.

AHI Filesave failed-start ownership recheck (OD179): reread the complete Filesave `_AHIsub_AllocAudio`, `_AHIsub_FreeAudio`, `_AHIsub_Start` and `_AHIsub_Stop` paths against AHI `ControlAudio` and `FreeAudio` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-main.c:69-406`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:697-735,1000-1020`). A failed Start returns its error directly to `ControlAudio` without stopping, so playback and recording buffers can remain allocated while the control is retained. On final control release after a successful subdriver allocation, AHI invokes `AHIsub_Stop(PLAY|RECORD)` before Filesave's `FreeAudio`, which does release those buffers. A failure in Filesave's earlier `AllocAudio` follows the AHI allocation-error cleanup route and involves requesters/signals, not these Start buffers. OD179 was withdrawn after the caller trace confirmed buffers are owned by the live control and reclaimed on retry or final FreeAudio; no persistent leak was established. Runtime failure timing and external clients remain open.

IFFParse rejected-header follow-up (OD1402; no new candidate): reread `OpenIFF`, `GetChunkHeader`, `PushContextNode`, `GoodType`, the DOS/clipboard cleanup hooks and selected Printer preferences and `C:Clip` read callers (`workbench/libs/iffparse/{openiff.c:73-139,basicfuncs.c:27-70,184-246,goodtype.c:42-85,dosstreamhandler.c:60-79,clipboardfuncs.c:116-157}`; `workbench/prefs/printer/prefs.c:94-110`; `workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:252-266`). A first noncomposite chunk inherits the zero type of the root context; `GoodType(0)` rejects it inside `PushContextNode`, so it does not reach `OpenIFF`'s post-success noncomposite branch. The supported error path remains OD1402: after `GetChunkHeader` fails, `OpenIFF` overwrites that error with the cleanup hook result, and both selected hooks can return zero while `IFFF_OPEN` remains clear. `CloseIFF` then returns immediately on that unopened handle and `FreeIFF` frees only the embedded root; the selected callers close their own DOS or clipboard handles. No separate stream-allocation leak or successful noncomposite-open claim is credited. Custom stream-handler cleanup contracts and runtime malformed-input behavior remain open.

Serial/parallel opener-race correction (OD82): the selected LDDemon `OpenDevice` replacement holds a per-name semaphore across the Exec open vector (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:369-391,469-494,533-559`), excluding same-name open/open interleavings. Its `CloseDevice` replacement invokes the close vector under only local `Forbid()` and does not acquire that semaphore (`lddemon.c:597-624`); the selected serial and parallel open/close bodies still permit an open to publish a unit after a concurrent final close has decided to free it (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:135-143,199-215,233-269`; `workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_init.c:135-143,188-204,222-253`). The detailed OD82 entry below records this SMP open/close overlap. ExecOpenDevice holds local Forbid through the open vector, excluding the task-level interleaving on one CPU; on SMP the close on another CPU can still free the unit. The affected file rows below are reconciled; no runtime interleaving was run. The six Unix, PC and native m68k parent `NewUnit` constructors were rechecked for OD4241: each sets its used-unit bit even when object creation returns null; the selected device open callers check that null result, so retries cannot clear the reservation through ordinary close. External/direct HIDD callers, pre-LDDemon startup and actual SMP timing remain open.

USB printer zero-length write follow-up (OD1051; no new candidate): `CopyToPAR` submits a final `CMD_WRITE` even when `Read` returns zero, so an empty file or an exact multiple of its 4096-byte buffer reaches this case (`workbench/c/CopyToPAR.c:147-186`). With a live worker, `psdStreamWrite` clears its OUT-stream error and skips the transfer branch when length is zero, returning zero without waiting (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5256-5266,5299-5303,5460-5464`); the printer worker then replies (`rom/usb/classes/printer/printer.class.c:705-723`). This does not add a zero-length hang. The worker still reads `psdGetStreamError` from its optional IN stream after the write, so on an output-only printer the selected zero-length request also follows OD1051's wrong-error path. No transfer was run.

Keyboard command result follow-up (no new candidate): reread the complete selected `beginio`, `writeEvents` and `abortio` paths with input.device's one-event reader (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:265-551`; `rom/devs/input/processevents.c:25-35,216-251`). `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` checks the minimum result-field span and sets `io_Actual` only after filling that result; `KBD_READMATRIX` copies at most `min(KB_MATRIXSIZE, io_Length)` and publishes that count. `KBD_READEVENT` changes a no-data request to queued/nonquick, then the queue drain replies it; the selected input reader supplies room for one `InputEvent`, so its ordinary path is neither a zero-length read nor an undersized query. `abortio` replies a pending read before storing `IOERR_ABORTED`, which is already OD1007, while the event-chain sentinel and reset-handler counting remain OD32 and OD14. A separate failure in this selected command/result path was not established. Direct unusual request sizes, opener overlap and hardware timing remain open; no device command was run.

Keyboard Close caller-contract recheck (OD2303; pending-read path not credited): reread Open, Close, pending-read enqueue, AbortIO and the interrupt-side drain (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:129-255,347-382,529-551,658-691`). Close removes and frees its `KBUnit` without walking `kb_PendingQueue`; if a client closes while one of its reads remains queued, later drain would dereference that freed unit through the request. Exec's `CloseDevice` contract requires the client to finish outstanding I/O before closing, and the selected input.device does not show an ordinary close-with-live-read path here. This is therefore recorded as a caller-contract violation rather than a separate driver candidate. OD2303 is detailed in AROS-other-drivers.md: successful Open and Close mutate `kb_kbunits` under processor-local Forbid only. The selected ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP packages include keyboard.device, and separate valid request units can be opened or closed concurrently on different CPUs. AddTail/Remove multi-store interleavings can corrupt the list or race a traversal/free. No device or concurrent operation was run; external client scheduling remains unmeasured.

USB printer command-caller follow-up (OD1052): the build-listed `CopyToPAR` utility selects `usbparallel.device` when its USB option is set, opens unit zero, and sends each file chunk through synchronous `DoIO(CMD_WRITE)` (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:13`; `workbench/c/CopyToPAR.c:101-159`). Printer `devOpen` accepts a retained unit with `ncp_Task == NULL`, and `devBeginIO` queues CMD_WRITE without a signal when that task is absent (`rom/usb/classes/printer/dev.c:74-105,252-264`). Thus a workerless unit zero supplies an in-tree synchronous waiter for the existing finding; ordinary hardware timing and any nonzero-unit caller remain open. No command was run.

OD75 report reconciliation: restored the detailed finding after the tracker referenced it but the report contained no OD75 section. The selected `Printer_Unit` passes an uninitialized stack `PrinterPrefs`; `Printer_LoadPrefs` accepts a complete PTXT chunk as its only success requirement, leaving absent/wrong-sized/unreadable PUNT, PDEV or PGFX fields indeterminate (`driver.c:734-783`; `prefs.c:55-60,105-155,163-207`). `pd_SyncPrefs` consumes PUNT/PGFX values; if startup reaches close, an indeterminate PDEV unit number indexes the ten-element parent lock/unit arrays (`driver.c:466-492`; `printer_intern.h:49-55`). This remains separate from OD2016, which covers a complete but inconsistent PDEV chunk. The selected editor normally exports all four chunks; the trigger requires partial, hand-edited or older input. No malformed preferences were loaded.

USB Ethernet reconnect-key comparison (OD2011): all eight selected `asixeth`, `cdceth`, `davicometh`, `ethwrap`, `pegasuseth`, `rndis`, `moschipeth` and `lan78xx` class bodies match a retained unit with `strcmp(stored_128_byte_ID, DA_IDString)` after copying at most 127 source bytes. Poseidon composes its full ID from product and serial descriptors plus numeric fields (`poseidon.library.c:3545-3547`), and its descriptor reader permits enough characters for a longer combined ID (`:2450-2501`). Thus a long-ID reconnect misses the old unit and allocates another. This does not make the ordinary two-identical-device OD2008 collision apply to these Ethernet classes: Poseidon adds a clone count to simultaneous duplicate IDs (`:3531-3543`). A follow-up direct search of class `strcmp`/`strncpy` ID operations found this fixed-buffer comparison pattern in these eight classes; mass storage instead compares retained ID pointers and remains within the disk report. Runtime USB strings, config selection and eventual unit-number exhaustion remain open.

USB class startup failure `Forbid`/`Permit` cross-check (OD2010): reread numbered bind-success and bind-failure exits in `rom/usb/classes/stir4200/stir4200.class.c:173-271`, `lan78xx/lan78xx.class.c:252-274`, `hub/hub.class.c:99-135`, `bootmouse/bootmouse.class.c:143-165`, `ptp/ptp.class.c:233-255` and `egalaxtouch/egalaxtouch.class.c:161-183`. STIR4200 alone among these selected paths executes a second active `Permit` after its earlier binding `Permit` when task startup fails. The apparent repeated `Permit` in the other examined snippets is paired with an active `Forbid` around binding-list insertion, or belongs to a separate release/GUI function. This is a selected-path comparison, not a proof about every class or all worker cleanup.

USB build/interface inventory extension (MassStorage implementation stays in the disk report):

Cross-scope worker-startup recheck (2026-10-14): traced Workbench USB MassStorage `StorageTask` startup through its unit-pool allocation and constructor handshake. The `mss_unit_t` allocation result is dereferenced before the worker's `if (unit)` guard, and the constructor waits for a ready signal sent only after successful unit setup; this is recorded as DISK-327 in the disk report. The six MassStorage C units remain excluded from this driver ledger and assigned to disk scope. No runtime allocation failure was induced.

AHI worker publication follow-up (OD1999): traced `CreateNewProc`'s pre-publication `NP_UserData` assignment and `AddTask` against all AHI subdriver parent-side `tc_UserData` stores and worker reads. The immediate-read SMP race extends from the always-listed Device loopback worker to selected Void, Filesave playback/recording and ac97 workers, plus conditional hosted OSS; all use the same late parent-side assignment. ALSA, PulseAudio and WASAPI workers first wait for the parent's explicit `SIGF_SINGLE`, while checked Raspberry Pi HDMI, I²S and PWM workers spin until the field is nonnull. Toccata also starts a process then writes `tc_UserData`, and its m68k assembly entry reads the field immediately (`Toccata/toccata.c:234-248`; `asmfuncs.a:74-82`). It is not in the current driver `SUBDIRS` list; the only aggregate reference is the developer-source `bindist` copy loop (`Drivers/Makefile.in:39-83,115-118`), so it is not a selected runtime driver for this report. Its legacy m68k-only entry also lies outside the Exec SMP trigger. No cross-CPU schedule was run. A common `NP_UserData` creation tag would remove the publication gap without a spin loop.

Non-AHI task-data publication contrast (no new candidate): searched parent writes to `tc_UserData` in maintained network and hosted-input drivers. Selected BCMGENET and DWMAC unit constructors set their task's unit pointer before `AddTask` (`workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/bcmgenet_unit.c:410-425`; `dwmac/dwmac_unit.c:1148-1163`), and the Linux-hosted input helper likewise sets its params pointer before publishing the task (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxinput/linuxinput_inputtask.c:176-200`). Those checked workers cannot observe the specific late-write gap in OD1999. Other task creation APIs and interrupt callbacks remain outside this contrast; this was a targeted publication check, not a full new audit of those large files.

m68k lowlevel init dependency follow-up (OD1998): the architecture manifest selects `lowlevel_amiga.c`; its init hook dereferences `GfxBase->DisplayFlags` immediately after an unchecked `TaggedOpenLibrary(TAGGEDOPEN_GRAPHICS)` (`arch/m68k-amiga/lowlevel/lowlevel_amiga.c:12-18`). This is distinct from the generic lowlevel cleanup finding OD3285 and other partial-init cleanup paths. A successful graphics open is closed in the hook; failed-open and real m68k boot behavior remain untested.

Lowlevel input and interrupt teardown recheck (no new candidate): reread `lowlevel_init.c:73-157,207-268` with input.device's selected `IND_ADDHANDLER` path (`rom/devs/input/input.c:149-159`; `processevents.c:291-304`), plus `addkbint.c`, `remkbint.c`, `addvblankint.c`, `remvblankint.c` and Exec's `AddIntServer`/`RemIntServer`. The handler-registration command unconditionally enqueues the supplied allocated handler on the worker path; its unchecked `DoIO` result does not establish a separate ordinary failure once the device is open. Its allocation-success but later init-failure lifetime remains OD3285; partial-allocation cleanup, Utility ownership, and keyboard-interrupt-list synchronization are separate paths not re-audited in this pass. The public VBlank API embeds one interrupt node and expects a matching removal before the client exits; the current sources do not establish a separate valid-call teardown failure beyond that caller lifetime contract. Repeated removal, external callback lifetime and real interrupt delivery remain open.

m68k LowLevel timer and Amiga-init source pass (OD9721 added; 2026-10-25): reconciled the architecture-specific manifest and `make.opts` with the generic LowLevel manifest, then read all four Amiga timer overrides (`arch/m68k-amiga/lowlevel/{addtimerint,remtimerint,starttimerint,stoptimerint}.c`, 141 `cloc 2.06` code lines), `lowlevel_amiga.c` (19), and the four generic timer stubs (58). Traced CIA timer-vector install/removal through the selected `AddICRVector`/`RemICRVector` implementations and searched all maintained callers; no direct in-tree timer API caller was found, so interval range, invalid-handle behavior and callback-client lifetime remain external-contract questions. Rechecked the earlier lowlevel graphics dependency candidate against boot resident ordering: the Amiga boot image scans both ROM ranges, graphics is priority 65 and LowLevel defaults to priority zero, so normal order satisfies the dependency. The NULL dereference remains conditional on graphics open/init failure; added it as OD9721 instead of describing ordinary boot as affected. No build, boot, timer or hardware operation was run; source-only.

Usergroup per-task owner initialization follow-up (OD1997): `UserGroup__Init` sets `owner = FindTask(NULL)` on the root base (`workbench/libs/usergroup/usergroup.c:219-239`); `usergroup.conf` requests `pertaskbase`; generated OpenLib copies the root to a later task's duplicate without a usergroup OPENLIB hook (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1320-1389`). The duplicate retains the loader's owner pointer, and `ug_OpenUnit` rejects a different current task (`usergroup.c:249-259`). Selected legacy `getpwent` and group lookups reach that helper only when security.library forwarding is inactive (`getpwent.c:226-257`; `usergroup_security.c:63-75`). This is independent of OD1910's explicit `UGT_OWNER` contradiction and OD1996's per-task close cleanup. OD1910's stale init citation and per-open wording were corrected in its original paragraph. No multi-task call was run.

Usergroup per-task netinfo cleanup follow-up (OD1996): traced `usergroup.conf` `pertaskbase` through generated OpenLib's root-base `CopyMem` and final CloseLib's `__freebase` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1320-1389,1472-1502`). There is no usergroup CLOSELIB hook. Successful legacy `getpwent`/`getgrent` access stores a port, request, device/unit and buffer on the duplicate (`workbench/libs/usergroup/usergroup.c:249-295`; `base.h:73-78`), but `CleanupNIO` runs only from the root EXPUNGELIB hook (`usergroup.c:201-216,321-343`). `endpwent`/`endgrent` close units, not the port/request/buffer. Normal successful per-task close thus loses owned resources; cross-task ownership and security.library forwarding remain separate contracts. No library was loaded.

OD9868 selected HID caller check: `HUA_KEYMAP` submits press/release codes through `nSendRawKey`, which chooses `IND_ADDEVENT` after AROS input.device opens (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1124-1135,5584-5594,6516-6527`). This supplies a maintained producer for the command-first simultaneous-signal case. Keyboard.device replies are processed later than the repeat-timer branch (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:459-484`), so its ordinary read path does not supply that exact ordering.

Input-device key-repeat simultaneous-signal follow-up (OD9868): reread `ProcessEvents`' `Wait` mask, command-first `IND_ADDEVENT` processing, `ABORT_KEYTIMER_REQUEST` macro, and the later key-timer branch (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:49-52,262-277,344-368,459-480`) with Exec `WaitIO` and `GetMsg`. A completed timer reply and raw-key release can be present in the same wake: the release removes the reply and clears the signal, but the saved wake mask still enters the timer branch. That branch does not test the dequeued message or `keyrepeat_state`, emits a repeat after release, and rearms the timer. This is separate from the existing stopped-input stranded-reply and unrelated-key cancellation findings. Timer-device behavior after a simultaneous new press/rearm, other event producers, and runtime scheduling remain open; no input event was run.

AHIRecord FLAC finalization follow-up (revalidated as OD9773): traced `SaveSlave`'s checked `FLAC__stream_encoder_process_interleaved` result through the encoder's one-sample overread, pending-frame finish, STREAMINFO MD5/sample/frame-size rewrite, and saver teardown (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:2999-3026,3090-3103`; `FLAC/stream_encoder.c:1320-1385,2035-2108,2529-2633`). An I/O failure in finish returns false, but the saver discards it and never sets `WriteError`. The default 32,768-frame capture batch does not eliminate the final buffered frame because the encoder waits for an extra sample before writing each block. OD1992 was withdrawn after selected integer-encoder bit tracing: zero-extended 16-bit values serialize identically in independent and mid/side frames, so decoded-audio corruption was not established. OD2226 follows capture-buffer ownership through RecordFuncS, the coalescing saver signal and HDAudio callbacks; the next callback overwrites a completed buffer if the saver has not finished consuming it. AIFF/WAVE header/seek/close reporting is covered by GD2577; FLAC finish-result handling is OD9773; ignored FLAC `fclose()` status is OD10504. Other encoder metadata/seek errors and runtime I/O failure remain open; no file was recorded.

Bundled FLAC decoder resize-recovery follow-up (revalidated as OD9772): traced a successful small frame, failed first allocation during growth, and public flush/reset into another small frame (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/FLAC/stream_decoder.c:959-1037,1305-1354,2015-2052,2523-2544`; `FLAC/stream_decoder.h:1366-1416`). Resize frees the old output/residual pointers but leaves their capacity values unchanged on failure; the next frame can pass the stale fast path and write through null. This requires a decoder client that retries after memory pressure; default AHIRecord recording does not use the decoder. Other partial-allocation failure states, frame validity and runtime recovery remain pending; no decoder was run.

Bundled FLAC integer-only seek follow-up (revalidated as OD9774): traced `FLAC__stream_decoder_seek_absolute` through metadata processing, public 64-bit length callbacks, unknown total-sample handling and the selected `FLAC__INTEGER_ONLY_LIBRARY` seek formula (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/FLAC/stream_decoder.c:1171-1234,2976-3111`; `AHIRecord/mmakefile.src:25`). With no seek table, a zero target gives a one-sample upper bound; a byte search span at least `0xffffffff` enters the large-span branch and right-shifts that difference to a zero divisor. Bundled FILE callback support for large files is target-`off_t` dependent; the callback API itself accepts a 64-bit length. Other seek bounds, valid large-file clients and runtime behavior remain pending; no stream was sought.

Bundled FLAC metadata-reader follow-up (revalidated as OD9771): traced the decoder's metadata dispatcher, APPLICATION/unknown payloads, Vorbis comments, cue sheets and pictures through their allocation, read-failure and success-only cleanup paths (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/FLAC/stream_decoder.c:1431-1919`). After a nonzero payload allocation, EOF or callback abort returns before cleanup of the local block, so decoder finish cannot reclaim it. This is a decoder-client path, not default AHIRecord recording. STREAMINFO/SEEKTABLE length validation, metadata callback ownership, malformed field counts and wider decoder behavior remain pending; no stream was decoded.

Unix-hosted serial HIDD factory/unit follow-up (no new candidate): reread the complete `UXSer__Hidd_Serial__NewUnit`/`DisposeUnit` pair and `UXSerUnit__Root__New`/`Dispose`, active Write/SetBaudrate/SetParameters/Start/Stop/GetCapabilities/GetStatus, and the disabled async setup (`arch/all-unix/hidd/serial/{SerialClass,SerialUnitClass}.c`). The parent factory restricts ordinary unit indices to 0–3 and auto-selects a free slot; it still marks a slot used after failed construction (OD4241). Direct unit-class construction bypasses that bound (OD889), and a failed UnixIO object creation reaches disposal with a null UnixIO and descriptor zero (OD890). The successful host-file-open branch skips termios/async registration under `#if 0` (OD63); active baud, framing and break methods remain OD64/OD1440/OD65. The receive/write-ready callback functions are compiled but not registered by this selected constructor, so their direct behavior was not promoted as an active independent fault. UnixIO return contracts, generated class dispatch and actual host-terminal behavior remain pending.

AHI-Handler shared-device unit and partial-open teardown follow-up (OD1950): traced each `ACTION_FIND*` handle's parsed `UNIT=` through `AllocAudio`, the first `OpenDevice` and AHI's `io_Unit` assignment, both read/write `CopyMem(AHIio, ...)` sites, and `ACTION_END`/`FreeAudio` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:299-380,423-450,651-682,736-753,931-977`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:295-317`). Under first-open allocation failure, `AHIDevice` remains nonzero and the error path decrements the count and passes null to `DeleteIORequest`/`DeleteMsgPort`; both Exec deletion functions explicitly accept null (`rom/exec/{deleteiorequest,deletemsgport}.c`). No separate null-teardown candidate is credited. Concurrent packet ordering, other device-unit configurations and runtime I/O remain pending.

AHI-Handler open-name and format-entry recheck (no new candidate): reread the complete `ACTION_FINDINPUT`/`ACTION_FINDOUTPUT`/`ACTION_FINDUPDATE` branch, `ACTION_WRITE` format sniff and `ReadCOMMchunk` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:299-383,538-605,890-920`) against DOS's `fs_Open` packet producer (`rom/dos/fs_driver.c:29-62`) and the public AROS BSTR representation (`compiler/include/dos/bptr.h:62-98`). A first write shorter than its four- or twelve-byte sniff remains OD141. The COMM scan can encounter a truncated chunk, but OD141 already covers its out-of-bounds field reads; format-specific downstream effects need a separate complete AIFF/AIFC input and were not promoted here. Other direct packet senders and runtime parser behavior remain pending.

AHI-Handler invalid-read retry check (OD1949): traced `InitHData`'s early `initialized` assignment and validation exits through the selected `ACTION_READ` first and second packet paths (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:279-291,348-357,401-423,1070-1125`). A parseable invalid `BITS=17` leaves zeroed `totallength`; first read returns `ERROR_OBJECT_WRONG_TYPE`, but retry skips validation and returns ordinary zero-byte EOF with cleared packet error. `ACTION_WRITE` reruns `InitHData` while `buffer1` is null, so this particular error-to-EOF transition is read-specific. Other configuration and stream retry paths remain pending.

AHI-Handler default-pointer lifetime check (OD1948): traced `ParseArgs`' optional numeric output pointers, `InitHData`'s local defaults and persistent `data->args` assignments, then the first-write allocation failure and retry (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:988-1054,1070-1154,591-607`). The second `InitHData` call sees nonnull saved default pointers and dereferences them after the prior invocation's automatic variables have ended. This lifetime error needs both an omitted option and first `buffer1` allocation failure for the selected write retry; same-frame stack reuse can hide its visible effect, so no runtime failure is claimed. First-read retry skips reinitialization after `data->initialized` becomes true; it is not an additional trigger for this candidate. Other configuration retry paths remain pending.

AHI-Handler write-request failure ordering (OD1947): traced the first complete playback buffer, `ACTION_WRITE` retry, and `PlayAndSwap` swap/allocation order (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:591-638,723-770`), with the default total length and buffer size (`:1070-1085,1137-1154`). If the first `writereq1` allocation fails after the filled buffer is swapped into `buffer2`, a later positive write swaps the buffers back and submits the previously unfilled buffer instead. The error return preserves the handle and does not restore pointers. This is distinct from OD1946's incomplete first-use buffer/request setup; later second-request failure and close-time behavior remain pending.

OD1946 close-path extension: after a first-read allocation failure, `data->readreq` can be nonnull without receiving the copied open AHI request or a `SendIO` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:425-452`). The selected `ACTION_END` branch checks only that pointer and calls `AbortIO`/`WaitIO` before `FreeHData` (`:648-667`); Exec `AbortIO` dispatches through the request's `io_Device` field (`rom/exec/abortio.c:44-55`). Thus closing the still-open file immediately after this error can use an uninitialized device pointer. This is the same partial-setup root as OD1946's retry paths, now recorded as an additional trigger and consequence.

AHI-Handler first-I/O retry check (OD1946): traced the selected `ACTION_FIND` zeroed `HandlerData` allocation, first `ACTION_READ`/`ACTION_WRITE` buffer and request allocations, later-packet first-use tests, `PlayAndSwap`, and `WaitIO` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:348-379,423-501,591-638,648-672,723-770`; `rom/exec/{abortio,waitio}.c`). The read path leaves a successful `buffer1` across a later allocation failure; a second read skips request setup and can call `WaitIO` on null or uninitialized `readreq`. If the request allocation itself succeeded, closing immediately instead reaches `ACTION_END`'s `AbortIO` on that nonnull but not-yet-copied request; Exec dispatches via its uninitialized `io_Device` field. The write path leaves `buffer1` and zero `data->length` after `buffer2` fails, so a positive retry cannot consume input; if zero-length `PlayAndSwap` calls succeed, the loop does not terminate. The DOS packet error leaves the file handle open, so retry and close are valid client responses; `FreeHData` later frees partial pointers but cannot undo the invalid `AbortIO`. This is a distinct allocation-state root from OD142's small configured buffer. A maintained client retrying after this exact allocation failure was not found. Other AHI-Handler packet retry and teardown paths remain pending.

Netinfo message-port signal-owner recheck (no new candidate): traced the opening task's temporary `CreateMsgPort`/`DeleteMsgPort` pair (`workbench/devs/netinfo/netinfo.c:158-188`) and the worker's embedded `nid_Port`/`nid_NotifyPort` setup, shared signal allocation and teardown (`workbench/devs/netinfo/server.c:86-136,153-209`; `base.h:70-83`) against Exec's `CreateMsgPort`, `DeleteMsgPort` and `FreeSignal`. Other client-created reply ports and shutdown interleavings remain pending.

ACPI thermal entry-index and cleanup recheck (no new candidate): reread every function in the selected thermal init and class C files (`rom/hidds/acpi/thermal/acpithermal_init.c:25-148`; `acpithermal_class.c:16-316`) with the selected SysExplorer telemetry enumeration (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Power/power_window_cl.c:250-305`). ACPI power-meter init and telemetry recheck (no new candidate): reread both selected C bodies (`rom/hidds/acpi/powermeter/acpipowermeter_init.c:25-246`; `acpipowermeter_class.c:16-328`) against the selected SysExplorer power telemetry enumerator (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Power/power_window_cl.c:250-305`). OD1744 is restored with the scalar `_PMM` versus package-reader mismatch and the selected SysExplorer consequence; OD3417 covers skipped superclass disposal; OD1753 covers failed-value substitution; OD2445 covers the `OOP_ObtainAttrBase` null-bucket dereference; OD3418 covers the `OOP_ObtainAttrBases` nonfinal-failure infinite loop used by the selected ACPI initializers. ACPI fan module and telemetry recheck (no new candidate): reread both selected C bodies in `rom/hidds/acpi/fan` (`acpifan_init.c:25-182`; `acpifan_class.c:20-341`) together with the selected SysExplorer telemetry enumeration (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Power/power_window_cl.c:250-305`). ACPI battery telemetry and buffer-ownership recheck (no new candidate): reread all helper and dispatch functions in `rom/hidds/acpi/battery/acpibattery_class.c:16-407` against its selected Power/Telemetry caller path and ACPICA allocation callbacks. Input-device producer and event-chain recheck (no new candidate): reread the complete selected `rom/devs/input/{input,support,processevents}.c` command, queue and worker bodies with keyboard `KBD_READEVENT` and gameport `GPD_READEVENT` producers (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:347-385,405-505`; `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:390-420,710-784`). The worker allocates one `InputEvent` for each persistent read and sets each request length to that structure's size, so these selected keyboard/gameport replies do not provide a multi-event chain for `AddEQTail` to traverse. Keyboard `writeEvents` rejects an undersized buffer and clears `io_Error` on its normal fill path. This does not restore withdrawn OD47's missing valid error producer. Netinfo expunge-order recheck (OD1902): confirmed that `nid_Task` aliases the embedded request port's `mp_SigTask` and is set on successful worker startup (`workbench/devs/netinfo/base.h:71-82`; `server.c:111-124`). The idle low-memory sweep calls `RemDevice` for a zero-open device (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:739-760`); its generated expunge path frees the base immediately after the hook returns (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1535-1590`). The death-message worker then drains ports and calls `ObtainSemaphore(nid->nid_Lock)` on that base (`server.c:154-210`). On a single CPU, Exec's `Forbid` around expunge prevents the worker from completing before the free (`rom/exec/remdevice.c:65-83`). OD1902 now names this exact cleanup access; concurrent SMP timing, segment unloading and runtime behavior remain unverified. No device was run.

Gameport VBlank lifetime follow-up (`rom/devs/gameport/{gameport.c,gameport.conf}`, `rom/exec/{addintserver,remintserver}.c`, `tools/genmodule/writestart.c`): reread device init, first-open failures and close. Init registers the embedded `gp_VBlank` node once with `AddIntServer(INTB_VERTB)` before any opener; failed opens leave the base and its node alive, and close frees only the per-open unit. The selected module declares `options noexpunge`, and the generator omits last-close expunge and teardown for that option (`writestart.c:1506-1546`). Thus the missing explicit `RemIntServer` does not establish a routine unload-time dangling VBlank node; no new candidate is credited. OD2305 details the separately allocated per-open unit leak on failed Open, and OD1192 the unbalanced cached OOP attribute reference on successive opens. Boot shutdown and external direct-vector behavior remain outside this checked path; no device was run.

PC timer failed-init rollback refinement (`arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c`, `rom/exec/{remresetcallback,remove}.c`, `compiler/autoinit/functions.c`): if IRQ registration fails, generated rollback invokes `hw_Expunge` before the reset callback was ever registered. Its first null IRQ removal faults under EK09. If that call is guarded, the next unconditional `RemResetCallback` still passes the unlinked zero-initialized node to `Remove`, which dereferences its null list links. This is a second cleanup obligation within the same failed-init path, not a separately counted runtime outcome while the earlier fault masks it. Record both registration states when repairing rollback; no failure was induced.

PC timer initialization/teardown cross-check (arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c, beginio.c; rom/timer/timer.conf, lowlevel.c): reread IRQ registration, reset callback, PIT setup, embedded VBlank request, failed-init returns and expunge hook against generated device lifetime. The common timer definition has noexpunge, so an ordinary last close cannot make its automatically requeued VBlank request an unload leak. Existing OD1564 unchecked SMP lock allocation and Exec EK09 null IRQ cleanup remain the supported failure paths; no separate routine-teardown candidate is added. Failed-init rollback, reset ordering and PIT hardware behavior remain open; no timer was run.

Netinfo manifest and worker-lifetime reconciliation (`workbench/devs/netinfo/{mmakefile.src,netinfo.c,server.c,base.h}`): the active common and quick targets name exactly seven local C bodies—`assert`, `netinfo`, `server`, `entries`, `groupunit`, `passwdunit` and `misc`—and every one has a ledger row with a full-body read. `NetInfo__DevOpen` waits on the worker's startup reply before publishing a unit, while `NetInfo__DevExpunge` only posts a death message and returns success (`netinfo.c:143-208,235-246`). On that message, `NetInfoPoll` still reads and frees base-owned ports, maps and the death request before clearing `nid_Task` (`server.c:154-210`), confirming OD1902's incomplete exit handshake. The two optional custom database paths are freed on startup failure (`server.c:139-149`) but not after a successful poll return (`:125-128`); the earlier ledger note retains that loss as conditional on an independently safe shutdown path, which the selected expunge route does not supply. Generated ABI, external request clients and teardown scheduling remain open. No worker was run.

Netinfo group-unit full-body recheck (`workbench/devs/netinfo/groupunit.c`): reread all five local operations—map initialization, group copy-out, direct-write copy-in, group-file parse/print and `NI_MEMBERS` enumeration—against the existing netinfo entry layout and usergroup `initgroups` caller. The copy-in text length is narrowed to the `UWORD ge_tlen` while retaining full strings (now detailed as OD2261); its final `*mem = NULL` writes the already-observed null terminator back unchanged; OD1925 is withdrawn because this is not a defect for valid writable input. `GetGroups` emits each matching record rather than deduplicating GIDs (OD2262), and the fixed usergroup result buffer remains its selected caller limit. The parser's `strsep` delimiter pass and null-third-field handling remain covered by OD1899 and the prior row; no additional distinct candidate was established here. Direct group `CMD_WRITE` clients and unusual on-disk group records remain unverified, and no request or file parse was run.

Zorro III slot-metadata consumer follow-up (`arch/m68k-amiga/expansion/configboard.c`): the board's actual `cd_BoardAddr` uses aligned `newslot`, while `cd_SlotAddr` records pre-alignment `z3Slot` (`:53-69`). A source search found DenebClockport copies that slot field into a synthetic ConfigDev (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/DenebClockport.c:226-259`), but its hardware address calculation uses `cd_BoardAddr`; the copy does not establish a wrong-address operation. The DenebClockport build listing is commented out in its local manifest (`denebusb/mmakefile.src:10`). No additional candidate is credited without an affected selected consumer; external users of the public slot metadata remain open.

PoPo popup-action locking follow-up (OD1927): the selected Disable Port/Power Cycle Port dispatcher checks `pog_Device` validity and reads hub/binding state under `Forbid` alone (`rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c:1520-1548`); its own event handler uses `psdLockReadPBase` for the same device-list traversal, and device removal moves nodes under the corresponding write lock (`popo.gui.c:809-823`; `poseidon.library.c:2125-2150`). `psdGetNextDevice` does not lock internally (`poseidon.library.c:3667-3695`), and Exec SMP Forbid is processor-local. The report limits the consequence to a list/target race because exact UI output depends on scheduling. Binding-lock and hub-class teardown details remain open; no concurrent click/removal was run.

PoPo event-port teardown follow-up: `pPoPoGUITask` creates `po_MsgPort` and registers it with `psdAddEventHandler`; cleanup calls `psdRemEventHandler` before deleting the port (`rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c:104-115,409-417`). The selected Poseidon broadcaster holds `ps_ReentrantLock` while traversing hooks and calling `PutMsg`, and `psdRemEventHandler` takes that same semaphore, removes the hook, drains remaining queued messages with replies, then returns (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6622-6704`). This checked path does not send a new event to the deleted PoPo port after removal. External event-hook clients remain open. Worker shutdown ordering is now recorded as OD4469 for the ExecSMP expunge interleaving; no event or task schedule was run.

Printer per-unit registration failure recheck: `Printer_Unit` publishes its `pu` device before process startup and calls `RemDevice((struct Device *)pd)` on creation or handshake failure (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:764-856`). This is the same base address: `struct PrinterUnit` begins with `struct PrinterData pu_PrinterData`, whose `pd_Device` is its leading device member (`workbench/devs/printer/printer_intern.h:33-47`; `compiler/include/devices/prtbase.h:88-92`). The apparent `pd` versus `pu` pointer mismatch is therefore not a separate wrong-base defect. The publication-before-ready window is already OD1889, and a failed startup reply-port allocation after process creation is detailed as OD4287. Other worker-start and expunge scheduling cases remain open; no printer process was run.

Printer worker-start and port-initializer follow-up (no new candidate): reread the `Printer_Unit` `AddDevice`/`CreateNewProcTags`/startup handshake and both `pd_DriverTask` and `pd_Init` entry paths (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:405-463,525-568,764-859`). If process creation fails, the parent follows `RemDevice` without a worker to cancel; the selected failure after successful process creation but before a startup message is detailed as OD4287. `initMsgPort` clears its embedded `MsgPort` after a successful signal allocation (`driver.c:74-91`) and does not call Exec's usual spinlock initializer, but an unlocked `spinlock_t` has zero lock state (`compiler/include/aros/types/spinlock_s.h:34-60`); this file's `memset` supplies that value, so the missing initializer call alone does not establish a lock defect. `pd_Init` calls the segment expunge hook after later underlying-device/timer setup failures but not if `ped_Init` itself returns an error (`driver.c:410-463`); the sole aggregate-selected PostScript segment's `ps_Init` only stores `SysBase`/`PD` and always returns zero (`workbench/printers/postscript/postscript.c:278-293`), so no selected partial-segment-initialization leak is credited. Other segments and runtime startup timing remain open; no worker was run.

Speech request and audio-slot recheck: reread `SpeechWorker`, `GetRequest`, `FinishRequest`, `beginio` and `abortio` together with `AcquireAudio`, `PlaybackPCM`, `PlaybackWait` and `PlaybackFinish` (`workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:105-245,393-518,611-728`). A queued write is dequeued and published as `sb_Current` under `sb_Lock`; AbortIO holds that lock to distinguish the current request from a request still in the command port. A queued Flush/Reset removed by AbortIO decrements its control count before reply. Playback waits only on slots marked in flight and drains each completed request with `WaitIO`; a successful final close sends a separate release request. No distinct selected-path double reply, lost queued control or audio-slot reuse was established by this pass. OD3210 now records the confirmed speech/narrator last-Close release-handshake allocation failure: failure to allocate the temporary reply port/request skips each device’s audio-release command while Close reports success. OD3211 now records the confirmed renderer remainder drop: `SCRenderFrames` emits only full 512-byte blocks and discards its remainder at each `SynthSentence` boundary; the narrator.device and speech.device targets, plus Say’s WAV sink, cannot recover bytes they never receive. External callers, actual audio-device timing and generated vectors remain open; no speech request was run.

Clipboard replacement-write caller recheck (OD30): reread `writeCb`'s `MODE_NEWFILE` failure after it clears the cached size and advances the write ID (`workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c:723-755`) against the selected IFFParse `ClipStreamHandler` write branch (`workbench/libs/iffparse/clipboardfuncs.c:91-103`). The stream forwards the device's `DoIO` error, but that does not roll back the device state; a later read still sees the old file as empty. This strengthens OD30 with a selected writer, without adding a duplicate candidate. Actual file-open failure and other direct clients remain untested.

Netinfo sequential-read retry follow-up (now detailed as OD2263): `ReadCmd` advances `nip_Ent` before its group `copy_out` can return `NIERR_TOOSMALL` (`workbench/devs/netinfo/entries.c:177-197`; `groupunit.c:69-86`). The selected `getgrent` error branch returns null but leaves its `setent_done` flag and cached unit in place; its next call issues another `CMD_READ` without resetting that cursor (`workbench/libs/usergroup/getgrent.c:238-266`; `usergroup.c:275-294`). This confirms omission of the oversized group across calls, not merely a theoretical direct-client retry. `initgroups` uses the separate `NI_MEMBERS` command and handles a too-small result explicitly. No large group record or sequential read was run.

Clipboard failed-open caller recheck (OD1917): compared `clipboard.device`'s failed unit-allocation return with the generated Open vector and Exec `OpenDevice`, then traced the selected IFFParse `OpenClipboard` failure branch (`workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c:216-289`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1232-1265`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:99-125`; `workbench/libs/iffparse/openclipboard.c:65-105`). Controller consumer caller census correction (OD9860/OD9861 added; 2026-10-26): the prior note for OD1512/OD1797 incorrectly said that notification delivery had no 32-consumer limit. `CTRL_FANOUT_MAX` is 32 and `ctrl_DeliverEvent()` does stop appending at that capacity, while `ctrl_ConsumerAttach()` has no corresponding rejection (`controller_intern.h:31`; `controller_notify.c:148-175,194-201`). Added OD9860 for matching consumers beyond the first 32 receiving no event. The same audit confirmed the existing-device initial salvo snapshots at most 64 IDs (`controller_notify.c:203-231`) even though subsystem registration has no 64-device limit; added OD9861 for newly attached subsystem consumers missing DeviceAdded for pre-existing devices after the 64th. The checked-in caller census remains unchanged: only the public constructor attaches consumers, no in-tree client exercising either threshold was found, and the Controller module aggregate edge is commented. These are conditional API-capacity defects. This correction supersedes the quoted prior conclusion; no controller or event was run.

Controller consumer constructor follow-up: reread the entire tag parser and constructor failure branch (`workbench/hidds/controller/controllerclass.c:100-280`) against callback, signal and port delivery (`controller_notify.c:24-129`). A consumer is attached only after its signal ring or port message array is allocated, and failure invokes the superclass disposer before attachment; this does not add a partially attached consumer to OD2883. Queue depth is reset from zero to the default and capped at `CTRL_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH`, and `ctrl_RingPush` checks fullness before writing. The public signal-bit tag is masked to the 32-bit signal range. Direct consumer clients and callback/port lifetime behavior remain open; no constructor allocation failure or notification was run.

Usergroup timer-init failure follow-up: `TimeInit` can return `-1` after successfully opening timer.device if its version is below 36 (`workbench/libs/usergroup/time.c:76-90,137-141`). The caller treats that as library initialization failure and invokes `UserGroup__Expunge` (`usergroup.c:225-238`), whose `TimeCleanup` closes a nonnull `TimerBase` and clears it (`usergroup.c:203-215`; `time.c:144-152`). Thus this selected failure path does not leave the timer device open; no separate candidate is added. The timer clock epoch, locale offset convention and retry behavior after later initialization failures remain open. No old-version timer or failed initialization was run.

Netinfo ordinary file-parser length recheck: reread `ParsePasswd` and `ParseGroup` (`workbench/devs/netinfo/{passwdunit,groupunit}.c:248-307,222-277`) against the local delimiter splitter and `stpcopy` (`misc.c:23-48`; `entries.h:85-90`). For a newline-terminated seven-field password record, `np - field[0] - (field[4] - field[2])` removes exactly the UID and GID text plus their two separators, leaving five string lengths plus five NUL bytes. For a normal group record such as `staff|*|42|alice,bob
`, the corresponding subtraction leaves name, password and member text plus their NULs and the pointer count includes one terminator. No ordinary-line allocation-size mismatch was established from these formulas. OD1899 remains the earlier null group ID before validation; OD1903 remains the skipped newline-free final line. Exotic empty/repeated member delimiters and numeric parse outcomes still need a separate check; no database file was read.

OD2261 copy-primitive verification: the local `stpcopy` copies through the terminating NUL and returns the byte **after** it (`workbench/devs/netinfo/entries.h:85-90`). Thus both the input and output converters advance across all five password strings or each group string, as assumed in OD2261; the `UWORD` stored length can understate the actual amount copied even though the allocation used the full `ULONG` length. This recheck rules out a mistaken interpretation based on the standard `stpcpy` return convention. No request was run.

Netinfo long-record copy bounds (now detailed as OD2261): compared public password/group record layouts and both `copy_in`/`copy_out` methods with `WriteCmd` and `ReadCmd` (`workbench/devs/netinfo/{include/netinfo.h,entries.h,passwdunit.c,groupunit.c,entries.c}`). Both copy-in methods allocate and copy an `ULONG` text size but store it in a `UWORD`; the copy-out methods validate only the narrowed length before copying all retained strings. A direct write with 65,536 aggregate text bytes followed by a read into the advertised result size therefore reaches an out-of-bounds result write. On-disk parsing is limited to a 1,024-byte line and does not provide this trigger; the checked-in `usergroup.library` clients read/search but no direct writer was found. No long record or request was run.

Netinfo custom database-path and shutdown follow-up: reread the worker's `SYS/userdb`/`SYS/groupdb` `GetVar` and `StrDup` setup, map filename borrowing, both startup failure and normal `NetInfoPoll` teardown, and the generated device expunge vector (`workbench/devs/netinfo/{server,passwdunit,groupunit}.c`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1535-1590`). Selected DOS `GetVar` NUL-terminates a default text-variable read even when its 128-byte buffer fills (`rom/dos/getvar.c:225-278`), so the later `StrDup` does not overread a truncated string. Its global newline scan nevertheless evaluates `buffer[j]` before `j < i`: a full 128-byte no-newline variable causes a one-byte read beyond netinfo's stack buffer before termination. That dependency is DOS finding D12, now supplied with this selected caller, not a separate netinfo candidate. The caller ignores `IoErr()`'s full variable length and stores a 127-byte prefix for a longer configured path. This is now included in OD1897: both map constructors retain the prefix and `InternalSetEnts` opens it on an ordinary query (`passwdunit.c:45-62`; `groupunit.c:47-62`; `entries.c:371-396`), so the read can fail or select a different prefix-named file without any direct writer. The original OD1897 update-buffer overflow still requires direct `CMD_WRITE`/`CMD_UPDATE` use. Startup failure frees custom duplicate paths, but successful worker teardown does not; those allocations would be stranded when the base is freed. On the ordinary single-CPU expunge route, OD1902's earlier asynchronous base-free fault prevents claiming a clean standalone shutdown leak, while on SMP cleanup/free timing remains unresolved. The retained DOS library open remains OD1896. No independent shutdown path-string loss is credited until a selected shutdown order establishes it. No worker was run.

Unix parallel Stop/Start caller follow-up: reread both hosted parallel HIDD classes and selected parallel.device open/write/callback and command paths (`arch/all-unix/hidd/parallel/{ParallelClass,ParallelUnitClass}.c`; `workbench/devs/parallel/{parallel_init,parallel_interrupthandlers}.c`). The backend `Start` calls its write-ready callback before clearing `stopped`, so a direct HIDD restart during a pending write would initially see zero bytes from `Write`. Selected parallel.device does not call that method: its `CMD_START` and `CMD_STOP` branches are both no-ops and fail to reply asynchronously (already OD718). An exact repository C-call search found no other direct `HIDD_ParallelUnit_Start/Stop` invocation. OD60 still covers query clearing pending read/write bits; OD835, OD888-891 cover the checked hosted read and construction failures. No independent selected restart finding is credited. External HIDD method clients, host interrupt timing and parallel hardware behavior remain open; no device request was run.

Input-device command and worker recheck: compared `beginio`'s accepted commands and quick/nonquick result handling (`rom/devs/input/input.c:105-183`) with the worker's command-first dispatch, stop/start gating, event forwarding, timer, keyboard and gameport branches (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:250-580`). The unchecked previous `io_Error` on queued completions is already OD887; stopped-source reply signals cleared before resume are OD2516; direct `IND_ADDEVENT` qualifier and unsupported-class behavior is OD1195; the incomplete keyboard mask and later mouse/gameport qualifier propagation are OD46; key-repeat cancellation on an unrelated release is OD1786. `IND_WRITEEVENT` bypassing qualifier and repeat state is already OD1196/OD1788 for selected USB keyboard paths. Clipboard transaction recheck: reread the selected `clipboard.device` command dispatcher and the complete read/update paths (`workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c:336-721,867-917`) against the already recorded IFFParse clipboard hook and RAM-backed write behavior. Clipboard failed-open accounting (OD1917): reread the selected `clipboard.device` Open hook's new-unit allocation branch against the generated device Open vector, its `set_call_devfuncs` Boolean semantics, Exec `OpenDevice`, and LDDemon's forwarding wrapper (`workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c:216-289`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1232-1265`; `compiler/libinit/libinit.c:53-79`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:99-125`; `rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:533-564`). Generated Open increments `lib_OpenCnt`, then Exec clears the failed request's device pointer; LDDemon forwards without closing that count. The separate early invalid-unit and too-small-request branches return false, so this finding is limited to failure after directory setup. Broader partial-open clients and runtime allocation failure remain open; no device open was run.

Netinfo worker and caller dispatch follow-up: reread the complete `netinfo.c` and `server.c` worker/open/close/BeginIO/AbortIO paths with the base layout, selected `usergroup.library` request wrapper and common command table (`workbench/devs/netinfo/{netinfo,server,entries}.c`; `workbench/devs/netinfo/base.h`; `workbench/libs/usergroup/{usergroup,getpwent,getgrent,initgroups}.c`). `NI_END` sizes the command table and `BeginIO` rejects command indices at or above it, so no ordinary table-overrun candidate was established.
