Hosted Linux PCI config-access recheck: read both `ReadConfigLong` and `WriteConfigLong` in `arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/driverclass.c:95-121` against the generic byte/word wrappers (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:75-126`) and device accessors (`pcideviceclass.c:78-113`). The backend selects a dword register by masking its two low offset bits, and the generic wrappers extract or replace the addressed byte or word within that dword. No byte-lane or ordinary 256-byte config-space offset defect was established from these paths. Cross-task and host-process access to the shared CF8/CFC ports, extended-config calls, and actual host I/O behavior remain open; this check does not credit a new candidate.

Hosted Linux PCI high-BAR mapping check (OD1893): the generic device parser preserves both halves of a 64-bit memory BAR and returns an `IPTR` base (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:665-690,805-829`), but the hosted x86-64 backend narrows `(IPTR)PCIAddress >> 12` into `ULONG offs` before its raw `mmap2` call (`arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/driverclass.c:123-149`). The first omitted page bit corresponds to a physical base at 16 TiB. This is a separate high-address truncation from OD1892's within-page offset loss; successful mapping of a wrong region depends on the host and BAR layout. No selected firmware BAR placement, configured image inclusion or runtime mapping was established.

OpenSBI ACPI PCIDT range and BAR-map recheck: reread full `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_acpi.c:1-395` with the ECAM address helper and PCI BAR Base producer (`pcidt_access.c:570-590`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:805-829`). MCFG records can name a nonzero starting bus; the selected ECAM helper computes `(bus - busStart) << 20`, so the absolute-bus-offset defect in the separate ACPICA PCI glue (OD999) is not duplicated here. The ACPI mapper rounds the physical BAR base down and its size up separately; for an ordinary valid power-of-two BAR, alignment prevents a sub-page BAR from crossing a page, while a BAR at least one page long is page-aligned. This check therefore does not credit a missing tail page for a valid BAR. Ignored `PCIDT_Map` failures for high 64-bit BARs and 4 GiB length truncation remain OD2564/OD2565. Rechecking `pcidt_acpi_mapbars()` also found that `if (!szlo || szlo == 0xffffffff) size = 0` discards a valid 4 GiB BAR whose low mask word is zero; this is an additional ACPI path to the unmapped BAR/unchanged `MapPCI()` outcome already tracked by OD2565, not a separate consequence. Invalid MCFG bus ranges, nonconforming BAR values, real firmware layouts and actual hardware mapping remain open. No PCI bridge was run.

Hosted Linux PCI descriptor lifetime recheck (OD851): read both `PCILx_Init` and `PCILx_Expunge` (`arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/pcilinux_init.c:36-105`) with its module config and generated expunge-hook path (`pcilinux.conf:1-27`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1550-1585`). The configured module does not disable expunge. Initial admission still ignores failed `/dev/mem` open when `iopl` succeeded. After a successful open, a permitted expunge removes the PCI driver but never calls its defined host `__NR_close`, so the descriptor survives module teardown; OD851 now records both branches of that descriptor's lifetime. Actual image inclusion, a successful unload and host descriptor behavior remain untested. No module was loaded.

Hosted Linux PCI byte-address mapping check (OD1892): compared the selected `PCILx__Hidd_PCIDriver__MapPCI` page-number/length/result sequence (`arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/driverclass.c:123-149`) with the public MapPCI byte-address contract and generic memory-BAR attribute extraction (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:157-174`; `pcideviceclass.c:805-829`). The backend drops the low 12 physical-address bits when forming `mmap2`'s offset and returns the page start without adding them back; it also maps only the caller's original length. This is a successful-map wrong-register-offset case for a non-page-aligned BAR, distinct from OD1891's failed-map result. The PCI client census found direct BAR mapping in graphics, HDAudio and network devices, but no checked-in producer or configured firmware layout establishes a non-page-aligned BAR on this hosted target, so that trigger remains conditional. Host unmap ownership, physical BAR placement and runtime behavior remain open. No host map was run.

Hosted Linux PCI mapping-result/client follow-up (OD851/OD1891): reread `arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/{pcilinux_init,driverclass}.c` and its explicit module manifest against the generic PCI MapPCI result and selected HDAudio BAR0 consumer (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:157-174`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/hda_hidd.c:162-185`). OD851's unchecked `/dev/mem` open can leave a bad descriptor at startup. Independently, a raw `mmap2` failure after a successful open is returned as a nonzero negative `IPTR` from MapPCI; the configured HDAudio attachment rejects only zero and can pass it on as a register base (OD1891). The exact image containing both optional/explicit targets, host failure mode and subsequent controller access remain conditional; no PCI map or audio device was run.

DesignWare I²C transaction and device-method recheck (OD848/OD849/OD1865/OD1866): reread the selected `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/{dwi2c_class,dwi2c_hw}.c` transaction, FIFO, STOP, programming and adapter methods against `workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cdeviceclass.c:60-150` and the OpenSBI boot target. `WriteRead` holds the controller semaphore across `DWI2C_HWTransfer`; the transfer normalizes null buffers to zero lengths, rejects an empty transaction, and bounds address before programming. Its read loop limits outstanding commands to `rxDepth`, drains only until the requested length and has a stall bound, so this pass found no separate local request-buffer overrun for a valid `rxDepth`. The selected device `WriteBytes`/`WriteVec` still use primitive methods rejected by this controller (OD848), and `WriteWord` still submits two bytes from its three-byte buffer (OD849). `dwi2c_waitstop` checks STOP_DET before TX_ABRT if both are reported simultaneously; whether the selected hardware can expose both bits together with an unsuccessful transfer needs a controller-status contract, so no new candidate is credited. Runtime FIFO depth, simultaneous status behavior and external direct method callers remain open. No I²C transaction was run.

Printer per-unit multi-opener lifecycle follow-up (OD1890): reread the entire selected parent open path (`workbench/devs/printer/printer.c:53-100`), per-unit open/close/expunge vectors, worker command loop and `pd_Close` (`driver.c:95-187,466-492,526-667`), the selected PostScript open callback (`workbench/printers/postscript/postscript.c:558-565`) and LDDemon's close/unload wrapper (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:599-624`). The parent refuses a second open through `printer.device`, but its unit is also published by a configurable separate device name. A direct opener of that name reaches the per-unit vector, which does not increment its base open count or reject an existing owner. Closing the direct request sends the single worker its terminal `CMD_CLOSEDEVICE`, clears the parent's slot, and expunges the base while the parent opener can still hold it. This is OD1890, separate from OD1889's earlier publication-before-port window and OD388's failed close-port allocation. No checked-in caller uses the configured per-unit name directly; external/dynamic callers, request timing and actual segment unloading remain untested. The custom Expunge raw `Remove`/`FreeMem` and concurrent per-unit AddDevice consequence has been folded into the cross-report Exec finding EK271 because it shares the same missing DeviceList write lock; no separate OD finding is counted.

Printer unit publication and worker-startup cross-check (OD1889): traced the selected `printer.device` parent opener, its configurable per-unit `AddDevice` publication, per-unit open/BeginIO vectors, worker startup message and `pd_Init` port initialization (`workbench/devs/printer/printer.c:69-93`; `driver.c:95-115,171-187,408-413,538-549,764-850`) through Exec lookup, zeroed `MakeLibrary`, `PutMsg` and `AddTail` (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:98-117`; `makelibrary.c:109`; `putmsg.c:64-89`; `addtail.c:49-62`). The parent holds its unit semaphore until the startup handshake finishes and is excluded from this race. A separate direct open by the published per-unit name can enter while the worker has not initialized `pd_Unit`; message insertion then uses zeroed list links. OD4287 details the separate failed-reply-port worker-lifetime branch. No checked-in direct per-unit-name client was established, so OD1889 requires an external or dynamically named client; scheduling and running printer behavior remain untested.

Serial parameter transaction follow-up (OD1888): reread selected PC, OpenSBI RISC-V, hosted Unix and native m68k `SetParameters` methods against the public HIDD tag definitions, their baud-change helpers and `serial.device`'s `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` caller (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:363-431,678-695`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:352-419,666-707`; `arch/all-unix/hidd/serial/SerialUnitClass.c:443-508,678-723`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/serial/SerialUnitClass.c:258-289`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:788-804`). PC and RISC-V commit earlier tag values before a later invalid tag makes the method fail; both defer LCR programming until success, so a failed call can leave internal framing out of step with hardware and a later baud change can apply it. Their `TAG_SET_MCR` branch writes hardware immediately, even before complete validation. Unix also mutates state on a false return, but its termios writer is compiled out; m68k validates its supported fixed mode without those mutable fields. The selected device caller's invalid-stop-bit route also hits existing OD58 and cannot be used to claim ordinary later recovery. External direct HIDD clients and UART hardware remain open; no parameter call was run.

OpenSBI PCIDT virtual-IRQ ownership cross-check (OD850/OD1409/OD1411/OD1412): reread the selected bridge's MSI target and reservation sequence (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:724-772`), device vector acquisition (`pcidt_deviceclass.c:145-174`), controller programming (`pcidt_access.c:363-465`) and module expunge hook (`pcidt_init.c:55-77`) against OpenSBI `KrnAllocIRQ`/`KrnFreeIRQ` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/allocirq.c:27-115`; `freeirq.c:51-58`). PCIDT requests at most its fixed vector count, halves failures, retains each successful bridge reservation for the boot-selected module lifetime, and contains no selected `KrnFreeIRQ` release. Its per-device vector occupancy is separate from the kernel virtual-IRQ bitmap; repeated obtains and absent releases are already OD850, while target-page retention on failed reservation and unchecked IRQ-controller registration are OD1409/OD1411. The unlocked per-device vector choice remains OD1412. This cross-check establishes no ordinary PCIDT caller for EK539's invalid-release arguments and adds no duplicate finding. External PCI clients, bridge hardware, and future removable-module cleanup remain open; no PCI or IRQ operation was run.
OpenSBI multi-bridge MSI registration failure recheck (OD1411 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the failure path from the `KrnModifyIRQA()` four-slot controller table (`kernel_intern.h:191-199`; `modifyirq.c:89-112`) through PCIDT discovery’s eight-bridge cap (`pcidt.h:42,164`), successful virtual-range reservation and `PCIDT_MSIInit()` readiness (`pcidt_driverclass.c:724-772`; `pcidt_access.c:363-379`), ignored registration result, and device `ObtainVectors()`/`PCIDT_MSIEnable()` path (`pcidt_deviceclass.c:145-174`; `pcidt_access.c:412-465`). On the fifth distinct MSI-capable DesignWare bridge with available virtual sources, failed registration leaves `msiReady` true and the endpoint path can still report vector acquisition success; no controller record fans out its pending status. This is the existing OD1411, not a new ID. The selected OpenSBI boot package includes PCIDT (`boot/mmakefile.src:109`; `pcidt/mmakefile.src:15-16,32-33`); ACPI-discovered bridges set `msiIrq=0` and do not trigger this path. No firmware topology, PCI endpoint, or interrupt was exercised; source-only.

RISC-V UART DLAB timeout follow-up (OD1887): traced the bounded transmitter-empty poll, unconditional divisor-latch sequence, DW UART busy-detect note/handler and 16550 offset aliases (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:688-707,743-746`; `dwuart_io.h:19-27`; `compiler/include/hardware/uart.h:9-15`). If the wait expires while the transmitter is still busy and the controller discards the DLAB-setting LCR write as described locally, the next two writes address TX and IER rather than DLL and DLM. The method still returns success to selected serial.device. Hardware timing and actual LCR rejection remain untested; this conditional path is distinct from OD1885's no-clock return and OD1886's overflowing divisor.

OD1887 serial.device interrupt-gating recheck (2026-10-17): traced `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` from `Disable()` at line 716 through the baud HIDD call and to the sole matching `Enable()` at line 811, then followed the OpenSBI HIDD's only THRI refill call (`serial_init.c:713-812`; `dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:738-741`). The selected OpenSBI configuration is single-hart; while this call polls TEMT, the UART interrupt handler cannot refill the transmit FIFO. Bytes already loaded can still drain in hardware, but pending software data cannot advance. Updated OD1887's trigger and confidence: timeout with a character still in flight can lead to the locally documented discarded DLAB write and subsequent aliasing; timing and controller behavior remain conditional. Updated both detailed copies; no UART output was run. Source-only.

RISC-V UART divisor-width follow-up (OD1886): `set_baudrate` accepts 50..115200 and computes `inputClock/(speed*16)` but writes only its low two bytes to the DLL/DLM latches (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:666-707`; `dwuart_io.h:34-45`). With a described 100 MHz input clock and 50 baud request, the quotient is 125000 and the programmed 16-bit value is 59464, giving approximately 105 baud by the same formula; the helper and selected serial.device still report/store success. A clock-provider configuration with no local rate is separately OD1885. The bounded TEMT wait's distinct DLAB-rejection path is now OD1887. No UART or board was run.

RISC-V DesignWare UART clock-source follow-up (OD1885): traced FDT `clock-frequency` default zero through port discovery, unit construction, `set_baudrate`, `SetBaudrate` and selected `serial.device` bookkeeping (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/dwuart_init.c:123-128`; `SerialUnitClass.c:142-149,327-340,666-707`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:765-782`). A valid changed rate returns success without a divisor write when the board uses a separate clock provider and omits this local frequency property. The generic device then stores the requested rate as if applied. The stale HIDD rate cache is consolidated with the PC equivalent in OD1736. The actual clock-provider topology and hardware speed remain unverified; no UART request was run.



OpenSBI DesignWare UART firmware-input recheck (no new candidate): reread the complete selected discovery, init and expunge path against the shared FDT property helper and the unit register/IRQ callers (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/dwuart_init.c:49-179`; `arch/riscv-all/linklibs/fdt/fdt.c:165-217`; `SerialUnitClass.c:193-261,712-747`; `dwuart_io.h:19-65`). The status gate treats an absent property as enabled; valid `ok`/`okay` values follow that path, while disabled values are skipped. Register-shift, access-width, size, clock and one-cell interrupt data are passed onward as described in the per-file ledger; no independent defect was established without an invalid or board-specific property contract. `FDT_GetReg`'s lack of parent-range translation and its cell-count bounds remain tracked as EK285/EK779, not duplicated here. A source-tree inventory found no `.dts`, `.dtsi`, `.dtb` or `.dtbo` input; this module receives `KRN_FlattenedDeviceTree` from firmware (`dwuart_init.c:157-166`). Actual status, register span, parent ranges, clock provider and PLIC encoding therefore remain unverified. No UART, FDT or hardware path was run.

DesignWare I²C constructor sentinel recheck (OD1155): `DWI2C__Root__New` starts `unit` at `(IPTR)-1`, searches controller MMIO bases, then compares `unit >= (IPTR)psd->ctrlCount` before indexing (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_class.c:61-112`). `IPTR` is unsigned in this checkout (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:83-91`), so the unmatched sentinel is the maximum pointer-width value and the bounds check rejects it. The selected RTC bridge supplies its FDT-derived bus base and checks a null bus-object result (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/battclock/battclock_i2c.c:70-94`). This confirms OD1155's failed-bus consequence for an unmatched mux-channel address and rules out a separate before-array access claim. Controller enumeration, generic I²C device helper methods and the exact board topology retain the row-level open contracts; no I²C operation was run.

Console zero-length caller recheck (OD1190): `rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:363-366` does set `conreadio->io_Length = 0`, but only while preparing the request for `OpenDevice` in the handler's plain-device mode. Its `startread` resets the length to one for that mode or `CONSOLEBUFFER_SIZE` for console.device immediately before `SendIO` (`:644-659`). This confirms that the zero-length `CMD_READ` trigger remains limited to a direct console.device client in the checked selected handler path. The console worker's paste-signal branch calls `answer_requests(NULL)` after `pasteData`, but `pasteData` has already called `answer_requests` with the owning unit (`rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:145-172,257-273`); the NULL call is redundant, not an additional stranded-read finding. External clients and scheduling remain open; no I/O was run.

MinGW timer-device failed-start rollback: reread `arch/all-mingw32/timer/timer_init.c:45-132` and its selected `rom/timer/timervblank.c:20-58` helper against generated failed-init ordering (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:40-74`). After `KrnAddIRQHandler`, `Timer_Init` installs the VBlank server and starts host timer 1; if `StartClock` returns failure, `_set_libinit` invokes expunge hooks before freeing the failed module base. `vblank_Expunge` removes the linked VBlank server and `Timer_Expunge` removes the IRQ token and closes the host library handle. A failure before VBlank insertion leaves its zero-initialized node unlinked, and its expunge hook skips removal. This check does not add a dangling failed-start callback to OD2546/OD1878 or EK672. Host `SetWaitableTimer` failure semantics, runtime delivery and wider shutdown ordering remain open. No timer was started.

Speech/narrator playback and resource caller recheck: reread the selected `workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:88-244,245-517,519-719` and `workbench/devs/narrator/narrator.c:115-335,335-530` worker, sink, audio acquisition and final-close sequences against `workbench/libs/speechcore/aros_resource.c:12-68`. A missing `dos.library` base makes the optional resource loader return null without calling DOS; both devices then use built-in voice or translator data, so this is not a null-DOS call finding. Both final-close commands are queued to their own synthesis worker; the current render's finish/error path waits for or aborts in-flight audio requests before that worker can process `ReleaseAudio`, so the checked ordinary close ordering does not establish a playback-buffer use-after-free. OD3210 now records the shared speech/narrator close-allocation failure, and OD3211 still covers the renderer's unsent partial output. External direct requests, audio.device completion timing and narrator mouth-read status semantics remain open. No speech/audio request was run.

Gameport first-open concurrency correction (OD1884 withdrawn): the initial read of `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:186-279` and generic `rom/exec/opendevice.c:88-133` suggested that two CPUs could pass the shared null checks simultaneously. The selected LDDemon OpenDevice replacement obtains a per-device object semaphore before calling the original Exec vector and releases it after the Open hook returns (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:385-397,469-493,533-555`). Thus ordinary gameport opens are serialized, and the inferred duplicate consumer/buffer sequence is not credited. Pre-LDDemon or direct-original-vector callers were not established. OD43 is detailed in AROS-other-drivers.md: BeginIO can see an empty ring before enqueueing while a cross-CPU mouse callback publishes an event and checks an empty pending queue, leaving the later-enqueued read unserviced until another event. No concurrent open was run.

Print backend direct-caller census (OD873-OD874 scope): searched checked-in C and headers under `rom`, `arch`, `compiler` and `workbench` for the file/tool device names and reread `printer.device`'s `pd_Init`, `pd_PWrite` and `CMD_FLUSH` dispatch (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:218-241,405-455,587-596,690-710`). Printer preferences can select `printtofile` and the worker opens two requests on that unit, substantiating OD873's in-tree multi-opener route. The worker sends only `CMD_WRITE` to the backend and handles `CMD_FLUSH` itself; no checked-in direct caller of either backend sends `CMD_UPDATE`, `CMD_FLUSH`, or an unsupported first command. OD874 therefore stays a direct-device API candidate rather than a demonstrated printer-worker path. `printtotool` has no checked-in name selection beyond its module itself; user-configured printer device names remain possible. Generated, external and binary clients are still pending. No print job was run.

Printer file/tool DOS-error narrowing candidate recheck (former OD1883 withdrawn; 2026-10-25): reread both synchronous `BeginIO` write branches (`workbench/devs/printtofile/printtofile.c:77-120`; `workbench/devs/printtotool/printtotool.c:110-153`) against DOS `Write`, the standard DOS error definitions, and Exec's signed-byte `io_Error` field. A standard value such as `ERROR_DISK_FULL = 221` is observed as signed -35, but the low eight bits are preserved and all checked-in standard DOS errors fit that byte. No selected direct-client contract proves that callers require the original signed LONG representation or fail to recover/use the byte code. Therefore this is not retained as an independent bug; stale OD15/OD873-874 cross-references in the former note were not carried forward. The source-level OD76 semaphore failure and OD77 directory-lock leak remain independently supported. No write failure or direct device request was run; source-only.

PC IPMI expunge recheck (OD1687): read the selected firmware-driver registration and `smbios-ipmi.conf` against generated expunge, `rom/oop/removeclass.c:47-59`, and `rom/oop/basemetaclass.c:498-523`. The generated shutdown removes and disposes the OOP class; `OOP_RemoveClass` only unlinks the public class node, and the metaclass dispose releases its class metadata and dispatch tables without testing for live instances. The registered hardware-root children are not removed in the selected initializer, which strengthens the conditional lifetime consequence already described in OD1687. The exact host action that requests expunge remains outside this source-only check; no teardown was run.

Serial/parallel reset and printer-abort caller recheck (OD57/OD61): reread both `CMD_RESET`/`CMD_FLUSH` branches and receive/write callbacks (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:567-648`; `serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-94,132-175`; `workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_init.c:483-540`; `parallel_interrupthandlers.c:21-102,109-176`) against printer.device's two underlying requests (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:200-242,419-433,590-595`). OD61 already covers reset's stale active pointers, so no duplicate reset candidate was added. Printer `CMD_FLUSH` calls `AbortIO` on both requests unconditionally even when completed or never sent, and `WaitIOStd` marks completed ones idle; the selected serial/parallel abort vectors route all non-active-read requests through `Remove` without checking queue membership (`serial_init.c:872-905`; `parallel_init.c:618-652`; `rom/exec/remove.c:49-62`). OD57 now includes this selected idle-flush trigger as well as its active-write trigger. Backend completion timing and actual printer flush behavior remain untested; no I/O ran.

Late keyboard opener qualifier follow-up (OD1877): reread the selected open, key callback, per-unit event decoder and ring size (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:159-165,347-379,437-477,608-644`; `keyboard_intern.h:24,75-81`). After a held Shift press plus 127 other events, the shared writer wraps to zero while its matrix still records Shift down. A newly opened zeroed unit sees cursor zero equal to the writer and queues a read; with the earlier opener idle, the next ordinary key completes that read without a Shift qualifier because the new unit has consumed no modifier event. This adds OD1877, distinct from OD1580's pre-open replay and OD1876's `CMD_CLEAR` skip. OD1876 now also states the complementary clear-a-buffered-press sequence, which leaves Shift absent while held. The selected input worker has one opener; no checked in-tree second opener or runtime timing was established. External clients and platform event ordering remain open; no keyboard was run.

Serial/parallel large-read recheck (OD11): reread both selected receive callbacks (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-94`; `workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_interrupthandlers.c:21-102`) with their `CMD_READ` submission paths. Their local `UWORD` destination offsets wrap at 65,536 bytes even though request `io_Length` and `io_Actual` are wider, so a 65,536-byte request does not complete at that boundary and later bytes overwrite the start of its buffer. The report now states this exact direct-client trigger. The separate serial buffered-copy helper uses a `UWORD` count, but its valid single-pass ring occupancy is below that boundary because the unit ring length is itself `UWORD`; OD11 no longer treats the helper alone as evidence of the wrap. External callers and actual receive timing remain open; no data was received.

Keyboard clear/qualifier follow-up (OD1876): reread the complete event-state path in `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:159-165,307-309,347-379,437-477,608-644` with the per-opener fields in `keyboard_intern.h`. `CMD_CLEAR` skips all unread ring entries by moving only `kbu_readPos`, while `kbu_Qualifiers` changes only when `writeEvents` consumes modifier entries. A client that consumed Shift-down, then skips a buffered Shift-up, receives its next key with Shift still set; the callback's independent physical matrix has already cleared it. The selected input.device worker has no `CMD_CLEAR` call, so this is limited to a direct API sequence and no in-tree trigger is asserted. HIDD/platform timing and wider external clients remain open; no key sequence was run.

OpenSBI long-timer arithmetic recheck: `usec2tick`'s 64-bit intermediate would overflow for a 22-day interval at the selected EFI fallback's 10 MHz timebase (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/timer/ticks.c:25-28`). However, `Timer0Setup` converts only the head of the MICROHZ request list (`:83-109`). The selected `USE_VBLANK_EMU` build inserts a recurring 20 ms MICROHZ request (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/timer/make.opts`; `timer_init.c:60-82`) and requeues it before each return from the timer IRQ (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:286-318`). That request remains ahead of a 22-day client request, so the checked long interval never reaches this conversion in the selected build. The generic completion path also checks the original elapsed request time (`lowlevel.c:279-285`). No candidate is credited from the overflow observation; disabled-VBlank variants and altered VBlank frequency remain separate configuration questions. No timer was run.

Console request-lifecycle follow-up: reread the full `beginio` and `abortio` bodies in `rom/devs/console/console.c:265-464` against the worker's command-port dequeue, pending-read insertion and completion (`rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:454-492,529-578`). `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` writes a too-short error into `io_Error` and then overwrites it with the local zero error on quick completion (now detailed as OD2249); all checked in-tree query callers use a full result structure. Every `CMD_READ`, including length zero, still queues to the worker; a zero-length request without buffered input waits for input (OD1190). The worker holds `consoleTaskLock` across GetMsg, pending-list insertion and reply, and AbortIO takes the same lock before removing and replying, so this checked dequeue path does not establish a second abort/remove race. The selected CON: handler's reads use one byte or its positive fixed buffer size and its close path aborts/WaitIOs an outstanding console read (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:644-658,1238-1261`); no ordinary selected zero-length read or close-with-pending-read trigger was found. Direct clients, generated vector dispatch, worker shutdown and cross-task close remain open; no I/O was run.

OpenSBI DesignWare I²C address-path follow-up (OD1866): reread the complete 251-line `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_class.c` body against public HIDD address types, the generic device-class constructor/getter and `DWI2C_HWTransfer`. WriteRead and ProbeAddress both mask `(shifted_address >> 1)` to seven bits before invoking the hardware helper (`dwi2c_class.c:151-200`); its own `> 0x7f` refusal is consequently unreachable for those callers (`dwi2c_hw.c:405-414`). An unsupported shifted `0x1d0` aliases target `0x68`, so the API can return a probe or transfer result for a different slave. The selected RTC obtains its address from FDT and shifts it (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/battclock/battclock_i2c.c:100-119`); whether firmware supplies an out-of-range value is open. The class's unsupported byte methods still return false as OD848 describes; Root Get still delegates generic timing attributes. No hardware or malformed-address call was run.

OpenSBI DesignWare I²C transfer follow-up (OD1865): reread all 13 functions in the 437-line `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_hw.c` body and its two direct class callers (`dwi2c_class.c:151-200`). The FIFO read/write loops bound stalls and inspect transmit aborts; the selected `WriteRead` and `ProbeAddress` methods hold the controller semaphore throughout `DWI2C_HWTransfer`. The distinct result-path defect is the ignored final `dwi2c_enable(FALSE)` return after STOP: its helper can report a failed status handshake, while the transfer still returns its earlier success and the next transfer requires a successful disable before reprogramming (`dwi2c_hw.c:146-163,193-198,423-436`). OD1865 limits the consequence to the reported controller state and a possible later transfer failure; it does not claim wrong bytes on the completed transfer. Firmware timing, exact enable-status hardware behavior and other clients remain open. OD2245 is detailed in the report: with a known input clock, the driver applies fixed 100/400-kHz timing counts regardless of other accepted `clock-frequency` values. Full offset inventory found `IC_COMP_PARAM_1` at `0xf4` as the highest 32-bit access; discovery accepts any nonzero FDT span, maps only its page-rounded range, then probes that register before validating a minimum `0xf8` span (OD2508). No in-tree DTB with a short span was found; no DTB or controller was run. No controller operation was run.

Generic I²C delay-unit follow-up (OD1864): `I2C_UDelay` requests seconds as `delay / 10000` but microseconds as `10 * (delay % 10000)` (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c:40-49`), making a 10,000-unit delay one second rather than the 100 milliseconds implied by its own ten-microsecond remainder and the selected Nouveau adapter's explicit ten-microsecond tag conversion (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:233-241`). The selected bus constructor and Root Set permit arbitrary HoldTime/RiseFallTime values (`i2cclass.c:419-456,465-539`), and inherited bit-level operations call this helper. The Sam440 bit-level subclass is a selected compatible backend, but defaults are 2/5 and no checked in-tree client sets either delay to 10,000 or more. Thus OD1864 is a conditional public-configuration finding; exact timer and hardware effects were not run. Earlier OD1151 and OD1817 concern zero or concurrent timing updates, not this conversion boundary.

Generic I²C bus/timer follow-up: reread the complete selected `workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c` body from its timer-backed delay through inherited bit/byte, Address/Probe/Stop, WriteRead, attributes and init/dispose hooks. OD1152's distinction holds: WriteRead keeps `driver_lock` around the whole transaction, while device-class WriteBytes/WriteVec invoke individually locked primitives. Rechecked its reusable timer request against Exec `DoIO`/`WaitIO` (`rom/exec/doio.c:50-77`; `waitio.c:52-87`): the request uses the current task as its temporary reply signal target, and a nonquick completion is removed from the reply-port queue before the next delay; this does not establish a stale queued-reply fault. The reserved `SIGB_SINGLE` signal can be shared with other task activity, but WaitIO rechecks the request's message state after a wake, so an unrelated signal alone does not complete this delay. The selected Sam440 bit-level subclass and battery-clock caller remain the concrete inherited-transfer path; external clients, interrupt timing and physical I²C behavior remain open. No timer or bus operation was run.

Generic I²C device-class method follow-up: reread all 14 method bodies in `workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cdeviceclass.c:31-372`, including the one-transfer Read/Write/WriteRead helpers, byte and word variants, multi-byte/vector loops, and Root New/Get/Set. The full-transaction methods delegate to the bus's `I2C_WriteRead`; OD849 remains the independent three-byte word buffer submitted with length two. OD848 and OD1152 remain confined to `WriteBytes` and `WriteVec`, which use individually dispatched Address/PutByte/Stop steps. The selected RISC-V and Sam440 battery clocks instead call WriteRead directly, and a repository method-call search found no selected C caller of the byte-array/vector or word-write methods. A search of selected I²C device constructors and these clocks found no post-construction `OOP_SetAttrs` client for device timing attributes; Root Set's unsynchronized field updates and its lack of superclass forwarding therefore remain external-client contract questions rather than new numbered findings. Exact hardware timing, generated OOP dispatch and external clients remain open; no bus transaction was run.

Cross-scope I²C caller census recheck: the selected IntelGMA and Radeon display probes and Sam440/OpenSBI battery clocks call the device's `WriteRead` route; Nouveau's DRM compatibility adapter also creates a temporary device for `WriteRead` and `Write` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:21-86`). That adapter's allocation and transfer-dispatch defects remain graphics GD276–GD277, while its generic I²C timing stays at the default HoldTime/RiseFallTime and does not establish OD1864's long-delay trigger. VMwareSVGA carries a byte-identical compatibility copy, but its bus-registration caller has not been established (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:21-86`); do not generalize Nouveau's selected trigger to it. The shared `I2C_WriteRead` body returns false on address/byte failure and leaves callers to honor that result, which IntelGMA and Radeon do not (graphics GD5979/GD205). External direct users of the exported byte/word/vector helpers remain open.

Keyboard event-result recheck (OD1008): `BeginIO` clears `io_Error` but leaves `io_Actual` untouched for `KBD_READEVENT` (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:267-280,347-379`). The shared `writeEvents` helper computes event capacity, may stop after fewer records when the unit catches up to the ring writer, and terminates the linked event chain; it never stores the number of bytes written (`:398-495`). Both immediate completion and the queued callback's `ReplyMsg` use that helper (`:369-379,665-684`). `KBD_READMATRIX` on the same request does set `io_Actual` (`:341-345`), giving OD1008 a concrete stale-value reuse sequence for a direct keyboard client. The selected input.device one-event consumer reads the event and error rather than this count (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:478-515`), so no forwarding failure is asserted. The short-buffer callback instead replies with `IOERR_BADLENGTH`, as the keyboard row records; this is separate from gameport's OD1191. No request sequence was run.

USB/HIDD directory inventory follow-up: all 96 `.c` files under `rom/usb/classes`, all 11 under `rom/bluetooth/classes`, all six under `arch/i386-pc/drivers`, and all 11 under `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd` have individual rows in this ledger. Under `rom/hidds`, 55 of 102 C files have other-driver rows; the 47 without such rows are precisely in the graphics HIDD directories (`gfx`, `efifbgfx`, `hidd`, `vesagfx`) or disk HIDD directories (`ata_pci`, `scsi/wd33c93`), which have separate region reports. These counts establish local path inventory only; individual build selection, callers, hardware contracts and completed audits still require the row-level checks.

Core-device directory inventory follow-up: a recursive C-file comparison under `rom/devs` found 89 current `.c` files. All 21 files in its non-disk directories (`console`, `gameport`, `input` and `keyboard`) have individual rows in this ledger: 15, 1, 4 and 1 respectively. Two `trackdisk` C files also have cross-review rows here; the remaining 66 files are in `ahci`, `ata`, `nvme`, `scsi`, `sdcard` and `virtio`, which belong to the separate disk/block review; this inventory does not establish that every listed body or caller is fully audited. The five printer, four audio, three serial, three parallel and five Filesave AHI C files under `workbench/devs` also each have individual rows. A title-similarity check prompted a direct recheck of OD397 and OD409: their `CmdTrackType` allocation/copy defects appear in separate selected `via-rhine/handler.c:378-422` and `rhine/request.c:735-783` bodies with separate module manifests, so both remain as affected-driver findings rather than being withdrawn as same-source duplicates. Wider build manifests and caller contracts remain open.

USB Ethernet packet-type finding reconciliation: OD1261 duplicated the same seven selected `cmdTrackType` failed-allocation paths and missing `Permit` already recorded by OD1210. The latter also covers Bluetooth PAN. The USB `devBeginIO` dispatcher calls `cmdTrackType` directly and completes its request without balancing the task's Forbid nesting (for example `rom/usb/classes/pegasuseth/dev.c:1166-1178,1220-1294`); that extra consequence is now folded into OD1210. OD1261 is withdrawn, not a new defect. No allocation failure was run; external SANA clients remain open.

Virtual USB queue-lock scope recheck (former OD1691): `AttemptSemaphore` forwards the task as exclusive owner; `InternalAttemptSemaphore` reverses its queue-count increment and returns false when a different task owns the semaphore (`rom/exec/attemptsemaphore.c:53-56`; `rom/exec/semaphores.c:164-209`). All four handler-task queue passes ignore that false result, traverse and remove queue nodes without the producer lock, and then call `ReleaseSemaphore` (`rom/usb/vusbhc/vusbhci_device.c:58-102`; producers obtain the matching locks in `rom/usb/vusbhc/vusbhci_commands.c:1065,1104,1139,1174`). Release decrements semaphore nesting/count before its optional ownership alert (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:80-100`). The code-level defect remains conditional on concurrent producer activity while the worker fails its try-lock. However, exact target search finds no checked-in parent dependency on `kernel-usb-vusbhci`; the module is only defined by its standalone manifest (`rom/usb/vusbhc/mmakefile.src:4-11`) and is omitted from the `kernel-usb` aggregate (`rom/usb/mmakefile.src:6-16`). Therefore this is an optional, explicitly built module candidate, not a demonstrated selected in-tree device path; it is not counted in the active findings report pending target-selection evidence. No transfer was run.

Clip finalization follow-up (OD1843): `toClip` marks its text copy successful before closing two unknown-size chunks; both `PopChunk` results are discarded, and the command caller returns `RETURN_OK` from that flag (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:160-171,213-239`). IFFParse can fail on either size rewrite or padding write (`workbench/libs/iffparse/popchunk.c:77-150`); clipboard.device routes the writes to its DOS backing file (`workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c:775-795,835-862`). The selected clipboard IFF seek hook updates only a logical offset, so no propagated seek failure is claimed. This is distinct from OD1842's body short write and GD1417's ConClip caller. The full Clip command body, backing-handler error timing and actual finalization behavior remain open; no failure was run.

Clipboard short-write propagation follow-up (OD1842): the selected RAM handler's `WriteData` writes available bytes, can stop when `AddDataBlock` fails, and returns the positive prefix count while setting `IoErr` (`rom/filesys/ram/filesystem.c:876-960`; `commands.c:637-668`). Clipboard.device records that count in `io_Actual` and treats only `-1` as an error (`workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c:835-864`). The IFFParse clipboard stream forwards only `DoIO`'s error for `IFFCMD_WRITE`, while `WriteStream` and `WriteChunkBytes` account for the full requested length (`workbench/libs/iffparse/clipboardfuncs.c:91-103`; `basicfuncs.c:392-425`; `writechunkbytes.c:58-84`). Selected Clip compares that falsely full result with its text length, sets `ok`, and returns `RETURN_OK` from its caller (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:160-171,218-239`). This is distinct from OD1399's read count and OD810's padding writes. Exact allocation-failure timing, later chunk finalization and external clients remain open; no short write was run.

Clipboard final-close follow-up (OD1841): traced `CMD_UPDATE` from `beginio` through `updateCb`'s unchecked `Close`, posted-reader signal, hook notification and successful request reply (`workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c:336-340,494-498,867-917`). DOS `Close` returns the selected handler's `ACTION_END` result (`rom/dos/close.c:68-81`). RAM's `CmdEnd` rejects closing a changed file while its volume is write-protected, and `CmdWriteProtect` can turn that state on (`rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:510-545,2532-2557`). Thus a failed final close can still be announced as a successful update; the IFFParse clipboard cleanup discards the update result independently (`workbench/libs/iffparse/clipboardfuncs.c:143-150`). This is separate from OD810's unchecked gap writes and OD12's failed read. Handler-specific failure timing, external direct clients and runtime write-protection changes remain open; no close failure was run.

Speech-device partial-init and queue-ownership recheck: `Init` opens DOS and Utility, explicitly closes acquired bases when Utility or worker-task creation fails, and registers only `ADD2INITLIB` (`workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:519-576`). RP1 synthetic xHCI BAR caller follow-up (OD1839): traced config initialization and writes through generic PCI BAR probing, public Base0 setting, `MapPCI` and the selected xHCI controller (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/rp1/rp1_pci.c:38-91,151-155`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciutil.c:68-94`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:664-691,1236-1247`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_controllerclass.c:82-106`). The constructor's all-ones sizing probe restores the original BAR, and ordinary selected xHCI startup only reads it. A direct public Base0 setter or config writer can instead persist a new BAR; the RP1 backend changes the synthetic value but has no register relocation and returns the new value as the mapped pointer. The result is recorded as a conditional client-triggered bug, not an ordinary boot failure. Other PCI clients and hardware behavior remain open; no device was run.

RP1 synthetic PCI DMA allocation follow-up: traced `PCIRP1__Hidd_PCIDriver__AllocPCIMem` and `FreePCIMem` through the selected pcixhci aligned-allocation wrapper and the AArch64 mapping implementation (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/rp1/rp1_pci.c:179-244`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_arospci.c:473-506`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mapglobal.c:17-28`; `mmu.c:139-231,309-338`). The xHCI wrapper stores the exact original allocation pointer for `FREEPCIMEM`, including its bounds-driven retry. RP1 stores its raw pointer and rounded mapping size in the two pointer words immediately before the returned page-aligned address; the requested extra page covers alignment loss and this metadata for ordinary nonoverflowing sizes. A successful AArch64 map has already created the page-table levels needed to restore the same virtual span to write-back memory on free, so the unchecked restore result alone does not establish a normal allocation-failure path. If a large map fails after earlier descriptors were edited, RP1 frees its backing allocation while those edits remain, but the partial-map defect is already EK89 and the selected xHCI size/cross-table sequence has not been established. The public size is `ULONG`, so on AArch64 the page-round expression can wrap for values near `ULONG_MAX`; that path yields a zero rounded length, and the selected `KrnMapGlobal` rejects length zero before the temporary page is released (`mapglobal.c:17-28`; `mmu.c:309-318`). It does not produce a successful undersized DMA buffer. The selected xHCI allocator callers pass controller-derived context/ring sizes and the lowest page size advertised by the controller (`xhci_controllerclass.c:339-452`; `xhci_hcd.c:1136-1147,1274-1300,1845-1851`), with the same base pointer returned to its paired free wrapper; no size-overflow caller or length mismatch was found. `xhciPageSize` returns zero if the controller's page-size bitmap is empty; scratch allocations then fail cleanly at the zero-size driver allocator, while earlier rings pass zero as their bounds. The valid-hardware status of an empty bitmap and any resulting boundary behavior remain an external controller-contract question, not a selected defect established here. Concurrent mapping changes and hardware effects remain open; no DMA allocation was run.

Akiko nvdisk backend dispatch and cleanup recheck: the m68k override initializes a semaphore and marks `nvd_location` with `AKIKO_LOCATION` only after detecting Akiko and allocating that semaphore (`arch/m68k-amiga/nvdisk/akiko.c:385-408`). `nvdisk_init` returns immediately on that success; otherwise it opens DOS and tries the filesystem storage location (`workbench/libs/nonvolatile/nvdisk/nvdisk_init.c:26-45`). Akiko's public read, write, delete, info, protect and list implementations obtain/release the same semaphore around EEPROM operations (`akiko.c:410-644`), and their checked successful image allocations are freed on the local exits. `NVDisk_ArchWrite` writes changed aligned 16-byte pages and propagates a page failure as `NVERR_FATAL`; delete/protect return a Boolean failure. Hardware timing, partial EEPROM write recovery, externally altered images and exact CD32 startup choice remain open; no hardware transaction was run.

Speech/narrator control-state follow-up: traced `CMD_STOP`, `CMD_START`, `CMD_RESET`, `CMD_FLUSH`, queued request abort and worker completion in both devices (`workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:438-515,647-723`; `workbench/devs/narrator/narrator.c:455-515,679-787`). STOP sets the stopped flag without waiting for the worker; START clears it and signals the worker, so a worker sleeping in the stopped loop can resume. RESET/FLUSH publish cancel and increment the pending-control count before queueing their request under the same device semaphore used by dequeue; removing a queued control in AbortIO decrements that count. No distinct lost-wakeup or missing-control-reply case was established in these selected paths. The narrator-specific last-queued-write mouth-read gap remains OD368. Cross-task state changes during audio completion, exceptional worker termination, and external command sequencing remain pending; no control sequence was run.

Virtual USB control-queue ownership follow-up (OD1814): traced the complete worker's control `ForeachNode` loop into the synchronous libusb control helper, `ReplyMsg`, Exec's reply-port insertion, and `WaitIO`/`DeleteIORequest` (`rom/usb/vusbhc/vusbhci_device.c:58-68`; `vusbhci_bridge.c:341-462`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-201`; `rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`; `putmsg.c:83-92`; `waitio.c:65-80`; `deleteiorequest.c:43-48`). Timer abort/completion exclusion: reread complete generic `AbortIO`, `BeginIO`, and the `TimerProcessMicroHZ`/`TimerProcessVBlank` completion loops (`rom/timer/abortio.c:45-91`; `beginio.c:45-78`; `lowlevel.c:264-402`). OD1810 start-failure qualification: `cmdStartRTIso` makes two `xhciStartIsochIO` calls after two successful prefill calls (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:1631-1650`). A failed `xhciInitIOTRBTransfer` leaves its PTD buffer-valid but neither active nor queued (`xhci_isoch.c:286-329`), so the second start call can select and retry the same PTD. Both preparation attempts must fail for the report's no-transfer/false-success outcome; if memory recovers for the second attempt, one PTD can start while the command still reports success. The finding now states this narrower trigger. Later retries may encounter still-buffer-valid slots; the selected controller normally provisions eight PTDs (`pcixhci.h:87`; `pcixhci_arospci.c:91`), so a single failed start does not prove all slots are exhausted. No failure was injected.

OD1811 withdrawal recheck (2026-10-09): the selected SonixcamTool selects the streaming alternate interface and completes camera/sensor setup before allocating the RT ISO handler, then performs only Start/Stop around snapshot capture. Its source does not switch the endpoint type or submit a competing non-ISO request on the stream endpoint while the RT handler is active. The stop/restart flag behavior remains an external ordering contract without a supported in-tree trigger, so OD1811 is withdrawn. Other controller completion and endpoint ownership checks remain open; no ISO run was performed.

Parallel.device close/abort ownership follow-up: reread the selected last-opener `Close`, `CMD_RESET`/`CMD_FLUSH`, and `AbortIO` with the printer-device caller (`workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_init.c:222-252,483-540,619-652`; `workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:466-492,583-596`). Close removes and frees the unit without draining its active or queued requests, while reset replies active requests without clearing their pointers; these are already OD872 and OD61. AbortIO distinguishes only an active read and sends an active write through `Remove` as though queued, already OD57. The queued-message flush does call `Enable()` after draining both queues (`parallel_init.c:503-539`), so no interrupt-disable leak is credited from the reset fallthrough. Backend callback timing and additional external clients remain pending; no printer or parallel transfer was run.

xHCI realtime-ISO prefill rejection check: `cmdStartRTIso` requests at most two PTDs and does not roll back the first if the second `xhciQueueIsochIO` returns an error (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:1631-1646`). The helper's only error is `UHIOERR_NAKTIMEOUT` when `xhciNextIsoPTD` returns NULL (`xhci_isoch.c:34-52,193-203`), while add-handler requires at least two slots and successfully initializes each before publishing the handler (`uhwcmd.c:1439-1512`; `xhci_isoch.c:144-190`). During the command's local `Disable` region, the first prefill marks only one distinct PTD `PTDF_BUFFER_VALID`, leaving another selectable. No selected single-threaded second-prefill failure trigger was established, so no separate rollback candidate is credited. Concurrent mutation or external hook changes to handler state remain open. This does not alter OD1810: transfer preparation happens later, after both prefill calls succeed.

xHCI realtime-ISO start-status follow-up (OD1810): traced the selected `UHCMD_STARTRTISO` dispatch through `cmdStartRTIso`, its two PTD prefill calls, `xhciStartIsochIO`, `xhciInitIOTRBTransfer` allocation failure, and Poseidon's synchronous `psdStartRTIso` result handling (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_dev.c:258-269`; `uhwcmd.c:1606-1650`; `xhci_isoch.c:286-329`; `xhci_schedule.c:217-268`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5630-5653`). The prefill phase reports its own errors; after successful prefill the void start helper can fail independently and the command still returns success. Partial start, stop and completion lifetimes need a further controller-specific trace. No device or allocation failure was run.

xHCI realtime-ISO allocation follow-up: `rom/usb/pcixhci/make.opts:6` enables `PCIUSB_WIP_ISO`, and BeginIO dispatches its add/remove commands (`pcixhci_dev.c:258-266`). `cmdAddIsoHandler` obtains a free node, allocates PTD slots, calls `xhciInitIsochIO`, and returns the node to the free list on each inspected allocation failure (`uhwcmd.c:1397-1528`). The EHCI initializer loses preallocated PTD nodes when it clears and replaces them (OD3815); xHCI frees each preallocated PTD before creating its descriptor-backed replacement (`xhci_isoch.c:144-190`) and its failure helper frees partially built slots (`:359-378`), so this particular leak is not shared. The caller-visible `urti_DriverPrivate1` backlink is set before controller initialization and is not cleared when that initialization fails (`uhwcmd.c:1502-1517`), but the checked start/remove commands search the active handler list instead of dereferencing the backlink (`:1545-1575,1607-1637`); broader external users of that field and realtime completion lifetimes remain pending. No ISO transfer was run.

Bluetooth hardware-task request ownership follow-up: reread `bAllocCore` allocation loops, common failure cleanup, timer open, `bFreeCore`, and the selected task's root-request lifetime (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2480-2565,2795-2835,3050-3102`). The request and buffer arrays are checked before use, and their partial allocations are released on failure. A failed timer `OpenDevice` deletes its request and clears the pointer before common cleanup, so it does not close an unopened request there. OD1279 is withdrawn after a selected startup trace: both `btSpawnSubTask` branches create a fresh task whose `tc_SigAlloc` starts from the system mask `0xFFFF`, leaving 16 user bits (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:1000-1040`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:249-251`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`); process `pr_MsgPort` uses reserved `SIGB_DOS` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:420-426`). Before the three calls at `hwtask.c:2811,2819,2827`, the worker only opens its already initialized parent library; the selected Bluetooth library OpenLib path uses no signal allocations (`bluetooth.library.c:113-190`; exact `AllocSignal` caller search in `rom/bluetooth` finds only these three calls). Thus no ordinary selected path can exhaust this fresh worker's mask before all three allocations succeed. No allocation failure was induced. No additional request-allocation candidate is credited from this path; asynchronous controller completion and external driver teardown remain open.

Card-resource debounce edge follow-up (OD1792): traced the level-6 interrupt's masking of card-change requests into the worker's two stable 100 ms samples and later 10 ms delay. The worker does not resample after that delay; it clears Gayle's pending requests before re-enabling interrupts (`arch/m68k-amiga/card/lowlevel.c:18-40,111-143`; `task.c:94-126`; `card_intern.h:80-96`). A removal followed by insertion during that final delay leaves `removed` set and loses the insertion edge. Hardware timing and a real card sequence remain untested.

Card-resource signal-allocation correction (OD1462 withdrawn): the selected m68k Amiga initializer creates the worker through `NewCreateTask` without a message-port tag (`arch/m68k-amiga/card/card_init.c:122-138`). `NewAddTask` assigns the fresh task Exec's default allocated-signal mask (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:239-251`), initialized to `0xFFFF` (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). `CardTask` calls `AllocSignal(-1)` before any other allocation of its own; the upper 16 signal bits remain free, so the formerly claimed exhaustion path is not reachable in this selected startup. The unchecked return remains a defensive code concern under an externally changed mask, not a counted bug candidate. No boot was run.

Console read/paste queue follow-up: traced `con_inject`, `pasteData`, `answer_requests`, command-port `CMD_READ`, `answer_read_request`, and `AbortIO` under `consoleTaskLock` (`rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:23-80,145-172,257-273,458-480,528-583`; `console.c:432-485`). `pasteData` calls `answer_requests` after it adds bytes, and `answer_requests` removes a queued request before replying; `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_D`'s later `answer_requests(NULL)` is redundant but does not leave that unit asleep. A later `CMD_READ` also calls `pasteData` before checking the unit buffer, so queued paste can complete a new read. OD1190 remains the zero-length read case, and OD2306 is detailed in the report: `con_inject` allocates per-unit paste nodes/buffers, `pasteData` frees them only after full consumption, and the SIGBREAKF_CTRL_D path only services units with queued reads (`consoletask.c:26-47,145-172,254-273`). No additional wakeup candidate was credited. External request validity and actual scheduling remain open; no I/O was run.

CharMap insert/delete and redraw sweep (OD1791): rechecked `charmap_resize` and `charmap_insert_chars` through the selected console CSI `@`/`P` parser, standard-console pixel scroll and CharMap full redraw. The initially suspected missing text-array shift was rejected after reading the complete insert helper (`rom/devs/console/charmapconclass.c:695-722`). The remaining mismatch is that insertion retains the suffix shifted beyond the visible width; a subsequent delete can bring that old character back on window-resize redraw. `CONU_CHARMAP` is an explicit selected OpenDevice unit. Other CharMap commands, resize geometry and external clients remain open; no console sequence was run.

Gameport/OOP ownership recheck (OD1192): `release_idbucket` locks and looks up the IID bucket, decrements it if found, and does nothing when absent (`rom/oop/support.c:183-207`). Thus repeated gameport opens definitely issue unmatched releases, but a visible bucket removal depends on another owner's live reference. OD1192 is now detailed with the class-held reference and the conditional repeated-open threshold; it remains a qualified existing candidate, not a new candidate from this pass. Wider OOP clients and runtime bucket state remain open.

USB keyboard repeat scope recheck (OD1788): traced bootkeyboard.class raw-key submissions through `IND_WRITEEVENT` (`rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:679-698,772-780`) and compared the separate general HID class. On a successful input.device open, HID sets `nch_OS4Hack` and its `nSendRawKey` selects `IND_ADDEVENT` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1124-1135,6516-6527`), which reaches input.device's repeat-state branch (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:344-369`). OD1788 is therefore specific to bootkeyboard.class and any other producer that persists with `IND_WRITEEVENT`; it does not establish missing repeat for the selected general HID path. No device or timer was run.

Input repeat-classification follow-up (OD1786-OD1787): read `IsQualifierKey` and `IsRepeatableKey` (`rom/devs/input/support.c:103-143`) against both worker repeat-arm branches (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:344-369,499-518`) and keymap's later repeatability filter (`rom/keymap/support.c:77-123`). Input intentionally treats every non-qualifier raw key as repeatable; keymap can suppress character conversion for keys whose repeatable bit is clear. This does not repair OD1786's cancellation of another held repeat key on release or OD1787's retained modifier bits on an allowed repeat. No extra candidate is credited for raw-key repeatability alone; no key sequence was run.

HID wheel-to-repeat caller check (OD1786): traced selected general HID `HUA_WHEEL` dispatch through `nSendRawKey` and its AROS `IND_ADDEVENT` choice (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1124-1135,5854-5939,6516-6527`). Wheel codes 0x7a-0x7d are non-qualifiers, so their press/release pair reaches both repeat-timer reset branches in input.device (`rom/devs/input/support.c:106-143`; `processevents.c:344-369`). The release cancels a timer for a held unrelated keyboard key, extending OD1786 to an ordinary cross-device action. The paired release also rules out a sustained synthetic wheel-repeat claim from this path. No device sequence was run.

Boot-keyboard transfer-length follow-up (OD1091): reread the interrupt pipe's `EA_MaxPktSize` acquisition and buffer allocation, the worker's success-only parser call, and `nParseKeys`'s fixed eight-byte accesses plus endpoint-sized old-key copy (`rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:457-479,490-506,789-793,850-884`). Poseidon exposes `psdGetPipeActual` separately from `psdGetPipeError` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4899-4919`; `rom/usb/docs/poseidon.doc:1578-1605`), but this worker reads only the error. The selected RISC-V OpenSBI PC xHCI path accepts TRB_CC_SHORT_PACKET as UHIOERR_NO_ERROR and records actual length; the boot-keyboard worker ignores that length and parses the reused buffer. OD1091 is detailed as OD2310 for a successful report shorter than the eight-byte boot layout. No such response was observed. OD1091's larger-than-eight advertised endpoint still crosses the fixed saved-array bound after an ordinary full-size report. USB controller runt-packet handling remains open; no report was transferred.

Boot-keyboard translation-table bound check: reread both 256-entry `usbkeymap` and `usbisakeymap` definitions (`rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:359-431`) against the parser's `UWORD keycode` loaded from a `UBYTE` current or old report slot and indexed in both key-up and key-down paths (`:498,617-635,706-726`). Every possible 0–255 byte index is represented, so the apparent unguarded lookup does not read past either table for a well-formed eight-byte boot report. Values mapped to 0xff and short-transfer/report-size handling remain separate behavior questions; no new index-bound candidate is credited. No report was parsed.

Input handler-list serialization check: reread `BeginIO`'s nonquick `IND_ADDHANDLER`/`IND_REMHANDLER` queueing (`rom/devs/input/input.c:149-171`), the worker's command-port drain and list mutations (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:275-304`), and its `ForwardQueuedEvents` traversal (`:94-125`). These operations run serially on the input worker for ordinary selected commands; an add/remove request cannot directly mutate the handler list on another CPU during that traversal. This does not resolve GD1967's different case, where a handler returns a null event chain and a later handler dereferences it, nor OD3285's missing removal on lowlevel expunge. Direct unsanctioned list writes and handler-internal lifetime contracts remain open; no events were run.

Boot-keyboard independent-repeat check (OD1788): searched the complete selected `bootkeyboard.class.c` for repeat, threshold, period, timer and both input-event command names; its only event submissions use `IND_WRITEEVENT`, and it has no independent repeat timer. The local manifest builds that class body plus the already tracked debug body (`rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/mmakefile.src:5-13`). OD1788 now explicitly excludes a class-local repeat mechanism from the checked source; external host/device firmware behavior and actual installed-class selection remain open. No keyboard was run.

Boot-keyboard repeat path follow-up (OD1788): traced the selected bootkeyboard.class previous-report filter, first-press and release `IND_WRITEEVENT` submissions (`rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:679-698,706-803`) against all input.device repeat-state writes and the `IND_WRITEEVENT` worker branch (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:344-369,397-415,460-518`). An unchanged held key produces no second USB key-down, and `IND_WRITEEVENT` never arms `keytimerio`, so a boot-keyboard-only press has no repeat source. This adds OD1788; installed-class selection and real keyboard timing remain unverified. No device was run.

Input repeat-qualifier follow-up (OD1787): traced both key-down copies into `keyrepeatie`, the qualifier-key bypass of the timer-cancel branch, keyboard.device's current qualifier publication, and the repeat timer's saved-event copy (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:344-369,460-518`). The timer adds `IEQUALIFIER_REPEAT` but does not merge `InputDevice->ActQualifier`; selected `MapRawKey` consumes `ie_Qualifier` from that event (`rom/keymap/maprawkey.c:80-95`). Holding a letter across a Shift change therefore produces repeats with the original Shift state. This adds OD1787, separate from OD1786's unrelated-key release cancellation. Layout-specific characters and runtime timing remain unverified; no keys were pressed.

Input key-repeat ownership follow-up (OD1786): reread both accepted raw-key producers in `rom/devs/input/processevents.c:344-369,482-518`, the timer reply/resubmission at :460-479, the sole `keyrepeatie`/`keyrepeat_state` storage at :143-155, and keyboard.device's independent key-up/down event forwarding (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:435-477,608-644`). A later B press replaces the active repeat event, but an earlier A release aborts the same timer without matching its saved code; B remains down and no repeat is armed. This adds OD1786 and is separate from OD2516's stop/resume reply loss. Actual keyboard timing and alternate input producers remain unverified; no key event was run.

Printer invalid-unit caller follow-up (OD68): reread parent `OpenDevice` (`workbench/devs/printer/printer.c:54-96`), Exec's error-field contract (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:104-136`), and selected `InitPrinter`/`PrintFiles` argument handling. Both tools pass a user-supplied unit to `OpenDevice` without checking the printer's ten-unit limit, providing in-tree routes to OD68's false success for unit 10 or greater. This strengthens the existing finding; no duplicate was added. Negative values enter the separately implemented system-printer path and are not part of OD68. No client was run.

Printer target metadata follow-up: read `workbench/devs/printer/mmakefile.src` and `printer.conf` and added both to the file ledger. The active device target selects `printer`, `driver`, `prefs`, `gfx` and `text`; the configuration binds `BeginIO` and `AbortIO` to the generated device vectors. Those selected C bodies already have separate rows. No new defect follows from the metadata alone; generated vector code and external printer segments remain open.

GraphicDump cancellation contract follow-up (OD1785): reread the selected `SendIO`/Ctrl-C/`AbortIO`/`WaitIO` sequence (`workbench/tools/GraphicDump.c:136-170`) against printer.device unit `AbortIO`, which returns `IOERR_NOCMD` without touching the request (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:191-198`), Exec's forwarding wrapper (`rom/exec/abortio.c:44-61`) and WaitIO's pending-request loop (`rom/exec/waitio.c:57-80`). A Ctrl-C before graphics print completion cannot cancel through this vector; the tool waits for the ordinary reply. The same path does not supply OD1658's negative `io_Error` trigger. Backend print duration and runtime Ctrl-C handling remain unverified; no command was run.

PCI network reset-callback family reconciliation: rechecked Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, EtherLink3, Nvidianet, Prism2 and Rhine `CreatePCIUnit`/`DeletePCIUnit` against Exec's always-TRUE `AddResetCallback` and direct `RemResetCallback` unlink (`rom/exec/addresetcallback.c:53-61`; `remresetcallback.c:45-50`). All six have a balanced normal destructor but bypass it after a failed IRQ registration while the reset node has been enqueued; the unified report finding is OD418. The older OD3101 Broadcom/Etherlink partial-registration entry has been withdrawn as duplicate/inapplicable: AROS `AddResetCallback` cannot fail, and its wrapper leak is separately covered by OD3335/OD2802. Successful wrapper-allocation failure before registration remains the separately recorded partial-wrapper leak in affected drivers. No duplicate findings were added. Hardware IRQ failure modes and concurrent reset remain unverified; no device was run.

Lowlevel requester-state and QueryKeys follow-up (OD1784): reread the selected `SystemControlA` tag walk (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/systemcontrola.c:139-183`) against DOS requester-window handling (`rom/dos/errorreport.c:91-94`; `rom/dos/displayerror.c:78`) and a selected save/restore caller (`workbench/c/iprefs/main.c:370-373`). `SCON_KillReq` suppresses requesters with `pr_WindowPtr = -1` but releases them with `pr_WindowPtr = 0`, losing a previously selected window; no direct selected in-tree tag caller was found. Also checked all repository C/header references to `QueryKeys`: the common selected function explicitly remains an unimplemented stub, with no architecture override or direct in-tree client found, so no additional candidate is credited from that stub. External clients and runtime requester behavior remain open; no call was run.

Wi-Fi preferences SSID serialization follow-up (OD1783): traced Broadcom scan bytes from firmware `ssid_len` through the SANA-II scan tag, Wi-Fi list selection, `DoConnect` and `MergePrefs` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1945-1989`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1285-1303`; `workbench/prefs/wifi/worker.c:982-1027,1275-1287,303-311`; `main.c:193-210`). No step strips a newline, while the bundled supplicant splits configuration at physical newlines and rejects an unterminated quoted assignment (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/config_file.c:39-79,130-169`). The emitted-value failure is separate from OD1780's comment match and OD1781's first-brace boundary. Actual AP beacon data, UI rendering and runtime connection remain open; no network or file operation was run.

Lowlevel library manifest reconciliation: compared every name in `workbench/libs/lowlevel/mmakefile.src`'s `lowlevel_init $(FUNCS)` build with this ledger: all 17 selected common C bodies have unique rows, including the four generic timer fallbacks, the joystick fallback and requesters. The native m68k `arch/m68k-amiga/lowlevel/mmakefile.src` lists seven architecture C bodies; all seven also have unique rows, with their two local headers and `make.opts` tracked. The m68k Amiga boot package selects the lowlevel kernel object (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:81,155`). This closes the manifest-named local C-file inventory for these two targets, not their external caller, CIA/potgo hardware, generated vector or configured-image checks; no device or library was run.

Wi-Fi preferences disconnect follow-up (OD1782): reread `StopSupplicant`, `RunConnect`, `DoDisconnect` and `DoStatus` (`workbench/prefs/wifi/worker.c:321-337,857-943,1142-1151,1299-1332`) against the bundled manager's main run/deinit path (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/main_amiga.c:90-145`). Unlike the connect path, disconnect ignores a timed-out stop, the disassociate I/O result and the status query's success; a transient link-down sample can therefore produce “disconnected” with the manager still active. OD373 separately covers the device's queued join. Manager exit timing and device runtime remain open; no disconnect was run.

Wi-Fi preferences quoted-brace follow-up (OD1781): compared `MergePrefs`'s first-`}` block boundary with the bundled supplicant's line-oriented close and quoted-string parser (`workbench/prefs/wifi/worker.c:274-311`; `workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/config_file.c:130-169`; `config.c:60-75`). A valid `ssid="A}B"` block is cut inside its value when that SSID is replaced, leaving the rest of the old block as stray top-level text before the new block. This is distinct from OD1780's comment-based false match. Saved-file grammar, target UI selection for unusual SSIDs and actual connect behavior remain open; no file was written.

Wi-Fi preferences network-block matching follow-up (OD1780): reread `MergePrefs` and `DoConnect` against the bundled supplicant's config lexer (`workbench/prefs/wifi/worker.c:257-299,1275-1287`; `workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/config_file.c:39-79,130-169`). The supplicant ignores a `# ssid="Cafe"` line in a valid `ssid="Home"` block, but the preferences tool's raw substring search treats it as Cafe and drops Home during merge. This is separate from OD1728's input-read failure and OD1729's unchecked output. `PrefsHaveNetwork`'s same raw search counts that commented Cafe and the Home block's `psk=` as a saved key (`worker.c:222-249`); `DoConnect` then skips its immediate password prompt, starts an unconfigured association attempt and, if Cafe was in the scan but does not associate, waits through timeout before reporting a wrong password and causing the UI to ask (`:1261-1273,1137-1158,1215-1227`; `main.c:319-326`). This is folded into OD1780 rather than counted separately. No file or network command was run.

Wi-Fi preferences duplicate correction: proposed OD1779 was removed after a report-wide source search found that OD1729 already covers `MergePrefs` ignoring `FPuts`, `Write`, `FPrintf` and `Close` failures (`workbench/prefs/wifi/worker.c:267-315`). OD1729's build scope was corrected to the Raspberry Pi Workbench-selected Wi-Fi preferences target; OD1728 separately covers input-read failure. This pass also rechecked `DoConnect`'s true-return branch and rollback (`:1275-1296`). Network-file grammar and configured image installation remain open; no preferences file was changed.

Wi-Fi preferences build and saved-file recheck (OD1728): the full `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-prefs`, whose active virtual architecture edge selects `workbench-prefs-wifi` when `AROS_TARGET_ARCH=raspi` (`config/mmakefile.src:16`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:9-25`; `workbench/prefs/wifi/mmakefile.src:5-18`). Reread `ReadPrefs`, `MergePrefs`, `SavePrefs`, `RestorePrefs` and `DoConnect` (`workbench/prefs/wifi/worker.c:196-316,1072-1102,1275-1296`): a failed existing-file read still becomes a null backup, is treated as an absent file and can lead to replacement or deletion. OD1728's source trigger remains valid, but its “optional direct-build only” label was wrong and has been corrected. Filesystem failure modes, configured image installation and Wi-Fi runtime remain open; no preferences file was changed.

USB shell-app build-scope correction: `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:7-22` places `kernel-usb-shellapps` in both active virtual `kernel-usb` and `kernel-usb-nopci` aggregates; `rom/usb/shellapps/mmakefile.src:3-10` selects six tools. Native m68k serial/parallel build-scope correction: the m68k Amiga boot target lists `kernel-workbench-devs-amiga-m68k`, whose active virtual edge selects `workbench-devs-amiga-m68k`; the serial and parallel HIDD manifests each add their modules to that target (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:78,94`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/serial/mmakefile.src:6-14`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/parallel/mmakefile.src:6-14`). HDA HIDD build-scope recheck (OD1391): `AROS` selects `workbench-complete`, which selects `workbench-hidds`; the local `#MM- workbench-hidds : hidd-hdaudio` is an active virtual MetaMake edge (`config/mmakefile.src:16`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:9-13`; `workbench/hidds/hdaudio/mmakefile.src:5-15`; `tools/MetaMake/dirnode.c:126-197`).
