The report and manifest row now mark the HIDD build-selected in the full Workbench aggregate. Controller capabilities, installation and runtime playback remain unverified; no hardware was run.

Network aggregate scope correction: the root `AROS` MetaMake target selects `workbench-complete`, which selects `workbench-devs`, then `workbench-devs-common`, then `workbench-devs-networks` (`config/mmakefile.src:16`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:11-14`; `workbench/devs/mmakefile.src:3-27`). The network aggregate names `workbench-devs-networks-dwmac-$(AROS_TARGET_CPU)` and `workbench-devs-networks-soc-$(AROS_TARGET_ARCH)`; the active virtual SoC-raspi target names BCM GENET (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-15,41-43`). Thus a full Workbench build with `AROS_TARGET_CPU=riscv64` selects DWMAC, and one with `AROS_TARGET_ARCH=raspi` selects BCM GENET. Prior notes treated `#MM-` as disabled and wrongly labeled these direct-build only. The finding scopes and manifest rows now reflect this chain. Target-variable resolution for each configured image, installation and driver runtime remain open; no network device was run.

BCM2711 PCIe MSI-registration candidate withdrawal (2026-10-12): the init hook ignores a null `KrnAddIRQHandler` result, but the PCI device `ObtainVectors` method rejects all MSI requests when `psd->msi_handle` is null (`driverclass.c:313-326`). The checked in-tree clients either fall back to legacy INTx (AHCI, NVMe and xHCI), or propagate MSI unavailability (Nouveau and VMware SVGA), so none programs a newly enabled endpoint MSI on this path. Bridge MSI status is cleared before vectors are opened (`pcie_init.c:412-413`). The unchecked registration is therefore not retained as an independent bug; OD932 remains the verified constructor-tag issue. Firmware and target hardware remain unverified.

Lowlevel VBlank registration and language-selection recheck: reread the complete selected `AddVBlankInt`, `RemVBlankInt` and `GetLanguageSelection` bodies against Exec's `AddIntServer`/`RemIntServer` and locale's `OpenLocale` (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/addvblankint.c:18-84`; `remvblankint.c:17-63`; `getlanguageselection.c:18-99`; `rom/exec/addintserver.c:55-77`; `remintserver.c:48-65`; `workbench/libs/locale/openlocale.c:83-191`). The VBlank setter and remover serialize their shared slot with `ll_Lock`; the ordinary one-add/one-remove sequence links and unlinks the embedded node. A stale or duplicate removal would pass the address-only handle check and could unlink a later registration, but that requires misuse of a consumed handle and no selected in-tree VBlank client was found, so no new candidate is credited. `GetLanguageSelection` still requests the nonnull disk-file branch of `OpenLocale` with an empty name (GD2013); its unterminated language table matters only if that branch actually returns a locale whose name is absent from the list, so it is not promoted to a separate candidate here. External VBlank clients, IRQ callback quiescence and locale-file resolution remain open; no call or interrupt was run.

Printer/PostScript command-buffer follow-up: reread the complete `Printer_Text_Command`, `doState` and `Printer_Text_Write` bodies against selected PostScript `PED_Commands`, `ps_DoSpecial`, `ps_ConvFunc` and the two `PrinterData` command-buffer extents (`workbench/devs/printer/text.c:17-352`; `workbench/printers/postscript/postscript.c:49-1005`; `compiler/include/devices/prtbase.h:81-82,113-119`). `buffmax` is 1,018 bytes, while the first buffer has 4,096 bytes and the second has 2,036; the selected `aSFC`/`aSBC` callback formats a short command, so this pass does not assert a separate PostScript `DoSpecial` write past the command-buffer allocation. The state machine bounds a numeric parameter at 100 before advancing; its selected `ESC M` unsupported-command result still reaches OD393's discarded error. Ordinary text still has OD70's unflushed tail and successive command calls still have OD1491's premature reuse of `pd_Stk`. Other segment callbacks, output-completion timing and external clients remain pending; no print request was run.

Mouse proxy construction and disposal follow-up: reread complete `MouseHW__HW__AddDriver`, `RemoveDriver`, `EnumDrivers`, `PushEvent` and `DriverData` constructor/callback/disposer bodies against generic `HW_AddDriver`/`HW_RemoveDriver` and `InputHW__HW__AddDriver` (`rom/hidds/mouse/subsystem.c:82-232`; `driverdata.c:23-112`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:173-222,266-306`; `rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:203-233`). Generic registration frees its private list node and disposes a constructed proxy on setup failure; the proxy constructor invokes superclass disposal if actual driver construction fails. The selected `TAG_IGNORE` rewrite acts on InputHW's local handler-tag array rather than an external caller's list. These paths do not add a partial-registration leak or caller-tag mutation candidate. OD1773's public returned-handle/removal mismatch and OD1774's discarded enum result remain; selected starters still have no successful `HW_RemoveDriver` call, so OD1773 is a direct-client claim. Driver destructor and hardware callback quiescence on future hot removal remain pending; no driver was registered or removed.

Lowlevel input-stop SMP follow-up (OD1777): the complete `SetInputState` owner/nest and temporary command path was reread against Exec's explicit local-only `Forbid` contract (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/systemcontrola.c:19-61`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:55-65`). Two CPUs can both observe a null owner; after A commits the first stop and B overwrites the owner and increments the nest, A sends `CMD_STOP`, A's later resume is refused and B's one resume sends no `CMD_RESET`. The input worker's stop/reset cases confirm the resulting stopped state (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:282-289`). No direct selected C client of this public lowlevel tag was found, so this remains a direct-client SMP candidate. The adjacent lowlevel signal-port release was checked against `CreateMsgPort`/`DeleteMsgPort`: it sets `mp_SigBit = -1` before deletion and changes action to `PA_IGNORE`, so the ordinary expunge path does not free that allocated bit twice. Other client and library-lifetime paths pending; no SMP schedule was run.

Lowlevel input registration and owner-state recheck: selected input.device `BeginIO` queues `IND_ADDHANDLER` and its worker enqueues the supplied handler without an error branch (`rom/devs/input/input.c:149-171`; `processevents.c:291-304`), so OD3286 remains limited to the missing handler allocation rather than an independently failing registration result. The complete `SystemControlA` and requester-gate bodies were reread. OD1618 was narrowed: an initial no-op resume retains an owner and blocks a different task's stop, but that same owner can release it by a later successful stop/resume pair; the stale reservation can outlive the owner if it exits. The requester gate's later third-party vector-patch case still lacks a selected client. No device command or owner interleaving was run; external clients remain pending.

Lowlevel input-handler allocation follow-up (OD3286): `LowLevelInputInit` returns `TRUE` after an input handler `AllocMem` failure, despite having skipped `IND_ADDHANDLER` (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/lowlevel_init.c:88-143`). The enclosing library initializer can then succeed (`:229-255`), while `GetKey` keeps its initial `0xff` because only the absent handler updates `ll_LastKey` (`getkey.c:51-55`; `lowlevel_init.c:39-61,72-78`). The complete selected `AddKBInt` and `RemKBInt` bodies were reread; registration can still accept callbacks, but without that input handler they are never scheduled. This is separate from OD3285's registered-handler expunge path and other partial port/request cleanup paths. Allocation failure and key delivery remain untested; wider client contracts pending.

Driver-tree inventory check: all local C/header/assembly paths in `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers` (239), `rom/hidds/acpi` (24), `rom/hidds/ipmi` (8), and `arch/all-pc/hidds` (25) have ledger rows. The CAMD tree now has all 52 local C/header paths represented; its previously missing `docs.c` is a 39-line documentation-only file omitted from the selected module manifest. These checks establish path accounting, not complete build-variant, caller or hardware review.

Network-driver inventory check: all 449 local C/header/assembly paths under `workbench/devs/networks` have rows in this ledger. The 110 paths under `rom/devs` absent from this ledger include separately assigned disk and console/device families; the directory total therefore cannot be used as an other-drivers completion measure without cross-report assignment. This is an inventory result only; existing per-driver caller and hardware gaps remain.

BCM GENET build and receive follow-up: `workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/mmakefile.src` supplies a direct `workbench-devs-networks-bcmgenet` target. The aggregate Raspberry Pi SoC edge is an active virtual MetaMake target in `workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:41-43`, and the full `AROS` Workbench aggregate reaches BCM GENET when `AROS_TARGET_ARCH=raspi`, independent of the boot manifests' explicit BWFM edge. OD541-OD555 and the BCM GENET portion of OD1355 therefore concern a full Workbench build for that target; configured image installation remains to check; their report labels have been corrected. The receive ring allocates 64-byte-aligned buffers at 1,536-byte strides (`bcmgenet_unit.c:222-237`); this satisfies the checked AArch64 cache-line geometry for the `CachePreDMA`/`CachePostDMA` pair in the driver's receive path. No partial-line DMA candidate is credited from that path; the separate conditional stale-data-on-reuse path through ARM32 CachePostDMA selection is tracked as EK9346 in the Exec/Kernel report. Other hardware and caller contracts remain open; no network device was run.

DWMAC selection follow-up: its local `mmakefile.src` supplies a direct RISC-V target and says the device-tree driver is built only when requested by a target. The network aggregate names that target only behind its active virtual `#MM-` edge (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-6`), and that aggregate expands `workbench-devs-networks-dwmac-$(AROS_TARGET_CPU)` to the RISC-V target when `AROS_TARGET_CPU=riscv64`. The DWMAC portions of OD1023 and OD1355 are now labeled build-selected for the full RISC-V Workbench aggregate; this changes build scope, not their source reasoning. The four DWMAC-specific findings identify the RISC-V module without claiming inclusion in every configured image.

USB inventory reconciliation: all 368 local `rom/usb` C/header paths now have one ledger row each. The 14 previously missing Bluetooth, STIR4200, LAN78xx and shell diagnostic support files have been read and classified. The five `ps3eye` GUI test files are tracked separately: the test program and two pure-image arrays are direct test-target inputs; the two video arrays are unselected by that manifest. Inventory completeness does not mean every USB body, test array, caller contract or hardware behavior has been audited.

Trident target inventory follow-up: `rom/usb/trident/mmakefile.src` names seven C files for the USB preferences program, and the RISC-V OpenSBI USB target explicitly selects `kernel-usb-trident` (`rom/usb/mmakefile.src:56-58`). A directory-to-ledger scan exposed 41 missing local C/header files: the seven translation units, their seven local headers, 25 directly included Mason icon data files, the directly included logo data and a catalog-version header. All 41 now have individual rows, as does the manifest. `ActionClass.c`, `DevWinClass.c`, `IconListClass.c`, `CfgListClass.c`, `Trident.c`, `debug.c` and `locale.c` have complete body reads. All 25 directly included Mason icon bodies and the logo passed static declared-size and ByteRun1 row-boundary checks; appearance and MUI rendering were not verified. Cross-library caller, ownership, parser, and notification contracts remain pending. No Trident UI was run.

Console worker exit caller follow-up (OD1652): the selected `console.device` initializer names its worker task `console.device` (`rom/devs/console/console.c:107-114`), and the selected `Break` command can find that task by `NAME` and send CTRL-C by default (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:9`; `workbench/c/Break.c:156-188,193-220`). Rechecked the worker's signal branch, pending command handling, input-device handler registration and unused cleanup helper. This establishes a normal in-tree command that reaches OD1652's explicit exit path; no shutdown or subsequent read was run. The console module is `noexpunge`, so ordinary expunge is not the trigger (`rom/devs/console/console.conf:1-8`).

Serial HIDD parameter-tag follow-up (OD1738): the complete `SetParameters` bodies in selected PC, RISC-V and Unix serial unit classes were compared with public `TAG_SKIP` and `TAG_MORE` semantics and the native m68k `NextTagItem` implementation. Their manual index loops process tags that a nonzero `TAG_SKIP` should suppress and reject a valid continuation; this requires a direct HIDD client because selected `serial.device` uses a flat list with `TAG_SKIP` count zero. A valid control-tag request was not run. PC's separate current-rate rejection and stale stored baud field remain OD1736.

PC/RISC-V serial restart follow-up (OD1737): both selected UART unit `Start` bodies call `serial.device`'s write callback before clearing their own `stopped` flag. A write submitted during `CMD_STOP` is retained as `su_ActiveWrite`; the callback retries it through the still-stopped HIDD `Write`, obtains zero, and leaves it pending. Restart therefore makes no write progress itself. A later transmit-empty IRQ may retry it, so indefinite stalling on these hardware targets is conditional; the hosted Unix no-retry path remains OD1460. The native m68k backend has the corrected flag-before-callback order. No UART sequence was run.

Input stop/resume API follow-up (OD2516): the selected lowlevel.library `SystemControlA` implementation handles `SCON_StopInput` by sending `CMD_STOP` on its first stop and `CMD_RESET` on its matching resume (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/systemcontrola.c:19-61,169-171`; `mmakefile.src:13-35`). Rechecked the input worker's command-first order and gated reply branches (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:263-290,440-539`) against Exec `Wait`'s consumed wake bits (`rom/exec/wait.c:125-138`). This establishes the public-library command pair, but no direct selected repository C client of this tag was found; OD2516 still requires an external or indirect client plus a device/timer reply and stop signal in the same wait result. No overlapping event sequence was run, and the other lowlevel input-state failure remains OD1619.

Expansion base relocation follow-up (OD1733): m68k binary-compatible initialization calls `ConfigChain` before relocating the library base to fast memory. The new MakeLibrary base is cleared, and the relocation moves only the board and mount lists plus kernelBase; Zorro II/III slot occupancy is lost. A later public board-configuration call can reuse prior addresses. The only selected in-tree C `ConfigChain` call found is the initial pre-relocation one, so the consequence remains conditional on a later external call. No relocation or subsequent board scan was run.

Motherboard RAM scan follow-up (OD1732): the full m68k Amiga `ConfigChain` body was rechecked against its `MemoryTest` assembly caller. `scanmbregion` breaks its outer loop when the first probe returns zero, or, after a usable prefix, when it successfully allocates a chunk at the first hole. Usable RAM beyond either hole in that same unsplit high or low segment is never reached. ROM-based recursion can divide the region into independently scanned segments, which limits the claim. This is separate from OD1044's early exit in the expansion RAM-board list. Physical memory layout and probe behavior remain untested.

Hosted battery-clock policy follow-up (OD1731): Unix `ReadBattClock` converts host time through `localtime`, while MinGW32 resolves `GetLocalTime`; both feed local calendar fields to `Date2Amiga`. Shared `SetClock LOAD` subtracts the locale GMT offset again when `LOCF_GMT_CLOCK` is set. The selected Locale preferences editor can set and save that flag (`workbench/prefs/locale/registertab.c:249-256,309-310`; `workbench/libs/locale/initlocale.c:316`), so it is a reachable configuration, though the default preferences clear it. With matching nonzero host and AROS zones, the offset is applied twice on either hosted target. Differing-zone and host-call failure behavior remains open. No hosted clock load was run.

Battery-clock build-selection follow-up: the generic `rom/battclock/mmakefile.src` and six maintained architecture override manifests were read against the five public vector bodies. The generic module selects read, reset, write and battery-memory vectors, then architecture manifests replace only their listed local bodies. M68k Amiga replaces all except reset; PC, MinGW32, Sam440, Raspberry Pi and OpenSBI replace their listed read/write bodies while retaining generic battery-memory stubs where no override is named; Unix replaces read and retains generic write and memory stubs. These are source-list conclusions, not generated-link or physical RTC verification. Seven manifest rows were added below; no new finding was credited.

SonixcamTool RT-iso teardown follow-up: `GetVideoSnap` saves but ignores `psdStopRTIso`'s return (`rom/usb/shellapps/SonixcamTool.c:1230-1249`), and `FreeSonixcam` frees frame buffers before removing the handler (`:904-917`). Poseidon forwards stop and removal through synchronous `DoIO` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5607-5626,5657-5676`). The selected xHCI build enables the RT-iso commands (`rom/usb/pcixhci/make.opts:6`); PC pciusb also enables them through its architecture option (`arch/all-pc/usb/pciusb/make.opts:1`), while the local generic pciusb option does not. xHCI's successful stop frees periodic transfer contexts and clears active PTD flags, and removal invokes that stop again (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_isoch.c:332-375`). A normal successful stop clears the software request and ring back-pointer, so no later class callback was established; however, xHCI can still complete already-submitted ISO TRBs after their IOReq has been reaped. OD3196 now records that controller-side DMA window and the selected caller that reads/frees its buffers after Stop; the precise completion timing remains controller-dependent. The earlier no-defect conclusion is withdrawn. No camera or controller sequence was run.

Selected printer-tool caller follow-up (OD1656–OD1659): `workbench/tools/mmakefile.src:6-12` builds `InitPrinter`, `PrintFiles` and `GraphicDump` into Workbench Tools. All three complete C bodies were read against printer.device's selected command worker and the PostScript `aRIN` callback. `InitPrinter` checks setup and reset results, and its failed-open cleanup reaches Exec's supported cleared-request CloseDevice path. `PrintFiles` has no propagated status from file printing and returns CLI success after open, datatype object or DTM_PRINT failures; OD1656 records this independently of the existing `Print` command finding. GraphicDump was also read in full: OD1657 records its printer-unit argument swap and OD1658 its unchecked signed error-text index; a printer graphics and BitMapScale caller cross-check establishes OD1659's moved-screen source-coordinate mismatch. Four scope rows were added below. Datatype-specific rendering and printer output completion remain pending; no printing was run.

Console input handoff follow-up: the full selected `rom/devs/console/cdinputhandler.c` body and the `consoletask.c:177-498` event consumer were reread with the input.device `IND_ADDHANDLER` queue path (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:291-304`). The handler copies one `InputEvent` by value into an allocated message while holding the shared console-unit list lock; the worker rechecks that unit against the live list before use. Activation-window `ie_EventAddress` is consumed before the asynchronous handoff, while the selected charmap gadget method only compares the later copied gadget address against its current `data->prop` fields and clears `activeGad` if `data->prop` is absent (`charmapconclass.c:1601-1654`). Raw-key conversion delegates to `MapRawKey`, whose selected body uses class, code and qualifier but not the copied event-address pointer (`rom/devs/console/rawkeyconvert.c:48-54`; `rom/keymap/maprawkey.c:82-88`). No dereference of a transient event-address pointee was established in these checked consumers. The explicit CTRL-C worker exit still leaves its input handler and port registered as OD1652 records. Other console classes, external unit/window teardown and cross-CPU callback timing remain pending; no event sequence was run.

Speech short-stream follow-up (OD9642): traced an accepted direct `SCSynthWith` custom-voice configuration through parsing, rewrite, prosody, duration assignment, compact/continuation, frame construction, contour and finishing. A 112-entry copy of the default voice with bit-10-only attributes, stressed/unstressed durations 1/2, one nonmatching valid rule in each rule array (with one test byte each in an encoded resource), mode 1 and `IY` input produces four frames. Without mouth output the first seven-frame smoother reads past the 40-byte frame allocation; with mouths the weighted smoother reads at offset 50 past the 50-byte combined allocation. For exactly four frames, `SmoothMouths` narrows the count to zero and performs no write. A second decoded-voice configuration sets only phoneme 0 stressed/unstressed durations to zero; its zero-ID slot passes SynthSentence's zero-duration check, producing total 3. The 16-bit mouth loop count then becomes 65,535 against nine allocated bytes, extending OD9642 to a later mouth-tail overrun if execution continues past the earlier frame overread. The decoder accepts zero duration bytes.  The checked-in default voice's terminal 24-frame duration prevents this trigger for ordinary synthesis. The resource decoder accepts the same 112-entry table shape with bit-10 attributes, one-frame duration bytes and shaped nonmatching rules; narrator.device loads a replacement voice from `DEVS:Speech/speech.iff` and forwards a valid mode-1 request. The checked-in resource remains unaffected. No synthesis was run.

New-style query follow-up: OD1012 was withdrawn after checking the public output structure and exact `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` call sites. The seven selected device implementations dereference a null `io_Data` when a direct caller falsely advertises a sufficiently large result buffer, but no valid selected request or acceptance contract for that malformed combination was established. Older row mentions of OD1012 record the inspected source path, not an active finding. The console short-buffer case formerly tracked as OD49 is now detailed as OD2249; the shared serial/parallel nonquick no-reply case formerly tracked as OD56 is now detailed as OD2250. Wider external API contracts and generated device-query callers remain open; no malformed request was run.

USB mouse-to-input follow-up: selected `rom/usb/classes/bootmouse/bootmouse.class.c:505-599` and `rom/usb/classes/egalaxtouch/egalaxtouch.class.c:713-762` submit complete, nonnull, single `InputEvent` buffers through synchronous `IND_WRITEEVENT` requests. Each sets `ie_NextEvent = NULL` before submission and waits with `DoIO` before reusing its event and request, so these callers do not establish the withdrawn malformed-event OD44 or a queued-buffer lifetime defect. Their mouse qualifiers contain button/motion state rather than keyboard modifier state. Intuition updates its own keyboard qualifier state from raw-key events (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2213-2218`) and maintains mouse-button state separately (`:506-509,861,1002,1199,1233-1253`); a mouse event lacking copied keyboard bits therefore does not by itself establish an Intuition modifier-loss finding. The boot-mouse wheel events and touchscreen tablet/button events use the same synchronous request. Other input handlers and physical report behavior remain pending; no event sequence was run.

Keyboard reset-counter follow-up (OD14): the full 701-line selected `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c` body was reread with Exec `DoIO` and the input.device, optional VMM and PFS3 reset-completion callers. `KBD_RESETHANDLERDONE` decrements `kb_nHandlers` without the `Disable` used for registration/removal, and `DoIO` directly invokes BeginIO. Two legitimate completions on different Exec SMP CPUs can lose a decrement, leaving the reset phase waiting; this extends OD14's previously recorded duplicate/removal cases. Queue-drain sentinel/stale-request paths remain OD32, the multi-opener missed completion remains OD1578, and the cross-CPU queue race is now detailed as OD2389 (legacy tracker label OD35). Remaining HIDD/platform callback timing and other external clients are open; no reset or SMP run was made.

Gameport request/translation follow-up: the full 795-line selected `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c` body was reread against the existing queue, abort, trigger and result findings OD39-OD43, OD1007, OD1191-OD1192 and OD1199; OD43 details the SMP empty-ring/check-to-enqueue lost wakeup, distinct from OD2118 partial-record publication. The mouse HIDD declares only Button1–Button3 (`rom/hidds/mouse/include/mouse.h:75-80`), and checked PC i8042, hosted Linux/X11/SDL, MinGW, serial and m68k Amiga producers use those IDs or override button fields for motion/wheel events. An unsupported fourth-button translation is therefore not a selected trigger from these sources. The selected input.device consumer knowingly replaces gameport's frame-count timestamp with `GetSysTime` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:547-550`), so that selected route does not propagate the device's frame count as wall-clock seconds. External direct gameport clients, unusual producer values and cross-CPU callback timing remain open; no new candidate added from this reread.

Gameport controller-type contract follow-up: the public header defines mouse, relative-joystick and absolute-joystick types (`rom/devs/gameport/include/gameport.h:47-51`), but the selected implementation initializes each shared type to no-controller, merely stores or returns it on `GPD_SETCTYPE`/`GPD_ASKCTYPE`, and frees only the per-open unit at Close (`gameport.c:129-134,282-293,346-368`). The mouse callback and event conversion do not consult the type (`:494-560,618-786`). The only in-tree setter located by exact-symbol search is input.device, which sets `GPCT_MOUSE` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:154,230-234`). Whether direct clients may expect a joystick-type selection to change input or a close to release a controller reservation requires external API semantics; neither is credited as a bug from this source-only check.

ACPI button namespace-walk follow-up: `ACPIButton_DeviceQuery` returns a failed `AcpiGetObjectInfo` status directly to `AcpiWalkNamespace` (`rom/hidds/acpi/button/acpibutton_init.c:118-133`), and the initializer only constructs namespace-discovered power, sleep and lid buttons when the overall walk returns `AE_OK` (`:293-361`). A later information failure would therefore skip registration even for handles saved earlier in the walk. The fixed-button path runs before this walk (`:238-285`) and is unaffected. Whether ACPICA can return such a failure for a namespace object on otherwise usable firmware, and whether the intended callback policy is to skip only that object, remain open; this is not credited as a candidate without that contract.

Input-HIDD listener traversal follow-up (OD2883): both event dispatch paths traverse `ihd_consumers` without pinning entries (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:94-113,240-257`), while `Input__Root__Dispose` unlinks under local `Disable()` and the root disposer frees the instance (`rom/hidds/input/inputclass.c:240-251`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-149`). This supports a conditional cross-CPU use-after-free when an active public consumer is disposed during fanout. Selected keyboard.device and gameport.device listeners remain resident in ordinary operation; no in-tree overlapping dispose path was established. OD2882 separately covers the first-consumer pending-buffer handoff race. No event or disposal overlap was run.

Mouse HIDD proxy callback-data follow-up: the shared input hub injects its default `InputHW__CallBackFunc` and consumer-list pointer before calling the mouse proxy constructor (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:204-237`; `rom/hidds/mouse/subsystem.c:92-113`). The proxy saves that callback/list pair, hides the injected handler tag only in the wrapper's local tag chain, and passes its own callback plus proxy pointer to the actual driver (`rom/hidds/mouse/driverdata.c:51-93`). Checked selected PC i8042, hosted Linux, MinGW GDI and SDL mouse registrations pass no custom handler/data tags (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_classinit.c:57-64`; `arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxinput/startup.c:14-29`; `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/startup.c:49-73`; `arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/startup.c:76-106`), so this route supplies the list that the default callback expects. The older X11 registration uses a separate consumer-side class and is not evidence for this proxy path. Custom direct registrations and event-lifetime contracts remain open; no new candidate credited.

Mouse HIDD public removal follow-up (OD1773 rechecked against GD6317; OD984 withdrawn): `MouseHW__HW__AddDriver` returns its registered proxy object (`rom/hidds/mouse/subsystem.c:92-113`), but `MouseHW__HW__RemoveDriver` calls its own overridden `HW_EnumDrivers`, which translates each proxy to its underlying driver before invoking `searchFunc`; that hook incorrectly treats the underlying object as a proxy and reads its first instance field (`:123-205`; proxy layout `rom/hidds/mouse/mouse.h:14-20`). The generic HW API promises that a returned AddDriver handle can be passed to RemoveDriver (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:148-160`), so OD1773 records the direct-client failure. OD984's prior public remove/re-add trigger is unsupported: this removal does not call the i8042 mouse destructor, and its constructor rejects a second instance while `mousehidd` is set (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseclass.c:46-55,91-98`). No checked in-tree successful mouse registration invokes this public removal; the apparent X11 cleanup caller is excluded by GD6317. Runtime and external clients remain pending.

Mouse HIDD enumeration result follow-up (OD1774): the generic `HW_EnumDrivers` loop treats each hook return as its stop/continue boolean (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:324-334,353-375`), but `MouseHW__HW__EnumDrivers` wraps the client hook in a `void` `enumFunc` that discards its `CALLHOOKPKT` return (`rom/hidds/mouse/subsystem.c:175-205`; hook invocation's `IPTR` result contract at `compiler/include/utility/hooks.h:82-89`). With multiple registered mouse proxies, neither requested early stop nor complete traversal is guaranteed by that wrapper. The user hook result may incidentally remain in the ABI return register on some targets, so the source-level contract defect is firmer than any specific traversal difference. Multiple-driver scheduling and external enumeration clients remain open; no runtime call was made.

Mouse PushEvent size-contract follow-up: the selected PC i8042 producer passes its underlying mouse object, not the proxy registration handle, and a pointer to its basic `pHidd_Mouse_Event` storage (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseps2.c:121-165`; `i8042_mouse.h:37-51`). Although shared `Mouse__Root__Get` advertises extended events by default, `i8042Mouse__Root__Get` overrides `aHidd_Mouse_Extended` with FALSE and reports relative coordinates TRUE (`i8042_mouseclass.c:102-120`). `MouseHW__HW_Input__PushEvent` therefore copies the four basic fields into its local extended record, sets the relative flag, and synchronously passes that record to the input hub (`rom/hidds/mouse/subsystem.c:207-230`; `rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:240-257`). No selected i8042 out-of-record flags read is established. Other producers and direct PushEvent callers remain open; no new candidate credited.

Mouse proxy basic-versus-extended event-width finding promoted to OD4470 (2026-10-23): unlike i8042, selected Linux input, SDL and serial-mouse classes emit the basic four-field `pHidd_Mouse_Event` and do not override `aHidd_Mouse_Extended` (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxinput/linuxinput_inputtask.c:58-103`; `arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdl_mouseclass.c:59-91`; `rom/hidds/serialmouse/drv_serial.c:580`; their selected class Get paths). The shared mouse superclass returns TRUE for that attribute (`rom/hidds/mouse/mouseclass.c:200-220`), so `DriverData__Root__New` marks them extended and its callback forwards their basic pointer without adding flags (`rom/hidds/mouse/driverdata.c:26-48,81-93`). The selected gameport consumer reads the absent fifth field as its event flags and later uses that value for `IEQUALIFIER_RELATIVEMOUSE` (`rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:494-501,536-541,652-655,742-761`). The shared input callback directly forwards the event pointer to consumers (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:94-113`); there is no intervening format conversion on this path. This candidate is now detailed as OD4470; it remains separate from OD1433, which covers Linux button-event X/Y initialization. The public event layouts differ by that UWORD (`rom/hidds/mouse/include/mouse.h:50-65`). Native m68k and PC i8042 explicitly opt out and are not included. Platform-specific startup, hardware event delivery and alternate direct clients remain pending; no event was run.

Poseidon custom-semaphore SMP follow-up (OD1602): `pLockSemExcl`, `pLockSemShared` and `pUnlockSem` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:492-675`) were traced through the public PBase wrappers and selected device-list allocation/removal (`:702-731,2205-2207,2297-2299`). The lock state and read/wait lists are protected only by `Forbid`; Exec documents that this does not exclude a different CPU on SMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-66`). `pInitSem` initializes the lock fields before its separate, fallible debug-info allocation; failure of that allocation alone does not leave the lock uninitialized (`poseidon.library.c:443-465`). Other custom-lock users, lock-borrowing semantics, target options and actual concurrent behavior remain pending; no SMP run was performed.

Poseidon removed-device ownership follow-up (OD1601): `psdAllocDevice` allocates and publishes the device record (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2270-2305`), while every successful no-user `pFreeDevice` cleanup removes it from the hardware list but leaves both the structure free and product-string free commented out (`:2158-2212`). An exact selected-library search found no later `psdFreeVec(pd)`; this is a source-supported per-removal retention. The source comment cites late `LockDevice` callers, so safe reclamation requires a lifetime design. External references, library expunge policy and live memory use remain pending; no attach/removal cycle was run.

Poseidon forced-removal pipe-lifetime follow-up (OD1600): `psdAllocPipe` gives each pipe a device use-count reference and, for a nondefault endpoint, an endpoint pointer (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4600-4642`). `psdRemHardware` can set a still-used dead device's count to zero and call `pFreeDevice`, which releases configurations and endpoints; a later `psdFreePipe` reads the freed endpoint in `pTearDownHWEndpoint` and decrements the reset `UWORD` count (`:4333-4353,2172-2207,1983-1997,1813-1833,1712-1720,4650-4678,1653-1668`). The selected mass-storage class has endpoint pipes, but its normal release may close them before the forced timeout. The candidate therefore requires a delayed class or external pipe holder; no live timeout was run. Expanded as OD3270 for Realtek8180: its USB unit holds one control plus 30 TX and 30 RX pipe references, and the binding-release signal reaches the unset UnitTask removal callback (OD3269), so a unit held open through the forced timeout leaves pipe pointers after Poseidon frees endpoint and hardware state. Caller, timeout, and later-close consequences are source-traced; no hardware removal was run.

Poseidon hardware-removal counter follow-up (OD1599): the full `psdRemHardware` dead-device walk (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4315-4383`) was traced through `pFreeBindings`, `pFreeDevice`, pipe use-count increment/decrement, and selected Trident and AddUSBHardware removers. The timeout counter is initialized once, incremented twice per busy pass, left at 29 after the first forced release and not reset for the next dead device. A second still-used device therefore misses equality with 30 and can keep the removal caller waiting. Device cleanup deliberately removes list nodes but does not free `PsdDevice` storage immediately; this is a teardown-progress finding, not a claim that the loop dereferences a freed device. External pipe-holder lifetimes and actual removal timing remain pending; no hardware was removed.

Hardware-removal event follow-up: `psdRemHardware` stops the hardware task, frees its name, display strings and `PsdHardware`, then sends `EHMB_REMHARDWARE` carrying the freed address (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4315-4383`). `psdSendEvent` copies that value into an asynchronous event note without dereferencing it (`:6670-6701`). The selected Trident `EHMB_REMHARDWARE` branch compares the value against stored hardware pointers and clears a matching row; it does not dereference the removed object (`rom/usb/trident/ActionClass.c:1962-1982`). This inspected path does not establish a use-after-free read. Reuse of the address before delivery, external event listeners and other event types remain pending; no removal sequence was run.

Poseidon hardware-worker signal follow-up (OD1598): the two message-port `AllocSignal(-1L)` results (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9157-9173`) were followed through normal-controller capability selection, `sigmask` construction, hardware publication, `Wait`, and teardown (`:9247-9296,9335-9336`). The byte-sized port fields turn a failed `-1` into 255; the selected PCI USB and xHCI controllers do not advertise QuickIO without the nondefault option. This is distinct from the USB class-worker signal findings. Signal exhaustion and controller execution were not run; other hardware-task error paths remain pending.

Poseidon buffered-read zero-length follow-up (OD1597): `psdStreamRead` completion, byte-count drain, pipe recycling and wait paths (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5047-5206`) were traced with the selected USB printer IN-stream setup and read worker (`rom/usb/classes/printer/printer.class.c:680-696,819-833`). Successful zero-byte completions accumulate on the ready list without increasing `pps_BytesPending`; after all pipes have done so, the read can wait with no free pipe able to produce another completion. The printer's short-packet termination setting does not reach its test for those entries. Selected xHCI event completion can publish `iouh_Actual = 0` with `UHIOERR_NO_ERROR` for a bulk short packet (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2481-2505,2971-3017,3090-3103`). Actual device timing and other controller/stream clients remain pending. No transfer was run.

Poseidon stream read/write follow-up (OD1596): full `psdStreamRead` and `psdStreamWrite` bodies (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5008-5468`) were read with the selected CDC ACM, PL2303 and CP210x serial setters and write callers. Their EOF mode supplies the public eight-byte `IOTArray`; the write-side terminator scan can read index eight because its lookahead lacks the `tcnt < 7` guard present in the read-side scan. Pipe-stream concurrency, partial-transfer accounting, async-mode contracts and wider clients remain pending. No serial request was run.

Poseidon pipe-stream follow-up (OD1595): the `PGA_PIPESTREAM` branch (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1271-1399`) was traced through `psdOpenStreamA`, `psdCloseStream`, `psdStreamFlush`, `psdAbortPipe`, and selected CDC ACM and mass-storage stream open/close callers. A failed per-pipe allocation leaves a null entry in a nonnull array, which passes the open-success check and is dereferenced on close; unchanged later attribute updates also dereference it. A failed pointer-array or backing-buffer allocation instead makes IN-stream open invoke close with a null array, which the initial flush indexes immediately. Pipe-stream data-flow, request completion, external clients and controller-specific behavior remain pending. No allocation failure was induced.

Poseidon stack sound-settings follow-up (OD1594): selected Trident `Action_Cfg_Snd_Changed` passes both sound filename tags to `psdSetAttrsA` (`rom/usb/trident/ActionClass.c:4504-4522`). The Poseidon `PGA_STACKCFG` branch frees a changed existing string before an unchecked `psdCopyStr` replacement (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1232-1246`), so one failed replacement leaves a null pointer that the next settings change sends to `strcmp`; the initial defaults at `:191-192` are also unchecked. The `poseidon.library.c` and `ActionClass.c` rows remain targeted with full bodies and wider caller/error-path checks pending. No allocation failure was induced.

PoPo GUI follow-up (OD1593): the existing `rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c` row remains body-inspected with caller and lifetime checks pending. The selected binding-event path (`:1005-1027`) updates an existing box through `pGenerateAddBox`; its changed-text timeout (`:679-684,719-729`) omits the sticky condition used by creation and the sticky control (`:1409-1420,1463-1476`). The periodic timer removes the shortened box (`:292-305`). The same file's timer request also adds a selected caller to Exec EK26; no new driver candidate was assigned for that shared completion-ordering issue. No GUI or timer interleaving was run.

Poseidon shell-command follow-up: all bodies of selected `PsdStackLoader.c`, `PsdErrorlog.c`, `AddUSBHardware.c`, `AddUSBClasses.c` and `PsdDevLister.c` were read, along with `debug.h`, `numtostr.h` and the copied USB HIDD class-ID header. OD1583 follows PsdErrorlog's traversal against the library's error-message producer/remover: DEBUG takes no PBase lock, while NOFLUSH/default take locks that the producer and remover do not use. `PsdDevLister`'s unchecked `CreateMsgPort` was traced to null-safe `DeleteMsgPort` and null-rejecting `psdAllocPipe`, so no crash is credited on that path. Its string-enumeration call led to a Poseidon descriptor-reader check; OD1584 was withdrawn after confirming that C post-increment passes the original buffer pointer to `psdDoPipe` and advances only the local decode pointer. Wider library/GUI bodies and caller/lifetime checks remain pending. Poseidon's removal-event calls also pass class, error-message and hardware pointers to `psdSendEvent` after freeing those objects (`poseidon.library.c:4374-4381,5819-5824,5894-5899`), and the public event header labels Param1 as the corresponding object. The checked Trident removal consumers compare the pointer only (`rom/usb/trident/ActionClass.c:1962-1983,2073-2101`); a selected dereference or contract requiring a live removal payload was not established, so no separate candidate is credited from that observation yet. No shell command or event sequence was run.

Poseidon parser/lookup follow-up: the selected `pGetDevConfig` caller at `poseidon.library.c:3584-3592` and its configuration, interface, endpoint and descriptor construction at `:8338-8705` were traced for OD1585 and OD1586. OD1588 follows the exported `psdFindInterfaceA` string-filter tags through its unguarded `strcmp` calls and interface-parser name/ID formatting allocations. A formatting failure can leave a null stored string; a later client using the corresponding valid filter can fault, although the selected in-tree callers checked use no string filters. OD1589 follows device descriptor string fallbacks through `pStripString` and device-ID allocation through `psdGetUsbDevCfg`/`psdSetUsbDevCfg`; both paths use null pointers on allocation failure. The class-scan `psdGetForcedBinding` call provides a later path for a null device ID, but does not change the earlier enumeration result. No enumeration or allocation-failure sequence was run.

Poseidon allocator follow-up (OD1582): the exported `psdAllocVec` and paired `psdFreeVec` bodies were read end to end (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:315-407`; `poseidon.conf:46-47`). The allocator's `ULONG` overhead addition can wrap before a nonzero `AllocPooled` call, so the returned storage need not cover its original public size; the releaser recomputes the same wrapped allocation length from the saved original size. Checked internal descriptor/object call sites pass small structure or byte-sized lengths, so no selected in-tree near-limit caller is claimed. Other allocator callers, pool configuration and the rest of the 9,797-line library body remain pending; no large allocation was run.

Correction to the earlier Poseidon allocator follow-up: PencamTool's public camera-header path is a checked-in caller that forwards a device-reported image size to `psdAllocVec()` before validating it (`rom/usb/shellapps/PencamTool.c:620-648`); this near-limit caller is already documented as OD9435. The shell-app target is explicitly buildable but is not reached by the checked-in default USB aggregate. This supersedes the earlier statement that no selected in-tree near-limit caller was claimed; no line-credit change.

Poseidon inventory and port-action follow-up: `rom/usb/poseidon/mmakefile.src:8-35` selects the 9,797-line `poseidon.library.c` plus five other local library C bodies, while the USB startup and shell-command targets select two more startup C bodies and five commands. The library source and 21 additional local C/header/manifest/interface files were absent from this ledger and are now tracked at their actual inspection levels; both tiny HIDD class bodies and the two manifests were read, while the large library and GUI bodies remain pending. A checkout-to-ledger path scan found no further missing files under `rom/usb/poseidon`, including its shellcommands subdirectory. The library hardware-task branch maps the numeric `PA_CALLBACK` value 3 to Exec's `PA_CALL` and installs `pQuickForwardRequest`/`pQuickReplyRequest` when a controller reports `UHCF_QUICKIO` (`poseidon.library.c:9071-9113,9248-9255`; `compiler/include/exec/ports.h:44-51`). Those callbacks use `RemHead` directly on message lists that `InternalPutMsg` protects with `mp_SpinLock` on SMP (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:78-94`); concurrent send/callback ownership needs a full audit. The selected in-tree PCI USB and PCI xHCI controllers set the capability only under `PCIUSB_QUICKIO`, and a repository definition search found no enabling definition (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:580-583`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:589-592`). Thus no default in-tree controller trigger is credited here; an external controller or changed build option could enter this path. No QuickIO run was performed.

Console paste-lifetime follow-up (OD2306): `con_inject` attaches separately allocated nodes and payloads to each unit's paste list. The worker frees a chunk only after copying it completely; its paste signal does not consume chunks without a pending read. `Close` and the selected subclass disposal paths do not drain the list, so closing after paste and before a read leaks the allocations. Exec's `CloseDevice` contract explicitly requires outstanding I/O to be finished first (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:35-40`), so a close with a still-pending `CMD_READ` is not credited as another device bug. The leak requires no outstanding I/O, but it does require close before a subsequent read consumes the paste; the selected CON: handler commonly keeps an asynchronous read active, so that timing remains conditional. No paste-and-close run was performed.

Input-worker command and wakeup recheck: the complete `rom/devs/input/processevents.c:263-604` loop was reread against `input.c:125-199` and its timer/read submission macros (`processevents.c:29-58`). Queued commands are processed before the timer, keyboard and gameport signals returned by the same `Wait`, confirming OD2516's stop/reply ownership interval; `CMD_START` and `CMD_RESET` only clear `Stopped`, with no reply-port drain. Both nonzero read-error branches use `continue` before resubmission and before later wakeups, the branch behavior formerly recorded as OD47. The selected full-sized requests and normal completion paths do not establish a failed read, so OD47 is withdrawn. The `IND_ADDEVENT` first-record qualifier assignment and accepted-class filter still support OD1195's direct-client ignored-class qualifier change, but no selected in-tree ignored-class sender was found in this pass. No further candidate is credited from these branches; external event senders and platform callback timing remain pending.

Keyboard queued-read follow-up (OD1578): rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:347-379,429-440,483-489,605-649,661-685 uses per-open unit read cursors but stops its shared pending-request drain when the first unit catches up. Two openers each waiting for one event leave the second request queued after a single key, even though that unit has not consumed it; the second read waits for a later key callback to trigger another drain. This is distinct from OD32's post-drain invalid unit access and OD35's cross-CPU queue race. The keyboard.c row below remains body-inspected with callers and platform callback timing pending; no two-opener runtime test was performed. OD1578 is now detailed in the findings report as a public multi-opener candidate; the selected input.device has one keyboard read request in flight, and no second in-tree KBD_READEVENT client was found.

Gameport queued-read follow-up (OD1579, OD2136): `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:183-208,396-434,494-561,575-607,618-642,725-786` has a per-open cursor and shared pending-list drain. One mouse event completes the first waiting read; when that unit catches the shared write cursor, the loop breaks with the second request still queued and its cursor behind (OD1579). Separately, if a one-event request consumes one buffered event while another remains, `fillrequest` returns TRUE, the drain removes the request and advances `ioreq` to the list tail sentinel; the post-loop `gpUn->gpu_flags` cleanup dereferences `io_Unit` from that sentinel (OD2136). The selected input.device has one gameport request in flight and no second in-tree GPD_READEVENT client was found; the direct public two-opener sequence establishing the sentinel trigger is source-confirmed in the 2026-10-14 follow-up. No runtime test was performed.

Late-open cursor follow-up (OD1580): keyboard and gameport Open allocate zeroed per-open units without initializing read positions from the shared writer (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:151-165`; `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:188-208`), and the selected input.device opens both, installs their HIDD callbacks, then submits initial reads without `CMD_CLEAR` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:183-250`; `keyboard.c:197-230`; `gameport.c:247-279`). A keyboard or mouse event during this setup window is buffered and read by the zero-cursor unit; no prior opener is required. However, on the selected m68k boot the input device priority is above Intuition, and no earlier checked-in user-facing input-handler registration was identified, so startup events may be consumed before a selected client can observe them. The finding remains conditional on an observable consumer/new-open cursor contract. This is distinct from existing-unit full-ring ambiguity in OD34/OD41; no event was generated.

Timer list-lock failure follow-up (OD1564): selected PC and ARM32 Raspberry Pi SMP timer initializers set `tb_ExecLockBase` and do not check the subsequent `AllocLock` result. The shared `rom/timer/lowlevel.c` insertions and completion walks plus PC deadline scan call `ObtainLock(tb_ListLock, ...)` when that base is nonnull but ignore its FALSE return. `rom/exec/exec_locks.c:176-205` confirms a failed lock allocation makes those calls no-ops. The ARM32 Raspberry Pi `smp` configuration releases secondary cores on BCM2836 (`boot.c:334-370`; `platform_bcm2708.c:89-147`), establishing the cross-CPU trigger. OpenSBI has the same conditional source but is excluded from the affected configurations: the configured target does not enable ExecSMP, and startup currently runs only the boot hart (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:41-43`). No low-memory boot or concurrent timer workload was run. OD1565 separately covers successful list-lock allocation followed by failed IRQ registration: generated failed-init rollback invokes the expunge hooks, which do not free the lock; the PC hook’s unguarded null IRQ removal remains Exec EK09.

The direct repository C `AllocLock(` search found only the generic timer initializer and three architecture timer variants as clients of this public vector. `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:373` constructs and publishes `execlock.resource` during Exec preparation on SMP, before normal timer module initialization; this supports OD1564's nonnull-resource/null-lock distinction. No independent other-driver `AllocLock` failure path was found in this checkout. Generated vector calls, nonliteral indirect calls and external clients remain outside that exact C-call search.

A current checkout-to-ledger scan finds all local `.c` and `.h` paths under `rom/devs` and `workbench/devs` represented here except paths assigned to the disk/block and display-monitor reports. The remaining raw gaps are 108 `rom/devs` paths in AHCI, ATA, NVMe, SCSI, SD card, VirtIO and trackdisk, and 426 `workbench/devs` paths in diskimage, fdsk/ramdrive, USB MassStorage and display monitors. The earlier census incorrectly assigned `netinfo.device` to another report; its 15 local files are now tracked below. This boundary inventory does not establish build selection or body/caller completeness for every row.

A combined coverage-ledger scan found the explicitly buildable `workbench/hidds/controller` module absent from all three revisit ledgers. Its local manifest lists seven C files and four supporting files, which now have individual rows; all seven C bodies have full reads. The only parent aggregate edge (`workbench-hidds`) is commented out, and a checkout-wide search found no active boot/package edge or in-tree client of the public controller API outside the module itself. OD9852-OD9858 and OD9860-OD9861 describe conditional defects reachable when this explicit target is built and used by external or alternate clients; OD2883 separately records the consumer-disposal race. No default-image inclusion or in-tree device producer/consumer is established. External callers and SMP contracts remain open.

An open-vector comparison across the sixteen USB class `dev.c` files that set `IOERR_UNITBUSY` found fourteen that replace it with `IOERR_OPENFAIL`, one (`lan78xx`) that preserves it, and one (`palmpda`) that takes a distinct successful deaf-open path. Ten previously missing selected `dev.c` inventory rows were added for that targeted check. All sixteen now have complete body reads or line-for-line comparison against a fully read sibling; their individual rows retain external caller, concurrency and device-lifetime gaps.

A recursive checkout-to-ledger scan found no missing `.c` or `.h` rows under `rom/devs/console` (20 paths), `rom/devs/keyboard` (4 paths), `rom/devs/gameport` (4 paths), or `rom/devs/input` (5 paths). The selected producer and handler-lifetime contracts retain their individual row statuses.

Local `rom/devs` reconciliation: excluding the seven disk-driver directories assigned to AROS-disk.md, the console, keyboard, gameport and input module directories contain 21 C files and 12 headers. The `rom/usb/pciusb/mmakefile.src` module names 15 local C sources; all exist and have body-inspected rows below. The optional USB HID class manifest (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/mmakefile.src`) names five implementation C files and one generated-stub source; all six existing C files have body-inspected rows below, along with its two local/public headers. The i386-PC and x86-64-PC boot manifests select `kernel-hidd-i8042`. Its module manifest lists seven compiled C files; eight local headers are also present. These 15 files were missing from the previous inventory and are now tracked below. PC i8042 event-path recheck: `i8042_kbd_irq_handler` reads controller bytes and calls the scan-code translator (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:68-99,545-575`); `KBDPUSHEVENT` invokes the cached input-HIDD method synchronously (`i8042_intern.h:85-98`). The input hub either copies an event into its bounded pending buffer when no consumer exists, or calls registered consumers directly (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:78-125,240-257`). The first keyboard consumer is linked and drains pending events during construction (`rom/hidds/input/inputclass.c:187-209`), and `keyboard.device` registers `keyCallback`, which writes its 128-entry ring and invokes the queued-read drain when necessary (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:197-206,605-649`). There is no per-event allocation or independent queue-failure return in this route. OD2882 covers the conditional first-consumer pending-buffer handoff race and OD2883 details callback/listener lifetime during concurrent disposal; OD34 covers full-ring ambiguity; OD2389 details the pending-read lost wakeup across CPUs. PC IOAPIC and input-task startup placement do not establish the required cross-CPU overlap; it remains conditional. IRQ removal versus delivery, setup-task shutdown and physical controller timing remain open. No new candidate is credited from this trace.

PC i8042 partial-registration recheck: `i8042_Init` creates the keyboard and mouse hubs separately, conditionally calls `HW_AddDriver` for each, increments its library open count only for successful registrations, and succeeds if at least one was installed (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_classinit.c:26-73`). The source explicitly permits a missing mouse. Thus failure of the second registration after the first succeeds is an accepted partial setup, not by itself an init-rollback defect. Driver removal and the matching open-count lifecycle remain pending; OD985 covers the separate Utility reference omitted by the expunge hook.

| `rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c` | Full 1,548-line source body reread function-by-function (2026-10-17); binding, wrappers, worker, initialization/cleanup, port state, control methods, suspend/resume and release traced | The Poseidon ROM startup adds `hub.class` before PCIUSB enumeration (`rom/usb/poseidon/usbromearlystartup.c:97-106`); the class module selects this body (`rom/usb/classes/hub/mmakefile.src:7-13`). Traced worker startup/discovery (`:97-128,390-529,711-724`), hub descriptor allocation/parsing (`:843-894`), status and connection events (`:525-724`), `nClearPortStatus` and `nConfigurePort` (`:1106-1399`), message/suspend handlers (`:1405-1548`) and their Poseidon callers (`poseidon.library.c:3695-3930`), cleanup (`:1080-1098`) and synchronous binding release (`:141-175`). OD3229 records the conditional worker teardown race after unmatched `Permit`; OD3231 records unchecked standard/SuperSpeed descriptor reads; OD3232 records both hub classes’ descriptor-sized interrupt transfers and port scans exceeding their four-byte change arrays at 32+ ports; OD3234 records disable/power-cycle flags using 32-bit masks despite descriptor-derived larger port counts; OD3235 records ExecSMP-unsynchronized shared binding-list append/remove/lookup operations; OD3236 records startup port-power commands proceeding despite reported hub-level over-current. Suspend/resume caller cross-check found no separate candidate. Rechecked `nConfigurePort` short `GET_STATUS` handling against the public pipe API and selected UHCI/xHCI completions: `psdDoPipe` returns `io_Error` while actual bytes remain separately observable through `psdGetPipeActual`; UHCI flags short packets as `UHIOERR_RUNTPACKET` unless explicitly allowed, while xHCI completion records the transferred byte count and can return success for a short successful completion. `nConfigurePort` does not check the actual count before reading both status words (`hub.class.c:1124-1128,1232-1247`). This established OD3394: xHCI explicitly maps `TRB_CC_SHORT_PACKET` to success while retaining the shorter actual count (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2490-2503`); standard and SuperSpeed hub configuration then read both status words without checking the count (`rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:1217-1227,1334-1348`). The trigger requires a short response from a malformed/nonconforming hub. UHCI normally reports `UHIOERR_RUNTPACKET`, so the finding is limited to selected xHCI with either standard or SuperSpeed hub class. Rechecked the reset-poll error exit in standard and SuperSpeed `nConfigurePort`: a failed `GET_STATUS` breaks the poll loop without invalidating `uhps`, then the recovery branch tests it for a low-speed power-cycle predicate (`hub.class.c:1231-1247,1333-1375`; `rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:1334-1354,1421-1465`), establishing OD3396 for little-endian standard and USB2-emulated root paths. The standard and SuperSpeed port-event handlers were cross-checked on non-timeout GET_STATUS errors: both clear all port-change flags and then skip state handling when the read fails, establishing OD3395 (`hub.class.c:630-641,1106-1164`; `rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:570-587,1067-1148`). The public `usbGetAttrsA`/`usbSetAttrsA` and `usbDoMethodA` bodies were also read (`hub.class.c:181-385`): SetAttrs intentionally returns zero; GetAttrs writes only recognized output tags; synchronous hub methods either execute on the worker itself or create/reply through a temporary message port. The port flag updates in DoMethod are covered by OD3234/OD3235; no independent defect was established in these wrappers. The remove-event-after-`psdFreeDevice` order was traced into `pFreeDevice` and the asynchronous popup handler: the `PsdDevice` record is intentionally retained and `pd_ProductStr` is preserved for that event (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2159-2210`; `popo.gui.c:968-1005`), so this is not recorded as a use-after-free. Remaining: selected Poseidon method callers, host-controller behavior outside the cited paths, and runtime/device behavior. Source-only. |

| `rom/usb/shellapps/SonixcamTool.c` | Complete 1,374-line source body reviewed cumulatively across setup/cleanup, I²C/register helpers, RTIso hooks/capture, image conversion/overlay, and PPM output; selected callers checked; hardware timing, external clients, and broader platform contracts remain open | The active `kernel-usb` and `kernel-usb-nopci` virtual aggregates select this target; checked PC, Raspberry Pi and RISC-V native boot targets reach one of those aggregates. The input hook returns length zero at the raw-buffer boundary; the done hook uses zero length to publish/reset a completed frame. Added OD3816 for PCIUSB OHCI/EHCI paths that skip zero-length PTDs/transfers and therefore do not call that done hook (`SonixcamTool.c:123-129,146-174,1217-1234`; `pciusb/ohci/ohci_isoch.c:405-425`; `pciusb/ehci/ehci_isoch.c:548-553,691`). UHCI queues a zero-length TD and can deliver the zero-length done callback. xHCI also stalls: its RTIso request setup leaves `rtn_IOReq.iouh_Length` zero in the clear-initialized unit pool; the request hook's zero length remains zero, queueing marks the PTD buffer-valid, and `xhciStartIsochIO` rejects it while the completion refill loop counts it as pending (`pcixhci_dev.c:92-93`; `pcixhci_arospci.c:206-220`; `pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:1491-1509`; `xhci_isoch.c:224-225,272-281,288-314`; `xhci_hcd.c:2797-2809`). The shell-app manifest selects SonixcamTool and the active USB aggregate dependencies include this target (build-scope correction at the USB shell-app note below). No camera, controller, or frame was used; source-only. OD3933: `main()` ignores PPM `FPrintf`, `Flush`, image `Write`, and `Close` results, then reports success and increments the capture count (`:1317-1329`); DOS API contracts permit short/error results (`rom/dos/{vfprintf,flush,write,close}.c`). The `kernel-usb-shellapps` manifest selects this tool, and checked USB package targets reach it through an active virtual aggregate (`rom/usb/shellapps/mmakefile.src:4-9`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:7-22,69-71`). OD3934: `AllocSonixcam()` ignores a failed `AllocSignal(-1L)` after creating its message port; capture later shifts that -1 into the callback `Signal()` and `Wait()` masks (`:820-823,1206-1217`; Exec failure contract `rom/exec/allocsignal.c:32-54,58-68`). Exhaustion of the current task’s allocatable signal bits can therefore prevent frame completion signaling and make capture wait indefinitely or use an unintended mask, depending on compiler/target behavior. Same-CPU memory-pool clearing was checked: it makes the sharpened two-pixel output border deterministic black, consistent with Bayer demosaic border handling, so no defect was credited for that effect. The whole file body is now reviewed; its release hook also has the OD9430 pre-task-initialization window. Hardware timing, external clients and broader platform contracts remain open. |

The public HIDD method has no minimum in its interface declaration (`workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hda.conf:33-41`), while `SetupStream` accepts zero and one; it writes LVI 0xffff for zero and LVI zero for one, then StartStream can set RUN without checking for a valid ring (`hdaclass.c:853-907,936-949`). Both selected AHI clients pass two buffers. The prior one-buffer/LVI-zero concern is not counted because no selected caller or interface contract establishes it as invalid. AHI computes `ahiac_MaxBuffSamples` as integer mix frequency divided by minimum player frequency after the HDA driver may raise mix frequency to a supported rate (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:257-267,510-518`; `HDAudio/main.c:105-110`); a zero DMA size would need a player rate at or above mix rate, outside AHI's documented ordinary timing range (`audioctrl.c:380-399`), so no selected normal-parameter zero-size candidate is credited. `SyncStreamBuffer` checks the buffer index against the configured count before touching DMA storage (`hdaclass.c:993-1004`); selected AHI interrupts supply their two-buffer flip index. OD2387 follows `Cause` into the AHI soft interrupt and confirms StopStream/FreeStream do not drain a callback already running on another CPU. Exec `Cause` explicitly queues an interrupt for later delivery when invoked from a hardware IRQ (`rom/exec/cause.c:25-57`), and selected AHI preferences start/stop a test tone via ControlAudio (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/support.c:1306-1327`); neither supplies a callback drain. Exact hardware behavior for zero-count and oversized DMA requests remains open; OD2138 now traces the oversized case through selected AHI tag handling into HDAudio, while controller response remains untested. OD1391 traces tag overflow into AHI converter verbs. OD2126 is now detailed in the report: SendCommand reads only the current RIRB write-pointer entry, so a later unsolicited entry can hide the solicited response; a two-entry ring can also wrap to the old pointer. The unchanged-pointer loop can hold `hc_VerbLock` for roughly 50 seconds. This remains public-API conditional; selected AHI codec paths do not enable unsolicited responses, and no controller sequence was run. DMA and hardware timing contracts remain open. Hardware-IRQ teardown follow-up (2026-10-15; no new finding): `HDA_Shutdown` masks controller interrupts, then calls subclass `HWExit` before freeing `hc_Streams` (`:504-556`). The selected PCI subclass removes the installed handler via the inherited `HIDD_PCIDriver_RemoveInterrupt` (`hda_hidd.c:188-200`; `pcidt_driverclass.c:967-976` overrides Add only), which reaches `KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:336-340`). ExecSMP `krnRunIRQHandlers` holds `kb_IntrSpinLock` read-locked across the complete callback, while removal obtains the write lock before unlink/free (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:125-142`; `remirqhandler.c:57-75`); on the selected UP path, `Disable` masks local interrupt delivery across unlink. Therefore an in-flight `HDA_IntCode` finishes before the stream array is freed on these paths. This synchronization does not drain the separate Cause-queued AHI softint callback; OD2898/EK8935 retain those callback-lifetime conditions. No IRQ or shutdown was run. |

Hosted Ethernet shutdown WaitPort/GetMsg caller recheck (OD11416 added; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): traced final Close and failed-first-open worker cleanup (`arch/all-unix/devs/networks/eth/init.c:221-235,269-280`) through worker termination (`iotask.c:365-385`) and generic Exec queue routines (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-105`; `waitport.c:62-96`; `getmsg.c:61-77`). `PutMsg()` links the exit message into `iosyncport`; the worker immediately `FreeVec()`s the same node. If the receiver does not run before that free, it then observes the queue head, dequeues it and reads it through `ReplyMsg()`, confirming the UAF race independently of the source FIXME. Exec `Signal()` reschedules a same-CPU waiter immediately only when its priority exceeds the running task's; the worker is created at priority 50 (`init.c:189-194`; `rom/exec/signal.c:395-425`), making the race possible for lower/equal-priority close/open-failure waiters, and ExecSMP permits concurrent dequeue. The exit-message `AllocVec()` result is unchecked as well, so allocation failure supplies NULL to `PutMsg()` and leaves the waiter without an exit acknowledgement. Added OD11416 with the scheduling condition stated. The hosted Ethernet device is an explicitly buildable target in the variant-less Linux device aggregate; package installation and runtime behavior remain unverified. No close or allocation failure was induced.

Therefore a failed RECORD-only start does not imply that existing PLAY must stop; the still-running playback task is expected. Finding 179 separately tracks the buffer allocated before a failed recording start. No playback task is left without an active direction by this trace.

Filesave recording cleanup/caller follow-up: reread `_AHIsub_Start`, `_AHIsub_Stop`, `_AHIsub_FreeAudio` and `RecSlave` together (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-main.c:183-406`; `filesave-recslave.c:49-173`). Direct clients, concurrent control/free calls, and driver-specific platform behavior remain open.

OD2087 follows the start-only address checks against `dma_build_control_blocks`: both sample transfers use the full `dmabuf_size`, while the CB chain uses aligned pointers, so a base below 1 GiB does not prove the complete DMA range is reachable. The trigger needs a successful `MEMF_31BIT` pool spanning the boundary; kernel memory flags a range ending below 2 GiB (`rom/kernel/kernel_memory.c:30-42`), so a 2-GiB identity-mapped Pi range can expose allocations above 1 GiB. The selected AArch64 Pi mapping is identity for these allocations; this remains distinct from OD2085's rejected-base leak. The addressability failure requires a returned `MEMF_31BIT` region at or above 1 GiB on a selected 64-bit Pi; the selected sound.datatype caller frees its control after Start failure. Address-check comparison against OD2086: the selected AArch64 kernel manifest resolves `virtualtophysical` to the generic identity implementation (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmakefile.src:54`; `rom/kernel/virtualtophysical.c:47-52`), and AArch64 boot maps its RAM range at the same addresses; on that path the RPiPWM pointer check and direct `GPU_BUS_ADDR(pointer)` use the same physical address. No separate pointer-versus-physical defect is credited for this 64-bit path. The selected sound.datatype caller reaches AHI_FreeAudio after AHI_ControlAudio reports Start failure (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3957-3963,4011-4054`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src`); AHI FreeAudio invokes Stop for the successfully allocated subdriver, confirming the sentinel/omitted-field cleanup path (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:718-727`). OD227-OD228 remain; OD1770 follows combined true Play+Record through AHI's one Start call, PWM's completed playback/DMA setup, and its later unsupported-record error with no rollback. Rechecked Stop's signal/wait against the worker: its `Wait` includes Ctrl-C, the worker clears `slavetask` before acknowledging exit, and Stop removes a nonnull IRQ token before freeing buffers (`rpipwm-main.c:370-430`; `rpipwm-playslave.c:175-199,270-284`). This ordering does not establish a normal early-free or null-removal defect; a hook or hardware stall remains a timing question. Buffer math was also checked against AHI `RecalcBuff`: the shipped stereo 16-bit mix type uses four bytes per frame, the allocated mix buffer is sized from the minimum player rate, and the worker clamps converted frames to `MaxBuffSamples`; the DMA allocation holds at least that many eight-byte frames. The 960–1088 PWM range keeps the 16-bit sample scaling below signed 32-bit overflow. These checks do not establish a normal buffer overrun. Shipped mode is stereo 16-bit, and `_GetAttr` advertises Record FALSE. Further hardware and firmware timing checks remain open. OD2161 traces the live stop path through the unchecked local DMA reset to buffer/control-block release; the hardware quiesce result remains unverified. OD2843 is restored in the detailed report for the distinct DMA buffer-length overflow: accepted MixFreq 536870913 with legacy MinPlayerFreq 1 yields MaxBuffSamples 536870913, the 32-bit frame-to-byte product wraps to eight, and the slave pre-fills the original frame count before acknowledging startup; this is separate from OD2162’s rate-search division by zero. OD2162 is detailed in the report: AHI passes the unbounded `AHIA_MixFreq` tag to RPiPWM, and the exact request 4,194,304 Hz makes `samplerate * R` wrap to zero at R=1024, so the rate-search loop divides by zero before DMA setup. `AHIDB_FrequencyArg` is documented as an index in `0..AHIDB_Frequencies-1`; the unguarded table access therefore has a documented caller precondition, and no separate finding is credited for out-of-range queries.  AllocAudio partial-failure cleanup traced through AHI: failed `AHIsub_AllocAudio` enters `AHI_FreeAudio`, which skips Stop but still calls the subdriver FreeAudio (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:511,520-521,718-727`); RPiPWM FreeAudio independently releases an acquired DMA channel, safely ignores signal `-1` through Exec `FreeSignal`, and frees driver data (`rpipwm-main.c:70-84,110-115`; `rom/exec/freesignal.c:48-56`). No additional AllocAudio partial-resource leak established.|

Void AHI startup-result follow-up: the optional Void subdriver is included in the selected AHI driver build (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Makefile.in:41`; `Void/Makefile.in:8-12`). `_AHIsub_Start` allocates the mix buffer, creates the process, waits for one master signal, and tests `dd->slavetask` to choose `AHIE_OK` versus failure (`Void/void-main.c:164-210`). If the worker's `AllocSignal(-1)` fails, it reaches the exit acknowledgement, sends that signal, and only then stores `dd->slavetask = NULL` (`Void/void-playslave.c:53-65,85-96`). On Exec SMP, the waiting parent can run between those writes, so OD2031's false-success result reaches AHI's selected `AHIsub_Start` control call (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:1007-1021`). On one CPU the worker's `Forbid()` holds the parent until the null store, so this specific interleaving is SMP-only. OD177 separately covers the retained mix buffer on a correctly reported start failure; OD178 separately covers unsupported combined play/record start. No process or allocation failure was run.
