This is distinct from OD2994 report-descriptor allocation and transfer handling. OD3272 now details the separate multi-report-ID case: the keyboard class stores modifier offsets without report IDs and ignores `msg->id`, so a Consumer Control report bit at offset zero can be interpreted as the keyboard modifier at the same offset (`hidclass.c:65-83`; `kbdclass.c:100-123,154-177`; `hid.c:297-303`). No descriptor or event was used. | OD3754 records that Ctrl-C worker exit does not emit key releases for held report state (`kbdclass.c:373-381`).
| `workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/mouseclass.c` | Full body and selected USB-hub caller checked; wider clients pending | OD3359 adds the accepted X-present/Y-absent report case: failed Y lookup leaves zeroed `rel_y`, and the worker consequently routes X-relative motion through absolute tablet conversion (`mouseclass.c:133-175,324-341`; selected Intuition scaling `inputhandler.c:2179-2188`). OD4093 records sparse Button Usage discovery stopping at the first missing ID, so later declared button fields are never read or mapped to input.device (`mouseclass.c:63-68,171-178,357-434`). Descriptor conformance and device-level impact remain unverified. | Mouse descriptor parsing, report callback, input task and teardown read; subclass descriptor-null concern dismissed against the superclass success path (`hidclass.c:264-266,314-335`), with OD21 also covering this subclass's unchecked report-buffer allocation and descriptor-transfer result; OD2247 covers unchecked worker stack setup; OD3564 covers ignored NewAddTask failure and unlaunched-task allocations; OD3565 restores the Task/MemList allocation-failure case (historical coverage-only OD2246/OD2810); OD2248 covers I/O setup. OD2806 covers the event-batch leak on input.device open failure; OD2186 covers the distinct task-pointer publication race; OD3565 covers the initial worker Task/MemList allocation failure and mouse null-task disposal (historical coverage ID OD2810). A suspected ten-event buffer overrun was dismissed: the current emitter writes at most one movement, three button and two wheel events per report (`mouseclass.c:324-465`), fewer than ten; candidate 1011 was rechecked against the full button-to-event branch and the selected Bluetooth HID fourth-button mapping: when only USB HID button 4 changes and there is no motion or wheel delta, `iec` stays zero and no input event is submitted. OD2246 follows failed `NewAddTask` ETask/context allocation into an unlaunched task pointer and unreclaimed stack MemList. OD2184 expands detach-signal loss while DOS remains unavailable through selected USB-hub disposal; OD2313 follows the batched keyboard Alt handoff through `ActQualifier` and ClickToFront; this worker also uses `PeekQualifier` to form mouse event masks and can preserve the stale value (`mouseclass.c:300-316,345-467`; `rom/devs/input/processevents.c:319-328,371-382`). OD2302 formalizes OD1918: the X and Y Input fields are parsed independently, but when their relative flags differ the worker sends both as coordinates in a single absolute tablet event. This is a valid, narrowly triggered descriptor case; no physical device was identified. Rechecked short-report question against the superclass and controller callbacks: mouse filters the report ID, but neither its parser nor `HidInterrupt` tests the completed payload length; `HidInterrupt` passes the allocated maximum as `report_length` and OHCI/UHCI callbacks do not expose an actual byte count through this method. Whether a short successful transfer reaches the callback and which bytes remain in its DMA buffer is controller-dependent, so no separate short-report finding is credited yet. Other lifecycle and input.device contracts pending. OD2298 follows an accepted absolute-axis HID logical range with maximum below minimum: `mouseclass` computes a zero tablet range and selected Intuition divides by it (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2179-2188`). The trigger is malformed device descriptor data; no USB input event was run. OD2301 follows valid signed absolute USB HID axes with a negative logical minimum: the mouse worker copies the signed value directly into an unsigned tablet coordinate instead of rebasing by the minimum, so a zero-valued midpoint maps to the screen origin; the cross-reference is in Graphics/Desktop. OD2300 follows a valid large absolute range into Intuition: screen width times tablet coordinate wraps in 32-bit ULONG before division, yielding an in-bounds but incorrect pointer location; the cross-reference is in Graphics/Desktop. No input event was run. OD2188 also covers the mouse worker's unchecked `InputEvent` batch allocation and direct report-event writes. OD2806 records the separate cleanup omission when `OpenDevice("input.device")` fails: the worker deletes its request/port and returns without `FreeVec(ie)` (`mouseclass.c:250-260`); OD2186 remains the distinct task-publication race on that failure path. OD2230 follows the complete signed wheel value through `hid_get_data`, the SPSC event record and the worker’s one-pair output; USB-IF Wheel counts and the older HID handler confirm that values beyond ±1 carry additional movement. Its correctly sized IOStdReq follows the same always-success-on-valid-length input.device Open hook (`rom/devs/input/input.c:88-110`), and the HID report callback signals its worker.  OD2247 also applies to the mouse constructor’s unchecked 10 KiB stack allocation and context setup (`mouseclass.c:191-219`; `arch/x86_64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:20,26,82-99`). No allocation failure was induced.  OD3565 restores the Task/MemList allocation-failure case: the constructor returns an object after either allocation fails, leaks a successful sibling allocation, and the mouse destructor signals the NULL task (`mouseclass.c:191-195,223,226-230`; `rom/exec/signal.c:158-172,262-303`). Historical coverage identifiers were OD2246/OD2810.  OD2248 applies to the mouse worker’s matching I/O setup and OpenDevice call (`mouseclass.c:245-252`; `rom/exec/createiorequest.c:84-100`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-98`). Rechecked worker exits against parent disposal: OpenDevice failure deletes request/port and clears the task field but omits `FreeVec(ie)` (OD2806); the parent can subsequently republish the exited task pointer (OD2186). Normal Ctrl-C handling closes the device, deletes request/port and frees `ie`; however, the worker only tests Ctrl-C after DOS becomes ready, so detach during prolonged DOS unavailability remains OD2184. No additional independent worker-exit defect established.  OD2810 traces the task/ MemList allocation failure through the successful New return, zero-cleared OOP instance data and unconditional Dispose signal; hub removal disposes the subclass and Exec Signal dereferences the NULL task. This is separate from OD2186's failed-open pointer-overwrite race. No allocation failure or removal was induced. OD3142 follows the selected X/Y `hid_locate` results into `hid_get_data` and the emitted tablet/relative pointer path; a byte-aligned 32-bit axis is the concrete valid-field trigger. No USB input report was handled. OD3143 traces a nonnegative-range relative axis through X/Y extraction into signed raw-mouse deltas; OD3144 follows parser-context allocation failure from the selected mouse report parsing path. OD3754 records that Ctrl-C worker exit does not emit button releases for held report state (`mouseclass.c:279-289`). OD3755 traces full-ring drop (`mouseclass.c:57-90`) to worker-only button-state updates (`:294-307,358-433`); UHCI NAKs do not call the report callback (`uhciclass.c:139-150`), and HID requests idle rate zero (`hidclass.c:253`), so a dropped release has no guaranteed retry.

USB HID mouse ring target-selection recheck (no SMP candidate retained): compared the HIDD HID-class package selectors with the selected target chains. Sam440's module chain selects `hidd-usb` but has no `ENABLE_EXECSMP` target definition (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:20-70`; `configure:11189-11206`); Efika's USB package is likewise a CHRP PPC target without an SMP variant (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/boot/mmakefile.src:83-91`; `configure:11266-11278`). The RISC-V64 boot package names `USB/hid`, but its kernel startup explicitly runs only the boot hart pending SMP bring-up (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:101-120`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:39-43`). The configure branches enabling Exec SMP are x86_64 `smp` and Raspberry Pi `smp` (`configure:10834-10837,11355-11360`); the x86_64 USB package uses the separate ROM Poseidon target and RasPi's package class list omits HID (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:10-16`; `arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:182-193`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:215-232`). The checked-in selected HIDD mouse-class paths therefore do not establish cross-CPU access to its plain `head`/`tail` fields. Single-CPU callback/task sequencing preserves the slot-before-head publication in this path; no additional ring finding is retained. This does not assess manually installing the optional HIDD class into an SMP system. No build or hardware run was performed.


LPe32002 event-queue configuration follow-up (OD2141): confirmed the driver is selected through the full Workbench common-device aggregate for x86_64, and `configure.in` enables `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for the x86_64 `smp` variant. The unprotected `ReportEvents` traversal can therefore overlap ExecSMP's locked `PutMsg`/`GetMsg` queue operations in a supported build when matching event reports and queue operations coincide. No device or interleaving was run.


LPe32002 event-port lock initialization check (OD2141): verified `CreateUnit` allocates every request port with `MEMF_CLEAR` before initializing the message list, and Exec's SMP spinlock defines zero as `SPINLOCK_UNLOCKED` (`unit.c:749-759`; `compiler/include/aros/types/spinlock_s.h:52-58`). The report finding is specifically that `ReportEvents` mutates the valid queue without acquiring this lock; it does not depend on an uninitialized-port-lock assumption. No concurrency test was run.

xHCI address-index candidate recheck: the 128-entry device-controller table is indexed without a local check, but all checked-in `iouh_DevAddr` producers are in Poseidon; `pAllocDevAddr` only issues 1–127, with zero used while enumerating, and the pipe attribute is unpack-only. No selected in-tree source path was found that supplies 128–255. Candidate 895 remains an external/malformed request contract question and is not counted as a demonstrated project-path bug. SET_ADDRESS `wValue >= 128` likewise has no ordinary Poseidon enumeration trigger. No USB request was submitted.

xHCI DMA result/length follow-up: rechecked `xhciPrepareDMABuffer` against the actual selected target hooks. Its discarded `CachePreDMA` return and possibly shortened length do not establish a current selected mismatch: generic x86 returns the input address; AArch64 native uses the identity `KrnVirtualToPhysical` body and the Raspberry Pi target maps ordinary RAM identity; OpenSBI's optional Zicbom replacement also returns the original address and does not alter the length. Non-identity buffer mappings, physical contiguity guarantees, cache-line ownership/coherency and other package targets remain open. No transfer was run.

OD2130 Rice-parameter range follow-up: traced the selected AHIRecord `FLAC16` encoder configuration (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:2882-2891,2945-2953`) through `stream_encoder.c:3204-3210,3264-3276` into the entropy writer. The 16-bit branch caps Rice parameters at `FLAC__ENTROPY_CODING_METHOD_PARTITIONED_RICE_ESCAPE_PARAMETER - 1` (14), so the block writer's `parameter`-based masks and shifts stay below the 32-bit boundary on this selected route (`bitwriter.c:541-545,557-560`). The exposed single-value Rice/Golomb helpers and the 5-bit Rice2 range are not selected by this FLAC16 caller. The remaining OD2130 concern is specifically the signed left shift of a negative residual during the normal block encoder; no compiler output or file was tested.


RISC-V DesignWare UART publication-window follow-up (OD2244): traced the selected OpenSBI unit constructor through serial.device `Open`, the HIDD Init callback, `findUnit`, and `RBF_InterruptHandler`. Receive IRQs are enabled before handler registration; after the callback is installed, the serial-device list node is still unpublished. A received byte in this window yields null from `findUnit`, then the receive handler dereferences the null unit while buffering. The separate simultaneous-open/close concern was closed for this target: OpenSBI currently runs only its boot hart and the Exec device vectors run under Forbid. No runtime interrupt was induced.

RISC-V DesignWare UART receive-before-publication recheck (OD2244): traced HIDD unit construction through `serial.device` open. The constructor enables UART receive interrupts, then registers `dwuart_int_handler` (`SerialUnitClass.c:193,215-218`); `serial.device` next installs `RBF_InterruptHandler` via `HIDD_SerialUnit_Init` and only afterward links `SerialUnit` into `UnitList` (`serial_init.c:170-184`). A receive interrupt in the post-Init/pre-AddHead interval causes `findUnit` to return NULL, after which nonempty data reaches the general-buffer path and dereferences `SU` (`serial_interrupthandlers.c:29-31,96-108`). Before the callback is installed the HIDD drops input safely, so the precise trigger is data arriving in the narrower callback-installed/list-not-yet-published window. No UART or timing was exercised.

OD2244 interrupt-window caller serialization check: Exec `OpenDevice` invokes the device open vector while task switches are forbidden, then calls `Permit` after it returns. The lock macro uses `LOCKF_FORBID`; Exec documents this as task-switch prevention, not interrupt masking. The HIDD’s `Enable()` between storing the callback and `serial.device`’s subsequent `AddHead` therefore leaves the same-CPU receive IRQ able to observe the unpublished unit. This excludes caller-level task switching as a blocker but does not prevent an IRQ in the window. No interrupt was induced.

RISC-V DesignWare UART MMIO span follow-up: traced every `serial_in/out` offset in `SerialUnitClass.c` through `dwuart_reg` and the FDT `reg-shift`, `reg-io-width`, `reg` size and `KrnMapGlobal` path. Ordinary 16550 offsets top out at 7; the conditional busy-detect handler also reads the DesignWare-only USR at offset `0x1f` (`dwuart_io.h:26-31`; `SerialUnitClass.c:719-746`). With the common shift 2 and width 4, that access requires a mapped span of at least `0x80` bytes. The node is admitted for both `snps,dw-apb-uart` and generic `ns16550a` compatibles, and no size/shift/width or DesignWare-extension check precedes access (`dwuart_init.c:40-43,94-137`). No selected OpenSBI DTB was found in the checkout to establish an undersized accepted span or a generic UART reaching IIR_BUSY; retain register-span and compatibility behavior as pending rather than promoting an unproven finding. No UART or device tree was run. The follow-up confirms the only direct `DWUART_USR` read is gated by `UART_IIR & 7 == DWUART_IIR_BUSY` (`SerialUnitClass.c:719-746`); ordinary configured accesses otherwise remain at 16550 offsets 0–7. No source evidence establishes a standard `ns16550a` generating the DesignWare-only busy code, so no generic-compatibility finding is credited from this branch.

RISC-V DesignWare UART state ownership follow-up: traced `HIDDSerialData.SerialUnits/usedunits`, `class_static_data.units[]`, and each discovered `dwuart_port` from OOP construction through serial.device open/close and HIDD disposal. The zeroed HIDD object starts with an empty unit bitmap; NewUnit reserves its slot after successful object construction, and DisposeUnit clears that slot after the unit's dispose method removes its IRQ/reset registrations and clears the IRQ-visible pointer under `Disable`. OpenSBI's selected configuration is single-hart, and OpenDevice/CloseDevice serialize the selected device vectors; no concurrent slot mutation is established. OD1562 remains the separate ignored IRQ-registration failure. No unit or hardware was opened.

OpenSBI DesignWare I²C fixed-profile caller recheck (OD2245): retraced FDT `clock-frequency` from `dwi2c_add` into the selected controller state, `DWI2C_HWCalcTiming` and both public transfer methods. The selected HIDD class exposes `WriteRead` and `ProbeAddress` but no bus-speed setter, so no later caller replaces the node's requested rate; `dwi2c_program` selects standard mode for `<= 100000` and fast mode above that, then writes the fixed profile minima computed from the controller input clock. OD2245 now covers accepted bus rates other than the fixed 100/400-kHz timing profiles when a discoverable input clock causes the driver to program those profile counts. The selected HIDD exposes no later bus-speed setter. No DTB or controller was run.

UHCI final-segment size recheck (OD2242): reread `uhci_QueuedTransfer` from descriptor-count calculation through each TD's token and buffer pointer. For length 65 and endpoint max packet 64, `ntd` is two, but the unchanged `length` makes both descriptor tokens request 64 bytes and advances the second buffer to offset 64; the one-byte remainder is not used. `BulkTransfer` forwards the public length unchanged, and the selected MassStorage `DirectSCSI` path forwards `msg->dataLen` without packet-size rounding. This confirms the one-byte-overrun example for final IN and OUT segments; no transfer was run.


BCM2708 USB OTG DMA edge recheck (OD1522 refined): followed the optional Pencam image header and bulk-IN transfer through `TransferImage`, Poseidon `psdDoPipe`/`psdAllocVec`, the HCD chunk/bounce rules, and ARM/AArch64 `CacheClearE`. Both selected kernels round cache operations to actual lines and use clean-invalidate on partial edge lines, so no neighboring-data loss is established for a quiescent line. OD1522 is narrowed to the conditional ExecSMP race described in its detailed section: a direct-DMA IN segment exceeds the 16 KiB bounce capacity, ends partway through an actual cache line, shares that line with another allocation, and another CPU writes that allocation during the pre/post DMA cache-maintenance interval. No checked-in caller establishes that overlap. No camera, image, cache event, transfer, or concurrent schedule was run.

BCM2708 USB OTG AbortIO caller cross-check: enumerated every selected `psdAbortPipe` call in `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c`, following its synthetic abort request through the hardware task to the HCD AbortIO result. Poseidon’s abort helper waits only for the abort command, but each selected caller then waits on the original pipe before reuse/free; `psdFreePipe` also enforces abort-and-wait for a still-pending request. Thus the HCD’s `-1` for an active channel does not by itself establish request lifetime loss in these callers. No new finding; no USB hardware or transfer was run.

USB HID failed-worker-construction follow-up (historical OD2246; restored as OD3564/OD3565 on 2026-10-17): rechecked the selected keyboard and mouse constructors against `NewAddTask`, `Exec_InitETask` and `PrepareContext`. Each stores `t` after ignoring the return; `InitETask` can fail at its own ETask allocation, and `NewAddTask` also returns NULL on context failure. Neither failed path launches the task, so its caller-built `tc_MemEntry` allocations have no RemTask owner; subsequent reports signal the stored unlaunched task. This is separate from OD2186's successful launch followed by an early worker exit before publication. No allocation failure or report was induced.

OD2244 RISC-V callback publication recheck (2026-10-09): traced DW UART unit construction through hardware interrupt enable, callback installation, and serial.device UnitList insertion (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:153-195,271-281`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:170-184`). The callback findUnit can return NULL between callback installation and list insertion; its nonempty receive path then accesses SU in the general-buffer branch (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-31,96-108`). The ordering and conditional fault in OD2244 are source-confirmed; no UART event was run.

OD2212 queue-lock initialization recheck (2026-10-09): the new unit allocation uses `MEMF_CLEAR`; both embedded queue ports are then explicitly memset to zero before list initialization (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:148-165`). `SPINLOCK_UNLOCKED` is defined as zero (`compiler/include/aros/types/spinlock_s.h:52`), so no separate uninitialized `mp_SpinLock` issue is added. `BeginIO` still queues through `PutMsg` while `AbortIO` performs an unlocked raw `Remove`; the concurrent SMP list-mutation finding remains.

OD2251 SMP private serial-queue recheck (2026-10-09): compared each selected USB serial device's BeginIO/AbortIO with its worker queue operations. PL2303 uses BeginIO AddTail and AbortIO Remove (`serialpl2303/dev.c:254-281,363-405`) against worker Remove/AddHead/drain (`serialpl2303.class.c:746-761,822-890`). CP210x uses corresponding device lines `:255-282,364-405` and worker lines `serialcp210x.class.c:638-768`; CDC ACM uses device `:254-281,363-404` and worker `cdcacm.class.c:807-951`; Palm PDA uses device `:304-331,427-468` and worker `palmpda.class.c:621-758`. Each relies on Forbid rather than a shared queue lock. Exec's Forbid documentation states its EXECSMP processor-local behavior (`rom/exec/forbid.c:39-52`). These drivers are included by `kernel-usb-classes-common` and the complete `kernel-usb-classes` aggregate (`rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:8-38`); disk-based `kernel-usb` and the Sam440 route select that aggregate (`rom/usb/mmakefile.src:4-12,53-55`; `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:66`). The finding remains conditional on an EXECSMP build. No runtime interleaving was exercised.


OD1925 withdrawn after selected request-contract recheck: `CopyGroupToEnt`'s `mem` loop advances until it points at the caller's NULL terminator; the final assignment writes NULL to that same slot, so valid writable input is unchanged. The public CMD_WRITE contract identifies an input record but does not promise acceptance of read-only storage, and the checked-in tree has no group CMD_WRITE caller. No fault on invalid buffer permissions is retained as a candidate.


Netinfo long-record read overflow follow-up (OD2261): traced direct password and group `CMD_WRITE` requests through their copy-in methods and `WriteCmd`, then sequential `CMD_READ` through `ReadCmd` and both copy-out methods. The full ULONG length controls allocation and string copies, while the stored UWORD lengths control `io_Actual` and the output-size tests. Thus a stored record with more than 65,535 aggregate string bytes can be copied beyond a read buffer sized to the advertised length. The optional device's in-tree usergroup wrapper has no password or group writer; this remains a public direct-device-client condition. Promoted to detailed OD2261; no request was issued.


Netinfo duplicate-membership caller follow-up (OD2262): traced repeated tokens preserved by ParseGroup/GetGroups into `initgroups` compaction, its `NGROUPS` clamp, and `setgroups`' verbatim credential copy. A duplicate in an early group plus 30 later distinct supplementary memberships and a distinct base GID yields 32 supplementary entries for 31 distinct memberships; the final distinct group is truncated despite fitting if the duplicate were collapsed. Promoted the former OD1921 candidate to OD2262; no credentials or database were changed.


Netinfo oversized sequential passwd/group caller follow-up (OD2263): confirmed `ug_OpenUnit` always supplies the 1,024-byte `MAXLINELENGTH` result buffer; both `getpwent` and `getgrent` set the unit cursor only on first iteration and retain `setent_done` after a failed `CMD_READ`. A valid many-member group expands beyond the result capacity through its pointer array; a valid 1,019-byte password line with a 1,000-byte GECOS value expands to about 1,063 bytes on 64-bit or 1,043 on 32-bit after adding the `NetInfoPasswd` structure. `ReadCmd` advances the cursor before copy-out, so either error skips that entry on the next call. `initgroups` uses `NI_MEMBERS`, so it is unaffected. Promoted OD1904 to detailed OD2263; no database or request was run.


IntelPro100 synchronization follow-up (OD2228): `DevBeginIO` either runs `ServiceRequest` under `unit->access_lock` or queues the request for UnitTask, which obtains the same semaphore before dispatch (`device.c:432-453`; `unit.c:1823-1830`; `request.c:154-234`). This serializes request-side tracker and multicast list changes with each other, but `RXInt` never obtains that semaphore. `DevAbortIO` also bypasses it, using only local `Disable` while unlinking and replying a pending read (`device.c:479-490`); RXInt directly traverses the opener and pending-read lists and dereferences entries (`unit.c:1013-1114`). Thus the ordinary request serialization does not protect the receive interrupt from cross-CPU AbortIO or opener/filter/tracker lifetime changes on ExecSMP; Exec documents Disable as local-CPU only (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), so the reply can let a client reclaim an IOReq while RXInt still reads it or CopyPacket writes it. OD2228 remains supported. No request or interrupt was run.
OD2194 serialization recheck: the event and port-change handlers run in separate spawned subtasks (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:4148-4156`). Disconnect takes `xhc_DevLock`, but none of the three scheduler families or `xhciActivateEndpointTransfer` acquires it. In the null-ring case, the helper removes and replies before control/bulk can reply again or interrupt/isoch can requeue the replied request. No transfer or disconnect was run.

### MinGW WINGDI selected target reconciliation

The MinGW boot target sets `MINGW32_HIDD := wingdi`; its active link dependency includes `kernel-hidd-wingdi-kobj`. That target selects the WINGDI module, its native host DLL and the GDI monitor program through the module manifest and active `#MM` edges (`arch/all-mingw32/boot/mmakefile.src:10-33`; `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/mmakefile.src:4-18,31-42`). The GDI monitor in turn selects an icon target using `AROS_TARGET_ICONSET`; configure defaults that variable to Gorilla (`configure.in:3089-3092`), so the Gorilla icon manifest and its two inputs are conditionally selected in the default configuration. Other configured icon-set names have not been reconciled for this monitor. This directory was missing from the previous inventory. The rows below add all eight selected C bodies, seven local headers, two manifests, the module definition and selected resource/icon inputs. Only the IRQ failure/cleanup slices of the keyboard and mouse bodies have been reviewed here; other body and caller checks remain open.

| File | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/mmakefile.src` | Selected module/native/monitor manifest reconciled | `FILES` selects six module C bodies; the active target edges also select `gdi_native.c`, `wingdi.rc`, and the `disk_startup.c` GDI monitor program. |
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi.conf` | Generated HIDD method ABI checked against genmodule and selected class bodies | The five configured classes/interfaces were matched to `tools/genmodule/config.c:2081-2249`, `oopsupport.c:65-123`, and their selected implementations; no configured-method/dispatcher mismatch found. `HIDD_WINGDI_USEFRIEND` is not defined by the selected module manifest, so the stale friend-attribute macro reference remains in an inactive block. Cursor-shape allocation arithmetic is tracked as an open bounds/caller question below, not credited as a finding yet. |
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/startup.c` | Full startup body read against root-class construction, registration, display creation and teardown callers | OD2272 covers legacy input registration signatures; OD2284 covers unchecked keyboard/mouse hardware-root creation. OD2286 covers initial display construction failing after `displaynum` increments, then the disk launcher under-creating the configured display count. `OOP_FindClass(CLID_Hidd_BitMap)` is a required target superclass and no separate null-class issue was established. Input-root objects are subsystem singletons, so startup does not own their disposal. The ignored initial `AddDisplayDriver` result is covered by OD2286. Host-library/module teardown and external callers remain open. |
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi_hostlib.c` | Full init/load/rollback/expunge body checked against generic module initializer and hostlib resource implementation | OD2292: after successful host-library load, a later `gdi_Startup` failure invokes expunge, which omits the User32 interface and handle. OD2293: partial host-library init locally drops/closes GDI (and possibly User32) then returns FALSE; generic init rollback invokes expunge and repeats the GDI interface drop/close because globals were not cleared. A failed GDI symbol-array allocation also leaves the already-closed handle in the global output slot for a second close during rollback. Host DLL export-failure behavior was traced; no DLL or allocation failure was induced. |
WinGDI disposer unmatched-Forbid pass (OD4004 added, 2026-10-19): traced `GDICl__Root__Dispose` and both selected teardown paths (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi_hiddclass.c:336-355,303-329`; `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:123-156`). The disposer calls `Forbid()` without `Permit()`; its constructor rollback and graphics startup rollback return to ordinary code with the nesting still active. Exec documents the matching-call requirement and scheduler effect (`rom/exec/forbid.c:35-60`; `permit.c:34-51`). Added OD4004. The source path was inspected; no allocation failure or rollback was induced. This reuses already credited Wingdi source and adds no line credit.
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi_hiddclass.c` | Graphics/display method bodies and selected HIDD callers inspected; OD4004 records unmatched Forbid in Root::Dispose; remaining contracts pending | OD2283: cursor replacement destroys an old cursor without synchronizing with the native WM_SETCURSOR callback. OD2286: `displaynum` increments before paired display-HIDD construction succeeds, affecting the later launcher count on allocation failure. OD2281 traces the first-display message-post handshake. Traced `DisplayDefault` through `driver_Setup` and WINGDI multi-display startup: graphics.library queries each new instance immediately after construction, so the class-static display pointer overwrite does not establish a selected registration error; later external attribute queries remain unverified. Reviewed bitmap copying, display list updates, cursor conversion, mode properties and GDI teardown. `ShowList` waits while forbidden; Exec `Wait` explicitly breaks/restores Forbid, so that alone is not a deadlock. Other display concurrency, bitmap lifetime and selected caller contracts remain open. |
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi_bitmapclass.c` | Full method body reviewed; external method callers remain pending | OD3355 covers unchecked readback/setup failure (the former OD2273 reference was absent from the detailed report and this concrete path is now recorded under OD3355); OD2274 covers asynchronous window close before DC/object release; OD2280 covers negative image dimensions wrapping scratch allocation sizes before unsigned conversion. Caller census: public WritePixelArray/ScalePixelArray dimensions are UWORD, and CopyBoxMasked forwards UWORD width/height; these selected in-tree routes do not establish negative sizes. The graphics.library BltBitMap route has signed sizes but clips and returns when either is nonpositive before the HIDD call (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:147-184). The HIDD method declaration itself uses signed WORD dimensions (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:545`), and no complete inventory of external OOP clients is available, so OD2280 remains a conditional contract-level candidate pending broader callers. New/dispose ownership, root attributes, draw modes, pixel operations, image conversion and update paths read. External bounds and caller contracts remain open. |
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi_kbdclass.c` | Full keyboard HIDD body and selected event callers inspected; broader lifecycle contracts pending | The MinGW32 WinGDI failed IRQ-node cleanup route is consolidated under current kernel finding EK09; no separate driver root finding is tracked. OD2290 follows the selected native focus-loss event into a single synthesized key release; keyboard.device clears only that key’s modifier bit, so an earlier modifier can remain latched. If the most recent key is released first, `last_key` becomes zero and focus loss sends no release for the still-held modifier. OD2279: IRQ handler is enabled before callback/context fields are initialized; qualify trigger to later driver-object creation while a display is active, since selected startup creates these objects before AddDisplayDriver. No in-tree re-add caller found. The callback chooses the extended table from bit 8, masks the scan code and bounds-checks before indexing; keyup prefix handling traced. Literal keypad mappings match selected i8042/Linux tables and legacy keymap entries. Callback and teardown contracts remain open. |
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi_mouseclass.c` | Full mouse HIDD body and selected native event callers inspected; broader lifecycle contracts pending | The MinGW32 WinGDI failed IRQ-node cleanup route is consolidated under current kernel finding EK09; no separate driver root finding is tracked. OD2291 traces focus loss with a held mouse button: native events are filtered while inactive, but the HIDD button mask persists and can suppress the first same-button press after refocus. OD2279: IRQ handler is enabled before callback/context fields are initialized; qualify trigger to later driver-object creation while a display is active, since selected startup creates these objects before AddDisplayDriver. No in-tree re-add caller found. Button, motion and wheel callbacks were traced; wheel narrowing preserves the signed delta on the selected Windows target. Windows XBUTTON1/2 messages are not translated, but the shared mouse HIDD exposes only Button1–Button3 (`rom/hidds/mouse/include/mouse.h:75-80`), so no fourth/fifth-button defect is established. The shared mouse proxy wrapper, event structure conversion and input-subsystem push path were traced through `rom/hidds/mouse/{driverdata,subsystem}.c`; each WINGDI event is copied with the appropriate relative-coordinate flag before dispatch, and no additional selected-caller defect was established. Remaining direct external callback and teardown contracts are open.  OD2295 follows concurrent `AddDriver` calls through generic hardware registration: its list lock is taken only after object construction, so both WINGDI constructors can pass the singleton check, add IRQ callbacks and overwrite `mousehidd`; normal startup creates one and no in-tree concurrent re-add caller was found. |
| `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi_native.c` | Full 473-line body, native callbacks, window creation, worker dispatch, IRQ setup/rollback and selected show/teardown callers inspected; remaining platform lifecycle checks pending | OD2274: bitmap callback reads raw `bitmap_data` from window userdata without teardown drain. OD2276: hook callback resides in `wingdi.dll`, but setup supplies the executable module handle and ignores failure; x86_64 has no key-message fallback. Former OD11103 candidate withdrawn: `KrnAllocSystemIRQ()` only returns free slots 2–255 after core initialization reserves 0 and 1; each cleanup call is reached only after the corresponding GDI field was assigned a successful allocation. OD2278: failed kernel IRQ-handler registration or later selected gdi_Startup failure posts quit and releases worker-owned state without joining the host thread; ordinary expunge has the same unsafe teardown, but its caller reachability is unconfirmed because startup retains an open reference. OD2272 supplies the selected startup failure path. OD2281: first display `PostThreadMessage` can beat the worker’s first User/GDI call, `SetWindowsHookEx`, and leave ShowList blocked waiting forever. Cursor conversion reviewed; OD2283 covers replacement versus callback lifetime. OD2290 covers focus loss while multiple host keys remain down; this path emits only one synthetic release using the last keydown. OD2291 follows the same deactivation path into mouse-message filtering; no mouse release or button-state reset is sent. Rechecked the native ack handoff against the selected keyboard and mouse handlers: both copy the event fields they consume before calling GDI_KbdAck/GDI_MouseAck, so the host may safely publish its next event before the callback finishes; no overwrite candidate retained. OD2281 is narrowed to a first display post before the worker reaches SetWindowsHookEx, its first User/GDI call. OD2348: traced `graphics.library/LoadView` through `ShowViewPorts` support detection, `ShowList` wait, `NOTY_SHOW` and `ShowDone`; host window creation failures are skipped but still signal completion, so a viewport remains blank until a later load retries it. The HIDD method returns TRUE as a support indicator, not an operation-success result. Other callbacks, userdata/show order and thread exit behavior reviewed; no additional issue established in those slices. |

OD2286 follows the selected default Gorilla `DISPLAYS=1` path after a failed initial construction that already incremented `displaynum`. Icon/CLI launch and cleanup paths otherwise traced; downstream display lifecycle remains open. |

IntelPro100 RX length follow-up: `CopyPacket` reads Ethernet addresses before validating the receive length and subtracts the 14-byte header into a `UWORD` for cooked reads (`workbench/devs/networks/intelpro100/unit.c:1195-1225`). The selected configuration sets `PROCB_CF1F_DISCARDRUNTS` (`unit.c:96-100`; flag definition `intelpro100.h:271-276`), but source does not establish whether every frame shorter than the Ethernet header is excluded from the `PROCB_CONTROLF_OK` path. No additional finding is promoted without that controller status contract. No packet was received; source-only.

USBDevice Configure follow-up: full implementation and selected HID/MassStorage callers rechecked. OD2324 traces a failed SET_CONFIGURATION transfer: `Configure` ignores the false return, publishes `dev->config` and interface state, and returns success; both selected class constructors ignore that return and continue. No device or transfer was run.

IntelPro100 embedded read-port initialization recheck (OD2228; no new finding): `DevOpen` allocates each `Opener` with `MEMF_CLEAR`, then initializes `read_port.mp_MsgList` and sets `mp_Flags = PA_IGNORE` without calling `InitMsgPort` (`workbench/devs/networks/intelpro100/device.c:292-302`). On the selected ExecSMP ABI the omitted `mp_SpinLock` and owner fields therefore begin zero; `KrnSpinInit` defines unlocked as zero and clears `s_Owner` (`compiler/include/aros/types/spinlock_s.h:47-54`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/spininit.c:18-34`). `PutRequest` uses `PutMsg`, whose queue insertion acquires that port lock (`request.c:1194-1199`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-94`). This does not establish an uninitialized-lock defect. RXInt still traverses/removes these message nodes without that port lock, and DevAbortIO only disables its local CPU, so OD2228 remains supported. No packet or abort was run.

Linux input reader-start failure caller recheck (OD2258/OD856/OD866; no new finding): a failed `create_inputtask` leaves `eh->inputtask == NULL`, but `Init_Hidd` still returns TRUE and priority-10 `LinuxInput_Startup` attempts both HIDD registrations and sets `lib_OpenCnt = 1` (`linuxinput_init.c:151-160`; `startup.c:19-35`). There is no retry or per-node removal. If `Expunge_Hidd` is nevertheless invoked, it passes each handler to `Kill_LinuxInput_inputtask`, which unconditionally calls `Signal(eh->inputtask, ...)`; the selected Exec `Signal` path dereferences `task` without a null check (`linuxinput_init.c:163-171`; `linuxinput_inputtask.c:242-246`; `rom/exec/signal.c:158-172`). The startup pin blocks ordinary final-close expunge, so this is limited to forced or failed-init rollback paths and overlaps OD856/OD866 rather than adding a separate finding. No task failure or expunge was induced.

Audio last-close handoff recheck (OD2033 promoted): confirmed the worker's `_CMD_CLOSE` frees ETASK and `et_portunits` before signaling, then `TaskBody` checks `io_Command` from the caller's request. `audio_CLOSE` restores the saved command immediately after that signal. On ExecSMP those operations can run concurrently; if restoration wins, the worker misses the exit check and loops through the freed ETASK/port. The slave priority is 127, so this finding's concrete overlap is cross-CPU rather than ordinary lower-priority preemption on UP. Distinct from OD2133's AHI ReplyMsg publication window, OD1880 and OD1189. No close interleaving was run.

Audio request-drain close recheck (no additional candidate): final `DevClose` sends `ADCMD_FREE` for all four unit bits and waits before calling `FreeSLAVE` (`workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:169-195`). `_ADCMD_FREE` routes each matching allocation through `ResetUnit`; that nulls the cached request and calls `FlushUnit`, which aborts/waits for active AHI I/O and replies to each queued CMD_WRITE and ADCMD_WAITCYCLE (`audio_commands.c:526-568,371-400,456-460`). Thus those per-unit work lists are drained in the ordinary serialized close path before `free_ETask`; no separate queued-list leak is credited from `free_EUnit` deleting the lists' containing unit. Overlapping external I/O with final close remains subject to client/device synchronization contracts and was not tested.

LPe32002 scheduler private-port allocation follow-up (OD2326): confirmed `CreateMsgPort` can return NULL when its memory or signal allocation fails (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:48-74`). The worker ignores both `reply_port` and `input` results (`workbench/devs/networks/lpe32002/unit.c:501-504`); its startup handshake precedes `WaitPort(reply_port)` and the `input->mp_SigBit` wait-mask construction (`:518-544`). The creator replies to the handshake and returns the unit (`:787-798`), while the worker has no corresponding post-handshake failure reply or cleanup. This is distinct from OD2074, where failures before the handshake leave the creator waiting forever, and from OD2073, where shutdown races worker initialization/teardown. No allocation failure or worker fault was induced.

USB configuration descriptor error-path recheck (OD2327, 2026-10-09): verified `GetDescriptor` returns the control-transfer Boolean directly (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbdeviceclass.c:267-280`); Configure ignores the short-header result, then ignores exhaustion of the three full-descriptor retries and reads descriptor fields from the pool allocation (`:531-575`). `AllocVecPooled` does not clear memory itself, but this stack creates its pool with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usb_init.c:122`; `rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:35-84`), so an all-failed full-descriptor fetch leaves zero fields. Configure still ignores failed `set_config`, stores `config == USB_UNCONFIG_NO` with no interfaces but returns TRUE (`usb_core.h:449`). The unchecked short-header read into stack `cd` remains a separate, qualified error path. Followed Configure into selected HID, hub and MassStorage construction (`hidclass.c:247-250`, `usbhubclass.c:127-143`, `MassStorage/storageclass.c:161-164`) and confirmed HID/MassStorage proceed without checking its result. Added OD2327 as distinct from OD2324: 2324 is a successfully fetched descriptor followed by a rejected SET_CONFIGURATION; 2327 is a failed descriptor fetch whose data is still parsed and published. No USB device or transfer was run.

Audio `ADCMD_PERVOL` maximum-period recheck (OD2325, 2026-10-09): traced the public `IOAudio.ioa_Period` field as UWORD (`compiler/include/devices/audio.h:45-53`), the selected dispatcher (`workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:96-99`; `audio_commands.c:1460-1477`), allocation-key validation and per-channel worker (`audio_commands.c:1415-1436`), and the frequency conversion (`:295-299`). The valid maximum of 65,536 Paula cycles has a zero 16-bit encoding; the checked m68k backend writes the period field directly to the 16-bit period register (`arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:362-390`; `audio_hardware.c:55-62`), while selected non-m68k AHI configurations pass the zero field into C division. `UnitCopyData` normalizes low periods but `UnitAHIPerVol` does not. The audio manifest selects this replacement for i386, x86_64, PPC and ARM while explicitly excluding m68k (`workbench/devs/audio/mmakefile.src:4-16`). Existing trigger and configuration scope remain supported; no request or hardware was exercised.


USB interface-table allocation error-path recheck (OD2328, 2026-10-09): confirmed `AllocVecPooled` may return NULL (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:25-36`) and Configure leaves the failure branch empty before publishing the descriptor and iterating `bNumInterface` (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbdeviceclass.c:556-568`). The first operation in `fill_iface` forms an `InterfaceData *` from `dev->interfaces[ifaceidx]` and later writes members through it (`:419-440`), so any nonzero interface count and failed table allocation reaches a null-base access. This is independent of OD2327's failed descriptor-fetch false success; OD2327 has zero interfaces under the selected clear pool, while OD2328 requires a successfully fetched descriptor with at least one interface. Selected Sam440 USB module inclusion is documented at `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:51`. No allocation failure or enumeration was run.


USB partial-interface failure ownership recheck (OD2329, 2026-10-09): traced `Configure`'s ascending interface loop and rollback (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbdeviceclass.c:563-575`): failure at index 1 or later frees endpoint arrays for completed earlier interfaces through `free_iface`, but `free_iface` does not clear the endpoint pointer (`:481-488`). `dev->config` and the interface table remain published. The selected HID constructor ignores Configure's Boolean result and then calls `GetEndpoint` (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:244-247,295-299`); GetEndpoint accepts the retained nonzero config and dereferences the freed array (`usbdeviceclass.c:597-615`). This supports a conditional UAF for a later interface failure after a prior interface with endpoints was populated, distinct from OD2328's null table on allocation failure. Sam440 selects the USB stack and HID class through its boot aggregate. No enumeration or allocation failure was run.

Console paste-source lifetime recheck (OD2306/OD806; no additional candidate): exact in-tree `con_inject` call sites are SnipMap paste and the standard console's two stack-built status replies (`rom/devs/console/snipmapconclass.c:88-96`; `stdconclass.c:763-779`). SnipMap holds `copyBufferLock` while `con_inject` copies the selected buffer into its separately allocated paste node; `SetConSnip` and `GetConSnip` use that same lock (`setconsnip.c:17-43`; `getconsnip.c:17-28`). The stack-built replies are copied synchronously before their methods return. During keyboard paste, the console worker already holds `consoleTaskLock`; recursive obtain is supported by Exec's same-owner semaphore path (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:102-112`), so `con_inject`'s nested acquire does not deadlock. These checks support OD2306's remaining-paste-on-unit-close leak and do not establish a borrowed source-buffer lifetime defect. No paste was injected.

Speechcore API boundary recheck (no new candidate): reread `SCTranslateWith`'s size_t-to-`long` remaining counter and embedded-NUL handling against both selected callers. `translator.library` rejects negative `LONG inputLength` before conversion (`workbench/libs/translator/translate.c:28-47`), limiting that public path to `LONG_MAX`; `speech.device` additionally caps `io_Length` at 65,535 before calling the core (`workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:315-330`). This closes the large-length signed-counter concern for selected callers. The text device validates UTF-8 over the explicit byte length, then the legacy translator treats NUL as end-of-input; because the v1 README does not state whether embedded U+0000 is supported, no partial-input/success finding is credited. `SCSynthWith` validates caller pointers and parameter ranges, and selected narrator/speech/Say sinks supply allocation and release callbacks; sentence storage checks its frame-size multiplication before allocation (`workbench/libs/speechcore/synth.c:229-289`; `synth_frames.c:116-143`). No translation or synthesis was run.

OpenSBI timer BeginIO request-class caller recheck (OD1416/OD1424, no new finding): followed `arch/riscv64-opensbi/timer/beginio.c` through common BeginIO and `Timer0Setup`. The override only re-arms after `common_BeginIO` reports a newly inserted head; `TR_ADDREQUEST` uses the shared MICROHZ/VBLANK queues and the unsupported EClock/WaitEClock requests take OD1416's unqueued, unreplied error path. `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` takes OD1424's successful-but-unreplied path. A source census found in-tree `UNIT_ECLOCK` opens in controller/HIDD, keyboard, lowlevel and legacy network setup, but no checked-in `TR_ADDREQUEST` caller on those units; the findings remain public API triggers. The `Timer0Setup` arm-after-list-lock-release pattern was compared with the OpenSBI kernel timer descriptor: this boot currently runs only its boot hart, so the analogous PC SMP rearm race is not credited to this target. No request or timer interrupt was issued.

OpenSBI timer AbortIO deadline recheck (OD1416, no new finding; 2026-10-14): traced generic `AbortIO` removal against the ordered `UNIT_MICROHZ` queue, OpenSBI `Timer0Setup`, the recurring VBlank request, and kernel deadline handling (`rom/timer/abortio.c:62-91`; `rom/timer/lowlevel.c:188-219,264-318`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/timer/ticks.c:67-109`; `kernel/kernel_timer.c:274-286`). Aborting the queue head does not rearm the platform timer, but the already programmed deadline belongs to the removed earliest request and therefore precedes or equals the next live request. It can produce an early timer interrupt; the handler processes no not-yet-due request and then rearms from the current queue head. The selected 20 ms VBlank request also remains as the recurring MICROHZ head. No missed later deadline was established. OD1416 remains the distinct invalid-Remove path for accepted unsupported EClock-unit requests. Current kernel execution is single-hart; no abort or timer was run.

Other-driver PS3Eye lifetime recheck: OD2333 follows Poseidon device-removal binding release into the app release hook and compares it with MUI `mDispose`. The device lock serializes binding release, but MUI `mDispose` frees the same pipes before it enters that binding synchronization; the shared pointer tests/frees remain unsynchronized. Callback-data lifetime beyond this pipe race remains open. No device removal/UI overlap was run.

OD2305 is detailed in AROS-other-drivers.md: gameport allocates a GPUnit before OOP/HIDD setup and leaks it on every subsequent failed Open because Exec does not call Close for failed opens. The selected input.device caller alerts and does not retry; repeat accumulation requires a direct caller retry. OD1192 remains a separate OOP attribute-reference imbalance. No failure or repeated open was induced.

OD1007 is detailed in AROS-other-drivers.md: keyboard.device and gameport.device call ReplyMsg before storing IOERR_ABORTED. Exec enqueues the reply and signals its owner before returning; on ExecSMP a different shared-port consumer can observe the prior status. No selected in-tree shared-port consumer was found, and no abort was run.

Serial OD2330 contract qualification: reread the public `IOExtSer` declaration (`compiler/include/devices/serial.h:22-36`) and searched checked-in `CMD_READ` clients. The header does not specify `io_Length == -1`, and no in-tree submitter was found. The selected `PORT:` handler forwards a signed DOS `Read` length unchanged, so a negative value could reach the branch, but DOS describes the argument as a byte count and does not document negative lengths as supported. Whether external clients rely on the serial convention remains unverified. OD2330 remains a source-supported conditional behavior candidate; external API contract/reachability is open.

Graphics/Desktop caller triage (GD2716): traced AHIRecord `PrintStatus` into its callers. The `WinTexts` arguments are fixed source literals (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:131-145,1308-1382,1985-1987`); the only dynamic `Counter` is a 20-byte buffer filled from two fixed format strings and passed with a maximum-width elapsed-time value (`:882,2611-2626,2977-2981`). These selected calls cannot supply a 32,768-byte text argument, so no GD2716 trigger was added.


AHI requester text-metric caller follow-up (GD2716): caller-supplied `AHIR_PositiveText`/`AHIR_NegativeText` are retained as STRPTRs, assigned to IntuiText, and passed to IntuiTextLength while sizing the selected requester (`Device/requester.c:197-201,499-503`; public tag definitions and contract `Include/C/devices/ahi.h:258-260,1182-1189`). No length check caps these labels; the fixed default labels are separate. No requester was opened.

WINGDI `gdi_native.c` lifecycle recheck: read the full native host body and traced module expunge through `gdigfx_expunge` and host-library cleanup. `GDI_Shutdown` posts `WM_QUIT` but immediately unregisters window classes, closes the input acknowledgement events and frees all system IRQs without waiting for the host thread; the keyboard/window callbacks can still be active or waiting on those shared resources. Reconfirmed and expanded OD2278 to cover both rollback and ordinary expunge; no duplicate finding was kept. Upgraded the file row to full body/selected lifecycle review. No host event or expunge was run.


WINGDI shared-definition review: compared the full `GDI_Control` declaration and all three host function tables against native DLL writers, IRQ readers, symbol arrays and lifecycle callers. The pointer-first shared register layout has matching field offsets on the selected 32- and 64-bit MinGW ABIs. The `GDI_Init` function-table declaration omits the `volatile` pointee qualifier present in the DLL definition, but no distinct runtime defect was supported from that type mismatch, so it is recorded for visibility without a finding. No build or host call was run.


WINGDI Windows structure ABI recheck: reviewed all `winapi.h` structures against actual shim call sites and checked the installed MinGW-w64 `BITMAP` and `ICONINFO` declarations, which are outside explicit packing blocks. The local pointer-bearing declarations remain under pack(4), and `SetCursorShape` passes both directly to Windows APIs. Folded the `BITMAP` evidence into existing Graphics/Desktop finding GD2713; no duplicate OD entry retained. No cursor update was run.


WINGDI keyboard table review: read both complete scan-code tables and the selected `KbdIntHandler`. The extended bit selects the 94-entry E0 table; the low-byte scan code is checked against the matching 89/94-entry bound before indexing, and unmapped entries are `NOKEY`. No table overread or state error was supported by the source. Physical keyboard mapping remains untested.


WINGDI default resources review: read the selected `wingdi.rc` version metadata and `GDI.info.src` tooltypes, and visually inspected the 47x49 RGBA Gorilla GDI icon. The icon sets `DISPLAYS=1`/`STARTPRI=128`; no additional runtime behavior is encoded in these inputs. Non-default icon-set variants remain outside this default-target check.


WINGDI module-definition/header review: matched every Root, Hidd_Gfx, Hidd_Display and Hidd_BitMap entry in `wingdi.conf` to selected local method bodies; generated method/vector output and target composition remain unbuilt. Read all of `wingdi_bitmap.h` and its callers. The `aHidd_GDIBitMap_Window` macro refers to missing `aoHidd_GDIBitMap_Window`, but no selected source expands it, so this remains a latent header inconsistency rather than a numbered selected-path finding.

Other Drivers OD2347 withdrawal: the PC i8042 parser ignores Y/X overflow bits, but rechecking the counter semantics and the downstream motion contract did not establish a consequence beyond the delta supplied by the device. Linux's standard PS/2 parser also ignores these flags. Removed the low-evidence candidate from the detailed report and index; the i8042 packet parser remains inventoried, with hardware behavior untested.

Other Drivers OD2348 caller recheck: followed the selected graphics `LoadView` path into WINGDI `ShowViewPorts`. Corrected the finding to distinguish the support return (`TRUE`) from native operation completion: after failed parent or child `CreateWindow`, the worker still signals `ShowDone`, and the HIDD returns supported; an empty one-viewport display remains blank until a later load retries. No Win32 failure was induced.

Other Drivers OD2349 AbortIO follow-up: confirmed a caller can remove a failed interrupt request from `hc_IntXFerQueue`, but the `cmdAbortIO` queue-removal path calls `TermIO` without `xhciFreePeriodicContext`/`xhciFinishRequest`. Explicit cancellation can reply the request while leaving `hu_DevBusyReq` and `iouh_DriverPrivate1` uncleared. No transfer or abort was run.


NetInfo OD1894 process-creation failure follow-up: verified the selected `CreateNewProcTags` failure path returns `NULL` after cleanup without delivering `NP_ExitData`; `NetInfo__DevOpen` ignores the result and waits for the sole startup reply sender while holding `nid_Lock` (`netinfo.c:158-184`; `createnewproc.c:593-669`; `server.c:31-35`). Kept distinct from OD2344, where a successfully started worker faults during map cleanup before replying. No allocation or task-creation failure was induced.


NetInfo OD1905 reload-result follow-up: traced the notification path through `EntHandleNotify`, `InternalSetEnts` and the selected `getpwnam`/`getpwuid` callers. A failed reload leaves the prior entry list allocated, returns it without a reload error, and matching old records are reported as successful lookups. The finding is conditional on a previously parsed map, change notification and subsequent open/allocation failure; no reload failure was induced.


PC timer OD1427 rearm interleaving follow-up: verified that both concurrent BeginIO paths can report a new queue head, while `Timer0Setup` releases its list read lock after capturing the current deadline and before its PIT writes. A later earlier-head rearm can therefore be overwritten by the first caller's stale longer delay on the selected x86-64 PC SMP configuration. No interrupt timing or hardware was exercised.

Hosted ALSA bridge source/caller recheck (OD2381-OD2386): traced the Linux `HAVE_ALSA`/`OPT_HOST_ALSA` build path, both bridge translation units, headers, driver init/cleanup, AHI allocation, playback worker and volume callers. Added OD2381 for a failed libc load reported as bridge-init success; OD2382 for an unpublished mixer handle when the `Master` element is absent; OD2383-OD2384 for unchecked mixer and PCM parameter allocations; OD2385 for PCM setup returning success after ignored setter/commit failures; and OD2386 for non-`EPIPE` negative writes increasing frame counts and moving the worker pointer backwards. Existing host-library load and device failures were not induced; source-only.
NVMe PRP cleanup follow-up (OD2359): rechecked `nvme_initprp`’s all-exit ownership against `nvme_dma_release` and the selected I/O caller. The entry-count wrap remains the concrete omission path in OD2359’s existing driver finding; normal failure cleanup posts every recorded data/list mapping and frees the aligned-list backing allocation with its recorded `alloc_total`. The DMA-map growth loop is bounded by the <=32-bit transfer and controller page-size shift, so the reviewed transfer limits do not establish a separate capacity/size multiplication wrap. DMA backend contiguity guarantees and hardware behavior remain pending; no I/O was run.
Bluetooth HCI device queue-abort recheck (OD1360): reread `devAbortIO` against the selected `bluetooth.class.c` queue-to-pending handoff. The abort path protects its list/pending checks only with local `Forbid`; the worker reads the queue head, removes it, publishes the pending pointer and starts `psdSendPipe` without a matching ownership lock (`dev.c:324-369`; `bluetooth.class.c:887-900`). On SMP, AbortIO can remove/reply the request between the worker's head read and ownership publication, after which the worker can continue using the replied request. This confirms the existing shared OD1360 finding; no Bluetooth-specific duplicate. Unit queue operation was not exercised; client and Poseidon scheduling remain pending.

USB2OTG expunge/worker ownership recheck (OD2422 strengthened): reconciled the optional BCM2708 package and device manifest with LDDemon’s selected `LDFlush` path. LDDemon scans `DeviceList` and calls `RemDevice` for a non-busy device with zero open count; RemDevice invokes the generated expunge path. USB2OTG’s hook deletes the pool but does not stop its infinite WorkerTask or abort/wait/close the timer request embedded in the freed unit. The task can resume in unloaded module code and access the released unit; the request retains pointers into the pool. Reconfirmed `TASKTAG_AFFINITY` receives the address of the unit’s embedded `cpumask_t`, while ETask cleanup later calls `KrnFreeCPUMask` on non-sentinel masks. No USB2OTG-specific remover exists, but the generic selected memory-pressure sweep supplies an expunge trigger when the optional package is loaded and idle. No device, memory-pressure event, timer, or task removal was run; source-only.

AHIRecord sampling-size/callback-contract recheck (OD2226 boundary): compared `RecordFuncS` against the AHI hook documentation and selected driver contracts. AHI documents the hook as regular and possibly interrupt-context, and defines `AHIDB_MaxRecordSamples` as the per-callback sample-frame count (`workbench/devs/AHI/Docs/ahidev.html:640-650`; `Device/modeinfo.c:313-315`). `StartSampling` allocates its capture buffers using `max(RecordData.bufferlen, LevelFrames)`, where `LevelFrames` is the queried per-callback maximum (`AHIRecord.c:2088-2103,2113-2119`). HDAudio reports 1,024 frames and calls the hook with 1,024-frame blocks (`Drivers/HDAudio/DriverData.h:37`; `interrupt.c:150-172`), so a single valid HDAudio callback fits the remaining/new capture buffer even when it crosses the internal chunk boundary. No independent single-callback overwrite was established; OD2226 remains the multi-callback producer/saver ownership race when the saver lags across a completed-buffer reuse. No recording or runtime callback was run.

AHIRecord stop-caller/ownership follow-up (OD2387): traced the UI Stop action, audio-mode change, startup-failure unwind, and tool shutdown callers into `StopSampling` (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:1105-1155,1233-1255,1367-1377,2159-2224`). The routine delays five ticks, requests `AHIC_Record=FALSE`, tears down the level task, finishes the saver, and frees all three callback-owned capture/conversion buffers; it does not wait for an in-flight RecordFunc to retire. The AHI core forwards stop to the selected driver without a generic callback-drain step (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:969-1014`), and `AHI_FreeAudio` likewise calls the driver Stop before FreeAudio (`:702-729`). This connects AHIRecord's buffer lifetime to HDAudio OD2387's queued soft-interrupt/callback race; it does not establish an independent app finding because the concrete unsynchronized callback lifetime is in the HDAudio Stop implementation. No runtime audio was used.


Serial CMD_RESET active-write backend follow-up (OD2388): rechecked that the reset branch's local `Disable` only masks local interrupts, clears the status flag, replies `su_ActiveWrite`, and then falls through to drain queued requests; it neither nulls the active pointer nor calls HIDD Stop (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:567-648`). The selected PC HIDD enables `UART_IER_THRI` during unit construction (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:229`), and its THRI branch calls `serialunit_write_more_data` whenever the UART reports THRI (`:726-731`). The selected m68k HIDD registers a persistent TBE server that invokes the saved callback (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/serial/SerialUnitClass.c:90-105,132-139`). The serial write-empty callback consumes `su_ActiveWrite` and does not test `STATUS_WRITES_PENDING` before resuming or replying it (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:137-184`). This confirms the selected backend callback reachability after reset; no in-tree client reset sequence or hardware timing was required for the code-level state inconsistency, and no I/O was run.


AHI DSP echo lifecycle follow-up (2026-10-11): added OD136 after checking the selected defaults (`MixFreq=44100`, minimum player rate `50`, `MaxBuffSamples=882`) and choosing public delay `0x3ffffc8e`; the sum reaches `0x40000000` and the four-byte sample-size product wraps to zero, while the destination offset becomes `0xfffff238`. Added OD137 after tracing both echo replacement through `update_DSPEcho` and active-effect teardown through `_AHI_FreeAudio`; neither path frees all separately allocated echo state. Added OD1577 for the SMP cancel/mix pointer interleaving; checked the always-listed Void worker plus `AHIS_UNKNOWN` fallback, and verified its active loop invokes the AHI mixer. SimplePlay sets effects during playback but cancels after Stop, so it does not prove the cancellation race; that trigger remains available to public callers. No audio was run.


VirtIO read-only status follow-up (OD2460): `virtio_controllerclass.c:85-100` negotiates `VIRTIO_BLK_F_RO`; `virtio_hw.c:282` stores the negotiated bit in `dev_ReadOnly`; `virtio_io.c:43-46` rejects writes while read-only, but `BeginIO` returns `io_Actual=0` for every `TD_PROTSTATUS` (`:195-199`). AFS `diskWritable` and SFS `writeprotection` both treat zero as writable (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:427-432`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:103-116`). Added OD2460 for selected x86 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V VirtIO builds when RO is offered. No I/O was run.


VirtIO `TD_PROTSTATUS` convention recheck (OD2460): compared its zero return with selected AROS block-device implementations and both named filesystem consumers. Hostdisk returns boolean `UNIT_READONLY`, FDisk returns `!unit->writable`, and DiskImage returns its `WriteProtect` flag; generic trackdisk forwards its cached hardware protection status (`arch/all-hosted/devs/hostdisk/hostdisk_device.c:621-624`; `workbench/devs/fdsk_device.c:619-622`; `workbench/devs/diskimage/device/{io.c:127-130,unit.c:374-377}`; `rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:518-521`). AFS and SFS both treat zero as writable (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:427-432`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:103-116`). VirtIO's `dev_ReadOnly` is already checked to reject writes, while its status branch still returns zero. This corroborates OD2460's result convention and the conditional filesystem behavior; no additional candidate was needed. No block device was queried.


VirtIO read-only filesystem-caller extension (OD2460): added PFS3 to the selected caller trace. `GetCurrentRoot` sets `g->diskstate = ID_VALIDATED` for zero `TD_PROTSTATUS` (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/volume.c:1026-1037`); later PFS3 rejects writes only for `ID_WRITE_PROTECTED` (`:861-873`) and omits write-protected protection flags for the root entry when `g->diskstate` is wrong (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/directory.c:851-854`). This confirms the VirtIO mismatch can also suppress PFS3's read-only state. The same caller census found a separate USB MassStorage status defect, recorded in disk scope as DISK-323: `cmd_ProtStatus` reports protection only for CD-ROM device type, although SCSI MODE SENSE defines a WP bit for direct-access media (`storage_device.c:94-97`; T10 SBC-3 §6.3.1). The driver does not query or cache that state and its write path returns `TDERR_NotSpecified` after reset/retry (`:244-292,300-349`); this remains separate from VirtIO OD2460 because it is an independent class implementation outside this report’s device-driver scope; see DISK-323 in the disk report. No filesystem mount or USB device was run.

RISC-V DesignWare UART failed-handler registration (OD2464; historical candidate OD1562): verified `KrnAddIRQHandler` returns NULL for invalid source IDs or failed `IntrNode` allocation and only unmasks/link-installs a source after allocation. The unit constructor ignores that result and returns its OOP object; serial.device publishes the unit after its nonnull check. A positive, accepted DT IRQ with registration failure therefore produces a successful open without receive or write-completion interrupts. The selected driver's IRQ-zero branch remains an intentional write-only port. No hardware or allocation failure was run.

OpenSBI DesignWare UART no-IRQ write-progress follow-up (OD2465): traced FDT's absent/short interrupt property to port admission, the explicit `irq == 0` constructor branch, `HIDD_SerialUnit_Write`, serial.device's active-write bookkeeping, and the only automatic remainder/reply callback. With no registered handler or polling loop, a short HIDD write remains active and receives no automatic completion callback; the only non-interrupt callback route requires an explicit Stop/Start sequence and makes one refill attempt. Kept separate from OD2464, which requires a positive IRQ whose handler registration fails. Build selection is split: OpenSBI BSP packages dwuart, while the general Workbench graph selects serial.device (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:103-112`; `workbench/devs/serial/mmakefile.src:8-13`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:9-18`); the finding requires the module installed alongside the BSP HIDD. No UART or I/O was run.

USB `lsusb` bus-cursor claim withdrawal (2026-10-21): the prior OD2466 note incorrectly said the tool never advances the bus iterator. Re-reading `main()` shows `OOP_GetAttr(usb, aHidd_USB_Bus, &bus)` executes inside the `do` loop, passing the previous bus pointer back as the cursor; `USB::Get` advances to its successor when storage is non-NULL (`main.c:101-116`; `usbclass.c:78-91`). The nontermination claim is withdrawn. This recheck found the distinct ignored final-attribute-base failure documented as OD4291. No utility or hardware was run.

Other Drivers report integrity audit (2026-10-11): the detailed findings text contains 70 literal `…N tokens truncated…` artifacts that fuse unrelated text into finding paragraphs. Rebuilt OD2287 from the pinned source and folded the hub OnOff/Dispose call sites into that existing finding. Sixty-nine affected detailed paragraphs remain to be restored or revalidated; until then, the detailed report text and its candidate count are not fully trustworthy.
