AHCI SCSI translation and CCB exhaustion recheck (2026-10-12; confirms DISK-012/DISK-013; no duplicate OD finding): traced READ/WRITE CDB decoding through `ahci_scsi_disk_io` and `ahci_get_ccb`. The CCB getter returns NULL immediately when its free list is empty; the ATA disk SCSI path then dereferences the result, while the ATAPI path returns `IOERR_UNITBUSY`, confirming DISK-013's concurrent-slot trigger. Standard INQUIRY/READ CAPACITY still use the CDB pointer for response storage, covered by DISK-012. Also noted a separate latent READ CAPACITY(10) saturation mismatch: for a device with more than 2^32 logical blocks, the code clamps the block count to 0xFFFFFFFF and subtracts one, returning 0xFFFFFFFE rather than SBC-3's FFFFFFFF sentinel; because DISK-012 currently leaves the response in the CDB, no separate user-visible OD consequence is established. SBC-3 T10/xxxx-D §5.10.2 confirms the sentinel rule (https://t10.org/ftp/t10/document.05/05-344r0.pdf). No SCSI command or hardware was run.

PCI interrupt-vector caller census recheck (2026-10-12; no additional PCIPC MSI count/index candidate): traced every direct selected call to `ObtainVectors`, `GetVectorAttribs`, and `ReleaseVectors` found under PC device, NVMe, AHCI, xHCI, VMware SVGA, and Nouveau sources. NVMe requests a variable maximum based on CPU count but negotiates and starts exactly one I/O queue (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:272-279,320-325,360-385`), so this selected path queries only vector index 0; AHCI, xHCI, VMware SVGA and Nouveau each request exactly one vector and query index 0. This does not add a selected reproducer for OD2419/OD2420's MSI rounding/base-index cases. PCIPC `ReleaseVectors` disables messaging but does not return reserved IRQs (`pcipc_deviceclass.c:560-645`), already covered by EK810; selected xHCI removes its handler before releasing vectors (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_arospci.c:417-432`), and NVMe controller shutdown releases only when the saved legacy IRQ differs from the original PCI line (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:160-167`). The source-level census found no further direct selected vector API caller in the searched trees. Other PCI implementations and externally supplied HIDD clients remain outside this census. No hardware or teardown was exercised.

AHCI interrupt completion and recovery pass (2026-10-12; confirms OD2562, no additional candidate in this slice): read `ahci_intr`, port interrupt dispatch, TFES/DHRS handling, fatal/fail-all bookkeeping, active-slot completion, callback handoff, and saved/pending queue restart (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:2609-2712,2712-3485`). Port bitmap slots derive from the 32-bit CI/SACT register; normal software active bits are intersected with saved hardware bits before indexing the CCB array, and the TFES slot is range-checked before CCB dereference. The exceptional stopped-DHRS + TFD.ERR path forms `&ap_ccbs[CCS]` before validation and dereferences it for the bootverbose diagnostic (`:3017-3029`), confirming OD2562's bounded diagnostic candidate; the later TFES path separately validates CCS at `:2888-2893`. Lock contention disables port interrupts and queues worker handling; normal completion runs while holding the port lock, and callbacks are followed by queue restart only after slot state changes. Fatal handling intersects the captured CI/SACT mask with current active bits, then completes only cleared bits. Timeout races, command enqueue/public I/O interleavings, and target-specific reset lifecycle remain open; no hardware error or command was run. Source-only.

AHCI active-timeout and queue-interleaving pass (2026-10-12; no new candidate): traced `ahci_issue_pending_commands`, activation-time callout setup, poll timeout handling, MPSAFE timeout callback signaling, port-worker timeout processing, completion cancellation, and saved-command restart (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:2220-2607,2683-2703,3930-3942,3952-4168,4173-4204`). Ordinary callouts start only after a CCB transitions from pending to on-chip, matching the stated timeout accounting rule; polling passes a non-NULL timeout callback in the selected `ahci_poll` callers (the earlier caller census remains applicable). Deferred on-chip timeouts set `ap_expired` and wait if stopping would race non-expired hardware work; the worker later removes expired CCBs under the port lock, updates active masks, restarts saved commands and re-enters nonblocking completion. Pending CCBs have no armed callout, so `ATA_S_PENDING` handling in the callout timeout routine is not reached through ordinary activation. Existing DISK-109 recovery ownership and DISK-127 pending-command scheduling findings remain distinct; no further timeout defect was established in this slice. Adjacent public-I/O concurrency, hard-reset caller lifecycle and remaining AHCI core paths are still open. Source-only; no timeout or hardware was run.


EMAC MAL allocation failure recheck (2026-10-15; OD929 restored from historical OD2407 alias): traced `AllocPooled`/`AllocVecPooled` failure returns through slab/ring initialization and unconditional MAL register programming (`mal.c:105-180`; `allocpooled.c:42-53`). The shared buffer can yield invalid descriptor buffer addresses; a failed ring is dereferenced during its fill loop. No fault injection or hardware was run.

EMAC MAL interrupt-registration failure recheck (2026-10-15; OD928 restored to linked report): followed all five MAL vector registrations through generic `KrnAddIRQHandler`, MAL status handling, EMAC Init, and unit start (`workbench/devs/networks/emac/mal.c:36-58,76-103,160-180`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:75-115`; `emac_init.c:53-64`). A failed interrupt-node allocation returns NULL, but no result is checked and the MAL controller and device units still start. The RXEOB handler is the only selected path that acknowledges EOB and drains RX descriptors; its absence leaves receive progress stalled. A missing TXEOB handler also skips status clearing. This is independent of OD2407's unchecked DMA/ring memory allocations. Target/package qualification remains as in OD2407: optional Sam440 target, module package edges commented out. No allocation failure, IRQ or hardware was induced. Source-only.
EMAC MAL IRQ-range qualification follow-up (2026-10-12): checked the two `GetPVR` branches against the Sam440 header and selected kernel manifest. Sam440 MAL IDs are 10-14; the PPC460EX UIC2 MAL IDs are 67-71 (`arch/ppc-sam440/include/asm/amcc440.h:372-377,506-517`), within the generic helper's `HW_IRQ_COUNT` range for this target (`rom/kernel/kernel_base.h:50-56`; `addirqhandler.c:79-115`). Therefore OD2579's confirmed NULL-return trigger is interrupt-node `AllocMem` failure, not an invalid platform vector. The Sam440 manifest selects the generic `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c` implementation; its local `intr.c` does not replace registration. No target build or allocation failure was run.


EMAC MAL RX-channel dispatch trace (2026-10-12; OD2580 added): followed both RX EOB status bits through `MALIRQHandler`/`MALMRE` into per-unit descriptor processing (`workbench/devs/networks/emac/mal.c:30-58`; `emac_unit.c:394-420,836-889`). The channel-1 bit is acknowledged, but both branches call `rx_int` for unit 0; unit 1 is explicitly assigned RX channel 1 and has its own `eu_LastRXSlot`. Consequently unit 1's receive ring is not drained through this handler. This elaborates the existing coverage note “second-channel dispatch (589)” into detailed OD2580. No receive event was run. Source-only.


NVMe I/O IRQ-registration failure trace (2026-10-12; OD2581 added): traced the I/O queue setup through `AddIntServer`, queue-count publication, `nvme_io` submission polling, CQ completion hook and worker signal (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:63-110,438-448`; `nvme_io.c:124-131,164-191`; `rom/exec/addintserver.c:64-67`; selected PC helper `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-110`). Registration is void and stores a nullable `KrnAddIRQHandler` token, yet `queuecnt` increments regardless; after 4,096 CQ polls, a later completion depends on the interrupt path to process and signal it. The selected queue can therefore strand a request after handler allocation failure until a later I/O submission happens to poll and drain the same CQ; subsequent submissions may incidentally rescue it, so this is not an unconditional permanent stall. This is separate from controller-level AddInterrupt failure handling in OD2365. No allocation failure, I/O or hardware was induced. Source-only.


EMAC MAC interrupt callback follow-up (2026-10-12; OD2582 added): traced `EMAC_Start` enable mask and per-unit `KrnAddIRQHandler` registration into `EMACIRQHandler`. The enabled error causes are PTLE/BFCS/ORE/IRE and conditionally SYE; the callback only emits a debug message, while MAL has separate DMA status handling. Recorded the dropped MAC status/error-event handling and lack of ISR acknowledgement in OD2582. MetaMake scope semantics and EMAC board-target correction (2026-10-12): confirmed in `tools/MetaMake/dirnode.c:126-197` that `#MM-` sets `FLAG_VIRTUAL` and contributes dependencies; `##MM-` lines are ignored. Reconciled EMAC findings OD2407-OD2416, OD2423, OD2579, OD2580 and OD2582 plus the associated source and caller notes: `AROS-sam440-ppc` actively depends on `workbench-complete`, `workbench-devs-networks-emac-powerpc` and `aros-tcpip-apps` through `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:4-10`; the architecture target merges `kernel-sam440-ppc` and `software-sam440-ppc`, which brings in `workbench-sam440-ppc` (`arch/ppc-sam440/mmakefile.src:10-15`). Thus EMAC and AROSTCP are selected when that board target is built, even though EMAC is absent from the generic `workbench-devs-networks` aggregate. The PC/shared-port WaitIO source trace is also confirmed against `audio_commands.c:789-805,976-999,1047-1112` and AHI's `TermIO` reply (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:256-292`): the four eaudio channel requests use the single `et_portahi` reply port; AHI can enqueue channel completions there while `FlushUnit` waits on one request. `workbench/devs/audio/mmakefile.src:4-15` reaches eaudio from the full Workbench aggregate on its listed i386, x86_64, ppc and arm targets. No interrupt, build or runtime interleaving was exercised.

AHCI DMA allocation failure-path recheck (2026-10-12; DISK-110 confirmed, no new OD candidate): followed the `ahci_dmamem_alloc` wrapper through `bus_dmamem_alloc_slab`, `bus_dmamem_alloc`, map loading, and port `nomem` cleanup (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:349-356,3740-3771`; `ahci_aros_bus.c:84-159`). Both slab `AllocVec` calls are checked and the partial slab header is freed; `bus_dmamem_alloc` returns `-ENOMEM` on slab failure; the wrapper then releases its cleared header and returns NULL, which the RFIS/command-list/table callers check and funnel through `freeport`. The remaining unchecked wrapper-header allocation (`ahci.c:3749`) is already DISK-110. The selected map-load shim invokes its callback and cannot fail. This pass found no separate later allocation-failure cleanup defect. No allocation failure or hardware was induced.

AHCI global-port bookkeeping recheck (2026-10-12; no new candidate): traced `ahci_init`'s PI scan and `sc_portmask` writes into all maintained `sc_numports`/`sc_portmask` references. `sc_numports` is assigned the final loop index but has no reader in the selected AHCI source; attach, interrupt dispatch, port startup and detach use the PI mask or indexed `sc_ports[]` array. The apparent count-versus-index mismatch therefore has no selected consumer consequence. The AROS `bus_space_subregion` implementation is an unconditional handle offset and returns success, so its error return in this loop is not an AROS trigger. No controller was run.

AHCI high-bit mask recheck (2026-10-12; OD2583 added with compiler-dependent consequence): compared every selected `1 << port/slot` bitmap operation in `ahci.c` and `ahci_attach.c` with the 32-bit PI/IS/CI/SACT fields, `AHCI_MAX_PORTS`, and the decoded NCS maximum. Valid index 31 reaches signed-int shifts in both port discovery/interrupt handling and slot active/timeout tracking. C leaves those expressions undefined for the selected i386/x86-64 base integer type. The consequence is qualified because this checkout has no selected controller/build artifact demonstrating a compiler lowering that loses the top bit. No hardware, interrupt or command was run.


EMAC Close/shared-client trigger recheck (2026-10-12; OD2408 retained with caller qualification): re-read the complete EMAC Open/Close vectors, Exec CloseDevice path, EMAC_Stop and the selected AROSTCP SANA-II opener. Open increments eu_OpenCount and commits the opener before calling unit->start; OpenDevice allows non-MINE sharing after the first nonexclusive opener (emac_init.c:119-168). Close calls unit->stop before unlink/free and never decrements the count (:171-196); EMAC_Stop clears IFF_UP, stops the shared MAL channels and resets the EMAC (emac_unit.c:177-211). AROSTCP calls OpenDevice on the configured device/unit with flags zero (workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:319-340), giving a selected shared-open route in the Sam440 image dependency (arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:4-10). No checked-in configuration establishing two simultaneous opens of one EMAC unit was found; the multi-opener trigger therefore remains conditional on duplicate interface configuration or another client. The opener-allocation failure still reaches Close after the count increment and before Start (emac_init.c:137-165). No interface was opened or hardware exercised.

EMAC MAL RX dispatch caller recheck (OD2580): verified `emac_init` creates units 0 and 1, the SANA-II Open vector accepts unit numbers through 1, and successful Open starts that unit (`emac_init.c:59-62,107-117,162-165`). `CreateUnit` binds `num` to `emb_MALRXChannels[num]`, while both RX EOB status branches still call unit 0 in `MALIRQHandler`; channel 1 therefore remains undrained on its own completion. This closes unit-1 reachability; external network-stack configuration and hardware remain untested.

Printer/PostScript close-to-segment-expunge follow-up (OD872/OD1890 scope, no new candidate): traced the selected unit CloseDevice vector through `driver.c:119-139,144-168`, `pd_Close` and `pd_DriverTask` (`:466-493,587-588,658-666`), and PostScript `ps_Close`/`PFLUSH` (`postscript.c:293-335,567-575`). The trailer calls `pd_PWrite`, whose alternating 16-byte static buffers are passed directly as the underlying request's `io_Data`; `pd_Close` then closes both backend requests before the worker replies to CMD_CLOSE, and the per-unit CloseDevice proceeds to Expunge only after that reply. This confirms OD872's async-write/last-close ordering and identifies a selected PostScript buffer whose lifetime ends with the segment expunge. It does not establish what a particular hardware backend accesses after its Close returns, so no independent segment-unload consequence is claimed. The direct per-unit multi-opener path remains OD1890; no print or device operation was run.

WINGDI generated class ABI and cursor-shape bounds follow-up (2026-10-12; no new candidate): reconciled all `.interface` method lists in `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi.conf` with genmodule parser/interface generation (`tools/genmodule/config.c:2081-2249`; `oopsupport.c:65-123`) and selected implementations in `wingdi_hiddclass.c`, `wingdi_bitmapclass.c`, `wingdi_kbdclass.c`, and `wingdi_mouseclass.c`; each configured class method has a matching implementation and class/interface identity, so no generated-dispatch mismatch was established. The header references `aoHidd_GDIBitMap_Window`, and a friend path references `aHidd_GDIBitMap_Drawable`, but the former has no selected use and the latter is behind `HIDD_WINGDI_USEFRIEND`, which the selected manifest does not define. Also traced the in-tree `ChangeExtSpriteA` cursor caller into `SetCursorShape`: the handler multiplies bitmap width and height by four in 32-bit `ULONG` before allocation (`wingdi_hiddclass.c:637-711`), but this pass did not establish a selected caller capable of presenting dimensions whose area overflows while a corresponding bitmap remains constructible. Keep this arithmetic/caller question open; no new finding is promoted. Source-only; no generated build or runtime operation was performed.

Generic I²C per-device timing follow-up (OD2585): audited `I2CDev::Root::New/Get/Set` and the full generic bus bit timing path. `HoldTime` and `RiseFallTime` are copied and reported on each device, but the transfer implementation reads only the bus instance fields; the parallel per-device timeout fields are consumed. The selected Sam440 bit-banged subclass inherits this core. No in-tree caller sets the timing overrides, so OD2585 remains conditional on an external or future client expecting per-device timing. No bus transaction was run.

Generic I²C 10-bit read-sequence follow-up (OD2586): compared `I2C_Address` and `I2C_WriteRead` against NXP UM10204 §3.1.11. Generic `Address` emits two address bytes whenever the low byte has the 10-bit `11110xx` prefix; the read phase reuses it after repeated START and emits an extra byte, while read-only sends an R header without first selecting the target using the W header and second byte. NXP specifies the repeated-start read header as the final address byte before target data. The generic bit-banged route is selected on Sam440, but no checked-in caller uses a 10-bit address. The OpenSBI DWI2C backend is 7-bit-only and is not counted as a 10-bit trigger. No I²C transaction was run.

OpenSBI DWI2C address-range follow-up (OD2587; promotes prior OD1866 coverage lead): traced both `WriteRead` and `ProbeAddress` through the shifted-address mask into `DWI2C_HWTransfer`. The mask makes the helper’s 7-bit range rejection unreachable; `0x1d0` aliases `0x68`. The selected RTC takes its value from FDT and shifts it, but no bad in-tree FDT value was found; arbitrary out-of-range public `UWORD` inputs reach the defective conversion. No bus or probe was run.

VirtIO configuration-generation follow-up (OD2589, 2026-10-12): traced the sole `virtio_hw_read_blk_config` call through controller construction and one-time unit capacity publication. The function reads `capacity`, block size and geometry without checking the common `config_generation`; the 32-bit i386-PC package selects the driver. The OASIS VirtIO 1.2 §2.5.1 requirements specify generation sampling/retry for non-atomic multi-byte config reads. Recorded the startup-only torn-snapshot candidate separately from OD2392's missed post-publication resize update. No device was run.

OpenSBI DesignWare UART failed-init attribute-base cleanup recheck (2026-10-12; no new candidate): `DWSer_Init` can return FALSE after one or both `OOP_ObtainAttrBase` calls, including absent FDT/no discovered UART (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/dwuart_init.c:173-206`). Checked generated `_set_libinit`: `initcalled` is set before initlib callbacks, so a false initlib result runs registered expunge callbacks in reverse order even when the class has `noexpunge` (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:54-69`; `dwuart_init.c:209-224`; class config `serial.conf`). `DWSer_Expunge` releases both attribute bases and zeros the globals. `OOP_ReleaseAttrBase` tolerates an absent bucket during rollback (`rom/oop/support.c:181-208`), so partial acquisition and no-device failure do not establish a retained reference here. The failed-init cleanup concern is closed; this does not address the separately tracked GD1216 unchecked attribute-base use during bucket-allocation failure. No module load was run.

OpenSBI DesignWare I²C timing/FIFO follow-up (2026-10-12; no new candidate): rechecked `DWI2C_HWCalcTiming`, `dwi2c_program` and `DWI2C_HWProbeFIFO` against their FDT inputs and transfer loops (`dwi2c_hw.c:40-60,68-138,192-254,308-352`; `dwi2c_init.c:147-155`). FIFO fields decode as depth-minus-one; an all-zero parameter word selects the configured fallback depth, while nonzero fields feed the bounded RX-command window. Compared that interpretation with the upstream DesignWare driver, which describes supported FIFO depths as 2–256 and accounts for implementations that do not implement `COMP_PARAM_1` ([Linux DesignWare I²C driver](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/i2c/busses/i2c-designware-common.c)). No distinct depth-one overrun candidate was established. The already reported OD2245 remains the timing issue: fixed standard/fast minima are used for other accepted bus-frequency values when a clock is known. No controller or bus was run.


NVMe `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` result lifetime recheck (2026-10-12; confirmed): traced the automatic `NSDSupported` array through assignment into the caller result and out of `BeginIO`, then followed selected NTFS and GRUB installer scans after `DoIO` returns; rechecked `rom/exec/doio.c:49-73`, which calls BeginIO synchronously and returns only after the quick query has unwound its automatic array. Added OD2591; no request was run.


NVMe device initialization ownership pass (2026-10-12): reread the complete 338-line `nvme_init.c` body and followed `ADD2INITLIB` ordering, generated false-init rollback, storage-root fallback, PCI enumeration callback, `HW_AddDriver`, and Open lookup. Existing OD2365, OD2366 and OD2406 cover attach/init/root-probe failures; added OD2592 for the distinct per-device record allocation failure that silently omits one controller without retry. Remaining work is controller shutdown and post-registration PCI ownership. No device or allocation failure was run.


NVMe reset callback and protocol shutdown recheck (2026-10-12): traced callback registration and priority through `ShutdownA`/`Exec_DoResetCallbacks` and checked CC.SHN requirements in NVMe Base Specification 1.4c §3.1.5, §7.6.2. Added OD2593 for disabling CC.EN without requesting Normal Shutdown; the data-persistence impact is conditional on a controller volatile cache and pending writes. No reset or hardware was exercised.


NVMe CC shutdown-write ordering refinement (2026-10-12): confirmed the reset handler’s first CC write clears IOSQES/IOCQES while preserving EN, before a later write clears EN (`nvme_controllerclass.c:113-115,136-139`). Controller initialization sets the required entry sizes and a successful bus startup would create I/O queues, but OD2876 shows the selected constructor never reaches that startup path; the I/O-queue precondition is limited to a direct/external AddBus caller. NVMe Base Specification 1.4c §3.1.5 makes changing those size fields with queues present undefined. Refined OD2593 to lead with this protocol violation and retain the missing SHN notification as a separate conditional durability concern. No reset or controller was exercised.


NVMe active namespace enumeration recheck (2026-10-12; confirmed): followed controller NN through the MaxUnits tag, bus pointer-array allocation, namespace loop and per-ID Identify command. NVMe Base Specification 1.4c defines NN as maximum valid NSID (Figure 251), permits sparse IDs (Figure 275 gives NN=1,000,000 with no more than 10 allocated NSIDs), and defines CNS=02h active-ID enumeration. Added OD2594: dense serial probing is proportional to NN, with unchecked table-size multiplication and a signed `int` counter on 32-bit. No controller was run.


NVMe unit-class representation recheck (2026-10-12; no additional finding): reread the complete unit class and linked constructor tags from `NVMEBus_Start`, then traced `au_UnitNum` through the bus Open decoder and `nvme_sector_rw` NSID derivation. The fixed Identify string copies are bounded by the zero-filled inherited instance storage; device/type/removable/model/serial/revision getters return the expected stable fields. OD2368 already covers the significant 12-bit namespace-index collision. No additional unit-class defect established.


NVMe namespace Identify timeout recheck (2026-10-15): verified `busehandle` is zeroed once before queue setup, then reused; `nvme_submit_admincmd` installs the handler without clearing `ceh_Status`, and `nvme_WaitTO` returns a signal mask that the namespace Identify caller does not test before consuming status/data (`nvme_busclass.c:275-288,483-499`; `nvme_queue_admin.c:43-65`; `nvme_timer.c:63-82`). After a successful previous command, an Identify timeout leaves status zero; the pre-cleared response has `ncap == 0`, so that namespace is skipped without failing bus startup. Added OD2860. Source-only; no controller was run.
NVMe admin Identify timeout lifetime recheck (2026-10-15): confirmed `NVME__Root__New` submits the controller Identify with stack `cehandle` and PCI DMA `buffer` (`nvme_controllerclass.c:386-410`), then frees the buffer on the timeout/error path (`:467-501`) without removing the handler from `cehandlers`; `nvme_WaitTO` only aborts the timer request (`nvme_timer.c:63-82`), and late admin completion writes the saved handler and releases its DMA map (`nvme_queue_admin.c:24-40,43-72`). Restored OD2361; no hardware or timeout was run.
NVMe admin completion dispatch recheck (2026-10-12; confirms existing findings): reread `nvme_queue_admin.c` and all in-tree admin submission/wait call sites. Handler/task pointers are initialized and non-null on every selected call; the immediate post-submit CQ poll closes the already-visible-completion sleep race. A phase-valid malformed command ID still indexes the handler table before bounds validation (OD2395), while a timeout still leaves the stack handler and DMA target installed for late completion (OD2361). No separate ordinary-path admin-dispatch defect established.


NetInfo database parser boundary recheck (2026-10-12; existing OD1899/OD1903/OD2261/OD2263 confirmed, no duplicate): reread the 48-line `strsep` helper and selected passwd/group parser and file-loader handoff (`workbench/devs/netinfo/misc.c:23-48`; `passwdunit.c:249-307`; `groupunit.c:215-279`; `entries.c:412-429`). The helper advances across empty fields as the passwd record grammar requires; the loader limits each parsed line to `MAXLINELENGTH` and discards incomplete overlong lines. The group parser's `StrToLong(id_s, ...)` still precedes the missing-field null check (OD1899), and the selected loader's final-line-without-newline behavior remains separately recorded in OD1903. No new parser defect established from ordinary bounded records. No database was loaded or request issued.


NVMe I/O completion and NLB boundary recheck (2026-10-12; no distinct candidate): traced the transfer cap from unit setup to request validation and completion (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:579-590`; `nvme_io.c:72-99,124-146`; `nvme_queue_io.c:28-88`). The advertised per-unit cap is bounded by both the controller MDTS and 65,536 LBAs; the I/O path rejects zero, misaligned, over-cap and out-of-range requests before encoding the 16-bit zero-based NLB. CQ status failure sets `io_Error` but leaves `io_Actual` untouched; because 64-bit commands also use `io_Actual` as the input high offset and no applicable local contract was established, this was not promoted. The omitted `NSCMD_TD_FORMAT64` write classification is only inside the optional NVME_DUMP_READS block, which is not defined in `nvme_queue_io.c` (the same spelling in `nvme_busclass.c` is translation-unit-local); no normal path reads write data for debugging. No device or I/O was run.


VirtIO used-length contract follow-up (2026-10-12; no new candidate): `virtio_process_used` reads each used element's `len` into `ulen` but discards it after status translation (`rom/devs/virtio/virtio_queue.c:251-293`). The selected transport is modern PCI rather than the legacy interface; the legacy-specific advice to ignore used lengths therefore does not settle modern semantics (`virtio_hw.c:112-115`; OASIS VirtIO 1.2 §5.2.6.3). The block section requires `VIRTIO_BLK_T_IN` to populate requested sector data and defines the completion status, but supplies no explicit driver requirement for rejecting a successful short used length (§5.2.6, §5.2.6.1-2). Consequently, this recheck does not establish a separate bug from source/spec evidence alone. Retain modern used-length interpretation and noncoherent DMA post-maintenance as open protocol/platform checks; no device response was observed.

| `rom/devs/console/stdconclass.c` | Full 1,019-line body and selected parser/superclass paths read; CSI erase/insert/delete, scrolling, cursor bookkeeping and resize paths inspected; class-variant integration and platform window clipping remain open | Added OD2595: when CSI P or CSI @ reaches the row end, count is capped to remaining columns and its pixel displacement equals the target width; `ScrollRaster` returns without clearing at `absdx >= width`. The selected module manifest includes `stdconclass`. The CSI mode follow-up checked parser limits and demos: `J` accepts no parsed parameters, while `K` accepts one but this implementation always fills cursor-to-EOL; the selected demos use only parameterless J/K (`support.c:525-526,801-815`; `developer/demos/cons.c:90-91`). No in-tree caller establishes nondefault erase-mode semantics, so this remains an API/compatibility question rather than a new finding. Validated grid limits keep the row/line scroll products within signed `LONG`; no new count-overflow candidate.  Remaining console escape-sequence behavior, other class variants and platform-specific window clipping remain open. No sequence was run. Window-shrink follow-up (2026-10-12; unresolved): in stdcon_newwindowsize, the horizontal-shrink branch sets x1 to the new GFX_XMAX + 1 and x2 to the same new GFX_XMAX, so x2 >= x1 is always false and that branch never fills a right-hand strip (:897-908). For actual layer size changes, Intuition backfills newly exposed strips when a non-superrefresh layer grows (`rom/hyperlayers/movesizelayer.c:398-412`); the default `LAYERS_BACKFILL` sentinel clears the strip (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:125-140`). Thus the failed shrink fill is not shown to expose stale pixels after a later grow in an ordinary default-backfill console window. A caller-supplied `WA_BackFill` hook may paint differently, and superbitmap layers skip this clear path. Manual CSI line-length changes do not resize the layer; whether raster contents beyond the new text extent should be cleared remains contract-dependent. Manual CSI line-length changes also publish cu_XMax before invoking this method (:741-760), so old_xmax is already the requested value and the shrink comparison cannot recover the former extent. Text-preservation/clear semantics remain unverified; no extra finding added. Follow-up (2026-10-13): rechecked this against the parser’s CSI `u` mapping and superclass geometry update; because the new manual width is stored before `Console_NewWindowSize`, the skipped-fill branch does not establish the proposed stale-pixel trigger. Actual window-resize shrink clips the strip, and Intuition’s default layer backfill handles newly exposed strips on growth. No separate finding is credited. |

Console/ScrollRaster caller boundary follow-up (2026-10-12): direct call-site review exposed OD2595 in standard console CSI delete/insert. The caller selects the background pen but relies on ScrollRaster to move and fill; its full-span early return leaves the old cell visible. Rechecked the public negative-bound case separately: selected UI callers clamp visible-area coordinates, while the public contract does not specify negative upper-left clipping, so no separate ScrollRaster finding is added. No scroll or terminal command was run.


Console CSI caller qualification (2026-10-12): confirmed `Console::GetDefaultParams` defaults both CSI insert (`@`) and delete (`P`) counts to one (`rom/devs/console/consoleclass.c:473-500`), and the selected standard console geometry makes the remaining-cell count times `XRSIZE` equal the inclusive raster span (`console_gcc.h:55,63,69`; `consoleclass.c:87-106`). This supports OD2595 for an omitted count at the last cell as well as an explicit count equal to the remaining cells. The selected CharMap console subclass also reaches this path: `makeCharMapConClass` derives from `STDCONCLASSPTR` (`charmapconclass.c:1728-1738`), and its line-buffer insert/delete helpers are followed by `DoSuperMethodA` (`:849-872`), so the superclass ScrollRaster no-op leaves the old raster cell visible there too. Other CharMap behavior and all remaining standard-console methods remain open. No terminal sequence was run.


Standard console command-body pass (2026-10-12): completed a full local read of `stdconclass.c:1-1019`, reviewing constructor/disposal guards, character writes, CSI erase/insert/delete and line scrolls, cursor render nesting, window-size changes, and class dispatch. OD2595 is confirmed for CharMap too because its subclass inserts/deletes its line model and then calls the standard superclass (`charmapconclass.c:849-872`; parent at `:1728-1738`). Added OD2596 after tracing parameterized CSI K through the one-parameter parser table to a handler that ignores the mode, and CSI J through its zero-parameter table into the printable-text fallback (`support.c:472-489,513-526,603-697`; `stdconclass.c:514-560`). No command sequence, GUI, or runtime was exercised.

CSI F/cursor bookkeeping follow-up (2026-10-12; no new finding): verified `C_CURSOR_PREV_LINE` contains one render after its unrender and vertical move (`stdconclass.c:412-422`). `WriteToConsole` wraps non-plain command input in one outer unrender/render pair (`support.c:160-185`); the nested method pair leaves the cursor hidden until that outer render, restoring the normal count and repainting once. The selected CSI table maps `F` to this command with one parameter and the default is one (`support.c:513-526`; `consoleclass.c:473-500`). No CSI sequence was run; class-variant integration and platform window clipping remain open.

Standard console resize follow-up (2026-10-12; no new finding): traced `C_SET_LINE_LENGTH`, `C_SET_PAGE_LENGTH` and `C_SET_TOP_OFFSET` through `Console_NewWindowSize`, superclass dimension updates and `stdcon_newwindowsize`'s shrink/cursor-relocation clears (`stdconclass.c:709-761,882-934`; `consoleclass.c:529-567`). The manual line/page length commands write `cu_XMax`/`cu_YMax` before calling `Console_NewWindowSize`, so the standard handler's `old_xmax`/`old_ymax` snapshots are already the requested values and cannot identify the former extent. This leaves old raster cells outside the newly limited character area potentially visible, but the command contract for preserving/clearing discarded text and caller expectations were not established, so no candidate is added. Regular IDCMP_NEWSIZE recalculates automatic bounds in the superclass before the shrink checks; its redraw and background-color contract remains open. No resize was run.


USB keyboard conversion-table bounds recheck (OD2597, 2026-10-12): counted 232 `uint8_t` conversion entries (`0x00`–`0xE7`) against `sizeof(keyconv)`, then traced report bytes from the HID descriptor-selected key field into `kbd->code[]` and the worker. Normal key-down/up filters evaluate `keyconv[value]` before the later range check; report bytes can represent `0xE8`–`0xFF`. Modifier usages pass through `HID_GET_USAGE` and are narrowed into `struct key_mod.key` (`uint8_t`), then indexed directly without a bound check. This confirms OD2597; descriptor/device behavior remains unexercised and external report-contract review is open.

USB HID mouse event-buffer and tablet-lifetime cross-check (2026-10-12; no new candidate): re-counted the worker's maximum buffered batch as one relative-motion event, up to six transitions for its three emitted buttons, and two wheel events, for at most nine entries in the ten-entry allocation (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/mouseclass.c:324-465`). The absolute-tablet branch sends one stack-backed `IENewTablet` through `IND_WRITEEVENT` with `DoIO`; input.device queues and forwards that event in its command task before replying the request (`rom/devs/input/input.c:149-164`; `processevents.c:397-421`; `support.c:19-29,38-94`), so this selected path consumes the pointer before the worker's stack frame resumes. The remaining absolute-axis issues are already described separately by OD2300-OD2302; no event was submitted.
Console CSI erase parser follow-up (2026-10-12; OD2596 caller path verified): `StringToCommand` recognizes either CSI byte form, tries the parameter-command parser, and if it returns false leaves `write_str` at the start of the original sequence before creating `C_ASCII_STRING` (`rom/devs/console/support.c:310-337,372-383,472-489`). The `J` table entry has zero parameters, so `CSI 1 J`/`CSI 2 J` are not dispatched as erase commands; the raw sequence is passed to console text output. The `K` entry accepts and stores one mode parameter, but `stdcon_docommand` ignores it and fills cursor-to-end-of-line (`support.c:513-526,801-817`; `stdconclass.c:514-536`). This confirms the distinct parser-rejection and handler-mode paths described in OD2596; no additional finding is counted and no sequence was run.

Console standard-class follow-up (2026-10-12): added OD2598 after tracing CSI `y` parameter parsing through `stdcon_docommand` and the shared signed-`WORD` ConUnit fields. `IPTR` overflow rejection does not prevent an in-range value such as 32768 from narrowing when stored as `cu_YROrigin`; subsequent grid recomputation accepts that origin. Standard and CharMap are selected routes. Source-only; no sequence was run. Other standard-class commands, external window-creation contracts and platform clipping behavior remain open.

Console CSI dispatch follow-up (2026-10-12): static comparison of every CSI table entry with the standard, base and CharMap `DoCommand` switches found `C_SET_LEFT_OFFSET` as the sole accepted command with no handler. Added qualified candidate OD2599 (medium confidence): parser consumes CSI `x`, but the effect is no-op; the checked source does not establish the intended offset semantics, so contract confidence remains limited. Other command and caller checks remain open. Source-only.

Usergroup lastlog read-error follow-up (2026-10-12; OD2602 added): confirmed DOS `Read` distinguishes -1 errors, short positive reads and EOF (`rom/dos/read.c:32-44`), but multi-user `getlastlog` collapses every non-record-sized result and failed `Open` into `never == TRUE`, then returns a zero-time static record (`workbench/libs/usergroup/getutent.c:328-359`). The vector documentation promises NULL on error and identifies ENOENT as the absent-entry case (`:295-301`); no direct checked-in C caller exists. The public error-versus-no-entry behavior is source-supported, while consequences depend on external caller policy. No file I/O was run.


Timer arithmetic cross-check: re-read SUBTIME and compared the source mutation with selected callers. The existing Efika shared-clock mutation remains part of OD1574; selected PC, AArch64, OpenSBI, OOP, AHCI, and sound callers did not establish an independent trigger. This does not close the broader timer or caller audit.

Keyboard reset-handler list follow-up (OD2603 added): traced reset-key `writeEvents` traversal against KBD_ADD/REM direct BeginIO calls and VMM cleanup (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:311-324,465-512`; `rom/exec/doio.c:52-74`; `workbench/system/VMM/reset_handler.c:119-126`). `Disable` is local-CPU only on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), and VMM frees the node immediately after unregistering; the initialized keyboard queue semaphore is not used for this list. Concurrent reset-key traversal and removal can therefore race the list and node lifetime. No event or SMP run was performed.

VirtIO change-interrupt follow-up (OD2604 caller qualification): `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` is omitted from `NSDSupported`; nevertheless, non-quick requests pass through a branch that leaves `done` false without registering a handler, and the shared return path clears quick mode without replying (`rom/devs/virtio/virtio_io.c:134-140,236-263`). AFS installs change interrupts only after `TD_GETGEOMETRY` reports `DGF_REMOVABLE` (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:377-390,402-420`), while VirtIO returns flags zero and identifies the unit as fixed/nonremovable (`virtio_io.c:211-229`; `virtio_unitclass.c:63-64,88-90`), excluding that AFS path. The selected SFS handler unconditionally sends `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` on successful filesystem setup (`rom/filesys/SFS/FS/filesystemmain.c:378`), then reuses the same request with `SendIO(TD_REMCHANGEINT)` during cleanup (`rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:167-195`; `filesystemmain.c:445,1368`). Unlike NTFS, SFS removal is non-quick and follows the valid removal branch, but BeginIO still inserts the linked node a second time before removing it once, leaving the list stale when `cleanupdeviceio` deletes the request (`deviceio.c:539-543`). This is the same OD2604 list-corruption condition through a distinct caller completion path. FAT and CDVDFS also contain generic setup, but their selected attachment gates against VirtIO remain open. Both selected SFS and NTFS trigger paths remain latent while OD2541 prevents ordinary VirtIO bus publication. Source-only.

VirtIO unit-identity follow-up (OD2605 added): the controller supplies short model/serial/revision strings, the bus duplicates each into `strlen+1` storage, and the unit constructor reads fixed 40/20/8-byte spans regardless of those NULs. The visible strings remain terminated and no metadata corruption is claimed; the invalid reads and potential fault/undefined behavior are detailed in the report. Source-only.

NetInfo update-path follow-up (OD2606 added): the selected server accepts global database paths up to 127 bytes (`server.c:40-55`; DOS `GetVar` text termination at `rom/dos/getvar.c:234-266`), while `UpdateCmd` appends `.new` and `.old` to separate 128-byte stack buffers with `strncat` limit 127 (`entries.c:270-282`). A configured path of 124 bytes or more overflows these buffers when CMD_UPDATE is issued. Repository call census found no in-tree CMD_WRITE/CMD_UPDATE caller; the public device API remains triggerable by clients. Source-only.

AHCI worker stop/signal lifecycle follow-up (2026-10-12; no new finding): traced `ahci_os_signal_port_thread` callers (port interrupts and timeout callback), worker signal snapshot/clear loop, `ahci_os_stop_port`, `ahci_port_free`, and controller detach (`ahci.c:2668,2758-2763,4005; ahci_aros.c:193-211,235-269; ahci.c:1015-1031; ahci_attach.c:790-823`). `atomic_clear_int` clears only the bits in the captured mask, so a different bit arriving after the snapshot remains pending; a repeated bit already in the local snapshot is still processed by that iteration. Detach disables controller interrupt processing and tears down the IRQ before it stops each worker, and port teardown waits for `ap_thread` to clear before freeing CCB/DMA resources. No independent signal-loss or worker-use-after-free candidate established. The selected callout cancel path was separately reconciled to DISK-111 below; this pass does not close broader AHCI interleavings or caller coverage. Source-only; no runtime or hardware exercised.
AHCI callout-cancel cross-report reconciliation (2026-10-12): checked the selected callout task against `DISK-111` (`../AROS-disk.md:1474-1479`). `callout_stop` signals and clears the task pointer without joining it; an already-running `ahci_ata_cmd_timeout_unserialized` can still touch its CCB and signal the port worker. `ahci_port_free` joins the port worker but not outstanding callout tasks before freeing CCBs. This is within DISK-111's existing callback-lifetime candidate, so no duplicate OD finding is added; its broader caller and teardown scope remains tracked there.

AHCI interrupt teardown synchronization follow-up (2026-10-12; no new finding): followed the selected `pci_alloc_1intr` result through `bus_alloc_resource_any`, `bus_setup_intr`, and detach's `bus_teardown_intr` (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_aros.c:101-132`; `ahci_attach.c:379-383,790-812`; `ahci_aros_bus.c:245-286,336-400`). Both the legacy INTx and obtained-vector routes pass a nonzero `RF_ACTIVE` flag, so the shim registers through `AddIntServer(INTB_KERNEL + res_tag, ...)` and removes through `RemIntServer`. The selected PC HIDD PCI driver's Add/Remove methods likewise use `KrnAddIRQHandler`/`KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:279-286,336-340`); the SMP kernel's remove path takes the IRQ-chain write lock used by `krnRunIRQHandlers` before freeing the node (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:57-78`; `addirqhandler.c:127-145`). Thus detach waits out an in-flight handler on this selected route before freeing its wrapper, resolving the attach file's `XXX interlock last interrupt` concern for these PC builds. Non-PC HIDD overrides and externally supplied drivers are outside this check. Source-only; no IRQ or detach was run.
AHCI DMA-sync length caller qualification (2026-10-12; no selected-target finding): `bus_dmamap_sync` seeds CachePreDMA/CachePostDMA length from `tag->dt_maxsegsz` (64 KiB for `sc_tag_data`), while AHCI advertises transfers up to 2 MiB and calls sync once for the full transfer (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_aros_bus.c:195-205`; `ahci_attach.c:517-531`; `ahci.h:395`; `ahci.c:2119-2145,2191-2200`). However, the only boot manifests selecting AHCI in this checkout are i386-PC and x86-64-PC (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:73`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66`), and selected x86 `CachePreDMA` explicitly returns the address without maintenance because the architecture is cache coherent (`rom/exec/cachepredma.c:68-75`). The apparent short range therefore has no cache-visibility consequence on the selected AHCI targets; no finding added. A future noncoherent target would need an architecture-specific review. Source-only; no transfer was run.
AHCI PRDT-size caller follow-up (2026-10-12; DISK-015 trigger bounded to direct callers): rechecked the public `HD_SCSICMD` path through `ahci_scsi_disk_io`/`ahci_load_prdt_callback` and selected in-tree SFS/PFS direct-SCSI clients (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_io.c:388-394`; `ahci_scsi.c:445-550`; `ahci.c:2119-2145,2160-2180`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:381-390,798-825`; `rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/disk.c:1543-1555`; AHCI device node at `ahci_cam_aros.c:311`). SFS chunks to `de_MaxTransfer`; PFS3 also caps each direct-SCSI chunk by the device's `de_MaxTransfer`; AHCI advertises 2 MiB. Those checked in-tree callers therefore do not reach the >4 MiB one-PRD overflow from DISK-015. The public HD_SCSICMD request path itself does not check the supplied `scsi_Length` against the advertised maximum, so direct clients can still exceed the contract and reach the existing candidate; no duplicate finding added. No SCSI request or transfer was run.
AHCI DMA-slab allocator caller/lifetime qualification (2026-10-12; no additional shim finding): traced all selected `bus_dma_tag_create`, `bus_dmamem_alloc/free`, and `bus_dma_tag_destroy` calls (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_attach.c:465-532,840-857`; `ahci.c:352,400-401,1015-1065,3741-3810`; `ahci_aros_bus.c:33-64,84-185`). The only tags passed to `bus_dmamem_alloc` are RFIS, command-header and command-table tags, each created with one segment; the 1,016-segment data tag is used only for map/load/sync. Thus the allocator's signed `1 << i`/64-bit segment-map concern cannot be reached by selected calls. `ahci_dmamem_free` does not return its slot to the slab, but all selected frees occur during port unwind or controller detach, and attach failure also enters full controller detach; the subsequent tag destroy frees every slab. No persistent leak or live selected path that reuses a freed slot was established. Source-only; no allocation failure or hardware was exercised.

AHCI partial-attach storage-enumeration follow-up (2026-10-12; OD2372 extended): followed a previously probed port's published unit through later-port attach failure, `ahci_cam_detach`/`ahci_UnregisterPort`, `ahci_port_free`, and the selected ShowConfig storage enumerator (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_attach.c:637-645,701-704,816-821`; `ahci_cam_aros.c:368-384`; `ahci_unitclass.c:50-70,92-99`; `rom/hidds/base/storage/storage_controllerclass.c:220-236`; `workbench/tools/ShowConfig/storage.c:61-82,106-149`). CAM teardown removes the `cam_sim` record only; it leaves the HIDD bus/unit objects registered and the unit's `au_Bus->ab_Port` pointing to freed `ap`. ShowConfig enumerates units and requests the Type attribute, but AHCI unit Get dereferences that chain before attribute dispatch. This is an ordinary post-failure stale-object path in addition to OD2372's reset callback and is now spelled out in that finding. It requires an earlier successful unit publication before a later port setup failure; no controller or enumeration was run.

EHCI generator follow-up (2026-10-12): rechecked `ehci.conf`'s `Root` methodlist (`New`, `Dispose`) against `ehci_init.c`'s matching `METHOD(EHCI, Root, ...)` bodies, then traced `methodlist` parsing in `tools/genmodule/config.c` and interface method-ID/message generation in `tools/genmodule/writeincinterfaces.c`. No additional method or body mismatch is indicated by the checked generator path; generated EHCI dispatch output remains unavailable and is still an explicit coverage gap. No controller or module runtime was exercised.

EHCI header follow-up (2026-10-12): audited `ehci.h` against the only selected C body and generated class setup. Its `BASE` macro names `struct ohcibase` instead of `struct ehcibase`, but this translation unit overrides `SD` immediately after including the header, and the only two EHCI method bodies return/do nothing without expanding `SD` or `BASE`; generated class setup stores the library base directly in `UserData` (`tools/genmodule/oopsupport.c`). No current selected execution path dereferences the mismatched cast, so this was not credited as a bug. Future method use or emitted dispatch remains outside verified runtime coverage.

PCIUSB EHCI completion/init follow-up (2026-10-12): rechecked `ehciCompleteInt` against the PCI interrupt wrapper, completion queue dispatch and request finish/free helpers, and traced `ehciScheduleSegmentValid` into both schedule-allocation attempts in `ehciInit`. The checked segment-length caller is the fixed, nonzero periodic/QH/TD/iTD/siTD schedule allocation; a failed high-memory check frees that allocation before retry, and `init_fail` releases the retained allocation/private arrays and clears `hc_CPrivate`. No zero-length segment or additional cleanup defect was established in these paths. This does not close the ledger's wider USB-client, DMA-segment/backend or hardware-lifecycle contracts; no interrupt, controller, or transfer was run.

PCIUSB EHCI root-port caller follow-up (2026-10-12): traced `ehciSetFeature`, `ehciClearFeature` and `ehciGetStatus` through the direct `devBeginIO` root-hub control-request path and checked `ehciCheckPortStatusChange` through the PCI interrupt path. OD2610 records the shared per-port change-map race: both contexts perform unprotected read-modify-write updates while acknowledging hardware W1C bits; ExecSMP's `Disable()` is local-CPU only (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`). Global port indices are validated before request dispatch (`uhwcmd.c:766-777,865-884`), the ISR caps local iteration and skips unmapped global ports (`ehci_hcport.c:53-80`), and the mapping producer bounds its tables (`pciusb_arospci.c:458-484,504-518,574-615`); no new bounds issue found. Finding count updated from 602 to 603 unique numbered report entries. No request, interrupt or SMP schedule was run; exact interleaving remains conditional.
OD2610 selected-delivery check: PCIPC inherits the generic `CLID_Hidd_PCIDriver` `AddInterrupt` implementation and its method list does not override that method (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc.conf:7,22-28`). Generic AddInterrupt installs `krnIRQwrapper`, which invokes the supplied handler (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:226-230,279-287`); this adds no caller-context serialization around root-hub `BeginIO`. This supports the conditional same-state overlap on ExecSMP; exact timing remains untested.
PCIUSB/xHCI root-hub actual-count reconciliation (2026-10-12): merged the duplicate PCIUSB candidate into existing OD904, which now covers both controller-family implementations; tracing the successful port `GET_STATUS` path through each HCI reader, `devBeginIO`/`TermIO`, Poseidon's persistent `PsdPipe` IO request and public `psdGetPipeActual` getter. The branch returns before the ordinary transfer path's `iouh_Actual=0`, does not set a four-byte result count, and pipe setup does not reset it; the selected hub class ignores the field, so the impact is limited to callers that query actual length. Other Drivers report count after duplicate reconciliation: 603 unique numbered entries. No USB transfer was run.
OD2610 xHCI delivery follow-up (2026-10-12): rechecked the PCI xHCI path after the PCIUSB pass. The registered `xhciIntCode` handler processes port-status events, updates `hc_PortChangeMap` and acknowledges PORTSC W1C bits; `xhciCompleteInt` and `xhciEventRingTask` handle completion/scheduling separately (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:3211-3224,3298-3350,2946-2958,4067-4076`; `xhci_hw.c:482-548`). The root-hub `GET_STATUS` / `CLEAR_FEATURE` helpers mutate the same per-port map from direct BeginIO. PCIPC is the inherited generic AddInterrupt backend; no SMP lock spans the request and interrupt-handler paths. OD2610 now covers this alongside PCIUSB EHCI's interrupt path. No interleaving was run.


Keymap reverse-mapping follow-up (2026-10-12; OD2612 added): compared the selected `MapANSI` scan bounds with the full default high-keymap type/data tables and `MapRawKey` string-output path. `MapANSI` searches high codes only through 0x67, while codes 0x6e–0x71 have valid Pause/F12/Home/End ANSI string descriptors, so those sequences return zero when no other mapping matches. The maintained `MapANSI` C callers found pass one-byte inputs; the user-visible reverse-mapping failure is therefore recorded for public external clients supplying the multi-byte strings. No conversion was run.


OD2354 scope recheck (2026-10-12): scanned every USB and Bluetooth `dev.c` containing `IOERR_UNITBUSY`, then followed the null-unit fallback and all relevant class manifests. The same overwrite also affects `davicometh`, `stir4200`, `rawwrap`, `cdcacm`, `serialcp210x`, `serialpl2303`, Bluetooth `btpan`/`btserial`, and `usbparallel.device` (`rom/usb/classes/{davicometh,stir4200,rawwrap,cdcacm,serialcp210x,serialpl2303,printer}/dev.c`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/{btpan,btserial}/dev.c`). The USB common-class aggregate and Bluetooth class aggregate include these class targets. Each affected path sets `IOERR_UNITBUSY` for a matched busy unit, then overwrites it when `io_Unit` remains null. Exec `OpenDevice` returns that final vector error. `lan78xx` explicitly preserves the busy error; rawwrap does not. Expanded OD2354 in the report; no second open was run.


OD2354 full-tree pattern classification (2026-10-12): exact assignments of a request `io_Error` to `IOERR_UNITBUSY` followed by a direct `IOERR_OPENFAIL` fallback were scanned across checked-in C sources. The complete USB/Bluetooth result includes ASIX, CDC Ethernet, Davicom, ethwrap, Moschip, Pegasus, RNDIS, USB Bluetooth, CDC ACM, CP210x, PL2303, STIr4200, RawWrap, usbparallel.device, Bluetooth PAN and Bluetooth serial. lan78xx preserves the error. The non-USB PCI network sources use a local `error` variable and separate rollback paths rather than this direct overwrite; for example, broadcom4400 and nvidianet call `CloseUnit` on open failure, which decrements the tentative unit count (`device.c:231-237,281-282,506-533`). SiS900's distinct rejected-open shutdown/count behavior remains OD2531. This scan did not replace the pending full caller/lifecycle audits of those network modules.

OD2354 reconciliation (2026-10-15): the detailed finding was absent despite the ledger's 2026-10-12 note that it had been expanded. Rechecked the busy-unit assignment and subsequent null-unit fallback in every USB/Bluetooth `dev.c` that sets `IOERR_UNITBUSY`; restored the candidate as OD2886 with exact class paths and excluded the `lan78xx` and PCI-network exceptions. The separate USB Bluetooth class path was included after direct source inspection. The finding records loss of the public busy-vs-open-failure distinction, not a broader resource or access-control claim. No second open was run.

OD2600 reconciliation (2026-10-15): the Broadcom 4400 `S2_DEVICEQUERY` note described an actual write past a caller-advertised four-byte result prefix. Re-read the complete handler and dispatcher, confirming the bounded copy is followed by unconditional `SizeSupplied` and `BPS` stores without a minimum-size check. Restored the source finding as OD2887; no short buffer was passed.

OD4241 reconciliation (2026-10-15; expanded 2026-10-20): confirmed the failed-construction reservation in Unix serial and checked the same result/used-bit sequence across all six Unix, PC and m68k serial/parallel parent factories. The selected serial.device/parallel.device callers discard their temporary unit records on a NULL return without calling DisposeUnit. OD2888 now tracks only the additional Unix serial null-UnixIO cleanup path. No object-allocation failure or device open was induced.

OD2008 reconciliation (2026-10-15): compared the PL2303, USB printer, and USB audio unit-reuse keys with Poseidon's per-device/per-interface binding storage and release path. Confirmed each can return a shared class record for two matching physical devices and then start another worker against overwritten record state. Restored as OD2889; no duplicate devices were attached or removed.

OD2353 reconciliation (2026-10-15): rechecked selected USB Ethernet `CMD_WRITE` enqueue, worker slot dequeue, active-transfer abort, and each class's shutdown cleanup. Confirmed eight classes leave the private write queue undrained while `nFreeEth` only drains the unit message port. Restored as OD2890; no disconnect or pending write was induced.

OD1664 status correction (2026-10-15): do not restore the historical failed-init rollback candidate on current evidence. Its proposed trigger requires the device/sub-library `devInit` callback's nested `OpenLibrary("utility.library", 0)` to fail, but each selected parent class already holds utility.library version 39 before calling `MakeLibrary`, and utility.conf marks the library noexpunge. Separately, a failed parent `MakeLibrary` makes the class initializer return failure rather than publish the partially initialized class; no selected expunge callback path to the NULL device-base dereference was established. The pointer dereference is present in source, but the required reachable trigger is not. Existing per-class rows retain this qualification; no finding is counted.

OD2372 AHCI subpath reconciliation (2026-10-15): restored the reachable AHCI case separately as OD2891. When MSI callback registration succeeds and a later attach step fails, `ahci_pci_detach` releases resources but does not unregister the callback; `ahci_release` then frees its containing `device_t`. The resulting stale callback is distinct from OD2561's earlier-port loss on the same unwind. No hardware failure or reset was induced.

OD2561 reconciliation (2026-10-15): the AHCI attach-loop candidate was also absent from the detailed report. Re-read the per-port `error == 0` loop, interrupt setup gate, failure return and `ahci_pci_detach`; confirmed an `ahci_port_alloc` failure stops enumeration and tears down already allocated ports instead of continuing as the adjacent comment states. Restored as OD2892, separate from the stale reset callback. No allocation failure or hardware was induced.

OD1652 reconciliation (2026-10-15): re-read the complete console worker exit and cleanup helper, console BeginIO, selected `C:Break NAME` path, and task-name initialization. Confirmed default CTRL-C can stop the worker, while handler and ports remain registered and later commands still queue to its dead port. Restored as OD2893; no task was stopped and no console request was issued.

OD2263 reconciliation (2026-10-15): traced the usergroup 1,024-byte passwd output buffer through NetInfo's line parser, expanded `NetInfoPasswd` size check, cursor advance, and `getpwent` error-to-NULL path. Confirmed a valid near-limit input can exceed the expanded output size and the failed copy advances past that record. Restored as OD2894; no passwd database was read or changed.

OD2261 reconciliation (2026-10-15): rechecked passwd/group direct-write copy-in, packed `UWORD` stored lengths, `io_Actual` reporting and copy-out. Confirmed aggregate lengths above 65,535 wrap for the size check while the full strings remain allocated/copied, allowing later read copies beyond a buffer sized to the reported length. Restored as OD2895; no direct request was issued.

OD932 PCIPC fallback reconciliation (2026-10-15): rechecked the selected PC IPC registration message, both ACPI/legacy branches, PCI AddHardwareDriver forwarding, generic HW_AddDriver and PCIPC Root New tag traversal. The legacy branch leaves `instanceTags` untouched before passing it to `GetTagData`; restored the PC-selected path as OD2896. No startup was run.

OD2610 reconciliation (2026-10-15): traced EHCI root-hub ClearPortFeature and PCI interrupt updates, and xHCI clear-feature calls against the event-ring task and PORTSC W1C acknowledgement. Confirmed both update `hc_PortChangeMap` without a shared lock; Exec `Disable()` only masks the current CPU on ExecSMP. Restored the race as OD2897; no port transition or clear request was run.

OD2387 reconciliation (2026-10-15): traced HDAudio's hardware ISR `Cause` call through Exec's deferred soft-interrupt dispatcher and the HDAudio AHI Stop path. Stop disables/frees stream state and playback/record buffers but does not wait for a callback already executing; the callback can have passed its pointer/active checks and continue against that freed state. Restored as OD2898; no callback or stream stop was run.

Standard console top-offset range follow-up (2026-10-12; OD2622 added): traced CSI `y` from the one-parameter table and IPTR decimal parser to the standard-class assignment, automatic `cu_YMax` calculation, and signed ConUnit fields (`support.c:568-573,746-801`; `stdconclass.c:709-718`; `consoleclass.c:529-567`; `include/conunit.h:45-56`). The parser rejects IPTR decimal overflow as `C_NIL`, but representable values are not bounded to the signed WORD field or available viewport height. At or beyond usable height, the automatic row maximum can be negative, invalidating cursor/range geometry. Added the qualified source finding OD2622. The class-chain caller pass confirms the same path in `CONU_CHARMAP` and `CONU_SNIPMAP`: CharMap defaults unhandled commands to StdCon (`charmapconclass.c:950-952,1728-1738`), SnipMap defaults to CharMap (`snipmapconclass.c:107-112,165-170`), and `console.c` selects these classes (`:191-202`). No window or terminal sequence was run.


EtherLink3 AROS wrapper completion recheck (2026-10-12): added OD2624 after tracing each wrapper-modified packet command through the callback restore points and immediate `ServiceRequest` reply. No packet callback is needed for unit-offline or invalid-multicast rejection, leaving the caller-visible `ios2_Data` value replaced. Wider client usage and other request paths remain pending; no request was issued.


EtherLink3 PCI wrapper-allocation rollback recheck (2026-10-12; consolidated into OD2802): confirmed all five AROS `WrapInt` calls allocate save records and partial failure skips `UnwrapInt` before registration. The same failure/cleanup pattern is now cross-checked in Rhine and Prism2 and covered by the shared OD2802 entry. No allocation failure or PCI card was exercised.


EtherLink3 Prometheus enumeration and ownership recheck (2026-10-12): no new finding. The provider builds its PCI board list at library initialization and only drains it during expunge; EtherLink3 retains its OpenLibrary reference while using the list. Count and indexed unit lookup therefore do not have an in-tree list-removal race. The PCI HIDD serializes owner acquisition, so candidate 739 is not promoted from these paths. Other Prometheus clients, HIDD enumeration failure, bus mapping and hardware behavior remain open. No library/device was run.

EtherLink3 Prometheus DMA buffer recheck (2026-10-12): no new finding. `CreateUnit` requests fixed Ethernet-buffer and descriptor sizes with alignment 1 or 8; `AllocDMAMemHook` stores the original allocation pointer and exact enlarged size before returning an aligned address, and `FreeDMAMemHook` passes that metadata unchanged to `Prm_FreeDMABuffer` (`unit.c:266-298,498-506`; `pci.c:938-951,979-995`; `prometheus.c:242-270`). The selected failure cleanup checks each DMA pointer through the hook and the hook ignores NULL. Zero-size and arbitrary external requests are not part of this caller path. No allocation or DMA was run.

Standard console top-offset cross-check (2026-10-12): separated OD2598's signed-WORD narrowing case from OD2622's in-range but out-of-viewport case. Checked the sequence where a valid manual page length is set first: `C_SET_TOP_OFFSET` assigns `cu_YMax` directly before calling `Console_NewWindowSize`, so the manual-page flag does not bound the new origin or preserve the validated range. No terminal sequence or window was used.

Raspberry Pi USB OTG per-open allocation recheck (2026-10-12; OD2626 added): followed `OpenUnit` through Exec `CreateMsgPort`, `CreateIORequest`, and `OpenDevice` (`usb2otg_core.c:30-47,223-227`; `rom/exec/createmsgport.c:51-76`; `createiorequest.c:60-77`; `opendevice.c:88-97`). Either failed allocation yields NULL; the driver passes that pointer into an unconditional Exec IORequest dereference after setting `hu_UnitAllocated`. This details the earlier OD1525 tracker candidate. Allocation rollback and timer/hardware behavior remain source-only; no failure was induced.

Raspberry Pi USB OTG multiple-open lifecycle recheck (2026-10-12; OD2627 added): traced `OpenUnit` success through the device Open/Close vectors and timer `DoIO` suspension (`usb2otg_core.c:30-48,294-317`; `usb2otg_device.c:451-489`; `rom/exec/doio.c:63-66`; `rom/exec/waitio.c:54-64`). A second open can return while the first is waiting; closing it clears the single open flag, so another open can re-enter controller initialization while the original client still owns the unit. No selected in-tree overlap schedule was established; public callers and runtime behavior remain untested.

AHCI polling callback and command-queue recheck (2026-10-12; no new finding): reread `ahci_poll`, the shared command start/queue helpers, timeout completion, and all selected `ahci_poll` call sites in `ahci.c` and `ahci_pm.c` (`ahci.c:2237-2285,2333-2590,3931-3934`; `ahci_pm.c:284,352,795,848`). Although the helper comment describes a nullable timeout callback, its expired path calls `timeout_fn(ccb)` unconditionally. Every selected call supplies `ahci_quick_timeout` or `ahci_ata_cmd_timeout`, so a null callback is not reachable through the selected AHCI paths. Polling holds the port critical section while it starts/drains the request; active timeout scanning uses the active masks, and command scheduling/timeout interleavings were separately followed in the preceding entry. No additional candidate established; a complete external AHCI API caller census and wider queue/recovery review remain open. Source-only; no I/O or timeout was run.

AHCI pending-queue transition recheck (2026-10-12; no new finding): reread `ahci_start`, `ahci_issue_pending_commands`, and the interrupt completion/restart handoff (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:2333-2365,2414-2605,3336-3432`). New CCBs enter the pending tail before scheduler checks; NCQ and standard commands are separated while either class is active, exclusive/autosense requests stop later scheduling, and command slots move out of the queue before their active masks and ONCHIP state are published. Completion clears the selected active bit/counter before callback and common restart runs after completion processing. The existing DISK-127 same-loop standard/EXCLUSIVE admission and OD2583 bit-31 shift remain the concrete scheduler findings; no separate queue unlink/restart defect was established in these branches. Caller interleavings outside the selected AHCI paths and full recovery ownership remain open. Source-only; no command was issued.

AHCI error-CCB recovery and saved-command restart review (2026-10-12; no new finding in this slice): reread `ahci_get_err_ccb`/`ahci_put_err_ccb`, NCQ error-log cleanup, `ahci_ata_cmd_timeout`, and `ahci_issue_saved_commands` (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:3532-3624,3631-3730,4017-4204`). Error-CCB reservation snapshots and temporarily clears active masks, then restores them only after the error CCB has completed; DISK-117's second-FIS failure still bypasses that restoration and remains separately documented. Timeout handling removes a pending CCB before completion, or records on-chip expiry, stops only once safe, removes each expired slot before invoking completion, and filters expired bits from saved hardware activity before restart. `ahci_issue_saved_commands` walks all 32 register-bit positions, but its selected callers supply a mask derived from tracked active CCBs or hardware state intersected with tracked masks; no ordinary selected path to an out-of-range slot was established. Stale hardware status and external controller behavior remain untested. Broader recovery/callout interleavings, port-multiplier error handling and adapter callers remain open. Source-only; no error or timeout was induced.

HDAudio mono playback finding recheck (2026-10-12; OD2157 strengthened): re-read AHI's stereo/HiFi mode negotiation and custom mode registration, HDAudio Start/Update and playback interrupt, then traced the format and allocation through the HIDD `SetupStream`. HDAudio's `get_hda_format` unconditionally sets `FORMAT_STEREO` (`misc.c:1582-1592`), while `_AHIsub_Start` sizes each buffer from the caller's stereo flag (`main.c:207-240`); `SetupStream` allocates exactly `msg->bufferSize` and places that length in each BDL entry (`workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:863-889`). The 16-bit and HiFi 24-bit interrupt loops copy 4 or 8 bytes per frame from mono buffers sized at 2 or 4 bytes per frame (`interrupt.c:78-103`). This confirms both CPU-side source overread and destination overwrite, plus a stereo hardware descriptor that consumes the undersized buffer. The existing custom `AHI_AddAudioMode` trigger and conditional build scope remain as documented; no duplicate finding or runtime claim added.


Other Drivers USB printer open recheck (OD2152, 2026-10-13): corrected the lock trace after rereading `OpenDevice`: it releases the DeviceList read lock before the vector call, while local Forbid persists through the call (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-100,109-131`). Under ExecSMP another CPU can enter the driver concurrently; the unit's `unit_OpenCnt` check and increment remain unprotected (`rom/usb/classes/printer/dev.c:78-100`). The `kernel-usb` aggregate selects the printer class, but the checked-in ExecSMP variants and USB boot manifests do not combine them: x86-64 PC has no USB boot target, Raspberry Pi selects USB2OTG/PCIXHCI without printer, and OpenSBI selects a limited class set. This is an explicit build-combination candidate, not a default-image workload. OD2152 remains conditional; no concurrent open was run. Source-only.

PTP zero-terminator error propagation recheck (OD2631, 2026-10-13): followed both `nGetPTPRsp` and `nGetPTPRspData` through their selected `nPTPRead` callers. Each ignores the result of its zero-length EPIn `psdDoPipe` call, overwrites `ioerr` with the subsequent response read, then resets `pr_IOErr` after response validation; callers rely on `nCheckPTPError` and may advance the file position. Added OD2631 for false-success handling when that intermediate transfer fails and the later response is accepted. No PTP device or I/O error was induced; source-only.

Raspberry Pi USB OTG root-hub status count recheck (2026-10-13; OD2635 added): followed standard device GET_STATUS through root-hub dispatch and Poseidon pipe reuse. The handler writes its 2-byte response but leaves `iouh_Actual` untouched; BeginIO only resets `io_Error`, TermIO does not normalize the count, and `psdGetPipeActual` returns the stale field under a documented actual-length contract (`usb2otg_hub.c:64-75`; `usb2otg_device.c:537-550`; `usb2otg_core.c:314-338,454-460`; `poseidon.library.c:4705-4731,4807-4862,4899-4907`; Poseidon docs `:1656-1671`). Hub.class consumes the status bytes and checks only the error; impact is qualified to API callers that query actual length. No request was issued. Source-only.

Raspberry Pi USB OTG root-hub count follow-up (2026-10-13; OD2635 broadened): the neighboring class `SET_FEATURE` handlers (including `PORT_RESET`) also report success without assigning `iouh_Actual`; these zero-data requests can expose an earlier transfer's count just like standard device GET_STATUS (`usb2otg_hub.c:158-278`, alongside `:64-75`). The selected hub-class port-reset and status callers check the I/O error/response bytes, not `psdGetPipeActual`; the finding remains scoped to consumers of that documented accessor. Other successful GET_STATUS branches set their lengths (`:416-495,500-519`), and CLEAR_FEATURE sets zero (`:378-408`). No request was issued; source-only.

NetInfo persistent-worker expunge recheck (2026-10-13; OD1902 detailed body restored): traced unit close, the `nid_Death` reply message, `NetInfoPoll` wake/cleanup, generated `ExpungeLib`, and Exec `RemDevice`. Close does not stop the worker; the expunge hook queues a shutdown reply but returns success without waiting. `RemDevice` holds `Forbid` until after generated expunge frees the base, so on single CPU the worker cannot consume the message before its `nid` storage is reclaimed. SMP also lacks a worker join/lifetime barrier. The selected `lddemon` low-memory sweep invokes `RemDevice` for zero-open devices (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:745-755`), supplying an in-tree removal trigger after an earlier open/close; no runtime teardown was performed.

Card tuple partial-read recheck (2026-10-13; OD1486 retained and restored as a detailed finding): `getbyte` zeroes its output and returns FALSE when the Gayle card-detect bit is clear (`arch/m68k-amiga/card/copytuple.c:27-40`; `lowlevel.c:139-144`), but the matched-tuple copy ignores those returns and returns TRUE (`copytuple.c:163-179`). If removal occurs after a supported RAM type, speed and size byte were read but while a declared trailing byte is being copied, `DeviceTuple` can use the valid prefix and does not know the trailing read failed (`card_init.c:56-60`; `devicetuple.c:27-98`). Both subsequent FORMAT and GEOMETRY `CopyTuple` calls then return FALSE because the card is absent; the negative checks therefore pass and `addpcmciaram` publishes the configured Gayle RAM range via `AddMemList` without another card-presence test (`card_init.c:20-32,60-65`). This is conditional on physical removal during that precise tuple-read window; no hardware event was exercised. The earlier withdrawal based on the format/geometry gates was incorrect because those are expected to be absent for RAM cards.

UIKit event-task signal-mask recheck (2026-10-13; OD2639): read all of `eventtask.c`, then traced `NewCreateTask` without `TASKTAG_TASKMSGPORT` through the `MEMF_CLEAR` task descriptor template (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:34-38`), `NewAddTask` signal initialization (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:241-252`), and `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc` setup (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The fresh task reserves only the system signal bits `0x0000FFFF`; `AllocTaskSignal(-1)` selects an available bit above them. This closes the speculative signal-allocation-exhaustion lead for this selected creation path, while confirming OD2639’s distinct pointer-publication interval. No iOS scheduling or interrupt was run.

UIKit event-worker signal and interrupt teardown recheck (2026-11-01; OD2639 retained; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): re-read `arch/all-ios/hidd/uikit/eventtask.c:31-75` and the `uikit_hiddclass.c` create/publish path. `EventTask` is entered through `NewCreateTask`, so its first `AllocSignal(-1)` operates on a fresh task whose user signal bits are free (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:241-252`; `prepareexecbase.c:319`); no exhaustion route is established. The worker stores the resulting mask before installing the VBL handler, waits on that mask plus Ctrl-C, and removes the handler after the stop signal. This does not close the separately tracked interval in which the interrupt can use `base->eventTask` before the parent publishes it (OD2639), nor establish UIKit callback/thread behavior.
