Generic I²C class/caller completion recheck (2026-10-15): reread the full selected `workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c` and `i2cdeviceclass.c` bodies, then searched all in-tree timing-attribute setters and device-method callers. This confirms existing OD1151/OD1817 distinctions for zero and concurrent timing updates, OD1864's unit-conversion boundary, OD2585's ignored per-device timing overrides, and OD2586's 10-bit read sequence; no selected in-tree caller supplies a zero rise/fall delay or per-device timing override. The selected Sam440 bus and RTC paths use default timing, while VMware/Nouveau compatibility buses supply timeout values but leave hold/rise-fall defaults intact. Rechecked transaction cleanup on failed address/byte operations, semaphore nesting/balance, timer request reuse against DoIO/WaitIO, and failed timer-open disposal; no new defect established. Generic WriteBytes/WriteVec locking and the WriteWord length mismatch remain existing conditional public-method candidates without checked in-tree clients. No timer, bus or device operation was run. Source-only.

Generic I²C compatibility-adapter direct-caller matrix follow-up (2026-10-22; no new OD): reconciled Nouveau's selected `i2c_bit_algo` bit-banged adapter plus the separate VMware DisplayPort AUX adapter, and searched all in-tree `i2c_transfer`, `i2c_master_recv`, `i2c_master_send`, and dynamic-client creation call sites (`workbench/hidds/{nouveau,vmwaresvga}/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:19-164,184-198,238-262`; Nouveau bit-bus registration at `drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/i2c/bus.c:247-250`; VMware's AUX-backed calls at `drm/display/drm_dp_helper.c:2408` and `drm/drm_edid.c:2179`). The active Nouveau `nvkm_rdi2cr`/`nv_rd16i2cr` readers use the supported two-message write/read shape, `nvkm_wri2cr`, BIOS writes, and DRM SCDC writes use the supported single-message write shape; VMware's selected EDID/SCDC reads use the AUX transfer route. A possible unsupported single-read path in Nouveau's `i2c_bit_xfer` has no current selected client route: its only `i2c_master_recv` callers are chip-client methods, but this compatibility layer's `i2c_new_client_device` always returns `ERR_PTR(-ENODEV)` (`linux_i2c.c:196-200`), and no other client constructor is selected. The Nouveau SIL164 secondary-probe caller submits a one-message zero-length write (`dispnv04/i2c/sil164_drv.c:375-389`); however, `sil164_drv.c` is absent from the explicit `AROS_DRM_NVIDIA_SOURCES` list in `workbench/hidds/nouveau/sources.drm.mak:81-115`, so this probe is not part of the selected HIDD build and is not used to claim an in-tree trigger. If compiled independently, its path would reach generic `I2C_Write`, whose `WriteRead` accepts zero write/read lengths without addressing the bus (`i2cdeviceclass.c:82-95`; `i2cclass.c:337-367`) and would report one completed message without probing. `I2C_FUNC_10BIT_ADDR` is not advertised and all selected address-tag constructors are 7-bit shifted addresses; this does not establish an in-tree 10-bit trigger for OD2586. General-call and external-client behavior remain unverified. No adapter, bus or device operation was run; source-only.

PCIUSB root-port reconciliation (2026-10-15; OD2778 consolidated into OD2897; OD2934 detail/index restored 2026-11-07 after anchor cross-check): traced the OHCI and UHCI interrupt producers, root-hub feature/status dispatch, common request delivery and xHCI immediate-completion path. Corrected the UHCI interrupt caller location to `uhci_hcd.c:837-848`. OD2897 now records the shared bitmap lost-update race across all selected HCD families; OD2782 remains separate because it concerns linked-list request mutation. Reconciled the 16-port cap and hub-client bitmap size against the `UWORD` merged bitmap, the two-byte interrupt response and fixed two-byte hub descriptor bitmap, confirming port 16 cannot be signaled or described; added OD2934. No USB hardware, port event or SMP interleaving was run. Source-only.

OHCI local port-count candidate recheck (2026-10-15; historical finding 966 withdrawn): `ohci_hcd.c` reads NDP into `hc_NumPorts`, and `ohciCheckPortStatusChange` indexes 16-entry `hc_PortNum`/`hc_PortChangeMap` arrays up to that count. The OpenHCI 1.0 specification §7.4.1 sets the maximum supported NDP to 15, so a conforming controller remains within bounds; the port-power mask shift is also below the 32-bit width. No valid-device out-of-bounds finding is retained. [OpenHCI 1.0 specification](https://www.cs.usfca.edu/~cruse/cs698s10/hcir1_0a.pdf). Source-only.

PC i8042 OD2336 report reconciliation (2026-10-15): restored the already-ledgered lock-key LED signal mismatch to the detailed report. Rechecked `NewCreateTask`'s initial signal allocation state, `CreateMsgPort`'s timer reply bit, and the controller task's subsequent `AllocSignal`: the normal successful route gets a high allocated bit, builds a shifted Wait mask, but passes/tests the unshifted bit index as a mask. The fallback `SIGBREAKB_CTRL_E` is also stored as an index and passed unshifted. The three IRQ scan-code cases update software LED state and send that malformed mask; the worker cannot match it against its wait mask. i386-PC and x86-64-PC KHIDDS selections include i8042. Restored OD2336; no keypress or hardware was exercised. Source-only.

LinuxInput OD2257 detailed-report reconciliation (2026-10-15): restored the coverage-tracked signal-number/mask handshake entry in the detailed report. The two `AllocSignal(-1)` calls allocate distinct bit indexes, but `create_inputtask` ORs and tests those indexes directly as masks, and the child signals with the raw indexes. When the indexes overlap as masks (for example the standard first pair 16/17), a child buffer-allocation failure's `nok_signal` intersects `ok_signal`; the parent can return the task as initialized. The child returns into AddTask's default `Exec_TaskFinaliser`, which calls `RemTask`, while the parent skips freeing the manually owned task and stack. The HIDD remains optional: `arch/all-linux/mmakefile.src` comments the LinuxInput target out of its default aggregate. No task or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

ACPI button signal caller cross-check (2026-10-15; no new finding): re-read the power hook's `Signal(sigTask, 1 << powerSig)` against the three-signal task's shifted `Wait`/tests. The producer and consumer use masks consistently after the service task publishes its bit indexes; allocation failure and early publication have separate existing OD998/OD2608 coverage. No duplicate signal-index/mask candidate is credited. No firmware event was delivered. Source-only.

Keyboard reset-handler race recheck (2026-10-15; OD2603 retained): re-read `DoIO`/BeginIO dispatch, both keyboard reset-list command handlers, `writeEvents` in immediate and queued-read paths, and VMM/USB/HID temporary-handler callers. The only protection in list mutation is `Disable`/`Enable`, whose selected ExecSMP contract is CPU-local; dispatch traverses and invokes the same list without a shared lock. VMM unregister synchronously removes then frees its published node without waiting for an already-running reset traversal, and the three reset-chord helpers publish a stack node with a NULL callback between Add and Remove. This confirms the report’s independent overlap triggers; no reset event or interleaving was run. Source-only.

PCIUSB root-hub immediate-response race follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2897 strengthened, no new ID): traced `pciusb_dev.c` UHCMD_INTXFER dispatch into `cmdIntXFerRootHub`. When a change map is pending, the routine copies the map to the request buffer and clears the shared bitmap without disabling interrupts; a controller port-change IRQ can run between those operations and have its bit erased on a uniprocessor as well as SMP. The report now distinguishes this immediate lost-update window from the separate ExecSMP race in queued delivery under local-only `Disable()`. No USB request or port event was run. Source-only.

PCIUSB root-hub client-path follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2897 trigger strengthened, no new ID): traced Poseidon root-device enumeration through address assignment and interrupt-pipe creation. The PCIUSB handler stores the root hub address on `SET_ADDRESS`, Poseidon copies the root device address into each pipe, and interrupt endpoints issue `UHCMD_INTXFER`; `cmdIntXFer` recognizes that request as root-hub I/O. This confirms the immediate response race is reachable through the selected hub client path. No hub or USB event was run. Source-only.


Other Drivers card.resource BeginCardAccess caller census (2026-10-15; no new finding): searched all maintained C/header/assembly references. The selected caller is the boot RAM-card probe in `arch/m68k-amiga/card/card_init.c:48`; it ignores the return, but its `CopyTuple` and `IfAmigaXIP` paths independently test current ownership before touching mapped card data. The only other apparent C caller, `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/ata/ata_amiga.c:697`, belongs to `ata_amiga_init`, but that source is not selected: `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/ata/mmakefile.src:8-10` includes only `waitnano`, and the generic ATA source manifest does not name `ata_amiga.c`. The selected `begincardaccess` vector only reports `handle == ownedcard && !removed`; it does not acquire a lock or hold the card present. No independent defect established for the in-tree caller; external callers and hardware-removal timing remain open. No card access was run. Source-only.


Other Drivers USB AddClass caller/error-path follow-up (2026-10-15): added OD2937 after tracing all local method calls through the HID and MassStorage initialization manifests. The void AddClass method has three unchecked pooled allocations before publishing the class node; callers ignore the method result because none exists. This is distinct from OD2201's concurrent list mutation and OD2209's cached library lifetime. No pool failure or HIDD init was induced. Source-only.


Other Drivers USB target-selection correction (2026-10-15; OD2937 scope): corrected the earlier misreading of `#MM` directives as comments. `workbench/devs/USB/mmakefile.src:2-13` defines an active `hidd-usb` aggregate. The generic `workbench-devs-common` list omits USB, but the Sam440 `AROS-sam440-ppc` path selects `hidd-usb` through `kernel-modules-sam440-ppc` (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:4-8,16-52`), and Efika selects its USB package, whose dependency is `hidd-usb` (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/boot/mmakefile.src:4-13,83-91`). OD2937 and the related stack findings therefore apply to those selected platform builds as stated by each trigger; explicit builds are also affected. No build was run. Source-only.


Other Drivers USB disconnect/address caller follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2914 confirmed): traced hub disconnect at `workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:536-547` into `USBDevice::Dispose`. The destructor disposes linked interface objects, releases allocated string buffers, deletes the pipe and timer, then delegates, but does not return `dev->address`; the only in-tree `HIDD_USB_FreeAddress` call remains the failed `usb_SetAddress` path in `USBDevice::New`. The address leak is therefore confirmed for the selected Sam440 and Efika USB package targets. Corrected the finding trigger to name those builds. No hotplug was run. Source-only.


Other Drivers shared input-subsystem producer caller follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2882/OD2883 retained): traced the selected PC i8042 keyboard and mouse producer wrappers. `i8042_classinit.c` caches the `moHW_Input_PushEvent` method for both subsystem objects (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_classinit.c:37-57`); keyboard and mouse event paths invoke those cached methods (`i8042_kbdclass.c:573`; `i8042_mouseps2.c:133-165`). These reach the shared input consumer traversal/pending-event branch at `rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:240-257`. This confirms the selected event producer route for the reported first-registration and disposal races, but does not establish an in-tree cross-CPU first-consumer overlap or consumer teardown overlap. No event or race was run. Source-only.


Other Drivers shared input pending-buffer bound recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): `IHD_PENDING_MAX` is 16 and `IHD_PENDING_EVSIZE` is 8 (`rom/hidds/input/input.h:30-31`). The subsystem stores an event only when its declared event size fits and the pre-consumer queue has remaining capacity; its header explicitly documents that events above the bound and events from subsystems with no declared size are dropped (`input.h:24-28`; `inputsubsystem.c:81-91`). This is an intentional bounded startup-recovery policy, not an unchecked write or an untracked overflow. OD2882 remains the separate SMP handoff race. No buffer saturation was induced. Source-only.


Other Drivers NVMe storage-bus caller census (2026-10-15; OD2876 caller boundary rechecked): a repository-wide call search found only two maintained `HIDD_StorageController_AddBus` invocations, both PCI ATA (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/probe.c:648`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/gayle_ata/probe.c:237`). The NVMe controller instead calls `HW_AddDriver` on its `CLID_Hidd_StorageController` object (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:440-466`), so its constructed bus does not reach the storage-controller bus list. This confirms OD2876 as the reachability blocker for the selected NVMe unit path; request-level candidates such as OD2591 and OD2841 remain conditional on a direct/external `AddBus` route until that registration is corrected. No controller or bus was started. Source-only.


Other Drivers shared input pending-buffer producer race (2026-10-15): added OD2938 after tracing `InputHW__BufferPendingEvent` through both default driver callbacks and direct `PushEvent`, then through `InputHW__HW__AddDriver` to the multi-instance `HW_AddDriver` implementation. Multiple driver objects share the same consumer list and pending count; two pre-consumer producers can reserve the same slot because the count/copy/increment sequence has no cross-CPU synchronization. This is separate from OD2882's producer/consumer-registration interleaving and OD2883's callback-node lifetime race. No checked-in simultaneously active producer pair or event interleaving was found/run. Source-only.

AHI CMD_STOP/START/FLUSH caller census (2026-10-15; OD2450 trigger retained, no new ID): searched maintained C and assembly beneath `workbench/devs/AHI` for IORequest assignments/submission and command use. The AHI device accepts STOP and FLUSH through its immediate `PerformIO` route and START through the queued unit task (`Device/devcommands.c:90-107,329-353`); the only non-implementation textual command names are `Test/examine_ahi/examine_ahi.c` display strings, not submissions. No selected in-tree client issues these three device commands, so OD2450 remains a public direct-client sequence: queue CMD_WRITE while stopped, then AbortIO or FLUSH before the matching START. The implementation documentation describes this API behavior (`devcommands.c:449-484,516-534,882-912`); client ownership and runtime queue behavior remain untested. The signed-priority-128 concern was already withdrawn after tracing SetTaskPri's self-priority comparison; no priority consequence is attributed here. Source-only.

Serial HIDD Start reachability and trigger recheck (2026-10-15; missed restart kick remains unpromoted): confirmed the PC serial HIDD is included in the i386-PC KHIDDS package and the DesignWare UART HIDD is in the OpenSBI RISC-V BSP, but `workbench/devs/serial/mmakefile.src` exposes serial.device only as a direct module target; it is absent from the checked PC `KDEVS`, RISC-V `BSP_DEVS`, and generic `workbench-devs-common` aggregate. A source census found no maintained client submitting `CMD_STOP`/`CMD_START` to this device. The precise restart sequence remains source-confirmed: serial.device calls Start under local Disable (`serial_init.c:652-659`); each HIDD calls WBE before clearing `stopped`, WBE's Write returns zero while stopped, and the selected PC/RISC-V THRI handlers read UART_IIR when the callback returns zero (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:439-456,726-730`; OpenSBI `SerialUnitClass.c:427-444,738-742`). The source does not establish whether this acknowledgement suppresses all future THRE notification on either controller; no independent command client or selected default device package is established. Keep this as an open platform/device contract question, not a confirmed permanent-stall report finding. Native m68k clears `stopped` before its callback. No UART request or IRQ was run. Source-only.


Linux mouse HIDD concurrent-registration recheck (OD1435 restored, 2026-10-15): traced the class's semaphore-protected duplicate check and later publication through legacy HIDD_Input_AddHardwareDriver, InputHW__AddDriver and generic HW__HW__AddDriver. Driver construction occurs before the generic list lock; two concurrent calls can pass the check, publish separate driver objects, and overwrite the event-handler singleton pointer. Either object's Dispose unconditionally clears the pointer. The selected LinuxInput startup performs one registration and no overlapping checked-in caller was found, so report reachability is limited to concurrent public/external registration. No event or registration was run. Source-only.

Linux and PC keyboard mapping reconciliation (OD2707–OD2708, 2026-10-15): restored the two concrete findings referenced in the coverage rows but absent from the report. The report now records F12-as-right-Amiga and the keypad multiply/minus/divide raw-code mismatches. The PC table explicitly documents the F12 substitution; no keyboard event was run.

Linux keyboard table semantic reconciliation (2026-10-15): corrected OD2708 to identify Linux/PC keypad divide as the abstract right-parenthesis code `0x5b`, not an undefined value. Restored OD2734 in narrowed form for dropped Scroll Lock/SysRq and misidentified Linefeed events. Removed NumLock from the defect claim after confirming `0x5a` is the legacy keypad-left-parenthesis abstract code and matches the selected PC table. Populated default-table mappings are now semantically compared against the abstract/public raw-key definitions; caller/device behavior remains untested.

The Linux keyboard semantic pass additionally confirmed that distinct Linux `KEY_LINEFEED` (101) and `KEY_PAUSE` (119) both map to `RAWKEY_PAUSE`; OD2734 includes this misidentification, conditional on a host reporting KEY_LINEFEED.

Linux input removal lifetime reconciliation (OD2260, 2026-10-15): restored the detailed report entry from the coverage notes after tracing both keyboard/mouse worker dispatch helpers, their Dispose methods, generic HW_RemoveDriver, and the selected in-tree removal call sites. Linux evdev bitmap-size reconciliation (OD1869, 2026-10-15): restored the finding in the detailed report. Verified `EV_MAX == 31`, the EVIOCGBIT size field is a byte count, `LONG` is 32 bits in AROS, UnixIO forwards the pointer unchanged, and native 64-bit evdev returns `BITS_TO_LONGS(EV_MAX) * sizeof(long) == 8` bytes. Qualified that the precise stack neighbor and resulting behavior depend on compiler layout; no ioctl was run.

Shared keyboard-HIDD caller pass (2026-10-15; no new candidate): read `rom/hidds/kbd/kbdclass.c` completely and traced the selected `keyboard.device` consumer into its callback registration and shared input consumer list. Shared input subsystem body/caller pass (2026-10-15; OD2882, OD2883, OD2938 rechecked; no additional finding): reread every function in `inputsubsystem.c`; confirmed the 16×8 pending-copy bounds, keyboard event-size opt-in, and mouse zero-size behavior against both event structures and subsystem constructors. The first-consumer cross-CPU handoff and consumer-disposal traversal remain OD2882/OD2883. PCIPC failed-init cleanup reconciliation (OD2759, 2026-10-15): restored the detailed finding from the coverage ledger after tracing priority-0 Utility open, priority-10 failure branches, generated rollback and both expunge callbacks. No failure was induced.

Mediator/Prometheus resource-allocation failure pass (OD2941, 2026-10-15): traced both identical helper copies through their selected board initializers, BAR scan and disposal. Mediator/Prometheus class-init allocation failure pass (OD2942, 2026-10-15): verified `OOP_NewObject` is unchecked before the `OOP_DoMethod` macro dereferences the PCI root object in both selected hardware-driver classes. Mediator/Prometheus Root::New rollback pass (OD2943, 2026-10-15): traced OOP_NewObject initial class-object argument through the pre-superclass failure branches and the HIDD/BaseMeta Root::Dispose chain. Both drivers dispose `o` before an instance exists. No module or failure path was run.

Mediator/Prometheus Root::New allocation rollback pass (OD2944, 2026-10-15): checked setup ordering, root allocation failure, the `HW_AddDriver` NULL cleanup, and both instance Dispose paths. PCI/ConfigDev state is changed before allocation; Prometheus resource lists also rely on Dispose. DWMAC transmit queue synchronization candidate recheck (2026-10-15; no additional finding): traced `DWMAC_TXIntF`'s lockless queue walk against `PutMsg`/`InternalPutMsg`, the write-port PA_SOFTINT action, `DWMAC_TXComplete`'s ring-reopen `Cause`, and SoftIntDispatch. A queue-port spinlock would be needed if these routines ran concurrently on multiple Exec CPUs. The selected DWMAC module is RISC-V64/OpenSBI only (`workbench/devs/networks/dwmac/mmakefile.src:16-20`); configure enables the platform SMP trampoline for this target but does not define `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` (`configure.in:2202-2229`; generic Exec SMP is separately gated), so the selected build has one Exec CPU. On that path, `PutMsg` protects the list update with local `Disable`, the producer is the single unit task, and the softint consumer runs serially; the hardware TX callback changes ring state and can queue a later softint but does not mutate the message list. Thus no independent selected queue-list race is established. This does not alter OD3225, the distinct BCM GENET RX-list synchronization issue on Raspberry Pi. No device or interrupt was run. Source-only.

HID constructor rollback follow-up (OD2947, 2026-10-15): traced the failed `HID::New` return through `OOP_DoSuperMethod`, Root instance allocation/object counting, `OOP_NewObject` return behavior, and USB class discovery. Confirmed later setup failure frees pooled members and decrements `lib_OpenCnt` but does not dispose the already allocated object; USB discovery retains no object after NULL. Added the low-memory configuration-descriptor allocation path as a concrete trigger. Existing OD2946 remains the distinct successful return after `AddInterrupt` failure. No allocation failure or USB device was exercised. Source-only.

Other Drivers heading reconciliation (2026-10-15): recounted the detailed report after OD2947; it contains 329 unique numbered OD headings. The AROS.md index count now matches. Broader selected-source and caller review remains incomplete. Source-only.

HID partial-object cleanup feasibility check (OD2947, 2026-10-15): checked the suggested unwind against `HID::Dispose` and both selected controllers. HID disposal always forwards `intr_pipe` to `RemInterrupt`; UHCI `RemInterrupt` dereferences `p->p_Intr` for NULL (`uhciclass.c:702-715`), while OHCI returns FALSE for the NULL pipe. Therefore the finding now calls for a partial-construction rollback or a null-safe destructor, rather than blindly invoking the current virtual Dispose path. No object was created or disposed. Source-only.

USBDevice failed-address constructor follow-up (OD2948, 2026-10-15): traced the zero-address path through `usb_SetAddress`, `OOP_CoerceMethod` disposal, the no-NULL-check descriptor wrapper and final open-count path. Verified current in-tree `USB::NewDevice` passes its allocated nonzero address and the OHCI/UHCI root-hub constructors pass address 1, so the concrete zero-address trigger is external/future. Kept separate from OD2910's exhaustion sentinel. No transfer failure or device was exercised. Source-only.

PC i8042 keyboard constructor completion-signal follow-up (OD2266/OD2320/OD2335; no additional candidate, 2026-10-15): reread the worker startup returns, constructor wait, and Exec Wait/semaphore signal semantics (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:139-263,295-325`; `rom/exec/wait.c:70-141`; `rom/exec/semaphores.c:121-154`). Every pre-IRQ worker failure sets `LEDSigBit` to -1 before signaling, and the parent uses the resulting sentinel to take the superclass-only cleanup path; NewCreateTask failure with no worker remains OD2320. A successful keyboard reset followed by a NULL IRQ handle still reports success, retained as OD2266 (cross-referenced to EK815); successful-object worker lifetime remains OD2335. The parent waits on reserved `SIGF_SINGLE` without first clearing it, so an unrelated signal to the creator could make Wait return early in principle. This pass did not identify a selected in-tree producer that signals this constructor task during that interval; no separate caller-qualified defect is promoted. No signal, task-creation, or IRQ-allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

PC i8042 scan-code decoder bounds follow-up (OD2809/OD2707/OD2708 at that pass; no new candidate, 2026-10-15): reread `i8042_kbd_process_irq_key` against both selected translation tables and `keys.h` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:363-432`; `stdkeytable.h:5-7`; `e0keytable.h:5-7`). The decoder strips the break bit before lookup and bounds-checks against the 89-entry standard and 94-entry E0 arrays; malformed and unmapped entries retain `NOKEY` and return before event dispatch. The E1 Pause path only advances on the expected 1D then 45 codes and clears its prefix on other codes. No out-of-range table access or separate sequence-state defect was established. The Scroll Lock case mismatch was subsequently promoted as OD11032; key-map value defects remain OD2707-OD2708. No keyboard event was generated. Source-only.

PC i8042 Ctrl-Alt-Delete reset-lock cross-check (2026-10-15; suspected deadlock not promoted): `ShutdownA` is called from the IRQ handler path (`i8042_kbd_irq_handler` -> `i8042_kbd_process_irq_key`), and the PC timer reset callback removes its IRQ token. The apparent self-deadlock against `kb_IntrSpinLock` does not hold for selected PC builds: `arch/all-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src` selects the PC `addirqhandler.c` override, whose `krnRunIRQHandlers` does not hold that generic read lock; the write lock in `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c` therefore has no same-chain reader to wait on in this path. The broader supervisor/interrupt-context contract for executing the reset callback chain remains open; no further consequence is promoted without a concrete selected failure. No reset was run. Source-only.

PCI Command/Status W1C follow-up (OD2949, 2026-10-15): traced generic `WriteConfigWord`, the BCM2712 override and `PCIE_WriteConfig` into the full-dword config write, then confirmed `isIO`/`isMEM`/`isMaster`/`paletteSnoop` and selected HDAudio Command updates as ordinary callers. A set W1C Status error can be cleared by that write. The impact remains conditional on a latched error at update time; no device was exercised. Additional caller pass: the shared NVHDMI `hda_hidd.c` repeats the HDAudio Command update, while the inspected VMware/Nouveau compatibility writes target PCIe Device Control, PMCSR, and other device-specific offsets rather than `PCICS_COMMAND`; no separate selected Command-write route was found there. Other PCI backends and direct callers remain pending. Source-only.

Other Drivers count reconciliation correction (2026-10-15): a fresh unique-heading recount after OD2949 finds 331 detailed findings (OD headings are not contiguous); corrected AROS.md. The earlier 329-after-OD2947 reconciliation note is historical and did not include later restored entries. Coverage remains incomplete. Source-only.

BCM2712 PCI MSI/MSI-X follow-up (2026-10-15; OD921/OD922/OD1145/OD1146 rechecked, no new finding): re-read vector allocation, capability selection, table bounds, mapping length, table programming, interrupt enable/disable and release (`driverclass.c:405-434,436-452,461-667`). The MSI-X mapping starts at the table base and requests `(first + count) * 16` bytes, which includes entries through `first + count - 1`; it is not short when `first` is nonzero. Global-versus-device-local indexing remains OD921, and `MapPCI` validating only the start address remains OD922. Release disables the capability before returning vector bits; the next successful obtain rewrites the allocated entries, so stale table contents alone do not establish another defect. A suspected W1C side effect from `ISAEnable`/`VGAEnable` was rejected: bridge control is at 0x3e, while bridge Status aliases the standard Status word at 0x06, so they are not in the same config dword. No endpoint, vector allocation, or interrupt was exercised. Source-only.

OHCI initialization/constructor pass (2026-10-15; OD2953–OD2956; OD2950 broadened): read all of `ohci_init.c` and `ohciclass.c`, traced the generic PCI enumeration callback and failed-init expunge behavior, and recorded the excess-device timer leak plus unchecked controller-construction DMA allocations. Other Drivers detailed count is 339 after four new findings. No target build, controller, allocation failure or runtime path was exercised. Source-only.

OHCI timer-path reconciliation (2026-10-15; OD2955): restored the previously coverage-only nullable timer finding after rechecking both selected consumers: BIOS handoff in PCI enumeration and power/reset delays in the OHCI root constructor. `ohci_CreateTimer` returns NULL on allocation/open failure and `ohci_Delay` dereferences it immediately. Other Drivers detailed count is 338. No timer failure or controller was exercised. Source-only.

OHCI hub-method range pass (2026-10-15; OD2956): read all of `ohcihub.c` and traced the selected USBHub worker, which iterates ports from 1 through the descriptor count. Three OHCI methods omit lower and/or upper bound checks before indexing the MMIO port-status array; recorded this only for invalid public HIDD callers because the selected in-tree worker supplies valid 1-based ports. Other Drivers detailed count is 339. No method or controller was run. Source-only.

OHCI interrupt-record disposal pass (2026-10-15; OD2958): traced `ohci_intr_t` allocation in AddInterrupt through the selected HID destructor RemInterrupt/DeletePipe sequence. Ordinary-pipe RemInterrupt is unimplemented and DeletePipe has no record-free path, leaving one pooled record per successfully registered HID endpoint disposed. OHCI completion-versus-disposal pass (2026-10-15; OD2959): traced the HCCA WDH done-list walk and its TD-to-pipe/ED/callback dereferences against HID Dispose and OHCI DeletePipe. The teardown unlinks/stops the endpoint but neither drains an already completed TD nor synchronizes the interrupt handler before freeing its referenced objects; local Disable covers only short list edits. No completion, disconnect or interrupt interleaving was run. Source-only.

OHCI completion-race target selection check (2026-10-15; OD2959): verified x86_64-pc actively selects `kernel-package-usb` in its boot manifest and builds SMP bootstrap code; unlike i386-pc, whose USB package edge is commented out. This establishes a selected SMP-capable USB build route for the conditional OHCI task/IRQ overlap. PCIUSB reset-callback close/reopen recheck (2026-10-15; OD2192 restored to detailed report): traced the reset node embedded in each PCIController through UHCI/OHCI/EHCI init, `Close_Unit`/`pciFreeUnit`, and the next `Open_Unit`/`pciAllocUnit`. Close never calls `RemResetCallback` and retains controller records; reopen calls `AddResetCallback` on the same node. Exec `AddResetCallback` unconditionally enqueues, and `Enqueue` does not remove an already-linked node; reset traversal has no cycle guard. Restored OD2192 with list-corruption and conditional traversal consequences. No device lifecycle or reset was run. Source-only.

VirtIO/NVMe/PCI xHCI reset-disposal reconciliation (2026-10-15; OD2372 restored, OD2960 added): confirmed VirtIO's registered controller is publicly removable with `HW_RemoveDriver`, and its disposer frees the instance without `RemResetCallback`; confirmed PCI xHCI expunge frees the `PCIController` containing its registered reset node without unlinking it. Both leave reset-list nodes in freed owner storage, with no in-tree removal callers found. Re-read NVMe separately: its Dispose override does not chain to Root, so public removal leaks the OOP instance/object count and does not free that reset node; recorded as OD2960 instead of repeating the stale-node-UAF claim. No device removal or reset was performed. Source-only.

Under the documented in-range caller contract and non-overflowing sample counts, every processed endpoint stays within the requested frame interval; first-frame interpolation uses cached data rather than an out-of-range adjacent read. OD4165 records the separate `CalcSamples` count overflow at low playback rates. Allocation extent and 8/16-bit variants remain pending. No audio was rendered. Source-only.

AHI 8/16-bit lofi source-index pass (2026-10-15; no new finding): reviewed all sixteen forward/reverse byte/word mono/stereo routines against `_AHI_SetSound` range construction and `CalcSamples`. For contract-valid ranges and a representable count, each frame index and both interleaved lanes remain within the requested source interval; these routines do not read interpolation neighbors. OD4165 records the `CalcSamples` sample-count overflow at low playback rates. Storage extent and destination allocation remain open. No audio was rendered. Source-only.

AHI native mixer destination-size pass (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced the timing-enabled RecalcBuff path's 65,535-frame clamp, selected frame sizes, padding and optional post-processing doubling against Mix's clear/write extent and wet/dry destination offset. Its maximum arithmetic fits the local signed int length and each pass stays within its reserved block. The AHIACF_NOTIMING path bypasses RecalcBuff, but no checked-in AHISF_MIXING provider omits AHISF_TIMING, so it is not reached by the audited in-tree providers. Hardware subdriver buffer allocation and WarpUp allocation remain open. No mixer or audio backend was run. Source-only.

AHI no-timing branch reachability recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced the AHIACF_NOTIMING selection and no-timing sizing branch, then searched every checked-in AHI provider's AHISF_MIXING return path. Each implementation that advertises mixing also advertises AHISF_TIMING, including Paula; no in-tree build-selected provider reaches the branch. Out-of-tree provider behavior remains outside scope. OHCI ClearPortFeature signal-ownership pass (2026-10-15; OD2962): traced the custom `PA_SOFTINT` port initialization, zeroed Root instance, change-feature cleanup, and generic hub-worker callers. The port never allocates a signal bit, yet cleanup clears `1 << mp_SigBit`; its zero bit is `SIGF_ABORT`, so a caller with that signal pending loses it. The source path is clear, but no selected in-tree abort producer for the hub worker was found; trigger remains caller-conditional. No port or signal was exercised. Source-only.

UHCI Root::New timer-request failure follow-up (OD2964, 2026-10-15): rechecked constructor allocation and open paths. The embedded-port VBLANK `CreateIORequest` result is passed directly to `OpenDevice`; Exec dereferences the request at `rom/exec/opendevice.c:96`. UHCI Root::Dispose timer lifecycle pass (OD2972; 2026-10-15): traced HubInterrupt rearming the embedded-port VBLANK request, timer AbortIO replying through ReplyMsg, and the destructor deleting the request/object without WaitIO or draining the port; the callback dereferences that request after GetMsg. Also confirmed the VBLANK request is not CloseDevice’d although the adjacent microhertz request is. UHCI Root::Dispose controller-stop pass (OD2973; 2026-10-15): compared the destructor stop/free sequence against Root::New and uhci_run. Added a conditional DMA-after-free candidate; disposal reachability remains unestablished. No controller teardown was run. Source-only.

UHCI transfer timeout and completion race trace (OD2974; 2026-10-15): followed ControlTransfer/BulkTransfer timeout reclamation against the interrupt handler’s ControlLS/ControlFS/Bulk chain walk, TD frees and signal path. UHCI control-transfer endian/caller trace (OD2975; 2026-10-15): traced `USBDevice::GetDescriptor` and initial enumeration request construction into the UHCI helper. Added OD2975 with Sam440 UHCI package and OHCI-only backend caveat. No big-endian transfer was run. Source-only.

Other Drivers DWMAC opener-list synchronization recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced `DWMAC_RXPacket` through `DWMAC_RXProcess` to `DWMAC_IntHandlerF` (`workbench/devs/networks/dwmac/dwmac_unit.c:284-386,548-567`) and compared its `dwu_Openers` traversal with `DWMAC_Open`/`DWMAC_Close` list publication/removal (`workbench/devs/networks/dwmac/dwmac_init.c:261-280`). The mutators use `Disable()` around list changes. Although local interrupt masking alone would not serialize another CPU on ExecSMP, the selected RISC-V64 OpenSBI kernel explicitly states SMP bring-up does not yet exist (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:42`; `kernel_traps.c:216`), so no supported cross-CPU race is established for this DWMAC configuration. The unit worker also does not call RX processing; the hardware interrupt path does. No runtime interrupt/close interleaving was run. Source-only.
DWMAC transmit-size and ring-buffer reconciliation (2026-10-15; no new finding): rechecked `DWMAC_TXIntF` against `CmdWrite` and `DWMAC_ConfigMTU`. The handler rejects non-raw payloads above MTU and raw payloads above MTU plus the Ethernet header (`dwmac_handler.c:84-110`); the queued transmitter adds the header only for non-raw frames, pads to `ETH_ZLEN`, and stores at most the accepted data length plus header. `DWMAC_BufSize` rounds `MTU + header + FCS` up to a 64-byte boundary (`dwmac_unit.c:924-988`), leaving room for the minimum-frame padding and keeping accepted raw frames in bounds. TX descriptors publish only after buffer construction; ring-full state stalls the request port and TX completion re-enables it. No out-of-range TX buffer write established on these checked paths. Raw short-frame semantics and DMA visibility still depend on SANA-II and platform contracts; no packet/device was used. Source-only.

UHCI header completion and zero-length transfer reconciliation (OD2976 confirmed; 2026-10-15): completed the previously partial 363-line `uhci.h` pass, comparing queue and TD structure layouts, register/token masks and length encoders with all local uses. Confirmed existing OD2976 precisely: a zero-length bulk call constructs no TD then dereferences its null local TD at the unconditional IOC write. Zero-length control status TDs intentionally use UHCI's 11-bit zero-byte length encoding and are a separate path. No new finding added; no transfer was run. Source-only.

VirtIO BeginIO synchronous-error/list recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced both read/write and flush queue-submission failure returns into the outer completion cleanup. Their helpers remove the request before submission, so the failure branch can reach a second `Remove`; however, the only `au_IOs` references in the selected VirtIO source are initialization, insertion and removal (`virtio_unitclass.c:46`; `virtio_io.c:76-79,113-120,147-152,267-270`), with no traversal or teardown consumer. The duplicate splice is therefore not credited as a present caller-visible defect. Rechecked the geometry buffer clear (`SetMem(geom,0,len)`) against the fixed `DriveGeometry` response size and found no selected caller passing a larger length; oversized-buffer semantics remain unresolved, so no finding is promoted. Existing OD2390/2396 bounds and OD2460 read-only status remain separate. No I/O or request interleaving was run; source-only.

PCIPC MSI non-power-of-two selected-caller recheck (OD2982 retained, trigger narrowed; 2026-10-15): AHCI and xHCI request exactly one vector, and Nouveau's `pci_enable_msi` also requests one. NVMe requests up to `KrnGetCPUCount()` and negotiates that queue count, but `hwqcnt` remains initialized to one (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:273-279,324-328,364`) and its selected queue setup/query uses only the first MSI vector (`:383-386`). Thus the PCIPC count-rounding/alignment defect remains supported for direct multi-vector HIDD requests; the inspected selected NVMe path does not establish delivery on an unreserved higher vector. No PCI device or interrupt was exercised. Source-only.

Generic PCI capability-offset boundary recheck (OD2981 retained; 2026-10-15): reread both walkers in `rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:116-165` against config-space limits and the PCIPC/NVMe/xHCI callers. Conventional offsets are four-byte aligned and values below `0x40` terminate the chain; extended offsets are bounded by the 12-bit field and loop limit. The confirmed defect remains the lack of cycle detection for conventional and extended chains; no additional boundary candidate established. No PCI config space was queried. Source-only.

AHCI per-port worker failure/attach cleanup recheck (OD2559 retained; 2026-10-15): searched every `AP_SIGF_THREAD_SYNC` access; `ahci_os_start_port` sets it before `kthread_create`, and only `ahci_port_thread` clears it (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_aros.c:193,222-228`). The wrapper returns `ENOMEM` for `NewCreateTask == NULL`, but the caller discards the result; `ahci_port_alloc` returns zero, so `ahci_pci_attach` reaches its post-interrupt poll with the bit still set. The detach cleanup is reached only through earlier nonzero attach errors and cannot recover this path. Confirms OD2559; no task failure or attach was induced. Source-only.

PCIPC legacy MSI zero-minimum countdown trace (OD2993, 2026-10-15): verified the legacy loop retains an explicit minimum of zero, calls KrnAllocIRQ with count zero after positive allocation failures, and wraps its UWORD counter indefinitely. The selected PC allocator forwards zero to core_APIC_AllocMSI, whose contiguous-run test cannot satisfy a zero-count request. MSI-X normalizes zero to one; all five selected direct HIDD clients request minimum one. Added OD2993 with the direct/external trigger qualified. No allocation or hardware was run. Other Drivers count: 404 OD. Source-only.

Both allocation and transfer failures are ignored before parser use; documented the null-buffer and invalid-buffer conditions in the detailed report. The finding therefore requires another exposed matching EHCI controller and is not established on those current routes. No controller was run. Source-only.


BCM GENET OD2933 caller/variant recheck (2026-10-15): distinguished the unit task queue path from the direct `BeginIO` fast path. A successful `AttemptSemaphore` invokes `BCMGENET_HandleRequest` in the caller task, while RX processing runs later in the unit task without `bgu_Lock`; tracker/multicast removals can free traversed nodes. Open/Close also mutate/free opener nodes outside that semaphore. Verified Exec documents `Disable` as CPU-local on SMP and configure enables `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for the Raspberry Pi `smp` variant, where the Workbench SoC aggregate selects bcmgenet. Tightened OD2933 to those supported paths; no request or hardware was run. Source-only.


BCM GENET IRQ-signal failure candidate withdrawn (OD2932, 2026-10-15): `BCMGENET_UnitTask` creates two message ports before its explicit `AllocSignal(-1)`. `CreateMsgPort` allocates one signal per successful port (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:50-74`); `AddTask` initializes a zero `tc_SigAlloc` from `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:249-251`), initialized to `0xFFFF` (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). This leaves the high 16 bits available, and the private unit task consumes at most three before requiring its IRQ bit; no selected startup call allocates the other bits. Thus signal exhaustion is not reachable through the selected task-creation path. Removed OD2932 from the detailed candidate count. No task was started or signal allocated. Source-only.

No new candidate established; ordinary ATA PIO read/write completion/error ordering remains open. No packet was sent. Source-only.

ATA ATAPI direct-SCSI/block caller trace (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced direct request initialization and validation plus READ/WRITE(10) wrapper chunking (`lowlevel.c:1112-1171,2389-2470`). Nonzero lengths require a data pointer, CDB length is bounded to the announced packet size, read/write chunk counts stay within the 16-bit READ/WRITE(10) field, and short successful data phases return an error. No additional candidate established in this slice. Packet data-length semantics and ordinary ATA PIO read/write IRQ completion remain open. No request was sent. Source-only.

ATA ATAPI readiness-probe failure trace (OD3000, 2026-10-15): confirmed `atapi_TestUnitOK` ignores DirectSCSI failure and reads a zero sense key as media-ready, including the initially absent-media state. Traced this transition into initialization, periodic removable-media checking, TD_CHANGESTATE and the read/write guards. Added a conditional false-present finding. No device or readiness request was run. Other Drivers report count: 415 OD. Source-only.

ATA PIO-write non-DRQ early-return recheck (OD2998 expanded, 2026-10-15): confirmed the completed initial readiness poll returns `HFERR_BadStatus` when DRQ is clear but leaves the previously installed `ata_IRQPIOWrite` handler active, just like the timeout return. The existing dispatcher and request reply path make this a second trigger for the same delayed-IRQ use of a completed request buffer. Expanded OD2998 instead of adding a duplicate. Read timeout path clears its handler. No status condition or IRQ was induced. Source-only.

ATA request queue and AbortIO trace (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced slow BeginIO publication, bus-task dequeue/dispatch/reply, and AbortIO removal under the selected port lock (`ata.c:768-896,1138-1161`). AbortIO can remove and reply only a request still linked on the port; otherwise it reports failure and leaves the active transaction alone. Slow requests leave per-unit UNITF_ACTIVE/UNITF_INTASK set, but source-wide search found no maintained reader of those unit flags; bus serialization uses separate `ab_Flags`. No present functional effect established, so no candidate added. Remaining command-handler and caller audit is open. Source-only.

ATA shared-port CMD_FLUSH scope trace (OD3001, 2026-10-15): confirmed CMD_FLUSH is immediate and drains the shared bus MsgPort unconditionally; the queue carries requests for both master/slave units. The Exec API specifies pending-command flush for the addressed unit. Added conditional cross-unit cancellation finding. No request was sent. Other Drivers report count: 416 OD. Source-only.

ATA change-interrupt SMP list trace (OD3002, 2026-10-15): verified AddChangeInt, RemChangeInt and TestChanged all rely on Forbid without a shared SMP spinlock. Exec Forbid is processor-local on ExecSMP; ForeachNode follows the current request’s ln_Succ after Cause, and selected FAT cleanup frees the request after synchronous Remove. Added conditional concurrent list/request-lifetime finding for x86-64-PC smp ATA builds. No SMP event was run. Other Drivers report count: 417 OD. Source-only.

ATA NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY size-contract trace (OD3003, 2026-10-15): verified the handler writes every NSDeviceQueryResult field and reports sizeof without checking io_Length. Cross-checked all searched selected storage/filesystem query callers, including BHFormat and SFS; they allocate and declare the complete structure, so trigger is limited to short direct-client buffers. Recorded the 514-byte TD_GETGEOMETRY branch as unassigned because no checked-in caller or confirmed contract was found. No query was sent. Other Drivers report count: 418 OD. Source-only.


ATA ordinary PIO IRQ data-count and completion trace (2026-10-15; no new finding): re-read `ata_IRQSetHandler`, `ata_IRQPIORead`, `ata_PIOWriteBlk`, `ata_IRQPIOWrite`, `ata_IRQNoData`, `ata_WaitBusyTO`, and the 32-/48-bit sector and multiple-sector callers (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:185-295,440-560,1938-2304`). For selected sector sizes and bounded command counts, initial per-interrupt lengths are the smaller of the multiple-sector block and remaining byte count; handlers advance pointer/remaining count and signal completion only after the final block. Read missing-DRQ and write premature completion set `HFERR_BadStatus`, while common no-data completion clears the bus handler and preserves the error. Ordinary interrupt timeout clears the handler; IDENTIFY fake completion is a separate path that samples status once and then reuses that sample while the handler remains installed (OD10307 below). No new buffer-bound or stale-handler path established in the normal IRQ completion paths. The first PIO-write poll still has the separately tracked OD2998 early exits. Whether a device status with ERR and DRQ simultaneously should trigger transfer suppression remains a protocol/device-semantics question and is not promoted as a finding from source alone. No ATA command or hardware was run. Source-only.


AHCI controller and bus reset-callback lifetime reconciliation (2026-10-15; OD2891 expanded): traced per-port `HW_AddDriver` registration and bus `Root__New` callback installation through a later implemented-port allocation failure, `ahci_pci_detach`, driver-list retention, and Exec reset dispatch. Confirmed successful bus objects remain registered under the controller while `ahci_port_free` releases their `ab_Port`; `ahciBus_Reset` later passes that stale pointer to port helpers. Expanded OD2891 to include this unconditional bus callback path separately from the MSI-only controller callback path. No allocation failure, bus removal, hardware or reset was run. Report count remains 418 OD. Source-only.


AHCI legacy IRQ registration failure trace (OD3004; 2026-10-15): followed `pci_alloc_1intr` legacy selection through `bus_setup_intr`, Exec `AddIntServer`, PC `KrnAddIRQHandler` allocation failure and `bus_teardown_intr`/`RemIntServer`. Confirmed setup returns success even when the stored kernel token is NULL; a later teardown passes NULL to `KrnRemIRQHandler`, which dereferences before checking. Added OD3004 with selected PC legacy-IRQ conditions. No allocation failure, I/O, detach or hardware was exercised. Other Drivers report count: 419 OD. Source-only.


AHCI library startup and failed-init reconciliation (2026-10-15; no new finding): re-read the complete `AHCI_Init` path, option parsing, optional log-resource branch, pool construction, OOP attr/method base acquisition, root-object fallback and generated INITLIB rollback. Confirmed DISK-321 for partial attribute-base acquisition retention; explicit Utility opens are closed on each local failure path. The optional `logInitialise` allocation failure is the shared API defect OD2185 and is not duplicated. No module initialization or allocation failure was run. Source-only.


AHCI pending media-notification list SMP recheck (OD2866 expanded; 2026-10-15): compared the monitor’s `Forbid`-only traversal with BeginIO’s `sim_Lock`-protected insert/remove and checked Exec’s explicit ExecSMP semantics. Expanded the existing TD_REMCHANGEINT relinking finding to include this independent overlapping-traversal trigger under the same broken list protocol. No concurrent request or media event was run. Source-only.


KMS converter finding/report reconciliation (2026-10-15; OD2355-OD2358 restored): re-read `OpenKeymap`, `parsekeymapseg`, the selected keymap writer, and DOS `UnLoadSeg`/internal segment freeing. Restored OD2355 for source-segment ownership on rejection and either conversion result; OD2356 for duplicate cleanup treating raw `AllocMem` output as a LoadSeg segment; OD2357 for high-descriptor sizing omitting copy padding (representable, with no shipped fixture established); and OD2358 for fixed-field reads without a loaded-segment extent check. No keymap was generated or loaded, and no malformed file, duplicate-load race or allocator failure was exercised. Report count: 423 OD. Source-only.

ATA packet-device read/write and PIO interrupt slice (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced `cmd_Read64`/`cmd_Write64` into the unit callbacks, confirmed packet units retain the initialized `ata_STUB_IO64` callbacks, and read `atapi_Read`/`atapi_Write`, `atapi_SendPacket`, `atapi_DirectSCSI`, and both ATAPI PIO DRQ handlers. PIO read/write cap data access at the remaining caller length and drain/pad the rest of the device-announced block; completion reports the bounded amount transferred. No independent defect established in these paths. Broader ATA command dispatch, normal ATA PIO ordering, and selected client contracts remain open. No packet or hardware transfer was run. Source-only.

ATA drive-fault and polled completion status follow-up (OD3007 added, 2026-10-15): traced bit 5 recognition in the missing-IRQ detector through `ata_IRQNoData` and DMA completion; DF-only completion leaves `au_cmd_error` zero. In `ATA=poll`, the final status is returned in `stout` but `ata_exec_cmd` does not inspect it, so an ERR/DF result can also be dropped absent an IRQ callback. `common_SetXferMode` consumes this command result; OD2997 remains the distinct unconditional READ/WRITE MULTIPLE setup consequence. No device or command was run. Source-only.

ATA/ATAPI drive-fault completion follow-up (OD3007 expanded, 2026-10-15): traced PACKET terminal status through `atapi_SendPacket` and `atapi_DirectSCSI`. The terminal classifier checks data-request, CHECK/ERR and handler error but not bit-5 DF; a DF-only final status with no handler error therefore returns packet success and Direct SCSI success. Expanded OD3007 to include the packet route. No device or packet was exercised. Source-only.

ATA device command-dispatch body/caller reconciliation (2026-10-15; no new OD): reread `cmd_Reset` through `cmd_TRIM`, the 32-/64-bit command tables, `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` handling and `BeginIO` quick/queued dispatch (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:41-50,292-629,633-785,792-896`). `CMD_UPDATE` remains DISK-010's successful no-op; `CMD_FLUSH`'s shared bus-port scope is OD3001; the Add/RemoveChangeInt queue protocol is OD3002; short query output is OD3003; SMART/TRIM outcomes are DISK-326/DISK-325. `TD_GETGEOMETRY`'s 514-byte IDENTIFY copy has no maintained caller and remains an external-contract question; no direct-dispatch defect was established beyond the tracked entries. The selected AFS/SFS/NTFS update callers are already traced in DISK-010 and the ATA supported-command list includes the selected paths. No request or device was run. Source-only.


ATA PIO-write initial-block and request-bound follow-up (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced all selected 28-/48-bit sector and multiple-sector write wrappers into `ata_exec_blk` and `ata_IRQSetHandler`. The block length is `part << au_SectorShift`; initialization sets `au_cmd_total` to that byte count and clamps the first `au_cmd_length` to the smaller of total and the multiple-sector block (`lowlevel.c:185-200,1213-1218,2118-2263`). `ata_PIOWriteBlk` advances the buffer by the clamped length, subtracts the same amount, and reduces the next block length to the remaining bytes (`:244-255`), so partial final multiple-sector groups do not overrun the command buffer in the examined wrappers. The initial readiness poll remains distinct: both OD2998 exits occur after handler installation but before common completion cleanup (`:706-710,757-772`). No request or device was exercised; ordinary IRQ/status semantics remain open. Source-only.


HDAudio hardware-IRQ versus softint teardown boundary (2026-10-15; no new OD): traced HDA Shutdown through PCI IRQ removal, Kernel IRQ-list synchronization and stream-array free. Selected generic removal waits for an active hardware handler on SMP and local interrupt masking covers UP unlink; the hardware ISR therefore does not access `hc_Streams` after the free. The later Cause-queued AHI playback/record callback uses a separate queue and is not drained by this removal, so existing OD2898/EK8935 remain distinct. No IRQ or shutdown was run. Source-only.


DWMAC TX ring wakeup interleaving recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): examined the suspected window where `DWMAC_TXIntF` sees a full ring and writes `PA_IGNORE` at return while `DWMAC_TXComplete` advances `dwu_TXTail` and only requeues when it sees `PA_IGNORE` (`workbench/devs/networks/dwmac/dwmac_unit.c:410-513,518-543`). Exec `SoftIntDispatch` calls `KrnSti` before the callback (`rom/exec/cause.c:177-188`), but the selected RISC-V64 OpenSBI kernel links the generic kernel implementation, whose `KrnSti` is explicitly a not-implemented stub (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/mmakefile.src:98`; `rom/kernel/sti.c:45-54`). Thus the callback is not shown to be interrupt-preemptible on this selected port, and the hypothesized lost-wakeup interleaving is not established for DWMAC. The same ring-state handoff could merit review on a port where softint callbacks run with hardware interrupts enabled, but DWMAC is not selected there. No runtime IRQ or packet was exercised. Source-only.


ATA SCSI-emulator body/caller pass (OD3008–OD3010; 2026-10-15): read all of `rom/devs/ata/scsiemu.c` and traced `HD_SCSICMD` dispatch through the ATA direct-access unit configuration, `au_Read32`/`au_Write32` block helpers and selected QuickPart/HDToolBox callers. Added OD3008 for READ/WRITE(10/12) LBAs above the ATA LBA28 range being sent through the 28-bit callbacks; OD3009 for CDB-driven transfers and fixed response writers that ignore `scsi_Length`; and OD3010 for opcode-field reads that ignore `scsi_CmdLength`, with QuickPart's one-byte INQUIRY fallback as a selected caller. Other callers checked in this slice provide full CDBs and sufficient response storage; this does not establish that all external callers are safe. No command, short-buffer condition or disk I/O was run. The broader ATA command/caller review remains open. Source-only.


ATA base-bus interface/method pass (2026-10-15; no new OD): rechecked `ATABus__Root__Get/Set`, `EnumUnits`, vector-copy defaults, `GetPIOInterface`, `GetDMAInterface`, base `SetXferMode`, `Shutdown`, and `Hidd_ATABus_Start` against `ATA_BusInterface`/PIO/DMA layouts and `ATA__Hidd_StorageController__SetUpBus` (`rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:500-1000`; controller caller `ata_controllerclass.c:125-158`). The selected controller obtains one mandatory PIO interface and at most one optional DMA interface before starting each constructed bus; selected PCI ATA and Gayle producers supply the required bus/PIO vector tables and data sizes. The bus destructor frees the stored interface allocations, and shutdown uses the selected bus alternate-control vector when present. No additional supported-path ownership or dispatch defect established in this slice. Repeated direct calls to the public Get-interface methods and arbitrary external vector tables were not established as maintained uses and remain API-contract questions; transfer behavior and broader bus/caller scope remain open. No bus, reset, or I/O was run. Source-only.


PCI ATA no-DMA shared-IRQ path (OD3011; 2026-10-15): traced `ata_PCI_Interrupt` registration from PCI ATA bus construction through the selected generic PC `PCIDrv::AddInterrupt`, `KrnAddIRQHandler`, and `krnRunIRQHandlers`. The no-DMA branch uses only ATA `BUSY` as its IRQ gate, while the kernel invokes all handlers on a shared IRQ. Traced the false callback into `Hidd_ATABus_HandleIRQ` and no-data/PIO completion. OD3011 records premature completion when an unrelated shared-line IRQ arrives while ATA has an active callback and reports nonbusy status. Probe admits selected PCI IDE channels with no DMA base. The selected m68k Gayle handler is source-gated by Gayle's own IRQ register and was not included in this finding; FastATA detection is compiled out by the absent `ENABLE_ATAPOWERFLYER` define, so its stub path is not treated as active. No target system, IRQ or I/O was exercised. Source-only.

BCM GENET device-tree address translation follow-up (2026-10-15; no new finding): rechecked `genet_reg`, `/scb/ranges` parsing and the selected `BCMGENET_Init` caller against `BCMGENET_Read`/`Write`. Translation validates that the complete `reg` window fits one range before assigning `hw->phys`; failure takes the documented BCM2711 fixed-base fallback. A successful but wider-than-`IPTR` translated address could narrow on a 32-bit target, but the selected BCM2711 address window is below 4 GiB and no supported in-tree DT route establishes a high physical base, so this remains an unsupported/malformed-tree possibility rather than a selected bug. The `#address-cells`/`#size-cells` arithmetic candidate remains OD2925. No DT or hardware was used. Source-only.

ATA initial write-poll/backend IRQ recheck (OD2998 refined, 2026-10-15): the first DRQ wait explicitly passes `irq=FALSE` to `ata_WaitBusyTO`, but that only selects the synchronous status-poll branch; it does not unregister/mask the already installed backend IRQ. Confirmed PCI ATA installs `ata_PCI_Interrupt` during bus construction and Gayle adds/enables its Exec interrupt server (`ata_pci_busclass.c:141-179`; `gayleata_busclass.c:55-99`). This supports the delayed IRQ route after either early return. No device or interrupt was exercised. Source-only.

ATA OD2998 request-buffer ownership recheck (2026-10-15): traced the PIO write buffer from `cmd_Write32`/`cmd_Write64`'s `IOStdReq(io)->io_Data` into `ata_exec_blk`, `ata_exec_cmd`, and `ata_IRQSetHandler` (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:166-214,230-288`; `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1188-1249,185-200,706-710`). Both first-phase error exits return to `HandleIO`; the bus-task path replies immediately after `HandleIO` returns (`ata.c:1148-1157`), and immediate callers receive their reply in `BeginIO` (`:824-838`). Corrected the detailed entry's terminology: the stale callback advances unit-level `au_cmd_data`/length/total fields while reading from the former request buffer; these are transfer fields in `ata_Unit`, not fields in the IORequest. PCI and Gayle handlers retain the dispatch route and can deliver a later DRQ interrupt, but its occurrence depends on device timing. Existing OD2998 remains conditional; no new finding. No I/O request or hardware was exercised. Source-only.

ATA bounce-buffer failed-DMA copy-back disposition (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced `ata_exec_blk`'s unconditional read-side copy after `ata_exec_cmd` (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1227-1237`) against the failed `DMA_Setup` return (`:716-721`) and selected x86 PCI DMA implementation. `CreatePool` applies `MEMF_CLEAR` to each `AllocPooled` allocation; the Exec allocator clears the returned chunk even when it comes from an existing puddle (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:1043`; `rom/exec/allocpooled.c:87-94`; `rom/exec/memory.c:1183-1185,671-673`). The PCI setup path can fail while constructing its PRD list (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/interface_dma.c:24-65,105-114`), but `ata_exec_cmd` returns before programming the ATA command/start after a failed setup (`lowlevel.c:716-747`). In that branch copy-back overwrites the caller's read buffer with the cleared bounce contents, while the selected ATA request path reports an error and `io_Actual == 0` (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:94-100,148-163`). The examined API does not establish a requirement that the buffer remain unchanged on failed reads, and this is not a stale-data disclosure because each allocation is cleared. No separate defect credited. No DMA or request was run. Source-only.


VirtIO failed bus-start cleanup follow-up (OD3012, 2026-10-16): traced worker and PCI IRQ publication (`virtio_busclass.c:165-185`), post-publication `FALSE` exits (`:187-196,222-225`), `Hidd_StorageController_AddBus` failure disposal (`storage_controllerclass.c:102-120`), bus disposal omissions (`virtio_busclass.c:101-109`), and later controller queue free without IRQ removal (`virtio_controllerclass.c:154-171`). Qualified this as a downstream/direct-call candidate because OD2541 currently prevents the selected controller from reaching AddBus and no direct in-tree AddBus caller was found. No device lifecycle or interrupt was run. Source-only.

e1000 TX message-port SMP caller/locking recheck (OD3014, 2026-10-16): reconciled the target route after the prior conditional caller note. `workbench-devs-common` selects the networks aggregate; its x86_64 branch names e1000, whose module target builds the normal device (`workbench/devs/mmakefile.src:5-12`; `workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-15`; `workbench/devs/networks/e1000/mmakefile.src:3-5,22-24`). Added OD3014 for the unprotected consumer-side list operations during cross-CPU producer overlap. Callback requeue overlap also aligns with EK8935 but is not duplicated as a separate Exec finding. OD3014 scope extension (2026-10-16): traced the event-list consumer in `ReportEvents` against `CmdOnEvent`'s `PutMsg` producer (`handler.c:580-614`; `unit.c:57-79`). A reachable call from the receive-interrupt RX-buffer failure path (`unit.c:456-465`) can walk/remove event waiters while the task worker inserts one; it likewise uses only local `Disable`, without the port spinlock. e1000 Init/Open/Close full-body and open-count contract follow-up (OD3015, 2026-10-16): read the full 504-line `e1000_init.c`, traced `ADD2OPENDEV`/`ADD2CLOSEDEV`, Exec OpenDevice/CloseDevice dispatch and every `e1ku_open_count` use. Open increments the count, but Close only unlinks/frees the opener; no count decrement or shared-flag reset exists in the selected source. SANA2OPF_MINE makes a direct trigger: first exclusive open succeeds, close leaves count nonzero and IFF_SHARED clear, and the next exclusive open is rejected IOERR_UNITBUSY. The opener-allocation failure path also increments before failure and calls CloseDevice without restoring it. Added OD3015; no device or request was opened. Source-only.
e1000 TX per-packet allocation failure trace (OD3016, 2026-10-16): followed `CmdWrite` queueing into `e1000func_TX_Int`. A NULL frame allocation leaves `error` initialized to zero and skips descriptor filling, but the callback still advances `i`, sets `next_to_watch`, removes/replies success, increments sent stats and writes the advanced TDT (`unit.c:195-205,276-303`; `handler.c:240-277`). Added OD3016 for false successful send completion and ring advancement after allocation failure. The DMA conversion failure branch was not included: the selected PC direct-bus PCI driver returns the CPU address, and other target mappings were not established. No allocation failure or transmission was induced. Source-only.

OD3016 TX preparation-failure branch extension (2026-10-16): followed the `tx_function == FALSE` path in addition to frame-allocation failure. It sets `S2ERR_NO_RESOURCES` but still assigns `next_to_watch`, advances the producer index, writes TDT, and leaves the newly staged buffer for later cleanup; `e1000func_clean_tx_irq` stops at the first completion descriptor without DD (`e1000.c:1090-1118`). Expanded OD3016 to include this branch while qualifying hardware ring-stall effect as controller-dependent. No callback or transmission was run.

RTL8139 TX queue/AbortIO ownership pass (OD3047, 2026-10-16): traced `CmdWrite` through the `PA_SOFTINT` write port to `RTL8139_TX_IntF`, then compared its head-read/removal ordering with public AbortIO and Exec `PutMsg`/`ReplyMsg` behavior. The TX consumer and AbortIO both remove/reply under local `Disable()` without the port spinlock; ExecSMP permits them to overlap across CPUs. Added a distinct conditional write-request ownership finding alongside (not duplicating) OD3037's event-port race. No request or interleaving was run. Source-only.

RTL8139 TX descriptor failure-accounting recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): traced `RTL8139_TX_IntF` copy-hook failure through its unconditional `tx_current` advance and no `TxStatus` register write, then traced `tx_dirty` retirement through the four hardware status registers. A failed copy can therefore leave a software-ring entry that was never submitted to hardware; whether it blocks retirement depends on the controller's status value for that unused/reused slot, which the checked-in reset/init path does not establish. AROSTCP supplies the `S2_CopyToBuff` hook and normally provisions an mbuf chain to MTU, while raw output can select `SANA2IOF_RAW`; no concrete selected caller was shown to exceed its provided chain in this pass. Kept this as an unresolved hardware/caller-contract question, not a report finding. No packet or device was run. Source-only.

RTL8139/AROSTCP TX-copy callback correction (2026-10-16): corrected the preceding descriptor recheck's callback interpretation. RTL8139's `opener->tx_function` is selected from `S2_CopyFromBuff`/`S2_CopyFromBuff16`/`S2_CopyFromBuff32` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/rtl8139_init.c:230-237`); AROSTCP maps `S2_CopyFromBuff` to `m_copy_from_mbuf` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/sana2copybuff.c:186-215,291`). Its TX caller sets `ios2_DataLength` from the packet's `m_pkthdr.len` and retains the packet as `ioip_packet` until completion (`if_sana.c:1249-1267`); the TX callback then copies that many bytes across the mbuf chain. The MTU-sized `ioip_reserved` chain is for the opposite, RX direction and is irrelevant to TX. With `DIAGNOSTIC` disabled, `m_copy_from_mbuf` has no short-chain check and dereferences NULL if the chain length is less than the packet-header length; with diagnostics enabled it returns FALSE, reaching RTL8139's software-index advance without a hardware descriptor write. No selected AROSTCP producer creating a packet-header/chain-length mismatch was established, and unused/reused hardware descriptor status still determines whether a failed-copy slot stalls retirement. Retain as caller/hardware questions; no additional finding. No packet or device was run. Source-only.

UHCI pipe-list/interrupt lifetime pass (OD3048, 2026-10-16): traced `uhci_Handler`'s Interrupts/ControlLS/ControlFS/Bulk list traversals against `uhci_CreatePipe`, `uhci_DeletePipe`, schedule rebuild, and selected USB enumeration/device pipe-method callers. CreatePipe's AddTail/rebuild has no interrupt exclusion; DeletePipe uses local Disable only and frees the removed pipe after re-enabling. The interrupt handler does not acquire the USB stack's task semaphore. Added OD3048, scoped the cross-CPU deletion case to x86_64-pc ExecSMP with the USB package and a matching UHCI controller; a single-CPU AddTail tearing claim was later withdrawn after checking forward-link publication order; see the qualification below. Distinct from OD2970's shared TD bitmap/page-list allocator and OD2974's TD-chain timeout-reclamation race. No controller or interleaving was run. Source-only.

UHCI nested callback-list follow-up (OD3048 strengthened, 2026-10-16): expanded the same synchronization finding after tracing both interrupt subscribers and the root-hub soft interrupt. `uhci_Handler` walks per-pipe `p_Intr`; `HubInterrupt` walks `uhci->intList`; task-side AddInterrupt appends to these lists without exclusion, while RemInterrupt searches before local Disable, removes with only local exclusion, then frees the record. Selected HID registration/removal reaches the per-pipe path. Kept this within OD3048's shared interrupt-visible list protocol; no second ID added. No interrupt or teardown was run. Source-only.

OD3048 single-CPU trigger qualification (2026-10-16): narrowed the finding after checking Exec `AddTail` store order (`rom/exec/addtail.c:55-66`). The node's forward links are initialized before it is published through the predecessor's `ln_Succ`, so the earlier note's claim that an interrupt on the same CPU necessarily sees a torn forward list during AddTail was too strong and has been removed from the detailed report. OD3048 now rests on the supported ExecSMP stale-reference case: `uhci_Handler` can traverse a pipe/callback list on one CPU while DeletePipe or RemInterrupt removes and frees its node after only local Disable on another. CreatePipe/AddInterrupt remain unsynchronized shared-list writers, but no independent single-CPU corruption consequence is credited. Source-only; no controller or interleaving was run.

UHCI zero-length control request follow-up (OD3049, 2026-10-16): traced `uhci_ControlTransfer`'s separate buffer-pointer branch and data-TD construction against every maintained `HIDD_USBDrv_ControlTransfer` caller. A zero-length request with a non-NULL buffer skips the `td` assignment loop, then writes `td->td_LinkPtr`; the public header and wrapper impose no null-buffer precondition. All selected in-tree no-data requests pass NULL, so retained this as an external direct-API conditional finding. Kept separate from OD2976's zero-length bulk-transfer path. No transfer or controller was run. Source-only.

## PCNet32 target and file coverage (2026-10-16)

The network aggregate explicitly lists `workbench-devs-networks-pcnet32-$(AROS_TARGET_CPU)` (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-15`). The local module maps both i386 and x86_64 aliases to `workbench-devs-networks-pcnet32-x86` and compiles `pcnet32_init.c`, `handler.c`, `unit.c` and `pcnet32.c` (`pcnet32/mmakefile.src:4-13`). Therefore these bodies are build-selected through the checked-in aggregate on i386 and x86_64; earlier ledger notes that called the target commented out/omitted are corrected here. The target-specific build itself was not run, and hardware/caller behavior remains untested.

| File | Status | Notes |

nForce busy-open count update recheck (OD3082 expanded; 2026-10-24): re-read the complete Open/Close control flow at `workbench/devs/networks/nForce/nforce_init.c:203-285`. The sharing predicate sets `error = IOERR_UNITBUSY`, but the following `unit->open_count++` remains inside the enclosing pre-check `if (error == 0)` and executes regardless of the newly set error. Failed Open then calls CloseDevice, whose close vector has no count rollback; ordinary Close likewise never decrements. Expanded OD3082 to include this distinct inflation route and the resulting stale shared/exclusive admission state. No lifecycle was run; OD3080 remains an earlier constructor blocker.

Sam440 EMAC startup-failure caller recheck (OD3133; 2026-10-16): traced the selected Sam440 target to the EMAC module and checked each request-port consumer. `WRITE_QUEUE` is used by SANA-II write submission and TX scheduling; `ADOPT_QUEUE` by orphan reads; `EVENT_QUEUE` by event requests. `CreateUnit` stores each nullable allocation, then unconditionally writes through `WRITE_QUEUE`; failures in the other queues remain NULL for later `PutMsg`/list dereferences. The caller does not clear `SIGF_SINGLE` before waiting, so it can block when that bit is clear or continue spuriously if a stale signal is pending; a worker-side `CreateMsgPort` failure instead signals the parent before the NULL input port is dereferenced in its Wait-mask construction. `Init` returns success after either unit result, and `Open` dereferences a NULL unit for accepted indices 0/1. The explicit `mii_rw` caller-serialization comment and single MII command/data register pair support the overlap. Corrected the trigger: an IRQ preempting Open on the same CPU is sufficient; ExecSMP is not required. The i386 nForce aggregate is the selected target. No IRQ or PHY transaction was run. nForce/RTL816x state-bit atomicity caller recheck (OD3088 scope expanded, 2026-10-16): traced the carrier helpers to every link-state writer in Open and the hardware interrupt handlers. Both headers implement `test_and_set_bit`/`test_and_clear_bit` as separate volatile read and write operations; both drivers publish Open's link result in task context after enabling link interrupts, while their installed IRQ callbacks also update carrier state. The IRQ-side `Disable` does not protect the interrupted task's sequence on a single CPU, so a carrier transition can be lost if preemption occurs between those source-level accesses. Retained SMP cross-CPU races and unrelated-word-bit interference as an additional scope. Revised OD3088 from ExecSMP-only to UP interrupt-preemption plus SMP cases; no target build or link transition was run. Source-only.

nForce worker signal/input queue path recheck (OD3083 sharpened, 2026-10-16): traced the worker's reply/input/timer `CreateMsgPort` order and subsequent four `AllocSignal` calls against Exec's signal allocation, Wait, Signal and port notification contracts. Traced selected BeginIO contention into `PutMsg(nu_input_port)` and the scheduler's shutdown-first branch. Because the branch tests the raw private signal number against the received mask, any overlap between that integer's set bits and the input port's one-hot signal can misclassify a queued request as shutdown; its request may then remain unanswered as the worker deletes its own ports. DeleteUnit also signals the raw number and frees unit-owned resources without a worker-exit handshake. Replaced OD3083's broad “may miss its exit branch” wording with the concrete false-shutdown condition and retained the use-after-free race. Exact allocated signal assignments were not run; successful startup remains conditional on OD3080. Source-only.

OD3083 decisive Exec signal-allocation recheck (2026-10-16; supersedes the preceding input-misrouting hypothesis): inspected `CreateNewProc`/`AddTask` initialization, `TaskSigAlloc`, `CreateMsgPort`, `AllocSignal`, and Wait's return calculation. Exec initializes new tasks with bits 0–15 reserved (`prepareexecbase.c:319`; `newaddtask.c:249-251`). The nForce worker creates reply/input/timer ports before any private AllocSignal, and its earlier initialization path has no other AllocSignal call; thus those ports receive bits 16–18 and the private shutdown signal is bit 19 (followed by 20–22). The Wait set includes input bit 17 and private bits 19–22; Wait returns only received bits in that set. `recvd & 19` can never match those high bits, and `Signal(..., 19)` also sets only low bits outside the wait set. The earlier proposed example with low input/private signal numbers was incorrect because it ignored Exec's reserved system signals; that false-shutdown impact is withdrawn. OD3083 now records the deterministic missed wake, indefinite worker wait, and immediate resource free, with post-free input wake as a conditional stale-state path. No task was run. Source-only.

No timer request is submitted by `udelay`; no cross-task reply-port race was found in the current implementation. Non-x86 timer precision and clock-adjustment behavior remain unverified. Source-only.

If one of those ports cannot allocate a signal, its earlier failure is already in OD2326 or the startup path in OD3152. No independent selected signal-exhaustion trigger is established. Source-only.
