Prism2 RX slot-reclamation edge recheck (OD3116, 2026-10-16): simulated the loop indices and pointer increments from source for ten occupied, nonmatching slots. After first-pass `i=0..9`, `buffer` is one-past the ten-slot allocation. On second-pass `i=10`, the code clears `rx_fragment_nos[0]`; for a new first fragment, `n == -1 && (frag_no & 0xf) == 0` short-circuits the following source-address comparison, so it returns the one-past pointer and stores `buffer_no=10`. RX copies the header/data through that pointer and later stores `rx_fragment_nos[10]`. Confirmed the selected cards aggregate declares i386, x86_64, m68k, and PPC variants and includes Prism2 (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:30-33,45-53`). OD3116 retained and its affected scope made explicit; no packet or device was run. Source-only.

AHCI port startup/teardown lifecycle follow-up (2026-10-16; no additional OD): traced port allocation publication, helper-thread creation and initial handshake through attach's `AP_SIGF_THREAD_SYNC` wait, then detach's controller interrupt shutdown, CAM detach, port stop, worker signal/join, register shutdown, CCB map destruction and DMA-memory release (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:253-491,1015-1085`; `ahci_attach.c:701-823`; `ahci_aros.c:181-252`). AHCI DMA-wrapper failure-unwind follow-up (2026-10-16; no additional OD): traced `ahci_dmamem_alloc` and `ahci_dmamem_free` into the selected AROS bus-DMA shim (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:3739-3798`; `ahci_aros_bus.c:118-170,207-214`). In this target, `bus_dmamem_alloc` either returns an error before claiming a slab slot or returns a slot with `map = vaddr`; `bus_dmamap_load` unconditionally invokes the one-segment callback and returns success. Therefore the apparent missing `bus_dmamem_free` after successful memory allocation plus map-load failure is not reachable in this selected implementation. Successful slots are returned to the slab by the common `ahci_dmamem_free` path; slab backing persists with the DMA tag. No allocation or map-load failure was induced. Source-only.


AHCI command-descriptor DMA slab boundary-allocation pass (OD3178, 2026-10-16): compared the two one-segment 4 MiB-boundary tags with per-port allocations, shim slab sizing, controller port/slot maxima, and attach rollback (`ahci_attach.c:442,482-514,637-644,701-704`; `ahci.c:400-401`; `ahci_aros_bus.c:67-145`; `ahci.h:53,408`). Each port allocates a separate nearly 4 MiB slab for each tag, retaining the backing until controller detach; at 32 ports this contributes about 256 MiB of boundary slack, for roughly 272 MiB of backing allocations and 16 MiB of descriptor payload at 32 slots. Added OD3178 for conditional attach failure under memory pressure. No allocation failure or hardware attach was exercised. Other Drivers detailed report count: 609 unique OD headings. Source-only.

AHCI DMA map/load/sync caller reconciliation (2026-10-16; no additional OD): traced all selected data-map and descriptor-map callers through `bus_dmamap_create/load/sync/unload` (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci.c:423,2124-2144,2193-2200,2348-2356,3346-3354,3755-3798`; `ahci_aros_bus.c:189-233`). The data tag's `maxsize` and segment limits are not enforced by the shim and `bus_dmamap_load` reports the pointer as one bus segment; the ignored low-address limit and raw-pointer DMA address are already OD2558, while direct SCSI requests exceeding the PRDT's 4 MiB encoding are covered by DISK-015. The shim's sync range is the tag's 64 KiB max segment, but the only selected AHCI manifests are PC x86 targets whose cache pre/post-DMA functions do no maintenance on coherent x86. No separate selected-target consequence established. No map, sync, or transfer was run; source-only.

Sam440 EMAC MAL ring/cache extent reconciliation (2026-10-16; no additional OD): checked `EMAC_MAL_Init`'s packet-buffer sizing, ring allocations and cache clear lengths against the 2×64 RX and 2×32 TX descriptor loops (`workbench/devs/networks/emac/mal.c:105-154`; ring constants in `emac.h:118-130`). The shared packet-buffer allocation formula reserves four times the sum of the ring counts, while the population loops consume twice that count; this is fixed extra pool consumption, not an undersized allocation. TX ring setup passes `RX_RING_SIZE` (64) to `CacheClearE` after allocating only `TX_RING_SIZE` (32) descriptors; the selected PPC `CacheClearE` uses `dcbf` to write back/invalidate the rounded cache-line range (`arch/ppc-all/exec/cachecleare.c:24-36`), so the extra 512-byte span can include adjacent pool data. This initialization pass supplies no evidence of lost data or a device-visible consequence, and the single-core Sam440 path has no concurrent descriptor consumer during setup. No new finding added. Cache-policy/hardware contracts and runtime DMA remain open; no board or network traffic was exercised. Source-only.

The code accepts lengths above the 1,544-byte buffer and 1,568-byte slot stride. USB Audio duplex sample-rate pairing follow-up (OD3191, 2026-10-16): traced recording/playback sibling matching against frequency-list construction and AHI mode publication/selection through sibling interface activation (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1225-1253,1844-1918,3375-3404,3489-3503,3133-3190`). The pairing predicates compare list length, minimum, maximum and only the first frequency; equal-metadata discrete lists can differ at an interior rate. AHI exposes/selects the playback rate and applies it to the recording interface without checking that sibling's list. Added OD3191 for conditional duplex rate mismatch. No descriptor or stream was used. Other Drivers detailed report count: 629 unique headings. Source-only.
USB Audio multiple-mode control routing and teardown recheck (OD3192 expanded, 2026-10-17): confirmed distinct mode records can pass `subLibAllocAudio`'s per-mode `nam_RTIso` guard and overwrite the unit-wide current-mode pointer. The control API sets update flags through its own audio-control mode, while the unit worker consumes them through that shared pointer. `subLibFreeAudio` then unconditionally clears the pointer, even when freeing an older mode; a later update through a newer still-live control wakes the worker, which dereferences NULL (`usbaudio.class.c:3271-3332,3577-3589,613-646,4090-4153`; AHI dispatch: `audioctrl.c:982-1004`). Expanded OD3192 to cover both misrouting and this conditional worker fault. No device, allocation sequence, or control request was run. Source-only.
USB Audio OD3177 current-mode wait qualification (2026-10-16): rechecked the detach wait against the newly traced per-mode allocation guard and unit-wide current-mode field (`usbaudio.class.c:3285-3289,3327-3332,3577-3589`). Because `subLibFreeAudio` clears the one pointer unconditionally, OD3177 is conditional on `nch_CurrentMode` remaining non-NULL and must not claim a reference-counted wait for every outstanding AHI control. Cross-referenced OD3192, which records the distinct multiple-mode overwrite/control-routing condition. Source-only.
USB Audio sibling-mode partial-allocation cleanup pass (2026-10-16; no additional finding): traced AHI's `AHI_FreeAudio` error path and every early return in `subLibAllocAudio`, including primary/sibling pipe and message-port creation, mode selection, and buffer allocation (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:656-660,718-728`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3285-3328,3410-3416,3489-3509,3577-3660`). `subLibFreeAudio` is called after suballocation failure; Poseidon's `psdFreePipe(NULL)`, `psdSetAltInterface(NULL, ...)`, and Exec's `DeleteMsgPort(NULL)` have explicit safe paths. The sibling zero-bandwidth path with no pipe leaves the interface at its existing zero-bandwidth alternate in software; no additional cleanup defect established in this slice. Existing per-mode/current-mode mismatch remains OD3192. No allocation failure or device was used; source-only.

USB Audio failed second-mode allocation/current-pointer recheck (OD3192 expanded, 2026-10-17): revisited AHI's failed AllocAudio cleanup against USB Audio's early-return branches (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:511,520-521,656-659,712-727`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3290-3325,3581-3589`). The AHI error label calls `AHI_FreeAudio`; `_AHI_FreeAudio` skips Stop when `AHISF_ERROR` is set but still calls the subdriver FreeAudio whenever the sublibrary was opened. Thus a second distinct mode can fail after `nam_PsdBase` is opened—for example at `CreateMsgPort`—and its cleanup unconditionally clears `nch_CurrentMode` even though the active first mode still owns that unit pointer. A later hardware-control update through the first mode follows the same worker NULL dereference as OD3192's older-mode-free branch. Expanded OD3192's trigger and consequences in both detailed report and index; this is the same unconditional-clear root, not a new ID. No allocation failure, AHI control or device was used; source-only.
USB Audio selector-control index caller trace (2026-10-16; no new OD): followed `AHIC_Input`/`AHIC_Output` tags through AHI ControlAudio dispatch, the class's `nam_NumInputs`/`nam_NumOutputs` gating, worker selector requests and `AHIDB_Inputs`/`AHIDB_Outputs` getters (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:982-997`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:613-643,570-584,4132-4156,4047-4073`). The getter returns the selector's actual `nau_NumInputs`; valid indices in that reported range address links populated by graph construction. The write path has no independent upper-bound validation, but no selected in-contract mismatch or stronger valid-index trigger was established in this pass, so no new finding was added. Arbitrary out-of-range client indices remain outside this candidate. Broader selector topology and caller behavior remain open; the file stays Partial. No device or control request was used; source-only.
USB Audio partial-duplex format and record-buffer follow-up (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced the fallback sibling pair through input buffer allocation, completion conversion and the selected AHI RecordFunc contract (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1882-1918,2704-2741,2966-3119,3489-3552`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:401-414`). Input callbacks explicitly advertise `AHIST_S16S`; the mono converters duplicate each sample to stereo, and stereo converters emit one stereo frame, matching the documented callback type. The input USB buffer is sized in source-frame units. This pass did not establish that the fallback's differing channel/resolution fields alone cause an output-buffer overrun; no memory-corruption candidate added. The separate frequency-list compatibility gap remains OD3191. Packet-size versus per-callback destination capacity under every endpoint interval remains open. No device or stream was used; source-only.
USB Audio per-packet recording destination capacity trace (OD3193, 2026-10-16): followed playback-derived `ahiac_BuffSamples`/`ahiac_BuffSize` through sibling buffer allocation, Poseidon RTIso request initialization, HCI interval scheduling, and `nInDoneHook`'s fixed stereo-S16 conversion (`usbaudio.class.c:1844-1874,2678-2742,2966-3021,3406-3412,3489-3507`; `poseidon.library.c:8483-8553`; `poseidon.library.c:4624-4627`; `pciusb/uhwcmd.c:1473-1481`; `pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:1501-1509`). A high-speed 8-kHz mono recording interface advertising bInterval 10 has a nominal 64-ms service interval and can return a 512-byte packet (512 one-byte samples); paired playback at interval 1 yields 800 samples/1,600 bytes of record destination, while the callback's stereo-S16 conversion writes 2,048 bytes. Added OD3193 for the conditional destination overrun. No descriptor, device or transfer was used. Other Drivers detailed report count: 631 unique headings. Source-only.
xHCI high-speed RTIso interval-unit recheck (OD3194, 2026-10-16): traced Poseidon high-/SuperSpeed endpoint interval normalization and pipe propagation into both xHCI endpoint-context setup and the independent RTIso request queue (`poseidon.library.c:8483,8525-8553,4624-4627`; `xhci_hcd.c:160-207,2225-2232`; `xhci_isoch.c:232-272`). The endpoint context treats `iouh_Interval` as a normalized microframe count, but `xhciQueueIsochIO` clamps it and applies a raw-bInterval exponent formula again before advancing `rtn_NextFrame`; bInterval 4 becomes a 16-ms RTIso frame step instead of 1 ms. Added OD3194 for conditional periodic-transfer pacing error. No controller or endpoint was exercised. Other Drivers detailed report count: 632 unique headings. Source-only.
OD3193/OD3194 interaction qualification (2026-10-16): the recording-buffer overwrite condition is based on the completed input byte count versus the two distinct allocations/conversion extents; it does not require a particular host request cadence. The high-/SuperSpeed xHCI scheduler's separate interval reinterpretation is OD3194. The bInterval 10 packet illustration in OD3193 describes the endpoint's nominal 64-ms service period; no claim of runtime scheduling or transfer behavior is made. Source-only.
OD3194 RTIso completion/requeue caller trace (2026-10-16): confirmed the computed request frame is consumed by the selected xHCI path. Isochronous completion clears the completed PTD and calls `xhciQueueIsochIO`/`xhciStartIsochIO` to refill the pending target (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2791-2810`); the queue uses `rtn_NextFrame` and increments it by the computed `interval_frames` (`xhci_isoch.c:255-272`), then passes that frame to the transfer TRB (`:305-329`; `:94-104`). This confirms the exponentiation mismatch controls subsequent request spacing rather than being dead arithmetic. No controller or transfer was used; source-only.

xHCI RTIso stop/restart state trace (OD3195, 2026-10-16): followed `xhciScheduleIsoTDs` submission-failure requeue, Stop's `xhciFinishRequest` cleanup, PTD flag clearing, and the subsequent Start selection (`xhci_isoch.c:34-52,96-137,286-350`; `xhci_periodic.c:40-46`; `xhci_hcd.c:997-1008,1065-1078,2433-2478`; `uhwcmd.c:1631-1650`). A failed ring submission restores `PTDF_QUEUED`; Stop removes/frees the request context but clears only ACTIVE and BUFFER_VALID; restart can refill the PTD, then start rejects it due to stale QUEUED. Added OD3195 for conditional failure to resume RTIso transfers. No controller or stream was used. Other Drivers detailed report count: 633 unique headings. Source-only.

OD3195 selected-caller confirmation (2026-10-16): traced AHI `AHIC_Play=FALSE/TRUE` through `AHI_ControlAudioA`'s `AHISub_Stop`/`AHISub_Start` dispatch (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:841-844,959-961,1006-1017`) into USB Audio `subLibStop`/`subLibStart`, which call `psdStopRTIso` and `psdStartRTIso` on the same mode handler (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3729-3741,3777-3805`). Poseidon submits `UHCMD_STOPRTISO` and `UHCMD_STARTRTISO` on the handler pipe (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5631-5678`). This confirms an in-tree stop-then-restart client path for OD3195; the triggering ring submission failure was not exercised. The SonixcamTool client also starts and stops its handler around capture, but its lifecycle does not independently establish restart of the same stale PTDs. Remaining ISO clients and controller lifecycle interactions stay under review. Source-only.

xHCI RTIso Stop hardware-quiescence and caller-buffer lifetime trace (OD3196, 2026-10-16): compared `cmdStopRTIso`/`xhciStopIsochIO` with `xhciFinishRequest`'s explicit note that TRBs can remain on the transfer ring until a later endpoint stop; traced active TRB DMA address construction and Poseidon's success return. The Stop path performs no endpoint stop or dequeue-pointer reset, whereas `xhciDestroyEndpoint` stops a running endpoint during later pipe teardown (`xhci_isoch.c:332-350`; `xhci_hcd.c:2433-2478,4299-4328`; `xhci_schedule.c:327-352`; `uhwcmd.c:1665-1697`; `poseidon.library.c:5657-5675,4650-4678`). Confirmed the selected SonixcamTool reads capture data after Stop and its cleanup frees capture buffers before removing the RTIso handler (`SonixcamTool.c:904-917,1240-1248`; `poseidon.library.c:5607-5626`). Added OD3196 for the conditional post-Stop DMA window. No device or transfer was run; exact controller completion timing remains untested. Other Drivers detailed report count: 634 unique headings. Source-only.

xHCI endpoint teardown command-failure trace (OD3197, 2026-10-16): followed `xhciDestroyEndpoint` to `xhciFreeEndpointContext`, then both endpoint Stop/Reset and Configure Endpoint Drop command results through `xhciCmdSubmit`. Stop/Reset errors are discarded; Configure Endpoint errors are logged without aborting; the DMA-visible ring is freed and its context pointers cleared unconditionally (`xhci_hcd.c:2306-2385,4299-4390`; `xhci_hw.c:48-55,127-162,398-458`). The bounded command helper returns -1 after a one-second timeout. Added OD3197 for the conditional ring lifetime failure if both quiescence operations fail while the endpoint remains live. No controller failure or endpoint teardown was run. Source-only.

USB Audio descriptor and Feature Unit response-length follow-up (OD3198, 2026-10-16): re-read the complete `nExamineAudioDescriptors` format/mode path and `nExamineAudioUnits` topology/control path (`usbaudio.class.c:1038-1309,1371-1925`) against Poseidon's exact-size descriptor storage and length API. The already-recorded OD3168-OD3172 cover descriptor count/extents and empty supported-rate tables; no duplicate finding was added for those paths. The Feature Unit GET_MIN/GET_MAX control requests ask for two bytes, but after any error-free `psdDoPipe` the code consumes both without checking `psdGetPipeActual` (`usbaudio.class.c:1764-1790`; `poseidon.library.c:4899-4907`). xHCI accepts short packets as success and records transferred bytes (`xhci_hcd.c:2496-2505,3099-3103`), yielding OD3198 for the indeterminate high byte/control range. No descriptor or device was used; source-only. Other Drivers detailed report count: 636 unique headings.

xHCI device-slot teardown failure follow-up (OD3197, 2026-10-16): traced disconnect through `xhciDisconnectDevice` and `xhciFreeDeviceCtx`. The device-wide `xhciCmdSlotDisable` result is ignored; teardown then removes the software/DCBAA references and frees endpoint contexts with `stopEndpoint=FALSE`, bypassing per-endpoint stop/drop before ring release. The Address Device failure unwind has the same ignored Slot Disable followed by DCBAA clear and endpoint-ring frees (`xhci_hcd.c:1499-1512`). Expanded OD3197 to include this independent failure path alongside endpoint Stop/Reset/Configure Drop failures. The controller’s retained activity after a failed slot command is conditional; no command failure/device removal was induced. Source-only.

Serial receive publication race follow-up (OD3199, 2026-10-16): traced CMD_READ from the flag store through `PutMsg`, then the PC HIDD interrupt callback into RBF_InterruptHandler. A remote ExecSMP CPU can service a receive interrupt in that interval, observe an empty request queue, clear STATUS_READS_PENDING and buffer input; BeginIO then queues a request without restoring the flag. Subsequent receives can leave it queued until another state-changing request. Qualified to ExecSMP plus PC serial HIDD and explicit serial.device build/use; no I/O was run. Source-only.

PC serial shutdown/lifecycle and receive-helper follow-up (OD1454/OD2779 recheck, 2026-10-16; no new candidate): confirmed the final-close sequence removes `su_Node` before calling HIDD disposal, while the PC HIDD removes its shared IRQ server and clears `csd->units[]` only inside the later Dispose method. The already-recorded OD1454 null-unit receive callback window is therefore a same-CPU interrupt window before RemIntServer, in addition to the cross-CPU case; kernel IRQ removal’s SMP reader lock only synchronizes once removal starts. Separately traced PC pair ownership: only the first-created unit registers the shared COM1/3 or COM2/4 IRQ server/reset node, and disposing that unit removes the server even if the sibling remains open (OD2779 remains distinct). Also rechecked `serial_support.c`: its two ring-copy helpers are called only from CMD_READ under `su_Lock` and local Disable; the input ring length and cursors are UWORD, so the helper’s UWORD copy count cannot wrap from consuming a single ring’s available bytes. An in-tree direct caller establishing the `io_Length == -1` sentinel contract was not found; caller buffer capacity remains an external request contract. No hardware or I/O was exercised. Source-only.

Serial negative-length read contract and large-read reconciliation (OD9/OD28/OD11; 2026-10-16): rechecked the public `IOExtSer` declaration, all repository `io_Length = -1` assignments, the debug serial test's submit paths, `CMD_READ`, both copy helpers and the receive callback. The test uses `-1` for CMD_WRITE only; its CMD_READ uses the positive count returned by `SDCMD_QUERY`, capped to the local buffer. No in-tree CMD_READ caller of the undocumented `-1` sentinel was found; `PORT:` can forward a negative DOS length, but the DOS interface specifies a byte count and does not establish negative lengths as supported. Keep OD9/OD28 conditional on clients relying on that implementation behavior. Reconfirmed OD11 already covers the callback's `UWORD indexDestBuf` wrap for valid ULONG-sized reads in serial.device and parallel.device; no duplicate finding added. No serial request or data was run. Source-only.

OpenSBI dwuart FDT/IRQ discovery recheck (OD2464 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced the full discovery routine through `FDT_GetReg`, default `reg-shift`/`reg-io-width`, local `clock-frequency`, the first-cell PLIC interrupt value, `KrnMapGlobal`, and unit construction/disposal. `FDT_GetReg` decodes the node's raw parent-bus address but does not translate parent `ranges`; no DTB is checked in, so whether supported firmware requires translating parent `ranges` remains unverified. Added out-of-range nonzero FDT IRQ (`>= IRQ_COUNT`, 1024) as another null registration result reaching OD2464; allocation failure remains the valid-IRQ path. Corrected the stale `findings 845-847` ledger text to the current OD IDs. No firmware image or hardware was exercised. Source-only.

SB128 report reconciliation (OD342/OD343/OD2163-OD2168, 2026-10-16): compared the active detailed report with the SB128 coverage rows and found those eight documented IDs absent from the report. Confirmed the helper's `card_init(card) < 0` branch is not reachable in the current complete `card_init` body, and did not restore that as a separate leak candidate. Prism2 scan-result follow-up (2026-10-16; OD3188 rechecked): traced the oversized-record failure through `P2ReadRec`, both `InfoInt` scan-result record IDs, task signal handling, and `SendScanResults`; the rejected positive signed lengths 2,002–32,766 leave the shared record unchanged, and the selected `S2_GETNETWORKS` consumer receives results through the existing queue path. No scan, firmware response, or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

EHCI generated-dispatch boundary follow-up (2026-10-16): re-read `ehci.conf`, the selected `ehci_init.c` bodies, module manifest, and init/expunge flow. The local Root::New returns NULL and Root::Dispose is empty; `EHCI_Init` performs PCI enumeration then returns FALSE, so successful runtime construction/dispatch through this class is not established. Kept OD2484 (hardware reset before failed init) and OD2950 (root USB object not disposed on failed init) as the selected source-derived effects; no extra finding from the declared but unproven runtime method path. Generated artifacts and a matching controller remain unverified. No module or controller was run. Source-only.

USB Audio GUI task-publication follow-up (2026-10-16; OD3200 added): traced `UCM_OpenCfgWindow` from the selected Poseidon popup through `nOpenCfgWindow`, both `psdSpawnSubTask` creation branches, the ExecSMP local-only `Forbid()` contract, and every `nGUITaskCleanup` exit. A fast child exit on another CPU can clear `nh_GUITask` before the caller assigns the spawn result, leaving a dead non-NULL value that suppresses subsequent opens. No task or GUI failure was run. Source-only.

USB Audio Type I subframe validation follow-up (2026-10-16; OD3201 added): traced format acceptance and mode construction into `nSelectAudioMode`; a zero `bSubframeSize` is not rejected by the channel/resolution filter, yields `nam_FrameSize == 0`, and reaches an unchecked bandwidth division on AHI allocation. Rechecked the common AHI allocation-failure cleanup: it invokes subdriver FreeAudio even when AllocAudio reports an error, and Exec documents DeleteMsgPort(NULL) as safe, so those cleanup paths did not yield a separate finding. No descriptor or allocation was exercised. Source-only.

USB Audio control-method follow-up (2026-10-16; OD3202 added): reviewed the AHI hardware-control entry points, worker flag processing, selector conversion, volume mapping, and AHI caller contracts. The public fixed-point range comes from the reported AHI attributes; tracing the 8.8 Feature Unit endpoints through the three worker multiplications establishes a signed-32-bit overflow for a valid 32768-unit range at unity. No device or control request was used. Source-only.

VirtIO used-ring acquire-order follow-up (OD3205, 2026-10-16): checked the completion reader against device-before-index publication and the selected RISC-V memory model. It reads `q_Used->idx`, then used `id`/`len` and request status with no hardware read barrier (`virtio_queue.c:251-268`). The queue semaphore is CPU-side and is acquired before the index load. Selected OpenSBI PCIDT uses ordinary coherent `AllocVec` memory for `AllocPCIMem` (`pcidt_driverclass.c:992-1019`); coherent DMA does not impose CPU load ordering under RVWMO. Added OD3205 separately from OD2391's driver-to-device write barrier. Both VirtIO paths remain latent behind OD2541's missing storage-bus registration. No device or I/O was run.

VirtIO used-index bounds follow-up (2026-10-16; no new malformed-index finding): confirmed the sole controller allocates a 128-entry power-of-two queue and checks the device maximum before selecting it (`virtio_controllerclass.c:105,110`; `virtio_hw.c:200-219`). At most the queue's available descriptors can be outstanding; a conforming device therefore cannot advance the 16-bit used index by more than the outstanding queue contents modulo 65536. The consumer computes ring slots modulo `q_Size` and caps `head` before indexing request storage (`virtio_queue.c:254-262`), while `q_LastUsedIdx` uses the same 16-bit wrap width as the protocol index. An out-of-contract index jump can cause stale-slot processing but does not by itself escape ring bounds; no separate valid-device defect was established beyond OD2867's full-width ID truncation and OD3205's missing read ordering. Other malformed device fields and teardown remain open. No device response was simulated.

VirtIO malformed capability/ring boundary follow-up (2026-10-16; no new confirmed defect): rechecked the used-ring `idx` snapshot, modulo slot derivation, request-slot bound, 128-entry selected queue, descriptor free-chain and controller queue setup. Conforming completion count is bounded by the queue's outstanding descriptors; an out-of-contract `idx` jump can replay stale slots, but the loop stays within the 16-bit index cycle and modulo ring storage, so no distinct valid-device bounds issue was established. `virtio_hw_map` does not validate PCI capability `cap_len`, BAR offset/length extents, or notify offset against mapped region length (`virtio_hw.c:54-109,200-227`). Those are malformed-device validation gaps; this pass did not establish a failure for a conforming modern VirtIO device, so no finding was added. No device response was supplied.

VirtIO block configuration snapshot consistency follow-up (2026-10-16; no separate finding): verified the transport exposes `config_generation` but `virtio_hw_read_blk_config` reads capacity, block size and geometry without a generation-before/after retry (`rom/devs/virtio/include/hardware/virtio.h:61`; `virtio_hw.c:249-282`). OASIS VirtIO 1.2 §2.5.1 says drivers SHOULD use the generation retry for multi-field and >32-bit reads; §3.2 permits caching configuration when changes are handled via notifications. This constructor snapshot occurs before bus start and is not refreshed. The concrete running-unit stale-capacity case, including ignored configuration interrupts and resulting old unit bounds, is already covered by OD2392. A distinct torn initial snapshot would require configuration mutation during this one-time initialization read; no separate impact beyond the existing capacity-change path was established, and the spec expresses the retry as SHOULD. No report finding added. Source-only.

VirtIO I/O submission and cache-completion recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): reread `virtio_io.c` and `virtio_queue.c` end to end, including every request removal, descriptor-chain allocation/free, cache hook and completion path. Confirmed OD2390 already covers missing end-of-transfer capacity validation; `AbortIO` remains OD2362; the second `Remove` after synchronous submit failure was checked against the unit list, which has no traversal/teardown consumer in the selected code, so no additional observable list defect was established. `CachePostDMA` is absent after completion, but the selected x86 path is coherent and OpenSBI PCIDT explicitly describes its controllers as cache coherent; no selected noncoherent backend was found, so this does not establish a selected-target stale-cache bug. Revalidated fixed queue size 128, descriptor bounds, and OD2867/OD3205 as distinct malformed-ID and ordering findings. No device, request, allocation failure or DMA was run. Source-only.
OD34 report/ledger reconciliation (2026-10-16): restored the detailed finding omitted despite the 2026-10-14 ledger note. The source confirms full-ring ambiguity after 128 unread callbacks; report now records direct-client and selected input.device CMD_STOP triggers. No runtime input was generated.
Keyboard concurrent first-open candidate withdrawn (2026-10-16): although keyboard.device itself has no first-open initialization lock, the selected lddemon OpenDevice wrapper obtains a per-device semaphore before delegating to ExecOpenDevice and holds it through the device Open vector (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:312-390,469-493,533-555`). Ordinary selected opens are serialized, so the proposed duplicate-consumer trigger was unsupported. No finding retained; direct calls bypassing the wrapper were not established as a selected client path.
Keyboard AbortIO pending-flag recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): `KBUF_PENDING` can remain set on one unit after its request is replied while another unit keeps the global pending list nonempty. However, ReplyMsg marks the request `NT_REPLYMSG` before queue publication (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:54-64`), while keyboard.device AbortIO requires `NT_MESSAGE` before removing/replying (`keyboard.c:533-545`); the stale per-unit flag alone cannot make that completed reply eligible for a second removal. OD1007 remains the distinct reply-before-IOERR_ABORTED race for an actually pending request. No request was issued.
Keyboard open/close synchronization cross-check (OD2303, 2026-10-16): selected lddemon serializes OpenDevice through its per-device semaphore, but its CloseDevice wrapper uses only local Forbid and directly invokes the close vector (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:598-623`). Thus overlapping opens alone are not the selected trigger for the keyboard unit-list race; concurrent closes on separate valid opens, or a close overlapping an open, remain possible on ExecSMP. No operation was run.

xHCI RTIso bounce-buffer lifetime refinement (OD3196 expanded, 2026-10-16): followed active transfer address selection through `xhciPrepareDMABuffer` and Stop cleanup. On 64-bit builds without controller AC64, high client buffers use a `MEMF_31BIT` bounce allocation; `xhciStopIsochIO` reaches `xhciFinishRequest`, which clears the ring back-pointers and frees that bounce allocation with zero completion length even though the queued TRB is not stopped/dequeued. This makes the post-Stop DMA lifetime issue include driver-owned freed bounce storage, in addition to caller-buffer access. No separate finding added. No controller or transfer was run. Source-only.

xHCI RTIso completion/removal synchronization pass (OD3206, 2026-10-16): traced `xhciHandleFinishedTDs` from the event task through the PTD/RTIso callback and pending-buffer refill, then traced `psdFreeRTIsoHandler` through synchronous UHCMD removal and xHCI PTD disposal. `cmdRemIsoHandler` frees per-PTD state under `Disable()`, but Exec documents this as processor-local on ExecSMP; no shared lock or event-task drain covers the completion walk. Confirmed `PCIUSB_WIP_ISO` is enabled by the selected xHCI target's `rom/usb/pcixhci/make.opts:6`. Caller census found SonixcamTool `FreeSonixcam` and USB Audio `subLibFreeAudio` (including sibling-handler cleanup) as in-tree free callers. Added OD3206 for a completion/removal overlap on another CPU. Other RTIso hooks and broader controller teardown remain pending; no handler or event was run. Source-only.

USB audio GetAttr tail review (OD3207, 2026-10-16): completed the remaining `subLibGetAttr` and `subLibHardwareControl` bodies at the file tail, tracing `AHIDB_Index` through AHI modeinfo and the Toccata frequency helpers. The fixed 100-kHz best-distance sentinel violates the public closest-rate result for far-out requests; added OD3207. Existing index accesses use caller-supplied AHI indices and are covered by OD3172 for the zero-rate-list case; no independent valid-index issue was established. Remaining file bodies and caller contracts remain open; no device or attribute query was run. Source-only.

USB Audio allocation frequency-order follow-up (OD3208, 2026-10-16): traced `AHIA_MixFreq` from AHI control creation into subdriver allocation and both USB endpoint selections. When a listed rate falls within its 100-kHz search threshold, the playback endpoint is programmed with the unadjusted requested rate, then AHI `ahiac_MixFreq` is changed to that listed rate; a failed SET_CUR is warning-only and allocation still succeeds. Duplex sibling selection occurs after the adjustment. Added OD3208, distinct from OD3191’s list-equivalence bug. No device or transfer was used; endpoint behavior after an unsupported SET_CUR remains device-dependent. Source-only.

USB Audio public attribute/control getter caller follow-up (2026-10-16; no new OD): re-read `subLibGetAttr` and `subLibHardwareControl` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3910-4162`) and traced frequency and selector attribute requests through AHI's selected preferences UI. `GetInputs`/`GetOutputs` first fetch their respective counts and then request each name only for `i` in `[0,count)` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/support.c:949-1017`); AHI mode setup likewise obtains frequency count before querying the selected frequency index (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/ahi.c:300-310,465-474,514-523`). USB Audio class-config reload and MUI worker follow-up (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced `libOpen`, `UCM_ConfigChangedEvent`, and `nLoadClassConfig` through Poseidon's periodic config-change broadcast and checked the class-config save path (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:60-103,458-470,2130-2440`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9435-9445`). The loader copies a matching `UAUD` chunk into the persistent base config under `Forbid` and releases the Poseidon library; its unconditional FALSE result is not consumed by the broadcast loop, and selected sibling USB class reload helpers use the same convention. The MUI worker increments the class open count before opening dependencies and funnels dependency/object/window failures through cleanup, which closes acquired libraries and drops the count. No independent defect established in these paths. MUI/GUI behavior was not run; source-only.

USB Audio binding identity and detach lifecycle recheck (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced class binding publication and release through Poseidon's per-interface binding slots (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:243-380`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6371-6410,6598-6613`). The apparent same-VID/PID cross-device match is not a supported candidate: `nch_UnitProdID`, `nch_UnitVendorID`, `nch_UnitIfNum`, and `nch_UnitAltIfNum` are only compared in this class and are never populated, while newly allocated units are MEMF_CLEAR; thus nonzero VID/PID does not satisfy that match. The `cfgnum` local is fetched but unused, but no incorrect caller-visible path from it was established. Rechecked `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding`'s active-task signal/wait against `nAudioTask` exit and `subLibFreeAudio`; retained OD3177 only for the qualified case where a non-NULL unit-wide current-mode pointer keeps the worker waiting. No binding, device removal or concurrent control was run; source-only.

USB Audio RTIso input completion-length cross-controller check (2026-10-16; no new OD): followed `nInDoneHook`'s use of `ubr_Length` against each selected AROS HCD completion path. UHCI sets it from the decoded actual-length field before `urti_InDoneHook` (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_isoch.c:453-477`); OHCI copies `iouh_Actual` before invoking the done hook (`rom/usb/pciusb/ohci/ohci_hcd.c:500-518`); EHCI accumulates packet actuals and publishes `iouh_Actual` before its RTIso callbacks (`rom/usb/pciusb/ehci/ehci_isoch.c:225-257`); xHCI publishes the event-derived `actual` before callback (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2774-2787`). This supports OD3193's use of actual input packet bytes for the conversion-size calculation and rules out a separate requested-versus-actual length mismatch in these completion paths. No transfer or HCD was run; source-only.

USB Audio binding startup failure cleanup (OD3209, 2026-10-16): traced class-record allocation/publication through both `psdSpawnSubTask` failure and `nAudioTask`/`nAllocAudio` failure. `nAllocAudio` can parse and allocate mode records before later port/pipe setup fails; neither failure path removes/frees the new `nh_Units` record, and its identity fields remain zero/unset so ordinary nonzero VID/PID retries do not reuse it. It is reclaimed only on class expunge. Added OD3209 as a conditional accumulation leak; no failure or retry was induced. Source-only.


Keyboard queued short-read drain follow-up (OD3212, 2026-10-16): traced `KBD_READEVENT` queueing before `writeEvents` validates event capacity, then expanded `ForeachNodeSafe` and followed its tail-sentinel state through the post-loop `kbUn->kbu_flags` cleanup. A queued request with `io_Length < sizeof(struct InputEvent)` makes `writeEvents` return TRUE; after it is removed/replied, empty-list traversal leaves `ioreq` at the tail sentinel, so cleanup interprets sentinel storage as an IORequest and writes through the resulting bogus `io_Unit`. Added OD3212. No event/request was issued; exact adjacent field depends on target layout. Source-only.


AHI AVX2 source-boundary follow-up (2026-10-16; no new finding): compared the four vector and scalar-tail loops in `addroutines_avx.c` with `CalcSamples`, segment transitions in `mixer.c`, and the `AHI_SetSound` documented source-range precondition (`sound.c:364-391,403-478,1210-1228`). Complete AVX2 chunks read only within the computed source sample count; each routine's endpoint-state fetch is the final selected sample, and the first-offset guard leaves initial-boundary handling to the scalar path. `AHI_LoadSound` retains a caller-provided address, so allocation validity itself remains the API caller's responsibility. The optional AVX2 object is not compiled by standard AROS x86 target flags; this path requires a custom AVX2-enabled build. OD3213 records that a custom 32-bit AVX2 build can still dispatch the AVX2 body without i386 OSXSAVE/XCR0 setup; standard i386 remains excluded. No valid-range AVX2 overread was established; no audio was mixed.

USB Audio zero-frequency sibling-match bounds recheck (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced accepted zero-rate modes from Type I parsing through AHI mode registration, AudioControl sibling matching, and the `AHIDB_Frequency` getter (`usbaudio.class.c:1220-1276,1851-1905,1938-1939`; `usbaudio.h:105`). `nam_FreqArray` is an embedded 64-entry array in a `MEMF_CLEAR` mode object, so comparing element zero during sibling matching is initialized and in-bounds even when `nam_NumFrequencies == 0`; it does not create a separate null/out-of-range read. The mode is still published with a zero rate count, and the direct indexed getter remains the separate OD3172 condition. No descriptor or query was used; source-only.

USB Audio downstream-fanout topology pass (OD3214, 2026-10-16): traced source-to-target edge construction through both Stage 4 graph walks and Stage 5 Feature Unit routing (`usbaudio.class.c:801-818,866-887,1580-1593,1712-1725`). The source-side eight-entry output list silently drops later fanout edges while target-side input links still retain them. A later volume-capable Feature Unit on an omitted branch can be found by reverse source traversal but miss root propagation and dereference NULL during Stage 5. Followed the failure to `nExamineAudioDescriptors` in the class startup task: successful mode discovery proceeds to `nExamineAudioUnits`/`nAddAudioModes`, so the NULL dereference occurs before startup can publish normal modes (`:2039-2077`); the generic startup failure cleanup closes AHI and signals the starter but does not convert the graph inconsistency into a handled descriptor error (`:2078-2114`). Keyboard pending-read drain same-unit check (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced two distinct `KBD_READEVENT` requests queued on one open unit through `writeEvents` and the `moreevents` break in `kbdSendQueuedEvents` (`keyboard.c:347-379,398-495,665-685`). If the first request consumes the last buffered event, the drain stops and leaves the second request pending; this is correct because the shared per-unit cursor has no event remaining. If the cursor is still behind the writer, the next request can consume subsequent buffered events. No stale-event/duplicate-read candidate follows. Kept OD927 limited to the distinct other-opener case, where the second opener still has an unread event at its own cursor. No request or keyboard event was issued; source-only.

Gameport trigger predicate follow-up (OD3215, 2026-10-16): traced GPD_SETTRIGGER into `gpu_trigger` storage, then through the active `fillrequest` branch. USB Audio timing-control update trace (OD3218, 2026-10-16): compared class allocation flags and the public `AHIA_PlayerFreq` contract with AHI's control dispatch. USB Audio returns `AHISF_MIXING` without timing; AHI documents zero as the value that disables timing, but `_AHI_ControlAudioA` still dispatches `AHIsub_Update` after setting zero. `subLibUpdate` divides by `ahiac_PlayerFreq >> 12` unconditionally; `subLibStart` repeats the same divisor (`usbaudio.class.c:3334-3345,3708-3723,3751-3771`; `audioctrl.c:382-389,946-955,1001-1005`). USB Audio `AllocAudio` early-failure and cleanup trace (2026-10-16; no new OD): followed Poseidon library open, timer/device setup, endpoint selection, later buffer failures and generic AHI rollback (`usbaudio.class.c:3278-3332,3589-3665`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:715-728`). CMI8738 helper-definition and selected-caller reconciliation (2026-10-16; no new OD): completed the `DriverData.h` field-consumer trace and direct in-tree C caller census for `misc.c` helpers. Confirmed `AllocDriverData`/`FreeDriverData` ownership via `driver-init.c`, bounded `WritePartialMask` values from `cmi8738hw.c`, `Linear2*Gain` callers, absence of a selected `SamplerateToLinearPitch` and `micro_delay` caller, and preservation of original DMA pointers by both aligned-buffer callers. Serial receive handoff backend census (OD2110, 2026-10-16): expanded the caller/backend trace from m68k and i386-PC to every checked-in HIDD that installs `serial.device`'s receive callback: Sam440, hosted Unix, and RISC-V OpenSBI in addition to those two. m68k supplies one byte per callback; PC/Sam440/RISC-V drain available UART bytes into a buffer, and hosted Unix forwards the returned read count. Thus the same stale successor offset applies to any backend callback ending exactly at the active request boundary. Serial test UI performs synchronous reads, and PPP/ModemManager use one reusable receive request, so no checked-in concurrent same-unit caller was found. Updated OD2110's affected-platform scope; no I/O was issued. Source-only.
parallel.device reused-request error-state follow-up (OD3219 expanded, 2026-10-17): rechecked the `CMD_FLUSH`→`CMD_WRITE` stale-abort path and traced supported `PDCMD_QUERY`/`PDCMD_SETPARAMS` against the default unsupported-command error. Those successful commands update status/parameters without clearing `io_Error`; a request previously completed with `IOERR_NOCMD` therefore reports failure despite performing the valid command. `DoIO` resets flags but not `io_Error` and returns the field after BeginIO. No in-tree exact failure/reuse sequence or device command was run. Source-only.

e1000 scheduler/constructor startup handshake allocation recheck (OD3222, 2026-10-16): traced scheduler reply/input-port and startup-message allocation results through the startup handshake and later input-port signal use; traced the constructor sync-port allocation and unchecked `CreateNewProcTags` result through its unconditional `WaitPort`; DOS `CreateNewProc` returns NULL on its allocation-failure path (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:216,669`). PCNet32 PCI-DMA allocation sentinel and selected backend reconciliation (OD3051/OD3053, 2026-10-16; no new candidate): checked the PCI HIDD contract against the selected x86 PCIPC class. The PCI HIDD documentation says AllocPCIMem may return `(APTR)-1` when unavailable (`rom/hidds/pci/doc/pci.en:145-148`), but the build-selected PCIPC class declares `CLID_Hidd_PCIDriver` as its superclass and overrides config access and MapPCI only (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc.conf:7,18-26`; i386/x86_64 boot manifests include `pcipc`). The inherited generic allocator returns NULL when its underlying AllocVec fails (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:194-211`), so OD3051/OD3053's NULL-failure trigger applies to this selected backend. The documented -1 sentinel remains relevant to other/unimplemented HIDD implementations; this review does not establish those as a selected PCNet32 path. No PCI memory was allocated. Source-only.
e1000 RX 82543 TBI final-byte offset audit (OD3223, 2026-10-16): compared `e1000func_clean_rx_irq`'s `last_byte` expression with `TBI_ACCEPT`'s explicit “last byte of the frame DMAed” contract and the packed Ethernet frame's 14-byte payload offset (`e1000.c:1303-1312`; `e1000_api.h:107-124`; `e1000.h:222-228`). The expression reads `length + 13` from the DMA buffer instead of `length - 1`; at default 1,522-byte RX allocation, length 1,518 reads offset 1,531. Traced activation to the selected 82543 TBI/SBP link path (`e1000_82543.c:1270-1315`) and length/allocation setup (`unit.c:639-653,656-701`). Added OD3223 for conditional OOB read and incorrect TBI acceptance. No frame or hardware path was exercised. Other Drivers report count: 685 unique OD headings. Source-only.
e1000 TBI adjustment helper/caller reconciliation (OD3223 recheck, 2026-10-16; no additional candidate): traced accepted-frame length through `e1000_tbi_adjust_stats_82543` and the caller's subsequent `length--` and CRC subtraction (`e1000.c:1308-1333`; `e1000_82543.c:395-463`). The helper's frame-length decrement adjusts hardware counters; the separate caller decrement removes the TBI carrier-extension byte before the ordinary CRC removal, so this ordering does not create a second delivered-length defect. The same call passes `frame->eth_packet_data` where the helper's `mac_addr` parameter is documented as the Ethernet destination; this makes its broadcast/multicast hardware-stat correction inspect payload bytes, but repository-wide field-use search found no consumer of `e1ku_hw_stats` or these adjusted B/M counters, so no caller-visible finding is promoted. OD3223 remains limited to the erroneous `last_byte` base offset and resulting conditional RX-buffer overread/classification. No packet or stats query was run. Source-only.
OHCI per-pipe timer OpenDevice caller/API reconciliation (OD2904/OD2955, 2026-10-16; no new candidate): checked `CreatePipe`'s unchecked `OpenDevice("timer.device", UNIT_MICROHZ, ...)` and its timed-transfer consumers (`ohcidriverclass.c:671-675,896-906,1066-1076`). Exec sets `io_Device` back to NULL on OpenDevice error, and SendIO dispatches through that field (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-123`; `sendio.c:55-62`), so a genuine failed per-pipe open followed by timed transfer would be invalid. However, the selected `timer.device` Open vector accepts every unit through UNIT_WAITECLOCK and only rejects larger values (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:407-429`); OHCI passes the valid UNIT_MICROHZ already used by its required controller timer. No separate selected failure trigger for this per-pipe OpenDevice was established beyond timer unavailability/setup, already covered by OD2955; OD2904 remains the unchecked allocation finding. No timer open or transfer was attempted. Source-only.

Printer device selected-caller audit (OD2699/OD57 recheck, 2026-10-16; no new finding): traced `Printer_Unit`'s startup handshake through `pd_DriverTask` and `pd_Init`, then checked the two persistent backend IORequests used by `pd_PWrite`, `pd_PRead`, `pd_PBothReady`, `CMD_FLUSH`, and `pd_Close` (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:218-300,403-492,538-667,764-851`). Confirmed OD2699's trigger is reachable after successful timer open when selected PostScript `PRS_PREINIT` rejects the settings; the failure path frees the embedded reply signal and closes backend requests, but omits `CloseDevice` for `pd_TIOR` before startup fails and the unit is removed. Confirmed printer `CMD_FLUSH`'s unconditional AbortIO calls are the selected idle-request path already covered by OD57. `pd_PRead` waits for the read after AbortIO, so its termination remains dependent on the selected backend's AbortIO completion behavior; no additional regression beyond existing abort findings was established. No printer startup, read, write, flush, or timer request was run. Source-only.

e1000 short-RX descriptor contract recheck (OD3028 confidence update, 2026-10-16): followed `e1000func_clean_rx_irq`'s 5-byte minimum, frame-error gate and cooked delivery into `CopyPacket` (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000.c:1292-1332,1392,1411`; `unit.c:399-401,431-460`). The 8254x Software Developer's Manual §13.7.34 states that RUC counts undersize frames that passed address filtering and have a valid CRC ([Intel manual](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/doc/manual/pci-pci-x-family-gbe-controllers-software-dev-manual.pdf)); this supports the error-free short-receive condition rather than leaving it solely hypothetical. A cooked length of 5–17 still clears the earlier `length <= ETH_CRCSIZE` test, loses four CRC bytes, and underflows the UWORD subtraction by the 14-byte Ethernet header. Raised OD3028's occurrence confidence to high while keeping the precise EOP/error-status behavior conditional on the selected controller. No NIC, frame, or callback was exercised. Source-only.

e1000 RX refill ownership/restart cross-check (OD3018 recheck, 2026-10-16; no additional finding): enumerated every checked-in caller of `e1000func_alloc_rx_buffers`, `e1000func_alloc_rx_buffers_fake`, `e1000func_configure`, and RX-resource setup/free. The allocating refill is called only by `e1000func_configure`, which is reached from the selected `Open` after successful ring-resource setup (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000.c:1053-1073`; `e1000_init.c:382-400`). Interrupt completion calls only `e1000func_alloc_rx_buffers_fake`, which advances the tail while reusing the buffer already owned by each ring slot (`e1000.c:1022-1048,1424-1436`). Thus OD3018's unchecked per-buffer allocation is an initial-Open descriptor-publication failure, not a repeated steady-state refill allocation failure. The PCI HIDD contract returns `(APTR)-1` for CPUtoPCI when DirectBus is unavailable, but the selected x86 PC PCIPC target uses the generic DirectBus mapping; no selected sentinel failure path is established (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:134-157`; `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc.conf:7,18-26`). Repeated shared Open reallocation and missing teardown remain OD3031; RX setup failure and failed-open rollback remain OD3020. No open, allocation failure, interrupt, or DMA was exercised. Source-only.

USB Audio Type I sample-depth-to-converter cross-check (2026-10-16; no new finding): followed `nExamineAudioDescriptors`' 24-bit branch (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1141-1219`) through mode publication, AHI allocation flags/buffer sizing, and playback/record converter selection (`:1929-1993,3264-3425,3480-3557`). Although the parser sets `nam_SampleType` to zero for 17–24-bit resolution, the only use of that field in this path is a commented-out assignment; the active dispatch keys on channel count and `bSubframeSize`, and 3-byte/4-byte 24-bit converters are present. The AHI mode is marked HiFi and its mixer buffer uses four bytes per channel sample. No defect follows from the zero metadata field alone. Descriptor extent validation remains covered by OD3169/OD3171, zero frame-size mode by OD3201, and 24-bit mono input sample-count fallthrough by OD3163. USB Audio input-selector index candidate withdrawn (2026-10-16; no finding): rechecked the previous candidate against the documented AHI selection contract and selector graph. `AHIDB_Inputs` returns the selector's `nau_NumInputs`, and graph construction fills entries for the reported range up to the fixed eight-entry capacity. The missing `AHIC_Input` range check therefore only permits an invalid value when a client violates the documented input-selection contract; the earlier caller audit found no selected in-tree caller doing so. The out-of-range case is not credited as a project bug. No control or device was used; source-only.


USB Audio player-softint re-cause caller recheck (EK8935 cross-check, 2026-10-16; no new finding): traced the normal `nOutReqHook` producer through the selected xHCI event task (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hw.c:523-548`) and Exec `Cause`'s task-mode delivery contract (`rom/exec/cause.c:42-55,84-126`). The request hook runs on the event task and calls `Cause` synchronously, so that same task cannot issue a second request-hook Cause while the first player callback is running. On device removal, `nReleaseHook` switches to `subLibPlayerIntDummy` and Causes it; the dummy runs Player/Mixer hooks before submitting its next timer request (`usbaudio.class.c:2747-2769,2596-2610`). The next PA_SOFTINT Cause therefore follows that callback's hook work; no same-node concurrent re-cause path was established. No additional USB Audio caller is added to EK8935. No event or timer was run; source-only.


parallel.device PDCMD_QUERY active-write caller follow-up (OD3220 expanded, 2026-10-16): checked both pending bits affected by `pu_Status = 0` and traced the selected hosted-Unix nonblocking writer. PDCMD_QUERY leaves the active-write pointer and byte counters untouched while clearing `STATUS_WRITES_PENDING`; the next CMD_WRITE bypasses the queue and can overwrite the active pointer/counters if the backend returns a partial count, or place its bytes ahead of the old remainder if accepted completely. The HIDD opens the terminal with O_NONBLOCK, registers a write-ready callback, and returns the underlying write count (`ParallelUnitClass.c:103-121,169-187,237-263`). Expanded OD3220 to include the write-order/lost-request consequence alongside the existing read hang. No request or callback was run; source-only.


parallel.device CMD_RESET fall-through correction (OD3221, 2026-10-16): re-read the complete switch and noticed that CMD_RESET has no break before CMD_FLUSH. Reset therefore drains and aborts both queued request ports through the following flush case; the earlier note incorrectly said queued requests survived. Rewrote OD3221 to retain only the active-pointer defect: the replied active read/write pointers remain published and can be consumed by a later input/read-ready callback or subsequent read. No reset or callback was run; source-only.


parallel.device zero-length CMD_READ callback-boundary audit (OD3224, 2026-10-16): traced the request path from CMD_READ enqueue and io_Actual = 0 through RBF_InterruptHandler's copy-before-completion test. A zero io_Length is not rejected; the callback writes at destination index zero, increments to one, and cannot satisfy its equality completion test, so all bytes in the delivered callback chunk are copied past the declared buffer and the request remains active. Added OD3224. No request or callback was run; source-only.


parallel.device receive progress-width audit (2026-10-16; duplicate of OD11, no new finding): compared IOStdReq's ULONG io_Length/io_Actual fields with RBF_InterruptHandler's UWORD indexDestBuf. The increment wraps after 65,535, making equality completion unreachable for larger requests; the callback also writes the wrapped cursor back to io_Actual at chunk boundaries and resumes at the start of the buffer. OD11 already covers the same serial and parallel defect. No request or callback was run; source-only.


parallel.device receive-callback full-width follow-up (OD11 cross-check, 2026-10-16; no new finding): verified ULONG io_Length/io_Actual against the UWORD local cursor and callback continuation; requests above 65,535 cannot complete and restart copying at the wrapped offset. Checked the adjacent zero-length boundary separately in OD3224. No request or callback was run. Source-only.

parallel/serial AbortIO recheck (OD57, 2026-10-16; corroboration, no new finding): traced BeginIO's partial-write publication into the active slot (outside either write queue) and both AbortIO vectors' read-only active special case. A pending active write therefore takes the generic Remove path despite not being linked; CreateIORequest clears request memory, while Exec Remove requires a linked node and dereferences its predecessor/successor. This independently confirms OD57's active-write scope. No request or abort was run. Source-only.


parallel.device first-open unit-list race recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): verified Exec OpenDevice drops the global DeviceList lock before calling the device vector, but the installed LDDemon OpenDevice wrapper holds its per-device ldon_SigSem from LDRequestObject through ExecOpenDevice and releases it only afterward (rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:391,469-497,547-553). Therefore ordinary first opens for the same device do not concurrently run parallel.device Open/NewUnit, despite UnitList and HIDD usedunits lacking their own lock. Direct calls that bypass the patched public OpenDevice path were not established; callback versus final-close lifetime remains open. Source-only.


parallel.device native HIDD receive-source audit (OD3226, 2026-10-16): compared the advertised/accepted CMD_READ path with native receive producers. The m68k ParallelUnit Init stores DataReceivedCallBack but installs only the CIA write-empty handler, whose body calls DataWriteCallBack; no m68k body invokes DataReceivedCallBack. The PC HIDD's only receive function is under #if 0 and its active unit Init merely stores callback pointers without registering a receive producer. Added OD3226, qualified for configurations that include the optional generic device and respective HIDD. No request or hardware was exercised.


parallel.device m68k HIDD Init failure recheck (OD3227, former OD2489/OD80, 2026-10-16): re-traced OpenResource("ciaa.resource") failure through the early FALSE return, the ignored HIDD_ParallelUnit_Init result and parallel.device's successful unit publication. A multi-byte CMD_WRITE can accept its first byte, then remain active because failed Init never stores the write callback or registers the CIA vector. Restored as OD3227 after finding the older candidate only in the coverage ledger, not in the current report. No resource failure or I/O was induced.


printer.device renderer-to-backend write-result audit (OD15/OD76 cross-check, 2026-10-16; no new finding): traced the selected PostScript renderer's `PFLUSH`/`ps_RenderFlush` through `Printer_Text_Write`, `pd_PWrite`, `pd_PBothReady`, and the outer CMD_WRITE reply (`workbench/printers/postscript/postscript.c:302-309,752-774`; `workbench/devs/printer/text.c:18-27,183-197,293-337`; `workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:218-255,609-617,658`). The renderer and text-buffer macros discard both wrapper return values; `pd_PWrite` also discards the prior asynchronous request's `io_Error`, and `pd_PBothReady` discards both completion errors, after which CMD_WRITE reports the full requested length. This is the existing printer backend error-loss path OD15, not an additional finding. Separately confirmed printtofile's drawer-lock failure can strand its unit semaphore, already covered by OD76 (`workbench/devs/printtofile/printtofile.c:20-51`). No print job, output file, or backend error was induced. Source-only.


USB Audio capture buffer / PCI host-controller completion audit (OD3228 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced `nInReqHook`/`nInDoneHook` and the single capture buffer (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2681-2730,3506-3510`) through xHCI, OHCI, UHCI and EHCI periodic scheduling. xHCI reuses the same handler buffer for two pending PTDs (`xhci_hcd.c:2795-2810`; `xhci_isoch.c:197-222,275-283`) and defers the done hook to event processing (`xhci_hcd.c:2777-2790`). PCI USB allocates a one-max-packet request buffer (`uhwcmd.c:1473-1481`); OHCI and UHCI each replenish two pending PTDs, calling the request hook once per PTD (`ohci_hcd.c:512-545`; `uhci_isoch.c:497-512`; `ohci_isoch.c:213-266`; `uhci_isoch.c:237-267`). Expanded OD3228 to these three backends. EHCI invokes its completion hook before requeueing the next one-packet request (`ehci_isoch.c:250-282,391-416,476-511`), so no same-handler overlap was established there. The generic PCI USB manifest selects all three companion HCD implementations; xHCI is separately selected in applicable target manifests. No device, transfer, or delayed completion was exercised; source-only.


USB Audio binding-allocation failure / hub-worker nesting and release recheck (OD3229 expanded, 2026-10-16): confirmed `usbForceInterfaceBinding` calls Permit on failed `AllocVec` without a preceding Forbid (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:303-312`); a new task's -1 `tc_TDNestCnt` shifts to -2 and `Wait` preserves/restores that value (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:236`; `permit.c:79-94`; `wait.c:84-90,122-126`). Traced the selected downstream-device class scan from the persistent per-hub `nHubTask` (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:711-724`) through shutdown (`:1084-1098`) and the synchronous binding release (`:150-175`). With the shifted count, cleanup Forbid leaves the scheduler test negative; if the task is switched after publishing `nch_Task = NULL` but before signaling, the release caller can observe NULL and free `nch` before the worker reads its ready-signal fields. Expanded OD3229 with this conditional stale-record race, directly reachable on single-CPU scheduling; no allocation failure, hub release, or schedule was induced. Source-only.


USB Audio shared unit-list SMP-synchronization audit (OD3230 expanded, 2026-10-16): checked both new-binding traversal/insertion and interface-release removal on `nh_Units` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:272-321,354-376`). Poseidon permits different hub workers to scan different devices under a shared PBase read lock and per-device write locks (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6290-6294,6183-6208`); the paths therefore do not serialize access to the class-wide list. Both insertion and removal are wrapped only in `Forbid()`, which Exec documents as processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:47-60`), while AddTail and Remove each update multiple links (`rom/exec/addtail.c:53-68`; `remove.c:47-64`). Expanded OD3230 to cover concurrent list mutations/traversal as well as duplicate unit allocation and resulting AHI mode replacement/removal (`usbaudio.class.c:1056`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:374-376,448-459`; `usbaudio.class.c:2082-2096`). No USB device, class binding, detach, mode registration, or SMP schedule was run.
USB Audio AudioControl topology/control-query cross-check (OD3164/OD3165/OD3170/OD3171/OD3176/OD3190/OD3191/OD3214 revalidated; no new finding, 2026-10-16): reread `nFindAudioUnit`, `nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, `nFlowDown`, `nFlowDownToUSBSink`, `nFlowUpToUSBSource`, `nFlowUp`, and all five `nExamineAudioUnits` stages (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:781-1925`). The parser's variable-edge and feature-control reads remain covered by OD3170; fixed-prefix/short-descriptor reads by OD3171; missing sources/cyclic links by OD3164/OD3165; output/input name-array fallback by OD3176; unmatched stream root and >8-edge root propagation by OD3190/OD3214; and incomplete duplex rate-list comparison by OD3191. The feature-unit volume query failure paths warn and retain cleared or partially populated dB bounds, but the selected path maps AHI volume to the device's range without a separate source-supported consequence beyond those existing candidates; no additional finding was promoted. Remaining descriptor producers, uncommon topologies, and device-specific control behavior remain open. No descriptor or device was used; source-only.

RTL8139 EEPROM/MII caller and bounds follow-up (2026-10-16; no new OD): checked the fixed EEPROM addresses and widths, bounded internal MII register map lookup, and four-byte PHY-address array against all selected helper callers. No source-level bounds issue found; silicon response/timing remains open. No hardware transaction was run.

RTL8139 capability and architecture-path follow-up (2026-10-16; no new OD): reconciled all accepted PCI IDs with their capability flags, unit creation, external versus internal PHY paths, and x86/non-PC delay selection. Each ID initializes the fields consumed by CreateUnit; the internal PHY fallback is address 32 and uses the range-checked register map. Silicon behavior remains open; no hardware access.

m68k Amiga keyboard HIDD request ownership follow-up (OD3240-OD3241, 2026-10-16): traced timerio allocation through OpenDevice and the generic driver removal/Dispose path. Failed allocation reaches OpenDevice’s request dereference; successful allocation is closed but not freed on disposal. The selected initializer has no in-tree removal path, so the latter trigger remains external. No allocation failure or removal was induced.

m68k Amiga keyboard reset-warning recheck (OD3242; legacy coverage label OD2002 reconciled, 2026-10-16): traced both `0x78` branches into keyboard.device reset-phase setup. The first warning is acknowledged by the HIDD without callback; only the second reaches reset handlers and begins the documented no-handshake forced-reset delay. No reset sequence was run; CIA warning timing remains hardware-dependent.

m68k Amiga keyboard HIDD singleton-guard follow-up (OD3243, 2026-10-16; reconciles legacy coverage ID OD857): confirmed `kbdhidd` is never assigned, generic HW_AddDriver has no class deduplication, and a second constructor overwrites the live `kbint.is_Data` before CIA AddICRVector returns the existing vector and causes the fatal alert. No duplicate registration or interrupt was run; no selected in-tree duplicate caller was found.

nForce repeated shared-Open DMA ownership pass (OD3244, 2026-10-16): traced the SANA-II shared admission and Open/Close callbacks into the selected `start`/`stop` function pointers. Every successful shared Open invokes `nv_open`, replacing both DMA buffer pointers; Close frees only the currently stored buffers. Added OD3244, distinct from OD3081's shared-client outage. No Open or allocation was run; source-only.

nForce descriptor-ring teardown ownership pass (OD3245, 2026-10-16): traced the selected PCIPC-inherited AllocPCIMem/FreePCIMem contract, the ring's one-time initialization allocation, the empty `nv_deinitialize`, per-open Close frees, and `DeleteUnit`'s `fe_priv` disposal. No path frees `np->rx_ring`; added OD3245, separately from OD3085's allocation-failure path. No allocation or unit removal was run; source-only.

nForce failed-Open cleanup/PCI-free contract pass (OD3246, 2026-10-16): traced all Open rejection/allocation-failure branches through `CloseDevice`, Exec's failed-open close semantics, the zeroed `fe_priv` packet-buffer fields, `nv_close`, and the selected PCIPC-inherited FreePCIMem method. Confirmed an initial failed Open can call FreePCIMem with NULL before `nv_open`; added OD3246, distinct from OD3081 and OD3084. No failed request or device was run; source-only.

USB Audio AHI mode-registration result follow-up (OD3248, 2026-10-16): traced each `AHI_AddAudioMode` call through the selected AHI database implementation. The API returns FALSE if database locking or copied-node allocation fails; `nAddAudioModes` ignores the result, and `nAllocAudio` publishes the class record and returns success regardless. Added OD3248 for formats silently missing from the AHI database after failed insertion. This is separate from OD3217's NULL name payload. No allocation failure or mode query was induced; source-only.
USB Audio mode-tag storage and pointer-lifetime cross-check (OD3248 follow-up, 2026-10-16; no additional finding): counted the selected `nam_Tags[12]` writes in `nAddAudioModes` (nine entries plus TAG_END) and compared them with AHI's tag-copy loop; no tag-array overrun was found. AHI copies the mode-name and driver strings into its database node but retains the `AHIDB_NepAudioMode` pointer as a direct value. The USB class retains parsed mode records on its class-unit list; ordinary `nFreeAudio` calls AHI_RemoveAudioMode before the eventual class-expunge free. This supports OD3248's insertion-failure consequence without establishing a separate pointer-lifetime issue. No binding/unbind or allocation failure was run; source-only.

AHI last-mode database retirement recheck (OD1442, 2026-10-16): expanded the prior coverage-only note through `LockDatabase`/`LockDatabaseWrite`, public semaphore lookup, `ObtainSemaphoreShared`, `ReleaseSemaphore`, and `_AHI_RemoveAudioMode`'s last-entry cleanup. A waiter retains the database pointer after lookup; releasing the write lock grants queued readers/writers, while the remover immediately unlinks and frees the database under only local `Forbid`. On one CPU the waiter resumes after the free; on ExecSMP it may run concurrently. Selected USB Audio teardown/addition and AHI mode-query paths establish callers of both operation types. Promoted OD1442 in the report. No operation or schedule was run; source-only.

AHI concurrent first-use publication recheck (OD1443, 2026-10-16; not promoted as a distinct mode-list finding): on ExecSMP, two `LockDatabaseWrite` calls can both find no ADB semaphore, allocate separate database objects and publish both with the same `ADB_NAME`; `AddSemaphore` serializes list insertion but does not check for an existing name. Traced all three `LockDatabaseWrite` call sites in `database.c`: `_AHI_AddAudioMode` first calls `AHI_RemoveAudioMode` and then reacquires via `FindSemaphore`; `_AHI_RemoveAudioMode` likewise reacquires before removing a mode. Thus no checked mutation writes to the private object returned by its initial absent-name creation before relookup, and separate concurrent mode lists or lost registrations were not established. A shadow empty semaphore object can remain while another same-name entry is active, but its independent functional consequence is unclear; do not count it as a finding. The waiter/free lifetime race from last-mode retirement is separately restored as OD1442. No concurrent calls were run; source-only.


Prism2 S2_SETKEY optional-counter caller recheck (OD3249, 2026-10-16): verified the SANA-II header and Prism2 command comment allow `ios2_StatData` to be NULL when unused; Prism2, Realtek8180 and Atheros5000 forward it, while their TKIP/CCMP paths unconditionally read six counter bytes. The configured SANA-II wpa_supplicant paths inspected supply non-NULL RSC buffers; the NULL-producing hostapd helper is not selected by a checked-in hostapd target. OD3249 remains a documented-API conditional for external clients, with no selected in-tree NULL trigger established. No request or device was run; source-only.

Standard and SuperSpeed USB hub per-port over-current lifecycle recheck (OD3250, 2026-10-16): traced the saved port status/change bits through each class's `nClearPortStatus`, port-power shutdown, and later connection-change removal branch (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:627-710,1110-1163`; `rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:576-660,1075-1135`). The SuperSpeed class is selected by USB ROM startup when USB3 is enabled (`rom/usb/poseidon/usbromearlystartup.c:104-110`). In both classes, when an existing child still reports connected, over-current handling cuts port power and clears the over-current latch but does not clear `nch_Downstream`, mark the `PsdDevice` disconnected, retire its bindings, or emit `EHMB_REMDEVICE`; those transitions require a separately reported connection-change bit with connection now absent. Expanded OD3250 from standard hub only to both selected hub classes, distinct from OD3236 startup handling of hub-level over-current. No hub or port event was run. `hub.class.c` remains only partially audited; this targeted pass does not close its remaining methods, callers, or backend behavior. Source-only.

Standard USB hub interrupt-timeout teardown recheck (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced the root interrupt timeout through `nHubTask` and `nFreeHub` (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:535-546,726-755,1029-1084`). The timeout marks the hub disconnected, synthesizes change bits for the tracked port bitmap, and sets the worker break signal; a per-port timeout is converted to a disconnected status so normal removal clears each successfully handled downstream slot. Any slot left after a failed status request is still retired by `nFreeHub`, which observes the disconnected hub and calls `psdFreeDevice`/sends `EHMB_REMDEVICE`. The hub record is then freed only after downstream teardown. This does not duplicate OD3250: that finding concerns an individual port over-current while the hub and child still report connected. No interrupt timeout, status error, or teardown was induced. The full hub class and controller interactions remain open. Source-only.

The unchecked descriptor extents remain OD3231, startup powering despite reported hub over-current remains OD3236, and the startup/task handoff race remains OD3229. No allocation failure, descriptor, hub, or worker was exercised. `hub.class.c` remains partially reviewed; other methods, full caller interactions, and controller behavior remain open. Source-only.

SuperSpeed hub aggregate-suspend failure follow-up (OD3251, 2026-10-16): traced `UCM_AttemptSuspendDevice` in both selected standard and SuperSpeed hub workers. Both attempt every child using `res &= psdSuspendDevice(pd)` and only stop hub activity if all succeed (`hub.class.c:1429-1448`; `rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:1534-1552`). Poseidon returns FALSE when a child binding refuses or its hub-port suspend fails (`poseidon.library.c:3805-3849`); successful earlier children already have their bindings suspended and `PDFF_SUSPENDED` set, but neither hub handler rolls them back on aggregate failure. The hub remains running. The selected Trident device-list suspend action reaches the public API (`ActionClass.c:4200-4214`). Added OD3251 for the partial hub-wide transition, distinct from OD3233 individual SuperSpeed protocol mismatch. No device or suspend request was run. Source-only.

Standard/SuperSpeed hub aggregate-resume failure pass (OD3252, 2026-10-16): both hub workers set `UCM_AttemptResumeDevice` success before iterating children and ignore each `psdResumeDevice` result (`hub.class.c:1450-1473`; `rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:1554-1578`). Poseidon resumes a child’s bindings only after its upstream `UCM_HubResumeDevice` succeeds; a failed port request leaves the child’s suspended state set and no binding recovery is reached (`poseidon.library.c:3904-3930`; standard `hub.class.c:1485-1535`; SuperSpeed `rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:1624-1652`). Realtek8180 CMD_FLUSH ordering recheck (2026-10-16; no new OD): followed `DevBeginIO` and the unit-task general-request queue through `ServiceRequest`/`CmdFlush` and `FlushUnit` (`device.c:390-418`; `unit.c:2656-2721,1365-1410`; `request.c:468-497`). A request that cannot acquire `access_lock` is appended to `GENERAL_QUEUE`; the unit task removes those messages in FIFO order and services each before taking the next. Thus a flush request queued behind earlier requests runs after them, while requests queued after the flush remain later work. `FlushUnit(..., EVENT_QUEUE, ...)` drains the write, management, adopt and event ports, then each opener's read and management ports. `SCAN_QUEUE` has no enqueue or consumer references in this driver; it is not a live pending-work queue. No CMD_FLUSH omission defect established. This is a targeted contract check, not full-file function coverage; `request.c` and `unit.c` remain open for the broader body/caller audit. No request was run. Source-only.

Atheros5000 AR5210 TX queue allocation pass (OD3293, 2026-10-16): traced `InitialiseAdapter` queue setup to AR5210 `ar5210SetupTxQueue`, then followed the failed second DATA queue index into management TX and offline HAL calls (`unit.c:599-613,944-946,2580-2589`; `hal/ar5210/ar5210_xmit.c:67-95,154-170,282-292,367-376,428-437`). Atheros5000 TX completion-status pass (OD3294, 2026-10-16): traced data and management completion through `ah_procTxDesc` and found both handlers discard `ath_tx_status` fields, retire the request and set `io_Error` to zero (`unit.c:2424-2455,2637-2660`).
