Atheros5000 key-index/key-length cross-check (OD3187 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced `S2_SETKEY` through `CmdSetKey` and `SetKey`, verified the four-entry key-array bound, 13-byte WEP member, fixed-size TKIP/CCMP copies, and unchecked `S2INFO_DefaultKeyNo` uses in configuration/TX encryption. Expanded OD3187, which already covers Prism2 and Realtek8180. The optional RX counter pointer issue remains separately qualified by OD3249. No key request or key material was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000 software CCMP replay-state cross-check (OD3120 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced `DecryptCCMPFragment` through `CCMPCheckIV` and `CCMPDecrypt`; the former stores the RX packet counter before the latter verifies MIC, so a failed-MIC frame can advance state before being rejected. Confirmed `InitialiseAdapter` selects this helper when hardware CCMP is unavailable. Expanded OD3120 from Prism2 to include Atheros5000 software CCMP. No frame or hardware was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000 RX reassembly retry cross-check (OD3274, 2026-10-16): read `GetRXBuffer` and its `RXInt` caller. When the first scan misses all ten busy slots for an unmatched source’s first fragment, the second pass clears slot zero but leaves the pointer at the allocation end and returns `buffer_no` as 10. RX processing writes through the one-past pointer and indexes the ten-element `rx_fragment_nos` array with 10. This is the Atheros5000-specific companion to OD3116 for Prism2/Realtek8180. No frame/device was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000 encrypted RX lower-bound pass (OD3295, 2026-10-16): traced RX descriptor admission into WEP/TKIP/CCMP fragment dispatch. The 30-byte total-length guard permits a derived encrypted body length of 0–7, while cipher helpers subtract their 8/12/16-byte overhead from `UWORD` without checking; hardware-decrypt branches can copy the wrapped result into reassembly storage. Added OD3295 with descriptor-zero-status delivery explicitly conditional because chipset handling of short encrypted frames was not verified. No frame or hardware was used. Source-only.


Wi-Fi fragment sequence-identity cross-check (OD3296, 2026-10-16): compared the full Sequence Control value passed into Prism2, Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 `GetRXBuffer` helpers. Each helper keys an in-progress slot by transmitter address but never checks the stored sequence-number bits; new first fragments can reuse a same-source partial slot, and later same-source fragments can append regardless of sequence. Added OD3296 for the three build-selected driver families. The retry-pointer defect is tracked as OD3116 for Prism2/Realtek8180 and OD3274 for Atheros5000. No frame/device was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000/Realtek8180 TKIP final-MIC lower-bound pass (OD3297, 2026-10-16): traced successful per-fragment TKIP processing into the final software Michael-MIC check. Neither RX caller checks the accumulated length before `TKIPDecryptFrame` subtracts eight from a `UWORD`, copies the received MIC and runs `UpdateMIC` over that length. A final fragment with valid per-fragment ICV but less than eight accumulated bytes therefore causes MIC reads and padding writes beyond reassembly storage before rejection. Added OD3297 for Atheros when `UNITF_HARDMIC` is clear and Realtek software-TKIP-MIC configurations. No frame/device was used. Source-only.


ATA PCI helper Sam440 target-selection reconciliation (2026-10-16): the earlier `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c` coverage row names the PC-selected PCI HIDD paths but omits Sam440. `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src` selects `kernel-ata` and `kernel-hidd-pciata` through `kernel-modules-sam440-ppc`; therefore `rom/hidds/ata_pci/interface_dma.c` is also selected there. OD2996 remains x86-only because its >4-GiB buffer trigger is not established on Sam440's 32-bit `IPTR`. The helper's `items > PRD_MAX` guard permits 257 entries, matching its allocated 257-entry per-table capacity; the LBA48 caller can request up to 65,536 sectors, so this count is source-reachable with a sufficiently large buffer, but no device-side 256-entry cap was established. No additional finding credited; DMA and hardware behavior remain untested. Source-only.


ATA PCI constructor cleanup Sam440 reachability recheck (OD2661 scope expanded, 2026-10-16): confirmed the selected Sam440 `kernel-modules-sam440-ppc` aggregate includes `kernel-ata` and `kernel-hidd-pciata`; the PCI ATA bus constructor allocates PRD memory before IRQ registration, then its failure path calls only superclass Dispose, while class-specific Dispose owns the matching `FreePCIMem`. Both selected Sam440 PCI HIDDs subclass generic `CLID_Hidd_PCIDriver`, and generic `AddInterrupt` returns FALSE when `KrnAddIRQHandler` fails. Expanded OD2661 from PC-only to include Sam440 when a bus-master ATA controller and the stated allocation/IRQ failure combination occur. No failure or hardware path was induced. Source-only.


ATA PCI no-DMA shared-IRQ Sam440 route check (OD3011 scope expanded, 2026-10-16): the selected Sam440 PPC440 PCI HIDD subclasses generic `CLID_Hidd_PCIDriver`; `PCIDevice_AddInterrupt` forwards each PCI `INTLine` to generic `AddInterrupt`, which registers through `KrnAddIRQHandler`. Sam440's UIC handler calls `krnRunIRQHandlers` for every asserted UIC vector, so a shared vector fans out to all registered handlers just as on PC. The PCI ATA probe admits a channel with `DMABase == 0`; on this route `ata_PCI_Interrupt` checks ATA `BUSY` only before forwarding to its active callback. Expanded OD3011 to the selected Sam440 PPC440 PCI configuration conditionally; actual no-DMA IDE hardware and line assignments were not established. No IRQ or ATA request was run. Source-only.
Keyboard final queued-read unit lifetime (OD3298, 2026-10-16): traced `kbdSendQueuedEvents` through `ReplyMsg` to the final `KBUF_PENDING` clear, keyboard Close's `FreeMem(KBUnit)`, and ExecSMP reply signaling. A request owner running on another core can consume the reply and close its unit before the handler's post-reply dereference. Added OD3298 conditionally for selected ExecSMP configurations; no request was issued and the race was not reproduced. Source-only.
Keyboard per-open pending-flag cross-unit recheck (2026-10-16; no additional finding): confirmed `KBUF_PENDING` is per `KBUnit` while `kb_PendingQueue` is global. When the drain empties requests from several units, it clears only the flag of the last request; other units can retain a stale flag. `AbortIO` still requires the supplied request to be `NT_MESSAGE` before removing it (`keyboard.c:533-545`), so an already-replied request cannot be removed just because its unit flag is stale. A later valid queued request sets the flag and is linked before it can be aborted. The stale flag alone therefore does not establish a client-visible failure; OD3298 remains the separate post-reply lifetime access. No request was issued. Source-only.
Gameport final queued-read unit lifetime pass (OD3299, 2026-10-16): traced `gpSendQueuedEvents` through `fillrequest`, request removal and `ReplyMsg` to the post-loop `GBUF_PENDING` clear (`gameport.c:49,571-605`). Close frees the request's `GPUnit`; ExecSMP reply signaling permits the owner to consume the final reply and close on another CPU before the clear. The callback invokes the drain synchronously from its mouse-event path (`:550-558`). Added OD3299 for the conditional cross-core stale-unit access. No request or device was used. Source-only.
Gameport AbortIO post-reply unit-lifetime cross-check (OD1007/OD3299, 2026-10-16; no duplicate finding): `AbortIO` also calls `ReplyMsg` before storing IOERR_ABORTED and before its final per-unit `GBUF_PENDING` clear (`gameport.c:467-479`). A cross-core shared-port consumer that reclaims the request can race either subsequent request access, already captured by OD1007; if it closes the owning device unit, the later flag clear is the same per-open unit lifetime consequence captured by OD3299. No separate candidate or request was added/run.
Gameport unit-index and trigger-query recheck (OD3215 scope, 2026-10-16; no new finding): Open rejects `unitnum > GP_MAXUNIT`, with `GP_MAXUNIT == 1` and `gp_cTypes[GP_NUNITS]` sized for two units, so the `GPD_ASKCTYPE`/`GPD_SETCTYPE` index remains bounded (`gameport.c:169-175,346-367`; `gameport_intern.h:24-26,50`). ASK/SET trigger requests require exactly one `GamePortTrigger` structure and use the open-unit field; the selected input.device sets a trigger but does not query it. The trigger predicate remains disabled in `fillrequest`, already detailed as OD3215; no separate query/index defect established. No request was issued. Source-only.
Gameport event-ring capacity/overrun pass (OD3300, 2026-10-16): traced allocation size, four-word record writes, modulo writer wrap and per-open read cursor (`gameport_intern.h:20-27,48-51`; `gameport.c:536-548,618-655`). After 100 unread callbacks, writer and reader positions coincide and BeginIO's equality test treats the full ring as empty. Added OD3300 for the conditional direct-client event loss; selected input.device's persistent one-event request does not establish a typical 100-event backlog. No callback or request was run. Source-only.
TimeDelay alib return-value and caller pass (OD3301, 2026-10-16): read the full helper and matched its return contract to its `DoIO` path. After successful timer.device open and completed `TR_ADDREQUEST`, it assigns one to the result even though the documented success value is zero; it also discards the request's `io_Error`. The only maintained direct callers found are Intuition menu delays, which ignore the return, so the delay still occurs there but caller-visible status is wrong for clients that check it. No timer request was run. Source-only.

## SD-card device source inventory and initial hotplug pass

Selection traced from `rom/devs/sdcard/mmakefile.src` through `arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src`, `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src`, and `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdcard/mmakefile.src`. The 32-bit Pi target selects the SDHOST backend; AArch64 carries SDHOST and Arasan/EMMC2 and selects the controller using the SoC peripheral base and card presence (`sdcard_bcm2708init.c:100-127`; SDHOST returns early on BCM2711/2712 in `sdcard_sdhost_init.c:139-148`). File-by-file review remains open; entries below mark only the focused initial pass, not completion.

No additional source-supported defect established in the local helper paths. SD-card reinsertion finding (OD3302, 2026-10-16): confirmed the hotplug sequence against the selected AArch64 SDHCI insertion/removal interrupts, one-unit BusUnits allocation, empty `ReleaseUnit`, off-by-one `>` check and later Open lookup. The report finding is conditional on card removal followed by reinsertion; no device or hardware was used. Source-only.
SD-card NewStyle query bounds pass (OD3303, 2026-10-16): traced the advertised query branch through `HandleIO` and compared its unbounded structure writes with `NSDeviceQueryResult` and the selected `input.device` length guard. Rechecked all direct in-tree query callers found (NTFS, BHFormat, GRUB); they set a full-size output request, so the defect remains a public direct-request candidate without a selected short-buffer trigger. No request was sent.

SD-card command-dispatch and geometry pass (2026-10-16; no new finding): read the complete command handlers, 32/64-bit translation tables, supported-command arrays, and the initial sector read/write loops (`sdcard_device.c:1-585`; `sdcard_ioops.c:119-556`). Confirmed geometry capacity is stored in sectors (`sdcard_bus.c:444`) and the geometry command reports that sector count; the 64-bit command IDs map to the corresponding handlers and card-capacity gating is present. The 32-bit media-range comparison is performed after byte offsets/lengths are shifted by the fixed nine-bit sector size, so the arithmetic does not overflow from valid ULONG request byte fields. The reviewed flush, change-interrupt, and geometry slices yielded no additional source-supported finding. Remaining SD-card command, bus, unit, and architecture paths remain open; this was a focused pass, not full-file completion. No request or device was used. Source-only.

SD-card Open/StartUnit failure propagation pass (OD3304, 2026-10-16): traced the device Open hook through Exec `OpenDevice` and `StartUnit`'s activation path. Open clears `io_Error` and increments `unit_OpenCnt` before activation; on CMD7 failure it only logs `StartUnit == FALSE`, so Exec returns success with `AF_Card_Active` unset. In addition, StartUnit ignores `WaitStatus` failure and can return TRUE, causing Open to publish an active unit without confirmed Transfer readiness. Added OD3304. The rest of unit registration/cleanup, signal failure, controller-specific commands and transfer completion remain under review. No card or hardware was used. Source-only.

SD-card BusTask signal-allocation failure pass (OD3305, 2026-10-16): verified that media and command signal allocation failures are detected but leave -1 in the fields, while the task wait mask, BusIRQ delivery, media dispatch and WaitCmd shift by those values. Only the separate task wake signal has a fallback. Added OD3305 for missed hotplug notification or failed command-completion waits under signal exhaustion. Bus startup failure handling and controller IRQ teardown remain open. No task or signal exhaustion was run. Source-only.

SD-card RegisterUnit CSD failure rollback pass (OD3306, 2026-10-16): traced the slot/count update ahead of CMD9 through each failed CSD exit and matched the retained non-NULL entry to Open's count/pointer check. The pool is created with `MEMF_CLEAR`, but the uninitialized unit fields still leave the entry unusable; no rollback occurs before `RegisterUnit` returns FALSE. Added OD3306. Remaining bus initialization/cleanup, signal handling callers, and architecture transfer paths remain open. No card was used. Source-only.

SD-card TD_PROTSTATUS caller pass (OD3307, 2026-10-16): compared the unconditional `io_Actual = -1` with the disabled flag check, normal-build write flags and both selected AFS/SFS write-protection callers. AFS and SFS require zero for writable status while the SD-card write handlers permit writes in normal builds. Added OD3307 for false read-only reporting. No filesystem or card was used. Source-only.

SD-card ADMA2 descriptor/bounce pass (2026-10-16; no new finding): traced descriptor allocation, 64-byte alignment, 32-entry capacity, 32 KiB per-descriptor cap, unaligned-buffer bounce path and DMA completion/cache handling (`sdcard_bus.c:675-844,1125-1150`). The generic transfer loop caps chunks at 128 sectors (64 KiB). When verification buffers are available, startup compares DMA reads with PIO and disables DMA on error/mismatch; if those temporary allocations fail, it leaves DMA enabled, but this pass did not establish that as a defect because the comparison is a validation aid rather than a documented prerequisite (`:848-892`). No unbounded descriptor write or clear fallback defect was established in these slices. ADMA2 initialization/resource lifetime and controller-specific IRQ/error handling remain open; this is a focused path pass, not full SD-card review. No DMA transfer or card was used. Source-only.

SD-card WaitCmd timeout/IRQ-state pass (OD3308, 2026-10-16): traced `WaitCmd`'s deadline initialization through the bus-task IRQ-seen branch and the subsequent bounded polling loop. The IRQ-seen branch uses an unbounded `Wait` before entering any deadline check; the command signal is only sent by response/error handling. Added OD3308 for the conditional bus-task stall if a later completion interrupt is lost. The full IRQ state machine, error-bit recovery, and architecture backends remain open. No command or hardware was used. Source-only.

SD-card backend initialization allocation/cleanup pass (OD3309-OD3310, 2026-10-16): read the applicable SDHOST and BCM SDHCI init branches. Both compute an aligned mailbox pointer from an unchecked allocation and index it on applicable board paths (OD3309). SDHOST allocates external control-block/bounce memory and a DMA channel before a later unit-table allocation, but its failure branch frees only pool objects; a control-block or channel failure also reaches a cleanup label that only frees the mailbox buffer (OD3310). AArch64 BCM cleanup, board register restoration, and the remaining SDHOST/SDHCI transfer implementation remain open. No board or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

SDHOST transfer DMA and command-completion pass (OD3311-OD3312, 2026-10-16): traced SDHOST's optional bounce allocation to data-command submission, then the DMA end poll, command-idle timeout, error-bit test, response extraction and error cleanup. The init path continues without a bounce buffer while SendCmd rejects data requests, despite the comment's direct-DMA fallback (OD3311); the post-transfer command-idle timeout is only debug-logged before the function may return success (OD3312). The generic chunk ceiling fits the configured bounce size; full SDHOST request semantics, DMA address/cache contracts, BCM SDHCI backend, and timer helper remain open. No transfer or hardware was used. Source-only.

Raspberry Pi SD-card MMIO timing/timer rollover pass (OD3313, 2026-10-16): read the full BCM byte/word/long MMIO accessor source and timer helper. `sdcard_CurrentTime` reads the 32-bit low timer counter; `sdcard_Udelay` and the BCM283x inter-write delay both compare against `start + interval` without wrap-safe subtraction. Added OD3313 for skipped intervals when calls cross the counter rollover. EMMC2 direct-write calls avoid the inter-write delay helper; other controller timing and generic timer.device usage remain open. No timing or hardware was run. Source-only.

SD-card MMC/SDSC frequency-setup helper pass (OD3314, 2026-10-16): traced MMCSwitch's 0/-1 return convention into MMCChangeFrequency and StartUnit's final 20/26/52 MHz choice; the `!= -1` condition is inverted and treats successful switching as failure, preventing high-speed flags/readback (OD3314). Read the SDSC SCR/CMD6 check and switch helper paths; no separate finding was established, but card response-field semantics remain to verify. No card or command was used. Source-only.

SD-card Scan worker-creation failure path (OD3315, 2026-10-16): traced Scan's controller-specific BusInit call, pending-task accounting, optional task-name allocation and NewCreateTask failure branch. The branch decrements the pending count but leaves initialization successful; the name-allocation failure also skips the bus silently. Added OD3315; per-bus hardware is configured before task creation, and SDHOST setup has already muxed pins/allocated DMA resources. Remaining task cleanup and device initialization rollback remain open. No task or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

SD-card bootwait/timer failure-path pass (OD3316, 2026-10-16): read the full resident wait callback and `timer.c`; timer.device OpenDevice failure returns from a one-tick delay, DoIO status is ignored, and the enclosing loop decrements its fixed tick budget regardless. Added OD3316 for a premature boot continuation when timer service fails while a bus task is pending. `Timer_Open` explicitly does not validate `mn_Length`, so bootwait's unusual message length is not promoted as a separate defect. No timer or boot was run. Source-only.

SD-card queue, completion, and worker lifetime recheck (2026-10-16): read `BeginIO`, `AbortIO`, `HandleIO`, `CMD_FLUSH`, `TD_ADDCHANGEINT`/`TD_REMCHANGEINT`, and the full `BusTask` wait/dispatch loop (`sdcard_device.c:273-404,549-703`; `sdcard_bus.c:1679-1801`). All commands currently take the worker path because `isSlow` returns TRUE for every command; `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` is intentionally retained without replying, and clears `UNITF_ACTIVE`; AbortIO explicitly returns without aborting. `CMD_FLUSH` replies only requests still in the shared bus queue, while the worker processes active I/O synchronously, so no separate active-request cancellation claim is established. Verified the failed TaskSig fallback is a bit index (`SIGBREAKB_CTRL_E == 14`) and is correctly shifted when constructing the Wait mask; no finding. Request dispatch/quick-completion and removal handling are now checked, but bus-task creation/teardown, full command-handler contracts, backend implementations, and much of the controller/error state machine remain open. No request or hardware was used. Source-only.

SD-card CSD geometry and 64-bit request-boundary pass (2026-10-16): traced SDSC and SDHC/XC CSD formulas into generated DOS geometry and unit sector capacity (`sdcard_bus.c:412-480`), then followed the 32-/64-bit command handlers and sector backends. No separate geometry arithmetic issue established for supported CSD field ranges. Checked apparent 64-bit `block + count` overflow candidate and withdrew it: byte offsets are first shifted by the configured sector shift of 9, constraining the sector value to at most 55 bits before addition, so this path cannot wrap a 64-bit sum. Remaining registration rollback, full command map, backend protocol/status contracts, and controller state transitions are open. No card or I/O was used. Source-only.

BCM SDHOST backend file pass (2026-10-16): read `sdcard_sdhost_init.c`, `sdcard_sdhost_bus.c`, `sdcard_sdhost_intern.h`, and the selected DMA resource reset/wait implementation. Traced pin setup, core-clock query, allocation and alignment, channel setup, bus registration, clock/power/width, per-command data programming, bounce-buffer path, cache handling, DMA start/poll, command idle/response, failure reset/FIFO drain, IRQ clearing, and synchronous WaitCmd/Finish hooks. OD3309-OD3312 remain the supported init-allocation, cleanup, absent-bounce, and ignored command-idle-timeout candidates. Init rollback follow-up expanded OD3310 after confirming the `bus`/`priv` pair cleanup is skipped when only one initial pooled allocation succeeds (`sdcard_sdhost_init.c:191-194,325-339`); the later DMA-resource cleanup gaps remain. A focused symbol census found no later `FreeMem`/`DMAFreeChannel` path for `dma_cb_raw`, `dma_bounce_raw`, or the allocated channel in the selected SDHOST source; the separate device-level no-expunge rollback leak remains OD3318. This pass found no separate source-supported issue in the other transfer branches. Full controller timing/errata semantics and card protocol behavior remain unverified from source alone; SDHOST applies only on BCM2835/2836-era targets, while BCM2711/2712 exit this backend and use EMMC2. No board, DMA transfer, or failure injection was run. Source-only.

BCM Arasan/EMMC2 selection and MMIO helper pass (2026-10-16): read the complete `sdcard_bcm2708init.c`, `sdcard_bcm2708bus.c`, `sdcard_intern.h`, `sdcard_bcm2708time.c`, and controller register definitions. Traced BCM2711 EMMC2-to-Arasan fallback by live card-present bits, BCM2712's distinct EMMC2 base/IRQ/mailbox offset, firmware clock/power queries, host clock-base override, register byte/word accessors, older-Arasan write spacing, and direct EMMC2 writes. Mailbox allocation failure remains OD3309; SD-card timer rollover delays remain OD3313 (shared SDHCI polls; Arasan inter-write delay is BCM2711 fallback only). ADMA allocation failure is a PIO fallback (`ADMASetup` returns FALSE and `SendCmd` leaves DMA mode clear), so the ignored allocation return is not independently promoted. Detailed SDHCI command/IRQ/ADMA paths were checked in the earlier focused bus pass; host-controller register/errata semantics and real board routing remain hardware-dependent. No board or MMIO was used. Source-only.

sdcard.device generated init rollback pass (OD3318, 2026-10-16): traced `CommonInit`'s pool creation and every later selected Raspberry Pi controller init hook into `ADD2INITLIB` ordering and compiler `_set_libinit` failure rollback. Backend init hooks may return FALSE after CommonInit succeeds; `sdcard.conf` sets `noexpunge`, no expunge-lib cleanup is registered, and generated rollback frees the device base after calling an empty expungelib set, leaving the separately allocated pool orphaned. Added OD3318. Distinct from OD3310's controller-specific partial object/DMA cleanup because this leaks the generic pool itself on any later failed init hook. No initialization failure was induced. Source-only.

sdcard.device Scan task-name ownership follow-up (OD3319, 2026-10-16): checked Scan task-name allocation and TASKTAG_NAME lifetime against NewCreateTaskA, whose implementation copies the supplied name into its task allocation. Scan does not release its 24-byte public buffer after either task-create result, so added OD3319 for the per-bus temporary name leak. One bus is configured per selected Raspberry Pi backend; no task was created. Source-only. The adjacent sprintf size lead was checked and not promoted: "SDCard bus:00 Subsystem" is 23 characters plus NUL, exactly fitting 24 bytes for selected bus number 0; %02u grows above 99, outside the one-bus selected configurations.

sdcard.device timer helper and unit Open/Close pass (2026-10-16): read complete timer.c/timer.h and the generic Open/Close paths. sdcard_OpenTimer cleans the message port/request after every failed open/allocation stage; sdcard_CloseTimer closes and disposes both; sdcard_WaitTO has no maintained caller, and BusTask retains its timer for its intentional infinite lifetime. Open/Close unit count changes balance on successful opens; the false-success activation path remains OD3304. The global unit index behavior is bounded by the selected one-bus builds (unit base zero); no separate issue established. Generic initialization rollback pool leakage is OD3318. No timer or unit open was executed. Source-only.

SDHCI task-context data-error propagation pass (OD3320, 2026-10-16): compared the normal BusIRQ PIO FinishData error path with both WaitCmd lost-IRQ/task-context recovery call sites. IRQ sets sdcb_CmdError on FinishData failure and enters reset/cleanup; recovery either gates only interrupt acknowledgment on the result or ignores it, then WaitCmd's final status checks only timeout and sdcb_CmdError. Added OD3320 for the conditional false-success case when a recovered PIO error occurs after inhibit clears. Other interrupt/error transitions, SMP listener claim races, and backend-specific status semantics remain open. No transfer was run. Source-only.

SD-card NSD command capability/dispatch reconciliation (OD3321, 2026-10-16): matched both capacity-specific SupportedCommands slices against map32/map64, immediate special cases, and handler behavior. The lists advertise HD_SCSICMD in both cases, but dispatch reaches cmd_DirectSCSI, which always returns IOERR_BADADDRESS; added OD3321. SFS's direct-SCSI fallback is avoided because this same list advertises NSCMD_TD_READ64, but direct command clients can rely on the false capability. Other advertised commands were matched to a dispatch entry or the explicit TD_GETDRIVETYPE/NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY special case; RAWREAD/RAWWRITE and unimplemented multiple/DMA operations are not listed. Remaining command caller/error contracts and external NSD clients remain open. No request was issued. Source-only.

SD-card media-change notification call-chain pass (OD3322-OD3323, 2026-10-16): followed card-present IRQ flagging through BusTask's insert/remove handling and compared those paths with the only cmd_TestChanged implementation/call sites. BusTask registers/releases the unit but does not automatically invoke cmd_TestChanged; TD_CHANGENUM merely returns the unit field and TD_ADDCHANGEINT only queues the request. The helper is invoked by an explicit TD_EJECT request even though the backend Eject is an IOERR_NOCMD stub, so a later such request can process a pending notification. Added OD3322 for missing automatic media-change API notification on card-detect-capable SDHCI/EMMC2 backends. Rechecked the flag-clear race: the helper's final unsynchronized clear can erase an IRQ-set event that arrives during its callbacks, despite the bus IRQ using the SMP lock; Forbid only prevents task switches, and TD_EJECT reaches this helper. Added OD3323 for that conditional lost transition. No card event or callback was generated. Source-only.

SD-card registration/remove concurrency and rollback recheck (OD3306 expanded; OD3324, 2026-10-16): re-read RegisterUnit from CSD command through geometry publication and compared its media-present update with BusIRQ's locked removal update. Expanded OD3306 to include the unsupported-CSD-structure return after the unit pointer/count, read/write callbacks and AF_Bus_MediaPresent have already been published; no rollback occurs before the caller can Open that unit. Added OD3324 for the separate in-flight removal window where RegisterUnit's unlocked late OR restores MediaPresent after the IRQ cleared it, leaving TD_CHANGESTATE and request checks stale and prompting BusTask to treat the pending event as insertion. No card event was generated. Source-only.
SD-card DOS-node publication caller pass (OD3325, 2026-10-16): traced RegisterUnit's MakeDosNode/AddBootNode path through `rom/expansion/addbootnode.c` and its documented BOOL result. AddBootNode can reject insertion on boot-node allocation/duplicate-name failure or DOS AddDosEntry failure; RegisterUnit ignores that result, returns TRUE and retains the allocated node without a retry/cleanup path. Added OD3325. Other expansion clients, actual DOS-list state and allocation-failure behavior remain untested. Source-only.
SD-card startup pending-task counter and BootWait caller pass (2026-10-16; no new finding): traced Scan's increment and NewCreateTask-failure decrement against BusTask's one-time startup decrement and `sdcard_Wait`'s bounded polling loop (`sdcard_init.c:58-96`; `sdcard_bus.c:1680-1732`; `bootwait.c:38-64,89-125`). Each successfully created bus task decrements once before entering its loop; the create-failure path decrements its own increment. The checked Raspberry Pi configurations register one bus, so no concurrent Scan increment/decrement interleaving was established in selected builds. The boot wait can time out and intentionally continues, and timer failure-as-elapsed-time remains OD3316. The separate unchecked signal allocation/shift paths remain OD3305. No task, timer or bus was created.
SD-card unit-table allocation and caller recheck (OD3302 retained, 2026-10-16; no new finding): traced the shared `sdcbu_UnitCnt` allocation/index path through both selected backend initializers, `RegisterUnit`, `Open`, and BusTask removal handling (`sdcard_bus.h:22-28`; `sdcard_bus.c:368-376,516-519,1744-1759`; `sdcard_init.c:149-164`; BCM init files at their unit-table setup). Each selected backend allocates one pointer-sized `sdcard_BusUnits`; SDHOST sets UnitMax=1 and BCM SDHCI uses `BCM2708SDUNIT_MAX`. The existing post-increment `>` check allows the next index and writes it before any rejection, matching OD3302; ReleaseUnit remains empty and does not reset the count or pointer. Both checked Raspberry Pi boot targets select a single backend/bus, so no nonzero unit-base cross-index trigger was established. No card insertion/removal was run.

SDHCI task-context completion-error propagation recheck (OD3320 expanded, 2026-10-16): reread complete `FinishData` and the associated WaitCmd lost-IRQ/final-listener recovery plus BusIRQ error branch. The IRQ path saves error status into `sdcb_CmdError`, resets, and signals; task-context recovery instead discards PIO failure returns, and its DMA FinishData branch always returns zero without checking `sdcb_BusStatus`. Expanded OD3320 to include missed/delayed IRQ ADMA completion with a data error and cleared inhibit bits. No controller status or transfer was generated. Source-only.

BCM Arasan/EMMC2 initializer and SDHCI reset/clock helper full-body pass (OD3326-OD3327, 2026-10-16): read the complete selected BCM initializer and traced its reset and clock calls through the generic SDHCI helpers and `StartUnit`. `SoftReset` breaks on timeout but returns void, so initialization continues to capability reads and RegisterBus; `SetClock` similarly breaks after internal-stable timeout and still enables the card clock. Added conditional false-success findings OD3326 and OD3327. Existing OD3309 covers the unchecked mailbox allocation; ADMA allocation failure intentionally falls back to PIO. Firmware tag response semantics, hardware reset/clock behavior, and teardown remain unverified. No board or failure was run.

BCM2835/2836 SDHOST initializer full-body and clock-query caller pass (OD3309-OD3311 rechecked; OD3328 added, 2026-10-16): read the complete selected initializer, traced every early return/failure label and allocations through the success registration path, confirming prior OD3309/OD3310/OD3311 conditions and no separate cleanup finding. SDHCI bus-task IRQ-installation and idle hotplug pass (OD3329, 2026-10-16): traced `KrnAddIRQHandler`'s nullable allocation result into BusTask, the conditional interrupt enable in `SDBusPostIRQInit`, and the idle Wait loop. The kernel implementation returns NULL if it cannot allocate the handler node; the bus task neither fails startup nor polls card presence when idle, so selected SDHCI card-detect service is absent in this case. Added OD3329, separate from OD3322's missing API notification dispatch after a delivered event. No handler allocation failure or card event was induced. Source-only.

OD3329 alternate-observer boundary recheck (2026-10-22): reread the selected SDHCI post-IRQ init, full BusTask startup-to-wait branch, and trackdisk media-change helpers (`sdcard_bcm2708init.c:58-70`; `sdcard_bus.c:1714-1760`; `sdcard_device.c:293-321,409-416`). Confirmed that a card already present is registered by the one startup check even if IRQ registration failed; thereafter `BusTask` waits without a hardware card-presence poll. `cmd_TestChanged()` checks only `AF_Bus_MediaChanged`, which is updated by BusTask's media event path; `TD_CHANGENUM` and `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` do not independently read controller state. Refined OD3329's wording to preserve the startup-present case and distinguish event APIs from hardware polling. No IRQ allocation failure or card event was induced; source-only.

SDHOST DMA transfer caller/state recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): traced the generic 32-/64-bit sector loops and protocol helper lengths into SDHOST `SendCmd`, then searched all selected references to `xfer_active`, `xfer_is_dma`, `dma_active`, and saved data fields. The sector callers cap chunks at 128 sectors (64 KiB); selected card-register transfers are 8, 64, or sector-multiple bytes, all divisible by four, so the ARM/non-ARM word-copy tail does not truncate any identified in-tree transfer. The transfer-state fields have no consumer beyond initialization/clear in this backend, so their stale values on error do not prove a separate state defect. OD3311 and OD3312 remain; DMA reset/cache/address contracts still need hardware-level evidence. No transfer or hardware was used. Source-only.

BCM SDHCI MMIO helper full-body/caller pass (2026-10-16; no new finding): read the complete `sdcard_bcm2708bus.c` (150 lines), including LED control, clock divisor, little-endian byte/word/long access, repeated PIO data-port reads, Arasan inter-write pacing, and EMMC2 direct writes. Traced selected generic callers: W1C interrupt-status clearing uses 32-bit writes, while byte/word read-modify-write helpers serve host, clock, power, reset, timeout, and transfer-control registers. No additional source-supported helper defect established. Command/IRQ state-machine, controller-specific register semantics, and hardware timing remain open; no MMIO was accessed.

SD-card generic transfer-loop completion pass (2026-10-16): read all four 32/64-bit read/write implementations and their command builders, chunk progression, byte accounting, stop-command/WaitCmd error handling and Reschedule points (`sdcard_ioops.c:119-556`); cross-checked `sdcard_device.c` range and alignment validation plus in-tree transfer callers. Chunk size is 128 sectors, so per-chunk byte shifts and full-request `io_Actual` remain within the 32-bit request-length range; block advancement cannot exceed the handler-validated capacity. Failed data or stop completion returns IOERR_ABORTED and does not count the failed chunk as completed. The remaining multiple/DMA entry points are explicit IOERR_NOCMD stubs and are not installed in unit vtables. No distinct defect established in these loops. External card response semantics and caller-buffer validity remain API/hardware contracts, not source findings from this pass. No I/O or card was used. Source-only.

SD-card protocol helper pass (2026-10-16): read complete `sdcard_sdscunit.c` and `sdcard_mmcunit.c`, traced `SDSCSwitch`, SCR reads, switch-status retries, MMC EXT_CSD switch/readback, and `WaitStatus` callers through `StartUnit` (`sdcard_bus.c:55-208`). OD3314 remains confirmed: MMCChangeFrequency interprets MMCSwitch's successful zero return as failure and its caller ignores the helper result. StartUnit also ignores status-wait and frequency negotiation results, but protocol setup failure behavior is not promoted separately here because the unit still has explicit basic transfer-mode setup and optional speed negotiation; card response semantics need external protocol/hardware validation. SDSC high-speed support/readback masks and busy retry fields were traced but not independently verified against the card specification. `AF_Card_MMC` is only consumed, not set in this selected source; this pass did not claim MMC support or add a dead-path finding. Remaining generic initialization rollback and host-side task/resource lifecycle are open. No card or command was used. Source-only.
SD-card device init/rollback full-body recheck (OD3315/OD3318/OD3319 retained, 2026-10-16): reread all local functions in `sdcard_init.c`, both selected controller-init callers and the generated init rollback. `CommonInit` cleanup handles its own early failure before pool creation; the later-hook pool leak is OD3318. Both bus `BusInit` vtable callbacks return void, so Scan has no status result to drop. Scan's false-success paths and temporary task-name leak remain OD3315/OD3319. SD-card device command/selected-caller pass (OD3303/OD3307/OD3321-OD3323 rechecked, 2026-10-16; no new finding): read the complete `sdcard_device.c` body and compared both capability-list variants, `map32`/`map64`, immediate cases, slow-command queueing and AbortIO result with selected SFS, Eject and HDToolBox callers. SFS expects write-protect and media-state queries and registers change callbacks; missing event dispatch and false protection status remain OD3307/OD3322. `C:Eject` first tries HD_SCSICMD and then TD_EJECT; the advertised-but-rejected direct-SCSI command remains OD3321. HDToolBox's geometry and SCSI commands match the dispatch paths. No separate command-map or completion defect established. No I/O request or device was used.

USB MassStorage TD_ADDCHANGEINT/TD_REMCHANGEINT cross-CPU caller pass (OD3330 added, 2026-10-16): traced the shared pending-request list through `cmd_AddChangeInt`, `cmd_RemChangeInt`, worker `DoChangeInt`, `ForeachNode`, and FAT `CleanupDiskHandler`. AArch64 Raspberry Pi's `smp` variant enables ExecSMP and its package selects both USB MassStorage and FAT; FAT removes the notification synchronously, then frees the request. Added OD3330 for the resulting conditional list traversal/request-lifetime race. No media or concurrency operation was run. Source-only.

SD-card sector I/O loop and caller recheck (2026-10-16; no new OD): read the full `sdcard_ioops.c` body and traced 32/64-bit helpers through `cmd_Read/Write32/64`. Selected callers bound sector counts by ULONG byte lengths and capacity checks; 128-sector chunks keep transfer-length shifts and per-chunk `act` increments within range. Multi-block byte totals advance only after data completion and a successful stop command. The legacy PIO/busy-wait stubs have no maintained references. Controller/firmware behavior remains hardware-specific; no transfer was run. Source-only.

SDHOST SendCmd/caller completion recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): reread the complete selected transaction path from request tags through `sdhost_dma_setup`, channel reset/CB programming, command issue, bounded DMA poll, cache/bounce copy, command-idle check, response unpack, and error cleanup (`sdcard_sdhost_bus.c:143-580`). No independent bus-address or completion defect was established because the selected `AllocMem(MEMF_PUBLIC)` allocations' address class is not proven high-mapped by this source pass. SDHCI reset/clock/power selected-caller pass (OD3326/OD3327 rechecked, 2026-10-16; no new finding): reread `SoftReset`, `SetClock`, and `SetPowerLevel`, then traced all selected calls in BCM SDBus initialization, SDHCI bus registration, card OCR negotiation, StartUnit speed changes, and command/data recovery (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_bus.c:114-160,320-341,521-649,925-937,1625-1636`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdcard/sdcard_bcm2708init.c:35-54,305-353`). Voltage selection uses the card/host OCR intersection on the selected path; no additional unsupported-voltage behavior established. Controller-specific reset completion, clock stability, and power sequencing remain hardware/firmware semantics; no register or card operation was run. Source-only.
AHIRecord S32S level-meter caller pass (OD3331 added, 2026-10-16): traced `RecordFuncS`'s buffer/type publication to the level task's per-frame index arithmetic, then checked the AHI S32S layout and selected Envy24HT 24-bit callback producer. On little-endian AROS, the `WORD` indices select the low halves of the two 32-bit channel samples, which can be zero while the high halves carry nonzero amplitude. Added OD3331 for the conditional meter display error; recording-buffer copy behavior was not included in this finding. No recording or UI action was run. Source-only.

AHIRecord deferred level-meter buffer pass (OD3332 added, 2026-10-16): traced the callback's borrowed-buffer validity through `RecordFuncS` publication, `Signal`/`Wait`, the level task's delayed scan, and Envy24HT's alternating capture halves. A subsequent hook call can overwrite the single pending pointer/length and coalesce the signal, or reuse a buffer while the scan is in progress; only level display is implicated because recording is copied synchronously. No timing or recording was run. Source-only.

Etherlink III caller/configuration census (2026-10-16; no new candidate): searched maintained source and package/configuration references outside the selected driver directory. The only direct name references are the commented AROSTCP example `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/Env/db/interfaces:90`, the cards aggregate manifest entry, and an RTL8139 comparison comment; no additional checked-in Etherlink3 caller was found. The Network Prefs default points to PCNet32, not Etherlink III (`workbench/prefs/network/prefsdata.h:34`; `prefsdata.c:267`). This limits local caller evidence for Etherlink paths to explicit user configuration and AROSTCP conventions. Generated package output, card.resource/Prometheus semantics, and broader SANA-II clients remain open. No device was opened or request issued. Source-only.

Etherlink III unit lifecycle cross-check (OD3115 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced `DevOpen` through `GetUnit`, PCI and PC Card find/create/`AddTail`, opener admission, and `CloseUnit`. The selected PCI path has no shared SMP-safe lock for unit publication or the opener count/list/final-close transitions, confirming duplicate PCI-unit setup, concurrent exclusive admission, and Open racing final deletion on ExecSMP. The PC Card code has the same source-level gaps, but its SMP-enabled configuration and Card Resource concurrency were not established, so the report does not claim an ExecSMP PC Card trigger. `GetPCCardCount` returns at most one and `GetUnit` consequently passes only index zero; `FindPCCardUnit` ignoring its index does not produce a separate wrong-unit candidate. No hardware or concurrent lifecycle operation was run. Source-only.

Etherlink III worker-startup caller recheck (OD3106 confirmed; no new finding): traced `CreateUnit` through the AROS `AddUnitTask` macro in `task.h` to `NewAddTask`, then compared its success contract with `UnitTask` initialization. `NewAddTask` launches the task and may run it immediately; `CreateUnit` checks only task-launch success and publishes the unit without waiting for the worker's three `AllocSignal(-1)` calls (`unit.c:414-438,2462-2485`; `task.h:53-59`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:141-164,278-292`). Therefore signal exhaustion remains an unchecked worker-startup failure after successful unit construction, as OD3106 states. The other `CreateUnit` resource cleanup paths were checked against `FreeDMAMemHook`, which explicitly accepts NULL DMA pointers; no separate partial-allocation cleanup candidate was established. No task, allocation failure, or hardware was run. Source-only.

Etherlink III PC Card index/platform boundary recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): traced public unit bounds through `GetUnit`, `GetPCCardCount`, `GetPCCardUnit` and `FindPCCardUnit` (`device.c:602-615`; `pccard.c:144-162,183-225`). The count is always zero or one, and the accepted PC Card unit number maps to index zero, so the cached-list head return cannot select a different PC Card index in the checked-in implementation. The PC Card Open/Close source has the same unsynchronized state edits as PCI, but the selected Card Resource/target combination was not established to run ExecSMP; OD3115's claimed cross-CPU trigger is limited to Etherlink PCI. No card was opened. Source-only.

Prism2 RX fragment-reassembly caller recheck (OD3296 confirmed; no new finding): traced the hardware RX loop through descriptor parsing, `GetRXBuffer`, fragment decryption/append, final-fragment dispatch and slot release (`unit.c:1575-1734,1772-1808`). `RXInt` passes all 16 Sequence Control bits, but `GetRXBuffer` selects any occupied slot with a matching source address and does not compare the stored sequence-number bits; the completion path has no later sequence validation before `DistributeRXPacket`. A new first fragment from the same transmitter can select an occupied slot, then the code overwrites the Ethernet header while retaining its old slot marker; subsequent fragments can continue assembling by address alone. This confirms Prism2's existing OD3296 scope; no packet or device was used. Source-only.

Prism2 WirelessManager key-caller reconciliation (OD3187 refined; OD3333 added, 2026-10-16): traced the selected `.config`/`drivers.mak` edge to `driver_sana2`, then followed WEP configuration and WPA PTK/GTK installs. Selected ordinary WEP and GTK indices are 0..3, pairwise keys use slot 0, and CONFIG_IEEE80211W is disabled; no selected high IGTK key-index trigger was established. The WEP parser accepts 14..16-byte values, which pass unchanged to Prism2; its software WEP `seed[16]` receives 3 IV bytes plus `key->length`, confirming a 1..3 byte stack-array overrun for those accepted config lengths (OD3334). Separately, the backend drops `set_tx` and sends no `S2INFO_DefaultKeyNo`; Prism2 therefore keeps its zero-initialized transmit slot even when a valid profile selects slot 1..3 (OD3333). Direct SANA-II callers can still trigger OD3187's out-of-range slot/default values. No key request, association or radio was used. Source-only.

Cross-driver AROS interrupt-wrapper rollback pass (OD3335 expanded, 2026-10-16): searched all network `WrapInt` implementations and traced constructors/teardown for Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, Etherlink III, NvidiaNet, Prism2 and Rhine. All selected AROS PCI constructors call `DeleteUnit` directly after partial wrapper failure or interrupt-registration failure, bypassing normal unwrapping. Etherlink III and Prism2 PC Card unit constructors share the partial-wrapper gap. Realtek8180 USB was checked separately: its failure helper unwraps wrappers, so it is excluded. No allocation failure or device initialization was run. Source-only.

Prism2 PCI backend-selection cross-check (2026-10-16; no new finding): traced the m68k PowerPCI/CyberStorm library opens into `GetPCICount`, `AllocCard`, and `FreeCard`. `device.c` opens `cybpci.library` only when `powerpci.library` fails (`device.c:181-184`), so the later assignments in the shared PCI dispatch cannot overwrite two simultaneously active backend results in the selected code path. AROS excludes both m68k backends and uses Prometheus (`pci.c:135-142,386-393`). Prometheus board enumeration/removal and attribute-query semantics remain external to this source pass. No PCI device was opened. Source-only.

Etherlink III AROS wrapper-callback caller pass (OD3335 expanded; no separate new finding): traced `AROSDevInit` wrapper registration, the `AROS_UFC` callback adaptation, and PCI/PC Card interrupt wrapper allocation through failure cleanup and normal teardown (`aros_device.c:128-130,434-466`; `device.c:635-690`; `pci.c:287-319,350-369`; `pccard.c:280-296,328-339`). Network driver wrapper-cleanup comparison (OD3335 expanded; 2026-10-16): compared all `WrapInt` call sites under `workbench/devs/networks` and checked each AROS initializer and failure/normal-delete path. IntelPro100 wrapper rollback scope check (2026-10-16; excluded from OD3335): its `WrapInt` allocates wrapper state only under `__amigaos4__` or `__MORPHOS__` (`workbench/devs/networks/intelpro100/pci.c:780-805`), so the shared `DeleteUnit` failure branch does not leak a wrapper allocation on AROS. SD-card DOS-node failure/retry caller recheck (OD3325 confirmed, 2026-10-16): traced `RegisterUnit`'s media-present flag publication before `MakeDosNode`/`AddBootNode` (`sdcard_bus.c:401-405,471-485`) into the bus worker's transition-only registration branch (`:1740-1759`). Since `AddBootNode` failure is ignored and leaves the media-present state set, the worker does not retry while the same card remains inserted; retry requires a later observed media-state transition. This confirms OD3325's conditional unavailable-DOS-node consequence. No insertion, removal or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

SD-card OD3308 backend-scope correction (2026-10-16): rechecked the `sdcb_WaitCmd` vtable assignments and build variants. OD3308 applies to the generic SDHCI `WaitCmd` installed by `sdcard_bcm2708init.c`; the AArch64 package includes the SDHCI and SDHOST variants and selects at runtime, while 32-bit ARM selects SDHOST only (`sdcard/mmakefile.src:11-24`). SDHOST performs commands synchronously and installs a no-op `WaitCmd` (`sdcard_sdhost_bus.c:375-382,558-565`), so it is excluded. Narrowed OD3308 to AArch64 Raspberry Pi configurations running BCM SDHCI. No command or hardware was run. Source-only.

SD-card generic bus implementation complete-body pass (2026-10-16; no new OD): completed a function-by-function read of `sdcard_bus.c:55-1801`, including the CSD response unpacker, voltage and clock helpers, ADMA, SDHCI command completion/recovery, interrupt dispatch and worker queue. Cross-checked every local callback through the selected BCM SDHCI/SDHOST vtables and their initialization/worker callers. CSD field extraction stays within the four-word response buffer for the call-site offsets; power negotiation passes the card/host OCR intersection to the backend. Existing OD3308 is limited to SDHCI because SDHOST uses synchronous `SendCmd` and its own no-op `WaitCmd`. Remaining uncertainty is controller/hardware timing, electrical behavior and external lifecycle contracts, not unread local function bodies. No device, command or failure was exercised. Source-only.

SD-card delay rollover caller-scope recheck (OD3313 refined, 2026-10-16): enumerated all `sdcard_Udelay` callers across SDHOST init/commands and generic SDHCI card initialization, reset, clock-stability and request polling. The shared helper is used by SDHOST and BCM SDHCI including EMMC2, so rollover can accelerate the selected SDHCI stability/reset loops as well as SDHOST delays. The EMMC2 clock-stability consequence overlaps OD3327 and is not counted separately. `BCM283xWriteLong` has a second absolute-deadline check; its vtable is installed only for the BCM2711 Arasan fallback, while EMMC2 uses direct writes (`sdcard_bcm2708init.c:102-146,259-270`). OD3313 scope expanded accordingly; no controller or timer was run. Source-only.

SD-card 32-bit read maximum-capacity boundary pass (OD3339 added, 2026-10-16): traced CMD_READ dispatch and advertisement against CSD v2 capacity derivation. At the maximum 22-bit C_SIZE, `sdcu_Capacity` is exactly 2^32 sectors; `cmd_Read32` masks it to 32 bits and rejects every nonempty read, including byte ranges representable by its ULONG offset. The 32-bit write handler compares the full capacity and is not included in this finding. No card or request was used. Source-only.

ACPICA physical map helper recheck (2026-10-16; no new OD): confirmed `AcpiOsMapMemory` returns the physical address cast as a pointer and `AcpiOsUnmapMemory` does nothing (`arch/all-native/acpica/acpios_aros.c:218-225`); `AcpiOsGetPhysicalAddress` is the inverse cast (`:228-232`). The checkout has no callers for these OSL functions. The selected x86-64 PC kernel uses an identity map with a minimum 128 GiB window capped at 512 GiB (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mmu.c:149-158`), so the helper alone does not prove an invalid access for mapped ACPI/PCI ranges. Calls involving addresses beyond that window remain a plausible but unverified concern; fetched ACPICA call sites and matching firmware/operation-region placement are absent. ACPICA PCI 16-bit fallback pass (OD3341 added, 2026-10-16): traced both PCI configuration OSL entrypoints through `find_pci` and the Segment 0 mechanism-1 fallback (`arch/all-native/acpica/acpios_aros.c:639-709`). SD-card MMC high-speed switch result follow-up (OD3314 expanded, 2026-10-16; no new finding): confirmed `SendCmd` and successful `WaitCmd` return zero, while failure is `-1`, so `MMCChangeFrequency` reverses the result test and skips readback after a successful switch. The EXT_CSD readback tests byte 0xB9 (`HS_TIMING`, current mode) before setting the high-speed flag; a failed switch with current mode zero does not set the flag, so the proposed separate overclock path is withdrawn. `StartUnit` ignores the helper result and defaults the host to 20 MHz when the flag is absent. No card or command was used. Source-only.


SD-card SDSC switch and SCR pass (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced `SDSCChangeFrequency` through the selected `StartUnit` caller and `SDSCSwitch` result convention. The helper uses `-1` for failure and zero for successful SendCmd/WaitCmd completion; SCR and switch-status data are read only after successful transfers, busy status is retried at most three times, and `AF_Card_HighSpeed` is set only after a successful switch response reports function 1. No independent defect was established in these paths. Card-side protocol behavior and physical cards remain untested. Source-only.

SDHOST initializer failure-path reconciliation (2026-10-16; no new OD): rechecked the unchecked aligned mailbox allocation against OD3309, then walked every post-GPIO failure exit and common label. OD3318 separately covers common pool retention when a later init hook fails; OD3328 covers accepted zero core-clock values. The inactive BCM2711/2712 branch frees the temporary mailbox allocation when non-NULL before returning, and optional bounce-buffer failure is already OD3311. No additional independent initializer failure was established. Firmware response details, pin ownership policy, and teardown semantics remain open; no board or failure injection was used. Trackdisk worker startup failure-path pass (OD3342 added, 2026-10-16): traced the selected PC initializer through `TD_InitTask` and its worker handshake (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:193-276,567-630,645-692`). The timer reply-port/request allocation results are unchecked; `CreateIORequest` returns NULL on either allocation failure or a NULL reply port, and `OpenDevice` dereferences the request before the worker sends the initializer its startup signal (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:50-74`; `createiorequest.c:57-76`; `opendevice.c:95-99`). Added OD3342 for this conditional startup fault/hang. Signal-bit exhaustion in the worker’s separate `AllocSignal` calls was not counted independently in this pass. No failure was induced. Trackdisk InitTask allocation-failure pass (OD3343 added, 2026-10-16): traced `TD_InitTask` allocation exits into the device init hook, its unconditional success return, Open, and both queued BeginIO branches (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:193-276,290-306,332-365,567-642`). Allocation failure returns zero, but the init hook ignores it after registering IRQ handlers; units remain absent because only the worker sets `tdu_Present`, and Open rejects them. The registered `td_floppyint` handler still dereferences missing task data if IRQ6 arrives. Corrected OD3343 to remove the unsupported later-BeginIO claim; added the persistent unusable-device and IRQ consequences. This is separate from OD3342 timer-request allocation failure. No failure or request was induced. Other Drivers detailed report count: 803 unique OD headings. Source-only.
Trackdisk worker signal-allocation caller recheck (no new OD, 2026-10-16): `TD_InitTask` passes a zero-cleared task to `NewAddTask`; `NewAddTask` initializes a zero signal-allocation mask to `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc`, and Exec initializes that mask to `0xFFFF` (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:574,610-623`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:249-251`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). Thus the new worker starts with signals 16-31 free, and its two `AllocSignal(-1)` calls plus the timer `CreateMsgPort` signal allocation cannot ordinarily exhaust the 16 available bits. The subsequent uses of those returned bits in `Wait`/`Signal` were traced (`trackdisk_hw.c:149-150`; `trackdisk_device.c:173,186,687-702`); no separate signal-allocation failure is established. Corrected OD3342's trigger to memory allocation failure only. No task or signal was run. Source-only.
AHIRecord main-task signal-allocation pass (OD3344 added, 2026-10-16): rechecked `CreateFile`, `StartSampling`, the UI `Wait` loop, level-worker notifications and both worker cleanup paths (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:1037-1086,1759-1776,2035-2069,2178-2197,2444-2478,2580-2602,2919-2922,2962-2970,3110-3117`). The parent-task `SaveSlaveSignal`, `AutoLevelSignal` and `LevelSlaveSignal` allocations are unchecked before negative-capable values are shifted into `Wait`/`Signal` masks. The level/save workers do check their own private signal allocations, which does not protect the parent's bits. Added OD3344 for the conditional failure of those handshakes/UI notifications. The module is built by the explicit optional target; no recording or signal exhaustion was induced. Other Drivers detailed report count: 804 unique OD headings. Source-only.

AHI Toccata legacy signal-allocation scope recheck (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced the master and slave signal setup, readiness handshake, cleanup and all `Wait`/`Signal` uses in `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Toccata/toccata.c:221-278,618-686`. The master checks its allocation before starting the process; the slave checks all four allocations, then frees its signals and notifies the master on either success or failure. Its unchecked `FreeSignal(-1)` calls are not counted as a finding without evidence that this API mishandles the failure sentinel. The file remains excluded by the current AHI driver manifest (`Drivers/Makefile.in:33-39,115-118`; coverage row 1847); its legacy task-entry publication race is already noted in the AHI worker publication follow-up but is outside the selected runtime scope. PC i8042 lock-key signal result-contract recheck (OD2336 retained, 2026-10-16): cross-checked the keyboard worker's `sig = 1L << LEDSigBit`, `Wait(sig)` and returned-mask test against all three lock-key producer calls (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:175-183,255-262,434-453`) and Exec `Signal`/`Wait` mask semantics (`rom/exec/signal.c:286-304`; `rom/exec/wait.c:70-137`). The worker waits on the shifted bit mask but tests the returned mask against the unshifted bit number; producers also pass that bit number as a mask. The successful route allocates bit 17 after the fresh worker's timer reply port consumes bit 16, so the producer mask cannot contain bit 17 and the worker test cannot match it. This confirms OD2336 for the selected i386-PC/x86-64-PC i8042 keyboard path; software lock state still changes, while LED refresh is not requested. No keyboard input or controller was used. Source-only.

PC i8042 keyboard IRQ-registration result caller pass (OD3345 added, 2026-10-16): traced the keyboard controller's `KrnAddIRQHandler` result through its unconditional readiness signal, the constructor's `LEDSigBit`-only success test, `HW_AddDriver` publication and `i8042_Init`'s success count (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:248-253,311-327`; `i8042_classinit.c:26-73`). The kernel returns NULL if IRQ-node allocation fails (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:87-115`), while controller reset already enables keyboard IRQ mode (`i8042_kbdclass.c:657-663`); the HIDD can therefore be counted as installed without a scan-code handler. Its later Dispose also passes the NULL handle to `KrnRemIRQHandler`, which dereferences before checking it (EK09). Added OD3345 for the selected i386-PC/x86-64-PC configuration and failure condition. No allocation failure or hardware input was induced. Other Drivers detailed report count: 805 unique OD headings. Source-only.

PC i8042 mouse IRQ-allocation branch comparison (OD2266/OD2802/OD2803 retained; 2026-10-16): compared the adjacent mouse setup worker with new OD3345's keyboard caller path (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseps2.c:207-230`; `i8042_mouseclass.c:60-105`). A NULL mouse IRQ handle is not silently published: successful reset reaches constructor's `!data->irq` rejection. If reset fails after a NULL registration, the worker calls `KrnRemIRQHandler(NULL)` before readiness, covered by EK09/OD2266. If reset succeeds despite the failed registration, the mouse reset callback is registered before the constructor rejects the object, leading to the stale callback path already covered by OD2802/OD2803 depending on registration and module rollback. Normal success Dispose has the same conditional null-removal API issue only when a NULL object escaped, which this constructor prevents. No separate mouse finding added; no allocation failure, controller or device was exercised. Source-only.

BCM GENET OD2933 direct-versus-queued RX lock proof (2026-10-16; finding retained, no duplicate): re-read `BCMGENET_BeginIO`, `BCMGENET_Close`, `bcmgenet_rx_packet`, and the IRQ-driven `BCMGENET_UnitTask` branch (`workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/bcmgenet_init.c:111-137,255-279`; `bcmgenet_unit.c:838-922,1103-1120`). `AttemptSemaphore` success means the caller enters `BCMGENET_HandleRequest` directly while holding `bgu_Lock`; a failed attempt queues to the worker. RX does not obtain that semaphore, and Close removes/frees its opener under only local `Disable`, so neither path mutually excludes the RX traversal. This confirms OD2933's direct `BeginIO` and final-close triggers; queued request handlers themselves remain serialized in the unit task. The SMP trigger remains selected through the Raspberry Pi `smp` variant; same-CPU task preemption also permits overlap where the caller can run while the worker is preempted. No packet, request, or concurrency was run. Source-only.

BCM GENET RX descriptor-length/FCS pass (OD3346 added, 2026-10-16): traced the descriptor BUFLEN extraction through pad removal, `bcmgenet_rx_packet`, raw/non-raw `bcmgenet_copy_packet`, `ios2_DataLength` and the receive callback (`workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/bcmgenet_unit.c:947-978,790-823`). The code removes only the two-byte RBUF alignment pad and explicitly retains the four-byte Ethernet CRC; ordinary reads subtract the Ethernet header but still publish CRC bytes as payload, while raw reads receive the frame plus CRC. Compared selected Rhine and RTL8139 paths, which subtract `ETH_CRCSIZE` before distribution (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:1032`; `rtl8139/unit.c:174-214`). Added OD3346 for the Raspberry Pi Workbench BCM GENET route. Exact buffer consequences depend on SANA-II clients; no packet or request was used. Other Drivers detailed report count: 806 unique OD headings. Source-only.

BCM GENET TX SANA-II length and descriptor boundary pass (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced `CmdWrite`'s raw/non-raw length limits through `BCMGENET_SendPacket`, `tx_function`, padding, DMA sync, CRC-append descriptor flag and TX completion (`workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/bcmgenet_handler.c:100-135`; `bcmgenet_unit.c:608-706,744-779`; `bcmgenet.h:268-282`). Non-raw input is capped at the 1500-byte MTU, then receives a 14-byte header; raw frames are capped at 1514 bytes. Both paths pad transmitted frames to 60 bytes, and hardware appends the FCS under the descriptor CRC flag. The 1536-byte transmit buffer accommodates the maximum accepted frame; descriptor length excludes the appended FCS and no checked path reads beyond the caller's supplied data because `tx_function` owns/copies the requested length. The structure matches selected DWMAC (`dwmac_unit.c:428-498`). No separate TX length or padding defect established; no packet or device was used. Source-only.

BCM GENET OD3346 SANA-II CRC-flag and comparative driver recheck (2026-10-16; finding retained): searched all checked-in C/header/doc sources for `SANA2IOF_CRC`/`SANA2IOB_CRC`; the only hits are the bit definitions in `compiler/include/devices/sana2.h:26-33`, with no AROS receive-side contract that requests or signals appended FCS bytes. Compared selected `workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:1032`, which subtracts `ETH_CRCSIZE` before `DistributeRXPacket`, and `rtl8139/unit.c:174-214`, which validates then subtracts the four-byte FCS before forwarding. BCM GENET explicitly retains the hardware-reported FCS in `ios2_DataLength` and its `rx_function` call; no selected in-tree behavior establishes this as intentional. OD3346 remains, with exact downstream buffer impact conditional on the SANA-II client's capacity/receiver. No packet or client was run. Source-only.

BCM GENET receive-FCS contract recheck (OD3346, 2026-10-17): compared all local evidence for receive-side CRC policy. BCM GENET's descriptor path removes only the two-byte pad and explicitly retains CRC. Retain OD3346 as a confirmed length difference with conditional API/client consequence; no packet or opener was exercised. Source-only.

Coverage-status reconciliation for the active Graphics/Desktop, Exec/Kernel and Other Drivers revisit (2026-10-17): counted Markdown file/artifact table rows rather than `grep Unreviewed` matches. Current tables contain 1,283 Graphics/Desktop rows, 1,660 Exec/Kernel rows, and 1,487 Other Drivers rows. The explicit `Not reviewed` rows in these three tables are only seven Other Drivers `LEGAL`/notes entries; none are code files. Coverage measurement baseline (2026-10-18; tracker-based and not total-scope completeness): extracted unique existing C/C++/assembly source and header paths from the file tables in the Graphics/Desktop, Exec/Kernel and Other Drivers ledgers, then ran `cloc` 2.06 by those path lists. The tables mention 4,039 unique existing code paths; `cloc` classified 4,009 and counted 921,854 code lines. A text-based status pass found explicit full-body-read evidence for 2,432 paths containing 548,314 code lines (59.5% of the code lines classified by `cloc`); 1,602 paths/370,236 code lines had only partial or open evidence, and five paths/3,304 code lines were explicitly marked unreviewed. The remaining 30 paths were not assigned a `cloc` language. This measures only code paths already mentioned in the ledgers; it does not include build-selected files absent from the tables, and “full body read” is not full caller/platform/lifecycle review. Treat 59.5% as a rough body-reading proxy, not an overall audit-completeness estimate or ETA. Source-only.

Coverage measurement refresh (2026-10-22; same tracker-based body-reading proxy): re-extracted unique existing C/C++/assembly source and header paths named in the current Graphics/Desktop, Exec/Kernel and Other Drivers coverage tables and ran `cloc` 2.06. SDSC CMD6 capability/switch response contract cross-check (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced `SDSCChangeFrequency`'s ACMD51/SCR read, CMD6 check-mode busy/status loop, group-1 support check and switch-mode result (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_sdscunit.c:43-140`) through the selected `StartUnit` caller and subsequent clock/bus-width setup (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_bus.c:87-171`). The 64-byte buffer covers the requested CMD6 status length; group 0 value 1 is checked for high-speed support, and the code intends to switch only after the check response reports the function not busy. The retry-exhaustion case was audited and no finding retained: after three busy responses, the fourth condition evaluation decrements the counter to zero, so switch mode is skipped. A non-busy response breaks with a positive counter and permits the intended switch. When the CMD6 helper instead returns failure, `StartUnit` ignores it and retains default-speed clock. Card response semantics remain unverified. Controller clock-stability failure remains OD3327. The separate MMC helper's inverted result test remains OD3314. Card-specific response semantics and host timing remain unverified; no card command was run.

Expansion RAM-board metadata-allocation rollback recheck (OD3349, 2026-10-17): traced the valid-size board predicate through `AllocMem(sizeof(struct mbChunkNode), MEMF_CHIP)`, sorted-list insertion, `CDF_PROCESSED`, and final `AddMemList` publication (`arch/m68k-amiga/expansion/configchain.c:403-450,349-358`; `rom/expansion/expansion_init.c:128-131`). Allocation failure inserts no node but still sets `CDF_PROCESSED`; startup has one maintained ConfigChain caller, so the board is omitted and not retried. This is distinct from OD3338, where successful node allocation and an unconditional loop break skip later board entries. Added OD3349. No board or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only.

m68k expansion scan/board-pass existing-finding recheck (OD3337/OD3338, 2026-10-17): followed both motherboard scans into the sorted shared list and proved the boundary intervals are adjacent when usable RAM crosses 128 MiB: the high scan starts at the split and the reversed low scan ends there, with both assigned priority 40 and identical flags (`configchain.c:362-390,286-313`). The merge moves the higher node's start to the lower start but preserves only the lower size (`:333-344`); publication then uses that shortened extent (`:349-358`). This confirms OD3337's trigger. For OD3338, the successfully queued valid board reaches the unconditional loop break; the only maintained ConfigChain caller is expansion startup (`rom/expansion/expansion_init.c:128-131`), so later qualifying boards are omitted from standard startup's one pass. An explicit later API call could process a still-unprocessed next board; the report now limits the persistent claim to normal one-shot initialization. No memory probe or board was run.

PC i8042 null-IRQ caller reconciliation (OD3345/OD3351, 2026-10-17): rechecked both keyboard and mouse callers against `KrnAddIRQHandler` and the shared `KrnRemIRQHandler` null dereference (EK815). The keyboard path ignores a failed IRQ registration, signals success and publishes an inert HIDD (OD3345); the mouse path removes a NULL IRQ token if registration fails and its subsequent reset/probe fails, before sending constructor completion (OD3351). Corrected the current keyboard/mouse source rows and EK815's caller references; older dated ledger entries retain their historical IDs. No IRQ allocation failure or controller behavior was induced. Source-only.

PC i8042 null-token reference reconciliation (2026-10-17): verified that EK815 is the current Exec/Kernel identifier for `KrnRemIRQHandler` dereferencing a null token before its guard. Corrected stale `EK09` references in current Other Drivers finding text and active i8042 source rows; historical dated audit entries remain unchanged. OD3345 covers the keyboard's published-null-token lifecycle, and OD3351 covers the mouse reset-failure branch before constructor completion. Source-only.

PC i8042 keyboard IRQ allocation failure follow-up (2026-10-23; OD3345 supported, no new finding): confirmed the kernel-side consequence from `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:88-110` and `arch/all-pc/kernel/ictl.c:19-41`. `ictl_enable_irq()` is called only inside the successful IRQ-node allocation branch; on allocation failure, no node is inserted and the PC interrupt-controller enable path is skipped. The HIDD then signals setup completion without checking the NULL token, and the constructor publishes the keyboard object as recorded in OD3345. This strengthens the source path for absent keyboard events; it does not establish controller timing or runtime behavior. Source-only.

Efika timer IRQ registration failure (OD3352, 2026-10-17): checked selected Efika package composition, timer initialization, kernel IRQ-node allocation/unmask behavior, SliceHandler completion and BeginIO request queuing. Merged OD3352 into the existing timer initializer row and separated the ordinary failed-init consequence from EK815: `timer.conf` is noexpunge, so the null-removal cleanup path requires direct/forced expunge; failed IRQ registration itself leaves the device reporting successful initialization without request completion. Remaining timer setup, firmware and hardware contracts are open. No allocation failure or hardware was exercised. Source-only.

USB Audio format classification follow-up (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `nExamineAudioDescriptors` handling of 20–24-bit formats into AHI mode registration and allocation/conversion (`usbaudio.class.c:1143-1215,1930-1985,3338-3375,3446-3485`). Although the parser assigns `ahisamtype = 0` for these formats with a comment that AHI has no matching sample type, that field is not published in the AHI tag list or used for buffer selection; `AHIST_M8S` is indeed zero, but conversion hooks are selected from channel count and USB subframe size, and AHI's HiFi mode is indicated separately by resolution. This apparent zero-type bug is not established. Existing descriptor-size findings OD3168/OD3169 remain the relevant malformed-descriptor paths; no USB stream or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio sample-load callback contract pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): read `subLibLoadSound`/`subLibUnloadSound` and traced the `AHI_LoadSound`/`AHI_UnloadSound` fallback in `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/sound.c:871-938,979-1000`. USB Audio's `subLibAllocAudio` advertises `AHISF_MIXING` (`usbaudio.class.c:3358-3365`), so `AHIS_UNKNOWN` from its unimplemented sample callbacks takes AHI's software-mixer storage path; unload then clears the generic sound slot. This is the intended mixing-driver fallback, not missing device support causing a failed load. AHI's `AHIACF_NOMIXING` route was not established for this mode. No sound was loaded or played. Source-only.

USB Audio mode-format and converter selection recheck (OD3169–OD3172, 2026-10-17; no new finding): traced `nExamineAudioDescriptors` through its Type I format parsing and mode registration, then followed the selected AHI allocation's `nam_Resolution`/`nam_NumChannels` dispatch to the playback and recording conversion hooks (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1094-1280,3440-3550`). The 24-bit branches assign `ahisamtype = 0`, which is the valid `AHIST_M8S` enum, but that field is not used to select the USB conversion hook (selection uses channel count and resolution); `ahiac_BuffType` is explicitly not overwritten with this field. Therefore the assignment alone does not establish incorrect 8-bit conversion and is not added as a finding. The existing descriptor extent, empty frequency-list, and 24-bit mono recording-count findings remain supported. This function's remaining selected-caller/configuration checks and the overall USB Audio body review are open. No descriptor, AHI query, device, or stream was used. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI mode-name ownership recheck (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced `nAddAudioModes`' `psdCopyStrFmt` allocation and immediate `psdFreeVec(ahimodename)` after `AHI_AddAudioMode` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1941-1987`) into the selected AHI implementation. `_AHI_AddAudioMode` computes the name length, allocates a database node, and copies `AHIDB_Name` into storage owned by that node before returning (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:358-450`); database removal frees the node allocation (`:474-529`). The caller's temporary name is therefore not retained by the selected AHI path, so no name-lifetime finding is added. AHI database allocation failure and external implementations remain outside this ownership conclusion; no mode registration or removal was run. Source-only.

USB Audio registered-mode private-pointer teardown recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced the `AHIDB_NepAudioMode` pointer retained verbatim in the selected AHI database node (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:413-440`) against USB class teardown (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2082-2094`). `nFreeAudio` removes every nonzero `nam_AHIModeID` from AHI before freeing audio-unit records or closing AHI; the parsed audio-mode records remain class-owned through this sequence and are released during class expunge. The private pointer therefore does not outlive its owner on this selected orderly teardown path. This does not resolve separate concurrent database-removal behavior already tracked as OD1442, nor failure/abnormal-unload paths not established here. No mode query, unbind, or teardown was run. Source-only.

USB Audio root-terminal finding deduplication (OD3190 retained; OD3353 withdrawn, 2026-10-17): compared the two report entries against the same `nExamineAudioDescriptors` → `nExamineAudioUnits` → `nAddAudioModes` path. USB Audio descriptor-parser and frequency-list overlap pass (OD3168–OD3172 rechecked; 2026-10-17): re-traced `nExamineAudioDescriptors` from AudioControl collection count through Type I fixed fields, discrete and continuous sample-rate decoding, and AHI mode publication/query. HDAudio AHI driver-init rollback caller pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): retraced `DriverInit`'s returns through the selected common `_LibInit` failure label into `_LibExpunge`/`DriverCleanup` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Common/library.c:460-461,494-500`). Partial DOS/stdC/HDA HIDD opens and attribute-base acquisitions are guarded and released by `ahi_hda_exit`; failure to construct the PCI subclass releases any acquired Meta attr base; failed controller wrapping releases the claimed PCI object; failed codec initialization releases its controller through `FreeDriverData` (`Drivers/HDAudio/hda_hidd.c:207-243,323-376,399-455`; `misc.c:108-185`). The all-controller/no-codec and driverdatas-allocation failure exits therefore do not add an independent init-time ownership leak.
