NVMe storage-bus startup reachability recheck (OD2876 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-17): re-enumerated all maintained `Hidd_StorageController_AddBus` call sites and traced NVMe's constructor registration. The only checked-in direct C caller found is ATA PCI (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/probe.c:648`); NVMe's selected constructor instead calls `HW_AddDriver` on its `CLID_Hidd_StorageController` object and ignores the failed registration result (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:440-466`; `nvme.conf:77-96`; storage hierarchy `rom/hidds/base/storage/storage.conf:68-83`). Envy24HT Revolution 5.1 I²C caller and historical-candidate reconciliation (OD3354 added, 2026-10-17): traced allocator failure and every checked-in `WriteBytesI2C` caller. WINGDI bitmap readback failure follow-up (OD3355, 2026-10-17): re-traced the complete `GDIBM__Hidd_BitMap__GetImage` path from scratch-buffer allocation through compatible DC/bitmap setup, selection, BitBlt, GetDIBits and pixel conversion. SDHCI command-start/wait caller reconciliation (OD3308/OD3320 rechecked, 2026-10-17; no new OD): reread `SendCmd` listener publication, command launch, `WaitCmd`'s bus-task versus non-bus-task branches, recovery, `BusIRQEntry` IRQ-seen publication, error signaling, and `BusTask` request dispatch (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_bus.c:897-1047,1265-1454,1478-1484,1679-1801`). The task's first observed controller IRQ permanently selects unbounded `Wait(signal)` on subsequent commands, bypassing its computed timeout and task-context lost-IRQ recovery; this is the existing OD3308 trigger. In `WaitCmd` task-context recovery, data listener ownership is claimed before `FinishData`, but failure results are not consistently propagated to `sdcb_CmdError`; the final result checks only timeout/error latch, consistent with OD3320. No independent defect separated from these entries. IRQ delivery, status transitions and bus behavior remain untested; source-only.



Trident config replacement failure paths restored to detailed report (OD1821, 2026-10-17): re-read all `ApplyDragAction` replacement branches and traced both into Poseidon. Device-form replacement removes target children before fallible `psdWriteCfg`/`psdAddCfgEntry`; entry-to-device replacement discards `psdSetUsbDevCfg`, whose existing-form route calls `psdReadCfg` that clears destination child forms before fallible `pAddCfgChunk` parsing (`CfgListClass.c:127-176,184-246`; `poseidon.library.c:6733-6784,7442-7565`). `MUIM_DragDrop` discards `ApplyDragAction` status and reports handled for accepted targets (`CfgListClass.c:324-344`). A failed existing-form `psdReadCfg` falls through to root-form creation in `psdSetUsbDevCfg`; if allocations recover, a duplicate device form can be added beside the partially cleared original. This confirms OD1821 as conditional configuration loss, partial replacement, or duplicate form state under a failed allocation or serialization step. Restored the finding because coverage retained it but neither detailed report nor index did. Broader list-refresh and external Poseidon callers remain open. No configuration or drag was run. Source-only.

BCM MMC clock-selection bitmask follow-up (OD3356, 2026-10-17): traced the only `AF_Card_HighSpeed52` setter in `MMCChangeFrequency` into `StartUnit`; the setter stores bit 27 while the selector masks with decimal 27, so the readback-confirmed 52 MHz state selects 26 MHz. The state is conditional because OD3314 currently rejects the successful switch result before setting the flag. No card or hardware was used. Source-only.
UHCI class complete-body reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new OD): reread `workbench/devs/USB/drivers/UHCI/uhciclass.c` in bounded sections from constructor and both interrupt handlers through Root disposal, pipe and transfer methods, hub status/features, string/device descriptors, and class init/expunge. USBHub worker-allocation failure-path review (OD3357-OD3358, 2026-10-17): traced `USBHub::New` through the selected `USB::NewDevice` hub-class dispatch, worker entry and `NewAddTask` failure results. The parent waits for `SIGF_SINGLE` even when Task/MemList allocation skips task creation or `NewAddTask` returns NULL; only `hub_process` sends that readiness signal. Separately, the unchecked 10-KiB stack allocation can populate task bounds and a MemEntry from NULL; selected Sam440 PPC `PrepareContext` writes frame terminators through the derived stack pointer before context allocation. Confirmed the generic USB stack is selected by the Sam440 USB aggregate and its PCI460 backend includes OHCI root-hub support. Added OD3357 and OD3358, distinct from OD2788/OD2789's library starter task. No failure, task creation, hub, or device was exercised. Source-only.

USB HID mouse missing-axis conversion review (OD3359 added, 2026-10-17): traced `USBMouse::New` report selection, `hid_locate` failure behavior and zeroed OOP instance fields into the report worker’s relative-versus-tablet branch and selected Intuition scaling. The class is included in `kernel-usb-classes-common`. No failure or module load was induced. Source-only.
LAN78xx multicast-range filter trace (OD3374, 2026-10-17): traced `S2_ADDMULTICASTADDRESSES` through inclusive endpoint storage, ethernet-task dispatch, the 512-bit VHF calculation, and NIC filter programming (`dev.c:525-595,702-738`; `lan78xx.class.c:641-656,993-1037`). The later full `nPTPRead()` and DOS `Read()` caller pass supersedes this earlier non-promotion: OD4443 records a successful short response being treated as the cached/requested length, and OD4444 records valid positive seek/read arguments wrapping the 32-bit range sum on multi-gigabyte objects. `nPTPWrite()` later received complete-function credit in the full file-write pass; that pass rechecked OD4430/OD4444 and added OD4445, and the zero-length return recheck added OD4458. Reviewed `nPTPFormatStore()` through `ACTION_FORMAT` and added OD4425: `nPTPFormatStore()` removes each old record before refresh and stages replacements on a temporary list; failed refresh drops a storage while reporting success, and a later format error returns before committing previously staged records. Traced `ACTION_RENAME_OBJECT` through the DOS rename caller and added OD4426: identical names exit before the move, while changed names reach `nSearchObject()` with an uninitialized local `buf` because the BSTR is never converted. Added OD4427 after tracing successful `MoveObject` and `SendObjectInfo` destination fallback state through `ACTION_PARENT` and path traversal: move updates the child list but not either cached parent field, while upload updates `poi_ParentHandle` without reconciling `poi_Parent`. Traced modified-file `ACTION_END` cleanup through `nPTPDeleteObject()`, `nFreeFH()`, DOS packet reply, and `rom/dos/close.c`; rechecked OD4428 because `Close()` frees its DOS handle after the failed `ACTION_END`, while the PTP handle and exclusive lock remain registered. Followed failed `nPTPSendObject()` cleanup through `nPTPFreeObjectInfo()` and `nFreeFH()`; added OD4429 because the object record is freed before `nFreeFH()` dereferences it to release the lock. Traced existing-file `ACTION_WRITE` from `nCreateFH()` into `nPTPWrite()` and added OD4430: in-range writes bypass buffer allocation, then read or copy through the NULL whole-file buffer. Traced raw DOS `Read()`/`Write()` forwarding and the PTP open/packet paths; added OD4431 because the class stores no per-handle mode, treats `FINDUPDATE` as `ACCESS_READ`, and accepts I/O without checking that mode. Traced metadata string decoding into `nPTPSendObject()` and `nSendPTPData()`; added OD4432 because two maximum valid 254-character strings plus fixed fields and dates require 1,140 bytes in the 1,024-byte output buffer, and a 255-character DOS name wraps the one-byte PIMA count. Traced `MODE_NEWFILE` through DOS `fs_Open()` to `ACTION_FINDOUTPUT`; added OD4433 because overwrite removes and frees the old object record before reading its parent pointer to update the directory date. Traced `ACTION_CREATE_DIR` through `nPTPSendObject()`, cache insertion, `nCreateLock()`, and DOS `CreateDir()`; added OD4434 because lock allocation failure is returned after the remote and cached directory have already been created. Traced PTP keyword parsing into the selected `ACTION_EXAMINE_*` output and DOS `Examine()`/`fixfib()`; strengthened OD4435 because the caller block is neither initialized nor cleared and commentless objects leave `fib_Comment` unchanged. Traced `ACTION_INFO`/`ACTION_DISK_INFO` capacity accumulation and added OD4436: the per-storage block shift is selected without considering the aggregate, which can wrap the 32-bit totals on devices exposing five near-2^47-byte storage units. Traced `ACTION_EXAMINE_NEXT` through DOS `ExNext()` and deletion/replacement; added OD4437 because the FIB retains a child pointer across calls while delete paths can free that unprotected object. Traced DOS `Info()` to `ACTION_INFO` and compared it with the synthetic root and storage IDs; added OD4438 because root `Info()` selects no storage record and falls back to one block. Traced required object/storage name allocations through `nPTPGetObjectInfo()`, `nPTPGetStorageInfo()`, directory/root insertion, and lookup/examination; added OD4439 because failed name allocation still publishes a record that later callers dereference. Later dated entries record complete function slices for PTP configuration, GUI/task lifecycle, startup/teardown, pathname and lock helpers, move/delete, `nPTPRead()`/`nPTPWrite()`, `nPTPSendObject()`, ObjectInfo/StorageInfo and their free helpers, session and ID-array helpers, `nPTPFormatStore()`, DeviceInfo parsing, the shared command/data transfer helpers, PIMA date conversion, and DOS info/examine dispatch; findings now extend through OD4458. The complete 4,054 C code lines now receive full-body credit; ledger-wide non-overlapping coverage and the remaining per-file inventory have not been freshly reconciled. CDC ACM full-body and selected serial-write cross-check (OD3366-OD3367, 2026-10-17): read the full 1,174-line `cdcacm.class.c` and 488-line `dev.c`, including binding, unit startup, command queues, transfer completion, abort and teardown. Added OD3366 for `devOpen` enqueueing SDCMD_SETPARAMS then using `GetMsg` on the input queue as its completion wait; traced OpenDevice's synchronous open-vector call, its Forbid interval, caller-owned reply port, and SMP-local Forbid semantics. Added OD3367 after a selected USB-class search found matching OUT-write/IN-error getter pairs in CDC ACM, Palm PDA, printer, PL2303 and CP210x; Poseidon's getter reads the passed stream's own error field. These findings describe source behavior; no device, open, transfer, or SMP interleaving was run. Other CDC ACM functionality was read in this pass, but broader class caller and detach behavior remain open.

USB serial receive-buffer arithmetic follow-up (OD3368, 2026-10-17): followed public `IOExtSer.io_RBufLen` through the CDC ACM, PL2303 and CP210x `nSetSerialMode` calculations into Poseidon `PGA_PIPESTREAM` reallocation and read-ahead `psdSendPipe`. All three use 16 pipes; `io_RBufLen == ULONG_MAX` yields a rounded per-pipe size of `0x10000000`, whose 16-pipe ULONG product wraps to zero. Poseidon's allocator still returns a non-NULL header-backed pointer for a zero-byte request, then read-ahead uses the large per-pipe length at per-pipe offsets. Added OD3368. No request, stream resize, or transfer was run. Other stream-size limits and host-controller behavior remain open. Source-only.

USB serial open/close queue follow-up (OD3366 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): compared the CDC ACM open path against Palm PDA, CP210x and PL2303. All four post `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` to the unit input port, then `GetMsg` from that same port before returning; their workers instead `ReplyMsg` from `nSetSerialMode`. Palm PDA's `devClose` also posts `CMD_INVALID` and performs the same same-port wait; its worker's handler sends the device-specific close notification before replying. Exec OpenDevice/CloseDevice both invoke vectors synchronously under Forbid, and the reply destination remains the caller's request port. Expanded OD3366 to these four open paths and Palm's close path. No device operation was run. Source-only.
BTSerial OpenDevice same-port setup-wait cross-check (OD3366 expanded; 2026-10-25): traced `devOpen()`'s queued `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` and same-unit-port `GetMsg()`/`WaitPort()` loop (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/dev.c:120-127`) against Exec `OpenDevice()`'s synchronous vector call under `EXEC_LOCK_LIST_READ_AND_FORBID` through its final Permit (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-114,130-135`; `rom/exec/exec_locks.h:46-50,58-62`). The BTSerial worker drains the same unit port and replies to `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` using the caller request's reply port (`btserial.class.c:656-658,694-697`), so if that worker wins the cross-CPU dequeue, Open waits on the empty unit port and misses the reply. On the single-CPU path, local Forbid keeps the worker from running and the opener can consume its own queued message; BTSerial's `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` has no line-coding side effect, so no skipped-setting claim is added for this driver. The BTSerial target is explicitly buildable but its aggregate edge is commented; no direct maintained `OpenDevice()` caller exists. Expanded OD3366 and its index configuration/trigger wording; no body-line credit changed because the device and worker bodies were already fully read. No device open or schedule was run; source-only.

USB serial worker signal-exhaustion recheck (2026-10-17; no new finding): compared CDC ACM, Palm PDA, PL2303, CP210x and printer worker startup allocations with Exec's `AllocSignal(-1)` contract and the existing Poseidon partial-stream-allocation candidate OD1595. The worker-created unit message ports and abort signals are not checked before their signal numbers are shifted into `PSA_AbortSigMask`; if a worker genuinely exhausts its user signals, the resulting mask can be invalid. However, the selected workers begin with Exec's normal user-signal pool and allocate only a small fixed number of signals during startup, so no ordinary selected-path exhaustion trigger was established. The stream-open allocation failures already route through OD1595 and do not establish a separate signal bug. No worker or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

USB printer request-queue pass (2026-10-17): reread printer `devOpen`/`devClose`/`devBeginIO`/`devAbortIO` and the complete worker request loop (`rom/usb/classes/printer/dev.c:46-158,217-386`; `printer.class.c:560-770`). Confirmed the existing cross-stream `psdGetStreamError(EPInStream)` after `psdStreamWrite(EPOutStream)` is the printer instance of OD3367. Traced read/write queue removal around blocking stream calls, AbortIO's in-flight-write signal path and queued-request removal, worker shutdown draining and close's flush signal; no additional independent defect established in this pass. Transfer completion ordering, concurrent close/removal, and full class lifecycle remain open. No device requests were run. Source-only.

Poseidon buffered-read and printer AbortIO contract pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced `psdStreamRead`'s buffer accounting, partial-packet copies, read-ahead submission and abort-mask wait (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5009-5204`) against the printer worker's dequeue/read/requeue path and `devAbortIO` (`rom/usb/classes/printer/printer.class.c:680-701`; `dev.c:328-384`). The worker removes a read request from its abort-search queue while synchronously in `psdStreamRead`; `AbortIO` then returns failure if that request is in flight. Exec's documented AbortIO contract explicitly allows abort to fail (“may or may not be done”), so this alone does not establish a driver defect. Buffered-read packet copies are bounded by `remlen`, which is clipped to the caller's remaining requested length; the full `-1` read-all special case is explicitly discouraged in Poseidon. Other negative lengths and external direct stream clients remain open. No USB request was run. Source-only.

USB Audio 24-bit mono capture completion recheck (OD3163 sharpened, 2026-10-17): traced nInDoneHook packet byte counts through the frame-size switch and the selected 24-bit mono converter. The three-byte case falls through from divide-by-3 to shift-right-2, making 3-, 6-, and 9-byte packets produce count zero. nRec24BitMono then enters its do-while body once and decrements the zero ULONG to ULONG_MAX, continuing reads from the USB packet buffer and writes to the bounded AHIBuffer; larger packet counts remain quartered. Expanded OD3163 from truncation alone to the conditional conversion overrun. No USB descriptor, packet, or stream was exercised. Source-only.

USB Audio 24-bit stereo input byte-selection recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): re-traced the selected nRec24BitStereo hook with the pointer's initial one-byte advance (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3068-3086,3531-3537`). The two output words read source offsets 1–2 and 4–5 of each six-byte stereo frame, so they retain the high 16 bits of each 24-bit channel and skip each low-order byte, matching nRec24BitMono's 24-to-16 conversion intent (`:3046-3065`). The apparent stereo offset mismatch is not a defect. The separate nInDoneHook frame-count fallthrough/zero-count underflow remains OD3163. No packet was processed. Source-only.

xHCI controller startup failure unwind audit (OD3369, 2026-10-17): traced both post-interrupt `xhciInit` failure exits through `pciAllocUnit` and `Open_Unit`. The reset callback is registered and PCI interrupt registration is attempted before the halted/fatal-status returns; worker tasks may also have started before the final halted return. Failed allocation releases HIDD ownership but bypasses `pciFreeUnit`, the normal teardown. The PCI interrupt handler remains only if registration succeeded. Added OD3369 for the incomplete rollback and stale callback/task risk. No controller or failure was induced. Source-only.

xHCI worker creation failure audit (OD3370, 2026-10-17): traced `psdSpawnSubTask` allocation failure returns against both worker spawn sites in `xhciInit`, the later online flag publication, and each worker's consumer role. Either NULL spawn is ignored, allowing success without event completion/scheduling or port-change processing. Added OD3370. No task allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

PCI xHCI reset-callback close/reopen follow-up (OD2192, 2026-10-17): compared `xhciInit`'s `AddResetCallback` with the shared PCIUSB `pciFreeUnit` and xHCI `xhciFree` teardown. Neither removes the embedded callback; successful close preserves the controller node, and reopen calls `xhciInit` with that same node. Expanded OD2192 from UHCI/OHCI/EHCI to include PCI xHCI. No unit was opened or reset. Source-only.

xHCI worker readiness and prerequisite audit (OD3371, 2026-10-17): traced each worker's timer-open and signal-allocation results. Both signal the init task before testing those results, then exit on failure; the event completion interrupt later unconditionally uses the task pointer and event signal. Added OD3371 for premature readiness and invalid post-failure interrupt signaling. No task/resource failure or interrupt was induced. Source-only.

xHCI worker stale-task-pointer lifetime follow-up (OD3371, 2026-10-17): confirmed `psdSpawnSubTask` allocates the task and stack in a MemList attached to `tc_MemEntry` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1491-1507`); Exec documents that task MemEntries are freed when the task dies (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:149-150`), and `ServiceTask` frees the entries after task removal (`rom/exec/service.c:64-90`). The exiting worker's stored `xet_Task` pointer can therefore become dangling before the unconditional completion interrupt signals it (`xhci_hcd.c:2946-2958`). This strengthens OD3371's lifetime evidence; no task or interrupt was run.

PCI xHCI normal-close DMA and worker teardown audit (OD3372, 2026-10-17): traced `Close_Unit` through `pciFreeUnit`, `xhciFreeHCMem`, private-state free, PCI-memory free, and subsequent PCI busmaster/IRQ deactivation. The event and port tasks have unbounded signal waits and no shutdown path; their timers/signals close only on task exit. Added OD3372 for the free-before-quiesce window and orphaned task resources. No unit was closed and no DMA/interrupt was induced. Source-only.

PCI xHCI ledger reconciliation (2026-10-17): mapped the xhci_hcd.c / xhci_hw.c / xhci_hcport.c row's legacy candidates to current detailed entries: 905's command/event `ringio` reset leak is now OD3373; 907's unchecked worker spawn is OD3370 and readiness-before-prerequisite checks is OD3371; 908/913's normal-close worker/private-state and interrupt ordering is consolidated as OD3372; 911's late initialization failure unwind is OD3369. The current detailed report had no matching standalone entries for these legacy labels; the mappings above consolidate the ledger's findings rather than claim duplicates. Confirmed `xhc_OPR` is the DMA command ring, not the MMIO operational-register block (`xhci_controllerclass.c:379-392`). Wider task teardown and interrupt synchronization contracts remain open.

xHCI controller-class partial-allocation recheck (OD3373, 2026-10-17): verified `pciFreeAligned` safely ignores zero/unallocated MemEntry addresses, so the staged DMA-allocation `init_fail` unwind does not double-free absent entries (`pcixhci_arospci.c:473-505`). It still omits separate `ringio` allocations, as recorded in OD3373; the Root Dispose override only delegates to its superclass and does not own/free `hc_CPrivate` (`xhci_controllerclass.c:549-552`). No allocation failure or controller was used. Source-only.

xHCI extended-capability traversal termination recheck (OD3284, 2026-10-17; no new finding): the loop increments `xhciECPOff` by `nextcap << 2` and exits when `nextcap` is zero (`xhci_controllerclass.c:151-155,260-264`). Every nonzero link advances to a larger offset until an integer wrap; a capability cycle within the mapped BAR is therefore not supported by the pointer arithmetic. The BAR-bound issue remains OD3284; a bad chain can keep advancing beyond the declared aperture. No controller registers were read. Source-only.

xHCI Intel port-routing pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced the controller-class vendor gate and config accesses (`xhci_controllerclass.c:266-285`): for Intel vendor ID it copies USB3PRM to USB3_PSSEN and USB2PRM to XUSB2PR, then applies the LynxPoint quirk only for product 0x8c31. The source comment identifies PCH port multiplexing and one tested LynxPoint product; no evidence in this tree establishes the supported Intel product-ID range or another affected layout, so broader chipset assumptions remain open rather than being reported as a defect. No config space was read or written.

SD-card NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY contract/caller recheck (OD3303 retained, 2026-10-17; no new finding): confirmed `sdcard_device.c:565-578` writes the full `NSDeviceQueryResult` without validating `io_Length`; `input.device` checks the required result prefix before writing (`rom/devs/input/input.c:126-145`), and NVMe checks full-structure size (`nvme_io.c:311-324`). The selected in-tree NTFS caller supplies a full result buffer (`workbench/fs/ntfs/disk.c:362-389`); SysExplorer's analogous query code is under `#if (0)` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Storage/storage_enum.c:234-255`). This supports OD3303's conditional direct-short-buffer trigger and establishes no selected in-tree short-buffer caller. No request was sent. Source-only.
SD-card request dispatch and completion recheck (OD3303/OD3321/OD3339/OD3350 retained, 2026-10-17; no new finding): traced the complete `HandleIO` dispatch (`sdcard_device.c:549-615`), `BeginIO` quick/deferred selection (`:642-689`), bus-task dequeue/reply (`sdcard_bus.c:1763-1798`), and `TD_ADDCHANGEINT`/`TD_REMCHANGEINT` pending-request handling (`sdcard_device.c:293-318,386-398`). All requests are deliberately classified slow, so supported calls reach the bus task and are replied unless `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` is intentionally retained pending a change. `CMD_FLUSH` drains the bus message port (`:272-287`), but the selected unit registration associates one card unit with each physical bus path (`sdcard_bus.c:368-376`); no independently addressable unit sharing the queue was established, so no cross-unit flush defect is supported. `TD_GETGEOMETRY` checks exact output length before writing (`:419-448`). Previously tracked query bounds, false HD_SCSICMD capability, maximum-capacity 32-bit reads, and write-protection status remain; no new candidate promoted. No request/card was used. Source-only.
LAN78xx TX length and RX aggregation bound pass (OD3374 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-17): traced S2_WRITE dispatch through `cmdWrite` and the sole `nWritePacket` caller, plus the bulk-IN completion through `lan78xx_handle_rx_buffer` and `nReadPacket` (`dev.c:320-361`; `lan78xx.class.c:568-620,676-681,1058-1146,1201-1329`). `cmdWrite` rejects lengths above `RAWPKT_SIZE`/`ETHERPKT_SIZE` before queueing, so the later `ULONG` additions and copy do not receive an unbounded selected request length. RX command length is checked against the actual completed transfer before payload delivery, and packet size has an additional `ETHER_MAX_LEN` bound. The apparent TX overflow lead is not supported on the selected caller path; no further finding promoted. No request or transfer was run. Source-only.
LAN78xx hardware-init readiness/error propagation trace (OD3375, 2026-10-17): followed `psdSpawnSubTask` readiness from `usbForceDeviceBinding` through `nEthTask` and into the post-bind command loop (`lan78xx.class.c:255-274,514-547,909-928,1697-1842`). The task signals before initialization; the binder checks only the task pointer; explicit initialization failure is ignored. Added OD3375 for a unit accepted despite failed startup. No hardware or failed control request was used. Source-only.
LAN78xx link-timer failure dependency trace (OD3376, 2026-10-17): confirmed the timer setup chain is optional, `ncp_LinkUp` is zeroed at unit allocation and mutated only by the timer-driven `lan78xx_link_poll`, and RX transfer arming is gated on that flag (`lan78xx.class.c:202-204,528-560,626-638,963-975,1911-1941`). Added OD3376 for silent timer setup failure leaving a bound online interface without RX or link transitions. No timer/allocation failure or device was exercised. Source-only.
LAN78xx flush-versus-active-write trace (OD3377, 2026-10-17): followed `CMD_FLUSH`/`AbortRW` against both queued and worker-owned writes (`dev.c:375-390,1419-1424`; `lan78xx.class.c:572-594,676-681,700-706,1142-1144`). The active request is removed from `ncp_WriteQueue` before submission and lives only in `ncp_WritePending`; flush returns success after draining queues but leaves this pointer and USB transfer untouched. Added OD3377. No write or flush was issued. Source-only.
LAN78xx S2_CONFIGINTERFACE hardware/caller trace (OD3378-OD3379, 2026-10-17): followed the SANA-II request's software address copy, task dispatch, nSetOnline path, and every `lan78xx_set_macaddr` call (`dev.c:471-505`; `lan78xx.class.c:641-648,949-975,1662-1675`). The only hardware-programming call is at init; the queued config handler does not update RX_ADDR/perfect-filter registers. Also compared seven selected USB Ethernet handlers' `0x80` first-byte test with their multicast validators' `& 1` test; they accept group station addresses and reject some valid unicast addresses. Checked AROSTCP passes the factory `ss_hwaddr` and found no selected in-tree override/invalid-address caller. Added OD3378 and OD3379; no request or device was used. Source-only.
USB Ethernet RX/Close/AbortIO cross-CPU lifetime recheck (OD3380 expanded, 2026-10-17): compared all eight class `nReadPacket`/`nReadIOReq` receive traversals with each device `devClose` and `devAbortIO`. All RX paths traverse BufMan/request lists under local `Forbid` (LAN78xx uses `Disable`); Close removes BufMan and frees it without aborting/draining its RX queue, and AbortIO removes/replies a matching request under the same local-CPU exclusion. Exec documents both calls as processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:52-60`; `disable.c:50-58`). Thus the LAN78xx race already recorded in OD3380 applies to all seven peers. Confirmed x86_64 PC USB package and `smp` selection (`rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:10-38`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:6-15`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:9-15`; `configure.in:1668-1669`). Corrected the prior note: Close does not abort the opener RX queue. Conditional on RX overlapping Close/AbortIO; no request or interleaving was run. Source-only.
USB Ethernet packet-statistics node ownership cross-check (OD3381 broadened, 2026-10-17): compared RX and TX `FindPacketTypeStats` plus counter updates in all eight selected USB Ethernet classes against each `cmdUntrackType`. All workers use the returned pointer after an unlocked lookup; all eight `S2_GETTYPESTATS` handlers also copy from the returned node under only local `Forbid`/`Disable`. Seven untrack paths use local `Forbid`, LAN78xx uses local `Disable`, and each unlinks then frees the stats node after leaving that region. Exec documents both exclusions as processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:52-60`; `disable.c:58-61`). Broadened OD3381 from LAN78xx to all eight, conditional on packet/update overlapping `S2_UNTRACKTYPE`; no request, packet, or interleaving was run. Source-only.
LAN78xx binding-failure publication trace (OD3382, 2026-10-17): followed insertion into `nh_Units`, the spawn and `nAllocEth` failure exits, resource teardown, and `devOpen`/async command dispatch (`lan78xx.class.c:188-211,255-275,748-838,873-906`; `dev.c:69-115,471-505,1003-1027`). Failure leaves the unit node in the list with no worker, while Open accepts it and deferred commands remain in the unit message port. Added OD3382. No failure or request was induced. Source-only.
LAN78xx unbind with AROSTCP pending-read caller trace (OD3383, 2026-10-17): followed queued `CMD_READ` ownership through `usbReleaseDeviceBinding`, task shutdown, `nFreeEth`, and AROSTCP's OFFLINE event callback (`dev.c:274-301,1419-1424`; `lan78xx.class.c:277-301,735-740,873-906`; `if_sana.c:536-551,1193-1218`). Release cleanup drains the unit command port but not opener RX queues, and the selected caller does not abort its pending reads on OFFLINE. Added OD3383 conditional on outstanding reads during USB removal. No device or request was used. Source-only.
LAN78xx RX delivery callback, runts, and frame-bound pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): followed USB aggregate length validation through `lan78xx_handle_rx_buffer`, `nReadPacket`, and `nReadIOReq` (`lan78xx.class.c:1058-1146,1158-1270,1277-1329`). RX validates each command length against the completed transfer before stripping FCS and dispatching; the Ethernet maximum is checked before callback/copy use. Raw delivery restores the Ethernet header to the checked payload length, cooked delivery excludes it, and SANA-II read/orphan enqueue paths validate the buffer-manager copy callback. Filter rejection leaves a request queued while later openers are still searched; copy failure replies that opener's request with buffer error and does not prevent delivery to other openers. Shared-flag behavior across openers was checked and correctly records delivery if any opener accepts the frame. No new finding. The current independent RX/Close and stats-list lifetime candidates remain OD3380/OD3381; no packet or callback was run. Source-only.
LAN78xx TX framing and caller-bound pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): followed `cmdWrite` through write-queue dispatch and the sole `nWritePacket` caller (`dev.c:320-361`; `lan78xx.class.c:676-681,1073-1146`). The BeginIO path validates cooked/raw data length before queueing; TX framing accounts for the optional Ethernet header, enforces `LAN78XX_TX_BUFFER_SIZE`, copies only the validated length, and zero-pads short frames within the checked total. The `CMD_FLUSH` omission for an active transfer remains OD3377. No new finding; no request or transfer was run. Source-only.
LAN78xx SANA-II event-wait teardown trace (OD3384, 2026-10-17): followed `cmdOnEvent` mask validation and queueing through `nDoEvent(S2EVENT_OFFLINE)` and `nFreeEth` (`dev.c:928-966`; `lan78xx.class.c:735-740,873-906,1040-1059`). OFFLINE subscriptions are replied, but event requests with nonmatching masks remain queued and teardown does not drain them. Added OD3384 conditional on a non-OFFLINE event wait at removal. No device or request was used. Source-only.
USB Ethernet class ID truncation/duplicate-worker comparison (OD3385, 2026-10-17): reconciled all eight selected Ethernet classes' 128-byte key fields, 127-byte copies, full incoming-ID comparisons, and worker startup ordering (`asixeth/asixeth.class.c:236,271,305-309`; `cdceth/cdceth.class.c:249,284,317-321`; `davicometh/dm9601eth.class.c:216,251,284-287`; `ethwrap/ethwrap.class.c:238,273,306-309`; `lan78xx/lan78xx.class.c:192,228,255-260`; `moschipeth/moschipeth.class.c:184,219,252-256`; `pegasuseth/pegasus.class.c:283,318,352-355`; `rndis/rndis.class.c:213,248,281-284`; headers all declare 128-byte key fields). Their parent `kernel-usb-classes-common` selects these classes; Poseidon generates a longer full ID and invokes binding per unbound device (`poseidon.library.c:2364-2375,2482-2496,3545-3547,6294,6450-6478`; `poseidon.doc:497-499`). A maximum-length shared product string can truncate before unique serial suffixes; a second bind reuses the record and starts a worker without checking existing task state. Extended OD3385 to all eight classes; the detailed single-task release consequence is traced in LAN78xx. No descriptor or device was used. Source-only.
USB Ethernet queued RX and orphan-read teardown (OD3383, 2026-10-17): rechecked all eight selected `S2_READORPHAN` enqueue paths (`asixeth/dev.c:1084`; `cdceth:1089`; `davicometh:1084`; `ethwrap:967`; `lan78xx:996`; `moschipeth:1089`; `pegasuseth:1084`; `rndis:973`) and their unit binding cleanup. Folded the orphan queue into OD3383 alongside pending `CMD_READ` queues; no USB removal or I/O was run.

USB Ethernet `devOpen` BufMan-failure divergence recheck (OD3386 revised; OD3397 added, 2026-10-17): compared the allocation-failure branches across all eight selected classes. Only LAN78xx returns `IOERR_OPENFAIL` after BufMan allocation failure and fails to roll back `ncp_OpenFlags` (`lan78xx/dev.c:98-105,134-146`), so OD3386 is restricted to LAN78xx. The other seven classes have no failure branch: in non-DEBUG builds they continue successfully with `ioreq->ios2_BufferManagement` still pointing to the caller tag array; `devClose` subsequently casts that field to `BufMan`, calls `Remove`, and `FreeVec` (`asixeth/dev.c:105-149,180-193`; same shape in cdceth, davicometh, ethwrap, moschipeth, pegasuseth, rndis). In DEBUG builds their `KPRINTF` evaluates BufMan fields after failed allocation and dereferences NULL (`debug.h` in each class). Added OD3397. No allocation, Open or Close was run. Source-only.
USB Ethernet last-close Open-flag reset comparison (OD3387, 2026-10-17): compared post-decrement `unit_OpenCnt` tests against MINE gating in seven selected class devices (`asixeth/dev.c:81,175-178`; `cdceth/dev.c:81,174-177`; `davicometh/dev.c:81,174-177`; `ethwrap/dev.c:81,174-177`; `moschipeth/dev.c:81,174-177`; `pegasuseth/dev.c:81,174-177`; `rndis/dev.c:82,175-178`). Added OD3387. No open or close was run. Source-only.

HID parser and selected constructor cross-check (OD3144/OD3389/OD3390 retained, 2026-10-17): re-read `hid_start_parse`, `hid_get_item`, `hid_maxrepid`, `hid_report_size`, and `hid_locate` alongside the generic HID, keyboard, and mouse constructors. SD-card speed-negotiation retry follow-up (OD3314/OD3356 retained, 2026-10-17; no new finding): re-read the selected SDSC and MMC mode-switch helpers against `StartUnit`. The SDSC SCR query fails closed after three unsuccessful reads; CMD6 test mode has three bounded busy retries, but exhaustion leaves timeout zero, so the subsequent switch gate is not entered; no SDSC busy-retry finding is retained; when that command instead fails, the helper leaves `AF_Card_HighSpeed` clear so `StartUnit` keeps the legacy 25 MHz clock. MMC's separate `MMCSwitch` result inversion and the 52-MHz bit-position/mask mismatch remain OD3314/OD3356. `MMCChangeFrequency` also ignores `WaitStatus` inside `MMCSwitch`, but because the current inverted return check exits on every successful send/wait-command result, no distinct additional consequence is established. No card command or hardware was used. Source-only.

Atheros5000 `CMD_FLUSH` queue-order recheck (no new finding): traced `DevBeginIO`'s serialized `GENERAL_QUEUE` fallback (`device.c:408-420`), `UnitTask` FIFO drain under `access_lock` (`unit.c:2826-2881`), `ServiceRequest` completion/reply path (`request.c:175-275`), `CmdFlush` (`request.c:493-498`), and `FlushUnit` (`unit.c:1381-1435`). The flush drains WRITE through EVENT queues and each opener's read/mgmt ports; queued general requests ahead of it are dispatched first, and later requests remain ordered behind it. `SCAN_QUEUE` has no producer in this driver. This recheck did not establish a CMD_FLUSH defect; broader unit/caller review remains open. No request or device was run. Source-only.

Atheros5000 unit tail/event/stats pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): read `ResetHandler`, `UpdateStats`, `ReportEvents`, and traced their request/event callers (`unit.c:865-1000,1660-1684,1958-1966,2070-2080,2168-2182,2687-2800`; `request.c:1050-1062,1080-1130`). UnitTask and broader HAL/caller review remain open. No device or event request was run. Source-only.

Atheros5000 UnitTask signal-allocation recheck (2026-10-17; no new finding): `UnitTask` does not check its three `AllocSignal(-1)` results before shifts and Wait (`unit.c:2826-2837`). Traced the task allocator: `CreateUnit` zero-allocates the Task and selected `AddUnitTask`/`NewAddTask` fills a zero `tc_SigAlloc` from `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc` (`unit.c:402-427`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-251`); the selected system mask reserves bits 0-15 (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`), leaving 16 general signals. The fresh task uses only three signals here, so exhaustion is not supported by the ordinary selected creation path; no failure finding added. UnitTask/caller and chipset/HAL review remain open. No task or device was run. Source-only.


Atheros5000 channel-discovery failure follow-up (OD3391, 2026-10-17): traced `InitialiseAdapter` through `ath_hal_init_channels`, its invalid-regulatory-domain early exits, selected AR5211/AR5212 EEPROM attach, and later `ConfigureAdapter` iteration. The HAL can attach after reading (without validating membership of) the regulatory-domain word; channel discovery then returns before writing `*nchans`, while the caller copies the uninitialized local into `unit->channel_count`. `ConfigureAdapter` uses that value to walk the 100-entry allocated channel array. Added OD3391. No EEPROM or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio unit-graph propagation pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, `nFlowUp`, `nFlowDown`, `nFlowUpToUSBSource`, `nFlowDownToUSBSink`, and the stages in `nExamineAudioUnits` that connect units, assign terminal roots, propagate channels, and attach modes (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:800-1010,1370-1905`). Standard USB hub binding-startup handshake pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `usbAttemptDeviceBinding`, `usbForceDeviceBinding`, `nHubTask`, and `nAllocHub` startup success/failure notification. On success, `nAllocHub` stores `nch_Task` before returning and the worker signals the binder; on initialization failure, its unwind closes partial resources, clears `nch_Task`, and signals before the binder frees `nch`. If task creation itself fails, the binder frees its allocated record without waiting. No unpaired wait or post-free worker access was established in these branches. Hub port behavior and the rest of the function-by-function audit remain open; no hub or failure was exercised. Source-only.

Standard USB hub synchronous control-method pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `usbDoMethodA` cases for port-control and worker-directed suspend/resume/binding methods, `nHandleHubMethod`, per-call reply-port allocation/deletion, `nHubTask` reply processing, and `nFreeHub`'s queued-message drain. A failed reply-port allocation avoids queueing; successful queue entries are replied by the worker or teardown drain before the caller deletes its reply port. The check/PutMsg and `nch_Task` publication still rely on `Forbid()` around shared state; ExecSMP teardown interleavings need a separate complete lock/lifetime pass and are not marked clear here. Hub class remains partially audited; no request or device was used. Source-only.

Standard USB hub control-call concurrency cross-check (OD3235, 2026-10-17; no separate finding): the maintained PoPo GUI invokes `UCM_HubPowerCyclePort`/`UCM_HubDisablePort` directly with the hub device and port (`rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c:895-901,1538`); `psdDoHubMethodA` checks parent/binding pointers without an SMP lock (`poseidon.library.c:6032-6050`). The class then traverses `nh_Bindings`, sets per-hub flags, and reads/signals `nch_Task` under `Forbid()` (`hub.class.c:282-318`). Binding release removes and frees the same record after `Forbid()` (`:142-175`). On ExecSMP this concurrency is covered by OD3235's shared-list and node-lifetime race; no second issue is credited for the same unsynchronized protection. No GUI command or binding teardown was run. Source-only.

Moschip USB Ethernet TX length and copy-bound pass (OD3397 boundary checked; no new finding, 2026-10-17): traced the sole `cmdWrite` queueing path into the class worker and `nWritePacket` (`rom/usb/classes/moschipeth/dev.c:335-379`; `moschipeth.class.c:751-758,1343-1408`). The caller rejects raw payloads above `RAWPKT_SIZE` and cooked payloads above `ETHERPKT_SIZE`; `nWritePacket` adds the Ethernet header only for cooked writes, copies exactly the validated payload, and pads short frames to `ETHER_MIN_LEN`. The two 2048-byte write buffers (`moschipeth.class.h:28`) contain the maximum checked packet plus this header/padding. The observed direct NULL dereference after BufMan allocation failure is compiled only under `DEBUG`; the non-DEBUG successful-Open invalid-field path remains OD3397. No request, transfer, or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only.
USB Ethernet orphan-reader fan-out trace (OD3398 added, 2026-10-17): followed the unmatched-packet branch in all eight class receive workers and `nReadIOReq` through queue removal/reply. Each worker iterates the entire global `ncp_OrphanQueue`; `nReadIOReq` removes and replies to every visited request. The adjacent comments say only one caller should get the orphan packet, and selected PCI AROS network drivers copy it to the request-port head only. Added OD3398, conditional on multiple pending orphan requests and a packet unmatched by regular reads. The exact SANA-II contract is not present in the repository; this qualification is recorded in the detailed finding. No packet was received. Source-only.
USB Ethernet `S2_TRACKTYPE` allocation-failure exclusion pass (OD3399 added, 2026-10-17): compared all eight class implementations. Seven call `Forbid` before `AllocVec` and return `S2ERR_NO_RESOURCES` without `Permit` on allocation failure (`asixeth/dev.c:818-858`; `cdceth:823-863`; `davicometh:818-858`; `ethwrap:701-741`; `moschipeth:823-863`; `pegasuseth:818-858`; `rndis:707-747`). Added OD3399; no allocation failure or request was induced. Source-only.
ASIX AX88178/AX88772 aggregated receive-length pass (OD3400 added, 2026-10-17): traced pipe completion actual length into `nReadPacket` and checked the inverse-length prefix, rounded record bound, loop pointer/remaining-length update, and TX framing. RX validates an even-rounded record size but advances only by its unrounded size (`asixeth.class.c:1883-1904`); a one-byte pad on odd records is then treated as the next prefix. The RX worker passes actual pipe length directly (`:743-760`), while TX emits variable lengths above minimum (`:1658-1668,1710-1733`). Added OD3400 for the selected AX88178/AX88772 devices; no USB transfer was run. Source-only.

USB Ethernet minimum receive-length comparison (2026-10-17; no new finding): compared all eight `nReadPacket` length guards and callers. ASIX, CDC, Davicom, Moschip, and Pegasus require `ETHER_MIN_LEN`; ethwrap and RNDIS require only an Ethernet header; LAN78xx rejects RX command error (`RED`) but its packet callback has no minimum-length guard (`asixeth.class.c:1920-1921`; `cdceth.class.c:1811`; `dm9601eth.class.c:1703`; `ethwrap.class.c:1189,1204`; `lan78xx.class.c:1201-1225,1306-1319`; `moschipeth.class.c:1579`; `pegasus.class.c:1918`; `rndis.class.c:1041,1057`). Davicom initialization omits `RX_PASS_RUNT` while enabling `RX_DISCARD_CRC` (`dm9601eth.class.c:1384-1395`). The local source does not establish whether ethwrap/RNDIS sources or LAN78xx hardware can deliver runt frames in these configurations, or whether accepting such frames violates their caller contract; no finding added on this evidence. No packet or device was used. Source-only.

USB serial/printer OUT completion-status recheck (OD3367, 2026-10-17; duplicate candidate withdrawn): traced queued CMD_WRITE dispatch through the worker for PL2303, CP210x, CDC ACM, printer, and Palm PDA classes, then checked Poseidon stream error storage and query semantics. USB Audio hardware-control, allocation rollback, and descriptor-construction pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `subLibHardwareControl` through the selected AHI `AHIC_*` dispatcher, the `nAudioTask` update consumer, and `nGetInputUnit` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:571-780,4080-4163`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:979-1000`). USB Audio Type I format sample-rate extent pass (OD3171 expanded, 2026-10-17): verified the Type I descriptor has an eight-byte fixed header followed by a count-controlled discrete frequency list or a six-byte continuous range (`compiler/include/devices/usb_audio.h:385-396`). `nExamineAudioDescriptors` caps the discrete count at 64 but reads three bytes per retained entry, and reads six continuous-range bytes at `tSamFreq0`; it never requests or checks `DDA_DescriptorLength` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1225-1259`). RTL8139 S2_TRACKTYPE rollback cross-check (OD3071 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced `CmdTrackType` and `CmdUntrackType` plus Open/Close ownership (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/handler.c:396-514`; `rtl8139_init.c:318-352,388-409`). The global tracker is incremented before duplicate detection and baseline allocation; a new global node is linked before baseline allocation. Duplicate and low-memory failures return errors without reversing that state, and UntrackType requires an opener baseline before decrementing the unit reference, so neither failure can be balanced through that opener. RTL8139 correctly handles failure of the global tracker allocation itself, so its case is the later rollback defect only. This extends shared finding OD3071; Close's broader successful-track cleanup remains OD3038. The target is available through the network cards aggregate on i386, x86_64, m68k and PPC (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:45-54`) when selected. No request or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

RTL8139 multicast range bookkeeping and RX filter pass (2026-10-17; no distinct transactional defect): traced the S2 add/remove wrappers, `AddMulticastRange`, `RemMulticastRange`, `AddressFilter`, and `rtl8139nic_set_rxmode` (`handler.c:779-827`; `unit.c:723-751,1210-1312`; `rtl8139.c:320-329,530-580`). Exact duplicate ranges increment `add_count`, and only the final matching remove unlinks/frees the range and decrements the unique-range count. USB Audio hardware-control update flags and AHI dispatcher recheck (OD3167 expanded, 2026-10-17): re-read all five set/query branches in `subLibHardwareControl` against the selected `AHI_ControlAudioA` dispatcher (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:978-999`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:4105-4157`). The AHI dispatcher invokes the subdriver synchronously and adds no lock around the shared mode values or `nch_UpdateFlags`; all five setters OR a bit then signal the same worker. The worker reads current shared values, performs synchronous control transfers, then clears the entire flag word (`:613-762`). This confirms OD3167's lost-update interleaving for each control flag, not just volume: any update arriving after the worker checked its bit but before the unconditional clear can be acknowledged by a pending signal while its flag is erased. Expanded OD3167's scope; no separate candidate. Source-only.

Added OD3448; callers may receive an error status for an abort that succeeded. No request was aborted. Source-only.

Sam440 AMCC440/460 and Efika PCI HIDD body pass (OD3449, 2026-10-17): reread all three selected `driverclass.c` bodies (205, 221 and 295 lines) and traced their init/rollback hooks through generated autoinit and OOP attr-base refcount code. OD3449 records AMCC460's model-mismatch rollback releasing shared attr-base refs acquired by the earlier-loaded AMCC440 HIDD on 440EP builds. Rechecked existing OD2884, OD2942, OD2949, OD3409 and OD3410; no additional source-supported issue established in the other reviewed methods. PCI configuration-space hardware semantics and later OOP client behavior remain unverified. No module or hardware was exercised. Source-only.


USB HID absolute tablet scaling caller closure (OD2300 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced a valid 24-bit unsigned absolute X report through `hid_get_data`, `USBMouse::New`, the worker's `IENewTablet`, input.device and Intuition. With logical range 0..16,777,215 and X=3,000,000, the extraction remains positive (below bit 23), and a 1,920-pixel screen should map it to 343; Intuition's 32-bit multiplication wraps to 1,465,032,704 and yields 87 (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid.c:438-461`; `mouseclass.c:135-158,324-343`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2179-2188`). Sam440 and Efika package routes select this class. This establishes a maintained caller for OD2300 without relying on the 32-bit extraction edge (OD3142) or a value above the signed midpoint (OD3143). No descriptor/device/event was used. Source-only.

Bluetooth HID GUI tracking-signal allocation failure trace (2026-10-17; candidate not promoted): `bGUITask` does not check `AllocSignal(-1)` before shifting its result into the GUI wait mask (`bthid.gui.c:1610-1618`); the report task sends the corresponding shifted signal (`bthid.class.c:970-976`), and Exec documents `-1` on allocation failure (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:42-47`). Both paths therefore use an invalid shift count when the GUI task has exhausted its allocatable signals. Since producer and consumer derive the bit from the same field, and no selected second wait/consumer conflict was established, this pass did not establish a distinct user-visible failure beyond the undefined/invalid mask behavior. OD3516 scheduling premise recheck (2026-10-17): confirmed both worker tasks are created at priority 50 and Exec `Signal` documents immediate dispatch only when the awakened task is higher priority than the signaling task (`eth/init.c:185-194`; `tap/init.c:244-253`; `rom/exec/signal.c:127-130`). For a blocked lower-priority Open/Close caller, the worker continues through `FreeVec(msg)` and exits before the caller dequeues the queued message. Tightened OD3516's trigger and confidence statement; no task schedule was run.

USB MassStorage StorageDev_Init allocation/registration recheck (OD2822 retained; 2026-10-17): reread the complete selected init chain. `Storage_Init` releases acquired OOP attr bases if `CreatePool` fails, and on pool success it returns TRUE even if the temporary USB-root `OOP_NewObject` fails; the USB stack startup scan still discovers the registered class library, as already recorded in the HID init row. At priority 1, `StorageDev_Init` allocates `mss_device_t` plus the function-table prefix from that pool, adds the prefix to the raw address, dereferences the result, registers the device and returns TRUE without testing the allocation (`storage_init.c:61-82,106-107`; `storage_device.c:784-803,811-812`). This confirms OD2822 and its allocation-failure trigger; no second init/registration finding was established. No allocation failure or class load was induced. Source-only.

USB MassStorage AddDevice/vector-owner lifetime cross-check (OD2822 retained; no new OD): traced the device-base prefix allocation through `MakeFunctions`, `AddDevice`, `SumLibrary`, and the USB class-library lifetime. The function table reserves the negative vector prefix and `MakeFunctions` installs the eight vectors; `SumLibrary` skips checksumming because the zero-cleared device base does not set `LIBF_SUMUSED`. The registered `usbmss.device` base is pool-owned and has no checked-in `RemDevice` caller, but the USB stack stores the `OpenLibrary` reference in `ec_LibBase` for each discovered class and does not close these references during normal class removal; USB stack expunge deletes its class list/pool without closing them, matching existing OD2209. Therefore class-library expunge does not establish a distinct dangling-device route during ordinary USB stack operation; the uncovered issue remains OD2822’s unchecked initial device allocation, with OD2209 accounting for the retained external-class reference on USB expunge. No class load, device open or expunge was run. Source-only.

USB Audio real-time callback teardown boundary pass (2026-10-17; OD3517 follow-up): traced `subLibFreeAudio` through Poseidon STOP/REMOVE. The initial pass had not established callback quiescence; later controller-side tracing promoted the confirmed ExecSMP cross-CPU gap as OD3517, with separate xHCI and PCIUSB UHCI/EHCI/OHCI expansions recorded below. OD3163's recording-hook conversion behavior, OD3167's unsynchronized control flags, and OD3174's ignored start result remain distinct. The selected PCIUSB UHCI/EHCI/OHCI and PCI xHCI callback/stop interleavings are now covered by OD3517; Deneb and follow-on queue scheduling remain open. No audio stream, callback or teardown was run. Source-only.

USB Audio UHCI recording-hook versus teardown synchronization (OD3517 added, 2026-10-17): completed the controller-side callback trace. UHCI interrupt completion calls `uhciHandleIsochTDs`, which invokes the RTIso done hook inline; Poseidon StopRTIso synchronously submits `UHCMD_STOPRTISO`, but the PCI command only unlinks PTDs and clears flags. ExecSMP `Disable` is local to the current processor, and no common lock/drain joins stop to a completion already running on another CPU. USB Audio then frees `nam_AHIBuffer` after stop, while `nInDoneHook` writes/converts that buffer and calls the AHI sampler. Added OD3517 for concurrent active capture teardown on the selected PC UHCI/ExecSMP path. xHCI uses a separate event-task path; `xhciHandleFinishedTDs` calls the callback before freeing its periodic context, while stop removes contexts without joining an already executing event-task callback. The selected PC PCIUSB UHCI/EHCI/OHCI and PCI xHCI HCD paths therefore support OD3517. Deneb and follow-on queue scheduling remain open; no stream or teardown was run. Source-only.

USB Audio high-speed interval fixed-point boundary follow-up (OD3173 expanded, 2026-10-17): evaluated the selected high-speed interval normalization and `subLibStart` arithmetic for a 48 kHz mix (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8525-8553`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2629-2672,3721-3723`). At legal `bInterval=11`, Poseidon exposes 1024 microframes; treating that as milliseconds makes the 16.16 sample increment `3,221,225,472` (`0xC0000000`), outside signed LONG/Fixed range. The playback request hook uses this increment in its sample-count and `ubr_Length` calculations. Expanded existing OD3173 with the explicit overflow consequence; no duplicate finding added. No stream or endpoint was used. Source-only.

USB Audio xHCI callback teardown follow-up (OD3517 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced selected xHCI RTIso capability and stop path through `xhciStopIsochIO`/`xhciFreePeriodicContext` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:586-587,1665-1700`; `xhci_isoch.c:332-354`; `xhci_periodic.c:40-45`). The independent xHCI event task runs `xhciHandleFinishedTDs`, which calls RTIso done hooks while consuming the periodic request (`xhci_hw.c:524-540`; `xhci_hcd.c:2701-2810`). Stop removes request contexts and clears ring back-pointers but does not wait for the event task to finish a callback it already entered; its local `Disable` does not synchronize across ExecSMP processors. Expanded OD3517 to include this backend because the same USB Audio capture buffer is freed after stop. No xHCI device or stream was used. Source-only.

USB Audio PCIUSB EHCI/OHCI completion-stop cross-check (OD3517 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): traced the shared PCIUSB `cmdStopRTIso` dispatch to EHCI/OHCI descriptor unlink/reset (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:1707-1716`; `ehci/ehci_isoch.c:694-720`; `ohci/ohci_isoch.c:530-568`) and both completion paths to inline RTIso hook calls (`ehci/ehci_hcd.c:1097-1134`; `ehci_isoch.c:250-259`; `ohci/ohci_hcd.c:1310-1345,512-522`). The command's `Disable` is local on ExecSMP; no cross-CPU completion drain was found. Expanded OD3517 to cover PCIUSB's three HCD variants as well as PCI xHCI. Deneb remains outside the SMP trigger. No controller or stream was used. Source-only.

Deneb RTIso stop/callback boundary check for OD3517 (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced the Deneb `UHCMD_STOPRTISO` dispatch and `cmdStopRTIso` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:602-608`; `uhwcmd.c:1501-1539`) against `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos` and its interrupt caller (`uhwcmd.c:3333-3385,3668-3673,5326-5334`). Deneb clears the RT done mask and active PTD state with local interrupts disabled; completion hooks run synchronously inside the hardware interrupt handler on this single-CPU m68k target. A task-context teardown cannot overlap an already-running handler on a second processor, and a deferred done bit is filtered by the cleared busy/RT masks. Thus Deneb is not included in OD3517's ExecSMP cross-core trigger; broader Deneb request/transfer semantics remain open. No Deneb device or stream was used. Source-only.

OpenSBI PCIDT MSI release recheck (OD3520 added, 2026-10-17): verified the PCIDT method list omits ReleaseVectors, the inherited generic method is a no-op, and every successful PCIDT MSI obtain permanently sets a bridge occupancy bit after enabling device MSI. Traced the selected NVMe release call and qualified ordinary startup as blocked by OD2876. Other external/direct clients can still exhaust the finite bridge pool by repeated obtain/release cycles. No MSI operation was run. Source-only.

OpenSBI PCIDT vector-minimum/API-index recheck (OD3521 refined, 2026-10-17): compared the public PCI method contract with PCIDT and generic PCIPC/RP1/BCM2712 implementations. PCIDT neither reads the minimum requirement nor honors the requested vector index; it configures one MSI message, whereas the other checked backends validate unsupported minima. NVMe requests Max=CPU count but currently hard-codes one I/O queue (`hwqcnt=1`), leaves the assignment from negotiated queue count commented, and only configures index zero; xHCI also requests one vector. No current in-tree multi-vector trigger established; external/future clients remain the trigger. No request was issued. Source-only.

OpenSBI HIDD manifest-to-ledger reconciliation (2026-10-17): swept every C/header/manifest/config file under `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd`. PCIDT, dwuart and dwi2c are selected through the BSP HIDD list. The only missing local rows were the dwuart and dwi2c manifests and generated definitions; added all four with method/build-edge checks. No hardware or generated module was run. Source-only.
OpenSBI battclock/boot file-set reconciliation (OD2648/OD2662 detail restored, 2026-10-17): compared the OpenSBI package and architecture-specific battclock manifest against local selected files. Added individual battclock, USB ROM startup, and associated Exec boot/include manifest rows; all local battclock and USB startup files now have one row. Restored OD2648's malformed RTC-date conversion and OD2662's permanent I2C setup-reference leak to the detailed report and index, with 998 unique OD entries. The generic boot manifest row was repaired into a valid table row after insertion. No RTC, USB startup, build, or failure was run. Source-only.

NVMe failed-attachment rollback recheck (OD2365 restored to detailed report and index, 2026-10-17): verified the early timer-open failure against generic `HW_AddDriver` cleanup and PCI `Obtain`/`Release`, then checked the post-superclass stages against list publication and destructor reachability. The selected PCIPC failure after admin-queue IRQ registration but before Identify submission is concrete: failed `AllocPCIMem` frees `dev_Queues[0]` and the pointer array without removing the kernel IRQ handler; the non-NULL controller is not linked into `nvme_Controllers`, and generic setup accepts it. Inherited PCIPC `AddInterrupt` registers through `KrnAddIRQHandler`; the kernel IRQ walker calls every handler on a shared line, and `NVME_AdminIntCode` dereferences its queue argument. Narrowed the stale-pointer consequence to a later interrupt on that shared INTx line; the completed Identify-error branch instead retains an allocated unlisted controller/queue/handler, while timeout-after-submit remains separately OD2361. OD2365 restored; no new OD number. No allocation failure, PCI interrupt or teardown was run. Source-only.

PCI reset-callback finding consolidation (2026-10-17): verified the registration and teardown branches in all six Prometheus PCI network drivers. Expanded OD418 from Rhine to Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, Etherlink III, NvidiaNet, Prism2 and Rhine; each calls `AddResetCallback` even after `AddPCIIntServer` changes `success` to FALSE, then frees the unit through `DeleteUnit`/`FreeCard` without the normal `RemResetCallback` cleanup. With AROS `AddResetCallback` always returning TRUE, OD3101’s Broadcom/Etherlink partial-registration claim duplicated this same failure route; its separate wrapper-allocation issue is covered by OD3335 and OD2802, so OD3101 was withdrawn. The family-level wrapper leak is independently OD3335. The IRQ failure and later reset remain source-level triggers; none was induced.

PCIPC candidate reconciliation (2026-10-17): detailed findings OD3522-OD3525 were transferred from the Graphics/Desktop ledger after confirming they concern the selected PC PCI driver. The segment and high-BAR findings remain OD2417 and OD2985; their GD duplicates were withdrawn. PCI class, firmware and caller coverage remains open. Source-only.

PCI expunge root-identity correction (OD3526, 2026-10-17): the earlier OD3278 review verified that `CLID_HW_Root` is a shared singleton but did not compare it with PCI_Init's preferred `CLID_Hidd_System` registration receiver. These are distinct singleton objects; expunge removes from the wrong root, ignores failure, then manually disposes the still-registered PCI object. The default PC manifest does not select kernel-hidd-system and PCIPC is noexpunge, so the finding is restricted to optional/manual configurations. No module was loaded or expunged. Source-only.

ARM clock-query caller/error-path recheck (OD3527 retained, 2026-10-17; no new finding): traced `GCIT_ProcessorSpeed` from SysMon's per-core refresh through `ARM_AnswerTag` into `GetCurrentProcessorFrequency` and `vcQueryClock` (`workbench/system/SysMon/processor.c:99-123`; `arch/arm-native/processor/getcpuinfo.c:138-139`; `processor_frequency.c:80-100`). The first nonzero measured clock is cached per `ARMProcessorInformation`; failed measured queries fall back to setpoint, then maximum, while zero leaves the cache retryable. `MBoxCall` serializes the request, bounds its write-ready and response loops, and returns failure distinctly; the caller treats failure as zero. The selected mailbox implementation does not validate the VideoCore property response/status words before consuming the returned rate, but this pass did not establish a concrete erroneous nonzero result on a documented firmware failure path, so no additional finding is credited. OD3527 remains the established cache-line ownership violation. No clock query, mailbox transaction, or hardware was run. Source-only.

Current behavior remains an unclassified VFPv2 result and false VFPv1 init diagnostic; restoring only the commented line would instead make the VFPv3 init branch report VFPv3. Updated OD3531 to include the alias and the distinct-bit requirement. No boot or hardware was used. Source-only.

The checked-in misc diagnostic passes uninitialized local storage for both and prints the results. Added OD3539; no query or diagnostic was run. Source-only.

ARM processor topology caller recheck (no new finding, 2026-10-17): traced shared topology allocation and zero initialization, ARM `Processor_FillTopology`, `GetCPUInfo`, `GetCoreInfo`, and `GetCPUTopology`. Shared initialization establishes `pt_Count == cpucount`, logical IDs, and flat fallback IDs; ARM only refines valid MPIDR entries, and `GetCoreInfo` bounds-checks before dispatch. The public topology pointer remains resource-owned. A failed optional topology allocation leaves the pointer NULL and current ARM tag paths use fallback values; no separate caller failure was established. Source-only.
SD-card shared bus/unit field-consumer census (2026-10-17; no new OD): searched every declared `sdcb_*`, `sdcu_*`, `sdcbu_*`, and `sdcard_*` field across generic SD-card code and selected BCM2708/SDHOST backends, then traced listeners, IRQ status/error latches, DMA state, media flags, task signals, unit tables, change notifications, capacities, function callbacks, and the base's pending-task counter through their direct callers. Existing findings cover the concrete stale/uninitialized/error paths encountered (OD3302/3304/3305/3315/3320/3324/3350). `sdcb_CmdError` is reset by the serialized command producer and latched by its IRQ path; late-controller IRQ semantics remain unverified. The AArch64 Pi build includes both backend initializers, but their peripheral-base guards register SDHOST on the earlier SoCs and SDHCI on BCM2711/2712, not both for one selected base (`sdcard_sdhost_init.c:113-126`; `sdcard_bcm2708init.c:101-130`). No additional source-supported field-consumer defect established; hardware/error timing and external callers remain open. Source-only.
OD3528 task-creation contract recheck (2026-10-17): verified the selected Exec `NewCreateTaskA` contract explicitly returns NULL on failure and returns NULL when its `NewAllocEntry` or `NewAddTask` path fails (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:79-80,190-191,257-272`). The ARM initializer ignores this result after placing the associated signal in `waitmask`; the selected Raspberry Pi `smp` configure branch defines ExecSMP and its boot package includes `processor.resource` (`configure.in:2195-2198`; `arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:183`; `arch/arm-native/processor/mmakefile.src:7-12`). This confirms OD3528. No task-creation failure or boot was induced. Source-only.

PCI Command byte-write W1C caller follow-up (OD2949 expanded, 2026-10-17): confirmed generic, BCM2711, BCM2712 and Efika `WriteConfigByte` implementations read and rewrite the full containing config dword. Searched direct local `WriteConfigByte` callers: checked RTL816x dynamic offsets resolve to 0x69/0x79, other RTL816x calls use 0x81/latency/cache-line, PCIUSB UHCI writes 0x40, HDAudio uses codec/link registers, and Nouveau writes 0x68; none writes PCI Command bytes. Keep byte form conditional on public API use; the selected Efika Radeon trigger is word form. No config write or W1C status was exercised. Source-only.

Bluetooth HID action scaling intermediate-width check (OD3540 added, 2026-10-17): confirmed `LONG` is signed 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-39`), a 16-bit variable item can retain logical range 0..65535 and decode 65535 (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2016-2019,2228-2247,4175-4224`), and action scaling multiplies the input delta by output span before division (`:4529-4535`). Bluetooth HID relative mouse-delta accumulator path (OD3541 added, 2026-10-17): traced the `HUA_MOUSEPOS` delta-X/Y additions (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:4925-4936`) through input-item dispatch and the worker's message-drain/flush ordering (`:862-875,955-970`) to the relative InputEvent assignment and accumulator reset (`:5697-5713`). The report can encode both fields in eight bytes and retain positive bounds no greater than LONG_MAX (`:2016-2019,2228-2247,4175-4224`; type width `compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-39`). If `CheckIO` reports pending, the selected timer AbortIO removes the request, marks it `IOERR_ABORTED`, and calls `ReplyMsg` before returning (`rom/timer/abortio.c:69-90`); if it reports complete, the request is already a reply message and is drained with `GetMsg` (`ohcihub.c:208-212`). USB HID failed worker-publication follow-up (OD3564; historical coverage-only OD2246 restored, 2026-10-17): confirmed the keyboard and mouse constructor behavior against both `NewAddTask` NULL returns and `RemTask` ownership. USB HID initial worker-allocation failure recheck (OD3565; historical coverage-only OD2246/OD2810 restored, 2026-10-17): traced the keyboard/mouse Task and MemList allocations through the skipped setup conditional and returned object. USB HID worker detach-before-DOS-init recheck (OD2184 restored to detailed report, 2026-10-17): traced each worker's first `Wait` through its `dos_not_ready` branch against the subclass Dispose signal and the USB hub's disconnect disposal (`kbdclass.c:329-374,241-257`; `mouseclass.c:238-294,226-235`; `usbhubclass.c:536-547`). Keyboard's `if/else` always skips Ctrl-C processing on that first wake, even if opening DOS succeeds; mouse skips it only when DOS open still fails, because a successful open falls through to its separate `if (!dos_not_ready)` check. Both destructors send only one Ctrl-C and do not join the worker, so the stated early-disconnect timing leaves the worker waiting with its input.device request/port open. Restored OD2184 rather than duplicating the existing coverage-only candidate; no runtime route was exercised. Source-only.

USB HID worker-stack allocation failure recheck (OD2247 restored to detailed report, 2026-10-17): confirmed the keyboard and mouse constructors both build `tc_SPReg` from unchecked `sp`, then call `NewAddTask` (`kbdclass.c:206-234`; `mouseclass.c:191-219`). The Sam440 PPC USB package selects the generic USB stack and its classes; PPC stack-down configuration and `SP_OFFSET=0x10` make the NULL-derived register near `0x27f0`, which selected `PrepareContext` writes before allocating its context (`arch/ppc-all/include/aros/cpu.h:26,82`; `arch/ppc-sam440/exec/preparecontext.c:19-31`; boot dependency `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:51`). USB HID mouse event-ring producer/consumer recheck (2026-10-17; no additional finding): followed `HidInterrupt` through `Cause` to the report callback and worker (`hidclass.c:65-84`; OHCI WDH caller `ohcidriverclass.c:353-392`; `mouseclass.c:45-86,278-305`). The callback fills one ring slot before advancing `head` and signals the task; the worker copies the slot fields before advancing `tail`. Both cursors stay in `[0, RING_SIZE)`, and the fill calculation correctly adds `RING_SIZE` when the head wraps below the tail, reserving one slot to distinguish full from empty. No ring-bound or independent cursor-order defect established in this sequential producer/consumer path. The broader completion/removal lifetime remains covered by OHCI OD2958/OD2959; no USB report or interleaving was run. Source-only.

Trackdisk Exec task-creation failure follow-up (OD3566, 2026-10-17): traced successful TD_InitTask-side TaskData/stack/MemList allocations through the unchecked NewAddTask result and unconditional startup Wait. AHI audio.device capture-offset width pass (OD3572 added, 2026-10-17): inspected all six RecM/S 8/16/32-bit converters and the local `struct sample` definition (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devsupp.c:32-35,43-179`). AHI audio.device first-read idle-delay pass (OD3573 added, 2026-10-17): traced zero-cleared unit construction and `RecordOffDelay` state (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:444-447`; `device.h:140`) through ReadCmd startup/queueing, first-buffer FillReadBuffer completion and FeedReaders shutdown (`devcommands.c:983-1094`). PL011BT missing-mailbox capability recheck (OD3577 added, 2026-10-17): traced `OpenResource("mbox.resource")` through successful init and the advertised capability mask to `PL011BTSetPower`'s `firmware_gpio_set` return (`pl011bt_init.c:306-324,138-149,514-533`; interface comment in `pl011bt.conf:7-19`). Deneb RTIso start/stop/removal state-machine recheck for OD3517 (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `cmdStartRTIso`, `cmdStopRTIso`, `cmdRemIsoHandler`, and `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos` through the interrupt dispatch (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1317-1529,1533-1588,3333-3745,5326-5334`). Completion callbacks run inline while the Deneb hardware interrupt handler processes the done map; stop/removal disable local interrupts, clear the relevant `hu_IsoRTDone`, `hu_IsoBusy`, and `hu_IsoRTMask` bits, and deactivate or detach both PTDs before reenabling interrupts. A later handler masks the hardware done map with `hu_IsoBusy` and only dispatches realtime callbacks for bits still in `hu_IsoRTMask`. On the selected single-CPU m68k backend, a task-context stop cannot overlap a callback already executing in the interrupt handler, and deferred bits are filtered by the cleared masks. OD3517 therefore remains scoped to the cross-CPU PCIUSB/xHCI backends; broader Deneb transfer scheduling, buffer alignment, and callback contract review remain open. No device, stream, or interrupt was exercised. Source-only.

Deneb RTIso OUT-hook word-copy boundary pass (OD3578 added, 2026-10-17): traced both startup-prefill and recurring OUT-completion copies (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1380-1432,3700-3740`) against `IOUsbHWBufferReq`'s hook-adjusted byte length and scatter/gather flag contract (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:103-113`). The backend rounds each segment's source-word count up with `(ubr_Length + 3) >> 2`; when a hook sets `UBFF_CONTBUFFER` on a non-longword-aligned segment, the next segment starts at the advanced buffer pointer while the hardware destination advances by rounded words, matching the local FIXME about continuous-mode havoc. Added OD3578 for the packet-byte shift and rounded source load. No maintained Deneb RTIso OUT-hook producer or checked-in `UBFF_CONTBUFFER` setter was found, so the trigger remains external-client conditional. No stream or hook was run. Source-only.

Deneb unit close and embedded worker lifetime pass (OD3582 added, 2026-10-17): traced `Close_Unit`'s controller stop, interrupt removal, Ctrl-C signal, fixed timer delay and `FreeVec(unit)` against the embedded `Task`/stack layout and `uhwDMATask` exit path (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:502-525,5374-5401`; `denebusb.h:277,328`). The function has no completion handshake before freeing storage. A worker still executing a PIO copy or delayed past the 10-ms wait can continue through the unit or return into Exec's task finalizer, which removes the embedded Task (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:52-55`). Added OD3582 with the scheduler/work-duration condition explicit; no device close or task timing was run. Remaining command state machines and hardware contracts stay open. Source-only.

Deneb NAK timer, soft interrupt, and interrupt completion boundary pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced unit setup of `hu_NakTimeoutReq`/PA_SOFTINT and the first `Cause`, the NAK timer's frame counter and timeout loops, both timer re-submission paths, and teardown's PA_IGNORE/AbortIO/10-ms delay before unit free (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:64-112,280-525,4774-4826,4842-4990,5265-5370`). The handler sends the next timer request after each callback; close prevents new soft-interrupt delivery and aborts the outstanding request before freeing the unit. Timeout expiration clears the corresponding ATL/interrupt NAK map through `FreeATL`/`FreeInt`. No separate finding retained from this pass. This was source tracing only; no timer, NAK, or close path was run. Deneb command completion, abort, and timeout edge cases remain under review.

Deneb AbortIO active ATL/DMA ownership pass (OD3584 added, 2026-10-17): traced the queue removal and ATL/INT/ISO PTD scans in `cmdAbortIO` through `FreeATL`/`FreeInt`/`FreeIso` and `devAbortIO` termination (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1626-1774,1778-1866`; `dev.c:658-687`). Deneb discrete OUT buffer-boundary pass (OD3585 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced `CopyMemShuffle` and its ordinary bulk/control/isochronous callers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:38-47,2498-2505,4402-4409,4712-4724`), then followed the aligned large bulk-OUT path through `CachePreDMA` and `MMS_LENGTHBYTES` programming (`:4300-4318`). Deneb control completion special-request recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed successful control status completion into the `CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT)` and `SET_ADDRESS` toggle-table updates (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2748-2772`) and compared `wValue` construction in Poseidon (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4693-4701`).
