Deneb ordinary isochronous OUT copy cross-check (OD3585 scope clarification, 2026-10-17): the ISO scheduler directly copies `(ptd_BufLen + 3) >> 2` longwords from `iouh_Data` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4715-4725`), confirming that a non-multiple-of-four request also reads beyond its logical caller-buffer extent on this path. This is already included in OD3585, which also covers control, bulk and interrupt OUT; no additional finding was needed. No transfer was run; source-only.

Deneb interrupt completion/scheduling caller pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `devBeginIO` through `cmdIntXFer`, the queued request, `uhwSoftInt`, `uhwHandleFinishedInts`, `FreeInt`, and Poseidon pipe construction (`dev.c:529-639`; `uhwcmd.c:936-958,2784-3004,3957-4188,4790-4821`; `poseidon.library.c:4532-4548,4612-4627`). Async enqueue clears `IOF_QUICK`, so the completion helper's unconditional `ReplyMsg` is valid on this path. Error, NAK-timeout, short-packet, IN-copy, continuation, free/reply ownership, and the non-split MULT programming (`uhwcmd.c:4082-4092`) were checked; the rounded OUT tail read remains OD3585. No independent issue was established in this interrupt path. Split-timing and controller-register semantics remain open. No endpoint or transfer was exercised; source-only.

Deneb worker-task startup failure caller reconciliation (OD3581 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): followed `Open_Unit`'s `AddTask` result across all three selected targets (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:452-484`; `mmakefile.src:25-44`). In `NODMA` builds the task performs signaled PIO copies; in `denebdmausb`, level-6 DMA completion signals this same task and returns, and only the task invokes `uhwHandleDMAInt` to advance the state machine (`uhwcmd.c:2180-2198,5000-5052,5281-5299,5372-5401`). The existing OD3581 is therefore applicable to DMA completion/reply stalls as well as PIO transfer stalls; the report and index now state both effects. No new finding. Creation failure and hardware behavior were not induced; source-only.

Deneb close/worker lifetime target reconciliation (OD3582 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): compared `Close_Unit`'s controller shutdown, Ctrl-C signal, fixed 10-ms delay and `FreeVec(unit)` with the worker's wait loop and task layout (`uhwcmd.c:502-525,5374-5401`; `denebusb.h:277,328`). The task checks/processes `SIGF_SINGLE` before observing Ctrl-C at loop exit; its DMA-build state machine performs register-memory copies and accesses the unit/controller mapping, while `NODMA` variants also copy through the worker. Since the task and stack reside in the freed unit allocation and there is no exit handshake, OD3582 applies to all three targets, not just PIO builds. Expanded the report and index. This is a source-level lifetime/scheduling condition; no timing or hardware run was performed.

Deneb control request endian/caller reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new finding): followed Poseidon's `psdPipeSetup`/`psdDoPipe` SET_ADDRESS request into the raw USB setup packet and the completed control-state handler (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:3364-3365`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2750-2770`). Because `wValue` and `wIndex` remain wire-order bytes in `UsbSetupData`, the m68k big-endian `wValue >> 3` calculation intentionally converts SET_ADDRESS's address byte into the endpoint-toggle table's `address << 5` base; it is not a separate endian bug. The subsequent loop still clears only indices 0..30, leaving endpoint 15 IN stale on address reuse as documented by OD3649. Ordinary control setup/data/status transitions, short-packet handling, allocation fallback, and caller publication were reread; no further deterministic source defect established. Split hub timing/status interpretation and hardware PTD semantics remain open. No request or controller was used; source-only.

Deneb controller initialization error propagation pass (OD3653 added, 2026-10-17): traced `uhwOpenTimer`/`uhwHWInit` and their Open_Unit/CMD_RESET callers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:65-115,117-266,461-484,530-552,569-585`). The hardware init error exits precede global/controller interrupt enable; both callers discard the error. The standard `CMD_RESET` vector then treats the connected bit alone as operational, so a connected-but-not-enabled port can return success after reset failure. Checked Poseidon's selected enumeration caller and distinguished its `UHCMD_USBRESET` dispatch to `cmdUsbReset`, which does not call `uhwHWInit`; the report now limits the false-success consequence to standard `CMD_RESET` callers. Timer allocation cleanup itself checks each nullable object, and `uhwDelayMS` is called only with fixed small constants in this file; no separate issue established. No board, port state, timer failure, or reset was exercised; source-only.

Deneb `UHCMD_USBRESET` contract/caller pass (OD3654 added, 2026-10-17): compared the command body with the USBHardware autodoc and both in-tree Poseidon call sites (`uhwcmd.c:601-615`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:589-612`; `poseidon.library.c:4148-4156,4255-4259`). The Deneb vector only queries `PORTSC1`, returns success for a connected port, and does not perform a root-port reset. Poseidon's checked-in call is the initial probe directly after opening Deneb, whose `uhwHWInit` already reset the port; the second call only occurs when that probe path did not complete. No repeated in-tree bus-reset call was found, so the report limits impact to later/external API use and avoids asserting the initial enumeration call is broken. Sibling PCIUSB/xHCI implementations contain similar FIXME state-only handlers; that does not change Deneb's explicit documented command contract. No reset was issued; source-only.

OD3654 Poseidon reset-call reachability recheck (2026-10-17): the source has two syntactic calls, but the later one at `poseidon.library.c:4255-4259` is guarded by `!resetdone`. Every control-flow path reaching it has already returned from the initial probe reset and set `resetdone = TRUE` at `:4163-4164`; allocation or `UHIOERR_HOSTERROR` failures return before the normal-hub branch (`:4136-4161`). Thus the second site is unreachable in this function as written. The only reachable in-tree `UHCMD_USBRESET` is the initial probe at `:4152`, following Deneb `Open_Unit`'s reset attempt; the ignored reset failure there is already OD3653. OD3654 remains scoped to later/external clients issuing a new reset after devices have been enumerated. No reset or enumeration was run. Source-only.

OD3655 independent source recheck (2026-10-17): reread the entire `uhwGetUsbState` helper and all three USBOPER/USBRESUME/USBSUSPEND handlers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:529-704`) against the command contracts (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:560-583,618-669`). The helper assigns OPERATIONAL from connection alone and independently ORs SUSPENDED from PORTSC1; each command handler only invokes the helper and tests a status bit, with no controller register writes. Poseidon continues to mark root-bus suspend/resume unsupported and has no selected call site. Existing OD3655 remains scoped to direct HCD callers; no additional finding established. No bus transition was run. Source-only.

OD3656 interval qualification (2026-10-17): rechecked `cmdAddIsoHandler` and `cmdStartRTIso` SOF-map assignment against the completion handler's sole success-path rearm/toggle (`uhwcmd.c:1181-1206,1360-1474,3408-3427,3774-3788`). The two PTDs have distinct interleaved masks for intervals below eight frames, but the default 8–511-frame branch and >511 branch assign identical masks. Tightened the finding to the guaranteed condition (a halted PTD stays inactive and its private error is not delivered) and made missing cadence conditional on interval/status semantics. Updated the index; no controller or RTIso stream was exercised. Source-only.

OD1736 baud-cache recheck (2026-10-17): traced the OpenSBI constructor's preference copy and initial `set_baudrate`, the HIDD setter's equality guard, and serial.device's independent zero-initialized `su_Baud` comparison/error handling (`dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:154-164,201,327-340`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:767-783`). With a supported preference baud, the constructor programs the UART but retains that value as the HIDD cache; a first serial.device request for the same rate is sent because `su_Baud` is still zero, then rejected by the HIDD's false default return. After a different baud is successfully programmed, the HIDD cache remains the constructor rate, so a request to restore that rate is likewise rejected although hardware is at the intervening rate. This is distinct from OD2536's invalid legacy default selector value 5, whose constructor programming attempt itself fails. Added the finding to the top-level index; no request or UART was used. Source-only.

Deneb bus state-command behavior and caller reconciliation (OD3655 added, 2026-10-17): compared `cmdUsbOper`, `cmdUsbResume`, and `cmdUsbSuspend` with the USBHardware command contracts and the shared state helper (`uhwcmd.c:530-552,628-704`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:560-583,618-669`). All three handlers only read `PORTSC1`; the helper sets OPERATIONAL on connection even if it also sets SUSPENDED. This makes USBOPER/USBRESUME return success without resuming a connected suspended bus, while USBSUSPEND rejects a connected active bus without issuing suspend. Poseidon explicitly marks root-bus suspend/resume unsupported and no selected in-tree caller sends these commands (`poseidon.library.c:3823-3827,3920-3924`); the report therefore limits impact to direct HCD clients. No bus transition was run; source-only.

Deneb RTIso halted-completion/rearm pass (OD3656 added, 2026-10-17): traced `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos` status handling and the two-PTD Add/Start/alternate schedule (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1070-1220,1334-1432,3333-3793`). A hardware HALT writes an error to the internal request copy but bypasses the only PTD rearm and `rtn_NextPTD` toggle; the public RTIso structure has no error callback and does not reply this private IOReq. A failed PTD therefore remains inactive in the ping-pong stream without owner notification, while its partner may continue. Selected USB Audio supplies only input/done hooks for its stream (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3212-3231`). Added OD3656 conditionally on the controller reporting a recoverable HALT/PID/babble status; whether each status can safely be retried requires controller semantics. No stream or hardware was exercised; source-only.
OD3499 AHCI port-multiplier caller confirmation (2026-10-17): verified that `ahci_pm_port_probe` issues both target-15 probe FISes through `ahci_poll(..., ahci_quick_timeout)` and returns timed-out CCBs through `ahci_put_err_ccb` on retry/final cleanup (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_pm.c:111-128,284-288,352-356,386-400`). The parent recovery flow is the selected AHCI port-reset/probe path; the direct timeout callback is shared with `ahci_port_softreset` and `ahci_read_ncq_error` (`ahci.c:1406,1437,3684`). This confirms the report's PM-probe trigger is a direct selected call path, not just a generic description. The panic still requires the hardware CI/SACT state to remain active after the stop attempts. No probe or hardware operation was run. Source-only.

AHCI OD2560 withdrawal after caller-state audit (2026-10-17): the code-level overwrite is real, but its stale-type consequence was not reachable in the selected caller flow. The only enabled `ahci_pm_softreset` caller is the PM state machine after `ahci_pm_hardreset` has set `at_type` to NONE; successful first/second reset cycles do not assign a type until after the comparison, so it takes the NONE branch. The only direct invocation with a previously cached type is under `#if 0` in `ahci.c:1848-1854`. Removed OD2560 from the detailed report and AROS index; retained the reviewed-but-withdrawn conclusion in the file ledger. No reset or hardware action was run. Source-only.

OpenSBI battclock I²C caller-lock and FDT bus-selection recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `ReadBattClock` and `WriteBattClock` through `ReadClockData`/`WriteClockData` to lazy `BattClock_I2CDevice` creation (`readbattclock.c:25-80`; `writebattclock.c:25-91`; `battclock_i2c.c:58-138`). Both public operations hold `bb_Lock` across the device lookup, probe and transfer, so the shared bus/device pointers are not concurrently initialized or disposed by those selected callers. Rechecked `BattClock_FindBus` against the selected FDT traversal API (`battclock_init.c:42-70`; `arch/riscv-all/linklibs/fdt/include/fdt.h:38-44`): traversal is depth-first and the API exposes no parent lookup; the implementation's last-seen chip-bus assumption can misassociate unusual trees with nested/multiplexed buses, an already recorded firmware-tree limitation rather than a confirmed defect for supplied platform trees. No RTC, device tree or transaction was run. Source-only.

Generic I²C WriteWord finding restored to detailed report/index (OD3657, 2026-10-17): rechecked `Hidd_I2CDevice.WriteWord`'s three-byte buffer and two-byte `I2C_WriteRead` length (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cdeviceclass.c:99-110`) through the generic wrapper (`:157-164`). The low byte is not sent. Existing caller census found no direct in-tree WriteWord caller; the finding is retained for public/direct HIDD clients and the detailed report/index entries have been restored. No method call or bus transaction was run. Source-only.

OpenSBI DWI2C/generic-device byte-method compatibility pass (OD3658 added, 2026-10-17): traced generic `WriteBytes` and `WriteVec` to the bus `Address`/`PutByte` primitives (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cdeviceclass.c:111-147`) and verified the selected DesignWare overrides return `FALSE` for both primitives (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_class.c:226-242`). Since the OpenSBI manifest selects both generic `i2c` and `dwi2c`, non-empty public methods fail before transmitting. No in-tree caller was found; scope is direct clients. Added detailed report and index entries. No bus transaction was run. Source-only.

USB Ethernet RX/Close/AbortIO ExecSMP finding recheck (OD3380 retained, 2026-10-17): reread the ASIX receive path from opener-list traversal through `nReadIOReq` (`rom/usb/classes/asixeth/asixeth.class.c:1773-1863,1933-1975`) against `devClose`'s BufMan unlink/free (`dev.c:175-198`) and `devAbortIO`'s pending-read removal/reply (`:1298-1354`). RX dereferences BufMan callbacks and the queued IO request and copies packet data before unlink/reply; Close frees the BufMan without draining its RX queue, and AbortIO can remove/reply the same queued request while RX is processing it. The RX traversal's Forbid and Close/AbortIO Forbid do not synchronize cross-CPU on ExecSMP per `rom/exec/forbid.c:52-60`; LAN78xx's Disable variant has the same processor-local limitation (`disable.c:50-61`). The existing OD3380 scope across all eight peers remains supported by the shared class/device-file audit; no new distinct candidate established. No packet or interleaving was run. Source-only.
OpenSBI PCIDT duplicate-compatible discovery trace (OD3659 added, 2026-10-17): traced FDT compatible-list matching (`arch/riscv-all/linklibs/fdt/fdt.c:219-247`), the separate `snps,dw-pcie` and `ultrarisc,dw-pcie` scans (`pcidt_driverclass.c:43-49,627-636`), repeated window/device setup and bridge count (`:701-779`), root bus-object assignment (`:790-804`), and `KrnMapGlobal`'s underlying MMU mapper, which overwrites existing mappings and returns success (`kernel_mmu.c:150-190`). A node listing both supported strings is therefore accepted and published twice. Repository search found no in-tree DTS declaring either compatible; firmware trigger remains conditional. Added OD3659 with this limitation. No FDT or PCI hardware was used; source-only.
OpenSBI PCIDT `ranges` and BAR assignment follow-up (2026-10-17; no new OD): reread the complete FDT `ranges` tuple parser, BAR sizing/allocation loops, 64-bit BAR mapping, PCI-to-CPU translation and selected `MapPCI` consumers (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:107-469,854-895`). The nonidentity 32-bit translation gap and single-retained-64-bit-window behavior are already covered by OD2566/OD2567. The ignored map return is now separately detailed as OD11215 for the high CPU-side I/O/MEM32 range that `PCIDT_MapAt` explicitly rejects, while bridge setup and identity-address exposure continue. OD11214 separately covers the un-clipped MEM32 ATU span crossing a 4 GiB CPU boundary; OD3983 remains the related but distinct MEM64 clipping case. No new distinct defect credited. Device-tree cell-layout variation and actual firmware range values remain unverified. No PCI device or hardware was used; source-only.
OD3659 registration-path confirmation (2026-10-17): followed `PCIDT_InitClass` from `pcidt_discover` to its `for (i < bridgeCount)` `moHidd_PCI_AddHardwareDriver` loop, then through `PCIDT__Root__New` consuming the next stored bridge (`pcidt_driverclass.c:1035-1083,783-804`). This confirms each duplicate entry causes a second distinct bus-driver registration attempt with the same bridge windows/configuration state, strengthening the duplicate publication consequence; the common PCI enumerator's handling of identical bus topology and firmware occurrence remain conditional. No driver object or PCI hardware was created.
OD3659 common PCI setup consequence confirmation (2026-10-17): followed the duplicate registration calls through deprecated `PCI__Hidd_PCI__AddHardwareDriver` into `HW_AddDriver` and `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:561-565,104-160`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:174-205`). Each driver instance scans the host bridge's bus and calls `InsertDevice` for found functions. Thus, if FDT discovery publishes the same bridge twice, the common setup path creates a second set of PCI device objects for the same bus/functions, giving clients duplicate device instances. This confirms the source consequence but not that a deployed firmware FDT contains both compatibles. No PCI driver or device was instantiated.

Serial zero-length write matrix follow-up (OD839 restored, 2026-10-17): followed `serial.device` CMD_WRITE and the write-empty callback through PC, Sam440, OpenSBI, Unix and m68k HIDD implementations. The PC/Sam440/OpenSBI do-while methods write `Outbuffer[0]` and return one byte for zero length when THRE is ready; serial.device then underflows its unsigned remaining length and the callback continues at `io_Data + 1`. Unix passes zero to host `write`, while m68k returns before reading the pointer. Restored the detailed report/index entry for the existing OD839 candidate. The serial.device module is optional; no zero-length request or UART was run. Source-only.

BWFM SANA-II RX request-delivery pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed `CMD_READ` queue insertion and `AbortIO`/`Close` removal against the RX pump's `rx_deliver` matching, RAW/cooked length calculation, filter and buffer-management hooks, request unlink/reply and packet statistics (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:306-405,1180-1228,1857-1878,1912-1940`). The receive path rejects frames shorter than `ETH_HLEN`, leaves filtered requests queued, and serializes queue-node lifetime with the unit semaphore while it invokes the opener callbacks. This pass did not establish an independent defect; callback reentrancy semantics and external SANA-II hook contracts remain unverified, as do broader read/write variants and the rest of the file. No frame or callback was run. Source-only.

BWFM SANA-II write-dispatch and framing follow-up (OD3592 confirmed, 2026-10-17): traced `CMD_WRITE`, `S2_BROADCAST` and `S2_MULTICAST` dispatch into `tx_request`, including the broadcast destination assignment, RAW versus cooked framing, `S2_CopyFromBuff`/16/32 hook selection at open, frame-size/error handling, `BWFMTxData` status propagation and packet/type statistics (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:78-98,652-716,1130-1145,1881-1890`). OD3592's cooked `ETH_HLEN + ios2_DataLength` wrap occurs before the maximum-frame check and then passes the unbounded original payload length to the copy hook; it therefore applies to all three dispatched write commands in cooked mode. RAW mode assigns the data length directly and checks it before invoking the hook. No second distinct TX defect established; hook contract and completion semantics remain externally dependent, and the rest of the file remains open. No request or transmission was run. Source-only.

BWFM multicast/tracker state and statistics-query pass (OD3612 confirmed, 2026-10-17): traced duplicate multicast reference counting, overflow-to-allmulti accounting, list serialization, firmware `mcast_list`/`allmulti` iovars and the selected AROSTCP IPv4/IPv6 add/delete callers (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:932-1107,1747-1753`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1742-1778`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/netinet/in.c:686-750`; `netinet6/in6.c:669-750`). OD3612 is confirmed: the state is accepted and iovar failures are ignored, while the stack relies on `io_Error`. Tracker allocation and refcount operations are serialized; per-type snapshots are copied under the same lock. Global stats are copied without the lock while RX/TX update under it, but this pass found no stronger API-level consequence than a potentially inconsistent telemetry snapshot and did not promote a separate finding. No multicast command, firmware error or stats query was issued. Source-only.
Serial `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` error-unwind and caller expansion (OD58 expanded, 2026-10-17): followed `beginio`'s lock/interrupt scope through all three input-buffer allocation, baud validation and HIDD framing failure branches (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:328-331,713-824,875-879`). Confirmed the PC, Sam440 and OpenSBI HIDDs reject unsupported baud, data length or stop bits; `serialtest` and the selected Port handler expose non-quick `DoIO` callers. Expanded OD58 rather than keeping the duplicate OD3660. No request, UART or allocation failure was exercised; source-only.
Serial CMD_RESET active-write detailed finding restoration (OD2388, 2026-10-17): rechecked `CMD_RESET` against the entire write-empty handler and callback registrations. Reset replies the active request but preserves `su_ActiveWrite`, `su_NextToWrite` and `su_WriteLength`; the callback does not gate on the cleared pending bit and can continue transmitting from the returned buffer and reply again. PC THRI and m68k TBE registrations prove selected callback routes; no maintained in-tree CMD_RESET caller was found. Restored OD2388 to the detailed report and index. No request or interrupt was run; source-only.
Serial queued-break command dispatch pass (OD3661 added, 2026-10-17): traced `SDCMD_BREAK` with `SERF_QUEUEDBRK` from BeginIO into `su_QWriteCommandPort` and the sole write-empty consumer (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:823-844`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:137-184`). The consumer interprets the dequeued IOExtSer fields as a normal write, never invokes `HIDD_SerialUnit_SendBreak`, and may copy from `io_Data`; the immediate branch does invoke SendBreak. No maintained in-tree `SDCMD_BREAK` caller was found. Added OD3661 with direct-client trigger; no request or serial output was run. Source-only.
Serial active-write AbortIO ownership pass (OD3662 added, 2026-10-17): traced active versus queued writes from BeginIO and the write-empty callback into `abortio` (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:449-525,884-910`; `serial_interrupthandlers.c:149-184`). The active request is not linked on the queue, but AbortIO's non-active-read branch unconditionally calls `Remove`; it then replies without clearing `su_ActiveWrite` or its offset/remaining state. Exec Remove's linked-node precondition and the callback's later dereference/reply establish distinct immediate list-corruption and deferred stale-request consequences. No maintained active-write AbortIO caller was found; no request or interrupt was run. Source-only.
Serial CMD_START restart ordering restoration (OD1737, 2026-10-17): rechecked the selected PC, Sam440 and OpenSBI `Start` and `Write` methods against serial.device's active-write callback. Each restart invokes the callback before clearing the HIDD stopped flag; each `Write` therefore returns zero, with no retry after the flag is cleared. Kept the possible indefinite wait conditional on later hardware transmit-empty interrupt behavior, and recorded the m68k ordering difference. Restored the detailed report and index entry from the coverage-only candidate. No UART sequence was run; source-only.

Deneb caller-buffer alignment pass (OD3663 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): searched all `ULONG *` casts and `CopyMemShuffle` call sites in `uhwcmd.c`, then checked the public USBHardware alignment contract and Poseidon's pointer assignment (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:127-132`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4705-4723`). Confirmed the same longword assumption in control, bulk, interrupt and isochronous caller-buffer copies, including `iouh_Actual` continuation offsets (`uhwcmd.c:2582-2587,2623-2640,2688-2693,2909-2921,2973-2978,3243-3260,3293-3298,4130-4135,4408,4718-4723`). Odd addresses fault on 68000/010; the m68k-amiga CPU option and architecture linker comment establish the affected build class (`configure.in:2874-2900`; `boot/mmakefile.src:235`). Expanded OD3663 beyond its initial interrupt-IN example. Outgoing RTIso request-hook buffers use a separate hook/buffer-request API contract and were excluded pending review of their own alignment guarantees. No caller, transfer, or hardware was run; source-only.

Deneb request dispatch, query and DMA-tail follow-up (2026-10-17; no new finding): reread `cmdQueryDevice`, all ordinary transfer enqueue handlers, `TermIO`, `FreeATL/FreeInt/FreeIso`, `cmdAbortIO`, `uhwHandleDMAInt`, `uhwLevel6Int`, and `uhwDMATask` (`uhwcmd.c:706-960,1602-1878,4995-5403`). QueryDevice writes only caller-requested outputs selected by `FindTagItem`; the queueing handlers clear QUICK before returning `RC_DONTREPLY`; the selected abort vector owns replies for removed requests, while completed active requests are completed by the PTD helpers. The DMA interrupt only signals the worker when `hu_DMAPTD` is published, and the worker's signal path dispatches the state machine; allocation and teardown races around that state remain under review. No additional deterministic, in-scope defect was established in this pass. No request, interrupt, or hardware was exercised; source-only.

Deneb ordinary ATL control completion follow-up (2026-10-17; no new finding): read `uhwHandleFinishedATLs` setup, optional data, short-packet, continuation, status and endpoint-toggle transitions against the matching control scheduler and selected Poseidon request fields (`uhwcmd.c:1967-2783,3796-3956`; `poseidon.library.c:4705-4750`). The selected control stage updates `iouh_Actual` only for data stages, handles SET_ADDRESS after the status stage, and completes through `FreeATL`; caller-buffer alignment is included in OD3663, and the address-toggle clear boundary is OD3649. No additional deterministic error path was established. This closes the ordinary ATL control state-machine question for the examined functions; split-transfer controller semantics and concurrent cancellation remain open. No control request or hardware was exercised; source-only.

Duplicate-finding reconciliation (OD3663 withdrawn, 2026-10-17): the expanded caller-buffer alignment candidate is the same issue already documented as OD3603, which covers the control, bulk, interrupt and isochronous PIO casts, odd `iouh_Actual` offsets, the DMA-to-PIO fallback for unaligned bulk buffers, and the 68000/010 fault condition (`AROS-other-drivers.md:2283`). Removed OD3663 from the detailed report and index. The intervening OD3663 coverage entries are historical notes superseded by this correction; no additional finding is credited. This follows a fresh search of all `ULONG *` casts and `CopyMemShuffle` uses; RTIso request-hook buffers remain outside OD3603 pending their separate API alignment contract.
RTIso alignment contract follow-up to OD3603 (2026-10-17): checked `IOUsbHWBufferReq` and its hook call sites. The public structure provides `UBYTE *ubr_Buffer` plus byte length and has no alignment requirement (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:103-113`); Deneb's RTIso IN/OUT hook paths cast that pointer to `ULONG *` and advance it by hook-supplied byte counts (`uhwcmd.c:1397-1414,3605-3645,3708-3725`). Expanded OD3603's scope addendum and index to include this same unaligned longword fault for direct/external hook buffers; no separate finding. No maintained in-tree Deneb hook producer demonstrated an odd pointer. No hook or transfer was run; source-only.
Sonixcam selected-caller follow-up to OD3603 (2026-10-17): the selected `rom/usb/shellapps/SonixcamTool.c` installs an RTIso IN request hook and sets `ubr_Buffer` to `nch_CurrIsoBuf + nch_IsoBufPos`; its done hook advances `nch_IsoBufPos` by each returned byte count (`:118-126,136-183,831-840`). Therefore an odd-sized received packet can make the next buffer pointer odd. Deneb's RTIso IN copy casts the hook pointer to `ULONG *` once any remaining full words exist (`uhwcmd.c:3605-3645`). Added this concrete selected producer to the OD3603 scope addendum; manifestation remains conditional on camera packet lengths and later data. No camera, hook, or transfer was run; source-only.
Sonixcam target-selection correction (OD3603, 2026-10-17): `SonixcamTool` is listed in `kernel-usb-shellapps`, but that target is not reached by the default kickstart package graph because the parent `kernel-usb` and `kernel-usb-amiga-m68k` dependency declarations are commented out (`rom/usb/shellapps/mmakefile.src:4-9`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:5-12`). Reworded the report/index to scope the selected in-tree caller to explicitly building the optional shell-app target; this does not change the public USBHardware contract finding or its external-client trigger. No package was built.

Deneb RTIso hook continuation and selected caller pass (2026-10-17; OD3603 retained, no new finding): followed RTIso IN/OUT callbacks through `ubr_Length`, automatic buffer advance, `UBFF_CONTBUFFER`, and the selected Sonixcam/audio hooks (`uhwcmd.c:1388-1421,3581-3735`; `SonixcamTool.c:118-183`; `usbaudio.class.c:2640-2720`). Sonixcam bounds each incoming packet against its fixed raw-buffer extent and stops continuation on overflow by setting the length to zero; the next pointer still advances only by accepted byte counts, preserving the odd-offset trigger already captured under OD3603. The selected USB Audio hooks do not request scatter/gather continuation; their frame-size/count logic and switching remain under the separate audio-class review. No hook sequence or transfer was run; source-only.

PCI HIDD setup/removal candidate recheck (OD3636/OD3637 retained, 2026-10-17): reread the full `pciclass.c` setup, device publication, IRQ assignment, `FindBridge`, enumeration, removal, legacy wrappers, and singleton New/Dispose bodies against the generic HW driver locks/contracts and PCI device Owner/Obtain methods (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:61-170,216-340,395-691`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:174-205,228-300`; `pcideviceclass.c:488-510,1208-1216`). `InsertDevice` takes `dev_lock` only around list insertion, while the later IRQ-routing and failure-diagnostic traversals and `FindBridge` remain unlocked; removal unlinks/disposes under `dev_lock`, confirming OD3636. The Owner getter still bypasses `ownerLock`, and Obtain publishes under that separate lock, confirming OD3637's check/use window. Generic HW driver registration/removal uses a separate driver-list semaphore, so it does not serialize these PCI list operations. No default selected runtime removal caller or new independent issue was established; both retained findings remain conditional on public concurrent add/remove or remove/obtain calls. No operation or interleaving was run; source-only.
BWFM SANA-II link-state caller pass (OD3660 added, 2026-10-17): compared the `joined` writer in control-worker `do_associate` after successful `BWFMJoin` (`bwfm_dev.c:1502-1530`) with the `S2_GETSIGNALQUALITY` dispatch read and its immediate BAD_STATE branch (`:1755-1774`). The writer takes `unit->lock`; the reader does not. Confirmed the command is included in `supported_commands` (`:88-100`) and Raspberry Pi `target_variant=smp` enables ExecSMP in `configure.in:2194-2199`. No selected in-tree signal-quality caller was found. Corrected the initial note: the RX pump writes `joined=0` via `link_down`, while successful join publication is in the control worker. Source-only.
BWFM OD3613 RX-delivery race follow-up (2026-10-17): re-read the RX pump's `online` gate and its call into `rx_deliver` (`bwfm_dev.c:529-530`) against `S2_OFFLINE`'s locked read flush (`:1666-1671,1593-1610`) and `rx_deliver`'s later list lock (`:308-331`). A frame can pass the gate before offline, then the pump can resume after the flush and a late-enqueued CMD_READ; `rx_deliver` has no second online check and can complete that request after offline. Expanded existing OD3613 and its index consequence rather than adding a duplicate. No frame or request was used; source-only.
BWFM TX length and buffer-bound recheck (OD3592/OD3601 retained, 2026-10-17): verified the SANA-II cooked path computes `14 + ios2_DataLength` in 32-bit arithmetic before checking the 1,518-byte stack buffer, then calls the opener copy hook with the unbounded original payload length (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:652-692`). RAW requests assign the length directly and are checked before the hook. Traced the sole in-tree caller of exported `BWFMTxData`: after the device check, it passes at most 1,518 bytes, but the public resource vector independently computes `16 + ethlen`, rounds the wrapped result, and later copies the original `ethlen` into a 2,048-byte static frame (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2112-2133,2193-2196`). Thus OD3601 is a separate public-vector boundary; the checked in-tree caller is bounded, while an oversized direct vector caller is not. No request, callback, or resource vector was invoked. Remaining caller/API contract and lifecycle review stays open; source-only.

BWFM firmware filename, file-read, and auto-join preferences pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced board-compatible extraction and bounded filename construction (`bwfm_dev.c:129-207,727-773`), exact-size file allocation/read/close handling (`:209-239`), and the two-line SSID/passphrase parser into the bounded `BWFMJoin` arguments (`:835-909`; `bwfm_init.c:2353-2374,2433-2455`). The filename buffer covers the maximum accepted board name and fixed suffix; overlong board names fall back to the generic NVRAM filename. Read failures close the file and discard partial buffers. The preferences parser caps copies to its local arrays and the converter caller terminates the SSID explicitly. `fw_board_name` does not call `OF_CloseKey`, but the selected `rom/openfirmware/of_init.c:105-112` implementation is a no-op, so this is not a resource leak in this tree. Preference truncation of overlong values may make invalid credentials fail to join, but the supported format/semantics for such overlong values are not established, so it is not promoted. No firmware, filesystem, or association was exercised. Device startup recovery and firmware command semantics remain open; source-only.

BWFM SANA-II event, query, and read-flush helper pass (2026-10-17; existing candidates retained, no new finding): reread the full event matcher and detached-reply list (`bwfm_dev.c:1362-1407`), GETCRYPTTYPES pool allocation (`:1333-1354`), GETNETWORKINFO pool/tag/BSSID/optional-SSID flow (`:1541-1590`), and read flush lock/ReplyMsg sequence (`:1593-1609`). Event request detachment still has the AbortIO ownership gap OD3623; state snapshot/latch ordering is OD3614. Query allocations check their required pool/allocation results, while GETNETWORKINFO deliberately makes SSID optional if its additional pool allocation fails and retains the BSSID result; selected SANA-II consumer use and whether that partial result violates the public tag contract need separate caller/spec confirmation. Flush replies queued reads while holding the same unit lock used by pump delivery; the separate enqueue-after-offline-flush window is OD3613. No request, pool failure, or event was exercised. Remaining request dispatch and selected caller contracts remain open; source-only.
Sam440 EMAC TX length-width recheck (OD3180 expanded, 2026-10-17): re-read `CmdWrite` through TX worker buffer construction, copy-hook call, descriptor publication and the selected AROSTCP hook (`workbench/devs/networks/emac/handler.c:222-263`; `emac_unit.c:548-552,570-668`; `emac.h:103-130`; `mal.c:105-149`; AROSTCP `sana2copybuff.c:190-212`). Confirmed `ios2_DataLength` is ULONG while both TX locals are UWORD. The worker passes only the narrowed count to the callback, so lengths above 65,535 can report success after sending the low-16-bit prefix; when the narrowed count exceeds the 1,554-byte cooked or 1,568-byte raw slot stride, the callback copy crosses the neighboring slot. `CmdWrite` has no max-length guard, but the selected AROSTCP raw-output path rejects lengths beyond its if_mtu and if_sana caps that at the device MTU; direct SANA-II clients remain the trigger. Expanded existing OD3180 rather than adding a duplicate: its earlier “every request above slot stride” phrasing did not account for the UWORD truncation. No request, hook or hardware was used. Source-only.

Sam440 EMAC over-MTU transmit consequence check (OD3180 expanded, 2026-10-17): compared the worker's cooked packet assembly (`emac_unit.c:592-635`) with `ETH_MTU=1500`, `ETH_MAXPACKETSIZE=1518`, the 1,544-byte per-slot object, and 1,568-byte slot stride (`emac.h:103-130`; `mal.c:105-149`). Because `CmdWrite` has no length guard, cooked requests of 1,501 bytes or more are still copied and queued when their hook accepts them, even before the copy reaches the slot boundary; the transmitted frame therefore exceeds the device's advertised payload MTU. Kept this within OD3180's missing full-width/bounds validation rather than creating a second no-validation finding. The checked-in AROSTCP writer remains capped; no direct-client request or transmission was run. Source-only.
Sam440 EMAC autonegotiated gigabit mode trace (OD3664 added, 2026-10-17): compared the PHY advertisement/1000BASE-T control writes (`workbench/devs/networks/emac/emac_hw.c:243-263`; `emac.h:288-298`) with `EMAC_miiphy_speed`/`duplex`'s BMCR and 10/100 ANLPAR-only reads (`emac_hw.c:173-224`) and `EMAC_Start`'s bridge/MAC speed configuration (`emac_unit.c:100-142`). The resolver can only return 10 or 100 even though the PPC460EX-B branch has explicit 1000-Mbit configuration; it never reads PHY_1000BTSR, making the gigabit branch unreachable. Added OD3664 conditional on PHY and partner negotiating 1000BASE-T. No hardware/link was used; PHY wiring and actual gigabit negotiation remain unverified. Source-only.

PCI HIDD enumeration contract follow-up (2026-10-17): reviewed `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-449`) against the documented tag sequence (`rom/hidds/pci/include/pci_hidd.h:38-46`), PCI API documentation (`rom/hidds/pci/doc/pci.en:50-90`), and the checked-in callers found by repository-wide search. The unsigned tag-index subtraction safely rejects tags below `TAG_USER`; all nine documented contiguous attributes map to the corresponding table slots. Enumeration deliberately holds `dev_lock` shared while callbacks run, preserving device object lifetime against exclusive removal; a callback that synchronously adds a bus driver would wait on the same semaphore, but no selected in-tree EnumDevices callback was found to register/remove a bus driver, so this conditional reentrancy concern is not promoted as a finding. Existing removal and ownership findings OD3563/OD3637 remain the concrete lifecycle issues. Source-only; no callback was executed.

Mediator/Prometheus PCI BAR exhaustion follow-up (OD3670 added, 2026-10-17): compared both `PCIInitialize` loops (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/pci-mediator/driverclass.c:184-231`; `pci-prometheus/driverclass.c:85-132`) with their duplicated `AllocPCIResource` free-list mutation (`pci_resource.c:54-99` in both directories). A successful BAR consumes/splits/trims the list immediately; if a later BAR allocation fails, the loop sets the command value to zero and breaks but does not restore the earlier allocation, then continues scanning later functions. Thus a disabled function can retain resource space during the remaining scan and cause later allocations to fail under constrained bridge windows. Added conditional OD3670. Mediator disposes the lists after its scan; Prometheus retains them with its instance, but neither behavior releases the earlier range before subsequent functions in the same scan. No board, BAR sizing cycle or exhaustion condition was exercised; source-only.

PCIUSB IRQ failure cleanup follow-up (OD3669 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced registration failure beyond the UHCI/EHCI/OHCI startup call sites to `pciFreeUnit` and the public unit-close path (`pciusb_arospci.c:753-768`; `uhwcmd.c:342-355`). The HCD startup names `hc_PCIIntHandler` before discarding the `PCIXAddInterrupt` result (`uhci_hcd.c:1142-1152`; `ehci_hcd.c:1635-1646`; `ohci_hcd.c:1848-1860`), while cleanup tests only that name, then calls `HIDD_PCIDevice_RemoveInterrupt`. On Sam440's inherited generic PCI method, failed `KrnAddIRQHandler` leaves the token NULL; generic removal forwards it to `KrnRemIRQHandler`, which dereferences the handle before its null check (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-55`). Since failed handler registration does not make HCD init fail, `pciAllocUnit` can succeed and a later close reaches this conditional fault. Expanded OD3669 to record both absent interrupt service and NULL-token teardown. No failure or close sequence was induced; source-only.
PCI device-class bridge-window pass (OD3667 added, 2026-10-17): traced type-1 prefetchable-window attribute accessors (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:919-924,1299-1305`) against the defined low and upper register offsets (`rom/hidds/pci/include/hardware/pci.h:158-161`) and PCITool's selected range display (`rom/hidds/pci/pcitool/main.c:477-481`). The getter shifts the complete low register, including the non-address low nibble, and never reads upper dwords; the setter writes only the low register. Added OD3667 for incorrect range metadata and incomplete 64-bit programming. No setter caller was established in the checked-in tree; selected PCITool confirms the read path. No bridge was used; source-only.
PCI device-class Expansion ROM address/caller pass (OD3668 added, 2026-10-17): traced `RomBase` initialization/get (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:697-700,772-774`) against the type-0 BAR's decode-enable bit and the selected Nouveau `pci_enable_rom`/`pci_map_rom` path (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_pci.c:36-43,383-403`; BIOS caller `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/bios/shadowpci.c:61-79`). PCIUSB generic interrupt-registration caller pass (OD3669 added, 2026-10-17): traced `PCIXAddInterrupt` (`rom/usb/pciusb/pciusb_arospci.c:804-808`) through the inherited generic `PCIDrv__Hidd_PCIDriver__AddInterrupt` return (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:279-287`) to `KrnAddIRQHandler` returning NULL for an IRQ outside `HW_IRQ_COUNT` or failed node allocation (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:75-96`). The PCIUSB UHCI, EHCI and OHCI startup call sites discard the Boolean and enable controller interrupt sources immediately afterward (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_hcd.c:1144-1152`; `ehci/ehci_hcd.c:1637-1646`; `ohci/ohci_hcd.c:1850-1860`). Added OD3669 for the conditional missing-interrupt-service path. No handler allocation failure, controller or request was induced; source-only.
Generic PCI mapping inheritance check (2026-10-17): compared `PCIDrv__Hidd_PCIDriver__MapPCI` and address conversion (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:128-178`) with all checked-in PCI HIDD class manifests. PCIPC, Linux PCILinux, Efika, BCM2711, BCM2712 and OpenSBI PCIDT provide mapping overrides; the Sam440 AMCC440 backend inherits DirectBus identity mapping. Its selected kernel explicitly maps the `0x80000000-0xa0000000` PCI memory window identity-to-identity with cache-inhibit attributes (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/mmu.c:318-319`; bridge window constants in `include/asm/amcc440.h:717-720`), consistent with the generic DirectBus assumption. Mediator/Prometheus also inherit DirectBus behavior, but their selected device mapping callers and bridge address translation remain open; this check does not close their mapping audit. No device mapping was performed; source-only.
M68k PCI bridge DirectBus caller follow-up (2026-10-17): inspected Mediator and Prometheus class manifests and PCI resource initialization (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/pci-mediator/driverclass.c:82-95,170-220`; `pci-prometheus/driverclass.c:61-120,150-203`). PCI HIDD enumeration contract follow-up (2026-10-17): reviewed `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-449`) against the documented tag sequence (`rom/hidds/pci/include/pci_hidd.h:38-46`), PCI API documentation (`rom/hidds/pci/doc/pci.en:50-90`), and the checked-in callers found by repository-wide search. The unsigned tag-index subtraction safely rejects tags below `TAG_USER`; all nine documented contiguous attributes map to the corresponding table slots. Enumeration deliberately holds `dev_lock` shared while callbacks run, preserving device object lifetime against exclusive removal; a callback that synchronously adds a bus driver would wait on the same semaphore, but no selected in-tree EnumDevices callback was found to register/remove a bus driver, so this conditional reentrancy concern is not promoted as a finding.
