PCI xHCI IRQ failure caller pass (OD3669 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced the xHCI-specific IRQ paths (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:4067-4120`) and close cleanup (`pcixhci_arospci.c:420-432`, `uhwcmd.c:342-366`). Both generic `PCIXAddInterrupt` and MSI `AddIntServer` results are ignored; the handler node is named before registration, while `pciFreeUnit` later treats the name as proof of success and removes it. OpenSBI's selected boot package loads `USBHardware/pcixhci` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:104`) and its PCIDT backend overrides AddInterrupt to unmask INTx then forward to the generic method (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:967-977`). On failure, the stored IRQ token remains NULL and removal reaches the kernel's pre-guard dereference. HCD init proceeds to success if controller start otherwise succeeds, so unit close can reach this fault. Expanded OD3669 to cover PCIUSB on Sam440 and PCI xHCI on OpenSBI PCIDT. No failure or close was induced; source-only.
Network worker signal-allocation follow-up (OD3671, 2026-10-18): traced Rhine, Prism2 and Atheros5000 `UnitTask` setup through `AllocSignal(-1)` and the directly shifted masks (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:1731-1742`; `prism2/unit.c:3831-3843`; `atheros5000/unit.c:2827-2838`). Each unit task is launched by `CreateUnit` without a startup handshake, and each `DevBeginIO` queues requests on its general port when `AttemptSemaphore` fails (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:315-341`, `device.c:409`; `prism2/unit.c:313-339`, `device.c:431`; `atheros5000/unit.c:402-428`, `device.c:419`). Thus allocation failure can leave an accepted unit with malformed wait masks; exact effect depends on target shift behavior and subsequent event/request activity. Added OD3671, as an extension to OD3106's same defect pattern. Confirmed these target variants through `workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src`; Prism2 and Rhine are in the active cards aggregate, while Atheros5000 is selected by the GNU-toolchain branch; Atheros5000 uses its separate GNU dependency. No device, signal exhaustion, or request was run. The broader AllocSignal caller inventory is still open.
VIA-Rhine scheduler shutdown follow-up (OD3672, 2026-10-18): compared `AllocSignal`'s returned bit number (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:70-143`) with `Wait`'s one-hot mask result (`rom/exec/wait.c:75-80`) and traced scheduler setup, shutdown test, and `DeleteUnit` cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/unit.c:719-733,938-966`). The worker waits on shifted bits but tests the returned mask against raw `signal_0`; deletion also passes that number directly to `Signal`, then frees its request ports, private state, MMIO mapping, and unit without joining the task. Added OD3672. All signal allocations are also unchecked. A wider review of this driver and of the remaining network callers is still open. No device or teardown was run; source-only.
LPe32002 worker signal-allocation follow-up (OD3673, 2026-10-18): reread the scheduler after its startup handshake through its wait loop (`workbench/devs/networks/lpe32002/unit.c:526-555`) and `DeleteUnit` signal path (`:827-831`) against Exec's `AllocSignal` failure return (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:24-68`). All four allocations are unchecked and shifted into the wait set; failure of signal 0 also breaks the shutdown signal dependency. Added OD3673, distinct from OD3153's handshake race and missing join. The broader LPe32002 file/caller audit remains open. No worker or allocation failure was induced; source-only.
Network AllocSignal caller inventory (2026-10-18): repository search finds 20 C/header source files under `workbench/devs/networks` with direct `AllocSignal` calls. Reviewed the failure handling and mask construction in BCM GENET (`bcmgenet_unit.c:1020-1055`), BWFM RX/control workers (`bwfm_dev.c:468-476,596-609`), RTL8029 (`rtl8029/driver.c:1753-1768`), PPP (`ppp/init.c:82-84,112-116,259-275`), and RTL8139 (`rtl8139/unit.c:806-824,852-856,1163`) and found no additional unchecked-failure mask defect in those paths: BCM GENET only enables the optional IRQ bit after success, BWFM falls back to timer/polling, RTL8029 checks allocation, PPP exits on failure, and RTL8139 validates all four allocations before acknowledging setup. Existing findings cover nForce (OD3083), PCNet32 (signal-exhaustion trigger rechecked; no reachable exhaustion established), SiS900 (OD3089), e1000 (OD2436), RTL816x/Broadcom4400 signal-exhaustion candidates rechecked and withdrawn, Intel Pro/100/Etherlink III/Realtek8180 (OD3106), and the newly reviewed Rhine/Prism2/Atheros5000 (OD3671), VIA-Rhine (OD3672), LPe32002 and nvidianet (signal-exhaustion triggers rechecked; no reachable exhaustion established). This reconciles the `AllocSignal` issue family for network-driver source files only; the project-wide direct-call inventory spans 184 C/header files and remains open. No task, signal exhaustion, packet, or request was induced. Source-only.
Virtual Bluetooth HCI signal-allocation candidate withdrawal and HID target pass (2026-10-18): traced `AllocSignal(-1)` in `vbthci_UnitTask` through the selected `CreateNewProcTags`/`CreateNewProc` allocation path (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_device.c:48-56`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:231-235,401-405,546-550`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:248-251`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The new process is zero-cleared and receives the default `TaskSigAlloc` mask (`0xFFFF`), leaving the upper 16 signal bits available; this worker allocates its unit-port bit before any other signal allocations. Signal exhaustion is therefore not established on this selected startup path. Withdrew OD3675 from the report and index. Also read all 103 lines of `vbthci_hid.c` and traced every report descriptor/input-report caller in `vbthci_peer.c:138-158,407-419,451-470,1158-1190`: report capacities match the 3-byte mouse and 8-byte keyboard reports; the keyboard CoD/LE appearance selectors agree with the fake-device records, and no independent defect was established. No task, device, or report was run; source-only.
Virtual Bluetooth pending-read queue ExecSMP cross-CPU pass (OD3724 strengthened, 2026-10-18): traced `BTCMD_READACL` enqueue/delivery and shutdown flush against device `AbortIO` (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:473-504`; `vbthci_peer.c:64-82`; `vbthci_device.c:165-198`). Confirmed the AbortIO walk/removal of the unit message port bypasses its `mp_SpinLock`, which `GetMsg` and `PutMsg` take (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:64-72`; `putmsg.c:80-91`); the pending-read list is protected only with `Forbid()`, which Exec documents as local-processor-only on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). Retained OD3724 for an overlapping public AbortIO; no in-tree caller was found. No request or interleaving was run; source-only.
Virtual Bluetooth event-message shutdown ownership cross-check (2026-10-18; no additional OD): traced the selected Bluetooth hardware task's synchronous event-port registration/removal and teardown (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2856-2864,3044-3057,3068-3077`). It removes the event port before issuing `CMD_FLUSH`, continues collecting device replies, drains and replies queued event messages, and only then closes the root device request. `vbthci_CloseUnit` signals and waits for the unit task before freeing its state (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_device.c:82-99`); the unit task also stops its timer and returns outstanding event messages before deleting its reply port (`vbthci_unit.c:617-647`). This selected caller order does not establish an event-message/reply-port lifetime defect. Other external event-port clients and timeout behavior remain outside this trace. No task or event was run; source-only.
USB MassStorage worker signal candidate correction (OD3676 withdrawn; OD3893 added, 2026-10-18): re-read `nAllocMS()` failure control flow and Exec signal/message-port implementations (`massstorage.class.c:1737-1740,1832-1855`; `rom/exec/createmsgport.c:49-64`; `freesignal.c:55-64`; `allocsignal.c:105-112`). If the embedded-port `AllocSignal(-1)` fails, the UBYTE signal field receives 255; the immediately following `CreateMsgPort()` in the same task also cannot allocate a signal, so `nAllocMS()` returns NULL and `nMSTask()` never publishes a ready worker. This contradicts the old claim that the LUN can become ready with an invalid command-worker signal; withdrew OD3676 and removed it from both report indexes. The failure unwind nevertheless unconditionally calls `FreeSignal(255)`, which reaches an unchecked `1L << 255`; added OD3893 for that invalid cleanup argument, with target/compiler-dependent consequences. No signal exhaustion or USB device was induced. Source-only.
Poseidon USB HID GUI signal caller pass (OD3677, 2026-10-18): traced `nGUITask`'s tracking-signal allocation through the MUI NewInput wait and cleanup, then traced the HID event worker's matching `Signal` producer (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:1596-1607,1711-1715`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:988-995`). Neither path checks for `AllocSignal` failure; the feature-dependent producer and consumer both shift the failed value. Added OD3677 for the optional USB HID class target. This is separate from Bluetooth HID's settings GUI finding OD3498. No signal exhaustion, device, or GUI was exercised; source-only.
BWFM SANA-II `handle_request` command-dispatch pass (OD3678 added; 2026-10-18): read the complete request switch from S2_DEVICEQUERY through CMD_FLUSH (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1610-1930`) against its helpers and selected WirelessManager calls. Reconfirmed OD3646's S2_DEVICEQUERY capacity metadata overwrite, OD3660's unlocked joined read, and existing event/read/TX ownership findings. The NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY branch checks only for NULL `io_Data`, then writes all NSDeviceQueryResult fields and full `io_Actual` without checking `io_Length` (`:1829-1854`); the selected caller provides a full result object (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:928-929,978-982`). Added OD3678 as a BWFM instance of OD3074's short-buffer pattern, with only a direct short-buffer caller as the trigger. Other BWFM scan/association and lifecycle review remains open. No request was issued; source-only.
BWFM escan record/IE bounds and selected-consumer pass (OD3598/OD3599 rechecked; no additional candidate, 2026-10-18): traced `bwfm_event_pop`'s 2,048-byte cap and the escan parser's event, result-header, BSS-count, record-length and IE subranges (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1394-1410,1800-2032`) into `get_networks` and WirelessManager's result/tag consumption (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1248-1332`; `workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:708-766`). Per-record `bilen <= remain` bounds BSS traversal. OD3598 remains: `ieoff + ielen` can wrap as 32-bit `ULONG` before validation, and the subsequent capped copy may exceed the validated record. The invalid-IE diagnostic's `ies[0:2]` read is inside `D(...)`; this resource defines `DEBUG 0`, so the debug macro removes its arguments in this target. The missing-timer fallback busy delay was not promoted: it does not yield, but the RX pump runs at priority 5 and selected callers do not establish a same-or-higher-priority scan caller that can starve it. OD3599's shared event queue/static result set remains the separate concurrent-scan ownership issue. Changed OD3598 wording to identify malformed firmware input without implying adversarial activity. No firmware event, scan, or caller was run; source-only.
BWFM scan fallback qualification correction (2026-10-18): the prior note's phrase “selected callers do not establish a same-or-higher-priority scan caller” was stronger than the inspected evidence. The direct selected scan call is traced, but its task priority was not followed through process creation. Retain only the narrower conclusion: fallback busy-wait does not itself prove starvation because the scheduler may preempt it; no separate timer-failure finding is promoted until the caller priority and selected scheduler path are traced.
Network `DeleteUnit`/`RemTask` allocation-failure cross-check (2026-10-18; no new finding): re-read the eight maintained network unit constructors and cleanup paths for Intel Pro/100, Rhine, Realtek8180, Prism2, nvidianet, Broadcom4400, Etherlink3 and Atheros5000. Each stores the separately allocated worker stack in `tc_SPLower` before calling its `AddUnitTask`/`NewAddTask` wrapper, then sets `UNITF_TASKADDED` only on successful publication; constructor failure funnels through `DeleteUnit`. Intel Pro/100 and Rhine unconditionally pass `tc_SPLower` to `FreeMem` when the task record exists, while the others guard some or all stack cleanup with the task-added flag or non-NULL stack check. This difference is not a defect for stack-allocation failure: Exec `FreeMem` explicitly returns for a NULL block (`rom/exec/freemem.c:69-72`), and the task records are allocated cleared. A task-add failure occurs after stack bounds are installed, so the stack is available for cleanup. Existing driver-specific `NewAddTask` failure candidates remain the relevant findings; no additional `RemTask` or stack-cleanup bug established. No allocation failure or task was induced; source-only.
input.device reset-handler signal-allocation caller trace (OD3679 added, 2026-10-18): traced `ProcessEvents`' unchecked `1L << AllocSignal(-1)` into `ResetHandler`, the task `Wait`/completion branch, and the selected keyboard.device reset-handler registration/dispatch/completion protocol (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:67-75,198,264-266,578-598`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:326-336,497-517`). The reset handler signals the input task only when the stored mask is nonzero, and keyboard.device does not decrement its active reset-handler count until `KBD_RESETHANDLERDONE`; therefore signal exhaustion can leave the registered input handler unable to complete its reset phase. Added OD3679, conditional on failure yielding an unusable mask and a later keyboard reset sequence. The input.device module is selected by `rom/devs/input/mmakefile.src:10`; no signal exhaustion or reset was run. Source-only.
SCSI bus sleep-signal inventory correction (2026-10-18; no finding): a fresh repository-wide identifier search shows `sb_SleepySignal` appears only in its field declaration and the assignment/fallback in `BusTaskCode` (`rom/devs/scsi/scsi.h:158`; `scsi.c:990-993`). The earlier 2026-10-16 note incorrectly described lowlevel sleep/wakeup paths as uses of this SCSI field; ATA has separate helpers, while SCSI does not read the assigned value in any wait or signal operation. The allocated bit is therefore reserved for the bus task until its lifetime ends, but no task-local signal exhaustion consequence or user-visible behavior was established. No SCSI task or bus was run; source-only.
ATA trackdisk command-handler continuation (2026-10-18; no new finding): read `cmd_Remove`, `cmd_ChangeNum`, `cmd_ChangeState`, `cmd_ProtStatus`, `cmd_GetNumTracks`, Add/RemoveChangeInt, `cmd_Eject` and both `cmd_GetGeometry` buffer variants (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:354-482`) against the command map, unit fields and available SFS/AFS/PFS3/HDToolBox callers. Media presence and write-protection state are direct projections of `au_Flags`/`au_DevType`; eject calls the unit backend then refreshes media-change state. The Add/RemoveChangeInt list operations share the already-covered ExecSMP local-Forbid issue OD3002; no separate handler defect emerged. The 514-byte identify-data branch has no checked-in caller, while the DriveGeometry branch callers provide the expected fixed structure. Remaining ATA command handlers, transfer completion/error ordering, caller contracts outside the selected paths, and platform hardware behavior remain open. No request or device was used; source-only.
ATA read/write dispatch and low-level chunking continuation (2026-10-18; no new finding): traced `CMD_READ`/`CMD_WRITE` and their 64-bit variants through `cmd_Read32/64` and `cmd_Write32/64` into the selected `au_Read32/64` and `au_Write32/64` vectors and `ata_exec_blk` (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:54-290`; `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1171-1250,1938-2088`). Byte offset/length alignment is checked before conversion to sectors; 64-bit requests reject zero length, while zero-length 32-bit requests reach the low-level chunk loop with count zero and issue no ATA command, returning zero actual bytes. Positive requests are split into command-sized chunks, and actual byte counts are set by the low-level vector only after success; the device command handler propagates its error and returned actual count. Reconfirmed OD2999's 28-bit/48-bit selector boundary; no separate zero-length or completion-order issue established. DMA buffer ownership, hardware responses, and broader caller/completion interleavings remain open. No transfer or device was used; source-only.
PC serial IRQ-server reopen lifecycle recheck (OD2779 expanded, 2026-10-18): traced first unit construction, shared `intHandler` sentinel setup, `RemIntServer`, and serial.device final-close/first-open paths. `PCSerUnit__Root__Dispose` removes the shared server but never clears `irq->is_Node.ln_Name`; a subsequent `PCSerUnit__Root__New` uses that field as its registration guard and therefore cannot reinstall the server or reset callback. `serial.device` opens the HIDD library and creates its HIDD object in module initialization, then releases them only from the device expunge hook (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:77-97,281-291`), so an ordinary unit close leaves the shared sentinel in the still-live HIDD base. The issue is reachable with a single unit's open-close-reopen cycle, in addition to closing the first-created unit while its paired port remains open. Updated OD2779 and the index; no port or IRQ was used. Source-only.
Input reset-signal candidate reconciliation (OD3679 withdrawn, 2026-10-18): repeated the `ProcessEvents` startup trace and compared it with the existing OD45 withdrawal. NewCreateTaskA initializes `tc_SigAlloc` from Exec's `TaskSigAlloc` value `0xFFFF`, leaving 16 task-usable signals; the input task allocates one command-port bit plus four reply-port bits and the reset bit, so ten remain. No other checked-in task-local signal allocation occurs in the input worker before or after this setup. The failure precondition is therefore not established for the selected fresh task; the unchecked shift remains a robustness observation. Removed OD3679 from the detailed report and AROS.md index; its underlying weak candidate was already recorded as withdrawn OD45. No task or reset was run. Source-only.

BWFM EAPOL packet-type promotion and selected CMD_READ caller recheck (2026-10-18; no new driver finding): checked the type widths and full receive-request handoff (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-66`; `bwfm_dev.c:308-367,1857-1885`) against the selected WirelessManager SANA-II client (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:1014-1033,764-781`). `UWORD` is unsigned 16-bit; its value `0x888e` promotes to positive `int` and then zero-extends to `ULONG`, so the comment at `bwfm_dev.c:314-315` claiming it sign-extends to `0xffff888e` is incorrect. The client's EAPOL `CMD_READ` request sets `ios2_PacketType = ETH_P_EAPOL` (`0x888e`), which matches the receive-side cast and can be delivered when queued. The no-reader diagnostic applies only when no opener has a matching pending read; it is not caused by this promotion. No packet was received. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI mode-publication/task-readiness interleaving (OD3680 added, 2026-10-18): traced `nAllocAudio`'s `CreateMsgPort` → `nExamineAudioUnits` → `nAddAudioModes` → `nch_Task` assignment order (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1940-1987,2000-2051`). `AHI_AddAudioMode` copies the mode tags, including the driver-owned `NepAudioMode` pointer, into the globally locked database before releasing the lock and returning (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:358-369,445-458`). `_AHI_AllocAudioA` looks up the published ID and passes its database tags to `AHIsub_AllocAudio` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:457-512`); USB Audio `subLibAllocAudio` retrieves the mode pointer into `ahiac_DriverData` (`usbaudio.class.c:3271-3291`). AHI's control path dispatches hardware-control tags to the sublibrary (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:982-995`); USB Audio updates mode state and signals `nch->nch_Task` without checking it (`usbaudio.class.c:4090-4153`). The record is allocated `MEMF_CLEAR`, so a just-added mode's unit task remains NULL until the post-loop assignment. Exec Signal dereferences the supplied task pointer (`rom/exec/signal.c:170-172,183-196,254-300`). Added OD3680 for a concurrent AHI client selecting a newly published mode and setting a control before worker publication. No device or AHI control was used; source-only.

USB Audio AHI attribute-index contract pass (2026-10-18; no additional OD): traced `AHIDB_Frequency`, `AHIDB_Index`, `AHIDB_Input`, and `AHIDB_Output` through `subLibGetAttr` and the selected `ahi.device` `AHI_GetAudioAttrsA` dispatcher (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3932-3945,4048-4074`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:286-303,364-388,461-503`). The public AHI contract explicitly constrains `AHIDB_FrequencyArg` to `[0, AHIDB_Frequencies-1]` and input/output args to the corresponding advertised count; the normal requester obtains the count and clamps its selected frequency level before querying (`requester.c:388-400`). Thus the direct array lookups do not establish a separate defect for contract-compliant indices. The automatic max-frequency query with zero advertised rates remains OD3172; output-name capacity and selector semantics remain OD3176/OD3457. No tag list or mode query was issued. Source-only.

ATA NewStyle query contract and caller census recheck (OD3003 retained, 2026-10-18): compared `HandleIO`'s `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` branch with `NSDeviceQueryResult`'s size/extension contract and the bounds-checked input, gameport, keyboard, console, ramdrive, and narrator implementations (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:714-728`; `compiler/include/devices/newstyle.h:14-28`; representative checks `rom/devs/input/input.c:126-145`, `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:320-340`, `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:285-306`, `workbench/devs/ramdrive_device.c:265-285`). ATA remains OD3003: it dereferences `io_Data` and writes every result field without verifying a non-NULL buffer or `io_Length >= sizeof(struct NSDeviceQueryResult)`. Repository search of maintained trackdisk probes found their callers set a full local result structure (`workbench/fs/ntfs/disk.c:383-388`; SFS `FS/deviceio.c:407-414`, `SFSdisplay.c:211-219`, `SFSfindobjects.c:207-215`; FAT `rom/filesys/fat/disk.c:121-127`; AFS `rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:528-531`; PFS3 `rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/disk.c:2045-2052` and `pfsdoctor/device.c:609-612`; partition support `rom/partition/partition_support.c:62-68`). No maintained short-buffer caller was found; OD3003's trigger remains a direct caller contract violation or an external client passing an undersized/missing result buffer. `BeginIO` classifies the query as immediate and calls `HandleIO` synchronously before reply (`ata.c:778-783,811-839`), so the writes occur during the caller's request. No request was sent. Source-only.

ATA bus-task timer and DMA-pool startup failure pass (OD3681/OD3682 added, 2026-10-18): traced BusTask resource initialization against `ata_OpenTimer`, `ata_WaitTO`, `ata_setup_unit`/`ata_Identify`, `ata_exec_blk`, and Exec `AllocPooled` (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:1029-1083,1129-1135`; `timer.c:23-59`; `lowlevel.c:480-490,780-788,1188-1215,1274-1339,1640-1668`; `waitto.c:22-30`; `rom/exec/allocpooled.c:76-93`). Added OD3681: failed timer setup leaves NULL `ab_Timer`; device identify reaches `ata_WaitTO` and faults before BusTask releases `DetectionSem`, which can strand coldstart `ata_BootWait`. Added OD3682: failed bounce-pool creation leaves a NULL handle later passed to `AllocPooled` for high-address DMA buffers on 64-bit targets. These are separate from OD2995's task-creation failure, which leaks the semaphore before the bus worker starts. The timer and pool paths were source-traced only; no allocation, timer, scan, or DMA operation was induced. The remaining low-level transfer protocol, hardware completion/error ordering, and platform caller audits remain open. Source-only.


Keyboard event-ring producer/reader wrap pass (OD3683 added, 2026-10-18): traced `keyCallback`'s unconditional ring write and 128-entry wrap against `writeEvents`' per-unit cursor equality/consumption (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:359-366,435-495,608-629`; `keyboard_intern.h:32,40,78`). There is no full marker or overflow policy; after 128 arrivals without that unit consuming, writer and reader indices coincide and the backlog appears empty, with later events overwriting unread slots. Added OD3683, scoped to a stalled direct keyboard.device opener or a lagging opener among multiple units; the selected input.device usually maintains a one-event read, so no ordinary single-reader trigger is claimed. The full keyboard BeginIO, event decoder, callback, and pending-read drain were reread; earlier reset, qualifier, queue-drain, event-count, and local-only list findings remain cross-referenced. Other keyboard HIDD/platform callback timing and wider caller lifecycle audits remain open. No event or device was used; source-only.


Keyboard HIDD producer-context and OD3683 caller-scope follow-up (2026-10-18; no new finding): traced two selected producer implementations into the generic `keyCallback` ring writer. Amiga keyboard invokes the registered callback directly from its CIA interrupt after reading the serial data register (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/keyboard/kbdclass.c:39-83,176-183`); LinuxInput reads host event records in its input task and forwards EV_KEY events through `HIDD_LinuxKbd_HandleEvent` (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxinput/linuxinput_inputtask.c:49-52,89-110`). Both converge on the same callback installed by keyboard.device (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:197-213`). This confirms the event ring receives callbacks in interrupt and task contexts, while OD3683's observable loss still requires an opener cursor to lag the shared writer by a full ring; the selected input.device's one-event read is not evidence of a routine overrun. No backend event was generated. Other platform producers and callback/disposal timing remain open; source-only.


PCI ATA DMA error-status completion trace (OD3684 added, 2026-10-18): traced the PCI interrupt's bus-master status sample/acknowledgement into ATA's DMA completion callback and the PCI `DMA_GetResult` vector (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/ata_pci_busclass.c:43-65`; `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:274-289,717-729`; `rom/hidds/ata_pci/interface_dma.c:153-158`). The interrupt acknowledges by writing the sampled status plus both W1C error/interrupt bits before calling the callback; the callback's DMA result helper then rereads the cleared status, so an otherwise unreported bus-master error can be lost and a completion may carry no error. The AMD SP5100 register reference confirms the bus-master error bit is W1C and represents PCI target/master abort or parity errors (same reference URL in OD3684). Added OD3684 for PCI bus-master ATA only; Gayle does not use this status path. No transfer or hardware was exercised.


Gameport shared timestamp counter follow-up (OD3685 added, 2026-10-18): revisited historical coverage candidate OD1875 against the complete `Open`, VBlank tick, `GPD_READEVENT`, and `fillrequest` paths (`rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:103-117,159-282,390-433,618-771`; `gameport_intern.h:46,75-78`). Each open allocates an independent read cursor, while all readers share one `gp_nTicks`; `fillrequest` stores that counter in the event and resets it. Two units can therefore consume the same buffered event but receive different frame-count timestamps if the second reads before another VBlank. The selected input.device explicitly replaces the frame count with `GetSysTime` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:547-550`), so the finding is restricted to direct clients using returned timestamps. Restored OD3685 as a detailed finding; no event or request was issued.


input.device IND_ADDEVENT qualifier-transition trace (OD3686 added, 2026-10-18): traced the command's initial qualifier assignment and per-event comparison/update against all `ActQualifier` consumers and the selected USB HID keyboard batch producer (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:327-328,373-394,447-454,539-545`; `peekqualifier.c:35-40`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/kbdclass.c:263-273,430-455`). The code comment says to process when an event qualifier differs, but the `==` condition only updates on equality; a Control-up plus Shift-up report creates successive Shift and no-modifier qualifiers in one `IND_ADDEVENT` batch, leaving `ActQualifier` stuck at Shift. The event records retain their own qualifiers, but PeekQualifier, timer events, and subsequent mouse event key bits consume the stale shared state. Added OD3686; no report or request was generated.

Serial callback backend scope follow-up (OD1454, 2026-10-18; no new ID): inspected the Sam440 receive path and confirmed it invokes the generic callback from its software interrupt handler (`arch/ppc-sam440/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:450-462`), while disposal clears the HIDD unit slot before disabling UART interrupts (`:180-195`). The generic serial close ordering could produce the same null lookup if this backend were selected. However, the Sam440 serial HIDD is a standalone module target (`serial.hidd/mmakefile.src`) and is not listed in the active Sam440 boot package graph inspected for this audit, so it is not added to OD1454 affected configurations. Hosted Unix callback-producing AsyncIO registration and abort paths are under `#if 0`; its lack of receive callback remains covered by OD63. OpenSBI remains an affected backend because disposal removes its IRQ handler only after generic UnitList unlink. Source-only; no interrupt or close was run.

IND_ADDEVENT qualifier finding reconciliation (OD3686, 2026-10-18): the two-modifier-release batch confirms stale shared `ActQualifier`; this overlaps the historical OD2313 Alt-handoff/PeekQualifier effect. KMS reads per-event qualifier/code rather than `ActQualifier`, and its chain-tail loss is the separate OD882-derived finding OD3687. Do not merge OD3687 into OD3686. No event batch or handler was run. Source-only.

OD3686/KMS duplicate-scope correction (2026-10-18): a direct re-read of `kms_InputHandler` shows it compares each RAWKEY event's `ie_Qualifier` and `ie_Code` and does not consult input.device `ActQualifier`/`PeekQualifier` (`workbench/libs/kms/kms_library.c:71-103`). Therefore OD2313's stale Alt-handoff qualifier effect overlaps OD3686, but OD882's KMS event-chain loss is distinct from stale ActQualifier and is now detailed as OD3687 after confirming that ForwardQueuedEvents passes the full chain once and kms_InputHandler returns NULL after examining only its head. The prior reconciliation note incorrectly grouped OD882 with the stale-qualifier manifestation; report wording corrected. No handler chain or event was run. Source-only.

OD882/KMS event-chain candidate validation (OD3687 added, 2026-10-18): traced the full queue handoff (`rom/devs/input/support.c:17-27,38-58`; `processevents.c:94-125,327-394`) through the selected KMS handler (`workbench/libs/kms/kms_library.c:71-103`). `ForwardQueuedEvents` passes the linked chain once per handler; KMS inspects only the head and returns NULL on a switch match, dropping all tail events. Corrected the prior coverage claim: the first event's equality branch flushes the previously empty queue, then enqueues that event; later different-qualifier events can remain chained, so a two-event batch suffices. Selected HID keyboard submits batches up to 16 events (`kbdclass.c:249-273,430-455`). Added OD3687 as the distinct KMS consumer defect; OD3686 remains the separate stale shared-qualifier state defect, with historical OD2313 overlapping only the latter. No chain or device was run. Source-only.

OD3687 preference/configuration trigger follow-up (2026-10-18): confirmed the example qualifier-only hotkey is representable in Input preferences: `ipeditor.c` stores `KMS_CODE_NOKEY` when no regular switch key is selected and persists the chosen qualifier (`workbench/prefs/input/ipeditor.c:472-485`; `KMS_CODE_NOKEY` definition `compiler/include/libraries/kms.h:21-22`). `RAWKEY_CONTROL` is 0x63 within KMS's inclusive qualifier-key test range 0x60–0x67 (`compiler/include/devices/rawkeycodes.h:74,88,94`; `kms_library.c:91-94`). Strengthened OD3687's concrete trigger; no preference was saved or event sent. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II interface-name parser and caller pass (OD3688 added, 2026-10-18): traced `wpa_supplicant_init_iface`'s non-NULL/maximum-length checks and direct `wpa_drv_init(wpa_s, wpa_s->ifname)` call (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:1950-1985`) through `wpa_driver_sana2_init` (`src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:936-966`). The caller does not validate the driver's expected colon separator; absent `:`, `strrchr` returns NULL, which is used in pointer subtraction for `strncpy` and then as `atoi(end + 1)`. The SANA-II ops are registered in the selected driver table (`src/drivers/drivers.c:68,133`). Added OD3688; no malformed name or driver was used. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II constructor-allocation failure unwind check (2026-10-18; no new finding): compared `wpa_driver_sana2_init`'s `device_name`, message-port and base-request allocation failures through its shared deinit call (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:932-958,1090-1093; deinit :881-917`) against Exec helper NULL behavior. `CreateIORequest(NULL, ...)` returns NULL (`rom/exec/createiorequest.c:58-72`); `DeleteIORequest`, `DeleteMsgPort`, and `FreeVec` all explicitly guard NULL (`deleteiorequest.c:54-58`; `deletemsgport.c:53-57`; `freevec.c:48-52`). These partial-allocation paths do not establish an additional null-cleanup defect. This does not close request-callback or whole-driver lifetime review. No allocation failure or driver init was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II association-event metadata/caller pass (2026-10-18; no new finding): traced CONNECT from the completed S2_ONEVENT callback through S2_GETNETWORKINFO and EVENT_ASSOC (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:802-831`) into supplicant association-info handling (`wpa_supplicant/events.c:979-1023,1113-1135`). A missing/failed GETNETWORKINFO result yields NULL request IEs and length zero; the consumer loops only while the pointer is non-NULL, skips the request-IE reset when absent, and continues association processing. This alone does not establish a failure. Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 source do not implement S2_GETNETWORKINFO/S2INFO_WPAInfo, while Prism2 and BWFM do; the examined code therefore does not justify treating those missing optional metadata implementations as a general association failure. This closes only the association-metadata question; event ordering, error propagation, request lifetime, and remaining SANA-II callbacks remain open. No device/event was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II scan completion and Prism2 error-path pass (OD3689 added, 2026-10-18): traced the async `S2_GETNETWORKS` reply into scan-result handling (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:872-875,216-252`) and compared it with the selected Prism2 offline branch (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/request.c:1631-1658`). The callback does not inspect `io_Error`; the client leaves `ios2_DataLength` untouched and sets `ios2_StatData` to a two-item input tag list before submission; Prism2 offline completion sets an error but leaves these fields untouched. Following a successful nonempty scan, the stale positive count makes the client cast the current input tag list to a pointer array and dereference a numeric tag ID as a tag-list pointer. Added OD3689. No radio, scan, or request was run. Source-only.

OD3689 selected-device/error-trigger refinement (2026-10-18): checked S2_GETNETWORKS support and result initialization across the selected SANA-II backends. Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 omit S2_GETNETWORKS and are classified by this client as user-space-MLME devices; Prism2 and BWFM advertise it. BWFM initializes `ios2_DataLength` to zero and `ios2_StatData` to NULL before scanning (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1262-1270`), so its shown failure paths do not preserve a stale positive count. Prism2's result builder also leaves the submitted input tag list and prior count in place on pooled-result allocation failure (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/unit.c:2766-2783,2881-2890`), matching the stale-result parse defect. Refined OD3689 to include this second Prism2 trigger; finding remains limited to Prism2. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II association callback error/ownership pass (OD3690/OD3691 added, 2026-10-18): traced `wpa_driver_sana2_associate` through its `CloneTagItems`, synchronous `S2_SETOPTIONS` call, SSID copy and return (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:382-445`) into the supplicant caller's negative-only failure check and timeout selection (`wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:1246-1256,1277-1288`). The callback stores failures but always returns zero, suppressing the caller's failure path. Its temporary allocated SSID buffer is not freed after the clone is synchronously consumed or on error. WirelessManager SANA-II scan-argument and Prism2 key-counter caller pass (2026-10-18; no additional finding): confirmed selected `wpa_supplicant_scan` zero-initializes its params and increments `num_ssids` on the wildcard or directed-scan paths before dispatch (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/scan.c:250,295,314-376`); user-space-MLME scans also build `ssids[0]` before dispatch (`wpa_supplicant/mlme.c:2123-2135`). Thus the SANA-II scan callback's read of `params->ssids[0]` is within a populated inline array for these selected callers. Traced RSN PTK install: it always passes an 8-byte local zero RSC; WPA PTK install passes the EAPOL key's inline RSC, both length six (`src/rsn_supp/wpa.c:494-533`), so the selected Prism2 TKIP/CCMP key paths' counter dereferences are not reached with a NULL counter from this caller. No supplicant, key, or scan was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II association-frequency pass (OD3692 added, 2026-10-18): traced zero-initialized `params.freq` for no-BSS association (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:1193-1205`) and the `ap_scan=2` caller (`wpa_supplicant/scan.c:89-114`) through the unconditional SANA-II channel-tag calculation (`src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:390-398`) into Prism2 `SetOptions` and adhoc `ConfigureAdapter` (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/unit.c:929-962,673-679`; `device.h:260`). WirelessManager SANA-II hardware-mode/rate data caller pass (OD3632 rechecked; 2026-10-18): verified successful allocation sizes against every initialized entry (`driver_sana2.c:548-624`): B mode has 14 entries including channel 14 at 2484 MHz and four 802.11b rates; G mode has 13 entries for channels 1–13 and twelve rates. WirelessManager SANA-II soft-MAC keepalive/disassociation lifetime pass (OD3693 added, 2026-10-18): traced `set_associd` through the recurring stay-alive callback, selected Atheros5000/Realtek8180 `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` command lists, SANA-II event masks, and MLME deauth/disassoc reporting (`driver_sana2.c:524-530,692-705,839-846,1061-1068`; both device request.c:83-115; `wpa_supplicant/mlme.c:191-211,943-1001`). WirelessManager SANA-II shared request scan/callback ownership pass (OD3694 added, 2026-10-18): followed the request allocated at init through async scan `SendIO` and completion dispatch, then all major synchronous users (`driver_sana2.c:133-153,159-213,351-378,382-445,507-520,640-720,765-775,872-875`). The same `drv->request` remains in flight for S2_GETNETWORKS while callbacks rewrite its command and buffer fields and call DoIO. That can invalidate the device's pending scan inputs and prevent the reply switch from recognizing the scan completion. Hard-MAC selection is based on S2_GETNETWORKS support; selected Prism2 and BWFM advertise it. Added OD3694. No request overlap was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II scan-pool teardown ownership pass (OD3695 added, 2026-10-18): traced pool creation and attachment to the async base request (`driver_sana2.c:177-209`), normal result deletion (`:306-314`), and dynamic interface removal into driver deinit (`wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:2193-2224`; deinit `driver_sana2.c:881-918`). Deinit aborts/waits for `drv->request` but does not delete its scan pool before deleting the request and driver state; the normal result callback is skipped during teardown. `wpa_supplicant_cleanup()` cancels only the scheduled scan timeout (`scan.c:468-472`), and the SANA-II ops table has no `cancel_scan`, so normal shutdown can reach deinit with the request still active. Added OD3695, separate from OD3630's pre-submit allocation-failure leak. No interface or scan was removed. Source-only.

OD3695 teardown cleanup refinement (2026-10-18): verified the supplicant interface deinitializer calls `wpa_clear_keys` before `wpa_drv_deinit` (`wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:2102-2119`). If keys are not already marked cleared, that routine issues four `S2_SETKEY` callbacks (`:441-477`) through the same base request (`driver_sana2.c:351-378`), replacing its scan-pool `ios2_Data` pointer before the driver abort/wait. Since the pool handle is not held in independent driver state, cleanup cannot recover it from the request, and the normal scan-result deleter is skipped. Refined OD3695 to explain why merely inspecting the request during deinit is insufficient; no interface or scan was removed. Source-only.

OD3694 selected Prism2 consequence refinement (2026-10-18): verified `SendScanResults` takes `pool = request->ios2_Data` and uses it in `AllocPooled` for the results array and per-result tag lists (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/unit.c:2744-2783`). WirelessManager SANA-II empty-scan result allocation check (2026-10-18; no new finding): checked whether a successful zero-network scan fails because `get_scan_results` calls `os_zalloc(0)` for its result-pointer array (`driver_sana2.c:231-245`). Prism2 OD3156 rejected per-beacon descriptor trace (2026-10-18): refined the existing malformed-beacon finding after checking the `P2_INFO_SCANRESULT` caller. `P2ReadRec` returns FALSE without writing when a positive signed record length exceeds `FRAME_BUFFER_SIZE` (unit.c:3636-3652), but `InfoInt` ignores that result and proceeds whenever the info-event body length exceeds four (`:2505-2519`). `rx_descriptor` is initially cleared and then reused, so the parser consumes an empty or previous descriptor; its data length and IE parsing then follow the already-reported unchecked-subtraction/unbounded-GetIE path (OD3156). The descriptor bound is 1,596 bytes (`:60-61`); positive even record lengths above this through 32,766 are rejected. Expanded OD3156's affected trigger; no new finding or ID. No record or scan was run. Source-only.
