On a read error, `CF_FreeResources` frees the current buffer and collection node (and may free the newly stored LCI), but the handler does not return before dereferencing `lci`/`collitem` and publishing them. Added OD3741 for this cleanup/fallthrough lifetime bug. No mode file or failing stream was used. Source-only.

PCI EnumDevices selected storage-callback pass (2026-10-18; no additional candidate): traced AHCI, NVMe, and VirtIO block callbacks from `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-449`) into their selected handlers (`rom/devs/ahci/bus_pci.c:72-118`; `rom/devs/nvme/nvme_init.c:226-263`; `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_init.c:188-260`) and the public callback/ownership contracts (`rom/hidds/pci/doc/pci.en:24-76`; `pcideviceclass.c:456-510`). PCI holds `dev_lock` shared throughout callback execution, preventing concurrent exclusive list removal; each successful candidate claims the device through the owner semaphore before retaining it, and the losing claimant frees its temporary wrapper. VirtIO's requirements narrow vendor first and its callback correctly applies legacy-versus-modern block subtype filters; NVMe and AHCI use class/subclass/interface requirements. The callbacks' void return matches the documented notification contract. No independent defect was established in this slice. Allocation failure silently skips a candidate in each callback, but the API has no callback error result and no selected recovery contract establishes a separate bug. Remaining PCI enumerators in networking, USB, graphics/audio, the full device-method path, and backend/platform configuration have not been covered by this pass. No enumeration was run; source-only.

PCI EnumDevices OHCI/UHCI/EHCI callback startup pass (OD2953 rechecked, 2026-10-18): traced the three selected PCI class/interface callbacks and their `OHCI_Init`/`UHCI_Init`/`EHCI_Init` enumeration callers (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/{OHCI,UHCI,EHCI}/*_init.c`). Confirmed OD2953: OHCI creates an opened timer request before checking its static eight-device cap, then returns on excess without its normal timer cleanup; no additional finding was added. Existing OD2951 and OD2964 already cover EHCI/OHCI/UHCI timer setup and unchecked timer use. UHCI's callback creates its timer only after the cap check, while EHCI's per-match timer allocation/open and BIOS-handoff paths are already covered by OD2951. USB PCI callbacks do not claim PCI-device ownership, unlike AHCI/NVMe/VirtIO; no distinct collision consequence from selected in-tree callers has yet been established, so this remains an open lifecycle question rather than a finding. No controller was enumerated or timer failure induced. Source-only.

<a id="lpe32002-createunit-request-port-rollback-pass-od3743"></a>
LPe32002 CreateUnit request-port rollback pass (OD3743 added, 2026-10-18): followed the selected PCI enumerator (`workbench/devs/networks/lpe32002/lpe32002_init.c:101-128`) into `CreateUnit`'s queue-port allocation loop (`unit.c:747-766`) and `DeleteUnit` cleanup (`:858-875`). The queue enum sets `WRITE_QUEUE` to index 0 (`lpe32002.h:114-122`). If that allocation fails, the loop sets `success` false, never stores a port pointer, but the unconditional `lpeu_request_ports[WRITE_QUEUE]->mp_Flags` write dereferences NULL before the fail label; added OD3743. For a later-index failure, later loop iterations still allocate but no longer publish their pointers, so those allocations are not visible to `DeleteUnit` and leak. Existing OD3152/OD2326 cover worker startup and worker reply/input ports; they do not cover this constructor-owned request-port array. No PCI probe or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

<a id="lpe32002-embedded-delay-timer-contract-pass-od3744"></a>
LPe32002 embedded delay-timer contract pass (OD3744 added, 2026-10-18): traced unit timer setup and close (`workbench/devs/networks/lpe32002/unit.c:668-676,875-877`) into the firmware-ready and bootstrap-mailbox polling loops (`lpe32002_hw.c:57-90,111-164`) and Exec `DoIO` (`rom/exec/doio.c:53-70`). The constructor ignores `OpenDevice` failure; with `io_Device == NULL`, `DoIO` returns -1 immediately, and both loops ignore that result while decrementing fixed counters. Firmware readiness is therefore polled without the documented 1-ms delay and can be reset/retried prematurely; mailbox completion also loses its 100-µs pacing. Added OD3744, distinct from OD3152's child scheduler timer resources and handshake. No device or timer failure was exercised. Source-only.
PCI HIDD public enumeration/removal caller census (2026-10-18; no new candidate): rechecked `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices`, deprecated add/remove wrappers, `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver` and singleton Root dispose (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-691`) against `pci_hidd.h` tags/callback ABI and checked-in call sites. The match table has nine UBYTE entries for the nine contiguous public `TAG_USER` criteria, so the `sizeof(attrTable)` indexing is entry-count correct. PCI enumeration holds the shared `dev_lock` through attribute filtering and hook calls; this protects device-node lifetime, while existing reports cover reentrant/remove lifetime limits. Enumerated direct `EnumDevices` users across PCI bus/device drivers and tools, plus deprecated remove calls from PCIPC/PCIDT and platform backends. The selected PCIDT/PCIPC expunge callers return the method result so a failed hardware-driver removal prevents successful expunge; no separate caller error was found. Not every one of the device-driver enumeration callbacks has yet been inspected, so this does not close the pciclass.c row or its platform-specific caller scope. Source-only.

LPe32002 constructor allocation and mapping rollback recheck (OD3743-OD3744 confirmed; no additional candidate, 2026-10-18): followed the full `CreateUnit()` failure flow from zeroed unit allocation through BAR0/BAR3 mapping, embedded timer open, bootstrap mailbox, queue/DMA setup, request-port allocation, worker handshake, and `DeleteUnit()` cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/lpe32002/unit.c:593-882`). A single BAR mapping failure reaches guarded unmapping for whichever mapping succeeded; mailbox/descriptor allocations are likewise checked before later use, and teardown null-checks them. Confirmed OD3743: request-port allocation failure leaves `success` false but the loop continues and the unconditional WRITE_QUEUE flag store occurs before fail cleanup; successful ports allocated after that failure are not published and leak. Confirmed OD3744: the embedded timer open result is ignored, and the hardware delay loops ignore failed `DoIO`, collapsing nominal polling delays. Rechecked worker signal allocation against OD3673 and the prior coverage qualification: creation of three worker message ports consumes three user signal bits, leaving enough of the 16 user bits for four subsequent allocations when those ports exist, so no independent signal-exhaustion trigger is added. `lpe_Scheduler` failure/teardown cases remain represented by OD2326, OD3152 and OD3153. This closes only the constructor resource-rollback slice; external client lifetimes, generated vector behavior, and device/firmware contracts remain open. No PCI mapping, allocation, timer, worker or hardware failure was induced. Source-only.

Envy24HT PCI device ownership pass (OD3745 added, 2026-10-18): traced the AROS `Enumerator` hook and `ahi_pci_find_device()` result through both `DriverInit` discovery passes into `AllocDriverData()` and `FreeDriverData()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24HT/pci_aros.c:82-139`; `driver-init.c:80-85,143-146`; `misc.c:475-520,587-614`). The callback retains a matching object without claiming it; the selected adapter has no `HIDD_PCIDevice_Obtain` call. `EnumDevices` holds the shared device-list lock only through callbacks, whereas `HW_RemoveDriver` later checks `Owner` and disposes unowned device objects (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:422-448,490-513`; `pcideviceclass.c:456-510`); Envy24HT subsequently dereferences its stored object for config access and interrupt removal. Added OD3745, scoped to conditional underlying PCI-driver removal while the audio card remains live. The build route is the `HAVE_ASMIO` non-x86_64 AHI driver aggregate (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Makefile.in:46-57`); actual backend removal overlap and default noexpunge policy remain conditional. No device or driver was operated. Source-only.

Envy24 PCI device ownership pass (OD3745 expanded, 2026-10-18): followed each matching object from the adapter callback through `ahi_pci_find_device()`, the temporary `foundCards` list, and delayed `AllocDriverData()` initialization into `FreeDriverData()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/pci_aros.c:82-139`; `driver-init.c:91-129,155-179`; `misc.c:188-264`). The selected adapter has no `HIDD_PCIDevice_Obtain` or Release call, while the retained object is used by card setup and teardown. This confirms that OD3745 applies to both AHI variants and that Envy24 has an additional interval between enumeration and card setup. Its build is selected with the `HAVE_ASMIO` non-x86_64 driver aggregate (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Makefile.in:46-57`). No PCI object or audio card was operated. Source-only.

Native AHI PCI-object ownership cross-driver pass (OD3745 expanded, 2026-10-18): compared the AROS AHI PCI enumeration adapters against the `HIDD_PCIDevice_Obtain` call inventory and traced retained results into card initialization/cleanup. CMI8738, SB128 and VIA-AC97 match the Envy24/Envy24HT pattern: their callbacks return borrowed PCI objects, later card setup stores each in card data, and cleanup uses the saved object for config/interrupt methods. Their build entries share the `HAVE_ASMIO` aggregate (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Makefile.in:46-57`). HDAudio and NVHDMI were excluded because their callbacks claim matching devices before publishing them in the controller array (`hda_hidd.c:290-325`). The legacy `ac97` enumerator only reads candidate attributes and configures I/O directly without retaining the PCI object, so it is not included. Other PCI consumers outside AHI remain unreviewed. No PCI object, controller or audio card was operated. Source-only.

Legacy AHI AC97 PCI enumerator caller pass (2026-10-18; no additional OD): traced every class/subclass match through the support-table filter, `OOP_SetAttrs`, BAR/IRQ queries, DMA descriptor setup, and `DriverInit`'s `cardfound` result (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/ac97/ac97-init.c:65-167,177-220`). Unlike the five OD3745 adapters, the callback does not save the PCI `device` pointer: it copies the I/O bases and IRQ into the singleton `ac97Base`, then disposes only its temporary PCI-class object after enumeration. This rules out a retained PCI-object dereference in this path. The callback does continue after a successful match and overwrites those singleton hardware fields on each later match; the source does not state whether multiple supported controllers are supported or define a preferred-device policy, so I did not promote last-match selection as a defect. Whether active raw I/O/IRQ/DMA remains valid if the underlying PCI driver is removed is also unresolved; no maintained removal overlap was established. Existing OD2178-OD2181 cover separate worker, allocation, and expunge paths. The selected build route is the `HAVE_ASMIO` AHI aggregate (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Makefile.in:46-57`). No PCI device, audio controller or removal was exercised. Source-only.

HDAudio/NVHDMI claimed-controller allocation rollback pass (OD3746 added, 2026-10-18): retraced enumeration claims through controller subclass construction, HDA Setup/HWInit, both card-data allocators, their `DriverInit` loops, failed-codec cleanup, and controller release (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/hda_hidd.c:141-205,306-392`; `HDAudio/misc.c:108-120,144-163`; `HDAudio/driver-init.c:95-128`; shared NVHDMI `hda_hidd.c`, `hdmi.c:110-160`, and `driver-init.c:79-113`). Array-allocation failure releases every controller, failed HDA wrapper construction releases its device claim, and failed codec setup reaches `FreeDriverData()` and controller release. In contrast, failure of the initial per-card `AllocVec` returns NULL before the controller is stored in card state; neither caller releases that controller. Added OD3746 for the resulting lost controller handle/PCI claim and skipped HDAExit path. This closes the ownership rollback slice only; HDA hardware, map/unmap semantics and broader audio caller behavior remain open. No controller or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

HDAudio/NVHDMI HDA base Setup rollback boundary recheck (2026-10-18; no additional finding): traced `HIDD_HDA_Setup` through the selected PCI subclass and base `HDA_Shutdown` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/hda_hidd.c:120-135,141-205`; shared NVHDMI implementation; `workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:431-501,504-556`). A subclass `HWInit` failure returns before `hc_MMIO` is recorded, so base shutdown does not invoke `HWExit`; the PCI subclass may already have enabled decode/bus-master bits, and this precise early-return path remains OD2234. Once `HWInit` returns a non-null mapping, later reset, codec, stream, CORB or RIRB initialization failures enter `HDA_Shutdown`: it masks controller interrupts, removes any reset callback, invokes `HWExit`, frees each partially allocated ring/stream block, clears state, and lets failed Root.New dispose the wrapper; the selected caller then releases the PCI claim. This narrows OD2234 to early subclass-init failures and supports no additional HDA allocation-cleanup finding. PCI mapping lifetime and controller/hardware response remain unverified. No controller or failure was induced. Source-only.

CMI8738 PCI adapter partial-init rollback recheck (2026-10-18; OD3745 remains the separate post-enumeration issue): traced `ahi_pci_init()`'s OOP library, PCI attribute-base and temporary PCI class-object acquisition sequence (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/CMI8738/pci_aros.c:35-60`) into the common library's `DriverInit` failure rollback (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Common/library.c:456-462,489-500`) and `DriverCleanup()`/`ahi_pci_exit()` (`CMI8738/driver-init.c:205-230`; `pci_aros.c:62-69`). Every partial-acquisition failure returns FALSE; cleanup releases whichever non-NULL resources were acquired. The found PCI device itself remains unclaimed after enumeration and is retained for later config/interrupt methods, confirming OD3745's separate conditional lifetime issue. No module load, PCI enumeration or driver removal was run. Source-only.

SB128 AC’97-to-AK4531 volume write caller reconciliation (2026-10-18; no additional finding): traced all in-tree `ak4531_ac97_write()` callers in `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/SB128` (`sb128hw.c:619,630`; `misc.c:949-953,977-989`). The guard at `misc.c:264` uses bare nonzero register constants after the first comparison, so it does not filter the register as its form suggests. However, every selected caller supplies one of the supported volume registers or `AC97_RECORD_SELECT`; for an unrecognized value the subsequent switch reaches its diagnostic default without issuing a codec write. No user-visible defect follows from the guard for the checked callers. This is a targeted helper/caller pass, not closure of SB128 hardware behavior or its remaining caller contracts. No codec write was performed. Source-only.
Bluetooth library delay/task/string helper caller reconciliation (2026-10-18; no additional OD): re-read `btDelayMS`, `btSpawnSubTask`, `btCopyStr`, `btSafeRawDoFmtA` and `btCopyStrFmtA` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:870-1044`). `btDelayMS` copies the opened timer request, substitutes a stack reply port, and calls synchronous `DoIO`; callers use it for deliberate retry/boot delays (`objects.c:152`; `config.c:770`; `hwtask.c:3056`; selected btpan/btserial/bthid retry paths), so ignoring the void DoIO result has no separately established state corruption. `btSpawnSubTask` checks required name/entry, checks `CreateNewProcTags`/`NewAllocEntry`/`AddTask` results, and frees the task `MemList` if `AddTask` fails; traced callers either test the returned task or intentionally treat optional GUI creation as best-effort. `btCopyStr` callers pass non-NULL strings or guard nullable names; the selected formatter helper uses the Exec `RawDoFmt` callback for length/output, bounds writes to the supplied capacity, and forces final NUL when capacity is nonzero. This narrows the caller-helper pass only; unrelated library vectors and lifecycle/API contracts remain open. Source-only; no runtime failure was induced.

Bluetooth library address/UUID/string normalization helper pass (2026-10-18; no additional OD): read `bStripString`, `bAddrToStr`, `bStrToAddr`, `bUUID16To128`, `bUUID128To16`, and `bUUIDToStr` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:1095-1213`) and checked selected SDP/HCI callers. `bStripString` compacts into the same allocation and only writes the literal `<empty>` when the original whitespace-only allocation is at least eight bytes; the SDP service-name allocation and HCI remote-name allocation each reserve the original input length plus NUL. Address/UUID string formatters write fixed-size outputs (18 and 37 bytes respectively), matching their selected caller buffers. `bStrToAddr` has no selected in-tree caller, so no caller-level malformed-input contract is claimed. No additional local defect established; public direct callers and broader API contracts remain open. Source-only.
Bluetooth error-removal event pointer lifetime (OD3747 added, 2026-10-18): traced `btRemErrorMsg()` unlink/free order and event publication (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:229-243`), the public `BEHMB_REMERRORMSG` Param1 contract (`bluetooth/include/libraries/bluetooth.h:422`), `btSendEvent()`'s asynchronous pointer copy (`classes.c:712-740`), and the selected Preferences subscriber's `BEHMB_ADDERRORMSG`-only refresh (`prefs/ActionClass.c:1182-1215`). This is a distinct payload/object case from OD3732 (`BEHMB_REMCLASS`). Source-only; no event subscriber or removal was run.

OD3747 removal trigger cross-check (2026-10-18): selected callers remove messages during Bluetooth library expunge (`bluetooth.library.c:209-213`), Preferences' explicit DoFlush (`prefs/ActionClass.c:1109-1114`), and BTErrorLog's default post-print flush (`shellcommands/BTErrorLog.c:103-112`). The report's trigger is therefore reachable through ordinary selected cleanup/flush paths; no claim is made that the in-tree Preferences event consumer dereferences the dangling payload.

Bluetooth service/endpoint constructor failure-path recheck (2026-10-18; OD3726 retained, no duplicate): traced `bAllocService`/`bAllocEndpoint` list insertion (`objects.c:303-343`) through incoming RFCOMM acceptance, SDP service parsing, and GATT service/characteristic enumeration (`hwconn.c:597-655,1620-1700,1945-2050`). Confirmed OD3726's partial incoming-service state is the distinct case where later reuse treats the empty endpoint-list sentinel as an endpoint. Other inspected service/characteristic allocation failures either leave a skipped/missing service or are handled as absent endpoints in the selected GATT continuation; no separate memory-safety defect was established in this pass. Device-lock ownership is provided by the relevant callers; a complete service-object lifetime audit remains open.

Bluetooth hardware duplicate-registration race boundary (2026-10-18; no new OD): `btAddHardware()` checks `bFindHardware()` before the worker opens the controller and only publishes the hardware node after successful bring-up (`objects.c:62-114`; `hwtask.c:2417-2432,2946-2951`), so the library check and publication are not an atomic reservation. Reconciled the selected hardware producers: USB `bluetooth.class` routes through `usbbluetooth.device`, whose `devOpen()` rejects a second opener for the same unit (`rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/dev.c:73-102`); `vbthci.device` likewise checks/publishes one unit under `vb_Lock` (`hardware/vbthci/vbthci_device.c:41-74`). Thus concurrent duplicate calls on those selected transports lose at the device OpenDevice gate rather than publishing two radios. Other external HCI devices accepted by the public name/unit API are not inventoried here, so the generic race remains an external-device boundary, not a retained in-tree finding. Source-only.
Bluetooth L2CAP service-record encoding (OD3748 added, 2026-10-18): compared the L2CAP branch's `bt_sdp_encode_sequence_header()` arguments and emitted element widths (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:1622-1628`) with the writer contract/encoder (`stack/protocols/sdp/sdp.c:42-105`) and selected server iterator/attribute assembly (`sdp.c:245-275`; `sdp_server.c:109-126`). The public tag contract allows `BSVP_L2CAP`/PSM (`bluetooth/include/libraries/bluetooth.h:338-345`); direct in-tree creator census found only RFCOMM in btserial, and the checked-in SDP server test record is likewise RFCOMM. No runtime or protocol transaction was run.
Bluetooth SDP service-record lifetime cross-check (OD3749 added, 2026-10-18): traced `bSDPRecordAt()`'s read-lock scope and borrowed `bsr_Attrs` pointer (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:539-560`) into `bt_sdp_server_handle()` matching/serialization (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/sdp/sdp_server.c:288-350`), then compared against `btRemServiceRecord()` removal/free order (`objects.c:1668-1684`) and the selected `btserial.class` register/expunge lifecycle (`classes/btserial/btserial.class.c:61-64,86-93`). The SDP callback runs synchronously from the hardware-task ACL path (`hwconn.c:574-578,3420-3434`), while class expunge is an independent library teardown path. A refcount or copied record snapshot is needed to extend lifetime beyond list lookup. Source-only; no concurrency was run.

Bluetooth SDP service-search UUID matcher standards cross-check (2026-10-18; no additional finding): reviewed `bt_sdp_record_matches()`/`contains_uuid()` against Bluetooth Core Specification 6.1, SDP §2.5.2. The service-search pattern intentionally matches each UUID anywhere in record attribute values, so the matcher’s recursive search over the complete attribute stream is consistent with the protocol; it is not limited to ServiceClassIDList. [Bluetooth Core Specification, Service Discovery Protocol, §2.5.2](https://www.bluetooth.com/wp-content/uploads/Files/Specification/HTML/Core-61/out/en/host/service-discovery-protocol--sdp--specification.html). Source and specification review only.
Bluetooth SDP server continuation ownership (OD3750 added, 2026-10-18): compared the server contract's one-instance-per-L2CAP-channel requirement and per-instance response buffer (`rom/bluetooth/stack/include/btcore/sdp_server.h:1-7,33-43`) with the single `cn_SDPServer` field (`bluetooth/hwtask.h:250-253`), the shared connection listener context/event callback (`hwconn.c:565-578,921-927`), and L2CAP's per-accepted-channel allocation plus copied listener user data (`stack/protocols/l2cap/channel_manager.c:227-270`). Continuation requests require state fields in `bt_sdp_server_handle()` (`sdp_server.c:269-281`). A second SDP channel's OPENED callback reinitializes the shared state, so the first channel's continuation is lost. No multi-channel traffic was run.
Bluetooth SERVICEGONE dispatch recheck (OD3751 corrected, 2026-10-18): verified `btSendEvent()` filters each message by `beh_MsgMask` (`classes.c:726-740`), then compared the internal handler registration mask (`:828-832`) with the intended `BEHMB_SERVICEGONE` consumer (`:881-895`). The event bit is absent, so the internal cleanup case is unreachable. Rechecked the consequence against `bsv_Gone` skip conditions in class scan and RFCOMM reuse (`classes.c:291-300`; `hwconn.c:613-619`) and `bClearServices()` preserving bound services (`hwconn.c:1725-1732`). Corrected the earlier OD3751 draft: its asserted internal event-task UAF race was unsupported because that task does not subscribe to the event; the retained finding is the missed subscription and resulting stale bound service/class reference. External subscriber lifetime is not claimed here. No connection was run.

USB HID keyboard report-state allocation follow-up (OD3752 added, 2026-10-18): re-read the keyboard constructor's descriptor-derived `loc_keycnt` and pooled allocations (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/kbdclass.c:147-191`), then traced the unconditional `CopyMem` in `ParseReport` (`:99-120`) back to the HID interrupt callback (`hidclass.c:65-82`) and selected USB HID constructor/dispatch route (`hidclass.c:226-335`). Either missing state buffer is dereferenced on the next report because worker creation/publication continues after these allocations; this is separate from OD2994 report-buffer failure and OD3564/OD3565 worker setup. No allocation failure or USB report was induced.


USB HID keyboard report-state synchronization follow-up (OD3753 added, 2026-10-18): traced the single `code`/`prev_code` pair from `ParseReport` into worker comparisons (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/kbdclass.c:99-120,351-575`), verified `Signal` sets a received bit rather than counting notifications (`rom/exec/signal.c:295-304`), and followed selected OHCI/UHCI completion paths through `Cause` to the registered HID callback (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:350-391`; `workbench/devs/USB/drivers/UHCI/uhciclass.c:92-158`; `rom/exec/cause.c:29-33`). The callback can replace the state pair while the worker consumes it or before it handles an earlier report, losing transitions under the stated overlap. This differs from OD3752's allocation-failure null dereference and OD3389's usage-table bounds issue. No device or report timing was exercised.


USB HID held-input disconnect follow-up (OD3754 added, 2026-10-18): checked USB hub child disposal (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:543-549`), keyboard/mouse Ctrl-C destructors and worker exits (`kbdclass.c:241-257,373-381`; `mouseclass.c:226-235,279-289`), and the report-driven release generation paths (`kbdclass.c:459-581`; `mouseclass.c:306-433`). Neither teardown emits release events for its remembered key/button state. The selected input.device event path applies submitted raw events and qualifiers without associating state with the originating USB object (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:312-342`). This is independent of OD2184's early-detach worker lifetime behavior. No device or input event was run.


USB HID mouse event-ring saturation follow-up (OD3755 added, 2026-10-18): traced `RING_SIZE == 8` and the one-slot-empty full test (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid.h:146-148`; `mouseclass.c:57-75`), then followed dequeued reports into button transition calculation and `buttonstate` updates (`mouseclass.c:294-307,358-433`). Full-ring callbacks drop the report before queuing it. UHCI suppresses callbacks for NAK status (`uhciclass.c:139-150`), while HID setup requests idle rate zero (`hidclass.c:253`); therefore no retry is guaranteed for a lost button release when the device reports only state changes. No ring saturation or device report was induced.

WASAPI host-library error-string cleanup follow-up (OD3756 added, 2026-10-18): traced both error-producing bridge calls through `hostlib_load_so()` to the MinGW HostLib implementation. Failed `LoadLibrary`/`GetProcAddress` paths allocate error text with `FormatMessage(FORMAT_MESSAGE_ALLOCATE_BUFFER...)`; `HostLib_FreeErrorStr` routes to `LocalFree`, but neither bridge failure path calls it. Followed `WASAPI_Init` failure through AHI `LibInit` and `_LibExpunge` to `DriverCleanup`; the local error pointer is not retained for cleanup. No Windows host or failure was run.

BWFM SANA-II device-query and interface command recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread `S2_DEVICEQUERY`, `S2_GETSTATIONADDRESS`, `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE`, `S2_ONLINE` and `S2_OFFLINE` dispatch with the unit initialization and state/event helpers (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1620-1672`). The query bounds its copy to the caller-reported `SizeAvailable` and writes back the copied size; station-address copies use the fixed six-byte API fields. The selected AROSTCP caller serializes online/offline transitions under its stack lock as already recorded in the OD3613/OD3614 qualification; direct clients and the required ordering of join completion versus online/offline events remain unverified. Reconfirmed `struct sample` is four bytes while all six converters multiply consumed frames by pointer size (`devsupp.c:37-40,61,85,108,132,155,179`); `AHI_SampleFrameSize(AHIST_S16S)` is four (`sound.c:1248-1268`), and `RecordFunc()` reports `ahirm_Length << 2` bytes (`device.c:990-1003`). The CMD_READ contract returns `io_Offset` for continuation, and the selected AHI-Handler preserves it when resubmitting after the initial zeroed request (`devcommands.c:679-692`; `AHI-Handler/main.c:437-450,488-518`). `FillReadBuffer()` subtracts that value from the next capture extent and advances the source pointer by it (`devcommands.c:1028-1080`). Reinstated OD3572 in the detailed report and linked the index to its anchor. No request, audio or device was used; source-only.


AHI capture-buffer handoff report restoration (OD3570, 2026-10-18): restored the detailed finding after verifying the index and coverage ledger referenced no report entry. Rechecked the borrowed-buffer lifetime in the public `AHIA_RecordFunc` contract (`audioctrl.c:401-418`), audio.device's one-slot pointer/length publication and deferred task consumption (`device.c:912-943,990-1003`; `devcommands.c:982-1008,1020-1088`), and HDAudio's interrupt callback with alternating 1,024-frame DMA buffers (`interrupt.c:130-171`; `DriverData.h:37`; `main.c:270-311`). The callback may overwrite the saved slot before processing, and signal bits can coalesce; the two HDAudio buffers can be reused if processing spans later callbacks. Linked the report-index entry to `#od3570`. No callback, device or timing was run; source-only.

ATA TD64 `io_Actual` error-result contract follow-up (2026-10-18; no new OD): compared `cmd_Read64`/`cmd_Write64` early returns with their successful low-level actual-byte assignments (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:106-164,222-289`; `lowlevel.c:2027-2112`) and selected FAT, AFS, and CDFS callers (`rom/filesys/fat/disk.c:220-259`; `rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:596-619`; `rom/filesys/cdfs/bcache.c:390-415`). A failed 64-bit request may retain its input high-offset word in `io_Actual`, but these selected callers branch on the returned error and do not consume `io_Actual` on failure; the local trackdisk header does not document the error-result contract. Therefore this is not promoted as a finding. Successful request counts are set by the selected low-level vectors. Reconfirmed OD2999's 28/48-bit selector boundary and OD2996's separate unchecked bounce-allocation path. No request or device was used; source-only.
ATA DMA chunk-error and bounce-read copy follow-up (2026-10-18; no new OD): read the full `ata_exec_blk` body and the DMA setup/completion/cleanup portion of `ata_exec_cmd` (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1188-1248,690-810`) against all selected sector/multiple/DMA vector wrappers (`:1950-2112`). Chunk requests stay within the ATA command limits and the bounce allocation is released after success or error. One behavior remains contract-dependent: for a bounced DMA read, `ata_exec_blk` copies each chunk from the bounce area to the caller after `ata_exec_cmd` even when that command returns an error; the vectors set `*act = 0` before execution and leave it zero on error. In particular, DMA setup failure can cause a copy before the device was started. No local API contract promises an unchanged output buffer on failure, so this is not promoted. Existing OD2996 covers the distinct NULL-allocation case. No I/O or failure was induced; source-only.
ATA PIO multiple-sector short-transfer boundary recheck (2026-10-18; suspected overrun rejected): compared the `ata_Read/WriteMultiple32/64` command-block sizes with `ata_IRQSetHandler` and both PIO callback paths (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:185-197,216-271,1975-2030,2160-2298`). Although the device's reported multiple-sector size initializes `blklen`, `ata_IRQSetHandler` sets the first `au_cmd_length` to `min(piolen, blklen)`; the read/write handlers then reduce the next chunk length to the remaining byte count after each complete block. Thus a request shorter than the configured multiple-sector size, or a final partial block, does not by itself overrun/overread the caller buffer. No new OD. The separate failed SET MULTIPLE setup behavior remains OD2997. No disk or transfer was exercised; source-only.

EMU10kx CAMD companion call-contract pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced CAMD's selected `OpenDriver`/`CloseDriver` calls and zero-based port enumeration through the EMU10kx companion to the published hooks (`workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:24-70,258-267`; `CAMD/emu10kx.c:47-60,233-257,282-333`; `emu10kx-camd.c:35-105,116-145`; `emu10kx-init.c:145-182`). ATA low-level command/completion cross-check (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread the full `ata_exec_cmd`, `ata_WaitBusyTO`, common IRQ dispatch, PIO read/write and DMA completion paths (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:440-807`; `rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:27-43`) against the `ata_exec_blk` 28-/48-bit chunk loop and every ATA block wrapper (`lowlevel.c:1188-1238,1935-2289`). Confirmed the initial PIO-write timeout and no-DRQ returns bypass handler cleanup (OD2998), and the >32-bit DMA bounce allocation result is not checked before setup (OD2996); the subsequent timeout path does call `DMA_End`, and ordinary PIO-read completion and shared IRQ timeout clear the active handler. DMA read bounce data is copied after a command error, but callers report zero actual bytes on that error, so this pass does not establish a distinct public buffer-validity violation. DMA setup failure before command issue returns aborted; ATAPI bulk DMA setup failure falls back to PIO. Remaining ATA controller/backend transfer ordering, cache/DMA contracts, and hardware completion semantics remain open. No request, device, timeout, or transfer was run; source-only.

PCI device-object teardown lock check (2026-10-18; no additional candidate): inspected the generic PCIDevice `Root_New` and ownership methods plus every PCI-specific dispose method (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:562-616,491-510,1084-1228`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:688-691`). The device class initializes its owner semaphore at construction and defines no custom dispose method; PCI's root dispose body is empty. Thus `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver` disposing nodes while holding the exclusive device-list semaphore (`pciclass.c:490-513`) has no synchronous dispose callback in these classes that re-enters the device list. This does not resolve the already-recorded OD3563/OD3636/OD3637 lifecycle findings, and does not establish a new lock-reentrancy defect. No object was disposed; source-only.

xHCI synchronous command timeout/ring reclamation pass (2026-10-18; no distinct finding): followed `xhciCmdSubmit` timeout handling (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hw.c:128-159`) through `xhciQueueTRB` free-space accounting and command completion (`xhci_hcd.c:845-910,3553-3680`). A timeout returns failure without advancing the command-ring `end`; only a later completion event advances it. This can leave ring capacity occupied if the completion is never processed, but the reviewed selected failure path overlaps OD907's missing/unusable event worker and does not establish a separate ordinary trigger or recovery defect beyond that initialization failure. A late completion is recorded by its ring index and reclaims that slot, so timeout alone does not demonstrate stale result reuse. Concurrent controller reset and timeout recovery remain open. No command or controller was run; source-only.

xHCI reset CNR timeout/error-path pass (OD3782 added, 2026-10-18): re-read `xhciReset` and both selected `xhciInit` readiness checks (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:3798-3905,4084,4116-4140,4168-4259`) against the xHCI 1.2 CNR requirement in USBSTS §5.4.2. The reset path polls CNR for 200 ms but proceeds to write CONFIG, DCBAAP, CRCR and event-ring runtime registers without checking the final bit; the caller's second timeout only warns if CNR remains set, then continues startup. Added OD3782 for the conditional not-ready initialization path. Selected package evidence: OpenSBI RISC-V lists `USBHardware/pcixhci` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:104`); AArch64 Raspberry Pi package lists it (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:217`). No reset or controller was run; hardware outcome remains conditional. Reference: [Intel xHCI specification](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/technical-specifications/extensible-host-controler-interface-usb-xhci.pdf).


BWFM CMD_WRITE/S2_OFFLINE overlap (OD3783 added, 2026-10-18): compared `tx_request` and `S2_OFFLINE` dispatch (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:652-700,1666-1672,1887-1901`) with `BWFMTxData`'s tx-credit wait, which releases `bwfm_Sem` while sleeping and has no device-online check before sending (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2135-2176,2178-2198`). Exec `SendIO` invokes BeginIO directly (`rom/exec/sendio.c:48-59`), so another task can complete S2_OFFLINE while CMD_WRITE is blocked waiting for credit. The write is not in any driver-maintained pending-write queue and is not aborted; after credit arrives it can transmit and return success although the unit is offline. SANA-II Revision 7 requires S2_OFFLINE to abort all pending reads and writes with S2ERR_OUTOFSERVICE and reject hardware-touching requests while offline ([SANA-II Revision 7, S2_OFFLINE](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/SANA-II_Revision_7#S2_OFFLINE)). Added OD3783 for this conditional in-flight-write contract violation. AROSTCP serializes its online/offline transitions, but the SANA-II device is shareable and another client may issue the transition; no concurrent request, radio or hardware was used. Source-only.

BWFM Close and worker-lifetime recheck (2026-10-18; no additional candidate): reread `close`, `start_pump`, and both worker entry loops (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:592-640,1180-1227`). Close holds `unit->lock` while draining that opener's queued reads and event requests, removes it from the opener list, then frees its state; the RX pump's read delivery uses the same lock, so those queued-object lifetimes are synchronized. The pump and control worker intentionally have no stop path and increment the device open count for their lifetime, preventing library expunge while they retain the base. Their independent creation failures remain OD3595/OD3596; this pass did not establish a new defect in normal lifetime retention. Synchronous in-flight operations such as CMD_WRITE, S2_GETNETWORKS and S2_SETKEY are not represented in the close-drained queues; their caller/CloseDevice concurrency contract remains unverified. No request, task shutdown or device close was run; source-only.


xHCI CNR timeout to caller-unwind recheck (OD3782 qualified against OD3369, 2026-10-18): followed `xhciReset` from the unchecked CNR timeout into `xhciInit`'s interrupt/reset/task setup and three controller-start attempts, then through `pciAllocUnit` failure and `Open_Unit` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:3870-3913,4084,4117-4240,4264-4265`; `pcixhci_arospci.c:319-345`; `uhwcmd.c:251-278`). Persistent CNR violates readiness ordering and may still reach a nominally successful init (OD3782); if startup instead remains halted through all attempts, the failed return bypasses `pciFreeUnit`, matching OD3369's existing callback/interrupt/task rollback finding. Kept the cleanup consequence within OD3369 rather than adding a duplicate. No controller, IRQ or failed startup was induced; source-only.

xHCI PCI controller-class/root startup caller recheck (OD3784, 2026-10-18): traced `pciInit`'s root fallback and ignored `XHCIControllerOOPStartup` result (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_arospci.c:195-200`) through class-creation failure (`xhci_controllerclass.c:566-604`), the guarded `HW_AddDriver` registration (`pcixhci_arospci.c:238-252`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:140-205`), and `Open_Unit`'s successful unit startup path (`uhwcmd.c:228-278`; `pcixhci_arospci.c:319-379`). If root acquisition or class startup fails, the loop publishes no USB-controller HIDD instances, yet `pciInit` and potentially `Open_Unit` still succeed. Added OD3784 for this conditional absent-controller-registration path. This is distinct from OD3369's post-registration controller-start rollback and OD2421's failed PCI-HIDD scan retry. No allocation failure, device open or USB enumeration was induced; source-only.

OD2059 report/index consistency repair and ownership recheck (2026-10-18): the coverage rows already referenced OD2059 for VirtIO, PCIUSB and xHCI, but a search of the current other-driver report and AROS index found no report/index entry. Re-traced constructors at `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_controllerclass.c:121-145`, `rom/usb/pciusb/pciusb_arospci.c:269-291`, and `rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_controllerclass.c:529-553`; generic HIDD documents `aHidd_HardwareName` as not copied, stores it raw, and frees only `hd_Name` on Dispose (`rom/hidds/hidd/hiddclass.c:105-139,293-318,347-354`). The three caller Dispose paths do not release the allocated buffers, and the registration callers do not recover the allocation on `HW_AddDriver` failure. Restored OD2059 in the report and index; this xHCI pass confirms the existing shared finding rather than adding another ID. No HIDD object was created or removed; source-only.

xHCI scratchpad arithmetic/page-size configuration recheck (OD3727, 2026-10-18): verified `xhciPageSize` selects the least significant set PAGESIZE bit and maps bit 15 to 128 MiB (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:1136-1147`); `XHCSPARAMS2` decoding combines two five-bit fields, so a count of 33 is representable (`xhci_controllerclass.c:418-423`). The Intel xHCI specification §5.4.3 defines page size as 2^(n+12) bytes and states 128 MiB is the maximum possible page size ([specification](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/technical-specifications/extensible-host-controler-interface-usb-xhci.pdf)). With only bit 15 set and count 33, the 32-bit `ULONG` allocation product wraps to 128 MiB while the loop still emits 33 page-spaced pointers. Both active package lists include `pcixhci.device` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:217`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:104`). This confirms the existing conditional OD3727; no additional finding. The actual register combination and successful wrapped allocation were not exercised.

xHCI HW_AddDriver failure propagation recheck (OD3784 expanded, 2026-10-18): `pciInit` discards every `HW_AddDriver` result (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_arospci.c:238-252`), while the generic HW method returns NULL if it cannot allocate a DriverNode, construct the object, or complete setup (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:140-205`). Unit creation and `pciInit` success remain independent of that return, and `Open_Unit` proceeds into `pciAllocUnit` (`uhwcmd.c:228-278`). Thus failure at the per-controller registration step also permits a unit to initialize without publishing a USB-controller object. This is the same externally visible registration gap as class/root setup failure and is included in OD3784, not a duplicate. No allocation or HIDD setup failure was induced; source-only.

xHCI controller-object consumer and impact qualification (OD3784, 2026-10-18): checked the system-root lifetime and all in-tree USB references to `CLID_Hidd_USBController`. `CLID_Hidd_System` returns the singleton system HW root (`rom/hidds/base/system/system_class.c:13-34`; singleton behavior documented in `rom/hidds/hidd/hwroot.c:21-36`), and generic HW enumeration visits registered driver objects (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:353-377`). SysExplorer enumerates that same root and inserts generic HIDD objects using `aHidd_HardwareName` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_main.c:70-150,393-405`), so omitted registration has a concrete hardware-inventory consequence. A repository-wide search found no selected Poseidon transfer path consuming these HIDD controller instances; therefore removed the earlier claim that the USB stack loses port/transfer access. OD3784 is retained as a conditional false-success/incomplete-HW-inventory issue, not a USB service outage. No HIDD enumeration or device was run; source-only.

xHCI header ring-lock and command-producer SMP audit (OD3785, 2026-10-18): read all `xhci_hcd.h` inline helpers/macros and traced every selected ring-lock/command-ring use. `xhciRingLock` is only local interrupt disabling (`xhci_hcd.h:212-219`); Exec documents that `Disable` needs a spinlock for shared state in ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:47-62`). `xhciQueueTRB` changes the shared command ring indices/TRB and `xhciCmdSubmit` reserves the associated result slot without a cross-CPU lock (`xhci_hcd.c:872-913`; `xhci_hw.c:52-158`). The port worker reaches `xhciCmdSlotEnable` via `xhciCreateDeviceCtx` (`xhci_hcport.c:767-773`; `xhci_hcd.c:1367-1368`), while the event worker can submit endpoint-configuration commands through its async scheduler (`xhci_hw.c:523-550`; `xhci_schedule.c:134-175`). AArch64 Raspberry Pi's `smp` target variant defines `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` (`configure.in:2196-2199`) and packages pcixhci (`boot/mmakefile.src:217`). Added OD3785 for the conditional cross-CPU command-ring race. The port/link-state inline helpers' protocol table bounds are checked; the RINGFROMTRB alignment contract remains satisfied by the aligned ring allocations described in OD905. Architecture-specific MMIO barrier scope and broader controller event ordering remain open. No controller or concurrent command was run; source-only.

xHCI AArch64 doorbell ordering pass (no additional finding, 2026-10-18): traced all `xhciRingDoorbell` call sites (`xhci_hw.c:136,335`; `xhci_async.c:382`; `xhci_periodic.c:139,143`) back to `xhciInsertTRB`, which cleans each published TRB with `CacheClearE` before the doorbell (`xhci_hcd.c:451-497`). On the selected RP1 path, `AllocPCIMem` maps descriptor buffers as Normal Non-Cacheable (`rp1_pci.c:182-205`; AArch64 `krnMMUMap` maps `MAP_WriteThrough` as Normal Non-Cacheable, `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmu.c:301-333`), and `CacheClearE` completes with `dsb ish` (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:138-150`). The xHCI BAR is Device-nGnRnE (`PCIBcm2712__Hidd_PCIDriver__MapPCI`, `driverclass.c:245-267`; AArch64 MMU mapping, `mmu.c:301-333`). This per-TRB completion prevents a pending descriptor store from being deferred past the doorbell on this route; the extra `dmb ishst` did not establish a separate defect here. Other AArch64 PCIDriver mapping variants and OpenSBI cache/DMA ordering remain open; no controller was used.

OpenSBI xHCI descriptor/cache-maintenance boundary pass (2026-10-18; no additional finding): followed command/event/transfer-ring publication through `xhciInsertTRB`, context/event-ring reads and writes, and the selected OpenSBI Exec hooks (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:451-497,576,625-626,835`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:40-53,104-143`). OpenSBI `CacheClearE` performs a memory fence and remote instruction fence, not data-cache maintenance; the optional Zicbom hook is installed only for `CachePreDMA`/`CachePostDMA`. However, the selected PCIDT backend explicitly documents the PCI controllers as cache coherent and allocates xHCI DMA memory from ordinary RAM (`pcidt_driverclass.c:992-1019`), so this source pass does not establish a selected noncoherent xHCI path or a new cache finding. It does not prove the platform coherency assumption against every external firmware/device-tree configuration, nor check all OpenSBI PCI drivers' use of that assumption. No controller, DMA, or cache behavior was exercised; source-only.

OpenSBI xHCI memory-to-doorbell ordering cross-check (2026-10-18; no additional finding): checked whether `CacheClearE`'s `fence rw,rw` was the only ordering between TRB publication and the RISC-V MMIO doorbell. `xhciRingDoorbell` invokes `XHCI_MMIO_BARRIER()` immediately before the volatile doorbell write (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hw.c:35-45`); the selected RISC-V definition is `fence iorw, iorw` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.h:299`). This orders memory writes before the I/O doorbell on the selected OpenSBI path, so no separate missing-doorbell-order finding is established. The coherent-DMA platform assumption and other controller event/MMIO ordering remain subject to the preceding note; no device was used.

Serial SDCMD_SETPARAMS error-unwind report/index reconciliation (OD58, 2026-10-18): compared the detailed finding with the existing source/caller ledger. The report only named PC as a selected rejecting backend, while the coverage row already recorded PC, Sam440 and OpenSBI. Rechecked the three backend methods and the non-quick `DoIO` callers in serialtest and the Port handler; corrected the detailed report and top-level index to show the selected backend and caller scope. The direct error returns still bypass `Enable`, `ReplyMsg`, and the common unit-semaphore release. No request or HIDD call was run; source-only.

EHCI reset/failed-init finding restoration (OD2484, 2026-10-18): compared the EHCI file table and earlier reconciliation notes with the detailed report and top-level index. Coverage described an existing finding, but the report/index lacked its ID; restored OD2484 in both. Re-read `Enumerator`'s handoff/reset/interrupt-disable/unconfigure/port-owner writes and `EHCI_Init`'s unconditional FALSE after PCI enumeration (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/EHCI/ehci_init.c:59-187,196-243`), then checked the class constructor stub and selected package boundaries (`:261-268`; `workbench/devs/USB/drivers/EHCI/mmakefile.src`; Sam440 PCI460's EHCI simulator is under `#if 0`, Efika selects OHCI). Qualified the consequence to a matching controller being reset without an initialized EHCI HIDD; no checked default route establishes live-controller impact. OD2484 remains distinct from OD2950's failed-init USB-object leak and OD2952's HCCPARAMS/port-owner count error. No module or controller was run; source-only.
xHCI reset/readiness check reconciliation (OD3782, 2026-10-18): re-read the complete post-HCRST wait and register programming in `xhciReset` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:3857-3905`) and both selected `xhciInit` paths through init success/failure (`:4084-4140,4168-4259`). Both OpenSBI RISC-V and AArch64 Raspberry Pi package lists select `pcixhci.device`. OD3782 remains supported; the subsequent failed-start cleanup case is already tracked by OD3369. No new ID or report change. Controller behavior is conditional and untested; source-only.


Bluetooth string-chunk caller census (OD3773 expanded, 2026-10-18): searched every maintained `btGetStringChunk` call. Besides the core `DEVNAME`/`NAME` consumers in `bApplyDevConfig`, the selected optional BTHID class `bLoadItem` copies five saved action strings with `strncpy` limits 255/79; when an imported chunk lacks a NUL and is shorter than that limit, the bounded copy still reads beyond the `len + 1` returned allocation (`bthid.class.c:5907-5930`; fixed destination sizes `bthid.h:205-212`). Updated OD3773 to include this selected-target-dependent consequence. No config was loaded and no class/action was created. Source-only.


Bluetooth IFF parser candidate deduplication (2026-10-18): the newly drafted OD3786 was withdrawn after checking the existing detailed report; OD3766 already records the same `bAddCfgChunk()` parent-extent overread, recursive FORM path, import trigger, and validation requirement. Re-read OD3765-OD3767: they separately cover undersized top-level FORM allocation, chunk extent overread, and partial replacement / false-success behavior. Bluetooth config serializer size and output pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): checked `bGetFormLength()`'s recursive size calculation against `bInternalWriteForm()`'s header/chunk/child writes and the `btWriteCfg()` allocation (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/config.c:286-309,1312-1325,1433-1451`). MassStorage large-block emulation CopyMemQuick contract pass (OD3787 added, 2026-10-18): traced `nRead64()`/`nWrite64()` fallback selection, 512-byte request constraints, `insideblockoffset`, one-block staging and caller-buffer copies (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:2646-2722,2755-2830,2900-2915,3058-3087`). Length and staging offsets are 512-byte multiples, but caller `io_Data` alignment is not checked before `CopyMemQuick`; the public helper requires ULONG-aligned pointers (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:30-45`). Added OD3787 as conditional on large-block emulation and a non-ULONG-aligned request buffer. Searched maintained call sites; no in-tree caller deliberately supplies that alignment. No device or I/O was used. Source-only.


MassStorage Max Transfer persisted-value validation pass (OD3788 added, 2026-10-18): traced class and per-device config loading into `cdc_MaxTransfer` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:941-947,994-1000`), compared the six-entry UI cycle and auto-detection limit (`:5370-5378,5667-5670,6344-6356`), and enumerated every transfer-size shift consumer (`:2655,2764,2895,3066,5228,5336,6295`). No range validation is applied to the saved field before these shifts. Added OD3788 for width-dependent undefined shift and malformed transfer sizing when the persisted value is outside 0–5. xHCI shared address-zero controller mapping and enumeration routing pass (OD3789 added, 2026-10-18): traced same-PCI-device controller grouping and per-function controller objects (`pcixhci_arospci.c:88-94,194-230`), per-controller root-port scan/reset writes to shared `hu_DevControllers[0]` (`xhci_hcport.c:308-309,776-779`), `xhciPrepareTransfer()` controller selection before route-aware device-context lookup (`xhcidevice.c:59-67`; `xhci_schedule.c:112-120`), and Poseidon's root-port/route-string request population (`poseidon.library.c:4507-4518`). `USB::NewDevice()` holds the bus driver's enumeration lock, but the separate per-controller port task updates the shared mapping outside that lock. Added OD3789 for conditional wrong-controller selection if another function's root-port scan/reset overwrites slot zero during address-zero enumeration. No hardware or request was used. Source-only.


AHIRecord FLAC bitmath active-caller precondition pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): rechecked the four helper bodies in `workbench/tools/AHIRecord/FLAC/bitmath.c` against all maintained C call sites. Both Golomb helper call families in `bitreader.c`/`bitwriter.c` are under `#if 0` and are not selected execution paths. Active encoder/decoder calls to `ilog2(order)` use an LPC order constrained positive at the selected call sites; `stream_encoder.c`'s block-size logarithm is reached after nonzero block-size validation. `fixed.c` calls `ilog2(err)` only after its caller has a positive residual error and the helper also returns before logarithms when `err <= n`; its intermediate rbps is asserted positive before the second logarithm. The partition estimator explicitly substitutes 1 when `rmax` is zero (`stream_encoder.c:3894`). Signed wide helper's negative branch increments before negation, avoiding direct negation of the minimum signed value. This targeted pass closes the helper preconditions for selected callers; broader FLAC encoder/decoder review remains open. No audio was encoded or decoded; source-only.


BWFM auto-join/S2_OFFLINE transition ordering check (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `S2_ONLINE` through synchronous `try_join()`/`BWFMJoin()` and its final `unit->online = TRUE` store against `S2_OFFLINE`'s `FALSE` store/read flush/event sequence (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:880-908,1660-1672`; `bwfm_init.c:2349-2357,2504-2577`). The source admits BeginIO requests can overlap from separate clients, so an external concurrent S2_OFFLINE can complete while S2_ONLINE is blocked in the auto-join and then be overwritten by the late online store. However, the selected AROSTCP up/down path holds its `splimp()` semaphore across its synchronous S2_ONLINE/S2_OFFLINE DoIO (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:620-645,849-866,878-913`; `kern/kern_synch.c:474-499`), so no selected same-stack ordering trigger was established. `S2_OFFLINE` caller semantics for independent direct SANA-II clients are not documented in the checked sources; retained as an external concurrency/API-contract question rather than a new finding. Related but distinct existing OD3783 covers a write already blocked on TX credits when offline returns. No request or radio was used; source-only.


BWFM worker-start findings reconciled to detailed report (OD3595/OD3596, 2026-10-18): verified both process-creation results remain unchecked (bwfm_dev.c:615-640), firmware success is published before worker startup (:778-823), DOS returns NULL on process-creation error (rom/dos/createnewproc.c:62-70), and Open returns success despite missing workers (:1157-1177). Direct consumers are unique: bwfm_pump drains BWFMRxFrame (:454-496), while bwfm_ctrl alone runs do_associate (:583-609,1502-1532). Confirmed queue_associate accepts/publishes the job without a control task (:1471-1492) and later opens skip worker startup when fw_loaded is true (:733-735). Restored separate OD3595 and OD3596 detailed entries and changed the index from one grouped summary to two linked findings. No allocation failure or network request was induced. Source-only.

MassStorage one-sector fake-geometry termination pass (OD3799 added, 2026-10-18): traced READ CAPACITY last-LBA semantics into `dg_TotalSectors`, checked class default patch flags and the `TD_GETGEOMETRY` dispatch, then followed `nFakeGeometry()` factorization/fallback (`massstorage.class.c:912,1341-1346,2111-2115,2163-2205,2363-2374,2558-2562`). One sector produces a zero LBA, the fallback decrements total sectors from one to zero, and the next iteration shifts zero forever in the even-factor loop. Added OD3799 to the report and index. No device or request was used; source-only.

MassStorage START_STOP command completion recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): read `nStartStop()` and traced its normal BeginIO path (`dev.c:203-209,245-267`) through worker dispatch/reply (`massstorage.class.c:1348-1353`) and the startup-only UFI call (`:1315-1320`). BeginIO initializes `io_Error` before queueing; the helper sets it on transport error, and successful callers therefore return the initialized zero. The startup temporary request ignores the returned status. The SimpleSCSI early-success branch likewise receives initialized `io_Error` for BeginIO callers. No independent completion-status bug established. No request or USB device was used; source-only.

MassStorage large-block READ/WRITE emulation and request-result pass (OD3790 rechecked; no new finding, 2026-10-18): reread all of `nRead64Emul()` and `nWrite64Emul()` with `nRead64()`/`nWrite64()` dispatch, block-size discovery fallback, `devBeginIO()` initialization and the unit-worker reply path (`massstorage.class.c:1355-1379,2645-2881,2883-3000,3012-3031`; `dev.c:203-210,245-267`). Reconfirmed OD3790: emulation helpers can return allocation failure without setting `io_Error`, while the worker ignores return values; normal CMD_READ/CMD_WRITE zero `io_Actual` before dispatch. Transport errors do update `io_Error`; no second result-propagation defect established. The functions were read in full, but direct-SCSI and block-size assumptions are tracked separately under OD3791/OD3798. No USB device, allocation failure or request was exercised; source-only.

MassStorage non-emulated write and seek path recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): read complete `nWrite64()` and `nSeek64()` bodies and compared their dispatch, offset conventions, CDB fields, errors and byte counts with `nRead64()` (`massstorage.class.c:3003-3169,1355-1379`). Non-emulated writes mirror read chunking, preserve the 64-bit high LBA for WRITE(16), update partial completion after each successful transport, and store transport errors before worker reply. Seek uses SEEK(10) and therefore only submits the low 32-bit LBA when the high offset field is nonzero. No maintained caller was found that uses this command as range validation or relies on its result to address later data I/O, so the source pass did not establish a distinct caller-visible defect. Unaligned paths share the recorded rounded-block-shift concern OD3798. No device or request was used; source-only.

MassStorage UAS endpoint and stream setup/teardown pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `nUasCollectEndpoints()` descriptor length/type checks, endpoint direction/transfer selectors, endpoint completeness return, and `nUasInitStreams()` fallback/cleanup through `nAllocMS()` success and `nFreeMS()` teardown (`massstorage.class.c:1436-1557,1559-1643,1665-1695,1815-1835,1878-1885`). Pipe-usage descriptors read byte 2 only after a three-byte minimum; class-specific endpoint descriptors read byte 3 only after a four-byte check. Partial stream setup calls `nUasDisableStreams()`, which closes any open stream and resets both endpoint stream bases; inability to enable streams leaves UAS on its non-stream pipe path. No additional endpoint or stream-ownership defect established. Descriptor semantics from external USB specifications and host-controller behavior remain outside this source-only pass. No device or stream was used.

MassStorage removable-task startup retry pass (OD3800 added, 2026-10-18): traced `nMSTask()` start conditions and one-shot `ncm_ForceRTCheck` clear through `nStartRemovableTask()` and `nAllocRT()` failure cleanup, then identified the shared task’s periodic media/change-count/automount work (`massstorage.class.c:1041-1068,1322-1335,1413-1414,3910-4192`). A failed spawn or timer/port/request setup wakes the waiter and returns FALSE, but the LUN task ignores it and waits without a startup retry; fixed-media forced mounting is lost and removable polling waits for another signal. Added OD3800. No task, timer, device, or media event was exercised; source-only.

MassStorage MODE SENSE page-length accounting follow-up (2026-10-18, caller consequence confirmed 2026-10-22): rechecked `nGetModePage()` from the 255-byte zero-fill and MODE SENSE response through block-descriptor advance and completeness validation (`massstorage.class.c:1913-1927,1953-2005`) against `nGetGeometry()` page 0x03/0x04/0x05 consumers and its `nFakeGeometry()` fallback (`:2394-2454,2558-2562`). The helper subtracts `res[3]` after advancing `res` by the original descriptor length, so the remaining-length value is based on the page body byte rather than the descriptor length. This can falsely reject a valid geometry page or accept a short page; the selected geometry readers use the in-bounds, initially zeroed 255-byte array and then either decline unusable fields or fall back to later mode pages/synthetic geometry. This pass alone did not establish a distinct caller-visible consequence; the 2026-10-22 geometry recheck then connected the accepted truncated-page state to OD3797's zero-head division path. No SCSI response or device was used; source-only.


Bluetooth class registration allocation-failure trace (OD3801, 2026-10-18): followed `btAddClass()`'s class-record and two string allocations through enqueue/publication, then traced config parsing into `btClassScan()` and forced device/service binding comparisons (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:72-88,303-310,337-345,379-390`; `config.c:647-661,763-764`; `bluetooth.library.c:870-882`). A successful class-record allocation followed by failed class-name copy leaves `bc_ClassName` NULL in the class list; configured forced binding compares its owner with that pointer using `strcmp`. Added OD3801. The independently unchecked full-path copy lacks the same demonstrated dereference and is not separately promoted. No allocation failure or scan was run; source-only.

Bluetooth event-handler removal lifecycle recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): re-read the exact `btRemEventHandler()` body and its BTCtrl, Preferences cleanup, and event-task stop callers (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:688-710,937-941`; `shellcommands/BTCtrl.c:163`; `prefs/ActionClass.c:1689`). The method acquires and releases `bt_ReentrantLock` exactly once, removes the handler while synchronized with `btSendEvent`, replies to queued messages, then frees the hook; the event task clears its stored hook after removal. No duplicate semaphore acquisition or separate stale-hook path was found. This corrects the initial suspicion from a truncated/combined source read. No event handler or concurrent send/remove was run; source-only.


Bluetooth loader FORM-length boundary expansion (OD3765, 2026-10-18): rechecked the existing short-length header overwrite against the upper end of the 32-bit length domain and Preferences Import (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/config.c:146-157`; `prefs/ActionClass.c:982-988`). Besides lengths 0–3, values `0xfffffff9`–`0xffffffff` wrap `len + 8` to 1–7 bytes before the same 12-byte header copy. Kept this under OD3765 because both ranges are the same allocation/header-size defect; removed the duplicate OD3802 entry. `AllocPooled(0)` returns NULL, so `0xfffffff8` is not included. No malformed file or allocation was used. Source-only.


Bluetooth HCI event parser and transport-bound pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read the complete selected event path in `hwtask.c` (`bNameReqComplete`, `bHandleInquiryResult`, `bHandleLEMeta`, `bHandleEvent`) and `hwconn.c::bConnHandleEvent`, then traced the event header/command-completion parsers and iterator bounds in `rom/bluetooth/stack/{protocols/hci/hci.c,core/controller/command_queue.c}`. Each fixed-field event branch checks the minimum parameter length before indexed reads; inquiry result count arithmetic is bounded by the one-byte count, and extended advertising data is clamped to remaining event bytes before parsing. The three `bHandleEvent` call sites pass the HCI declared event size from a fixed-size `BTHCIEventMsg`. The selected H:4 receiver first reassembles a complete packet from its event length byte and copies no more than the fixed event structure; the USB class fills/retries to the declared payload length before posting; virtual HCI caps payload length at 255 before copying (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bluetooth/h4bthci/h4bthci_unit.c:31-52,70-134,150-184`; `rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/bluetooth.class.c:682-762`; `rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:47-68`). No independent memory-bound or malformed-event consequence was established. The HCI connection-state machine's non-event paths, transport hardware behavior, and real controller responses remain open; no event or device was used. Source-only.

Bluetooth ACL TX request and credit accounting follow-up (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread the complete selected `bStartACLWrite()` queue walk and `bHandleDevReply()` reply path, then traced controller credits through the Number Of Completed Packets event and selected H:4, USB, and virtual-HCI `BTCMD_WRITEACL` implementations (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2619-2678,2722-2770`; `hwconn.c:2992-3024`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bluetooth/h4bthci/h4bthci_unit.c:237-248,299-304`; `rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/bluetooth.class.c:774-788,887-893`; `rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:505-524`). The stack decrements a bearer credit when submitting a write and replenishes credits only from controller completion events; transport-error replies clear the request slot, count the error, and continue the queue without restoring a credit. This is a potential lost-credit path if a failed transport write was not accepted by the controller, but the selected USB completion API does not establish acceptance semantics for partial/error transfers, and H:4 only reports errors for invalid ownership/arguments or a persistently full FIFO (the latter can occur after a partial write). No independent user-visible credit-loss finding is promoted without a demonstrated transport-error case where the controller does not issue completion. The BT request/reply and event-accounting slice is now read; external transport completion semantics and HCI controller behavior remain open. No device, request, or forced transport error was used; source-only.

Bluetooth ACL queue versus connection teardown (OD3802 added, 2026-10-18): traced `bSendACLPacket()` queue insertion and handle storage through credit/slot stalls, `bConnDown()` freeing the connection, the sole non-shutdown queue drains, and later reply/completion-driven `bStartACLWrite()` dispatch (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:140-163,1019-1121,2992-3024,4091-4111`; `hwtask.h:170-177`; `hwtask.c:2633-2677`). A queued packet survives connection teardown; when the queue is next serviced, a missing handle lookup falls through to the classic credit pool and the packet is still submitted. Added OD3802 for post-disconnect stale ACL transmission, with delivery to a different peer explicitly conditional on controller handle reuse. No connection, queue pressure, or handle reuse was exercised; source-only.

Bluetooth disconnect versus connection-specific HCI callback lifetime pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): audited every `bConnDown()` caller and every `bSubmitCmd()` callback registration that carries a `BtHWConn *`. `bConnectStatusCB` is the only connection-specific HCI command completion callback; it is attached to Create Connection commands (`hwconn.c:1134-1145,1148-1204`). The command queue removes its outstanding slot and timeout before invoking the callback (`rom/bluetooth/stack/core/controller/command_queue.c:5-30,33-52`), and its default five-second timeout is shorter than `bConnTick()`'s twenty-second connection-attempt teardown (`command_queue.h:28-29`; `hwconn.c:3965-3994`). The five-second queue timeout retires a missing-response callback before the twenty-second connection-attempt timeout. Relative ordering of a successful Create Connection command response and the subsequent connection event relies on the HCI controller event contract, which was not independently checked in this source-only pass. The other command callbacks use the longer-lived `BtHWCore`; connection-owned L2CAP/SDP/GATT/SMP callbacks are driven by that connection's event/tick processing and no separate deferred callback source was established after removal. No extra connection-pointer callback use-after-free was established in this slice; event-ordering contract remains an explicit external gap. No command response or disconnect was run; source-only.

Bluetooth dual-bearer encryption-state consistency pass (OD3803 added, 2026-10-18): traced the separate BR/EDR and LE connection slots, per-link `cn_Encrypted` fields, Classic Connection Complete encryption state, both encryption-change event variants, device flag updates, partial disconnect publication, and public attribute packing (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:856-862,1062-1077,2872-2907,3028-3046`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:1326`; public declaration `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/include/libraries/bluetooth.h:137`). Classic Connection Complete writes `cn_Encrypted` without synchronizing the device flag; later encryption events overwrite one shared `BDFF_ENCRYPTED` flag without checking the other connection, and `bConnDown()` leaves it unchanged when the second bearer remains connected. Added OD3803 for inaccurate public `BDA_IsEncrypted` under dual-bearer transitions. Searched the repository for in-tree consumers and found none; caller impact is through the public API. No connection or event was run; source-only.

Bluetooth unpair versus in-progress Classic pairing (OD3804 added, 2026-10-18): traced public `btUnpairDevice()` and the selected Preferences stored-config removal caller through `BTPRI_UNPAIR`, connection disconnect submission, Authentication Complete, Encryption Change, `bPairingDone()`, Link Key Notification, and device config serialization (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:1506-1517`; `rom/bluetooth/prefs/ActionClass.c:904-914`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:2224-2252,3036-3049,3094-3104,3154-3170,3561-3577`). Unpair clears keys but leaves the active connection pairing state and callbacks intact; successful completion can set bonded/registered again and save the record after the unpair caller returns. Added OD3804 with the required pre-disconnect event ordering explicit. No pairing, unpair, or controller event was run; source-only.


Bluetooth connection teardown and ACL credit follow-up (2026-10-18): re-read `bConnDown()`, `bFreeHWEndpoint()`, `bConnUp()`, L2CAP endpoint callbacks, `bStartACLWrite()`, and the Number Of Completed Packets branch. Confirmed the queued ACL packet persistence and dispatch behavior already documented as OD3802; queued writes retain the handle and payload but are not removed by connection teardown. Examined whether a completion arriving after handle teardown can mis-credit the independent LE pool: current code falls back to BR/EDR when `bFindConnByHandle()` returns NULL, but the Bluetooth Core HCI specification requires no Number Of Completed Packets notification after the disconnection event invalidates the handle, so that timing is not credited as a separate defect ([Core Specification HCI functional specification](https://www.bluetooth.com/wp-content/uploads/Files/Specification/HTML/Core-54/out/en/host-controller-interface/host-controller-interface-functional-specification.html)). Endpoint queues are flushed and endpoint callback contexts freed in the same hardware-task event path; manager state is embedded in the connection and is no longer reached through the connection lookup after teardown. Remaining: broader connection setup/failure, retry/timer and cancel lifetimes, complete endpoint caller census, SDP/GATT client state/ownership, data-buffer contracts, and transport/runtime behavior. No connection or controller event was run; source-only.

Bluetooth connection creation and retry slice (2026-10-18): read the connection allocator/up/down paths, create-command status callback, BR/EDR and LE command parameter setup, one-at-a-time connect scheduler, explicit/automatic bearer selection, LE advertisement wait/fallback, device-gone disconnect, Classic bonded auto-connect backoff, and connection tick timeouts (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:891-1132,1134-1427,3910-4083`). Bluetooth SMP crypto implementation and random-source pass (OD3808 added, 2026-10-18): read the full 263-line `rom/bluetooth/stack/core/security/smp_crypto.c`, its public header, and all of `test_smp_crypto.c` without running tests. The Bluetooth Core RNG requirement is linked in OD3808. The documented logical AND/NAND/ANDNOT/OR and bitwise AND/NAND/ANDNOT/OR/XOR map to their corresponding implementation forms. Divide-by-zero is explicitly skipped. Signed division's LONG_MIN/-1 boundary was not credited as a new finding because this pass did not establish a supported in-tree or normal GUI path that supplies LONG_MIN. Other BTHID action families, async action-message lifetime and full HID caller/configuration review remain open. No action or variable mutation was run; source-only.

BTHID queued-action release caller cross-check (OD3465 strengthened, 2026-10-18): traced Bluetooth core `BEHMB_SERVICEGONE` through `btReleaseSvcBinding()` to BTHID's wait-for-HID-task and binding free (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:881-893`; `bthid.class.c:294-348`). The dispatcher queue is separate and its records retain binding/action pointers (`:4883-4902,5488-5502,6365-6371`); neither service release nor task teardown drains/waits for that dispatcher work. This confirms peer service removal as a selected release route for the existing conditional stale-action finding. No disconnect or scheduling interleaving was run; source-only.


Optional ROM USB HID variable-operation symmetry pass (OD3462/OD3548/OD3552 expanded, 2026-10-18): compared the remaining exposed operation cases across both `HUA_VARIABLES` switches and their GUI tables. The USB HID handler also lacks `HUAT_ASSNOT`; it also shifts by unchecked `value`. Its `nch_LocalVars` are unsigned `ULONG`, but `nh_GlobalVars` are signed `LONG`, so OD3552 was expanded only to the USB global target (unsigned local overflow is defined wrap). The matching GUI operation map is at `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:104-112`; handler cases are at `hid.class.c:6238-6311`; target declarations at `hid.h:554,776`. Updated existing shared findings; no duplicate IDs. The USB HID target remains optional and incomplete outside these focused action paths. No operation was run; source-only.


Bluetooth service-release/device-expunge channel-lock cross-check (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `btReleaseSvcBinding()`'s device write lock through the class release callback into BTHID's worker stop and `bFreeHid()` channel abort/wait/free (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:590-603`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:329-348,1030-1043,1142-1157,1260-1288`). `btFreeChannel()` can invoke deferred `bFreeDevice()` when the last device use drops (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:1095-1131`), so checked expunge ordering: public `btFreeDevice()` clears `BDFF_DELEXPUNGE` before releasing bindings, while the `btRemHardware()` path releases bindings before calling internal `bFreeDevice()` (`objects.c:117-157,409-443`). In those selected orders, the callback's channel teardown does not reach the deferred-expunge reacquisition while another task holds the device write lock. Hardware `BTPRI_CLOSECHANNEL` handling also updates endpoint use and replies without acquiring that device lock (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:3678-3699`). No independent deadlock established in these paths; other external release callers and hardware shutdown interleavings remain open. No channel or disconnect was run; source-only.

USB mass-storage large-block emulation allocation-failure propagation pass (OD3823 added, 2026-10-18): traced `nRead64()`/`nWrite64()` emulation dispatch into both `*64Emul()` staging allocation failures, then followed the helper return through `nMSTask()` and `devBeginIO()` request initialization (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:2676-2683,2785-2792,2902-2915,3073-3086,1355-1380`; `dev.c:191-205`).
