Read `nVerifyAudioStreamDevice()`, `usbAttemptInterfaceBinding()`, `usbForceInterfaceBinding()`, and `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:166-390`) against the selected Poseidon class-scan/release entry points. The verifier's AudioControl header version and `bInCollection` reads precede descriptor-extent validation; these remain OD3168/OD3171, and no separate acceptance-path defect was established. Publication-before-startup failure remains OD3209; free-unit selection/publication across independent scans remains OD3230. The allocation-failure `Permit()` without a matching local `Forbid()` remains OD3229, with the selected Poseidon caller's task nesting and consequence already documented there. Release removes the record before signaling and waiting for the worker to clear `nch_Task`; the reviewed ordering did not establish a separate lifetime defect beyond those findings and the selected RTIso/device-removal coverage in OD3177/OD3206. Descriptor backing lifetime, external concurrent forced-binding clients, and actual worker scheduling remain unverified. No interface or device was used. Source-only.


## Deneb DMA interrupt-to-worker handoff and bounds follow-up (2026-10-18; no additional finding)

Re-read the DMA setup and state transitions in `uhwLevel6Int()`, `uhwDMATask()`, and `uhwHandleDMAInt()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4240-4330,4996-5260,5270-5403`), including ATL completion updates at `:2110-2418`. Hardware DMA completion is acknowledged in the level-6 handler and queued to the per-unit task; the task calls the common completion routine only while `hu_DMAPTD` is non-NULL. The NODMA build instead signals that same task when software copies are ready. One DMA is active per unit (`:4250-4255`), so the single-bit signal does not by itself demonstrate lost completion coalescing in the reviewed path. Large IN transfers select DMA only for longword-aligned request length and data address; OUT requires aligned address and rounds each DMA copy to a longword, matching OD3578/OD3585's caller-buffer tail concern (`:4250-4264,4314-4321`). IN `iouh_Actual` is increased from the PTD's completed transfer count before the DMA state machine decides whether to continue or retire the PTD (`:2127-2141`); the DMA completion handler's rounded actual-minus-offset calculation therefore had no supported underflow path in the traced selected flow. Existing abort/cache ordering findings OD3584 and OD3704 remain applicable. This pass did not verify controller interrupt timing, DMA cache guarantees, or abort interleavings during the worker handoff; no transfer or device was run. Source-only.

NVMe PRP list-page translation contract cross-check (2026-10-18; no new OD): revisited `nvme_initprp()`'s chaining pointers and list-page DMA mapping against the selected PC, Raspberry Pi 5, and OpenSBI backends. The generic PC `CPUtoPCI` returns identity for a direct bus (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:134-144`), and x86 `CachePreDMA` is coherent identity (`rom/exec/cachepredma.c:45-77`); the BCM2712 backend returns an inbound-window PCI address or its failure sentinel (`driverclass.c:278-294`); the RISC-V PCIDT backend translates addresses inside its configured remap VA window and otherwise returns identity (`pcidt_driverclass.c:867-878`), while its selected Zicbom hook performs cache maintenance and returns the same address (`cpu_init.c:104-129`). The PRP list pages are independently passed through `CachePreDMA` before their DMA mapping is appended (`nvme_prp.c:192-215`); chained entries are translated from their CPU address through `CPUtoPCI` (`:172-182`). No discrepancy was established for these selected direct/remap-window contracts. External PCI drivers with non-identity/non-windowed DMA mappings, arbitrary caller buffers outside the mapped range, and physical contiguity remain unverified; the existing conditional OD2359 arithmetic candidate and its caller qualification are unchanged. No hardware or transfer was used; source-only.

PCI xHCI DMA helper caller recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): followed `xhciQueuePayloadTRBs()` through `xhciPrepareDMABuffer()` into `xhciQueueData_IO()` and the ring writer (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_schedule.c:47-99,327-367`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:915-960,1065-1128`). The helper's returned pointer and current `dmalen` are passed directly to the TRB builder, which emits one or more sequential TRBs covering exactly that length; successful setup records the bounce allocation and direction, while queue failure releases the bounce buffer. Reconciled selected Exec hooks: generic x86 identity, AArch64 native identity translator, and RISC-V Zicbom identity/unchanged-length; no selected hook shortens the length in this checkout. Thus the generic API's possible translated address/shortened extent is not a demonstrated defect for these checked target paths. External DMA mappings, caller buffer ownership/cache-line sharing, and completion/teardown remain open under the existing coverage rows. No USB transfer or device was used; source-only.

Realtek8180 `CreateUnit`/`DeleteUnit` staged-allocation and USB caller recheck (OD3260/OD3269 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): reconciled the unit allocation stages, failure cleanup, task start and selected `CreateUSBUnit`/`DeleteUSBUnitInternal` callers (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/unit.c:105-417`; `usb.c:116-133,242-290,382-410`; `task.h:27-59`). The only maintained `CreateUnit` caller passes the static `unit_tags` containing all ten required hooks; the partial-missing-hook path would reach `DeleteUnit` with a NULL `FreeDMAMem`, but no selected caller supplies that malformed set, so it is not promoted. Once the hook table validates, partially allocated DMA entries are safe to release through the selected `FreeDMAMemHook` -> `FreeVec`, whose public implementation explicitly accepts NULL (`rom/exec/freevec.c:27-28,47-49`). Reconfirmed OD3260: after stack allocation and assignment to `tc_SPLower`, failed `AddUnitTask` leaves `UNITF_TASKADDED` clear, so `DeleteUnit` frees the task structure but skips the stack release (`unit.c:288-303,354-364`). Reconfirmed OD3269: `UnitTask` unconditionally calls `unit->removal_function` on the signaled removal path (`:2694-2699`), while a repository-wide search finds no assignment to that callback; USB `ReleaseBindingHook` can signal the task after unit publication (`usb.c:670-689`). The `card_inserted_signal` path likewise has no producer in this driver, so it is not a selected independent trigger. `InitialiseAdapter` failure sets `UNITF_HAVEADAPTER` before its result is tested; the ensuing cleanup calls `DeinitialiseAdapter`, whose selected body only writes the LED/GPIO off values (`unit.c:239-245,402-415`), and no distinct harmful cleanup consequence was established. No allocation failure, task, USB device, or removal was exercised; source-only.

AR5416 reset-result caller cross-check (2026-10-18; no new finding): confirmed the full reset body's failure paths (`hal/ar5416/ar5416_reset.c:117-190,237-257,275-280,359-360,407-411`) set `HAL_STATUS` and return `AH_FALSE`; the successful path returns `AH_TRUE`. The selected function is installed by `ar5416_attach.c:84` and called from `unit.c:788`, where `ConfigureAdapter()` discards both the boolean and status and proceeds to transmit-power/receive setup, as captured by OD3292. This is the same result-handling defect already recorded, not a new reset-specific candidate. The `(HAL_CHANNEL_INTERNAL *)chan` cast at `ar5416_reset.c:207` remains valid for the shared leading channel fields per `ah_internal.h:126-129`; no cast finding. Calibration/register semantics and broader caller/platform coverage remain open. Source-only.

AR5416 target-power candidate recheck (OD3875 retained, 2026-10-18): verified `fbin2freq(AR5416_BCHAN_UNUSED, ...)` returns the sentinel value 255 unchanged (`hal/ah_eeprom_v14.c:232-241`). Normal channel frequencies exceed 255, so the initial comparison at `ar5416_reset.c:1713/1773` is false for an empty table; the scan exits with `i == 0`, and the fallback reads `powInfo[i - 1]` at `:1728/1788`. V14 parser acceptance and selected power-table call paths were already traced in OD3875. Candidate remains valid and conditional on an EEPROM table with no populated piers. No EEPROM or hardware was used. Source-only.

AR9280 per-chain periodic calibration cross-check (OD3944 added, 2026-10-18): traced `ah_setAntennaSwitch` installation and fixed-B mask assignment through reset's calibration-chain register, percal mask replacement/counting, and IQ/ADC-gain/ADC-DC post-processing. For RX mask `0x2`, the framework passes `numChains == 1`, while all three post-processors loop over index 0 and access chain-0 sample/register slots. The selected unit calls `ah_perCalibration()` (`unit.c:796`) but repository search found no caller of `ah_setAntennaSwitch`; finding is conditional on an external client selecting fixed B. No hardware or calibration was run. Source-only.

AR5416 ADC DC signed-arithmetic pass (OD3945 added, 2026-10-18): traced signed `HAL_CAL_SAMPLE.s` collection into the post-processor's `uint32_t` I temporaries and subtraction, multiplication, division, mask and register write. AR9280 uses one periodic sample with `PER_MIN_LOG_COUNT == 2`, yielding divisor 128; Q operands are signed. A negative I even-minus-odd delta not divisible by 64 yields a 9-bit correction one count more negative than signed truncation would; expected hardware rounding is not documented, so functional confidence is medium. Checked the callback installation and selected unit periodic-calibration call. No hardware or calibration was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II signal-table/release recheck (OD3627-OD3629 reconciled, 2026-10-18): re-read selected `driver_sana2.c` init/deinit and `eloop_amiga.c` registration/wait paths. Confirmed OD3629: failed `realloc()` returns -1, caller ignores it, and the port bit is omitted from `eloop_run()`'s mask; async requests can be queued while the supplicant reports a valid driver. Confirmed OD3628: the separately allocated event request is waited but not freed. OD3627 remains conditional: no unregister exists and dynamic removal frees the callback context, but the checked-in config has `CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE` disabled and no live-removal caller; normal global teardown follows `eloop_run()` and is not itself a stale-callback window. The remaining trigger requires an external live-removal caller and later reuse of that signal bit. No allocation or interface lifecycle was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II request/scan teardown recheck (OD3694/OD3695 refined, 2026-10-18): confirmed the request-overlap trigger through the selected hard-MAC CONNECT event: the separate `S2_ONEVENT` callback dispatches `EVENT_ASSOC`, the hard-MAC supplicant handler queries BSSID, and `get_bssid()` rewrites the same base request still submitted for `S2_GETNETWORKS` (`driver_sana2.c:133-153,159-210,802-829,872-875`; `events.c:1135-1145`). Prism2 stores that IORequest pointer in its scan queue (`prism2/request.c:1631-1648`); the callback later switches on its current command, so a query completion can be misclassified and the scan result may never be delivered. For OD3695, confirmed shutdown cleanup cancels only the scan timer, not the active device request; SANA-II provides no `cancel_scan` op. Deinit aborts/waits for the base request but never deletes the pool; key clearing may overwrite the request field holding its handle. Normal shutdown with an outstanding scan is sufficient; external live removal remains another trigger. No request, scan, or interface was exercised. Source-only.


WirelessManager SANA-II association SSID ownership recheck (OD3946 added, 2026-10-18): traced the temporary SSID allocation through `CloneTagItems`, synchronous `S2_SETOPTIONS`, tag-list release, and the selected `.associate` callback caller. The cloned tags are freed but the `os_zalloc(MAX_SSID_LEN + 1)` buffer is not; each successful buffer allocation is leaked on both request success and failure paths. This is distinct from OD3626's suppressed callback errors. No association or allocation was run; source-only.

USB Audio Type I frame-size validation pass (OD3947 added, 2026-10-18): traced `bSubframeSize` from the public descriptor layout (`compiler/include/devices/usb_audio.h:385-395`) through mode classification, `nam_FrameSize` assignment, AHI mode registration and `nSelectAudioMode()` rate-limit calculation (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1140-1217,1929-1986,2037-2046,3134-3166`). Added OD3947 for zero-size division by zero and the one-byte/16-bit mismatch that selects the 8-bit converter; both are separate from OD3171 descriptor extent and OD3172 empty-rate findings. No device or allocation was used; source-only.

USB Audio class-config reload and GUI task exit follow-up (OD3200 rechecked; no new finding, 2026-10-18): read `nLoadClassConfig()`, `nOpenCfgWindow()`, GUI startup, save/reload event dispatch, and `nGUITaskCleanup()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2130-2157,2160-2182,2185-2376,2370-2394`) against all three in-file reload callers (`:106,325,496`) and Poseidon's selected `psdSpawnSubTask()` paths (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1434-1509`). GUI creation, library-open failures and task schedules were not induced. Source-only.

USB HID Wacom zero-length report follow-up (OD3921 expanded, 2026-10-18): rechecked the interrupt completion order against the full Wacom parser and the default tablet action path (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:899-919,1599-1817,4348-4378,4940-4949,991`). The worker calls `nParseWacom()` before the `buflen > 0` generic-parser guard and reuses `nch_EPInBuf`; an empty transfer after a recognized Intuos-family packet leaves the old report ID in byte zero. The Intuos-family branch can return TRUE from this stale ID, process the stale synthetic report, and bypass the documented ZLP-ignore path. `HUA_ALWAYS` tablet mappings run even for unchanged values, and the worker flushes after each completion, so repeated stale actions are a supported consequence. Expanded OD3921 and the AROS.md summary; this is the same unchecked Wacom packet-length boundary, not a separate finding. No device, packet, or event was used; source-only.
USB HID SET_REPORT failure/retry trace (OD3948 added, 2026-10-18): followed `HUA_OUTPUT`/`HUA_FEATURE` state mutation into the report touched flags and `nFlushEvents()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6068-6137,6365-6427`), checked the synchronous pipe error contract (`rom/usb/docs/poseidon.doc:1105-1145`), and verified that unchanged input values do not normally invoke actions again (`hid.class.c:4940-4949`). Confirmed output actions are reachable from built-in tablet LED mappings (`:4120-4150`) and output/feature actions are configured in the HID Control GUI (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:1111-1160,2224-2260`). Added OD3948: after a failed transfer the action's updated value remains, but its touched flag is cleared, so the report is not retried absent a later action that touches it. Separate USB HID implementation from Bluetooth finding OD3473. No device, report, or transfer was used; source-only.

USB Audio unit-graph traversal and volume-resolution recheck (OD3164/OD3165 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): read `nFindAudioUnit`, `nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, `nFlowDown`, `nFlowDownToUSBSink`, `nFlowUpToUSBSource`, `nFlowUp`, `nFindLogVolume`, and the Stage 2–5 traversal in `nExamineAudioUnits` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:782-919,1312-1367,1371-1620`). USB Audio Feature Unit decoding and duplex-pair follow-up (OD3170/OD3191 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): re-read AudioControl Stage 5 Feature Unit handling and the full recording/playback sibling-matching loops (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1673-1809,1840-1923`). The following `nAddAudioModes()` pass publishes playback modes and their sibling-linked input capabilities. USB Audio AHI mode-name allocation/caller trace (OD3949 added, 2026-10-18): traced `nAddAudioModes()` through Poseidon's formatter, AHI database insertion, `AHI_GetAudioAttrs()` and the selected AHI requester (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1942-1987`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1033-1049`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:384-430`; `modeinfo.c:452-459`; `requester.c:1337-1340`). Virtual Bluetooth failed-start unit ownership recheck (OD3950 added, 2026-10-18): traced the device opener's ready wait and failure free (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_device.c:54-76`) through worker prerequisite setup, unconditional early ready signal, and partial-resource cleanup (`vbthci_unit.c:550-571,628-653`). Virtual Bluetooth peer pairing-command minimum-length pass (OD3951 added, 2026-10-18): traced `BTCMD_WRITEHCI`'s actual buffer extent through `vbt_HandleCommand()`'s parameter clamp (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:233-249,495-497`) into all pairing-reply cases in `vbtp_HandleCommand()` (`vbthci_peer.c:859-975`). Bluetooth GATT below-default MTU long-read trace (OD3952 added, 2026-10-18): compared the two-byte response parser and client negotiation/continuation path (`stack/protocols/att/att.c:34-44`; `stack/protocols/gatt/gatt_client.c:60-80,244-278`) with ATT default/request constants (`stack/include/btcore/att.h:46`; `gatt_client.h:45-47`) and the selected HOGP report-map read callback (`stack/profiles/hogp/hogp_client.c:230-247`). The Core Specification says a below-default exchanged MTU leaves ATT_MTU at default 23; current code records a parsed value such as 22, then treats a 22-byte fragment as final because it expects 21. Added OD3952. `core.files` selects this code for the optional `linklibs-btcore` target, but the aggregate is commented out and no in-tree runtime HOGP caller exists beyond host tests. Reviewed the valid 100-byte negotiation test and unsupported-exchange fallback test; neither exercises a below-default value. No runtime test, packet, or device was used. Source-only.

Bluetooth hardware-task startup and shutdown recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): re-read `bOpenHCIDevice()`, `bQueryHCIDevice()`, `bAllocCore()`, `bFreeCore()`, ACL read/write posting and reply handling, `bTick()`, the `bHWTask()` start/ready/error/shutdown path, and the selected `btAddHardware()`/`btRemHardware()` readiness callers (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2416-3100`; `objects.c:80-110,147-181`). H:4 shutdown finding OD2936 caller recheck (2026-10-18; no duplicate): followed the selected startup-posted ACL reads through `bHandleDevReply()` and shutdown (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2601-2612,2722-2755,3013-3017,3050-3076,3082-3086`) into the Raspberry Pi H:4 adapter request switch, `AbortIO`, and `h4bthci_CloseUnit()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bluetooth/h4bthci/h4bthci_unit.c:306-373,447-473`; `h4bthci_device.c:96-115`). USB Audio streaming-format descriptor parser complete-body recheck (OD3171/OD3172/OD3947 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): reread `nExamineAudioDescriptors()` from descriptor lookup through AHI mode publication (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1037-1309,1928-1991`) and compared its data accesses with Poseidon's exact-`bLength` descriptor allocation (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2030-2046`). USB Audio alternate-setting bandwidth-estimate and high-speed transaction-multiplier caller recheck (OD3173 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): traced `nSelectAudioMode()`'s selected endpoint attributes and bandwidth estimate (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3133-3173`) through Poseidon's descriptor decoding (`poseidon.library.c:8464-8486,8528-8553`) and pipe-flag construction (`:4528-4549`). High-speed `wMaxPacketSize` is split into base `pep_MaxPktSize` and `pep_NumTransMuFr`; Poseidon passes the latter as the HCD MULT flag, while USB Audio's estimate uses only base max-packet size. The estimate modifies `nam_MaxFreq`, but the driver's active `subLibGetAttr` implementation returns the frequency list/count and has its min/max cases commented out (`usbaudio.class.c:3918-3937`); mode allocation does not use the adjusted `nam_MaxFreq` to cap its selected rate. Thus no separate user-visible transaction-multiplier defect was established from this estimate alone. The active high-speed interval-unit mismatch, including its max-frequency estimate effect and playback pacing, remains OD3173. No endpoint, pipe, stream, or host controller was exercised. Source-only.

Atheros5000 reset-callback owner lifetime pass (OD3972 added, 2026-10-18): traced registration of the unit-embedded reset callback (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:392-395`; `pci.c:258`), non-supervisor dispatch and completion handshake (`rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:31-38,128-153`), then final `CloseDevice()` into `DeletePCIUnit()`/`DeleteUnit()` (`device.c:537-550`; `pci.c:303-325`; `unit.c:474-523`). `RemResetCallback()` only unlinks; it does not join an already executing callback (`rom/exec/remresetcallback.c:49`). PCI network reset-callback in-flight owner race cross-driver comparison (OD3972 expanded, 2026-10-18): compared the AROS reset-node construction, registration and final-close paths in Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, EtherLink3, NvidiaNet, Prism2 and Rhine (`unit.c` callback `is_Data` setup at `:392-395,:302-305,:392-398,:298-303,:299-304,:304-309`; `pci.c` registration at `:258,:257,:305,:258,:295,:267`; final unlink and DeleteUnit at `pci.c:311-325,307-319,358-369,309-319,347-358,318-328`). All six reset callbacks dereference the unit/HAL during shutdown (`unit.c:2687-2705,1892-1907,2371-2386,1901-1912,2632-2646,1627-1642`), and each `DeleteUnit()` frees the embedded callback owner (`unit.c:522,415,514,412,432,416`). A final `CloseUnit()` removes the callback but has no completion wait for a support task already executing it; ExecSMP `Forbid()` does not serialize against another CPU. HDAudio reset callback teardown race review (OD3973 added, 2026-10-18): HDA's `hc_ResetHandler` is embedded in `HDAData`, registered with `is_Data = hc` after successful hardware setup, and invoked by Exec's non-supervisor reset support task (`workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hda_intern.h:105-116`; `hdaclass.c:219-239,489-497`; `rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:31-38,121-153`). `HDA_Shutdown` unlinks the callback but does not join that task before `HWExit` and freeing CORB/RIRB/stream state; `HDA__Root__Dispose` then frees the instance (`hdaclass.c:504-560,603-608`; `remresetcallback.c:45-49`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-149`). OpenSBI DesignWare UART reset-callback overlap check (2026-10-18; no new OD): followed `DWSerUnit_ResetHandler` through its embedded `unitsdh` callback and normal final-close disposal (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:53-71,203-208,237-265`; `SerialClass.c:90-115`). Exec reset dispatch passes the callback node to a support task, but the current OpenSBI kernel explicitly parks secondary harts until SMP bring-up (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:41-42,773`), and this handler's body does not yield or wait. The cross-CPU dispose overlap from OD3972/GD5324 is therefore not established for this selected target; no separate reset race is promoted. The normal close removes the callback before superclass disposal; no UART or reset was run. Source-only.

M68k-Amiga serial HIDD baud/capability boundary cross-check (OD1611 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-18): reread the complete selected `SerialUnitClass.c` body and serial.device parameter caller (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/serial/SerialUnitClass.c:183-397`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:767-783`). The lower advertised baud bound computes to 108, but `SERPER_BAUD` masks oversized divisors before `SetBaudrate`'s maximum check; 108 is therefore another manifestation of OD1611, not a separate capability-only bug. Repository-wide search found no maintained `HIDD_SerialUnit_GetCapabilities()` caller; the capability-method caller contract remains external. No serial request or hardware behavior was run.


USB Audio resume/release lifetime pass (OD3974 added, 2026-10-18): traced `usbDoMethodA(UCM_AttemptResumeDevice)` and `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()` through Poseidon's `psdResumeDevice`/`psdResumeBindings` and `psdHubReleaseIfBinding` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:471-515,344-371,2070-2117`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:3850-3898,3913-3933,6588-6613`; `rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:1422-1425`). Poseidon releases the device lock before its resume traversal, while release clears the binding under that lock and then waits for the Audio worker to delete its message port; the retained resume path dereferences the task port and signals the task without validating either field. Added OD3974 for the conditional stale/NULL port and task access, distinct from OD3971's concurrent AHI `FreeAudio` cleanup. The class record remains partial; its remaining methods, callers, and broader Poseidon lifecycle are open. No device, transfer, resume, release, or schedule was exercised. Source-only.

USB Audio player-frequency zero caller recheck (OD3218 retained, 2026-10-19): traced the AHI public frequency contract and setter dispatch through the subdriver Update/Start calls (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:382-389,946-955,1001-1005`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3693-3772`). Zero is the documented timing-disabled value; `AHIC_PlayerFreq` stores it, skips only AHI's timing-buffer recalculation, and still calls `AHIsub_Update`. USB Audio's update path and playback start divide by `ahiac_PlayerFreq >> 12`, confirming the existing zero-divisor trigger and the separate Start route described by OD3218. No additional finding added. No AHI control, stream, or device was used; source-only.


Deneb DMA completion state-machine and worker pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): read the full `uhwHandleDMAInt()` and `uhwDMATask()` bodies and reconciled each state transition with ATL data completion, DMA-done interrupt signaling, startup and close (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1968-2430,4230-4340,4996-5264,5270-5359,5374-5401`; selected manifest `mmakefile.src:20-39`). In the input path, ATL completion increments the actual count and marks short packets terminal before entering the matching low/high DMA-read completion state; the state machine copies the aligned remainder and frees the PTD only after the required copy finishes. In the output path, the second-buffer prefetch can overlap the active PTD; its completion state either activates the already-prefetched next bank or stages a further bounded chunk, while PTD byte count continues to track unrounded request bytes. The level-6 handler acknowledges the DMA status and signals the worker only while `hu_DMAPTD` is non-NULL; the worker handles a single pending completion signal and exits on Ctrl-C. No independent state-transition defect was established in these bodies. Previously reported rounded OUT-buffer reads, reply/cache ordering, abort cleanup, and worker-lifetime findings remain separate. Hardware/controller timing and remaining NAK/AbortIO overlap cases are still open; no controller, request, DMA transfer, or schedule was run. Source-only.

xHCI root-hub change-bitmap completion race (OD3978, 2026-10-19): traced immediate completion from the device command dispatch to `cmdIntXFerRootHub()` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_dev.c:212-238,uhwcmd.c:1267-1269`). Its existing-bitmap branch copies shared `hu_RootPortChanges` then clears it without exclusion (`uhwcmd.c:1036-1052`); `xhciIntCode()` is an interrupt handler and ORs new change bits into the same field (`xhci_hcd.c:3211-3218,3355-3359`). The later queued-request path does use `Disable()` around delivery and clearing (`uhwcmd.c:1893-1924`), but that does not protect immediate completion. Added OD3978: a distinct port change arriving after the copy and before clear is lost from the hub interrupt bitmap. No transfer or interrupt was run. Source-only.


xHCI root-hub AbortIO completion follow-up (OD3979, 2026-10-19): traced `devAbortIO()` through `cmdAbortIO()` and compared its root-hub queue branch against the controller queue completion branches (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_dev.c:325-329`; `uhwcmd.c:1798-1806` and subsequent queue cases). The root-hub branch removes and reports successful abort without setting the aborted error or replying; the Exec API documents successful AbortIO as setting `IOERR_ABORTED`, with WaitIO still required (`rom/exec/abortio.c:24-35`). Poseidon `hub.class` explicitly aborts its outstanding EP1 request then waits before worker cleanup (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:752-756`); `psdAbortPipe()` documentation also requires the subsequent wait (`rom/usb/docs/poseidon.doc:707-716`). Added OD3979 for pending requests in the optional xHCI root-hub interrupt queue. No request or device was exercised. Source-only.


HDAudio SetupStream zero-count validation pass (OD3980 added, 2026-10-19): traced the complete `SetupStream` allocation/register path through `StartStream` and both selected AHI callers (`workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:844-949`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/main.c:238-240,287-289`; `NVHDMI/main.c:205-207`). Count zero passes the only upper-bound check, creates a zero-entry BDL allocation, skips filling it, writes CBL zero and `bufferCount - 1` to LVI, then returns success; StartStream does not test BufferCount. The Intel HDA specification §3.3.39 defines LVI as the index of the last valid BDL descriptor, confirming the underflow's invalid programming. Selected HDAudio/NVHDMI paths both pass two buffers, so reachability is limited to public external HIDD clients. Added OD3980 and index entry. No controller or stream was run; source-only.

SDSC CMD6 response-layout pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): cross-checked `SDSCSwitch` mode/argument and `SDSCChangeFrequency` word masks (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_sdscunit.c:15-39,43-133`) against the SD Association Physical Layer Simplified Specification v7.10 §4.3.10.4, especially the 512-bit Switch Function Status field map. USB Audio Feature Unit volume-channel pass (OD3981 added, 2026-10-19): traced `nExamineAudioUnits`' master/left/right volume-mask construction and GET_MIN/GET_MAX channel selection into `nAudioTask`'s `UAF_MASTER_VOLUME` writes and the selected `subLibHardwareControl(AHIC_OutputVolume)` path (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:646-679,1740-1800,4090-4128`). OpenSBI PCIDT 64-bit BAR low-address mapping pass (OD3982 added, 2026-10-19): reread the `pcidt_map64bars()` address decode and its `MapPCI` consumer (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:395-469,880-895`). The scanner skips every 64-bit BAR with upper address dword zero before checking whether it lies in the remembered 64-bit PCI window. The PCI BAR memory-type field identifies a 64-bit BAR independently of the assigned address value; an address below 4 GiB can therefore be in a valid 64-bit FDT aperture. `MapPCI` later translates any address in that aperture to `mem64Va`/the remap window and does not check that the BAR span was actually mapped. Added OD3982 for a selected driver dereference of such a BAR; only the final retained 64-bit window remains in scope under OD2567. No matching firmware assignment or hardware was available; source-only.


OpenSBI PCIDT DesignWare 64-bit ATU-span reconciliation (OD3983 added, 2026-10-19): compared `PCIDT_SetupOutboundWindows()`'s low-32-bit ATU limit handling with `pcidt_map64bars()` and `MapPCI` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_access.c:288-340`; `pcidt_driverclass.c:395-469,880-895`). The new outbound region is clipped to the next 4-GiB boundary, while BAR mapping and translation use the complete retained FDT 64-bit window. A BAR beyond that segment is not necessarily forwarded; retained firmware outbound regions may cover some such addresses, so OD3983 is limited to uncovered BARs. The ACPI fallback and ECAM path do not program this DWC outbound ATU path. No matching firmware/ATU state or hardware was available; source-only.

AHCI selected command caller/interleaving pass (2026-10-19; no additional finding): traced every `ahci_ata_cmd`, `ahci_start`, `ahci_issue_pending_commands`, `ahci_port_intr`, and `ahci_poll` call in the selected AHCI source set. SCSI async submitters hold `ap_lock` across setup and `ahci_ata_cmd` (`ahci_scsi.c:564-567,732-734`); `ahci_cam_attach` is called with the port lock held and retains it across probe, while deliberately dropping it only around SIM registration (`ahci_cam_aros.c:336-360`; selected callers `ahci_attach.c:765-778`, `ahci_busclass.c:233-241`). The AROS nonblocking interrupt lock hook always fails, so the hardware interrupt path disables port interrupts and defers completion handling to the worker, which acquires `ap_lock` (`ahci_aros.c:284-286`; `ahci.c:2664-2702`). Polling callers execute `ahci_port_intr(ap, 1)` and active-timeout checks synchronously from `ahci_poll` while in the serialized port context (`ahci.c:2237-2270`); all selected poll calls provide a timeout callback. This closes the selected command-engine submit/completion interleaving slice without establishing a new defect; unrelated CAM adapters, teardown and hardware timing remain open. Source-only; no command or device was exercised.

SANA-II scan completion/result-array layout recheck (OD3976 retained, 2026-10-19): re-read the selected WirelessManager SANA-II scan submission, completion dispatch and `get_scan_results` parser against the public `TagItem` layout and Prism2 `S2_GETNETWORKS` result contract (`driver_sana2.c:183-209,216-309,872-875`; `compiler/include/utility/tagitem.h:19-24`; `prism2/request.c:1600-1654`; `prism2/unit.c:2800-2892`). The failed-request stale fields are reinterpreted as an `IPTR` array; the exact first value depends on 32-bit versus 64-bit `TagItem` layout, so the report now describes the invalid pointer-width read rather than saying the tag alone is the pointer. A previous nonzero result count controls parsing, and the event handler still ignores `io_Error`; no additional finding beyond OD3976. The SANA-II fallback IE allocation is sized from its 16-bit IE length; the no-IE fallback uses the returned SSID's `strlen`, but a selected well-formed Prism2 SSID is limited to the protocol's 32-byte field apart from the already tracked malformed-record copy/termination findings OD3158/OD3189. SANA-II soft-MAC devices Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 do not advertise `S2_GETNETWORKS`, so this particular completion bug does not apply to those two selected soft-MAC configurations. No scan or device was run; source-only.

SANA-II scan-pool failure trigger recheck (OD3630 retained, 2026-10-19): confirmed the pre-submission pool leak can occur after successful `CreatePool()`: non-managed pools can be returned with only the compact pool handle allocated, while the first `AllocPooled()` lazily requests an actual puddle (`rom/exec/createpool.c:113-129,161-198`; `allocpooled.c:87-93`). Refined OD3630's trigger/evidence; no request or memory failure was induced. Source-only.

PCNet32 address-application candidate withdrawal (OD3645, 2026-10-19): rechecked the candidate against the full selected SANA-II state gate. `CmdConfigInterface()` changes the init-block address only when `IFF_CONFIGURED` is clear, then sets that flag (`workbench/devs/networks/pcnet32/handler.c:328-352`); `CmdOnline()` refuses an unconfigured unit and only invokes the driver's `start` when it is not already up (`:650-684`). Therefore the first accepted configuration necessarily precedes the `pcnet32_open()` controller initialization, and later reconfiguration is rejected. The earlier claim that an accepted post-open address update changes only an already-running init block was based on the setter without its caller precondition. Withdraw OD3645; no device or request was used. Source-only.

PCNet32 OD3645 withdrawal correction (2026-10-19): the 2026-10-19 withdrawal note above reversed the actual lifecycle order. `ADD2OPENDEV` invokes the SANA-II Open vector, which calls `unit->start(unit)` before the first accepted `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE`; the latter changes `fep_pcnet_init_block->phys_addr` only, with no controller restart (`workbench/devs/networks/pcnet32/pcnet32_init.c:223-245`; `handler.c:328-352`; `pcnet32.c:286-295,297-350`). The `IFF_CONFIGURED` gate permits this first configuration after Open, and later `S2_ONLINE` does not restart an already-up unit. Restored OD3645 to the detailed report and index, scoped to a client configuring a different station address; the maintained AROSTCP path configures the queried address. The prior withdrawal remains here as audit history but is superseded by this correction. No device or request was used. Source-only.

PC serial shared IRQ ownership recheck (OD2779 expanded; 2026-10-19): reread the PC serial HIDD parent/unit constructors and disposer against the shared COM1/3 and COM2/4 interrupt handlers and the generic serial.device Open/final-Close callers (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialClass.c:25-29,67-115`; `SerialUnitClass.c:60,130-185,243-278,699-755`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:133-184,233-262`). Serial CMD_RESET active-read callback overlap pass (OD3989 added; 2026-10-19): traced reset's active-read reply and local `Disable()` against the complete RBF callback and PC UART receive path (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:567-606`; `serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-93`; `arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:526-549,713-719`; `rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`). The receive callback loads `su_ActiveRead` once, does not acquire `su_Lock`, writes directly to its `io_Data`, and can reply on completion; reset on another ExecSMP CPU clears status and replies the same request without cross-CPU exclusion. Added OD3989 as a separate conditional read-buffer lifetime/double-reply race from OD2388's write callback continuation. Updated detailed report, index and per-file ledger. No request, interrupt or race was run; source-only.


PC/OpenSBI serial receive staging bound recheck (OD836 not promoted; 2026-10-19): reread the PC receive loop and OpenSBI callback/IRQ route (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:524-551,678-695,713-719`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:512-532,727-732`). Both use a 513-byte stack array and increment the receive length until the UART reports no data, with no explicit array bound. The PC setter caps baud at 115200 and both paths drain the UART FIFO synchronously; the source does not establish a receive rate/latency that can refill the FIFO through 513 iterations during one callback. Since OD836 existed only as a coverage reference and not as a detailed report/index finding, removed the claim that it is confirmed and recorded it as an unproven bounds candidate. No serial input or UART was used.


Serial CMD_RESET duplicate-reply consequence recheck (OD3989 qualified; 2026-10-19): traced the second callback `ReplyMsg()` through Exec's implementation (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`). It does not inspect prior reply state; it marks `NT_REPLYMSG` and calls `InternalPutMsg()` again. Qualified the report and index to state duplicate reply-port delivery and continued writes to the returned buffer, leaving caller-specific effects conditional. No reply port or request was used.


PC serial HIDD IRQ-removal lifetime pass (OD3990 added; 2026-10-19): traced selected `AddIntServer`/`RemIntServer` kernel-token handling (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:64-67`; `remintserver.c:52-55`) through generic removal/free, the generic SMP-locked walker and the PC override's unlocked IRQ-chain walk (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:59-73`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:125-142`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:116-131`). Followed PC unit disposal from server removal through `CSD->units[]` clearing, UART shutdown and superclass disposal, plus serial.device final-close disposal (`SerialUnitClass.c:251-276`; `serial_init.c:233-262`). The PC IRQ callback can already have loaded the unit pointer while another CPU removes/frees it; IOAPIC destinations default to CPU0 unless affinity overrides them (`acpi_ioapic.c:408-438`). Added OD3990 as the selected serial-driver lifetime consequence of EK31, distinct from OD2779's shared-handler ownership. No unit close or interrupt was run.


Serial SDCMD_SETPARAMS receive-ring lifetime pass (OD3991 added; 2026-10-19): traced the generic BeginIO semaphore and local interrupt scope through the ring resize (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:321-325,713-750`) against the entire PC receive callback route and ring append path (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:526-551,713-719`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:96-124`). `STATUS_CHANGING_IN_BUFFER` is set and cleared only by the resizing caller; the producer does not test it, take the semaphore, or otherwise join before `FreeMem(OldInBuf, ...)`. AHI preferences unit/mode-list allocation and selected MUI caller pass (OD3992 added, 2026-10-19): traced selected `AHI_MUI` composition (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/Makefile.in:47-52`) through `main()`, `NewSettings()`, `NewUnit()`, `GetUnits()`, `GetModes()`, `AddUnit()`, `List2Array()` and `GetNode()` (`ahi.c:166-170,208-270`; `support.c:703-724,847-857,863-918,924-945,1211-1228`). `GetUnits()`/`GetModes()` return NULL on list-allocation failure, while their selected callers unconditionally pass those results into `List2Array()`, which dereferences `list->lh_Head`; additionally, ignored failures of every default `AddUnit()` can leave an empty list that `NewUnit()` dereferences through a NULL `GetNode()`. Added OD3992 for the conditional AHI preferences crash. The earlier suspected overlong Workbench PUBSCREEN tooltype was not promoted: only the nonselected BGUI/Commodities GUI implementations consume `screenname`; the selected MUI implementation ignores it, and the shipped `Makefile.in` builds only `AHI_MUI`. Caller/event behavior beyond the traced settings update remains open. No app or allocation failure was run; source-only.

AHI MUI unit/mode event and metadata ownership pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): traced selected `ACTID_UNIT`/`ACTID_MODE` notifications through `FillUnit()`, `NewUnit()`, `NewMode()`, `GUINewUnit()` and `GUINewMode()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/gui_mui.c:288-337,985-1003`; `ahi.c:238-446`; `gui_mui.c:317-420`). The MUI mode-off value is `-1` and is preserved as `~0` through `NewUnit()`/`NewMode()`; the event path does not reinterpret it as a valid mode index. The six metadata getter results are static buffers/catalog strings, so `strlen()` inputs are nonnull in the checked helpers; Text class `OM_SET` duplicates `MUIA_Text_Contents` with `StrDup()` before returning (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/text.c:145-176`), so freeing `GUINewMode()`'s temporary buffer after `set()` does not leave the widget pointing at freed storage. A unit with no eligible modes can leave the prior mode's metadata buffers displayed because `NewMode(~0)` does not clear them; this is a stale-information UI case, not promoted in this pass because its practical consequence is limited to the inactive information panel and no incorrect mode is selected or saved by that state alone. Reported OD3992's separate allocation-failure null dereference remains. AHI attribute implementation and driver-specific return-value contracts remain open; no mode or GUI was used.

AHI SoundDT41 update error propagation pass (OD3994 added, 2026-10-19): traced allocation and SetVar failure returns from `UpdateSoundDT41Prefs()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/support.c:435-492`) through the `SaveSettings()` hook (`:1117-1124`) and selected MUI Save/Use event cases (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/gui_mui.c:938-947`). Deneb active non-DMA AbortIO and queue synchronization pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): traced `cmdAbortIO()` across waiting control/interrupt/ISO/bulk/root-hub queues and active ATL/interrupt/ISO PTDs, with `devAbortIO()` setting `IOERR_ABORTED` and invoking `TermIO()` only after a successful removal (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1778-1866`; `dev.c:665-695`). Waiting queue insertion uses local interrupt exclusion before `Cause(hu_SoftInt)` (`uhwcmd.c:815-958`), and each active non-DMA branch clears its hardware PTD, endpoint busy slot, and PTD request before releasing resources; it does not re-reply the request. This pass found no distinct interrupt/ISO abort defect in the selected single-CPU m68k path. Active ATL DMA cleanup remains OD3584; CMD_FLUSH's active-DMA reply/cache ordering remains OD3704; cross-interrupt PTD/controller effects and USB bus reset with live requests remain open. Cross-checked `CMD_RESET`'s documented hardware reset contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:166-191`) against `cmdReset()`/`uhwHWInit()`; the existing OD3583 covers live descriptors being cleared without retiring/replying their requests. No request, controller or reset was exercised. Source-only.

AHI WarpUp ELF32 section-header layout recheck (2026-10-19; no new OD): checked the local `Elf32_Shdr` field order and widths against the ELF32 ABI and the loader's table allocation/indexing (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/elfloader.c:220-231,454-465,538-575`). It contains the standard ten 32-bit fields (40 bytes), including one `sh_entsize`; the table is allocated from `e_shnum * e_shentsize`, and no extra-structure-member/OOB defect is established for standard ELF32 PPC objects. Kept malformed entry-size/table-range validation separate from this false lead; the selected WarpUp loader failure and partial-parse cleanup paths remain OD3996/OD3997. No ELF object was loaded or executed. Source-only.

Deneb aborted-PTD pending-done-bit interleaving check (2026-10-19; no new OD): followed the completion-bit path after active non-DMA AbortIO clears a PTD and returns its slot (`uhwcmd.c:1778-1866`). `uhwHandleFinishedATLs()` consumes each pending bit before transfer scheduling and skips completion when `ptd_IOReq` is NULL (`:2028-2043`); therefore a still-pending bit cannot by itself complete a subsequently queued request in that slot on the selected single-CPU soft-interrupt ordering. Interrupt/ISO completion handlers and hardware-specific clearing semantics remain broader open work. No IRQ or abort was run. Source-only.

USB Audio Feature Unit volume cascade recheck (OD3981 confirmed, 2026-10-19): reread the Feature Unit channel-mask construction and each AHI output/input-gain/monitor-volume write loop (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1712-1762,644-762,4090-4128`). The implementation addresses master, left and right controls independently and writes the same selected dB value to every advertised bit; it uses the range queried from the selected first control. The USB Audio 1.0 specification states that master controls affect all channels and are cascaded after individual channel controls (§3.5.5); its Volume Control request separately addresses each channel (§5.2.2.4.3.2). This confirms that a device exposing both master and per-channel volume controls can apply the same attenuation at both stages, subject to those controls accepting the value. OD3981 remains conditional on the descriptor and ranges; no report/index change or line credit was needed, and no USB device or control request was used. Source-only.

RPiPWM hardware-access caller pass (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced OF pin query from `DriverInit`, GPIO mux setup, firmware mailbox clock enable/rate/release, clock-manager readback/fallback, PWM bias/start ordering, DMA control-block construction and current-level/stop sequence through selected callers (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/RPiPWM/rpipwm-init.c:21-26`; `rpipwm-main.c:164-250,276-342,385-430`). A malformed `brcm,pins` count above the four-entry limit currently leaves fallback pins active, but the external firmware-property validity contract is not established, so no candidate is promoted. Raspberry Pi AHI worker-task/IRQ lifetime pass (OD4001 added, 2026-10-19): compared the PWM, HDMI and I²S DMA callbacks' `slavetask` check/`Signal()` calls with each worker's clear-and-ack exit and the driver's wait-then-`KrnRemIRQHandler()` Stop ordering (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/RPi{PWM,HDMI,I2S}/...`). `CreateNewProc` defaults to asynchronous (`NP_Synchronous=FALSE`) and owns the Process, stack and name in `tc_MemEntry` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:121-143,401-421,543-555`); `RemTask()` queues the exiting Process for service-task cleanup and the service task frees the memory once it sees `TS_INVALID` (`rom/exec/remtask.c:82-113,130-163`; `rom/exec/service.c:37-90`). The cancelable signal-IPI drain cannot cover a callback delayed before entering `Signal()` (`rom/exec/signal.c:89-106,208-234`). Generic IRQ removal's writer lock waits for callback completion but is reached only after the master is signaled, so it cannot keep that Process alive during the gap. The callback does not explicitly snapshot the field; on a cross-CPU overlap the unsynchronized use can pass a stale task pointer after teardown, or NULL if a later load observes the clear. Exact load behavior depends on generated code. Added OD4001 across all three variants and corrected the earlier HDMI candidate reference; generic driver-buffer release remains protected by handler removal. No SMP schedule, task exit, or hardware IRQ was run. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI hardware-control hook/caller contract pass (2026-10-19; OD3167/OD3238/OD3457 retained, no new OD): reread the complete `subLibHardwareControl()` method and adjacent attribute hooks (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3812-4161`), then traced all recognized hardware-control tag cases through `_AHI_ControlAudioA()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:915-1005`) and the asynchronous worker (`usbaudio.class.c:613-762`). The caller forwards set/query values directly with no lock, and the worker clears the shared flag word only after synchronous control transfers; this is the already documented OD3167 lost-update window. `AHIC_Input` stores any supplied index and the worker later follows the selected input pointer, confirming OD3238's stale saved-input condition. `AHIC_Output` similarly accepts an index without bounds checking, but its worker path only sends the resulting selector value when a selector unit exists; invalid values produce a failed USB request/log rather than a distinct memory-safety consequence, while the advertised-output-without-selector mismatch is OD3457. Query hooks return cached settings; unknown tags return FALSE. The inspected setters intentionally return `AHIS_UNKNOWN` for software-mixer fallback. No additional independent defect established. This recheck overlaps previously credited hooks and adds no source-line credit; full USB Audio descriptor, external-caller, and lifecycle coverage remains partial. No control call, transfer, or device was run. Source-only.
USB Audio mode-info attribute index-contract pass (2026-10-19; OD3172/OD3207 retained, no new OD): read the complete `subLibGetAttr()` body and AHI's `AHI_GetAudioAttrsA()` tag handling/documented index ranges (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3895-4080`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:290-306,377-388,450-535`). The driver directly indexes frequency, input and output arrays; the public mode-info contract defines each corresponding argument as an index in `[0,count-1]`, so an invalid external argument alone is not promoted as a distinct driver finding. Under valid indices, `AHIDB_Frequency` returns the stored rate, and selector names follow the stored topology. The fixed nearest-rate threshold and zero-frequency mode conditions remain the separately documented OD3207 and OD3172 paths. Input/monitor range queries use `nGetInputUnit()` and thus retain OD3238's stale selected-input path; output-volume range access is gated by the root's volume-control flag. No additional in-tree valid-range defect established. This pass reuses previously credited code and adds no source-line credit. No attribute query or device was run; USB Audio and broader external-caller coverage remain partial. Source-only.
Bluetooth config-tree mutation/string-helper follow-up (OD3766/OD3767/OD3772 rechecked, no new OD; 2026-10-19): reread the selected config-tree helpers for allocation, removal, replacement, serialization, CRC and string chunks (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/config.c:1271-1576`), then traced `btReadCfg`/`btAddCfgEntry` callers in Bluetooth HID, PAN, Preferences Import and the selected disk-loader path. `btReadCfg` still clears the prior children before recursive import; declared child extents are copied before the parent remainder is checked, confirming OD3766/OD3767. `bAddCfgChunk` removes an existing chunk before attempting a larger replacement allocation; selected fixed-size CDC/keymap replacements fit the existing capacity after removal, while HID GUI action forms deliberately clear their children before rebuilding, so this pass did not establish a distinct in-tree stale-chunk loss beyond OD3767's failed-import behavior. `btMatchStringChunk`'s loop compares a differing next character before checking whether the query ended, so the suspected ordinary prefix match is not present for NUL-terminated strings. `bGetStringChunk` copies the declared data length into a length-plus-one allocation; maintained string-chunk producers store `strlen+1`, and no distinct selected valid-input defect was established. Rechecked that `bWriteCfg`/`btGetCfgChunk` call `bUpdateGlobalCfg` while holding the shared config semaphore; the live-tree mutation and concurrency interleaving remain OD3772. No config import, allocation failure, save, or concurrent mutation was run. The Bluetooth config parser's broader extent validation, all public mutation contracts, and failure reporting remain partial. Source-only.
Filesave OD2160 input-source reachability recheck (2026-10-19; no duplicate): followed the stereo `FORMAT_S16` branch from `AHIsub_Start()`'s successful FileRequester call to `PlaySlave` opening `dd->fs_FileReq->fr_File` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-main.c:217-305`; `filesave-playslave.c:265-283`). ASL defines `STRINGA_MaxChars` as the maximum number of characters and sets the filename gadget to `MAX_FILE_LEN == 257`; selection clones the gadget's complete text into `fr_File` (`compiler/include/intuition/gadgetclass.h:467-470`; `workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.h:36-39`; `filereqhooks.c:878-880,1779-1790`). Thus the UI can supply a filename at or beyond the 253-byte `strncpy` limit. The local copy is not guaranteed NUL-terminated before `strlen`, confirming OD2160's source trigger; the actual read past the stack array and suffix-write extent still depend on uninitialized tail bytes. No requester or file was opened, and no new source-line credit was added because the Filesave body and these lines were already credited. Source-only.
Filesave stereo S16 second-output open failure pass (OD4002 added, 2026-10-19): traced the two `MODE_NEWFILE` opens and common `PlaySlave` cleanup through the AHI `_AHIsub_Start()` handshake (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-playslave.c:265-283,549-567`; `filesave-main.c:291-295`). The left output is created/truncated before the right open is attempted; if that second open fails, the worker clears its task pointer and signals, and Start returns `AHIE_UNKNOWN`. DOS `Open()` documents `MODE_NEWFILE` as deleting/replacing the prior file (`rom/dos/open.c:40-52`). Added OD4002 to the detailed Other Drivers report and AROS index. This is distinct from OD3401's successful startup followed by later `CMD_WRITE` allocation failure. The filesave source bodies and cited caller lines were already credited; no new source-line count. No file or audio request was used. Source-only.

Filesave AIFF/AIFC/WAVE emitted-size and sample-frame recheck (OD1546/OD1547/OD2018 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): traced the complete sample conversion/byte-count loop and final format-header rewrites (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-playslave.c:311-381,438-460,469-538`) against the fixed-width writer headers and selected AHI-Handler chunk reader. AIFF/AIFC and WAVE emit signed 16-bit samples, so every `bytesWritten` increment is `samples * 2` and is even; the suspected odd SSND/BODY padding gap is not reachable for these formats. 8SVX is the byte-sample exception and explicitly writes the required odd-byte pad before its header rewrite (`:470-478`), matching existing OD2018 coverage. Stereo sample-frame counters represent per-channel frames while data-byte counts include both channels. The native-long LP64 header-layout issue remains OD1546, and AIFF/AIFC payload consumers beyond AHI-Handler remain outside this pass. No sample file was generated or parsed. Source-only.

Sam440 serial IRQ-array extent follow-up (OD4006 added, 2026-10-19): compared `GetIRQs(int *irq)` and its four element stores (`serial_init.c:27,40-54`) with its call through `&csd->cs_IRQ[0]` (`:69`) and the adjacent `UBYTE cs_IRQ[4]`/`cs_Unit[4]` layout (`serial_intern.h:57-66`). On the PPC32 target the four int stores span 16 bytes, extending 12 bytes into unit-pointer storage before the IRQ-registration loop reads it (`:71-72`). Serial-class break command comparison (no new finding, 2026-10-19): compared every checked-in serial-device `SDCMD_BREAK` branch in USB CDC-ACM, CP210x, PL2303, Bluetooth RFCOMM, rawwrap and PalmPDA (`rom/usb/classes/{cdcacm,serialcp210x,serialpl2303,rawwrap,palmpda}/dev.c`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/dev.c`) with each selected worker handler. USB Audio volume-range mapping caller recheck (OD3202 retained, no new finding, 2026-10-19): traced Feature Unit signed 8.8 GET_MIN/GET_MAX fields through `nFindLogVolume()`, AHI mode-info range queries, `AHI_ControlAudioA()`, and the three worker mappings for output, input-gain, and monitor values (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1312-1367,1740-1800,640-762,3990-4050,4090-4130`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/{modeinfo.c:450-535,audioctrl.c:915-1005}`). The fixed `0..0x10000` AHI range is the normalized control range; the worker maps it to the device-reported dB bounds, so the helper alone does not establish a second range defect. Reconfirmed OD3202: the signed 32-bit `Fixed` multiplication can overflow at a valid 32,768-unit dB span when unity `0x10000` is applied; output volume, input gain, and monitor controls use the same expression. USB Audio binding-readiness recheck for OD3974 (2026-10-19): traced `usbForceInterfaceBinding()` through the worker readiness wait into `nAllocAudio()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:310-351,1993-2059`). On successful startup, the worker creates `nch_TaskMsgPort` and its EP0 pipe, then stores `nch_Task` immediately before returning; the binder waits for the ready signal and returns the binding only if `nch_Task` is non-NULL. This rules out the hypothesized resume of a normally published binding during incomplete startup. It does not close OD3974: after publication, `psdResumeDevice()` drops the device lock before `psdResumeBindings()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:3913-3933`), while release clears the interface binding under that lock and blocks until the worker deletes its port (`:6588-6613`; Audio `:344-371,2070-2117`). Resume can therefore retain the binding across release and arrive during/after worker teardown; `UCM_AttemptResumeDevice` still dereferences the unchecked port/task fields (`usbaudio.class.c:503-506`). Tightened OD3974's startup scope accordingly; no additional finding or line credit. No device or scheduling behavior was run. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI mode-allocation rollback pass (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced `subLibAllocAudio()` partial setup and every explicit `AHISF_ERROR` return through AHI's allocation error label and `_AHI_FreeAudio()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3240-3555,3571-3668`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:511-520,652-658,702-741`). AHI invokes the subdriver `FreeAudio` callback even when `AllocAudio` reports failure. Once the Poseidon handle is acquired, USB Audio's callback cleans the optional timer request/device, primary and sibling ports/pipes/buffers, RTIso handlers, and the Poseidon handle; `nSelectAudioMode()` failure after interface selection is routed through this cleanup, which restores the zero-bandwidth alternate when one is recorded. No independent rollback defect was established in these paths. Already-covered issues involving early `nch_CurrentMode` clearing and concurrent teardown remain OD3971; descriptor, frequency and buffer arithmetic candidates remain separately tracked. This focused pass adds no line credit to the partial USB Audio translation unit; no allocation failure, mode, USB device or AHI call was exercised. Source-only.

Envy24 AHI entry-point full-body and Start rollback caller pass (2026-10-19; OD2744/OD2745/OD2490 rechecked, no additional finding): reread all of `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/main.c` (747 lines), including audio allocation/free, update, Start/Stop, GetAttr and HardwareControl, then traced `AHIC_Play`/`AHIC_Record` through AHI `_AHI_ControlAudioA()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:1007-1014`). AHI returns the Start error without issuing Stop; this supports OD2744's partial-allocation/retry ownership case. Its FreeAudio callback later calls Stop with both flags, but Envy24 Stop frees only resources whose `is_playing`/`is_recording` flags were set, leaving allocations made before a failed Start's state publication unowned; repeated Start can overwrite those pointers. A later caller-count correction withdrew OD2745: the current Envy24 initializer records only one matching PCI object, so a nonzero AudioID card cannot be selected through this build path. Frequency/input/output indexed getters rely on the documented AHI index ranges; invalid public arguments do not establish another finding. No audio device, card, allocation failure or playback/recording was exercised. Source body now fully read; PCI/board initialization, interrupt scheduling and codec/GPIO hardware behavior remain separate caller/platform gaps. Source-only.

Envy24 reset callback lifetime and report reconciliation (OD2743 restored, 2026-10-19): re-read `AddResetHandler()`, `ResetHandler()`, `AllocDriverData()` and `FreeDriverData()` against Exec `AddResetCallback()`/`Enqueue()`/`doresetcallbacks()` and the shared AHI subdriver expunge path (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/misc.c:216-267,600-623`; `driver-init.c:155-179`; `rom/exec/addresetcallback.c:52-61`; `rom/exec/enqueue.c:67-98`; `rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:115-153`; `Drivers/Common/library.c:483-519`). Confirmed the callback node and code are static module storage, its data is the last card pointer set, and common expunge frees card state without unlinking the callback; later reset traversal retains the stale node. The existing coverage row had OD2743, but detailed report and index omitted it. Restored OD2743 in both artifacts, scoped to AROS builds selecting the optional Envy24 driver, successful card initialization, subsequent expunge, then reset traversal. The initial note suspected that the static node could be reused across cards; the 2026-10-20 caller-count correction below found that `DriverInit` adds one vendor/device pair and searches once, so repeated registration during one initialization is not established. OD2743 remains scoped to the single-card expunge path. No card, expunge or reset was exercised. Source-only.

Envy24 EEPROM minimum-length caller pass (OD4017 added, 2026-10-19): rechecked the EEPROM length byte, payload loop, PCI config/GPIO consumers and card-init return path (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/misc.c:275-277,340-359,363-453`). Length is treated as total bytes including six header bytes, but card initialization always consumes seven payload bytes. Values below 13 leave at least one byte of local `eeprom[128]` uninitialized; values at or below six skip the payload loop completely. The stale bytes are then written to codec/AC-link/I2S/S/PDIF config and GPIO mask/data/direction registers before initialization reports success. Added OD4017 for this lower-bound case, distinct from OD2738's oversized-length stack overwrite and OD2739's busy-timeout stale read. A low failed read can produce the same small-value path, but no duplicate transport finding is added. No EEPROM or card was used. Source-only.

Envy24 EEPROM finding/report reconciliation (OD2738/OD2739 restored, 2026-10-19): verified the existing coverage descriptions against `card_init()`'s fixed `eeprom[128]`, unbounded `size = length - 6` loop, and `read_i2c()`'s unchecked 65,536-poll expiry (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/misc.c:102-112,275-277,340-359`). OD2738 covers the upper-bound stack overwrite (reported total above 134); OD2739 covers use of stale data when the controller remains busy through the poll. OD4017 separately covers the lower-bound uninitialized bytes when total length is below 13. No device or EEPROM was read. Source-only.

USB HID report/index integrity correction (OD4009/OD4010, 2026-10-19): reread the action-message producer, shared dispatcher, reload/unbind cleanup and sound-cache methods (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1005-1070,1321-1459,5554-5575,6142-6175,7044-7048,7089-7310`; `hid.h:833-838`). xHCI endpoint-context and Poseidon teardown caller reconciliation (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced the sole selected `xhciDestroyEndpoint` callback registration through Poseidon's `pTearDownHWEndpoint` and `psdFreePipe` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:599-601`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1654-1669,4650-4677`). Poseidon frees the shared endpoint's hardware request and nulls the pointer after invoking the callback; xHCI clears `iouh_DriverPrivate2` when it owns an endpoint context and reference-counts prepared endpoint contexts under `xhc_DevLock`. On device removal, `xhciFreeDeviceCtx` detaches a still-referenced context by nulling `ectx_Device`, leaving final release to the callback, which then frees the context without touching the removed device (`xhci_hcd.c:2312-2362,4409-4445`). This caller/lifetime trace supports existing OD3197's command-failure ring-release concern; no independent shared-pipe reference defect established. No pipe teardown or controller was run. Source-only.

xHCI finished-request worker full-body reconciliation (2026-10-19; OD3206/OD3517 retained, no new finding): reread both complete queue walks in `xhciHandleFinishedTDs` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2701-2943`) and the event-task call/scheduling order (`xhci_hw.c:523-550`). Periodic requests are decoded from `dpCC` or NAK timeout; RTIso requests call the direction-specific completion hook, then free/recycle periodic state and may queue replacement buffers. This confirms OD3206's event-worker use of PTD/RTIso state across a callback while handler removal can free it, and OD3517's callback-versus-stop buffer lifetime exposure. Ordinary periodic requests free context before reply. Async requests translate completion status, optionally reset a stalled EP0, free async request context, perform control-transfer postprocessing from saved device state, then reply. No separate completion ordering or list mutation defect was established from this body; external AbortIO interactions and actual concurrent scheduling remain conditional/unrun. Source-only.

xHCI transfer-event completion decoder and caller boundary pass (2026-10-19; no new finding): reread all of `xhciIntWorkProcess()` and its two selected event-ring callers (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2972-3117,3280-3550,3620-3680`). Transfer events derive the residual from the 24-bit event status; ordinary requests clamp residuals larger than the requested length before calculating actual bytes, release the DMA bounce mapping using that bounded extent, clear matching setup/data/status `ringio` entries, and store the actual length. The command-completion caller uses the same helper only for command-ring slots carrying an asynchronous IOReq; synchronous command slots have no ringio request and bypass it. The wrapped bookkeeping range correctly skips the reserved link TRB. No independent transfer-length or index defect established in the checked ordinary path; malformed event contents, controller ordering, and event-versus-request teardown overlap remain untested/conditional and are tracked elsewhere. Source-only.

xHCI command submission/slot-result completion caller recheck (OD3785 retained, 2026-10-19): reread the whole synchronous `xhciCmdSubmit()` and async submit helper plus command wrappers (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hw.c:52-159,286-340,346-478`), the command-ring writer (`xhci_hcd.c:872-913`), and selected producer sites. Synchronous submit reserves a command TRB, initializes its `xhc_CmdResults[queued]` sentinel, rings the doorbell, then polls that slot for up to one second; command completion copies the event into the same result slot and advances the ring. The only producer exclusion is `xhciRingLock()`'s local `Disable()`/`Enable()`, and `xhciCmdSubmit()`'s surrounding Disable is likewise processor-local on ExecSMP. The selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP manifest packages xHCI; its port task can submit Enable Slot while the independent event task can submit endpoint configuration during transfer scheduling (`xhci_hcport.c:767-779`; `xhci_hcd.c:1367-1368`; `xhci_hw.c:523-550`; `xhci_schedule.c:134-175`). This confirms existing OD3785's shared command-ring producer race and its selected two-task trigger; no separate timeout-slot reuse issue established in this slice. Controller concurrency and timeout were not exercised. Source-only.

xHCI async command-wrapper reachability qualifier (2026-10-19; no new finding): searched every checked-in `xhciCmdDeviceAddress` and `xhciCmdSubmitAsync` reference. All three direct Address Device callers pass `ioreq == NULL` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:1499-1502`; `xhcidevice.c:214-215`), so the async command-completion branch is not selected by an in-tree caller at this snapshot. OD3785 remains grounded in the synchronous port-task `Enable Slot` and event-task `Configure Endpoint` producers; no async command path is needed for its trigger. External callers are not part of this optional driver interface. Source-only.

USB Audio mode publication and teardown ownership recheck (2026-10-19; OD3166/OD3209/OD3248/OD3949 retained, no new finding): reread `libExpunge`, `nAddAudioModes`, `nAllocAudio`, and `nFreeAudio` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:110-138,1929-2118`) and traced `AHI_AddAudioMode`/`AHI_RemoveAudioMode` allocation, database insertion and deletion (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:358-460,507-547`). Atheros5000 final-close request-port lifetime trace (OD4018 added, 2026-10-19): followed `CloseUnit()`'s last-open branch through `DeletePCIUnit()` and `DeleteUnit()`. The request-port loop frees each `MsgPort` before checking `UNITF_ONLINE`; online cleanup then calls `GoOffline()` and `FlushUnit()`, which invokes `GetMsg()` on freed `request_ports[0..MGMT_QUEUE]`. Exec `GetMsg()` reads the port spinlock on ExecSMP and its message-list head on all targets. The close path does not first go offline. Added OD4018 for final close after online with no earlier offline; no device, close, or queued request was exercised. Source-only.

SANA-II final-close/offline teardown family pass (OD4018 expanded, 2026-10-19): compared Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, EtherLink3, Intel Pro/100, nvidianet, Prism2, Realtek8180, and Rhine `DeleteUnit()`/`GoOffline()`/`FlushUnit()` bodies and their `CloseUnit()` last-open branches. All eight free `request_ports[]` before the still-online check; online cleanup then flushes those ports through `GetMsg()`. The matching final-close routes do not first send the unit offline. Expanded OD4018 to cover the copied implementation family, with per-file line references. No device, close, or I/O was exercised. Full unrelated network-driver coverage, PCI/USB hardware behavior, and concurrent close/request interactions remain open. Source-only.


Network request-port teardown boundary check (OD4018 scope, 2026-10-19): searched all maintained `workbench/devs/networks/**/unit.c` request-port frees. EMU10kx AROS PCI enumeration and DriverInit loop recheck (OD4019 added, 2026-10-19): traced `Enumerator()` and `ahi_pci_find_device()` through PCI `EnumDevices()`'s full-list traversal and each `DriverInit()` count/fill loop (`pci_aros.c:79-133`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:421-448`; `emu10kx-init.c:119-136,217-245`). With two matching objects, the finder excludes only the previous pointer and alternates the first two matches; the count loop cannot terminate.
