AHI PCI finder-pattern boundary check after OD4019 (2026-10-19; no finding extended): searched the selected AROS PCI wrappers for the same `prev_dev`/first-different-device callback and traced callers in CMI8738, SB128, VIA-AC97, Envy24, and Envy24HT. The first four use bounded `for` loops over their vendor/product tables, making one finder call per table entry; Envy24HT makes a single lookup in each of its two setup phases. None uses the EMU10kx unbounded `while (find_next != NULL)` card-count loop, so the proven two-card alternation does not establish their nontermination. Multiple-identical-card completeness in those drivers remains unverified and is not added to OD4019. No driver initialization or PCI hardware was run. Source-only.

SANA-II access-lock/last-close trigger boundary (OD4018 and EK8880 follow-up, 2026-10-19): traced Prism2 `DevBeginIO()` and `ServiceRequest()` against the worker and `CloseUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/device.c:296-305,426-440,538-568`; `request.c:182-285`; `unit.c:385-417,3818-3888`). One task can own `access_lock` while servicing a synchronous BeginIO; a concurrent request is queued, then the unit worker can block in ObtainSemaphore until the first service releases it. Final Close deletes the worker before freeing the unit. However, this sequence only creates the targeted waiter-at-last-close condition if the final open is closed while its own request remains active; the examined driver code does not establish that as a supported client lifecycle. This refines the conditional RemTask waiter scenario and does not change OD4018 (the independent freed-request-port flush finding); no additional device finding or trigger claim is added. No I/O or close was run.

Deneb DMA interrupt-to-worker completion boundary recheck (OD3704 retained, no new OD; 2026-10-19): traced `uhwLevel6Int()` Mach DMA status acknowledgement and signal handoff (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:5267-5354`) into the sole active `uhwDMATask()` consumer and `uhwHandleDMAInt()` state switch (`:4996-5264,5374-5401`). The apparent direct `uhwHandleDMAInt()` call in the level-6 handler is inside `#if 0`; active completion is deferred to the worker, which rechecks `hu_DMAPTD` before dispatch. Terminal DMA-IN branches call `FreeATL`; its reply-before-`CachePostDMA` order remains the already documented OD3704 path. The state branches and interrupt handoff yielded no additional independent completion/ownership defect in this pass. No controller interrupt, DMA request, abort or worker schedule was exercised; source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II soft-MAC channel-selection caller recheck (2026-10-19; no additional finding): traced `wpa_driver_sana2_set_channel()` through the driver-op table and `WPA_DRIVER_FLAGS_USER_SPACE_MLME` selection into `ieee80211_sta_associate()` (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:640-653,987-995,1107`; `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:1243-1247`; `wpa_supplicant/mlme.c:2649-2652`). Association stores the selected channel/frequency and ignores the channel callback's return before starting authentication or IBSS search. The same callback's result is checked and causes a scan channel to be skipped in `mlme.c:2777-2785`. The selected soft-MAC Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 request tables support `S2_SETOPTIONS`; their handlers call `ConfigureAdapter()` when online but return successful completion unconditionally (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/request.c:1559-1578`; `realtek8180/request.c:1557-1576`). Thus a concrete in-tree channel-set failure observable by this association caller was not established; the ignored error remains a caller-contract gap for devices that can return a `S2_SETOPTIONS` failure, but it is not promoted as a selected-driver bug. Broader channel/regulatory behavior and hardware failure propagation remain open. No radio operation was run; source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II association error-propagation recheck (OD3626 retained, 2026-10-19): reread the full `wpa_driver_sana2_associate()` body and its selected supplicant caller (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:382-445`; `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:1243-1256,1270-1292`). Confirmed three independent suppressed error classes: SSID/tag allocation and `S2_SETOPTIONS` errors are stored in `err` but the callback unconditionally returns 0; each of four WEP key install/clear results is discarded. The supplicant treats only a negative callback result as failure and otherwise follows its ordinary association timeout. Thus simply returning the positive `DoIO()` code would still not satisfy the callback contract; error mapping must be negative. The association callback is selected for hard-MAC SANA-II devices (`S2_GETNETWORKS` advertised); user-space-MLME devices take `ieee80211_sta_associate()` instead. OD3626 already captures this behavior; no duplicate finding added. SSID length is bounded by selected supplicant/BSS inputs to 32 bytes in the paths checked, so the fixed 33-byte local allocation did not yield an additional in-tree overflow finding. No association or I/O failure was induced; source-only.

Card resource internal-layout and selected-caller audit (2026-10-19; no new finding): the common header contains only the library node and `CardMemoryMap`; the active m68k-Amiga variant uses its separate, expanded `arch/m68k-amiga/card/card_intern.h` and initializes its own ownership/task state. The common resource functions are explicitly dummy stubs in `rom/card/card_init.c`; actual PCMCIA consumers (`arch/m68k-amiga/devs/ata/ata_amiga.c`, Prism2 and EtherLink3 PCCard drivers) are target-specific and resolve through the Amiga variant's `GetCardMap`/`OwnCard`. The m68k map is a static constant (`arch/m68k-amiga/card/getcardmap.c:8-15`), so no uninitialized common `cmm` consumer or independent layout defect was established. No card hardware or client was run. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI partial-allocation failure unwind recheck (2026-10-19; no new OD): traced every failure return in `subLibAllocAudio()` through AHI's `_AHI_AllocAudio()` error label and `_AHI_FreeAudio()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3271-3331,3489-3509`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:481-521,656-659,712-735`). Once the USB class has opened Poseidon, AHI calls the class `subLibFreeAudio()` even when allocation reports `AHISF_ERROR`; its null-initialized handles and partial buffers/requests are conditionally released, and Exec `DeleteMsgPort(NULL)` is a no-op (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:51-61`). Failures before the class stores driver data leave the control block clear from `AHIAllocVec(..., MEMF_PUBLIC|MEMF_CLEAR)` on the selected native backend. Thus timer-request, port, pipe, interface-selection, and buffer allocation failures in this path did not establish an independent resource leak or null-free defect. Existing OD3208 remains the frequency programming/order finding. No failure was induced and no USB stream was run; source-only.

USB Audio mode-name finding ID reconciliation (2026-10-19): the just-added OD4020 duplicated the earlier, fully detailed OD3949 path from `psdCopyStrFmt()` failure through AHI mode insertion to the requester name dereference (`usbaudio.class.c:1942-1987`; Poseidon formatter; AHI database/mode-info; requester `:1337-1340`). Removed OD4020 from the report and master index, removed its duplicate activity note, and updated the per-file row to point to OD3949. No second independent defect or new line credit established; the USB Audio source review remains partial. Source-only.

Poseidon RTIso handler-list teardown synchronization audit (OD4021 added, 2026-10-19; no line credit): traced device-removal iteration under `pd_Lock` through saved-next release-hook traversal, RTIso registration/removal, and USB Audio duplex allocation/free (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2240-2249,2319-2341,5555-5592,5607-5625`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3489-3503,3590-3597`). The remover's device semaphore does not serialize `psdFreeRTIsoHandler`, which unlinks under only local `Forbid`; Exec documents that Forbid on ExecSMP is processor-local (`rom/exec/forbid.c:51-57`). A concurrent duplex AHI free can therefore free the sibling node already held in `nextprt`, which the device-removal loop dereferences on its next iteration. Added OD4021, separate from OD3517's completion/softint use-after-free. Trigger remains conditional on SMP overlap; no schedule or USB removal was run. USB Audio source review remains partial; no line credit. Source-only.

OD4021 caller-lock recheck (2026-10-19; retained, no new finding/line credit): verified AHI's public `_AHI_FreeAudio()` calls subdriver `Stop` and then `FreeAudio` without acquiring Poseidon's device semaphore (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:712-735`); USB Audio teardown has no `psdLockReadDevice`/`psdLockWriteDevice` call. Thus the second caller is not serialized by the `pd_Lock` held during `pFreeDevice()`'s release-hook walk. In duplex mode the `sibnam` RTIso node is the one unlinked/freed first, so if it is the saved `nextprt`, the next loop condition dereferences freed storage. `Forbid` contributes only local scheduler exclusion on ExecSMP. OD3517 remains distinct: it covers controller completion/deferred-interrupt use of audio buffers and AHI state after stop, not the Poseidon list iterator's saved-next lifetime. Source-only; no concurrent free or device removal was run.

Nouveau/VMware SVGA MMIO helper caller and return-contract pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): compared both byte-sized helper bodies and their source-list inclusion with the target-specific `KrnMapGlobal()` results. The RISC-V mapper returns nonzero on success and zero on failure (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_mmu.c:149-195`); AArch64 forwards `mmu_map_range()`'s same success/failure convention (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmu.c:305-337`). The helper's `if (!KrnMapGlobal(...)) return NULL` check therefore handles those branches consistently. The x86 branch skips the call and returns the physical address; Nouveau's two maintained caller addresses are within the x86-64 initial identity map. The legacy 32-bit ARM mapper is a no-op returning zero, so this helper reports failure rather than claiming an unmapped address is usable. VMware's copy has no checked-in caller. Credited the 84 C code lines (42 each) after the previous reconciled totals (Other Drivers 191,294 / 378,995; weighted 442,185 / 786,380): Other Drivers is now 191,378 / 379,079 = 50.5%, and weighted overall is 442,269 / 786,464 = 56.2%. This is another incremental correction, not a fresh inventory/status reconciliation. No helper, hardware, or mapping was run. Source-only.

Nouveau PCI compatibility wrapper caller pass (OD9566 added; 2026-10-24): read all 430 physical lines / 364 `cloc 2.06` C lines of Nouveau `linux_pci.c` and compared the full body to VMware's 431-line / 365-code-line counterpart; differences are target labels and VMware's additional `aHidd_PCIDevice_isIO` enable tag. Traced the selected `pci_get_domain_bus_and_slot()` bridge lookup through `dispnv04/hw.c`, `dispnv04/arb.c`, and `nvkm/subdev/fb/ramnv1a.c`. The latter checks NULL, but the NV04 memory-clock paths for supported integrated GeForce2/GeForce4 MX IDs 0x01a0/0x01f0 pass NULL from the compatibility stub to `pci_read_config_dword()`, whose wrapper dereferences `pdev->oopdev`; the selected CRTC mode-set path calls the arbitration helper. Added OD9566. Other wrapper APIs were reviewed for selection and call shape; `pci_get_class()` and `pci_get_device()` have no selected in-tree Nouveau caller. No GPU, PCI config access, or modeset was run; source-only. Broader hardware semantics and external API clients remain open.

Nouveau/VMware PCI disable lifecycle recheck (OD9567 narrowed; 2026-10-24): re-read both selected compatibility wrappers, their selected suspend/removal callsites and the PCI HIDD setter chain. Corrected the finding's scope: `pci_disable_device()`'s relevant Linux API effect is disabling bus mastering, while this port's wrapper is empty; `pci_clear_master()` only clears the local `is_busmaster` flag. The generic HIDD superclass clears the command-register bit when `isMaster` is false. PCIDT's `Root__Set` calls the superclass before applying its true-only interrupt-unmask side effect, so that subclass does not prevent the clear. Removed the unsupported claim that `pci_disable_device()` should clear I/O or memory decode. No PCI function or transition was run; source-only.

Nouveau/VMware SVGA DRM compatibility inventory and helper passes (2026-10-19): parsed both `sources.drm.mak` lists and compared every existing local `drm-compat/*.c` path against the ledger. Added rows for the 32 missing source paths (16 per target), totaling 11,992 `cloc 2.06` code lines. Re-read both 77-line `linux_compat.c` bodies and confirmed byte equality (`39` combined `cloc` code lines). `RB_GENERATE(linux_root, ...)` uses `panic_cmp`, but checked-in Nouveau/VMware tree callsites use Linux's `rb_link_node()` plus `rb_insert_color()` and do not call generated `RB_INSERT`/`RB_FIND`; no comparator-stub defect was established. Both DRM mode files call `list_sort()` with `drm_mode_compare()`, whose negative result means the left mode is better; the helper's `cmp > 0` adjacent swap moves less favorable entries later and terminates after a pass without swaps. No independent ordering defect established. Then read both `linux_firmware.c` bodies (142 combined `cloc` code lines) and traced all selected Nouveau request sites and release paths; the VMware target has no in-tree caller. File-size, exact-read and allocation failure cleanup is consistent in the inspected paths; no new issue established. Read both byte-identical `linux_dma.c` bodies (420 combined `cloc` code lines), including scatterlist construction/copy/iteration and DMA map/sync wrappers; traced the selected VMware TTM scatterlist map/unmap/page-iterator flow and Nouveau GSP SG table allocation/map/error cleanup. No independent defect established in those selected paths. Read both `linux_irq.c` bodies (158 combined `cloc` code lines; target-specific names/logging differ) and traced Nouveau install/removal plus VMware threaded handler install/uninstall. Added OD4035: queued VMware thread work can still dereference the freed common IRQ entry because `free_irq()` does not cancel/drain `thread_work` before `kfree(entry)`. Then read both byte-identical `linux_dma_fence_array.c` bodies (162 combined `cloc` code lines); callback reference accounting and any/all completion paths were inspected, but neither target has an in-tree caller of this API and no issue was established for an observed call path. Read both full `linux_dma_fence.c` bodies (970 combined `cloc` code lines; VMware has an additional wait diagnostic block), traced the selected regular wait/signal/callback users, and searched for wait-any callers. Added OD4036: the wait-any API dereferences its callback-array allocation without checking for failure when `count > 0`; no selected in-tree callsite was found. Finally, read both `linux_workqueue.c` bodies (632 combined `cloc` code lines; only init names and queue labels differ), traced private queue create/destroy sites, and checked queue cancellation/drain behavior. Added OD4037: `destroy_workqueue()` flushes, stops and signals its worker but never frees the separately allocated queue descriptor. Then read the byte-identical `linux_idr.c` bodies (1,272 combined `cloc` C lines), cross-read both `include/linux/idr.h` wrappers and traced selected DRM connector-index plus VMware GMR/MOB allocations and releases. Added OD4038: `ida_alloc_max()`/`ida_alloc_range()` pass inclusive maxima to `ida_simple_get()`'s exclusive-end API; selected connector and GMR callers lose the top advertised ID, with zero/one GMR capacity edge cases also checked. Finally, read both `linux_mem.c` bodies (636 combined `cloc` C lines), audited page/coherent-DMA helpers and traced selected GSP coherent allocations through the Nouveau cache-sync calls. Added OD4039 for metadata-allocation failure leaving returned coherent blocks absent from later cache-sync iteration, and OD4040 for cross-CPU list traversal/mutation protected only by local `Forbid()` on ExecSMP. Nouveau/VMware compatibility code lines without full-body credit now total 7,561. The nine helper pairs contribute 4,431 reviewed C lines. Nouveau/VMware timer-process startup consequence expansion for OD4046 (2026-10-20): split the two CreateMsgPort failure cases and traced them through Exec `PutMsg`. When reply-port allocation fails but command-port allocation succeeds, startup still signals readiness, the process exits, and the first timer command can be stranded on the orphan command port while its caller blocks in `WaitPort`. When command-port allocation fails, the retained dead-process fast path later passes NULL to `PutMsg`; the selected Exec implementation forwards it to `InternalPutMsg` and dereferences `port->mp_SpinLock`/`mp_MsgList` without a null check (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:60-66,83-87`). Expanded OD4046 in the detailed report and AROS index with both distinct consequences. Selected vblank/higher-level timer users remain as previously traced; no allocation failure or timer operation was induced. No line credit; both `linux_time.c` bodies were already fully credited. Source-only.

Nouveau timer-process module-unload lead recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD): `exit_timerbase()` closes and deletes the shared template timer request, while the per-driver timer process has no stop/join path (`linux_time.c:58-71,288-321`). The selected module configuration is `noexpunge` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau.conf:1-5`); genmodule omits expunge support under `OPTION_NOEXPUNGE` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:252,1506-1546`), and the AROS DRM glue documents that its device does not go away while the HIDD remains loaded (`drm-aros/drm_drv.c:31-34`). Thus ordinary selected module unload/DRM removal does not establish the proposed close-template-versus-live-timer race; no finding is added. System shutdown and forced external unload semantics were not established. Source-only.

USBDevice method declaration-order cross-check (2026-10-19; prior generated-header concern withdrawn): `usb.conf:49-62` lists the methods in an order different from `include/usb.h:123-136`. Rechecking the generator showed this is only the class `methodlist`: `readsectionclass_methodlist()` stores names and symbolic `moHidd_USBDevice_*` constants for class dispatch (`config.c:2081-2089,2225-2266`). `writeincinterfaces()` emits headers only from top-level `##begin interface` sections (`config.c:2273-2281`, `writeincinterfaces.c:310-316`); none exists in the USB stack, OHCI, or UHCI configs. Thus those configs do not emit `interface/Hidd_USBDevice.h`, and the differing declaration order does not assign method IDs or alter public dispatch. The earlier claim that generated method IDs differed was incorrect; no bug is retained. The USB public header and stub rows were added to inventory and are now body-reviewed as stated above. Source-only.

SD-card boot-wait/timer API candidate recheck (OD3316 retained; 2026-10-19): traced `sdcard_bootwait_delay` through `OpenDevice`, `DoIO`, generic `common_BeginIO`, and Exec `DoIO`. NVMe request-client name census (2026-10-19; no new finding): searched all checked-in C/header/assembly sources for `nvme.device` and NVMe command/request usage outside `rom/devs/nvme`. The only literal device-name consumer is InstallAROS's default name (`workbench/tools/InstallAROS/ia_driveselectclass.c:88`); the selected GRUB installer and FAT/NTFS probes are documented in the existing row, and general filesystems address a configured block device without hardcoding this driver name. This does not cover runtime configuration or external clients, which remain open. No device request or mount was run; source-only.


NVMe init rollback and Utility-base cleanup recheck (OD4053 added; 2026-10-19): traced all `NVME_Init` returns after `TaggedOpenLibrary(TAGGEDOPEN_UTILITY)` (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_init.c:80-158`) through the NVMe module config and generic `_set_libinit` rollback. The kernel-resource failure explicitly closes Utility; the `NVME=disable`, pool failure, OOP-base failure, and both storage-root failure returns do not. The root-failure path also returns after pool and optional bases are acquired without deleting/releasing them. The module has no `ADD2EXPUNGELIB` cleanup and generated failed init frees the base after registered rollback hooks, so these manual resources are not recovered. Added OD4053; corrected the stale NVMe-row reference to VirtIO-only OD2366. No failure was induced; source-only.



Deneb unit-bound candidate recheck (OD3580 qualified, 2026-10-19): traced the public `OpenDevice` unit argument through `devOpen()` into `Open_Unit()` and compared its `unitnr > MAXUNITS` guard with `MAXUNITS == 32` and `hd_Units[32]` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:281-320`; `uhwcmd.c:281-335`; `denebusb.h:331,349`). Unit 32 is accepted and the out-of-bounds slot is read before `FindConfigDev()` is called, so the trigger does not require a 33rd physical board; publication would also write out of bounds if such a board were present. The active m68k-Amiga `workbench-complete` USB parent graph selects `kernel-usb-amiga-m68k`, the `usb-poseidon-deneb` aggregate, and all three variants (`workbench/mmakefile.src:9-25,29`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:24-26`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/mmakefile.src:18-19`); the trigger still requires a caller to submit unit number 32. No target was built and no device was opened; source-only.

Deneb OD3704 caller-context correction (2026-10-19): rechecked every reviewed caller of `FreeATL()` around DMA retirement. `CMD_FLUSH` (`uhwcmd.c:973-1041`) and the normal DMA state-machine branches (`:2161-2287`) hold `Disable()` across reply and cache cleanup, so the earlier broad claim for those paths was incorrect. The remaining candidate is the ATL error/NAK-timeout retirement from `uhwHandleFinishedATLs()` (`:2073-2099`), reached by `uhwSoftInt()` (`:4774-4799`) without an enclosing task-switch exclusion. `FreeATL()` replies before reading the request again for `CachePostDMA()` (`:1635-1659`); a higher-priority waiting reply task can therefore run in that gap in the selected single-CPU m68k path. The finding and index are narrowed accordingly. Optional DMA target only; no runtime or hardware test.

USB timer-setup failure paths and lifecycle candidate correction (OD4054 added, 2026-10-19): rechecked both timer setup sites in `USB_ProcessStarter()` and `usb_process()` against `CreateMsgPort`, `CreateIORequest`, `OpenDevice`, `DoIO` and `SendIO`. The request/port creation and device-open results are unchecked; Exec's selected implementations make the NULL request dereference at `OpenDevice` and the unopened-device submission paths concrete (`usb_init.c:54-68`; `usbprocess.c:204-231`; `rom/exec/createiorequest.c:57-76`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:96-123`; `rom/exec/sendio.c:50-56`). Added OD4054 as a conditional startup-failure candidate, distinct from OD4052's failed worker-process/reply-port handshake. Reconciled OD4051: the earlier statement that ordinary expunge leaves the timer request, port and open timer device is not an independently reachable cleanup finding, because the retained root object's open-count reference prevents ordinary expunge; the separate OD4051 candidate is the permanent module self-reference. No timer, allocation failure, or device load was induced; source-only.

VIA-Rhine failed-open cleanup caller recheck (OD4034 expanded, 2026-10-19): traced opener-allocation failure through the direct `CloseDevice()` call into Exec's close dispatch (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/via-rhine_init.c:231-279`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:95-119`; `closedevice.c:63-85`). Because the unit open count and flags are set before `AllocVec(struct Opener)`, and the Close hook stops but never decrements the count, a first `SANA2OPF_MINE` open that fails this allocation leaves `open_count == 1`, `IFF_SHARED` clear, and no opener node; later opens return `IOERR_UNITBUSY`. Expanded OD4034 and its index to include this failure route. This target is explicitly buildable but omitted from the architecture/aggregate edges; no allocation failure or device was run. Source-only.

VIA-Rhine scheduler queue-drain caller recheck (OD4026, 2026-10-19): traced `BeginIO()`'s failed `AttemptSemaphore()` branch through clearing `IOF_QUICK`, `PutMsg()` to `rhineu_input_port`, and the task signal wait (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/via-rhine_init.c:327-335`; `unit.c:724-759`). When that request arrives while the scheduler owns `rhineu_unit_lock`, it is queued and wakes the worker. The `while (GetMsg(input) != NULL);` loop consumes all queued requests; its following block always runs with `io == NULL`, then acquires the lock and calls `handle_request()`, which dereferences `request->ios2_Req.io_Command` immediately (`handler.c:97-105`). Confirmed a lock-contention trigger from the selected API path; no runtime request was submitted. The worker's separate port/signal-allocation failure paths remain tracked under OD4027/OD3609 and were not revisited here. Source-only.


VIA-Rhine scheduler startup and signal teardown recheck (OD3671, OD3672, OD4027 expanded; 2026-10-19): re-read the scheduler from port creation through its timer/message handshake, signal allocation and wait/exit loop, then followed `CreateUnit()` and `DeleteUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/unit.c:669-766,890-966`) against Exec `AllocSignal`, `Signal` and `Wait` contracts (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:70-143`; `signal.c:128-150`; `wait.c:75-80`). Expanded OD4027: the worker also dereferences unchecked `AllocVec(sizeof(struct Message))` before acknowledging startup; `reply_port` and `input` creation are unchecked, so failure can acknowledge a worker that later dereferences NULL. Expanded OD3672: scheduler waits on one-hot masks, but tests the received mask against raw `signal_0`; `DeleteUnit()` likewise passes that bit number as the `Signal()` mask and frees worker-owned unit/port/MMIO state without joining the task. Reconfirmed OD3671's unchecked signal-allocation failure; the `1 << -1` case is undefined C behavior and its exact target effect is not claimed. The normal/debug VIA-Rhine recipe is explicit, while its architecture and aggregate edges are disabled. No task, allocation failure, signal exhaustion, timer device, or adapter was exercised; source-only.


USB multiport hub descriptor length caller recheck (OD3895 expanded, 2026-10-19): re-traced the OHCI Root descriptor producer and the generic USBHub `GetHubDescriptor` control-request producer against the shared descriptor struct. Both use a fixed 9-byte length while the hardware or returned descriptor can advertise eight or more ports; the generic worker consumes `bNbrPorts` but not removable/power bitmaps. Expanded OD3895 to include both OHCI roots and generic external hubs, retaining the qualification that no checked-in worker behavior depends on the truncated masks. No hub descriptor or controller was queried. Source-only.


OHCI PCI enumerator cap/timer cleanup recheck (OD2953 confirmed; no new finding, 2026-10-19): re-read the complete `Enumerator` and `OHCI_Init` path (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohci_init.c:42-108,112-168`) against the 8-entry storage limit (`ohci.h:224,278-283`) and `HIDD_PCI_EnumDevices` callback loop (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:424-445`). The callback allocates/opens its timer before testing `counter == MAX_OHCI_DEVICES`; each additional matching OHCI PCI function therefore returns without `ohci_DeleteTimer`. The counter increments only after a controller is recorded, so the cap path itself does not index beyond the fixed arrays. Timer-setup failure during BIOS handoff remains OD2955. BAR mapping, port-register reads, and actual controller behavior remain hardware-dependent and unverified. No PCI inventory, timer, or controller was exercised. Source-only.


USB hub rescan timer cleanup race recheck (OD2468 expanded, 2026-10-19): re-read `hub_process`, `USBTimer`/`USBTimerDone`/`USBDeleteTimer`, timer-device reply, Exec `ReplyMsg`/`InternalPutMsg`, and task-removal ownership. `USBTimer` stores the current hub task in the timer reply port and submits the 10-second rescan asynchronously; `evt_Cleanup` deletes only `hub->tr`, replies, and returns, leaving local `rescan` pending. The selected timer implementation later replies that request through `InternalPutMsg`, whose PA_SIGNAL action calls `Signal` on the stored task pointer; `NewAddTask`'s task MemList is freed by `RemTask` after entry return. Expanded existing OD2468 to record this conditional stale-task signal as well as the already documented timer/device/port leak. Trigger requires disposal before the armed rescan completes. No hub teardown, timer completion, or task signal was run. Source-only.


USB hub cleanup reply-port and rescan signal follow-up (OD2287/OD819 confirmed; no duplicate, 2026-10-19): re-read `USBHub::Dispose`, `OnOff`, `hub_process` event/signal dispatch, `USBTimer` signal allocation and Exec `WaitPort`/reply-port behavior (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:204-215,278-292,628-718`; `misc.c:123-150`; `rom/exec/waitport.c:62-85`). Both cleanup and OnOff use an unchecked `CreateMsgPort()` before `PutMsg`/`WaitPort`; the NULL reply-port and `WaitPort(NULL)` path is already OD2287. The worker also uses the raw signal index returned by `USBTimer` as a Wait mask and fails to clear it after consuming the request; the missed wake, delayed rescan, and subsequent empty `WaitPort` path are already OD819. These are distinct from OD2468’s pending timer request retaining a pointer to the task after cleanup. No port allocation, signal exhaustion, timer, or hub method was exercised. Source-only.


Deneb command-query and QuickIO caller-contract pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): read `cmdReset`, `cmdUsbReset`, `cmdUsbResume`, `cmdUsbSuspend`, `cmdUsbOper`, `cmdQueryDevice`, `cmdNSDeviceQuery`, and their `devBeginIO` dispatch (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:569-800,1548-1610`; `dev.c:545-640`). Checked QueryDevice output writes against `<devices/usbhardware.h>`, the usbhardware.device documentation, and the selected Poseidon query caller (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:187-220`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:513-555`; `poseidon.library.c:9130-9140,9215-9255`). Poseidon initializes optional endpoint callbacks to NULL; Deneb does not handle those tags, so unsupported callbacks remain NULL. NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY size/format input checks and its RC_DONTREPLY handling match the selected `devBeginIO` completion branch. Although the driver advertises UHCF_QUICKIO and state-command comments prohibit interrupt context, the selected Poseidon PA_CALLBACK handlers only forward/abort queued pipe transfers (`poseidon.library.c:9072-9093`); the checked root-reset requests use the ordinary synchronous pipe path, and no selected interrupt-context caller of the state commands was found. The command-query routines therefore add no new defect from this source/caller slice. Remaining Deneb scope includes the still-partial 5,403-line implementation's hardware register/timing contracts, split scheduling, allocation failures, and abort/completion interleavings listed in the file row; no device or request was used. Source-only.

Deneb level-6 interrupt registration and open/close ordering pass (OD3582/OD3653 rechecked; no separate finding, 2026-10-19): traced the complete `Open_Unit()` registration sequence and `uhwHWInit()` interrupt-enable writes against `uhwLevel6Int()` and `uhwDMATask()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:117-245,452-486,502-525,5267-5368,5372-5401`). The handler is registered before `uhwHWInit()` and before `AddTask()`, but the hardware's global interrupt enable is written only at the end of successful initialization; before the worker is added, `hu_DMAPTD` remains NULL and the DMA handler does not signal it. `Open_Unit()` ignores `uhwHWInit()`'s error and still adds/publishes the worker/unit, already covered by OD3653. `Close_Unit()` disables the controller, removes the interrupt server, signals the worker, waits a fixed 10 ms, then frees the unit; the missing worker-exit join and its embedded storage lifetime are OD3582. No additional independent interrupt-registration defect was established. Hardware initialization, interrupt timing, and worker scheduling were not run; source-only.

Deneb ordinary and realtime ISO split-scheduling caller pass (OD3578/OD3604/OD3705 rechecked; no additional finding, 2026-10-19): read the full ordinary `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()` split branch, `cmdAddIsoHandler()` PTD setup, `cmdStartRTIso()` frame scheduling, and the recurring `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos()` OUT/IN rearm path (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4532-4770,1090-1233,1350-1482,3333-3795`). Compared request flags, hub/port values, endpoint packet size and frame interval against the public USBHardware fields and Poseidon's `psdAllocRTIsoHandler()`/Start path (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:39-48,88-100,157-175`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:90-116,438-495`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5555-5605,5630-5658`). Existing findings retain the independently established RTIso OUT rounded segment read (OD3578), dropped high-speed ISO multiplier (OD3604), and split per-microframe error status omission (OD3705). The inspected scheduling pass did not establish an additional independent defect; precise ISP1760 split scheduling semantics and real controller timing remain unverified. No controller, endpoint, or transfer was used; source-only.

Deneb control and interrupt split-PTD setup pass (no new finding, 2026-10-19): read `uhwScheduleCtrlPTDs()` and `uhwScheduleIntPTDs()` split branches and traced setup/data/status-stage reuse through `uhwHandleFinishedATLs()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1968-2784,3797-4189`). Checked that the request's split hub/port and low-speed flag are copied into the setup PTD, the shared PTD retains those fields through control data/status transitions, and interrupt PTDs set their split start/complete-split fields and select IN/OUT token from the request direction. Compared `UHFF_SPLITTRANS`, low-speed, hub/port, interval, and command contracts with the public header/docs and selected Poseidon request construction (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:39-48,157-175`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:90-116,224-249,306-328`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8470-8495`). No additional source-level defect was established in these setup paths; controller-specific scheduling semantics and real split timing remain open. No device or transfer was used; source-only.

Deneb timer-helper and NAK-timer shutdown pass (OD3582/OD3886 rechecked; no separate finding, 2026-10-19): re-read `uhwOpenTimer()`, `uhwDelayMS()`, `uhwCloseTimer()`, their `Open_Unit()`/`Close_Unit()` callers, and the recurring NAK timer callback (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:65-110,117-266,335-488,502-525,4825-4990`). Open failure paths delete whichever request/port was acquired; each checked delay is a fixed small millisecond value and is called only after successful timer open. The NAK request copies the opened timer request's device/unit fields, replaces the reply port with the embedded PA_SOFTINT port, and requeues only at the end of its callback. Close disables further callback delivery, calls AbortIO before closing the opened request, and does not reuse the NAK request; the selected timer.device AbortIO removes a pending request and replies synchronously (`rom/timer/abortio.c:49-93`), while PA_IGNORE suppresses the reply action (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:100-120`). No independent timer setup, arithmetic, or request-lifetime defect was established; the separate embedded worker lifetime remains OD3582, and wrap-unsafe NAK deadline comparison remains OD3886. No timer, expiry, or close was run; source-only.

Deneb bulk PTD allocator/DMA selection and request admission pass (OD3584/OD3585/OD3886 rechecked; no new finding for selected AROS m68k build, 2026-10-19): read the complete `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` allocation, DMA selection, PTD publication and retry setup against `cmdBulkXFer()`, ATL completion/release, and `FreeATL()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:850-911,1626-1700,1968-2784,4192-4531`). Large requests allocate the largest available contiguous granule run and are continued through subsequent PTDs; temporary lack of a run leaves the request queued for a later scheduling pass. The DMA mapping-shortening branch exits its `while(usedma)` without clearing `usedma`, which would continue with DMA fields but no valid mapped operation if `CachePreDMA()` returned a shorter contiguous span. However, the selected m68k Exec implementation (`arch/m68k-all/exec/cachepredma_.S:72-75,90-120`) returns the original address and leaves the input length unchanged, so that branch is not reachable in the reviewed AROS m68k configurations; it is not retained as an AROS finding. The ordinary non-DMA rounded OUT-buffer read remains covered by OD3585, active-DMA AbortIO by OD3584, and wrap-unsafe NAK deadline comparison by OD3886. Cache/DMA behavior on non-AROS external Exec implementations and hardware timing remain outside this conclusion. No request, allocation failure, DMA mapping, or device was exercised; source-only.

USB Audio GUI task-publication race recheck (OD3200 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): traced `nOpenCfgWindow()` through both `psdSpawnSubTask()` branches and `nGUITaskCleanup()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2160-2180,2200-2219,2282-2287,2309-2315,2370-2394`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1452-1465,1481-1510`). The DOS path returns after `CreateNewProcTags()` has added the process (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:543-556`); the no-DOS AROS path returns after `AddTask()` publishes the task (`poseidon.library.c:1502-1507`). Neither helper waits for the child to finish startup before `nOpenCfgWindow()` assigns its returned pointer. The child can take an immediate library-open/application/window-open failure exit and set `nh_GUITask = NULL` first; caller `Forbid()` does not serialize that cross-CPU store on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). The later assignment can then retain a dead pointer, and subsequent config-window requests only test the field as a boolean. This confirms the already detailed OD3200; no duplicate ID or runtime schedule added. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI sound-method fallback and buffer-ownership pass (no new OD, 2026-10-19): read `subLibSetVol`, `subLibSetFreq`, `subLibSetSound`, `subLibSetEffect`, `subLibLoadSound`, `subLibUnloadSound`, and the selected AHI load/unload dispatch (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3812-3892`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/sound.c:870-936,978-1000`). The USB Audio methods all return `AHIS_UNKNOWN`, which is the AHI contract for falling through to the software mixer; `subLibAllocAudio()` sets `AHISF_MIXING` for these modes (`usbaudio.class.c:3344-3348`). Consequently, for ordinary sample types AHI stores the caller's sample address/type/length in its own `ahiac_SoundDatas` table and marks it unavailable on unload, while the USB class does not claim or free the sample memory. In no-mixing controls AHI returns the sublibrary result directly; USB Audio does not advertise those controls. No separate method-result or buffer-ownership defect established. External AHI clients must still honor the documented sample lifetime and sound-index API contracts; no sound was loaded or played. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI attribute-query contract and indexed lookup pass (OD3207 confirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-19): read all of `subLibGetAttr()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3895-4075`) and compared its supported tags, defaults and indexed table accesses with AHI's `AHI_GetAudioAttrsA()` dispatch and documented ranges (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:293-306,367-385,461-505`). Traced the nearest-rate query to AHI Preferences `NewMode()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/ahi.c:304-305`) and confirmed it passes saved frequencies directly into `AHIDB_Index`; the fixed 100,000 threshold can therefore leave index zero when all advertised rates are farther away, matching existing OD3207. `AHIDB_FrequencyArg`, `AHIDB_InputArg`, and `AHIDB_OutputArg` are documented as indices within the corresponding count, and the selected AHI dispatcher passes them to the subdriver without normalization; their unchecked array reads do not establish a defect for contract-conforming queries. Unsupported tags return the caller's default, and absent `NepAudioMode` does likewise. `AHIDB_Outputs`/`AHIDB_Output`'s selector and fallback behavior is separately covered by OD3457. This pass found no additional independent attribute-query defect. USB Audio class row remains partial; other descriptor, topology, lifecycle, and stream paths remain open. No query or device was used; source-only.

USB Audio AHI hardware-control dispatch and selector caller pass (OD3238/OD3457 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): read all of `subLibHardwareControl()` and traced its public dispatch through AHI `ControlAudio` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:960-1000`) plus saved preference application (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:743-790`) into the USB worker (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:613-630,4082-4172`). Confirmed input selection is stored and signalled without index validation, and the worker's later `nGetInputUnit()` dereference makes a stale saved index on a replacement topology the existing OD3238 path. Output selection's unconditional success with no Selector Unit and the worker's selector-gated request remain OD3457. The remaining volume/gain/monitor controls store fixed-point arguments, set their update flags and wake the class task; the selected AHI caller forwards the supplied controls directly, and no additional independent control-dispatch defect was established in this slice. Device topology and live concurrent control calls remain untested. Source-only.

USB Audio mode-descriptor projection/body recheck (OD3171/OD3172/OD3494/OD3947 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): read all of `nExamineAudioDescriptors()` and compared the fixed-layout casts and variable rate walks with `PsdDescriptor.pdd_Length` and the USB Audio 1.0 structure definitions (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1037-1312`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon_intern.h:436-450`; `compiler/include/devices/usb_audio.h:206-217,374-395`). Confirmed OD3171 covers the unvalidated header/general/format/endpoint extents and rate-array length; OD3172 covers registering modes with no projected frequencies; OD3494 covers the 64-entry truncation; OD3947 covers inconsistent subframe size versus resolution. Rechecked channel/resolution mapping and frequency sorting: the zero `nam_SampleType` assigned for 24-bit modes is not consumed by the selected converter or AHI control path (`usbaudio.class.c:3373,3457-3498`), so it does not establish a separate defect. The frequency arrays used for selection are separately filtered/sorted, and no further independent mode-projection issue was established. Descriptor verification and remaining topology/caller/error-path review stay partial; no descriptor or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio endpoint-bandwidth/mode-selection pass (OD3208 retained; OD4056 added, 2026-10-19): traced `nSelectAudioMode()` from alternate-interface selection through endpoint attributes and bandwidth calculation, then followed the selected rate through `subLibAllocAudio()`, `AHIDB_Frequency` queries, and `nOutReqHook()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3134-3173,3375-3404,3932-3936,2641-2672`). OD3208 remains the distinct unadvertised-request ordering/nearest-rate issue. Added OD4056: when the endpoint payload-derived ceiling is below a discrete advertised rate, the code lowers only `nam_MaxFreq`; it leaves `nam_FreqArray` visible and accepts an exact requested match, so frame-derived request lengths can exceed the endpoint's declared capacity. Example: 48 kHz stereo 16-bit requires 192 bytes per 1 ms interval while a 96-byte endpoint caps the calculated rate at 24 kHz. The exact host-controller/device completion behavior was not exercised. Source-only.

VIA Rhine shared-opener SANA-II caller recheck (OD4034 refined; no new finding, 2026-10-19): traced AROSTCP `iface_make()` opening its configured SANA-II device (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:319-334`) and WirelessManager opening the configured device/unit (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:940-965`). On AROSTCP deinit, `sana_down()` issues `S2_OFFLINE` only while `lib_OpenCnt == 1`, then closes its own request once (`if_sana.c:158-179,903-915`). With WirelessManager still holding the device open, AROSTCP skips Offline; VIA Rhine's Close vector nevertheless unconditionally stops the shared unit, confirming this selected maintained caller sequence for OD4034. This caller pass does not establish that both clients are configured for every deployment; no device or close sequence was run. Source-only.


PCIDT shared-source MSI dispatch review (OD4057 added, 2026-10-19): traced one synchronous `AddHardwareDriver()` registration per discovered bridge into per-bridge `DWC_MSI_INTR0_STATUS` setup, `KrnModifyIRQA()` slot selection, `krnFindMSIController()` and the PLIC claim/complete loop. A repeated PLIC source matches and overwrites the prior slot, while dispatch polls only the stored controller; an uncleared first-controller line is eventually masked by the stuck-source guard. Added OD4057, conditional on distinct DesignWare bridges sharing an MSI PLIC source. This is separate from OD1411's table-capacity failure on more than four distinct sources. No checked-in board FDT establishes the topology; no IRQ or hardware was used. Source-only.


USB Audio INITLIB failure rollback recheck (OD3239 confirmed; 2026-10-19): traced the selected `kernel-usb-classes-usbaudio` module type through genmodule’s `usbclass` resident-autoinit selection and failed-init wrapper (`rom/usb/classes/audio/mmakefile.src:9-14`; `tools/genmodule/config.c:825-830`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1180`). `libInit` is in INITLIB and `libExpunge` in EXPUNGELIB (`usbaudio.class.c:150-152`); `_set_libinit` invokes expunge callbacks when INITLIB returns false (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:60-69`). The cleared outer base leaves `nh_SubLibBase` NULL if Utility open or nested `MakeLibrary()` fails, and `libExpunge` dereferences it before checking (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:108-110`; `usbaudio.class.c:66-100,110-118`). A nested allocation failure also strands the acquired `nh_UtilityBase` reference. This confirms existing OD3239; the duplicate report entry has been removed. No module load or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

USB Audio worker/control and stream-callback recheck (OD3167/OD3174/OD3193/OD3228/OD3971 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): re-read the complete `nAudioTask()` update dispatch and shutdown loop, `nOutReqHook()`, `nInReqHook()`, `nInDoneHook()`, `nReleaseHook()`, and USB Audio `subLibStart`/`subLibUpdate`/`subLibStop`/`subLibFreeAudio` paths (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:588-780,2620-2775,3570-3807`). Cross-checked start/update/control dispatch through selected AHI `AHI_ControlAudioA()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:931-999`) and RTIso request/release callbacks. The worker's unprotected shared update flags and clear-after-transfer remain OD3167; output/input buffer callback behavior remains OD3228/OD3193; ignored RTIso start errors remain OD3174; the worker/FreeAudio shutdown overlap remains OD3971. No additional independent defect established in this subset. This does not close the translation unit's remaining open caller, descriptor, and lifecycle scope; no AHI control, USB stream, device removal, or callback schedule was exercised. Source-only.

Other Drivers report duplicate-ID structure repair (OD4009/OD4010, 2026-10-19): each detailed USB HID finding had also been left as an unheaded paragraph beneath OD4008, while a shorter recovered copy appeared later under its own heading. Promoted the fuller analyses to their own OD4009 and OD4010 sections, removed the duplicate recovered sections, and retained the compact index entries. USB HID configuration and LowLevel list-lifetime pass (OD3923/OD3928 confirmed; OD4060 added, 2026-10-19): read `nLoadItem()`/`nSaveItem()` in full and traced every local load caller (`nAddItemAction`, `nLoadActionConfig`) and Store/Default GUI caller (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1462-1477,2445-2501,6614-6758`; `hid.gui.c:2399-2462`). ROM USB HID main worker and allocator full-body pass (OD4061 added; existing OD3920/OD3937/OD4009/OD4010/OD3948 rechecked, 2026-10-19): read all of `nHidTask()`, `nAllocHid()`, and `nFreeHid()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:709-1349`) and traced successful binding readiness, optional GUI startup, interrupt input dispatch, config reload, quit actions, abort/wait and cleanup against `usbForceInterfaceBinding()`/`usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()`. USB HID shared dispatcher, sound and Intuition action caller recheck (OD3936/OD4009/OD4010/OD3483 retained; OD4062 added, 2026-10-19): re-read `nInstallLastActionHero()`, `nDispatcherTask()`, `nLastActionHero()`, and the sound cache bodies, then checked the action producer and selected DOS/Intuition/layer contracts (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:5554-5577,6145-6178,6953-7310`; `rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:60-86`; `rom/hyperlayers/whichlayer.c:31-45,63-74`; `rom/intuition/closewindow.c:374-410,459-483`). DOS documents that asynchronous `SystemTags` closes supplied filehandles when the child exits, so the shell-action handle retention is intentional; the synchronous/error branches close it locally. OD3936 still covers concurrent dispatcher startup, OD4009 queued `nch`/`nha` lifetime, OD4010 failed sound-load cache and OD3483 key-string conversion failure. Added OD4062 because `HUAT_ACTWINDOW` uses `WhichLayer()` under `LayerInfo` but dereferences the returned `Layer *` after unlocking, when `CloseWindow` can delete it under that lock. Other `nLastActionHero` screen/window action lifetimes and the rest of this class remain open. No action, DOS process, window, or device was run. Source-only.

USB host-controller bus-state command cross-driver recheck (OD3655 expanded; 2026-10-19): compared Deneb's `cmdUsbResume`/`cmdUsbSuspend`/`cmdUsbOper` against the corresponding PCIUSB, PCI xHCI, and selected Raspberry Pi USB2OTG handlers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:628-704`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:434-524`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:442-524`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/usb/usb2otg/usb2otg_core.c:603-642`). All only inspect state and return success/offline; none carries out the documented transition. Checked command dispatch and Poseidon's root-bus suspend/resume paths: Poseidon explicitly leaves these commands unsupported and the in-tree request paths do not issue them, so OD3655 remains limited to direct USBHardware clients. Expanded the existing finding and index rather than adding duplicates. No HCD request or state transition was run; source-only.
Deneb RTIso registration allocation-bound pass (OD3889/OD3604 reconfirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-19): reread `cmdAddIsoHandler()`'s PTD-pair search, 16-node free list, and large-area granule sizing (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1044-1255`), then traced its selected caller `psdAllocRTIsoHandlerA()` and endpoint-size source (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5555-5605,8476-8550`). The driver scans for a free adjacent PTD pair before removing a node; the unit owns 16 RTIso nodes and 32 ISO PTDs, so the unchecked `RemHead()` cannot be reached after exhausting RTIso nodes while a free PTD pair remains. Poseidon passes the parsed endpoint `pep_MaxPktSize`, and its selected descriptor path clamps isochronous sizes to 1,024 bytes before handler allocation; the resulting `slicesize`/granule-mask arithmetic stays within the Deneb map for those in-tree requests. The public direct-HCD path does not independently validate arbitrary malformed packet-size fields, but no valid in-tree request reaches the suspected overflow; no new finding is retained. This closes only the inspected registration allocation/size boundary, not split scheduling, hardware timing, or broader callback ownership. No allocation failure or request was induced; source-only.
Deneb split interrupt TT-flag consumption cross-controller pass (no new OD; 2026-10-19): compared `uhwScheduleIntPTDs()`'s split-PTD fields with the flags built by Poseidon's selected `psdAllocPipe()` path and `pGetTTInfo()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3957-4190`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4497-4505,4578-4593,7946-7982`). Poseidon supplies TT think-time bits and `UHFF_TT_MULTI`, but the Deneb scheduler does not consume either flag; the analogous xHCI endpoint-context path explicitly consumes both (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:1353,1452,1931,1952`). The public header describes these as TT timing/topology data (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:160-184`). However, the selected Deneb ISP1760 PTD definitions use a controller-specific split descriptor, and checked-in source/docs do not establish whether its integrated translator scheduling requires these values or what observable failure omission causes. No finding is promoted; Deneb split scheduling/hardware timing remains open pending a controller contract source. No hub or transfer was used; source-only.
USB host-controller bus-reset command cross-driver caller trace (OD3654 expanded; 2026-10-19): compared Deneb, PCIUSB, PCI xHCI and Raspberry Pi USB2OTG `UHCMD_USBRESET` dispatch/handlers against the documented reset contract (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:601-615`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:411-429`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:420-438`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/usb/usb2otg/usb2otg_core.c:585-601`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:589-612`). Deneb/PCIUSB/xHCI perform no port reset and can acknowledge success from current state/software bookkeeping. USB2OTG returns based on the request's `iouh_State` without querying or resetting hardware. Traced Poseidon's root request allocation (`CreateIORequest` uses `MEMF_CLEAR`, `rom/exec/createiorequest.c:62-68`), pipe copy (`poseidon.library.c:4511-4524`), initial reset and fatal error handling (`:4152-4160`), and configuration cleanup (`:7311-7313`); no selected source writes `iouh_State` into the USB2OTG root request, so the initial command returns `UHIOERR_USBOFFLINE`. Poseidon treats only `UHIOERR_HOSTERROR` as fatal at this call site and continues after the offline result (`poseidon.library.c:4152-4160`), so no enumeration failure is claimed; the request nevertheless receives a false-offline status and no reset operation occurs. Expanded OD3654 with the shared no-reset behavior and the concrete USB2OTG caller result. No controller or enumeration was run; source-only.
PCIUSB/xHCI standard CMD_RESET command contract expansion (OD3654 expanded; 2026-10-19): traced both `cmdReset()` handlers through `uhwGetUsbState()` and BeginIO dispatch (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:363-393,pciusb_dev.c:212-214`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:372-402,pcixhci_dev.c:214-216`) against the `CMD_RESET` contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:166-191`). Each handler delays 1 ms, then calls a helper that unconditionally writes `UHSF_OPERATIONAL`; neither resets the controller nor a port. Added these standard-command false-success paths to OD3654 alongside the existing `UHCMD_USBRESET` implementations. USB2OTG `cmdReset()` likewise checks only `iouh_State`, but returns offline for the cleared Poseidon root request; Poseidon ignores `UHIOERR_USBOFFLINE`, so no startup failure is claimed (`usb2otg_core.c:561-577`; `poseidon.library.c:4152-4160`). Deneb's standard `CMD_RESET` does call `uhwHWInit()` and remains excluded here; its failed-init masking is OD3653. No command or reset was run; source-only.
Deneb/Poseidon RTIso free-stop caller census (2026-10-19; no new OD): re-read Poseidon's `psdFreeRTIsoHandler()`/`psdStartRTIso()`/`psdStopRTIso()` and Deneb `cmdRemIsoHandler()`/`cmdStopRTIso()`, then classified every direct `psdFreeRTIsoHandler()` and `psdStopRTIso()` caller in `rom/usb`. USB Audio `subLibFreeAudio()` stops each allocated primary/sibling handler before freeing it; partial `AllocSonixcam()` cleanup frees only handlers never started; `GetVideoSnap()` stops successful starts before `FreeSonixcam()` later releases the handler. Deneb's stop command returns success for a registered handler and does not expose an in-tree failed-stop-before-free path. Poseidon's Free wrapper itself does not update `pd_IOBusyCount`; if an external caller frees an active handler without Stop, that accounting can remain elevated, but no public precondition/documentation establishes whether Free-on-active is supported, so this remains an API-contract lead and is not promoted. No stream, device removal or stop failure was induced; source-only.

AHCI media-monitor early-exit lifetime audit (OD4064 added; 2026-10-19): traced startup signaling, timer/message-port/request failure cleanup, retained `sim_Monitor`, CAM probe-failure detach, and Exec task return/reclamation (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:55-71,140-151,171-182,200-219,354-382`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:107,260-272`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:52-56`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:121-151`; `rom/exec/service.c:46-89`). USB Audio AudioControl graph-flow caller pass (2026-10-19; no additional OD): traced `nFindAudioUnit`/`nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, all four recursive flow helpers, and Stage 2-5 callers (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:782-1034,1413-1595`). The input-array capacity is explicitly limited to eight with a warning before parsing mixer/selector and processing/extension links (`:1424-1468`); downstream selector metadata has the same fixed eight-entry bound, so this is an acknowledged support limit rather than an unreported overflow. Unresolved source IDs remain OD3164; recursion through cyclic graph links remains OD3165. `nFlowDown` reads `nau_InputUnit[0]`, but its selected Stage 5 callers start from output units reachable through an input terminal's recorded output links; a missing source is not connected by `nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, while an output-terminal missing-source traversal is already OD3164. No independent valid-topology failure established. Descriptor extent, mode registration, and remaining class callers remain open; no descriptor or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio Feature Unit level-mapping caller audit (OD4065 added; 2026-10-19): traced `nFindLogVolume()` and the GET_MIN/GET_MAX control queries into AHI `AHIDB_Min/Max*` results, `AHIC_OutputVolume` sublibrary dispatch and the worker's SET_CUR conversion (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1313-1367,1764-1790,644-681`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:982-988`). The class advertises 0.0-1.0 Fixed values, then interpolates those values linearly in a Feature Unit's dB range. Cross-checked the selected VIA-AC97 AHI implementation, which advertises 0.0-1.0 and converts linear Fixed amplitude through its dB gain table (`via.c:746-750,801-805`; `misc.c:575-623`). For a -24-to-0 dB endpoint range, 0.5 maps to -12 dB in USB Audio (about 0.25 amplitude) versus the VIA table's nearest -7.5 dB step (gain about 0.42), near the -6.02 dB continuous 0.5-amplitude value. Added OD4065 for the intermediate-level mismatch; this is distinct from OD3202's signed arithmetic overflow on wide ranges and OD3981's cascading Feature Unit controls. Input gain and monitor volume use the same USB conversion. No AHI call or USB control request was made. Broader sublibrary caller and control-range coverage remains open. Source-only.

USB Audio selected-mode, allocation, and rollback pass (2026-10-19; no additional OD): read complete `nSelectAudioMode`, `subLibAllocAudio`, and `subLibFreeAudio` bodies and traced the selected AHI `_AHI_AllocAudioA` failure path (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3134-3653`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:481-520,657,702-742`). Exact-match frequency membership and mode-local endpoint parameters were traced, but descriptor-specific controller behavior and external AHI callers remain open. No audio allocation, USB request or device was run. Source-only.

Deneb split-interrupt schedule input/caller cross-check (2026-10-19; no additional OD): traced Poseidon pipe creation’s `UHFF_SPLITTRANS`, hub address/port and endpoint interval propagation into Deneb `uhwScheduleIntPTDs()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4568-4591,4625-4628`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4052-4146`) against the public interval units and split-hub contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:91-111,247-250`; `compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:160-184`). The full/low-speed split branch uses the millisecond interval to choose its start-split microframe and arms the selected PTD’s complete-split mask; the high-speed non-split branch consumes Poseidon’s normalized microframe interval. Did not establish a separate error in this selected interval translation. `UHFF_TT_MULTI` and TT think-time handling remain hardware-specific open questions because the checked ISP1760 PTD definitions expose no matching field; no behavior claim is made without the controller programming contract. No USB schedule or device was run. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary request abort and PTD-pressure requeue pass (2026-10-19; no additional OD): reread `cmdAbortIO`, `devAbortIO`, `TermIO`, `FreeATL/FreeInt/FreeIso`, and the relevant control/bulk/interrupt/iso queue submission and scheduler retry paths (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:800-1005,1602-1867,3957-4530,4778-4834`; `dev.c:520-692`). Every queued transfer clears `IOF_QUICK` before it can remain pending; successful queue removal is completed once by `devAbortIO`/`TermIO`, while PTD-backed cancellation detaches the request before type-specific retirement. The active ATL DMA-abort null dereference remains OD3584; the examined interrupt/ISO retirement paths do not share its DMA cache-post branch. When a scheduler stops for exhausted PTDs or controller-local buffer granules, transfer completion returns those resources and the completion soft interrupt reruns queued schedulers. No separate lost-reply or allocation-pressure stall established in these selected paths. The full ATL error/abort state cross-product and controller DMA stop latency remain open; no request, low-memory condition, or abort was induced. Source-only.

Deneb NODMA transfer-task versus AbortIO ownership pass (OD4066 added, 2026-10-19): followed `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` PIO fallback through the priority-12 worker, `uhwHandleDMAInt()` and active AbortIO retirement (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4251-4321,465-479,4995-5028,1635-1669,1778-1830`; `dev.c:679-686`). `uhwDMATask()` checks `hu_DMAPTD` and calls the handler without protecting that handoff, while the handler dereferences the PTD before its first `Disable`; AbortIO can clear the pointer between the check and call, causing a NULL dereference. A second window after handler entry lets AbortIO retire the PTD before the NODMA copy branch; the resumed handler can see `PTDT_FREE`, choose its copy-from-controller branch, and write through the retained `hu_DMAAddr` after completion. Added OD4066 to the detailed report and AROS index, scoped to `denebusb`/`denebz2usb` (`mmakefile.src:31-45`); DMA-enabled `denebdmausb` remains covered by OD3584. No transfer or schedule was run. Source-only.

`workbench/devs/audio/mmakefile.src:3-16,22-26` reaches the `eaudio` target from `workbench-devs-complete` for i386, x86_64, PPC and ARM, and explicitly excludes m68k. The module's `FILES` selects `libfunctions.c`, `audio_commands.c`, `objpoollite.c`, and `audio_esys.c`; the local `audio.conf` and `audio_intern.h` also feed its generated build. These paths were missing from the per-file inventory despite existing targeted caller notes elsewhere in this ledger.

Generator-derived vector source and selected runtime dispatch are understood; target-generated output/build remains unverified. |
| `workbench/devs/audio/audio_intern.h` | Full 250-line declaration read; ETASK/EUNIT initialization, selected consumers, and global task-state lifetime traced; broader external-client/cross-command ownership matrix remains open | `STOLEN_SIG` aliases Ctrl-C (OD4089); TSYS `ts_calltask` shared completion slot (OD4074); startup failure mismatch (OD4067); `global_eta` stale after final close and used by failed-open cleanup (OD4068). `ETASK` is allocated through `enode_AllocNode(..., MEM_TYPE)` where `MEM_TYPE` includes `MEMF_CLEAR`; each `EUNIT` comes from `CreateIORequest()`, which allocates `MEMF_PUBLIC|MEMF_CLEAR`. The four channel records are fully created before worker dispatch; partial initialization returns NULL before dispatch. Field zero-init assumptions are therefore established for the checked allocator paths. |
| `workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c` | Full 2,410-line function-body pass completed; checked-in ADCMD callsites catalogued; caller concurrency and nondefault eaudio build selection remain conditional | OD4087 is retained as a conditional finding: `setup_Units()` replaces the active-channel mask rather than preserving earlier live allocations, allowing a later accepted allocation to treat an earlier owner's channel as free and reset it without priority arbitration (`audio_commands.c:41-117,456-460`). The `workbench/devs/audio` `eaudio` module has no active default dependency edges (`mmakefile.src:4-15`), so this is not claimed for a default image. Prior ledger passes covered `free_ETask`/`init_ETask`, audio request draining, `FlushUnit`, shared AHI reply-port use, and `ADCMD_PERVOL`; see OD2325 and the WaitIO caller trace. OD4067 follows `TaskBody` signaling the original request reply port on `init_ETask()` failure instead of waking the opener on `STOLEN_SIG` (`:1031-1036,1210-1215`). OD4068 follows `audio_FREE` dereferencing NULL `global_eta` on cold-start task-creation failure and a stale ETASK/port pointer after a previous successful final close when a later `CreateNewProc()` fails (`:1894-1905`; teardown `:744-765,1210-1215`; `audio_esys.c:47-54,76-81`). OD4069 traces the `AllocateProc()` NOWAIT failure back to first-Open auto-allocation (`:97-197,1998-2025`) and the selected caller census: sound.datatype’s six-entry map, speech.device’s four-entry `AudioMasks`, and narrator.device’s default or caller-provided mask list; each fails to close after Open reports the allocation error. OD4082 covers the `ioa_Length & 15` truncation: a valid 16-entry map is treated as empty and returns a zero-channel success (`audio_commands.c:97-98,214-216`), unlike the ROM loop capped at 16 (`arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:129-149`). The selected narrator.device forwards caller-supplied `narrator_rb.ch_masks`/`nm_masks` without a count limit, but checked-in Say and Speak callers each use four masks; 16 alternatives require an external narrator.device client or a future caller. OD4070 now records the UWORD wrap starvation path: retaining one waiter while 65,535 queued allocations are canceled wraps `et_allocated` to zero, causing `ReAllocateUnits()` to skip the still-nonempty list (`:474-480,2118-2122`); later queue additions can also leave the counter below the list length. OD4071 covers the active `ADCMD_WAITCYCLE` branch clearing quick mode without placing the request on `eu_waitcyclelist` (`:1559-1572`); the public wrapper then suppresses the reply for an unchanged unit mask and completion only drains the list (`:1517-1534,1187,1491-1501`). OD4072 covers `_ADCMD_SETPREC()` testing its consumed `unit` mask after the loop, so `ReAllocateUnits()` is never reached for a valid selected unit (`:2354-2373,2385-2390`); the retry matters because the allocator may steal from a now-lower-priority owner (`:138-185`). OD4073 traces `CMD_STOP` aborting the internal AHI request then clearing `eu_usingme` without replying or preserving the client write (`:1738-1747`); `CMD_START` only drains a separate wait list (`:1619-1632,1658-1663`). The sound datatype Pause/Play path uses STOP/START (`dispatch.c:3056-3065,3074-3078,3428-3432`). The full transition also loses a retained `eu_audioio` cache when `StartWaiting()` dequeues a queued request and `UnitCopyData()` overwrites that slot before starting the new request (`:310-339,1619-1630`); an active, cached and queued trio can therefore lose two owners. Expanded OD4073; no separate ID. OD4074 records the shared `ts_calltask` completion slot used by synchronous command wrappers without BeginIO serialization (`audio_intern.h:93-103`; `audio_commands.c:1323-1332,1688-1697,1774-1784,1894-1905,1973-1982`; `libfunctions.c:26-120,159-198,215-280`). OD4075 covers the no-op `ADCMD_FINISH` handler compared with ROM abort/synchronous-cycle behavior (`audio_commands.c:1350-1387`; `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:266-295`). OD4076 covers `CMD_RESET` flushing requests without clearing `UNIT_STOP`, which causes subsequent writes to be queued by `_CMD_WRITE()` (`audio_commands.c:371-403,411-446,599-640`), unlike ROM reset (`audio.c:297-313`). OD2325 records the existing `ADCMD_PERVOL` zero-period candidate: the Paula maximum 65,536-cycle value is encoded as zero in UWORD `ioa_Period`, which reaches division in the selected AHI backend (`audio_commands.c:295-299,1415-1434`; `audio.device_readme:182-187`). `CMD_CLEAR`/`CMD_UPDATE` were compared with ROM `ADCMD_NULL_f` and show no additional selected behavior mismatch; `ADCMD_LOCK` remains inconclusive because the ROM source itself documents it as never returning, while its handler retains the request on the misc list. OD4078 covers `FlushUnit()` clearing active ownership without replying, omitting the `eu_audioio` pre-cache, and the later CMD_WRITE path that starts that cached request; `CMD_RESET` leaves the cache attached after its direct flush; `ADCMD_FREE` reaches `ResetUnit()`, which silently clears the cached pointer before flush (`audio_commands.c:371-403,411-446,456-460,517-540,599-640`). OD4079 also covers active/pre-cache AbortIO success status and active-abort queue starvation: clearing `eu_usingme` does not invoke `UnitReWrite()`, while TaskBody skips an already-returned internal AHI request with no active owner (`audio_commands.c:1092-1188,1218-1275,2063-2093,2128-2138`). OD4081 covers `_ADCMD_FREE()` adding mismatched-key channel bits to its returned mask despite not releasing those channels (`:533-560`). OD4083 covers zero-key `CMD_WRITE` and `CMD_READ` acceptance in eaudio and ROM Paula: free channels use key zero, which passes both command handlers’ direct equality checks (`audio_commands.c:599-611,1819-1857`; `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:108-126,396-454`). Eaudio additionally maps an empty CMD_READ mask to channel 0 and can report success with NULL data. Selected maintained clients allocate first; the trigger is an external/future caller that issues these commands before allocation. OD4084 covers the AHI completion branch ignoring `eu_ahireq.ahir_Std.io_Error`: finite client writes are forced to success and infinite writes retry even after an AHI error (`audio_commands.c:1092-1185`; AHI error/reply path `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:823-875,256-292`). OD4086 covers the shared-command post-dispatch request dereference: TaskBody reads the request command after `process_UnitsCmd()` returns (`:1192-1204`), while the selected `audio_FREE()` wrapper signals its caller before replying the request (`:1894-1915`) and `DevClose()` uses that path on the caller IORequest (`libfunctions.c:157-199`). On ExecSMP, the caller can receive the reply and reuse the request before TaskBody reads the command. The final-close race is confirmed separately: `_CMD_CLOSE()` frees the ETASK/ports then signals, and `audio_CLOSE()` restores the request command after waking, before TaskBody performs its CMD_CLOSE test (`audio_commands.c:744-768,1192-1204,2175-2205`). The `CMD_WRITE` path is not credited as a returned-request UAF because its wrapper waits for TaskBody's STOLEN_SIG before BeginIO returns (`:2038-2058`). The slave priority is 127; these overlap claims remain scoped to ExecSMP. No interleaving was run. Recent full-range checks covered `ADCMD_WAITCYCLE`/CMD_READ channel-slot invariants and START/STOP/RESET completion order; the apparent NULL-slot dereference was not promoted because successful worker initialization creates all four EUNIT records. Remaining body review, command cross-product, unit/task lifecycle and backend callers remain open. |

If `CreateNewProc()` fails, `InitSLAVE` returns without a worker and the caller's `DevClose` reaches the null `global_eta` path, OD4068. The only checked-in `FreeSLAVE` caller is `DevClose` on final close (`libfunctions.c:191-198`); it checks `ts_slavetask` then calls `audio_CLOSE`, whose worker teardown frees `global_eta` but does not clear it (OD4068), and signals before the worker's final `TaskBody` command check (OD4086). eaudio command-dispatch and priority/metadata handlers full-range recheck (2026-10-19; existing findings retained): reread the complete `process_UnitsCmd()` switch (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:667-735`) and the complete `_CMD_CLEAR`, `_CMD_UPDATE`, `_ADCMD_SETPREC` plus public wrappers (`:2216-2408`), tracing each through `BeginIO` (`libfunctions.c:37-109`) and the selected Paula `ADCMD_NULL`/SETPREC command cases (`arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:218-248,480-512`). The internal dispatcher receives only BeginIO-recognized commands plus its private ABORTIO/CLOSE messages; no reachable unsupported command falls through the switch. No additional finding. OD4084 AHI error-retention boundary recheck (2026-10-22; no new OD): re-read `TermIO()` and the entire selected `WriteCmd()` error exit (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:256-297,823-875`). `WriteCmd()` sets `ahir_Std.io_Error` before calling `TermIO()`; `TermIO()` snapshots that value for logging, frees any allocated Extras, and replies without clearing or replacing `io_Error`. On the caller side, the AHI reply message carries the same embedded request back to `TaskBody()`, where cycle bookkeeping runs without testing that field (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:1092-1188`). This rules out AHI cleanup/reply as the source of the missing status and confirms OD4084 is the eaudio consumer defect. No IO request or failure was induced; source-only.

USB Audio bandwidth finding HCD caller recheck (OD4056 strengthened, 2026-10-19): followed the `nOutReqHook()` rate-derived `ubr_Length` into PCIUSB UHCI and OHCI isochronous schedulers (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2641-2672`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_isoch.c:571-603`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ohci/ohci_isoch.c:313-331,431-470`). UHCI caps only at its host-controller ISO maximum before encoding one TD's translation length; it does not enforce the endpoint-specific `iouh_MaxPktSize`. OHCI derives its packet count from that endpoint size and advances the next frame by packet count times interval, spreading an over-capacity one-interval buffer across multiple frames. This strengthens OD4056's consequence from an oversized API request to controller scheduling behavior; it does not add an independent OD. PCIUSB includes both HCD implementations (`rom/usb/pciusb/mmakefile.src:10-17`), and the Sam440 boot menu loads the PCIUSB device (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/menu.lst:51,111`). No descriptor, USB device, controller or audio stream was used. Source-only.

Eaudio CMD_READ zero-key/free-channel caller pass (OD4083 expanded; 2026-10-19): traced the selected BeginIO dispatcher into `audio_READ()` and `_CMD_READ()`, then compared its channel/key checks with ROM Paula `ADCMD_READ_f()` and the public allocation state (`workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:32-35,49-52`; `audio_commands.c:22-37,1819-1857`; `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:108-126,437-454`). A free EUNIT starts with zeroed `eu_allockey`; zero-key reads therefore pass the same equality used by writes, mark a free channel selected and report success. In eaudio an empty channel mask additionally maps through `writechn[0]` to channel 0 and can return NULL data as success. The selected maintained callers found allocate before use; no new maintained trigger was established. Expanded OD4083 instead of duplicating the shared zero-key root. No I/O request was sent; source-only.

eaudio TaskBody bad-key CMD_WRITE reply-lifetime pass (OD4086 added, 2026-10-19): traced each per-channel worker dispatch after GetMsg (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:1051-1089`) into `_CMD_WRITE()`'s mismatched-key completion (`:642-655`). The non-quick branch calls `ReplyMsg()` before returning, but TaskBody then dereferences `ioaudioreq` to obtain `mn_ReplyPort->mp_SigTask` and signals it. eaudio STOP/START prefetched-write ownership recheck (OD4073 expanded, 2026-10-19): traced the complete STOP state transition and `StartWaiting()` restart from active/cache/queue occupancy (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:310-339,599-640,1619-1632,1715-1766`). OD4086 ExecSMP scheduling and final-close recheck (2026-10-19; finding narrowed and expanded): traced the request reply/signal ordering against the slave process's priority 127, Exec's single-CPU Signal priority rule and SMP signal path (workbench/devs/audio/audio_esys.c:39-45; rom/exec/signal.c:17-82,127-130; rom/exec/replymsg.c:26-64; rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-106). Followed the last-CloseDevice path through FreeSLAVE()/audio_CLOSE(), _CMD_CLOSE() freeing ETASK ports before signaling, caller restoration of the request command, and TaskBody()'s post-dispatch close check (workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:191-198; audio_esys.c:76-82; audio_commands.c:745-768,1192-1204,2175-2205). Eaudio temporary reply-port signal-target audit (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced every `mp_SigTask` reassignment in `audio_commands.c` through its worker-side signal and restoration (`audio_PERVOL`, `audio_ALLOCATE`, `audio_WRITE`, `audio_ABORTIO`; lines 1460-1478,1998-2027,2038-2058,2145-2167). The caller temporarily routes `STOLEN_SIG` to its own task and clears that task's bit before enqueueing. Concurrent callers using distinct reply ports therefore do not share this field; overlapping use of the same reply port by different tasks could race the temporary recipient assignment, but no selected in-tree shared-port caller or contract requiring cross-task port sharing was established, so this remains unpromoted. Existing OD4074 is the concrete independent race in the global `ts_calltask` slot. No command or concurrency was run; no line credit. Source-only.


OD4088 DoIO/SendIO consequence cross-check (2026-10-19): traced the wrapper's IOF_QUICK-dependent branch against Exec's public callers (`rom/exec/sendio.c:48-57`; `rom/exec/doio.c:50-73`). SendIO initializes flags to zero, so an early stale-bit wake reaches ReplyMsg while the worker-queued request remains linked; ReplyMsg sets NT_REPLYMSG and InternalPutMsg appends the same node without removing the worker-list link (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:63-88`). DoIO initializes IOF_QUICK, so the wrapper returns without ReplyMsg but DoIO sees the bit still set and returns without WaitIO. Expanded OD4088 to cover both premature completion outcomes. No request was submitted; source-only.
