Added OD4089: a new Ctrl-C arriving during the wait is mistaken for completion and discarded; DoIO then skips WaitIO because IOF_QUICK remains set, while non-quick wrappers can reply before the worker handles the queued request. This is separate from OD4088's pre-existing reply-port bit and overlaps OD4074's signal-routing commands only in command membership, not trigger/root cause. No signal or request was induced; no line credit. Source-only.

HID signed Usage-value shift pass (OD4092 added, 2026-10-19): re-read short-item integer assembly and Global Usage Page composition in `hid_get_item`, then checked the valid high-bit Usage/Page representations against the USB-IF HID Usage Tables. One- and two-byte payloads are sign-extended before Usage Page `<< 16`, and four-byte payload assembly shifts a promoted `UBYTE` by 24, whose sign-bit result is implementation-defined when representable as `unsigned int`; the negative signed Usage Page shift independently remains undefined for valid high-bit pages. Added OD4092 to the detailed report and index. Existing OD3142/OD3143 concern report-field extraction, while OD3145-OD3147 concern bounds/state. No descriptor or device was used; source-only.

VIA Rhine S2_DEVICEQUERY short-buffer/caller pass (later consolidated into OD3073, 2026-10-20): re-read the complete command dispatch and `CmdS2DeviceQuery()` (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/handler.c:97-180,273-297`), compared the field offsets in `compiler/include/devices/sana2.h:145-156`, and traced the selected AROSTCP query caller (`if_sana.c:346-350`), which supplies `sizeof(struct Sana2DeviceQuery)`. The handler copies only `min(SizeAvailable, sizeof(...))` then writes BPS, MTU, HardwareType, SizeAvailable and SizeSupplied unconditionally; there is no minimum-size guard, and short `SizeAvailable` therefore leaves later stores outside the advertised buffer. Deneb SET_ADDRESS toggle-base endianness recheck (OD3892 narrowed/confirmed, 2026-10-20): traced Poseidon's `psdPipeSetup()` storing `wValue` with `AROS_WORD2LE()` through the selected Deneb completion handler. On the big-endian m68k target, `wValue >> 3` therefore converts the little-endian in-memory value to `device_address << 5`, matching the 32-entry block used by `devadrep`; this is not an additional wrong-base defect. The remaining OD3892 is precisely the `epnum < 31` bound, which clears offsets 0–30 but leaves offset 31 (endpoint 15 IN) stale. The table is zeroed only at unit allocation, and Poseidon reuses freed addresses. No new finding or line credit. No address assignment or transfer was run; source-only.

Poseidon AddUSBClasses list, duplicate-name and mutation-lock pass (OD4117/OD4118 added, 2026-10-20): traced the selected `AddUSBClasses` command from its `SYS:Classes/USB` ExAll loop through `psdGetAttrs(PA_ClassList)`, the duplicate check, `psdAddClass()`, and the final `psdClassScan()` (`shellcommands/mmakefile.src:4-19`; `AddUSBClasses.c:86-163`; `poseidon.library.c:5971-6025`). The command compares only `strlen(puc->ln_Name)` bytes against the candidate filename (`:113-134`), so an existing class name that is a strict prefix of a distinct candidate causes the candidate to be skipped; Poseidon's own `psdAddClass()` duplicate test uses exact `FindName` equality (`poseidon.library.c:5720-5728`; `rom/exec/findname.c:76-85`). Added this prefix false-skip to the command's coverage note, conditional on such custom class names. Also confirmed the command's `Forbid()` traversal is not protected against cross-CPU class-list mutation in ExecSMP: `psdRemClass()` removes under PBase write lock and frees the node afterward (`poseidon.library.c:5767-5770,5818-5824`), while Exec documents Forbid as processor-local on SMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`); added OD4117. Separately, `psdAddClass()` checks with `FindName` under local Forbid, releases it, allocates, then enqueues under the PBase write lock, so concurrent same-name calls can both insert; added OD4118. The command is an explicit shell target; no class directory scan, concurrent caller, or device was used. Source-only.

PPP buffer-management callback ownership and Open-failure recheck (OD4121 added, 2026-10-20): traced Open, failed-open rollback, BeginIO queueing, Incoming_IP_Packet/SendPacket completion, AROSTCP's Open and per-request BufferManagement propagation, and the selected BT PAN device's per-open BufMan pattern. PPP writes CopyToBuffer into LIBBASE before validating CopyFromBuff; the missing-tag failure decrements the open count but leaves the new callback in place. Queued reads and writes later call those device-global pointers rather than the request's BufferManagement context. AROSTCP uses one tag table and one open, so its selected path does not itself trigger the mismatch; the public device accepts additional opens through its unit/open counters, and a second external opener can expose it. Added OD4121 with the failed-partial-open trigger and successful-incompatible-open variant. The PPP aggregate edge is disabled, so this remains an explicit optional target. This pass earns no whole-file line credit: handler.c and init.c already have body credit. No second open or packet was run; source-only.

PPP multi-open Close/serial ownership trace (OD4122 added, 2026-10-20): followed the successful Open count updates into Close, the CloseSerial macro and EasySerial cleanup, plus AROSTCP sana_down/CloseDevice sequencing and PPP read-queue completion. Two successful opens are accepted and increment unit_OpenCnt, but every Close frees LIBBASE->ser before decrementing the count; the final-close condition is empty. AROSTCP avoids S2_OFFLINE while another device opener remains but still closes its own handle, so PPP closes the shared serial connection while another opener survives. New requests then see ser == NULL; pending Rx_List requests are not completed by CloseSerial. Added OD4122, conditional on the second opener. This is separate from OD4121's per-open callback replacement on failed Open. No multi-open or serial close was run; source-only.

Deneb RTIso add/remove pool and caller recheck (OD3889 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced `cmdAddIsoHandler()`/`cmdRemIsoHandler()` through unit initialization and Poseidon's `psdAllocRTIsoHandlerA()`/`psdFreeRTIsoHandler()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1044-1320,386-423`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5555-5627`). Unit initialization seeds 16 free RTIso nodes and 32 free ISO PTDs; add requires a free adjacent PTD pair, removes one node, and consumes the pair while Disable is held; remove clears the RTIso back-links, frees both PTDs, and returns the node in the same critical section. The selected Poseidon allocator restricts this API to ISO endpoints and derives MaxPktSize from the selected endpoint. This rules out a separate reachable empty-node condition in the checked in-tree lifecycle; arbitrary malformed direct low-level requests and hardware register behavior remain open. The off-by-one contiguous-granule scan remains OD3889. No request, allocation failure, or controller operation was run; source-only.


Deneb interrupt dispatch and softint routing pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): reread uhwLevel6Int(), uhwSoftInt(), and uhwNakTimeoutInt() with the DMA worker and bridge/ISP register definitions (arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4774-4994,5265-5401; deneb.h:110-115; isp1760.h:50,96). If bridge DMA and ISP status bits are simultaneous, the early DMA return postpones internal ISP status handling after the bridge W1C write. Deneb split-interrupt interval encoding recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD pending controller-contract confirmation): compared uhwScheduleIntPTDs()'s split branch (arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4052-4081) with Poseidon's speed-specific endpoint interval initialization and propagation (rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8470-8484,8540-8575,4625-4628) and ISP1760 field comments (isp1760.h:375-379). xHCI synchronous command wrapper caller census (2026-10-20; no new OD, no whole-file credit): followed every direct `xhciCmdSubmit()` call and the selected wrappers in `xhci_hw.c:346-479` through callers in `xhci_hcd.c`, `xhci_schedule.c`, and `xhcidevice.c`. Slot enable failure frees the not-yet-submitted device context; Address Device failure attempts Disable Slot but ignores its result before clearing DCBAA and freeing the input context (existing OD4127, conditional on timeout plus failed slot quiescence). Hub-slot Configure Endpoint failure leaves the existing hub context allocated and reports failure. EP0 Evaluate Context failure rebuilds the input context to its prior max-packet size; endpoint Configure failure frees only a newly allocated software endpoint context, while the command input context remains owned by the device. Endpoint Reset and Set TR Dequeue failures return without freeing the ring or device context. This census did not find a separate immediate DMA-context free after timeout beyond OD4127. Command-ring result-slot reuse, concurrent command submissions, and controller recovery remain open; no timeout or controller operation was run. Source-only.

USB2OTG scheduler DMA/cache edge recheck (OD9473 added, 2026-10-24): followed direct IN DMA through `SetupChannel()` and `AdvanceChannel()` and reconciled the cache operation with the selected ARM-native `CacheClearE()` implementation. Transfers over the 16 KiB bounce size bypass bounce when the buffer base is 64-byte aligned, even if the IN length has a partial tail line. `CacheClearE()` promotes partial-line invalidation to clean+invalidate; if a neighboring CPU object dirties that shared line while DMA is active, post-DMA clean can write stale received bytes back. Traced a checked-in unrounded-length producer in `PencamTool::TransferImage()` through `psdAllocVec()` and `psdDoPipe()`; its allocation alignment is 16 bytes, so 64-byte alignment and concurrent adjacent-object mutation are conditional rather than guaranteed. BWFM S2_CONFIGINTERFACE/ONLINE/OFFLINE and event-mask caller recheck (2026-10-20; OD3614/OD3594/OD3611 retained, no new OD): traced the `handle_request()` cases through `report_events()`'s lock/latch/reply path and the selected WirelessManager `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE`, conditional `S2_ONLINE`, `S2_ONEVENT`, and event-rearm calls (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1362-1407,1650-1723`; `driver_sana2.c:835-880,990-1015,1059-1072`). `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` intentionally sets the interface online without associating; the selected WirelessManager caller expects that distinction and only sends `S2_ONLINE` for the already-configured response. Existing OD3614 covers the level-state snapshot versus event-list insertion gap; OD3594 covers the separate CMD_FLUSH omission; OD3611 covers emitted TX-error bits rejected by the supported mask. A zero S2_ONEVENT mask passes the unsupported-bit test and is queued, so it cannot match any future event; the local SANA-II header defines the event bits and BAD_EVENT code but does not state whether an empty mask is a valid request. WirelessManager's selected masks are nonzero. Retain zero-mask handling as an unresolved public API-contract question rather than a separate finding until validity is established. No request, state transition or radio operation was run; source-only.

PPP asynchronous serial TX buffer lifetime pass (OD4135 added, 2026-10-20): traced the selected PPP `WritePacket()` path through `SendPacket()` and `send_IP_packet()` into `SendBYTES()` and Exec `SendIO()`, then followed SANA-II completion through `TermIO()`. The IP path encodes into a stack-local `struct packet`; `SendBYTES()` gives `p.header` to the serial request and returns immediately after asynchronous submission, then `SendPacket()` replies the SANA-II request without waiting for serial completion. Added OD4135 for the conditional use of expired stack storage by a still-active serial `CMD_WRITE`. The control-protocol `SendPPP_Packet()` path uses synchronous `DoBYTES()` and is excluded. The PPP module is directly buildable but omitted from the default `workbench-devs-networks` aggregate. No serial operation or packet was run; source-only.

PPP serial RX event-loop and teardown caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced the serial request ports through `PPP_Process()` and `CMD_READ_Ready()` (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/init.c:98-120,154-167,259-269`), then rechecked `QueueSerRequest()` and `_CloseSerial()` (`serial.c:191-253`). The process consumes at most one completion from each single outstanding RX/TX request per wake, routes RX `io_Actual` bytes into the PPP decoder, and resubmits after the read completes. An SDCMD_QUERY error marks the serial connection not-OK; the next main-loop pass closes it, while shutdown aborts/waits and drains both request ports before deleting their ports and buffers. The observed SendIO `io_Error` check occurs immediately after asynchronous CMD_READ submission and cannot establish the eventual completion status, but the worker later receives the completion and the next SDCMD_QUERY supplies the existing device-loss check; no separate consequence was established in this pass. This does not resolve device-specific SDCMD_QUERY/CMD_READ contracts or external concurrent control/Close calls. No serial device or request was run; source-only.

ModemManager duplicate serial-helper caller cross-check for OD4135 (2026-10-20; no new OD): searched all `SendBYTES()` references and found only the PPP `send_IP_packet()` caller plus the separate ModemManager helper definition; ModemManager has no call to `SendBYTES()`. Its selected command/reply paths call `DoStr()` → `DoBYTES()` → `DoIO()` (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/ModemManager/misc.c:215-291,366-380`), which waits for completion before returning, so stack or temporary command buffers remain live through serial transfer. OD4135 remains scoped to the PPP IP-data `send_IP_packet()` path. The helper bodies were already credited; no line credit added. No modem command or serial I/O was run; source-only.

PPP OD4135 serial-device consumer-side lifetime confirmation (2026-10-20; no new OD): followed the accepted asynchronous request beyond `SendBYTES()`. The selected `serial.device` `CMD_WRITE` path passes `io_Data` directly to `HIDD_SerialUnit_Write`; if the first call cannot write the whole range, it retains the original request as `su_ActiveWrite` or queues the request (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:449-493,515-543`). The write-empty interrupt handler later indexes `io_Data` by `su_NextToWrite` and performs another HIDD write before replying the IORequest (`serial_interrupthandlers.c:132-178`). Thus no copy is made that would end the caller-buffer lifetime requirement when `SendIO()` returns. Combined with `send_IP_packet()`'s local `struct packet p` and `WritePacket()`'s immediate `TermIO()` after `SendPacket()`, this confirms the OD4135 trigger specifically when serial output is not accepted in the first synchronous HIDD write; complete-first-write timing avoids the dangling period. Source-only; no serial operation run and no line credit added.

Eaudio OD4086 synchronous CMD_WRITE caller-boundary correction (2026-10-20): re-read `audio_WRITE()` after the earlier generic post-ReplyMsg claim. It temporarily redirects the reply-port signal task to the current BeginIO caller, queues the request, waits for TaskBody's `STOLEN_SIG`, restores the original task, and only then returns (`audio_commands.c:2038-2058`). Therefore the bad-key `_CMD_WRITE()` `ReplyMsg` followed by TaskBody's per-channel signal is not treated as a normal caller-reuse-before-worker-access trigger. Retained OD4086 on the independently selected shared-command `ADCMD_FREE` path and final close: the wrapper replies after `TaskBody()` may still need the request command, and the close wrapper restores `io_Command` after the worker has freed its ETASK and signaled but before the post-dispatch check. Updated the detailed report, index wording and source ledger; no behavior was run. Source-only.

Eaudio extended-command selected-caller census (2026-10-20; no new OD): searched all checked-in C/assembly references to `ADCMD_*`. `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c` is the only caller outside the eaudio implementation and selected ROM Paula implementation; its playback path issues `ADCMD_PERVOL` and allocates through first Open. Network worker signal-exhaustion candidate recheck (OD3106 and OD3671 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): traced Intel Pro/100, Etherlink III, Realtek8180, Rhine, Prism2, and Atheros5000 task allocation through the AROS `AddUnitTask` macro and `NewAddTask()` into each worker's first signal allocations. Each `struct Task` is allocated with `MEMF_CLEAR`, no caller sets `tc_SigAlloc`, and `NewAddTask()` replaces zero with `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc == 0xffff` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-252`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). This leaves sixteen allocatable signal bits; the selected worker paths allocate one to four before any wait and perform no earlier signal allocation. Therefore the unchecked `AllocSignal(-1)` results and negative shifts are real source conditions, but exhaustion is not reachable through the selected task-creation paths; the earlier absence-of-handshake argument did not establish the trigger. Withdrew both findings and removed them from the report/index and current file-row candidate lists. OD3672 remains separate: VIA-Rhine has a signal-number/mask mismatch and frees worker-owned state without joining. No task or signal operation was run; source-only.


Nvidianet worker signal-exhaustion candidate recheck (OD3674 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): traced `CreateUnit()`'s cleared `struct Task` allocation (`workbench/devs/networks/nvidianet/unit.c:309-312`) through the AROS `AddUnitTask` macro (`task.h:57-62`) and `NewAddTask()`'s default signal mask (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-252`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The worker's first body operation requiring a private signal allocates only one bit (`unit.c:1994-2002`); there is no preceding task-local signal allocation. With sixteen signal bits available, exhaustion is not reachable through this selected startup path. Withdrew OD3674 from the report and index; no task or signal operation was run. Source-only.


LPe32002 worker signal-exhaustion candidate recheck (OD3673 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): traced `CreateNewProcTags()` through `CreateNewProc()` and `AddTask()` to the Exec default signal mask, then counted the worker's earlier port signals before its four private allocations. The fresh process starts with `tc_SigAlloc == 0xffff` (sixteen allocatable bits); three successful `CreateMsgPort()` calls consume at most three, leaving at least thirteen for the four later `AllocSignal(-1)` calls (`workbench/devs/networks/lpe32002/unit.c:501-538`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:531-550`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-252`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). Thus exhaustion is not reachable through this selected startup path. Unchecked creation of the reply/input ports and missing worker join remain separately tracked by OD2326 and OD3153; no signal-exhaustion finding retained. No process or signal operation was run; source-only.


nForce worker-startup failure contract recheck (OD3056 retained, 2026-10-20): verified the exact `CreateNewProc()` NULL-on-error contract (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:62-70`) and the selected `WaitPort()` loop that waits repeatedly while no message is queued (`rom/exec/waitport.c:62-86`) against `CreateUnit()`'s unconditional process creation and startup wait (`workbench/devs/networks/nForce/unit.c:1093-1106`). On task-creation failure the worker cannot send the handshake, and the caller has no failure branch to clean up or return; this confirms the existing constructor-hang candidate. Kept it within OD3056, shared with PCNet32 and SiS900; no separate ID. No allocation or worker startup was induced; no source-line credit added. Source-only.


PCNet32 worker signal-exhaustion candidate recheck (OD3057 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): traced `CreateNewProcTags()` through the DOS process startup and counted child-task signal use before the shutdown `Wait` loop. The fresh process uses Exec's default `TaskSigAlloc == 0xffff`, leaving sixteen user signal bits (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:68-69,543-550`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-252`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The worker creates three message ports (reply, input and timer) before four private `AllocSignal(-1)` calls, and the module contains no other signal allocation (`workbench/devs/networks/pcnet32/unit.c:954-993`). With all three ports successfully created, at most seven of sixteen user bits are consumed; the unchecked failure return is therefore not reachable through this selected startup path. Withdrew OD3057 from the report/index. OD3056's independent process-start handshake failure and OD3083-style signal number/mask mismatches in other drivers are unaffected. No worker or signal operation was run; source-only.


SiS900 worker-signal availability recheck (OD3089 narrowed, 2026-10-20): followed `CreateNewProcTags()` from `CreateUnit()` to the worker and counted all task-local signal allocations before `Wait` (`workbench/devs/networks/sis900/unit.c:698-737,953-964`). The new DOS process receives the default sixteen user signal bits; the worker first creates reply, input and timer ports, then allocates four private signals, with no other direct signal or message-port allocations in the module (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:68-69,543-550`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-252`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). With all three ports created, at most seven of sixteen bits are consumed, so the unchecked -1 path is not reachable through this selected startup. Retained OD3089 for the independent bit-number/one-hot-mask mismatch and free-before-worker-exit ordering; removed signal exhaustion and its proposed allocation-failure fix from the detailed wording. No process or signal operation was run; source-only.


Network worker signal exhaustion candidate correction (2026-10-20): removed OD3098 and OD3103 from the active report and index. RTL816x creates a fresh DOS worker with the default `tc_SigAlloc=0xffff`; its two message ports and four private signals consume six of sixteen user signals, so the three later allocations cannot fail from exhaustion in that startup path (`rtl816x/unit.c:628-646`; `prepareexecbase.c:319`; `newaddtask.c:249-251`). Broadcom4400 creates its unit task through `NewAddTask` (`task.h:57-61`; `unit.c:335`), which installs the default signal mask when `tc_SigAlloc` is zero; `UnitTask` then allocates its signal in that task (`unit.c:1982-1999`), so exhaustion is likewise unsupported by the selected startup path. Corrected the network signal inventory's active findings list accordingly.

E1000 shutdown signal correction (2026-10-20): merged OD3017 into OD2436, removed duplicate OD3017 from report/index, and narrowed OD2436. On a fresh scheduler task, three ports consume bits 16-18 and the four private allocations succeed at 19-22; raw Signal(19) does not wake a Wait on bits 16-22, and `recvd & 19` cannot match those awaited bits. The additional signal-exhaustion claim was removed. The independent no-join/free-before-worker-exit defect remains. Historical checkpoints above retain their original dated claims and are superseded by this correction.

OD3773 withdrawn after Bluetooth pool-flag audit (2026-10-20): the earlier claim that `btGetStringChunk()` and BTHID action strings may be unterminated was based on treating `AllocPooled()` as non-clearing. The Bluetooth library creates `bt_MemPool` with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:95`), `btAllocVec()` allocates all these buffers from that pool (`:269-299`), and Exec `AllocPooled()` passes the pool requirements into `InternalAllocPooled()` (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:87-93`), whose allocator clears the allocated block when `MEMF_CLEAR` is set (`rom/exec/memory.c:661-673`). Thus `bGetStringChunk()`'s extra `len+1` byte is zero; for BTHID's fixed-capacity `strncpy`, the destination's final byte is zero even when the copy count omits the source terminator. This invalidates the reported core C-string overread, BTHID short-source overread, and proposed long-string destination-boundary consequence. Removed OD3773 from the detailed report and `AROS.md`; prior ledger entries are superseded by this correction. No config was loaded. Source-only.

Added OD4137 for the conditional close-versus-drain use-after-free, distinct from OD4125's ring-index wrap. Confirmed the class is optional in the aggregate and has explicit CPU-specific targets (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/mmakefile.src:4-11`). No CAMD client, USB device, or concurrent close was run. Source-only.

Deneb DMA-task stack-size check (2026-10-20; no OD): confirmed `Open_Unit()` provides the embedded task exactly 512 bytes (`denebusb.h:328`; `uhwcmd.c:472-479`) and `uhwDMATask()` directly calls `uhwHandleDMAInt()` only on its DMA signal (`:5374-5401`). RPi HDMI playback worker/IRQ lifetime recheck (OD4001 strengthened, 2026-10-20): followed `_AHIsub_Stop()` through worker signaling/wait, `KrnRemIRQHandler()`, DMA stop and buffer cleanup (`rpihdmi-main.c:314-345`) against the worker's `Forbid(); slavetask=NULL; barrier; Signal(master);` exit sequence (`rpihdmi-playslave.c:181-194`) and the IRQ handler's unsynchronized task-field check/use (`rpihdmi-dma.c:187-206). Cross-checked Exec/kernel semantics: Exec documents Forbid as local-CPU-only under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`); IRQ dispatch holds the shared read lock during callbacks (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:120-142`), and KrnRemIRQHandler acquires its write side before unlink/free (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:59-75`). Because the driver waits for task exit before taking that write lock, handler removal does not pin the Process during the earlier worker shutdown. The callback does not explicitly copy the field; its concurrent check/use can race the clear, with stale-pointer or NULL manifestation depending on the load reaching Signal. Task memory is queued for asynchronous cleanup as RemTask marks it invalid (`rom/exec/remtask.c:109-163`; `rom/exec/service.c:37-90`). OD4001 remains supported and scoped to an ExecSMP cross-core overlap; no task/IRQ interleaving was run. The shared Exec task/Signal sources were also compared with EK832: that finding concerns queued async IPI raw-pointer lifetime, while OD4001's window exists before the IRQ callback enters Signal and no Signal IPI has yet been committed. No duplicate Exec finding added. No source line credit for driver bodies; broader driver caller/configuration and hardware timing checks remain open. Source-only.

Deneb RTIso registration/start/stop/release caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced the 16-node free pool and paired PTD allocation at unit setup through `cmdAddIsoHandler`, `cmdStartRTIso`, `cmdStopRTIso`, and `cmdRemIsoHandler` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:405-421,1060-1260,1270-1315,1329-1484,1501-1541`). NVHDMI connection-list response format pass (OD4154 added, 2026-10-20): compared the complete `setup_hdmi_codec()` converter/pin scan with Intel HDA Specification §§7.3.3.3 and 7.3.4.11. The spec marks long form in length bit 7, requires an even starting entry index, and returns two 16-bit entries; short form uses an index divisible by four and returns four bytes. NVHDMI masks bit 7, always uses `entry & ~3`, and shifts by `(entry % 4) * 8`, so long-form lists are decoded and selected with the wrong entry/index. The parser runs in both `card_init()` and Start-time route re-selection; added OD4154 with the codec-order condition explicit. Source-only; no codec or display audio was exercised.

Deneb control-transfer scheduler pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): read `cmdControlXFer` and the complete `uhwScheduleCtrlPTDs` setup/PTD publication path (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:797-838,3797-3955`) against the selected `dev.c` dispatch and the public USB hardware endpoint/address ranges (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:234-248`). UHCI OD2974 timeout/completion serialization recheck (2026-10-20): re-read both timeout branches and `uhci_FreeTD()` against the interrupt-handler ControlLS/ControlFS/Bulk retirement loops (`uhciclass.c:175-298,777-798,845-866`; `hardware.c:186-224`). Refined the race: the timeout walk is not protected as a whole; `uhci_FreeTD()` reenables local interrupts after changing the allocator bitmap, before the caller advances `p_FirstTD`. A pending USBINT can therefore preempt on the same CPU and retire the chain before the timeout task resumes; ExecSMP adds cross-CPU exposure because Disable is local only. Updated OD2974 and the master index to avoid making SMP a prerequisite. The x86_64-pc SMP boot manifest selects `kernel-package-usb`, while UHCI still requires a matching controller; Sam440's checked PCI460 backend is OHCI-only. No controller, transfer, or interrupt interleaving was run. This is targeted concurrency-path evidence and adds no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Deneb EHCI status acknowledgement contract follow-up (2026-10-20; no OD): re-read `uhwNakTimeoutInt()` alongside `uhwLevel6Int()` and `uhwHWInit()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:117-277,4774-4994,5265-5370`; `isp1760.h:29-30,286-293`). Startup enables `EHSF_TDDONE`, `EHSF_PORTCHANGED`, and `EHSF_FRAMECOUNTOVER`; the NAK timer reads `EHCI_USBSTS`, writes back every asserted bit, and only consumes FRAMECOUNTOVER for counter extension. The level-6 path separately handles ISP PTD-done maps and ISP interrupt-pending bits. This creates a hardware-contract question about whether clearing EHCI USBSTS TDDONE/PORTCHANGED can suppress any needed Deneb event, but the checked-in source does not show how those EHCI status bits relate to ISP1760's independent PTD maps/port-change signals. No lost event or user-visible consequence is established, so no finding is promoted. Controller register behavior and the remainder of the 5,403-line translation unit remain open. No status bit or hardware was exercised. Source-only.


Deneb NODMA CMD_FLUSH versus DMA-task handoff follow-up (OD4066 expanded, 2026-10-20): traced `dev.c`'s `CMD_FLUSH` dispatch into `cmdFlush()`'s active ATL loop and `FreeATL()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:554-557`; `uhwcmd.c:973-1005,1626-1684`). In the NODMA target, FreeATL clears `hu_DMAPTD` and retires the PTD while `uhwDMATask()`'s signal-check/handler handoff remains unprotected; it has no revalidation after the check and the handler dereferences `hu_DMAPTD` before disabling task switches. A higher-priority flush can therefore produce the same NULL-PTD window as AbortIO, or the stale buffer-copy window after handler entry. Expanded OD4066's caller and trigger to include CMD_FLUSH; this is the same shared-state race, not a second ID. No flush, transfer, task schedule or device was exercised. Source-only.

ATA DirectSCSI-to-SCSIEmu caller-path confirmation (OD3010 rechecked, 2026-10-20): read `cmd_DirectScsi()` and the `SCSIEmu()` opcode paths alongside the public `SCSICmd` definition and QuickPart's `QPDisk__Func_IdentifyDrive()` fallback (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:483-505`; `rom/devs/ata/scsiemu.c:51-62,155-216`; `compiler/include/devices/scsidisk.h:21-33`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:88-120`). Packet devices validate minimum/maximum CDB length in `atapi_DirectSCSI()` (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1112-1129`), while ATA direct-access dispatch reaches `SCSIEmu()` without that validation. QuickPart first submits one-byte ATA IDENTIFY, then submits a one-byte SCSI INQUIRY with `scsi_CmdLength=1`; the emulator reads INQUIRY fields at bytes 1, 2 and 4. This independently confirms OD3010's concrete in-tree caller and narrows the contrasted validation behavior by device type. The caller expects its one-byte ATA command to be rejected by the SCSI emulator before falling back; no command was issued and no new finding or line credit was added. Broader direct-SCSI opcode/data-buffer validation and ATA command handlers remain open. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary ISO buffer-release rescheduling pass (OD4157 added, 2026-10-20): re-read the complete ordinary `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()` allocation-failure path, `FreeIso()`, `cmdRemIsoHandler()`, `uhwSoftInt()`, and the level-6 RTIso completion routing (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1270-1313,1742-1761,4532-4774,4780-4831,5326-5345`). Deneb ATL bulk-IN/OUT DMA completion state recheck (OD3585/OD3584/OD4066 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-20): re-read the data-IN and data-OUT completion state transitions in `uhwHandleFinishedATLs()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2124-2475`) against the scheduler's DMA setup and buffer extents (`:4192-4530`) plus `FreeATL()` cache/reply order (`:1626-1684`). Deneb bulk OUT word-copy bounds recheck (OD3585 confirmed, 2026-10-20): traced the ordinary bulk scheduler's small-buffer PIO OUT copy plus the `CopyMemShuffle()` implementation under the selected AROS build (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:37-44,4254-4277,4404-4409`) against the documented bulk request byte-count contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:197-206,240-246`). The AROS helper copies only `size >> 2` words, but the caller rounds `ptd_BufLen` up to a multiple of four before passing it; for any non-multiple-of-four PIO OUT chunk, that reads the final one to three bytes beyond the declared data extent. This confirms the existing OD3585 and does not warrant a duplicate finding. The bulk OUT continuation path applies the same rounding at `uhwcmd.c:2498-2505`. Deneb zero-length bulk request reused-PTD state audit (OD4160 added, 2026-10-20): traced `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` through PTD allocation and unconditional DW0 length encoding, `FreeATL()` teardown, and bulk OUT completion accounting (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4239-4255,4329-4409,4381-4385,1635-1670,2477-2480`) against the documented bulk transfer byte-count contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:197-206,240-246`) and Poseidon's `psdDoPipe()` caller (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4620-4627,4708-4725`). A zero-length request bypasses the only `ptd_BufLen` initialization, while `FreeATL()` retains the previous slot value; Poseidon forwards its `len` argument directly for bulk endpoints, making zero-length requests reachable through the in-tree caller. Reuse after a nonzero transfer therefore encodes stale length into the next hardware PTD, and the OUT completion path adds the reported count to `iouh_Actual` without bounding it by the request length. Added OD4160 to the detailed report and master index. No request or device was exercised; the Deneb translation unit remains partial, with no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Deneb high-speed ISO continuation cadence pass (OD4164 added, 2026-10-20): resolved the earlier hardware-frame-selector question using the selected USBHardware contract and checked-in ISP1760 PTD definitions (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:111-113`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8525-8548`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/isp1760.h:375-379,417-420`). Poseidon supplies high-speed ISO intervals in power-of-two microframes. Deneb's initial scheduler puts the requested frame in DW2 and microframe activity in DW4; continuation calculates the next requested frame by adding `ceil(interval/8)`, but compiles out that DW2 encoding and instead schedules at `EHCI_FRINDEX + 8`, one frame later (`uhwcmd.c:3283-3308`). For intervals above eight microframes, that is earlier than the requested two-or-more-frame gap. Added OD4164, limited to multi-packet high-speed ISO requests with interval >8; the API-field mutation remains the separate OD4163. No controller operation was run, and Deneb `uhwcmd.c` remains partial with no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Deneb ISO frame-zero caller comparison follow-up (OD3890 retained, no new finding, 2026-10-20): re-read `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()` through PTD activation and its `uhwSoftInt()` caller, then compared selected PCIUSB ISO-frame initialization (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4532-4780,4780-4842`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ehci/ehci_isoch.c:390-439`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_isoch.c:250-310`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ohci/ohci_isoch.c:240-290`). Deneb copies `iouh_Frame & 0x1f` directly into the PTD frame-number bits and does not use its current FRINDEX when initially scheduling ordinary ISO; Poseidon’s selected `psdDoPipe()` leaves the persistent frame field at zero. The selected EHCI/UHCI/OHCI paths instead interpret zero as unspecified and choose a future frame with lead time. This reinforces OD3890’s trigger but does not settle whether the ISP1760 waits for modulo-32 recurrence or retires a missed frame: the checked-in PTD comments identify frame-number bits but not missed-frame behavior. Keep the manifestation conditional; no hardware operation or transfer was run and no whole-file line credit is claimed. Source-only.

Generic PCI delayed-claim contract evidence (OD3885 retained/strengthened, 2026-10-20): checked the public `HIDD_PCI_EnumDevices()` method text and `HIDD_PCIDevice_Obtain()` contract against the removal implementation. Enumeration promises a callback for each device but gives no callback-only ownership requirement; `Obtain` is documented as the exclusive-use lock. More directly, `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver()` itself says drivers may defer ownership until after enumeration and calls removal in that state dangerous (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:473-478`). The implementation nevertheless scans Owner under `dev_lock` and disposes after the scan, while Obtain only serializes with `ownerLock` (`:489-512`; `pcideviceclass.c:488-510`). This supports OD3885's delayed-claim/removal overlap as a source-confirmed contract gap; selected in-tree callers claim in the enumeration callback, so impact remains external/public-client conditional. No enumeration or removal was run; no new ID or line credit. Source-only.

AHI CalcSamples low-rate count-bound and caller pass (OD4165 added, 2026-10-20): rechecked `CalcSamples()` against `_AHI_SetFreq()`, `_AHI_SetSound()`, and the selected `Mix()` loop. At 48 kHz mix rate, 1 Hz is quantized to `Add == 0x10000`; a valid 40,000-frame sample produces quotient 2,621,439,999, which narrows to a negative 32-bit `LONG`. `Mix()` then skips the add routine, cannot decrement the count, and never enters its zero-count end-of-sound branch. The public AHI documentation permits 1 Hz playback and describes signed 32-bit sample arrays with ULONG lengths; the example M32S buffer requires 160,000 bytes. Added OD4165 to the detailed report and index. Reconciled eight stale AHI coverage references that named OD2801 (the unrelated Rhine tracker finding) as the sample-count issue; the Rhine report and request-dispatch history retain the genuine OD2801 attribution. No audio or arithmetic execution was performed; source-only.

Envy24HT capture callback cadence and ping-pong phase pass (OD4166 added, 2026-10-20): reconciled the full `interrupt.c` RDMA handler and callback against `_AHIsub_Start()`'s `INTLEN` setup, the 1,764-frame per-half allocation and the advertised recording rates. At the advertised 192 kHz rate the configured half interval is approximately 9.2 ms. Added OD4166, distinct from OD2490's callback/Stop buffer lifetime. AHI Preferences-to-EMU10kx input-index caller pass (OD4167 added, 2026-10-20): traced the installed MUI preferences path from mode selection through retained `ahiup_Input`, the inclusive count clamp, MUI numeric setter/notification ordering, label/slider refresh, Save/Use persistence, `ahi.device` preference loading and `AHIC_Input` dispatch into EMU10kx. `AHIDB_Inputs` is a count with valid indices ending at count-1; the MUI numeric maximum first clamps its displayed value, then the unchanged numeric-value set is ignored before the notification hook can repair `state.InputSelected`, so `FillUnit()` persists the count-valued state. EMU10kx and VIA-AC97 report eight inputs and index eight-element `InputBits` arrays; SB128 reports six inputs and indexes a six-element table. None validates the selector before the lookup. Added OD4167 for a mode switch that carries an index >= the new mode's count, saves it as the count, and later applies it to one of these selected drivers. A concrete path switches the same unit from EMU10kx input index 7 to an available six-input SB128 mode, persisting 6 for the later SB128 open. This is distinct from OD3238's USB Audio topology replacement and OD314's Envy24HT frequency-count mismatch. Updated the AHI Preferences, EMU10kx, VIA-AC97 and SB128 ledger rows. Existing GetAttr array-index candidates remain unpromoted because the public range contract and selected name enumerators cover indices below count; this pass concerns a saved setter index produced by the preferences UI. No GUI, preference file, audio control or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio global configuration load pass (2026-10-20; no new finding): read the full `nLoadClassConfig()` body and its `libOpen`, interface-binding, and `UCM_ConfigChangedEvent` callers (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:60-110,308-326,484-501,2129-2154`). Traced the `UAUD` chunk initialization and `ClsGlobalCfg` layout (`:70-75`; `usbaudio.h:24-28`): this configuration struct currently contains only the 8-byte IFF chunk header, so the `CopyMem` payload length is clamped to zero. `psdGetCfgChunk()` returns a separately allocated, full-length copy and the loader frees it (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:7121-7148`); `psdGetClsCfg()` returns the Poseidon-owned form (`:7421-7438`), which is not freed by this caller. Eaudio audio.device nested Open-error cleanup/semaphore recheck (OD4068 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): re-read the complete library-vector source (`workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:26-282`) and the `Init()` setup, then checked Exec `InternalObtainSemaphore()` semantics (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:50-119`). `Open()` holds `emasys0.es_devsem` when an error path calls `DevClose()`, which obtains the same semaphore; Exec explicitly increments `ss_NestCount` when `ss_Owner == ThisTask`, and the nested close releases only its nesting level. Thus the nested call does not deadlock and does reach the `ADCMD_FREE` cleanup described in OD4068. The code-line count is 195 (`cloc 2.06`), versus 298 physical lines. This confirms that the nested lock does not invalidate OD4068; full external-client and cross-command lifecycle coverage remains open. No open, semaphore contention or failure was induced. Source-only.

USB Audio configuration GUI worker pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): re-read `nOpenCfgWindow`, `nGUITask`, and `nGUITaskCleanup` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2159-2401`) against `usbDoMethodA`'s `UCM_OpenCfgWindow` caller and Poseidon's `psdSpawnSubTask` task/process creation (`usbaudio.class.c:470-500; rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1434-1490`). GUI task creation is serialized by the local `Forbid`, its returned task is stored before `Permit`, and the worker increments the class library's open count before opening MUI, Intuition, and Poseidon. Each dependency/object/window-open failure reaches the shared cleanup; the normal Save/Use path exits through `nGUITaskCleanup`, which disposes the application, closes the opened bases, clears `nh_GUITask`, and drops the open count. Save failure remains unreported to the user, but this class currently serializes only the empty eight-byte config header as already noted in the global-config pass. No independent GUI lifecycle defect established. Cross-CPU module unload synchronization around the `psdSpawnSubTask` handoff was not established; this remains a partial class review, with no GUI or task run. Source-only.

USB Audio GUI/class-expunge handoff recheck (OD4170 added, 2026-10-20): revisited the cross-CPU synchronization gap left open by the GUI worker pass. If class removal wins the scheduling race before the new worker increments the count, generated expunge can free the parent base while it remains in the worker's `tc_UserData`; the hook's sublibrary reference check and generated teardown were traced (`usbaudio.class.c:110-141`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:58-69`; `rom/exec/makelibrary.c:97-108`). VMware SVGA command-buffer manager full-body pass (OD4183 added, 2026-10-20): read all 1,406 physical lines of `vmwgfx_cmdbuf.c` (776 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`), including queue processing, command-buffer allocation and commit, DMA/MOB pool setup, preemption/error recovery, idle waits and teardown. Traced selected `vmw_fallback_wait()` and overlay stop ioctl callers. Added OD4183: `vmw_cmdbuf_idle()` discards an error from its interruptible `vmw_cmdbuf_cur_flush()` and proceeds to an idle predicate that checks queued/in-flight/error lists but not the still-current command buffer (`:627-648,693-749`). In the selected overlay stop ioctl, a command-reserve failure reaches this wait with `interruptible=true` (`vmwgfx_overlay.c:177-199,422-445`; `vmwgfx_irq.c:153-180`). If a signal interrupts acquisition of `cur_mutex` while another submitter still has committed commands buffered in `man->cur`, the manager can report idle while those commands were never flushed; `vmw_fallback_wait()` may then also observe an idle device and let the overlay retry proceed without the intended ordering barrier. The trigger requires that narrow concurrent-buffered-command and signal-interruption state; no signal, command, or device was exercised. Crediting 776 lines and one full-body path moves the represented checkpoint from 153,513/270,754 to 154,289/270,754 (56.98%) and 545/598 to 546/598 paths (91.30%). Deneb interrupt OUT buffer-tail bounds pass (OD4231 added, 2026-10-20): traced `cmdIntXFer()` admission through the soft-interrupt scheduler and `uhwScheduleIntPTDs()`'s OUT staging copy, then compared the transfer length with the USBHardware contract (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:936-970,3958-4138`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:408-414`). USB Audio format-width finding consolidation (OD4228 withdrawn into OD3947, 2026-10-20): rechecked the Type I parser, mode-frame sizing, sample-converter selection and playback/record conversion bodies (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1139-1217,1943-1953,2557-2584,2739,2858-3010,3134-3166,3448-3482,3506-3528`). Both the former OD3947 cases (zero or too-small subframe) and OD4228's wider-than-AHI-frame read arise because the parser stores `bSubframeSize` independently of `bBitResolution`, while mode construction sizes AHI frames from resolution and converter dispatch uses subframe size. BTCore L2CAP Configure Request continuation/caller pass (OD4232 added, 2026-10-20): traced the parser's retained `flags` field into `handle_configure_request()`, its fixed-zero Configure Response, inbound-complete transition, subsequent CONFIG-state gate, and selected `bluetooth.device` channel-manager use (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/l2cap/signaling.c:184-201`; `channel_manager.c:283-320,493-517`; production path previously traced at `hwconn.c:701-719,736-753`). Compared with Bluetooth Core 6.2 L2CAP §4.4: a continued request is a valid multi-packet configuration; each request fragment requires a response whose continuation state reflects the request, and only the final request completes the configuration event. Added OD4232: if outbound configuration has already completed, this implementation can mark inbound configuration complete and open on the first fragment; it then silently drops later fragments after the state becomes OPEN. This is separate from OD3962's unsupported mandatory option handling and OD3963's outbound MTU enforcement. No line credit (the signaling and manager bodies were already credited); no peer or packet was used. Source-only.

BTCore L2CAP Configure Response continuation follow-up (OD4232 expanded, 2026-10-20): reread `bt_l2cap_sig_parse_configure_response()` and `handle_configure_response()` against the response continuation rules in Core 6.2 L2CAP §§4.4-4.5 (`signaling.c:237-257`; `channel_manager.c:323-352`). A continued response requires the requester to issue null-option Configure Requests until the peer sends a response with continuation cleared. This manager instead clears the pending identifier, sets `outbound_config_done`, and may open the channel; it sends no follow-up request, so later responses cannot match the cleared identifier. Folded this into OD4232's same unsupported continuation-state handling, alongside the already traced inbound request-fragment case; no duplicate finding added. The documented single-round-trip limitation explains absent negotiation loops but does not make the current success/open transition accurately handle the peer's valid continuation. No line credit; no peer or packet was used. Source-only.

BTCore L2CAP response CID correlation pass (OD4233 added, 2026-10-20): traced successful Connection Response, Configure Response, and Disconnection Response handling from their parsers through channel lookup/state mutation (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/l2cap/signaling.c:87-108,237-258,292-307`; `channel_manager.c:198-225,323-352,383-397`). The manager correlates on identifier/state but does not compare Connection/Configure response SCID with the local CID or Disconnection response CIDs with the stored local/remote endpoints. Checked the Bluetooth Core 6.2 requirements (§§4.3, 4.5, 4.7): those response fields identify/correlate the endpoints, and mismatched disconnection CIDs should be discarded. Added OD4233, including the stale-response-after-identifier-wrap condition; connection pending/failure response CIDs remain exempt because the spec permits them to be invalid. Rechecked selected production caller path via OD3963's Bluetooth device integration trace. No line credit; no peer, device or packet was used. Source-only.

USB MIDI shared output-buffer capacity pass (OD4234 added, 2026-10-20): traced `nParseMidiOut()` across its 16-adapter loop, the 8,192-byte buffer allocation, and the selected embedded CAMD OpenPort/Transmit hooks (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:518-535,724-731,854-859`; `camd/poseidonusb.c:108-132,140-158`). The 2,040-packet condition bounds each adapter's inner `do` loop only; a later nonempty adapter still processes one event even if the shared count is already at the limit. One port carrying 2,040 one-byte realtime messages plus one pending event on each of nine later ports produces 2,049 packets (8,196 bytes) into the 8,192-byte allocation; 16 ports can reach 2,055 packets (8,220 bytes). Added OD4234 to the detailed report and index. The class is selected through `kernel-usb-classes-common` when the parent USB graph builds `kernel-usb-classes` (`rom/usb/mmakefile.src:4-13`; `rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:10-19`); its CPU aliases are listed in the local manifest. CAMD USB-MIDI OpenPort failure-contract recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced the embedded driver's `OpenPort` callback through `usbCAMDOpenPort()` and CAMD's `OpenDriver()` result handling (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c:139-159`; `camdusbmidi.class.c:387-431`; `workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:24-58`). A no-device or adapter-buffer allocation failure returns NULL from `usbCAMDOpenPort`; the embedded wrapper then forms `&CAMDPortBases[portnum]->ca_ActivateFunc`. `ca_ActivateFunc` is the first `CAMDAdapter` field (`camdusbmidi.h:18-21`), so the source does not establish a distinct non-NULL invalid `MidiPortData` value on the selected targets; CAMD's caller explicitly treats NULL as an OpenPort failure and unwinds its receiver process. No separate finding promoted. The broader multi-port output-buffer bound in OD4234 was rechecked against all event-emission cases in `nParseMidiOut()` (`camdusbmidi.class.c:518-733`): each successful event increments shared `goodpkt` once and emits one four-byte packet; after one port reaches 2,040, each later nonempty port can emit once before its loop condition is tested. This supports the existing 2,055-packet upper bound across 16 ports. No build, MIDI stream, device or allocation failure was exercised; source-only.

Deneb timer and hardware initialization full-function pass (OD3653/OD4158 rechecked; no new OD, 2026-10-20): read complete `uhwOpenTimer()`, `uhwDelayMS()`, `uhwCloseTimer()`, and `uhwHWInit()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:65-267`), then traced every `uhwHWInit()` call into `Open_Unit()` and `cmdReset()` (`:453-484,560-585`) plus `devOpen()` success propagation (`dev.c:310-326`). Timer message-port/request/device cleanup is paired across the checked success and failure paths; `uhwDelayMS()` is only called after successful timer setup in these two paths. `uhwHWInit()` returns host error for either root-port polling timeout, but `Open_Unit()` ignores the result and continues task startup, while `cmdReset()` ignores it and reports from current port state; these are already the OD3653 initialization-error behavior. `cmdUsbReset()` remains the separately documented state-only reset defect OD4158. Deneb `Open_Unit()`/`Close_Unit()` full-function and `devOpen()`/`devClose()` caller pass (OD3581/OD3582/OD3653/OD4161/OD4229 rechecked; no new OD, 2026-10-20): read both complete unit lifecycle functions (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:281-525`) and traced the driver entry/close callers (`dev.c:281-326,351-383`). Confirmed the range check permits index `MAXUNITS` before accessing the `hd_Units[MAXUNITS]` array (OD4161); `Open_Unit()` calls the embedded worker `AddTask()` without checking its nullable result before publishing the unit (OD3581); the board/slot and timer failure cleanup is otherwise paired through the examined failure labels; CPU detection retains the precedence defect limited to the returned description flag (OD4229); and the `uhwHWInit()` return is ignored before open succeeds (OD3653). `Close_Unit()` disables hardware and timer activity, signals the worker, waits a fixed delay, then frees the unit without a termination handshake (OD3582). `cmdUsbReset()` is separately OD4158; it does not share the startup initialization issue. These existing findings cover the distinct supported paths found here; no additional independent failure was established. ATA timer helper manifest and caller reconciliation (OD3681/EK8800 rechecked, 2026-10-20): checked `ATA_DEVICEFILES` against the coverage rows and found that `timer.c` and `waitto.c` had been discussed in the OD3681 ledger text but lacked individual file rows. Read both complete bodies (49 and 38 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) and traced `ata_OpenTimer()` callers in the controller daemon, `BusTaskCode()`, and `ata_InitBus()`. The daemon signals startup failure on NULL; `ata_InitBus()` guards the timer and skips scan; `BusTaskCode()` stores NULL without checking it, then the selected `ata_setup_unit()`/`ata_WaitBusyTO()` route calls `ata_WaitTO()` before releasing `DetectionSem`, confirming existing OD3681. `ata_WaitTO()` always waits for any submitted timer I/O to complete before return, but its signed `1 << mp_SigBit` expression can reach bit 31 from `CreateMsgPort()` automatic allocation; this is the same source-language condition tracked under EK8800, not a separate finding. SCSI's similarly named helper files are defined by `kernel-scsi` but no reviewed platform parent selects that module; the Exec ledger already excludes this unselected target. The SD-card timer row already exists at `:5137`; `sdcard_WaitTO()` has no maintained caller, while the bus task retains its opened timer for its worker lifetime. No new issue established beyond OD3681/EK8800, and no signal exhaustion, allocation failure, timer operation, or device scan was run. Source-only.


ATA manifest helper and controller-startup recheck (OD2573/OD2574 restored; OD2995/OD3681 cross-checked, 2026-10-20): compared all ten `ATA_DEVICEFILES` entries with the coverage table. `waitnano.c` and `bootwait.c` were selected but lacked individual Other Drivers file rows; full bodies and relevant callers were read and rows added. USB2OTG periodic-promotion ring ownership check (OD4130 follow-up, 2026-10-20; no new finding): searched every hu_PromRingF/D/Dev/Pos reference. SOF and watchdog paths write the eight-slot ring, while the only reader formats recent entries in watchdog diagnostics (`usb2otg_intr.c:967-970,3571-3574,3757-3764`). `usb2otg_process_pending()` schedules from `hu_IntXFerScheduled` and never consumes ring entries (`:2706-2790`), so wraparound in the diagnostic ring cannot discard scheduled requests. The distinct 128-node list-walk cutoff remains OD4130. No IRQ or scheduler was run; source-only.

USB2OTG FinishedXfers drain-bound reachability recheck (2026-10-20; no new finding): enumerated every producer of hu_FinishedXfers in usb2otg_intr.c, usb2otg_schedule.c and usb2otg_intern.h. IRQ and watchdog completions claim/clear a specific hu_Channel entry; SetupChannel setup failures are reached only from ScheduleCtrlTDs (one channel), ScheduleBulkTDs (two iterations), and ScheduleIntTDs (the finite periodic channel range). The unit exposes exactly eight hu_Channel entries (usb2otg_intern.h:277,541-549); each claimed channel has at most one hc_Request, and each normal completion path transfers that request to FinishedXfers once. Thus a valid non-corrupt queue is bounded by the eight hardware channels per dispatch phase, far below the 2048 drain guard in usb2otg_process_pending() (`usb2otg_intr.c:2725-2760`). The guard's remaining purpose is protection from corrupted/multi-node cyclic list state; leaving more than 2048 entries after its break is not a normal supported workload. Withdraw the earlier tentative backlog concern: no separate defect or candidate is retained. No queue corruption or completion was induced; source-only.

USB Audio Type I mode descriptor parser and endpoint-input recheck (OD3168-OD3173 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): reread all of nExamineAudioDescriptors() (rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1038-1311) and traced its psdFindDescriptor results and endpoint attributes into mode publication and nSelectAudioMode (:1190-1290,1929-1987,3134-3168; Poseidon endpoint construction rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8467-8561). In particular, Poseidon normalizes a zero SuperSpeed isochronous interval to one before converting it to service intervals, so the USB Audio bandwidth divisor is not zero from that endpoint field on the selected parser path. USB mass-storage CopyMemQuick per-chunk length-contract recheck (OD3787 expanded; OD3798 retained separately, 2026-10-20): reread nRead64Emul/nWrite64Emul and trace the block-size source through READ CAPACITY and the request fallback (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:2061-2071,2646-2880,2900-2915,3058-3087`). The top-level length/offset checks require 512-byte alignment, but each emulation copy clamps datalen by ncm_BlockSize - insideblockoffset and performs no four-byte tail copy. With an accepted 513-byte block size, a 512-byte request at offset 512 reaches 1-byte and 511-byte CopyMemQuick calls; generic and selected m68k implementations copy only full ULONGs, so those chunks lose bytes even with aligned pointers. This is the length-contract branch of OD3787, distinct from its unchecked io_Data alignment branch and OD3798’s separate non-power-of-two LBA/offset conversion. No SCSI device, request or copy was run; source-only.

OD3787 caller-alignment evidence qualification (2026-10-20): checked the pointer type used by the affected ordinary read/write path. The destination/source is IOStdReq.io_Data (APTR, compiler/include/exec/io.h:29-42); the earlier citation to SCSICmd.scsi_Data (UWORD *) describes HD_SCSICMD and does not prove the CMD_READ/CMD_WRITE buffer contract. The independent non-multiple-of-four internal datalen case remains the concrete lost-byte path. Source-only.

USB mass-storage Bulk-Only CopyMemQuick alignment-contract follow-up (2026-10-20; not promoted): checked the other `CopyMemQuick` caller in `nScsiDirectBulk()` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_bulk.c:296-302`). Its destination `umscbw.CBWCB` is byte offset 15 in `UsbMSCmdBlkWrapper`, declared under `#pragma pack(1)` (`compiler/include/devices/usb_massstorage.h:31-51`); the source `scsicmd->scsi_Command` is also a byte-command buffer. Both pointers therefore lack a source-level ULONG-alignment guarantee, while the API requires both aligned and a multiple-of-ULONG length (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:30-45`). The call is gated on CDB length >=16 and copies exactly 16 bytes, so its length requirement is satisfied. Did not add a separate finding: no selected-target compiler output or ABI evidence was established for the actual stack placement of `umscbw`, and no concrete supported caller buffer misalignment was traced. Keep as an explicit target-layout/caller follow-up. No build, device, or command was run; source-only.

USB mass-storage short-autosense public-entry reconciliation (OD3795 confirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced the selected `usbscsi.device` worker's `HD_SCSICMD` dispatch (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:1378-1385`) to `nScsiDirect()`, which clears only `scsi_SenseActual`, caps `scsi_SenseLength` only when it exceeds 18 under `PFF_SIMPLE_SCSI`, and dispatches to the configured Bulk/CBI/CB/UAS transport (`:3173-3210,3590-3610`). For a short non-NULL sense buffer, the simple-SCSI filter does not reject undersized lengths, and its allowed-command cases reach the same transport dispatch. The Bulk parser still reads sense offsets 2, 12 and 13 without checking `scsi_SenseActual` or declared length (`massstorage_bulk.c:555-600`); CBI copies only the declared length then reads offsets 2 and 12 (`massstorage_cbi.c:301-318`). Confirmed this is the Poseidon `usbscsi.device` path, separate from the `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage` HIDD-backed device implementation. Existing OD3795 trigger/consequence remain accurate. No command, device or short buffer was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage UAS autosense boundary comparison (OD3795 scope narrowed to CB/CBI/Bulk; no new UAS finding, 2026-10-20): checked `nUasDoCommand()`'s direct Sense IU path and REQUEST SENSE fallback (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_uas.c:64-170,219-239`). Sense IU copying clamps to the received payload extent, the IU-reported sense length and caller `sense_len`; this backend does not parse sense-key/ASC bytes afterward. A short caller buffer therefore does not reach the same unchecked offsets identified for Bulk/CBI, and is left as a short `SenseActual`. This confirms OD3795 must remain limited to CB/CBI/Bulk behavior; no UAS defect promoted. No UAS IU or command was used; source-only.

OD3793 UAS status-IU minimum-length/tag boundary recheck (2026-10-20): re-read the status parser and packed IU definitions (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_uas.c:126-170`; `compiler/include/devices/usb_massstorage.h:110-130`). The fixed `UasStatusIU` is 16 bytes, but the parser accepts `actual_len >= 3` as sufficient to take byte 2 as the status; it does not require a complete status IU or check the status IU's tag against the submitted command. It also does not validate the IU identifier before deciding the returned status. For fewer than three bytes the initialized GOOD value remains unchanged; the selected status pipe accepts runt packets. This confirms and sharpens OD3793's false-success/misattributed-completion branches; no separate finding. A complete Sense IU has a different variable length and is separately bounded for copying, so this note does not treat every non-16-byte response as invalid. No status IU or command was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage overlength CDB transport audit (OD4236 added, 2026-10-20): traced public `HD_SCSICMD` queuing to `nScsiDirect()` and the class configuration path that can disable default Simple SCSI filtering (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/dev.c:249-266`; `massstorage.class.c:912,1382-1385,5558-5560,6013-6022`). No SCSI command/device was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage Bulk autosense pointer-alignment pass (OD4237 added, 2026-10-20): traced `HD_SCSICMD` sense-buffer ownership to the Bulk REQUEST SENSE transfer and the subsequent signature check (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_bulk.c:430-469,538`; public field `compiler/include/devices/scsidisk.h:21-33`). `scsi_SenseData` is a byte pointer with no alignment promise; after at least eight received bytes the code dereferences it as `ULONG *`. USB mass-storage CBI/Bulk retry autosense-state pass (OD4238 added, 2026-10-20): traced the `0x80` autoretry flag through both transport loops and the SCSICmd outputs (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_cbi.c:155-162,287-318,399-404`; `massstorage_bulk.c:266-275,428-469,546-628,698-704`; `massstorage.class.c:3186-3188`). OD4239 translation-path extension (2026-10-20): extended the existing short-CDB finding after tracing `xlate` selection and each translation branch. ATAPI, floppy-ATAPI and UFI subclasses enable `xlate` regardless of `scsi_CmdLength` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:3190-3195`); the READ/WRITE/SEEK(6), MODE SELECT(6), and MODE SENSE(6) cases then read command bytes 1-5 (`:3459-3523`) with no minimum-length validation. A one-byte READ(6) on a packet subclass can feed adjacent bytes into the translated READ(10) LBA/count. No command or device was used; source-only.

Poseidon ATAPI/UFI MODE SENSE/SELECT translation allocation-failure pass (OD4240 added, 2026-10-20): traced both staging allocations through translated-command dispatch and completion (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:3460-3465,3480-3531,3596-3612,3615-3651`). If `psdAllocVec(scsi_Length+4)` fails, MODE SENSE/SELECT translation still sets `usecmd10`, leaving the command data pointer/length at caller values and sending the MODE SENSE(10)/MODE SELECT(10) CDB. The no-staging epilogue reports transport status/actual without converting MODE SENSE(10) data back to the six-byte layout. Added OD4240; trigger requires the packet subclass translation and staging allocation failure, and MODE SELECT/unsupported MODE SENSE cases generally require Simple SCSI filtering disabled. No allocation failure, command or device was used; source-only.
OD4240 transport-boundary recheck (2026-10-20): followed the MODE SENSE/SELECT translation fallback into each selected transport. CBI, Bulk and UAS derive their data-phase extent from `scsi_Length` (`massstorage_cbi.c:169,217,245`; `massstorage_bulk.c:294,335`; `massstorage_uas.c:184-200`). On staging allocation failure, `scsicmd10` retains the caller pointer and original length; transport therefore honors that length while sending/receiving the mismatched MODE SENSE/SELECT(10) payload. Tightened OD4240 to a data-format/device-command mismatch and removed any implication of an established buffer overrun. No command or device was used; source-only.
PC serial shared-IRQ removal primitive recheck (OD2779, 2026-10-20): checked the exact Exec/kernel operation beneath unit disposal. `RemIntServer(INTB_KERNEL + n, irq)` passes `irq->is_Node.ln_Succ` to `KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/exec/remintserver.c:51-55`); the PC kernel implementation unlinks and frees the opaque `IntrNode` (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-75`) without changing the caller-owned `Interrupt` node's `ln_Name`. Each stores the `OOP_NewObject` result and sets `usedunits` unconditionally, while disposal requires a non-NULL pointer match before clearing the bit. `OOP_NewObject` returns NULL when `root_new` cannot allocate the instance (`rom/oop/newobject.c:75-83,104-113`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-131`). Deneb USB `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` input/output and completion pass (2026-10-20; no new OD, partial-file credit only): reread `cmdNSDeviceQuery()` and its `devBeginIO()` dispatch/RC_DONTREPLY handling (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1540-1600`; `dev.c:545-623,630-639`), checked the local AROS result layout against `NSDeviceQueryResult`, and traced the query caller in `PartitionNsdCheck()` (`compiler/include/devices/newstyle.h:12-28`; `partition_support.c:45-85`). On invalid input the helper sets IOERR_NOCMD and completes the request itself, while the dispatcher honors RC_DONTREPLY; quick requests are not replied by `TermIO()`. Deneb bulk public-caller endpoint contract and zero-length reachability recheck (OD3585/OD3889/OD4160 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced Poseidon `psdAllocPipe()` endpoint setup through `psdDoPipe()` into Deneb `cmdBulkXFer()` and `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4478-4634,4705-4739`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:850-875,4212-4375`). Deneb DEBUG ATL dump branch pass (no new OD, 2026-10-20): read `uhwDebugATLs()` and all selected call sites (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1878-1965,4864-4919`). The helper is compiled only with `DEBUG`; its repeated volatile reads use the ISP1760 PIO data window after programming the `ISP_MEMORY` start address, consistent with the selected read-window pointer and other word-stream copies in the driver (`uhwcmd.c:371-380,2433-2447,2621-2634`; `isp1760.h:61`). DEBUG-only diagnostics and the controller's PIO read behavior remain untested; no whole-file credit. Source-only.

CAMD cluster relocation failure and report/index reconciliation (OD1497 restored, 2026-10-20): re-traced the public `SetMidiLinkAttrsA()` caller into `SetClusterForLink()`, `UnlinkMidiLink()`, `NewCluster()`, and both direction-specific `AddCluster*()` paths. CAMD cluster-iterator synchronization recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD): searched all local `NextCluster()` calls and found only the function's documented example. It holds `LockCAMD(CD_Linkages)` across traversal; `LockCAMD` obtains the global semaphore shared, while cluster list publication/removal requires the exclusive semaphore. This protects `last` and its successor for callers following the documented contract; external misuse remains outside checked-in call paths. No line credit. Source-only.

Nouveau/VMware DRM workqueue ownership recheck (OD4037 retained, 2026-10-20): reread the full `linux_workqueue.c` body and traced every direct private queue allocation/destruction found in the selected target trees. Successful `alloc_workqueue()` returns the same independently `kzalloc()`ed descriptor; only process-creation and signal-allocation failures call `kfree(wq)`. `destroy_workqueue()` flushes, sets `stopping`, signals the worker and returns without joining or freeing it; there is no later descriptor-free API. Confirmed normal per-device/per-manager pairs in TTM init/fini, Nouveau DRM init/fini including `fail_wq`, NVKM display constructor/destructor, DP MST topology init/destroy, VMware VKMS init/cleanup, and VMware/Nouveau `kthread_destroy_worker()` (which frees only its wrapper). The two system queue instances are global and not destroyed through normal use. Therefore the report's per-successful-private-queue leak is supported; the selected normal teardown paths do not reclaim the allocation, and repeated device/manager lifecycle accumulates descriptors. Worker-exit synchronization also means any eventual descriptor release must wait until the signaled worker has finished reading it. No queue, driver teardown, or worker timing was run. Source-only.

Deneb `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` contract and local-caller recheck (no new OD, 2026-10-20): reread `cmdNSDeviceQuery()` and its dispatch/`RC_DONTREPLY` path, compared the structure with `compiler/include/devices/newstyle.h`, and searched in-tree query initializers/callers. The header defines `DevQueryFormat` and `SizeAvailable` as fields reset for each query; local filesystem callers initialize both to zero, while device implementations populate them as output. Deneb's zero-only input check is consistent with that contract. `developer/debug/devtest/devtest.c:test_nsd_devicequery()` leaves the prefilled `SizeAvailable` poison value intact, but it is a trackdisk probe and does not establish a Deneb caller path. No new driver defect established; external callers and any alternate NSD specification remain outside this source-only check. No query was issued. Source-only.

Deneb active DMA AbortIO caller recheck (OD3584 confirmed, no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced `devAbortIO()` through `cmdAbortIO()` for queued requests and active ATL/INT/ISO PTDs, then followed the active ATL cleanup into `FreeATL()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:650-690`; `uhwcmd.c:1602-1684,1778-1868`). The active ATL branch clears `ptd_IOReq` before `FreeATL()`; when that PTD is `hu_DMAPTD`, the cleanup snapshots NULL and dereferences it for `CachePostDMA()`. This confirms detailed finding OD3584. Poseidon's abort helper submits a companion abort message and waits, so its pipe teardown reaches the same selected device AbortIO vector (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4778-4801,9080-9086`). The direct Deneb DMA target is selected by the m68k USB aggregate (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/mmakefile.src:25-30`); the request must be active, ATL-backed and DMA-eligible. Non-DMA and queued/INT/ISO abort paths do not enter this exact NULL `FreeATL()` branch. No transfer, abort or hardware was run. Source-only.

NVHDMI DriverInit discovery-capacity and failure-unwind pass (2026-10-20; OD3746 retained, no new finding): traced `DriverInit()` through the common AHI `_LibInit`/`_LibExpunge` path, `ahi_hda_init`/`ahi_hda_exit`, bounded PCI discovery and all local card-array/card-data outcomes (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/NVHDMI/driver-init.c:35-136`; `Common/library.c:378-468,483-514`; `NVHDMI/hda_hidd.c:253-320,323-374,390-454`; `hdmi.c:110-160`). HDA partial-init cleanup checks each resource before releasing it; no independent cleanup defect established. No allocation failure, PCI device, controller or audio operation was exercised. RPiHDMI SoC register-table and selected-consumer pass (OD2839 retained; 2026-10-20): read both SoC table bodies and their shared type/access declarations (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/RPiHDMI/rpihdmi-bcm2712.c`, `rpihdmi-bcm283x.c`, `rpihdmi-soc.h`, `rpihdmi-hwaccess.h`), then traced all table selection and field consumption through `rpihdmi-init.c`, `rpihdmi-main.c`, DMA setup and `hdmi_mai_init/stop`. The BCM2712/2711 mutable tables are admitted only after DT node, register-block and nonzero DREQ checks; the BCM283x const table is selected only for its supported peripheral-base values. `IPTR` is used for mapped register bases/offsets, while `mai_data_bus` carries the DT bus address into the DMA control block. Credited 90 C code lines across the two SoC table bodies; struct/accessor body review was already recorded. RPiHDMI DT `reg-names` candidate recheck (2026-10-20; no finding promoted): traced `find_element_index()` against the selected Raspberry Pi OpenFirmware provider (`rpihdmi-init.c:48-75`; `arch/{arm-raspi,aarch64-raspi}/boot/devicetree.c:36-50`; `rom/openfirmware/of_init.c:132-156,174-215`). The helper calls `strcmp()` before checking whether the string terminator lies within `OF_GetPropLen()`. The Pi boot parser stores `op_value` as a pointer into the full FDT structure rather than allocating an exact-size per-property string, so the available source does not establish that the read leaves the containing blob or that a valid `reg-names` stringlist produces a wrong index. A truncated/malformed firmware property remains a conditional robustness concern. Corrected stale coverage references that called this OD2839; OD2839 is the unrelated NVMe hardware-name allocation finding. No firmware blob or device was inspected or run. Source-only.
