VMware MST fallback GUID generator concurrency pass (OD4242; 2026-10-20): traced the VMware copy of `get_random_u32()` through the byte-wise `guid_gen()` and topology validator, and checked the selected probe-worker and resume callers. The seed is a file-static value with non-atomic read/modify/write updates; probing takes `mgr->probe_lock`, while resume takes `mgr->lock`, so the reviewed code does not serialize both GUID-generation routes. A same-manager collision could misroute a later GUID-addressed broadcast notification; no interleaving or hardware behavior was tested. This mirrors GD5640 for Nouveau's copy. No whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Nouveau/VMware compatibility clock conversion and timeout-caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): checked the shared `jiffies.h` conversions against selected callers of `dma_fence_wait_timeout()`, `dma_resv_wait_timeout()`, timer arming, DisplayPort sideband waits, and scheduler sleeps. The selected finite reservation/fence waits are 2, 15 or 30 seconds; the delayed-delete path uses `MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT`, which `dma_fence_wait_timeout()` special-cases as an infinite wait before converting to microseconds. The selected I2C bit-bus timeout is 2,200 microseconds. Thus the 32-bit `jiffies_to_usecs()` product does not wrap for the reviewed in-tree call values. `drm_gem_dma_resv_wait()` has no in-tree caller, and the selected `EXPORT_SYMBOL` compatibility macro is empty (`include/linux/export.h:8-11`), so no external module entry path is selected here; arbitrary values remain outside the reviewed call graph. Re-read the exact-deadline loop in `timer_do_arm()` and the short-period `drm_dp_mst_wait_tx_reply()` caller; no additional wrap defect was established beyond OD4178's wall-clock basis. No timer, fence, or device operation was run; no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Nouveau delayed-work cancellation race follow-up to OD4177 (2026-10-20): traced `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` through its `del_timer()` pending-bit fast return, queued-work cancellation and `flush_work()`. Timer expiry clears pending before the delayed-work callback calls `queue_work()`, leaving a window where cancellation sees neither pending timer nor queued work and returns before the callback queues. The selected `drm_kms_helper_poll_disable()` uses this API; during suspend it sets `poll_running` false but leaves `poll_enabled` true, so late output-poll work may still probe connectors and reschedule. `drm_kms_helper_poll_fini()` also relies on the same cancellation before clearing `poll_enabled`. Expanded OD4177 with these selected delayed-work consequences; no duplicate ID added. Race timing and runtime behavior were not exercised. Source-only.

Nouveau scheduler current-record allocation failure trace (OD4243 added, 2026-10-20): followed the selected HIDD constructor's `drmOpen()` through the AROS `drm_file_alloc()` callback to `nouveau_drm_open()`. On first `current` use in an Exec task, `compat_current()` allocates and may return NULL; `nouveau_drm_open()` immediately reads `current->comm`. Added OD4243 for the conditional null dereference during Nouveau device initialization. VMware's remaining `current` fields are in optional MKS stats code not selected by the checked configuration; its `signal_pending(current)` compatibility stubs ignore their argument and do not establish the same dereference. No task record allocation or HIDD open was induced. This adds caller trace only; scheduler source was already fully credited. Source-only.

Nouveau wait-queue/completion selected-caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced six active wait-event call sites in selected Nouveau DRM users: MST sideband reply, atomic and vblank waits, PMU synchronous reply and clock-state wait (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/display/drm_dp_mst_topology.c:1252-1331`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/drm_atomic_helper.c:1897-1922`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/drm_vblank.c:1300-1323,1848-1870`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/pmu/gt215.c:75-83,115-123`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/clk/base.c:332-342`). Each checks its terminal condition before sleeping and again after wake; the traced producers update the condition before `wake_up()`/`wake_up_all()`, so no lost-wakeup path was established in these callers. Reviewed completion timeout use in atomic flip cleanup; the completion implementation preserves `complete()` tokens and `complete_all()` state as expected by the selected call. The separate `drm_file` event-read wait has no selected AROS reader; the AROS glue says its event queues are unread (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-aros/drm_drv.c:434-435`). `signal_pending()` is a constant-false compatibility stub, but no AROS signal-interruption contract or selected caller requiring `-ERESTARTSYS` was established; do not promote Linux-style interrupted-wait behavior as a standalone AROS bug without that integration contract. These checks do not cover every caller of exported waitqueue/completion helpers or device-specific scheduling. No hardware, wait, or interrupt was run. Source-only.

USB Audio full-translation-unit and finding-ledger reconciliation (2026-10-21): completed the body pass of all 4,163 physical lines of `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c` (3,330 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`), including the earlier partial regions. Rechecked the existing parser, graph, descriptor, AHI negotiation, converter, allocation/cleanup, task and callback candidates against the corresponding method bodies and selected Poseidon/AHI callers. OD3163 is confirmed: a three-byte mono capture frame enters `case 3`, divides by three, then falls through and divides by four again; zero resulting samples reach `nRec24BitMono`'s do-while converter, whose unsigned count underflows and continues beyond the intended buffer. OD3229's unmatched `Permit()` path is confirmed; the separate OD4147 tracking entry duplicated that same branch, so it is now an alias of OD3229 and its ExecSMP PC/ARM/AArch64/RISC-V counter checks have been merged into OD3229. Crediting 3,330 lines and one path to the latest represented checkpoint of 172,836/270,754 lines and 582/598 paths yields 176,166/270,754 = 65.06% and 583/598 = 97.49%; both denominators are carried forward and the VMware source inventory is known to be incomplete, so these remain ledger proxies rather than a fresh Other Drivers census. PC timer VBlank `SendIO` receiver follow-up (2026-10-20; no new finding): traced the selected `arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c` request submission through `common_BeginIO()` and the `TimerProcessMicroHZ()` expiry path (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:77-128,267-321`). `SendIO()` clears `IOF_QUICK` and resets the message node type, but the embedded VBlank request is recognized specially on expiry: it is removed, VBlank processing runs, the next deadline is computed and the same request is reinserted, then processing continues without `ReplyMsg()`. The repeated request therefore is not a generic reply-port completion or stale-node reuse path; it is deliberately retained as the timer's periodic driver request. No request was submitted or timer run. Source-only.

PCIPC MSI vector caller requirement recheck (OD2987/OD2993 retained, 2026-10-21): searched the complete checked-in `HIDD_PCIDevice_ObtainVectors()` call set and read each selected PC-capable caller's request and result path. NVMe requests Min=1/Max=CPU count, obtains the negotiated queue count, but currently creates one I/O queue (`hwqcnt=1`) and queries vector index 0; AHCI, xHCI, Nouveau and VMware request exactly one vector and query only index 0. Thus the PCIPC `vectmin > table_size` behavior and zero-minimum MSI countdown still lack a selected caller trigger. xHCI releases vectors when its native-vector attribute remains invalid; Nouveau/VMware release and report ENODEV when their IRQ attribute is invalid. AHCI does not check the initialized `-1` sentinel after `GetVectorAttribs()`, but the selected PCIPC `ObtainVectors()` success paths program MSI-X table data or MSI config before returning TRUE, and the corresponding index-zero attribute read obtains that programmed value; the generic fallback `ObtainVectors()` returns FALSE, so AHCI takes INTx there. No independent selected AHCI bad-attribute path was established. No additional vector-count contract defect established; PCIPC MSI-X BAR-span/address checks, MSI count rounding/base-index behavior, destination APIC-ID assumption, and non-releasing APIC allocation remain tracked in their existing findings. No vector request or hardware interrupt was run; source-only.

Atheros5000 TKIP MIC caller/extent recheck (OD3297 retained; no new candidate, 2026-10-21): traced RX descriptor length admission and `ieee_length` initialization through the selected TKIP fragment-decrypt function table, successful-fragment accumulation, the final-fragment `UNITF_HARDMIC` gate, `TKIPDecryptFrame`, and the `rx_frames` allocation (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:1545-1561,1603-1641,218-221,659-669`; `device.h:96`; `encryption.c:1080-1103`). Confirmed the complete-frame checker is entered only for a completed fragment whose preceding per-fragment check succeeded, when software MIC checking is selected. For `ieee_length < 8`, subtracting `sizeof(mic)` wraps the UWORD; the helper reads the expected MIC from the wrapped offset, writes the eight-byte padding there, and reads `size/4+2` words from that buffer before returning a MIC mismatch. This refines OD3297’s concrete out-of-range read/write sites; it is not a separate finding. Reachability still depends on a malformed final TKIP fragment passing its per-fragment integrity check. No packet, device, or runtime memory behavior was exercised; source-only.

Atheros5000 RX-fragment slot-pressure reachability check (OD3274 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-21): searched all `rx_fragment_nos` writes and traced slot admission/release through `GetRXBuffer()` and `RXInt()` (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:1572,1621-1625,1669-1671,1737-1776`; allocation and initialization `:218-221`; array declaration `device.h:127`). A first fragment sets a slot's sequence marker; the RX path releases that slot only when a fragment without `WIFI_FRM_CONTROLF_MOREFRAGS` is processed. There is no independent expiry/reaper. Thus ten valid first fragments without their terminal fragment can hold all ten slots, after which an eleventh first fragment forces the retry loop to clear logical slot zero while its pointer has advanced one buffer past the ten-slot allocation; it returns `buffer_no == 10`, which `RXInt` later uses against the ten-entry marker array. This confirms OD3274's in-tree reachability condition and distinguishes it from the separate same-source/different-sequence reassembly issue OD3296. No packet or device was used; source-only.

NetInfo startup/expunge and usergroup caller recheck (OD1894/OD1896/OD1902/OD2344 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-21): re-read the selected first-use path from `usergroup` entry points through `ug_OpenUnit`/`OpenDevice`, `NetInfo__DevOpen`, process creation and the worker startup reply. Rechecked DOS base acquisition before temporary port/request allocation and absent close on those failures/worker exit (OD1896), plus the expunge hook return into generated synchronous base disposal before worker cleanup (OD1902). A suspected open-device retention on `ug_OpenUnit` buffer-allocation failure was not promoted: the device/unit is cached for later retry and `CleanupNIO` closes both units through `endpwent`/`endgrent` before deleting the shared request/port. The normal selected usergroup path uses synchronous `DoIO`; no in-tree `AbortIO` caller was found for netinfo. No allocation failure, device open, expunge or concurrent request was induced; direct external device callers and runtime scheduling remain open. Source-only.

Nouveau current-task compatibility record SMP interleaving pass (OD4244, 2026-10-21): compared the complete `task_records`/`next_pid` creation paths in both Nouveau and VMware `drm-compat/linux_sched.c`, then traced selected `current` macro callers and kthread startup. Realtek8180 FlushUnit/CMDFLUSH queue-ownership recheck (no new OD, 2026-10-21): read the complete `FlushUnit()` and traced both callers: `CMD_FLUSH` drains request ports through `EVENT_QUEUE` and passes `IOERR_ABORTED` (`request.c:480-497`), while `GoOffline()` clears the online flag first, drains through `MGMT_QUEUE`, then reports OFFLINE (`unit.c:956-964`). `FlushUnit()` also drains every opener's read and management-message ports (`unit.c:1365-1408`); selected `GetMsg()` protects each port list with the ExecSMP spinlock (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:56-71`). It does not establish whether the public CMD_FLUSH contract requires canceling already-submitted USB transfers held in the TX ring, so no finding is added and that contract/caller question remains open. No request or USB transfer was run; no new line credit. Source-only.


Realtek8180 rate-helper and management-duration pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): read `GetDuration()` and `AckRate()` completely and traced their three TX call sites through data and management frame construction (`unit.c:2007-2296,2298-2417,2543-2619`). The constructor initializes TX rate to 11 Mbps and management rate to 1 Mbps; `SetOptions(S2INFO_Band)` changes them only to 54/2 Mbps for 802.11g or 11/1 Mbps for 802.11b (`unit.c:132-136,1034-1048`). `AckRate()` has explicit mappings for every selected value, including management 2 Mbps to 2 Mbps; the uninitialized local result for an unsupported rate is not reached through these in-tree assignments. `GetDuration()` receives nonzero selected rates and the frame lengths remain subject to existing raw/oversize TX findings OD3275/OD3276. This closes the selected rate-helper input mapping only; external mutation of unit fields, chipset airtime semantics and remaining Realtek caller/hardware contracts remain open. No frame or device was used; no new line credit. Source-only.


Realtek8180 same-endpoint USB submission-order contract recheck (OD3266 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced the 30 TX pipe allocations for one bulk OUT endpoint and 30 RX pipe allocations for one bulk IN endpoint (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/device.h:158-159`; `usb.c:535-550`), concurrent RX submission (`usb.c:284-290`), per-slot TX dispatch (`unit.c:2030-2035,2224-2228`; `usb.c:1073-1084`) and RX slot rearm (`usb.c:751-763,1103-1114`). Poseidon forwards each pipe request to the hardware task, which issues SendIO and counts multiple requests in flight (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4742-4778,9277-9293`). The public USB hardware contract explicitly requires endpoint-scoped DATA0/DATA1 tracking and in-order queueing of multiple requests to the same endpoint (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:67-82`); its CMD_FLUSH contract also covers in-progress and queued transfers (`:140-159`). The in-tree UHCI/OHCI HIDD classes create per-pipe queue/toggle state, but I found no selected implementation connecting those HIDD methods to Poseidon's `UHCMD_BULKXFER` device-request path; treating their state as proof of a violation would be unsupported. Therefore the prior completion-order concern remains open at the host-controller backend boundary and no new Realtek defect is promoted. The detailed transfer result issue remains OD3266. No device, host controller, or transfer was run; no line credit. Source-only.

Realtek8180 receive reassembly-to-SANA-II distribution pass (OD3257/OD3258/OD3259 rechecked, no new finding, 2026-10-21): traced `RXInt()` descriptor length, fragment lookup/append/decrypt, final-fragment handling and `DistributeRXPacket()` through `CopyPacket()` and the unit RX scratch allocation (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/unit.c:1467-1609,1638-1672,1696-1868`; `device.h:145-157,211-233`). Reconfirmed OD3257's missing upper bound against the 1,552-byte data area after the descriptor; OD3258's non-SNAP branch leaves `buffer` pointing at prior `rx_buffer` contents; and OD3259's missing `ETH_MAXPACKETSIZE` distribution guard passes the computed length to the opener callback without checking posted capacity. Compared the same SNAP/non-SNAP choice and MTU guard in the selected Prism2 and Atheros5000 copies. Also followed the RX completion path: USB descriptor construction derives its pointer from the completion length (OD3255) and offline completions are dropped without rearming (OD3265). These are existing report entries, not new discoveries; this slice adds no line credit because `unit.c` was already counted as a partially reviewed path. No packet, request, device or hardware was used. Source-only.

Realtek8180 encryption translation-unit pass and OD3295 extension (2026-10-21): read all 2,126 physical lines (1,865 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`) of `workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/encryption.c`; traced WEP/TKIP/CCMP fragment wrappers, per-frame TKIP MIC helpers, replay state, RC4 CRC and AES/CCMP extent handling against `InitialiseAdapter()`'s selected function table and `RXInt()`/`TXInt()` callers (`unit.c:760-795,1467-1555,2070-2185`). Confirmed OD3295 also applies to Realtek8180: `RXInt()` permits an encrypted body length of zero and dispatches the configured cipher, while the WEP/TKIP/CCMP readers or decryptors subtract their respective overheads from an unchecked `UWORD`; the underflow can reach large copies or crypto reads. Expanded OD3295 in the detailed report and master index to include Realtek8180 and its 28-byte receive floor, while retaining Atheros5000's separate path. OD3297 remains the distinct completed-frame TKIP MIC check. Compared the body against the Prism2 copy; differences are its m68k conditional integrity implementation, not an additional selected Realtek issue in this pass. Lookup tables were read but no cryptographic test vectors, packet, key request or hardware were exercised. Source-only.

Realtek8180 EEPROM/radio power-table and caller pass (OD4251 added, 2026-10-21): traced both 14-entry EEPROM location arrays, `GetPower()`/`GetPowerPair()`, unit allocation/default channel, `SetPower()`'s CCK/OFDM indexing and channel-code branches, then initial `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` and online `S2_SETOPTIONS` callers (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/radio.c:125-136,279-323,352-429,515-528`; `unit.c:115-136,461,849-861,1024-1029`; `request.c:650-655,1557-1568`). The EEPROM loop stores entries in indices 0–13, while the public/selected channel values and RF code use channels 1–14; channel 14 consequently consumes an untouched zeroed entry and channels 1–13 are shifted. Added OD4251 to the detailed report and index, keeping invalid-channel bounds separately in OD3283. Read the EEPROM bit-serial transaction helpers; their timing and register behavior remain unverified. No EEPROM, radio, request or hardware operation was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 busy-delay helper and selected-caller pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): read both complete delay helpers and traced every in-tree caller in `eeprom.c`, `radio.c` and `unit.c` (`timer.c:44-79`; caller inventory from `rg BusyMicroDelay|BusyMilliDelay` in the selected driver). `BusyMilliDelay` multiplies only fixed caller values no greater than 500 ms by 1,000; direct microsecond callers pass fixed values no greater than 10. Rechecked the apparent reversed comparison against `rom/timer/cmptime.c:25-36`: `CmpTime(dest,src)` returns -1 when `dest > src`, so `while(CmpTime(deadline,time) < 0)` waits while the deadline remains later than the sampled current time. Its initial comparison uses the duration value before the first current-time sample; no material defect was established for the selected post-startup callers. Added a complete timer-helper row; no new finding or line credit. No delay or timer operation was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 radio translation-unit body follow-through (OD4251 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-21): completed reading the remaining PHY and RF serial access helpers (`radio.c:557-831`) and rechecked the generation-specific USB direct-write branch against the common bit-banged path. ReadRadio/WriteRadio pin selection, clock/data sequencing, and restoration were source-traced; no additional defect was established without the RTL8225/R8180 register contract. Updated the file row from targeted to full-body read while keeping hardware semantics open. Source-only; no radio operation was run.
UIKit bitmap offset/render-caller recheck (OD3006/OD2794 retained; 2026-10-21): re-read the QBitmap Get/Set and UpdateRect methods against the configured method list, generic `ScrollVPort()` and graphics display compositor selection. Confirmed `ScrollVPort()` writes signed offsets through `QBitmap__Root__Set`, then reads the cached values back into `ViewPort`; UIKit reports nonzero composition flags, so generic display setup does not create the software compositor used to validate them. The mixed signed/unsigned upper-bound comparisons therefore retain OD3006’s conditional offset-state corruption. Separately, the configured `ShowViewPorts()` implementation returns TRUE without rendering, retained as OD2794; this limits OD3006’s claim to stored ViewPort state. The current class body and caller evidence produced no additional independent candidate. No iOS HIDD or viewport operation was run. Source-only.

USB Audio OD3163 completed-input length caller recheck (2026-10-21; finding confirmed, no duplicate): verified parser acceptance of 24-bit mono and three-byte frame assignment, `nRec24BitMono` selection, and RTIso hook installation (`usbaudio.class.c:1141-1159,1210-1213,3207-3219,3513-3533`). This supports OD3163’s packet trigger; no audio descriptor, transfer or device was used. Other USB Audio body/caller work remains partial. Source-only.

USB Audio shared RTIso hook ownership pass (OD4252 added, 2026-10-21): traced per-unit Hook writes in `nSelectAudioMode` through `psdAllocRTIsoHandler` tag packing into each handler’s `IOUsbHWRTIso` hook pointers, then through PCIUSB UHCI’s request-hook dispatch (`usbaudio.class.c:3207-3229`; `poseidon.library.c:5577-5587,9766-9775`; `compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:90-98`; `uhci_isoch.c:259-265`). Confirmed that AHI creates a distinct audio-control object per `AHI_AllocAudioA` call, USB Audio only rejects reusing the same mode’s `nam_RTIso`, and one class record can publish multiple streaming modes (`audioctrl.c:472-521`; `usbaudio.class.c:3271-3290,1074-1083,1192-1219,1935-1986`). Added OD4252 for the first active handler retaining a pointer to a per-unit Hook whose `h_Data` is overwritten by the second mode; distinct from OD3192’s `nch_CurrentMode` routing/clear issue. No stream was run. USB Audio translation-unit and wider device/HCD contract review remain partial. Source-only.

USB Audio OD4252 active-mode guard and HCD coverage recheck (2026-10-21; retained): checked the entire `nch_CurrentMode` reference inventory (`usbaudio.class.c:501,615,765-772,3332,3589`): it is not consulted before allocation, so it does not serialize distinct mode IDs. Reconfirmed `AHI_AllocAudioA` constructs a new control on each call and `CreateAudioCtrl` has no unit-exclusive check (`audioctrl.c:141-170,223-253,472-521`). Compared request-hook dispatch in PCIUSB UHCI, PCIUSB OHCI, and PCI xHCI (`uhci_isoch.c:259-265`; `ohci_isoch.c:235-241`; `xhci_isoch.c:209-215`); each dereferences the hook pointer retained in `IOUsbHWRTIso`. This strengthens OD4252 trigger coverage; it remains distinct from OD3192. No audio control or stream was allocated. Source-only.


Sam440 battclock read-failure caller pass (OD4253 added, 2026-10-21): traced the selected `ReadBattClock()` path through bus creation, address probe, device construction, `Hidd_I2CDevice_WriteRead`, and `Date2Amiga()` (`arch/ppc-sam440/battclock/readbattclock.c:27-108`; `workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cdeviceclass.c:157-162`; `workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c:330-369`; `rom/utility/date2amiga.c:52-64`). A created bus object reaches conversion even when probe/device construction fails, and the transfer Boolean is ignored; `date` is uninitialized unless a successful object path fills it. `Date2Amiga` indexes its month table without validation. Added OD4253 to the report and index. Confirmed the Sam440 boot module graph selects the generic and AMCC440 I2C HIDDs and loads `battclock.resource` (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:16-23,47-49`; `boot/menu.lst:12,34`); `SetClock` is a direct consumer. Generic I²C device timing-attribute reconciliation (OD4323 added, 2026-10-22): rechecked `I2CDev::Root::New/Get/Set` and the generic `I2C::PutByte/GetByte/WriteRead` delay uses (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cdeviceclass.c:200-233,326-372`; `i2cclass.c:231-321`). The device constructor accepts per-device HoldTime/RiseFallTime tags, and Get/Set preserve those fields, but the inherited bit-level transfer methods read these two delays from `tDrvData` on the shared bus. Other per-device timeouts are read from `tDevData`, confirming the discrepancy is limited to hold/rise-fall. Searched checked-in device constructor tags and setters: no selected caller overrides these per-device fields, so promoted OD4323 as a conditional public-API behavior with medium caller-contract confidence, not as a demonstrated in-tree device failure. Generic class and Sam440 bit-bus selection are already tracked above; no new line credit. No bus or timing operation was run. Source-only.

VideoCore GPU MemHeader failed-init unwind pass (OD4324 added, 2026-10-22): traced `VideoCoreGfx__Support__Init()` from mailbox GPU-range discovery through `InitMem()`, `InitCursor()`, `InitDMA()`, graphics.library open and `AddDisplayDriver()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_init.c:101-197`). `InitMem()` links the library-base-embedded `MemHeaderExt` into Exec's MemList (`vcgfx_memory.c:225-249`) before later operations can fail; the only shared failure cleanup frees the mailbox buffer and attribute bases and does not unlink that node. Confirmed a selected failure return is reachable from `AddDisplayDriverA()`'s `DD_NO_MEM` path (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:164-169`) and other setup errors. Exec's `AvailMem()` invokes the managed header's `mhe_Avail` (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:365-378`); this header reports `mh_Free`, while its allocation callback returns NULL (`vcgfx_memory.c:36-42,218-223`). Added OD4324 for the lingering unavailable GPU range after a post-InitMem failure. The loader's failed-library-base lifetime was not required to establish this finding and is not claimed. BCM2712 exits before GPU memory setup. No module failure, mailbox response, or memory query was induced; source-only. VC4 local source and broader HVS/display-platform review remain partial.

OD4324 Exec allocator-consequence qualification (2026-10-22): read the complete `nommu_AllocMem()` list walk and `nommu_AvailMem()` managed-header paths (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:23-83,309-378`). When `mhe_Alloc()` returns NULL, normal allocation continues to the next matching MemHeader; therefore the VideoCore failure leaves an inaccurate `AvailMem(MEMF_CHIP)` total, but this source does not establish that it blocks allocations from later headers. Narrowed OD4324's stated consequence accordingly and removed the conditional stale-module-base claim, which was unnecessary to establish the defect. No allocation or memory query was run; no source-line credit. Source-only.


Sam440 battclock write-path follow-up (no new finding, 2026-10-21): read the complete `WriteBattClock()` body and traced `Amiga2Date`, SetClock’s save path and time-preferences conversion (`arch/ppc-sam440/battclock/writebattclock.c:27-128`; `workbench/c/SetClock.c:154-165`; `workbench/prefs/time/prefs.c:46-54`). The old-register transfer result is ignored and a later write is attempted, but this buffer is zero-initialized and no checked-in source identifies the board RTC’s preserved control-bit semantics; no separate defect is promoted. Marked those hardware and failure-reporting contracts open in the file row. No RTC or caller was used. Source-only.

Atheros5000 AR5211 shared-table concurrency recheck (OD3825/OD4227 scope split, 2026-10-21): re-read `ar5211SetRf6and7()` and reset callers, plus `ar5211SetTransmitPower()`/`ar5211SetPowerTable()`/`ar5211SetRateTable()` and the per-unit `access_lock`, request service, and card-insertion reset paths (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_reset.c:298-328,419-423,1058-1154,1336-1387,1397-1506,1514-1708`; `unit.c:167-169,2814-2860`; `request.c:142-155,629-655,1559-1570`). Confirmed independent unit tasks can invoke reset/configuration without a shared HAL lock. Split the existing duplicate description: OD3825 now covers only the file-static RF register vectors (`ar5211Rf6n7`, conditionally `ar5211Mode2_4`); OD4227 covers function-static power-calibration scratch across AR5211, AR5416, and AR9285. No additional issue established in this caller/locking pass. Other AR5211 reset paths, EEPROM semantics, and remaining Atheros5000 source rows are still open; this is not a full driver review. No card, reset, request, or interleaving was run. Source-only.
Atheros5000 reset API caller census extension (OD3292 existing coverage, 2026-10-21): `rg` found one direct in-tree `ah_reset()` invocation, in `ConfigureAdapter()` (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:788`). Its three direct callers are `CmdConfigInterface`, online `CmdSetOptions`, and the unit task’s card-insertion branch (`request.c:653,1569`; `unit.c:2855`); all reach it in the per-unit task/request paths. `ConfigureAdapter()` discards the Boolean and `HAL_STATUS`, but that separate false-success behavior is already OD3292. No duplicate finding added. This closes only the checked-in direct reset caller census; external HAL clients and hardware contracts remain open.

AHI Preferences input/output label-array allocation failure pass (OD4254 added, 2026-10-21): traced selected `AHI_MUI` construction and mode-change flow through `NewMode()` to `GUINewMode()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/gui_mui.c:302-314,406-424,998-1002`; `ahi.c:278-328,436-439,591-608`). Both `GetInputs()` and `GetOutputs()` return NULL if their combined array/string allocation fails (`support.c:952-981,988-1017`), but `NewMode()` publishes those results unconditionally and the label helpers read element zero before checking the pointer. `workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/Makefile.in:49-52` selects `AHI_MUI` as the installed executable; alternate ClassAct/BGUI UIs are not required for the finding. Added OD4254 for positive reported item counts with the corresponding allocation failure. No memory pressure or GUI was induced. Source-only.

AR5211 regulatory noise-floor candidate caller and domain recheck (OD3824 retained, 2026-10-21): traced `ar5211CalNoiseFloor()` through the only two callers, reset and long periodic calibration (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_reset.c:475-482,734-755,985-1020`), then checked `ath_hal_getnfcheckrequired()` against the selected channel's `regDmnFlags` and the MKK table's `NEED_NFC` entries (`hal/ah_regdomain.c:528-574,2825-2832`). The loop always exits with `i == 3`; therefore `i <= N(runtime)` returns true regardless of sample outcomes. Failed samples clear `rawNoiseFloor`, including after an earlier passing sample, so the final failed attempt can leave zero while still reporting success. Refined OD3824's trigger and consequence accordingly; no duplicate added. The precise radio conditions producing above-threshold readings remain hardware-dependent. No channel or measurement was used; source-only.

AR5211 noise-floor frequency-adjustment helper caller pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced `ar5211GetNfAdjust()` through its attach-time function-pointer installation and shared `ath_hal_getChanNoise()`/`ath_hal_process_noisefloor()` consumers (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_attach.c:337`; `hal/ah_internal.h:250,331-332`; `hal/ah.c:772-851`). Public channel-noise lookup rejects a channel with no `ath_hal_checkchannel()` mapping before calling the adjustment helper; bulk processing iterates only the HAL's populated internal channel table. The adjustment table's sentinel iteration therefore receives positive, selected channel values on these in-tree paths; the apparent zero-channel overrun is not reachable through the checked callers. Values above the final threshold use the high-frequency adjustment entry. Compared the generic AR5212 path and made no independent finding. External private HAL callers and RF noise-floor calibration semantics remain open. No channel or radio was used; source-only.

AR5211 transmit-power-limit input/caller pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced the apparently unclamped `AR_PHY_POWER_TX_RATE_MAX` write in `ar5211SetTxPowerLimit()` (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_reset.c:1324-1329`) through every in-tree call. The internal rate-table call passes its computed `pRatesPower[0]` after target-power, regulatory, edge and rate-scaling limits (`:1514-1707`); the packed rate table masks each entry to six bits (`:1688-1705`). The only direct device caller is `ConfigureAdapter()`, which passes the fixed `TX_POWER == 40` half-dBm value (`unit.c:53,797`), below `MAX_RATE_POWER == 63` (`hal/ah_eeprom.h:126-127`). The checked caller census did not establish a value above the field/rate limit, so no in-tree finding is established from the raw register write; unusual EEPROM contents and external internal-HAL clients remain open. No radio or power register was used. Source-only.


RTL8139 TX completion scheduling-context recheck (OD3111, 2026-10-21): confirmed `RTL8139_TX_IntF` is an Exec soft interrupt installed in `rtl8139u_tx_int` and scheduled by `Cause()` from TX and timeout paths (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/unit.c:321-345,496,620,1052-1055`). `SoftIntDispatch` explicitly enables interrupts before calling each handler (`rom/exec/cause.c:176-184`). `ReplyMsg` publishes through `InternalPutMsg`/`Signal`; `Signal` documents immediate start for a higher-priority waiter and its uniprocessor path calls `Reschedule()`, whose enabled-interrupt branch invokes `KrnSchedule()` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`; `putmsg.c:81-99`; `signal.c:117-145,385-419`; `reschedule.c:55-80`). Thus the RTL8139 post-reply packet-type read can race caller reuse on a uniprocessor when the waiting reply task has higher priority, as well as on ExecSMP; no SMP-only qualification is warranted. Updated OD3111 in the detailed report and index with this Exec scheduling evidence; no new finding. No request or task switch was run. Source-only.

AHI AddAudioModes existing-candidate restoration and caller qualification (2026-10-21): reconciled the full 338-line body and selected AHI CLI/API/manual paths against the pre-existing file-ledger candidates. No command, descriptor directory, mode database or display was exercised. Source-only.


Input-device handler caller null-chain census (2026-10-21; no new OD): searched every C/header `IND_ADDHANDLER` and `IND_REMHANDLER` use in the pinned tree. Direct handler registrations are Intuition, FreezeDemon, console.device, KMS, PopupMenu, commodities CxTree, and lowlevel; MUI application-level handlers use a separate dispatch path. Read each selected handler entry against `ForwardQueuedEvents()` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:94-119`): FreezeDemon, console, lowlevel, and CxTree iterate/check for null; Intuition seeds its own returned chain; KMS can return NULL on a consumed switch key (`workbench/libs/kms/kms_library.c:71-95`); PopupMenu dereferences the incoming event in a do-while loop (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/pminput.c:20-98`). This confirms the existing selected KMS-to-PopupMenu candidate GD1967, but no separate finding. MUI application handlers and the traced in-tree input producers did not establish another null-consuming sequence. External handler contracts and other platform-specific producers remain open. No input event or handler was run. Source-only.


Keyboard pending-read lost-wakeup candidate restored (OD2389, 2026-10-21): verified the two-sided check/enqueue interleaving in `BeginIO` and `keyCallback` (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:362-379,621-646`). `Disable()` is CPU-local under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), and the initialized `kb_QueueLock` is not acquired in either path (`keyboard_intern.h:31-32`; sole code use is `InitSemaphore` at `keyboard.c:118`). If the reader checks empty, a remote callback publishes the key and sees no pending request, then the reader enqueues, the callback has already skipped `kbdSendQueuedEvents`; the key remains in the ring until a later callback. The selected input.device owns one read and waits for its reply, making the stall visible to the normal path. Restored OD2389 from the coverage-only candidate to the detailed report and index. Selected ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP manifest paths are documented in the finding. No key or cross-CPU schedule was run. Source-only.


PPP timer-open failure cleanup pass (OD4256 added, 2026-10-21): traced `OpenTimer()` failure to `CloseTimer()` and Exec's OpenDevice/AbortIO contracts. OpenDevice clears `io_Device` after an open-vector error; CloseTimer nevertheless calls AbortIO on every allocated request, which dispatches via that NULL device. The selected PPP init path calls OpenTimer and expects a NULL result to unwind startup (`init.c:91-92`). Added OD4256; the ModemManager copy has a similar helper but its executable selection remains unverified and is not claimed here. No timer device failure or PPP startup was induced; serial.c already has full-body line credit. Source-only.


Deneb public request-wrapper/quick-I/O pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): re-read AROS `devBeginIO()` and `devAbortIO()` dispatch and traced `IOF_QUICK`/message-node state through `TermIO()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:523-639,658-690`; `uhwcmd.c:1602-1621`). Each queued control, bulk, ISO and interrupt transfer clears `IOF_QUICK` before linking the request and returning `RC_DONTREPLY` (`uhwcmd.c:811-832,853-874,894-918,935-957`); synchronous commands return through `TermIO()`, which preserves quick completion or replies non-quick requests. Compared this with Exec `DoIO()`/`SendIO()` quick-bit setup (`rom/exec/doio.c:48-68`; `sendio.c:44-60`) and USBHardware request-field ownership documentation (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:120-125`). The selected wrapper does not establish a generic pending-request false-quick or missed-reply defect. Public command semantics, cancellation interleavings and ISP1760 hardware timing remain partial; no device or request was run. Source-only.

Deneb UHCMD_QUERYDEVICE tag-output and Poseidon caller pass (2026-10-21; OD4230 confirmed, no duplicate): read `cmdQueryDevice()`'s full tag switch and the USBHardware tag/result contract, then traced every tag in Poseidon's selected 13-slot stack TagItem array through `DoIO()` into copied PsdHardware fields and callbacks (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:718-795`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9130-9132,9200-9250`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:513-555`). Poseidon supplies correctly sized ULONG/STRPTR output storage for the implemented tags; `iouh_Actual` counts the matched tags, and Description/DriverVersion/Capabilities are written. UHA_Version and UHA_Revision remain the existing OD4230: their handlers are compiled out while Poseidon initializes those outputs to zero and stores them. No additional tag-buffer or result-count defect established; no device query was run. Source-only.

Deneb CMD_FLUSH contract and RTIso boundary pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): compared `cmdFlush()`'s five queued request lists and three scheduled PTD pools (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:973-1041`) with the USBHardware `CMD_FLUSH` contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:143-160`) and Poseidon's shutdown caller (`poseidon.library.c:9290-9310`). The contract names in-progress/queued CONTROL, ISO, INT and BULK transfer requests; RTIso is a separately registered, long-lived handler with explicit `UHCMD_STOPRTISO`/`UHCMD_REMISOHANDLER` operations and is not a pending transfer IORequest. The omission from `cmdFlush()` therefore does not establish a separate defect. Poseidon's device-release callback and class teardown provide the RTIso cleanup path; prior OD4140/OD4152/OD4163/OD3884 findings remain distinct. No flush or device shutdown was run. Source-only.


USBHub interrupt-signal assignment and OHCI registration caller pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the generic hub's `HubInterrupt` callback through `HIDD_USBDrv_AddInterrupt()` and the selected OHCI per-pipe interrupt queue (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:62-72,145-153`; `workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:453-531`). `HubData.sigInterrupt` is zero-initialized with the OOP instance and has no assignment in the checked USB stack; consequently the callback signals bit 0 and `hub_process()` waits on bit 0 (`usb.h:123`; `usbhubclass.c:628-630,684`). This is the reserved `SIGF_ABORT` bit. The same bit does deliver ordinary hub-change wakeups, and cleanup is performed via a message, not this signal. No selected in-tree producer or documented hub-task abort contract establishes a lost-cancellation consequence, so this signal overlap is not promoted as a standalone defect. It is distinct from OD2962, where OHCI `ClearPortFeature` clears the *calling task's* bit 0. No USB interrupt or abort signal was run. Source-only.

OHCI root-hub port-argument and worker error-path pass (OD2956 scope narrowed; 2026-10-21): traced all selected `USBHub` calls to `PortReset`, `GetPortStatus`, `ClearPortFeature`, and `SetPortFeature` (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:319-344,452-468,477-498,501-598`). Normal `hub_enable()`/`hub_disable()` and `hub_explore()` enumerate ports from 1 through the descriptor's `bNbrPorts`; the reset and status calls use the current loop port, so the unchecked zero/upper bounds in OHCI `PortReset` and missing lower-bound checks in `ClearPortFeature`/`SetPortFeature` are not reached by these selected worker paths. `GetPortStatus` does check both bounds. The weak/malformed descriptor fallback is at least one port, but the descriptor's advertised port count itself is trusted and bounds the same loops; descriptor validation remains a separate scope. `PortReset` remains an externally callable HIDD boundary candidate (OD2956), not a demonstrated normal hub-worker fault. Also rechecked generic `hub->children` allocation and use; its unchecked allocation and later indexed access are already OD2239, and nested-hub child disposal is already OD2469. No additional finding from this caller pass. No port method, allocation failure, malformed descriptor, or hardware was exercised; source-only.

OHCI RHSC interrupt-to-softint recheck (existing RHSC row retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced the complete selected handler branch from WDH/RHSC status collection through disable/ack, one-second timer submission, hub `Cause()` delivery, not-running `pendingRHSC` handling, and the timer soft-interrupt rearm (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:278-444`; `ohcihub.c:70-90,265-284`). Poseidon custom semaphore and nested hub-scan concurrency pass (OD1602 restored/expanded, 2026-10-21): re-read `pLockSemExcl`, `pLockSemShared`, `pUnlockSem`, and the complete `psdBorrowLocksWait` transfer/reclaim path (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:492-675,735-973`) against ExecSMP `Forbid()` semantics (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). Traced nested hub concurrency: `nHubTask` signals its creator before scanning downstream devices (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:408-440`); the parent class scan waits through `psdBorrowLocksWait` while holding the PBase shared lock and device write lock, then can continue sibling scans as the child scans its downstream ports (`poseidon.library.c:6270-6295,6490-6496`). Separate CPUs can therefore mutate the common `ps_Lock.pls_ReadLocks` and wait/borrow records concurrently; ordinary `AddHead` interleaving can lose a reader node while `pls_SharedLockCount` is incremented, and `pUnlockSem` then cannot release the absent record. Restored the absent OD1602 detail and short AROS.md index entry, expanded from the earlier lock-acquisition-only note to include borrowing and this selected caller trigger. No lock, hub, device, or concurrent schedule was exercised; source-only.

USB CAMD MIDI input buffer/parser caller pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the selected `nHidTask()` endpoint completion through `psdGetPipeActual()` into `nParseMidi()` (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:487-505,736-772`). The input transfer is submitted with the fixed 1,024-byte buffer; `nParseMidi()` reads a record only while at least four bytes remain, advances exactly four bytes per record, and derives the adapter index from the low four bits of the first byte's high nibble (0–15), within the 16-entry adapter array. Incomplete trailing bytes are ignored. This closes the selected input-buffer bound and index path; callback scheduling and external CAMD receiver lifetime remain as previously recorded under OD4137/OD4257. No USB transfer or callback was run; source-only.

Traced `bf_CopyTo` and `bf_CopyFrom` through completion: `IntCode()` ignores the receive callback BOOL before reporting data length and success; `SendPacket()` ignores the transmit callback BOOL and proceeds to DMA. AROSTCP `m_copy_to_mbuf()` returns FALSE before assigning `ioip_packet` when its reserved chain is short (`sana2copybuff.c:229-280`); RTL8029 still marks an all-ones destination as broadcast and completes success (`driver.c:1154-1164`), after which `sana_read()` dereferences the still-NULL packet while setting `M_BCAST` (`if_sana.c:936-947`). This is a conditional crash consequence; selected AROSTCP allocation normally accommodates the advertised MTU and bounded RTL8029 receive buffer, so no ordinary in-tree capacity-failure trigger is established. AROSTCP's `m_copy_from_mbuf()` returns FALSE for a short chain only in `#if DIAGNOSTIC`; without it, the short-chain path dereferences NULL (`sana2copybuff.c:190-215`). So the in-tree transmit FALSE path is diagnostic-only; direct SANA-II callbacks remain the general trigger. PPP explicitly propagates callback errors. No callback or packet was run. Source-only.

CAMD USB MIDI transmit ring and callback-sentinel recheck (OD4125 strengthened; OD4266 added, 2026-10-21): traced CAMD's `Transmitter()` no-data return (`workbench/libs/camd/miditodriver.c:182-220`) and the selected `GetFromCAMD()` storage/wakeup loop (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c:115-132`) through the USB task's `Wait()`/`nParseMidiOut()` consumer (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:487-507,519-533`). The no-data value `0x100` is stored into a byte slot as zero; when `ca_SysExMode` is active, the consumer treats low-bit-clear bytes as SysEx payload and emits a continuation packet after three (`:703-724`), supporting OD4266's conditional output-corruption finding. Also refined OD4125's boundary: with read=0/write=4095, one-empty-slot capacity is already full; the producer writes slot 4095, masks the next cursor with 4096, publishes 4096, and can iterate again before its final Signal to write at index 4096. If the consumer runs first, its `(write + size - read) & (size-1)` length becomes zero and does not repair the cursor. The existing report now records this sequence and the conditional task timing. The module manifest selects this optional class through `kernel-usb-classes-common` on its declared CPU aliases; the code path is not part of every default ROM. No CAMD stream, USB device, task schedule, or memory boundary was exercised. Source-only.


RTL8029 receive ring count and destination-capacity pass (OD4267 added, 2026-10-21): traced the selected `IntCode()` receive path through `PacketReceived()` and `GetPacket()` and checked the `UnitData` member extent (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:180,1131-1165,1335-1384`). The ring header supplies a 16-bit count; `PacketReceived()` passes it to `GetPacket()` without validation, and `GetPacket()` writes `(len + 1) / 2` words into `ud_RxBuffer[768]` (1,536 bytes). A corrupted or otherwise invalid count over 1,536 bytes therefore writes past the fixed destination into adjacent `UnitData` fields before the packet reaches the SANA-II callback. The configured RTL8029 receive ring and ordinary Ethernet frame range fit this buffer, so no ordinary frame is claimed as a trigger; the candidate is conditional on a bad count in the NIC ring/header. Added OD4267, recommending validation of count and next-page/status before DMA copy and ring advancement. The exact chipset count/status contract and hardware error behavior remain open. No device, packet or ring corruption was induced. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II EAPOL send and selected state-machine caller pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the selected `send_eapol` callback from `wpa_supplicant_eapol_send()`/`wpa_ether_send()` into `wpa_driver_sana2_send_eapol()` and the EAPOL supplicant send callbacks (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/wpas_glue.c:98-105,126-190`; `src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:507-521,1097-1104`; `src/eapol_supp/eapol_supp_sm.c:623-641,832-852`). SANA-II uses the shared request only for synchronous `DoIO`; the async read/event traffic has distinct request allocations, and the selected Amiga event loop dispatches supplicant callbacks serially. `wpa_ether_send()` propagates the `DoIO` result, but EAPOL Start/Logoff/Response callbacks ignore it; their state-machine counters/timers still advance. The state machine increments its transmission counters even if the callback reports failure; these counters are only exposed by its debug MIB output, and no selected caller relies on them. A failed individual frame can still delay/fail its protocol exchange, but this is the underlying write failure rather than a separate request-ownership defect, so no additional driver finding is promoted. This pass adds no full-file line credit; the supplicant translation unit and broader callback lifecycle remain partial. No request, frame or device was used; source-only.

AHCI monitor-registration failure caller recheck (OD4063 retained, 2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the sole `ahci_RegisterPort()` caller through its lock release/reacquire and error branch (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:336-365`), then rechecked the monitor's startup signal and `NewCreateTaskA()` failure return (`:61-71,154-184`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:257-272`). AHCI port registration allocation/unwind distinction (OD4063 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): checked the `AllocPooled()` failure branch in `ahci_RegisterPort()` against its sole caller and `ahci_cam_detach()` (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:154-184,336-383`). The distinct later `NewCreateTask()` failure remains OD4063: by then the unit is published, and the caller blocks before it can reach detach. No allocation failure or attach was induced. AHCI change-notification list lock and request-reuse recheck (OD2866 retained, 2026-10-21): reread the media-monitor list walk and the BeginIO insertion/completion paths (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:123-136`; `ahci_io.c:246-251,399-410,442-447`). Also reconfirmed that every BeginIO first inserts the request node, including `TD_REMCHANGEINT`; when a still-linked `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` request is reused, this rewrites its links and one completion-side Remove cannot restore the original list. E1000 `DeleteUnit()` teardown caller recheck (2026-10-21; OD2436 retained, no new OD): traced `e1000_init.c` expunge through `DeleteUnit()` and compared the parent frees with `e1000func_Schedular()` shutdown cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000_init.c:224-235`; `unit.c:578-594,1079-1111`). No distinct defect established in the checked teardown sequence; constructor failure/handshake paths remain under canonical OD3222 (OD2437 was later withdrawn as a duplicate), and broader timer/device behavior remain open; the current source tracker credits the full 1,195-line `unit.c` body. For each of the battery, AC-adapter and power-meter initializers, final private-IID name-allocation failure zeros the bases; its `Handle` tag becomes zero, `GetTagData` stops at TAG_DONE and the constructor stores NULL while returning an object. The callers count that object and report module initialization success. Battery/adapter methods expose NotPresent and PowerMeter builds no entries. Exact source: `rom/hidds/acpi/{battery/acpibattery_init.c,acad/acpiacad_init.c,powermeter/acpipowermeter_init.c}`; constructors under corresponding `*_class.c`; generator/parser `tools/genmodule/config.c:682-685,1663-1665,1917-1928`, `writeincinterfaces.c:99-126`; tag traversal `rom/utility/gettagdata.c:68`, `compiler/arossupport/libfindtagitem.c:7-18`. Added OD4294 to report/index. No ACPI scan or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

ACPI AC-adapter final-attrbase path and package-selection recheck (OD4294 retained; 2026-10-25): re-read the selected `ACPIACAd_Init()` path from the five-entry descriptor list through `GetTagData()` and `HW_AddDriver()` (`rom/hidds/acpi/acad/acpiacad_init.c:123-166`; `acpiacad_class.c:47-80`). Confirmed the shared failure cleanup zeroes the handle descriptor, the first generated `Handle` offset is zero, and `TAG_DONE` prevents the constructor from seeing the supplied ACPI handle; `HW_AddDriver()` can still count the resulting object as registered. Verified the class appears in the x86-64 PC ACPI package (`boot/mmakefile.src:81-94`) and RISC-V OpenSBI BSP HIDD list (`boot/mmakefile.src:104-118`). This is already OD4294, not a new finding; non-final helper hang and namespace-node cleanup remain OD3418 and OD3415. No firmware scan, allocation failure or registration was run; no body-line credit.

BTHID Shell-action and asynchronous handle-ownership pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced `HUA_SHELL` through `bLastActionHero()` and its selected GUI/configuration fields (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:6395-6418`; `bthid.gui.c:1081,2228-2229,2487,3020-3021,3278-3284`). The handler closes `fhandle` after synchronous completion or launch error, and leaves it open only after a successful asynchronous `SystemTags()` launch. DOS documents that async SYS_Input/SYS_Output/SYS_Error handles close when the child exits (`compiler/include/dos/dostags.h:103-117`); `SystemTagList()` marks ownership transferred by clearing its `*_opened` flags for async success (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:492-497`). The helper's unchecked `ExtArg` allocation after successful process creation is already D32 in the DOS report (`systemtaglist.c:402-414`) and was not duplicated. No separate BTHID handle-lifetime defect established. No command or child process was run. Source-only.

BTHID Activate-window active-screen lifetime follow-up (OD4295 added, 2026-10-21): followed `HUAT_ACTWINDOW`'s `ActiveScreen` read under `LockIBase()` through the later `LayerInfo` access (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:6424-6435`) and selected `CloseScreen()` removal/update under the same lock followed by screen-object disposal outside it (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:353-400,279-291`). A concurrent successful close of the empty active screen can invalidate the saved screen pointer before BTHID locks or reads `LayerInfo`; added OD4295 as distinct from OD4156's later freed-layer access and OD4290's queued-window pointer. Requires the optional Bluetooth HID class and configured action. No screen or action was run; source-only.

BTHID service-binding publication and release-lock follow-up (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced `bAttemptServiceBinding()`/`bForceServiceBinding()` through the Bluetooth core's per-device service snapshot and binding-in-progress flags (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:169-290`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:280-375`). A single core scan marks all pending services before attempting them and invokes attempts sequentially; BTHID adds each successfully initialized binding to `nh_Interfaces` before returning, so the dual-bearer duplicate guard has no selected same-scan gap. `btReleaseSvcBinding()` calls the class release method while holding the device write lock (`classes.c:590-604`); BTHID stops and joins its worker, whose teardown aborts/waits/frees report channels (`bthid.class.c:294-349,1141-1158,1260-1291`). The checked channel abort and close-control paths are handled by the hardware task without reacquiring `bd_Lock` (`objects.c:1095-1131,1198-1221`; `hwconn.c:3678-3700`), so this pass does not establish the suspected lock-order deadlock. Any synchronous in-flight channel wait versus link shutdown remains a separate untested lifecycle question. No service binding, worker, or device was run. Source-only.

BTHID report-channel and staged worker-initialization pass (OD4296 added, 2026-10-21): traced `bOpenReportChannels()`'s Classic and HOGP channel setup, Report Reference lookup, per-report input-buffer allocation, failure unwind through `bCloseReportChannels()` and `bAllocHid()`, then successful delivery to `bHandleReport()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:820-900,1056-1257`). Added OD4296: a failed/short Report Reference read leaves `rtype == 0`, so later output/feature selection cannot match exact types 2/3. An unknown-type endpoint is additionally admitted as an input channel only when it advertises notify/indicate; `BEA_CanRead` here means device-to-host notify/indicate flow, not GATT Read permission. Reviewed `bAllocHid()`'s staged open/port/request/channel/report cleanup; the failure exits release the acquired resources in the inspected branches, and no independent cleanup defect was established. No runtime/device or allocation failure was used; the BTHID translation unit remains partial and no full-file line credit is claimed. Source-only.

OD4296 trigger qualification (2026-10-21): cross-checked endpoint enumeration and `BEA_CanRead` against `hwconn.c:1866-1875,2022-2037` and `bluetooth.h:255`. BTHID GUI-release completion ordering recheck (OD3479 retained, 2026-10-21): reread both cleanup tails (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.gui.c:1786-1792`; `bthidctrl.gui.c:408-414`) and the service-release callback plus Bluetooth core caller (`bthid.class.c:294-349`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:590-604`). Both GUI tasks clear their respective published task pointer and signal the release waiter before the final `nhb->nhb_ClsBase->nh_Library.lib_OpenCnt` access. The callback observes each NULL pointer, then waits for the HID task and frees `nhb` before returning to the caller. Exec explicitly limits `Forbid()` to the calling CPU on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:40-57`), so it does not order that final access against the release task on another CPU. This confirms the existing conditional OD3479; the two GUI cleanup paths share one ownership/order defect. No separate candidate added. No GUI task, service release, or interleaving was run. Source-only.


RTL8029 receive ring header and count-validation recheck (OD4267 retained, 2026-10-21): followed `IntCode()` through `RingBufferNotEmpty()`, `PacketReceived()`, and `GetPacket()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:1131-1165,1335-1384,1564-1578`). `RingBufferNotEmpty()` only compares `ud_NextPage` with the controller's `CURRENT_PAGE`; it does not validate ring-page ranges or the packet header. `PacketReceived()` takes the upper 16 bits of the four-byte header as `len`, does not check header status, count against the 1,536-byte `ud_RxBuffer`, or `nextpage` against `[RX_BUFFER, BUFFER_END)`, and passes the count directly to `GetPacket()`. `GetPacket()` reads `(len + 1) / 2` words, so a count above 1,536 bytes overruns `ud_RxBuffer`; the resulting length is also used for SANA-II delivery. The configured ring spans pages `0x46..0x7f`, but this software path does not establish that the header count/page fields are valid before copying or advancing. This corroborates OD4267; ordinary Ethernet frame bounds remain within the buffer, so the finding remains conditional on malformed/corrupt ring metadata. Exact chipset status/count semantics remain open. No device or malformed header was used; source-only.

RTL8029 short receive-count and SANA-II callback recheck (OD4265/OD4267 qualified, 2026-10-21): traced `IntCode()`'s non-raw `len - (offset << 1)` argument to the selected AROSTCP `m_copy_to_mbuf()` and `sana_read()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:1131-1165`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/sana2copybuff.c:229-281`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:936-947`). For an invalid ring count below 14, unsigned `ULONG` subtraction wraps to a very large length. AROSTCP's callback exhausts the reserved mbuf chain and returns FALSE without setting `ioip_packet`; RTL8029 ignores the result and replies success. If the matching delivered frame is broadcast, `sana_read()` dereferences its still-NULL local packet pointer while applying the broadcast flag. This qualifies the prior OD4265 statement that no in-tree receive failure trigger was established and records the separate low-count consequence under OD4267; it remains conditional on invalid/corrupt controller metadata plus a packet-type match and broadcast destination. No frame, callback, or device was run. Source-only.

RTL8029 SANA-II online/configuration ordering pass (OD4297 added, 2026-10-21): traced `S2_ONLINE()` and `S2ConfigInterface()` through `GoOnline()` and `HardwareInit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:957-1018,1246-1300`). `S2_ONLINE` succeeds without `UF_CONFIGURED`; configuration then masks all interrupts through `HardwareInit()` but skips `GoOnline()` because `UF_ONLINE` remains set, leaving the software state online without the normal interrupt setup. Compared with selected Intel Pro/100 and BTPAN handlers, which return `S2ERR_BAD_STATE`/`S2WERR_NOT_CONFIGURED` before online, and traced selected AROSTCP/WirelessManager callers, which configure first. Added OD4297, conditional on direct SANA-II clients using online-before-config. No device or command sequence was run. Source-only.

RTL8029 state-command statistics side-effect pass (OD4298 added, 2026-10-21): traced `S2Online()` and `S2ConfigInterface()` around their `ClearGlobalStats()` calls, the reset fields, and `S2GetGlobalStats()` copyout (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:774-781,957-1018,1034-1048`). Both commands zero packet counters and update `LastStart` before rejecting duplicate/invalid requests, making the failed operation caller-visible through the stats query. Added OD4298; no counters or request sequence were run. Source-only.

RTL8029 SANA-II packet-type tracking dispatch/caller check (no finding, 2026-10-21): traced `DevBeginIO()` immediate command dispatch, `NSDSupported[]`, and AROSTCP's optional `SSF_TRACK` calls (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:294-311,526-553`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:481-505`). The driver omits `S2_TRACKTYPE` from both its dispatch and advertised NSD-supported command list, so it returns `IOERR_NOCMD` rather than silently claiming tracking support; AROSTCP logs tracking failure and continues. No additional defect established for this intentionally unsupported optional command. No request was issued. Source-only.

PC i8042 mouse setup-task affinity and pre-reset IRQ qualification (OD2331/OD2332 scope recheck, no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced `i8042_mouse_init_task()`'s `NewCreateTask(TASKTAG_PC, ...)` into the task-tag parser and Exec ETask initialization (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseps2.c:188-224`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:116-147`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:131-169`). `TASKTAG_PC` selects the task entry point and no affinity tag is supplied; under ExecSMP the new task inherits its creator's affinity mask, or defaults to the creating CPU if there is no parent ETask. The mouse class registers IRQ12 before reset, then performs the reset under `Disable()` while the controller's mouse-interrupt enable is cleared during the reset sequence (`i8042_mouseps2.c:212-224,382-435`). The driver does not establish which task/CPU invokes module initialization or whether its inherited mask includes the IRQ destination, so the pre-reset cross-CPU IRQ overlap remains a platform/startup gap rather than a new finding. No task, IRQ, or controller was run. Source-only.

PC i8042 disposal versus active IRQ callback recheck (EK9263/OD4299 added, 2026-10-21): compared the selected PC override of `krnRunIRQHandlers()` with the generic dispatcher and `KrnRemIRQHandler()` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:115-132`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:120-143`; `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-75`). The generic reader lock serializes removal, but the PC override never takes it; removal therefore does not wait for an in-progress callback on another CPU before freeing the `IntrNode`. Traced both i8042 Dispose methods through immediate superclass disposal (`i8042_kbdclass.c:335-345`; `i8042_mouseclass.c:94-102`) and added EK9263 plus driver-specific OD4299, conditional on ExecSMP cross-CPU overlap during public driver removal. No event or concurrent schedule was run; source-only.

Printer startup-port failure versus asynchronous Process lifetime recheck (OD4287 strengthened, 2026-10-21): matched the `CreateNewProcTags()` call and second `CreateMsgPort()` failure branch in `Printer_Unit()` with DOS Process defaults and Exec task cleanup (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:526-544,768-851`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:115-143,555-578`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:82-163`). `NP_Synchronous` defaults FALSE, and the printer caller does not override it; a successful process creation therefore returns asynchronously. The child waits on its own `pr_MsgPort` before initialization, while parent startup-message creation failure falls through to `RemDevice()`, whose printer-unit Expunge frees the zero-open unit. No stop/reply message or child join occurs on that branch. This confirms OD4287's stranded Process and stale `tc_UserData` lifetime condition; exact scheduling and DOS segment-unload hook effects remain untested. No worker, allocation failure or expunge was run; source-only.

Printer startup-failure branch separation recheck (OD2699/OD4287 retained as distinct, 2026-10-21): reread `pd_Init()` and the startup handshake (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:403-463,526-566,768-851`) against the selected PostScript `PRS_PREINIT` rejection already traced in the printer caller audit (`:440-458`). OD2699 is the child-side path after startup-message receipt: timer.device opens successfully, `PRS_PREINIT` rejects settings, and cleanup omits `CloseDevice(&pd->pd_TIOR)` before freeing the signal and returning failure. OD4287 is the earlier parent-side startup-reply-port allocation failure: no startup message is sent, the child remains waiting on its own port, and RemDevice frees the unit. The consequences and ordering differ; neither pass establishes runtime occurrence. No startup, device open, or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

E1000 Open ring-helper unwind and finding-boundary recheck (OD3015/OD3020/OD3023 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): reread the complete selected `Open`/`Close` hooks (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000_init.c:264-443`) and both TX/RX per-ring and aggregate setup/free helpers (`e1000.c:646-824,846-920`). Each aggregate setup helper frees earlier rings when a later ring fails, and each per-ring helper releases its own allocations on its internal allocation/alignment failures. Thus OD3020 is specifically the cross-stage failure where the one selected TX ring setup succeeds and the subsequent RX ring setup fails; the Open caller does not release that successful TX ring. Confirmed OD3015's count increment precedes opener allocation and no checked Close path decrements it, and OD3023's successful shared Open path reaches `request_irq()` again with the same embedded interrupt nodes while active Close has no removal call. The module manifest selects e1000 for the x86 network targets; this pass adds helper-level boundaries to the existing findings but does not change their conditions or confidence. No allocation failure, Open/Close, interrupt, or hardware operation was run; source-only.

E1000 request-port partial-allocation failure boundary recheck (OD3033 expanded; no new ID, 2026-10-21): followed all four `REQUEST_QUEUE_COUNT` allocation iterations and the common `DeleteUnit()` cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/unit.c:1006-1023,1084-1095`; queue indices in `e1000.h:113-118`). A first-index failure leaves `WRITE_QUEUE` NULL for the unconditional `mp_Flags` write. A failure at `ADOPT_QUEUE` or `EVENT_QUEUE` makes the sticky `success` flag false, but later successful allocations are not saved to the unit's pointer array; `DeleteUnit()` therefore cannot release those MsgPorts. Expanded OD3033 to retain both consequences under the single failed-construction loop. No memory pressure, constructor or PCI enumeration was induced; source-only.

Poseidon USB-MIDI CAMD callback ABI and selected build pass (OD4301 added, 2026-10-21): compared both embedded wrapper declarations with `MidiDeviceData`'s documented register assignments and `camd.library`'s direct function-pointer calls (`compiler/include/midi/camddevices.h:41-52`; `workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:38-70`; `rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c:139-176`). The `Flags=0` rejection in OD4300 prevents CAMD's current AROS loader from invoking those callbacks; recorded OD4301 as the latent next defect if the format flag is corrected or that gate is bypassed. Traced the source into the generated relocatable `poseidonusb` object embedded by camdusbmidi.class and then written under `DEVS:Midi` for CAMD (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/mmakefile.src:7-27`; `camdusbmidi.class.c:198-210`). The class's declared CPU edges are i386, x86_64, ARM, AArch64 and PPC; its m68k static binary is a separate branch. Added OD4301. No build, CAMD port open/close, MIDI stream, or USB device was exercised. Source-only.

Poseidon USB-MIDI CAMD format-flag loader trace (OD4300 added, 2026-10-21): followed USB interface binding through creation of the embedded driver file under `DEVS:Midi` and CAMD's initialization-time directory scan (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:188-216`; `workbench/libs/camd/init.c:43-54`). The generated `MidiDeviceData.Flags` field is zero (`camd/poseidonusb.c:35-47`), while the public header says AROS supports only new format and CAMD's selected AROS loader rejects `Flags&1 == 0` before invoking Init or allocating port entries (`compiler/include/midi/camddevices.h:57-58`; `workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:240-260`). Added OD4300 for the resulting non-registration of the USB MIDI CAMD ports; this is separate from OD4301's callback register mismatch if the flag is corrected or the loader gate is bypassed. The declared non-m68k CPU aliases use the embedded relocatable object; no CAMD initialization, USB binding, or MIDI device was run. Source-only.


USB HID and Bluetooth HID LowLevel expunge rollback recheck (OD4302 added; OD3466 consequence corrected, 2026-10-21): compared both selected class `libExpunge()` implementations and installers with Exec `SetFunction()`'s return-and-replace semantics (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:95-125,469-481`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:110-145,509-520`; `rom/exec/setfunction.c:89-121`). In each class, if vector 5 is still owned but vector 22 has a competing replacement, the first restore removes that class's vector-5 hook; the second restore returns the competitor, which the mismatch branch puts back before returning FALSE. Thus vector 5 is left at its saved predecessor and vector 22 at the competing function; the class retains its non-NULL LowLevel base, so later installer calls skip and expunge remains refused. Corrected OD3466's prior claim that the second class hook remained installed; added OD4302 for the independent ROM USB HID class implementation. The USB HID module is selected by the `kernel-usb-classes` target (`rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:30-39`; `hid/mmakefile.src:4-10`). No competing patch or expunge was run; source-only.

USB printer binding failure lifecycle pass (OD4303 added, 2026-10-21): traced fresh unit insertion and worker startup/wait through `nAllocPrinter()` failure cleanup, `devOpen()` unit selection, and `devBeginIO()` write queue/signal behavior (`rom/usb/classes/printer/printer.class.c:183-259,770-851`; `rom/usb/classes/printer/dev.c:46-100,152-229`). USB printer device-vector recheck after startup-failure finding (OD4303 cross-check, 2026-10-21): reread all 465 physical lines of `rom/usb/classes/printer/dev.c` (345 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`), including init/expunge, Open/Close, BeginIO/AbortIO, device-query and TermIO. USB printer support-file and build-selection pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): read the complete `printer.h`, `printer.class.h`, `dev.h`, `common.h`, `debug.h`, `debug.c`, `mmakefile.src`, and `printer.conf` (238 C/C++ code lines across the source/header files by `cloc 2.06`, plus metadata). USB HID class binding and library lifecycle focused pass (OD3920/OD3936/OD4302 rechecked; no new OD, 2026-10-21): reread `libInit`, `libOpen`, `libClose`, `libExpunge`, `usbAttemptInterfaceBinding`, `usbForceInterfaceBinding`, and `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:38-318`) and traced the task-ready handshake into `nHidTask()`/`nAllocHid()` plus Poseidon `psdSpawnSubTask()` and `psdBorrowLocksWait()` (`poseidon.library.c:735-1015,1433-1512`). USB HID configuration-chunk failure-path and API contract pass (OD4304 added, 2026-10-21): traced class-default and per-binding HIDC/KMAP copy paths through Poseidon `psdGetCfgChunk()` and `psdWriteCfg()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:484-629`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6913-6941,7121-7153`). USB HID Wacom format-branch and synthetic-item boundary recheck (OD3921 retained; no duplicate, 2026-10-21): reread all of `nParseWacom()` and `nDetectWacom()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1599-2033`) and matched each parser branch to its synthetic item fields and the actual-length interrupt caller. PenPartner, Graphire/Graphire4, PL/PL2 and PLX check their fixed minimum lengths before field reads; Intuos/Intuos3/Cintiq still accept recognized report IDs without minimum-length checks, including ID 12 reads of bytes 5-6, confirming OD3921. `nDetectWacom()` creates at most the fixed report/collection/item set from the static product table; per-item allocation failures omit only that optional synthetic control, and its return is intentionally ignored because the caller detects setup through `nch_WacomMode`/`nch_WacomColl` (OD3921 remains the report defect). No distinct pressure-conversion contract was established from the selected source alone. No tablet or transfer was used. Source-only.

BCM2711 PCI DMA size-rounding boundary recheck (2026-10-22; no new OD): read `PCIBcm2711__Hidd_PCIDriver__AllocPCIMem()` against the public `ULONG Size` contract and the selected AArch64 mapper (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/driverclass.c:243-276`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mapglobal.c:17-28`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmu.c:305-318`). `ULONG` is 32-bit; for requests above the largest page-roundable size, the 32-bit addition in `PCIMEM_ROUND()` wraps and produces zero. `krnMMUMap()` rejects zero length, so the allocator frees `raw` and returns NULL before publishing an undersized buffer. Requests at the exact aligned upper boundary retain a 4 GiB mapped length and fail through allocation if that range is unavailable; no truncation path established. The checked-in PCI DMA caller census found no near-4-GiB request. This closes only the size-rounding candidate for the BCM2711 override; other mapping and caller contracts remain as recorded. No allocation or map was run; source-only.

No worker, allocation failure, device or playback was run; source-only.

AHI_NextAudioID missing-prior-ID sentinel and caller recheck (OD4309 added, 2026-10-22): traced `_AHI_NextAudioID()`'s absent-ID search through the MinList sentinel and the `GetTagData`/`LibFindTagItem`/`LibNextTagItem` implementation (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:282-307`; `database.h:32-40`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:35-41`; `compiler/include/utility/tagitem.h:19-25`; `compiler/arossupport/{libgettagdata,libfindtagitem,libnexttagitem}.c`). The sentinel's flexible-array tag pointer is the database's version/name tail, not a tag list. A removed ID from the documented iterator protocol makes the search call `GetTagData` on those bytes. The initial analysis established the 64-bit overread; the pointer-width recheck below extends it to 32-bit AROS as well, where the 8-byte TagItem stride reaches beyond the database object. Neither path is bounded by the tag scanner. Whole-repository `AHI_NextAudioID` call census found the selected `_AHI_BestAudioIDA` loop (`modeinfo.c:709-724`), the AHI requester (`requester.c:1317-1324`), and AHI Preferences `GetModes()` (`AHI/support.c:863-915`) pass the previous returned ID back on the next iteration; `AddAudioModes` and `ahi.device` startup use `AHI_INVALID_ID` to repeatedly query the first item and do not carry stale IDs. Confirmed selected USB Audio `nFreeAudio` removes modes during interface teardown (`usbaudio.class.c:2081-2095`). The trigger requires removal between iterator calls and another mode keeping the database alive, separating OD4309 from OD1442. No query, removal or runtime memory access was run. Source-only.


AHI_NextAudioID sentinel-width recheck (OD4309 expanded, 2026-10-22): independently laid out `AHI_AudioDatabase`, the embedded `MinList`, sentinel `MinNode`, and `TagItem` for both pointer widths. The sentinel tag pointer starts at `ahidb_Version`; the database's initialized name contributes a nonzero pseudo-tag `"base"` at byte offset 16. On 64-bit, `TagItem` stride 16 makes the next tag read start at offset 32, beyond the 21-byte version/name payload and at-most-7-byte tail padding. On 32-bit, stride 8 makes the next read start at offset 24, beyond that payload and at-most-3-byte padding. `LibNextTagItem()` has no allocation-bound check and stops only at a control tag or NULL; neither embedded pseudo-tag is `TAG_DONE`. Expanded OD4309 from 64-bit-only to both pointer widths. Existing selected caller/removal chain remains as documented; no iteration or removal was performed. Source-only.

AHI database-retirement ownership recheck (OD1442 retained, 2026-10-22): re-read `_AHI_RemoveAudioMode()`'s final-entry branch beside `LockDatabase()`, `LockDatabaseWrite()`, `UnlockDatabase()`, `ReleaseSemaphore()` and `RemSemaphore()`. The remover holds the database write semaphore while unlinking the last node, then enters local `Forbid`, releases the semaphore (which grants/signals existing waiters), removes the public semaphore node and frees the database before `Permit()`. A waiter that already completed `FindSemaphore()` retains the object pointer; single-CPU scheduling postpones it through the free, while ExecSMP `Forbid` does not block another CPU from running the granted waiter. The AHI reader and writer lookup paths still establish users of that pointer. OD1442 remains distinct from OD4309, which requires the database to survive because other modes remain and faults during the next enumeration's missing-ID scan. No semaphore operation or interleaving was run; source-only.

The table below covers the local HIDD C/C++ sources and directly used compatibility headers only; the Mesa link-library sources, generated GalliumCoreAPI files and their generators require separate inventory. `cloc 2.06` over the 17 tracked local C/header files reports 3,980 C lines and 521 header lines (4,501 total).

OD4322 covers ignored mailbox transport returns and unchecked property-tag response status on firmware frees. Imported Mesa callers and platform/firmware contracts remain open. |
