USB2OTG expunge/worker ownership recheck (OD2422 strengthened): reconciled the optional BCM2708 package and device manifest with LDDemon’s selected `LDFlush` path. LDDemon scans `DeviceList` and calls `RemDevice` for a non-busy device with zero open count; RemDevice invokes the generated expunge path. USB2OTG’s hook deletes the pool but does not stop its infinite WorkerTask or abort/wait/close the timer request embedded in the freed unit. The task can resume in unloaded module code and access the released unit; the request retains pointers into the pool. Reconfirmed `TASKTAG_AFFINITY` receives the address of the unit’s embedded `cpumask_t`, while ETask cleanup later calls `KrnFreeCPUMask` on non-sentinel masks. No USB2OTG-specific remover exists, but the generic selected memory-pressure sweep supplies an expunge trigger when the optional package is loaded and idle. No device, memory-pressure event, timer, or task removal was run; source-only.

AHIRecord sampling-size/callback-contract recheck (OD2226 boundary): compared `RecordFuncS` against the AHI hook documentation and selected driver contracts. AHI documents the hook as regular and possibly interrupt-context, and defines `AHIDB_MaxRecordSamples` as the per-callback sample-frame count (`workbench/devs/AHI/Docs/ahidev.html:640-650`; `Device/modeinfo.c:313-315`). `StartSampling` allocates its capture buffers using `max(RecordData.bufferlen, LevelFrames)`, where `LevelFrames` is the queried per-callback maximum (`AHIRecord.c:2088-2103,2113-2119`). HDAudio reports 1,024 frames and calls the hook with 1,024-frame blocks (`Drivers/HDAudio/DriverData.h:37`; `interrupt.c:150-172`), so a single valid HDAudio callback fits the remaining/new capture buffer even when it crosses the internal chunk boundary. No independent single-callback overwrite was established; OD2226 remains the multi-callback producer/saver ownership race when the saver lags across a completed-buffer reuse. No recording or runtime callback was run.

AHIRecord stop-caller/ownership follow-up (OD2387): traced the UI Stop action, audio-mode change, startup-failure unwind, and tool shutdown callers into `StopSampling` (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:1105-1155,1233-1255,1367-1377,2159-2224`). The routine delays five ticks, requests `AHIC_Record=FALSE`, tears down the level task, finishes the saver, and frees all three callback-owned capture/conversion buffers; it does not wait for an in-flight RecordFunc to retire. The AHI core forwards stop to the selected driver without a generic callback-drain step (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:969-1014`), and `AHI_FreeAudio` likewise calls the driver Stop before FreeAudio (`:702-729`). This connects AHIRecord's buffer lifetime to HDAudio OD2387's queued soft-interrupt/callback race; it does not establish an independent app finding because the concrete unsynchronized callback lifetime is in the HDAudio Stop implementation. No runtime audio was used.


Serial CMD_RESET active-write backend follow-up (OD2388): rechecked that the reset branch's local `Disable` only masks local interrupts, clears the status flag, replies `su_ActiveWrite`, and then falls through to drain queued requests; it neither nulls the active pointer nor calls HIDD Stop (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:567-648`). The selected PC HIDD enables `UART_IER_THRI` during unit construction (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:229`), and its THRI branch calls `serialunit_write_more_data` whenever the UART reports THRI (`:726-731`). The selected m68k HIDD registers a persistent TBE server that invokes the saved callback (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/serial/SerialUnitClass.c:90-105,132-139`). The serial write-empty callback consumes `su_ActiveWrite` and does not test `STATUS_WRITES_PENDING` before resuming or replying it (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:137-184`). This confirms the selected backend callback reachability after reset; no in-tree client reset sequence or hardware timing was required for the code-level state inconsistency, and no I/O was run.


AHI DSP echo lifecycle follow-up (2026-10-11): added OD136 after checking the selected defaults (`MixFreq=44100`, minimum player rate `50`, `MaxBuffSamples=882`) and choosing public delay `0x3ffffc8e`; the sum reaches `0x40000000` and the four-byte sample-size product wraps to zero, while the destination offset becomes `0xfffff238`. Added OD137 after tracing both echo replacement through `update_DSPEcho` and active-effect teardown through `_AHI_FreeAudio`; neither path frees all separately allocated echo state. Added OD1577 for the SMP cancel/mix pointer interleaving; checked the always-listed Void worker plus `AHIS_UNKNOWN` fallback, and verified its active loop invokes the AHI mixer. SimplePlay sets effects during playback but cancels after Stop, so it does not prove the cancellation race; that trigger remains available to public callers. No audio was run.


VirtIO read-only status follow-up (OD2460): `virtio_controllerclass.c:85-100` negotiates `VIRTIO_BLK_F_RO`; `virtio_hw.c:282` stores the negotiated bit in `dev_ReadOnly`; `virtio_io.c:43-46` rejects writes while read-only, but `BeginIO` returns `io_Actual=0` for every `TD_PROTSTATUS` (`:195-199`). AFS `diskWritable` and SFS `writeprotection` both treat zero as writable (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:427-432`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:103-116`). Added OD2460 for selected x86 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V VirtIO builds when RO is offered. No I/O was run.


VirtIO `TD_PROTSTATUS` convention recheck (OD2460): compared its zero return with selected AROS block-device implementations and both named filesystem consumers. Hostdisk returns boolean `UNIT_READONLY`, FDisk returns `!unit->writable`, and DiskImage returns its `WriteProtect` flag; generic trackdisk forwards its cached hardware protection status (`arch/all-hosted/devs/hostdisk/hostdisk_device.c:621-624`; `workbench/devs/fdsk_device.c:619-622`; `workbench/devs/diskimage/device/{io.c:127-130,unit.c:374-377}`; `rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:518-521`). AFS and SFS both treat zero as writable (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:427-432`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:103-116`). VirtIO's `dev_ReadOnly` is already checked to reject writes, while its status branch still returns zero. This corroborates OD2460's result convention and the conditional filesystem behavior; no additional candidate was needed. No block device was queried.


VirtIO read-only filesystem-caller extension (OD2460): added PFS3 to the selected caller trace. `GetCurrentRoot` sets `g->diskstate = ID_VALIDATED` for zero `TD_PROTSTATUS` (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/volume.c:1026-1037`); later PFS3 rejects writes only for `ID_WRITE_PROTECTED` (`:861-873`) and omits write-protected protection flags for the root entry when `g->diskstate` is wrong (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/directory.c:851-854`). This confirms the VirtIO mismatch can also suppress PFS3's read-only state. The same caller census found a separate USB MassStorage status defect, recorded in disk scope as DISK-323: `cmd_ProtStatus` reports protection only for CD-ROM device type, although SCSI MODE SENSE defines a WP bit for direct-access media (`storage_device.c:94-97`; T10 SBC-3 §6.3.1). The driver does not query or cache that state and its write path returns `TDERR_NotSpecified` after reset/retry (`:244-292,300-349`); this remains separate from VirtIO OD2460 because it is an independent class implementation outside this report’s device-driver scope; see DISK-323 in the disk report. No filesystem mount or USB device was run.

RISC-V DesignWare UART failed-handler registration (OD2464; historical candidate OD1562): verified `KrnAddIRQHandler` returns NULL for invalid source IDs or failed `IntrNode` allocation and only unmasks/link-installs a source after allocation. The unit constructor ignores that result and returns its OOP object; serial.device publishes the unit after its nonnull check. A positive, accepted DT IRQ with registration failure therefore produces a successful open without receive or write-completion interrupts. The selected driver's IRQ-zero branch remains an intentional write-only port. No hardware or allocation failure was run.

OpenSBI DesignWare UART no-IRQ write-progress follow-up (OD2465): traced FDT's absent/short interrupt property to port admission, the explicit `irq == 0` constructor branch, `HIDD_SerialUnit_Write`, serial.device's active-write bookkeeping, and the only automatic remainder/reply callback. With no registered handler or polling loop, a short HIDD write remains active and receives no automatic completion callback; the only non-interrupt callback route requires an explicit Stop/Start sequence and makes one refill attempt. Kept separate from OD2464, which requires a positive IRQ whose handler registration fails. Build selection is split: OpenSBI BSP packages dwuart, while the general Workbench graph selects serial.device (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:103-112`; `workbench/devs/serial/mmakefile.src:8-13`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:9-18`); the finding requires the module installed alongside the BSP HIDD. No UART or I/O was run.

Input first-consumer handoff recheck (OD2331): verified `Input__Root__New` protects ADDTAIL/replay/reset with `Disable`, while `InputHW__CallBackFunc` can buffer events from an interrupt callback and the pending count/buffer have no shared spinlock. Exec explicitly limits Disable to the current processor on SMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), confirming that it does not serialize a callback on another CPU. `input.device` creates its event task without an affinity tag (`rom/devs/input/input.c:68-72`); `NewCreateTaskA` forwards the current task as parent, and `Exec_InitETask` inherits the parent mask or pins to the creation CPU when the parent has none (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:253-260`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:265-273`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:101-165`). That task opens `keyboard.device`, which registers the first HIDD consumer (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:183-194`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:197-211`). Traced PC startup ordering: `kernel.post` priority 115 runs before the input device resident priority 30 (`arch/all-pc/kernel/platform_post.c:98-123`; `rom/devs/input/input.conf`); `smp_Initialize` calls `cpu_PrepareExec`, which pins the bootstrap task to CPU0 before setting `EXECF_CPUAffinity` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:321-339`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:28-60`). The event task therefore inherits CPU0 while registering the consumer, matching the IOAPIC legacy default CPU0 (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_ioapic.c:408-438`); no selected affinity change before registration was found. The selected PC route does not establish a cross-CPU schedule, so OD2331 remains conditional on another producer/construction path or external caller. No event or interleaving was run.

NVMe DOS geometry duplicate review (2026-10-11): merged the full-namespace `DE_HIGHCYL` versus selected `au_High` evidence into OD2459, which already covers the raw LBA copied to `DE_LOWCYL`; removed duplicate OD2472. OD2458 was withdrawn: the per-namespace `lbaStart = 0` assignment at `nvme_busclass.c:499-502` covers both fallback paths; returned-range bound validation remains pending. No device or filesystem request was run.
NVMe lower-bound validation follow-up (OD2474): traced startup `slba` into `au_Low` and the `nvme_sector_rw` transfer check; the check uses only `au_High`, so aligned requests below a nonzero selected range can pass. This is an inferred direct-I/O boundary defect; no device or I/O was run.

NVMe LBA Range Type array follow-up (OD2473): `nvme_queue_admin.c` preserves completion Dword 0 in `ceh_Result`, while `NVMEBus_Start` casts the data page to one `nvme_lba_range_type` and consults only entry zero. The NVMe Base Specification 1.4c completion count and multi-entry structure confirm that valid responses can contain more than one range (Figures 281–282). Later ranges/attributes are not represented by the single published unit. No controller response was run.

NVMe BeginIO dispatcher pass (2026-10-11): read the complete `nvme_io.c` dispatch and completion handoff (`:200-428`) against all command cases. Confirmed the advertised command array is zero-terminated and includes the implemented read/write, seek, geometry, query, update and status cases; output-length checks precede the `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY`/`TD_GETGEOMETRY` writes. `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` intentionally remains pending on non-quick requests and `TD_REMCHANGEINT` completes immediately, matching the analogous selected VirtIO/AHCI dispatch shape; no NVMe hotplug/media-change producer was established in the checked unit lifecycle, so no distinct candidate is promoted from that branch. The existing unsupported `AbortIO` finding remains OD2362. No I/O was run.

AHCI change-notification lifecycle recheck (OD2866): traced NTFS `SendIO(TD_ADDCHANGEINT)` and later `DoIO(TD_REMCHANGEINT)` on the same request through AHCI `BeginIO`, `sim_IOs`, and `ahci_PortMonitor`. Because every incoming command is first `AddHead`ed, removal reinserts the still-pending listener node; Exec list primitives do not detect or unlink existing membership. AHCI then removes once and reports completion, after which the NTFS client frees the request. The monitor later traverses the dangling list. The NTFS target is selected by the full Workbench aggregate (`workbench/fs/ntfs/mmakefile.src:3-15`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:9-17`); no interrupt or media-change event was exercised.

AHCI CAM unit-construction failure pass (OD2477): traced the successful identify path through GOOD-state publication, `OOP_NewObject`, `ahci_cam_attach`, and the bus EnumUnits callback. A null unit object is silently ignored and the probe still returns zero; the bus remains without `ab_Unit`, so storage enumeration sees no unit and the usual same-state scan has no retry trigger. No OOP allocation failure or hardware probe was run.

AHCI monitor task-lifetime recheck (OD2478): traced the early parent-ready signal, timer/port/request startup failures, monitor cleanup, default `TaskExitCode`/`RemTask`, service-task MemEntry reclamation and CAM-probe-failure detach. `sim_Monitor` remains non-NULL after child exit; teardown can signal it after reclamation. This is separate from DISK-113, whose trigger is NewCreateTask returning NULL before the task starts. Trigger also requires a probe failure and the reclaim-before-detach ordering; no task or allocation failure was run.

NVMe/VirtIO DOS mount-registration follow-up (OD2479): traced both `MakeDosNode` results and both `AddBootNode` calls through the bus-start return and storage-controller registration path. A NULL `MakeDosNode` result skips publication but is ignored, so the HIDD unit/bus still succeeds without a DOS entry. If node construction succeeds but `AddBootNode` returns FALSE for a duplicate, boot-node allocation failure or DOS-list insertion failure, the result is also discarded and the untransferred DeviceNode allocation leaks. No allocation or DOS registration failure was induced.

NVMe bus-constructor allocation follow-up (OD2480): traced Model/Serial/Revision tags from Identify Controller through `HW_AddDriver` into `NVMEBus__Root__New`. All three selected tags are non-NULL; each destination `AllocVec` is followed by `CopyMem` without a null check. This is separate from the existing unchecked unit-pointer-array allocation. No allocation failure was induced.

NVMe bus-removal scope check: generic HW exposes `HW_RemoveDriver`, but the NVMe storage-controller `RemoveBus` method explicitly returns FALSE with a TODO that unloading is unsupported (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:582-591`). The device module is configured `noexpunge` (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme.conf:1-8`), and no selected in-tree caller removing its PCI driver was found. Therefore the fact that bus/unit objects are not disposed on ordinary system lifetime is not promoted as a finding; partial-start cleanup remains a separate open path. No device removal was run.

E1000 unit lifecycle follow-up (OD2432/OD2433; adjacent cleanup checks): reread `CreateUnit`, its PCI enumeration caller, `Open`, module expunge and `DeleteUnit` (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/unit.c:703-1112`; `e1000_init.c:120-151,222-240,265-420`). PCI enumeration continues after a failed matching adapter, and `Open` resolves an exact unit number, confirming OD2432's observable gap when a later adapter succeeds. Both early allocation returns and late `DeleteUnit` cleanup fail to restore that assigned number; the unsupported-device branch is the only explicit rollback. `e1ku_hw_stats` is independently allocated and has no release in `DeleteUnit`, confirming OD2433 on both late setup failure and successful module expunge. The same function maps `flash_address`, but the selected generic PCIDriver `MapPCI` is a direct-bus address translation and its `UnmapPCI` is explicitly a no-op, so the absent flash unmap is not a separately established resource leak on the selected x86 targets. `CreateUnit` also opens an embedded `timer.device` request without a matching close; timer.device is configured `noexpunge`, and its selected Open vector only stores the device/unit in the request, so this does not demonstrate another current resource or unload failure. No PCI enumeration, allocation failure, unit open or expunge was run.


USB hub rescan-timer teardown recheck (OD2468): distinguished the unconditional cleanup leak from the narrower stale-task signal. `hub_process` creates/opens local `rescan` at startup and `USBCreateTimer` owns a port, IORequest and timer.device open (`usbhubclass.c:608-615`; `misc.c:143-162`). The only cleanup call is `USBDeleteTimer(hub->tr)` (`usbhubclass.c:657-661`), so any successful `rescan` creation is leaked on hub disposal even if no retry was scheduled. The additional stale `mp_SigTask` path still requires disposal before an armed retry completes; `USBTimerDone` clears the reply task only after it receives that completion (`misc.c:163-172`). No timer or hub was run.

ACPICA MCFG ECAM offset recheck (OD2483): traced `find_pci` selection through both read and write callbacks. The MCFG allocation base is for `StartBusNumber`, but the OSL offset uses the absolute bus; the selected OpenSBI PCIDT path subtracts `busStart`. The shared ACPICA OSL is selected in the i386-PC, x86-64-PC and RISC-V OpenSBI package graphs; upstream ACPICA source/call sites are external and absent, so invocation remains a condition rather than a traced caller. No PCI access was run.

Other Drivers finding-boundary recheck: OD2252 and OD2334 were duplicate descriptions of the same i8042 mouse timer request/port leak. Consolidated the extra reset-handler timer-use check into OD2334 and withdrew OD2252; no separate failure mode or resource owner distinguished the entries.

Other Drivers finding-boundary recheck: former ID OD2121 duplicated HDAudio finding OD2157, and former ID OD2367 duplicated NVMe startup-leak finding OD2380; both duplicates were removed and their distinct details merged into the retained entries. The EHCI file-table reference to OD2484 was stale: source review confirms a distinct conditional controller reset before unconditional failed INITLIB, now tracked as OD2484 with the selected-backend limitation stated. The serial CMD_RESET reference previously pointed to NVMe OD2380 by mistake and now points to serial OD2402.

2026-10-11 report-detail integrity recheck: restored missing detailed entries OD1198 (UHCI delay signal exhaustion), OD1463 (m68k boot card tuple truncation), OD1519 (PCITool vendor-index bounds/search), OD1609 (USBHub null interrupt pipe), and OD851 (hosted PCI descriptor close). OD1608's replacement-tail issue is already detailed as OD2442, and stale OD1608 references were corrected. OD1604 report-detail reconciliation (2026-10-11): restored the standalone entry after confirming `ohci_CreateTimer`'s NULL returns reach `ohci_Delay` from the selected OHCI constructor startup sequence. The finding is conditional on an enumerated controller and timer-request setup failure; no device was run.

Printer flush/AbortIO follow-up (OD57; rechecked as OD2488 during candidate reconciliation): traced both persistent printer IORequests through `CMD_FLUSH`, `WaitIOStd`/Exec `WaitIO`, and the serial/parallel AbortIO vectors. Completed reply nodes are removed by WaitIO and marked idle by the wrapper; the abort vectors then call raw `Remove` for every non-active-read request, although Exec Remove dereferences links without membership validation. The report now restores OD57 with the in-tree idle-request trigger and the separate partial-active-write path. No I/O was run.

Parallel HIDD initialization-result reconciliation (OD3227, former OD2489/OD80): traced native m68k `OpenResource("ciaa.resource")` failure through false `ParallelUnit::Init`, the ignored return in parallel.device Open, and the unit publication path. With no callback registration, a multi-byte write can retain an unserviceable remainder and queued reads have no receive producer. Envy24/Envy24HT deferred-record callback recheck (OD2490): traced each selected hard interrupt’s buffer-pointer publication and `Cause` call through Exec’s shared softint queue/dispatcher and each recording callback to its final buffer access and sampler hook. Both Stop methods mask the device and free the backing DMA buffers without removing or joining queued/running callbacks; Envy24HT’s `Delay(1)` is not a completion check. AHI `AHIC_Record = FALSE` reaches those Stop methods synchronously. The trigger is limited here to active record teardown overlapping deferred work on ExecSMP; no audio device or interleaving was exercised. This restores the prior orphaned OD2490 tracker lead as detailed OD2490.

Envy24 DriverInit failure-path recheck (OD2134 withdrawn; OD2142, OD2491, OD2492): checked AHI creation/cleanup against all return paths. AHI `CreateAudioCtrl` invokes `_AHIsub_AllocAudio`; both Envy24 and Envy24HT test the selected `driverdatas` slot and return `AHISF_ERROR` before `AHI_GetAudioAttrsA` dispatches `_AHIsub_GetAttr`. The Envy24HT `AHIDB_Frequencies` dereference and Envy24 `AHIDB_Inputs` dereference therefore lack a public caller after card-allocation failure, and both `FreeDriverData` helpers tolerate a NULL card. Withdraw OD2134 and remove its detailed entry. Separately, a failed `driverdatas` array allocation still returns FALSE with `cards_found > 0`, and common failure expunge indexes that NULL array before calling the per-card null check (OD2142, extended to both variants). Envy24 also has unchecked vendor-table/temporary-node allocations (OD2491) and never releases the successfully allocated global table on cleanup (OD2492). No allocation failure, driver load or hardware was exercised.


RP1 MSI-failure consumer recheck (OD928 disposition, 2026-10-11): traced `setup_msi`'s failed ObtainVectors return into `PCIRP1_Init`. USB INTIDs remain at the zero-initialized base values when vector acquisition fails, and each xHCI synthetic function is rejected by `!irq[i]` before `cfg_init`; if neither passes, `HW_AddHardwareDriver` is not called (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/rp1/rp1_init.c:120-141,177-212`; `rp1_pci.c:241-275`). Latest Other Drivers recheck: completed a reachability pass for USB worker event dispatch. Latest Other Drivers report update: reconciled CMI8738 `driver-init.c` against common AHI failed-init cleanup. RP1 registration rollback follow-up (OD929): a source-ordered cross-module pass confirmed that `RP1_Init` runs at resource priority 80 before `pcirp1.hidd` priority 70, obtains a 64-vector MSI-X allocation, and enables the two RP1 interrupt routes before publishing the resource. If `PCIRP1_Init` subsequently fails root/object/driver registration, `HIDD_PCI_AddHardwareDriver` discards the failure and the noexpunge module returns success; no call releases the endpoint's vectors. The 64 bridge `msi_used` bits remain occupied for the session along with the missing USB controller publication. The RP1 report row and OD929 now include this secondary resource-loss consequence. RP1 registration finding ID correction (2026-10-15): the preceding ledger references to OD929 are stale/misassigned; OD929 in the current detailed report is the unrelated AMCC440 EMAC DMA-allocation finding. ACPI fan `_FPS` telemetry bounds recheck (OD1746): compared the selected recursive integer walk with the ACPI 6.4 `_FPS` package schema. The walker includes outer Revision and all five fields in each P-state package; NoiseLevel and Power can each legally be 0xFFFFFFFF for unpopulated values. The stored extrema become the RPM telemetry bounds and the selected UI displays them; a valid sentinel therefore reaches the public max as signed -1. OD1746 is restored as a detailed report finding; no firmware was queried.

Generic I²C device-method reconciliation: promoted the existing OD849 `WriteWord` candidate into a detailed entry after confirming the three-byte subaddress/value buffer is passed to `I2C_WriteRead` with length two. This adds detail for an already tracked candidate and does not change the aggregate active-candidate count.

Generic I²C transaction-lock follow-up: expanded OD1152 after comparing device-level `WriteBytes`/`WriteVec` with bus-level `WriteRead`. The former release the per-instance semaphore between Address/PutByte/Stop calls; the latter holds it across the full transfer. Sam440 is the selected physical bit-bang backend, but its checked-in battery-clock clients use WriteRead; no transfer or race was run.


Serial `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` failure recheck (OD58): followed the selected PC HIDD tag loop with `serial.device`'s exact `{TAG_DATALENGTH, TAG_STOP_BITS, TAG_SKIP}` list. `SetParameters` stores a valid data length before validating stop bits and returns FALSE without writing UART_LCR if the latter is invalid (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:364-425`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:789-804`). PC serial-unit bounds recheck (OD2509): compared the class-local `bases[]` and `CSD(...)->units[]` extents with the accepted index condition and traced construction through the public unit-class ID and Root.New method declaration. The normal parent NewUnit validates only 0–3, but direct Root.New accepts 4 and subsequently indexes both four-entry arrays with it before issuing UART I/O. Card-resource timer follow-up (2026-10-11): traced the selected `CardTask` timer request through m68k Amiga timer.device's `UNIT_MICROHZ` `TR_ADDREQUEST` queue and completion interrupt. After successful OpenDevice, serial requests use the same request and the valid timer path replies with `io_Error=0`; no abort or concurrent resubmission is present. m68k timer startup dependency check (2026-10-11): `arch/m68k-amiga/timer/timer_init.c` dereferences the result of `TaggedOpenLibrary(TAGGEDOPEN_GRAPHICS)`. Kept this as an explicit pending initialization-order check; no finding promoted on an unresolved premise.


m68k timer startup dependency resolved (2026-10-11): graphics.library (resident priority 65) precedes timer.device (priority 50), but the selected `InitCode` ignores an `InitResident` failure and keeps traversing. Graphics `GfxInit` returns FALSE on hash-table allocation failure, generated initialization unwinds without publishing the base, `TaggedOpenLibrary` then returns NULL, and m68k timer init dereferences it at `InitCustom`/DisplayFlags. Unix timer option recheck (2026-10-11): reconciled the stale OD1417 inventory reference with the current detailed report. The selected timer parser stores positive `vblank` input in an 8-bit ExecBase field and multiplies it by an unchecked 32-bit tickrate; `vblank=256` or `vblank=128 tickrate=33554432` makes the rate zero before the interval division. Added OD2515. No host timer or boot-option case was run.


NVMe partial-start cleanup/result recheck (2026-10-11): traced every FALSE return in Hidd_NVMEBus_Start against the namespace-unit loop and found those returns occur before any unit is constructed; no separate unit-disposal-on-FALSE defect was established. However, the sole configured I/O queue failure branches do not return FALSE, leave queuecnt zero, skip all namespace construction, and still return TRUE; the storage controller retains that empty bus. Added OD2525 for this distinct false-success/missing-units result, separate from OD2453's Create SQ resource leak. Other Drivers detailed count: 514; aggregate active candidates: 2,600; withdrawn: 32. No controller was started; source-only.


NVMe queue allocator/free audit (2026-10-11): added the previously missing nvme_queue.c body to the per-file coverage ledger after reading the complete allocator and every caller. Staged allocation failures unwind local arrays and DMA buffers through the zero-initialized common free helper; fixed selected depths are positive. Hardware/worker teardown remains separately tracked under OD2360/OD2453, and OD2525 covers the caller-level false-success result. No new candidate added; counts unchanged at 514 Other Drivers findings, 2,600 aggregate active candidates, and 32 withdrawn. Source-only.


NVMe Expansion-open consequence recheck (2026-10-11): extended OD2371 after tracing its default-initialized unit through storage-controller retention, EnumUnits/Open, and BeginIO. When Expansion open fails, a unit still enters ab_Units with au_Bus left NULL; the first READ/WRITE dereferences that pointer in nvme_sector_rw before its length checks. This is a concrete task-fault consequence of OD2371, not a separate candidate. No library failure or I/O was induced; counts unchanged.


NVMe request-dispatch caller recheck (2026-10-11): traced BeginIO offset assembly for legacy and TD64 commands, the standard FAT/NTFS zero-length TD64 probe, geometry/device-query output bounds and quick/non-quick completion. The zero-length probe treats any result except IOERR_NOCMD as TD64 support, so nvme_sector_rw's IOERR_BADLENGTH is intentional. Existing OD2474 and OD2481/OD2482 cover the lower-range and namespace-range boundaries; no additional request-validation candidate was established. OD2371 was sharpened separately to the null-bus dereference before request validation. Counts unchanged; no request was run.


RTL816x SANA-II query capacity recheck (2026-10-11): traced `CmdS2DeviceQuery` through direct dispatch and the maintained AROSTCP query caller. The handler caps its initial copy but writes five result fields unconditionally, so a caller advertising only the four-byte `SizeAvailable` prefix is overrun. AROSTCP supplies the full structure; the short-buffer trigger remains public-client conditional. Added OD2526. The x86 network aggregate selects the driver targets on i386/x86_64. Other Drivers now has 515 detailed findings; aggregate active candidates are 2,602, with 32 withdrawn. No request was issued; source-only.


RTL816x Open rollback recheck (2026-10-11): traced the first opener's flags/count through startup errors and the RTL816x descriptor/ring/IRQ failure returns. A failed non-MINE opener leaves `IFF_SHARED` set when rolling the count back to zero; a later MINE open and subsequent non-MINE open are then both accepted. Added OD2527. No failure or open sequence was exercised. Other Drivers now has 516 detailed findings; aggregate active candidates are 2,603, with 32 withdrawn. Source-only.


RTL816x RX/list lifetime comparison (2026-10-11): cross-checked its PCI interrupt route and ISR list walks against the earlier IntelPro100 OD2228 analysis. RTL816x's IRQ callback traverses opener, multicast-range and type-tracker nodes while Open/Close and SANA-II handlers mutate/free them under local Disable only; the selected x86_64 route can deliver the IRQ on CPU0 while another task runs elsewhere. Expanded OD2228 to cover this second selected driver. No new finding ID; counts unchanged at 516 Other Drivers findings and 2,603 aggregate active candidates, with 32 withdrawn. No IRQ or list race was run. Source-only.


RTL816x queued AbortIO ownership recheck (2026-10-11): traced BeginIO queue publication through worker `GetMsg`/`ObtainSemaphore` and AbortIO's `NT_MESSAGE`/`Remove` predicate. Exec RemHead leaves the node type unchanged, so AbortIO can reply a request already detached but still owned by the waiting worker; added OD2528. The same review reconciled RTL816x's post-ReplyMsg unit-pointer dereference with OD598 (formerly the old OD443 cross-reference); the existing finding now names both EMAC and RTL816x. Counts: 517 detailed Other Drivers findings and 2,604 aggregate active candidates, with 32 withdrawn. No request interleaving was run. Source-only.

Network unit-number cross-check (2026-10-11): expanded OD2432 from e1000 to include RTL8139 and LPe32002 after tracing counter reservation, failed-construction cleanup, PCI callback iteration and each driver's exact-number Open lookup. Their failed probes can leave unit gaps, while RTL816x has the additional `MAX_UNITS` cutoff tracked separately as OD2529. Cross-checked the corresponding constructor and entrypoint rows; no allocation or PCI failure was induced. Counts unchanged.

RTL8139/LPe32002 final-close state follow-up (2026-10-11): promoted RTL8139 candidate 245 to OD2530 and confirmed the same `IFF_SHARED` persistence in LPe32002. Traced close count decrement, unit-sharing admission after reopen, AROSTCP flags-zero opening, and RTL8139 receive-mode setup; its stale `IFF_PROMISC` maps to `AcceptAllPhys`. SiS900 Open/Close recheck (2026-10-11): added OD2531 after following a rejected exclusive Open through its in-driver `CloseDevice` cleanup. The failed request increments `sis900u_open_count`; its Close stops the shared NIC and reports OFFLINE, while no Close path decrements the count. Selected AROSTCP opens with flags zero and establishes the shared-open state. No request sequence or hardware was run.

RTL8139/SiS900 Open-size cleanup recheck (2026-10-11): added OD2532 after following each short-length Open rejection to its explicit `CloseDevice` call. Both leave `io_Unit` null until after the size check; Exec still dispatches Close based on `io_Device`, and each selected Close path dereferences the null unit. This remains a malformed public-request trigger; no short request was issued.

SiS900 ring ownership follow-up (2026-10-11): added OD2533 after tracing descriptor-ring allocations in CreateUnit, per-slot buffer allocations in every `sis900func_open`, and both final Close and Expunge cleanup. Repeated accepted Opens overwrite the buffer-pointer arrays without freeing prior buffers; DeleteUnit frees neither ring nor current buffers. No allocation or lifecycle sequence was run.

SiS900 unit-number cross-check (2026-10-11): expanded OD2432 to include SiS900 after tracing its pre-initialization `sis900b_UnitCount++`, every failed CreateUnit return/cleanup, per-ProductID PCI callback, and exact-number Open lookup. The count is never rolled back, so a failed supported adapter followed by a working one can leave conventional unit 0 unpublished. Counts unchanged. No PCI probe or failure was induced.

CharMap selection caller pass (2026-10-11): added OD2543 after tracing mouse press/release state into `charmapcon_copy` and the console task's Right-Command+C path. Starting a click-only replacement selection sets `select_line_min` and equal coordinates but leaves `select_line_max` from the prior selection; Copy does not gate on active/nonempty selection and uses that stale node. This pass also rechecked the inherited `CONU_SNIPMAP` class dispatch. External class/API callers and runtime behavior remain open; no sequence was run.

Console task registration-result check (2026-10-12): followed `consoleTaskEntry`'s unchecked `DoIO(IND_ADDHANDLER)` into selected `input.device`. BeginIO accepts the command as nonquick and queues it; the input worker unconditionally enqueues the supplied handler and replies. Once the device open and handler/port allocations succeed, no selected registration-error branch supports a separate candidate. The preexisting failed-open/allocation `Alert` path remains nonreturning, and CTRL-C cleanup remains OD1652. No input event or task was run.

ACPICA SCI registration failure follow-up (2026-10-12): added OD2544 after following `AcpiOsInstallInterruptHandler` through the selected PC `AddIntServer` and `KrnAddIRQHandler` routes. Wrapper allocation can succeed before the PC kernel IRQ-node allocation fails; `AddIntServer` returns void, so ACPICA still publishes the handler and returns `AE_OK`. A later remove forwards the null token into the existing EK815 defect. The ACPICA shared library is in i386-PC and x86-64-PC boot manifests. This is separate from OD1005's later power-button notification registration. No IRQ allocation failure or callback was run.
PC timer distant-deadline recheck (2026-10-12): resolved the earlier Timer0Setup interval-domain question as OD2545. A fresh/short-uptime PC can accept a representable `UNIT_MICROHZ` delay at or above `0x80000000` seconds without elapsed-time wrap; `Timer0Setup` then mistakes the positive unsigned delta for overdue, reloads the PIT at its two-count minimum, and repeats this after each timer IRQ while the request remains pending. The 32-bit signed `LONG`, unsigned timeval field, no smaller public maximum, IRQ handler and reload rate are traced to source. The approximately 68-year trigger is retained explicitly. Updated the detailed finding count from 533 to 534; no request or interrupt was run.
Timer AbortIO rearm and completion recheck (2026-10-12): traced `rom/timer/abortio.c` through list ordering and selected hardware schedulers. Removing the earliest deadline cannot delay the next live deadline because it is no earlier than the removed head; the PC's recurring internal `UNIT_MICROHZ` VBlank request also keeps `Timer0Setup` polling the queues at a 20 ms base cadence (`arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c:34-60,135-142,202-210`). Completion and abort serialize on the timer list write lock in the selected SMP path. No separate missed-deadline or unlink race established. The previously tracked OD1416 invalid Remove remains the unsupported accepted-EClock-request case; wider direct-client states remain open. No request was aborted; source-only.
Unix zero-rate caller recheck (2026-10-12): traced the hosted timer's option parser after comparing it with the Raspberry Pi zero-EClock finding. Explicit `vblank=0` and `tickrate=0` also reach the already-documented division by zero in OD2515; they are not a separate candidate from the positive narrowing/product-overflow cases. The Unix timer is selected by its active link target and embedded in `AROSBootstrap.conf`. No boot arguments were supplied; counts unchanged.
Unix timer high-rate interval follow-up (2026-10-12): expanded OD2515 after tracing the selected Linux-hosted timer's `it_value` construction. Valid positive boot options `vblank=255 tickrate=3922` produce 1,000,110 Hz, which integer-divides to a zero microsecond interval; Linux `setitimer` disarms `ITIMER_REAL` for a zero `it_value`, yet the init hook returns success. The consequence is loss of all SIGALRM-driven timekeeping, MICROHZ completion and VBlank delivery. Folded into OD2515 because the same unchecked option/rate conversion needs validation. No boot option was used; finding count unchanged.
MinGW timer rate-domain follow-up (2026-10-12): reconciled the old OD1420 ledger reference with the current detailed findings and added OD2546. The selected timer parser accepts `eclock=0`, which divides by zero when calculating its reported interval; `eclock=1001` reaches the host kernel's whole-millisecond `1000 / TimerHz` calculation as a zero period. Windows documents zero `lPeriod` as one-shot, and this timer has no subsequent StartClock call, so periodic EClock updates stop after at most one signal. The MinGW board package selects `timer` and bootloader arguments. OD1878 remains the separate non-divisor-rate time conversion mismatch; no host timer was started.
AHIRecord fixed-predictor accumulator bound recheck (2026-10-12; no new candidate): traced the selected encoder setup and buffer caller into `FLAC__fixed_compute_best_predictor` (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:2945-2955,3008-3011`; `FLAC/stream_encoder.c:135-145,677-690,904-905,1481-1500,3214-3222`; `FLAC/fixed.c:213-254`). AHIRecord sets 16 bits/sample and never sets a custom block size; compression levels 0–2 use 1,152 samples and levels 3–8 use 4,096. At 16-bit input, the fourth finite difference is bounded by 16 times the maximum sample magnitude; even 4,096 samples keep its unsigned sum below `UINT32_MAX`, so the narrow accumulator does not overflow on this maintained caller. Standalone users of the bundled FLAC encoder can choose larger blocks and remain outside this caller check; no encoder was run.
MinGW timer rate-input boundary recheck (2026-10-12; OD2546, trigger widened): `tb_eclock_rate` is `ULONG`, while `atoi` returns signed `int` (`rom/timer/timer_intern.h:64`; `timer_init.c:93-95`). Thus an unparseable argument becomes zero and takes the already-documented divide-by-zero path; a negative parsed value converts to a large unsigned rate and reaches host `StartClock` with a zero-millisecond period. This is the same unvalidated-setting defect and one-shot consequence as the >1,000 Hz case, not a separate finding. No command-line argument was supplied to a running target.
HID interrupt-report length/caller recheck (2026-10-12; no new candidate): followed the selected `HidInterrupt` path through `HIDD_USBDrv_AddInterrupt` and the HID base, mouse, and keyboard `ParseReport` implementations (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:65-83,288-316`; `hidclass.c:167-178`; `mouseclass.c:43-55`; `kbdclass.c:99-116`). For report-ID devices the callback advances the pointer by one byte but passes the original buffer length; however, the selected mouse and keyboard overrides ignore the length field and extract from the original allocation, while the base implementation only prints that many bytes when its report ID is unknown. Thus this mismatch did not establish an overread in selected consumers and is not added as a finding. DMA callback invalidation remains limited to the allocated `hid->buflen`. No USB device or report was exercised.
AHIRecord FLAC metadata-length writer/validator review (2026-10-12; candidate withdrawn): checked the oversized PADDING and adjusted Vorbis-comment length behavior. Although the writer can truncate a >24-bit block length, the only selected target compiling this FLAC code is AHIRecord and no in-tree caller invokes `FLAC__stream_encoder_set_metadata`; no selected project path supplies custom metadata. Retain this as an API robustness observation, not an active project finding. No stream was generated.
AHIRecord FLAC APPLICATION minimum-length review (2026-10-12; candidate withdrawn): a 0–3 byte APPLICATION metadata length would underflow the framing writer's unsigned `length - 4`, but the only selected target compiling this FLAC code is AHIRecord and no in-tree caller invokes `FLAC__stream_encoder_set_metadata`. This malformed-object case is not included as an active project finding. No malformed metadata was supplied.
AHIRecord FLAC metadata callback/error-path pass (2026-10-12; no new candidate): traced metadata serialization through `write_bitbuffer_` and `write_frame_`. Bitwriter allocation failure, verify-decoder rejection, and client write-callback errors return failure and set encoder state; the init caller stops at the failing block, and accumulated bitwriter data is released on callback failure. The complete repository caller census found no `FLAC__stream_encoder_set_metadata` call; `mmakefile.src` compiles the FLAC sources only into AHIRecord. No callback failure or stream was run.
Netinfo `NI_MEMBERS` buffer-capacity recheck (2026-10-12; OD1901): traced `initgroups`' 1,024-byte `ug_OpenUnit` buffer into `groups[0] = basegroup` and `io_Data = groups + 1`, with the original 1,024-byte `io_Length` retained. `GetGroups` therefore writes up to 256 four-byte GIDs through a 1,020-byte remaining allocation; the final element is one LONG out of bounds. Its `io_Actual` makes `initgroups` iterate through that same out-of-bounds element before its NGROUPS clamp. The loader's per-record length limit does not cap record count, so 256 short valid membership records fit. The installed default data has fewer matching memberships; no file was changed or `initgroups` call made.

Hosted Ethernet/TAP query-buffer recheck (OD2221): checked `Sana2DeviceQuery` layout, the maintained AROSTCP full-size request, Bluetooth PAN's short-size rejection, and the Unix Ethernet/TAP handler manifests. The candidate is specifically public-client conditional: both hosted handlers copy the full structure without reading `SizeAvailable`; no short request was issued. Source-only.

Hosted NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY completion cross-check (OD2250): expanded the existing serial/parallel finding after tracing the hosted Ethernet/TAP validation branches through their shared reply gates and the active Linux desktop target edge. `DoIO` retains the quick bit and returns the validation error; the no-reply case is limited to nonquick `SendIO` requests. No asynchronous query caller or request was found in-tree.

HID report-ID length cross-check (no new candidate): `HidInterrupt` passes `hid->buflen` while pointing at `buffer + 1` for numbered reports (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:74-82`). Rechecked all selected `ParseReport` implementations: the HID base method uses its own buffer/size, while keyboard and mouse implementations read descriptor-derived locations and do not consume `msg->report_length` (`hidclass.c:167-184`; `kbdclass.c:99-118`; `mouseclass.c:45-84`). The one-byte surplus length therefore does not independently establish an overread in the selected callbacks. Existing OD2524 and OD2522 report-layout defects remain distinct; no report entry added. Source-only; no USB report was delivered.

USBDevice configuration-transfer recheck (OD2550): selected OHCI and UHCI `ControlTransfer` return FALSE after a timeout or reported pipe error, but `Configure` ignores its initial header result and continues after all three full-descriptor reads fail. It then consumes uninitialized pooled descriptor fields to set configuration and build interface state; HID and MassStorage callers also ignore Configure status. Promoted the older OD23 candidate with the data-dependence and distinction from adjacent candidates explicit. No transfer or device was run.

USBDevice configuration-index recheck (OD2551): the public Configure method takes an index, but its initial header request is hardcoded to descriptor zero; the later full request uses the requested index and the index-zero length. Confirmed all in-tree HID, MassStorage and USBHub callers pass zero, so retained this as a public external-caller candidate and recorded that reachability limit. Differing configuration lengths make the parsed declared bound exceed the allocated prefix. No nonzero-index transfer was run.


AHCI display-name ownership pass (2026-10-12; OD2554): checked controller and per-port aHidd_HardwareName allocations against HW_AddDriver and the HIDD base class constructor/Dispose. HIDD stores this attribute as a borrowed pointer and frees only its duplicated aHidd_Name; ahci_release also frees the pooled controller record but not dev_revision. Therefore controller and channel-name allocations have no release on failed registration or object disposal, and the separately allocated revision leaks on attach-failure release. This is a bounded per-device leak, not a boot-stopping defect. AHCI attach, enumeration ownership, and ordinary lifecycle remain partial; no hardware was exercised.
AHCI media-monitor task-creation recheck (2026-10-12; confirms DISK-113, no duplicate OD): ahci_RegisterPort links the new cam_sim into ahci_Units before NewCreateTask and unconditionally waits for SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C. NewCreateTaskA can return NULL on allocation or NewAddTask failure; only ahci_PortMonitor sends the parent handshake. Updated DISK-113 with the Exec implementation references; the duplicate remains excluded from the Other Drivers finding list. No task-creation failure was induced.

AHCI CAM unregister pointer recheck (2026-10-12; no new finding): ahci_UnregisterPort frees ap->ap_sim without clearing it, but the selected call graph does not establish the second unregister needed for a use-after-free. ahci_cam_attach handles its own registration/probe failure by detaching; ahci_pci_detach is called only on attach setup failures before the later synchronous CAM scan; the Hidd_AHCIBus_Start caller is inside #if 0. Updated the disk report's awaiting-observation note to mark this as an unpromoted latent concern. Device attach/detach was not exercised.
AHCI selected-source ledger reconciliation (2026-10-12): compared all 15 C files in `rom/devs/ahci/mmakefile.src:11-25` against the Other Drivers coverage rows. Nine selected source rows were missing; added rows with explicit current-pass state, cross-references to earlier disk-scope evidence, and remaining review gaps. The current targeted `ahci_port_alloc` cleanup pass found no reachable pre-`ap_sc` cleanup fault because the selected inline bus-space subregion routine cannot fail. This does not complete AHCI; the 4,305-line core file and several platform/adapter sources still need full recheck.
AHCI timer adapter review (2026-10-12; OD2555): read the selected 167-line timer.c and traced all local callers in ahci_aros.c and ahci_cam_aros.c. The callout task initializes its returned signal mask to zero; if ahci_OpenTimer fails, it skips the wait and zero still passes the no-abort test, so it runs the expiry callback immediately. The callback marks and signals the active CCB; the helper can report ATA_S_TIMEOUT or begin port recovery. Kept separate from DISK-112's failed callout-task creation. OpenTimer failure also makes ahci_os_sleep return early; no additional distinct candidate was established. No timer failure or storage I/O was induced.

AHCI DMA backend recheck (2026-10-12; OD2558): traced each bus_dma_tag_create limit through the AROS tag implementation, allocator flags, selected x86-64 PC memory map, and programmed AHCI addresses. The adapter ignores lowaddr and maps virtual addresses directly; MEMF_ANY admits the 32-GiB-and-above high-memory header, and AHCI controllers without S64A cannot consume >4-GiB addresses. Promoted the conditional failure; requires a non-S64A controller and allocation from high memory. No device or DMA was exercised. Other AHCI sources and lifecycle remain pending.

AHCI bus adapter resource/interrupt pass (2026-10-12; no additional candidate): reread the complete selected `ahci_aros_bus.c`, tracing BAR and IRQ resource construction/release plus bus_setup_intr/bus_teardown_intr against the x86 PC kernel IRQ wrapper. The selected resource callers use BAR5; the resource-map null-handle fault remains OD2556, unchecked irq_handle allocation OD2557, and DMA bounds issue OD2558. Although the MSI/legacy selection compares flags to zero while AROS RF_ACTIVE is nonzero, the selected path routes the returned IRQ number through AddIntServer's INTB_KERNEL branch into KrnAddIRQHandler, and PCIPC supplies the allocated vector index for MSI, so no separate failure was established. AHCI callers, teardown interleavings and other selected sources remain pending; no device was exercised.

AHCI port-worker creation failure pass (2026-10-12; OD2559): followed the kthread_create wrapper's NewCreateTask result through ahci_os_start_port, ahci_port_alloc, and ahci_pci_attach's AP_SIGF_THREAD_SYNC wait. NewCreateTask returns NULL on allocation or NewAddTask failure; the wrapper reports ENOMEM but the caller discards it, leaving the handshake bit set. Attach waits indefinitely because only the missing worker clears it. Distinct from DISK-113, which concerns the CAM media-monitor task handshake. No failure or controller was run.

AHCI PCI BAR5 revision-read platform follow-up (2026-10-14; no new finding): traced `ahci_bus_Detect`'s direct `pci_read_config(BAR5)` dereference against selected targets. The boot manifests select AHCI and `pcipc` on i386-PC/x86-64-PC (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:73-75`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66-68`). PCI BAR5 is necessarily a 32-bit BAR (the last BAR slot cannot begin a 64-bit pair); the selected PC PCI driver initially identity maps 128 GiB and its `MapPCI` method maps addresses beyond that before first resource access (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:225-255`). Thus the AHCI BAR5 read address is already in the identity-mapped region for those selected targets. The BCM2711/BCM2712 bridges do translate PCI addresses to CPU windows (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/driverclass.c:216-232`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/hidd/pci-bcm2712/driverclass.c:245-269`), but their pinned boot manifests do not select the AHCI module; no selected configuration demonstrates a bad dereference. No hardware was accessed.

AHCI enumeration/init recheck (2026-10-12; no new candidate): reread all of `bus_pci.c` and `ahci_init.c`, including OOP base helper semantics, the HW_AddDriver return contract, PCI Obtain/Release ownership, pool clearing, and generated failed-init behavior. OD2552/OD2553 are confirmed with distinct unchecked-allocation and failed-registration consequences. DISK-321 is confirmed: failed OOP attribute-base array acquisition retains any successful references, while AHCI only releases them on the success-acquisition path. Utility references are closed on explicit AHCI_Init failure paths; no separate init-body candidate established. PCI BAR5 direct-read platform constraints and wider class/controller lifecycle remain pending; source-only, no hardware or allocation failure was exercised.

AHCI controller/unit class recheck (2026-10-12; no new candidate): reread the complete controller and unit class bodies and traced `HW_AddDriver`, CAM probe construction, EnumUnits and disposal. OD2372, OD2477 and DISK-126 account for the selected reset, null-bus false-success and port-multiplier unit lifetime/addressability paths. Unit metadata getters follow target zero, which is within the existing DISK-126 PM defect; direct-attached unit identity arrays include an extra zeroed terminator byte from Root object allocation. Controller RemoveBus intentionally rejects unloading, and no in-tree ordinary controller disposal caller was found. No additional class candidate promoted; external HIDD removal and full AHCI bus/lifecycle audit remain pending.

AHCI bus class full-file pass (2026-10-12; no new candidate): reread all Root, storage EnumUnits, SetUpBus/Shutdown and Open methods. Confirmed OD2372's stale reset callback and OD2554's borrowed name ownership. The normal selected attach caller uses `HW_AddDriver`; its controller SetUpBus callback is not invoked there. `Hidd_AHCIBus_Start` and `Hidd_AHCIBus_Open` have their active bodies disabled under `#if 0`, but no selected in-tree caller of StorageController_AddBus/Open was found, so no ordinary-path failure was promoted. External HIDD bus API behavior remains open; source-only.

AHCI PM/soft-reset recheck (2026-10-12; DISK-117 confirmed, OD2560 later withdrawn): rechecked the full prior `ahci_pm.c` read at the PM reset/error boundaries and traced direct/PM reset returns into `ahci_cam_probe`. Confirmed the final PM second-FIS timeout still reaches cleanup without `ahci_put_err_ccb` (DISK-117). The signature-mismatch error overwrite is present in PM soft reset, but caller-state tracing later showed its cached-type branch is not reached by selected callers; see the withdrawal audit below. Checked PM read failure zeroing, PM port count masking, 0..15 event loops and bounded helper access; no additional candidate established. No reset or hardware was run.

AHCI attach/detach full-file review (2026-10-12; OD2561): reread all of `ahci_attach.c` and followed the per-port allocation errors into the shared `error` loop condition, interrupt setup gate and detach cleanup. One implemented port's resource/setup failure prevents later ports and invokes controller detach, freeing ports that initialized successfully before it. This contradicts the local comment directing the loop to continue; separated the availability loss from OD2372, which documents the stale reset callback on that same cleanup path. Reset callback registration/removal, IRQ and BAR release, DMA tag rollback, startup waits and synchronous scan paths were checked. Other AHCI core paths remain pending; no hardware or induced failure was run.

AHCI core DMA helper recheck (2026-10-12; confirms DISK-110, no duplicate finding): inspected `ahci_dmamem_alloc/free`, map callback handling, PRDT load/sync/unload and the polling wait helpers; traced the DMA memory helper into port allocations and PRDT paths into command/NCQ callers. `kmalloc` is a direct `AllocVec` shim, confirming that `ahci_dmamem_alloc` can dereference a null wrapper allocation (DISK-110); the backend map-load failure path does destroy the map and free the wrapper. No independent issue was established in the bounded helpers, and OD2558 remains the separate DMA-address-bound defect. The AHCI core review is far from complete; reset, command scheduling and interrupt regions remain open. Source-only; no DMA or hardware was exercised.

AHCI core port-state review (2026-10-12; no new candidate): traced `ahci_port_init`, link-power capability predicates and all aggressive/medium/disabled transitions, then followed port and PM state-machine callers through worker startup, CAM probe/change and PM bitmap handling. PM target scans are bounded by `ap_pmcount` and the 16-entry target array; extra EINFO bits are passed only to bounded `ahci_pm_check_good` target slots. Power-management command failures are partly best-effort by design and no caller-visible inconsistent state was established beyond existing probe findings. The rest of the AHCI core, particularly command scheduling, interrupt completion, timeout recovery and hard-reset internals, remains pending. Source-only; no device or hot-plug event was run.

AHCI core port start/stop and direct soft-reset recheck (2026-10-12; confirms DISK-117 and DISK-109): inspected `ahci_port_start`, `ahci_port_stop`, CLO and the complete direct soft-reset routine, tracing callers in the direct/PM state machines, teardown, timeout recovery and port worker. The suspected OD2560 signature-mismatch consequence was later withdrawn after proving its cached-type branch is reached only by a disabled direct recovery call. Start/stop helper timeout returns are checked by reset and teardown callers in this slice; direct soft reset still ignores the return from its final `ahci_port_start`, but the downstream command start/recovery paths require a separate completion trace before judging impact, so no extra finding is promoted. Hard reset/COMRESET and command completion/recovery callers remain pending. Source-only; no hardware/reset was run.

AHCI COMRESET and hard-reset handoff review (2026-10-12; no new candidate): reread complete `ahci_comreset`, `ahci_port_hardreset`, `ahci_port_hardstop` and the PM-target hard-reset body. Traced all entries from direct/PM state-machine paths, including fallback COMRESET after a failed PM probe, detection result handoff, and hotplug cleanup. Existing DISK-109 accounts for active request completion after a failed command-engine stop; OD2555 accounts for wait wrappers that can return early on timer-open failure; DISK-110 covers unchecked AROS kmalloc-backed target storage; DISK-117 remains the PM/direct soft-reset follow-up. OD2560 is withdrawn because the signature-mismatch branch is only reachable from the disabled direct error-recovery call with an already-cached type; selected PM resets initialize the type as NONE before the soft-reset comparison. PM target reads/writes return errors in the principal probe decisions, while best-effort SERR clears do not establish an independent user-visible failure here. This pass is bounded to reset/hardstop and does not complete `ahci_pm.c` or the 4,305-line AHCI core; command scheduling, IRQ completion and timeout interleavings remain open. Source-only; no reset or hardware was run.

AHCI interrupt/error-slot recheck (2026-10-12; OD2562): traced global interrupt dispatch, nonblocking port lock deferral, task-file error processing, DHRS status handling, completion-slot walking and restart/recovery callers. The common TFES path validates CCS against `sc_ncmds`, but the separate stopped-DHRS/TFD.ERR path dereferences `ap_ccbs[CCS]` for a bootverbose message before jumping to that check. Promoted the bounded diagnostic out-of-range read with its controller-error and bootverbose preconditions explicit; normal command completions derive from the software active bitmap. The rest of AHCI command scheduling and timeout interleavings remain open. Source-only; no hardware error was induced.

AHCI poll/exclusive queue caller recheck (2026-10-12; qualifies pending observations and confirms DISK-127): enumerated every selected `ahci_poll` call in `ahci.c` and `ahci_pm.c`; all provide a non-null timeout function, so the generic NULL-callback concern is rejected for this build. Traced the only `ahci_beg_exclusive_access` caller to the port worker's one-time initial state-machine call, which runs before CAM attachment/public unit I/O; its PM operations are synchronous and serialized. Since the selected worker loop does not invoke the state machine again (DISK-125), the suspected wait on an unrelated timed-out public command is not reachable in the selected path. Rechecked `ahci_issue_pending_commands`: a first AUTOSENSE/EXCLUSIVE standard command can be followed in the same loop by an ordinary command before any active-state guard reruns, confirming DISK-127. Source-only; no I/O was run.

AHCI CCB pool and NCQ error-log pass (2026-10-12; confirms DISK-117 and DISK-128): re-read free-list get/put, reserved error-CCB save/restore, NCQ READ LOG completion and DMA wrapper free/error paths. Error-CCB reservation is restored on the ordinary exits in this core helper; the PM final-second-FIS omission remains DISK-117. The NCQ error-log page's 5-bit tag indexes `ap_ccbs` before validation against `sc_ncmds`, confirming DISK-128; corrected that report's source line span to the current pinned source. Error-log range remains conditional on an invalid/device-corrupted log. The wrapper's unchecked `kmalloc` remains DISK-110; map-load failure cleanup is complete. Source-only; no error log or allocation fault was induced.

AHCI core tail and transfer-NULL caller pass (2026-10-12; confirms DISK-013/128, no new finding): reread wait helpers, transfer get/put, command submission/completion, serialized/unserialized timeout handling, saved/quick-timeout replay and SET FEATURES. Traced every `ahci_ata_get_xfer` caller across CAM, SCSI and PM files. DISK-013 remains the distinct public disk-I/O path that dereferences a NULL transfer under CCB exhaustion; DISK-128 remains the invalid NCQ tag index. PM register helpers have no NULL checks, but their selected uses are serial in startup probe/reset before public storage I/O is exposed; no reachable exhaustion state was established. The other unchecked helper, `ahci_set_feature`, is only called from `ahci_port_link_pwr_mgmt`, which has no selected-tree caller. Thus neither suspicion is promoted separately. Body sections have now each received a targeted source pass, but caller/interleaving completeness and adjacent AHCI source files remain open. Source-only; no I/O or allocation failure was induced.

AHCI CAM glue full-file recheck (2026-10-12; confirms existing findings, no new candidate): reread all of `ahci_cam_aros.c` and followed Register/UnregisterPort, media-monitor task startup/exit, CAM attach/detach/change, transfer-mode and disk/ATAPI probe paths through their AHCI callers. Confirmed DISK-113/118, DISK-126, OD2430, OD2477, OD2478 and OD2866 remain distinct; their triggers and caller conditions are reflected in the existing reports. Verified the monitor's `device` argument is the AHCI library base, whose first field is the embedded `struct Device`, so its debug-name access is correctly based at offset zero. Rechecked the NCQ-depth reduction loop: it is entered only for negotiated depth >1, and free-list tag 0 is always eligible and reinserted, preventing an empty free list during the fixed iteration count; no null-transfer candidate is credited to that loop. Boot-node fallback and successful Expansion reference ownership remain DISK-118 and the existing leak note. External CAM lifecycle and SMP teardown interleavings remain outside this completed local-body pass; no CAM operation or hardware was run.

AHCI local formatter full-file review (2026-10-12; no new candidate): reread all 567 lines of `subr_prf.c`, traced `kvcprintf` through AROS debug output and ksnprintf callsites, and matched selected `%b` uses to static AHCI register descriptors. Bounded-output handling preserves a terminator when `size > 0`, handles `size == 0` without touching the destination, and returns the untruncated count. No selected format/argument mismatch or output-bound defect established. Descriptor bit 32 reaches a signed `1 << 31` expression in `%b`, which is a portability/undefined-behavior concern for diagnostic output; no manifestation on the selected compiler/build was established, so it remains unnumbered. `kvasnrprintf` has no in-tree AHCI caller. This closes the formatter’s local-source pass; AHCI cross-file review remains open. Source-only.
USBDevice OD2550 pool-clear semantic recheck (2026-10-12): traced `SD(cl)->MemPool` ownership to USB stack initialization (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usb_init.c:118-123`), `CreatePool(MEMF_PUBLIC|MEMF_CLEAR|MEMF_SEM_PROTECTED)`, `AllocVecPooled` to `InternalAllocPooled`, and its `MEMF_CLEAR` memset (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:90-93`; `memory.c:1038-1045,1183-1185,671-673`). This disproves the previous report/ledger claim that failed descriptor reads leave arbitrary pool bytes. Reclassified OD2550: after a valid header but three failed full-descriptor reads, `cdp` remains zeroed; `Configure` calls set_config(0), stores the USB_UNCONFIG_NO sentinel, has zero interfaces and returns TRUE (`usbdeviceclass.c:542-578`; `usb_core.h:449`). The selected HID/MassStorage constructors ignore that result and continue; `GetInterface` consequently returns NULL, which selected MassStorage dereferences at `storageclass.c:185-188` if its later descriptor lookup succeeds. Updated OD2550 and index text to the verified false-success/unconfigured-state trigger. The separate failed-header path still uses uninitialized stack `cd.wTotalLength`, but only proceeds when its value is positive and allocatable; not conflated with the pool-buffer finding. No transfer or device was run.
PC timer long-deadline arithmetic recheck (OD2545; distinguished from OD2537): followed the incoming timeval through `ADDTIME`, `Timer0Setup`'s `SUBTIME`, signed `LONG` comparison and PIT min clamp. A future normalized seconds difference >= `0x80000000` is reachable without deadline-addition wrap on a low-uptime PC; a near-threshold request with a high valid `tv_micro` avoids a subsecond borrow reducing the seconds field below the sign boundary. The IRQ's elapsed-time comparison still treats the queued deadline as future, while every Timer0Setup casts that delta negative and selects the minimum reload. OD2537 is a separate branch: the relative seconds plus uptime addition itself wraps to an earlier absolute timestamp, which the generic completion comparator regards as expired. No in-tree client submits a near-68-year wait, but the public `timerequest` has no smaller documented limit; both remain source-confirmed conditional API behaviors. No timer request or IRQ was run.
misc.resource free-index bounds recheck (2026-10-12; no finding): read the complete selected resource implementation and its manifest (`rom/misc/{allocmiscresource.c,freemiscresource.c,misc_init.c,misc.conf,mmakefile.src}`), plus the public unit definitions. `AllocMiscResource` rejects `unitNum >= MR_MAXUNIT` before indexing the array (`:61-73`); `FreeMiscResource` does not (`freemiscresource.c:53-57`), but its public note requires that the caller have allocated the resource first (`:31-34`), and an out-of-range unit cannot satisfy that contract. A repository-wide C/header search found no in-tree callers to establish an invalid-unit route. Treat invalid FreeMiscResource arguments as caller-contract violations for this review; no standalone bug is credited. Source-only.
CAMD OD1495 rollback recheck (2026-10-12; confirmed): repeated the source chain from `CreateNewProcTags` returning NULL (`camdwait.c:139-150`) through `InitCamd` failure and generated `_set_libinit` rollback (`init.c:39`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:55-69`). The failed worker never sets `camdwaitprocstatus` to 2 or initializes `camdwaittask`; expunge invokes `UninitCamd`, whose `UninitCamdTimer` skips only status 2 and otherwise signals the unset task (`camd_init.c:36-37`; `init.c:101-105`; `camdwait.c:154-159`). Exec `Signal` dereferences `task` in the ordinary path (`rom/exec/signal.c:296-303`), confirming OD1495. The separate pre-timer CLSemaphore-allocation branch remains OD1496. No process-creation failure or rollback was induced.
CAMD OD1496 early-allocation rollback recheck (2026-10-12; confirmed and distinct from OD1495): verified `InitCamd` allocates `CLSemaphore` before initializing any cluster lists and returns immediately on allocation failure (`workbench/libs/camd/init.c:25-38`). The registered `UninitCamd` expunge hook runs during failed INITLIB rollback (`camd_init.c:36-37`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:55-69`) and tests `midiclusters` with `IsListEmpty`; because the zeroed-but-uninitialized list has a NULL tail predecessor rather than its own address, the test reports nonempty, then the loop reads `node->ln_Succ` through its NULL head (`init.c:71-74`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:74-75`). Confirmed OD1496. This first-allocation case faults before timer cleanup; OD1495 is later, after lists are initialized, and reaches the null worker signal. No failure or rollback was induced.
NVMe OD2457 completion-walker caller recheck (2026-10-12; confirmed): followed the queue lock handoff in `nvme_process_cq` through both selected I/O-queue callers. The IRQ handler invokes the walker directly (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:63-73`), while each synchronous `nvme_sector_rw` BeginIO path independently polls the same queue (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_io.c:182-189`) after selecting its CPU queue (`:124-126`). The walker publishes its shared CQ head, drops `q_lock` for callback dispatch, then resumes from its unchanged local `head` after reacquiring the lock (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_hw.c:158-193`). The source contains both callers and the selected x86-64 package uses ExecSMP, but OD2876 shows the selected controller constructor never starts the bus; this queue race therefore requires a direct/external `Hidd_StorageController_AddBus` caller (none found in-tree). Conditional mechanics remain as described; ordinary selected NVMe I/O does not reach them. OD2395 remains a separate bounds issue requiring a phase-valid invalid command ID, not an ordinary duplicate walk. No request or interrupt interleaving was run.

NVMe namespace geometry/release follow-up (2026-10-12; no new candidate): re-read `Hidd_NVMEBus_Start` namespace Identify/Get Features handling, range publication, geometry setup, and its unit/boot-node continuation (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:470-671`), cross-checking the consumer bounds in `nvme_io.c:53-95` and packed Identify layouts in `nvme.h:268-298`. Confirmed existing OD2474 (I/O checks the upper range but not `au_Low`), OD2481 (LBA Range Type NLB is zero-based but treated as a count), and OD2482 (published range is not checked against current `nsze`); these are distinct range-start, range-length, and namespace-capacity conditions. Confirmed OD2370 remains the unchecked storage-ID allocation dereference at `:593-621`, and OD2371 covers absent Expansion leaving the created unit's transfer geometry unset. The debug-only LBAF enumeration can index past the fixed 16-entry array only if a controller reports `nlbaf > 15`, which is outside the selected 1.4-era structure's supported-format limit and is not promoted. `MakeDosNode` failure leaves the HIDD unit in the unit array, but the unit remains openable through the storage bus; no independent block-I/O failure was established from that fact. The rest of startup queue setup and partial-unit disposal remain open; no controller or I/O was run. Source-only.

NVMe queue negotiation/worker startup recheck (2026-10-12; confirms OD2453/OD2454/OD2525, no new candidate): traced Set Features(Number of Queues), optional MSI vector replacement, CQ-before-SQ creation, per-queue worker task creation, interrupt publication, queue-count gating and `nvme_alloc_queue` unwind (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:272-468`; `nvme_queue.c:24-102`). The selected setup hardcodes `hwqcnt = 1`, so it only uses I/O vector index zero; the PCIPC multi-vector GetVectorAttribs issues OD2419/OD2420 do not add another selected failure here. Confirmed OD2454: an unchecked null `q_IOTask` is stored in each I/O completion handler and signaled on completion. Confirmed OD2453: after CQ creation succeeds but SQ creation fails, the CQ, queue storage and worker are retained without an SQ; the overall false-success/no-units result is separately OD2525. Earlier queue allocation or CQ setup failures are also logged and skipped, after which the only-queue gate yields no namespace objects while Start still returns TRUE (OD2525). The initial Set Features timeout's PCI buffer/Expansion cleanup omission is included in OD2380. Controller reset, queue teardown after published work, and hardware-specific MSI delivery remain open; no controller, interrupt or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

NVMe I/O queue completion/teardown recheck (2026-10-12; confirms OD2457, no new candidate): traced selected BeginIO polling, shared PCI interrupt draining, `nvme_process_cq` lock release around hooks, callback DMA cleanup and signal/reply ownership (`rom/devs/nvme/{nvme_io.c:123-191,nvme_controllerclass.c:60-91,nvme_hw.c:121-217,nvme_queue_io.c:28-145,nvme_busclass.c:78-110}`). Confirmed OD2457's queue-level race mechanics: the interrupt and per-request poll can both enter the same queue only after the bus is started; OD2876 shows the selected controller path does not start it, and no in-tree direct AddBus caller was found. Under that direct/external precondition, each walker snapshots local cursor state, and callback dispatch occurs after dropping the spinlock. Repeated consumption can leave an old command ID associated with a later handler before the stale walker resumes; this is the existing finding's stale-cursor/slot-reuse consequence, not an independent report item. The driver I/O callback resets the DMA map before returning, and the reply task clears handler/hook pointers before freeing the ID, so a simple second callback before ID reuse does not establish an additional double-free. Queue disposal still requires fuller reset/removal lifecycle tracing; no CQ or request interleaving was run. Source-only.

NVMe completion-table malformed-ID bounds pass (2026-10-12; confirms OD2395, no new candidate): re-read the completion-ring phase acceptance and `command_id` dispatch in `nvme_hw.c:158-188,121-131` against both 64-entry admin and <=1,024-entry I/O queue allocations (`nvme_controllerclass.c:290`; `nvme_busclass.c:362-365`; `nvme_queue.c:59-74`). A phase-valid CQE ID is read before any range check and indexes `cehooks`, then the admin/I/O completion hook indexes `cehandlers` at that same value. This confirms OD2395's out-of-bounds read/possible invalid function-pointer call under a malformed or corrupted device completion. No additional independent bounds surface was found in this dispatch slice. Normal controller responses must echo IDs submitted by this driver, so the candidate remains a malformed-device recovery gap rather than an ordinary I/O trigger; no CQE or hardware error was induced. Source-only.

NVMe controller reset/disposal recheck (2026-10-12; confirms existing lifecycle findings, no additional reset candidate): traced `NVME_ResetHandler`, its registration point, `NVME__Root__Dispose`, queue-count updates, and the explicit no-unload `RemoveBus` contract (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:94-174,450-466,538-589`; `nvme_busclass.c:364-468`). The selected configuration compiles out the optional queue-delete/Set-Features reset commands unless `DISABLE_CONTROLLER_ONSHUTDOWN` is defined; reset still clears CC.EN and conditionally releases MSI vectors. The normal NVMe HIDD path explicitly refuses bus removal, so disposal of a successfully published controller is not an established ordinary trigger. The selected early failed-attach/dispose cases that can leave the embedded reset node or queue/interrupt/worker resources are already OD2365, OD2372 and OD2453/OD2454; on those paths cleanup defects originate in publication/rollback and do not justify duplicate reset findings. The single I/O queue means disposal's `q <= queuecnt` walk covers successful queue 1; failed queue setup before increment remains OD2453/OD2525. Actual hardware reset sequencing, external HW removal and shutdown-time IRQ delivery remain unverified. Source-only.

AHCI allocation caller recheck (2026-10-12; DISK-110 confirmed, OD2577 narrowed): checked `ahci_init`, `ahci_port_alloc`, ATA-target construction and `ahci_dmamem_alloc` against the direct `AllocVec` `kmalloc` shim and attach callers. The initialization-time null dereferences, including the DMA wrapper, are already consolidated in DISK-110. OD2577 is retained only for the distinct later consequence when `ap_err_scratch` is absent and NCQ recovery passes it through the success-reporting DMA shim before dereferencing it as the log page. No allocation failure, hardware or NCQ error was run. The exhaustive AHCI core/caller/interleaving review remains incomplete.

AHCI SCSI translation and CCB exhaustion recheck (2026-10-12; confirms DISK-012/DISK-013; no duplicate OD finding): traced READ/WRITE CDB decoding through `ahci_scsi_disk_io` and `ahci_get_ccb`. The CCB getter returns NULL immediately when its free list is empty; the ATA disk SCSI path then dereferences the result, while the ATAPI path returns `IOERR_UNITBUSY`, confirming DISK-013's concurrent-slot trigger. Standard INQUIRY/READ CAPACITY still use the CDB pointer for response storage, covered by DISK-012. Also noted a separate latent READ CAPACITY(10) saturation mismatch: for a device with more than 2^32 logical blocks, the code clamps the block count to 0xFFFFFFFF and subtracts one, returning 0xFFFFFFFE rather than SBC-3's FFFFFFFF sentinel; because DISK-012 currently leaves the response in the CDB, no separate user-visible OD consequence is established. SBC-3 T10/xxxx-D §5.10.2 confirms the sentinel rule (https://t10.org/ftp/t10/document.05/05-344r0.pdf). No SCSI command or hardware was run.

PCI interrupt-vector caller census recheck (2026-10-12; no additional PCIPC MSI count/index candidate): traced every direct selected call to `ObtainVectors`, `GetVectorAttribs`, and `ReleaseVectors` found under PC device, NVMe, AHCI, xHCI, VMware SVGA, and Nouveau sources.
