CopyToPAR short-read disposition (OD2649; 2026-10-13): promoted the earlier OD1926 lead after checking the utility’s full read loop, DOS `Read` result contract, and selected console-handler implementation. `con_read` can return a currently available positive count smaller than the request, while CopyToPAR exits successfully unless the count is exactly 4,096. Scope is conditional on using a handler such as CON: whose input can arrive in chunks; regular-file EOF short reads remain normal. DOS path alternatives and other handlers remain unreviewed. No runtime command was run.


UIKit event-task signal-mask recheck (2026-10-13; OD2639): read all of `eventtask.c`, then traced `NewCreateTask` without `TASKTAG_TASKMSGPORT` through the `MEMF_CLEAR` task descriptor template (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:34-38`), `NewAddTask` signal initialization (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:241-252`), and `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc` setup (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The fresh task reserves only the system signal bits `0x0000FFFF`; `AllocTaskSignal(-1)` selects an available bit above them. This closes the speculative signal-allocation-exhaustion lead for this selected creation path, while confirming OD2639’s distinct pointer-publication interval. No iOS scheduling or interrupt was run.

OpenSBI RTC candidate recheck (OD2648, 2026-10-13): reread the complete selected `ReadBattClock` path with `m41t11_FromBCD`, `Date2Amiga`, the OpenSBI battclock manifest and `SetClock LOAD` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/battclock/readbattclock.c:21-91`; `m41t11.h:39-58`; `rom/utility/date2amiga.c:55-98`; `workbench/c/SetClock.c:125-148`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/battclock/mmakefile.src:20-24`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:20-30`). Invalid nibbles such as seconds `0x0A` decode to in-range 10 and pass; February 31 passes the reader bounds and the generic day-offset conversion maps it into March. On failed bus read or stopped oscillator the function returns cached `bb_Time`, so those paths do not share the malformed-data consequence. `SetClock LOAD` uses the returned seconds without a validity flag. OD2648 remains supported with its conditional malformed-register trigger; the checked-in caller does not create such register contents. No RTC or clock command was run.


Atheros EEPROM v3 chipset-caller follow-up (2026-10-13; no new finding): traced the shared legacy parser through the selected AR5211 and AR5212 attach paths and their hardware EEPROM read callbacks. The 11a channel count is fixed at ten and matches parser arrays; paired frequency decode remains within indices 0..9. Both chips stop on failed hardware reads, propagate parser failure, and guard the detach hook. This closes the selected AR5211/AR5212 array-bound and read-error propagation questions only; size-extension fields, other chipset callers and physical EEPROM semantics remain open. No EEPROM was read. Source-only.

Atheros EEPROM size-extension bounds follow-up (OD2650): traced the v3 size-field calculation through AR5211 and AR5212 read callbacks. Their register headers specify a 10-bit EEPROM address, but the shared checksum loop does not cap encoded end location to 0x400 words; callbacks pass the offset directly to the address register. A nonzero upper field implies at least roughly 65K checksum iterations, and larger values can reach billions if out-of-range reads alias successfully; if hardware instead rejects them, attach returns an EEPROM read error. OD2650 records this conditional issue. The optional AR5312 parser caller is disabled by default and uses a caller-supplied pointer without a length argument; its external producer/buffer extent remain unknown and are excluded from OD2650. Physical format semantics remain open; no EEPROM/hardware accessed.

OD2650 attach/build-selection recheck (2026-10-13): confirmed `ah_eeprom_v3.o` is selected when either `AH_SUPPORT_AR5211` or `AH_SUPPORT_AR5212` is enabled (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/hal/Makefile.inc:66-82,126-130,167`), and both chip attach functions call `ath_hal_legacyEepromAttach` after their PCI EEPROM-size checks and jump to their failure path on any non-`HAL_OK` result (`ar5211_attach.c:301-304`; `ar5212_attach.c:476-479`). This confirms code-path propagation but does not establish that malformed extension metadata occurs on a physical supported board. For metadata above the 10-bit word-address range, the reader bodies still pass the whole offset to the address register; observed effects remain controller-dependent: read error ends attach, while successful aliasing permits the overlong XOR scan. No new finding is added, and the hardware-dependent part stays conditional at medium confidence.

OD2345 reply-publication recheck (2026-10-13): traced keyboard `ReplyMsg` through `InternalPutMsg`: the request is inserted on the reply port and its owner is signalled before the call returns (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:48-64`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-105`). The ordinary full-sized, one-event read takes the false `moreevents` break, leaving `ioreq` as the replied request; when the queue is empty, the post-loop `kbUn` macro dereferences its `io_Unit` (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:671-689,49`). This supports the documented cross-CPU request/unit lifetime race for a client that completes and closes the request immediately. The selected input.device keeps its one request open; no external client or interleaving was run.

VirtIO bus disposal caller reconciliation: `VirtIOBus__Root__New` allocates `ab_Units` (`virtio_busclass.c:63-99`), while `VirtIOBus__Root__Dispose` frees only name/serial/revision strings before superclass disposal (`:101-109`); no VirtIO-local array/unit cleanup exists. `Hidd_VirtIOBus_Start` stores its unit in that array (`:222-228`). The only selected controller startup currently reaches OD2541 before the bus object is instantiated (`virtio_controllerclass.c:145`; `OD2541` report entry), and `RemoveBus` is a stub returning FALSE (`:190-193`). Therefore the leak is tracked as an open direct/external or post-OD2541 lifecycle gap, not a selected-runtime finding. No object was constructed or disposed.

Console worker full-body recheck (OD1652/OD2306; no new candidate): reread all of `rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:1-590`, its input.device registration (`consoleTaskEntry:191-237`; `rom/devs/input/input.c:105-184`), and console BeginIO/AbortIO (`rom/devs/console/console.c:432-460`). The worker holds `consoleTaskLock` while draining commands, moving reads between the command port and `readRequests`, and replying them, so the selected abort path has no dequeue-to-reply gap. Its CTRL-C branch exits before acquiring the lock and reaches no teardown; this confirms OD1652's unregistered-handler/undrained-port path. Paste nodes are freed only after fully copied by `pasteData`; unit close disposes the unit without draining its paste list, confirming OD2306. `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_D` only pumps paste for units with queued reads, while each `CMD_READ` attempts a pump before deciding whether to queue; a paste with no reader is retained until later use or unit disposal. No additional independent failure was established in the selected read/event/reply path. External direct clients and runtime scheduling remain open; no device request was run.

Raspberry Pi USB OTG root-hub interrupt request ownership recheck (2026-10-13): traced `cmdIntXFer` enqueue (`usb2otg_hub.c:573-632`), `PendingIO` dequeue/copy/reply (`:634-671`), BeginIO completion dispatch (`usb2otg_device.c:537-645`), and AbortIO's `hu_IOPendingQueue` scan (`:656-754`). On ExecSMP, enqueue, dequeue and AbortIO's scan/removal all use `hu_Lock`; each also disables local interrupts. `PendingIO` removes the request before writing its response and calling `ReplyMsg`, so an AbortIO arriving after dequeue cannot remove or reply it and normal completion retains ownership. The CPU-0 soft-interrupt wrapper serializes `PendingIO` with the channel IRQ path. No double-reply or lost-owner interleaving was established in this root-hub path; hardware-generated port-change timing and external concurrent client behavior remain untested.

Raspberry Pi USB OTG concurrent-open trigger recheck (OD2627; 2026-10-13): verified the first-open wait and scheduler window from source. `OpenDevice` acquires the DeviceList lock with local Forbid, releases the lock before calling the device Open vector, and only calls Permit after that vector returns (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-100,109-131`). `OpenUnit` sets `hu_UnitAllocated` before controller initialization (`usb2otg_core.c:45-48`), then unconditionally performs a 100-ms `DoIO` timer wait (`:223-240`). `DoIO` waits for completion (`rom/exec/doio.c:63-66`; `rom/exec/waitio.c:54-64`), and Exec explicitly documents that `Wait()` breaks the forbid (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`; `rom/exec/permit.c:49-51`). Therefore a second task can enter `OpenUnit` during the first open's wait even on a uniprocessor; on ExecSMP, Forbid also only applies to the current processor. The earlier OD2627 overlap scenario is source-confirmed, while caller scheduling and the resulting hardware disruption remain unobserved.

Raspberry Pi USB OTG open-race selected Poseidon caller boundary (OD2627; 2026-10-13): traced the selected Poseidon hardware task's single `OpenDevice` loop, followed by `UHCMD_QUERYDEVICE` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9177-9233`). Root-hub enumeration later submits `UHCMD_USBRESET` on that opened HCD request (`:4109-4159`). This confirms that requests are issued immediately after that caller's OpenDevice returns, but the checked caller source does not establish two overlapping OpenDevice calls for the same USB2OTG unit. Keep OD2627's second-opener trigger conditional on another public device client or duplicate HCD opener; do not present it as an observed default Poseidon schedule. No hardware request was issued.

Atheros EEPROM out-of-range read timeout check (OD2650; 2026-10-13): verified each AR5211/AR5212 EEPROM read waits at most `AH_TIMEOUT` 1,000 polls (`ah.c:107-122`) for `READ_COMPLETE` and returns false if completion never appears (`ar5211_misc.c:70-81`; `ar5212_eeprom.c:38-49`). The attach loop then returns `HAL_EEREAD` immediately (`ah_eeprom_v3.c:1821-1824`); the very large checksum iteration count therefore requires out-of-range accesses to complete/alias rather than fail. This preserves the report's conditional wording; no hardware behavior was tested.

OD2650 checksum extent arithmetic recheck (2026-10-13; no separate wrap finding): the extension calculation is stored in `uint32_t`, while `i` is the 32-bit `u_int` typedef in `ah_osdep.h`. The largest encoded upper/lower value produces an end offset below `UINT32_MAX`; adding the `0xc0` base for the final read remains below the encoded end, and the loop counter reaches `eepMax` without wrapping. Therefore the reported issue is the missing 0x400 hardware-range validation and possible long successful/aliased read sequence, not a separate integer-wrap or infinite-loop defect. The 1,000-poll callback timeout bounds each failed hardware read as recorded above. No hardware behavior was tested.


ATA init cleanup follow-up (OD2658): verified the selected `kernel-ata` target enables both OOP base-array options. The attribute-base, method-base, and storage-root failure branches explicitly close Utility before returning false, after which generated INITLIB rollback invokes the registered expunge hook and closes the still-stored base again, decrementing utility.library's shared open count twice (utility.library is `noexpunge`). The CreatePool failure path leaves it for one close and is not affected. Added OD2658; no failure or library reference-count behavior was run. `ata_init.c` is also tracked in the separate disk report, but this exact duplicate-close path was not previously listed there.

OD2658 Utility count semantics recheck (2026-10-13): checked Exec's `CloseLibrary` dispatch and genmodule's generated library `CloseLib`. The latter decrements `lib_OpenCnt` unconditionally for a normal non-dupbase library; `OPTION_NOEXPUNGE` only suppresses the delayed-expunge branch, not the decrement (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1458-1471,1508-1514`). `struct Library.lib_OpenCnt` is UWORD (`compiler/include/exec/libraries.h:39-56`), so after ATA's explicit close returns the utility count to its prior value, rollback's hook performs a second unmatched decrement: it consumes another client count if nonzero, or wraps zero to 65535. The selected OOP attribute-release helper clears each field after release (`rom/oop/releaseattrbasesarray.c:54-63`), so the hook's second helper call skips those fields; no duplicate attr-base release is added to OD2658. The failed-init Utility count corruption remains supported; no allocation or library count was induced.


OOP attribute-base array caller census (2026-10-13; no new finding): searched every maintained C implementation callsite of `OOP_ObtainAttrBasesArray` (14 files) and checked the sentinel-list lengths, corresponding base fields, partial-prefix release, and selected generated-init rollback behavior. Existing cases reconcile to DISK-321 (AHCI partial-prefix leak), DISK-320 (PCI-ATA wrong-ID release after method-base failure), OD2366 (NVMe/VirtIO noexpunge init rollback resources), OD2431 (PCIUSB/xHCI partial-prefix leak), and OD2658 (ATA duplicate Utility close). The remaining callers either release the acquired prefix through their expunge hook or use a single-ID list. No additional issue was established in the helper or caller set; external OOP clients remain outside the census.


BCM2712 PCIe initializer full-body reread (2026-10-13; no new finding): traced device-tree property decoding, both trained/adopted bridge flows, translation windows, endpoint BAR setup, MSI discovery, selected Root::New registration, and generated noexpunge behavior across the full `pcie2712_init.c` body. Existing findings 923, 925, and 926 remain distinct. No additional source-confirmed defect was established; firmware range/property values, platform mapping, and hardware rollback behavior remain open. No board was run.


Serial interrupt-handler full-body reread (2026-10-13; no new finding): reread all 202 lines and reconciled active/queued read transitions, ring-buffer fallback, write callback completion, reset/stop state, AbortIO ownership and selected PC, m68k, RISC-V and hosted callback paths. Existing OD11, OD26, OD839, OD1454, OD2110, OD2244 and OD2388 remain distinct; the ring-buffer copy helpers stay within the one-empty-slot UWORD ring occupancy on the selected implementation. No additional source-confirmed issue established. Backend timing, external direct requests, and cross-CPU variants remain open; no serial data or interrupt was exercised.

Bluetooth connection timeout iterator review (OD3903; 2026-10-13): traced all `bConnDown` call sites and verified that event callbacks return from their dispatch, while `bConnTick` continues an outer `hc_Conns` iteration using a successor captured before timeout teardown. `bStartNextConnect` can free that saved successor when `bStartConnect` fails; the selected btcore command queue has a fixed 16-slot pool and returns `BT_ERR_NO_RESOURCES` when full, which `bSubmitCmd` propagates. This establishes a conditional dangling-list-iterator path for queued connection attempts. Added OD3903 with the HCI backend/queue-full trigger; no timeout or queue exhaustion was run.

Bluetooth service-refresh callback lifetime pass (OD2660; 2026-10-13): traced exported `btEnumerateServices` through the connected hardware-task request to the successful SDP completion and `bClearServices`. An open dynamic L2CAP channel retains its `bEndpointEvent` callback and endpoint pointer while local close waits asynchronously for peer response/timeout, but the refresh loop frees that endpoint immediately. Added OD2660; no scan or channel close was run.


ATA PCI construction rollback follow-up (OD2661; 2026-10-13): traced successful low-address DMA-buffer allocation through both interrupt-registration failure paths and the class-specific Root::Dispose. The constructor invokes superclass Dispose directly on failure, bypassing its own DMA-buffer release; AddBus returns NULL and the probe frees only its record/device reference. The apparent probe-record double-free hypothesis was rejected: that constructor path does not invoke PCIATABus__Root__Dispose, so the caller owns and releases those items. No allocation failure or hardware path was run.

Serial mouse disposal caller follow-up (2026-10-13): rechecked `test_mouse_serial` failure cleanup against `PCMouse__Root__New` and the PC serial HIDD (`rom/hidds/serialmouse/drv_serial.c:96-173`; `mouseclass.c:51-115`; `arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialClass.c:91-119`; `SerialUnitClass.c:245-282`). Probe failure disposes each rejected unit, frees the receive ring and serial object, and then the mouse constructor invokes superclass cleanup rather than its own destructor; successful objects retain those resources until the class destructor. The serial HIDD disposes only units still present in its table. No duplicate-release finding established. ISR quiescence and external callers remain open. OpenSBI's separate failed-IRQ registration acceptance remains OD2464 and was not duplicated here.


OpenSBI battclock I²C abandonment cleanup follow-up (OD2662; 2026-10-13): traced all `BattClock_I2COpen` failures after opening OOP and all `BattClock_I2CForget` callers. Driver-library failure leaves OOP open; attr-base failure closes the driver but not OOP or a successful peer base; lazy bus/probe/device failure disposes/closes the bus path but keeps OOP and both attr-base refs. The resource then stays in permanent no-RTC fallback and has no expunge hook. Small permanent reference/resource leak; no failure was induced.


Sam440 RTC failure-result recheck (OD2663; 2026-10-13): confirmed `date` is assigned only after both address probe and I²C-device construction succeed, yet `Date2Amiga` runs whenever the bus object exists. The seven-byte buffer is uninitialized and the BOOL from `WriteRead` is ignored (`i2cdeviceclass.c:157-162`); no `CheckDate` guards the decoded fields, and Date2Amiga indexes a 12-entry month table with the unchecked month. The selected SetClock LOAD applies this value to timer.device. Invalid BCD in an otherwise successful transfer shares the same unchecked-conversion path; no RTC contents were observed. This resolves the existing Sam440 RTC failure-path candidate into a detailed finding; no RTC/bus failure was induced.


Sam440 RTC write-result recheck (OD2664; 2026-10-13): traced the final eight-byte `WriteRead` result through the void `WriteBattClock` vector into SetClock SAVE and Time Preferences `SavePrefs`. No selected caller can detect a failed persistent write; Time Preferences still updates timer.device and returns TRUE. The existing OD1154 ledger candidate is now detailed as OD2664. No I²C failure was induced.

Nouveau/VMware AGP call and allocation follow-up (2026-10-13): checked the AGP bridge and TTM allocator helpers against both exact DRM source lists. Nouveau selects `drm-compat/linux_agp.c` (`sources.drm.mak:55`); VMware’s list does not include its copied `linux_agp.c` (`sources.drm.mak:52-74`). Neither list includes `drm/ttm/ttm_agp_backend.c`, so its `agp_allocate_memory` calls are not selected caller paths. Nouveau’s `nvkm_agp_init` entry is guarded by `CONFIG_AGP` (`drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/pci/agp.h:3-13`), and no defining target setting was found in the reviewed manifests. The source contains unchecked allocation results, but no active in-tree caller for those AGP entry points was established; no new finding is credited for the allocator. OD2674-OD2679 remain scoped to direct callers that invoke the public AGP interfaces; their consequences are source-confirmed, while current in-tree trigger/reachability is limited as noted in the findings.

OpenSBI DesignWare I²C caller-census follow-up (2026-10-13; no new candidate): searched the full checkout for `CLID_Hidd_I2C_DW`, `DWI2C_NAME`, and both controller-selection tags after tracing the generic `hidd.i2c.device` forwarding methods. The only active out-of-driver construction path is OpenSBI battclock (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/battclock/battclock_i2c.c:70-85,100-119,160`); its FDT address is shifted into the HIDD wire-address representation before probing and object creation. The example in `dwi2c.h` is documentation, not an additional caller. Thus OD1866's high-bit alias is reachable through the public class/API contract for external clients, while this checkout establishes only the firmware-derived battclock route and does not establish an invalid address there. OD2512 remains reachable through the generic public device `Write` method, although the selected battclock caller uses WriteRead. Existing distinction retained; no bus or firmware was run.

NextTagItem caller slice (2026-10-13; no new iterator finding): re-read `LibNextTagItem` and the Utility consumers PackBoolTags, MapTags, CloneTagItems/RefreshTagItemClones and FilterTagChanges. Their cursor handling matches the documented TAG_END/MORE/IGNORE/SKIP rules; in particular CloneTagItems reserves a cleared terminator slot and RefreshTagItemClones fills only visible tags. Checked the selected PCCard `ParseCfTableEntry` caller: when timing fields are absent it places TAG_SKIP at the first timing slot with count two, then resumes at the following I/O fields, which matches the iterator’s “skip this plus N” behavior. The broader 621 call-site census remains open; the pccard parser’s ignored allocation-failure return is separately detailed as OD3122. No allocation or iterator call was run.


Timer-device selection reconciliation (2026-10-13): traced `rom/timer/mmakefile.src` overrides through all eight architecture manifests and checked their parent package/link targets. The selected set includes PC, both Raspberry Pi targets, MinGW32, Unix, OpenSBI, m68k Amiga and Efika; Sam440 and native RISC-V use the generic code. This resolves the prior manifest-selection gap only; timer client, IRQ timing, concurrency and teardown review remain open. No target was built.


NetInfo OD1899 report restoration (2026-10-13): reconciled the active coverage-ledger reference with the detailed report and traced the exact malformed-row shape. A newline-terminated group line with no pipe separators yields a NULL third `strsep` result, which reaches `StrToLong` before validation; a final line without newline is intercepted separately by OD1903. Confirmed the standard `workbench-complete` path reaches the NetInfo common-target edge through MetaMake's recursive directory target scan. No file or request was run.


NetInfo aggregate-selection check (2026-10-13): confirmed OD1899 is in standard Workbench build scope. `workbench-complete` includes `workbench-devs-complete`; the common device aggregate includes NetInfo through its virtual dependency; MetaMake recursively scans and combines the manifest target definitions. This removes the prior package-selection uncertainty for the built target; runtime database contents remain unverified.


NetInfo FGets boundary recheck (2026-10-13): confirmed DOS FGets stores `buflen - 1` characters, so the loader passes at most 1,023 bytes and discards any continued chunk after a missing-newline test. OD1903 remains limited to the final unterminated record. The 1,023-byte payload plus newline boundary is ambiguous against the local maximum-length definition and the fixed 1,024-byte usergroup output buffer, so no separate candidate was added. No file was parsed.


OpenSBI DesignWare I²C discovery-order recheck (2026-10-13; no new finding): traced both compatibility passes, add-failure exits, unit assignment, and the fixed controller bound. Failed or disabled nodes do not consume a unit number, generic/specific aliases are not added twice, and eight accepted controllers use unique `i2c0` through `i2c7` names. Register spans, parent-bus address translation and clock-controller behavior still depend on external firmware inputs and remain open. No device tree or controller was used.


SiS900 packet-tracking caller/lifetime recheck (2026-10-13): traced selected AROSTCP configuration, default `SSF_TRACK`, `sana_run` tracking requests and `sana_deinit` close against SiS900 Open/Close and per-opener/global tracker records. Added OD2691 for leaked snapshots and tracker references on Close, OD2692 for the null-source `CopyMem` after a failed global tracker allocation, and OD2693 for user-count increments retained after duplicate-track rejection. AROSTCP's ordinary path establishes the close leak; no selected duplicate submission or allocation failure was run.


SiS900 RX softint lifetime recheck (OD2694, 2026-10-13): traced hardware IRQ scheduling through `Cause` and Exec's queue-pop/callback boundary, then compared RX's opener, message-port and tracker traversals with Close and UntrackType removal. On ExecSMP, local `Disable` in those writers does not serialize against a callback running on another CPU, and `free_irq` leaves already queued RX softints independent. Added one bounded cross-CPU list-lifetime finding covering the common callback/writer synchronization gap. No packet, close or SMP interleaving was run.
Bluetooth timeout iterator recheck (OD3903, 2026-10-13): traced `bConnTick`'s saved successor, timeout removal, `bStartNextConnect` list order, failed `bStartConnect` cleanup and `bConnDown` ownership. The first eligible waiting connection is the same list successor when it is queued immediately after the timed-out record; failed HCI submission frees it before `bConnTick` resumes at the saved pointer. The queue-full condition is concrete (`BT_CMDQ_MAX_PENDING` is 16 and submit returns `BT_ERR_NO_RESOURCES` when every slot is occupied); the hardware task's `bSubmitCmd` returns FALSE without retrying. OD3903 remains a conditional invalid list traversal, with exact reachability requiring at least one more pending node and queue exhaustion at retry time. Bluetooth remains optional and selected only by platform/package manifests; no controller, queue exhaustion or timeout was run.

Bluetooth L2CAP endpoint lifetime recheck (OD2660, 2026-10-13): reread `bClearServices`, successful SDP completion, `bEndpointClose`, the channel manager's retained callback/user-data fields, `finish_close`, and `bEndpointEvent`. The checked-in Preferences Rescan caller supplies the service-refresh request; an open dynamic channel remains in `WAIT_DISCONNECT_RSP` with its callback installed, and either a later disconnect response or retransmission timeout invokes that callback after `bClearServices` frees its endpoint context. This confirms the existing conditional stale callback context finding; radio and timer paths were not run.

L2CAP CID wrap and active-slot audit (OD2695, 2026-10-13): checked the complete local-CID allocator, both outgoing and incoming allocation sites, first-match local-CID lookup, and selected hardware-task endpoint open path. The allocator wraps to the first dynamic CID without consulting the eight-slot active channel table; preserving CID `0x0040` while allocating 65,472 further channels on one connection creates a duplicate and makes local-CID dispatch ambiguous. This is a rare long-uptime/churn condition; no channel was opened and no peer traffic was run.

Bluetooth L2CAP idle-close/reopen callback pass (OD2696, 2026-10-13): traced the public `btFreeChannel` close refcount, three-second idle-close timer, `bEndpointClose`, the channel manager's wait-for-disconnect state, `btAllocChannel`, subsequent device-I/O open, and delayed `bEndpointEvent(CLOSED)`. The selected path can reopen the same endpoint while its prior dynamic channel awaits response/timeout; that old callback ignores its CID and closes the endpoint state and flushes queues belonging to the new channel. Restored OD2696 in the detailed report with the old/new CID callback mismatch and request-flush consequence qualified; no channel or peer response was run.

Serial/parallel shared opener-count follow-up (OD2697-OD2698, 2026-10-13): OD2697 is restored in the detailed report and covers both serial and parallel UBYTE shared-opener counters; at 257 open handles the count wraps to one and a Close disposes the unit prematurely. Rechecked OD2698 against LDDemon: its per-device semaphore serializes selected Open vectors, so concurrent open/open increments and duplicate-first-open publication are not established and are withdrawn. CloseDevice does not take that semaphore and uses only local Forbid; two closes can both decrement a shared count of two to one on ExecSMP, leaving the serial or parallel unit/HIDD retained after both handles close. OD2698 is restored in the detailed report for the close/close lost-decrement leak; concurrent Open/Open was not promoted. x86_64-pc selects the PC HIDDs and full Workbench selects both devices. No open/close sequence or cross-CPU overlap was run.
Printer startup error cleanup follow-up (OD2699, 2026-10-13): verified that the selected PostScript `PRS_PREINIT` can reject saved pitch, spacing, or paper-size values after printer.device successfully opens its embedded timer request; the failure branch frees the reply signal and closes serial/parallel requests but leaves timer.device open, then the worker exits and `Printer_Unit` removes the unit and unloads its code. Restored OD2699 in the detailed report for the unmatched timer.device open on the PRS_PREINIT failure path. Source-only; no failing startup induced.
Filesave final-write cross-check (OD2700 withdrawn, 2026-10-13): the unchecked final data flush, format-header writes/seeks, and absent worker error handoff are already covered by OD1548. This recheck confirms generated sample counters are advanced before the final write and AHI Stop observes task termination only; no separate finding is retained. No filesystem error was induced.

input.device AbortIO caller-lifetime refinement recheck (OD1458, 2026-10-15): confirmed the no-op vector returns zero while a queued `IND_ADDHANDLER` can still be linked and later called. Exec explicitly requires `WaitIO` after `AbortIO`; freeing the supplied Interrupt node before that completion would violate the caller contract, so the stale-node consequence is excluded from the finding. OD1458 is limited to the false-successful cancellation and command still taking effect. The selected direct-caller census still finds no in-tree AbortIO on an input-device command; no request or event was run.
PC parallel poll and interrupt-mask follow-up (OD843, 2026-10-13): confirmed that `parallel.device` holds `Disable()` across the selected synchronous PC HIDD write. The selected method's BUSY/ERROR loop has no timeout or yield, and `parallel_usleep` is an I/O-delay macro; Exec documents that `Disable()` stops preemption on the current processor and is CPU-local under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:54-61`). Restored OD843 in the detailed report with the SMP impact scoped to the executing CPU; no printer port was exercised.

Gameport queue-drain follow-up (OD2701, 2026-10-13): expanded the earlier candidate 39 check against the exact `ForeachNodeSafe` loop semantics. When a final queued read fills but its unit cursor remains behind the event-ring write cursor, the loop exhausts at the list sentinel; the empty-list cleanup then uses the sentinel as `ioreq` through the `gpUn` macro and writes `gpu_flags` through an invalid unit pointer (`gameport.c:581-605`; `exec/lists.h:203-210`). A selected one-event input.device request has the necessary buffer size, but timing that accumulates a backlog on this route remains unestablished; the direct public gameport sequence is valid. Added OD2701 to the report. No event or request was run.

AbortIO vector cross-check (2026-10-13): rechecked the successful no-op AbortIO candidates against their actual vector return values and existing report entries. Clipboard's blocked posted-read case is already OD1429, and NVMe/AHCI/VirtIO are already OD2362. TAP `abort_io` returns `1`, which does not report a successful cancellation; removed the stale OD110 note. TAP's last-close-with-pending-read note OD111 depended on violating Exec `CloseDevice`'s documented outstanding-I/O precondition and lacked a selected violating caller, so it is withdrawn. No additional AbortIO finding was established by this pass.

Parallel.device shared opener-count follow-up (OD2702, 2026-10-13): traced the initial count, PARF_SHARED acceptance, UBYTE increment and last-close free branch. At 257 opens the count returns to one; one close then removes and frees a unit still referenced by 256 requests. The report records the high but unbounded direct-client trigger. No opens or closes were run.


Input.device AbortIO caller recheck (OD1458): reread `BeginIO`, the no-op abort vector, the command-port worker and selected `IND_WRITEEVENT` caller. BeginIO queues nonquick commands before returning; AbortIO returns zero without removing or marking them; the worker later performs and replies. The selected NTFS caller uses DoIO, and a direct AbortIO caller census found no in-tree request path, so the finding stays external-client scoped. No request was aborted.


Console input-handler setup failure recheck (2026-10-13): traced `initCDIH` allocation failure through `consoleTaskEntry`. The failed setup leaves no `consIHData.inputPort`, but the worker raises an AT_DeadEnd alert before reading that field; selected dead-end handling suspends or shuts down rather than returning to the dereference. No separate ordinary continuation candidate established. No allocation failure or alert was induced.


parallel.device opener-count caller recheck (OD2702, 2026-10-13): Exec OpenDevice looks up the device and calls its Open vector for each request without tracking or limiting opens per unit. The selected LDDemon wrapper serializes these calls but releases its temporary load/object reference after each one; it adds no persistent opener cap. Therefore the 257-open count remains reachable through repeated valid shared opens, though no such sequence was run.

audio.device ADCMD_PERVOL caller-contract recheck (OD2325): confirmed the worker validates channel allocation before calling `UnitAHIPerVol`, but passes `ioa_Period` unchanged and divides by it. The Paula-compatible public range includes 65,536 cycles, encoded as zero in UWORD; the m68k backend writes that value to the hardware period register, while the selected AHI backend divides by zero. The selected sound.datatype does not provide an in-tree instance of this trigger: its frequency field is UWORD and its positive-frequency conversion does not produce a zero UWORD period with the fixed AROS clock numerator. OD2325 remains a public/external IOAudio request case. No request was submitted.
audio.device ADCMD_PERVOL playback-update follow-up (OD2880): traced an ordinary nonzero period/volume update past OD2325's separate zero-period issue. `UnitAHIPerVol` updates only cached EUNIT values; the selected ahi.device snapshots frequency/volume into AHI_Play at request start, and the legacy audio.device snapshots independent repeat values before an infinite cycle. The Sound datatype's live PlayerProc sends ADCMD_PERVOL on selected frequency/volume changes while its audio.device session remains open. Thus the active sound and subsequent infinite repetitions retain old settings. Added OD2880. No playback or attribute update was run.

m68k Amiga card.resource change-counter recheck (2026-10-13): searched every `changecount` read/write and the `CardChangeCount` symbol across the checkout. `CardTask` is the sole writer and increments once per delivered task signal; the change-detect interrupt signals it but does not access the count (`arch/m68k-amiga/card/task.c:78-82`; `lowlevel.c:18-44`). The public reader performs one `ULONG` load (`cardchangecount.c:11-18`). The architecture-specific resource manifest selects this implementation for Amiga m68k (`arch/m68k-amiga/card/mmakefile.src:4-16`); the generic resource has separate no-hardware stubs, including a constant-zero CardChangeCount (`rom/card/mmakefile.src:10-19`; `rom/card/card_init.c:168-175`). No in-tree CardChangeCount caller was found. Signal coalescing/debounce and external expectations for how many physical transitions the counter represents remain unspecified, so no count-loss finding is promoted. No card event was induced.

Bluetooth connection lifetime recheck (OD3903/OD2660, 2026-10-13): revisited every `bConnDown` call site and the complete HCI command submission path. `bStartNextConnect` can synchronously free the saved next list node only on the queue-full submit failure already recorded in OD3903; timeout handling then resumes its cached-successor loop. Other teardown entry points run in the same hardware-task event loop and do not execute concurrently with its event/tick handlers. Rechecked the apparent connection-manager timer callback risk: L2CAP retransmission timers are linked into the timer list embedded in each `cn_L2CAP` (`channel_manager.c:542-569,795-800`), and `bConnTick` services that list only for connections still on `hc_Conns` (`hwconn.c:3961-3963,4036`). They are separate from `hc->hc_Timers`, whose entries are consumed by the worker before `bConnTick` (`hwtask.c:2702-2709`), so freeing a connection does not leave these local timers queued in the global list. No separate connection-timer UAF is established. OD2660 remains a distinct live-connection service-refresh case: its channel-manager close retains the callback and `hep` pointer until response/timeout after `bClearServices` frees the endpoint. The wider device-record, public-client and runtime interleaving review remains open. Source-only; no controller or connection was run.

Bluetooth idle-close endpoint-iterator recheck (2026-10-13; no new finding): traced `bConnTick`'s saved `enext` through both selected close paths. RFCOMM may report CLOSED synchronously when its DLC is not OPEN, but `bRFCOMMDlcEvent` only updates `hep` state and flushes request queues; it does not remove/free the endpoint. An open RFCOMM DLC instead closes asynchronously. L2CAP dynamic close may finish synchronously for a not-yet-open channel or later via the per-connection timer/peer reply, but `bEndpointEvent(CLOSED)` likewise does not mutate `cn_Endpoints`. Thus this loop's saved next endpoint remains linked on the inspected routes; the independently confirmed endpoint callback lifetime/state defects remain OD2660 and OD2696. Broader protocol and external callers remain open. No RFCOMM/L2CAP event was run.

Bluetooth incoming RFCOMM service-close event recheck (OD2703, 2026-10-13): followed service creation in `bRFCOMMAccept`, close notification in `bRFCOMMDlcEvent`, `btSendEvent` mask filtering and the internal event-task subscription. The worker's switch contains SERVICEGONE cleanup but its registered mask omits event bit 24, and the public header lacks the corresponding `BEHMF_SERVICEGONE` constant. A bound `bsv_Gone` record is skipped by class scan and by the incoming-channel reuse search; the servicegone branch therefore cannot release the binding or free that stale record. No RFCOMM event was run.

AHCI caller-path recheck (2026-10-13): traced disk BeginIO through the SCSI command, ATA queue, PRDT and AROS DMA adapter. This reconfirms OD2558: the no-S64A low-address bound is discarded and high addresses can reach descriptor or data DMA. The separate 64-KiB sync length mismatch remains uncredited on selected x86 packages because their CachePreDMA/PostDMA hooks do not require cache maintenance. SCSI pass-through validation and remaining timeout/device-geometry paths stay open; no transfer was run.

AHCI pass-through recheck (2026-10-13): followed `HD_SCSICMD` through disk/ATAPI translators, ATA completion, residual calculation and selected SFS/PFS clients. No duplicate OD finding was added: unchecked disk CDB lengths are already in DISK-012, CDB/count and data-length mismatch in DISK-121, and ignored residuals in DISK-122. Selected direct callers use matching ten-byte READ/WRITE CDB lengths and data counts; malformed external CDB lengths remain unverified. No SCSI command was issued.


Virtual Bluetooth unit signal-allocation caller check (2026-10-13; no finding): examined `vbthci_UnitTask`'s unchecked `AllocSignal(-1)` and followed the task through the selected `vbthci_OpenUnit`/`CreateNewProcTags` path. `NewAddTask` assigns a zero `tc_SigAlloc` the system mask `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc`; Exec initializes that mask to `0xFFFF`, reserving signals 0-15, so this new worker has free signal 16 when it makes its first allocation (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:249-251`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The allocation-failure shifts and cleanup therefore have no selected trigger through this fresh-task path and are not promoted. Existing close/open lifetime and broader request-caller checks remain open; no task was started. Source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth unit close/reopen ordering check (2026-10-13; no new driver finding): traced the per-unit semaphore and both worker lifetimes. Close clears `vb_Units[unitnum]` while holding `vb_Lock`, then signals and waits for the old worker before freeing that unit (`vbthci_device.c:82-99`). A racing open can therefore start a distinct unit object while the old one drains; the worker path uses its `unit` argument and does not consult `vb_Units`, whose only reads/writes are open, close and expunge checks (`:27-33,45-76,84-86`). No cross-unit dereference was established. Generic concurrent device-base lookup/open/expunge synchronization is separately tracked in EK271. No task or open/close overlap was run. Source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth event-reply shutdown caller check (2026-10-13; no selected lifetime finding): traced `vbt_SendEvent`'s reply-port ownership and the unit task's bounded pending-message drain against the selected Bluetooth `hwtask`. The selected consumer replies each event after synchronous `bHandleEvent`; its close path unregisters the event port, flushes pending device requests, drains and replies queued events, then calls `CloseDevice` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:1849-1852,2916-2919,3044-3076`). Since consume and close are ordered by the same task, no in-tree outstanding event was found when the virtual unit's 250ms reply wait expires. External clients that retain or fail to reply a message remain unverified; no event or close was run. Source-only.


Bluetooth Preferences stale-device removal recheck (OD2705, 2026-10-13): traced `Populate` through the selected Connect helper, Bluetooth library control submission, USB interface release, `btRemHardware`, delayed event delivery and device/hardware cleanup. `bFreeDevice` intentionally retains the `BtDevice` allocation, but hardware teardown frees its `BtHardware`; the stale scan record therefore reaches the freed hardware through `bd_Hardware`, rather than requiring the device record itself to be freed. Expanded OD2705 to include DevWin persistent selected-device pointer and Rescan action after removal. This path was not run; wider Bluetooth preference caller and task-lifetime checks remain open.


Bluetooth Preferences event-subscription setup recheck (OD2706, 2026-10-13): checked `bluetoothprefs.c`'s library/class setup and ActionClass's `MUIM_Setup`/`MUIM_Cleanup` against `btAddEventHandler`, `btSendEvent`, and the manual Restart refresh. `CreateMsgPort` failure skips registration while setup still returns TRUE; hook-allocation failure returns NULL but the caller still installs an input handler on an event port with no producer. Added OD2706 for the resulting missed live updates, scoped to setup-time allocation failure; no allocation failure or UI session was induced.


Bluetooth Preferences IconList display and ownership check (2026-10-13; no finding): traced per-instance BodychunkObject and List_CreateImage ownership through cleanup and every selected list display hook. The MUI TextEngine parses the full pointer with HexToIPTR; its explicit NULL-image path draws nothing, so CreateImage failure is not a demonstrated crash. `DeviceIconFor` returns only indices 11-16 for device icons and fixed navigation/status values all remain within ICON_COUNT=17. `%08lx` specifies a minimum width, not a truncation width; the selected 64-bit LP64 targets retain the IPTR value in `unsigned long`. No separate list-icon defect established; no UI or allocation was run.

| `rom/devs/ata/ata.c` | **Full 1,163-line body read; 822 `cloc 2.06` C lines reviewed** at the pinned snapshot; selected command handlers, dispatch, immediate/queued completion and caller paths traced across the disk and other-driver audits | Selected ATA device module (`rom/devs/ata/mmakefile.src:18-42`). OD2999 records the strict exclusive-end threshold in `cmd_Read64`/`cmd_Write64`: an end equal to `0x0fffffff` is representable by LBA28 but is sent to the 64-bit vector, which stays `ata_STUB_IO64` when IDENTIFY lacks LBA48 (`:140-159,256-285`; `ata_unitclass.c:53-60,90-97`; `lowlevel.c:1410-1444`). The wrapper accepts equality with reported capacity, so a qualifying non-LBA48 device can reject a valid boundary request as `CDERR_NOCMD`. OD3000 traces `cmd_TestChanged` calling `atapi_TestUnitOK` and confirms false-present state affects `TD_CHANGESTATE` and the removable read/write guards (`:315-327,373-383`; `lowlevel.c:2323-2382`). The queued AbortIO path removes only requests still linked on the message port and replies them under the platform queue lock (`ata.c:845-896`); no dequeue/abort race was established. Slow BeginIO sets per-unit UNITF_ACTIVE/UNITF_INTASK flags, but source-wide references show no maintained reader of those unit flags; the bus task uses its own `ab_Flags` field (`:811-818,1143-1160`), so no present functional consequence is credited for the stale per-unit bits. OD3001 records CMD_FLUSH draining the shared bus port without filtering requests by unit, so a flush on one master/slave unit aborts queued requests on its sibling (`ata.c:292-306,765-777,811-827`; `ata.h:40,188-195`; `ata_busclass.c:686-697,1044-1068`; Exec per-unit flush contract). OD3002 records the change-interrupt list using local-only Forbid for AddHead/Remove/traversal on ExecSMP; `ForeachNode` dereferences the current node after callback dispatch, and selected FAT teardown frees its request immediately after Remove (`ata.c:315-344,407-428`; `forbid.c:58-60`; `lists.h:195-201`; `fat/main.c:328-346`). Gameport sentinel-writer reachability follow-up (OD2701, 2026-10-14): replaced the unresolved backlog assumption with a direct public two-opener sequence. Each Open creates a distinct zeroed `GPUnit` (`gameport.c:199-206`); one-event reads from two units both queue at an empty ring (`:390-432`). Callback one services the first request and breaks when its cursor catches the writer, leaving the second request behind. Before the first client resubmits, callback two services the stale second cursor: its one-event buffer fills but one newer event remains, so `moreevents` stays true; after removing the sole request, `ForeachNodeSafe` exits with `ioreq` at the tail sentinel, and the post-loop `gpUn->gpu_flags` write uses the sentinel as a request (`:581-598,603-605,645-786`; `exec/lists.h:203-209`). `mouseCallback` calls the drain synchronously (`:550-558`; `AROS_INTC1` wrapper in `interrupts.h:117-126`). The selected input.device single stream does not prove this route; direct public multiple opens do. The candidate trigger is now source-established without relying on an unbounded event burst. No mouse callback or request was run.

OD2701 consolidation / OD2136 reachability recheck (2026-10-14): merged OD2701 into OD2136 because both describe the same `gpSendQueuedEvents` post-loop `gpUn->gpu_flags` invalid write. The two-opener sequence establishes reachability through valid public Opens without relying on cross-core callbacks or event backlog; OD2136 retains the cross-core route as an additional conditional path. OD1579 remains separately tracked for the earlier queued-reader liveness failure. OD2701 is recorded as withdrawn duplicate in the report, and `../AROS.md` now summarizes OD2136. Corrected OD2136's `mouseCallback` source lines to `gameport.c:536-561`. No request, event or interleaving was run.

Gameport OOP attribute-base refcount confirmation (OD1192, 2026-10-14): `OOP_ObtainAttrBase` increments the shared IID bucket reference count for each obtain (`rom/oop/obtainattrbase.c:71-87,130-134`), while `release_idbucket` blindly decrements the bucket and frees it at zero without tracking which caller owns each reference (`support.c:180-205`). The selected keyboard and mouse HIDD initializers each obtain and retain their own `IID_Hidd_Input` reference (`rom/hidds/kbd/kbd_init.c:20-36`; `rom/hidds/mouse/mouse_init.c:26-42`). Gameport obtains only while its cached field is zero, but releases on each open reaching line 269; therefore the first successful open balances its new reference, while later opens consume references held by the HIDD class owners. A subsequent `OOP_GetAttrBase` then returns zero after bucket removal, and a later obtain creates a new numeric base (`getattrbase.c:66-103`; `obtainattrbase.c:73-90`). The exact number of direct opens to bucket exhaustion depends on other live IID owners; the selected one-open input.device path does not trigger it. No OOP refcount was changed at runtime.

OD2040 H:4 receive-stall recheck (2026-10-14): restored the previously ledger-only candidate to the report after following UART error propagation through the complete H:4 parser/read loop. The PL011 ISR logs parity/framing/break errors but still enqueues the byte (`pl011bt_init.c:229-250`); an ACL length whose full frame exceeds the 4,096-byte `hu_RX` capacity remains incomplete (`h4bthci_unit.c:37-50,160-189`). Once the buffer is full, the worker repeatedly calls `PL011BTRead` with zero capacity and receives zero, so no further bytes are consumed and no parser recovery occurs (`h4bthci_unit.c:447-462`; `pl011bt_init.c:591-606`). The selected stack's normal outgoing ACL request buffer is 1,028 bytes and does not constrain incoming frames. No controller, malformed frame, or UART error was exercised. Source-only.

H:4 outbound-length/caller recheck (2026-10-14): followed selected `btcore` sends through the transport operations and Bluetooth hardware task into `h4bthci_QueueRequest`. L2CAP caps ACL fragment payloads at 512 bytes and emits a 4-byte ACL header (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/l2cap/channel_manager.c:67-92,542-554`); the hardware task accepts `bSendACLPacket` lengths only from 4 through `HC_ACLBUFSIZE` (1,028), then copies into an equally sized write buffer and issues BTCMD_WRITEACL (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:140-163`; `hwtask.h:31-35`; `hwtask.c:2633-2677`). Command sends are bounded by the allocated 3+255-byte HCI command buffer before copying (`hwtask.c:76-104`; `hwtask.h:321`). H:4 prepends one type byte and drains short UART writes, so the selected command/ACL caller lengths do not overrun the resource path. The shared transport table maps send_sco/send_iso to the ACL sender, but no selected btcore caller invokes either and no finding is promoted. Source-only; no packet was sent.
