SDL bitmap 24-bit color-expansion stride recheck (2026-10-14): confirmed OD2774 duplicates OD2716; withdrew the duplicate and retained OD2716 as the detailed finding. The pointer stride is four bytes against three-byte pixels; row crossing depends on SDL pitch and width. No surface or blit was run. Source-only.

Keyboard.device failed-open ownership recheck (OD2304, 2026-10-14): reread the complete 701-line keyboard.device body and verified the allocation/error/close chain. `Open` allocates the `KBUnit` before `OOP_ObtainAttrBase` and before opening/constructing `keyboard.hidd`; every subsequent failure returns with `io_Error` without freeing or linking that unit (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:160-165,180-187,197-225`). `OpenDevice` has already set `io_Unit` to NULL, the device overwrites it with the allocation, and the failure path clears only `io_Device` (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:96-98,109-120`); `CloseDevice` skips the driver Close vector when `io_Device` is NULL (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:70-92`). This confirms the per-failed-attempt leak. A repository-wide direct-open census found input.device, DOSBoot, PFS3, USB bootkeyboard, USB HID and optional Bluetooth HID; checked call sites make single setup/probe attempts rather than demonstrating an automatic retry loop. Repeated caller retries remain a public API trigger; no allocation, HIDD failure, or retry was induced. No change to OD2304's conclusion.


Gameport ring publication recheck (OD2118, 2026-10-14): restored the missing detailed finding after reconciling the coverage ledger's reference to finding 2118 against the report, where no such section existed. Re-read `mouseCallback`, `BeginIO/GPD_READEVENT`, `fillrequest`, Exec Disable semantics and the ring dimensions. The writer increments `gp_writePos` once per word; an immediate reader treats any difference from its per-unit `gpu_readPos` as available input and consumes a full four-word record. On a different CPU, a reader between those stores can consume stale coordinates/flags and misalign the per-unit cursor. The x86_64 PC SMP target selects i8042 mouse and gameport; its selected input.device consumer queues an empty-ring request and no selected immediate-reader interleaving was established. The report now confines the trigger to a direct immediate reader or cross-core producer overlap. No input or interleaving was run.

Poseidon QuickIO callback/list-lock audit (OD2776, 2026-10-14): completed the callback-to-Exec path left open by the inventory pass. `InternalPutMsg` releases the SMP `mp_SpinLock` before synchronously invoking `PA_CALL`; both Poseidon callbacks then drain the port list with raw `RemHead`. Multiple producer CPUs can therefore race in one list drain, and the reply list can also be drained by `GetMsg` during the task's shutdown flush. QuickIO is conditional on `UHCF_QUICKIO`; the only checked PCI USB and xHCI producers set it under `PCIUSB_QUICKIO`, with no enabling definition found in this checkout. Recorded OD2776 as a configuration-conditional SMP queue race and retained the no-default-controller qualification. No controller or concurrent operation was run.

Poseidon xHCI root-hub-count recheck (OD2777 withdrawn, 2026-10-15): withdrew the apparent missing USB2 root hub after tracing the selected OpenSBI `pcixhci.device` root-hub model. `pcixhci_arospci.c` assigns both `hu_RootHubXPorts` and `hu_RootHubPorts` from the full xHCI root-port count (`:357-358`); when the SuperSpeed root hub enumerates, its descriptor advertises that full count (`uhwcmd.c:917-932`). The selected `hubss.class` explicitly treats a root hub marked synthetic-SuperSpeed as using the USB2-style port-status layout while covering both USB2 and USB3 ports (`rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:752-759`). Thus Poseidon's `phw_NumRootHubs == 1` default and skip of a second normal hub (`poseidon.library.c:4212-4217,4404`) match this HCD's combined-root-hub design; no missing USB2/USB1 visibility finding is supported. No device or controller was run.

xHCI root-hub notification race follow-up (OD2778, 2026-10-14): traced the xHCI event interrupt's `hu_RootPortChanges` OR against both root-hub interrupt completion paths. `cmdIntXFerRootHub` copies the bitmap and clears it without disabling interrupts; `uhwCheckRootHubChanges` does so under local `Disable()`, which does not serialize another ExecSMP CPU. A change bit set between copy and whole-bitmap clear can be lost after the xHCI event path acknowledges the corresponding PORTSC bits. The AArch64 Raspberry Pi package selects pcixhci and USB startup, and its `smp` target enables ExecSMP. Recorded OD2778 as a conditional notification-liveness defect; no event interleaving or device was run.

OD2778 selected hub-client confirmation: the selected `hubss.class` and `hub.class` locate an interrupt-IN endpoint and allocate a pipe (`rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:807-815`; `hub.class.c:832-854`), then issue recurring `psdSendPipe` requests for its port-change bitmap (`rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:404,1555`; `hub.class.c:450,1453`). Poseidon's selected `psdAllocPipe` maps interrupt endpoints to `UHCMD_INTXFER` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4608-4617`), which reaches xHCI `cmdIntXFerRootHub`. Thus the pending root-hub interrupt request needed for OD2778 is used by the selected hub stack; this distinguishes the unit bitmap delivery race from OD2610's per-controller port-change-map race, whose root-port control-request trigger remains unestablished for in-tree clients. No USB request or interrupt was run.
PC serial paired-unit teardown follow-up: added OD2779 after tracing `serial.device` first-open/final-close into `PCSerUnit__Root__New` and `Dispose`. A shared IRQ server is registered by only the first COM1/3 or COM2/4 unit and removed with that unit even if its pair remains open; the second unit does not own a reset node or reinstall the server. This differs from OD1454's in-flight receive window. No device or interrupt was run. Source-only.

BCM2712 PCI MSI-vector caller follow-up: checked every in-tree `ObtainVectors`/`GetVectorAttribs`/`ReleaseVectors` use against `PCIBcm2712Dev__Hidd_PCIDevice__*`. The only selected direct caller of this backend is RP1 resource initialization, which requests its 37–64 range once and then queries interrupt indexes 31 and 36; RP1's synthetic xHCI devices use a separate backend. The shared PCI xHCI, AHCI and NVMe callers use other PCI backends in their selected platform packages. No selected overlapping obtain/release schedule on the BCM2712 bridge was established, so OD1145/OD1146 remain API-level conditional candidates pending external or hot-plug caller contracts. Source-only; no vectors were allocated.
Generic bit-banged I²C timeout follow-up (OD1151/OD1817, 2026-10-14): promoted the existing zero-rise/fall SCL polling candidate OD1151 and concurrent zero-HoldTime ACK-loop candidate OD1817 to detailed entries after re-reading `RaiseSCL`, `PutByte`, bus `Root.New`/`Root.Set`, and the selected Sam440 bit-bang methods. The static zero HoldTime case remains rejected: `PutByte` passes HoldTime as `RaiseSCL`'s timeout, so zero exits before the ACK loop. The separate concurrent case is possible because Root.Set does not take the hardware semaphore and can change HoldTime after `RaiseSCL` captured the positive timeout but before the ACK loop reads the shared field. The selected Sam440 battery-clock clients use defaults; no bus operation or setter race was run.
FELSunxi binding-startup trace (2026-10-14; candidate restored as OD9830): the MUI-construction failure path skips the task ready signal while `ForceDeviceBinding` waits in `psdBorrowLocksWait` with Poseidon locks borrowed. The earlier OD1086 identifier had no report/index entry. Subsequent manifest reconciliation found the class only as an explicit target; the claim that a complete disk-class aggregate selected it is withdrawn. See OD9830 and the 2026-10-26 per-file ledger below. No USB scan or allocation failure was run.

Console worker teardown follow-up (OD1652, 2026-10-14): traced the Break path beyond the registered input handler to the lifetime of `ConsoleDevice->consoleTask` and `commandPort`. `TASKTAG_TASKMSGPORT` adds a port allocation to the worker MemEntry, and the default task finalizer routes the exiting worker through `RemTask` to the Exec service task, which frees that allocation (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:23-33,148-152,213-235`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:51-55`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:130-163`; `rom/exec/service.c:58-84`). The device retains both pointers; later CMD_READ reaches `PutMsg` on the freed port, while a StdCon window-status reply synchronously calls `con_inject` and `Signal` on the freed task pointer. This supersedes the prior wording that requests merely accumulate on the command port; its post-reclamation state is freed storage. The pre-existing OD1652 coverage row records the worker/handler cleanup gap; this supplement records the concrete selected stale-pointer callers. Also rechecked the initial ignored IND_ADDHANDLER DoIO: `CreateIORequest` allocates cleared storage, and selected input.device unconditionally enqueues/replies for the supported command, so no separate registration-failure finding is established. No task was broken and no I/O was run. Source-only.

Keyboard reset-handler SMP caller follow-up (OD2603, 2026-10-14): rechecked list dispatch against the selected HID reset-chord helpers. `writeEvents` invokes `is_Code` while traversing the list; boot-keyboard, USB HID and Bluetooth HID each briefly enqueue a stack `Interrupt` whose `is_Code` is NULL, then remove it after reading the predecessor links (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:497-512`; `rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:538-555`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6555-6574`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:5820-5839`). A concurrent reset-key traversal can therefore encounter the temporary record as well as the VMM unregister/free case already detailed in OD2603. This remains one list synchronization/lifetime finding, conditional on overlapping reset handling; no separate ID was added. No reset event or SMP interleaving was run. Source-only.

Keyboard reset-key producer follow-up (OD2603, 2026-10-14): the selected PC i8042 driver emits code `0x78` when Ctrl and both Meta keys are held, then pushes it through the HIDD keyboard path (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:538-570`). `keyboard.device` registers `keyCallback` as an input HIDD consumer, buffers the event, and delivers it to `writeEvents` through `KBD_READEVENT` (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:203-209,347-379,608-635`). This establishes the reset event path for OD2603 on the PC i8042 configuration; an independent handler-removal or temporary-registration overlap is still required. No key event was generated. Source-only.

PC i8042 ACPI accumulator follow-up (OD2783 withdrawn, 2026-10-24): the prior note incorrectly treated any nonzero accumulator as a mouse match. The callback sets `ACPI_PS2DEV_KEYBOARD` (bit 0) or `ACPI_PS2DEV_MOUSE` (bit 1), and the disable check masks specifically for the mouse bit. A keyboard-only match therefore leaves the mouse bit clear and sets `PS2F_DISABLEMOUSE`; shared accumulator reuse is not a bug. The ACPICA implementation is fetched upstream and absent from this checkout; no ACPI namespace or physical controller was tested.

PC i8042 keyboard task handoff recheck (OD2320/OD2321, 2026-10-14): re-read the 56-line keyboard state header, full setup worker, object constructor and Exec task creation result contract. Confirmed instance storage is cleared by Root::New, `CtrlTask` is not populated until after three fallible setup operations, and `TASKTAG_USERDATA` stores the parent task only in the worker's `tc_UserData`. The two existing findings remain distinct: no task exists after failed `NewCreateTask`, while early worker setup failures dereference the unset instance pointer before the parent signal. Updated the header's caller/lifecycle ledger row. No task or device failure was induced.

PC i8042 lock-key LED recheck (OD2336, 2026-10-14): followed the three lock-key scan-code cases into `Signal`, then compared the allocated signal number, worker wait mask, receive test and fallback `SIGBREAKB_CTRL_E` value with Exec's signal-set contract. The producer sends the bit number and the worker tests with the bit number, while `Wait` uses the shifted mask; ordinary lock-key presses therefore do not wake the LED worker. The fallback is likewise passed as a number rather than a mask. This confirms OD2336; the keyboard state is still updated in software and no physical key/LED was exercised.

PC i8042 report reconciliation (OD1685/OD1686, 2026-10-14): found both candidate IDs in coverage but no detailed report sections. Restored OD1685 for the unbounded RESET/DISABLE retries after repeated `RESEND`. Restored OD1686 with narrower wording: `i8042_wait_for_input` consumes a byte without ACK validation, after which the LED helper performs an unconditional second port read; losing a key scan byte depends on a second byte arriving at that point. No controller timing was exercised.

PC i8042 write-ready caller follow-up (OD2056, 2026-10-14): traced the selected keyboard-first registration into the mouse reset task and its auxiliary-port setup. The shared helper drains OBF before the mouse reset later disables the keyboard, so a pending scan byte can be read and discarded during setup. The helper also returns void after exhausting its bounded IBF wait, and its write wrappers continue issuing commands. Qualified the latter's device effect as hardware-dependent. No key, controller wait or write timeout was exercised.

Keyboard event-ring follow-up (OD34 restored, 2026-10-14): confirmed the 128-slot ring has only a write cursor and per-open read cursors; the producer wraps without occupancy/overrun detection, while `KBD_READEVENT` treats equal cursors as empty (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard_intern.h:24,39-40`; `keyboard.c:347-376,608-629`). A full unread lap is indistinguishable from empty and subsequent writes overwrite unread entries. The selected input.device normally keeps one read pending but can stop consuming replies under CMD_STOP; direct keyboard.device clients can also leave the ring unread (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:262-266,482-530`). Restored OD34 as a detailed report entry; no key burst was generated.

PC i8042 keyboard lifecycle recheck (OD2266/OD2335; no additional candidate): traced each `i8042_kbd_controller_task` failure return through `i8042Kbd__Root__New`. Timer/port setup and no-keyboard failures set `LEDSigBit` to -1 before the constructor invokes the superclass Dispose method directly; these branches do not enter `i8042Kbd__Root__Dispose` or pass an uninitialized IRQ token to `KrnRemIRQHandler`. By contrast, after a successful controller reset the task may store a NULL `KrnAddIRQHandler` result and still signal successful construction, which is the already-detailed OD2266 path to EK815. Successful construction followed by disposal leaves the worker and timer request alive as OD2335 records. No controller or allocation failure was run.

xHCI root-hub interrupt queue follow-up (OD2782, 2026-10-14): rechecked the `hu_RHIOQueue` consumer against all same-list mutators and selected ExecSMP semantics. `cmdIntXFerRootHub` appends and `cmdAbortIO` removes under local `Disable`; `uhwCheckRootHubChanges` drains/removes under local `Disable` from the xHCI completion interrupt as well as other event/task paths. Exec explicitly says this does not serialize other CPUs, and Exec AddTail/Remove update linked pointers without a lock. With a root request already pending, a concurrent BeginIO/AbortIO can race the drain, detaching a queued request or leaving it pending after the change bitmap is cleared. Added OD2782 distinct from OD2778's lost-bitmap update. Selected Poseidon hub interrupt-IN use was already confirmed in the OD2778 caller follow-up; no queue or USB event was run.

input.device Stop/Start caller recheck (OD2516, 2026-10-14): verified Exec `Wait` clears every bit in the supplied wait mask, not only the branch the worker later handles (`rom/exec/wait.c:126-139`). While running, input.device includes all keyboard, gameport and timer reply signals; it handles command messages first, so a simultaneous CMD_STOP sets `Stopped` before the corresponding reply branches, which are skipped. Their one-shot requests are neither dequeued nor resubmitted; the signal is already cleared, and later CMD_START/CMD_RESET changes only `Stopped`. `lowlevel.library` exposes this stop/resume path through `SCON_StopInput` (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/systemcontrola.c:19-56,169-171`); no direct in-tree caller of that tag was found. This confirms the public control-path trigger already described in OD2516; no request or stop sequence was run.

Hosted SDL keyboard/event follow-up (OD2709/OD2713/OD2712/OD2722, 2026-10-14): reread the selected SDL keyboard class, keymap, complete event worker and startup rollback. The keymap sentinel `0xff` is forwarded on both transitions, with the release bit already set, confirming OD2709. The event worker's `active` flag is reinitialized each batch, confirming the separately numbered inactive-window mouse dispatch in OD2713. Startup launches this worker before SDL video initialization (OD2718), and later failure cleanup can remove it without removing its stack-backed VBL interrupt (OD2712); failed mouse-driver registration removes the keyboard HIDD while its cached pointer remains visible to the active event worker (now detailed as GD5048). These are separate triggers/consequences already captured by those findings; no additional SDL keyboard candidate was established. No SDL event or startup failure was induced.

PC timer rearm follow-up (OD1427, 2026-10-14): inspected the IRQ0 handler after the BeginIO race. `TimerInt` calls `Timer0Setup` after processing the MICROHZ list; that helper releases its list read lock before programming the PIT. On ExecSMP, a CPU0 IRQ rearm can therefore snapshot an older head, then be overtaken by a CPU1 BeginIO insertion/rearm, and finally overwrite the shorter PIT delay with its older snapshot. This is the same stale-deadline mechanism as the two-BeginIO interleaving, not a separate ID. No IRQ or timer interleaving was run.

Hosted timer initialization cross-check (2026-10-14): compared the Unix and MinGW selected `Timer_Init` hooks and manifests against common initialization, host timer start, and rollback. Unix starts `setitimer` only after all frequency/period fields are populated; MinGW installs its VBlank server before setting EClock fields, but the shared VBlank handler's `EClockUpdate` is a no-op on this target and no client timer requests are published before the module finishes. Both host timer hooks are the sole arch-specific source in their `kernel-timer` manifests. Existing OD2515/OD2546/OD1878 rate and host-period findings cover the malformed/quantized frequency paths; no additional startup-order defect established. No host timer or init failure was induced.

Envy24HT DMA-stop caller follow-up (OD2756, 2026-10-14): traced the selected AHIRecord executable's input list and recording commands into the driver. AHIRecord enumerates every advertised `AHIDB_Inputs` index and label, sends the selected list index as `AHIC_Input`, then submits `AHIC_Record=TRUE` during start and `FALSE` during `StopSampling` (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:1827-1875,2133-2145,2171-2173`). Envy24HT advertises four inputs for PHASE22 and provides indexed descriptions through `AHIDB_Input` (`main.c:734-752`), so its digital indexes are reachable through this selected recording client. `workbench/tools/AHIRecord/mmakefile.src:7-32` builds the client; `Drivers/Makefile.in:43-57` includes Envy24HT when `HAVE_ASMIO` is set on non-x86_64 hosts. This confirms a maintained UI caller for OD2756; no recording or hardware was used.

Keyboard opener-list SMP follow-up (OD2303, 2026-10-14): re-read `Open` and `Close` together with the selected Raspberry Pi SMP manifests and Exec's `Forbid` contract. Both `AddTail` and traversal/`Remove`/`FreeMem` are protected only by local `Forbid`, so a conforming open can race another unit's close as well as two closes racing each other (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:227-253`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). Exec's CloseDevice contract allows closing a completed request (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:29-40`); the selected ARM and AArch64 boot manifests include keyboard.device and enable ExecSMP for the `smp` variant (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:123-125`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:123-125`; `configure.in:2197`). The detailed finding now includes both interleavings. No device or concurrent operation was run.
Keyboard concurrent first-open candidate recheck (OD2881 withdrawn): although `keyboard.device` has no local lock around its first-open HIDD setup (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:197-217`), both selected Raspberry Pi boot packages include LDDemon (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:182`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:215`). Its `OpenDevice` replacement holds an `LDObjectNode` semaphore across the original Exec OpenDevice call (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:369-391,469-497,533-555`), serializing ordinary opens by device name. No checked-in pre-LDDemon concurrent keyboard opener or direct original-vector caller was established. Therefore the duplicate HIDD-consumer scenario is not retained as a selected-trigger finding; report/index count reduced. OD2303 remains supported for open/close overlap because the selected LDDemon CloseDevice wrapper does not use the same per-object semaphore.


USB hub OOP-allocation caller follow-up (OD2470, 2026-10-14): rechecked the failed-root-allocation return through `OOP_NewObject` and `USBHub::New` into `HIDD_USBHub_OnOff`. The wrapper dereferences the null object's class pointer before dispatch, confirming the existing caller finding. No OOP allocation failure or USB device was induced.

OpenSBI DWI2C ProbeAddress caller recheck (OD2590, 2026-10-14): corrected the earlier claim that no selected caller exists. `battclock.resource` calls the probe with `bb_Addr << 1`, a write-form shifted address; DWI2C discards that direction and queues a one-byte read. The selected M41T11 path later writes an explicit register address and the checked register map establishes no read-to-clear/FIFO side effect, so no RTC corruption is credited. Retained the public HIDD mismatch for write-only or read-side-effect targets. No I²C transaction was run.

HID periodic-report completion recheck (2026-10-14; no duplicate finding): re-read `HidInterrupt` and the selected OHCI/UHCI completion paths. `HidInterrupt` receives only the registered `HidData *`, derives the report ID from the buffer, and passes the configured `hid->buflen` as the parse length (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:65-82`); neither callback input contains a per-completion byte count. OD2340 and OD2341 already cover OHCI and UHCI non-success completions being delivered to HID without status validation. OD1606 separately covers UHCI splitting a report larger than the endpoint packet into multiple TDs and rearming only its first TD. This pass resolves the source-side short-completion path and folds it into OD2066 rather than creating a duplicate: OHCI calls `Cause` for each completed interrupt TD without testing `TD_CC_MASK` or actual length (`ohcidriverclass.c:318-391`); UHCI calls the registered callback when the TD has completed and is not NAKed (`uhciclass.c:131-166`). `HidInterrupt` passes configured `hid->buflen` and the parser does not receive the completion byte count (`hidclass.c:65-82`); the reusable buffer is not cleared between transfers. Thus an error or short completion can supply partial/current plus prior/zero bytes as a full report. No hardware transfer was run; exact controller completion behavior remains unverified. No USB device or transfer was run.

IPMI SDR traversal follow-up (OD2784, 2026-10-14): traced the selected `C:IPMI SENSORS` call through `DoSensors` and the HIDD `SendCommand` response length. The record loop detects only a self-link or `0xFFFF`; a multi-record next-ID cycle has no count/visited bound and repeats. OD2784 is restored in the report as a conditional CLI hang for malformed BMC repository data. No controller was queried.

OD2365 PCI-claim rollback recheck (2026-10-14): verified the selected timer-open failure before superclass object allocation, then followed NULL through HW_AddDriver temporary-node cleanup. PCIDevice Obtain persists a separate owner string that only Release clears; NVME_Probe drops the enumerator record after RemHead and frees/releases neither on failure. OD2365 remains confirmed. No controller or PCI state was changed.

SDL bitmap coordinate-bounds follow-up (2026-10-14; no finding): the SDL `PutPixel`/`GetPixel` methods compute direct offsets without checking coordinates, consistent with the HIDD method contract (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1361-1380` states PutPixel does not check coordinates). The selected graphics.library `ReadPixel`/`WritePixel` caller routes through `do_pixel_func`; `GetRPClipRectangleForBitMap` clips to the bitmap rectangle because `BITMAP_CLIPPING` is enabled (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:41`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:236-281,1064-1082`). Thus the normal selected public caller does not pass out-of-bitmap coordinates to the SDL offset calculation. Direct OOP callers must satisfy the method's coordinate contract; bounds review for other pixel-operation inputs and surface lifetime remains open. Source-only.

SDL framebuffer-surface lifetime recheck (OD2799, 2026-10-14): followed `SDLGfx::Show` through `SDL_SetVideoMode` and the later `OOP_SetAttrs` that replaces surface/geometry/pixfmt, then checked every bitmap method's use of `bmdata->surface`. The mode call uses `sdl_lock`; direct pixel paths and the surface-field replacement do not share that semaphore, and direct pixel methods cache `pixels`/`pitch` before their optional SDL surface lock. The graphics view-change semaphore does not guard ordinary drawing (see GD4061 for the related but distinct BitMap HIDD/pixfmt metadata swap). SDL 1.2 upstream `SDL_video.c` notes that a backend may free the previous mode surface; invalidation is backend-dependent, so OD2799 is conditional/medium-confidence for its stale-pointer consequence. No display or drawing operation was raced. Source-only.

PC i8042 mouse IRQ-allocation follow-up (OD2802, 2026-10-14): traced `KrnAddIRQHandler`'s NULL-on-allocation-failure return through mouse reset and the parent HIDD constructor. The reset path still sets the controller's mouse-interrupt bit and enables the mouse; the constructor then rejects and disposes the object because `data->irq` is NULL. The preceding keyboard handler leaves mouse-tagged output-buffer bytes unread. This is distinct from OD2266's absent-mouse/null-removal route and OD2334's timer-request leak; its controller-level effect is qualified because hardware/PIC behavior was not exercised. Manifest `arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/mmakefile.src:7-15` selects the mouse implementation. Source-only; no runtime or allocation fault injection.

PC i8042 retained reset-callback failure-path follow-up (OD2803 restored in the detailed report, 2026-10-14): traced a detected mouse with failed IRQ-node allocation through `i8042_mouse_reset`, the mouse class's NULL return, `HW_AddDriver`, `i8042_Init`'s open-count result and generated failed-InitLib cleanup. If no other i8042 driver succeeds, the module unloads while `cs_ResetInt` remains on Exec's reset-handler list; Exec later invokes the stored module callback and data pointer. This is separate from OD1560's failed-init cleanup with driver instances already registered. Source-only; no module load failure or reset.

IPMI short-record follow-up (OD2804, 2026-10-14): rechecked SDR chunk accumulation through the post-loop type dispatch. A zero-byte chunk breaks the read loop but does not skip parsing; the parser accepts `offset >= 8`, then reads `rec[12]` and `rec[13]` without verifying those bytes arrived. This is an uninitialized local-buffer read affecting sensor-type and threshold output, not an out-of-array access; the guarded `rec[7]` sensor number is received. No controller was queried.

Timer EClock client-boundary recheck (OD1416; 2026-10-14, no new finding): the source-wide `UNIT_ECLOCK` hit in `workbench/libs/camd/camdwait.c:66-75` is under `#ifndef __AROS__`; the AROS branch opens `UNIT_VBLANK` and later submits `TR_ADDREQUEST` on that request (`:101-105`). The selected controller HIDD opens `UNIT_ECLOCK` solely to retain the device base and call `ReadEClock`, with an explicit comment that its request is never sent (`workbench/hidds/controller/controller_init.c:56-68`; `controller_reading.c:28`), then closes it on expunge (`controller_init.c:98`). The Amiga keyboard HIDD also uses `ReadEClock` with its separate m68k timer implementation. These selected paths do not supply the generic unsupported asynchronous-unit trigger; OD1416 remains scoped to clients that submit `TR_ADDREQUEST` on `UNIT_ECLOCK` or `UNIT_WAITECLOCK` to a target using the generic implementation. No timer request was submitted.

Poseidon USB class release follow-up (2026-10-14, OD2812 added): traced selected bootkeyboard, bootmouse, generic HID, and egalaxtouch release callbacks through Poseidon device/interface release and each worker’s abort/wait cleanup. `psdAbortPipe` silently returns if its synthetic abort-request allocation fails; the worker then waits without timeout on the still-pending request and cannot clear its task pointer. Poseidon calls these hooks under the device write lock. No allocation failure or device release was induced. Other HCD completion behavior remains open.


MassStorage generated-wrapper follow-up (2026-10-14; no new finding): read every `storage_stubs.c` method wrapper and reconciled its IID/offset, message layout, and return conversion against `mstorage.h`, `mstorage.conf`, local class methods, and selected task/device callers. SDIO readiness timeout caller trace (OD2853): `SDIOEnableFunction`'s 50-iteration loop exits with `err == 0` when CMD52 transactions succeed but the requested `CCCR_IO_READY` bit never appears; it sets an error only when a CMD52 read fails (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdio/sdio_init.c:1422-1445`). Selected `bwfm_init` checks function 1's return and immediately begins backplane setup (`:541-551`; read helper `bwfm_init.c:113-125`), so the false success passes an unready function into initialization. The later function-2 call ignores the return independently; OD2853 is scoped to the erroneous readiness result at function 1. No card or timeout was exercised. Source-only.

BWFM data-function enable caller trace (OD2854): after observing firmware-ready, `BWFMStartFirmware` calls `SDIOEnableFunction(2)` without testing the result, leaves `err == 0`, and returns success (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1606-1618,1647-1680`). `load_firmware` converts that result directly into `fw_loaded = TRUE` (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:778-781`), which bypasses later retries. This CMD52-error path is separate from OD2853's SDIO function-1 readiness loop. No hardware error was induced. Source-only.

BWFM SDIO byte-helper and host-IRQ registration recheck (2026-10-14; no additional in-tree finding): traced `SDIOReadByte`/`SDIOWriteByte` result handling through every selected `bwfm_read_1`/`bwfm_write_1` call. The byte API intentionally exposes no write status and returns its initialized zero byte if CMD52 fails; selected clock bring-up checks the resulting clock bits and ALP timeout, so no separate selected consequence was established in this pass. `sdio_do_probe` marks the card present before installing its host IRQ node and does not reject a NULL `KrnAddIRQHandler` result, but the selected BWFM device defines `BWFM_USE_IRQ` as 0 and relies on its adaptive polling RX pump (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:48-58,454-485,530-580`); the unregistered IRQ therefore does not break the checked in-tree receive path. External direct SDIO interrupt clients, alternate BWFM interrupt configurations and hardware behavior remain open. No transport error or IRQ allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

SDIO public function-number bound review (OD2855): `sdio.conf` exports `uint32_t func` for CMD52/CMD53 and enable/block-size operations without an accompanying range contract (`:16-21`). The selected implementation shifts it directly by 28 into the command argument (`sdio_init.c:922-932,958-997`); the 3-bit field shares bit 31 with `SDIO_ARG_RW_WRITE` (`sdio_private.h:58-65`). An invalid `func=8` on `SDIOReadByte` therefore sets the write bit while encoding function 0, with zero write data. Selected BWFM uses only functions 1 and 2; no invalid in-tree caller was found. No command was issued. Source-only.

Other Drivers USB rescan signal-mask correction (2026-10-15): withdrew OD822 after tracing the exact Sam440 signal allocation sequence. `hub_port` retains signal 16, and `USBTimer` reacquires 17, so the raw `sigmask` value 17 overlaps the zero-initialized hub interrupt bit 0. EMAC shared-open follow-up (2026-10-15): restored OD2408, OD2461, and OD2462 after tracing accepted shared opens and close handling through EMAC start/stop, Exec OpenDevice/CloseDevice waiting, and generic timer queue insertion. OD2408 is conditional on multiple openers and captures unconditional stop plus missing open-count decrement; OD2461 is the distinct repeated-start path; OD2462 requires overlapping starts and reuse of the single per-unit timer request while it is queued. EMAC failed-open rollback follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2408): traced the opener-allocation failure after `eu_OpenCount++` through the driver's `CloseDevice` call and Exec CloseDevice dispatch. Because the request still has its device/unit, driver Close invokes `EMAC_Stop` even though no opener was registered; this can stop an existing shared client and leaves the count increment unreverted. Expanded OD2408 to include this selected failure path. No allocation failure or hardware was induced. Source-only.

HID singleton-root construction recheck (2026-10-15; OD1456 restored): re-read keyboard and mouse singleton constructors, generic HW root allocation, OOP_NewObject locking boundary, selected PC i8042 driver registration, and HIDD consumer attachment through each class-static cached root. Other Drivers USB hub timer-state recheck (2026-10-15; OD819 expanded, no new ID): traced `hub_process` across its post-timer retry state. When a bit-0 hub interrupt overlaps the erroneous decimal-17 `sigmask`, `USBTimerDone` consumes the reply and frees signal 17; `hub_process` does not clear `sigmask` after that call and only assigns it again if `hub_explore` returns true (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:684-718`; `misc.c:143-150`). If exploration returns false, a later bit-0 hub interrupt still passes `sigset & sigmask` and invokes `USBTimerDone` with an empty reply port. `WaitPort` loops on the empty list and waits on the port's old signal (`rom/exec/waitport.c:62-85`), so the hub worker can remain blocked. Folded this stale-mask consequence into OD819 alongside the missed timer wake; same root mask/state bug, so no duplicate ID. No hub or timer was run. Source-only.

Other Drivers USB class-registration recheck (2026-10-15): qualified the `extClassList` race note and restored the low-memory finding as OD2864. `MOD_NAME_STRING` is generated from the module name and `hidd` suffix (`tools/genmodule/writeinclibdefs.c:80-100`); selected HID and MassStorage modules are named `hid.hidd` and `mstorage.hidd` (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/{HID,MassStorage}/mmakefile.src`). The selected startup `ScanDirectory` stores the matching filename as `ec_ShortName`, before the parent loads those libraries, so their normal `AddClass` calls find an existing record and do not append. The earlier ledger claim that those initializers establish a concurrent AddTail writer was overstated. `AddClass` remains an unsynchronized public writer for a name absent from the list, and `ScanDirectory` remains an unsynchronized writer, but no maintained concurrent mutating caller pair was established; keep OD2201 as a conditional external/public-call lead, not as verified selected overlap. Independently, startup scanning checks the record allocation but not either following string allocation before `CopyMem`, while `AddClass` checks none of its three allocations. The scanner runs before USB process startup acknowledgment; OD2864 now details the resulting conditional fault/hang. No allocation failure or concurrency was run. Source-only.


Other Drivers Rhine DMA cache-address recheck (2026-10-15; OD2800 restored): traced TX/RX descriptor allocations through `AllocDMAMemHook` to Prometheus `Prm_AllocDMABuffer` and confirmed per-slot pointers refer to separately allocated rings, while later cache-maintenance calls pass the inline pointer arrays (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:178-227,255-269,1018-1027,1447-1449,1515-1516,1551-1552`; `device.h:146-149`; `pci.c:675-694`; `workbench/libs/prometheus/board.c:571-600`). The selected Rhine target is in the Workbench m68k network-card aggregate (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:30-33,45-52`), and the m68k 68040/060 cache helpers apply maintenance to the supplied address and size (`arch/m68k-all/exec/cachepredma_.S:83-125`; `cachepostdma_.S:105-139`). `MEMF_31BIT` does not prove cacheability, so stale descriptors remain conditional on the platform mapping. Added OD2800 with that qualification. No hardware or runtime behavior was tested. Source-only.


Other Drivers Rhine request-dispatch recheck (2026-10-15; OD409 restored and OD2801 added): read all 1,547 lines of `workbench/devs/networks/rhine/request.c` and traced `ServiceRequest` through `DevBeginIO`'s unit semaphore and the tracker list structures. `CmdTrackType` does not stop after `TypeTracker` allocation failure; successful later snapshot allocation reaches `CopyMem(tracker, ...)` with a null source (OD409). It also increments or publishes the shared reference before duplicate-opener validation and snapshot allocation, with no rollback on either rejection/failure; `CmdUntrackType` only decrements when an opener snapshot exists (OD2801). `TypeTracker` and `TypeStats` share the copied prefix, with `user_count` only after `stats` (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/ethernet.h:43-58`); the copy size itself does not overrun the source. No tracker allocation, duplicate request, or runtime behavior was induced. Other request-client and completion-lifecycle contracts remain pending. Source-only.


Other Drivers Rhine type-statistics follow-up (OD410): compared packet-type key formation across `CmdTrackType`, `CmdUntrackType`, `CmdGetTypeStats` and `FindTypeStats` (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/request.c:735-737,834-836,908-916`; `unit.c:843-860`). Other Drivers Rhine PCI-construction rollback recheck (2026-10-15; OD418 restored and OD2802 added): traced `CreatePCIUnit` registration order and failure cleanup through the selected AROS reset callback, PCI HIDD interrupt dispatch, Rhine wrapper helpers, and `DeleteUnit`/`DeletePCIUnit`. A failed `AddPCIIntServer` does not prevent `AddResetCallback`; the selected Exec implementation always enqueues successfully, but construction failure calls `DeleteUnit` directly and leaves the reset node pointing at the freed unit (OD418). Separately, an allocation failure partway through the five `WrapInt` calls takes the same cleanup path without unwrapping earlier successful calls; AROS init sets the wrapper code nonnull and normal deletion explicitly frees those records (OD2802). No IRQ or memory failure was induced and no reset was run. PCI interrupt-controller behavior and hardware lifecycle remain unverified. Source-only.


Other Drivers Rhine first-open SMP recheck (OD2865): traced `OpenDevice` through `DevOpen`, `GetUnit`, `GetPCIUnit`, `CreatePCIUnit` and `AllocCard` into Prometheus owner acquisition. `GetPCIUnit` has no lock or post-failure rescan around list lookup and publication (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/pci.c:150-166,184-205,225-287`; `device.c:198-222,559-572`). `OpenDevice`'s list lock is released before calling the device vector; its ExecSMP `Forbid` applies only on the current processor (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:93-105,120-135`; `exec_locks.h:46-50`; `forbid.c:53-60`). A same-unit first-open overlap can therefore have both callers miss, with Prometheus ownership admitting only one and the losing `DevOpen` returning `IOERR_OPENFAIL` without rescanning (`board.c:275-304`; `pcideviceclass.c:488-509`). No concurrent open was run; timing remains conditional. Source-only.


Rhine build-selection ledger correction (2026-10-15): corrected the timer row's prior claim that the card aggregate edges were commented out. The active `#MM-` parent rules select the card aggregate for i386, x86_64, m68k and PPC; the card aggregate includes Rhine (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:30-33,45-53`). This is active MetaMake syntax, distinct from the disabled `##MM-` form used in `workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-5` and throughout optional dependency declarations. The local Rhine `%build_prog` supplies its source list (`rhine/mmakefile.src:8-11`). Consequently selected Rhine findings remain in scope; via-rhine remains the separate unreachable target. Source-only.

VirtIO used-ring ID-width follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2867): re-read the selected queue header and full completion loop. `virtq_used_elem.id` is ULONG (32-bit), while the local `head` is UWORD; the `head < q_Size` guard therefore cannot reject values whose high 16 bits are nonzero and low bits name an active slot. Such a response clears that request’s InUse flag, frees its descriptor chain and replies early. Corrected the prior ledger statement that the ID was bounds-checked before narrowing. This remains conditional on a malformed device response. No device or I/O was run. Source-only.

VirtIO split-ring allocation and device-size check (2026-10-15; no additional candidate): rechecked `vq_alloc_size` arithmetic and ring offsets against the selected fixed `virtio_alloc_queue(dev, 0, 128)` call and `virtio_hw_setup_queue`. For 128 entries the allocator uses 12 KiB with descriptor, available-ring and used-ring regions starting on successive 4 KiB boundaries; the AVAIL/USED_EVENT allowance adds space rather than shortening either ring. Queue setup rejects an absent or smaller device queue before publishing the configured size and addresses (`virtio_hw.c:200-230`). The generic allocator accepts larger `int` sizes but has only the selected fixed-size caller; no in-tree overflow trigger was established. No queue or device was run. Source-only.

VirtIO PCI capability mapping contract recheck (2026-10-15; no additional confirmed finding): compared `virtio_hw_map` and queue-notify pointer construction with the common PCI HIDD contract and selected PCIPC/RISC-V PCIDT methods. `BaseN` exposes the configured BAR address; `SizeN` exposes the probed size, while `MapPCI(PCIAddress, Length)` performs the CPU mapping/translation (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:805-884`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:157-178`; `pci.conf:62`). `virtio_get_bar` uses only `BaseN`; capability `offset`/`length` and BAR size are not checked before pointer formation, and notify offset/multiplier are not bounded against the mapped aperture (`virtio_hw.c:25-41,63-104,200-230`). PCIPC maps BAR ranges outside its identity-mapped window, and RISC-V PCIDT translates its 64-bit aperture (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:218-246`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:842-894`). This corroborates existing OD2393 for raw BAR address translation; the unchecked malformed/out-of-range capability case remains an open validation item because no defect for a conforming device was established. No PCI device or hardware was exercised. Source-only.

VirtIO reset and feature-state tail recheck (2026-10-15; no additional confirmed finding): read the remaining `virtio_hw.c` reset, 64-bit feature read/write, FEATURES_OK negotiation, queue registration, DRIVER_OK transition and block-config capture (`:121-287`) against the constructor and bus-start callers. VirtIO confirmed-candidate report reconciliation (2026-10-15; superseded stale missing-heading list): rechecked current detailed report headings for OD2362, OD2363, OD2390, OD2391, OD2392, OD2393, OD2396, OD2446, OD2460, OD2542, OD2604, OD2704, OD2805 and OD2842. VirtIO request-boundary restoration (2026-10-15; OD2390 and OD2396): reread the complete `virtio_blk_rw` validator and request construction (`virtio_io.c:29-86`). The guard checks only the starting logical block against `au_High`; it does not account for request length, confirming a request crossing the last block is submitted. Length alignment is checked, but byte-offset alignment is not; `off64 >> 9` silently drops low offset bits before queue submission. Restored both findings to the detailed report and index, explicitly recording that normal in-tree unit submission is currently unreachable because OD2541 prevents the selected constructor from registering a storage bus. No caller with an unaligned offset, device or I/O was run. The other coverage-ledger-only VirtIO candidates remain subject to individual reachability and contract review.

VirtIO AbortIO contract restoration (2026-10-15; OD2362): compared the device vector with Exec's AbortIO contract and the queue completion owner. The vector returns zero despite declaring cancellation unsupported, while the request remains in its slot and completes only through the used-ring path; Exec specifies zero for a successful abort and `IOERR_ABORTED` in the request. Restored this mismatch to the detailed report and index. The existing selected controller registration failure OD2541 currently prevents normal in-tree request submission; no external abort client was established, so the active reachability limitation is explicit. No device or request was run.

VirtIO CMD_UPDATE/FLUSH contract restoration (2026-10-15; OD2363): traced the no-feature branch from `CMD_UPDATE` through `virtio_blk_flush`, which returns with success and submits no request. Confirmed selected AFS describes this command as disk sync and returns success; SFS and NTFS also issue it. Checked OASIS VirtIO 1.2 §5.2.6.2: absent offered FLUSH, persistence of completed writes is permitted but not required. Restored the conditional false-sync finding with explicit persistence and OD2541 reachability qualifications. No VirtIO device or filesystem action was run.

VirtIO split-ring publication barrier restoration (2026-10-15; OD2391): compared `virtio_submit_blk_request` with VirtIO 1.2 §2.7.13.3.1. The descriptor and available-ring writes are followed only by an empty inline asm compiler barrier before the device-visible available-index update; the required architecture hardware barrier is absent. Confirmed the OpenSBI RISC-V manifest selects the VirtIO device and that Zicbom cache-maintenance fences, when installed, occur before descriptor construction and do not order these later writes. Restored the finding with the OD2541 reachability qualification; no RISC-V device or I/O was run.

VirtIO configuration-change restoration (2026-10-15; OD2392): followed the PCI ISR byte through the interrupt handler and task, then traced block capacity from its one-time constructor snapshot into the published unit bounds. The handler discards ISR bits and the worker drains only used entries; no config reread or unit update exists. OASIS VirtIO 1.2 §3.2.1 and PCI ISR status requirements confirm configuration-change notification semantics. Restored the conditional live-capacity-change finding, qualified by OD2541 preventing normal selected bus startup. No device, resize or I/O was run.

VirtIO SIZE_MAX request-limit restoration (2026-10-15; OD2446): traced offered-feature negotiation, config reads, DOS `DE_MAXTRANSFER`, request construction and descriptor mapping. The driver negotiates SIZE_MAX but never reads `cfg->size_max`; it advertises 2 MiB, then maps the full I/O request as one data segment without splitting. OASIS VirtIO 1.2 defines the field as the maximum size of any segment. Restored the conditional over-limit finding, with OD2541 reachability qualification. No device or request was run.

VirtIO read-only status restoration (2026-10-15; OD2460): traced negotiated RO into `dev_ReadOnly` and the read/write guard, then compared `TD_PROTSTATUS` with selected AFS, SFS and PFS3 handling. The command reports writable (`io_Actual=0`) for every device, while those filesystems interpret zero as writable/validated and writes are subsequently rejected. Restored to the report and index; OD2541 still blocks the normal selected bus path. No device or filesystem operation was run.

VirtIO modern used-length restoration (2026-10-15; OD2704): rechecked `virtio_process_used` from used-element read to IORequest reply. It discards `ulen` and reports `vr_DataLength` for every successful completion. OASIS VirtIO 1.2 §2.7.8.3 says drivers must not assume data beyond used length; the selected transport requires VERSION_1, excluding the legacy interface exception. Restored the conditional short-read candidate and the OD2541 reachability caveat. No device or I/O was run.

VirtIO change-request lifecycle restoration (2026-10-15; OD2604): traced selected NTFS `SendIO(TD_ADDCHANGEINT)` and cleanup `DoIO(TD_REMCHANGEINT)`/free through VirtIO BeginIO and Exec list primitives. The first call leaves the node pending in `au_IOs`; the second re-adds the same node, rejects the quick removal command, removes once, then NTFS frees it. Later list insertion/removal follows the dangling request node. Restored with the OD2541 normal-startup limitation. No NTFS mount or cleanup ran.

VirtIO blk_size geometry restoration (2026-10-15; OD2805): followed the optional config field through `dev_BlkSize`, capacity division, floor-log2 shift, DOS block size and request alignment. A non-power-of-two value such as 1536 makes unit bounds count 1536-byte blocks while requests/DOS geometry use 1024-byte blocks, exposing only two thirds of the underlying capacity. OASIS VirtIO 1.2 does not impose a power-of-two constraint on the block `blk_size` field. Restored with the explicit non-power-of-two response trigger and OD2541 reachability qualification. No device or I/O was run.

Linux hosted mouse button follow-up (OD1433): rechecked the selected EV_KEY producer through LinuxMouse, the mouse proxy, gameport buffering and queued reads. Button-event x/y are uninitialized in the producer and copied unchanged into gameport event data. Added OD1433; the Intuition path does not establish pointer movement from those coordinates, so impact is scoped to consumers reading gameport button-event coordinates. No event/read was run. Source-only.

Linux hosted keyboard autorepeat follow-up (OD1868): traced host EV_KEY value 2 through Linux input task and LinuxKbd into input.device. Value 2 is forwarded as an unmarked down event; input.device aborts an active repeat timer and starts the initial threshold again, while its own generated repeats alone receive IEQUALIFIER_REPEAT. Added OD1868 with cadence/settings qualification. No host event was run. Source-only.

Linux hosted horizontal-wheel follow-up (OD2737): reread EV_REL translation and the shared gameport wheel consumer. The selected producer forwards REL_X, REL_Y and REL_WHEEL but drops REL_HWHEEL; gameport supports horizontal direction via the mouse event x field and RAWKEY_NM_WHEEL_LEFT/RIGHT. Added OD2737 scoped to Linux gameport clients. No host event/read was run. Source-only.

Linux hosted media-key follow-up (OD2735): verified KEY_COMPOSE is 127, common Linux media transport codes are 163-166, and the Linux input task rejects codes above KEY_COMPOSE before its fixed 128-entry table. AROS defines media raw keys and the Android backend maps corresponding transport keys. Added OD2735; no host event was run. Source-only.

Linux hosted enumeration failure follow-up (OD2254): verified negative EVIOCGBIT results propagate unchanged from UnixIO ioctl. LinuxInput enumeration immediately continues without incrementing the node index or closing the descriptor, so the same node is reopened indefinitely and later nodes are not considered. Restored OD2254 with the host-query trigger qualification. No ioctl failure or startup was induced. Source-only.

Linux hosted keyboard capability follow-up (OD1434): verified enumeration requires both EV_KEY and EV_REP to mark CAP_KEYBOARD, while the worker accepts EV_KEY code events independently. A key-event node without repeat capability is discarded before its key events can be read; descriptor leakage for discarded nodes is OD2255. Restored OD1434 with the external capability trigger qualified. No host node was tested. Source-only.

USB MassStorage unknown-command follow-up (OD2823): traced HandleIO status initialization and default dispatch. Commands above HD_SCSICMD that fall outside the NSCMD_TD_READ64..FORMAT64 range return with io_Error still zero and bypass cmd_Invalid; 0xC004 is one such value. Restored OD2823 as a direct unsupported-command false success. No request/device was used. Source-only.

USB MassStorage inline completion follow-up (OD2820): confirmed SendIO clears IOF_QUICK, while immediate commands go directly to HandleIO and neither BeginIO nor HandleIO replies them; the unit task ReplyMsg path only sees queued slow requests. Existing checked-in geometry caller uses DoIO, so documented trigger is a direct asynchronous caller. Restored OD2820. No request was issued. Source-only.

USB MassStorage AbortIO follow-up (OD2821): compared the device vector with Exec AbortIO contract and pending unit-task handling. The vector returns zero but neither cancels nor marks the request aborted; queued slow requests remain for normal task processing. Direct caller search found the MassStorage task aborting timer.device requests only, so recorded this as an external/direct-client trigger. Restored OD2821. No request was aborted. Source-only.

USB MassStorage device-init allocation follow-up (OD2822): traced init priority order from Storage_Init pool creation to StorageDev_Init. AllocPooled can return NULL, but the initializer adds the function-table prefix and immediately writes through the adjusted result without a check, then returns success. Added OD2822 scoped to device-object allocation failure. No OOM condition was induced. Source-only.

USB MassStorage NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY follow-up (OD2844): verified the handler writes the full result without checking io_Length and compared the minimum-length checks in input.device and RAM disk. Restored OD2844, cross-referencing DISK-102 as the same validation class in a different driver. No request was sent. Source-only.

UIKit native-bridge null-release and caller recheck (2026-10-15; no finding): traced every local `native_api.m` bridge caller through UIKit HIDD startup/disposal and Quartz bitmap construction. A null bitmap context is passed to `CGContextRelease` during the existing failure unwind; Apple's Core Graphics contract states this is permitted. `CGColorSpaceRelease` has the same null tolerance. `OpenDisplay(0)` failure is checked by the HIDD constructor, and the bitmap view bridge has no selected caller. Screen/window, pixel-layout and event-loop host behavior remain runtime-dependent and were not exercised. Source-only.

UserGroup passwd/group shared iterator reset follow-up (OD2879; 2026-10-15): confirmed that legacy `setpwent` and `setgrent` both write one base-wide `setent_done` despite independent per-unit NetInfo cursors. After one database sets the flag, first iteration of the other skips `CMD_RESET`; its newly opened cursor remains NULL and `ReadCmd` reports not found. Since the shared flag stays set, subsequent reads remain on that uninitialized cursor until the corresponding explicit `set*ent` reset. Conversely, `endpwent`/`endgrent` clear the same flag while closing only their own unit, so the next read of the other already-open stream resets and repeats its cursor from the beginning. The security-backed wrappers are separate. Added OD2879 to the detailed report. No database iteration was run; source-only.

ATA controller expunge caller follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2899): rechecked the `ata_expunge` success branch against selected `HW_RemoveDriver`, OOP disposal dispatch, ATA's overridden Root::Dispose, and Root disposal's allocation free. `HW_RemoveDriver` already disposes the controller and its override unlinks/stops it; `ata_expunge` then removes/dereferences the freed node, calls superclass Dispose again, and FreeMem's instance data. This occurs only when the controller's child-driver list is empty, so HWRoot permits removal. No controller teardown was run. The post-registration controller cleanup slice is resolved; broader ATA caller/platform coverage remains open.

The finding's expunge trigger includes retained controllers with attached buses. Source-only.

ATA controller child-bus teardown follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2899 caller trace strengthened): followed storage `AddBus`/`RemoveBus` into ATA `SetUpBus`, the generic `HW_RemoveDriver` disposal path, and ATA controller/bus `Root::Dispose`. `RemoveBus` explicitly returns FALSE (`ata_controllerclass.c:115-125`); `ata_expunge` does not call it, while generic driver removal invokes controller disposal directly. The controller disposer stops its daemon and delegates to StorageController/Root without enumerating or disposing child buses; the bus objects own reset callbacks and PIO/DMA interface buffers (`ata_busclass.c:589-608`). This confirms the attached-bus lifetime consequence already recorded in OD2899; no separate candidate added. No bus or teardown was run. Source-only.

Unix serial unit disposal failure-path follow-up (OD2888, 2026-10-15): traced `UXSerUnit::New`'s UnixIO-object allocation failure into `OOP_DisposeObject` and `UXSerUnit::Dispose`. Root.New allocates zeroed instance storage (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:119`); before any descriptor is opened, `unixio` remains NULL and `filedescriptor` remains 0, while Dispose tests only `filedescriptor != -1` and calls `Hidd_UnixIO_CloseFile` (`arch/all-unix/hidd/serial/SerialUnitClass.c:98-106,251-272`). Thus the partial-construction cleanup attempts dispatch through a NULL UnixIO receiver. If construction returns NULL, NewUnit also publishes the NULL slot and used bit without rollback; OD2888 now records both consequences under the shared allocation-failure trigger. No allocation failure or OOP method was induced. Source-only.


NetInfo LDDemon expunge ordering recheck (OD1902, 2026-10-15): traced the selected `LDFlush` device sweep into `RemDevice` and the generated expunge vector. LDDemon holds `Forbid`; NetInfo's successful `DevExpunge` uses `ReplyMsg` to queue the death message but returns without joining the worker, and generated expunge removes/frees the base before `RemDevice` returns. On a single CPU the worker cannot consume that message until after LDDemon's `Permit`, so its cleanup accesses freed instance storage. If `AttemptSemaphore(nid_Lock)` fails, DevExpunge still returns TRUE without queuing shutdown; ExecSMP can also overlap the worker and base teardown. Updated OD1902 to remove the unnecessary SMP-only timing qualification. No driver was loaded or expunged. Source-only.

RISC-V DWMAC device-tree PHY selection (2026-10-15; OD2900): traced `dwmac_phyaddress` through DWMAC probe and unit PHY initialization. The reader ignores the MAC's standard `phy-handle` and chooses the first MDIO child `reg`, which misselects a non-first attached PHY or rejects initialization if the first address is empty. The driver is selected by the RISC-V Workbench network aggregate; no target DTB or hardware was available. Report/index count is now 254 OD. Coverage remains open. Source-only.

RISC-V DWMAC/FDT caller follow-up (2026-10-15): checked the full shared FDT parser contract used by DWMAC and traced `FDT_GetReg` through discovery. The depth-limited ancestor lookup and checked-tuple arithmetic are already recorded as EK285/EK779, so no duplicate Other Drivers entries were added. DWMAC's own candidate remains OD2900; no RISC-V board DT source/blob is present to establish an affected deployed PHY ordering. Updated the file ledger to close the parser/caller slice while leaving firmware topology open. Source-only.

RISC-V DWMAC clock-specifier follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2901): traced `clock-names` indexing through the raw `clocks` cell lookup and MDIO divider selection. Because provider-specific `#clock-cells` arguments occupy cells between phandles, an earlier clock with arguments shifts the target entry away from `clocks[index]`. The target firmware topology is unavailable, so the candidate remains conditional. Source-only.

DWMAC unit-create PHY error path recheck (2026-10-15; no new candidate): traced the ignored `DWMAC_PHYInit` result through unit creation, admin-online handling and periodic `DWMAC_PHYGetLink` polling. A responding PHY is required by library init; the unit's administrative online state is separate from negotiated link, and polling can report link state later. The ignored transient reset/autonegotiation failure remains a concern under hardware failure, but no independent incorrect API result beyond unavailable physical link was established, so no report entry was added. No PHY or interface was operated. Source-only.

DWMAC non-coherent DMA cache follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2902): compared the driver's `DWMAC_SYNC`/ring ownership paths with selected RISC-V `CacheClearE` and Zicbom DMA hooks. The driver uses only CacheClearE for descriptors/RX buffers and does not prepare packet buffers or complete device writes with CachePreDMA/CachePostDMA; selected CacheClearE fences but does not maintain data-cache lines. The driver comment assumes a coherent MAC port, so affected platform topology remains unverified. No network traffic or DMA was run. Source-only.

e1000 shutdown signal and worker-lifetime recheck (2026-10-15; OD2436 restored to detailed report): traced `AllocSignal` return values through the scheduler's shifted Wait set, unshifted shutdown test, and DeleteUnit's unshifted Signal call. Exec returns a signal bit number, but Signal/Wait operate on masks. DeleteUnit also frees the unit and hardware state immediately without joining the worker, whose shutdown branch still uses those fields. The x86 PC e1000 manifest is selected; no unit was expunged. Counts now include this restored candidate. Source-only.

e1000 scheduler private-port failure follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2437 restored to detailed report): verified both `CreateMsgPort` results are unchecked. A missing reply port reaches `WaitPort(NULL)` after the parent has received a reply with a null reply port; a missing input port faults while constructing the wait mask after the startup handshake. In both cases unit creation treats the handshake as success. No allocation failure or unit startup was induced. Source-only.

e1000 delay follow-up (2026-10-15; OD2434 withdrawn, OD2435 restored): checked the selected PC timer's `Timer_Open` and e1000 startup ordering. `UNIT_MICROHZ` is accepted, and e1000 only reaches reset after its separate `UNIT_VBLANK` open succeeds, so the unchecked microsecond open did not establish an independent selected failure path; removed OD2434 as unsupported. Separately restored OD2435 after tracing the unconditional no-op `e1000_msec_delay_irq` into the selected 82541/82543 generic PHY configuration-done callback (documented 10 ms delay), family link-recovery/configuration sequences, and management-host polling. Added the detailed report entry; no NIC or timer request was run. Candidate count increases by one net (258 to 259); coverage remains open. Source-only.

e1000 forced-speed timing caller refinement (2026-10-15; OD2435): traced the 82543 10-Mbps forced-speed branch into the polarity-reversal workaround and the generic PHY link poll. The selected call requests twenty 100-ms intervals, but the helper used for each interval is a no-op; the workaround can return before link-partner parameters settle. Tightened the detailed trigger and consequence. No PHY interaction was run; counts unchanged at 311 GD, 353 EK, and 259 OD. Source-only.
