Realtek8180 RX fragment-pool fallback cross-check (OD3116 expanded, 2026-10-16): confirmed Realtek8180 has the same modulo slot-table/unmodded pointer and index mismatch already recorded for Prism2. Expanded the shared report entry; no duplicate finding retained. No frame or device was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 worker-signal allocation cross-check (OD3106 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced all three UnitTask signal allocations and negative-shift mask construction (`unit.c:2656-2667`) through CreateUnit's no-handshake task publication, contended BeginIO queueing and USB removal signaling. Expanded the existing shared signal-exhaustion finding to include Realtek8180; no separate finding added. No signal exhaustion or task was induced. Source-only.


Realtek8180 RX non-SNAP distribution cross-driver pass (OD3258, 2026-10-16): compared `DistributeRXPacket` with Prism2 and Atheros5000. Realtek initializes `buffer` to the uninitialized scratch `rx_buffer`, copies only in the SNAP branch, and then parses/delivers through that buffer for all frames; the two sibling drivers select `frame` when not SNAP. Added OD3258. No traffic or device was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 RX maximum-frame-size comparison pass (OD3259, 2026-10-16): compared Realtek `DistributeRXPacket`/`CopyPacket` with Prism2 and Atheros5000. Those implementations gate callback delivery on `ETH_MAXPACKETSIZE`; Realtek does not and overwrites the request length with the reconstructed packet length before calling the client RX hook. Added OD3259; caller-side buffer consequences remain conditional on hook behavior. No frame/callback was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 task-creation rollback follow-up (OD3260, 2026-10-16): traced 4-KiB stack allocation through AROS `NewAddTask` failure on ETask allocation into `DeleteUnit` cleanup. The stack is freed only when `UNITF_TASKADDED` is set, which is set after the failing call. Added OD3260. No allocation failure or unit creation was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 partial-construction cleanup cross-check (OD3260 retained; 2026-10-16): verified the selected USB caller supplies every required I/O hook, and its `FreeDMAMemHook` delegates to Exec `FreeVec`; the Exec contract explicitly treats NULL as a no-op (`usb.c:121-133,1047-1052`; `rom/exec/freevec.c:40-49`). Thus partially allocated NULL DMA entries do not add a second cleanup fault on the selected AROS USB route. The `AddUnitTask` failure branch still leaks the separately allocated stack because `DeleteUnit` guards that free with `UNITF_TASKADDED`; see OD3260. No allocation failure or unit lifecycle was run. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB unit-index lookup trace (OD3261, 2026-10-16): traced GetUnit through GetUSBCount, GetUSBUnit, FindUSBUnit and AllocDevice's indexed Poseidon enumeration. FindUSBUnit always returns the list head without comparing the requested index, while GetUSBUnit creates a unit for the requested index only on a NULL lookup. Added OD3261 for multiple compatible adapters. No device or OpenDevice call was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB open/close synchronization cross-check (OD3115 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced `DevOpen` through `GetUnit`/`GetUSBUnit` and the `usb_units` list, plus `CloseUnit` final removal. The list, `open_count` and sharing admission have no shared SMP-safe lock; the earlier verified Exec OpenDevice semantics permit parallel Open vectors on SMP. Expanded the Prism2 concurrency finding to Realtek; separate USB index mismatch is OD3261. No Open/Close or USB device was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 required-library initialization pass (OD3262, 2026-10-16): verified DevInit records but does not validate `OpenLibrary(poseidon_name, ...)`; first unit lookup unconditionally calls Poseidon APIs through `poseidon_base`. A failed Poseidon open therefore leaves the device initialized but makes a later unit-open path call through a NULL library base. Added OD3262. No library failure or device open was induced. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB control-hook error pass (OD3263, 2026-10-16): traced ReadControlPipe/WriteControlPipe through psdDoPipe's explicit disconnected-device error path and all six register hooks. Read hooks discard errors and return uninitialized locals; write hooks discard errors and cannot report failure to adapter callers. Added OD3263. No transfer/device was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 binding-release/last-close lifetime cross-check (OD3264, 2026-10-16): traced DeleteUSBUnitInternal into DeleteUnit task/unit freeing while `context->unit` remains non-NULL, against Poseidon `psdFreeDevice` holding its device lock and synchronously dispatching the registered app-binding release hook. The hook signals `unit->task` without a shared lock; expanded teardown review with OD3264 for the conditional ExecSMP overlap. No device removal/Close was run. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB offline/online RX-pipe lifecycle pass (OD3265, 2026-10-16): traced GoOffline and GoOnline against RXPipeInt, RXInt's ReceiveFrame requeue and the USB ReceiveFrameHook. Offline completions are removed without requeue, GoOffline leaves the hardware/RX pipes active, and GoOnline does not resubmit buffers. Added OD3265 for cumulative RX-pool loss after offline traffic. No transfer/device was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB TX completion status pass (OD3266, 2026-10-16): followed psdSendPipe's disconnected error completion through TXPipeInt and RetireTXSlot. The returned pipe pointer and Poseidon error status are ignored; the request is completed with io_Error zero and success counters incremented. Added OD3266. No transfer/device was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB endpoint-selection pass (OD3267, 2026-10-16): traced the expected bulk endpoint lookups to Poseidon's psdAllocPipe NULL-endpoint semantics. Missing bulk endpoints are accepted as default EP0 control pipes, allowing unit setup to proceed with unusable data transfers. Added OD3267, qualified for descriptor/interface mismatches on compatible IDs. No USB device was enumerated. Source-only.


Realtek8180 soft-interrupt teardown lifetime pass (OD3268, 2026-10-16): traced PA_SOFTINT pipe ports through Exec Cause/SoftIntDispatch and the AROS wrapper allocation/free path. Cleanup aborts pipes, then frees wrapper data without removing queued callbacks or waiting for dispatched callbacks; added OD3268 for the conditional ExecSMP overlap. No device or deletion was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180/Poseidon endpoint-lifetime cross-check (2026-10-16): checked whether the 30 TX and 30 RX pipes against one endpoint each overwrite or prematurely free shared HCD endpoint state. `pPrepareHWEndpoint` creates `pep_IOReq` only when absent and reuses it for later pipes; Realtek teardown aborts and waits every pipe before `FreeDevice` frees the pipes. `psdFreePipe` tears down the shared endpoint context on the first freed pipe, but this occurs only after the pending transfers were drained. No additional active-pipe lifetime defect established in this path. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB removal-callback caller pass (OD3269, 2026-10-16): traced Poseidon ReleaseBindingHook's card-removed signal to UnitTask's unconditional removal_function call. The MEMF_CLEAR unit field has no assignment anywhere in the Realtek8180 sources; USB unit_tags install no such hook. Added OD3269. No device removal/task execution was run. Source-only.


Realtek8180/Poseidon forced hardware-removal caller pass (OD3270, 2026-10-16): expanded the existing OD1600 candidate after tracing Realtek's 61 persistent pipe references and RX requeue into `psdRemHardware`'s forced use-count zeroing, endpoint/configuration destruction, hardware free, and later pipe abort/free paths. OD3269's unset removal callback is a selected in-tree reason cleanup may not release those references. No hardware removal or later close was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 synchronous control-pipe signal/caller check (2026-10-16): considered whether the control port hangs because its action is not assigned. `AllocVec(MEMF_CLEAR)` leaves `mp_Flags` zero, and Exec defines zero as `PA_SIGNAL` (`compiler/include/exec/ports.h:43-48`); each register helper sets `mp_SigTask`/`mp_SigBit` before `psdDoPipe` (`usb.c:785-799,820-834`). Poseidon `ReplyMsg` routes through `InternalPutMsg`, which signals under that default action, and `psdWaitPipe` waits on the same bit (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:50-64`, `putmsg.c:94-106`, `poseidon.library.c:4817-4820`). The selected lifecycle runs initialization before publishing the unit, SANA-II requests on the one UnitTask, and teardown after stopping it; no additional shared-control-pipe concurrent caller established. No hang finding added. Source-only.


Realtek8180 USB complete-source and binding-construction/removal pass (OD3273, 2026-10-16): read the remaining `usb.c` setup, partial-failure cleanup, callback, control-pipe, DMA and frame-hook bodies; traced `psdClaimAppBinding` through Poseidon `pFreeBindings`/`psdHubReleaseDevBinding`. The hook can run after `AllocDevice` releases the base lock but before `CreateUSBUnit` assigns `context->unit`; in that case the callback returns without clearing the binding pointer, while Poseidon frees the binding. Added OD3273 for the subsequent setup/cleanup lifetime hazard. Rechecked null binding cleanup against Poseidon’s null guard. `psdSendPipe` either enqueues an operation or replies a disconnected completion; it returns void, so the driver has no synchronous send-status result to check. The full USB glue local body has now been read. Rechecked the `S2_WRITEMGMT` path through `request.c` and `MgmtTXInt`; it confirms existing OD3256, so no duplicate finding was added. Endpoint completion order, controller/HCD contracts, other `unit.c` caller paths and external unit behavior remain open. No USB operation/device was used. Source-only.


Realtek8180 management TX caller cross-check (OD3256 retained, no new finding, 2026-10-16): traced S2_WRITEMGMT dispatch through the request validation/queue path and `MgmtTXInt`. `CmdWriteMgmt` checks online state but not length; `MgmtTXInt` narrows ULONG `ios2_DataLength` to UWORD, then copies it into the fixed `FRAME_BUFFER_SIZE` slot; representable lengths 1,553–65,535 confirm OD3256. The finding records this overrun; the duplicate proposal from this pass was withdrawn. Other `unit.c` paths and hardware-specific contracts remain open. No request/frame was submitted. Source-only.

Realtek8180 retry-pointer duplicate reconciliation (2026-10-22): OD3116 already covers the same modulo-slot/unmodded-pointer and index defect for Prism2 and Realtek8180. OD3274 is narrowed to the distinct Atheros5000 implementation; this older Realtek note is retained as review history. No frame or device was used. Source-only.

Realtek8180 S2_WRITE copy-bound pass (OD3275 added, 2026-10-16): traced `CmdWrite` validation and queueing to `TXInt`'s shared scratch allocation and configured copy hook (`request.c:428-460`; `unit.c:201-202,2047-2074`; `device.h:132-133`). No driver-side max-length guard precedes the full request-length copy into a 1,514-byte buffer. The result depends on an accepted overlength request and copy-hook behavior; no request or hook was run. Main TX completion, remaining unit functions, selected callers, and adapter contracts remain open. Source-only.

Realtek8180 raw TX minimum-length pass (OD3276 added, 2026-10-16): traced `CmdWrite`'s missing raw-length validation into `TXInt`'s UWORD payload calculation and subsequent frame copy (`request.c:428-453`; `unit.c:2074-2104,2159-2162`; `device.h:130-138,155-157`). Raw lengths below 14 wrap on header subtraction and feed an oversized copy. No request was run. Remaining Realtek unit/caller/hardware contracts and subsystem reviews remain open. Source-only.

Realtek8180 USB TX completion identity/order cross-check (2026-10-16; candidate left open): traced per-slot TX pipe allocation and submission (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/usb.c:528-543,1073-1084`), `TXPipeInt` discarding the completed pipe handle (`:708-720`), and FIFO `tx_out_slot` retirement (`unit.c:2419-2456`). Poseidon's host task can have multiple requests outstanding (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9275-9294`), but the selected HCD's guarantees about same-endpoint transfer completion ordering were not established. No distinct ordering defect is promoted pending that contract; OD3266 remains the verified ignored-error finding. Source-only.

Realtek8180 UnitTask signal-allocation check (2026-10-16; no new finding): read the complete `UnitTask` signal setup and startup path (`unit.c:288-303,2644-2711`) against Exec `NewAddTask` and `AllocSignal` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:241-251`; `allocsignal.c:79-103`). The task starts with the system-reserved low 16 bits marked allocated and otherwise clear; UnitTask is the new task's entry function and immediately allocates only three signals, so normal entry has free user bits. The unchecked failure branch exists, but the reviewed selected startup does not establish a reachable allocation-failure trigger; no signal-exhaustion finding is promoted. The UnitTask callback-null removal path remains OD3269. No task or signal allocation was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 event-port SMP synchronization pass (OD3277 added, 2026-10-16): traced `ReportEvents` traversal/removal against `S2_ONEVENT` enqueue (`unit.c:2486-2509`; `request.c:1100-1127,1762-1768`) and Exec's required message-port spinlock in PutMsg/GetMsg (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-92`; `getmsg.c:61-72`). `ReportEvents` uses local Disable only, leaving the event list unprotected from cross-CPU mutation. No event request or race was run. Source-only.
Exec/OOP disposal caller recheck (no new OD, 2026-10-16): `PCI_Expunge` passes the shared `CLID_HW_Root` singleton to `HW_RemoveDriver`; this path creates no per-expunge receiver, and no disposal leak was established (`pci_init.c:81-103`; `hwroot.c:46-66`; `hwclass.c:266-300`). No module expunge was run. Counts unchanged: 701 GD, 423 EK, 739 OD. Source-only.
Exec/OOP disposal caller recheck (OD3278 withdrawn, 2026-10-16): the apparent PCI expunge root leak was false. `OOP_NewObject(..., CLID_HW_Root, ...)` reaches `HWRoot__Root__New`, which creates `csd->hwroot` only if absent and returns that shared singleton on subsequent calls (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwroot.c:46-66`). PCI expunge therefore does not allocate a new receiver per cycle; the shared root is subsystem-owned and no per-expunge leak was established. Removed OD3278 and restored the prior report count. No module was loaded or expunged. Counts: 701 GD, 423 EK, 739 OD. Source-only.
PCI attribute-base expunge reconciliation (OD3279 restored, 2026-10-16): matched all five entries in `PCI_Init`'s `OOP_ObtainAttrBasesArray` to the `pci_staticdata` field order and `PCI_Expunge` releases. The first `IID_Hidd` base (`psd.hiddAB`) is omitted, leaving its shared OOP reference held across expunge. Restored this source-verified candidate under OD3279; old OD914 ledger reference was stale. No init or expunge was run. Counts: 701 GD, 423 EK, 740 OD. Source-only.
USB Audio `subLibAllocAudio` partial-failure cleanup pass (2026-10-16; no new OD): traced each early return in `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3264-3564` through AHI's allocation caller and free path (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:510-526,656-657,702-735`). AHI calls `AHIsub_FreeAudio` even when `AHIsub_AllocAudio` returns `AHISF_ERROR`; the class cleanup handles partially initialized state using null checks and releases the Poseidon library, timer request/device, task ports, pipes, RT ISO handlers, and allocated buffers (`usbaudio.class.c:3571-3666`). The examined partial allocation returns therefore do not establish a leak. `subLibAllocAudio` remains Partial: this pass did not cover the complete class body, AudioControl-unit semantics, or all transfer/callback lifetimes. Source-only; no device or failure injection was run.

Realtek8180 multicast-filter synchronization pass (OD3280, 2026-10-16): traced SANA-II add/delete dispatch through `AddMulticastRange`/`RemMulticastRange` and compared mutations with `RXInt`'s `AddressFilter` traversal (`request.c:196-203,1418-1448,1490-1527`; `unit.c:1156-1238,1578-1580,1883-1917`). RX arrives through the selected USB `PA_SOFTINT` pipe port, while SANA-II requests are serviced by UnitTask (`usb.c:465-480,740-764`; `unit.c:2650-2698`). List changes use only local `Disable()` and deletion frees the node; ExecSMP requires a shared lock for cross-CPU data. Added OD3280 for the conditional concurrent traversal/removal lifetime fault. No request, packet, or schedule was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 SANA-II type-stat teardown check (OD3071/OD3281, 2026-10-16): re-read `CmdTrackType` and traced opener initialization, `DevClose`/`CloseUnit`, and final `DeleteUnit` (`request.c:752-805`; `device.c:261-268,313-320,513-545`; `unit.c:347-391`). OD3071 already covers the Realtek allocation-failure/duplicate/no-rollback branches, so those were not duplicated. Unlike the seven drivers plus Etherlink III enumerated by OD3072, Realtek8180 Close frees the opener without freeing `initial_stats`; final unit deletion also does not drain `type_trackers`. Added OD3281 for the missing close-path leak coverage. No request or close was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 management-frame receive queue synchronization pass (OD3256/OD3282, 2026-10-16): rechecked S2_WRITEMGMT and S2_READMGMT dispatch against management TX/RX callbacks. OD3256 already covers unchecked management TX length. For receive, `CmdReadMgmt` reaches `PutRequest`/`PutMsg`, while `DistributeMgmtFrame` directly calls `RemHead` on each opener's `mgmt_port.mp_MsgList` (`request.c:1712-1729,1762-1766`; `unit.c:1575-1577,1940-1954`). Exec `PutMsg` uses the message-port SMP spinlock; raw `RemHead` does not (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-92`). The selected USB RX callback calls `RXInt`, which delivers non-beacon management frames into this consumer (`usb.c:465-480,740-764`; `unit.c:1575-1577`). Added OD3282 for the conditional queue race. No request/frame/schedule was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 packet-type statistics directionality cross-check (OD3254 expanded, 2026-10-16): followed a length-coded type through `S2_TRACKTYPE`, RX accounting, TX accounting, and `S2_GETTYPESTATS` (`request.c:752-760,928-936`; `unit.c:1770-1779,2241-2250`). Tracking and RX accounting canonicalize values at or below ETH_MTU to ETH_MTU, but TX lookup and GETTYPESTATS use the raw value. Expanded OD3254 to include omitted TX counts/bytes as well as failed query lookup. No request or packet was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 channel option / power-table bounds pass (OD3283, 2026-10-16): traced `S2_SETOPTIONS` through `SetOptions`, `CmdSetOptions`, `ConfigureAdapter`, and `SetPower` (`request.c:1557-1570`; `unit.c:849-861,1024-1029`; `radio.c:352-362,429`; `device.h:145,265-266`). The channel tag is stored without a range check; an online reconfiguration with stored channel 15 indexes past both arrays, which contain entries 0 through 14. Added OD3283. A selected WirelessManager caller forwards its chosen channel unchanged (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:637-650`); no request or hardware was used. Source-only.

xHCI extended-capability BAR-bound pass (OD3284 added, 2026-10-16): traced Base0/Size0 into `MAPPCI` and compared the mapped-length contract with HCCPARAMS1 ECP and successive `nextcap` dereferences (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_controllerclass.c:80-92,147-264`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:160-177`). No retained BAR extent or per-capability bound exists; malformed offsets can be read beyond the register aperture. Added OD3284 as conditional hardware-data robustness/correctness candidate; fault behavior depends on target mapping. No hardware was used. Broader xHCI callers and platform MMIO behavior remain open. Source-only.

xHCI OD3284 backend qualification (2026-10-16): checked the selected MapPCI dispatch and implementations after adding OD3284. The controller passes BAR Size0, but backends differ: PCIPC page-maps the requested span, BCM2712 passes it to KrnMapGlobal, and RP1 returns an address in its already mapped BAR window while ignoring Length. Tightened report wording to claim unchecked reads beyond the declared BAR extent and make a page fault conditional on platform mapping; no hardware path was exercised. Source-only.

Realtek8180 AddressFilter range-comparison follow-up (2026-10-16; no new OD): rechecked the six-byte address normalization in `AddressFilter` against `AddMulticastRange`/`RemMulticastRange` and `FindMulticastRange` (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/unit.c:1156-1192,1211-1239,1260-1284,1883-1921`). Both sides convert the first four and final two address bytes through the same BE helpers; the lexicographic inclusive lower/upper comparisons match that representation, and broadcast bypasses multicast filtering. No additional comparison defect established. The unsynchronized removal/free lifetime remains OD3280; no range mutation or packet was run. Source-only.

USB Audio Start/Stop AHI caller cross-check (OD3174 and OD3162 revalidated; 2026-10-16; no new OD): traced `subLibStart`/`subLibStop` through `_AHI_ControlAudioA` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3692-3808`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:959-1015`). For active playback and recording, the class discards `psdStartRTIso`'s result and sets `AHIE_OK`, while AHI returns that subdriver result to the caller, confirming OD3174. The fallback playback stop sets the timer port to PA_IGNORE and calls AbortIO without WaitIO; restart re-enables the port and causes the timer callback to reuse the request, matching OD3162. No additional state transition defect established in these methods. The class manifest's `kernel-usb-classes-usbaudio` target is included by `kernel-usb-classes-common`, then `kernel-usb-classes` and `kernel-usb-nopci` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/mmakefile.src:7-15`; `rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:9-44`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:17-22`). The AArch64 Raspberry Pi full-system target requests `kernel-usb-nopci` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:157-159`), so this class is on that selected build route. No device, control call, or timer was run. Source-only.


Atheros5000 unit lifecycle follow-up (OD3260 expanded, 2026-10-16): read `CreateUnit` and `DeleteUnit` (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:117-552`) and checked the selected AROS `AddUnitTask` macro (`task.h:54-61`) against `NewAddTask`/`InitETask` failure (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:270-272`; `exec_util.c:111-123`). If stack allocation succeeds and ETask allocation then fails, `UNITF_TASKADDED` remains clear and `DeleteUnit` skips freeing `task->tc_SPLower`; expanded shared OD3260 to include Atheros5000. Partial-init DMA/resource cleanup was checked on the selected PCI-hook path; no independent finding established. The other unit functions, PCI attach/detach interleavings, chipset/HAL behavior and full file/caller review remain open. No allocation failure, task or device was run. Source-only.


Atheros5000 AR5210 TX queue allocation pass (OD3293, 2026-10-16): traced `InitialiseAdapter` queue setup to AR5210 `ar5210SetupTxQueue`, then followed the failed second DATA queue index into management TX and offline HAL calls (`unit.c:599-613,944-946,2580-2589`; `hal/ar5210/ar5210_xmit.c:67-95,154-170,282-292,367-376,428-437`). AR5210 maps DATA only to queue 0 and returns -1 for the second active allocation; the driver ignores the reset failure and later HAL consumers index the invalid queue. Added OD3293 for the conditional Atheros5000 GNU/PCI build with an AR5210 device. Other HAL families and the rest of `unit.c` remain open. No hardware/request was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000 TX completion-status pass (OD3294, 2026-10-16): traced data and management completion through `ah_procTxDesc` and found both handlers discard `ath_tx_status` fields, retire the request and set `io_Error` to zero (`unit.c:2424-2455,2637-2660`). Checked AR5210, AR5211, AR5212 and AR5416 HAL implementations, which populate nonzero `ts_status` for excessive retries, filtering and FIFO underrun (`hal/ah_desc.h:37,60-64`; implementation ranges recorded in OD3294). Added conditional false-success finding. No hardware or request was used; other unit functions, additional caller contracts and full driver review remain open. Source-only.


Atheros5000 key-index/key-length cross-check (OD3187 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced `S2_SETKEY` through `CmdSetKey` and `SetKey`, verified the four-entry key-array bound, 13-byte WEP member, fixed-size TKIP/CCMP copies, and unchecked `S2INFO_DefaultKeyNo` uses in configuration/TX encryption. Expanded OD3187, which already covers Prism2 and Realtek8180. The optional RX counter pointer issue remains separately qualified by OD3249. No key request or key material was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000 software CCMP replay-state cross-check (OD3120 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced `DecryptCCMPFragment` through `CCMPCheckIV` and `CCMPDecrypt`; the former stores the RX packet counter before the latter verifies MIC, so a failed-MIC frame can advance state before being rejected. Confirmed `InitialiseAdapter` selects this helper when hardware CCMP is unavailable. Expanded OD3120 from Prism2 to include Atheros5000 software CCMP. No frame or hardware was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000 RX reassembly retry cross-check (OD3274, 2026-10-16): read `GetRXBuffer` and its `RXInt` caller. When the first scan misses all ten busy slots for an unmatched source’s first fragment, the second pass clears slot zero but leaves the pointer at the allocation end and returns `buffer_no` as 10. RX processing writes through the one-past pointer and indexes the ten-element `rx_fragment_nos` array with 10. This is the Atheros5000-specific companion to OD3116 for Prism2/Realtek8180. No frame/device was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000 encrypted RX lower-bound pass (OD3295, 2026-10-16): traced RX descriptor admission into WEP/TKIP/CCMP fragment dispatch. The 30-byte total-length guard permits a derived encrypted body length of 0–7, while cipher helpers subtract their 8/12/16-byte overhead from `UWORD` without checking; hardware-decrypt branches can copy the wrapped result into reassembly storage. Added OD3295 with descriptor-zero-status delivery explicitly conditional because chipset handling of short encrypted frames was not verified. No frame or hardware was used. Source-only.


Wi-Fi fragment sequence-identity cross-check (OD3296, 2026-10-16): compared the full Sequence Control value passed into Prism2, Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 `GetRXBuffer` helpers. Each helper keys an in-progress slot by transmitter address but never checks the stored sequence-number bits; new first fragments can reuse a same-source partial slot, and later same-source fragments can append regardless of sequence. Added OD3296 for the three build-selected driver families. The retry-pointer defect is tracked as OD3116 for Prism2/Realtek8180 and OD3274 for Atheros5000. No frame/device was used. Source-only.


Atheros5000/Realtek8180 TKIP final-MIC lower-bound pass (OD3297, 2026-10-16): traced successful per-fragment TKIP processing into the final software Michael-MIC check. Neither RX caller checks the accumulated length before `TKIPDecryptFrame` subtracts eight from a `UWORD`, copies the received MIC and runs `UpdateMIC` over that length. A final fragment with valid per-fragment ICV but less than eight accumulated bytes therefore causes MIC reads and padding writes beyond reassembly storage before rejection. Added OD3297 for Atheros when `UNITF_HARDMIC` is clear and Realtek software-TKIP-MIC configurations. No frame/device was used. Source-only.


ATA PCI helper Sam440 target-selection reconciliation (2026-10-16): the earlier `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c` coverage row names the PC-selected PCI HIDD paths but omits Sam440. `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src` selects `kernel-ata` and `kernel-hidd-pciata` through `kernel-modules-sam440-ppc`; therefore `rom/hidds/ata_pci/interface_dma.c` is also selected there. OD2996 remains x86-only because its >4-GiB buffer trigger is not established on Sam440's 32-bit `IPTR`. The helper's `items > PRD_MAX` guard permits 257 entries, matching its allocated 257-entry per-table capacity; the LBA48 caller can request up to 65,536 sectors, so this count is source-reachable with a sufficiently large buffer, but no device-side 256-entry cap was established. No additional finding credited; DMA and hardware behavior remain untested. Source-only.


ATA PCI constructor cleanup Sam440 reachability recheck (OD2661 scope expanded, 2026-10-16): confirmed the selected Sam440 `kernel-modules-sam440-ppc` aggregate includes `kernel-ata` and `kernel-hidd-pciata`; the PCI ATA bus constructor allocates PRD memory before IRQ registration, then its failure path calls only superclass Dispose, while class-specific Dispose owns the matching `FreePCIMem`. Both selected Sam440 PCI HIDDs subclass generic `CLID_Hidd_PCIDriver`, and generic `AddInterrupt` returns FALSE when `KrnAddIRQHandler` fails. Expanded OD2661 from PC-only to include Sam440 when a bus-master ATA controller and the stated allocation/IRQ failure combination occur. No failure or hardware path was induced. Source-only.


ATA PCI no-DMA shared-IRQ Sam440 route check (OD3011 scope expanded, 2026-10-16): the selected Sam440 PPC440 PCI HIDD subclasses generic `CLID_Hidd_PCIDriver`; `PCIDevice_AddInterrupt` forwards each PCI `INTLine` to generic `AddInterrupt`, which registers through `KrnAddIRQHandler`. Sam440's UIC handler calls `krnRunIRQHandlers` for every asserted UIC vector, so a shared vector fans out to all registered handlers just as on PC. The PCI ATA probe admits a channel with `DMABase == 0`; on this route `ata_PCI_Interrupt` checks ATA `BUSY` only before forwarding to its active callback. Expanded OD3011 to the selected Sam440 PPC440 PCI configuration conditionally; actual no-DMA IDE hardware and line assignments were not established. No IRQ or ATA request was run. Source-only.
Keyboard final queued-read unit lifetime (OD3298, 2026-10-16): traced `kbdSendQueuedEvents` through `ReplyMsg` to the final `KBUF_PENDING` clear, keyboard Close's `FreeMem(KBUnit)`, and ExecSMP reply signaling. A request owner running on another core can consume the reply and close its unit before the handler's post-reply dereference. Added OD3298 conditionally for selected ExecSMP configurations; no request was issued and the race was not reproduced. Source-only.
Keyboard per-open pending-flag cross-unit recheck (2026-10-16; no additional finding): confirmed `KBUF_PENDING` is per `KBUnit` while `kb_PendingQueue` is global. When the drain empties requests from several units, it clears only the flag of the last request; other units can retain a stale flag. `AbortIO` still requires the supplied request to be `NT_MESSAGE` before removing it (`keyboard.c:533-545`), so an already-replied request cannot be removed just because its unit flag is stale. A later valid queued request sets the flag and is linked before it can be aborted. The stale flag alone therefore does not establish a client-visible failure; OD3298 remains the separate post-reply lifetime access. No request was issued. Source-only.
Gameport final queued-read unit lifetime pass (OD3299, 2026-10-16): traced `gpSendQueuedEvents` through `fillrequest`, request removal and `ReplyMsg` to the post-loop `GBUF_PENDING` clear (`gameport.c:49,571-605`). Close frees the request's `GPUnit`; ExecSMP reply signaling permits the owner to consume the final reply and close on another CPU before the clear. The callback invokes the drain synchronously from its mouse-event path (`:550-558`). Added OD3299 for the conditional cross-core stale-unit access. No request or device was used. Source-only.
Gameport AbortIO post-reply unit-lifetime cross-check (OD1007/OD3299, 2026-10-16; no duplicate finding): `AbortIO` also calls `ReplyMsg` before storing IOERR_ABORTED and before its final per-unit `GBUF_PENDING` clear (`gameport.c:467-479`). A cross-core shared-port consumer that reclaims the request can race either subsequent request access, already captured by OD1007; if it closes the owning device unit, the later flag clear is the same per-open unit lifetime consequence captured by OD3299. No separate candidate or request was added/run.
Gameport unit-index and trigger-query recheck (OD3215 scope, 2026-10-16; no new finding): Open rejects `unitnum > GP_MAXUNIT`, with `GP_MAXUNIT == 1` and `gp_cTypes[GP_NUNITS]` sized for two units, so the `GPD_ASKCTYPE`/`GPD_SETCTYPE` index remains bounded (`gameport.c:169-175,346-367`; `gameport_intern.h:24-26,50`). ASK/SET trigger requests require exactly one `GamePortTrigger` structure and use the open-unit field; the selected input.device sets a trigger but does not query it. The trigger predicate remains disabled in `fillrequest`, already detailed as OD3215; no separate query/index defect established. No request was issued. Source-only.
Gameport event-ring capacity/overrun pass (OD3300, 2026-10-16): traced allocation size, four-word record writes, modulo writer wrap and per-open read cursor (`gameport_intern.h:20-27,48-51`; `gameport.c:536-548,618-655`). After 100 unread callbacks, writer and reader positions coincide and BeginIO's equality test treats the full ring as empty. Added OD3300 for the conditional direct-client event loss; selected input.device's persistent one-event request does not establish a typical 100-event backlog. No callback or request was run. Source-only.
TimeDelay alib return-value and caller pass (OD3301, 2026-10-16): read the full helper and matched its return contract to its `DoIO` path. After successful timer.device open and completed `TR_ADDREQUEST`, it assigns one to the result even though the documented success value is zero; it also discards the request's `io_Error`. The only maintained direct callers found are Intuition menu delays, which ignore the return, so the delay still occurs there but caller-visible status is wrong for clients that check it. No timer request was run. Source-only.

## SD-card device source inventory and initial hotplug pass

The 32-bit Pi target selects the SDHOST backend; AArch64 carries SDHOST and Arasan/EMMC2 and selects the controller using the SoC peripheral base and card presence (`sdcard_bcm2708init.c:100-127`; SDHOST returns early on BCM2711/2712 in `sdcard_sdhost_init.c:139-148`). File-by-file review remains open; entries below mark only the focused initial pass, not completion.
