Selected BWFM callsites pass non-null in-scope buffers and appropriate transfer lengths. The final data-end error false-success is already OD3560; no additional independent defect was established in this slice. No controller or transfer was run. Remaining public API boundary/failure and interrupt lifetime reviews remain open. Source-only.

Broadcom SDIO IRQ task-registration reachability recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `SDIOSetInterrupt` through BWFM's wrappers (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2678-2698`) to the device RX-pump code (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:52,464-472`): `BWFM_USE_IRQ` is fixed at 0, so the selected in-tree caller uses adaptive polling and does not register a task or arm card signaling. `sdio_do_probe` still installs the host handler after card detection, but the resource's base signal-enable mask excludes the card interrupt until `SDIOSetInterrupt`; thus the unchecked handler-allocation result is not shown to break this selected polling path. External clients and alternate configurations remain unverified. No task teardown or IRQ was induced. Source-only.

PCI HIDD driver-removal object ownership recheck (OD3563 added, 2026-10-17): traced `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:451-517`) against generic `HW_RemoveDriver` semantics (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:228-253`) and device publication (`pciclass.c:61-94,104-170`). The method checks the requested driver object's devices for owners, then its deletion loop disposes every device in the shared list, irrespective of driver association or ownership. The selected in-tree cleanup path is `PCIPC_Expunge()` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_init.c:54-78`), which calls the legacy RemHardwareDriver method; `PCI__Hidd_PCI__RemHardwareDriver` enumerates same-class driver instances and calls `HW_RemoveDriver` (`pciclass.c:626-658`). This corrects the earlier `pcipc_driverclass.c:645-660` citation, which is the attribute-base expunge hook, not the removal wrapper. The first-driver order and refusal behavior constrain the collateral trigger, so OD3563 requires an unowned target and another instance's live owned object. No PCI driver was removed. Remaining PCI API caller and backend lifecycle checks stay open. Source-only.

Bluetooth HID variable arithmetic overflow trace (OD3552 added, 2026-10-17): traced `HUA_VARIABLES` target selection/storage and ADD/SUB/MULTIPLY operations (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:5527-5575`; LONG arrays `bthid.h:625,845`). The GUI offers those operations and can redirect values from constants or action variables (`bthid.gui.c:104-112,841-860,3153-3163`); scalar input can also supply a valid 32-bit LONG-range value (`bthid.class.c:2228-2247,4200-4224`). A multiply target 2 by 1,073,741,824 exceeds LONG_MAX. No action or input was used. Division, modulo, and shift edge cases are tracked separately. Source-only.

BTHID special RawKey selector display recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): compared the 128-entry GUI enumeration with `specialrawkeys`/`specialextrawkeys` (`bthid.gui.c:221-280`; `numtostr.c:1887-2002`). Bluetooth HID variable division signed-minimum boundary (OD3555 added, 2026-10-17): traced the `HUA_VARIABLES` divisor check and signed `/` operation (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:5577-5582`), 32-bit signed LONG definition (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:34-39`), and signed 32-bit report extraction (`bthid.class.c:4190-4203`). Bluetooth HID Abs-to-Rel signed-range arithmetic trace (OD3556 added, 2026-10-17): followed the 32-bit ReportSize missing-logical-bounds fallback to `0x80000000..0x7fffffff` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2143-2158`), signed LONG item storage (`:2236-2238`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:34-39`), and the GUI-selected Abs-to-Rel path (`bthid.gui.c:728-734,3097-3100`) into `bDoAction`'s delta and range arithmetic (`bthid.class.c:4484-4488`). This is separate from scaling's constant-range division in OD3460. BTHID remaining action-family and full caller paths remain open. Source-only.

Bluetooth HID condition-evaluation and selected GUI operator reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new OD): read `bDoAction`'s full condition operand selectors, comparator switch, false-condition return, and value-substitution switch (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:4537-4879`). Compared all 16 condition labels/values with the GUI arrays (`bthid.gui.c:40-58`): equality/order, logical AND/NAND/OR/XOR/ANDNOT, and boolean-valued bitwise AND/NAND/OR/XOR/ANDNOT all have matching dispatch cases. Bluetooth HID action-trigger dispatch and report caller pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): compared Down/Up/Any/Always/NaN GUI values (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.gui.c:37-38`) with flag definitions (`bthid.h:243-248`), `bDoAction` trigger gating (`bthid.class.c:4475-4482`), and scalar/array caller semantics (`:4272-4275,4376-4397,4421-4445`). Bluetooth HID array logical-range and allocation-bound trace (OD3557 added, 2026-10-17): followed array item signed logical bounds into the cap, map-size, allocation and initialization loop (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2269-2310,2353-2355`). The `LogicalMax - LogicalMin` guard can overflow before applying the 65,535 cap; `MapSize` and map allocation products are then unchecked. A span wider than LONG_MAX is representable by two signed descriptor bounds; on 32-bit targets with wrapping arithmetic, undersized wrapped allocations can be followed by MapSize-count initialization writes. No report descriptor or binding was used. Exact runtime manifestation depends on target compiler/allocator behavior. This is distinct from scalar signed-extraction shifts OD3463. Source-only.

Bluetooth HID report-descriptor item-length caller recheck (OD3452 confirmed, no new finding, 2026-10-17): traced exact-length descriptor acquisition/allocation in `bReadReports` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1521-1532,1537-1577`) into `bParseReport`'s prefix-only loop bound and short/long item decoding (`:1987-2028`). Bluetooth HID Report ID width/narrowing caller trace (OD3558 added, 2026-10-17): traced Global Report ID parsing into the report record (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2539-2541,2035-2056`), `ULONG` record field and `UWORD nhb_MaxReportID` (`bthid.h:502-515,565-571`), then max-ID assignment, map allocation and full-width map index (`bthid.class.c:1615-1621,1657-1667`). OHCI root-hub port-feature caller/register cross-check (2026-10-17; no new OD): revisited `ohcihub.c:97-120,139-262` against the selected USBHub class and OHCI register definitions. Maintained USBHub exploration, power-on/off, and reset callers enumerate ports from 1 through `bNbrPorts` (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:463-466,482-485,502-507,566`), so the OHCI feature methods' missing `port >= 1` guard is not reached by these selected call paths; direct external HIDD clients remain a contract gap. OHCI RHSC timer-cancel/reuse recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed the previously open `ClearPortFeature` cancellation into timer.device `AbortIO` and message reply. If `CheckIO` reports pending, the selected timer AbortIO removes the request, marks it `IOERR_ABORTED`, and calls `ReplyMsg` before returning (`rom/timer/abortio.c:69-90`); if it reports complete, the request is already a reply message and is drained with `GetMsg` (`ohcihub.c:208-212`). The OHCI soft-interrupt callback also drains the reply and exits on `IOERR_ABORTED` (`ohcihub.c:265-275`). No independent overlapping-request reuse defect established in these paths. The unresolved question remains whether hardware reasserts a still-pending RHSC after the driver's W1C/one-second disable/re-enable sequence (`ohcidriverclass.c:404-428`; callback `ohcihub.c:278-284`); source alone does not settle controller semantics. No timer or controller was run. Source-only.

USB HID failed worker-publication follow-up (OD3564; historical coverage-only OD2246 restored, 2026-10-17): confirmed the keyboard and mouse constructor behavior against both `NewAddTask` NULL returns and `RemTask` ownership. The constructor stores the task pointer regardless of setup result; failed ETask/context initialization does not schedule the task or free the caller's `tc_MemEntry`, whose normal reclamation is in task removal. Extended the report with the distinct post-allocation task-setup failure. No task failure or report was induced. Source-only.

USB HID initial worker-allocation failure recheck (OD3565; historical coverage-only OD2246/OD2810 restored, 2026-10-17): traced the keyboard/mouse Task and MemList allocations through the skipped setup conditional and returned object. Confirmed the zero-cleared NULL worker pointer suppresses report handling; mouse Dispose unconditionally passes that NULL pointer to Exec Signal. A successful sibling allocation is leaked. This is separate from stack-allocation failure OD2247 and post-allocation `NewAddTask` failure OD3564. No allocation failure or device removal was induced. Source-only.

USB HID worker detach-before-DOS-init recheck (OD2184 restored to detailed report, 2026-10-17): traced each worker's first `Wait` through its `dos_not_ready` branch against the subclass Dispose signal and the USB hub's disconnect disposal (`kbdclass.c:329-374,241-257`; `mouseclass.c:238-294,226-235`; `usbhubclass.c:536-547`). Keyboard's `if/else` always skips Ctrl-C processing on that first wake, even if opening DOS succeeds; mouse skips it only when DOS open still fails, because a successful open falls through to its separate `if (!dos_not_ready)` check. Both destructors send only one Ctrl-C and do not join the worker, so the stated early-disconnect timing leaves the worker waiting with its input.device request/port open. Restored OD2184 rather than duplicating the existing coverage-only candidate; no runtime route was exercised. Source-only.

USB HID worker-stack allocation failure recheck (OD2247 restored to detailed report, 2026-10-17): confirmed the keyboard and mouse constructors both build `tc_SPReg` from unchecked `sp`, then call `NewAddTask` (`kbdclass.c:206-234`; `mouseclass.c:191-219`). The Sam440 PPC USB package selects the generic USB stack and its classes; PPC stack-down configuration and `SP_OFFSET=0x10` make the NULL-derived register near `0x27f0`, which selected `PrepareContext` writes before allocating its context (`arch/ppc-all/include/aros/cpu.h:26,82`; `arch/ppc-sam440/exec/preparecontext.c:19-31`; boot dependency `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:51`). Restored historical OD2247 with this selected PPC consequence; distinct from OD3358's USB hub task and OD2789's USB starter task. No allocation failure or task setup was induced. Source-only.

USB HID mouse event-ring producer/consumer recheck (2026-10-17; no additional finding): followed `HidInterrupt` through `Cause` to the report callback and worker (`hidclass.c:65-84`; OHCI WDH caller `ohcidriverclass.c:353-392`; `mouseclass.c:45-86,278-305`). The callback fills one ring slot before advancing `head` and signals the task; the worker copies the slot fields before advancing `tail`. Both cursors stay in `[0, RING_SIZE)`, and the fill calculation correctly adds `RING_SIZE` when the head wraps below the tail, reserving one slot to distinguish full from empty. No ring-bound or independent cursor-order defect established in this sequential producer/consumer path. The broader completion/removal lifetime remains covered by OHCI OD2958/OD2959; no USB report or interleaving was run. Source-only.

Trackdisk Exec task-creation failure follow-up (OD3566, 2026-10-17): traced successful TD_InitTask-side TaskData/stack/MemList allocations through the unchecked NewAddTask result and unconditional startup Wait. The selected i386 route can reject task creation on ETask or CPU-context allocation failure; no worker then exists to send `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_F`, and the caller does not free its preallocated state. Recorded separately from OD3343's earlier TaskData/stack/MemList allocation failure, which returns through TD_InitTask and leaves the device init hook reporting success. No failure or boot was induced. Source-only.

AHI audio.device capture-offset width pass (OD3572 added, 2026-10-17): inspected all six RecM/S 8/16/32-bit converters and the local `struct sample` definition (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devsupp.c:32-35,43-179`). AHI-Handler capture-offset caller correction (OD3572 strengthened, 2026-10-17): re-read the double-buffer resubmission path (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:498-518`). It reuses the completed CMD_READ request but does not reset `io_Offset`, unlike the initial request setup at `:445`; this is the selected in-tree caller trigger. AHI audio.device first-read idle-delay pass (OD3573 added, 2026-10-17): traced zero-cleared unit construction and `RecordOffDelay` state (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:444-447`; `device.h:140`) through ReadCmd startup/queueing, first-buffer FillReadBuffer completion and FeedReaders shutdown (`devcommands.c:983-1094`). PL011BT missing-mailbox capability recheck (OD3577 added, 2026-10-17): traced `OpenResource("mbox.resource")` through successful init and the advertised capability mask to `PL011BTSetPower`'s `firmware_gpio_set` return (`pl011bt_init.c:306-324,138-149,514-533`; interface comment in `pl011bt.conf:7-19`). Deneb RTIso start/stop/removal state-machine recheck for OD3517 (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `cmdStartRTIso`, `cmdStopRTIso`, `cmdRemIsoHandler`, and `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos` through the interrupt dispatch (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1317-1529,1533-1588,3333-3745,5326-5334`). Completion callbacks run inline while the Deneb hardware interrupt handler processes the done map; stop/removal disable local interrupts, clear the relevant `hu_IsoRTDone`, `hu_IsoBusy`, and `hu_IsoRTMask` bits, and deactivate or detach both PTDs before reenabling interrupts. A later handler masks the hardware done map with `hu_IsoBusy` and only dispatches realtime callbacks for bits still in `hu_IsoRTMask`. On the selected single-CPU m68k backend, a task-context stop cannot overlap a callback already executing in the interrupt handler, and deferred bits are filtered by the cleared masks. OD3517 therefore remains scoped to the cross-CPU PCIUSB/xHCI backends; broader Deneb transfer scheduling, buffer alignment, and callback contract review remain open. No device, stream, or interrupt was exercised. Source-only.

Deneb RTIso OUT-hook word-copy boundary pass (OD3578 added, 2026-10-17): traced both startup-prefill and recurring OUT-completion copies (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1380-1432,3700-3740`) against `IOUsbHWBufferReq`'s hook-adjusted byte length and scatter/gather flag contract (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:103-113`). The backend rounds each segment's source-word count up with `(ubr_Length + 3) >> 2`; when a hook sets `UBFF_CONTBUFFER` on a non-longword-aligned segment, the next segment starts at the advanced buffer pointer while the hardware destination advances by rounded words, matching the local FIXME about continuous-mode havoc. Added OD3578 for the packet-byte shift and rounded source load. No maintained Deneb RTIso OUT-hook producer or checked-in `UBFF_CONTBUFFER` setter was found, so the trigger remains external-client conditional. No stream or hook was run. Source-only.

Deneb unit close and embedded worker lifetime pass (OD3582 added, 2026-10-17): traced `Close_Unit`'s controller stop, interrupt removal, Ctrl-C signal, fixed timer delay and `FreeVec(unit)` against the embedded `Task`/stack layout and `uhwDMATask` exit path (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:502-525,5374-5401`; `denebusb.h:277,328`). The function has no completion handshake before freeing storage. A worker still executing a PIO copy or delayed past the 10-ms wait can continue through the unit or return into Exec's task finalizer, which removes the embedded Task (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:52-55`). Added OD3582 with the scheduler/work-duration condition explicit; no device close or task timing was run. Remaining command state machines and hardware contracts stay open. Source-only.

Deneb NAK timer, soft interrupt, and interrupt completion boundary pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced unit setup of `hu_NakTimeoutReq`/PA_SOFTINT and the first `Cause`, the NAK timer's frame counter and timeout loops, both timer re-submission paths, and teardown's PA_IGNORE/AbortIO/10-ms delay before unit free (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:64-112,280-525,4774-4826,4842-4990,5265-5370`). The handler sends the next timer request after each callback; close prevents new soft-interrupt delivery and aborts the outstanding request before freeing the unit. Timeout expiration clears the corresponding ATL/interrupt NAK map through `FreeATL`/`FreeInt`. No separate finding retained from this pass. This was source tracing only; no timer, NAK, or close path was run. Deneb command completion, abort, and timeout edge cases remain under review.

Deneb `CMD_RESET` versus outstanding transfer ownership pass (OD3583 added, 2026-10-17): traced the public reset contract and command dispatch to `uhwHWInit` (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:166-182`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:548-557`; `uhwcmd.c:116-186,395-414,569-578`). Hardware reset clears the PTD region and completion maps, while queued lists, PTD request pointers and software busy/free/active maps remain unchanged. Added OD3583, conditional on reset while I/O is outstanding; no reset or transfer was run. Continue through Deneb command state machines and abort/completion ordering.

Deneb AbortIO active ATL/DMA ownership pass (OD3584 added, 2026-10-17): traced the queue removal and ATL/INT/ISO PTD scans in `cmdAbortIO` through `FreeATL`/`FreeInt`/`FreeIso` and `devAbortIO` termination (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1626-1774,1778-1866`; `dev.c:658-687`). For an ATL DMA PTD, `cmdAbortIO` sets `ptd_IOReq` NULL before `FreeATL`; the DMA branch there dereferences the local request for `CachePostDMA`. Added OD3584 for the DMA-enabled large-transfer abort path. Queued and INT/ISO paths do not take this FreeATL DMA branch. No transfer or AbortIO was run; continue checking DMA completion/abort ordering and flush interactions.

Deneb discrete OUT buffer-boundary pass (OD3585 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced `CopyMemShuffle` and its ordinary bulk/control/isochronous callers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:38-47,2498-2505,4402-4409,4712-4724`), then followed the aligned large bulk-OUT path through `CachePreDMA` and `MMS_LENGTHBYTES` programming (`:4300-4318`). The DMA route programs `(ptd_BufLen+3)&~3` bytes while CachePreDMA receives the original byte length; transfers that do not remain DMA eligible fall back to the same rounded buffer copy. Compared against the public byte-count contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:194-248,270-294`). Expanded OD3585: DMA eligibility does not require an OUT transfer length divisible by four. Separate from RTIso hook segmentation in OD3578. No transfer was run; completion/state review remains open.

Deneb bulk PTD reuse and zero-length request pass (OD3586 added, 2026-10-17): traced PTD field assignment in `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs` through `FreeATL` and confirmed `ptd_BufLen`/`ptd_BufStart` are set only when request length is nonzero, while release leaves both fields intact (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1635-1670,4268-4390`). Cross-checked that the public API accepts a byte length without a positive minimum (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:194-248`). Added OD3586 for zero-length bulk requests reusing a previously used ATL slot; no request was run. Continue command state and completion review.

Deneb ordinary control/bulk/interrupt/isochronous PTD scheduling pass (2026-10-17; OD3585/OD3586 retained; no additional finding): read queue-to-PTD allocation and register publication for `uhwScheduleCtrlPTDs`, `uhwScheduleIntPTDs`, `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs`, and `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3796-4774`). Checked PTD availability and large-area allocation against per-command request extent and the corresponding buffer-copy paths. Confirmed the buffered OUT rounded-longword reads recorded in OD3585 and the zero-length bulk stale-field case in OD3586. Interrupt buffers larger than the small PTD region and isochronous requests use one granule per scheduled PTD; their completion continuation, interval interpretation, and hardware scheduling behavior remain open. No USB request or controller was run.

Deneb control completion special-request recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed successful control status completion into the `CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT)` and `SET_ADDRESS` toggle-table updates (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2748-2772`) and compared `wValue` construction in Poseidon (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4693-4701`). Poseidon stores the USB setup word in little-endian form; on m68k the raw `wValue >> 3` yields the address shifted into the table's `device<<5` base, so the apparently unusual shift is not an indexing bug. No control request was run. Remaining control status/error and data-stage paths stay open.

Deneb ordinary isochronous completion and multi-packet continuation pass (OD3587 added, 2026-10-17): traced done-map dispatch and `uhwHandleFinishedIsos` through actual-byte update, continuation test, frame advance, buffer refill and `FreeIso` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3007-3324`). The code rearms only when `Actual + MaxPktSize < Length`; with exactly one packet or a partial packet remaining it releases and replies instead. Cross-checked the public packetized ISO request contract and Poseidon's ISO endpoint command selection (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:442-450`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4603-4613`). Added OD3587; no transfer was run. Broader timing and split-transaction behavior remain open.

Deneb ATL DMA partial-chunk completion trace (2026-10-17; OD3584/OD3585 retained; no additional finding): followed `PTDT_DATAINDMA` and `PTDT_DATAOUTDMA` completions through `DMASM_IN_WAITING_LOW/HIGH`, `DMASM_IN_READING_LOW/HIGH`, and OUT prefetch state transitions, including request `iouh_Actual`, `hu_DMAOffset`, `hu_DMAAddr`, `hu_DMAPhyAddr`, and PTD rearm (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2138-2444,4998-5270`). Confirmed the OUT final chunk pads `hu_DMALength` while retaining byte `ptd_BufLen` for the USB PTD; this is covered by OD3585. Active DMA AbortIO's pointer clearing remains OD3584. Broader abort/flush races, map failures, and controller DMA ordering still need review; no hardware or request was exercised.

Deneb DMA completion interrupt and worker follow-up (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread the full `uhwHandleDMAInt`, level-6 DMA interrupt branch and `uhwDMATask` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4996-5265,5277-5350,5372-5402`) against `deneb.h` register definitions and the unit constructor/closer (`:452-490,502-523`; `deneb.h:101-115`). The MACH interrupt exposes only a DMA-finished bit, which the ISR acknowledges before waking the per-unit worker; the worker advances one state-machine step and starts any subsequent transfer. This confirms OD3581's required-worker dependency and OD3582's missing join on teardown. The PIO-under-threshold IN branches copy the rounded actual byte count and then release the PTD, so their stale `hu_DMALength` offset increment is not consumed by a later chunk; each new DMA request resets the address/offset, so no separate data-corruption candidate is established from that bookkeeping. DMA hardware ordering, error behavior beyond the defined done bit, and broader abort/controller interleavings remain open. No interrupt, transfer or device was exercised; source-only.

Deneb interrupt interval producer/consumer contract check (2026-10-17; unresolved, no OD): traced Poseidon's endpoint descriptor normalization (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8483-8604`) into `iouh_Interval` assignment (`:4627`) and Deneb's interrupt PTD encoder (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4058-4116`). Poseidon passes high-speed intervals as powers of two in microframes, while full-speed interrupt intervals remain descriptor milliseconds; Deneb encodes short values in `hu_IntSOFMap` and longer values via `iouh_Interval >> 1` in the PTD microframe/interval field. The local field comment describes millisecond interval encoding, but no ISP1760 datasheet or executable hardware contract is checked in here, so the apparent scale mismatch is not promoted to a finding. No endpoint or bus schedule was run. This hardware interval behavior remains open pending authoritative controller documentation.

GPIOSetPull SoC register-map cross-check (OD3589 added, 2026-10-17): compared all four public GPIO vector branches with selected SDIO's documented BCM pull-register split (`gpio_init.c:171-208`; `sdio_init.c:322-362`). `GPIOSetPull` always uses `GPIO+0xE4` for a non-RP1 peripheral base, but BCM2835/6/7 require timed `GPPUD/GPPUDCLK`; only BCM2711 uses `GPPUPPDN`. ARM32 Raspberry Pi boot selects the BCM2708 resource through its parent; AArch64 Pi includes `kernel-gpio-bcm2708` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:137`). Added OD3589; no hardware operation or electrical behavior was tested.

Broadcom SDIO block-size setup failure caller check (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed BWFM's unchecked `SDIOSetBlockSize(1,64)` and `(2,512)` results (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:541-543`) through the cache update in `SDIOSetBlockSize` and the CMD53 selector. A failed size write leaves that cache entry zero, so subsequent transfers use byte mode capped at 512 bytes; firmware writes are already rounded to <=512-byte chunks (`bwfm_init.c:704-748`), and no selected failure consequence was established from the ignored results alone. Existing OD2853/2854/2855/3560/3562 remain distinct. No card or transfer was exercised. Source-only.

## Broadcom BWFM firmware/upload source inventory and trace (2026-10-17)

The ARM32 and AArch64 Raspberry Pi distfiles targets depend on `workbench-devs-networks-bwfm`, and both boot manifests include the BCM2708 BWFM resource (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:29-37,139`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:23,141`). The network aggregate selects the device (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:43`); its manifest depends on the resource's generated includes. This is an active selected path for Raspberry Pi images, with firmware/NVRAM loaded from disk at runtime. The firmware startup caller has been traced through file reads, text-to-binary NVRAM conversion, RAM-layout checks, upload, CPU activation, ready polling, and `fw_loaded` publication. OD3590 records the missing combined firmware/NVRAM extent check. This paragraph records the initial firmware-path checkpoint and is superseded by the later BWFM full-body, API, SDIO, scan, TX/RX and lifecycle review entries below; external firmware ABI, hardware behavior and broader caller closure remain open.

BWFM GLOM malformed-subframe bounds trace (OD3591 added, 2026-10-17): traced GLOM descriptor lengths through `bwfm_rx_glom`, `bwfm_frame_eth`, the shared queue and `bwfm_glom_pop` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1216-1337`; pump/API caller `:2210-2250`, `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:454-496`). The first subframe's 12-byte superframe prefix is subtracted from unsigned `subtot` before the minimum-length check; values below 12 wrap, bypassing the later embedded-frame extent test. Queue pop clips only to caller capacity, not the 32-KiB aggregate buffer. Added OD3591 with an explicit retained-buffer-tail condition for a static-buffer overread. No frame or card was used; all other RX/TX and glom sequencing remains open. Source-only.

BWFM cooked transmit length and copy-hook trace (OD3592 added, 2026-10-17): followed selected BeginIO write/broadcast/multicast dispatch into `tx_request`, opener hook setup, frame-size check, `BWFMTxData` and TermIO (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:652-700,1880-1890`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2112-2200`). `ULONG` is 32-bit; cooked `ETH_HLEN + ios2_DataLength` wraps before the 1,518-byte check, then the original length is passed to the copy hook at `txbuf + ETH_HLEN`. Added OD3592; raw writes are bounded by the pre-copy buffer check. No request was run; remaining device vectors and caller bounds remain open. Source-only.

BWFM pending-request ownership and CMD_FLUSH trace (OD3593–OD3594 added, 2026-10-17): followed CMD_READ and S2_ONEVENT queue insertion through rx/event completion, AbortIO, Close, OFFLINE and CMD_FLUSH (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1099-1214,1593-1712,1887-1925`). CMD_READ queues are per opener but `flush_reads(unit)` iterates all openers; pending S2_ONEVENT is held in a separate unit list and CMD_FLUSH never drains it. Close handles both lists for the specific opener; selected SANA-II peers filter flush by `ios2_BufferManagement` and abort event queues as well (`rom/usb/classes/asixeth/dev.c:390-408`). Added separate OD3593 and OD3594 for cross-opener cancellation and stranded event waits. No requests were issued. Source-only.

BWFM process-startup allocation-failure trace (OD3595–OD3596 added, 2026-10-17): traced both `CreateNewProcTags` results through DOS's documented nullable process-creation result, firmware-loaded publication, Open return and worker consumers (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:615-640,725-823,1157-1162,1471-1492,1789-1792`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:54-75`). The RX pump is the only selected caller of `BWFMRxFrame`; the control worker is the sole `do_associate` consumer. Both creation failures are unhandled, and `fw_loaded` prevents later opens from retrying startup. Added OD3595/OD3596 separately for stranded receive processing and acknowledged-but-unhandled associations. No process failure or open was induced. Source-only.

BWFM SANA-II packet/statistics command pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `CMD_READ`, raw/cooked RX delivery and TX writes through `rx_deliver`, `tx_request`, and `handle_request` (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:310-400,663-719,1590-1945`). Confirmed received lengths exclude Ethernet headers for cooked reads and include them for raw reads; callbacks receive exactly the advertised length. The `UWORD` packet type is unsigned and compares zero-extended to `ios2_PacketType`, so the EAPOL sign-extension comment is stale rather than a demonstrated mismatch. TX tracker and device counters are updated under `unit->lock`, and `S2_GETTYPESTATS` copies under the same lock; `S2_GETGLOBALSTATS` copies the aggregate without locking (`:1737-1748`). This permits an incoherent concurrent snapshot, but all fields are 32-bit `ULONG` counters and no SANA-II requirement for an atomic multi-counter snapshot was established, so no finding is credited. Raw TX bounds the frame before invoking the hook; cooked TX's `ULONG` addition wrap is already OD3592. No request or frame was issued. Source-only.
BWFM signal-quality value/caller contract pass (OD3665 added; OD3660 rechecked, 2026-10-17): read `S2_GETSIGNALQUALITY` against `Sana2SignalQuality`, its command-list advertisement, and the selected Prism2 implementation (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:95-98,1755-1778`; `compiler/include/devices/sana2wireless.h:78-83`; `workbench/devs/networks/prism2/request.c:1549-1563`). Reconfirmed OD3660's unlocked `joined` read against `link_up`'s lock. No checked-in signal-quality caller or query was found; no request or link transition was run. Source-only.

All listed SANA-II and wireless commands have dispatch cases; standard `S2_GETSPECIALSTATS`, `S2_READORPHAN`, `S2_READMGMT`, `S2_WRITEMGMT`, and `S2_GETRADIOBANDS` are omitted rather than falsely advertised. `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` checks `io_Data` for NULL but writes the full result without checking `io_Length` (`:1829-1850`). It therefore does not establish a short-buffer failure or rejection on the checked network-device paths. Source-only.
BWFM shared TX framing/credit pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced the only selected `BWFMTxData` caller (`bwfm_dev.c:692`) through its static frame, SDPCM sequence/credit check, and `bwfm_frame_rw` to SDIO function 2 (`bwfm_init.c:827-838,2112-2200`). The semaphore covers frame construction and write, so concurrent device writes cannot overwrite the shared frame. `txseq` advances only after a credit is acquired and immediately before the frame is written; the selected RX and control-response paths update `txmax` while holding the same semaphore (`:941,1098,1287`). A failed low-level SDIO write occurs after sequence advancement; the subsequent protocol resynchronization behavior depends on host/controller/firmware semantics not established from this snapshot, so no independent finding is promoted. No SDIO operation or frame was issued. Firmware credit and transport-error recovery remain open.
BWFM online/join state caller recheck (OD3613, OD3614, OD3660 retained; 2026-10-17): reread every `unit->online`/`unit->joined` access in `bwfm_dev.c` against `CMD_READ`, `rx_deliver`, `S2_ONEVENT`, `S2_OFFLINE`, `link_up/down`, `try_join`, `S2_GETSIGNALQUALITY`, and the control worker (`:426-530,660-664,875-890,1650-1722,1755-1777`). Confirmed OD3613's pre-lock online test and enqueue/drain race, OD3614's level-state snapshot and listener queue gap, and OD3660's plain joined read against locked link-up writes. `try_join` also tests `joined` without the lock before its synchronous `BWFMJoin`; multiple direct concurrent S2_ONLINE requests could both pass that check and serialize separate joins on the resource semaphore. No selected in-tree caller issues concurrent S2_ONLINE, and the device's intended caller sequencing/spec guarantee was not established, so this is recorded as an unresolved direct-client concurrency question rather than another finding. No request or link transition was run. Source-only.

BWFM asynchronous join/disassociation ordering trace (OD3597 added, 2026-10-17): compared `queue_associate`'s synchronous disassociate path with the control worker's snapshot and join sequence (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1421-1444,1502-1532`). The worker clears the shared pending bit and releases the unit lock before `BWFMJoin`; disassociation only clears that bit, so a copied job can still execute after disassociation returns if scheduling places the two calls in that window. Added OD3597. No request or schedule was run; other association and scan contracts remain open. Source-only.

BWFM escan IE bounds trace (OD3598 added, 2026-10-17): traced partial-result event sizing, per-BSS `length` validation, IE `offset`/`length` checks, post-check copy cap, and SANA-II/WirelessManager IE handoff (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1908-2023`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1255-1328`; `workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:216-278`). The IE extent comparison can wrap in 32-bit `ULONG` arithmetic before a 256-byte copy cap, so it does not prove the copy fits in the declared BSS record. Added OD3598. The remaining BWFM scan result variants and concurrency/error behavior remain open. No malformed event was supplied. Source-only.

BWFM concurrent scan ownership trace (OD3599 added, 2026-10-17): followed S2_GETNETWORKS from inline BeginIO dispatch through the function-static results buffer, BWFMScan's shared listener/ring reset, bus-semaphore release during event polling, and global BWFMScanIE storage (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1255-1273,1782,1904-1909`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1778-1810,1888-1891,1997-2033,2803-2825`). No scan-wide lock or per-request event/result state spans the transaction. Added OD3599. No concurrent request was issued. Source-only.

BWFM public control-vector length review (OD3600 added, 2026-10-17): traced exported BWFMIovar's `uint32_t` length through its 256-byte temporary-buffer check and copy, then checked all in-tree callers. `ULONG` is 32-bit; the addition can wrap before the guard, while the copy receives the unmodified length (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1742-1767`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:34-39`). The checked-in multicast caller uses at most 16 addresses plus the fixed count and the allmulti caller passes four bytes (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:942-958`), so this is limited to direct callers of the exported resource API. Added OD3600 with that limitation. No API call was made. Source-only.

BWFM key/IE parsing bounds pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `S2_SETKEY` through `BWFMSetKey` and `bwfm_wsec_key`, and `S2INFO_WPAInfo` through `BWFMJoin` and `bwfm_ie_security` (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1800-1828,1411-1437`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2300-2350,2603-2674`). `BWFMSetKey` rejects key lengths larger than its fixed key-data array before copying; the IE parser validates the outer IE length, each fixed header, suite counts and suite extents before reading. No independent bounds defect established. Firmware cipher/index semantics, API pointer validity and actual negotiation remain unverified. Source-only.

BWFM exported TX-vector extent trace (OD3601 added, 2026-10-17): traced BWFMTxData's `uint32_t ethlen` through 32-bit framed-length/padding arithmetic and its static 2,048-byte buffer, then checked the only in-tree caller (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2112-2133,2188-2196`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:655-692`). `tx_request` bounds its frame before calling the vector; direct callers of the exported resource API do not receive that protection. Added OD3601 with the in-tree limitation explicit. No API call was made. Source-only.


BWFM post-ready transport publication recheck (OD2854 strengthened; no new OD, 2026-10-17): followed FWREADY success through `SDIOEnableFunction(2)`, `bus:rxglom=0`, BCDC framing and device publication/open (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1606-1618,1647-1676,825-840,971-983`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:778-819,1158-1170`). Folded this qualified adjacent setup failure into OD2854 and removed a duplicate candidate. No SDIO failure or open was induced. Source-only.

BWFM AI core reset/activation error-path trace (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed `bwfm_ai_disable` and `bwfm_ai_reset` through ARM-CR4 and CM3 passive-state setup, SOC-RAM sizing, and `bwfm_set_active` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:232-285,401-453,438-489,798-820,1560-1620`). Reset/disable timeout is diagnostic-only and callers continue; on firmware start, activation is followed by a 2-second FWREADY/DEVREADY poll before success. On attach/passive setup, later firmware loading and ready wait provide downstream detection, but whether a timeout can leave a usable yet incorrect core state is not established from source. No candidate promoted; core reset/recovery semantics remain open pending deeper silicon behavior review. Source-only.

BWFM mailbox-read failure propagation trace (OD3602 added, 2026-10-17): followed `SDIOReadExt` error return through `bwfm_read_4`'s `0xffffffff` sentinel, `bwfm_dev_read`, the FWREADY/DEVREADY bit test, mailbox acknowledgement, firmware-start return, and selected device `fw_loaded` publication (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdio/sdio_init.c:1371-1386`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:115-125,775-778,1606-1614,1638-1680`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:778-819`). Since both readiness flags are set in all-ones, a failed read satisfies the success condition; the subsequent write error is also not checked. Added OD3602 for false startup success on mailbox read failure. No transfer failure or device startup was induced. Source-only.

BWFM OD3602 lower-layer qualification (2026-10-17): checked `sdio_command` and `sdio_rw_extended` error propagation (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdio/sdio_init.c:742-907,958-1017`). Command-response errors, per-block data errors and timeouts return nonzero through `SDIOReadExt`; the final data-end error can be swallowed and is already OD3560. Qualified OD3602 to errors actually reported by the SDIO layer, avoiding duplicate attribution of OD3560. No controller error was induced. Source-only.

BWFM CLM upload and association-parameter trace (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `BWFMLoadCLM` chunk/BEGIN/END sizing into the 300-byte iovar and 512-byte dcmd limits (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2047-2098,1015-1026,877-890`), then followed S2_SETOPTIONS SSID/passphrase/WPA-IE capture into the fixed association buffers, control worker and `BWFMJoin` (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1421-1485,1502-1527`; `bwfm_init.c:2349-2431,2282-2347`). CLM chunks fit their intermediate buffers and the control-frame cap; the selected association caller bounds copied SSID/passphrase/IE lengths, while `BWFMJoin` independently caps SSID and passphrase copies and the IE parser checks its declared extent and suite counts. No additional size defect established in this slice. Firmware acceptance of configuration changes, raw external resource callers, and broader association/key lifecycle semantics remain open. No firmware or association was run. Source-only.

BWFM RX pump and signal-lifetime caller trace (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed `BWFMRxFrame`'s SDPCM dequeue, GLOM pop and event/data handoff through the sole selected RX pump caller and the `BWFMEventPost`/SANA delivery paths (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2210-2259,2678-2710,2770-2790`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:459-585`). `BWFM_USE_IRQ` is fixed to 0 in the selected device, so its normal path does not register or wait on the SDIO interrupt signal; with a timer it polls with bounded adaptive delay, and without one it falls back to `Delay(1)`. Worker tasks have no shutdown path and increment the device open count when successfully created, so the device remains resident for their lifetime; allocation-failure and publication consequences are already OD3595/OD3596. No separate signal or ownership defect established in this selected configuration. The exported IRQ registration/re-arm path remains unreviewed for external clients. No task, interrupt or frame was run. Source-only.

USB Audio stale-input preference trigger recheck (2026-10-17; OD3238 trigger corrected): traced AHI Device preference restoration (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:645-686`) and `AllocHardware` control call (`:743-786`) through public AHI dispatch (`audioctrl.c:983-986`) into USB Audio `AHIC_Input` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:4132-4140`). The selection update sets `UAF_SELECT_INPUT` and signals the worker; while processing any pending update the worker calls `nGetInputUnit(nam)` unconditionally at `:683`, before clearing `nch_UpdateFlags` at `:762`. Thus a stale saved index on a mode with selector inputs can trigger the unchecked array dereference directly when the worker handles the selection update; the earlier report’s requirement for a later input-gain/monitor query was incorrect. This remains conditional on a saved index exceeding the replacement topology’s selector count. No device or preference file was used; source-only.

USB Audio public AHI attribute/control caller-contract pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): checked `subLibGetAttr`'s indexed frequency/input/output accesses and hardware-control input/output selection (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3935-3936,4047-4075,4132-4158`) against AHI's documented index ranges (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:367-384`) and selected preferences UI callers. `AHI_GetAudioAttrs` explicitly documents the index values as in-range; the UI obtains counts then requests each input/output with a loop index below that count (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/ahi.c:303-320`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Examples/Low-level/HardDiskRecord/HardDiskRecord.c:268-302`). Those accesses are contract-valid in these callers. The stale persisted `AHIC_Input` mismatch remains OD3238 because it applies a saved selector index without validating it against the replacement topology; it is not evidence of invalid index use by the documented attribute callers. No independent in-contract defect established; other direct AHI clients and USB Audio entry points remain in scope for continued review. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI allocation-failure unwind pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `subLibAllocAudio`'s early returns after subdriver data publication, Poseidon/timer acquisition, message-port/pipe creation, mode selection, primary buffer allocation, and duplex sibling setup (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3263-3555`) through AHI `_AHI_AllocAudioA` failure handling and `_AHI_FreeAudio` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:481-520,708-728`). AHI calls the subdriver FreeAudio hook even when the subdriver allocation result has AHISF_ERROR; the hook's NULL checks cover nullable pipes/buffers/requests, and Exec documents `DeleteMsgPort(NULL)` as safe (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:19-25,51-58`). The hook clears `nch_CurrentMode` and releases any initialized resources; no distinct primary-mode resource leak or invalid free established in these inspected failure branches. Interface alternate-setting restoration when no zero-bandwidth alternate exists is already OD3361; binding-record rollback is OD3209. Duplex-specific startup cleanup and concurrent teardown are not closed by this pass. Source-only.

Deneb interrupt OUT buffer-copy recheck (2026-10-17; OD3585 expanded, no duplicate): traced request transfer length through `uhwScheduleIntPTDs`, which sets `ptd_BufLen` to the request or current granule, then copies `(ptd_BufLen + 3) >> 2` longwords from `iouh_Data` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4068-4147`). `uhwHandleFinishedInts` uses the same rounded-word source read when it schedules a continuation chunk (`:2968-3012`). The USBHardware API defines `iouh_Length` as a byte count and states interrupt data is split into `iouh_MaxPktSize` packets, without requiring word-aligned length or storage (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:374-395`). A non-longword-sized final OUT chunk therefore causes the same one-to-three-byte read past that chunk's requested extent as the paths in OD3585. This is the same copy primitive/root cause, so OD3585 now includes interrupt scheduling and continuation. No transfer was run. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary interrupt completion and continuation pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed interrupt completion-map dispatch into `uhwHandleFinishedInts` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2784-3035,4798-4805,5304-5315`). A completed IN PTD copies at most the remaining `iouh_Length` and records overflow; a short packet terminates with `UHIOERR_RUNTPACKET` unless `UHFF_ALLOWRUNTPKTS` is set; otherwise a full chunk rearms the PTD while `iouh_Actual < iouh_Length`, capping the final chunk. These branches match the documented byte count, packetization, and runt-packet flag (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:374-395`). OUT continuation's rounded caller read is included under OD3585. This pass does not validate ISP1760 status-field semantics, interrupt interval encoding, split-transaction scheduling, or retry timing; those remain open. No request or hardware was run. Source-only.

Deneb interrupt interval input normalization pass (2026-10-17; no new OD established): traced `pep_Interval` construction through Poseidon's `AllocPipe`: full/low-speed interrupt values stay in frames (milliseconds), low-speed values below 8 are raised to 8, and high-/SuperSpeed `bInterval` is bounded then converted to `2^(bInterval-1)` microframes (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8483-8605`). The values are copied into interrupt requests without further conversion (`:4620-4630`); this matches the public API's USB 1.1 millisecond / USB 2.0 125-microsecond units (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:107-116`). Deneb's split and non-split PTD encoders branch on these normalized values (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4055-4117`). The C source/register comments alone do not establish whether all interval encodings map to the intended ISP1760 service cadence, particularly high-speed values above one frame; no hardware manual or runtime schedule was checked, so no correctness claim or new finding is made. ISP1760 interval-field semantics and split-transaction timing remain explicitly open. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary interrupt NAK retry/timeout pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `UHFF_NAKTIMEOUT` from request admission through `uhwScheduleIntPTDs`, NAK completion retry, periodic timeout sampling, and `FreeInt` cleanup (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4148-4162,2870-2900,4844-4988,1700-1725`). The driver stores deadlines in the extended 125-µs frame counter, converts the documented millisecond timeout to microframes with `<<3`, retries active NAK PTDs until the deadline, and clears the per-PTD timeout map on release. The timeout sampler handles the controller's frame-counter-overflow status before rebuilding the high counter bits; its 100/250ms polling intervals are below the 1.024s 13-bit microframe-counter wrap. No independent timeout accounting or stale-map defect established in this source trace. This does not verify controller register timing or simultaneous timer/level-6 access beyond the existing interrupt exclusion review. No request or hardware was run. Source-only.

Deneb caller-buffer alignment audit (2026-10-17; OD3603 added): checked `iouh_Data` use across PIO control, bulk, interrupt and isochronous IN/OUT completions and scheduling. These paths cast the caller byte pointer, sometimes advanced by actual bytes, to `ULONG *` and dereference it (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2435-2455,2505-2510,2582-2588,2623-2635,2688-2694,2909-2922,2973-2980,3243-3256,3293-3300,4130-4137,4718-4725`). The API explicitly says even alignment is not guaranteed (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:124-132`); the m68k linker script confirms odd longword accesses fault on 68000/010 (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/kobj-romtag.ld:23-24`). Bulk DMA checks 4-byte alignment and falls back to PIO when the base is unaligned (`uhwcmd.c:4261-4265,4327-4355`), leaving an odd pointer exposed. This is distinct from OD3585's rounded tail access, since a multiple-of-four request length with an odd start still faults. No request or hardware was run. Source-only.


Deneb active-PTD AbortIO reply ownership recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): checked `cmdAbortIO` exactly: in each active ATL/INT/ISO branch it clears `ptd->ptd_IOReq` before calling `FreeATL`, `FreeInt` or `FreeIso` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1820-1863`). Each helper's `ReplyMsg` is conditional on a non-NULL local request, so these calls do not reply; after `cmdAbortIO` returns true, `devAbortIO` sets IOERR_ABORTED and `TermIO` performs the sole request reply (`dev.c:679-686`; `uhwcmd.c:1605-1623`). The proposed double-reply candidate was unsupported and was removed from the report and index. OD3584 remains distinct: `FreeATL` later dereferences that NULL local request only when handling its DMA cleanup branch. No request or reply port was run. Source-only.

Deneb ATL DMA completion/state-machine pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced single-PTD ownership from `uhwScheduleATLPTDs` through `hu_DMAPTD` assignment, cache setup, buffer-valid sequencing, `uhwLevel6Int` notification, `uhwDMATask`, and `uhwHandleDMAInt` state transitions (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4251-4355,4458-4506,4995-5263,5280-5401`). Only one ATL PTD can own DMA at a time; allocation falls back to the PIO buffer path for unsuitable addresses, lengths or an occupied DMA slot. DMA-IN final copy length is rounded to the request's rounded extent, and DMA-OUT padding is covered by OD3585. Normal completion releases the PTD and clears `hu_DMAPTD`; error/abort handling clears it through `FreeATL`, with the existing abort cache-cleanup NULL dereference documented in OD3584. No separate stable-state or completion-order defect was established in the traced transitions. DMA-task creation failure and shutdown/join remain OD3581/OD3582, and allocation/cache/hardware behavior was not exercised. Source-only.

BWFM EROM core-discovery and attach-caller pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced the DMP component/port walk and register-address extraction (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:285-398`) through the core table and attach validation (`:521-635`). Enumeration caps writes at `BWFM_MAX_CORES` (24; `bwfm_private.h:18-26,57-58`); `bwfm_dmp_get_regaddr` distinguishes component boundaries and EOT, while a reported SDIO backplane-read failure becomes all-ones/EOT (`bwfm_init.c:113-125`, descriptor mask and EOT in `bwfmreg.h:88-93`). Attach validates the CPU/RAM needs and requires ChipCommon, 802.11, and SDIO cores before any later unconditional dereferences (`:578-630`); `bwfm_get_pmu`'s ChipCommon dereference is therefore safe in this call chain (`:204-216`). No independent bounds or missing-core dereference established for the selected attach path. The scanner is still not explicitly bounded by an EROM byte range; absent a hardware-defined end marker, malformed/corrupt EROM could continue reading descriptors. No EROM or SDIO error was induced. Source-only.

BWFM RX/TX framing and selected SANA-II handoff pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `bwfm_rx_read`'s SDPCM header/checksum, rounded FIFO read and 2 KiB frame bound; `bwfm_frame_eth`'s data-offset/BDC-header extents; GLOM sub-frame validation/queue offsets and truncation; `BWFMRxFrame` dispatch; and the RX pump's event/data handoff into `rx_deliver` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1074-1149,1265-1347,2210-2254`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:308-394,459-547`). The selected pump supplies a non-null `ETH_FRAME_LEN` buffer and is the only RX FIFO consumer; bus access and the shared GLOM queue are serialized by `bwfm_Sem`. Oversize/malformed ordinary frames are rejected after the FIFO header has been consumed, so a device-side malformed frame can leave unread payload and desynchronize subsequent reads; no supported firmware/AP path producing such a frame was established, and this is not promoted as a finding. Traced `BWFMTxData`'s static staging buffer, padded-length cap, credit wait (releases the bus semaphore for the RX pump), and FIFO write against `tx_request`'s `ETH_FRAME_LEN` bound and opener callback (`bwfm_init.c:2111-2196`; `bwfm_dev.c:632-682`); the selected caller caps data before callback/copy, and staging is serialized. No additional selected-path size or ownership defect established. No frame or hardware transfer was run. BWFM external resource callers and hardware-specific FIFO/error recovery remain open.

USB Audio AHI stream start/stop contract reconciliation (2026-10-17; existing OD3174, no duplicate): traced AHI's `AHIsub_Start` dispatch and stop/free sequencing (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:583-628,648-690`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3692-3748,3777-3807,3570-3650`). Playback and recording start each call `psdStartRTIso` but ignore its result and set `AHIE_OK`; the established OD3174 already captures this false-success behavior. `subLibStop` stops the requested RTIso path and `subLibFreeAudio` stops, frees handlers, then releases buffers, with callback-quiescence tracked separately as OD3517. No additional independent start/stop defect established in this pass; no stream was run. Other AHI controls, callback timing and Deneb backend teardown remain open.

Deneb AbortIO/CMD_FLUSH request-completion reconciliation (2026-10-17; OD3584 retained, no duplicate): rechecked `devAbortIO`'s pending-message gate and `TermIO` after `cmdAbortIO`, plus queued-request removal and ATL/INT/ISO PTD scans (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:658-687`; `uhwcmd.c:1612-1628,1778-1866`). The active PTD path clears `ptd_IOReq` before its Free helper, suppressing the helper's conditional ReplyMsg; `devAbortIO` then gives the request one termination reply. This invalidated an earlier double-reply suspicion; OD3584 remains the distinct DMA cleanup null dereference when the cleared PTD is `hu_DMAPTD`. CMD_FLUSH sets IOERR_ABORTED and frees each queued or active PTD under Disable (`uhwcmd.c:973-1051`); it preserves each active PTD's request pointer until the helper performs reply and DMA cache cleanup. The ISO scheduler publishes one request per PTD and completion either replies or requeues it, so the AbortIO first-match scan does not leave sibling PTDs from one ordinary request (`uhwcmd.c:4532-4774`). Disable plus interrupt/task scheduling behavior is single-CPU for this m68k target; no concurrent SMP path applies. No request or controller was exercised. Reset-vs-I/O OD3583, DMA abort OD3584, and remaining hardware completion ordering stay tracked/open.


Deneb high-speed interrupt multiplier producer/consumer trace (OD3604 added, 2026-10-17): traced Poseidon's HS endpoint descriptor multiplier extraction and `UHFF_MULTI_2/3` pipe-template flags (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8477-8484,4534-4545`) into Deneb `uhwScheduleIntPTDs`. The scheduler programs `MaxPktSize` and translation length but omits `QHA0F_MULTI_*`; its candidate multiplier code is commented (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4000-4004,4058-4070,4110-4115`), whereas the bulk scheduler programs those bits (`:4419-4431`). This initial reading incorrectly concluded that a high-speed interrupt endpoint with MULT=2/3 was programmed for one transaction per microframe and added OD3604 for that path; the full scheduler branch recheck below found that the non-split interrupt path does set QHA0F_MULTI_1/2/3, so this interrupt claim is withdrawn. The ISO scheduler's separately commented multiplier handling is noted but not promoted here because its buffer/request contract needs additional analysis. No endpoint or controller was exercised; source-only.


Deneb high-speed isochronous multiplier follow-up (OD3604 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced Poseidon's endpoint MULT extraction/pipe flags through the selected USB Audio `psdAllocRTIsoHandler` calls (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8477-8484,4534-4545`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3215-3231`) into Deneb `cmdAddIsoHandler` and `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1090-1150,1160-1221,4532-4774`). RTIso copies flags but each alternating PTD buffer is only `MaxPktSize`; neither PTD gets `QHA0F_MULTI_2/3`. Ordinary ISO's multiplier bits are also commented out and each PTD length is capped at one `MaxPktSize`. This initial follow-up correctly identified the isochronous multiplier omission but incorrectly retained the interrupt scope; the later full interrupt-scheduler recheck below narrows the current OD3604 finding to isochronous endpoints only. The single-packet storage limitation remains. No stream or endpoint was used; source-only.

Deneb split-transaction interrupt caller/consumer pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced Poseidon's TT hub/port/think-time derivation into `UHFF_SPLITTRANS`, `UHFF_LOWSPEED`, split hub address/port and `UHFF_TT_MULTI` pipe flags (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4500-4505,4578-4593`) and then Deneb's interrupt PTD split fields and completion byte accounting (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4058-4099,2820-2991`). Deneb uses the split hub address/port, low-speed flag, start-split position and complete-split mask; completion selects the split-transaction transfer-count field. No independent state or bounds defect established. Exact ISP1760 TT scheduling and `UHFF_TT_MULTI` semantics cannot be proven from checked-in source/docs, so interval/microframe behavior remains open and is not promoted. No hub or transfer was exercised. Source-only.

OpenSBI dwuart serial-unit constructor rollback/reset-callback check (2026-10-17; no new OD): re-read `DWSerUnit__Root__New` from superclass construction through callback registration and IRQ setup, then followed normal final close through `serial.device` to `DWSerUnit__Root__Dispose` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:77-261`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:233-258`; `dwuart/SerialClass.c:104-129`). No fallible constructor branch remains after `AddResetCallback`; a failed nonzero IRQ registration still returns the constructed unit (OD1562), and normal disposal removes the IRQ handle then reset callback before superclass disposal. Thus no separate failed-construction callback leak is established. Cross-CPU reset dispatch remains the generic EK59 lifetime concern; no UART/reset was run. Source-only.

ATA polling-option PIO completion check (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced the `ATA=poll` tooltype (`rom/devs/ata/ata_init.c:210-219`) through `ata_WaitBusyTO` and `ata_exec_cmd` (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:440-568,582-790`) to `Hidd_ATABus_HandleIRQ` (`rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:22-43`). The option forces the wait helper to poll BSY instead of waiting on the task signal, but it does not clear the bus IRQ handler or bypass the controller's interrupt dispatch. PIO read/write data handlers are still installed before command issue and consume the data phases when hardware IRQs arrive; the final task-side status read merely clears a pending status interrupt. Thus no missing PIO transfer in polling mode is established. IRQ delivery during transfers and board/controller behavior remain untested. Source-only.

PC i8042 Utility-reference finding restored (OD985, 2026-10-17): restored the missing detailed finding and index entry after reconciling the existing per-file row. `i8042Kbd_InitAttrs` successfully opens Utility before the class initializer; its expunge hook checks `!cs_UtilityBase`, so it skips the required close. If the later `i8042_Init` returns FALSE because neither keyboard nor mouse driver was installed, generated startup invokes expunge hooks and frees the failed module base; Exec's `CloseLibrary(NULL)` is a no-op, so the real Utility reference remains open (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_init.c:38-45,59-81`; `i8042_classinit.c:28-73`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:60-69`; `rom/exec/closelibrary.c:55-77`). The trigger is limited to successful early initialization followed by failed driver registration. No module load failure was induced. Source-only.

OpenSBI DesignWare I²C FDT status-property boundary check (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `dwi2c_enabled`'s two-character tests through the selected shared `FDT_GetPropStr` implementation (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_init.c:106-116`; `arch/riscv-all/linklibs/fdt/fdt.c:212-217`). The string helper discards the property length and returns its in-place pointer; a malformed one-byte `status` property could make the driver's second-byte test read beyond that property. The source tree contains no selected OpenSBI DTS/DTSI descriptors to establish such a value, and the FDT string contract requires a NUL-terminated string, so this malformed-input edge is retained as an open firmware/parser-boundary question, not a numbered driver finding. No DTB was supplied or opened; source-only.

OpenSBI DesignWare I²C timing arithmetic boundary check (2026-10-17; no new OD): re-read the input-clock conversion and SCL/SDA count arithmetic (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_hw.c:71-139`). The fixed high/low timing expressions use UQUAD intermediates and their supported FDT clock-frequency input range cannot overflow that intermediate; resulting counts are narrowed to ULONG. The configurable SDA hold expression narrows its UQUAD quotient to ULONG before comparing with the 16-bit hardware limit, so sufficiently extreme input-clock and `i2c-sda-hold-time-ns` values can wrap below the saturation threshold. No checked-in OpenSBI DT descriptor establishes such multi-gigahertz/seconds-scale inputs, and the practical hardware timing contract is not established from this source set; retain as an input-boundary question, not a numbered finding. No DTB or controller was run; source-only.

Deneb interrupt PTD continuation/retry pass (2026-10-17; no MULT finding on the interrupt path): reread `uhwHandleFinishedInts` against `uhwScheduleIntPTDs` and the interrupt-request queue (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2784-3006,3957-4164`). The NAK-active branch retains its PTD unless the configured frame timeout expires; completion updates per-endpoint toggle and actual count, clamps inbound copies to the remaining caller length, and either reuses the staging buffer for the next chunk or releases the PTD. The rounded longword OUT staging copy from caller storage is OD3585. A stalled endpoint is completed as NAKTIMEOUT only when UHFF_NAKTIMEOUT was requested. The full non-split interrupt PTD branch encodes `QHA0F_MULTI_1/2/3` from the request flags (`:4082-4092`), so the earlier interrupt MULT concern is withdrawn; the separate ordinary and RTIso ISO multiplier omission is tracked as OD3604. Split-transaction hardware timing remains open. No endpoint, request or controller was exercised. This closes only this interrupt completion/scheduler source slice; other Deneb request classes and hardware behavior remain partial. Source-only.


Deneb interrupt-multiplier finding correction (OD3604 narrowed, 2026-10-17): re-read the complete selected `uhwScheduleIntPTDs` PTD construction branch. Unlike ordinary/RTIso scheduling, its non-split interrupt path does set `QHA0F_MULTI_1/2/3` from `UHFF_MULTI_2/3` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4082-4092`); split transactions are the separate full/low-speed TT path. The previous OD3604 claim that high-speed interrupt PTDs omit the multiplier was incorrect and is withdrawn. OD3604 now applies only to the ordinary and RTIso isochronous paths, where multiplier programming remains absent and storage is limited to one `MaxPktSize`. The earlier 2026-10-17 interrupt-expansion ledger entry is superseded by this correction. No endpoint or controller was exercised; source-only.


Deneb ordinary isochronous zero-byte completion follow-up (OD3587 expanded, 2026-10-17): rechecked the `len && (Actual + MaxPktSize < Length)` continuation gate in `uhwHandleFinishedIsos` against the public packetized ISO request contract. In addition to the existing one-packet/final-partial strict-boundary cases, a zero-byte successful PTD completion bypasses continuation even when `iouh_Actual < iouh_Length`, then falls through to `FreeIso`. This extends the same premature-completion defect conditionally on the controller reporting an empty/missed ISO packet as successful rather than an error. No device/controller was exercised; source-only.

AHCI PRDT map-load and completion path recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): re-read `ahci_load_prdt`, its callback and `ahci_unload_prdt` against both callers: the NCQ error-log read (`ahci.c:3656-3689`) and normal ATA command path (`:3921-3949,3953-3985`). The shim does not store `data` in the dummy map passed to CachePreDMA/PostDMA, but boot manifests select AHCI only on x86 PC, where selected Exec hooks do no cache maintenance and return the input address; the apparent NULL-map issue does not establish a selected-target fault (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:73`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66`; `rom/exec/cachepredma.c:68-75`; `cachepostdma.c:56-68`). AHCI SCSI CDB-length candidate recheck (OD3237 retained, 2026-10-17): compared both `HD_SCSICMD` dispatch branches and SCSI translators (`ahci_io.c:388-396`; `ahci_scsi.c:332-352,443-489,582-615`). Bluetooth HID binding/channel cleanup follow-up (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced bAllocHid success/failure through bOpenReportChannels, task readiness signaling, the binding caller, bReleaseServiceBinding, and bFreeHid (bthid.class.c:240-290,294-345,904-1043,1056-1158,1162-1291). The read-buffer failure unwind was checked against allocator semantics: btAllocVec uses a Bluetooth pool created with MEMF_CLEAR, and Exec AllocPooled clears allocations, so untouched nhb_ReadBuf slots are NULL. The worker nhb_Task publication occurs only after report setup succeeds, and release waits for the worker to clear it before binding storage is reclaimed. No distinct setup/teardown defect established in these selected paths; broader GUI/control task and channel contracts remain open. Source-only.

NVMe admin timeout caller expansion (OD2361/OD2860, 2026-10-17): traced all Hidd_NVMEBus_Start admin waits against the shared stack busehandle and nvme_WaitTO. Namespace Identify and LBA Range Get Features both proceed based on ceh_Status without checking the returned signal mask; Get Features can interpret a zero-filled range page as no configured range and publish the full namespace, even when HIDE was configured. Expanded OD2860. Queue Create timeouts can be followed by later admin commands reusing the same stack handler; any late completion after bus-start return reaches the expired handler and may DMA into the freed 8 KiB response buffer (OD2361). The initial Set Features no-signal return bypasses buffer and Expansion cleanup, and timer-open failure after buffer allocation bypasses buffer cleanup (OD3622). The bus remains an external/direct AddBus route under selected-controller blocker OD2876. No device or timeout was run. Source-only.

NVMe early-start cleanup boundary recheck (2026-10-17; OD3622 confirmed and narrowed): verified the initial allocation/open order and every early return in `Hidd_NVMEBus_Start` (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:257-268,307-319,667-675`). Normal completion frees the buffer and closes Expansion. The ordinary final cleanup unconditionally calls `CloseLibrary(ExpansionBase)`, but this is not an additional defect: `TaggedOpenLibrary` may return NULL (`rom/exec/taggedopenlibrary.c:89-111`) and `CloseLibrary(NULL)` is explicitly legal (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:35-40,64-89`). OD3622 remains limited to skipped cleanup on the two early paths. No allocation/open failure or device was run; source-only.

BCM2712 PCI boot-time Command/Status caller follow-up (OD2949 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced `Root::New` through `PCIE_BridgeSetup` to `SetupEndpoint` (`driverclass.c:74-88`; `pcie2712_init.c:893-975`). The setup path reads PCI config dword 0x04, ORs `PCICMF_MEMDECODE`, and writes the complete dword (`:875-876`), so it echoes any set write-one-to-clear Status bits. This happens before endpoint driver setup for the first downstream endpoint. Expanded OD2949 to include this selected Pi 5 boot-time route; the same condition remains required (a relevant Status error bit must already be latched). No board or config access was run; source-only.
BCM2712 trained-endpoint BAR0 sizing review (OD3638 added, 2026-10-17): traced the `data->trained` call into `SetupEndpoint` and its BAR probe/assignment sequence (`pcie2712_init.c:828-876,973-975`). BAR type detection permits a 64-bit BAR and the final assignment writes its upper address dword, but the sizing probe writes/reads only offset 0x10 and calculates a `ULONG` size from the low mask. A 64-bit BAR size requiring upper mask bits is therefore truncated or read as zero before alignment/window-fit checks. Added OD3638, conditional on a trained link and a 64-bit BAR0 at endpoint 0:0. No matching endpoint, link training or board was exercised; source-only.
BCM2712 trained-endpoint BAR attribute candidate withdrawn (OD3639, 2026-10-17): rechecked `SetupEndpoint` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/hidd/pci-bcm2712/pcie2712_init.c:839-858`) against PCI BAR semantics and the local comment that all-ones probing returns only writable bits. The low memory-BAR type/prefetch fields are hardware-defined read-only attributes, so writing the aligned base address with a zero low nibble does not establish that hardware clears them; the earlier report's lost-attribute claim was unsupported and OD3639 has been removed from the report and index. Linux's PCI probe follows the same hardware contract: it decodes the type from the original BAR and writes back the original value after probing ([Linux `drivers/pci/probe.c`](https://code.googlesource.com/linux/torvalds/linux/+/3cb12d27ff655e57e8efe3486dca2a22f4e30578/drivers/pci/probe.c)). OD3638's separate incomplete 64-bit size probe remains. No hardware or configuration transaction was run.
BWFM chip topology and upload-path focused pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): reread EROM descriptor iteration, core-table publication, required-core checks, passive/reset sequencing, SOCRAM/TCM sizing and `bwfm_ram_write` through the selected `BWFMAttach` / `BWFMStartFirmware` callers (`bwfm_init.c:144-697,703-753,1564-1601`; `bwfm_dev.c:740-778`). The upload writer rounds final chunks to 64 bytes; the known supported RAM bases are 32-KiB aligned, but malformed EROM bounds, SDIO failure/readback behavior, chip-specific RAM layout, and padding at the RAM end need device/spec evidence before treating the padding as a separate defect. BWFM ordinary RX frame-length rejection follow-up (OD3640 added, 2026-10-17): traced `bwfm_rx_read`'s 12-byte header read, length/checksum checks, rounded body bound, and callers `BWFMRxFrame`/the RX pump (`bwfm_init.c:1074-1102,2210-2255`; `bwfm_dev.c:492-497`). When a structurally checksum-valid `frmlen` exceeds the static 2-KiB buffer, the function returns before reading the body. GLOM's own comment states that leaving announced FIFO bytes unread desynchronizes subsequent reads (`bwfm_init.c:1201-1205`). Added OD3640 for the oversized-frame recovery path; malformed headers whose length cannot be trusted remain a separate recovery question. No SDIO transfer or frame was used; source-only.
BWFM RX ethernet framing and GLOM queue bounds pass (OD3640/OD3591 rechecked, 2026-10-17; no further finding): traced `bwfm_frame_eth`, event classification, GLOM subframe extraction/queue publication, queue pop and the pump buffer size (`bwfm_init.c:1110-1159,1216-1380,2218-2249`; `bwfm_dev.c:458-459,496-530`). Ordinary BCDC/data-offset checks bound the frame start and body to the decoded SDPCM payload; queued offsets/lengths use a 32-KiB backing store and UWORD metadata, while the already-reported first-subframe underflow OD3591 remains the exceptional path that can bypass those bounds. The pump's 1,518-byte buffer covers the configured Ethernet frame limit; larger caller buffers are truncated by the public API and no selected oversized-frame client was found. Added OD3640 for the earlier oversized raw SDPCM frame which is rejected before its FIFO body is drained. No additional defect established in the inspected queue/frame paths; full firmware frame-contract semantics remain open. No frame or pump was run; source-only.
BWFM control-poll receive-buffer follow-up (OD3640 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced `bwfm_dcmd`'s 512-byte response buffer and interleaved EVENT/DATA/GLOM handling (`bwfm_init.c:877-1005`). Its valid-header oversized check returns at `:934-938` before reading the payload, unlike the ordinary 2-KiB RX path's equivalent check (`:1092-1098`). Since the same control loop explicitly expects interleaved network data while polling, a normal Ethernet-sized packet can exceed this 500-byte payload limit; unread FIFO data then corrupts frame alignment and the command fails. Expanded OD3640 to include this selected in-tree control-poll path, distinct buffer limit, and ordinary traffic trigger. No request or packet was run; source-only.

BWFM GLOM first-subframe bound recheck (OD3591 retained, 2026-10-17; no duplicate): re-read descriptor length parsing and queue publication in `bwfm_rx_glom`, `bwfm_frame_eth`, and `bwfm_glom_pop` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1247-1337`). BWFM TX credit, timer fallback, and selected SANA-II caller pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `tx_request` through `BWFMTxData` and `bwfm_frame_rw` (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:645-696`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2112-2202,1425-1468`). BWFM receive delivery and per-opener pending-read pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `BWFMRxFrame` output sizing into `rx_deliver`, selected SANA-II opener callbacks, packet filtering, read removal/reply, and stats accounting (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2210-2259`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:308-396,1854-1883`). PCI IRQ bridge-walk termination trace (OD3648 added, 2026-10-17): re-read `AssignIRQ` and `FindBridge` against setup and device-scan callers (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:104-192,216-319`). For a nonzero PCI interrupt pin, an unmatched route repeatedly follows the bridge whose secondary bus equals the current bus; there is no visited-bus/hop bound, so a malformed cyclic bridge mapping can keep the synchronous `HW__HW__SetUpDriver` call from returning. Added OD3648, conditional on a supplied routing table, unmatched pin and cyclic firmware/configuration topology. No PCI hardware or malformed topology was used; source-only.
OD3648 PCIPC caller applicability follow-up (2026-10-17): traced the selected ACPI PCIPC setup's per-host-bridge routing-list initialization and passed instance tag into `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:71-110,477-482,604-626`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:174-205`). The PCI class receives a non-NULL routing-list pointer for each ACPI host bridge even when the list has no matching entries, so an unmatched pin reaches the bridge-parent walk; legacy PCIPC setup omits the routing tag and does not trigger this exact path. The malformed cyclic bus mapping condition remains untested. Source-only.
