BWFM SANA-II transmit copy-hook caller trace (OD3592 confirmed, 2026-10-17): re-read `tx_request` and the opener initialization path (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:652-692,1127-1138`) and confirmed that `S2_CopyFromBuff`, `S2_CopyFromBuff16`, and `S2_CopyFromBuff32` are accepted as caller-supplied hooks. In cooked mode the code forms the 32-bit frame length before checking it, then invokes the selected hook with the original `ios2_DataLength` and `txbuf + ETH_HLEN`; the guard does not constrain that callback length when the addition wrapped. The reviewed AROSTCP code at `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:900-1038` is the receive/poll path and does not supply or constrain the write hook, so it neither removes nor independently demonstrates the condition. Existing OD3592 remains a direct SANA-II caller-contract finding; manifestation requires a client hook that copies the requested count. No write request or hook was run. Other BWFM write variants and lifecycle remain open. Source-only.

BWFM write-command dispatch follow-up (OD3592 applies to all three cooked write forms, 2026-10-17): traced `handle_request` dispatch (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1881-1889`). `S2_BROADCAST` overwrites the destination then falls through; `CMD_WRITE` and `S2_MULTICAST` call the same `tx_request` without a separate length validation. Therefore each reaches the same cooked-length addition and hook call when not RAW; no command-specific mitigation or additional independent defect was found in this dispatch slice. No request was issued; direct SANA-II client behavior beyond this shared path remains open. Source-only.

BWFM configured-station-address candidate recheck (OD3647 retained, 2026-10-17): searched all BWFM references to `cur_etheraddr`, `hwaddr`, and `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE`, then traced `S2_GETSTATIONADDRESS` and `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` beside `BWFMGetMAC` (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:784-789,1644-1657`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1686-1710`). The only firmware MAC read is at initialization; configuration copies the caller address into `unit->hwaddr`, while cooked TX uses that software field, and no later firmware MAC SET or refresh exists in the selected sources. The selected AROSTCP open path queries then configures the same address (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:355-382,465-475`), so the mismatch remains specific to a client that supplies a different address. Existing OD3647 is retained with that client condition; firmware RX-filter behavior is still unverified. No request or card was used. Source-only.
PCNet32 startup allocation/status recheck (OD3650 added, 2026-10-17): traced `pcnet32_open`'s two per-open DMA allocations through its `oom` branch, function return, successful Open vector and later `S2_ONLINE` (`workbench/devs/networks/pcnet32/pcnet32.c:297-324,331-440`; `pcnet32_init.c:241-246`; `handler.c:667-687`). If either allocation fails, initialization and `IFF_UP` publication are skipped but the callback still returns zero; Open ignores the result, while S2_ONLINE treats zero as success. A one-sided successful allocation remains stored and is overwritten on retry. Added OD3650 with false success and partial-buffer leak consequences; no allocation failure or device was induced. Source-only.
PCNet32 OD3650 close/teardown consequence check (2026-10-17): followed the one-sided DMA-allocation failure through `Close` and `DeleteUnit` (`workbench/devs/networks/pcnet32/pcnet32_init.c:251-277`; `unit.c:1367-1404`; `pcnet32.c:445-476`). `Close` invokes `unit->stop` only when `IFF_UP` is set; the failed-start path leaves it clear, so `pcn32_close` does not free the surviving RX/TX allocation. `DeleteUnit` then frees `fe_priv` without freeing those packet buffers. This strengthens OD3650's partial-allocation leak: it can persist through failed-open-client close and unit deletion, even without a successful retry; the report's retry-overwrite case remains another path. No allocation failure or teardown was induced. Source-only.
Realtek8180 OD3263 initialization-caller trace (2026-10-17): followed the USB register hooks into `InitialiseAdapter` and `ReadEEPROM` (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/unit.c:422-496`; `eeprom.c:99-111`). An unchecked `LELongIn(RXCONF)` selects `eeprom_addr_size`, which controls the number of EEPROM address bits used while reading the default MAC; later, the reset polling loop decides `success` from `ByteIn(COMMAND)` (`unit.c:488-505`). The hooks ignore `psdDoPipe` errors and the IN hooks return locals not initialized before the transfer (`usb.c:785-801,855-861,909-916,936-943`). On a disconnect/error, the reset read therefore does not reliably establish reset completion; if the returned local happens to test clear, initialization may proceed despite the failed control transfer. `CreateUnit` then sets `UNITF_HAVEADAPTER` unconditionally after `InitialiseAdapter` and publishes the unit only if its return remains true (`unit.c:241-245,262-278`). This confirms OD3263's caller consequence without claiming deterministic false success or duplicating OD3273's pre-publication release-hook race. No transfer or device was used. Source-only.

BWFM `bwfm_init.c` attach/control/scan source recheck (2026-10-17; no new OD): re-read SDIO register access, EROM/core enumeration, required-core validation, passivation/RAM sizing, ALP and firmware startup, SDPCM control response bounds, event-ring ownership, timer setup/cleanup, scan-result BSS/IE parsing, CLM chunk upload, and exported TX/RX entry points (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:63-2250`). The malformed first GLOM subframe case still matches OD3591: a subframe length below the 12-byte prefix underflows unsigned `subtot`, bypasses the later embedded-frame extent check, and can publish an offset/length beyond the 32-KiB saved-frame buffer; `BWFMRxFrame` later delivers queued frames under the same semaphore. The scan parser validates each BSS record extent before reading fixed fields and caps copied IEs; its diagnostic-only invalid-IE byte reads are behind `DEBUG 0` and do not add a selected-build defect. The event and glom buffers are serialized by `bwfm_Sem`; no new issue was established in the reviewed regions. This does not complete the file audit: chip-core/reset assumptions, mailbox/error semantics, data-channel flow control and firmware key lifecycle still require full function/caller reconciliation. No frame, card, timer, or firmware was used. Source-only.

BWFM core-reset error propagation review (OD3651 added, 2026-10-17): traced `bwfm_ai_disable`/`bwfm_ai_reset` timeout branches through `bwfm_set_passive`, `bwfm_do_attach`, `BWFMAttach`, and the selected device firmware loader (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:232-283,400-435,638-699`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:741-759`). Reset poll expiry is not returned; passivation and attach continue, and `bwfm_do_attach` publishes `bwfm_attached` true. `bwfm_write_4` ignores transfer status and `bwfm_read_4` maps reported errors to all-ones, so an SDIO transfer failure can enter the same unchecked path. Added OD3651 for conditional false-success attachment after a failed required core reset. Distinct from OD3602's later firmware-ready mailbox read. No hardware or transfer failure was induced. Source-only.

BWFM coverage status clarification: the preceding attach/control/scan pass recorded no additional issue in its reviewed behaviors; the separate required-core reset timeout/error-propagation path was subsequently added as OD3651. Deneb interrupt completion/scheduling caller pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): traced `devBeginIO` through `cmdIntXFer`, the queued request, `uhwSoftInt`, `uhwHandleFinishedInts`, `FreeInt`, and Poseidon pipe construction (`dev.c:529-639`; `uhwcmd.c:936-958,2784-3004,3957-4188,4790-4821`; `poseidon.library.c:4532-4548,4612-4627`). Deneb worker-task startup failure caller reconciliation (OD3581 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): followed `Open_Unit`'s `AddTask` result across all three selected targets (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:452-484`; `mmakefile.src:25-44`). In `NODMA` builds the task performs signaled PIO copies; in `denebdmausb`, level-6 DMA completion signals this same task and returns, and only the task invokes `uhwHandleDMAInt` to advance the state machine (`uhwcmd.c:2180-2198,5000-5052,5281-5299,5372-5401`). The existing OD3581 is therefore applicable to DMA completion/reply stalls as well as PIO transfer stalls; the report and index now state both effects. No new finding. Creation failure and hardware behavior were not induced; source-only.

Deneb close/worker lifetime target reconciliation (OD3582 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): compared `Close_Unit`'s controller shutdown, Ctrl-C signal, fixed 10-ms delay and `FreeVec(unit)` with the worker's wait loop and task layout (`uhwcmd.c:502-525,5374-5401`; `denebusb.h:277,328`). The task checks/processes `SIGF_SINGLE` before observing Ctrl-C at loop exit; its DMA-build state machine performs register-memory copies and accesses the unit/controller mapping, while `NODMA` variants also copy through the worker. Since the task and stack reside in the freed unit allocation and there is no exit handshake, OD3582 applies to all three targets, not just PIO builds. Expanded the report and index. This is a source-level lifetime/scheduling condition; no timing or hardware run was performed.

Deneb control request endian/caller reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new finding): followed Poseidon's `psdPipeSetup`/`psdDoPipe` SET_ADDRESS request into the raw USB setup packet and the completed control-state handler (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:3364-3365`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2750-2770`). Because `wValue` and `wIndex` remain wire-order bytes in `UsbSetupData`, the m68k big-endian `wValue >> 3` calculation intentionally converts SET_ADDRESS's address byte into the endpoint-toggle table's `address << 5` base; it is not a separate endian bug. The subsequent loop still clears only indices 0..30, leaving endpoint 15 IN stale on address reuse as documented by OD3649. Ordinary control setup/data/status transitions, short-packet handling, allocation fallback, and caller publication were reread; no further deterministic source defect established. Split hub timing/status interpretation and hardware PTD semantics remain open. No request or controller was used; source-only.

Deneb controller initialization error propagation pass (OD3653 added, 2026-10-17): traced `uhwOpenTimer`/`uhwHWInit` and their Open_Unit/CMD_RESET callers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:65-115,117-266,461-484,530-552,569-585`). The hardware init error exits precede global/controller interrupt enable; both callers discard the error. The standard `CMD_RESET` vector then treats the connected bit alone as operational, so a connected-but-not-enabled port can return success after reset failure. Checked Poseidon's selected enumeration caller and distinguished its `UHCMD_USBRESET` dispatch to `cmdUsbReset`, which does not call `uhwHWInit`; the report now limits the false-success consequence to standard `CMD_RESET` callers. Timer allocation cleanup itself checks each nullable object, and `uhwDelayMS` is called only with fixed small constants in this file; no separate issue established. No board, port state, timer failure, or reset was exercised; source-only.

Deneb `UHCMD_USBRESET` contract/caller pass (OD3654 added, 2026-10-17): compared the command body with the USBHardware autodoc and both in-tree Poseidon call sites (`uhwcmd.c:601-615`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:589-612`; `poseidon.library.c:4148-4156,4255-4259`). The Deneb vector only queries `PORTSC1`, returns success for a connected port, and does not perform a root-port reset. Poseidon's checked-in call is the initial probe directly after opening Deneb, whose `uhwHWInit` already reset the port; the second call only occurs when that probe path did not complete. No repeated in-tree bus-reset call was found, so the report limits impact to later/external API use and avoids asserting the initial enumeration call is broken. Sibling PCIUSB/xHCI implementations contain similar FIXME state-only handlers; that does not change Deneb's explicit documented command contract. No reset was issued; source-only.

OD3654 Poseidon reset-call reachability recheck (2026-10-17): the source has two syntactic calls, but the later one at `poseidon.library.c:4255-4259` is guarded by `!resetdone`. Every control-flow path reaching it has already returned from the initial probe reset and set `resetdone = TRUE` at `:4163-4164`; allocation or `UHIOERR_HOSTERROR` failures return before the normal-hub branch (`:4136-4161`). Thus the second site is unreachable in this function as written. The only reachable in-tree `UHCMD_USBRESET` is the initial probe at `:4152`, following Deneb `Open_Unit`'s reset attempt; the ignored reset failure there is already OD3653. OD3654 remains scoped to later/external clients issuing a new reset after devices have been enumerated. No reset or enumeration was run. Source-only.

OD3655 independent source recheck (2026-10-17): reread the entire `uhwGetUsbState` helper and all three USBOPER/USBRESUME/USBSUSPEND handlers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:529-704`) against the command contracts (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:560-583,618-669`). The helper assigns OPERATIONAL from connection alone and independently ORs SUSPENDED from PORTSC1; each command handler only invokes the helper and tests a status bit, with no controller register writes. Poseidon continues to mark root-bus suspend/resume unsupported and has no selected call site. Existing OD3655 remains scoped to direct HCD callers; no additional finding established. No bus transition was run. Source-only.

OD3656 interval qualification (2026-10-17): rechecked `cmdAddIsoHandler` and `cmdStartRTIso` SOF-map assignment against the completion handler's sole success-path rearm/toggle (`uhwcmd.c:1181-1206,1360-1474,3408-3427,3774-3788`). The two PTDs have distinct interleaved masks for intervals below eight frames, but the default 8–511-frame branch and >511 branch assign identical masks. Tightened the finding to the guaranteed condition (a halted PTD stays inactive and its private error is not delivered) and made missing cadence conditional on interval/status semantics. Updated the index; no controller or RTIso stream was exercised. Source-only.

OD1736 baud-cache recheck (2026-10-17): traced the OpenSBI constructor's preference copy and initial `set_baudrate`, the HIDD setter's equality guard, and serial.device's independent zero-initialized `su_Baud` comparison/error handling (`dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:154-164,201,327-340`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:767-783`). With a supported preference baud, the constructor programs the UART but retains that value as the HIDD cache; a first serial.device request for the same rate is sent because `su_Baud` is still zero, then rejected by the HIDD's false default return. After a different baud is successfully programmed, the HIDD cache remains the constructor rate, so a request to restore that rate is likewise rejected although hardware is at the intervening rate. This is distinct from OD2536's invalid legacy default selector value 5, whose constructor programming attempt itself fails. Added the finding to the top-level index; no request or UART was used. Source-only.

Deneb bus state-command behavior and caller reconciliation (OD3655 added, 2026-10-17): compared `cmdUsbOper`, `cmdUsbResume`, and `cmdUsbSuspend` with the USBHardware command contracts and the shared state helper (`uhwcmd.c:530-552,628-704`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:560-583,618-669`). All three handlers only read `PORTSC1`; the helper sets OPERATIONAL on connection even if it also sets SUSPENDED. This makes USBOPER/USBRESUME return success without resuming a connected suspended bus, while USBSUSPEND rejects a connected active bus without issuing suspend. Poseidon explicitly marks root-bus suspend/resume unsupported and no selected in-tree caller sends these commands (`poseidon.library.c:3823-3827,3920-3924`); the report therefore limits impact to direct HCD clients. No bus transition was run; source-only.

Deneb RTIso halted-completion/rearm pass (OD3656 added, 2026-10-17): traced `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos` status handling and the two-PTD Add/Start/alternate schedule (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1070-1220,1334-1432,3333-3793`). A hardware HALT writes an error to the internal request copy but bypasses the only PTD rearm and `rtn_NextPTD` toggle; the public RTIso structure has no error callback and does not reply this private IOReq. A failed PTD therefore remains inactive in the ping-pong stream without owner notification, while its partner may continue. Selected USB Audio supplies only input/done hooks for its stream (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3212-3231`). Added OD3656 conditionally on the controller reporting a recoverable HALT/PID/babble status; whether each status can safely be retried requires controller semantics. No stream or hardware was exercised; source-only.

USB Ethernet RX/Close/AbortIO ExecSMP finding recheck (OD3380 retained, 2026-10-17): reread the ASIX receive path from opener-list traversal through `nReadIOReq` (`rom/usb/classes/asixeth/asixeth.class.c:1773-1863,1933-1975`) against `devClose`'s BufMan unlink/free (`dev.c:175-198`) and `devAbortIO`'s pending-read removal/reply (`:1298-1354`). RX dereferences BufMan callbacks and the queued IO request and copies packet data before unlink/reply; Close frees the BufMan without draining its RX queue, and AbortIO can remove/reply the same queued request while RX is processing it. The RX traversal's Forbid and Close/AbortIO Forbid do not synchronize cross-CPU on ExecSMP per `rom/exec/forbid.c:52-60`; LAN78xx's Disable variant has the same processor-local limitation (`disable.c:50-61`). OD3659 registration-path confirmation (2026-10-17): followed `PCIDT_InitClass` from `pcidt_discover` to its `for (i < bridgeCount)` `moHidd_PCI_AddHardwareDriver` loop, then through `PCIDT__Root__New` consuming the next stored bridge (`pcidt_driverclass.c:1035-1083,783-804`). OD3659 common PCI setup consequence confirmation (2026-10-17): followed the duplicate registration calls through deprecated `PCI__Hidd_PCI__AddHardwareDriver` into `HW_AddDriver` and `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:561-565,104-160`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:174-205`). Serial zero-length write matrix follow-up (OD839 restored, 2026-10-17): followed `serial.device` CMD_WRITE and the write-empty callback through PC, Sam440, OpenSBI, Unix and m68k HIDD implementations. Unix passes zero to host `write`, while m68k returns before reading the pointer. Restored the detailed report/index entry for the existing OD839 candidate. The serial.device module is optional; no zero-length request or UART was run. Source-only.

BWFM SANA-II RX request-delivery pass (2026-10-17; no new OD): followed `CMD_READ` queue insertion and `AbortIO`/`Close` removal against the RX pump's `rx_deliver` matching, RAW/cooked length calculation, filter and buffer-management hooks, request unlink/reply and packet statistics (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:306-405,1180-1228,1857-1878,1912-1940`). BWFM SANA-II write-dispatch and framing follow-up (OD3592 confirmed, 2026-10-17): traced `CMD_WRITE`, `S2_BROADCAST` and `S2_MULTICAST` dispatch into `tx_request`, including the broadcast destination assignment, RAW versus cooked framing, `S2_CopyFromBuff`/16/32 hook selection at open, frame-size/error handling, `BWFMTxData` status propagation and packet/type statistics (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:78-98,652-716,1130-1145,1881-1890`). OD3592's cooked `ETH_HLEN + ios2_DataLength` wrap occurs before the maximum-frame check and then passes the unbounded original payload length to the copy hook; it therefore applies to all three dispatched write commands in cooked mode. RAW mode assigns the data length directly and checks it before invoking the hook. No second distinct TX defect established; hook contract and completion semantics remain externally dependent, and the rest of the file remains open. No request or transmission was run. Source-only.

BWFM multicast/tracker state and statistics-query pass (OD3612 confirmed, 2026-10-17): traced duplicate multicast reference counting, overflow-to-allmulti accounting, list serialization, firmware `mcast_list`/`allmulti` iovars and the selected AROSTCP IPv4/IPv6 add/delete callers (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:932-1107,1747-1753`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1742-1778`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/netinet/in.c:686-750`; `netinet6/in6.c:669-750`). Tracker allocation and refcount operations are serialized; per-type snapshots are copied under the same lock. Global stats are copied without the lock while RX/TX update under it, but this pass found no stronger API-level consequence than a potentially inconsistent telemetry snapshot and did not promote a separate finding. Serial `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` error-unwind and caller expansion (OD58 expanded, 2026-10-17): followed `beginio`'s lock/interrupt scope through all three input-buffer allocation, baud validation and HIDD framing failure branches (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:328-331,713-824,875-879`). Serial CMD_RESET active-write detailed finding restoration (OD2388, 2026-10-17): rechecked `CMD_RESET` against the entire write-empty handler and callback registrations. Reset replies the active request but preserves `su_ActiveWrite`, `su_NextToWrite` and `su_WriteLength`; the callback does not gate on the cleared pending bit and can continue transmitting from the returned buffer and reply again. PC THRI and m68k TBE registrations prove selected callback routes; no maintained in-tree CMD_RESET caller was found. Restored OD2388 to the detailed report and index. No request or interrupt was run; source-only.
Serial queued-break command dispatch pass (OD3661 added, 2026-10-17): traced `SDCMD_BREAK` with `SERF_QUEUEDBRK` from BeginIO into `su_QWriteCommandPort` and the sole write-empty consumer (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:823-844`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:137-184`). The consumer interprets the dequeued IOExtSer fields as a normal write, never invokes `HIDD_SerialUnit_SendBreak`, and may copy from `io_Data`; the immediate branch does invoke SendBreak. No maintained in-tree `SDCMD_BREAK` caller was found. Added OD3661 with direct-client trigger; no request or serial output was run. Source-only.
Serial active-write AbortIO ownership pass (OD3662 added, 2026-10-17): traced active versus queued writes from BeginIO and the write-empty callback into `abortio` (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:449-525,884-910`; `serial_interrupthandlers.c:149-184`). The active request is not linked on the queue, but AbortIO's non-active-read branch unconditionally calls `Remove`; it then replies without clearing `su_ActiveWrite` or its offset/remaining state. Exec Remove's linked-node precondition and the callback's later dereference/reply establish distinct immediate list-corruption and deferred stale-request consequences. No maintained active-write AbortIO caller was found; no request or interrupt was run. Source-only.
Serial CMD_START restart ordering restoration (OD1737, 2026-10-17): rechecked the selected PC, Sam440 and OpenSBI `Start` and `Write` methods against serial.device's active-write callback. Each restart invokes the callback before clearing the HIDD stopped flag; each `Write` therefore returns zero, with no retry after the flag is cleared. Kept the possible indefinite wait conditional on later hardware transmit-empty interrupt behavior, and recorded the m68k ordering difference. Restored the detailed report and index entry from the coverage-only candidate. No UART sequence was run; source-only.

Deneb caller-buffer alignment pass (OD3663 scope expanded, 2026-10-17): searched all `ULONG *` casts and `CopyMemShuffle` call sites in `uhwcmd.c`, then checked the public USBHardware alignment contract and Poseidon's pointer assignment (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:127-132`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4705-4723`). Outgoing RTIso request-hook buffers use a separate hook/buffer-request API contract and were excluded pending review of their own alignment guarantees. Deneb request dispatch, query and DMA-tail follow-up (2026-10-17; no new finding): reread `cmdQueryDevice`, all ordinary transfer enqueue handlers, `TermIO`, `FreeATL/FreeInt/FreeIso`, `cmdAbortIO`, `uhwHandleDMAInt`, `uhwLevel6Int`, and `uhwDMATask` (`uhwcmd.c:706-960,1602-1878,4995-5403`). QueryDevice writes only caller-requested outputs selected by `FindTagItem`; the queueing handlers clear QUICK before returning `RC_DONTREPLY`; the selected abort vector owns replies for removed requests, while completed active requests are completed by the PTD helpers. The DMA interrupt only signals the worker when `hu_DMAPTD` is published, and the worker's signal path dispatches the state machine; allocation and teardown races around that state remain under review. No additional deterministic, in-scope defect was established in this pass. No request, interrupt, or hardware was exercised; source-only.

Deneb ordinary ATL control completion follow-up (2026-10-17; no new finding): read `uhwHandleFinishedATLs` setup, optional data, short-packet, continuation, status and endpoint-toggle transitions against the matching control scheduler and selected Poseidon request fields (`uhwcmd.c:1967-2783,3796-3956`; `poseidon.library.c:4705-4750`). This closes the ordinary ATL control state-machine question for the examined functions; split-transfer controller semantics and concurrent cancellation remain open. Duplicate-finding reconciliation (OD3663 withdrawn, 2026-10-17): the expanded caller-buffer alignment candidate is the same issue already documented as OD3603, which covers the control, bulk, interrupt and isochronous PIO casts, odd `iouh_Actual` offsets, the DMA-to-PIO fallback for unaligned bulk buffers, and the 68000/010 fault condition (`AROS-other-drivers.md:2283`). This follows a fresh search of all `ULONG *` casts and `CopyMemShuffle` uses; RTIso request-hook buffers remain outside OD3603 pending their separate API alignment contract.
RTIso alignment contract follow-up to OD3603 (2026-10-17): checked `IOUsbHWBufferReq` and its hook call sites. The public structure provides `UBYTE *ubr_Buffer` plus byte length and has no alignment requirement (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:103-113`); Deneb's RTIso IN/OUT hook paths cast that pointer to `ULONG *` and advance it by hook-supplied byte counts (`uhwcmd.c:1397-1414,3605-3645,3708-3725`). Expanded OD3603's scope addendum and index to include this same unaligned longword fault for direct/external hook buffers; no separate finding. No maintained in-tree Deneb hook producer demonstrated an odd pointer. No hook or transfer was run; source-only.
Sonixcam selected-caller follow-up to OD3603 (2026-10-17): the selected `rom/usb/shellapps/SonixcamTool.c` installs an RTIso IN request hook and sets `ubr_Buffer` to `nch_CurrIsoBuf + nch_IsoBufPos`; its done hook advances `nch_IsoBufPos` by each returned byte count (`:118-126,136-183,831-840`). Therefore an odd-sized received packet can make the next buffer pointer odd. Deneb's RTIso IN copy casts the hook pointer to `ULONG *` once any remaining full words exist (`uhwcmd.c:3605-3645`). Added this concrete selected producer to the OD3603 scope addendum; manifestation remains conditional on camera packet lengths and later data. No camera, hook, or transfer was run; source-only.
Sonixcam target-selection correction (OD3603, 2026-10-17): `SonixcamTool` is listed in `kernel-usb-shellapps`, but that target is not reached by the default kickstart package graph because the parent `kernel-usb` and `kernel-usb-amiga-m68k` dependency declarations are commented out (`rom/usb/shellapps/mmakefile.src:4-9`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:5-12`). Reworded the report/index to scope the selected in-tree caller to explicitly building the optional shell-app target; this does not change the public USBHardware contract finding or its external-client trigger. No package was built.

Deneb RTIso hook continuation and selected caller pass (2026-10-17; OD3603 retained, no new finding): followed RTIso IN/OUT callbacks through `ubr_Length`, automatic buffer advance, `UBFF_CONTBUFFER`, and the selected Sonixcam/audio hooks (`uhwcmd.c:1388-1421,3581-3735`; `SonixcamTool.c:118-183`; `usbaudio.class.c:2640-2720`). The selected USB Audio hooks do not request scatter/gather continuation; their frame-size/count logic and switching remain under the separate audio-class review. PCI HIDD setup/removal candidate recheck (OD3636/OD3637 retained, 2026-10-17): reread the full `pciclass.c` setup, device publication, IRQ assignment, `FindBridge`, enumeration, removal, legacy wrappers, and singleton New/Dispose bodies against the generic HW driver locks/contracts and PCI device Owner/Obtain methods (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:61-170,216-340,395-691`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:174-205,228-300`; `pcideviceclass.c:488-510,1208-1216`). `InsertDevice` takes `dev_lock` only around list insertion, while the later IRQ-routing and failure-diagnostic traversals and `FindBridge` remain unlocked; removal unlinks/disposes under `dev_lock`, confirming OD3636. The Owner getter still bypasses `ownerLock`, and Obtain publishes under that separate lock, confirming OD3637's check/use window. Generic HW driver registration/removal uses a separate driver-list semaphore, so it does not serialize these PCI list operations. No default selected runtime removal caller or new independent issue was established; both retained findings remain conditional on public concurrent add/remove or remove/obtain calls. No operation or interleaving was run; source-only.
BWFM SANA-II link-state caller pass (OD3660 added, 2026-10-17): compared the `joined` writer in control-worker `do_associate` after successful `BWFMJoin` (`bwfm_dev.c:1502-1530`) with the `S2_GETSIGNALQUALITY` dispatch read and its immediate BAD_STATE branch (`:1755-1774`). BWFM OD3613 RX-delivery race follow-up (2026-10-17): re-read the RX pump's `online` gate and its call into `rx_deliver` (`bwfm_dev.c:529-530`) against `S2_OFFLINE`'s locked read flush (`:1666-1671,1593-1610`) and `rx_deliver`'s later list lock (`:308-331`). A frame can pass the gate before offline, then the pump can resume after the flush and a late-enqueued CMD_READ; `rx_deliver` has no second online check and can complete that request after offline. Expanded existing OD3613 and its index consequence rather than adding a duplicate. No frame or request was used; source-only.
BWFM TX length and buffer-bound recheck (OD3592/OD3601 retained, 2026-10-17): verified the SANA-II cooked path computes `14 + ios2_DataLength` in 32-bit arithmetic before checking the 1,518-byte stack buffer, then calls the opener copy hook with the unbounded original payload length (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:652-692`). RAW requests assign the length directly and are checked before the hook. Traced the sole in-tree caller of exported `BWFMTxData`: after the device check, it passes at most 1,518 bytes, but the public resource vector independently computes `16 + ethlen`, rounds the wrapped result, and later copies the original `ethlen` into a 2,048-byte static frame (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2112-2133,2193-2196`). Thus OD3601 is a separate public-vector boundary; the checked in-tree caller is bounded, while an oversized direct vector caller is not. No request, callback, or resource vector was invoked. Remaining caller/API contract and lifecycle review stays open; source-only.

BWFM firmware filename, file-read, and auto-join preferences pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced board-compatible extraction and bounded filename construction (`bwfm_dev.c:129-207,727-773`), exact-size file allocation/read/close handling (`:209-239`), and the two-line SSID/passphrase parser into the bounded `BWFMJoin` arguments (`:835-909`; `bwfm_init.c:2353-2374,2433-2455`). The filename buffer covers the maximum accepted board name and fixed suffix; overlong board names fall back to the generic NVRAM filename. Read failures close the file and discard partial buffers. The preferences parser caps copies to its local arrays and the converter caller terminates the SSID explicitly. `fw_board_name` does not call `OF_CloseKey`, but the selected `rom/openfirmware/of_init.c:105-112` implementation is a no-op, so this is not a resource leak in this tree. Preference truncation of overlong values may make invalid credentials fail to join, but the supported format/semantics for such overlong values are not established, so it is not promoted. No firmware, filesystem, or association was exercised. Device startup recovery and firmware command semantics remain open; source-only.

BWFM SANA-II event, query, and read-flush helper pass (2026-10-17; existing candidates retained, no new finding): reread the full event matcher and detached-reply list (`bwfm_dev.c:1362-1407`), GETCRYPTTYPES pool allocation (`:1333-1354`), GETNETWORKINFO pool/tag/BSSID/optional-SSID flow (`:1541-1590`), and read flush lock/ReplyMsg sequence (`:1593-1609`). Flush replies queued reads while holding the same unit lock used by pump delivery; the separate enqueue-after-offline-flush window is OD3613. No request, pool failure, or event was exercised. Remaining request dispatch and selected caller contracts remain open; source-only.
Sam440 EMAC TX length-width recheck (OD3180 expanded, 2026-10-17): re-read `CmdWrite` through TX worker buffer construction, copy-hook call, descriptor publication and the selected AROSTCP hook (`workbench/devs/networks/emac/handler.c:222-263`; `emac_unit.c:548-552,570-668`; `emac.h:103-130`; `mal.c:105-149`; AROSTCP `sana2copybuff.c:190-212`). Confirmed `ios2_DataLength` is ULONG while both TX locals are UWORD. The worker passes only the narrowed count to the callback, so lengths above 65,535 can report success after sending the low-16-bit prefix; when the narrowed count exceeds the 1,554-byte cooked or 1,568-byte raw slot stride, the callback copy crosses the neighboring slot. `CmdWrite` has no max-length guard, but the selected AROSTCP raw-output path rejects lengths beyond its if_mtu and if_sana caps that at the device MTU; direct SANA-II clients remain the trigger. Expanded existing OD3180 rather than adding a duplicate: its earlier “every request above slot stride” phrasing did not account for the UWORD truncation. No request, hook or hardware was used. Source-only.

Sam440 EMAC over-MTU transmit consequence check (OD3180 expanded, 2026-10-17): compared the worker's cooked packet assembly (`emac_unit.c:592-635`) with `ETH_MTU=1500`, `ETH_MAXPACKETSIZE=1518`, the 1,544-byte per-slot object, and 1,568-byte slot stride (`emac.h:103-130`; `mal.c:105-149`). Because `CmdWrite` has no length guard, cooked requests of 1,501 bytes or more are still copied and queued when their hook accepts them, even before the copy reaches the slot boundary; the transmitted frame therefore exceeds the device's advertised payload MTU. Kept this within OD3180's missing full-width/bounds validation rather than creating a second no-validation finding. The checked-in AROSTCP writer remains capped; no direct-client request or transmission was run. Source-only.
Sam440 EMAC autonegotiated gigabit mode trace (OD3664 added, 2026-10-17): compared the PHY advertisement/1000BASE-T control writes (`workbench/devs/networks/emac/emac_hw.c:243-263`; `emac.h:288-298`) with `EMAC_miiphy_speed`/`duplex`'s BMCR and 10/100 ANLPAR-only reads (`emac_hw.c:173-224`) and `EMAC_Start`'s bridge/MAC speed configuration (`emac_unit.c:100-142`). The resolver can only return 10 or 100 even though the PPC460EX-B branch has explicit 1000-Mbit configuration; it never reads PHY_1000BTSR, making the gigabit branch unreachable. Added OD3664 conditional on PHY and partner negotiating 1000BASE-T. No hardware/link was used; PHY wiring and actual gigabit negotiation remain unverified. Source-only.

PCI HIDD enumeration contract follow-up (2026-10-17): reviewed `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-449`) against the documented tag sequence (`rom/hidds/pci/include/pci_hidd.h:38-46`), PCI API documentation (`rom/hidds/pci/doc/pci.en:50-90`), and the checked-in callers found by repository-wide search. The unsigned tag-index subtraction safely rejects tags below `TAG_USER`; all nine documented contiguous attributes map to the corresponding table slots. Enumeration deliberately holds `dev_lock` shared while callbacks run, preserving device object lifetime against exclusive removal; a callback that synchronously adds a bus driver would wait on the same semaphore, but no selected in-tree EnumDevices callback was found to register/remove a bus driver, so this conditional reentrancy concern is not promoted as a finding. Existing removal and ownership findings OD3563/OD3637 remain the concrete lifecycle issues. Source-only; no callback was executed.

Mediator/Prometheus PCI BAR exhaustion follow-up (OD3670 added, 2026-10-17): compared both `PCIInitialize` loops (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/pci-mediator/driverclass.c:184-231`; `pci-prometheus/driverclass.c:85-132`) with their duplicated `AllocPCIResource` free-list mutation (`pci_resource.c:54-99` in both directories). A successful BAR consumes/splits/trims the list immediately; if a later BAR allocation fails, the loop sets the command value to zero and breaks but does not restore the earlier allocation, then continues scanning later functions. Thus a disabled function can retain resource space during the remaining scan and cause later allocations to fail under constrained bridge windows. Added conditional OD3670. Mediator disposes the lists after its scan; Prometheus retains them with its instance, but neither behavior releases the earlier range before subsequent functions in the same scan. No board, BAR sizing cycle or exhaustion condition was exercised; source-only.

PCIUSB IRQ failure cleanup follow-up (OD3669 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced registration failure beyond the UHCI/EHCI/OHCI startup call sites to `pciFreeUnit` and the public unit-close path (`pciusb_arospci.c:753-768`; `uhwcmd.c:342-355`). The HCD startup names `hc_PCIIntHandler` before discarding the `PCIXAddInterrupt` result (`uhci_hcd.c:1142-1152`; `ehci_hcd.c:1635-1646`; `ohci_hcd.c:1848-1860`), while cleanup tests only that name, then calls `HIDD_PCIDevice_RemoveInterrupt`. On Sam440's inherited generic PCI method, failed `KrnAddIRQHandler` leaves the token NULL; generic removal forwards it to `KrnRemIRQHandler`, which dereferences the handle before its null check (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-55`). Since failed handler registration does not make HCD init fail, `pciAllocUnit` can succeed and a later close reaches this conditional fault. Expanded OD3669 to record both absent interrupt service and NULL-token teardown. No failure or close sequence was induced; source-only.
PCI device-class bridge-window pass (OD3667 added, 2026-10-17): traced type-1 prefetchable-window attribute accessors (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:919-924,1299-1305`) against the defined low and upper register offsets (`rom/hidds/pci/include/hardware/pci.h:158-161`) and PCITool's selected range display (`rom/hidds/pci/pcitool/main.c:477-481`). The getter shifts the complete low register, including the non-address low nibble, and never reads upper dwords; the setter writes only the low register. Added OD3667 for incorrect range metadata and incomplete 64-bit programming. No setter caller was established in the checked-in tree; selected PCITool confirms the read path. No bridge was used; source-only.
PCI device-class Expansion ROM address/caller pass (OD3668 added, 2026-10-17): traced `RomBase` initialization/get (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:697-700,772-774`) against the type-0 BAR's decode-enable bit and the selected Nouveau `pci_enable_rom`/`pci_map_rom` path (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_pci.c:36-43,383-403`; BIOS caller `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/bios/shadowpci.c:61-79`). Added conditional OD3668. No device or ROM was mapped; source-only.
PCIUSB generic interrupt-registration caller pass (OD3669 added, 2026-10-17): traced `PCIXAddInterrupt` (`rom/usb/pciusb/pciusb_arospci.c:804-808`) through the inherited generic `PCIDrv__Hidd_PCIDriver__AddInterrupt` return (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:279-287`) to `KrnAddIRQHandler` returning NULL for an IRQ outside `HW_IRQ_COUNT` or failed node allocation (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:75-96`). The PCIUSB UHCI, EHCI and OHCI startup call sites discard the Boolean and enable controller interrupt sources immediately afterward (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_hcd.c:1144-1152`; `ehci/ehci_hcd.c:1637-1646`; `ohci/ohci_hcd.c:1850-1860`). Generic PCI mapping inheritance check (2026-10-17): compared `PCIDrv__Hidd_PCIDriver__MapPCI` and address conversion (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:128-178`) with all checked-in PCI HIDD class manifests. Enumeration deliberately holds `dev_lock` shared while callbacks run, preserving device object lifetime against exclusive removal; a callback that synchronously adds a bus driver would wait on the same semaphore, but no selected in-tree EnumDevices callback was found to register/remove a bus driver, so this conditional reentrancy concern is not promoted as a finding. PCI xHCI IRQ failure caller pass (OD3669 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced the xHCI-specific IRQ paths (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:4067-4120`) and close cleanup (`pcixhci_arospci.c:420-432`, `uhwcmd.c:342-366`). Both generic `PCIXAddInterrupt` and MSI `AddIntServer` results are ignored; the handler node is named before registration, while `pciFreeUnit` later treats the name as proof of success and removes it. OpenSBI's selected boot package loads `USBHardware/pcixhci` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:104`) and its PCIDT backend overrides AddInterrupt to unmask INTx then forward to the generic method (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:967-977`). On failure, the stored IRQ token remains NULL and removal reaches the kernel's pre-guard dereference. HCD init proceeds to success if controller start otherwise succeeds, so unit close can reach this fault. Expanded OD3669 to cover PCIUSB on Sam440 and PCI xHCI on OpenSBI PCIDT. No failure or close was induced; source-only.
Network worker signal-allocation follow-up (OD3671, 2026-10-18): traced Rhine, Prism2 and Atheros5000 `UnitTask` setup through `AllocSignal(-1)` and the directly shifted masks (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:1731-1742`; `prism2/unit.c:3831-3843`; `atheros5000/unit.c:2827-2838`). Each unit task is launched by `CreateUnit` without a startup handshake, and each `DevBeginIO` queues requests on its general port when `AttemptSemaphore` fails (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:315-341`, `device.c:409`; `prism2/unit.c:313-339`, `device.c:431`; `atheros5000/unit.c:402-428`, `device.c:419`). Thus allocation failure can leave an accepted unit with malformed wait masks; exact effect depends on target shift behavior and subsequent event/request activity. Added OD3671, as an extension to OD3106's same defect pattern. Confirmed these target variants through `workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src`; Prism2 and Rhine are in the active cards aggregate, while Atheros5000 is selected by the GNU-toolchain branch; Atheros5000 uses its separate GNU dependency. No device, signal exhaustion, or request was run. The broader AllocSignal caller inventory is still open.
VIA-Rhine scheduler shutdown follow-up (OD3672, 2026-10-18): compared `AllocSignal`'s returned bit number (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:70-143`) with `Wait`'s one-hot mask result (`rom/exec/wait.c:75-80`) and traced scheduler setup, shutdown test, and `DeleteUnit` cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/unit.c:719-733,938-966`). The worker waits on shifted bits but tests the returned mask against raw `signal_0`; deletion also passes that number directly to `Signal`, then frees its request ports, private state, MMIO mapping, and unit without joining the task. Added OD3672. All signal allocations are also unchecked. A wider review of this driver and of the remaining network callers is still open. No device or teardown was run; source-only.
LPe32002 worker signal-allocation follow-up (OD3673, 2026-10-18): reread the scheduler after its startup handshake through its wait loop (`workbench/devs/networks/lpe32002/unit.c:526-555`) and `DeleteUnit` signal path (`:827-831`) against Exec's `AllocSignal` failure return (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:24-68`). The broader LPe32002 file/caller audit remains open. No worker or allocation failure was induced; source-only.
Network AllocSignal caller inventory (2026-10-18): repository search finds 20 C/header source files under `workbench/devs/networks` with direct `AllocSignal` calls. Reviewed the failure handling and mask construction in BCM GENET (`bcmgenet_unit.c:1020-1055`), BWFM RX/control workers (`bwfm_dev.c:468-476,596-609`), RTL8029 (`rtl8029/driver.c:1753-1768`), PPP (`ppp/init.c:82-84,112-116,259-275`), and RTL8139 (`rtl8139/unit.c:806-824,852-856,1163`) and found no additional unchecked-failure mask defect in those paths: BCM GENET only enables the optional IRQ bit after success, BWFM falls back to timer/polling, RTL8029 checks allocation, PPP exits on failure, and RTL8139 validates all four allocations before acknowledging setup. Existing findings cover nForce (OD3083), PCNet32 (signal-exhaustion trigger rechecked; no reachable exhaustion established), SiS900 (OD3089), e1000 (OD2436), RTL816x/Broadcom4400 signal-exhaustion candidates rechecked and withdrawn, Intel Pro/100/Etherlink III/Realtek8180 (OD3106), and the newly reviewed Rhine/Prism2/Atheros5000 (OD3671), VIA-Rhine (OD3672), LPe32002 and nvidianet (signal-exhaustion triggers rechecked; no reachable exhaustion established). This reconciles the `AllocSignal` issue family for network-driver source files only; the project-wide direct-call inventory spans 184 C/header files and remains open. No task, signal exhaustion, packet, or request was induced. Source-only.
Virtual Bluetooth HCI signal-allocation candidate withdrawal and HID target pass (2026-10-18): traced `AllocSignal(-1)` in `vbthci_UnitTask` through the selected `CreateNewProcTags`/`CreateNewProc` allocation path (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_device.c:48-56`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:231-235,401-405,546-550`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:248-251`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The new process is zero-cleared and receives the default `TaskSigAlloc` mask (`0xFFFF`), leaving the upper 16 signal bits available; this worker allocates its unit-port bit before any other signal allocations. Signal exhaustion is therefore not established on this selected startup path. Withdrew OD3675 from the report and index. Also read all 103 lines of `vbthci_hid.c` and traced every report descriptor/input-report caller in `vbthci_peer.c:138-158,407-419,451-470,1158-1190`: report capacities match the 3-byte mouse and 8-byte keyboard reports; the keyboard CoD/LE appearance selectors agree with the fake-device records, and no independent defect was established. No task, device, or report was run; source-only.
Virtual Bluetooth pending-read queue ExecSMP cross-CPU pass (OD3724 strengthened, 2026-10-18): traced `BTCMD_READACL` enqueue/delivery and shutdown flush against device `AbortIO` (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:473-504`; `vbthci_peer.c:64-82`; `vbthci_device.c:165-198`). Confirmed the AbortIO walk/removal of the unit message port bypasses its `mp_SpinLock`, which `GetMsg` and `PutMsg` take (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:64-72`; `putmsg.c:80-91`); the pending-read list is protected only with `Forbid()`, which Exec documents as local-processor-only on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). Retained OD3724 for an overlapping public AbortIO; no in-tree caller was found. No request or interleaving was run; source-only.
Virtual Bluetooth event-message shutdown ownership cross-check (2026-10-18; no additional OD): traced the selected Bluetooth hardware task's synchronous event-port registration/removal and teardown (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2856-2864,3044-3057,3068-3077`). It removes the event port before issuing `CMD_FLUSH`, continues collecting device replies, drains and replies queued event messages, and only then closes the root device request. `vbthci_CloseUnit` signals and waits for the unit task before freeing its state (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_device.c:82-99`); the unit task also stops its timer and returns outstanding event messages before deleting its reply port (`vbthci_unit.c:617-647`). This selected caller order does not establish an event-message/reply-port lifetime defect. Other external event-port clients and timeout behavior remain outside this trace. No task or event was run; source-only.
USB MassStorage worker signal candidate correction (OD3676 withdrawn; OD3893 added, 2026-10-18): re-read `nAllocMS()` failure control flow and Exec signal/message-port implementations (`massstorage.class.c:1737-1740,1832-1855`; `rom/exec/createmsgport.c:49-64`; `freesignal.c:55-64`; `allocsignal.c:105-112`). If the embedded-port `AllocSignal(-1)` fails, the UBYTE signal field receives 255; the immediately following `CreateMsgPort()` in the same task also cannot allocate a signal, so `nAllocMS()` returns NULL and `nMSTask()` never publishes a ready worker. This contradicts the old claim that the LUN can become ready with an invalid command-worker signal; withdrew OD3676 and removed it from both report indexes. The failure unwind nevertheless unconditionally calls `FreeSignal(255)`, which reaches an unchecked `1L << 255`; added OD3893 for that invalid cleanup argument, with target/compiler-dependent consequences. No signal exhaustion or USB device was induced. Source-only.
Poseidon USB HID GUI signal caller pass (OD3677, 2026-10-18): traced `nGUITask`'s tracking-signal allocation through the MUI NewInput wait and cleanup, then traced the HID event worker's matching `Signal` producer (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:1596-1607,1711-1715`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:988-995`). BWFM SANA-II `handle_request` command-dispatch pass (OD3678 added; 2026-10-18): read the complete request switch from S2_DEVICEQUERY through CMD_FLUSH (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1610-1930`) against its helpers and selected WirelessManager calls. The NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY branch checks only for NULL `io_Data`, then writes all NSDeviceQueryResult fields and full `io_Actual` without checking `io_Length` (`:1829-1854`); the selected caller provides a full result object (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:928-929,978-982`).
