BWFM SANA-II opener buffer-hook caller contract (2026-10-18; no new finding): traced OpenDevice's static `buffer_tags` in the selected WirelessManager client into BWFM `open()` tag extraction and per-opener storage, then through the actual `S2_CopyToBuff` receive and `S2_CopyFromBuff` transmit call argument order (`driver_sana2.c:60-77,960-967`; `bwfm_dev.c:1110-1137,352-363,686-694`). The selected AROS hook performs `CopyMem(src, dest, size)` and returns TRUE, matching both call directions; the callback remains valid for the opener lifetime. Other external SANA-II buffer hooks may fail or impose different constraints; their behavior and packet-stat semantics remain unverified. No callback or packet was run. Source-only.

Hosted Ethernet init/close and worker-startup full-body recheck (2026-10-18; existing OD2215/OD2216/OD3515 retained): reread `arch/all-unix/devs/networks/eth/init.c` in full, checked its selected module manifest, `eth_iotask`, SANA-II command dispatch, UnixIO poll/add-interrupt contract, and Exec `OpenDevice` invocation (`eth/mmakefile.src:6-8`; `iotask.c:258-359`; `command.c:34-350`; `arch/all-unix/hidd/unixio/unixio_class.c:110-155,828-875`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:70-110`). Invalid `unitnum` still reaches out-of-range cleanup (OD2215). First-open sync-port/task and worker resource failures remain the combined OD2216 path; ignored `AddInterrupt` failure is the distinct non-Darwin receive-stall OD3515. `Close` stops the worker before closing the packet descriptor, then frees trackers and unit state; no separate teardown defect established for a valid, fully opened unit. `OpenDevice` keeps task switching disabled around the device Open vector, but this alone does not establish cross-CPU serialization of the unit refcount on every hosted platform. No additional finding promoted. Host interface operations, startup failures, and concurrent opens were not exercised; caller/platform synchronization and external SANA-II lifecycle contracts remain open. Source-only.

BWFM automatic-join preferences and caller recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): read `load_wifi_prefs` and `try_join` in full and traced the sole `S2_ONLINE` caller in AROSTCP plus the link-state writer (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:835-910,1658-1664`; `if_sana.c:850-872`; `bwfm_dev.c:423-452`). The parser bounds the SSID to 32 bytes and key to 63 bytes in 33-/64-byte caller buffers, skips CR/LF, blank and whole-line comment records, and passes explicit lengths to `BWFMJoin`; the subsequent terminator writes fit. Missing preferences fail closed without joining. A successful join publishes `joined` through `link_up`; failed joins leave it unset, while the stored requested SSID can remain for `S2_GETNETWORKINFO`'s guarded state path. The `joined` check in `try_join` and the `online` mutations/reporting are not synchronized as a single transition with concurrent `S2_ONLINE`/`S2_OFFLINE`; this is within the already-open concurrent online-state review, and this caller trace does not establish a distinct supported interleaving consequence. No credentials, association or event was used. Source-only.

BWFM online/offline serialization qualification (2026-10-18; OD3613/OD3614 scope refinement, no new OD): verified the selected AROSTCP transition path beyond the earlier `sana_up`/`sana_down` trace. `sana_ioctl` holds `splimp()` across its `SIOCSIFFLAGS` and `SIOCSIFADDR` handling, including synchronous `S2_ONLINE`/`S2_OFFLINE` requests (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:620-646,688-733,849-913`). Production `spl_n` acquires the shared `spl_semaphore` for every nonzero level, so these selected network-stack transitions are serialized across tasks (`kern/kern_synch.c:474-540`; design note `Readme.md:73-78`). Thus the opposing online/offline command race is not established through this in-tree AROSTCP path. `S2_ONEVENT` is still an asynchronous external request that can overlap the transition and retains the independently demonstrated snapshot/latch/queue gap OD3614. Direct external SANA-II clients do not inherit AROSTCP's stack lock; their transition serialization remains unverified. No request was issued. Source-only.

Atheros5000 CreateUnit/ DeleteUnit allocation-unwind recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread the constructor allocation and teardown path against the only selected PCI creator (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:117-552`; `pci.c:78-83,218-230,572-588`). The selected `unit_tags` always supplies both DMA hooks; `CreateUnit` rejects a missing hook pair, but that theoretical internal caller path is not reachable through the checked-in PCI creator, so the NULL `FreeDMAMem` cleanup call is not promoted. The selected free hook explicitly accepts NULL DMA buffers, matching the partial-allocation loops in `DeleteUnit`. Reconfirmed OD3260: after allocating `task` and its 4-KiB stack, failed `AddUnitTask` leaves `UNITF_TASKADDED` clear; cleanup frees the Task but only frees `tc_SPLower` when that flag is set (`unit.c:400-430,482-496`). Other creation-failure cleanup releases initialized request ports, DMA buffers/descriptors, vectors, and attached HAL state. PC-card CreateUnit is not a caller in this target; the PCI path is the checked-in construction route. No allocation, HAL operation, or unit creation was run. Source-only.

Atheros5000 InitialiseAdapter/HAL result cross-check (2026-10-18; OD3292/OD3293/OD3391 retained, no new OD): reread the full initializer and matched its channel, TX-queue, capability and reset calls to the selected AR5210/AR5211/AR5212 HAL methods (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:549-692`; respective attach tables and `hal/ar521[012]/ar521[012]_xmit.c`). `ah_init_channels`' unwritten output on failure is OD3391; the ignored `ah_resetTxQueue` after the second DATA queue is OD3293 on AR5210, whose only DATA queue was allocated by the first call. AR5212 allocates distinct free DATA queues; AR5211 instead returns its already-active DATA queue 0 for the second request, creating the shared-QCU/separate-ring condition now included in OD3293. Reset/error propagation remains covered by OD3293 on AR5210. Capability queries select software/hardware cipher handlers based on returned status; the following TKIP-MIC set is a best-effort capability configuration and the code falls back to software MIC when `UNITF_HARDMIC` is absent. No independent supported-card failure consequence established. No HAL or radio operation was run. Source-only.

BWFM S2_ONEVENT and online-state transition cross-check (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `begin_io` directly into `handle_request` (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1903-1910`), confirming SANA-II commands may enter from callers independently of the RX pump. `S2_ONEVENT` snapshots `unit->online` before taking `unit->lock`, consumes latched edges under the lock, releases it, then later takes it again to enqueue (`:1675-1722`); `report_events` scans and latches under that lock (`:1362-1396`). This confirms OD3614's state-transition/event snapshot-to-enqueue window. Separately, `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE`, `S2_ONLINE`, and `S2_OFFLINE` write `unit->online` without the lock, while the RX pump reads it without the lock (`:529`, `:1651-1671`); an in-flight frame can therefore race a transition, but the inspected path does not establish a distinct post-completion invariant violation beyond transitional frame delivery, so no new finding is promoted. Selected AROSTCP and WirelessManager callers consume the online/offline events to maintain interface/supplicant state (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:543-600,858-909`; `workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:802-883`). Concurrent command ordering, broader online-state contracts, and RX-pump lifecycle remain open. Source-only; no requests, frames, or concurrency were run.

SDSC capability-helper caller cross-check (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced the complete `SDSCChangeFrequency` SCR/read and CMD6 check/switch helper (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_sdscunit.c:43-141`) through `StartUnit` and `Open` (`sdcard_bus.c:77-133,177-191`; `sdcard_init.c:146-172`). The helper's error return is ignored, but high-speed selection is published only after successful switch-status readback; without that flag, `StartUnit` selects the 25-MHz SD fallback. Four-bit capability can still be published from a successfully read SCR and is applied only after successful ACMD6 command completion. No separate false-speed or bus-width state was established from the ignored helper result. The distinct ignored `WaitStatus` return and false-success activation remain OD3304; OD3327 is the independent internal-clock-stability timeout in `SetClock`. The three-busy CMD6 retry exits with timeout zero and correctly skips the switch. Corrected the SDSC coverage row's stale OD3327 description. Command/response semantics and hardware behavior remain external; no card command was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager association IE pool-lifetime caller check (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced the SANA-II event-port association path from `S2_GETNETWORKINFO` pool allocation through `wpa_supplicant_event(EVENT_ASSOC)` and pool deletion (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:795-832`). The selected `wpa_supplicant_event` dispatch is synchronous (`wpa_supplicant/events.c:1590-1602`); `wpa_supplicant_event_associnfo` scans the request IE before returning (`:979-1024`), and `wpa_sm_set_assoc_wpa_ie` copies the selected WPA/RSN IE into its own allocation (`src/rsn_supp/wpa.c:2428-2455`). Thus deleting the GetNetworkInfo pool after event delivery does not invalidate the stored association IE. Allocation failure for the copy is propagated only within the WPA setter; the event's behavior on that failure and the SANA2 driver passing a length from `ie[1]` remain caller/error-contract areas for a separate malformed-response review. No association event or pool was run. Source-only.
Prism2 WPA IE copy-size boundary reconciliation (OD3121 refined, 2026-10-18; no new OD): followed `S2INFO_WPAInfo` through `SetOptions` and confirmed the length-byte read and fixed 100-byte destination are already covered by OD3121. The selected WirelessManager association path uses an 80-byte generated IE buffer and passes only its pointer; it does not establish the oversized trigger. Refined OD3121 to distinguish direct-client oversized/inconsistent tags from the bounded selected association path. Removed duplicate draft OD3698. No options request or copy was run.
Prism2 SetKey follow-through reconciliation (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced S2_SETKEY through `CmdSetKey` and `SetKey`, confirming unchecked slot index and WEP data length are already covered by OD3187; traced `S2INFO_DefaultKeyNo` into later key-array consumers, also OD3187. WirelessManager's parser accepts WEP lengths up to 16 and the SANA-II callback forwards them unchanged, so 14–16-byte values reach the Prism2 WEP key copy when that association path is used. Prism2 sets `UNITF_HARDWEP` alongside `UNITF_HASWEP` for hardware-reported WEP capability (`unit.c:536`), but the Intersil branch sets `UNITF_HASWEP` alone (`:561-565`); the latter selects software WEP and confirms OD3334's 14–16-byte seed overrun trigger for that supported variant (`:597-610,768-785`). Removed duplicate draft IDs OD3699/OD3700; existing OD3187/OD3334 retain the findings. No key request or transmission was run.
Deneb RTIso callback/teardown check against USB Audio OD3517 (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced USB Audio `subLibFreeAudio`'s stop, handler removal, then buffer free (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3592-3637`) through Poseidon's synchronous `psdStopRTIso` (`poseidon.library.c:5657-5677`) and `psdFreeRTIsoHandler` (`:5607-5627`) into Deneb's BeginIO dispatch (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:598-610`). Unlike the selected PCIUSB/xHCI paths in OD3517, Deneb runs `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos` inline from `uhwLevel6Int` (`uhwcmd.c:5326-5334`), not on another completion task. `cmdStopRTIso` disables interrupts while clearing each PTD's active word and the `hu_IsoRTMask`, `hu_IsoBusy` and `hu_IsoRTDone` bits (`:1501-1544`); Deneb's m68k `Disable` clears the custom-chip master interrupt enable and increments the interrupt nesting count (`arch/m68k-amiga/exec/disable.S:69-72`). On re-enable, the level-6 handler masks done bits with `hu_IsoBusy` and `hu_IsoRTMask` before invoking the hook (`uhwcmd.c:5328-5334`), so stopped PTDs do not dispatch a stale completion. `cmdRemIsoHandler` repeats the interrupt exclusion, clears the RTIso backlink/PTD node pointers, and only then returns the handler node to the free list (`:1278-1311`). No Deneb counterpart to OD3517's cross-CPU in-flight callback/free interleaving was established; other Deneb scheduling and hardware semantics remain open. No stop, interrupt, or stream was run. Source-only.

Deneb RTIso completion buffer-length and rearm follow-through (2026-10-18; OD3656 and OD3578 retained, no new OD): read the full `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos` success and halt branches (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3333-3788`). Successful IN completion gives the actual hardware byte count to the request hook, copies the hook-returned byte count from the internal buffer, advances the caller buffer by that returned count and subtracts it from the remaining count when `UBFF_CONTBUFFER` is set. OUT completion likewise trusts hook lengths and rounds each source read up to whole `ULONG`s; this is already covered by OD3578's per-piece alignment/boundary issue and OD3603's odd-address issue. The generic API exposes a byte pointer and length but does not document a maximum/return-length invariant (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:90-113`). The selected USB Audio IN hook chooses a frame-aligned amount from its queued audio count and points into its owned USB buffer (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2650-2686`); the selected optional Sonixcam hook only reduces the reported length to zero when the destination buffer would overflow (`rom/usb/shellapps/SonixcamTool.c:116-130`). Neither inspected caller establishes an over-length trigger. An arbitrary external hook returning more than the hardware-reported byte count could make the copy read past the internal PTD buffer and, with continuation, underflow the remaining count; left as an unverified external callback-contract concern rather than a finding. Independently confirmed OD3656: HALT writes an error only into the private IOReq and skips PTD rearm and `rtn_NextPTD` toggle (`:3401-3427,3778-3788`), leaving that service slot inactive without an owner-visible error callback. No hook, controller status, transfer, or stream was run. Source-only.

Deneb worker creation and close-order follow-through (2026-10-18; OD3581/OD3582 retained, no new OD): checked the selected AROS `AddTask` implementation and return contract: it returns the nullable result of `NewAddTask` (`rom/exec/addtask.c:62-94`), whose ETask/context initialization can fail (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:270-272,305-309`). `Open_Unit` ignores that result after publishing the embedded Task and before returning the unit (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:468-486`), confirming OD3581's no-worker path. On close, `Close_Unit` signals Ctrl-C, delays a fixed 10 ms, then frees the unit containing both task and stack (`:502-525`; `denebusb.h:277,328`). The worker waits for single-signal or Ctrl-C, processes `SIGF_SINGLE` first if both are pending, then tests Ctrl-C at the loop condition (`:5372-5401`); there is no completion signal/handshake. This confirms OD3582's possibility of active DMA/PIO work or task finalization after the fixed delay. No task allocation failure, signal ordering, close, or hardware was exercised; source-only.

Deneb isochronous MULT caller and descriptor cross-check (OD3604 revalidated, 2026-10-18; no new finding): the USBHardware API documents `UHFF_MULTI_1/2/3` as the high-speed transactions-per-microframe selector (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:455-483`). Poseidon decodes endpoint `wMaxPacketSize`'s MULT field into `pep_NumTransMuFr` (`poseidon.library.c:8476-8484`), sets the corresponding request flag for high-speed endpoints (`:4528-4547`), and routes isochronous endpoints through `UHCMD_ISOXFER` with `pep_MaxPktSize` as the per-transaction size (`:4603-4628`). Deneb ordinary ISO allocates one 1-KiB granule, caps `ptd_BufLen` to one `MaxPktSize`, and has the QHA0 multiplier writes commented out (`uhwcmd.c:4590-4679`); its RTIso path allocates two `MaxPktSize` slices and also omits multiplier bits (`:1079-1087,1160-1221`). The split-transaction full/low-speed branches are separate and are not part of OD3604. USB Audio is a selected Poseidon RTIso caller (`usbaudio.class.c:3212-3231`). This confirms the finding's high-speed ISO scope and one-transaction capacity consequence; no USB endpoint, controller, or stream was exercised. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary ISO request-length caller cross-check (OD3587 revalidated, 2026-10-18; no new finding): the API states `UHCMD_ISOXFER` transfers the requested amount, split into `iouh_MaxPktSize` packets (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:438-455`). Poseidon's generic `psdDoPipe` copies caller `len` directly into `iouh_Length` before queueing (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4705-4735`); its stream writer also submits packet-aligned `remlen` values through `psdSendPipe` without restricting a request to one packet (`:5160-5189`). Deneb's ordinary ISO completion uses strict `iouh_Actual + iouh_MaxPktSize < iouh_Length` to decide whether to rearm (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3283-3315`), so an exact two-packet request stops after the first full packet, and any request with one packet or less remaining also cannot continue. Both the documented generic request contract and selected Poseidon call paths support multi-packet request lengths. This confirms OD3587's scope; no pipe, stream, or controller was exercised. Source-only.

Deneb USB bus-state command contract reconciliation (OD3653/OD3654/OD3655/OD3583 rechecked, 2026-10-18; no new finding): compared BeginIO dispatch (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:548-578`) and all five handlers against `usbhardware.device` documentation (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:166-182,560-672`). `CMD_RESET` calls `uhwHWInit` and discards its return before testing only port-connected state; the distinct `UHCMD_USBRESET` does not call reset logic at all, only queries state. USBOPER/USBRESUME/USBSUSPEND are also state queries with no port/controller writes; `uhwGetUsbState` labels a connected-but-suspended port operational, enabling false-success from USBOPER/USBRESUME. This supports keeping OD3583 (controller reset erases active descriptors without freeing software requests), OD3653 (reset/init failure masked by connected state), OD3654 (USB reset command does not assert reset), and OD3655 (transition commands do not transition) distinct. Poseidon returns unsupported for root-bus suspend/resume (`poseidon.library.c:3823-3827,3920-3924`), so no selected Poseidon caller trigger was established for OD3655; direct HCD clients remain the trigger. No request, reset, port state, or hardware was exercised. Source-only.

BWFM first-open setup race consequence expansion (OD3619, 2026-10-18; same finding, no new ID): rechecked the entire `open` -> `load_firmware` -> `BWFMStartFirmware` -> `start_pump` path (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:733-820,1137-1174`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:1547-1567,1607-1629`). The unsynchronized zero-refcount test precedes `load_firmware`; both callers can pass its initial `fw_loaded` check. Although `BWFMStartFirmware` serializes with `bwfm_Sem`, it has no already-running guard and unconditionally writes the image and activates the firmware CPU, so both successful callers may restart firmware sequentially. `start_pump` also has a check-then-create sequence without a shared lock; simultaneous calls can create two RX pumps and two control workers while the base retains only the last pointers. This broadens OD3619's consequence alongside the already documented list-reinitialization race; firmware/worker outcomes require both overlapping startup paths to succeed. No firmware, open, process, or schedule was run. Source-only.

BWFM SDPCM invalid-header FIFO-position follow-through (OD3640 scope expanded, 2026-10-18; same finding, no new ID): `bwfm_rx_read` reads the 12-byte header from fixed-address function-2 FIFO, then returns zero for checksum mismatch or `frmlen < 12` without consuming any body bytes (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:827-840,1082-1097`). `BWFMRxFrame` converts that to “no frame,” after which the pump can acknowledge/clear the card interrupt (`:2210-2255`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:492-535`). The synchronous `bwfm_dcmd` poll similarly returns `-1` on those header conditions after consuming only the header (`:919-930`). On subsequent reads the FIFO therefore resumes at the rejected frame's body; this is the same desynchronization cause as OD3640's oversized-frame paths, not a separate finding. Empty `frmlen == 0 && cksum == 0` is excluded because the code treats it as no pending frame. No malformed frame, SDIO error, or device was exercised. Source-only.

BWFM packet-type tracker ownership pass (2026-10-18; no new finding): traced `S2_TRACKTYPE`/`S2_UNTRACKTYPE` and `S2_GETTYPESTATS` through the locked tracker list (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1022-1100,1725-1735`) and compared with AROSTCP's selected setup caller (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:481-504`) and peer SANA-II dispatch. BWFM refcounts repeated tracking requests and removes/frees a tracker on the matching final untrack; close does not implicitly untrack, but the selected AROSTCP setup path also does not issue untrack, and peer implementations do not establish close-owned tracker lifetime. No concrete leak or stats-lifetime contract violation established. Tracker list initialization remains covered by OD3619's concurrent-first-open race. Source-only.

BWFM buffer-hook result/statistics follow-up (2026-10-18): traced opener hook installation and receive/transmit use (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1127-1140,334-400,652-718`) against `Sana2PacketTypeStats`, selected peer implementations, and SANA-II Revision 7. Hook failure is reflected in IOSana2Req error fields; TX additionally emits buffer/software/TX events. RX consumes the read and sets `S2ERR_NO_RESOURCES`/`S2WERR_BUFF_ERROR`, but still treats the frame as delivered for type statistics. The specification defines PacketsReceived/BytesReceived as stats for reads satisfied and BytesReceived as data, supporting OD3702; whether PacketsDropped includes failed caller copies remains unclear because its definition specifically says packets received with no pending reads. No hook was forced to fail. Source-only.

BWFM SANA-II mandatory callback Open check (OD3703 added, 2026-10-18): traced `open()` tag parsing through opener publication and later CMD_READ/TX callback use (`bwfm_dev.c:83-84,1100-1177,342-379,652-688`). Missing mandatory `S2_CopyToBuff` or `S2_CopyFromBuff` leaves the zero-cleared callback NULL but does not fail Open; later matching I/O returns a buffer error. Checked selected AROSTCP, WirelessManager and `wifi` tag lists; all pass both required callbacks. Added OD3703, scoped to external/malformed clients, against SANA-II Revision 7's mandatory-tag/Open failure contract. No open or packet request was run; source-only.

BWFM S2_SETKEY selected-helper and caller recheck (2026-10-18; no new finding): reread the complete `BWFMSetKey` helper and its `handle_request()`/WirelessManager callers (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2603-2674`; `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1798-1825`; `workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:349-372`). The helper bounds key length to the fixed key-data array before copying, validates cipher enum values, serializes firmware calls with `bwfm_Sem`, and returns the `wsec_key` result. The ignored `wsec` read/write failures and false success are already OD3618. Key pointer validity, firmware key-index limits and cipher/key-length semantics are caller/firmware contracts not established here, so no further finding is promoted. No key or firmware response was exercised; source-only.

Deneb ordinary isochronous interval and frame-advance review (2026-10-18; no new OD): compared the hardware API interval units (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:111-114,438-455`) with Poseidon's endpoint normalization and pipe copy (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8483-8553,4624-4627`) and Deneb's ordinary ISO SOF-map selection and continuation frame update (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3283-3288,4683-4704`). Poseidon supplies frame/microframe interval counts in the documented units, and Deneb rounds the continued frame offset upward to whole frames; the SOF-map tiers are controller-specific and no source contract establishes a separate mismatch. Existing OD3587 remains the independently confirmed premature completion when request bytes remain; OD3585 retains the ordinary ISO OUT rounded-word caller-buffer read. No controller or transfer was exercised. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary request abort/reply ownership pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `devAbortIO` through `cmdAbortIO`, queue removal, and active ordinary ISO PTD teardown (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:650-691`; `uhwcmd.c:1778-1869`). For an active ISO request, `cmdAbortIO` disables the PTD, clears the endpoint owner, nulls `ptd_IOReq`, and calls `FreeIso`; consequently `FreeIso` releases hardware/buffer bookkeeping without replying the request, after which `devAbortIO` sets `IOERR_ABORTED` and calls `TermIO` exactly once. Queued requests are removed and use the same caller-side completion. No independent ordinary ISO abort double-reply or lost-reply path established. Broader CMD_FLUSH active/queued reply behavior remains under OD3593/OD3594; no abort or flush was executed. Source-only.

Deneb DMA request completion ordering recheck (OD3704 added, 2026-10-18): followed `FreeATL` from normal DMA completion and `CMD_FLUSH` through reply and cache cleanup (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:973-1051,1641-1659,5169-5254`). The helper calls `ReplyMsg` before `CachePostDMA`, then dereferences the replied IORequest for length, buffer and direction. Exec `Signal` explicitly reschedules immediately when a higher-priority waiting task becomes ready (`rom/exec/signal.c:350-420`), so a client can consume an IN buffer before cache post-processing or reuse request storage before the helper finishes. Added OD3704 separately from OD3584's AbortIO-specific null request dereference. No DMA request or flush was run; source-only.

Deneb bulk DMA fallback and state-machine completion pass (2026-10-18; no new AROS finding): read `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs`'s short-`CachePreDMA` fallback and all `uhwHandleDMAInt` terminal/intermediate state branches (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4200-4400,4995-5265`). The scheduler does leave `usedma` set after a short mapping, which would bypass the PIO allocation/type setup; however, selected m68k AROS `CachePreDMA` dispatches to `CachePreDMA_00` or `_40` (`arch/m68k-all/exec/cachepredma.c:22-48`), and neither implementation adjusts `*length` (`cachepredma_.S:72-80,84-123`), so the short-map branch is not established for the selected AROS target and is not promoted. Completion branches use the shared `FreeATL`; OD3704 remains applicable to DMA completion and CMD_FLUSH because `FreeATL` replies before `CachePostDMA`. No transfer or cache mapping was exercised. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary ISO completion copy-bound recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): followed active/error status branches, hardware transfer-count extraction, IN copy cap and packet continuation (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3020-3330`) against the per-PTD allocation and translation length (`:4550-4770`). HALT/error statuses bypass data copy; the normal IN path caps reported `len` against remaining caller request length before copying, while PTD translation length is initialized from `min(iouh_MaxPktSize, remaining request bytes)`. No source-supported route was found for a normal completion to report more bytes than that PTD's programmed transfer extent. OD3587 remains the proven continuation-condition defect; split-transaction register interpretation and physical-controller status guarantees remain unverified. No transfer or controller was used. Source-only.

Deneb split ISO/interrupt completion status cross-check (OD3705 expanded, 2026-10-18): compared both completion gates with ISP1760 rev. 06 Tables 76 and 78 (`https://docs.rs-online.com/5807/0900766b80da2fcf.pdf`, pp. 75-76, 78-79). The controller defines H for stalled/halted status and X for transaction error independently. `uhwHandleFinishedIsos` checks H at `uhwcmd.c:3053-3072` but, when H is clear and the PTD is inactive, does not inspect per-microframe DW4 status before accounting and `FreeIso` (`:3162-3218`); the request retains `UHIOERR_NO_ERROR` from `devBeginIO` (`dev.c:539-544`). `uhwHandleFinishedInts` likewise gates error mapping only on H (`:2833-2872`) and reads DW4 status only in DEBUG. For split interrupt-IN, an X-only short result reaches the ordinary runt check; `UHFF_ALLOWRUNTPKTS` suppresses `UHIOERR_RUNTPACKET`, so this path can also complete with success (`:2902-2998`). Poseidon maps its public allow-runt pipe/stream setting into this flag (`poseidon.library.c:1371-1373,9693`; `poseidon_intern.h:526`). The USBHardware API says `io_Error` reports transfer errors (`usbhardware.doc:438-455` for ISO; `:337-344` for control and the shared completion contract). Expanded OD3705 to cover ISO generally and interrupt-IN when runt packets are allowed. The interrupt case without that flag may instead be misreported as a runt packet, not success. No hub or transfer was used; source-only.

Other Drivers report reconstruction (2026-10-18): rebuilt `AROS-other-drivers.md` from the 1,089 unique OD entries preserved in `AROS.md`; all entries now have stable report anchors. The recovery note distinguishes long index narratives from short index summaries and does not claim recovery of text absent from the index. This coverage ledger remains the detailed per-file/source-cross-check record. Build-selected audit remains incomplete. Source-only.

Deneb shared-header and type-layout pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read `uhwcmd.h`, `hccommon.h`, `myregargs.h`, and `denebusb.h` against the selected driver definitions and uses. Confirmed the endpoint arrays cover the computed address/endpoint/direction indices and recorded the target-specific assumptions in the file row. `declgate.h`, `deneb.h`, and `isp1760.h` remain open for full body/constant cross-checks; no controller access or build was performed. Source-only.

Deneb controller/header definition pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): completed local reads of `isp1760.h`, `deneb.h`, and `declgate.h` against the existing `denebusb.h` and `uhwcmd.h` field consumers. Reconciled selected AROS/MorphOS preprocessor branches and the active 9-granule memory-map offsets. The undefined-name IMAP aliases are unused macro definitions and do not expand in the selected source census; no defect was promoted. No compile or controller access was performed. Source-only.


Deneb full ATL-completion body pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread `uhwHandleFinishedATLs` from entry through all completion cases (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1967-2782`), including PID/babble/halt and NAK retirement, bulk DMA IN/OUT short-packet and terminating-ZLP handling, buffered bulk copies, control setup/data/status transitions, toggle updates, and `FreeATL` paths. Reconciled the DMA branches with the worker state machine and buffer scheduler (`:4200-4400,4995-5265`) and the controller's byte-count definitions (`isp1760.h:384-396`). The under-threshold IN copy uses the computed rounded actual length; its stale `hu_DMALength` offset update is followed by `DMASM_NOP` and PTD release, while each new DMA request resets the address and offset, so no subsequent copy consumes that value. Rounded OUT source reads remain OD3585; active abort NULL cleanup remains OD3584; completion-before-cache-sync remains OD3704. No further independent defect established. Hardware status semantics, split behavior, and broader abort/completion interleavings remain open. No transfer or hardware was exercised; source-only.


Deneb ordinary ISO completion and scheduling body pass (2026-10-18; OD3587/OD3604/OD3705 rechecked, no new finding): read `uhwHandleFinishedIsos` and `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs` end-to-end (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3007-3328,4531-4772`), tracing request dequeue, PTD and granule allocation, split versus high-speed field construction, OUT staging, frame/interval selection, done-map dispatch, status handling, IN copy cap, packet continuation and `FreeIso` reply. Rechecked OD3587's strict continuation bound against `iouh_Length` and selected Poseidon multi-packet requests, OD3604's high-speed multiplier omission against the 1-KiB/one-`MaxPktSize` staging allocation, and OD3705's independent split H/X status bits against the hardware Tables 76 and 78. The per-microframe status extraction is DEBUG-only and reached only under H; normal split ISO completion therefore does not report an X-only transaction error. No further independent issue established. Device timing, ISO interval/microframe behavior, physical controller guarantees, and live caller lifetimes remain open. No transfer or controller was used; source-only.


Console ConSnipHook reader/writer synchronization trace (OD3706, 2026-10-18): confirmed Add/Rem serialize list mutations with `copyBufferLock`, while CharMap copy's initial emptiness test and SnipMap paste's route-selection test run unlocked. CharMap can skip a live named ConClip port after seeing a hook, then observe an empty list in its later locked delivery pass if the last hook is removed in between; the buffer changes without either hook or port notification. The class and vectors are selected by `rom/devs/console/mmakefile.src`; no checked-in C registration caller exists, so trigger remains an external hook client overlapping teardown. SnipMap's analogous stale route can bypass or spuriously select external paste delivery. No hook, copy/paste, or concurrency was run. Source-only.


Console ConSnipHook callback-removal lifetime trace (OD3707, 2026-10-18): verified the CharMap `ForeachNode` loop obtains the next link from the current hook after `CALLHOOKPKT` returns; callback execution remains within `copyBufferLock`. `InternalObtainSemaphore` increments nesting for the owning task, so same-task `RemConSnipHook` returns recursively; Exec `Remove` updates neighbors but leaves the removed node's own links unchanged. A callback that unregisters and frees its caller-owned node therefore leaves the iterator reading `ln_Succ` from freed storage. No in-tree C registrant exists, so the trigger is external API use. No hook or copy was run. Source-only.


RISC-V OpenSBI timer abort/rearm follow-up (2026-10-18; no additional OD): traced selected generic `AbortIO` with the OpenSBI override. Abort removes/replies to a queued request under disabled interrupts and the timer-list lock but does not call `Timer0Setup`, so aborting the MICROHZ head can leave its old absolute `kpt_Deadline` in the kernel descriptor. The kernel still arms the earlier of that deadline and its periodic `kpt_NextTick`; when the stale deadline eventually fires, `krnTimerTick` dispatches the timer handler, whose `Timer0Setup` recomputes the deadline from the current queue. The source establishes at most an unnecessary one-shot IRQ at the canceled deadline, not a lost completion or stopped periodic tick; I did not promote it. Future multi-hart synchronization and firmware behavior remain open. No timer request was submitted or aborted. Source-only.

USB Audio high-rate allocation/timer follow-up (OD3208 expanded, 2026-10-18): traced requested `AHIA_MixFreq` from AHI `CreateAudioCtrl` (copied directly, defaulted only when zero) through `AHIsub_AllocAudio` and `UpdateAudioCtrl` (which does not clamp the mix rate). USB Audio parses at most 64 listed rates and discards values above 64,000 Hz (`usbaudio.class.c:1220-1248`); its nearest-rate search leaves a request unchanged when every listed value is at least 100,000 Hz away (`:3375-3404`). `subLibStart` then left-shifts the retained 32-bit MixFreq before deriving `nam_SampleFrac` (`:3717-3723`), and `nOutReqHook` uses that fraction to calculate output sample counts and USB transfer lengths (`:2641-2672`). For 192,000 Hz the shift wraps to 3,992,977,408 and division yields 3,992,977, rather than the 12,582,912 16.16 units per millisecond required by the requested rate. Expanded OD3208 with this independent timing consequence of its distant unsupported-rate branch; endpoint behavior remains device-dependent. No allocation, AHI start, or transfer was run. Source-only.

USB Audio interface binding and release lifecycle pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): re-read `usbAttemptInterfaceBinding`, `usbForceInterfaceBinding`, `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding`, `nAllocAudio`/`nFreeAudio`, expunge, and the Poseidon method dispatch (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:110-155,224-390,1995-2128,471-510`). The release path denies requests, removes the binding node, signals the worker, waits for `nch_Task` to clear, and only then queries the still-bound interface/device for its status message. Successful task setup owns the audio units and normal worker cleanup releases them; library expunge frees the retained mode records and unit record. The allocation-failure branch's unmatched `Permit` is already OD3229; retry state and worker/device removal interactions remain represented by existing binding/lifecycle findings. No separate supported caller-visible defect established in this slice. Concurrent/duplicate Poseidon binding callback serialization was not established and remains open; no interface or task was run. Source-only.

USB Audio duplex AHI-allocation rollback closure (2026-10-18; no new OD): closed the previously noted duplex-specific startup cleanup gap by enumerating the exits after the primary mode is selected and `nch_CurrentMode` is published, through playback buffer/converter setup and the recording sibling's message port, pipe, alternate selection/RTIso handler, and buffers (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3263-3555`). On every error return, AHI `_AHI_AllocAudioA` routes the failed suballocation through `_AHI_FreeAudio`, which invokes the subdriver FreeAudio hook even with `AHISF_ERROR` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:500-520,712-728`). `subLibFreeAudio` checks the partially initialized sibling and primary handler/pipe/buffer/request fields, frees handlers created before later failures, and closes the shared Poseidon reference once (`usbaudio.class.c:3570-3685`; `psdFreeRTIsoHandler` accepts NULL and removes/frees the handler and its pipe at `poseidon.library.c:5608-5634`). No independent duplex startup leak or invalid cleanup established in these exits. Interface restoration where no zero-bandwidth alternate was recorded remains OD3361; the class-record rollback remains OD3209. No allocation failure or audio device was exercised. The class file remains partial; broader negotiation, callback concurrency, and worker teardown reviews remain open. Source-only.

USB Audio RTIso stop/free backend coverage (OD3517 scope recheck, 2026-10-18): compared Poseidon's `psdStopRTIso`/`psdFreeRTIsoHandler` sequence against selected PCIUSB UHCI/EHCI/OHCI, PCI xHCI, and m68k Deneb implementations (`poseidon.library.c:5608-5675`; `pciusb/uhwcmd.c:1679-1721`; `pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:1653-1695`; `denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1264-1315,1495-1543`). PCIUSB and xHCI teardown still do not join completion work already executing on another CPU, confirming OD3517's ExecSMP PC scope. Deneb masks local interrupts while disabling its two scheduled PTDs and while removing handler state; its m68k backend is outside the report's cross-CPU trigger, and no additional single-CPU in-flight callback path was established from the examined stop/remove sequence. Device-removal `nReleaseHook` calls Stop before class binding teardown (`poseidon.library.c:2220-2255`); USB Audio's callback changes recording/playback state but does not free buffers itself (`usbaudio.class.c:2747-2774`), so buffer ownership still remains with the later AHI FreeAudio path. No stream, device removal, or concurrency was exercised. Broader HCD event-queue synchronization and other class consumers remain outside this focused closure. Source-only.

USB Audio deferred player-softint teardown follow-up (OD3517 expanded, 2026-10-18): traced UHCI's interrupt completion handler into `uhciHandleIsochTDs`, its refill of the periodic endpoint, and `uhciQueueIsochIO` invoking `nOutReqHook` (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_hcd.c:837-850`; `uhci_isoch.c:440-442,508-510`; `usbaudio.class.c:2620-2647`). On player-interval expiry, `nOutReqHook` updates `nam_AudioCtrl` then calls `Cause` for `nam_PlayerInt`; Exec documents that Cause from real interrupt context queues work for later and `SoftIntDispatch` removes and executes the handler with interrupts enabled (`rom/exec/cause.c:29-34,84-122,169-188`). Neither `subLibStop` nor `subLibFreeAudio` removes or joins this soft interrupt; after the driver hook returns, `_AHI_FreeAudio` frees the player/mixer hooks and `AHIAudioCtrl` (`usbaudio.class.c:2543-2610,3570-3637,3780-3808`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:701-746`). On ExecSMP, a pending or already dequeued PlayerInt on another CPU can therefore outlive RTIso stop and access the released AHI control, hooks or mode buffers. Expanded OD3517 to include this playback path and qualified it specifically to PCIUSB UHCI; no IRQ, soft interrupt or concurrent free was run. The previously documented capture completion-hook path and its PCIUSB/xHCI scope remain unchanged. Source-only.

BWFM blocking S2_ONLINE/join completion ordering follow-up (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `begin_io` into `handle_request(S2_ONLINE)` and `try_join` through `BWFMJoin`'s three-attempt, 200-tick-per-attempt event wait (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:881-911,1660-1664,1903-1910`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2349-2360,2500-2550`). `try_join` can call `link_up`/report CONNECT before the outer handler sets `unit->online` and reports ONLINE; an intervening OFFLINE from another client could also complete before that old S2_ONLINE resumes. The selected AROSTCP online/offline caller serializes these transitions under `splimp`/`spl_semaphore` (prior 2026-10-18 trace at this ledger's online/offline serialization entry), so this does not establish a default in-tree reproducer; direct external SANA-II request ordering and the required event-order contract remain unverified. Kept as an open caller-contract/concurrency question, not a new finding. This refines OD3614's event snapshot/latch ordering context; no request, join, or radio was exercised. Source-only.

USB Audio fallback-timer softint teardown extension (OD3517 expanded, 2026-10-18): followed Poseidon's `psdFreeDevice` release-hook walk (`poseidon.library.c:2242-2249`) to USB Audio's registered `RTA_ReleaseHook` and playback `nReleaseHook` (`usbaudio.class.c:3204-3229,2747-2769`). The release hook changes the PlayerInt callback to `subLibPlayerIntDummy`, causes it, and enables timer fallback; that callback calls AHI Player/Mixer hooks and arms the timer request (`:2596-2610`). Neither drains a PlayerInt already queued/running, and a running dummy handler can re-arm after an abort. Expanded OD3517 and affected-trigger text to include this device-removal fallback path, distinct from the UHCI request-refill producer but sharing the missing softint quiescence. Poseidon cross-hub-class address reservation pass (OD3709 added, 2026-10-18): traced `psdEnumerateDevice` and `pAllocDevAddr` against both hub workers, their per-class `nh_Adr0Sema` instances, and the selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi package (`poseidon.library.c:2345-2360,3292-3298`; `hub.class.c:17-29,105-115,1211-1232,1305-1314`; `rom/usb/classes/hubss/hubss_class.c:41-46,91-101,1260-1285,1303-1310`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:157,165,227`). Two different `PsdDevice` locks and the two independent class-base semaphores do not serialize the scan/reservation of one shared `phw_DevArray`; on SMP both class workers can read one empty slot before either publishes its device pointer. Added OD3709, conditional on overlapping downstream enumeration by the two selected hub classes on one controller. No transfer, address allocation, or race was run; source-only.


Hub port-change bitmap bounds qualification (OD3232 rechecked, 2026-10-18): recalculated the status bitmap extent at 32 ports (`(nch_NumPorts + 8) >> 3` is 5 bytes) against both four-byte members and the subsequent port-index reads. The fifth byte overwrites `nch_Downstream` only on 32-bit layouts without padding; on 64-bit layouts the compiler may insert alignment padding, so the report no longer claims adjacent-pointer corruption there. The port-32 array read remains out of bounds on both layouts. The current AROS targets include 32-bit m68k/ARM hub-class builds as well as 64-bit builds. OD3232 retained with the consequence qualified; no hub or transfer was run. Source-only.

Bluetooth `btAllocVec` allocation-size arithmetic pass (OD3710, 2026-10-18): traced the exported `ULONG` vector ABI through its addition, pool allocation, alignment, bookkeeping writes and matching free-size recomputation (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.conf:44`; `bluetooth.library.c:265-326`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`). The overhead sum is narrowed to 32-bit `ULONG`; a near-limit size can wrap to one, which is nonzero and accepted by `AllocPooled`, before `btAllocVec` stores the header outside the requested allocation. Added OD3710 and indexed it. This is conditional on an unusually large caller request; no allocation was run. The review here covers only the allocator pair in `bluetooth.library.c`; its remaining library methods, callbacks and teardown paths remain open. Source-only.

Bluetooth core event-worker startup slice (OD3711, 2026-10-18): traced `libOpen`'s state/result sequence through `bStartEventHandler`, `btSpawnSubTask`, every worker setup gate, cleanup, and selected event producers (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:174-189,977-1030`; `classes.c:760-789,820-959`; `classes.c:91`; `objects.c:103`). The worker reports readiness only after it has registered the event hook; failed setup returns FALSE to `bStartEventHandler`, but `libOpen` ignores it and retains `bt_StackInit = TRUE`. Added OD3711 for successful-open reporting without the required internal class-scan/event worker; external event-hook delivery is not claimed to stop. This source slice is limited to event-worker startup and producers; the remainder of these library/class files and broader worker ownership remain open. No task or failure was induced. Source-only.

Bluetooth library failed-open timer cleanup pass (OD3712, 2026-10-18): traced the `OpenDevice` success branch through `bt_GlobalCfg` allocation failure, the shared failed-open return, `bt_StackInit` assignment, and `libExpunge`'s guarded `CloseDevice` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:120-132,174-187,231-233`). Bluetooth removal-event pointer recheck (no new finding, 2026-10-18): `btRemHardware` sends `BEHMB_REMDEVICE` after `bFreeDevice` has detached the device and released its names/services/semaphore; however, the device structure itself is deliberately not freed because tasks may still call `LockDevice`; when its use count is zero it is unlinked from the dead-device list but its pool allocation remains (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:355-405`; public `btFreeDevice` at `:414-442`). This does not support the suspected immediate device-structure use-after-free. The same function does send `BEHMB_REMHARDWARE` after freeing the `BtHardware` allocation (`:171-183`), but the selected Preferences subscriber uses that event only to close its hardware window and refresh from the stack, without dereferencing `Param1` (`rom/bluetooth/prefs/ActionClass.c:1182-1186`). The public header gives the parameter type but does not specify whether removal-event parameters remain valid (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/include/libraries/bluetooth.h:313,413-416`), and no checked-in consumer dereferencing the removed hardware pointer was found. I did not promote an external-client lifetime expectation into a definite defect; API lifetime and outside clients remain open. Source-only.

Bluetooth class-removal event payload follow-up (OD3732, 2026-10-18): traced `btRemClass()` through class and string deallocation and into `btSendEvent()`'s event-note copy. Unlike the hardware removal API comment, the public event definition explicitly specifies `BEHMB_REMCLASS` Param1 as `bc` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/include/libraries/bluetooth.h:418`); it is queued only after the object is freed (`classes.c:146-158,712-740`). The selected Preferences consumer ignores the pointer for class removal, but other public subscribers that use the documented parameter receive a dangling pointer. Added OD3732 with that conditional scope. Also traced classic SDP `bAllocService()` publication and GATT service enumeration allocation: `cn_EnumCount` is clamped to `BT_GATT_CLIENT_MAX_SERVICES` before filling the matching fixed arrays (`hwconn.c:1924-1934`; `hwtask.h:235-236`; cap in `stack/include/btcore/gatt_client.h:29`), and later GATT-characteristic handling checks for a missing `BtService`. No independent allocation or array-bound defect was established in this slice. Source-only.

Bluetooth class-scan binding-decision follow-up (OD3733, 2026-10-18): read the complete `bDeviceClassScan()` body and its `btClassScan()` caller. `hassvcbinding` is only assigned TRUE; on the no-existing/no-successful-service-binding path, its two later reads control forced device binding and fallback device binding without any initialization (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:260,291-305,377-379`). The event broadcaster's selected triggers call `btClassScan()` after registration/connection/service changes and Preferences/shell also expose direct scans (`:826-831,892-919`; `prefs/ActionClass.c:1625`; `shellcommands/AddBTClasses.c:157`). Added OD3733. Subsequent counter synchronization trace is recorded as OD3734; no device was scanned. Source-only.

Bluetooth binding-count synchronization follow-up (OD3734, 2026-10-18): reconciled every maintained `bc_UseCnt` mutation and read. Increments occur from class scans under a shared base lock, while device/service release decrements occur under only each device's lock; class removal checks the count after unlinking under the exclusive base lock but later releases bindings outside that lock. The shared lock admits multiple readers; its bookkeeping `Forbid()` is not an SMP lock, and Exec documents that Forbid is CPU-local in ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). This supports lost updates across concurrent scans/releases and premature class teardown, separate from OD3725's corruption of the custom semaphore's own reader bookkeeping. Added OD3734, scoped to ExecSMP. No binding or concurrent schedule was run. Source-only.

Bluetooth app-binding versus class-scan ownership follow-up (OD3735, 2026-10-18): traced the service binding-in-progress marker through `bDeviceClassScan()` and its later commit, then compared it with `btClaimAppBindingA()`'s locked check and publication. App claim checks for existing committed bindings but not in-progress service callbacks; after an app claim sets `BDFF_APPBINDING`, the scan publishes its successful service binding without rechecking. This contradicts the scan's own early guard that normally excludes app-bound devices. No maintained direct app-binding caller was found, so the finding is scoped to external public API clients overlapping an automatic/requested scan. Added OD3735; no claim or scan was run. Source-only.

Bluetooth release-callback and unbind traversal pass (2026-10-18; no additional finding): read `btReleaseDevBinding()`, `btReleaseSvcBinding()`, and `btUnbindAll()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:541-656`) with all maintained `btUnbindAll()` and release callers. The unbind walker drops the base read lock before each release and restarts from the list head, avoiding use of a traversal cursor across callback execution; no maintained direct `btUnbindAll()` call was found. Traced selected BTHID, btserial, and btpan service-release callbacks: they signal/join their workers, whose cleanup aborts/waits/frees channels. The hardware task handles channel abort and close control messages through `bHandleChannel()` / `BTPRI_CLOSECHANNEL` without acquiring the per-device lock (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2232-2255`; `hwconn.c:3678-3697`), so this slice did not establish that the wrapper's held device lock deadlocks normal worker cleanup. Long-running GATT/SDP operations, external class release methods, and all callback re-entry contracts remain open. Source-only.

Bluetooth BTHID duplicate-binding guard recheck (OD3736, 2026-10-18): followed the per-device `nh_Interfaces` duplicate scan through binding allocation, worker startup/readiness wait, and later list insertion (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:224-277`). The duplicate check and insertion are separately protected by `Forbid()`, with task startup and a wait between them. `bDeviceClassScan()` can make disjoint 16-service snapshots when more than 16 eligible services exist (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:288-301`); overlapping scans can therefore invoke the BTHID guard on distinct HID services for one device before either inserts its binding. This violates the source's explicit one-physical-device HID invariant. Added OD3736 for selected BTHID builds and the stated trigger; no hardware or scan was run. Source-only.

Bluetooth class-scan service-batch continuation pass (OD3737, 2026-10-18): traced the `svcs[16]` collection through binding attempts, marker clearing, return, and the event broadcaster's coalesced scan trigger (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:288-301,333-375,377-410,892-919`). One pass never examines eligible services after the first 16 and does not queue a continuation. ## Hosted Ethernet first-open concurrency disposition (2026-10-18)

Rechecked `arch/all-unix/devs/networks/eth/init.c:85-244` through `OpenDevice` (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:90-110`) and the Exec lock macros (`rom/exec/exec_locks.h:46-50,82-86`). `OpenDevice` calls the device Open vector after releasing the DeviceList lock but before its final `Permit()`; the lock macro's plain `EXEC_UNLOCK_LIST` does not Permit. The selected hosted Linux x86 branches define platform SMP support (`configure.in:1436-1437,1460-1461`), while `ENABLE_EXECSMP` is assigned only in the native x86-64 SMP and Raspberry Pi SMP variant branches (`configure.in:1667-1670,2195-2198`), not in the hosted Linux/FreeBSD target branches. Exec's documented Forbid serialization therefore prevents two task-level OpenDevice callbacks from concurrently running this first-open/refcount sequence on the selected hosted builds. The selected driver manifest remains `arch/all-unix/devs/networks/eth/mmakefile.src:6-8`. No independent first-open race is promoted. This narrows the earlier open question for those configurations; alternate direct Open-vector entry and external modified builds were not established. No device was opened and no failure was induced. Existing OD2215, OD2216 and OD3515 remain as recorded above.

## Linux PCIDriver mapping-failure return pass (OD3728, 2026-10-18)

Traced the selected x86 Linux PCI HIDD `MapPCI` implementation through all local USB controller callers. `PCILx__Hidd_PCIDriver__MapPCI` invokes the raw `mmap2` syscall and returns the syscall result without error normalization (`arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/driverclass.c:123-148`); Linux mapping errors are negative/nonzero `MAP_FAILED` results, not NULL ([Linux `mmap(2)` return value](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/mmap.2.html)). The xHCI, EHCI and OHCI callers test only the pointer's nullness, then read registers (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_controllerclass.c:90-108`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ehci/ehci_hcd.c:1262-1273`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ohci/ohci_hcd.c:1753-1763`). Added OD3728 for the shared sentinel-contract mismatch. The devices are optional USB targets and no host mapping or controller was used.

## Hosted TAP MTU setting parser pass (OD3729, 2026-10-18)

Traced the optional TAP MTU environment value from `GetVar()` into `tap_read_mtu()` and the MTU/frame-buffer consumers (`arch/all-unix/devs/networks/tap/init.c:19-44,197-218`; `tap.h:64-71`). `StrToLong()` returns the parsed character count and stops at the first nondigit (`rom/dos/strtolong.c:28-30,59-77`), but the caller checks only `> 0` and the numeric range; a valid in-range prefix followed by junk is accepted. Added OD3729 for the malformed-config acceptance. `GetVar()` null-terminates this text-mode value, including when the supplied buffer truncates it (`rom/dos/getvar.c:41-68,130-155`), so this is not an unterminated-buffer issue. No environment setting or TAP device was used.

Hosted TAP random-MAC and UnixIO poll-error follow-up (OD3730, 2026-10-18): rejected the repeated-MAC candidate after tracing `rand()` to the selected StdC implementation: each stdc.library open seeds its per-task base from `time(NULL)` (`compiler/crt/stdc/rand.c:92-104`), so the source does not establish an unseeded fixed stream. Compared Ethernet and TAP poll-drain loops with UnixIO `poll_fd()` (`unixio_class.c:110-135,971-987`): a host poll failure becomes `-1`, and each caller's `continue` reaches `while (events)` with `events == -1`, bypassing the outer task-signal wait. Added OD3730 for both workers. No random stream, host poll error or device was exercised.

Linux Unix-packet descriptor lifetime and caller-result pass (2026-10-18; OD3511 retained, no additional finding): traced every `OpenPacket`, `ClosePacket`, receive/send, fd-query and MAC-query method in `unixpkt_class.c` against the hosted Ethernet initialization and worker callers. Open failures close any created host descriptor and free the wrapper; the Ethernet caller checks packet-open, fd and MAC-query results before task startup. Close frees the wrapper even when host `close()` reports failure, but the semantics of descriptor state after host close errors vary and the selected caller is disposing its final ownership, so I did not promote an independent leak. The interface-wide `IFF_PROMISC` mutation and missing restore remain OD3511. No packet, ioctl or close failure was induced.
