`CmpTime()` full caller census (2026-10-18; no new finding): searched the entire checked-in source tree for direct C/header/assembly calls and checked every active expression against the documented `-1 = dest greater`, `0 = equal`, `+1 = dest less` result. Efika timer queue/completion, touchscreen deadline, six network watchdogs, nForce link timeout, and seven network busy-delay implementations use the expected operand order. Busy-delay callsites use fixed durations or bounded Atheros PHY-delay expressions: a 14-bit source field scales to at most 11,912 µs plus 100 µs, and ar5210 reset waits are at most 20,000 µs. Operand order remains consistent with the documented comparison result. A zero-duration call may perform one sample comparison before returning. The Sis900 match is commented out. Updated the `cmptime.c` row to complete checked-in direct-caller status; external callers, time adjustment, and rollover remain open. Source-only.

Atheros `OS_DELAY` numeric-bound follow-up (2026-10-18; no new finding): completed the dynamic-argument trace left open by the `CmpTime()` caller census. The ar5210 `waitTime` parameter is supplied only `10` or `AR_RC_SETTLE_TIME=20000`; the additional ar5211 `searchTime` path receives only runtime values `{0,2,7}`, making its maximum 25,088 µs (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/hal/ar5211/ar5211_reset.c:868-901,991-1002`). The ar5211/ar5212/ar5312/ar5416 `synthDelay` starts from `AR_PHY_RX_DELAY` masked by `0x3fff`, is divided by 10 or multiplied by 4 then divided by 22, and is rate-scaled by at most four plus `BASE_ACTIVATE_DELAY=100`. Its maximum expression is 11,912+100 µs, safely representable by the HAL delay's signed `int` parameter. All remaining `OS_DELAY` calls in the selected HAL source use constants. This closes numeric range only; physical clock timing, scheduling latency and hardware behavior remain untested. Source-only.

AR5211 interrupt mapping/caller pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read the full `ar5211_interrupts.c` body, mapped common/RX/TX/fatal bits against `ah.h` and `ar5211reg.h`, and traced the registered callbacks into `unit.c:1466-1495`. AR5211 key-cache / S2_SETKEY caller pass (OD3832 added; 2026-10-18): read the complete `ar5211_keycache.c` body and traced selected key-cache calls through `SetKey()`, `ConfigureAdapter()` and receive/transmit callback selection. AR5211 transmit queue and descriptor pass (OD3293 expanded; 2026-10-18): read the complete `ar5211_xmit.c` body and traced both `InitialiseAdapter()` DATA queue allocations plus the separate normal/management rings and completion handlers. Its `SetTxDP()` notes that writes while TXE is asserted have no effect, while the device submits independent descriptor chains for the two software rings; expanded OD3293 to cover this alias and conditional stalled-request consequence. AR5212 interrupt body/caller pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read the complete `ar5212_interrupts.c` body, compared its common/RX/TX/fatal and beacon-misc mappings with `ah.h` and `ar5212reg.h`, and traced `ah_intrTxqs` accumulation into `ar5212GetTxIntrQueue()` and the selected `StatusInt()` caller. AR5212 PHY/rate table source pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read all static rate tables and `ar5212GetRateTable()`, then traced the selected SANA-II configuration and reset-time duration setup (`unit.c:706-744`; `ar5212_reset.c:2579-2617`) through `ath_hal_setupratetable()` (`ah.c:391-422`). Failure paths restore temporary CCK mode fields and publish status. AR5212 board-value/reset follow-up (OD3845 added; 2026-10-18): traced `ar5212SetBoardValues()` from its reset caller through the selected 11a/11b/11g/turbo EEPROM fields and `OS_REG_RMW_FIELD`. The v3 EEPROM fields are signed 8-bit, and the PGA register field inserts them using a signed left shift by eight. Added OD3845 for negative settings; the ADC field uses shift zero and is not implicated. No EEPROM or reset was used. The rest of `ar5212_reset.c` remains open. Source-only.

AR5212 XPA timing packing follow-up (OD3846 added; 2026-10-18): the adjacent `ee_txEndToXPAOff[arrayMode] << 24` also needs unsigned-promotion review. The EEPROM parser stores an unrestricted 8-bit value in `uint16_t`, and values 128..255 overflow the signed `int` result before register packing. This is implementation-defined signed conversion rather than undefined behavior; no selected compiler mispacking was established, so OD3846 is withdrawn. OD3845 remains separate because it shifts a negative signed PGA value. No EEPROM or reset was used. Source-only.


AR5212 spur-mitigation function/caller pass (OD3847-OD3848 added, 2026-10-18): read all of `ar5212SetSpurMitigation()` and traced calls from AR5212 reset/channel setup, AR5312 reset and AR5416 reset. The EEPROM spur selection accepts offsets symmetrically within 87 units (twice that in turbo), so a selected spur below the channel reaches signed negative left shifts in frequency/bin calculations (OD3847). The pilot mask accepts `curBinOffset == 32`, forming signed `1 << 31` (OD3848). The early maximum-bin check does not reject that boundary because it checks the pre-center bin before adding 25. No EEPROM or hardware was used. This is a function-level pass; the reset translation unit and its remaining functions/callers are still open. Source-only.


AR5212 antenna-switch, spur-channel, and chip-power-limit follow-up (2026-10-18; no new OD): read the complete `ar5212SetAntennaSwitchInternal()`, `ar5212IsSpurChannel()` and `ar5212GetChipPowerLimits()` bodies. Traced antenna-switch calls through the reset board setup and public set-switch callback; EEPROM parser masks all eleven switch entries to six bits before the packing shifts, and channel-mode selection rejects other flags. `ar5212IsSpurChannel()` is used only by board setup to conditionally program fast ADC state. `ar5212GetChipPowerLimits()` is registered in the HAL vector; its TP-scale table index is bounded by `ath_hal_setcapability()` (`HAL_TP_SCALE_MIN == 4`) and attach initializes it to zero. No checked-in direct caller was found and no additional local defect was established; callers that provide channel arrays remain external. Source-only.


AR5212 rate/power-table and calibration caller pass (OD3849 added; 2026-10-18): read complete `ar5212SetTransmitPower()`, `ar5212SetRateTable()`, `ar5212GetTargetPowers()` and `ar5212GetLowerUpperValues()` bodies. Traced selected reset/channel change callers, TX-power limit callback and chip-power-limit vector, the AR5111/AR5112 backend bounds, EEPROM target-power parser/checksum/clear allocation, and the `HAL_TP_SCALE_MIN` validator. Added OD3849 for sparse target-power EEPROM slots being counted without compaction, so the consumer's shortened prefix can include a zero row and omit later valid calibration. The default selected backend/parser contract is source-traced; actual board EEPROM values and RF calibration remain unverified. The v3 parser decodes fixed edge/power slots but applies no active-CTL edge count/order/contiguity validation. The consumer stops at the first zero edge; empty active tables invoke the zero-length helper reads, and an interior zero truncates later regulatory edges before selecting the power cap. AR5212 helper-tail follow-up (2026-10-18; no new OD): read complete `ar5212GetMaxEdgePower()`, `interpolate()`, `ar5212SetRateDurationTable()`, and `ar5212SetIFSTiming()` bodies with their reset callers. `GetMaxEdgePower()` assumes at least one sorted, contiguous active CTL edge; that invalid-EEPROM case is OD3850. AR5212 channel/reset helper pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read complete `ar5212SetChannel()`, `ar5212ChannelChange()`, `ar5212SetOperatingMode()`, `ar5212PhyDisable()`, `ar5212Disable()`, `ar5212ChipReset()`, `ar5212ResetCalValid()`, and `ar5212SetResetReg()` bodies. `ar5212Reset()` validates channel band/modulation, maps the channel and validates opmode before the selected calls. The synthesizer-only `ar5212ChannelChange()` call from `ar5212Reset()` is under `#if 0`; it is not in the compiled fast-change path. `SetOperatingMode()` receives the validated modes from reset/PCU setup; its unsupported default leaves mode bits cleared, but no selected caller supplies an unsupported value. `ResetCalValid()` is an unconditional compatibility stub matching AR5210/AR5211 and has no checked-in caller; unlike the AR5416 implementation it does not model calibration cache state, but no selected consumer consequence was established. `SetResetReg()` masks PCI reset on PCIe, polls only MAC/BB bits and updates PHY-power bookkeeping from the requested reset state; callers propagate failures. Full `ar5212Reset()` body and hardware-specific reset sequencing remain open. Source-only.


AR5212/AR5312 reset TX-power field encoding pass (OD3851 added; 2026-10-18): traced the early revised-PHY TXPWRADJ programming through the v3 EEPROM delta decode and `SM()` macro. The later channel-14 PCDAC delta can be negative but is separately narrowed to `uint16_t` before its helper call; absent evidence about supported EEPROM calibration bounds, no additional issue was promoted. AR5212 antenna-switch API pre-reset validation trace (OD3852 added; 2026-10-18): followed the registered `ar5212SetAntennaSwitch()` from its PHY-off/no-current-channel early branch through attach initialization, `ar5212SetBoardValues()`, and `ar5212SetAntennaSwitchInternal()`. The early branch caches arbitrary enum values and returns success, but reset-time internal validation rejects values outside the three declared enum constants; board setup ignores that failure, so reset continues with the switch setting unapplied. AR5212 chip-reset and periodic-calibration body pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read complete `ar5212ChipReset()`, `ar5212PerCalibrationN()` and wrapper bodies, traced chip-reset callers from attach and `ar5212Reset()`, and traced the selected public calibration callback into `unit.c:796`. Chip reset only branches on reset-validated channel flags (attach supplies NULL); the fixed mode/PLL write ordering and delay are internally bounded. The IQ result retry always refreshes all measured values and division is guarded by nonzero denominators. Negative coefficients are valid within the declared field ranges but are passed to signed-shifting `OS_REG_RMW_FIELD`; added OD3853. `chainMask` is not used by this implementation, but the checked-in unit calls the single-chain wrapper and no in-tree `PerCalibrationN` caller was found; no distinct defect established. Hardware calibration values and multi-chain external API expectations remain open. Source-only.


AR5212 periodic IQ coefficient field-encoding pass (OD3853 added; 2026-10-18): traced measured I/Q values through denominator guards, coefficient clamps, register field definitions and the `OS_REG_RMW_FIELD` macro. The clamps intentionally preserve negative signed coefficients, but the macro left-shifts them before masking; added OD3853. The AR5211 implementation explicitly converts its masked coefficient values to `uint32_t` before shifting and is not affected by this specific finding. No calibration or register operation was run. Deneb RTIso hook-length/continuation pass (2026-10-18; no additional finding): compared the public `IOUsbHWBufferReq` contract (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:90-113`) with the RTIso IN/OUT hook loops and selected USB Audio callbacks (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3592-3681,3700-3775`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2620-2693`). IN supplies the received byte count and permits hook adjustment; continuation consumes the adjusted prefix and carries the remaining PTD bytes forward. Selected Audio OUT hook sizes are computed from the mode’s sample-frame counters, and the API does not state a separate callback length cap in the header. The Deneb output loop has no explicit destination-slice cap, but this pass did not establish a valid selected caller exceeding its per-PTD slice, so no defect is added; direct external hook-contract bounds remain open. The zero-MULT controller behavior from OD3604 and split-transaction field semantics are not inferred from these hook contracts. No stream or callback was run. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary ISO zero-frame scheduling pass (OD3890 added, 2026-10-18): traced request initialization and submission from Exec `CreateIORequest()` through Poseidon pipe creation/`psdDoPipe()` into Deneb `cmdIsoXFer()` and `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()` (`rom/exec/createiorequest.c:63-70`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4512-4514,4705-4729`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:892-919,4704-4705`). The root request is zero-filled, pipe construction copies it, and the generic pipe caller does not set `iouh_Frame`; Deneb directly packs its low five bits as the ISO frame target. Selected PCIUSB EHCI/UHCI/OHCI paths interpret zero as unspecified and choose a future frame with lead time (`ehci_isoch.c:418-439`; `uhci/uhci_isoch.c:289-307`; `ohci/ohci_isoch.c:265-286`). Added OD3890 for Deneb's missing default-frame normalization. The exact ISP1760 missed-frame consequence remains conditional because its frame-match semantics are not documented in this source set; no transfer or controller was used. Distinct from OD3884 continuation cadence and OD3587 packet-count completion. Source-only.

UHCI RTIso frame-wrap candidate recheck (OD3812 retained, 2026-10-18): reread the automatic and explicit-frame branches in `uhciQueueIsochIO`, descriptor start, active-PTD timeout walker, and the frame-counter update. The RTIso automatic path computes `current_frame + lead` in `ULONG`, stores through the public `UWORD ubr_Frame`, then copies that narrowed value into the `ULONG ptd_FrameIdx`; the post-assignment resync repeats the narrowing and cannot repair it after 0xffff (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_isoch.c:290-342`; field types `pciusb.h:70,216`, `usbhardware.h:103-108`). The active descriptor timeout compares the full frame counter against the truncated PTD index plus a small interval-based window (`:392-399`). `uhciStartIsochIO` schedules the frame-list slot using that stale PTD index (`:555-603`). Counter extension remains 32-bit across 11-bit hardware wraps (`uhci_hcd.c:820-833`). The report's concrete example is consistent: current=65530, interval=1 yields intended 65538 -> stored 2 -> PTD index 2, which is already beyond the four-frame timeout window. Existing OD3812 retained; no new finding. No stream or controller was run; source-only.

PCIUSB UHCI descriptor-pool synchronization pass (OD3891 added, 2026-10-18): traced `uhciAllocTD`/`uhciFreeTD` from the shared head and inline helpers through task-context `UHCMD_ADDISOHANDLER`/`uhciInitIsochIO` allocation and rollback, and the completion interrupt's isoch frees/refill allocations. `devBeginIO` calls the command handler directly; RTIso setup leaves its allocation loop outside `Disable`; the helpers have no lock. Added OD3891 as an interleaving-dependent descriptor-pool race with medium confidence in the manifestation and no runtime reproduction. Existing UHCI HIDD OD2970 concerns its separate bitmap allocator; this finding is specific to PCIUSB's `UhciHCPrivate` linked TD pool. Source-only.

PCIUSB/PCI xHCI first-open state recheck (OD2421 and OD2152 detailed, 2026-10-18): traced both `Open_Unit` implementations through `pciInit`, unit publication, and Exec `OpenDevice`. `hd_ScanDone` is set before discovery and remains true on PCI-HIDD or per-unit allocation failure; both implementations append units incrementally. Added OD2421 for the no-retry/partial-discovery state. Exec releases its device-list lock before entering the device Open vector; `Forbid` remains around the vector but is local-CPU-only on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-114`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). A second CPU can therefore see scan-done and search before the target unit is appended, producing a transient false 'unit does not exist' open failure. Added OD2152; no concurrent open or allocation failure was run. The x86-64 PC SMP manifest selects the USB package and PCIUSB; other platform configurations remain to be reconciled. Source-only.

PCI HIDD setup/removal and owner-claim synchronization recheck (OD3636/OD3637 detailed, 2026-10-18): confirmed generic `HW_AddDriver` runs `SetUpDriver` before publishing the new node, PCI `InsertDevice` locks individual appends, but PCI setup's IRQ-routing/diagnostic traversals do not retain `dev_lock`; removal obtains that lock and disposes/unlinks entries (`hwclass.c:181-199`; `pciclass.c:61-94,130-204,451-517`). Thus whole setup is not mutually excluded from removal even though individual inserts are. Rechecked the separate owner synchronization: `Obtain` takes `ownerLock`, `aHidd_PCIDevice_Owner` reads its link name without the lock, and PCI removal relies on that getter while holding only `dev_lock` (`pcideviceclass.c:488-510,1214-1216`; `pciclass.c:489-512`). Cross-checked checked-in removal paths in Efika, Sam440 and hosted Linux, plus owner callers across PCIUSB, xHCI, storage, networking and graphics. No ordinary in-tree startup overlap was established; both candidates remain conditional on concurrent public add/remove or claim/remove use. Restored OD3636 and OD3637 detail in the report with medium manifestation confidence; no HIDD operation was run. Source-only.

USB Audio allocation rollback recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread the complete `subLibAllocAudio()`/`subLibFreeAudio()` region and traced its post-failure call through `_AHI_AllocAudioA()` to `_AHI_FreeAudio()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3263-3670`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:457-512,654-746`). Each early allocation/setup error reaches `subLibFreeAudio`; `nch_CurrentMode` is set only after primary mode selection and is cleared by cleanup; the cleanup checks optional RTIso/pipe/buffer/timer resources, and Exec `DeleteMsgPort(NULL)` is documented safe. The frequency/endpoint ordering and pre-worker mode-record retention remain OD3208 and OD3209. No independent defect established in this rollback slice. The Audio class file remains partial: remaining method bodies, descriptor/caller contracts and device-removal lifetime still need review. No allocation failure or USB/AHI operation was induced; source-only.

USB Audio worker, removal and control-update caller recheck (2026-10-18; OD3167/OD3177/OD3238 retained, no new OD): traced `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()` through the task break/wait and `nAudioTask()`'s active-mode drain into `nFreeAudio()` (`usbaudio.class.c:366-395,600-777,2081-2115`). The release path removes the class record, signals shutdown, and waits for the worker to clear `nch_Task`; the worker deliberately waits for `nch_CurrentMode` to be freed before releasing its AHI/USB resources, confirming OD3177's conditional teardown stall. Separately, `AHI_ControlAudioA()` dispatches control tags directly without serializing calls (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:931-999`); USB Audio ORs shared update bits and signals its worker (`usbaudio.class.c:4105-4152`), whose synchronous `psdDoPipe()` operations are followed by an unconditional whole-word flag clear (`:613-762`), confirming the OD3167 lost-update interleaving. `nGetInputUnit()`'s unchecked selector index remains the OD3238 path. No new independent defect established. The class's broader callback, descriptor and control contract review remains partial; no task, control transfer or device removal was run. Source-only.

Deneb control OUT chunk extent/report-ledger consistency recheck (OD3585, 2026-10-18): reread the PTDT_SETUP and PTDT_SDATAOUT completion paths (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2552-2590,2675-2695`) against the USBHardware `iouh_Length` byte-count and odd-length/no-padding contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:127-132,240-246`). Both initial and continuation control OUT chunks copy `(ptd_BufLen + 3) >> 2` words from the request buffer, confirming the one-to-three-byte final-chunk overread already detailed in OD3585. The per-file row above understated OD3585's scope by naming only bulk and interrupt routes; its detailed report also covers control and ISO OUT paths. No separate finding added; no request was submitted. Source-only.

Deneb control-transfer stage/accounting pass (2026-10-18; OD3585 retained, no new OD): reread `uhwScheduleCtrlPTDs()` and the ATL `PTDT_SETUP`, `PTDT_SDATAIN/OUT`, and `PTDT_STERMIN/OUT` transitions (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1967-2783,3796-3955`). Successful SETUP completion requires exactly eight bytes; zero-length requests proceed directly to the status stage with direction derived from `bmRequestType`; nonzero requests select data direction likewise. IN data copies are capped to the remaining `iouh_Length`, partial chunks advance `iouh_Actual`, and a short packet uses `UHFF_ALLOWRUNTPKTS` before status-stage transition. The odd-length OUT overread remains OD3585. The checked request documentation describes `iouh_Length` but does not establish the relationship callers must maintain with setup `wLength`; no in-tree caller mismatch was established in this pass, so no separate finding is added. Caller construction, PTD hardware semantics, and abort/error interleavings remain open; no request was submitted. Source-only.

Deneb control request length caller contract resolved for selected stack (2026-10-18): followed every checked-in direct `UHCMD_CONTROLXFER` producer to the Poseidon pipe wrapper. `psdDoPipe()` sets `iouh_Length = len` and, for endpoint-zero pipes, sets setup `wLength` from the same `len` before queueing the IO request (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4705-4730`); `psdSendPipe()` uses the same assignments (`:4735-4767`). The selected Poseidon control API therefore does not establish a mismatch between request length and setup wLength for Deneb. Replaced that item in the preceding control-stage note's open scope with external/direct USBHardware clients, whose field contract is not established by the checked in-tree caller census. No control request was sent. Source-only.


Deneb SET_ADDRESS data-toggle reset pass (OD3892 added, 2026-10-18): traced successful status-stage handling for SET_ADDRESS through the device/endpoint/direction toggle index, completion update, next interrupt transfer, and Poseidon address release/reallocation (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1647,2759-2768,2831,4145`; `denebusb.h:326`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2200-2203,2345-2364`). The clear loop omits slot base+31, which maps to endpoint 15 IN; a recycled address can therefore retain a DATA1 toggle for the next device. Added OD3892 to the detailed report and index; restored the missing OD3891 index entry during the consistency check. No device or transfer was used. Source-only.


USB MassStorage live configuration publication pass (OD3894 added, 2026-10-18): traced `UCM_OpenBindingCfgWindow`/`nOpenBindingCfgWindow` into the GUI subtask's `tc_UserData`, its direct writes to the live `ncm_CDC`/`ncm_CUC` structures during Save/Use, `nStoreConfig` into Poseidon's `pCheckCfgChanged` event, and `UCM_ConfigChangedEvent`/`nLoadBindingConfig` copies back into live units (`massstorage.class.c:850-865,964-1010,5426-5435,6011-6110,6128-6134`; `poseidon.library.c:7354-7415,8192-8222`). Traced active consumers in `nGetModePage`, the unit worker's `cuc_AutoMountFAT` decision and filesystem mount environment construction (`massstorage.class.c:1930-1953,4044-4054,5228-5256`). No shared lock or worker pause protects these accesses; the reload's Forbid is processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). Added OD3894 for mixed configuration revisions during concurrent request/automount handling. The class is selected through `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:62`; GUI-user timing and runtime manifestation remain source-only. No GUI, I/O or concurrent update was run. Source-only.

Deneb RTIso completion callback/copy pass (2026-10-18; no additional OD): traced IN PTD byte-count extraction through `IOUsbHWBufferReq` callback adjustments, 32-bit card-memory reads, odd-byte carry across partial scatter/gather chunks, done-hook ordering, and automatic destination advancement (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3332-3678`). Compared the hook contract (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:90-113`) and USB Audio's selected input hook (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2679-2737`): the contract frames length adjustment as a partial copy, and the selected hook substitutes its destination without increasing the received count. No supported in-tree trigger was found for the speculative case where a hook increases the byte count beyond the completed PTD payload; that is not promoted as a finding. Existing OD3228/OD3517 cover selected callback buffer reuse/lifetime concerns, while OD3585/OD3705 cover separate controller-copy and split-status behavior. Completion state, device scheduling/register semantics, and external hook implementations remain open. No device or transfer was used; source-only.

Deneb RTIso start/stop and error-rearm follow-up (2026-10-18; no additional OD): reread `cmdStartRTIso()`, `cmdStopRTIso()`, the completion rearm branch and the DMA-worker done-map handoff (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1329-1478,1501-1538,3332-3785,5320-5341`). Start publishes both PTDs under local `Disable()` with their active mask and clears stale done bits; stop clears both hardware active words and removes both bits from the active/done maps before returning. A completed non-HALT PTD is reprogrammed and the node's next-PTD index advances; a HALT PTD instead records the mapped error and does not rearm or advance. This pass does not establish whether ISP1760's ISO HALT status is recoverable for this stream API or represents a terminal controller condition, so the apparent stopped-slot behavior is left as an open hardware-semantics question, not promoted to a defect. No device, DMA completion, or error status was exercised; source-only.

PCIPC registration-return lead recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): followed both legacy and ACPI host-bridge `OOP_DoMethod()` calls in `PCIPC_InitClass()` into `PCI__Hidd_PCI__AddHardwareDriver()` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:606-642`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:561-599`). The method implementation is `void` and has no registration status result to discard, so the ledger's earlier “discarded bus-registration return” lead is not a supported bug and is withdrawn as a candidate. PCI base object creation is checked before registration. The unchecked ACPI host-bridge-node allocation and immediate dereference remain the distinct OD3525 case. No class registration or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

OHCI root-hub OnOff return-path check (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `OHCI::OnOff` through its USBHub superclass and checked in-tree callers. The superclass sets `hub->enabled`, queues the worker event and waits, then currently returns FALSE unconditionally (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:278-294`); OHCI assigns that result when enabling, but independently changes HCFS, sets `running`, and fires pending RHSC work (`drivers/OHCI/ohcihub.c:57-89`). Selected attach/enumeration callers ignore the method result (`stack/usbclass.c:138-145,325-330`), and the public header supplies no result contract beyond BOOL (`include/usb.h:472`). Therefore the false result alone is not promoted as a maintained caller-visible defect; external HIDD caller expectations remain open. No hub method was invoked.

OHCI/UHCI failed-init support-object cleanup recheck (OD2950 expanded, 2026-10-18): confirmed `sd.pci` is created before enumeration and neither failed-init expunge hook disposes it (`OHCI ohci_init.c:127-168,171-185`; `UHCI uhci_init.c:164-207,210-224`). EHCI disposes its temporary PCI HIDD after enumeration (`ehci_init.c:208-242`). This leaves an additional allocated support object on OHCI/UHCI no-match or pool-failure returns, distinct from the already-recorded USB root object retention but sharing the same missing failed-init unwind; included under OD2950. No module was loaded. Source-only.

Bluetooth synchronous firmware-command cancellation recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced `bHciDoSync()`’s task-break return through the checked-in firmware loader’s stack response buffer, the hwtask loop, and hardware removal (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:1794-1810,1819-1870,2960-3053`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/firmware.c:43-51,111-160`; `rom/bluetooth/firmware/rtlfwcommon.h:81-100`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:164-171`). If Ctrl-C arrives without a completed command event, `bHciDoSync()` re-raises the signal before returning; the outer loop then exits after its next wait, and shutdown drains queued HCI event messages with `ReplyMsg()` rather than `bHandleEvent()`, so the retained completion callback cannot copy into the loader’s expired stack response. If the event is drained inside `bHciDoSync()`, its callback runs before the loader returns. No stale-response write is established. No command, signal, or removal was induced; source-only.

Bluetooth HCI core allocation and I/O teardown pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): reread `bAllocCore()`/`bFreeCore()` and traced the first HCI-unit open, pending-request counter, CMD_FLUSH and request disposal (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2477-2600,2722-2779,3038-3084`; USB HCI device `rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/dev.c:214-278`; worker `bluetooth.class.c:838-886`). `btAllocVec()` obtains zeroed storage from the library’s `MEMF_CLEAR` pool, every request and buffer allocation is checked, and the partial-failure cleanup guards each request while freeing any allocated buffers; failed timer `OpenDevice` deletes and nulls its request before shared cleanup. The selected USB HCI worker’s CMD_FLUSH aborts and replies queued requests and aborts/waits active ACL transfers; normal teardown closes the device before `bFreeCore()` deletes its request objects. The 30-second forced counter reset only covers a noncompliant or nonreturning external HCI driver, and no selected in-tree case was established. No allocation failure or device close was run; source-only.


Bluetooth HCI worker startup/ready handshake pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced both `btSpawnSubTask()` branches into the `bHWTask()` startup and `btAddHardware()` wait (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:977-1025`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:82-109`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2780-2960,3070-3100`). New tasks begin with the standard free user-signal mask; the three manual message-port signal allocations therefore do not have a selected exhaustion trigger before use, consistent with the earlier OD1279 withdrawal. A successful bring-up publishes `bth_Task` before signaling the waiter. Failed open/bring-up paths reach common cleanup, clear `bth_Task`, and signal the same waiter before returning; the caller checks `bth_Task` and frees the unpublished hardware object on failure. The early bluetooth.library OpenLibrary failure would return without signaling, but the spawning call is executing through an already-open reference to this library, so a selected ordinary failure trigger was not established. No startup, allocation failure, or device open was induced; source-only.


Bluetooth HCI command-queue saturation and hardware-setting caller pass (OD3896 added, 2026-10-18): traced the fixed 16-slot pool exhaustion return from `bt_cmdq_submit()` through `bSubmitCmd()` and the synchronous `BTPRI_SETLOCALNAME`, `BTPRI_SETSCANMODE`, and `BTPRI_SETCOD` paths (`rom/bluetooth/stack/include/btcore/command_queue.h:23-25`; `stack/core/controller/command_queue.c:71-102`; `bluetooth/hwtask.c:126-136,2280-2337`; public packed attributes and setter `bluetooth.library.c:1264,1282-1283,1673-1694`). Each handler ignores a false submit result, updates local cached state first, and replies success; the selected public control wrapper waits only for that handler reply, not the HCI completion. Added OD3896. The trigger requires all command slots occupied, such as a burst while the controller has not returned command events. No command was submitted and no hardware was used. Source-only.


Bluetooth scan command-admission/state pass (OD3897 added, 2026-10-18): traced the public discovery control through its worker handler, Classic/LE command submissions, completion callbacks and duration timer (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:1379-1400`; `bluetooth/hwtask.c:126-136,565-581,1224-1276,1313-1474`; `rom/bluetooth/stack/core/controller/command_queue.c:71-102`). Foreground discovery marks itself pending/active and reports success regardless of queue-admission failure; with no callback for rejected commands it later emits the normal finish event without starting the radio operation. The background path similarly sets `hc_BgScanActive` after unchecked submissions, while its error callback only handles commands that entered the queue, so the periodic update will not retry a lost submission. Added OD3897, conditional on all 16 command slots being occupied. No scan or queue saturation was induced; source-only.


Bluetooth discovery ClearOld retirement/event pointer recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced the `BDSA_ClearOld` loop through `btFreeDevice()`/`bFreeDevice()` and `btSendEvent(BEHMB_REMDEVICE, bd, ...)` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:1333-1347`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:378-442`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:712-740`). The removed device allocation is intentionally retained on `bth_DeadDevices` (“cannot free this vector -- tasks might still call LockDevice”), so the event argument is not a freed allocation at this point; selected Preferences handles `BEHMB_REMDEVICE` by refreshing its lists without dereferencing `p1` (`rom/bluetooth/prefs/ActionClass.c:1180-1192`). This does not add a new stale-pointer finding. The separate raw borrowed device-pointer race between BTCtrl and `BDSA_ClearOld` is already tracked as OD3717. No device was removed and no event was sent; source-only.


Bluetooth remote-name channel retirement/completion pass (OD3898 added, 2026-10-18): followed public channel allocation and the selected BTCtrl `BTPR_REMOTENAME` caller through task queueing, Remote Name Request submission/completion, device removal in Preferences Forget, and the name-queue/discovery wait predicates (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:377-442,1052-1088,1183-1195`; `bluetooth/hwtask.c:637-640,1475-1583,2384-2395`; `rom/bluetooth/prefs/ActionClass.c:1103-1106`; `shellcommands/BTCtrl.c:256-275`). Client remote-name channels increment `bd_UseCnt` but are still removed from the active list; discovery `HCNameNode`s retain raw device pointers without a use reference. In either case completion lookup then fails and leaves the request pointer set, preventing queue advancement; a client channel is also left unreplied. Expanded OD3898 to cover both selected paths under the Forget overlap. No channel, removal, or controller response was run; source-only.


Bluetooth remote-name active-channel abort follow-up (OD3898 expanded, 2026-10-18): traced `btAbortChannel()` into the hardware-task abort message and `bHandleChannel()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:1198-1228`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2237-2262`). A queued name channel is unlinked and replied immediately; an active channel is detached from `hc_NameReqChannel` and replied aborted while its `hc_NameReqDev` remains reserved until the controller response arrives. With the device still active, `bNameReqComplete()` later clears that reservation and advances the name queue, so ordinary active-request abort does not create a second independent stall. If the device was already retired, the response follows OD3898’s active-list-miss branch and the reservation remains stuck. No channel, abort, or controller event was run; source-only.


Bluetooth discovery-name stop and worker teardown follow-up (OD3898 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-18): traced `bStopDiscovery()` queue-node cleanup and its active-request wait, plus shutdown reply/flush order and `bFreeCore()` queue-node reclamation (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:1439-1470,2570-2600,3020-3105`). Stopping discovery removes all not-yet-submitted `HCNameNode`s, resets its count and waits for an active request to complete before emitting discovery-finished; normal shutdown replies queued client name channels and the active client channel before the controller flush, then frees remaining internal name nodes. These paths do not add a distinct defect when the device remains active. If it was retired first, the active-list lookup still misses the response and OD3898 applies. No discovery, abort, or shutdown was run; source-only.


Bluetooth LE reconnect-list command completion audit (OD3899 added, 2026-10-18): traced `bLEListsSync()` through resolving-list/accept-list clear/add steps, command completion status, final count and auto-connect selection (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:902-1048,1148-1215`; `rom/bluetooth/stack/core/controller/command_queue.c:172-230`). The index advances before each add; `bListsStepCB()` logs but continues after a failed add. Synchronization is marked clean before commands run, and the final accept-list count uses attempted entries, so a failed entry is omitted without retry and the controller auto-connect path may be armed with no actually installed candidates. Added OD3899. No command, queue timeout, or controller was exercised; source-only.


Bluetooth LE privacy-resolution failure fallback pass (OD3900 added, 2026-10-18): traced capability selection through `LE Set Address Resolution Enable` completion, list-sync completion, reconnect strategy selection and the host background-scan gate (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:783-821,1018-1036,1125-1235`). The failed enable only updates `hc_ResolvingOn` and logs a host-resolution fallback; it does not change `bth_LEReconnect`. In resolving mode, auto-connect still arms the controller accept-list procedure, and `bBgScanUpdate()` will not start host scanning. Added OD3900, conditional on an eligible peer using a resolvable private address. No controller command or connection was exercised; source-only.


Bluetooth LE auto-connect cancel queue-admission pass (OD3901 added, 2026-10-18): traced `bAutoConnDisarm()` into queue admission, immediate failure handling and `bAutoConnDone()` against deferred discovery and pending connection callers (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:126-136,1091-1117,1383-1389`; `rom/bluetooth/stack/core/controller/command_queue.c:71-102`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:1160-1172`). On no command slot, the cancel is not sent but the armed/cancel flags are cleared and dependent radio work is resumed without an HCI completion. Added OD3901, conditional on full command queue and the controller procedure remaining active. No command, scan, connection, or queue saturation was exercised; source-only.

Bluetooth LE successful-connection allocation-failure pass (OD3902 added, 2026-10-18): traced both LE Connection Complete subevents, known-device lookup, connection-record allocation, controller-managed auto-connect state and ACL-handle dispatch (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:3289-3359,3427-3430`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:870-889`). A successful event for a known peer with no preallocated LE connection object returns immediately if `btAllocVec` fails, without disconnecting or retaining the new handle; the auto-connect completion path also remains marked armed. The incoming/auto-connect paths do not require that a connection object exist beforehand. Added OD3902. No allocation failure, event or controller was induced; source-only.

Bluetooth connection timeout iterator candidate restored (OD3903, 2026-10-18): rechecked the saved `next` pointer in `bConnTick()`, timeout removal, `bStartNextConnect()` ordering and failed command submission (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:1014-1128,1208-1220,3965-3994`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:127-137`; `rom/bluetooth/stack/include/btcore/command_queue.h:23-25,81-82`). When the timed-out connection's immediate successor is the next queued attempt, and all 16 HCI command slots are in use, the scheduler's failed submission calls `bConnDown()` on the cached successor; the tick loop then resumes through the freed node. Restored the detailed finding and index as OD3903 because earlier coverage notes retained this candidate while those deliverables did not. No timeout or queue saturation was run; source-only.

Bluetooth service-refresh endpoint callback lifetime candidate restored (OD3904, 2026-10-18): traced the selected public `btEnumerateServices()` API through `BTPRI_ENUMSERVICES`, successful SDP/GATT enumeration and `bClearServices()`; checked the Preferences Rescan caller and BTCtrl services option (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:1551-1563`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:1705-1723,1815-1825,3514-3528`; `rom/bluetooth/prefs/DevWinClass.c:275-281`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/shellcommands/BTCtrl.c:330-338`). `bClearServices()` closes then frees every non-closed endpoint. For an open dynamic L2CAP channel, the manager retains `bEndpointEvent` and its `BtHWEndpoint *` user data while waiting for peer response/timeout (`hwconn.c:701-719,736-753`; `stack/protocols/l2cap/channel_manager.c:134-158,701-715`); its later CLOSED callback dereferences the freed endpoint (`hwconn.c:202-219,285-330`). NVMe SGL page-size and initial-capacity arithmetic cross-check (2026-10-18; no new OD): traced the controller CAP.MPSMIN/MPSMAX clamp into `dev->pageshift`/`pagesize` and the sole `nvme_initsgl()` caller (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:302-315`; `nvme_io.c:72-118`; `nvme_sgl.c:61-100`). Both capability encodings have a 4-KiB base, and the clamp selects a shift no lower than the controller's MPSMIN and no higher than MPSMAX while bounding it by host `PAGESHIFT`, so the selected initialized controller does not pass a zero page size to the division. The selected caller rejects zero lengths, sector misalignment and lengths above `au_MaxTransfer`; namespace setup bounds that transfer by 65,536 LBAs and `ULONG_MAX` (`nvme_busclass.c:579-591`). The initial segment-count addition can wrap for near-`ULONG_MAX` lengths, but subsequent descriptors grow the SGL array incrementally, and checked transfer bounds plus selected cache hooks do not establish a resulting SGL overwrite. Existing external cache-hook contracts and physical/PCI DMA-window behavior remain open. No device or transfer was used; source-only.

## PCI IRQ pin and routing-table field contract recheck (2026-10-18)

Rechecked `AssignIRQ` in `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c` against PCI-device initialization and the selected PC ACPI routing-table producer. `aHidd_PCIDevice_IRQLine` is populated from `PCICS_INT_PIN`, while the separate `aHidd_PCIDevice_INTLine` is populated from `PCICS_INT_LINE` (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:644-650`). The PC ACPI parser stores `_PRT`'s zero-based `Pin` plus one in `re_IRQPin` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:278-280`), and `AssignIRQ` correctly matches that pin, then writes the selected GSI to `INTLine` (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:221-255`). The similarly named fields therefore do not establish a swapped line/pin bug. The parser currently zero-initializes `re_PCISegNum` and neither consumer uses it; segment behavior remains unverified for multi-segment PCI systems, with no such selected target path established here. No new finding promoted. Source-only; no PCI hardware or routing table was used.

## PCIPC MSI-X versus legacy MSI minimum-count branch recheck (2026-10-18)

Compared the two `ObtainVectors` count-selection branches in `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_deviceclass.c`. MSI-X normalizes a requested zero minimum to one before its `vectcnt >= vectmin` loop (`:388-430`), so the legacy MSI zero-minimum unsigned countdown condition in OD2993 does not apply to the MSI-X branch. MSI-X still lowers a nonzero minimum above its table capacity to the capacity and can return success with fewer vectors than requested (OD2987, `:423-430,431-482`). The five selected direct HIDD callers request minimum one; the distinct trigger is a public client requesting more vectors than the device table supports. No new finding promoted. Source-only; no vector request was issued.

## Review body-read coverage estimate (2026-10-18)

Ran `cloc` over unique existing `.c`, `.h`, C++ and assembly paths named in the Graphics/Desktop, Exec/Kernel and Other Drivers coverage tables. To avoid treating targeted slices as full file reviews, counted a path's code lines as body-reviewed only when at least one ledger row explicitly says `full`, `entire` or `complete` file/source/body read (optionally with a line count); any path with no such wording is counted as pending for this proxy. Results: Graphics/Desktop 114,071 / 268,824 code lines (42.4%); Exec/Kernel 61,639 / 167,798 (36.7%); Other Drivers 134,423 / 491,604 (27.3%). Across the deduplicated union: 307,669 / 911,441 lines (33.8%) across 3,954 existing paths; 31 table paths did not exist at the recorded relative path and were excluded. These are strict source-body-read estimates from tracked paths, not audit-completion percentages: the inventory includes conditional/unselected and related paths, does not prove current target selection, and gives no credit for caller/platform/configuration/error/ownership/concurrency/lifecycle closure. The report and ledger rows remain authoritative for those open checks. Recalculate after further full-file reviews; do not use this estimate as a completion claim or ETA by itself.

## USB mass-storage BeginIO versus hot-unbind drain review (OD3905, 2026-10-18)

Audited the previously partial `devBeginIO`/`devAbortIO` path against the per-LUN worker and Poseidon release callback (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/dev.c:197-360`; `massstorage.class.c:1311-1425,1861-1897,698-740`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6588-6613`). The per-LUN unit port is zero-cleared with the unit allocation and its zero spinlock state is the documented `SPINLOCK_UNLOCKED`; that is not a separate missing-init finding. However, admission is not synchronized: `devBeginIO` checks `ncm_DenyRequests` before `PutMsg`, while release sets it and wakes the worker, whose `nFreeMS` changes the port to `PA_IGNORE` and drains only once. A sender preempted after observing FALSE can resume after the worker has drained and exited, leaving a queued request with no consumer/reply. This is OD3905, conditional on an I/O submission overlapping hot-unbind. Poseidon reaches this callback through `psdHubReleaseIfBinding`; the selected package manifests include this USB class on ARM Raspberry Pi, AArch64 Raspberry Pi and RISC-V OpenSBI. `SendIO` invokes BeginIO without a surrounding Forbid (`rom/exec/sendio.c:48-58`), and Exec explicitly limits Forbid to the local processor on SMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-63`); no in-flight I/O or unbind was run. The unused `ncm_XFerPending`/`ncm_XFerQueue` fields in `devAbortIO` were not promoted separately because AbortIO documents that cancellation may fail and requires the caller to WaitIO (`rom/exec/abortio.c:24-35`).

## USB HID report item bounds pass (OD3906, 2026-10-18)

Reviewed the item loop and short/long item decoding in `nParseReport` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2602-2690`) and traced its selected `nReadReports` caller. The loop tests only that an item prefix byte remains; long items read their next two header bytes and skip the encoded payload without checking the end pointer, while short items read 1/2/4 payload bytes based only on the prefix size. The caller allocates `nhr_ReportBuf` to the HID descriptor's advertised report length and invokes the parser after a successful fetch (`:2216-2232`), so an incomplete final item can read outside that exact allocation during binding. Added OD3906, conditional on a malformed report descriptor; no USB device or descriptor was used. This is a focused boundary slice, not a complete `nParseReport` body review; its semantic branches, action-family callers, and teardown paths remain open.


## USB HID global stack POP follow-up (OD3907, 2026-10-18)

Traced the parser's Global PUSH/POP handling against Exec list initialization and the selected `nReadReports()` caller (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2216-2232,2617-2623,3207-3239`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:85-94`). `NewList()` sets `lh_Tail` to NULL; PUSH links the saved state, but POP reads `lh_Tail` and dereferences it, so any descriptor containing a valid POP faults during report parsing. Added OD3907. The HID parser remains a focused review: the complete parser body and broader binding/lifecycle callers have not been closed, and no device or descriptor was used.


## USB HID descriptor framing follow-up (OD3908, 2026-10-18)

Reviewed `nReadReports()` descriptor acquisition, buffer sizing, short-transfer handling, field accesses, and report-descriptor entry loop (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2070-2232`; `compiler/include/devices/usb_hid.h:45-55`). After allocating `nch_HidDesc` to `bLength`, the code only logs when `actlen < 6` and continues; it also only logs a descriptor-count/length mismatch and still iterates `bNumDescriptors`. This permits field and entry reads beyond the copied allocation for truncated or internally inconsistent HID descriptors. Added OD3908. This is a caller/framing slice; remaining `nReadReports()` result handling, broader binding callers and teardown remain open. No device or transfer was used.


## USB HID parse-error dump bounds pass (OD3909, 2026-10-18)

Traced the exact-size report buffer from `nReadReports()` into `nParseReport()` error branches and `nDebugReport()`/`nDebugMem()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2216-2232,2543-2571,2587-2597,2798-2801,2843-2846,3103-3106,3236-3239,3246-3249,3391-3404`). `nDebugMem()` formats only the remaining bytes in its final row but unconditionally evaluates 16 `rptr[]` arguments, producing a read past the allocation for non-16-byte lengths. Added OD3909. This is a focused error-path slice; broader HID action and lifecycle reviews remain open. No device or descriptor was used.


## USB HID short input-report length check (OD3910, 2026-10-18)

Traced the reused interrupt receive buffer from `psdSendPipe()` through completion actual-length retrieval, report-ID selection and each `nProcessItem()` call (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:892-945,2264-2305,1262-1266,4833-4895`). The path accepts `UHIOERR_RUNTPACKET` and any nonzero `buflen`, does not compare it against the selected report's required input size, and the item decoder has no buffer-length argument. The buffer is reused without clearing between submissions, so absent tail bytes can retain prior input values. Added OD3910, conditional on a short report after nonzero values in omitted fields; no device or transfer was used. The HID input and broader lifecycle audit remains open.


## USB HID zero-count array decode recheck (OD3911, 2026-10-18)

Traced `ReportCount` initialization and parser acceptance into array item construction, item-map publication and the live interrupt input path (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2836-2848,2918-2942,3024-3027,933-945,4974-5003`). The parser explicitly does not reject zero count; for a non-variable Input item with usage and nonempty range it links the item and requests a zero-byte payload buffer. `psdAllocVec(0)` still requests header/alignment bytes and returns a pointer if `AllocPooled` succeeds (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:331-368`), so the item can survive allocation checks. The decoder casts zero to `UWORD` and enters a do/while that decrements it, yielding 65,536 writes. Added OD3911, conditional on the descriptor item reaching live input processing and allocations succeeding; no device or input was used.

## PC i8042 controller-task parent publication recheck (OD2321, 2026-10-18)

Rechecked the `NewCreateTask` caller and early worker failures against task-tag semantics (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:139-177,311-325`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:65,140-142`). The constructor passes its task via `TASKTAG_USERDATA`, which initializes the child task's `tc_UserData`; it does not initialize `data->CtrlTask`. The worker only assigns `data->CtrlTask = FindTask(0)` after message-port creation, I/O-request allocation and `OpenDevice("timer.device")`. Each earlier failure dereferences `data->CtrlTask->tc_UserData` before signaling, corroborating OD2321 and the constructor's wait. No allocation failure or device open was induced.

USB HID report-parser full-body and signed-value pass (OD3912 added, 2026-10-18): read `nParseReport()` from initialization through cleanup (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2602-3448`), then traced the selected `nReadReports()` binding caller, interrupt input loop, and scalar decoding (`:2216-2232,917-945,4833-4895`). The signed two-byte descriptor-value and aligned input-value paths shift a negative `BYTE`; the four-byte paths use sign-bit shifts whose conversion is implementation-defined, while the independent negative signed shifts remain undefined; generic signed bit-field extraction starts from -1 and left-shifts it. Added OD3912 for compiler-dependent decoding of valid signed bounds/input values. The Designator Maximum branch writes `designmin` rather than `designmax` (`:3325-3335`), but a direct use census found `nhi_DesignIndex` is stored only and never consumed elsewhere in this class, so no current behavior defect is established. Full `nProcessItem` action handling, remaining class callers/action families, and lifecycle are still open; no descriptor or device was used. Source-only.

USB HID `nProcessItem` array and state-initialization pass (2026-10-18; no new OD): read the full decoder (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:4833-5128`) and traced its live interrupt caller, the disabled polling branch, and Wacom's separate synthetic-report caller (`:818-945,1801-1815`). The apparent uninitialized `nhi_OldValue`/`nhi_OldBuffer` issue is not supported: `nhi` and its array buffer are allocated through `psdAllocVec`, whose Poseidon pool is created with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:124-125,329-349`). The array decoder's current/old buffer lengths and `UWORD` loop are separately covered by OD3911 for zero count; no second defect was established in that branch. The remaining `nDoAction` behavior and broader class/action/lifecycle coverage stay open. No device or report was used. Source-only.

USB HID report-width decoder bound pass (OD3913 added, 2026-10-18): traced `ReportSize` from global-item parsing through `nhi_Size`, report-length/buffer sizing, item-map publication and the selected nonzero interrupt-input caller (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2836-2841,2895,3030,2264-2317,891-945`). USB HID wheel-delta action and default-mapping pass (OD3914 added, 2026-10-18): traced the full `HUA_WHEEL` branch to `nSendRawKey` event emission and checked the user wheel modes plus default usage mapping (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:3954-3959,5854-5928`; `hid.gui.c:76-78,1028-1047`). SD-card CMD_FLUSH shared-port candidate recheck (2026-10-18; no new finding): inspected the full `sdcard_device.c` path and the selected bus/slot setup. `cmd_Flush` drains the bus message port and replies every queued request `IOERR_ABORTED` (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_device.c:272-286`), which would be cross-unit cancellation if a bus exposed multiple units. The selected SDHCI and SDHOST backends each configure one SD-card slot per bus (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdcard/sdcard_bcm2708init.c:286-292`; `sdcard_sdhost_init.c:292-298`); `BeginIO` queues all commands because `isSlow` returns TRUE, and `BusTask` serially removes and dispatches requests (`sdcard_device.c:631-671`; `sdcard_bus.c:1767-1791`). Thus the queue drain does not establish a sibling-unit failure on selected configurations, and it cannot race the currently dispatched request on the same bus task. Existing OD3302 already covers the distinct hotplug-created out-of-bounds unit-table entry. No CMD_FLUSH was issued. Source-only.

## USB Audio alternate-interface selection follow-up (2026-10-18; no additional finding)

Read `nSelectAudioMode()` end to end (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3133-3262`) and traced both primary and duplex-sibling calls from `subLibAllocAudio()` (`:3328-3329,3501-3503`). It selects the alternate interface, obtains the matching isochronous endpoint and its interval/max-packet attributes, computes a bandwidth-derived maximum, sends optional sample-frequency and pitch controls, then allocates the direction-specific RTIso hooks. A missing endpoint or RTIso allocation returns failure to the caller's cleanup path; USB control-transfer failures only warn, as already covered by OD3208. The max-frequency calculation divides by `nam_FrameSize * nam_Interval`; frame size is derived from parsed channel and subframe-size fields (`:1212`), while interval comes from the selected endpoint descriptor (`:3163-3166`). This source pass did not establish a supported zero value or other concrete descriptor route that reaches a divide-by-zero, so no finding is added. The selected RTIso allocation path and cleanup ownership were checked against OD3517 and the allocation rollback recheck at `:3263-3670`. Broader descriptor validity guarantees, controller interval interpretation, and callback/device timing remain open; no device or transfer was used. Source-only.


## USB Audio binding and teardown lifecycle follow-up (2026-10-18; existing findings rechecked)

Read `nVerifyAudioStreamDevice()`, `usbAttemptInterfaceBinding()`, `usbForceInterfaceBinding()`, and `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:166-390`) against the selected Poseidon class-scan/release entry points. The verifier's AudioControl header version and `bInCollection` reads precede descriptor-extent validation; these remain OD3168/OD3171, and no separate acceptance-path defect was established. Forced binding first chooses a free unit number, then checks for a matching device/interface record, publishes new records before worker startup, and waits on the task-ready signal. Publication-before-startup failure remains OD3209; free-unit selection/publication across independent scans remains OD3230. The allocation-failure `Permit()` without a matching local `Forbid()` remains OD3229, with the selected Poseidon caller's task nesting and consequence already documented there. Release removes the record before signaling and waiting for the worker to clear `nch_Task`; the reviewed ordering did not establish a separate lifetime defect beyond those findings and the selected RTIso/device-removal coverage in OD3177/OD3206. Descriptor backing lifetime, external concurrent forced-binding clients, and actual worker scheduling remain unverified. No interface or device was used. Source-only.


## Deneb DMA interrupt-to-worker handoff and bounds follow-up (2026-10-18; no additional finding)

Re-read the DMA setup and state transitions in `uhwLevel6Int()`, `uhwDMATask()`, and `uhwHandleDMAInt()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4240-4330,4996-5260,5270-5403`), including ATL completion updates at `:2110-2418`. Hardware DMA completion is acknowledged in the level-6 handler and queued to the per-unit task; the task calls the common completion routine only while `hu_DMAPTD` is non-NULL. The NODMA build instead signals that same task when software copies are ready. One DMA is active per unit (`:4250-4255`), so the single-bit signal does not by itself demonstrate lost completion coalescing in the reviewed path. Large IN transfers select DMA only for longword-aligned request length and data address; OUT requires aligned address and rounds each DMA copy to a longword, matching OD3578/OD3585's caller-buffer tail concern (`:4250-4264,4314-4321`). IN `iouh_Actual` is increased from the PTD's completed transfer count before the DMA state machine decides whether to continue or retire the PTD (`:2127-2141`); the DMA completion handler's rounded actual-minus-offset calculation therefore had no supported underflow path in the traced selected flow. Existing abort/cache ordering findings OD3584 and OD3704 remain applicable. This pass did not verify controller interrupt timing, DMA cache guarantees, or abort interleavings during the worker handoff; no transfer or device was run. Source-only.

The generic PC `CPUtoPCI` returns identity for a direct bus (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:134-144`), and x86 `CachePreDMA` is coherent identity (`rom/exec/cachepredma.c:45-77`); the BCM2712 backend returns an inbound-window PCI address or its failure sentinel (`driverclass.c:278-294`); the RISC-V PCIDT backend translates addresses inside its configured remap VA window and otherwise returns identity (`pcidt_driverclass.c:867-878`), while its selected Zicbom hook performs cache maintenance and returns the same address (`cpu_init.c:104-129`). PCI xHCI DMA helper caller recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): followed `xhciQueuePayloadTRBs()` through `xhciPrepareDMABuffer()` into `xhciQueueData_IO()` and the ring writer (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_schedule.c:47-99,327-367`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:915-960,1065-1128`). The helper's returned pointer and current `dmalen` are passed directly to the TRB builder, which emits one or more sequential TRBs covering exactly that length; successful setup records the bounce allocation and direction, while queue failure releases the bounce buffer. Reconciled selected Exec hooks: generic x86 identity, AArch64 native identity translator, and RISC-V Zicbom identity/unchanged-length; no selected hook shortens the length in this checkout. Thus the generic API's possible translated address/shortened extent is not a demonstrated defect for these checked target paths. External DMA mappings, caller buffer ownership/cache-line sharing, and completion/teardown remain open under the existing coverage rows. No USB transfer or device was used; source-only.

Realtek8180 `CreateUnit`/`DeleteUnit` staged-allocation and USB caller recheck (OD3260/OD3269 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): reconciled the unit allocation stages, failure cleanup, task start and selected `CreateUSBUnit`/`DeleteUSBUnitInternal` callers (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/unit.c:105-417`; `usb.c:116-133,242-290,382-410`; `task.h:27-59`). The only maintained `CreateUnit` caller passes the static `unit_tags` containing all ten required hooks; the partial-missing-hook path would reach `DeleteUnit` with a NULL `FreeDMAMem`, but no selected caller supplies that malformed set, so it is not promoted. Once the hook table validates, partially allocated DMA entries are safe to release through the selected `FreeDMAMemHook` -> `FreeVec`, whose public implementation explicitly accepts NULL (`rom/exec/freevec.c:27-28,47-49`). Reconfirmed OD3260: after stack allocation and assignment to `tc_SPLower`, failed `AddUnitTask` leaves `UNITF_TASKADDED` clear, so `DeleteUnit` frees the task structure but skips the stack release (`unit.c:288-303,354-364`). Reconfirmed OD3269: `UnitTask` unconditionally calls `unit->removal_function` on the signaled removal path (`:2694-2699`), while a repository-wide search finds no assignment to that callback; USB `ReleaseBindingHook` can signal the task after unit publication (`usb.c:670-689`). The `card_inserted_signal` path likewise has no producer in this driver, so it is not a selected independent trigger. `InitialiseAdapter` failure sets `UNITF_HAVEADAPTER` before its result is tested; the ensuing cleanup calls `DeinitialiseAdapter`, whose selected body only writes the LED/GPIO off values (`unit.c:239-245,402-415`), and no distinct harmful cleanup consequence was established. No allocation failure, task, USB device, or removal was exercised; source-only.

AR5416 reset-result caller cross-check (2026-10-18; no new finding): confirmed the full reset body's failure paths (`hal/ar5416/ar5416_reset.c:117-190,237-257,275-280,359-360,407-411`) set `HAL_STATUS` and return `AH_FALSE`; the successful path returns `AH_TRUE`. The selected function is installed by `ar5416_attach.c:84` and called from `unit.c:788`, where `ConfigureAdapter()` discards both the boolean and status and proceeds to transmit-power/receive setup, as captured by OD3292. This is the same result-handling defect already recorded, not a new reset-specific candidate. The `(HAL_CHANNEL_INTERNAL *)chan` cast at `ar5416_reset.c:207` remains valid for the shared leading channel fields per `ah_internal.h:126-129`; no cast finding. Calibration/register semantics and broader caller/platform coverage remain open. Source-only.

AR5416 target-power candidate recheck (OD3875 retained, 2026-10-18): verified `fbin2freq(AR5416_BCHAN_UNUSED, ...)` returns the sentinel value 255 unchanged (`hal/ah_eeprom_v14.c:232-241`). Normal channel frequencies exceed 255, so the initial comparison at `ar5416_reset.c:1713/1773` is false for an empty table; the scan exits with `i == 0`, and the fallback reads `powInfo[i - 1]` at `:1728/1788`. V14 parser acceptance and selected power-table call paths were already traced in OD3875. Candidate remains valid and conditional on an EEPROM table with no populated piers. No EEPROM or hardware was used. Source-only.

AR9280 per-chain periodic calibration cross-check (OD3944 added, 2026-10-18): traced `ah_setAntennaSwitch` installation and fixed-B mask assignment through reset's calibration-chain register, percal mask replacement/counting, and IQ/ADC-gain/ADC-DC post-processing. For RX mask `0x2`, the framework passes `numChains == 1`, while all three post-processors loop over index 0 and access chain-0 sample/register slots. The selected unit calls `ah_perCalibration()` (`unit.c:796`) but repository search found no caller of `ah_setAntennaSwitch`; finding is conditional on an external client selecting fixed B. No hardware or calibration was run. Source-only.

AR5416 ADC DC signed-arithmetic pass (OD3945 added, 2026-10-18): traced signed `HAL_CAL_SAMPLE.s` collection into the post-processor's `uint32_t` I temporaries and subtraction, multiplication, division, mask and register write. AR9280 uses one periodic sample with `PER_MIN_LOG_COUNT == 2`, yielding divisor 128; Q operands are signed. A negative I even-minus-odd delta not divisible by 64 yields a 9-bit correction one count more negative than signed truncation would; expected hardware rounding is not documented, so functional confidence is medium. Checked the callback installation and selected unit periodic-calibration call. No hardware or calibration was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II signal-table/release recheck (OD3627-OD3629 reconciled, 2026-10-18): re-read selected `driver_sana2.c` init/deinit and `eloop_amiga.c` registration/wait paths. Confirmed OD3629: failed `realloc()` returns -1, caller ignores it, and the port bit is omitted from `eloop_run()`'s mask; async requests can be queued while the supplicant reports a valid driver. Confirmed OD3628: the separately allocated event request is waited but not freed. OD3627 remains conditional: no unregister exists and dynamic removal frees the callback context, but the checked-in config has `CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE` disabled and no live-removal caller; normal global teardown follows `eloop_run()` and is not itself a stale-callback window. The remaining trigger requires an external live-removal caller and later reuse of that signal bit. No allocation or interface lifecycle was run. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II request/scan teardown recheck (OD3694/OD3695 refined, 2026-10-18): confirmed the request-overlap trigger through the selected hard-MAC CONNECT event: the separate `S2_ONEVENT` callback dispatches `EVENT_ASSOC`, the hard-MAC supplicant handler queries BSSID, and `get_bssid()` rewrites the same base request still submitted for `S2_GETNETWORKS` (`driver_sana2.c:133-153,159-210,802-829,872-875`; `events.c:1135-1145`). Prism2 stores that IORequest pointer in its scan queue (`prism2/request.c:1631-1648`); the callback later switches on its current command, so a query completion can be misclassified and the scan result may never be delivered. For OD3695, confirmed shutdown cleanup cancels only the scan timer, not the active device request; SANA-II provides no `cancel_scan` op. Deinit aborts/waits for the base request but never deletes the pool; key clearing may overwrite the request field holding its handle. Normal shutdown with an outstanding scan is sufficient; external live removal remains another trigger. No request, scan, or interface was exercised. Source-only.


WirelessManager SANA-II association SSID ownership recheck (OD3946 added, 2026-10-18): traced the temporary SSID allocation through `CloneTagItems`, synchronous `S2_SETOPTIONS`, tag-list release, and the selected `.associate` callback caller. The cloned tags are freed but the `os_zalloc(MAX_SSID_LEN + 1)` buffer is not; each successful buffer allocation is leaked on both request success and failure paths. This is distinct from OD3626's suppressed callback errors. No association or allocation was run; source-only.

USB Audio Type I frame-size validation pass (OD3947 added, 2026-10-18): traced `bSubframeSize` from the public descriptor layout (`compiler/include/devices/usb_audio.h:385-395`) through mode classification, `nam_FrameSize` assignment, AHI mode registration and `nSelectAudioMode()` rate-limit calculation (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1140-1217,1929-1986,2037-2046,3134-3166`). The parser accepts an otherwise-supported channel/bit-depth tuple with a zero subframe size, producing zero frame size; later mode allocation divides by `nam_FrameSize * nam_Interval`. Added OD3947 for zero-size division by zero and the one-byte/16-bit mismatch that selects the 8-bit converter; both are separate from OD3171 descriptor extent and OD3172 empty-rate findings. No device or allocation was used; source-only.

USB Audio class-config reload and GUI task exit follow-up (OD3200 rechecked; no new finding, 2026-10-18): read `nLoadClassConfig()`, `nOpenCfgWindow()`, GUI startup, save/reload event dispatch, and `nGUITaskCleanup()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2130-2157,2160-2182,2185-2376,2370-2394`) against all three in-file reload callers (`:106,325,496`) and Poseidon's selected `psdSpawnSubTask()` paths (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1434-1509`). The reload helper returns FALSE on both success and failure, but all callers ignore it; no caller-visible return-value defect was established. Startup library references and the GUI task's library open count are unwound on each checked failure/exit path. The early child-exit-before-parent-publication race remains OD3200; the paired `Forbid()` in cleanup is not a new finding because the child terminates immediately after cleanup, and Exec's current-task `RemTask()` exit path resets the task-disable nesting before rescheduling (`rom/exec/remtask.c:149-160`). GUI creation, library-open failures and task schedules were not induced. Source-only.

USB HID Wacom zero-length report follow-up (OD3921 expanded, 2026-10-18): rechecked the interrupt completion order against the full Wacom parser and the default tablet action path (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:899-919,1599-1817,4348-4378,4940-4949,991`). The worker calls `nParseWacom()` before the `buflen > 0` generic-parser guard and reuses `nch_EPInBuf`; an empty transfer after a recognized Intuos-family packet leaves the old report ID in byte zero. The Intuos-family branch can return TRUE from this stale ID, process the stale synthetic report, and bypass the documented ZLP-ignore path. `HUA_ALWAYS` tablet mappings run even for unchanged values, and the worker flushes after each completion, so repeated stale actions are a supported consequence. Expanded OD3921 and the AROS.md summary; this is the same unchecked Wacom packet-length boundary, not a separate finding. No device, packet, or event was used; source-only.
USB HID SET_REPORT failure/retry trace (OD3948 added, 2026-10-18): followed `HUA_OUTPUT`/`HUA_FEATURE` state mutation into the report touched flags and `nFlushEvents()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6068-6137,6365-6427`), checked the synchronous pipe error contract (`rom/usb/docs/poseidon.doc:1105-1145`), and verified that unchanged input values do not normally invoke actions again (`hid.class.c:4940-4949`). Confirmed output actions are reachable from built-in tablet LED mappings (`:4120-4150`) and output/feature actions are configured in the HID Control GUI (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:1111-1160,2224-2260`). Added OD3948: after a failed transfer the action's updated value remains, but its touched flag is cleared, so the report is not retried absent a later action that touches it. Separate USB HID implementation from Bluetooth finding OD3473. No device, report, or transfer was used; source-only.

USB Audio unit-graph traversal and volume-resolution recheck (OD3164/OD3165 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): read `nFindAudioUnit`, `nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, `nFlowDown`, `nFlowDownToUSBSink`, `nFlowUpToUSBSource`, `nFlowUp`, `nFindLogVolume`, and the Stage 2–5 traversal in `nExamineAudioUnits` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:782-919,1312-1367,1371-1620`). Descriptor source links are capped at eight edges per node, but self-links and cycles remain accepted; all four recursive flow walkers still lack an in-progress/visited mark, confirming OD3165. Missing source IDs still leave required input slots NULL and the Stage 4 `nFlowUp` output/feature-unit paths dereference slot zero, confirming OD3164. The `nFindLogVolume` logarithmic conversion body is entirely commented out and the live code exposes a normalized fixed range; device-specific min/max dB values remain used by the control-transfer conversion path, so this helper alone does not establish a separate defect. The class remains partial; no descriptor, USB device, or mode was used. Source-only.

USB Audio Feature Unit decoding and duplex-pair follow-up (OD3170/OD3191 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): re-read AudioControl Stage 5 Feature Unit handling and the full recording/playback sibling-matching loops (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1673-1809,1840-1923`). The control matrix advances `featptr` for every channel and `bControlSize` byte without checking descriptor extent, confirming OD3170. The value is accumulated in UWORD, but the recognized feature flags occupy bits 0-9 (`compiler/include/devices/usb_audio.h:157-176`); this pass did not establish a separate behavior defect from wider control elements. Reconfirmed OD3191: both pairing passes compare frequency count, min/max and only `nam_FreqArray[0]`, while the first pass additionally checks channels/resolution/frame size; interior discrete rate lists can differ. The following `nAddAudioModes()` pass publishes playback modes and their sibling-linked input capabilities. No descriptor, device or AHI stream was used; the remaining Audio class source, external mode callers, descriptor validity guarantees and runtime endpoint behavior remain open. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI mode-name allocation/caller trace (OD3949 added, 2026-10-18): traced `nAddAudioModes()` through Poseidon's formatter, AHI database insertion, `AHI_GetAudioAttrs()` and the selected AHI requester (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1942-1987`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1033-1049`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:384-430`; `modeinfo.c:452-459`; `requester.c:1337-1340`). The formatted-name allocation can return NULL; AHI skips its string copy but still inserts the tag with NULL data, and later `stccpy()` dereferences that source for the requester's normal 80-byte name query. Added OD3949 to the detailed report and index. No allocation failure or mode query was induced. USB Audio's other method/caller paths and platform/runtime behavior remain open; source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth failed-start unit ownership recheck (OD3950 added, 2026-10-18): traced the device opener's ready wait and failure free (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_device.c:54-76`) through worker prerequisite setup, unconditional early ready signal, and partial-resource cleanup (`vbthci_unit.c:550-571,628-653`). If event-reply/timer port or timer request creation fails, or timer.device cannot be opened, `vu_Task` stays NULL; the opener can wake and `FreeVec(unit)` while the worker is still cleaning up through the same structure. Added OD3950 for this conditional startup use-after-free. The selected module manifest is optional (`vbthci/mmakefile.src:3-13`). Existing CloseUnit waits for task termination after signaling shutdown; this does not protect the distinct failed-start path. No resource failure or device open was induced; source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth device-request/API caller matrix follow-up (2026-10-18; no additional OD): compared `BTCMD_*` definitions (`compiler/include/devices/bluetoothhci.h:46-55`) with `vbthci_QueueRequest()`/`vbt_HandleRequest()` (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:425-530`) and the selected Bluetooth hardware task. The selected stack sends QUERYDEVICE, ADDMSGPORT/REMMSGPORT, WRITEHCI, READACL, WRITEACL, and shutdown CMD_FLUSH (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2462-2471,2600-2611,2658-2674,2856-2866,3044-3057`); each has a corresponding implementation and the queued commands are replied by the worker. READEVENT and SCO setup/read/write are declared but have no in-tree callsites and fall through to IOERR_NOCMD; this simulator uses the event-message port and ACL transport, so no selected caller-visible regression is established. QUERYDEVICE trusts its caller's TAG_END-terminated tag list and output pointers, but the selected caller supplies a complete local array; malformed external tag lists remain an API precondition. Full HCI command-payload validation and external clients remain open. No I/O request or event was sent; source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth peer pairing-command minimum-length pass (OD3951 added, 2026-10-18): traced `BTCMD_WRITEHCI`'s actual buffer extent through `vbt_HandleCommand()`'s parameter clamp (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:233-249,495-497`) into all pairing-reply cases in `vbtp_HandleCommand()` (`vbthci_peer.c:859-975`). Five cases copy and/or compare six address bytes without checking that many parameters exist, so a direct caller with a correspondingly short request buffer can trigger a bounded-buffer overread. Added OD3951 with the malformed direct-request trigger; the selected `bSendCommand()` transport copies and reports the exact packet length (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:77-94`), and no in-tree truncated pairing packet was found. The finding remains limited to external/direct `BTCMD_WRITEHCI` clients; no device or command was used. Source-only.

Bluetooth GATT below-default MTU long-read trace (OD3952 added, 2026-10-18): compared the two-byte response parser and client negotiation/continuation path (`stack/protocols/att/att.c:34-44`; `stack/protocols/gatt/gatt_client.c:60-80,244-278`) with ATT default/request constants (`stack/include/btcore/att.h:46`; `gatt_client.h:45-47`) and the selected HOGP report-map read callback (`stack/profiles/hogp/hogp_client.c:230-247`). The Core Specification says a below-default exchanged MTU leaves ATT_MTU at default 23; current code records a parsed value such as 22, then treats a 22-byte fragment as final because it expects 21. Reviewed the valid 100-byte negotiation test and unsupported-exchange fallback test; neither exercises a below-default value. No runtime test, packet, or device was used. Source-only.
