Bluetooth hardware-task startup and shutdown recheck (2026-10-18; no new OD): re-read `bOpenHCIDevice()`, `bQueryHCIDevice()`, `bAllocCore()`, `bFreeCore()`, ACL read/write posting and reply handling, `bTick()`, the `bHWTask()` start/ready/error/shutdown path, and the selected `btAddHardware()`/`btRemHardware()` readiness callers (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2416-3100`; `objects.c:80-110,147-181`). H:4 shutdown finding OD2936 caller recheck (2026-10-18; no duplicate): followed the selected startup-posted ACL reads through `bHandleDevReply()` and shutdown (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2601-2612,2722-2755,3013-3017,3050-3076,3082-3086`) into the Raspberry Pi H:4 adapter request switch, `AbortIO`, and `h4bthci_CloseUnit()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bluetooth/h4bthci/h4bthci_unit.c:306-373,447-473`; `h4bthci_device.c:96-115`). It logs at 5 seconds and forcibly continues after 30 seconds, then closes the unit, whose worker exits without draining/replying the pending queues before the unit is freed. This is the already-recorded OD2936, not a second finding. Corrected the report/index source locations to the current pinned-file lines; no runtime shutdown was performed. Source-only.

USB Audio binding, config-loader result, and selected Poseidon caller pass (OD3229 retained; 2026-10-18): re-read `nVerifyAudioStreamDevice`, `usbAttemptInterfaceBinding`, `usbForceInterfaceBinding`, and `nLoadClassConfig` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:166-351,2130-2156`) against the selected `UCM_ForceInterfaceBinding` scan (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6348-6391`). USB Audio mode-close publication versus unplug teardown pass (OD3971 added, 2026-10-18): traced `subLibFreeAudio()` from the early `nch_CurrentMode = NULL` store through RTIso stop, buffer release, zero-bandwidth alternate restoration and pipe cleanup (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3580-3668`), against `nAudioTask()`'s NULL wait/exit and `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()`'s task join (`:349-367,755-772,2070-2115`). USB Audio worker complete-body recheck (OD3167/OD3238/OD3971 confirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-18): reread the complete `nAudioTask()` body (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:588-776`) after the mode-close/unplug trace. USB Audio streaming-format descriptor parser complete-body recheck (OD3171/OD3172/OD3947 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): reread `nExamineAudioDescriptors()` from descriptor lookup through AHI mode publication (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1037-1309,1928-1991`) and compared its data accesses with Poseidon's exact-`bLength` descriptor allocation (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2030-2046`). USB Audio alternate-setting bandwidth-estimate and high-speed transaction-multiplier caller recheck (OD3173 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-18): traced `nSelectAudioMode()`'s selected endpoint attributes and bandwidth estimate (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3133-3173`) through Poseidon's descriptor decoding (`poseidon.library.c:8464-8486,8528-8553`) and pipe-flag construction (`:4528-4549`). High-speed `wMaxPacketSize` is split into base `pep_MaxPktSize` and `pep_NumTransMuFr`; Poseidon passes the latter as the HCD MULT flag, while USB Audio's estimate uses only base max-packet size. The estimate modifies `nam_MaxFreq`, but the driver's active `subLibGetAttr` implementation returns the frequency list/count and has its min/max cases commented out (`usbaudio.class.c:3918-3937`); mode allocation does not use the adjusted `nam_MaxFreq` to cap its selected rate. Thus no separate user-visible transaction-multiplier defect was established from this estimate alone. The active high-speed interval-unit mismatch, including its max-frequency estimate effect and playback pacing, remains OD3173. No endpoint, pipe, stream, or host controller was exercised. Source-only.

The OS4-only interface-open path is not selected in the AROS build. Atheros5000 reset-callback owner lifetime pass (OD3972 added, 2026-10-18): traced registration of the unit-embedded reset callback (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:392-395`; `pci.c:258`), non-supervisor dispatch and completion handshake (`rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:31-38,128-153`), then final `CloseDevice()` into `DeletePCIUnit()`/`DeleteUnit()` (`device.c:537-550`; `pci.c:303-325`; `unit.c:474-523`). `RemResetCallback()` only unlinks; it does not join an already executing callback (`rom/exec/remresetcallback.c:49`). PCI network reset-callback in-flight owner race cross-driver comparison (OD3972 expanded, 2026-10-18): compared the AROS reset-node construction, registration and final-close paths in Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, EtherLink3, NvidiaNet, Prism2 and Rhine (`unit.c` callback `is_Data` setup at `:392-395,:302-305,:392-398,:298-303,:299-304,:304-309`; `pci.c` registration at `:258,:257,:305,:258,:295,:267`; final unlink and DeleteUnit at `pci.c:311-325,307-319,358-369,309-319,347-358,318-328`). USB Audio player-frequency zero caller recheck (OD3218 retained, 2026-10-19): traced the AHI public frequency contract and setter dispatch through the subdriver Update/Start calls (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:382-389,946-955,1001-1005`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3693-3772`). Deneb DMA completion state-machine and worker pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): read the full `uhwHandleDMAInt()` and `uhwDMATask()` bodies and reconciled each state transition with ATL data completion, DMA-done interrupt signaling, startup and close (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1968-2430,4230-4340,4996-5264,5270-5359,5374-5401`; selected manifest `mmakefile.src:20-39`). In the input path, ATL completion increments the actual count and marks short packets terminal before entering the matching low/high DMA-read completion state; the state machine copies the aligned remainder and frees the PTD only after the required copy finishes. In the output path, the second-buffer prefetch can overlap the active PTD; its completion state either activates the already-prefetched next bank or stages a further bounded chunk, while PTD byte count continues to track unrounded request bytes. The level-6 handler acknowledges the DMA status and signals the worker only while `hu_DMAPTD` is non-NULL; the worker handles a single pending completion signal and exits on Ctrl-C. No independent state-transition defect was established in these bodies. Previously reported rounded OUT-buffer reads, reply/cache ordering, abort cleanup, and worker-lifetime findings remain separate. Hardware/controller timing and remaining NAK/AbortIO overlap cases are still open; no controller, request, DMA transfer, or schedule was run. Source-only.

xHCI root-hub change-bitmap completion race (OD3978, 2026-10-19): traced immediate completion from the device command dispatch to `cmdIntXFerRootHub()` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_dev.c:212-238,uhwcmd.c:1267-1269`). Its existing-bitmap branch copies shared `hu_RootPortChanges` then clears it without exclusion (`uhwcmd.c:1036-1052`); `xhciIntCode()` is an interrupt handler and ORs new change bits into the same field (`xhci_hcd.c:3211-3218,3355-3359`). The later queued-request path does use `Disable()` around delivery and clearing (`uhwcmd.c:1893-1924`), but that does not protect immediate completion. xHCI root-hub AbortIO completion follow-up (OD3979, 2026-10-19): traced `devAbortIO()` through `cmdAbortIO()` and compared its root-hub queue branch against the controller queue completion branches (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_dev.c:325-329`; `uhwcmd.c:1798-1806` and subsequent queue cases). The root-hub branch removes and reports successful abort without setting the aborted error or replying; the Exec API documents successful AbortIO as setting `IOERR_ABORTED`, with WaitIO still required (`rom/exec/abortio.c:24-35`). Poseidon `hub.class` explicitly aborts its outstanding EP1 request then waits before worker cleanup (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:752-756`); `psdAbortPipe()` documentation also requires the subsequent wait (`rom/usb/docs/poseidon.doc:707-716`). HDAudio SetupStream zero-count validation pass (OD3980 added, 2026-10-19): traced the complete `SetupStream` allocation/register path through `StartStream` and both selected AHI callers (`workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:844-949`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/main.c:238-240,287-289`; `NVHDMI/main.c:205-207`). Count zero passes the only upper-bound check, creates a zero-entry BDL allocation, skips filling it, writes CBL zero and `bufferCount - 1` to LVI, then returns success; StartStream does not test BufferCount. The Intel HDA specification §3.3.39 defines LVI as the index of the last valid BDL descriptor, confirming the underflow's invalid programming. Selected HDAudio/NVHDMI paths both pass two buffers, so reachability is limited to public external HIDD clients. Added OD3980 and index entry. No controller or stream was run; source-only.

OpenSBI PCIDT 64-bit BAR low-address mapping pass (OD3982 added, 2026-10-19): reread the `pcidt_map64bars()` address decode and its `MapPCI` consumer (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:395-469,880-895`). The scanner skips every 64-bit BAR with upper address dword zero before checking whether it lies in the remembered 64-bit PCI window. The PCI BAR memory-type field identifies a 64-bit BAR independently of the assigned address value; an address below 4 GiB can therefore be in a valid 64-bit FDT aperture. `MapPCI` later translates any address in that aperture to `mem64Va`/the remap window and does not check that the BAR span was actually mapped. Added OD3982 for a selected driver dereference of such a BAR; only the final retained 64-bit window remains in scope under OD2567. No matching firmware assignment or hardware was available; source-only.


OpenSBI PCIDT DesignWare 64-bit ATU-span reconciliation (OD3983 added, 2026-10-19): compared `PCIDT_SetupOutboundWindows()`'s low-32-bit ATU limit handling with `pcidt_map64bars()` and `MapPCI` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_access.c:288-340`; `pcidt_driverclass.c:395-469,880-895`). The new outbound region is clipped to the next 4-GiB boundary, while BAR mapping and translation use the complete retained FDT 64-bit window. A BAR beyond that segment is not necessarily forwarded; retained firmware outbound regions may cover some such addresses, so OD3983 is limited to uncovered BARs. The ACPI fallback and ECAM path do not program this DWC outbound ATU path. No matching firmware/ATU state or hardware was available; source-only.

AHCI selected command caller/interleaving pass (2026-10-19; no additional finding): traced every `ahci_ata_cmd`, `ahci_start`, `ahci_issue_pending_commands`, `ahci_port_intr`, and `ahci_poll` call in the selected AHCI source set. SCSI async submitters hold `ap_lock` across setup and `ahci_ata_cmd` (`ahci_scsi.c:564-567,732-734`); `ahci_cam_attach` is called with the port lock held and retains it across probe, while deliberately dropping it only around SIM registration (`ahci_cam_aros.c:336-360`; selected callers `ahci_attach.c:765-778`, `ahci_busclass.c:233-241`). The AROS nonblocking interrupt lock hook always fails, so the hardware interrupt path disables port interrupts and defers completion handling to the worker, which acquires `ap_lock` (`ahci_aros.c:284-286`; `ahci.c:2664-2702`). Polling callers execute `ahci_port_intr(ap, 1)` and active-timeout checks synchronously from `ahci_poll` while in the serialized port context (`ahci.c:2237-2270`); all selected poll calls provide a timeout callback. This closes the selected command-engine submit/completion interleaving slice without establishing a new defect; unrelated CAM adapters, teardown and hardware timing remain open. Source-only; no command or device was exercised.

Serial CMD_RESET active-read callback overlap pass (OD3989 added; 2026-10-19): traced reset's active-read reply and local `Disable()` against the complete RBF callback and PC UART receive path (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:567-606`; `serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-93`; `arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:526-549,713-719`; `rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`). The receive callback loads `su_ActiveRead` once, does not acquire `su_Lock`, writes directly to its `io_Data`, and can reply on completion; reset on another ExecSMP CPU clears status and replies the same request without cross-CPU exclusion. PC/OpenSBI serial receive staging bound recheck (OD836 not promoted; 2026-10-19): reread the PC receive loop and OpenSBI callback/IRQ route (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/serial.hidd/SerialUnitClass.c:524-551,678-695,713-719`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:512-532,727-732`). Both use a 513-byte stack array and increment the receive length until the UART reports no data, with no explicit array bound. The PC setter caps baud at 115200 and both paths drain the UART FIFO synchronously; the source does not establish a receive rate/latency that can refill the FIFO through 513 iterations during one callback. Since OD836 existed only as a coverage reference and not as a detailed report/index finding, removed the claim that it is confirmed and recorded it as an unproven bounds candidate. No serial input or UART was used.

AHI preferences unit/mode-list allocation and selected MUI caller pass (OD3992 added, 2026-10-19): traced selected `AHI_MUI` composition (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/Makefile.in:47-52`) through `main()`, `NewSettings()`, `NewUnit()`, `GetUnits()`, `GetModes()`, `AddUnit()`, `List2Array()` and `GetNode()` (`ahi.c:166-170,208-270`; `support.c:703-724,847-857,863-918,924-945,1211-1228`). `GetUnits()`/`GetModes()` return NULL on list-allocation failure, while their selected callers unconditionally pass those results into `List2Array()`, which dereferences `list->lh_Head`; additionally, ignored failures of every default `AddUnit()` can leave an empty list that `NewUnit()` dereferences through a NULL `GetNode()`. AHI MUI unit/mode event and metadata ownership pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): traced selected `ACTID_UNIT`/`ACTID_MODE` notifications through `FillUnit()`, `NewUnit()`, `NewMode()`, `GUINewUnit()` and `GUINewMode()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/gui_mui.c:288-337,985-1003`; `ahi.c:238-446`; `gui_mui.c:317-420`). The MUI mode-off value is `-1` and is preserved as `~0` through `NewUnit()`/`NewMode()`; the event path does not reinterpret it as a valid mode index. The six metadata getter results are static buffers/catalog strings, so `strlen()` inputs are nonnull in the checked helpers; Text class `OM_SET` duplicates `MUIA_Text_Contents` with `StrDup()` before returning (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/text.c:145-176`), so freeing `GUINewMode()`'s temporary buffer after `set()` does not leave the widget pointing at freed storage. A unit with no eligible modes can leave the prior mode's metadata buffers displayed because `NewMode(~0)` does not clear them; this is a stale-information UI case, not promoted in this pass because its practical consequence is limited to the inactive information panel and no incorrect mode is selected or saved by that state alone. USB Audio Feature Unit volume cascade recheck (OD3981 confirmed, 2026-10-19): reread the Feature Unit channel-mask construction and each AHI output/input-gain/monitor-volume write loop (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1712-1762,644-762,4090-4128`). The implementation addresses master, left and right controls independently and writes the same selected dB value to every advertised bit; it uses the range queried from the selected first control. The USB Audio 1.0 specification states that master controls affect all channels and are cascaded after individual channel controls (§3.5.5); its Volume Control request separately addresses each channel (§5.2.2.4.3.2). This confirms that a device exposing both master and per-channel volume controls can apply the same attenuation at both stages, subject to those controls accepting the value. OD3981 remains conditional on the descriptor and ranges; no report/index change or line credit was needed, and no USB device or control request was used. Source-only.

Raspberry Pi AHI worker-task/IRQ lifetime pass (OD4001 added, 2026-10-19): compared the PWM, HDMI and I²S DMA callbacks' `slavetask` check/`Signal()` calls with each worker's clear-and-ack exit and the driver's wait-then-`KrnRemIRQHandler()` Stop ordering (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/RPi{PWM,HDMI,I2S}/...`). `CreateNewProc` defaults to asynchronous (`NP_Synchronous=FALSE`) and owns the Process, stack and name in `tc_MemEntry` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:121-143,401-421,543-555`); `RemTask()` queues the exiting Process for service-task cleanup and the service task frees the memory once it sees `TS_INVALID` (`rom/exec/remtask.c:82-113,130-163`; `rom/exec/service.c:37-90`). The cancelable signal-IPI drain cannot cover a callback delayed before entering `Signal()` (`rom/exec/signal.c:89-106,208-234`). Generic IRQ removal's writer lock waits for callback completion but is reached only after the master is signaled, so it cannot keep that Process alive during the gap. The callback does not explicitly snapshot the field; on a cross-CPU overlap the unsynchronized use can pass a stale task pointer after teardown, or NULL if a later load observes the clear. Exact load behavior depends on generated code. Added OD4001 across all three variants and corrected the earlier HDMI candidate reference; generic driver-buffer release remains protected by handler removal. No SMP schedule, task exit, or hardware IRQ was run. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI hardware-control hook/caller contract pass (2026-10-19; OD3167/OD3238/OD3457 retained, no new OD): reread the complete `subLibHardwareControl()` method and adjacent attribute hooks (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3812-4161`), then traced all recognized hardware-control tag cases through `_AHI_ControlAudioA()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:915-1005`) and the asynchronous worker (`usbaudio.class.c:613-762`). The caller forwards set/query values directly with no lock, and the worker clears the shared flag word only after synchronous control transfers; this is the already documented OD3167 lost-update window. `AHIC_Input` stores any supplied index and the worker later follows the selected input pointer, confirming OD3238's stale saved-input condition. `AHIC_Output` similarly accepts an index without bounds checking, but its worker path only sends the resulting selector value when a selector unit exists; invalid values produce a failed USB request/log rather than a distinct memory-safety consequence, while the advertised-output-without-selector mismatch is OD3457. Query hooks return cached settings; unknown tags return FALSE. The inspected setters intentionally return `AHIS_UNKNOWN` for software-mixer fallback. No additional independent defect established. This recheck overlaps previously credited hooks and adds no source-line credit; full USB Audio descriptor, external-caller, and lifecycle coverage remains partial. No control call, transfer, or device was run. Source-only.
USB Audio mode-info attribute index-contract pass (2026-10-19; OD3172/OD3207 retained, no new OD): read the complete `subLibGetAttr()` body and AHI's `AHI_GetAudioAttrsA()` tag handling/documented index ranges (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3895-4080`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:290-306,377-388,450-535`). The driver directly indexes frequency, input and output arrays; the public mode-info contract defines each corresponding argument as an index in `[0,count-1]`, so an invalid external argument alone is not promoted as a distinct driver finding. Under valid indices, `AHIDB_Frequency` returns the stored rate, and selector names follow the stored topology. The fixed nearest-rate threshold and zero-frequency mode conditions remain the separately documented OD3207 and OD3172 paths. Input/monitor range queries use `nGetInputUnit()` and thus retain OD3238's stale selected-input path; output-volume range access is gated by the root's volume-control flag. Bluetooth config-tree mutation/string-helper follow-up (OD3766/OD3767/OD3772 rechecked, no new OD; 2026-10-19): reread the selected config-tree helpers for allocation, removal, replacement, serialization, CRC and string chunks (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/config.c:1271-1576`), then traced `btReadCfg`/`btAddCfgEntry` callers in Bluetooth HID, PAN, Preferences Import and the selected disk-loader path. `btReadCfg` still clears the prior children before recursive import; declared child extents are copied before the parent remainder is checked, confirming OD3766/OD3767. `bAddCfgChunk` removes an existing chunk before attempting a larger replacement allocation; selected fixed-size CDC/keymap replacements fit the existing capacity after removal, while HID GUI action forms deliberately clear their children before rebuilding, so this pass did not establish a distinct in-tree stale-chunk loss beyond OD3767's failed-import behavior. `btMatchStringChunk`'s loop compares a differing next character before checking whether the query ended, so the suspected ordinary prefix match is not present for NUL-terminated strings. `bGetStringChunk` copies the declared data length into a length-plus-one allocation; maintained string-chunk producers store `strlen+1`, and no distinct selected valid-input defect was established. Rechecked that `bWriteCfg`/`btGetCfgChunk` call `bUpdateGlobalCfg` while holding the shared config semaphore; the live-tree mutation and concurrency interleaving remain OD3772. No config import, allocation failure, save, or concurrent mutation was run. The Bluetooth config parser's broader extent validation, all public mutation contracts, and failure reporting remain partial. Source-only.
Filesave OD2160 input-source reachability recheck (2026-10-19; no duplicate): followed the stereo `FORMAT_S16` branch from `AHIsub_Start()`'s successful FileRequester call to `PlaySlave` opening `dd->fs_FileReq->fr_File` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-main.c:217-305`; `filesave-playslave.c:265-283`). ASL defines `STRINGA_MaxChars` as the maximum number of characters and sets the filename gadget to `MAX_FILE_LEN == 257`; selection clones the gadget's complete text into `fr_File` (`compiler/include/intuition/gadgetclass.h:467-470`; `workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.h:36-39`; `filereqhooks.c:878-880,1779-1790`). The local copy is not guaranteed NUL-terminated before `strlen`, confirming OD2160's source trigger; the actual read past the stack array and suffix-write extent still depend on uninitialized tail bytes. No requester or file was opened, and no new source-line credit was added because the Filesave body and these lines were already credited. Source-only.
Filesave stereo S16 second-output open failure pass (OD4002 added, 2026-10-19): traced the two `MODE_NEWFILE` opens and common `PlaySlave` cleanup through the AHI `_AHIsub_Start()` handshake (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-playslave.c:265-283,549-567`; `filesave-main.c:291-295`). Filesave AIFF/AIFC/WAVE emitted-size and sample-frame recheck (OD1546/OD1547/OD2018 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): traced the complete sample conversion/byte-count loop and final format-header rewrites (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-playslave.c:311-381,438-460,469-538`) against the fixed-width writer headers and selected AHI-Handler chunk reader. AIFF/AIFC and WAVE emit signed 16-bit samples, so every `bytesWritten` increment is `samples * 2` and is even; the suspected odd SSND/BODY padding gap is not reachable for these formats. 8SVX is the byte-sample exception and explicitly writes the required odd-byte pad before its header rewrite (`:470-478`), matching existing OD2018 coverage. Stereo sample-frame counters represent per-channel frames while data-byte counts include both channels. The native-long LP64 header-layout issue remains OD1546, and AIFF/AIFC payload consumers beyond AHI-Handler remain outside this pass. No sample file was generated or parsed. Source-only.

USB HID shared action-message lifetime pass (OD4009 added, 2026-10-19): traced `nDoAction()`'s two action-message production branches, `nLastActionHero()` dispatch, configuration-reload tree replacement, `nFreeItem`/`nFreeReport`, per-binding task exit, `usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()` and class `libClose()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:80-97,1005-1070,1321-1459,5554-5575,6142-6175,7089-7239`; `hid.h:833-838`). Serial-class break command comparison (no new finding, 2026-10-19): compared every checked-in serial-device `SDCMD_BREAK` branch in USB CDC-ACM, CP210x, PL2303, Bluetooth RFCOMM, rawwrap and PalmPDA (`rom/usb/classes/{cdcacm,serialcp210x,serialpl2303,rawwrap,palmpda}/dev.c`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/dev.c`) with each selected worker handler. USB Audio volume-range mapping caller recheck (OD3202 retained, no new finding, 2026-10-19): traced Feature Unit signed 8.8 GET_MIN/GET_MAX fields through `nFindLogVolume()`, AHI mode-info range queries, `AHI_ControlAudioA()`, and the three worker mappings for output, input-gain, and monitor values (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1312-1367,1740-1800,640-762,3990-4050,4090-4130`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/{modeinfo.c:450-535,audioctrl.c:915-1005}`). The fixed `0..0x10000` AHI range is the normalized control range; the worker maps it to the device-reported dB bounds, so the helper alone does not establish a second range defect. Reconfirmed OD3202: the signed 32-bit `Fixed` multiplication can overflow at a valid 32,768-unit dB span when unity `0x10000` is applied; output volume, input gain, and monitor controls use the same expression. Existing OD3198 separately covers successful short GET_MIN/GET_MAX responses consumed without actual-length validation. No descriptor, control request, or device was used; source-only.

USB Audio binding-readiness recheck for OD3974 (2026-10-19): traced `usbForceInterfaceBinding()` through the worker readiness wait into `nAllocAudio()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:310-351,1993-2059`). On successful startup, the worker creates `nch_TaskMsgPort` and its EP0 pipe, then stores `nch_Task` immediately before returning; the binder waits for the ready signal and returns the binding only if `nch_Task` is non-NULL. This rules out the hypothesized resume of a normally published binding during incomplete startup. It does not close OD3974: after publication, `psdResumeDevice()` drops the device lock before `psdResumeBindings()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:3913-3933`), while release clears the interface binding under that lock and blocks until the worker deletes its port (`:6588-6613`; Audio `:344-371,2070-2117`). Resume can therefore retain the binding across release and arrive during/after worker teardown; `UCM_AttemptResumeDevice` still dereferences the unchecked port/task fields (`usbaudio.class.c:503-506`). Tightened OD3974's startup scope accordingly; no additional finding or line credit. No device or scheduling behavior was run. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI mode-allocation rollback pass (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced `subLibAllocAudio()` partial setup and every explicit `AHISF_ERROR` return through AHI's allocation error label and `_AHI_FreeAudio()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3240-3555,3571-3668`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:511-520,652-658,702-741`). AHI invokes the subdriver `FreeAudio` callback even when `AllocAudio` reports failure. Once the Poseidon handle is acquired, USB Audio's callback cleans the optional timer request/device, primary and sibling ports/pipes/buffers, RTIso handlers, and the Poseidon handle; `nSelectAudioMode()` failure after interface selection is routed through this cleanup, which restores the zero-bandwidth alternate when one is recorded. No independent rollback defect was established in these paths. Already-covered issues involving early `nch_CurrentMode` clearing and concurrent teardown remain OD3971; descriptor, frequency and buffer arithmetic candidates remain separately tracked. This focused pass adds no line credit to the partial USB Audio translation unit; no allocation failure, mode, USB device or AHI call was exercised. Source-only.

Envy24 AHI entry-point full-body and Start rollback caller pass (2026-10-19; OD2744/OD2745/OD2490 rechecked, no additional finding): reread all of `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/main.c` (747 lines), including audio allocation/free, update, Start/Stop, GetAttr and HardwareControl, then traced `AHIC_Play`/`AHIC_Record` through AHI `_AHI_ControlAudioA()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:1007-1014`). AHI returns the Start error without issuing Stop; this supports OD2744's partial-allocation/retry ownership case. Its FreeAudio callback later calls Stop with both flags, but Envy24 Stop frees only resources whose `is_playing`/`is_recording` flags were set, leaving allocations made before a failed Start's state publication unowned; repeated Start can overwrite those pointers. A later caller-count correction withdrew OD2745: the current Envy24 initializer records only one matching PCI object, so a nonzero AudioID card cannot be selected through this build path. Frequency/input/output indexed getters rely on the documented AHI index ranges; invalid public arguments do not establish another finding. No audio device, card, allocation failure or playback/recording was exercised. Source body now fully read; PCI/board initialization, interrupt scheduling and codec/GPIO hardware behavior remain separate caller/platform gaps. Source-only.

Envy24 EEPROM minimum-length caller pass (OD4017 added, 2026-10-19): rechecked the EEPROM length byte, payload loop, PCI config/GPIO consumers and card-init return path (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/misc.c:275-277,340-359,363-453`). Length is treated as total bytes including six header bytes, but card initialization always consumes seven payload bytes. Values below 13 leave at least one byte of local `eeprom[128]` uninitialized; values at or below six skip the payload loop completely. The stale bytes are then written to codec/AC-link/I2S/S/PDIF config and GPIO mask/data/direction registers before initialization reports success. Added OD4017 for this lower-bound case, distinct from OD2738's oversized-length stack overwrite and OD2739's busy-timeout stale read. A low failed read can produce the same small-value path, but no duplicate transport finding is added. No EEPROM or card was used. Source-only.

xHCI endpoint-context and Poseidon teardown caller reconciliation (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced the sole selected `xhciDestroyEndpoint` callback registration through Poseidon's `pTearDownHWEndpoint` and `psdFreePipe` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:599-601`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1654-1669,4650-4677`). Poseidon frees the shared endpoint's hardware request and nulls the pointer after invoking the callback; xHCI clears `iouh_DriverPrivate2` when it owns an endpoint context and reference-counts prepared endpoint contexts under `xhc_DevLock`. On device removal, `xhciFreeDeviceCtx` detaches a still-referenced context by nulling `ectx_Device`, leaving final release to the callback, which then frees the context without touching the removed device (`xhci_hcd.c:2312-2362,4409-4445`). This caller/lifetime trace supports existing OD3197's command-failure ring-release concern; no independent shared-pipe reference defect established. No pipe teardown or controller was run. Source-only.

xHCI finished-request worker full-body reconciliation (2026-10-19; OD3206/OD3517 retained, no new finding): reread both complete queue walks in `xhciHandleFinishedTDs` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2701-2943`) and the event-task call/scheduling order (`xhci_hw.c:523-550`). Periodic requests are decoded from `dpCC` or NAK timeout; RTIso requests call the direction-specific completion hook, then free/recycle periodic state and may queue replacement buffers. This confirms OD3206's event-worker use of PTD/RTIso state across a callback while handler removal can free it, and OD3517's callback-versus-stop buffer lifetime exposure. Ordinary periodic requests free context before reply. Async requests translate completion status, optionally reset a stalled EP0, free async request context, perform control-transfer postprocessing from saved device state, then reply. No separate completion ordering or list mutation defect was established from this body; external AbortIO interactions and actual concurrent scheduling remain conditional/unrun. Source-only.

xHCI transfer-event completion decoder and caller boundary pass (2026-10-19; no new finding): reread all of `xhciIntWorkProcess()` and its two selected event-ring callers (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:2972-3117,3280-3550,3620-3680`). Transfer events derive the residual from the 24-bit event status; ordinary requests clamp residuals larger than the requested length before calculating actual bytes, release the DMA bounce mapping using that bounded extent, clear matching setup/data/status `ringio` entries, and store the actual length. The command-completion caller uses the same helper only for command-ring slots carrying an asynchronous IOReq; synchronous command slots have no ringio request and bypass it. The wrapped bookkeeping range correctly skips the reserved link TRB. No independent transfer-length or index defect established in the checked ordinary path; malformed event contents, controller ordering, and event-versus-request teardown overlap remain untested/conditional and are tracked elsewhere. Source-only.

xHCI command submission/slot-result completion caller recheck (OD3785 retained, 2026-10-19): reread the whole synchronous `xhciCmdSubmit()` and async submit helper plus command wrappers (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hw.c:52-159,286-340,346-478`), the command-ring writer (`xhci_hcd.c:872-913`), and selected producer sites. Synchronous submit reserves a command TRB, initializes its `xhc_CmdResults[queued]` sentinel, rings the doorbell, then polls that slot for up to one second; command completion copies the event into the same result slot and advances the ring. The only producer exclusion is `xhciRingLock()`'s local `Disable()`/`Enable()`, and `xhciCmdSubmit()`'s surrounding Disable is likewise processor-local on ExecSMP. The selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP manifest packages xHCI; its port task can submit Enable Slot while the independent event task can submit endpoint configuration during transfer scheduling (`xhci_hcport.c:767-779`; `xhci_hcd.c:1367-1368`; `xhci_hw.c:523-550`; `xhci_schedule.c:134-175`). This confirms existing OD3785's shared command-ring producer race and its selected two-task trigger; no separate timeout-slot reuse issue established in this slice. Controller concurrency and timeout were not exercised. Source-only.

Atheros5000 final-close request-port lifetime trace (OD4018 added, 2026-10-19): followed `CloseUnit()`'s last-open branch through `DeletePCIUnit()` and `DeleteUnit()`. AHI PCI finder-pattern boundary check after OD4019 (2026-10-19; no finding extended): searched the selected AROS PCI wrappers for the same `prev_dev`/first-different-device callback and traced callers in CMI8738, SB128, VIA-AC97, Envy24, and Envy24HT. SANA-II access-lock/last-close trigger boundary (OD4018 and EK8880 follow-up, 2026-10-19): traced Prism2 `DevBeginIO()` and `ServiceRequest()` against the worker and `CloseUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/device.c:296-305,426-440,538-568`; `request.c:182-285`; `unit.c:385-417,3818-3888`). One task can own `access_lock` while servicing a synchronous BeginIO; a concurrent request is queued, then the unit worker can block in ObtainSemaphore until the first service releases it. Final Close deletes the worker before freeing the unit. However, this sequence only creates the targeted waiter-at-last-close condition if the final open is closed while its own request remains active; the examined driver code does not establish that as a supported client lifecycle. This refines the conditional RemTask waiter scenario and does not change OD4018 (the independent freed-request-port flush finding); no additional device finding or trigger claim is added. No I/O or close was run.

Deneb DMA interrupt-to-worker completion boundary recheck (OD3704 retained, no new OD; 2026-10-19): traced `uhwLevel6Int()` Mach DMA status acknowledgement and signal handoff (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:5267-5354`) into the sole active `uhwDMATask()` consumer and `uhwHandleDMAInt()` state switch (`:4996-5264,5374-5401`). The apparent direct `uhwHandleDMAInt()` call in the level-6 handler is inside `#if 0`; active completion is deferred to the worker, which rechecks `hu_DMAPTD` before dispatch. Terminal DMA-IN branches call `FreeATL`; its reply-before-`CachePostDMA` order remains the already documented OD3704 path. The state branches and interrupt handoff yielded no additional independent completion/ownership defect in this pass. No controller interrupt, DMA request, abort or worker schedule was exercised; source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II soft-MAC channel-selection caller recheck (2026-10-19; no additional finding): traced `wpa_driver_sana2_set_channel()` through the driver-op table and `WPA_DRIVER_FLAGS_USER_SPACE_MLME` selection into `ieee80211_sta_associate()` (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:640-653,987-995,1107`; `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:1243-1247`; `wpa_supplicant/mlme.c:2649-2652`). WirelessManager SANA-II association error-propagation recheck (OD3626 retained, 2026-10-19): reread the full `wpa_driver_sana2_associate()` body and its selected supplicant caller (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:382-445`; `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:1243-1256,1270-1292`). Confirmed three independent suppressed error classes: SSID/tag allocation and `S2_SETOPTIONS` errors are stored in `err` but the callback unconditionally returns 0; each of four WEP key install/clear results is discarded. The supplicant treats only a negative callback result as failure and otherwise follows its ordinary association timeout. Thus simply returning the positive `DoIO()` code would still not satisfy the callback contract; error mapping must be negative. The association callback is selected for hard-MAC SANA-II devices (`S2_GETNETWORKS` advertised); user-space-MLME devices take `ieee80211_sta_associate()` instead. OD3626 already captures this behavior; no duplicate finding added. SSID length is bounded by selected supplicant/BSS inputs to 32 bytes in the paths checked, so the fixed 33-byte local allocation did not yield an additional in-tree overflow finding. No association or I/O failure was induced; source-only.

Card resource internal-layout and selected-caller audit (2026-10-19; no new finding): the common header contains only the library node and `CardMemoryMap`; the active m68k-Amiga variant uses its separate, expanded `arch/m68k-amiga/card/card_intern.h` and initializes its own ownership/task state. USB Audio AHI partial-allocation failure unwind recheck (2026-10-19; no new OD): traced every failure return in `subLibAllocAudio()` through AHI's `_AHI_AllocAudio()` error label and `_AHI_FreeAudio()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3271-3331,3489-3509`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:481-521,656-659,712-735`). Poseidon RTIso handler-list teardown synchronization audit (OD4021 added, 2026-10-19; no line credit): traced device-removal iteration under `pd_Lock` through saved-next release-hook traversal, RTIso registration/removal, and USB Audio duplex allocation/free (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2240-2249,2319-2341,5555-5592,5607-5625`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3489-3503,3590-3597`). The remover's device semaphore does not serialize `psdFreeRTIsoHandler`, which unlinks under only local `Forbid`; Exec documents that Forbid on ExecSMP is processor-local (`rom/exec/forbid.c:51-57`). A concurrent duplex AHI free can therefore free the sibling node already held in `nextprt`, which the device-removal loop dereferences on its next iteration. Added OD4021, separate from OD3517's completion/softint use-after-free. Trigger remains conditional on SMP overlap; no schedule or USB removal was run. USB Audio source review remains partial; no line credit. Source-only.

OD4021 caller-lock recheck (2026-10-19; retained, no new finding/line credit): verified AHI's public `_AHI_FreeAudio()` calls subdriver `Stop` and then `FreeAudio` without acquiring Poseidon's device semaphore (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:712-735`); USB Audio teardown has no `psdLockReadDevice`/`psdLockWriteDevice` call. Thus the second caller is not serialized by the `pd_Lock` held during `pFreeDevice()`'s release-hook walk. In duplex mode the `sibnam` RTIso node is the one unlinked/freed first, so if it is the saved `nextprt`, the next loop condition dereferences freed storage. `Forbid` contributes only local scheduler exclusion on ExecSMP. OD3517 remains distinct: it covers controller completion/deferred-interrupt use of audio buffers and AHI state after stop, not the Poseidon list iterator's saved-next lifetime. Nouveau/VMware SVGA MMIO helper caller and return-contract pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): compared both byte-sized helper bodies and their source-list inclusion with the target-specific `KrnMapGlobal()` results. The RISC-V mapper returns nonzero on success and zero on failure (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_mmu.c:149-195`); AArch64 forwards `mmu_map_range()`'s same success/failure convention (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmu.c:305-337`). The helper's `if (!KrnMapGlobal(...)) return NULL` check therefore handles those branches consistently. The x86 branch skips the call and returns the physical address; Nouveau's two maintained caller addresses are within the x86-64 initial identity map. The legacy 32-bit ARM mapper is a no-op returning zero, so this helper reports failure rather than claiming an unmapped address is usable. VMware's copy has no checked-in caller. Credited the 84 C code lines (42 each) after the previous reconciled totals (Other Drivers 191,294 / 378,995; weighted 442,185 / 786,380): Other Drivers is now 191,378 / 379,079 = 50.5%, and weighted overall is 442,269 / 786,464 = 56.2%. This is another incremental correction, not a fresh inventory/status reconciliation. No helper, hardware, or mapping was run. Source-only.

Nouveau/VMware SVGA DRM compatibility inventory and helper passes (2026-10-19): parsed both `sources.drm.mak` lists and compared every existing local `drm-compat/*.c` path against the ledger. Nouveau/VMware timer-process startup consequence expansion for OD4046 (2026-10-20): split the two CreateMsgPort failure cases and traced them through Exec `PutMsg`. VIA-Rhine failed-open cleanup caller recheck (OD4034 expanded, 2026-10-19): traced opener-allocation failure through the direct `CloseDevice()` call into Exec's close dispatch (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/via-rhine_init.c:231-279`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:95-119`; `closedevice.c:63-85`). Because the unit open count and flags are set before `AllocVec(struct Opener)`, and the Close hook stops but never decrements the count, a first `SANA2OPF_MINE` open that fails this allocation leaves `open_count == 1`, `IFF_SHARED` clear, and no opener node; later opens return `IOERR_UNITBUSY`. Expanded OD4034 and its index to include this failure route. This target is explicitly buildable but omitted from the architecture/aggregate edges; no allocation failure or device was run. Source-only.

VIA-Rhine scheduler queue-drain caller recheck (OD4026, 2026-10-19): traced `BeginIO()`'s failed `AttemptSemaphore()` branch through clearing `IOF_QUICK`, `PutMsg()` to `rhineu_input_port`, and the task signal wait (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/via-rhine_init.c:327-335`; `unit.c:724-759`). When that request arrives while the scheduler owns `rhineu_unit_lock`, it is queued and wakes the worker. The `while (GetMsg(input) != NULL);` loop consumes all queued requests; its following block always runs with `io == NULL`, then acquires the lock and calls `handle_request()`, which dereferences `request->ios2_Req.io_Command` immediately (`handler.c:97-105`). Confirmed a lock-contention trigger from the selected API path; no runtime request was submitted. The worker's separate port/signal-allocation failure paths remain tracked under OD4027/OD3609 and were not revisited here. Source-only.

Expanded OD4027: the worker also dereferences unchecked `AllocVec(sizeof(struct Message))` before acknowledging startup; `reply_port` and `input` creation are unchecked, so failure can acknowledge a worker that later dereferences NULL. Expanded OD3672: scheduler waits on one-hot masks, but tests the received mask against raw `signal_0`; `DeleteUnit()` likewise passes that bit number as the `Signal()` mask and frees worker-owned unit/port/MMIO state without joining the task. Reconfirmed OD3671's unchecked signal-allocation failure; the `1 << -1` case is undefined C behavior and its exact target effect is not claimed. The normal/debug VIA-Rhine recipe is explicit, while its architecture and aggregate edges are disabled. No task, allocation failure, signal exhaustion, timer device, or adapter was exercised; source-only.

OHCI PCI enumerator cap/timer cleanup recheck (OD2953 confirmed; no new finding, 2026-10-19): re-read the complete `Enumerator` and `OHCI_Init` path (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohci_init.c:42-108,112-168`) against the 8-entry storage limit (`ohci.h:224,278-283`) and `HIDD_PCI_EnumDevices` callback loop (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:424-445`). The callback allocates/opens its timer before testing `counter == MAX_OHCI_DEVICES`; each additional matching OHCI PCI function therefore returns without `ohci_DeleteTimer`. The counter increments only after a controller is recorded, so the cap path itself does not index beyond the fixed arrays. Timer-setup failure during BIOS handoff remains OD2955. BAR mapping, port-register reads, and actual controller behavior remain hardware-dependent and unverified. No PCI inventory, timer, or controller was exercised. Source-only.


USB hub rescan timer cleanup race recheck (OD2468 expanded, 2026-10-19): re-read `hub_process`, `USBTimer`/`USBTimerDone`/`USBDeleteTimer`, timer-device reply, Exec `ReplyMsg`/`InternalPutMsg`, and task-removal ownership. `USBTimer` stores the current hub task in the timer reply port and submits the 10-second rescan asynchronously; `evt_Cleanup` deletes only `hub->tr`, replies, and returns, leaving local `rescan` pending. The selected timer implementation later replies that request through `InternalPutMsg`, whose PA_SIGNAL action calls `Signal` on the stored task pointer; `NewAddTask`'s task MemList is freed by `RemTask` after entry return. Expanded existing OD2468 to record this conditional stale-task signal as well as the already documented timer/device/port leak. Trigger requires disposal before the armed rescan completes. No hub teardown, timer completion, or task signal was run. Source-only.


USB hub cleanup reply-port and rescan signal follow-up (OD2287/OD819 confirmed; no duplicate, 2026-10-19): re-read `USBHub::Dispose`, `OnOff`, `hub_process` event/signal dispatch, `USBTimer` signal allocation and Exec `WaitPort`/reply-port behavior (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:204-215,278-292,628-718`; `misc.c:123-150`; `rom/exec/waitport.c:62-85`). Both cleanup and OnOff use an unchecked `CreateMsgPort()` before `PutMsg`/`WaitPort`; the NULL reply-port and `WaitPort(NULL)` path is already OD2287. The worker also uses the raw signal index returned by `USBTimer` as a Wait mask and fails to clear it after consuming the request; the missed wake, delayed rescan, and subsequent empty `WaitPort` path are already OD819. These are distinct from OD2468’s pending timer request retaining a pointer to the task after cleanup. No port allocation, signal exhaustion, timer, or hub method was exercised. Source-only.


Deneb command-query and QuickIO caller-contract pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): read `cmdReset`, `cmdUsbReset`, `cmdUsbResume`, `cmdUsbSuspend`, `cmdUsbOper`, `cmdQueryDevice`, `cmdNSDeviceQuery`, and their `devBeginIO` dispatch (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:569-800,1548-1610`; `dev.c:545-640`). Checked QueryDevice output writes against `<devices/usbhardware.h>`, the usbhardware.device documentation, and the selected Poseidon query caller (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:187-220`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:513-555`; `poseidon.library.c:9130-9140,9215-9255`). Poseidon initializes optional endpoint callbacks to NULL; Deneb does not handle those tags, so unsupported callbacks remain NULL. NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY size/format input checks and its RC_DONTREPLY handling match the selected `devBeginIO` completion branch. Although the driver advertises UHCF_QUICKIO and state-command comments prohibit interrupt context, the selected Poseidon PA_CALLBACK handlers only forward/abort queued pipe transfers (`poseidon.library.c:9072-9093`); the checked root-reset requests use the ordinary synchronous pipe path, and no selected interrupt-context caller of the state commands was found. The command-query routines therefore add no new defect from this source/caller slice. Remaining Deneb scope includes the still-partial 5,403-line implementation's hardware register/timing contracts, split scheduling, allocation failures, and abort/completion interleavings listed in the file row; no device or request was used. Source-only.

Deneb level-6 interrupt registration and open/close ordering pass (OD3582/OD3653 rechecked; no separate finding, 2026-10-19): traced the complete `Open_Unit()` registration sequence and `uhwHWInit()` interrupt-enable writes against `uhwLevel6Int()` and `uhwDMATask()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:117-245,452-486,502-525,5267-5368,5372-5401`). The handler is registered before `uhwHWInit()` and before `AddTask()`, but the hardware's global interrupt enable is written only at the end of successful initialization; before the worker is added, `hu_DMAPTD` remains NULL and the DMA handler does not signal it. `Open_Unit()` ignores `uhwHWInit()`'s error and still adds/publishes the worker/unit, already covered by OD3653. `Close_Unit()` disables the controller, removes the interrupt server, signals the worker, waits a fixed 10 ms, then frees the unit; the missing worker-exit join and its embedded storage lifetime are OD3582. No additional independent interrupt-registration defect was established. Hardware initialization, interrupt timing, and worker scheduling were not run; source-only.

Deneb ordinary and realtime ISO split-scheduling caller pass (OD3578/OD3604/OD3705 rechecked; no additional finding, 2026-10-19): read the full ordinary `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()` split branch, `cmdAddIsoHandler()` PTD setup, `cmdStartRTIso()` frame scheduling, and the recurring `uhwHandleFinishedRTIsos()` OUT/IN rearm path (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4532-4770,1090-1233,1350-1482,3333-3795`). Compared request flags, hub/port values, endpoint packet size and frame interval against the public USBHardware fields and Poseidon's `psdAllocRTIsoHandler()`/Start path (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:39-48,88-100,157-175`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:90-116,438-495`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5555-5605,5630-5658`). Existing findings retain the independently established RTIso OUT rounded segment read (OD3578), dropped high-speed ISO multiplier (OD3604), and split per-microframe error status omission (OD3705). The inspected scheduling pass did not establish an additional independent defect; precise ISP1760 split scheduling semantics and real controller timing remain unverified. No controller, endpoint, or transfer was used; source-only.

Deneb control and interrupt split-PTD setup pass (no new finding, 2026-10-19): read `uhwScheduleCtrlPTDs()` and `uhwScheduleIntPTDs()` split branches and traced setup/data/status-stage reuse through `uhwHandleFinishedATLs()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1968-2784,3797-4189`). Checked that the request's split hub/port and low-speed flag are copied into the setup PTD, the shared PTD retains those fields through control data/status transitions, and interrupt PTDs set their split start/complete-split fields and select IN/OUT token from the request direction. Compared `UHFF_SPLITTRANS`, low-speed, hub/port, interval, and command contracts with the public header/docs and selected Poseidon request construction (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:39-48,157-175`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:90-116,224-249,306-328`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8470-8495`). No additional source-level defect was established in these setup paths; controller-specific scheduling semantics and real split timing remain open. No device or transfer was used; source-only.

Deneb timer-helper and NAK-timer shutdown pass (OD3582/OD3886 rechecked; no separate finding, 2026-10-19): re-read `uhwOpenTimer()`, `uhwDelayMS()`, `uhwCloseTimer()`, their `Open_Unit()`/`Close_Unit()` callers, and the recurring NAK timer callback (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:65-110,117-266,335-488,502-525,4825-4990`). Open failure paths delete whichever request/port was acquired; each checked delay is a fixed small millisecond value and is called only after successful timer open. The NAK request copies the opened timer request's device/unit fields, replaces the reply port with the embedded PA_SOFTINT port, and requeues only at the end of its callback. Close disables further callback delivery, calls AbortIO before closing the opened request, and does not reuse the NAK request; the selected timer.device AbortIO removes a pending request and replies synchronously (`rom/timer/abortio.c:49-93`), while PA_IGNORE suppresses the reply action (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:100-120`). No independent timer setup, arithmetic, or request-lifetime defect was established; the separate embedded worker lifetime remains OD3582, and wrap-unsafe NAK deadline comparison remains OD3886. No timer, expiry, or close was run; source-only.

Deneb bulk PTD allocator/DMA selection and request admission pass (OD3584/OD3585/OD3886 rechecked; no new finding for selected AROS m68k build, 2026-10-19): read the complete `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` allocation, DMA selection, PTD publication and retry setup against `cmdBulkXFer()`, ATL completion/release, and `FreeATL()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:850-911,1626-1700,1968-2784,4192-4531`). Large requests allocate the largest available contiguous granule run and are continued through subsequent PTDs; temporary lack of a run leaves the request queued for a later scheduling pass. The DMA mapping-shortening branch exits its `while(usedma)` without clearing `usedma`, which would continue with DMA fields but no valid mapped operation if `CachePreDMA()` returned a shorter contiguous span. However, the selected m68k Exec implementation (`arch/m68k-all/exec/cachepredma_.S:72-75,90-120`) returns the original address and leaves the input length unchanged, so that branch is not reachable in the reviewed AROS m68k configurations; it is not retained as an AROS finding. The ordinary non-DMA rounded OUT-buffer read remains covered by OD3585, active-DMA AbortIO by OD3584, and wrap-unsafe NAK deadline comparison by OD3886. Cache/DMA behavior on non-AROS external Exec implementations and hardware timing remain outside this conclusion. No request, allocation failure, DMA mapping, or device was exercised; source-only.

USB Audio GUI task-publication race recheck (OD3200 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): traced `nOpenCfgWindow()` through both `psdSpawnSubTask()` branches and `nGUITaskCleanup()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2160-2180,2200-2219,2282-2287,2309-2315,2370-2394`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1452-1465,1481-1510`). The DOS path returns after `CreateNewProcTags()` has added the process (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:543-556`); the no-DOS AROS path returns after `AddTask()` publishes the task (`poseidon.library.c:1502-1507`). Neither helper waits for the child to finish startup before `nOpenCfgWindow()` assigns its returned pointer. The child can take an immediate library-open/application/window-open failure exit and set `nh_GUITask = NULL` first; caller `Forbid()` does not serialize that cross-CPU store on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). The later assignment can then retain a dead pointer, and subsequent config-window requests only test the field as a boolean. This confirms the already detailed OD3200; no duplicate ID or runtime schedule added. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI sound-method fallback and buffer-ownership pass (no new OD, 2026-10-19): read `subLibSetVol`, `subLibSetFreq`, `subLibSetSound`, `subLibSetEffect`, `subLibLoadSound`, `subLibUnloadSound`, and the selected AHI load/unload dispatch (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3812-3892`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/sound.c:870-936,978-1000`). The USB Audio methods all return `AHIS_UNKNOWN`, which is the AHI contract for falling through to the software mixer; `subLibAllocAudio()` sets `AHISF_MIXING` for these modes (`usbaudio.class.c:3344-3348`). Consequently, for ordinary sample types AHI stores the caller's sample address/type/length in its own `ahiac_SoundDatas` table and marks it unavailable on unload, while the USB class does not claim or free the sample memory. In no-mixing controls AHI returns the sublibrary result directly; USB Audio does not advertise those controls. No separate method-result or buffer-ownership defect established. External AHI clients must still honor the documented sample lifetime and sound-index API contracts; no sound was loaded or played. Source-only.

USB Audio AHI attribute-query contract and indexed lookup pass (OD3207 confirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-19): read all of `subLibGetAttr()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3895-4075`) and compared its supported tags, defaults and indexed table accesses with AHI's `AHI_GetAudioAttrsA()` dispatch and documented ranges (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:293-306,367-385,461-505`). Traced the nearest-rate query to AHI Preferences `NewMode()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/ahi.c:304-305`) and confirmed it passes saved frequencies directly into `AHIDB_Index`; the fixed 100,000 threshold can therefore leave index zero when all advertised rates are farther away, matching existing OD3207. `AHIDB_FrequencyArg`, `AHIDB_InputArg`, and `AHIDB_OutputArg` are documented as indices within the corresponding count, and the selected AHI dispatcher passes them to the subdriver without normalization; their unchecked array reads do not establish a defect for contract-conforming queries. Unsupported tags return the caller's default, and absent `NepAudioMode` does likewise. `AHIDB_Outputs`/`AHIDB_Output`'s selector and fallback behavior is separately covered by OD3457. This pass found no additional independent attribute-query defect. USB Audio class row remains partial; other descriptor, topology, lifecycle, and stream paths remain open. No query or device was used; source-only.

USB Audio AHI hardware-control dispatch and selector caller pass (OD3238/OD3457 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): read all of `subLibHardwareControl()` and traced its public dispatch through AHI `ControlAudio` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:960-1000`) plus saved preference application (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:743-790`) into the USB worker (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:613-630,4082-4172`). Confirmed input selection is stored and signalled without index validation, and the worker's later `nGetInputUnit()` dereference makes a stale saved index on a replacement topology the existing OD3238 path. Output selection's unconditional success with no Selector Unit and the worker's selector-gated request remain OD3457. The remaining volume/gain/monitor controls store fixed-point arguments, set their update flags and wake the class task; the selected AHI caller forwards the supplied controls directly, and no additional independent control-dispatch defect was established in this slice. Device topology and live concurrent control calls remain untested. Source-only.

USB Audio mode-descriptor projection/body recheck (OD3171/OD3172/OD3494/OD3947 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): read all of `nExamineAudioDescriptors()` and compared the fixed-layout casts and variable rate walks with `PsdDescriptor.pdd_Length` and the USB Audio 1.0 structure definitions (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1037-1312`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon_intern.h:436-450`; `compiler/include/devices/usb_audio.h:206-217,374-395`). Confirmed OD3171 covers the unvalidated header/general/format/endpoint extents and rate-array length; OD3172 covers registering modes with no projected frequencies; OD3494 covers the 64-entry truncation; OD3947 covers inconsistent subframe size versus resolution. Rechecked channel/resolution mapping and frequency sorting: the zero `nam_SampleType` assigned for 24-bit modes is not consumed by the selected converter or AHI control path (`usbaudio.class.c:3373,3457-3498`), so it does not establish a separate defect. The frequency arrays used for selection are separately filtered/sorted, and no further independent mode-projection issue was established. Descriptor verification and remaining topology/caller/error-path review stay partial; no descriptor or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio endpoint-bandwidth/mode-selection pass (OD3208 retained; OD4056 added, 2026-10-19): traced `nSelectAudioMode()` from alternate-interface selection through endpoint attributes and bandwidth calculation, then followed the selected rate through `subLibAllocAudio()`, `AHIDB_Frequency` queries, and `nOutReqHook()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3134-3173,3375-3404,3932-3936,2641-2672`). OD3208 remains the distinct unadvertised-request ordering/nearest-rate issue. Added OD4056: when the endpoint payload-derived ceiling is below a discrete advertised rate, the code lowers only `nam_MaxFreq`; it leaves `nam_FreqArray` visible and accepts an exact requested match, so frame-derived request lengths can exceed the endpoint's declared capacity. Example: 48 kHz stereo 16-bit requires 192 bytes per 1 ms interval while a 96-byte endpoint caps the calculated rate at 24 kHz. The exact host-controller/device completion behavior was not exercised. Source-only.

VIA Rhine shared-opener SANA-II caller recheck (OD4034 refined; no new finding, 2026-10-19): traced AROSTCP `iface_make()` opening its configured SANA-II device (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:319-334`) and WirelessManager opening the configured device/unit (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:940-965`). On AROSTCP deinit, `sana_down()` issues `S2_OFFLINE` only while `lib_OpenCnt == 1`, then closes its own request once (`if_sana.c:158-179,903-915`). With WirelessManager still holding the device open, AROSTCP skips Offline; VIA Rhine's Close vector nevertheless unconditionally stops the shared unit, confirming this selected maintained caller sequence for OD4034. This caller pass does not establish that both clients are configured for every deployment; no device or close sequence was run. Source-only.


PCIDT shared-source MSI dispatch review (OD4057 added, 2026-10-19): traced one synchronous `AddHardwareDriver()` registration per discovered bridge into per-bridge `DWC_MSI_INTR0_STATUS` setup, `KrnModifyIRQA()` slot selection, `krnFindMSIController()` and the PLIC claim/complete loop. A repeated PLIC source matches and overwrites the prior slot, while dispatch polls only the stored controller; an uncleared first-controller line is eventually masked by the stuck-source guard. Added OD4057, conditional on distinct DesignWare bridges sharing an MSI PLIC source. This is separate from OD1411's table-capacity failure on more than four distinct sources. No checked-in board FDT establishes the topology; no IRQ or hardware was used. Source-only.


USB Audio INITLIB failure rollback recheck (OD3239 confirmed; 2026-10-19): traced the selected `kernel-usb-classes-usbaudio` module type through genmodule’s `usbclass` resident-autoinit selection and failed-init wrapper (`rom/usb/classes/audio/mmakefile.src:9-14`; `tools/genmodule/config.c:825-830`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1180`). `libInit` is in INITLIB and `libExpunge` in EXPUNGELIB (`usbaudio.class.c:150-152`); `_set_libinit` invokes expunge callbacks when INITLIB returns false (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:60-69`). The cleared outer base leaves `nh_SubLibBase` NULL if Utility open or nested `MakeLibrary()` fails, and `libExpunge` dereferences it before checking (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:108-110`; `usbaudio.class.c:66-100,110-118`). A nested allocation failure also strands the acquired `nh_UtilityBase` reference. This confirms existing OD3239; the duplicate report entry has been removed. No module load or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

USB Audio worker/control and stream-callback recheck (OD3167/OD3174/OD3193/OD3228/OD3971 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-19): re-read the complete `nAudioTask()` update dispatch and shutdown loop, `nOutReqHook()`, `nInReqHook()`, `nInDoneHook()`, `nReleaseHook()`, and USB Audio `subLibStart`/`subLibUpdate`/`subLibStop`/`subLibFreeAudio` paths (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:588-780,2620-2775,3570-3807`). Cross-checked start/update/control dispatch through selected AHI `AHI_ControlAudioA()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:931-999`) and RTIso request/release callbacks. The worker's unprotected shared update flags and clear-after-transfer remain OD3167; output/input buffer callback behavior remains OD3228/OD3193; ignored RTIso start errors remain OD3174; the worker/FreeAudio shutdown overlap remains OD3971. No additional independent defect established in this subset. This does not close the translation unit's remaining open caller, descriptor, and lifecycle scope; no AHI control, USB stream, device removal, or callback schedule was exercised. Source-only.

Other Drivers report duplicate-ID structure repair (OD4009/OD4010, 2026-10-19): each detailed USB HID finding had also been left as an unheaded paragraph beneath OD4008, while a shorter recovered copy appeared later under its own heading. Report/index finding-ID sets remain in sync; this is editorial reconciliation, not new source coverage.

USB HID `nFlushEvents` producer/caller recheck (OD3948 confirmed; no new finding, 2026-10-19): re-read the complete `nFlushEvents()` output/feature transfer paths (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6352-6430`) and traced the dirty-state writes from `HUA_OUTPUT`/`HUA_FEATURE` (`:6099-6137`), low-level rumble updates (`nSetJoyPortAttrsA`, `:6927-6930`), and `HUAT_FLUSHEVENTS` (`:6192-6193`) into both the initial-action and regular input-worker flush calls (`:795,991`). Failed `psdDoPipe(SET_REPORT)` logs the error and then clears the corresponding per-report dirty bit; the action value remains cached, but unchanged input item values do not invoke the action again (`nProcessItem`, `:4940-4949`). Report-size bounds were cross-checked against `nGenerateOutReport()`/`nGenerateFeatReport()` and the parser/allocation findings OD3911/OD3913; no separate bounds issue is added from this slice. No transfer, report, or USB device was used. Source-only.

USB HID configuration and LowLevel list-lifetime pass (OD3923/OD3928 confirmed; OD4060 added, 2026-10-19): read `nLoadItem()`/`nSaveItem()` in full and traced every local load caller (`nAddItemAction`, `nLoadActionConfig`) and Store/Default GUI caller (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1462-1477,2445-2501,6614-6758`; `hid.gui.c:2399-2462`). Existing OD3928 remains the saved-action allocation failure reported as success, suppressing default mapping; OD3923 remains destructive in-place rebuild and ignored form/chunk insertion failures during save.
