Although port indices are checked before fixed-array indexing (OD3918 is the separate saved-action path), the hooks traverse `nh_Interfaces` while unbind removes and frees the same records under processor-local `Forbid`; added OD4060 for a joy-port call racing release on another ExecSMP CPU. The row remains partial; other HID class methods, lifecycle, and callers remain open. No config, joy-port call, device, or schedule was exercised. Source-only.

ROM USB HID main worker and allocator full-body pass (OD4061 added; existing OD3920/OD3937/OD4009/OD4010/OD3948 rechecked, 2026-10-19): read all of `nHidTask()`, `nAllocHid()`, and `nFreeHid()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:709-1349`) and traced successful binding readiness, optional GUI startup, interrupt input dispatch, config reload, quit actions, abort/wait and cleanup against `usbForceInterfaceBinding()`/`usbReleaseInterfaceBinding()`. OD3920 remains for the discarded HW-tree registration on later init failure or normal unbind; OD3937 remains for the unmatched `IID_Hidd` attribute-base acquisition; OD4009 covers the shared dispatcher retaining action pointers across reload/unbind; OD4010 covers caching failed datatype loads; OD3948 covers output/feature SET_REPORT failure. Added OD4061: a nonzero saved `cdc_PollingMode` selects a branch whose polling implementation is `#if 0`, skips interrupt input, and busy-loops. The field defaults false and is not exposed by the current GUI, but raw saved per-device config loading copies it and the full config chunk is persisted. No new issue beyond OD4061 was established in this worker/allocator pass. Full body credit is not added because this translation unit's aggregate line accounting remains incremental and the file-wide review is partial; other functions, class lifecycle and callers remain open. No USB device, config or task was run. Source-only.

USB HID shared dispatcher, sound and Intuition action caller recheck (OD3936/OD4009/OD4010/OD3483 retained; OD4062 added, 2026-10-19): re-read `nInstallLastActionHero()`, `nDispatcherTask()`, `nLastActionHero()`, and the sound cache bodies, then checked the action producer and selected DOS/Intuition/layer contracts (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:5554-5577,6145-6178,6953-7310`; `rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:60-86`; `rom/hyperlayers/whichlayer.c:31-45,63-74`; `rom/intuition/closewindow.c:374-410,459-483`). DOS documents that asynchronous `SystemTags` closes supplied filehandles when the child exits, so the shell-action handle retention is intentional; the synchronous/error branches close it locally. OD3936 still covers concurrent dispatcher startup, OD4009 queued `nch`/`nha` lifetime, OD4010 failed sound-load cache and OD3483 key-string conversion failure. Added OD4062 because `HUAT_ACTWINDOW` uses `WhichLayer()` under `LayerInfo` but dereferences the returned `Layer *` after unlocking, when `CloseWindow` can delete it under that lock. Other `nLastActionHero` screen/window action lifetimes and the rest of this class remain open. No action, DOS process, window, or device was run. Source-only.

USB host-controller bus-state command cross-driver recheck (OD3655 expanded; 2026-10-19): compared Deneb's `cmdUsbResume`/`cmdUsbSuspend`/`cmdUsbOper` against the corresponding PCIUSB, PCI xHCI, and selected Raspberry Pi USB2OTG handlers (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:628-704`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:434-524`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:442-524`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/usb/usb2otg/usb2otg_core.c:603-642`). All only inspect state and return success/offline; none carries out the documented transition. Checked command dispatch and Poseidon's root-bus suspend/resume paths: Poseidon explicitly leaves these commands unsupported and the in-tree request paths do not issue them, so OD3655 remains limited to direct USBHardware clients. Expanded the existing finding and index rather than adding duplicates. No HCD request or state transition was run; source-only.
Deneb RTIso registration allocation-bound pass (OD3889/OD3604 reconfirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-19): reread `cmdAddIsoHandler()`'s PTD-pair search, 16-node free list, and large-area granule sizing (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1044-1255`), then traced its selected caller `psdAllocRTIsoHandlerA()` and endpoint-size source (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5555-5605,8476-8550`). The driver scans for a free adjacent PTD pair before removing a node; the unit owns 16 RTIso nodes and 32 ISO PTDs, so the unchecked `RemHead()` cannot be reached after exhausting RTIso nodes while a free PTD pair remains. Poseidon passes the parsed endpoint `pep_MaxPktSize`, and its selected descriptor path clamps isochronous sizes to 1,024 bytes before handler allocation; the resulting `slicesize`/granule-mask arithmetic stays within the Deneb map for those in-tree requests. The public direct-HCD path does not independently validate arbitrary malformed packet-size fields, but no valid in-tree request reaches the suspected overflow; no new finding is retained. This closes only the inspected registration allocation/size boundary, not split scheduling, hardware timing, or broader callback ownership. No allocation failure or request was induced; source-only.
Deneb split interrupt TT-flag consumption cross-controller pass (no new OD; 2026-10-19): compared `uhwScheduleIntPTDs()`'s split-PTD fields with the flags built by Poseidon's selected `psdAllocPipe()` path and `pGetTTInfo()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3957-4190`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4497-4505,4578-4593,7946-7982`). Poseidon supplies TT think-time bits and `UHFF_TT_MULTI`, but the Deneb scheduler does not consume either flag; the analogous xHCI endpoint-context path explicitly consumes both (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:1353,1452,1931,1952`). The public header describes these as TT timing/topology data (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:160-184`). However, the selected Deneb ISP1760 PTD definitions use a controller-specific split descriptor, and checked-in source/docs do not establish whether its integrated translator scheduling requires these values or what observable failure omission causes. No finding is promoted; Deneb split scheduling/hardware timing remains open pending a controller contract source. No hub or transfer was used; source-only.
USB host-controller bus-reset command cross-driver caller trace (OD3654 expanded; 2026-10-19): compared Deneb, PCIUSB, PCI xHCI and Raspberry Pi USB2OTG `UHCMD_USBRESET` dispatch/handlers against the documented reset contract (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:601-615`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:411-429`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:420-438`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/usb/usb2otg/usb2otg_core.c:585-601`; `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:589-612`). Deneb/PCIUSB/xHCI perform no port reset and can acknowledge success from current state/software bookkeeping. USB2OTG returns based on the request's `iouh_State` without querying or resetting hardware. Traced Poseidon's root request allocation (`CreateIORequest` uses `MEMF_CLEAR`, `rom/exec/createiorequest.c:62-68`), pipe copy (`poseidon.library.c:4511-4524`), initial reset and fatal error handling (`:4152-4160`), and configuration cleanup (`:7311-7313`); no selected source writes `iouh_State` into the USB2OTG root request, so the initial command returns `UHIOERR_USBOFFLINE`. Poseidon treats only `UHIOERR_HOSTERROR` as fatal at this call site and continues after the offline result (`poseidon.library.c:4152-4160`), so no enumeration failure is claimed; the request nevertheless receives a false-offline status and no reset operation occurs. Expanded OD3654 with the shared no-reset behavior and the concrete USB2OTG caller result. No controller or enumeration was run; source-only.
PCIUSB/xHCI standard CMD_RESET command contract expansion (OD3654 expanded; 2026-10-19): traced both `cmdReset()` handlers through `uhwGetUsbState()` and BeginIO dispatch (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:363-393,pciusb_dev.c:212-214`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:372-402,pcixhci_dev.c:214-216`) against the `CMD_RESET` contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:166-191`). Each handler delays 1 ms, then calls a helper that unconditionally writes `UHSF_OPERATIONAL`; neither resets the controller nor a port. Added these standard-command false-success paths to OD3654 alongside the existing `UHCMD_USBRESET` implementations. USB2OTG `cmdReset()` likewise checks only `iouh_State`, but returns offline for the cleared Poseidon root request; Poseidon ignores `UHIOERR_USBOFFLINE`, so no startup failure is claimed (`usb2otg_core.c:561-577`; `poseidon.library.c:4152-4160`). Deneb's standard `CMD_RESET` does call `uhwHWInit()` and remains excluded here; its failed-init masking is OD3653. No command or reset was run; source-only.
Deneb/Poseidon RTIso free-stop caller census (2026-10-19; no new OD): re-read Poseidon's `psdFreeRTIsoHandler()`/`psdStartRTIso()`/`psdStopRTIso()` and Deneb `cmdRemIsoHandler()`/`cmdStopRTIso()`, then classified every direct `psdFreeRTIsoHandler()` and `psdStopRTIso()` caller in `rom/usb`. USB Audio `subLibFreeAudio()` stops each allocated primary/sibling handler before freeing it; partial `AllocSonixcam()` cleanup frees only handlers never started; `GetVideoSnap()` stops successful starts before `FreeSonixcam()` later releases the handler. Deneb's stop command returns success for a registered handler and does not expose an in-tree failed-stop-before-free path. Poseidon's Free wrapper itself does not update `pd_IOBusyCount`; if an external caller frees an active handler without Stop, that accounting can remain elevated, but no public precondition/documentation establishes whether Free-on-active is supported, so this remains an API-contract lead and is not promoted. No stream, device removal or stop failure was induced; source-only.

AHCI media-monitor task creation and registration wait audit (OD4063 added; 2026-10-19): traced `ahci_RegisterPort()` through its sole readiness signal, `NewCreateTaskA()` failure return, and `ahci_cam_attach()` caller (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:55-71,154-182,338-352`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:260-272`). A failed monitor creation leaves the unit published and the registering caller blocked in `Wait(SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C)`. This is distinct from OD2559's failed port-worker creation and `AP_SIGF_THREAD_SYNC` handshake. The successful-monitor early-exit path remains the separately tracked monitor lifetime candidate; no attempt was made to induce allocation failure. AHCI cam registration and teardown audit remains partial. Source-only.

AHCI media-monitor early-exit lifetime audit (OD4064 added; 2026-10-19): traced startup signaling, timer/message-port/request failure cleanup, retained `sim_Monitor`, CAM probe-failure detach, and Exec task return/reclamation (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:55-71,140-151,171-182,200-219,354-382`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:107,260-272`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:52-56`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:121-151`; `rom/exec/service.c:46-89`). A monitor can signal registration readiness then exit before later detach; Exec's service task reclaims its NewCreateTask allocation, while unregister signals the still-stored non-NULL pointer. Added OD4064 as a conditional stale-task access, distinct from OD4063's failed task creation (which hangs before readiness) and OD2559's port-worker handshake. Timing and failure injection were not tested. AHCI CAM lifecycle coverage remains partial. Source-only.

USB Audio AudioControl graph-flow caller pass (2026-10-19; no additional OD): traced `nFindAudioUnit`/`nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, all four recursive flow helpers, and Stage 2-5 callers (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:782-1034,1413-1595`). The input-array capacity is explicitly limited to eight with a warning before parsing mixer/selector and processing/extension links (`:1424-1468`); downstream selector metadata has the same fixed eight-entry bound, so this is an acknowledged support limit rather than an unreported overflow. Unresolved source IDs remain OD3164; recursion through cyclic graph links remains OD3165. `nFlowDown` reads `nau_InputUnit[0]`, but its selected Stage 5 callers start from output units reachable through an input terminal's recorded output links; a missing source is not connected by `nFindAndConnectAudioUnit`, while an output-terminal missing-source traversal is already OD3164. No independent valid-topology failure established. Descriptor extent, mode registration, and remaining class callers remain open; no descriptor or device was used. Source-only.

USB Audio Feature Unit level-mapping caller audit (OD4065 added; 2026-10-19): traced `nFindLogVolume()` and the GET_MIN/GET_MAX control queries into AHI `AHIDB_Min/Max*` results, `AHIC_OutputVolume` sublibrary dispatch and the worker's SET_CUR conversion (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1313-1367,1764-1790,644-681`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:982-988`). The class advertises 0.0-1.0 Fixed values, then interpolates those values linearly in a Feature Unit's dB range. Cross-checked the selected VIA-AC97 AHI implementation, which advertises 0.0-1.0 and converts linear Fixed amplitude through its dB gain table (`via.c:746-750,801-805`; `misc.c:575-623`). For a -24-to-0 dB endpoint range, 0.5 maps to -12 dB in USB Audio (about 0.25 amplitude) versus the VIA table's nearest -7.5 dB step (gain about 0.42), near the -6.02 dB continuous 0.5-amplitude value. Added OD4065 for the intermediate-level mismatch; this is distinct from OD3202's signed arithmetic overflow on wide ranges and OD3981's cascading Feature Unit controls. Input gain and monitor volume use the same USB conversion. No AHI call or USB control request was made. Broader sublibrary caller and control-range coverage remains open. Source-only.

USB Audio selected-mode, allocation, and rollback pass (2026-10-19; no additional OD): read complete `nSelectAudioMode`, `subLibAllocAudio`, and `subLibFreeAudio` bodies and traced the selected AHI `_AHI_AllocAudioA` failure path (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3134-3653`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:481-520,657,702-742`). The warning-only endpoint bandwidth ceiling with still-selectable over-capacity rates is already OD4056; zero or inconsistent Type I subframe sizing is OD3947; frequency lookup/adaptation behavior is covered by OD3207/OD3208; ignored RTIso start failure remains OD3174. AHI invokes FreeAudio on suballocation failure, and the examined cleanup closes the class-owned pipe, timer, buffers, RTIso handler and Poseidon reference, including partial sibling setup. `nSelectAudioMode` failure after changing the alternate interface reaches FreeAudio, which restores `nam_ZeroBWIF` when one was recorded; no distinct rollback defect established in this path. Exact-match frequency membership and mode-local endpoint parameters were traced, but descriptor-specific controller behavior and external AHI callers remain open. No audio allocation, USB request or device was run. Source-only.

Deneb split-interrupt schedule input/caller cross-check (2026-10-19; no additional OD): traced Poseidon pipe creation’s `UHFF_SPLITTRANS`, hub address/port and endpoint interval propagation into Deneb `uhwScheduleIntPTDs()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4568-4591,4625-4628`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4052-4146`) against the public interval units and split-hub contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:91-111,247-250`; `compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:160-184`). The full/low-speed split branch uses the millisecond interval to choose its start-split microframe and arms the selected PTD’s complete-split mask; the high-speed non-split branch consumes Poseidon’s normalized microframe interval. Did not establish a separate error in this selected interval translation. `UHFF_TT_MULTI` and TT think-time handling remain hardware-specific open questions because the checked ISP1760 PTD definitions expose no matching field; no behavior claim is made without the controller programming contract. No USB schedule or device was run. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary request abort and PTD-pressure requeue pass (2026-10-19; no additional OD): reread `cmdAbortIO`, `devAbortIO`, `TermIO`, `FreeATL/FreeInt/FreeIso`, and the relevant control/bulk/interrupt/iso queue submission and scheduler retry paths (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:800-1005,1602-1867,3957-4530,4778-4834`; `dev.c:520-692`). Every queued transfer clears `IOF_QUICK` before it can remain pending; successful queue removal is completed once by `devAbortIO`/`TermIO`, while PTD-backed cancellation detaches the request before type-specific retirement. The active ATL DMA-abort null dereference remains OD3584; the examined interrupt/ISO retirement paths do not share its DMA cache-post branch. When a scheduler stops for exhausted PTDs or controller-local buffer granules, transfer completion returns those resources and the completion soft interrupt reruns queued schedulers. No separate lost-reply or allocation-pressure stall established in these selected paths. The full ATL error/abort state cross-product and controller DMA stop latency remain open; no request, low-memory condition, or abort was induced. Source-only.

Deneb NODMA transfer-task versus AbortIO ownership pass (OD4066 added, 2026-10-19): followed `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` PIO fallback through the priority-12 worker, `uhwHandleDMAInt()` and active AbortIO retirement (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4251-4321,465-479,4995-5028,1635-1669,1778-1830`; `dev.c:679-686`). `uhwDMATask()` checks `hu_DMAPTD` and calls the handler without protecting that handoff, while the handler dereferences the PTD before its first `Disable`; AbortIO can clear the pointer between the check and call, causing a NULL dereference. A second window after handler entry lets AbortIO retire the PTD before the NODMA copy branch; the resumed handler can see `PTDT_FREE`, choose its copy-from-controller branch, and write through the retained `hu_DMAAddr` after completion. Added OD4066 to the detailed report and AROS index, scoped to `denebusb`/`denebz2usb` (`mmakefile.src:31-45`); DMA-enabled `denebdmausb` remains covered by OD3584. No transfer or schedule was run. Source-only.

eaudio allocation/reallocation accounting pass (2026-10-19; no new OD): compared `AllocateProc()` length parsing and success/error cases with the ROM Paula allocation loop, selected sound datatype, Narrator and Speech channel-map callers, and traced `ReAllocateUnits()`/`_CMD_ABORTIO()` queue accounting. The apparent `ioa_Length & 15` truncation was not promoted: no caller-visible bad result was established for the four-channel mask set and zero-mask behavior. Found that aborting a queued ADCMD_ALLOCATE removes the request but does not decrement `et_allocated` (`audio_commands.c:201-205,2118-2122`); normal reallocation drains by list head, but repeated stale counts can wrap the UWORD and then undercount actual queued requests, leaving requests unexamined after the next release. No request, allocation, or audio backend was run; source-only.

Keeping one waiter while canceling 65,535 other queued requests wraps the stale counter to zero; the next free skips the nonempty queue. The loop clears every bit from `unit`, making the subsequent `if (unit)` false for all valid nonzero requests, so queued requests are not reconsidered after a priority reduction. eaudio stop/start active-write ownership pass (OD4073 added; 2026-10-19): traced caller write ownership from `UnitInitAhi()` through AHI completion, then through `_CMD_STOP()`'s internal abort and `_CMD_START()`'s `StartWaiting()` path (`audio_commands.c:310-339,1094-1113,1619-1632,1658-1663,1738-1747`). No in-tree callers were found for either command. Added OD4075/OD4076 and index entries; no playback or command was run; source-only.

START resumes only by consuming queued writes via `StartWaiting`; no separate mismatch established. Multi-caller scheduling and hardware timing remain source-only open questions. eaudio command-dispatch and priority/metadata handlers full-range recheck (2026-10-19; existing findings retained): reread the complete `process_UnitsCmd()` switch (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:667-735`) and the complete `_CMD_CLEAR`, `_CMD_UPDATE`, `_ADCMD_SETPREC` plus public wrappers (`:2216-2408`), tracing each through `BeginIO` (`libfunctions.c:37-109`) and the selected Paula `ADCMD_NULL`/SETPREC command cases (`arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:218-248,480-512`). CLEAR/UPDATE are validation-only no-ops, matching the Paula null-command behavior; their output masks include only key-matched channels. SETPREC changes priority only on a key match, then checks `unit` after its loop has consumed every bit; for every valid nonzero mask `unit` is zero, so `ReAllocateUnits()` is skipped after priority changes (OD4072). The internal dispatcher receives only BeginIO-recognized commands plus its private ABORTIO/CLOSE messages; no reachable unsupported command falls through the switch. No additional finding. No request or allocation was issued; source-only.

eaudio allocation-wait list mutation and selected-client pass (2026-10-19; OD4070 revalidated, no duplicate): enumerated every `et_allocatelist` insertion/removal and `et_allocated` update (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:201-205,474-505,2118-2121`; field `audio_intern.h:177-178`). eaudio-to-AHI write-error and selected-client completion pass (OD4084 confirmed, 2026-10-19): followed the embedded `AHIST_M8S` AHI request from `UnitInitAhi()` through AHI's queued `CMD_WRITE`, `WriteCmd()`, and `TermIO()` to the reply port (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:310-331,1092-1185`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:82-115,256-297,823-875`). Verified AHI records synchronous `AHIE_HALFDUPLEX` and `AHIE_NOMEM` failures in `ahir_Std.io_Error` and replies the request, while TaskBody ignores that field; finite cycles are completed with `IONOERROR`, and zero-cycle requests resubmit unconditionally. Checked selected Speech and Narrator completion helpers (`speech.c:112-125`; `narrator.c:134-147`), which return failure when WaitIO reports a nonzero request error, so the audio device's success overwrite can mask a status these clients consume. No AHI request, recording conflict, allocation failure, or playback was exercised; source-only.

OD4084 AHI error-retention boundary recheck (2026-10-22; no new OD): re-read `TermIO()` and the entire selected `WriteCmd()` error exit (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:256-297,823-875`). `WriteCmd()` sets `ahir_Std.io_Error` before calling `TermIO()`; `TermIO()` snapshots that value for logging, frees any allocated Extras, and replies without clearing or replacing `io_Error`. On the caller side, the AHI reply message carries the same embedded request back to `TaskBody()`, where cycle bookkeeping runs without testing that field (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:1092-1188`). This rules out AHI cleanup/reply as the source of the missing status and confirms OD4084 is the eaudio consumer defect. No IO request or failure was induced; source-only.

The three findings represent different state transitions. No audio playback or attribute update was run; source-only.

USB Audio bandwidth finding HCD caller recheck (OD4056 strengthened, 2026-10-19): followed the `nOutReqHook()` rate-derived `ubr_Length` into PCIUSB UHCI and OHCI isochronous schedulers (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2641-2672`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_isoch.c:571-603`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ohci/ohci_isoch.c:313-331,431-470`). UHCI caps only at its host-controller ISO maximum before encoding one TD's translation length; it does not enforce the endpoint-specific `iouh_MaxPktSize`. OHCI derives its packet count from that endpoint size and advances the next frame by packet count times interval, spreading an over-capacity one-interval buffer across multiple frames. This strengthens OD4056's consequence from an oversized API request to controller scheduling behavior; it does not add an independent OD. PCIUSB includes both HCD implementations (`rom/usb/pciusb/mmakefile.src:10-17`), and the Sam440 boot menu loads the PCIUSB device (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/menu.lst:51,111`). No descriptor, USB device, controller or audio stream was used. Source-only.

Eaudio CMD_READ zero-key/free-channel caller pass (OD4083 expanded; 2026-10-19): traced the selected BeginIO dispatcher into `audio_READ()` and `_CMD_READ()`, then compared its channel/key checks with ROM Paula `ADCMD_READ_f()` and the public allocation state (`workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:32-35,49-52`; `audio_commands.c:22-37,1819-1857`; `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio.c:108-126,437-454`). A free EUNIT starts with zeroed `eu_allockey`; zero-key reads therefore pass the same equality used by writes, mark a free channel selected and report success. In eaudio an empty channel mask additionally maps through `writechn[0]` to channel 0 and can return NULL data as success. The selected maintained callers found allocate before use; no new maintained trigger was established. Expanded OD4083 instead of duplicating the shared zero-key root. No I/O request was sent; source-only.

The retention is bounded to one buffer per live control and has selected cleanup; no persistent leak finding is supported. AHI Start returns the driver error without immediate stop. No allocation failure, task creation, or audio control was run. Source-only.

eaudio TaskBody bad-key CMD_WRITE reply-lifetime pass (OD4086 added, 2026-10-19): traced each per-channel worker dispatch after GetMsg (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:1051-1089`) into `_CMD_WRITE()`'s mismatched-key completion (`:642-655`). The non-quick branch calls `ReplyMsg()` before returning, but TaskBody then dereferences `ioaudioreq` to obtain `mn_ReplyPort->mp_SigTask` and signals it. On ExecSMP, a client running on another CPU can reuse or release its IOAudio after ReplyMsg and before that dereference; the uniprocessor trigger is withdrawn because the slave priority is 127. Also traced shared-command completion: `TaskBody()` reads `ioa_Request.io_Command` after `process_UnitsCmd()` returns (`:1192-1204`), while wrappers such as `audio_FINISH()` and `audio_FREE()` can ReplyMsg before the worker continues (`:1395-1404,1894-1915`). Added OD4086 as a conditional request-lifetime race covering both post-completion accesses. No request or priority interleaving was run. This focused TaskBody slice is reviewed; the full 2,410-line `audio_commands.c` body and caller cross-product remain incomplete. Source-only.


eaudio STOP/START prefetched-write ownership recheck (OD4073 expanded, 2026-10-19): traced the complete STOP state transition and `StartWaiting()` restart from active/cache/queue occupancy (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:310-339,599-640,1619-1632,1715-1766`). STOP clears active `eu_usingme` but leaves `eu_audioio` and the write queue; START pops a queued write, and `UnitCopyData()` replaces `eu_audioio` before `UnitInitAhi()` starts it. For a channel with active, prefetched and queued writes, STOP loses the active request and START overwrites the cached request, leaving both uncompleted; if there is no queued request, the cache is not restarted. Expanded OD4073 to include cache ownership loss. The sound datatype pause/play caller remains traced; no request sequence or playback was run. Source-only.

Eaudio temporary reply-port signal-target audit (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced every `mp_SigTask` reassignment in `audio_commands.c` through its worker-side signal and restoration (`audio_PERVOL`, `audio_ALLOCATE`, `audio_WRITE`, `audio_ABORTIO`; lines 1460-1478,1998-2027,2038-2058,2145-2167). The caller temporarily routes `STOLEN_SIG` to its own task and clears that task's bit before enqueueing. Concurrent callers using distinct reply ports therefore do not share this field; overlapping use of the same reply port by different tasks could race the temporary recipient assignment, but no selected in-tree shared-port caller or contract requiring cross-task port sharing was established, so this remains unpromoted. Existing OD4074 is the concrete independent race in the global `ts_calltask` slot. No command or concurrency was run; no line credit. Source-only.


OD4088 DoIO/SendIO consequence cross-check (2026-10-19): traced the wrapper's IOF_QUICK-dependent branch against Exec's public callers (`rom/exec/sendio.c:48-57`; `rom/exec/doio.c:50-73`). SendIO initializes flags to zero, so an early stale-bit wake reaches ReplyMsg while the worker-queued request remains linked; ReplyMsg sets NT_REPLYMSG and InternalPutMsg appends the same node without removing the worker-list link (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:63-88`). DoIO initializes IOF_QUICK, so the wrapper returns without ReplyMsg but DoIO sees the bit still set and returns without WaitIO. Expanded OD4088 to cover both premature completion outcomes. No request was submitted; source-only.

HID signed Usage-value shift pass (OD4092 added, 2026-10-19): re-read short-item integer assembly and Global Usage Page composition in `hid_get_item`, then checked the valid high-bit Usage/Page representations against the USB-IF HID Usage Tables. One- and two-byte payloads are sign-extended before Usage Page `<< 16`, and four-byte payload assembly shifts a promoted `UBYTE` by 24, whose sign-bit result is implementation-defined when representable as `unsigned int`; the negative signed Usage Page shift independently remains undefined for valid high-bit pages. Added OD4092 to the detailed report and index. Existing OD3142/OD3143 concern report-field extraction, while OD3145-OD3147 concern bounds/state. No descriptor or device was used; source-only.

Allocation failure produces a NULL request passed to `OpenDevice`, whose body dereferences it; timer open failure leaves `io_Device` NULL, so each `DoIO` returns -1 and the caller nevertheless continues the port power/reset sequence. `OpenUnit` returns the unit regardless; device Open sets success on that non-NULL result (`usb2otg_device.c:468-483`). Added OD4101, distinct from Init rollback leak OD4098. No failure, timer operation, or port reset was induced; source-only.

VIA Rhine S2_DEVICEQUERY short-buffer/caller pass (later consolidated into OD3073, 2026-10-20): re-read the complete command dispatch and `CmdS2DeviceQuery()` (`workbench/devs/networks/via-rhine/handler.c:97-180,273-297`), compared the field offsets in `compiler/include/devices/sana2.h:145-156`, and traced the selected AROSTCP query caller (`if_sana.c:346-350`), which supplies `sizeof(struct Sana2DeviceQuery)`. The handler copies only `min(SizeAvailable, sizeof(...))` then writes BPS, MTU, HardwareType, SizeAvailable and SizeSupplied unconditionally; there is no minimum-size guard, and short `SizeAvailable` therefore leaves later stores outside the advertised buffer. This is the same API-contract defect already tracked for other network drivers; the consolidated OD3073 includes Broadcom4400 and VIA Rhine among its affected implementations. VIA's normal/debug module recipes are available but the architecture/aggregate edges are disabled, so no default-image claim is made. No short-buffer request was issued; no line credit changed because the file body was already credited. Source-only.

ROM USB HID shared SET_REPORT buffer and constant-padding cross-check (2026-10-20; no new OD): followed nReadReports()'s per-report size aggregation and shared endpoint-buffer allocation into nFlushEvents()'s Report ID prefix and both output/feature encoders (hid.class.c:2264-2318,1261-1267,6365-6428). The buffer is sized for the largest report and its initial pool allocation is MEMF_CLEAR (poseidon.library.c:124-125,331-368), but it is reused across different report IDs without clearing each payload. The checked encoder writes only parsed non-constant items; a later report can therefore retain prior payload bits in constant/padding positions. No selected in-tree device contract or observable consequence was established for those constant fields, so this remains a recheck note rather than a finding. OD3911's concrete zero-count encoder overrun is separate. No report or transfer was generated; source-only.

Deneb SET_ADDRESS toggle-base endianness recheck (OD3892 narrowed/confirmed, 2026-10-20): traced Poseidon's `psdPipeSetup()` storing `wValue` with `AROS_WORD2LE()` through the selected Deneb completion handler. On the big-endian m68k target, `wValue >> 3` therefore converts the little-endian in-memory value to `device_address << 5`, matching the 32-entry block used by `devadrep`; this is not an additional wrong-base defect. The remaining OD3892 is precisely the `epnum < 31` bound, which clears offsets 0–30 but leaves offset 31 (endpoint 15 IN) stale. The table is zeroed only at unit allocation, and Poseidon reuses freed addresses. No new finding or line credit. No address assignment or transfer was run; source-only.


Deneb DMA zero-remainder retirement correction (OD4055 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): re-read the exact `DMASM_IN_DONE_HIGH` and `DMASM_IN_DONE_LOW` branches and the `CopyMemShuffle()` loop. A zero remainder is below the DMA threshold, runs a no-iteration copy loop, then reaches `FreeATL()` in both branches (`uhwcmd.c:38-49,5175-5209,5221-5255`). `FreeATL()` clears the active DMA PTD and replies, so the alleged stuck request is not supported. Poseidon AddUSBClasses list, duplicate-name and mutation-lock pass (OD4117/OD4118 added, 2026-10-20): traced the selected `AddUSBClasses` command from its `SYS:Classes/USB` ExAll loop through `psdGetAttrs(PA_ClassList)`, the duplicate check, `psdAddClass()`, and the final `psdClassScan()` (`shellcommands/mmakefile.src:4-19`; `AddUSBClasses.c:86-163`; `poseidon.library.c:5971-6025`). The command compares only `strlen(puc->ln_Name)` bytes against the candidate filename (`:113-134`), so an existing class name that is a strict prefix of a distinct candidate causes the candidate to be skipped; Poseidon's own `psdAddClass()` duplicate test uses exact `FindName` equality (`poseidon.library.c:5720-5728`; `rom/exec/findname.c:76-85`). Added this prefix false-skip to the command's coverage note, conditional on such custom class names. Also confirmed the command's `Forbid()` traversal is not protected against cross-CPU class-list mutation in ExecSMP: `psdRemClass()` removes under PBase write lock and frees the node afterward (`poseidon.library.c:5767-5770,5818-5824`), while Exec documents Forbid as processor-local on SMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`); added OD4117. Separately, `psdAddClass()` checks with `FindName` under local Forbid, releases it, allocates, then enqueues under the PBase write lock, so concurrent same-name calls can both insert; added OD4118. The command is an explicit shell target; no class directory scan, concurrent caller, or device was used. Source-only.

Poseidon PsdErrorlog list-synchronization pass (OD1583 restored, 2026-10-20): matched all three command modes and the complete selected error-message append/remove implementations (`rom/usb/poseidon/shellcommands/PsdErrorlog.c:61-116`; `poseidon.library.c:5832-5900`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:48-60`). PPP buffer-management callback ownership and Open-failure recheck (OD4121 added, 2026-10-20): traced Open, failed-open rollback, BeginIO queueing, Incoming_IP_Packet/SendPacket completion, AROSTCP's Open and per-request BufferManagement propagation, and the selected BT PAN device's per-open BufMan pattern. PPP writes CopyToBuffer into LIBBASE before validating CopyFromBuff; the missing-tag failure decrements the open count but leaves the new callback in place. Queued reads and writes later call those device-global pointers rather than the request's BufferManagement context. AROSTCP uses one tag table and one open, so its selected path does not itself trigger the mismatch; the public device accepts additional opens through its unit/open counters, and a second external opener can expose it. Added OD4121 with the failed-partial-open trigger and successful-incompatible-open variant. The PPP aggregate edge is disabled, so this remains an explicit optional target. This pass earns no whole-file line credit: handler.c and init.c already have body credit. No second open or packet was run; source-only.

PPP multi-open Close/serial ownership trace (OD4122 added, 2026-10-20): followed the successful Open count updates into Close, the CloseSerial macro and EasySerial cleanup, plus AROSTCP sana_down/CloseDevice sequencing and PPP read-queue completion. Two successful opens are accepted and increment unit_OpenCnt, but every Close frees LIBBASE->ser before decrementing the count; the final-close condition is empty. AROSTCP avoids S2_OFFLINE while another device opener remains but still closes its own handle, so PPP closes the shared serial connection while another opener survives. New requests then see ser == NULL; pending Rx_List requests are not completed by CloseSerial. Added OD4122, conditional on the second opener. This is separate from OD4121's per-open callback replacement on failed Open. No multi-open or serial close was run; source-only.

A write queued while suspended wakes the worker, which skips serving it and returns to Wait; CMD_START clears the flag without signaling either waited-on port, so the write can remain queued until an unrelated channel or unit message arrives. Deneb RTIso add/remove pool and caller recheck (OD3889 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced `cmdAddIsoHandler()`/`cmdRemIsoHandler()` through unit initialization and Poseidon's `psdAllocRTIsoHandlerA()`/`psdFreeRTIsoHandler()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1044-1320,386-423`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5555-5627`). Unit initialization seeds 16 free RTIso nodes and 32 free ISO PTDs; add requires a free adjacent PTD pair, removes one node, and consumes the pair while Disable is held; remove clears the RTIso back-links, frees both PTDs, and returns the node in the same critical section. The selected Poseidon allocator restricts this API to ISO endpoints and derives MaxPktSize from the selected endpoint. This rules out a separate reachable empty-node condition in the checked in-tree lifecycle; arbitrary malformed direct low-level requests and hardware register behavior remain open. The off-by-one contiguous-granule scan remains OD3889. No request, allocation failure, or controller operation was run; source-only.


Deneb interrupt dispatch and softint routing pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): reread uhwLevel6Int(), uhwSoftInt(), and uhwNakTimeoutInt() with the DMA worker and bridge/ISP register definitions (arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4774-4994,5265-5401; deneb.h:110-115; isp1760.h:50,96). Confirmed level-6 dispatch acknowledges the Mach status register, routes DMA completion to uhwDMATask, and routes ISP internal status to the soft interrupt/RTIso handler. If bridge DMA and ISP status bits are simultaneous, the early DMA return postpones internal ISP status handling after the bridge W1C write. The local source names both bits but does not specify whether the ISP level reasserts the bridge bit after acknowledgement; therefore no lost-interrupt finding is promoted pending the hardware contract. Softint transfer queues and timer-driven frame-counter extension showed no new source-confirmed issue in this slice. No interrupt or DMA was exercised; source-only.


Deneb split-interrupt interval encoding recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD pending controller-contract confirmation): compared uhwScheduleIntPTDs()'s split branch (arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4052-4081) with Poseidon's speed-specific endpoint interval initialization and propagation (rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8470-8484,8540-8575,4625-4628) and ISP1760 field comments (isp1760.h:375-379). Poseidon preserves raw full-speed bInterval milliseconds and clamps low-speed interrupt intervals to at least 8 ms; Deneb selects encoded values at thresholds 4/8/16/32 and uses the final 16-unit value for all intervals at or above 32. This appears to cap long requested intervals, but the checked-in ISP1760 comment describes the interval field only generally and does not establish the actual cadence mapping for these combined values. The analogous PCIUSB EHCI path chooses periodic-tree QHs from iouh_Interval (rom/usb/pciusb/ehci/ehci_hcd.c:758-765), which is a different controller encoding and does not prove Deneb behavior. Retain this as an open hardware-contract question; do not add an interval defect until the PTD encoding semantics are established. Source-only; no bus or device used.

xHCI endpoint-prepare retry and Poseidon caller pass (OD4128 added, 2026-10-20): traced the new endpoint ring allocation and Configure Endpoint completion error in xhciPrepareEndpoint() into Poseidon's pPrepareHWEndpoint() failure cleanup, then followed a second prepare call. xHCI synchronous command wrapper caller census (2026-10-20; no new OD, no whole-file credit): followed every direct `xhciCmdSubmit()` call and the selected wrappers in `xhci_hw.c:346-479` through callers in `xhci_hcd.c`, `xhci_schedule.c`, and `xhcidevice.c`. Slot enable failure frees the not-yet-submitted device context; Address Device failure attempts Disable Slot but ignores its result before clearing DCBAA and freeing the input context (existing OD4127, conditional on timeout plus failed slot quiescence). Hub-slot Configure Endpoint failure leaves the existing hub context allocated and reports failure. EP0 Evaluate Context failure rebuilds the input context to its prior max-packet size; endpoint Configure failure frees only a newly allocated software endpoint context, while the command input context remains owned by the device. Endpoint Reset and Set TR Dequeue failures return without freeing the ring or device context. This census did not find a separate immediate DMA-context free after timeout beyond OD4127. Command-ring result-slot reuse, concurrent command submissions, and controller recovery remain open; no timeout or controller operation was run. Source-only.

The controller callback is enqueued before BAR-5 mapping and subsequent DMA/port/interrupt setup (`ahci_attach.c:379-409,421-445,536,703`); every later failure reaches `ahci_pci_detach`, which has no `RemResetCallback`, and `bus_pci.c` then calls `ahci_release`, freeing the `device_t` and embedded softc (`:52-59,201-205`; `ahci_intern.h:125,129`). No line credit added, no attach failure or reset was induced; source-only.

PPP serial RX event-loop and teardown caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced the serial request ports through `PPP_Process()` and `CMD_READ_Ready()` (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/init.c:98-120,154-167,259-269`), then rechecked `QueueSerRequest()` and `_CloseSerial()` (`serial.c:191-253`). The process consumes at most one completion from each single outstanding RX/TX request per wake, routes RX `io_Actual` bytes into the PPP decoder, and resubmits after the read completes. An SDCMD_QUERY error marks the serial connection not-OK; the next main-loop pass closes it, while shutdown aborts/waits and drains both request ports before deleting their ports and buffers. The observed SendIO `io_Error` check occurs immediately after asynchronous CMD_READ submission and cannot establish the eventual completion status, but the worker later receives the completion and the next SDCMD_QUERY supplies the existing device-loss check; no separate consequence was established in this pass. This does not resolve device-specific SDCMD_QUERY/CMD_READ contracts or external concurrent control/Close calls. No serial device or request was run; source-only.

PPP OD4135 serial-device consumer-side lifetime confirmation (2026-10-20; no new OD): followed the accepted asynchronous request beyond `SendBYTES()`. The selected `serial.device` `CMD_WRITE` path passes `io_Data` directly to `HIDD_SerialUnit_Write`; if the first call cannot write the whole range, it retains the original request as `su_ActiveWrite` or queues the request (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:449-493,515-543`). The write-empty interrupt handler later indexes `io_Data` by `su_NextToWrite` and performs another HIDD write before replying the IORequest (`serial_interrupthandlers.c:132-178`). Thus no copy is made that would end the caller-buffer lifetime requirement when `SendIO()` returns. Combined with `send_IP_packet()`'s local `struct packet p` and `WritePacket()`'s immediate `TermIO()` after `SendPacket()`, this confirms the OD4135 trigger specifically when serial output is not accepted in the first synchronous HIDD write; complete-first-write timing avoids the dangling period. Source-only; no serial operation run and no line credit added.

It temporarily redirects the reply-port signal task to the current BeginIO caller, queues the request, waits for TaskBody's `STOLEN_SIG`, restores the original task, and only then returns (`audio_commands.c:2038-2058`). Therefore the bad-key `_CMD_WRITE()` `ReplyMsg` followed by TaskBody's per-channel signal is not treated as a normal caller-reuse-before-worker-access trigger. Updated the detailed report, index wording and source ledger; no behavior was run. Source-only.

Network worker signal-exhaustion candidate recheck (OD3106 and OD3671 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): traced Intel Pro/100, Etherlink III, Realtek8180, Rhine, Prism2, and Atheros5000 task allocation through the AROS `AddUnitTask` macro and `NewAddTask()` into each worker's first signal allocations. nForce worker-startup failure contract recheck (OD3056 retained, 2026-10-20): verified the exact `CreateNewProc()` NULL-on-error contract (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:62-70`) and the selected `WaitPort()` loop that waits repeatedly while no message is queued (`rom/exec/waitport.c:62-86`) against `CreateUnit()`'s unconditional process creation and startup wait (`workbench/devs/networks/nForce/unit.c:1093-1106`). On task-creation failure the worker cannot send the handshake, and the caller has no failure branch to clean up or return; this confirms the existing constructor-hang candidate. Kept it within OD3056, shared with PCNet32 and SiS900; no separate ID. No allocation or worker startup was induced; no source-line credit added. Source-only.


PCNet32 worker signal-exhaustion candidate recheck (OD3057 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): traced `CreateNewProcTags()` through the DOS process startup and counted child-task signal use before the shutdown `Wait` loop. The fresh process uses Exec's default `TaskSigAlloc == 0xffff`, leaving sixteen user signal bits (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:68-69,543-550`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-252`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The worker creates three message ports (reply, input and timer) before four private `AllocSignal(-1)` calls, and the module contains no other signal allocation (`workbench/devs/networks/pcnet32/unit.c:954-993`). With all three ports successfully created, at most seven of sixteen user bits are consumed; the unchecked failure return is therefore not reachable through this selected startup path. Withdrew OD3057 from the report/index. OD3056's independent process-start handshake failure and OD3083-style signal number/mask mismatches in other drivers are unaffected. No worker or signal operation was run; source-only.


SiS900 worker-signal availability recheck (OD3089 narrowed, 2026-10-20): followed `CreateNewProcTags()` from `CreateUnit()` to the worker and counted all task-local signal allocations before `Wait` (`workbench/devs/networks/sis900/unit.c:698-737,953-964`). The new DOS process receives the default sixteen user signal bits; the worker first creates reply, input and timer ports, then allocates four private signals, with no other direct signal or message-port allocations in the module (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:68-69,543-550`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:250-252`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). With all three ports created, at most seven of sixteen bits are consumed, so the unchecked -1 path is not reachable through this selected startup. Retained OD3089 for the independent bit-number/one-hot-mask mismatch and free-before-worker-exit ordering; removed signal exhaustion and its proposed allocation-failure fix from the detailed wording. No process or signal operation was run; source-only.


Network worker signal exhaustion candidate correction (2026-10-20): removed OD3098 and OD3103 from the active report and index. RTL816x creates a fresh DOS worker with the default `tc_SigAlloc=0xffff`; its two message ports and four private signals consume six of sixteen user signals, so the three later allocations cannot fail from exhaustion in that startup path (`rtl816x/unit.c:628-646`; `prepareexecbase.c:319`; `newaddtask.c:249-251`). Broadcom4400 creates its unit task through `NewAddTask` (`task.h:57-61`; `unit.c:335`), which installs the default signal mask when `tc_SigAlloc` is zero; `UnitTask` then allocates its signal in that task (`unit.c:1982-1999`), so exhaustion is likewise unsupported by the selected startup path. Corrected the network signal inventory's active findings list accordingly.

E1000 shutdown signal correction (2026-10-20): merged OD3017 into OD2436, removed duplicate OD3017 from report/index, and narrowed OD2436. On a fresh scheduler task, three ports consume bits 16-18 and the four private allocations succeed at 19-22; raw Signal(19) does not wake a Wait on bits 16-22, and `recvd & 19` cannot match those awaited bits. The additional signal-exhaustion claim was removed. The independent no-join/free-before-worker-exit defect remains. Historical checkpoints above retain their original dated claims and are superseded by this correction.

OD3773 withdrawn after Bluetooth pool-flag audit (2026-10-20): the earlier claim that `btGetStringChunk()` and BTHID action strings may be unterminated was based on treating `AllocPooled()` as non-clearing. The Bluetooth library creates `bt_MemPool` with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:95`), `btAllocVec()` allocates all these buffers from that pool (`:269-299`), and Exec `AllocPooled()` passes the pool requirements into `InternalAllocPooled()` (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:87-93`), whose allocator clears the allocated block when `MEMF_CLEAR` is set (`rom/exec/memory.c:661-673`). Thus `bGetStringChunk()`'s extra `len+1` byte is zero; for BTHID's fixed-capacity `strncpy`, the destination's final byte is zero even when the copy count omits the source terminator. This invalidates the reported core C-string overread, BTHID short-source overread, and proposed long-string destination-boundary consequence. Removed OD3773 from the detailed report and `AROS.md`; prior ledger entries are superseded by this correction. No config was loaded. Source-only.

RPi HDMI playback worker/IRQ lifetime recheck (OD4001 strengthened, 2026-10-20): followed `_AHIsub_Stop()` through worker signaling/wait, `KrnRemIRQHandler()`, DMA stop and buffer cleanup (`rpihdmi-main.c:314-345`) against the worker's `Forbid(); slavetask=NULL; barrier; Signal(master);` exit sequence (`rpihdmi-playslave.c:181-194`) and the IRQ handler's unsynchronized task-field check/use (`rpihdmi-dma.c:187-206). Cross-checked Exec/kernel semantics: Exec documents Forbid as local-CPU-only under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`); IRQ dispatch holds the shared read lock during callbacks (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:120-142`), and KrnRemIRQHandler acquires its write side before unlink/free (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:59-75`). Because the driver waits for task exit before taking that write lock, handler removal does not pin the Process during the earlier worker shutdown. The callback does not explicitly copy the field; its concurrent check/use can race the clear, with stale-pointer or NULL manifestation depending on the load reaching Signal. Task memory is queued for asynchronous cleanup as RemTask marks it invalid (`rom/exec/remtask.c:109-163`; `rom/exec/service.c:37-90`). OD4001 remains supported and scoped to an ExecSMP cross-core overlap; no task/IRQ interleaving was run. The shared Exec task/Signal sources were also compared with EK832: that finding concerns queued async IPI raw-pointer lifetime, while OD4001's window exists before the IRQ callback enters Signal and no Signal IPI has yet been committed. No duplicate Exec finding added. No source line credit for driver bodies; broader driver caller/configuration and hardware timing checks remain open. Source-only.

CMI8738 IRQ-registration caller pass (OD3059 expanded; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced `ahi_pci_add_intserver()` through Exec `AddIntServer()` and kernel `KrnAddIRQHandler()` into CMI card publication and expunge cleanup (`CMI8738/pci_aros.c:280-305`; `misc.c:268-271,325-353`; `rom/exec/addintserver.c:62-67`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:75-115`; `rom/exec/remintserver.c:51-55`; `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-57`). `KrnAddIRQHandler()` can return NULL on allocation failure; AddIntServer stores that token in `is_Node.ln_Succ` but has no result, and the CMI wrapper unconditionally sets its global flag/returns TRUE. Card init then marks the card ready, and cleanup later sends the NULL token through RemIntServer to the generic remover, which reads `h->in_nr` before checking `h`. Extended existing OD3059 in both detailed report and `AROS.md`; CMI is selected by the AROS native `HAVE_ASMIO` aggregate; its initializer selects at most one matching device, so the previously suspected shared-flag multi-card cleanup does not apply to CMI. No new ID or line credit; no IRQ allocation failure, audio start, or expunge was induced. Source-only.

Deneb control-transfer scheduler and caller pass (OD3585 confirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-20): read `uhwScheduleCtrlPTDs()` in full (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:3797-3955`) and traced queued submission through `cmdControlXFer()`/device dispatch (`:803-832`; `dev.c:578-580`) and Poseidon `psdDoPipe()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4705-4734`). For a control pipe, Poseidon sets `iouh_Length` and setup `wLength` from the same `len`; Deneb emits SETUP, an optional direction-selected data phase, then the opposite-direction status phase. ATL/PTD exhaustion leaves the request queued; large data stages reserve one free granule and use bounded `ptd_BufLen` continuation chunks, while smaller stages use the per-PTD small ATL region. The rounded longword OUT-data reads in the SETUP completion/continuation path are already OD3585, not a separate issue. The successful path uses one endpoint-busy slot through the final `FreeATL`; no additional scheduler-state or rollback defect was established in the inspected range. No request, transfer or controller was run; no line credit claimed because the function was already within the partial source accounting. Broader Deneb ordinary-transfer, hardware timing and remaining error/reply paths remain open. Source-only.

AHCI TD_ADDCHANGEINT/TD_REMCHANGEINT request reuse audit (OD4150 added, 2026-10-20): checked the AHCI BeginIO list lifecycle against selected in-tree callers and Exec list primitives. AHCI inserts all requests before command dispatch and retains ADDCHANGEINT requests; PFS3, NTFS, and SFS change the command and reuse the same IORequest for REM (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/init.c:383-402`; `rom/filesys/ntfs/main.c:216-222,253-266`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:173-193`). Exec AddHead rewrites the node links without membership checks, and Remove assumes a valid list member (`rom/exec/addhead.c:56-69`; `rom/exec/remove.c:23-34,57-62`). Added OD4150 for list corruption and retained stale request nodes. Existing ATA/SCSI/SDCard implementations add only on ADD and remove the same request on REM (`ata.c:407-428`; `scsi.c:404-425`; `sdcard_device.c:386-407`), corroborating the command contract. No filesystem or device was exercised. This is a targeted AHCI command/caller path pass, not whole-file line credit. Source-only.

AHCI `sim_Flags` lost-update candidate restored as OD2430 (2026-10-20): confirmed both bits share one `ULONG`, while the monitor modifies `SIMF_MediaPresent` under `sim_Lock` and `ahci_cam_changed()` modifies `SIMF_OffLine` without that lock (`ahci_cam_aros.c:114-121,397-412`; `ahci_intern.h:150-154`). AHCI device init/open/close caller recheck (2026-10-20; OD2875 reconfirmed, no new finding): re-traced `AHCI_Init`, `AHCI_Open`, and `AHCI_Close` (`ahci_init.c:80-197,200-256`) against `OpenDevice` and `ahci_UnregisterPort`. Open walks `ahci_Units` and increments `sim_UseCount` only after finding a node; Close decrements it; unregister waits for the count only after it has obtained the unit pointer. The Exec OpenDevice system lock protects the global device list, not this private unit list, so concurrent open versus unregister/free remains the already documented OD2875 ExecSMP race. Init's explicit failure paths close Utility and unwind the pool/attribute bases as recorded in the file row; no additional reachable init/rollback defect was established in this pass. This confirms a narrow caller path and does not supersede broader AHCI lifecycle gaps or add whole-file line credit. No open, detach, or init failure was run. Source-only.

AHCI NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY supported-command pointer audit (OD4151 added, 2026-10-20): `BeginIO()` declares `NSDSupported` locally and returns its address through `NSDeviceQueryResult.SupportedCommands` (`ahci_io.c:190-221,254-265`). The selected NTFS caller issues synchronous `DoIO` then traverses the returned list after it returns (`workbench/fs/ntfs/disk.c:383-395`; `rom/exec/doio.c:49-73`). Added OD4151 for the dangling pointer and caller-visible post-return read. This parallels, but is separate from, NVMe OD2591 because it is a distinct driver implementation and supported-command table. PC boot device lists include AHCI, while direct `kernel-ahci` module edges are commented in the inspected boot makefiles; the affected configuration is scoped to systems that select/load AHCI. No query or mount was run. This is a targeted BeginIO caller audit, not whole-file line credit. Source-only.

AHCI host/unit numbering audit (2026-10-20; no new candidate): traced `ahci_HostCount` initialization, PCI enumeration callback assignments, successful ownership claim/increment, serial drain of the temporary device list, and per-port `sim_Unit = HostID * 32 + port` (`ahci_init.c:97-100`; `bus_pci.c:71-118,130-176`; `ahci_cam_aros.c:154-171`). Unsupported or already-owned PCI functions return before incrementing the host counter; accepted functions receive the current count, increment once, and are registered from the completed temporary list afterward. Port numbers originate from the bounded AHCI port loop (`ahci.c:309-317`). No duplicate or unbounded unit number was established within this selected single-enumeration path. Concurrent unit open versus unregister remains OD2875; concurrent enumeration/re-entry was not established by the selected init caller. This is a targeted caller-path check, not whole-file credit. No PCI enumeration was run. Source-only.

Deneb RTIso registration/start/stop/release caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced the 16-node free pool and paired PTD allocation at unit setup through `cmdAddIsoHandler`, `cmdStartRTIso`, `cmdStopRTIso`, and `cmdRemIsoHandler` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:405-421,1060-1260,1270-1315,1329-1484,1501-1541`). Add requires an available PTD pair before taking a node; remove clears the handler backlink and both PTD-node references, returns the pair and node to their respective free lists; start and stop find the registered handler under the controller’s single-CPU Disable section. Poseidon increments/decrements `pd_IOBusyCount` only when the hardware command returns success (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5630-5680`). The direct in-tree callers are USB Audio and Sonixcam: active paths stop before free, and Sonixcam’s setup-failure free occurs before its first start; no selected omitted-stop path was established. Reconfirmed OD4140’s distinct duplicate-stop accounting and OD4021’s device-removal/list-lifetime race. No controller register or endpoint schedule was exercised; hardware in-flight retirement and malformed descriptors remain open. This is a targeted lifecycle/caller pass, not full Deneb review or added LOC credit. Source-only.


Deneb RTIso zero-MaxPktSize descriptor and OUT-hook buffer-bound pass (OD4152 added, 2026-10-20): traced Poseidon's endpoint descriptor parsing and RTIso pipe setup through Deneb's `cmdAddIsoHandler()`/`cmdStartRTIso()` and the selected USB Audio OUT hook. A zero endpoint packet size passes the Poseidon ISO path; Deneb rounds it to zero granules and leaves the large-area free map unchanged, but the start path copies hook output and programs its returned transfer length without a bound check. The USB Audio hook derives frame lengths from sample rate/frame size, so a malformed zero-size OUT endpoint can produce a nonzero copy into unreserved ISP buffer RAM; paired PTDs also share the same base. Added OD4152 with the malformed-descriptor and Deneb RTIso conditions explicit. This is a targeted path review, not whole-file credit; other Deneb scheduling, descriptor, and hardware lifecycle paths remain open. No device/controller/audio operation was run. Source-only.


Deneb ordinary high-speed isochronous multiplier contract recheck (OD3884 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): followed Poseidon's parsed `pep_NumTransMuFr` through `psdAllocPipe()` into `UHFF_MULTI_2/3`, then checked `cmdIsoXFer()`, `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()`, and `uhwHandleFinishedIsos()` against the `UHCMD_ISOXFER` contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:441-478`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4534-4548,4607-4627`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:884-917,3008-3150,4532-4774`). Deneb accepts the request but deliberately leaves the high-speed MULT field unset; its comment says the current one-packet buffer path cannot keep up with multiplier endpoints. The request API documents the flags, but this pass did not establish a selected in-tree ordinary ISO caller requiring more than one packet per service interval, nor a distinct transfer-completion failure beyond OD3884's interval scheduling defect. Retain this as an explicit unsupported-capacity lead for direct HCD/API callers, not a separate numbered bug pending stronger caller-visible impact. No device or transfer was run; source-only.

SB128 Stop serialization and deferred-softint recheck (OD2167 retained, no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced the selected generic `AHI_ControlAudioA(AHIC_Play/AHIC_Record=FALSE)` call through its direct `AHIsub_Stop()` dispatch and `AHI_FreeAudio()` through Stop (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:959-970,1008-1014,702-747`). Neither caller drains the Exec softint or wraps the driver Stop call in Disable/Forbid; the public API also says these control tags must not be used from interrupt context (`audioctrl.c:902`). The SB128 Stop path masks/disables hardware and immediately frees DMA/mix storage (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/SB128/sb128hw.c:411-462`), while `CardInterrupt()` queues the embedded callback with `Cause()` after capturing the half-buffer pointer (`interrupt.c:55-86`), and Exec explicitly queues hardware-originated softints for later dispatch (`rom/exec/cause.c:42-101`). This supports OD2167's queued-record callback and in-flight-playback timing; it does not establish a separate defect or an occurrence rate. No AHI control, interrupt, or softint was run. No source-line credit; source-only.

Narrator audio-cancel flag caller recheck (no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced all `nb_Cancel` writers and audio-sink reads in the complete narrator worker path (`workbench/devs/narrator/narrator.c:83-89,110-116,127-145,430-455,492-520,621-627,750-784`; fields are `volatile UBYTE` in `narrator_intern.h:30-32`). Control/reset/flush/close and AbortIO paths publish the flag while holding `nb_Lock`, then signal the worker; the main cancellation predicate `WaitUntilRunning()` reads it under that same lock. `SinkWaitAudio()` and final output-error classification also read it without the lock (`:138,432-433`), but the volatile byte is reloaded and the checked caller path did not establish a deterministic missed-cancel or user-visible misclassification; no race finding is promoted on this evidence. ExecSMP scheduling and memory-model behavior were not exercised. The complete narrator body and selected Say/Speak callers were already credited; this focused flag trace adds no line credit. Source-only.

HDAudio counterpart and legacy ID reconciliation (OD4153 expanded, 2026-10-20): re-read `HDAudio/main.c` and traced the same allocation/stream failure ordering through `AHI_FreeAudio()` and the selected `sound.datatype` error cleanup (`main.c:207-245,256-260,358-375`; `audioctrl.c:718-727,1007-1021`; `dispatch.c:4011-4013,4047-4054`). NVHDMI Start stream-stage failure unwind pass (OD4153 added, 2026-10-20): traced `_AHIsub_Start()` allocation order and both HDA setup failure exits through the selected HDA HIDD wrappers and AHI `ControlAudioA`/`AHI_FreeAudio` paths (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/NVHDMI/main.c:176-212,236-242,277-300`; `hda_hidd.c:473-485`; `workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:804-841,844-899`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:1001-1021,718-727`). Added OD4153: the early errors bypass mix-buffer cleanup, normal Stop is gated by the still-false `is_playing`, and AHIsub FreeAudio does not release the retained mix buffer. The HDA HIDD returns NULL when no output stream is free and unwinds its own partial stream allocations on setup failure; those paths do not own the NVHDMI mix buffer. The NVHDMI body already has full-file credit; this caller/error-path trace adds no LOC credit. No stream or failure was induced. Source-only.

NVHDMI connection-list response format pass (OD4154 added, 2026-10-20): compared the complete `setup_hdmi_codec()` converter/pin scan with Intel HDA Specification §§7.3.3.3 and 7.3.4.11. The spec marks long form in length bit 7, requires an even starting entry index, and returns two 16-bit entries; short form uses an index divisible by four and returns four bytes. NVHDMI masks bit 7, always uses `entry & ~3`, and shifts by `(entry % 4) * 8`, so long-form lists are decoded and selected with the wrong entry/index. The parser runs in both `card_init()` and Start-time route re-selection; added OD4154 with the codec-order condition explicit. Source-only; no codec or display audio was exercised.

Network driver named-worker wait cross-reference (EK799, no new OD, 2026-10-20): rechecked RTL8139, RTL816x and PCNet32 `DeleteUnit` name polls and shutdown cleanup against the updated Exec/Kernel EK799 entry. All three driver bodies and their module recipes already have full-body inventory rows; EK799 captures the shared non-snapshot `FindTask` join risk and remains conditional on ExecSMP scheduling overlap and the driver being built/initialized. Other named calls in this directory are startup-presence checks or PPP stack-launch checks; no additional teardown waiter was found. No driver was run and no source-line credit added. Source-only.

The 4,163-line translation unit remains partially reviewed; other descriptor parsing, negotiation, callback and caller paths remain open. Source-only.

USB Audio unit-control and mode-association follow-up (2026-10-20; OD3172/OD3176 rechecked, no new finding): read `nExamineAudioUnits` stages 5 and the recording/playback sibling matcher (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1580-1926`).
