Deneb control-transfer scheduler pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): read `cmdControlXFer` and the complete `uhwScheduleCtrlPTDs` setup/PTD publication path (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:797-838,3797-3955`) against the selected `dev.c` dispatch and the public USB hardware endpoint/address ranges (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:234-248`). Queue insertion is under Disable/Enable and schedules the soft interrupt; the scheduler serializes the single control endpoint key per device, waits when no ATL PTD or large-transfer granule is free, and removes/publishes a request only after buffer resources are secured. Device address 0-127 and endpoint 0-15 produce a key within the 128*16 control slots. The setup PTD copies the fixed eight-byte setup packet and later completion paths handle data-stage continuation; no independent defect was established in this slice. Existing ATL completion/abort findings remain separately scoped. No transfer, hardware or allocation failure was run; the 5,403-line Deneb translation unit remains partially reviewed. Source-only.


UHCI OD2974 timeout/completion serialization recheck (2026-10-20): re-read both timeout branches and `uhci_FreeTD()` against the interrupt-handler ControlLS/ControlFS/Bulk retirement loops (`uhciclass.c:175-298,777-798,845-866`; `hardware.c:186-224`). Refined the race: the timeout walk is not protected as a whole; `uhci_FreeTD()` reenables local interrupts after changing the allocator bitmap, before the caller advances `p_FirstTD`. A pending USBINT can therefore preempt on the same CPU and retire the chain before the timeout task resumes; ExecSMP adds cross-CPU exposure because Disable is local only. Updated OD2974 and the master index to avoid making SMP a prerequisite. The x86_64-pc SMP boot manifest selects `kernel-package-usb`, while UHCI still requires a matching controller; Sam440's checked PCI460 backend is OHCI-only. No controller, transfer, or interrupt interleaving was run. This is targeted concurrency-path evidence and adds no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Deneb EHCI status acknowledgement contract follow-up (2026-10-20; no OD): re-read `uhwNakTimeoutInt()` alongside `uhwLevel6Int()` and `uhwHWInit()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:117-277,4774-4994,5265-5370`; `isp1760.h:29-30,286-293`). Startup enables `EHSF_TDDONE`, `EHSF_PORTCHANGED`, and `EHSF_FRAMECOUNTOVER`; the NAK timer reads `EHCI_USBSTS`, writes back every asserted bit, and only consumes FRAMECOUNTOVER for counter extension. The level-6 path separately handles ISP PTD-done maps and ISP interrupt-pending bits. This creates a hardware-contract question about whether clearing EHCI USBSTS TDDONE/PORTCHANGED can suppress any needed Deneb event, but the checked-in source does not show how those EHCI status bits relate to ISP1760's independent PTD maps/port-change signals. No lost event or user-visible consequence is established, so no finding is promoted. Controller register behavior and the remainder of the 5,403-line translation unit remain open. No status bit or hardware was exercised. Source-only.


Deneb NODMA CMD_FLUSH versus DMA-task handoff follow-up (OD4066 expanded, 2026-10-20): traced `dev.c`'s `CMD_FLUSH` dispatch into `cmdFlush()`'s active ATL loop and `FreeATL()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:554-557`; `uhwcmd.c:973-1005,1626-1684`). In the NODMA target, FreeATL clears `hu_DMAPTD` and retires the PTD while `uhwDMATask()`'s signal-check/handler handoff remains unprotected; it has no revalidation after the check and the handler dereferences `hu_DMAPTD` before disabling task switches. A higher-priority flush can therefore produce the same NULL-PTD window as AbortIO, or the stale buffer-copy window after handler entry. Expanded OD4066's caller and trigger to include CMD_FLUSH; this is the same shared-state race, not a second ID. No flush, transfer, task schedule or device was exercised. Source-only.

ATA DirectSCSI-to-SCSIEmu caller-path confirmation (OD3010 rechecked, 2026-10-20): read `cmd_DirectScsi()` and the `SCSIEmu()` opcode paths alongside the public `SCSICmd` definition and QuickPart's `QPDisk__Func_IdentifyDrive()` fallback (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:483-505`; `rom/devs/ata/scsiemu.c:51-62,155-216`; `compiler/include/devices/scsidisk.h:21-33`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:88-120`). Packet devices validate minimum/maximum CDB length in `atapi_DirectSCSI()` (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1112-1129`), while ATA direct-access dispatch reaches `SCSIEmu()` without that validation. QuickPart first submits one-byte ATA IDENTIFY, then submits a one-byte SCSI INQUIRY with `scsi_CmdLength=1`; the emulator reads INQUIRY fields at bytes 1, 2 and 4. This independently confirms OD3010's concrete in-tree caller and narrows the contrasted validation behavior by device type. The caller expects its one-byte ATA command to be rejected by the SCSI emulator before falling back; no command was issued and no new finding or line credit was added. Broader direct-SCSI opcode/data-buffer validation and ATA command handlers remain open. Source-only.

ATA TD_GETGEOMETRY contract and caller census (2026-10-20; no new OD): checked the public command definition, ATA's geometry/514-byte branches, and selected in-tree caller lengths (`compiler/include/devices/trackdisk.h:52,79-90`; `rom/devs/ata/ata.c:440-480`; `workbench/c/HDTool/deviceio.c:30-42`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:227-241`; `rom/filesys/cdfs/bcache.c:102-114`; `rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/volume.c:1123-1142`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_volumes.c:323-328`). The public header describes TD_GETGEOMETRY as returning `DriveGeometry`; all selected in-tree callers provide exactly `sizeof(struct DriveGeometry)`. No checked-in caller requests 514 bytes. The ATA-only 514-byte branch copies `DriveIdent` without setting `io_Actual`, but the checked-in API declaration does not define this extended form, so the intended compatibility contract and observable consequence remain unestablished; no finding is promoted. Other implementations vary between minimum-size and exact-size validation, so no length-policy defect is inferred from that comparison. No command was sent; source-only.

TD_REMOVE callback add/delete path across ATA, SCSI, SD-card and USB MassStorage (OD4155 added, 2026-10-20): compared all four `cmd_Remove()` implementations and each selected media-change dispatch (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:315-364`; `rom/devs/scsi/scsi.c:310-361`; `rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_device.c:293-339`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_device.c:64-70`; `storage_task.c:20-36`). Each rejects every request when a callback is already installed, before considering the NULL `io_Data` delete form. Traced the maintained DevTest flow: `test_addremchangeint()` installs a local `Interrupt` using `TD_REMOVE`, then issues a second `TD_REMOVE` with NULL data for deletion (`developer/debug/devtest/devtest.c:3110-3145,3338-3350`); the error leaves the unit pointer set, and later media-change dispatch can call that stale callback if the caller releases its state. Added OD4155 to the report and master index. No device request or media event was run. Source-only.

ATA CMD_UPDATE durability/caller recheck (DISK-010 confirmed, 2026-10-20; no OD duplicate): traced `CMD_UPDATE` through the slow-command mask and bus-task dispatch to `cmd_Update()`, which returns without a device operation (`compiler/include/exec/io.h:46-48`; `rom/devs/ata/ata.c:348-352,768-786,817-839,1127-1160`). Confirmed the ATA command header defines `ATA_FLUSH_CACHE` and `ATA_FLUSH_CACHE_EXT`, while the ATA source has no caller of either opcode (`rom/devs/ata/include/hardware/ata.h:66-67`; source search). Selected AFS, FAT, SFS, PFS3 and NTFS callers submit CMD_UPDATE as their sync step (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:575-587`; `rom/filesys/fat/disk.c:77-87`, `packet.c:451-462`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:54-60`; `rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/disk.c:2237-2248`; `workbench/fs/ntfs/disk.c:338-347`). This confirms the ATA portion of DISK-010; the durability consequence remains conditional on a device retaining acknowledged writes in volatile cache. No command, write or power-loss scenario was run. No new ID or line credit; ATA's remaining command paths and callers stay open. Source-only.

BWFM selected WirelessManager shutdown/close caller recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced `wpa_driver_sana2_deinit()`'s outstanding EAPOL, MLME, and event requests through AbortIO/WaitIO before CloseDevice (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:900-925`). The selected BWFM close hook drains queued per-opener reads and S2_ONEVENT requests under `unit->lock`, removes the opener, releases the lock, then frees it (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1180-1227`); the RX pump holds the same lock while delivering opener reads, preventing free-during-delivery. Its pump/control tasks retain the device library's open count for their lifetime (`bwfm_dev.c:615-644`), so the module base remains resident after ordinary client close. No selected shutdown path was found that frees the opener before its outstanding requests are cancelled or while RX delivery owns the lock. Direct clients' active-I/O-before-CloseDevice contract and other BWFM client lifecycles remain open; no request/task or hardware operation was run. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary bulk large-area allocation caller follow-up (OD3889 expanded, 2026-10-20): compared the bulk fallback scanner with the existing `cmdAddIsoHandler()` scan (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4329-4355,1099-1115`) against the selected nine-granule map (`isp1760.h:150-163`). In both, `cnt = MMAP_TOTAL_GRANULES - memsize` and test-before-decrement omit the terminal legal start. Traced the bulk allocation failure to the `break` before queue removal and reply (`uhwcmd.c:4192-4218,4329-4362`). Eight active one-granule RTIso handlers can leave only granule 8 free; a 128-byte request cannot use the small ATL area and is below the 4096-byte DMA threshold, then the large-area search misses that granule even after reducing its allocation to one and leaves the IORequest queued while those RTIso extents remain held. Expanded OD3889 in the Other Drivers report and master index to cover this shared bound defect and its bulk-stall consequence. No request, allocation pattern, transfer, or hardware was exercised. No whole-file line credit; the 5,403-line Deneb unit remains partial. Source-only.

USB Audio partial mode-registration ownership and unwind follow-up (historical OD4139 candidate; no separate leak candidate, 2026-10-20): traced every playback-mode tag build and `AHI_AddAudioMode()` result through `nAllocAudio()` success publication and `nFreeAudio()` teardown (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1937-1987,2041-2051,2087-2118`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:324-417,507-547`). Each mode receives its deterministic per-unit `nam_AHIModeID` before registration; AHI first removes that ID, then reports FALSE if its database lock or new node allocation fails. USB Audio ignores the result and exposes the task as ready, confirming the missing-mode consequence now retained under OD3248. During later free, `nFreeAudio()` calls `AHI_RemoveAudioMode()` for each nonzero ID; successfully registered earlier modes are removed. The earlier same-ID replacement-loss claim is not established for this USB Audio path: parsed modes receive incrementing IDs at `usbaudio.class.c:1277`, and no collision trigger was found. Partial registration does not establish an additional leaked AHI node or distinct cleanup defect in this path. AHI database failure and class teardown were not induced. This closes only the selected partial-registration teardown question; the 4,163-line USB Audio translation unit and broader descriptor/control/caller audit remain partial. Source-only.


Envy24 reset-callback caller-count correction (OD2743 retained, 2026-10-20): rechecked the full `DriverInit()` enumeration loop after the reset-node lifetime trace (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/driver-init.c:83-105,131-143`). It adds exactly one vendor/device table entry and calls `ahi_pci_find_device()` once per table entry, so this path selects at most the first matching device per library initialization. The function-static callback is therefore not shown being re-enqueued for a second matching card during one init; remove that multi-card overwrite/list-corruption implication. OD2743 remains for the confirmed single-card path: callback registration, missing `RemResetCallback()` in `FreeDriverData()`, freeing the card during common expunge, then later reset dispatch through retained node/code/data. No card, expunge or reset was exercised. Source-only.


Envy24 multi-card candidate audit and withdrawal (OD2745/OD2746 withdrawn, 2026-10-20): compared `DriverInit()` PCI identity setup and loop with `ahi_pci_find_device()` and fixed AHI mode IDs (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/driver-init.c:34-39,83-105,131-143`; `pci_aros.c:80-133`; `ENVY24.s:10,24,38,52`; `main.c:156-168`). The list has one vendor/device entry; the loop performs one search and saves at most its first matching PCI object. Each static mode ID has card-select bits `0x0000f000` equal to zero, and `_AHIsub_AllocAudio()` selects its CardData index from those bits. The current AROS load path therefore creates neither a second CardData entry nor a nonzero-card mode. Withdraw OD2745 (wrong GetAttr card) and OD2746 (shared interrupt removal flag across cards): their two-card triggers are unreachable under the selected caller path, despite local code that would misbehave if a second CardData were supplied. Duplicate identical-board support intent is not established, so no separate first-match omission finding is promoted. OD2743 remains the distinct single-card callback lifetime on expunge. No PCI device or AHI mode was enumerated at runtime. Source-only.

AHI PCI ownership contract and removal-path recheck (OD3745 retained, 2026-10-20): traced the HIDD contract from `EnumDevices()`'s shared-list lock and callback (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-448`) through `PCIDevice::Obtain/Release` owner-lock semantics and `AddInterrupt/RemoveInterrupt` delegation (`pcideviceclass.c:401-406,445-459,488-560`; `pcidriverclass.c:279-289`). `AddInterrupt` only calls the backend IRQ registration method; it does not set `Owner` or increment a lifetime count. `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver()` takes the exclusive list lock, rejects only matching devices with nonzero `Owner`, then removes and disposes the rest (`pciclass.c:451-516`). The PCI source itself says missing ownership makes driver removal dangerous and its interrupt accounting is not implemented (`pciclass.c:470-486`). Rechecked all six AHI adapters covered by OD3745 (Envy24, Envy24HT, EMU10kx, CMI8738, SB128, VIA-AC97): none calls Obtain/Release; HDAudio and NVHDMI are excluded because their callbacks claim devices. Deneb RTIso Start/Stop restart-state and direct-caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): read `cmdStartRTIso()` and `cmdStopRTIso()` in full (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1329-1540`) against `IOUsbHWRTIso`/`IOUsbHWBufferReq` hook contracts (`compiler/include/devices/usbhardware.h:90-113`) and every maintained `psdStartRTIso()`/`psdStopRTIso()` caller. Start reassigns both PTD frame positions, reconstructs output transfer lengths from the hook, and publishes both PTDs under the same single-CPU Disable section; Stop removes both from the active mask and clears their active status while retaining the alternating cursor for a later restart. The cursor is initially zero because `DenebUnit` is allocated with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`uhwcmd.c:335`), and its value after a stop is either valid slot 0 or 1. Sonixcam pairs each successful start with stop; USB Audio handles failures from these calls incompletely in existing OD3174/OD4140 scopes. Repeated Start/Stop accounting remains OD4140; no separate PTD restart-state defect established in these paths. No hardware, stream, or start/stop sequence was run; no whole-file line credit because these functions are already within the explicitly partial 5,403-line translation-unit accounting. Source-only.

Deneb ordinary ISO buffer-release rescheduling pass (OD4157 added, 2026-10-20): re-read the complete ordinary `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()` allocation-failure path, `FreeIso()`, `cmdRemIsoHandler()`, `uhwSoftInt()`, and the level-6 RTIso completion routing (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1270-1313,1742-1761,4532-4774,4780-4831,5326-5345`). The ordinary request remains queued when no large-area granule is available; RTIso removal returns its reserved allocation map but does not cause the soft interrupt that retries ordinary requests. RTIso-only done bits are completed inline and do not set `causeit`. Twelve valid 513-byte RTIso handlers can each consume two granules, and an ordinary request can occupy the remaining 25th granule while another queues; removing a handler frees capacity. Added OD4157 for the conditional missing-reschedule path. Other completions or new submissions can incidentally retry the queue, so the indefinite wait requires the stated lack of another trigger. No transfer, handler pool or hardware was exercised; no whole-file line credit because Deneb `uhwcmd.c` remains explicitly partial. Source-only.

Deneb ATL bulk-IN/OUT DMA completion state recheck (OD3585/OD3584/OD4066 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-20): re-read the data-IN and data-OUT completion state transitions in `uhwHandleFinishedATLs()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2124-2475`) against the scheduler's DMA setup and buffer extents (`:4192-4530`) plus `FreeATL()` cache/reply order (`:1626-1684`). Deneb bulk OUT word-copy bounds recheck (OD3585 confirmed, 2026-10-20): traced the ordinary bulk scheduler's small-buffer PIO OUT copy plus the `CopyMemShuffle()` implementation under the selected AROS build (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:37-44,4254-4277,4404-4409`) against the documented bulk request byte-count contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:197-206,240-246`). The AROS helper copies only `size >> 2` words, but the caller rounds `ptd_BufLen` up to a multiple of four before passing it; for any non-multiple-of-four PIO OUT chunk, that reads the final one to three bytes beyond the declared data extent. This confirms the existing OD3585 and does not warrant a duplicate finding. The bulk OUT continuation path applies the same rounding at `uhwcmd.c:2498-2505`. No request was run; no whole-file credit because `uhwcmd.c` remains partial. Source-only.

Deneb zero-length bulk request reused-PTD state audit (OD4160 added, 2026-10-20): traced `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` through PTD allocation and unconditional DW0 length encoding, `FreeATL()` teardown, and bulk OUT completion accounting (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4239-4255,4329-4409,4381-4385,1635-1670,2477-2480`) against the documented bulk transfer byte-count contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:197-206,240-246`) and Poseidon's `psdDoPipe()` caller (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4620-4627,4708-4725`). A zero-length request bypasses the only `ptd_BufLen` initialization, while `FreeATL()` retains the previous slot value; Poseidon forwards its `len` argument directly for bulk endpoints, making zero-length requests reachable through the in-tree caller. Reuse after a nonzero transfer therefore encodes stale length into the next hardware PTD, and the OUT completion path adds the reported count to `iouh_Actual` without bounding it by the request length. Added OD4160 to the detailed report and master index. No request or device was exercised; the Deneb translation unit remains partial, with no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Deneb active AbortIO done-map and reply ownership recheck (OD3584/OD4066 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-20): re-read `cmdAbortIO()` through `devAbortIO()` and `TermIO()`, and traced ATL/INT/ISO completion-map collection, PTD retirement, and the next `uhwSoftInt()` pass (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1576-1873,1968-2012,2784-2815,3008-3040,3333-3393,4780-4831,5265-5345`; `dev.c:658-688`). Deneb high-speed ISO continuation cadence pass (OD4164 added, 2026-10-20): resolved the earlier hardware-frame-selector question using the selected USBHardware contract and checked-in ISP1760 PTD definitions (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:111-113`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8525-8548`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/isp1760.h:375-379,417-420`). Poseidon supplies high-speed ISO intervals in power-of-two microframes. Deneb's initial scheduler puts the requested frame in DW2 and microframe activity in DW4; continuation calculates the next requested frame by adding `ceil(interval/8)`, but compiles out that DW2 encoding and instead schedules at `EHCI_FRINDEX + 8`, one frame later (`uhwcmd.c:3283-3308`). For intervals above eight microframes, that is earlier than the requested two-or-more-frame gap. Added OD4164, limited to multi-packet high-speed ISO requests with interval >8; the API-field mutation remains the separate OD4163. No controller operation was run, and Deneb `uhwcmd.c` remains partial with no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Deneb ISO frame-zero caller comparison follow-up (OD3890 retained, no new finding, 2026-10-20): re-read `uhwScheduleIsoPTDs()` through PTD activation and its `uhwSoftInt()` caller, then compared selected PCIUSB ISO-frame initialization (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:4532-4780,4780-4842`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ehci/ehci_isoch.c:390-439`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_isoch.c:250-310`; `rom/usb/pciusb/ohci/ohci_isoch.c:240-290`). The selected EHCI/UHCI/OHCI paths instead interpret zero as unspecified and choose a future frame with lead time. This reinforces OD3890’s trigger but does not settle whether the ISP1760 waits for modulo-32 recurrence or retires a missed frame: the checked-in PTD comments identify frame-number bits but not missed-frame behavior. Generic PCI delayed-claim contract evidence (OD3885 retained/strengthened, 2026-10-20): checked the public `HIDD_PCI_EnumDevices()` method text and `HIDD_PCIDevice_Obtain()` contract against the removal implementation. Enumeration promises a callback for each device but gives no callback-only ownership requirement; `Obtain` is documented as the exclusive-use lock. More directly, `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver()` itself says drivers may defer ownership until after enumeration and calls removal in that state dangerous (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:473-478`). The implementation nevertheless scans Owner under `dev_lock` and disposes after the scan, while Obtain only serializes with `ownerLock` (`:489-512`; `pcideviceclass.c:488-510`). This supports OD3885's delayed-claim/removal overlap as a source-confirmed contract gap; selected in-tree callers claim in the enumeration callback, so impact remains external/public-client conditional. No enumeration or removal was run; no new ID or line credit. Source-only.

AHI CalcSamples low-rate count-bound and caller pass (OD4165 added, 2026-10-20): rechecked `CalcSamples()` against `_AHI_SetFreq()`, `_AHI_SetSound()`, and the selected `Mix()` loop. At 48 kHz mix rate, 1 Hz is quantized to `Add == 0x10000`; a valid 40,000-frame sample produces quotient 2,621,439,999, which narrows to a negative 32-bit `LONG`. `Mix()` then skips the add routine, cannot decrement the count, and never enters its zero-count end-of-sound branch. The public AHI documentation permits 1 Hz playback and describes signed 32-bit sample arrays with ULONG lengths; the example M32S buffer requires 160,000 bytes. Added OD4165 to the detailed report and index. Reconciled eight stale AHI coverage references that named OD2801 (the unrelated Rhine tracker finding) as the sample-count issue; the Rhine report and request-dispatch history retain the genuine OD2801 attribution. No audio or arithmetic execution was performed; source-only.

OD3978 root-hub bitmap synchronization scope expansion (2026-10-20; existing ID retained): reread `uhwCheckRootHubChanges()` against its `xhciCompleteInt`, `xhciIntCode`, and port-task callers (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:1893-1924`; `xhci_hcd.c:2955,3358-3359,3757`; `xhci_hcport.c:515-517,789`) and compared its `Disable()` critical section with ExecSMP semantics (`rom/exec/disable.c:39-60`). NVMe SQ memory-to-doorbell ordering and CQ walker caller recheck (OD2451 restored/expanded, OD2457 confirmed; 2026-10-20): re-read the complete `nvme_hw.c` body and traced admin/I/O submissions through `nvme_submit_cmd`, plus CQ polling from synchronous admin and I/O waits and interrupt-driven controller/bus handlers. OD2457's shared cursor is advanced and published before callback lock release; a second walker can consume and acknowledge later entries while the first retains its old local cursor, then the first can resume from that stale position. Its existing ExecSMP and controller-startup conditions remain. For OD2451, traced SQ allocation to the selected PCIDriver allocators: BCM2711/BCM2712 map queue pages Normal Non-Cacheable; RISC-V PCIDT allocates coherent ordinary memory. In all paths the command copy precedes a volatile doorbell store with no pre-store DMA write barrier; AArch64's GIC sender separately uses `dsb` before its Device SGIR write. Restored OD2451 to the detailed report/index and expanded its target scope; the hardware reordering manifestation remains conditional. No NVMe transfer, interrupt, or race was run. Source-only.

Eaudio `FreeSLAVE` final-close caller pass (OD4068/OD4086 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced the only checked-in `FreeSLAVE()` call from `DevClose()` under the device semaphore (`workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:151-199`) through `audio_CLOSE()`, `_CMD_CLOSE()`, `free_ETask()` and `TaskBody()` (`audio_esys.c:76-81`; `audio_commands.c:745-768,1192-1205,2175-2205`). The stale `global_eta`/deleted-port failure on later task-creation failure is already OD4068; signaling the closer before the worker's post-dispatch command read and possible freed-port reuse is already OD4086. First-open task creation is serialized by the same nested device semaphore, and no additional FreeSLAVE race was established in the selected caller. Updated the file row; no line credit because the source body was already counted. No task, close or failure was induced. Source-only.

Nouveau/VMware synchronous DRM timer deletion and vblank cleanup pass (OD4177 added, 2026-10-20): compared both selected `linux_time.c` copies and timer compatibility headers, then traced timer expiry's `pending = FALSE` write before callback dispatch against `del_timer_sync()`/`timer_delete_sync()` and the in-flight callback path. Nouveau and VMware's `drm_vblank.c` copies are identical; `drm_vblank_init_release()` calls the compatibility synchronous delete before managed vblank state is freed. Traced scheduling into Nouveau NV04's default delayed vblank-disable path and VMware VKMS's selected vblank get/put path, including its guest-setting gate. Added OD4177 for `del_timer_sync()` and selected VMware `hrtimer_cancel()` teardown overlap on ExecSMP; UP overlap is qualified to a teardown task that preempts the priority-21 timer process. The VMware VKMS CRTC cleanup callsite also invokes `hrtimer_cancel()` before `drm_crtc_cleanup()`, leaving its in-flight simulator callback exposed to CRTC/device teardown. Existing OD4046/OD4047 remain separate startup and signal-exhaustion failures. A separate clock-source pass traced `GetSysTime()`/`TR_SETSYSTIME` against AROS `GetUpTime()` and selected Nouveau/VMware timeout callers; added OD4178. This follow-up adds no whole-file line credit. No display, timer, race, teardown or clock change was run. Source-only.

VMware SVGA command-buffer manager full-body pass (OD4183 added, 2026-10-20): read all 1,406 physical lines of `vmwgfx_cmdbuf.c` (776 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`), including queue processing, command-buffer allocation and commit, DMA/MOB pool setup, preemption/error recovery, idle waits and teardown. Traced selected `vmw_fallback_wait()` and overlay stop ioctl callers. Added OD4183: `vmw_cmdbuf_idle()` discards an error from its interruptible `vmw_cmdbuf_cur_flush()` and proceeds to an idle predicate that checks queued/in-flight/error lists but not the still-current command buffer (`:627-648,693-749`). In the selected overlay stop ioctl, a command-reserve failure reaches this wait with `interruptible=true` (`vmwgfx_overlay.c:177-199,422-445`; `vmwgfx_irq.c:153-180`). If a signal interrupts acquisition of `cur_mutex` while another submitter still has committed commands buffered in `man->cur`, the manager can report idle while those commands were never flushed; `vmw_fallback_wait()` may then also observe an idle device and let the overlay retry proceed without the intended ordering barrier. The trigger requires that narrow concurrent-buffered-command and signal-interruption state; no signal, command, or device was exercised. Crediting 776 lines and one full-body path moves the represented checkpoint from 153,513/270,754 to 154,289/270,754 (56.98%) and 545/598 to 546/598 paths (91.30%). Denominator carried forward, not a refreshed build-selected source census. Source-only.

BTCore L2CAP Configure Request continuation/caller pass (OD4232 added, 2026-10-20): traced the parser's retained `flags` field into `handle_configure_request()`, its fixed-zero Configure Response, inbound-complete transition, subsequent CONFIG-state gate, and selected `bluetooth.device` channel-manager use (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/l2cap/signaling.c:184-201`; `channel_manager.c:283-320,493-517`; production path previously traced at `hwconn.c:701-719,736-753`). Compared with Bluetooth Core 6.2 L2CAP §4.4: a continued request is a valid multi-packet configuration; each request fragment requires a response whose continuation state reflects the request, and only the final request completes the configuration event. Added OD4232: if outbound configuration has already completed, this implementation can mark inbound configuration complete and open on the first fragment; it then silently drops later fragments after the state becomes OPEN. This is separate from OD3962's unsupported mandatory option handling and OD3963's outbound MTU enforcement. No line credit (the signaling and manager bodies were already credited); no peer or packet was used. Source-only.

BTCore L2CAP Configure Response continuation follow-up (OD4232 expanded, 2026-10-20): reread `bt_l2cap_sig_parse_configure_response()` and `handle_configure_response()` against the response continuation rules in Core 6.2 L2CAP §§4.4-4.5 (`signaling.c:237-257`; `channel_manager.c:323-352`). A continued response requires the requester to issue null-option Configure Requests until the peer sends a response with continuation cleared. This manager instead clears the pending identifier, sets `outbound_config_done`, and may open the channel; it sends no follow-up request, so later responses cannot match the cleared identifier. Folded this into OD4232's same unsupported continuation-state handling, alongside the already traced inbound request-fragment case; no duplicate finding added. The documented single-round-trip limitation explains absent negotiation loops but does not make the current success/open transition accurately handle the peer's valid continuation. No line credit; no peer or packet was used. Source-only.

CAMD USB-MIDI OpenPort failure-contract recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced the embedded driver's `OpenPort` callback through `usbCAMDOpenPort()` and CAMD's `OpenDriver()` result handling (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c:139-159`; `camdusbmidi.class.c:387-431`; `workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:24-58`). A no-device or adapter-buffer allocation failure returns NULL from `usbCAMDOpenPort`; the embedded wrapper then forms `&CAMDPortBases[portnum]->ca_ActivateFunc`. `ca_ActivateFunc` is the first `CAMDAdapter` field (`camdusbmidi.h:18-21`), so the source does not establish a distinct non-NULL invalid `MidiPortData` value on the selected targets; CAMD's caller explicitly treats NULL as an OpenPort failure and unwinds its receiver process. No separate finding promoted. The broader multi-port output-buffer bound in OD4234 was rechecked against all event-emission cases in `nParseMidiOut()` (`camdusbmidi.class.c:518-733`): each successful event increments shared `goodpkt` once and emits one four-byte packet; after one port reaches 2,040, each later nonempty port can emit once before its loop condition is tested. This supports the existing 2,055-packet upper bound across 16 ports. No build, MIDI stream, device or allocation failure was exercised; source-only.

Paula eaudio ADCMD_WAITCYCLE completion recheck (OD4071 retained, 2026-10-20): reread the public command dispatch and synchronous wrapper (`workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:106-109`; `audio_commands.c:1510-1535`) against `process_UnitsCmd()` dispatch, `_ADCMD_WAITCYCLE()`, `ReplyWaitCycles()`, and `FlushUnit()` (`audio_commands.c:667-693,395-402,1187,1491-1501,1544-1584`). The active-playback branch clears `IOF_QUICK`, changes the unit mask, signals the wrapper, and returns without adding the request to `eu_waitcyclelist`; the wrapper then intentionally withholds `ReplyMsg()` while that mask remains changed. Neither cycle completion nor FlushUnit can find this request. The no-active-playback branch changes the mask back and allows the wrapper to reply, so the finding stays limited to active playback. The device README says external WAITCYCLE use was rarely tested and only tested by the device's own program (`audio.device_readme:73-75,232-239`); no maintained direct caller or runtime path established. No report text change or new ID; no audio request was run. Source-only.

Deneb timer and hardware initialization full-function pass (OD3653/OD4158 rechecked; no new OD, 2026-10-20): read complete `uhwOpenTimer()`, `uhwDelayMS()`, `uhwCloseTimer()`, and `uhwHWInit()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:65-267`), then traced every `uhwHWInit()` call into `Open_Unit()` and `cmdReset()` (`:453-484,560-585`) plus `devOpen()` success propagation (`dev.c:310-326`). Timer message-port/request/device cleanup is paired across the checked success and failure paths; `uhwDelayMS()` is only called after successful timer setup in these two paths. `uhwHWInit()` returns host error for either root-port polling timeout, but `Open_Unit()` ignores the result and continues task startup, while `cmdReset()` ignores it and reports from current port state; these are already the OD3653 initialization-error behavior. `cmdUsbReset()` remains the separately documented state-only reset defect OD4158. The run-state and configured-bit readbacks only log failures, but the checked caller/state paths did not establish an independent defect from the existing OD3653 trigger. No controller, timer, open, reset, or timeout was exercised; `uhwcmd.c` remains partial and earns no whole-file line credit. Source-only.


Deneb `Open_Unit()`/`Close_Unit()` full-function and `devOpen()`/`devClose()` caller pass (OD3581/OD3582/OD3653/OD4161/OD4229 rechecked; no new OD, 2026-10-20): read both complete unit lifecycle functions (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:281-525`) and traced the driver entry/close callers (`dev.c:281-326,351-383`). Confirmed the range check permits index `MAXUNITS` before accessing the `hd_Units[MAXUNITS]` array (OD4161); `Open_Unit()` calls the embedded worker `AddTask()` without checking its nullable result before publishing the unit (OD3581); the board/slot and timer failure cleanup is otherwise paired through the examined failure labels; CPU detection retains the precedence defect limited to the returned description flag (OD4229); and the `uhwHWInit()` return is ignored before open succeeds (OD3653). `Close_Unit()` disables hardware and timer activity, signals the worker, waits a fixed delay, then frees the unit without a termination handshake (OD3582). `cmdUsbReset()` is separately OD4158; it does not share the startup initialization issue. These existing findings cover the distinct supported paths found here; no additional independent failure was established. Unit arguments, task failures, board access, close timing, and hardware were not exercised. `uhwcmd.c` remains partial; no full translation-unit line credit. Source-only.


ATA timer helper manifest and caller reconciliation (OD3681/EK8800 rechecked, 2026-10-20): checked `ATA_DEVICEFILES` against the coverage rows and found that `timer.c` and `waitto.c` had been discussed in the OD3681 ledger text but lacked individual file rows. Read both complete bodies (49 and 38 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) and traced `ata_OpenTimer()` callers in the controller daemon, `BusTaskCode()`, and `ata_InitBus()`. The daemon signals startup failure on NULL; `ata_InitBus()` guards the timer and skips scan; `BusTaskCode()` stores NULL without checking it, then the selected `ata_setup_unit()`/`ata_WaitBusyTO()` route calls `ata_WaitTO()` before releasing `DetectionSem`, confirming existing OD3681. `ata_WaitTO()` always waits for any submitted timer I/O to complete before return, but its signed `1 << mp_SigBit` expression can reach bit 31 from `CreateMsgPort()` automatic allocation; this is the same source-language condition tracked under EK8800, not a separate finding. SCSI's similarly named helper files are defined by `kernel-scsi` but no reviewed platform parent selects that module; the Exec ledger already excludes this unselected target. The SD-card timer row already exists at `:5137`; `sdcard_WaitTO()` has no maintained caller, while the bus task retains its opened timer for its worker lifetime. No new issue established beyond OD3681/EK8800, and no signal exhaustion, allocation failure, timer operation, or device scan was run. Source-only.


ATA manifest helper and controller-startup recheck (OD2573/OD2574 restored; OD2995/OD3681 cross-checked, 2026-10-20): compared all ten `ATA_DEVICEFILES` entries with the coverage table. `waitnano.c` and `bootwait.c` were selected but lacked individual Other Drivers file rows; full bodies and relevant callers were read and rows added. Rechecked the controller class against `OOP_NewObject()` and Root allocation: if `NewCreateTask()` itself fails, the class New method returns FALSE and the wrapper returns that result without disposing the already allocated Root instance, restoring OD2573. If the task starts but its timer open or calibration fails, `DaemonCode()` signals the parent before setting `ac_Daemon`; the constructor accepts that signal and publishes the controller, and later disposal calls `Signal(NULL)`, restoring OD2574. The m68k/PC-specific selected caller paths and expunge disposer are traced in the detailed entries. The ATA bootwait and bus-worker timeout failures remain OD2995/OD3681; no duplicate was created. No task, timer, controller, or boot was run. Source-only.

USB Audio unsupported AHI sound/effect hook and generic fallback pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): read the complete `subLibSetVol`, `subLibSetFreq`, `subLibSetSound`, `subLibSetEffect`, `subLibLoadSound`, and `subLibUnloadSound` stubs (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3813-3893`) and traced the three less-covered effect/sample callbacks through AHI's selected generic wrappers (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/sound.c:665-708,866-913,975-998`). Each USB Audio stub returns the documented `AHIS_UNKNOWN` fallback value without modifying driver state; for mixing audio, `_AHI_SetEffect` and `_AHI_LoadSound` perform the generic software implementation, and `_AHI_UnloadSound` clears the generic sound type. The wrappers intentionally return the subdriver result when `AHIACF_NOMIXING` is set; no evidence in this selected path showed USB Audio returning that value as a class-specific capability. No separate hook defect established. No audio object or sample was used; the 4,163-line class remains partial and this pass earns no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

USB Audio `subLibGetAttr()` full-switch and AHI mode-info caller pass (OD3172/OD3176/OD3207 rechecked; no new OD, 2026-10-20): read the entire attribute switch (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3895-4080`) and traced frequency, input/output, volume and capability attributes through AHI's `AHI_GetAudioAttrsA` mode-info switch (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:440-545`) and its documented index ranges (`:290-306`). `AHIDB_Frequency` uses the caller's index directly and input/output selectors likewise rely on documented valid indexes; no selected AHI caller was found passing an out-of-range index. The zero-frequency mode path where AHI computes `count-1` and `subLibGetAttr` indexes the array remains OD3172; `AHIDB_Index`'s fixed 100-kHz nearest-match threshold remains OD3207; corrupted fallback output counts/names remain OD3176. This closes the complete GetAttr switch and selected generic caller only; the 4,163-line USB Audio translation unit and broader AHI client review remain partial. Source-only.

OD4130 selected multi-interface reachability follow-up (2026-10-20): verified that the default ARM package selects `USB/massstorage` and `USB2OTG`; Poseidon scans and binds each interface in the active configuration, the mass-storage class accepts CBI per interface and starts a worker for each binding, and the CBI data phase calls `psdSendPipe()` on the interrupt status pipe (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:182-189`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6388-6445`; `rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:211-255,645-661`; `massstorage_cbi.c:210-217`). Thus the selected class paths can supply more than 128 requests with a composite-device population under the 127-address cap; an illustrative source-level configuration is 65 devices with two CBI interfaces each. No checked-in firmware/device topology or NAK/interval schedule establishes an actual instance, so OD4130 remains conditional. Updated detailed report and index; no request or hardware was used.

USB2OTG periodic-promotion ring ownership check (OD4130 follow-up, 2026-10-20; no new finding): searched every hu_PromRingF/D/Dev/Pos reference. SOF and watchdog paths write the eight-slot ring, while the only reader formats recent entries in watchdog diagnostics (`usb2otg_intr.c:967-970,3571-3574,3757-3764`). `usb2otg_process_pending()` schedules from `hu_IntXFerScheduled` and never consumes ring entries (`:2706-2790`), so wraparound in the diagnostic ring cannot discard scheduled requests. The distinct 128-node list-walk cutoff remains OD4130. No IRQ or scheduler was run; source-only.

USB2OTG FinishedXfers drain-bound reachability recheck (2026-10-20; no new finding): enumerated every producer of hu_FinishedXfers in usb2otg_intr.c, usb2otg_schedule.c and usb2otg_intern.h. IRQ and watchdog completions claim/clear a specific hu_Channel entry; SetupChannel setup failures are reached only from ScheduleCtrlTDs (one channel), ScheduleBulkTDs (two iterations), and ScheduleIntTDs (the finite periodic channel range). The unit exposes exactly eight hu_Channel entries (usb2otg_intern.h:277,541-549); each claimed channel has at most one hc_Request, and each normal completion path transfers that request to FinishedXfers once. Thus a valid non-corrupt queue is bounded by the eight hardware channels per dispatch phase, far below the 2048 drain guard in usb2otg_process_pending() (`usb2otg_intr.c:2725-2760`). The guard's remaining purpose is protection from corrupted/multi-node cyclic list state; leaving more than 2048 entries after its break is not a normal supported workload. Withdraw the earlier tentative backlog concern: no separate defect or candidate is retained. No queue corruption or completion was induced; source-only.

USB Audio Type I mode descriptor parser and endpoint-input recheck (OD3168-OD3173 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): reread all of nExamineAudioDescriptors() (rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1038-1311) and traced its psdFindDescriptor results and endpoint attributes into mode publication and nSelectAudioMode (:1190-1290,1929-1987,3134-3168; Poseidon endpoint construction rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:8467-8561). The unchecked AudioControl collection count, variable Type I rate bytes, accepted frame-width mismatch, over-limit/empty frequency cases, and high-speed interval-unit conversion all match OD3168-OD3173/OD3947; no separate parser-path defect was established. In particular, Poseidon normalizes a zero SuperSpeed isochronous interval to one before converting it to service intervals, so the USB Audio bandwidth divisor is not zero from that endpoint field on the selected parser path. Missing zero-bandwidth alternates remain OD3361, and RTIso start failures remain OD3174. This closes the Type I descriptor-body slice only; the 4,163-line class, additional malformed descriptor forms, external device descriptors, and broader AHI callers remain partial. No descriptor, device, mode, or transfer was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage CopyMemQuick per-chunk length-contract recheck (OD3787 expanded; OD3798 retained separately, 2026-10-20): reread nRead64Emul/nWrite64Emul and trace the block-size source through READ CAPACITY and the request fallback (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:2061-2071,2646-2880,2900-2915,3058-3087`). The top-level length/offset checks require 512-byte alignment, but each emulation copy clamps datalen by ncm_BlockSize - insideblockoffset and performs no four-byte tail copy. With an accepted 513-byte block size, a 512-byte request at offset 512 reaches 1-byte and 511-byte CopyMemQuick calls; generic and selected m68k implementations copy only full ULONGs, so those chunks lose bytes even with aligned pointers. This is the length-contract branch of OD3787, distinct from its unchecked io_Data alignment branch and OD3798’s separate non-power-of-two LBA/offset conversion. No SCSI device, request or copy was run; source-only.

OD3787 caller-alignment evidence qualification (2026-10-20): checked the pointer type used by the affected ordinary read/write path. The destination/source is IOStdReq.io_Data (APTR, compiler/include/exec/io.h:29-42); the earlier citation to SCSICmd.scsi_Data (UWORD *) describes HD_SCSICMD and does not prove the CMD_READ/CMD_WRITE buffer contract. Updated the detailed finding to keep pointer misalignment conditional on caller-supplied alignment and retain no checked-in reproducer claim. The independent non-multiple-of-four internal datalen case remains the concrete lost-byte path. Source-only.

USB mass-storage Bulk-Only CopyMemQuick alignment-contract follow-up (2026-10-20; not promoted): checked the other `CopyMemQuick` caller in `nScsiDirectBulk()` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_bulk.c:296-302`). Its destination `umscbw.CBWCB` is byte offset 15 in `UsbMSCmdBlkWrapper`, declared under `#pragma pack(1)` (`compiler/include/devices/usb_massstorage.h:31-51`); the source `scsicmd->scsi_Command` is also a byte-command buffer. Both pointers therefore lack a source-level ULONG-alignment guarantee, while the API requires both aligned and a multiple-of-ULONG length (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:30-45`). The call is gated on CDB length >=16 and copies exactly 16 bytes, so its length requirement is satisfied. Did not add a separate finding: no selected-target compiler output or ABI evidence was established for the actual stack placement of `umscbw`, and no concrete supported caller buffer misalignment was traced. Keep as an explicit target-layout/caller follow-up. No build, device, or command was run; source-only.

USB mass-storage short-autosense public-entry reconciliation (OD3795 confirmed; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced the selected `usbscsi.device` worker's `HD_SCSICMD` dispatch (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:1378-1385`) to `nScsiDirect()`, which clears only `scsi_SenseActual`, caps `scsi_SenseLength` only when it exceeds 18 under `PFF_SIMPLE_SCSI`, and dispatches to the configured Bulk/CBI/CB/UAS transport (`:3173-3210,3590-3610`). For a short non-NULL sense buffer, the simple-SCSI filter does not reject undersized lengths, and its allowed-command cases reach the same transport dispatch. The Bulk parser still reads sense offsets 2, 12 and 13 without checking `scsi_SenseActual` or declared length (`massstorage_bulk.c:555-600`); CBI copies only the declared length then reads offsets 2 and 12 (`massstorage_cbi.c:301-318`). Confirmed this is the Poseidon `usbscsi.device` path, separate from the `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage` HIDD-backed device implementation. Existing OD3795 trigger/consequence remain accurate. No command, device or short buffer was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage UAS autosense boundary comparison (OD3795 scope narrowed to CB/CBI/Bulk; no new UAS finding, 2026-10-20): checked `nUasDoCommand()`'s direct Sense IU path and REQUEST SENSE fallback (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_uas.c:64-170,219-239`). Sense IU copying clamps to the received payload extent, the IU-reported sense length and caller `sense_len`; this backend does not parse sense-key/ASC bytes afterward. A short caller buffer therefore does not reach the same unchecked offsets identified for Bulk/CBI, and is left as a short `SenseActual`. This confirms OD3795 must remain limited to CB/CBI/Bulk behavior; no UAS defect promoted. No UAS IU or command was used; source-only.

OD3793 UAS status-IU minimum-length/tag boundary recheck (2026-10-20): re-read the status parser and packed IU definitions (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_uas.c:126-170`; `compiler/include/devices/usb_massstorage.h:110-130`). The fixed `UasStatusIU` is 16 bytes, but the parser accepts `actual_len >= 3` as sufficient to take byte 2 as the status; it does not require a complete status IU or check the status IU's tag against the submitted command. It also does not validate the IU identifier before deciding the returned status. For fewer than three bytes the initialized GOOD value remains unchanged; the selected status pipe accepts runt packets. This confirms and sharpens OD3793's false-success/misattributed-completion branches; no separate finding. A complete Sense IU has a different variable length and is separately bounded for copying, so this note does not treat every non-16-byte response as invalid. No status IU or command was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage overlength CDB transport audit (OD4236 added, 2026-10-20): traced public `HD_SCSICMD` queuing to `nScsiDirect()` and the class configuration path that can disable default Simple SCSI filtering (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/dev.c:249-266`; `massstorage.class.c:912,1382-1385,5558-5560,6013-6022`). At a 24-byte caller CDB, the Bulk-Only wrapper copies exactly 16 bytes and reports `scsi_CmdActual=16` (`massstorage_bulk.c:296-306`); UAS clamps `cmdlen` to 16 before copying into its fixed CDB field and likewise reports 16 (`massstorage_uas.c:102-106,187-200`). Neither rejects the request before transport submission. Added OD4236 to the detailed report and master index. The BOT/UAS wire fields limit the transmitted CDB to 16 bytes; effects beyond partial command submission depend on target handling, and callers can observe the shorter `scsi_CmdActual`. No SCSI command/device was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage Bulk autosense pointer-alignment pass (OD4237 added, 2026-10-20): traced `HD_SCSICMD` sense-buffer ownership to the Bulk REQUEST SENSE transfer and the subsequent signature check (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_bulk.c:430-469,538`; public field `compiler/include/devices/scsidisk.h:21-33`). `scsi_SenseData` is a byte pointer with no alignment promise; after at least eight received bytes the code dereferences it as `ULONG *`. Confirmed the Poseidon class package includes massstorage and the m68k USB target selects the package (`rom/usb/mmakefile.src:26-30,62-71`); an odd address can fault on 68k longword access. Added OD4237 separately from OD3795's short-buffer bounds issue, qualifying the isolated trigger as a buffer and received sense extent of at least 14 bytes, noting no checked-in odd-address caller was found, and keeping runtime manifestation target-dependent. No buffer or device was used; source-only.

USB mass-storage CBI/Bulk retry autosense-state pass (OD4238 added, 2026-10-20): traced the `0x80` autoretry flag through both transport loops and the SCSICmd outputs (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage_cbi.c:155-162,287-318,399-404`; `massstorage_bulk.c:266-275,428-469,546-628,698-704`; `massstorage.class.c:3186-3188`). A CHECK CONDITION autosenses into the public sense buffer and sets `scsi_SenseActual`; retryable Unit Attention does not cancel the CBI/Bulk retry. A subsequent successful attempt sets status GOOD but neither transport clears the prior sense count/data, and the top-level reset occurs only once before dispatch. Added OD4238, qualifying caller impact to consumers that inspect sense outputs on successful completion. The SenseActual output is described as the number of bytes received by the selected Eject caller (`workbench/c/Eject.c:120-123`). No command/device or retry was run; source-only.

Poseidon USB mass-storage short MODE SENSE CDB bounds pass (OD4239 added, 2026-10-20): traced `HD_SCSICMD` admission and unit-worker dispatch into `nScsiDirect()` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/dev.c:249-266`; `massstorage.class.c:1382-1385`). The default `PFF_SIMPLE_SCSI` filter switches on byte 0 and the MODE SENSE(6) case reads byte 2 without checking `scsi_CmdLength` (`massstorage.class.c:912,3198-3208,3228-3235`). Added OD4239 for a one-byte CDB buffer with MODE SENSE(6) opcode; distinguished it from OD2859 in the other MassStorage implementation and OD3883's separate response-buffer bounds. No request or device was used; source-only.

OD4239 translation-path extension (2026-10-20): extended the existing short-CDB finding after tracing `xlate` selection and each translation branch. ATAPI, floppy-ATAPI and UFI subclasses enable `xlate` regardless of `scsi_CmdLength` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:3190-3195`); the READ/WRITE/SEEK(6), MODE SELECT(6), and MODE SENSE(6) cases then read command bytes 1-5 (`:3459-3523`) with no minimum-length validation. A one-byte READ(6) on a packet subclass can feed adjacent bytes into the translated READ(10) LBA/count. Expanded OD4239 from only the Simple-SCSI MODE SENSE(6) access to cover this same missing-length-check root cause and its distinct reachable configuration. No command or device was used; source-only.

Poseidon ATAPI/UFI MODE SENSE/SELECT translation allocation-failure pass (OD4240 added, 2026-10-20): traced both staging allocations through translated-command dispatch and completion (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:3460-3465,3480-3531,3596-3612,3615-3651`). If `psdAllocVec(scsi_Length+4)` fails, MODE SENSE/SELECT translation still sets `usecmd10`, leaving the command data pointer/length at caller values and sending the MODE SENSE(10)/MODE SELECT(10) CDB. The no-staging epilogue reports transport status/actual without converting MODE SENSE(10) data back to the six-byte layout. Added OD4240; trigger requires the packet subclass translation and staging allocation failure, and MODE SELECT/unsupported MODE SENSE cases generally require Simple SCSI filtering disabled. No allocation failure, command or device was used; source-only.
OD4240 transport-boundary recheck (2026-10-20): followed the MODE SENSE/SELECT translation fallback into each selected transport. CBI, Bulk and UAS derive their data-phase extent from `scsi_Length` (`massstorage_cbi.c:169,217,245`; `massstorage_bulk.c:294,335`; `massstorage_uas.c:184-200`). On staging allocation failure, `scsicmd10` retains the caller pointer and original length; transport therefore honors that length while sending/receiving the mismatched MODE SENSE/SELECT(10) payload. Tightened OD4240 to a data-format/device-command mismatch and removed any implication of an established buffer overrun. No command or device was used; source-only.
PC serial shared-IRQ removal primitive recheck (OD2779, 2026-10-20): checked the exact Exec/kernel operation beneath unit disposal. `RemIntServer(INTB_KERNEL + n, irq)` passes `irq->is_Node.ln_Succ` to `KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/exec/remintserver.c:51-55`); the PC kernel implementation unlinks and frees the opaque `IntrNode` (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-75`) without changing the caller-owned `Interrupt` node's `ln_Name`. This confirms the serial HIDD's name-based installed sentinel remains stale after disposal, preserving OD2779's later-open path. No IRQ or unit was exercised; source-only.
Serial/parallel HIDD failed-unit publication pass (OD4241 expanded, 2026-10-20): compared all six Unix, i386-PC and m68k-Amiga parent `NewUnit` factories and their matching `DisposeUnit` methods. Each stores the `OOP_NewObject` result and sets `usedunits` unconditionally, while disposal requires a non-NULL pointer match before clearing the bit. `OOP_NewObject` returns NULL when `root_new` cannot allocate the instance (`rom/oop/newobject.c:75-83,104-113`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-131`). The selected serial.device and parallel.device open paths free their wrapper record and return an error on NULL without calling the parent disposer (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:170-195`; `parallel_init.c:162-184`). No allocation failure or device open was induced; source-only.

Deneb USB `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` input/output and completion pass (2026-10-20; no new OD, partial-file credit only): reread `cmdNSDeviceQuery()` and its `devBeginIO()` dispatch/RC_DONTREPLY handling (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1540-1600`; `dev.c:545-623,630-639`), checked the local AROS result layout against `NSDeviceQueryResult`, and traced the query caller in `PartitionNsdCheck()` (`compiler/include/devices/newstyle.h:12-28`; `partition_support.c:45-85`). The caller initializes `DevQueryFormat` and `SizeAvailable` to zero and supplies the full result size, matching the driver's input validation; on success the driver fills all result fields, returns actual/available sizes, and lets the common dispatcher complete the request once. On invalid input the helper sets IOERR_NOCMD and completes the request itself, while the dispatcher honors RC_DONTREPLY; quick requests are not replied by `TermIO()`. No separate defect established. `uhwcmd.c` remains partial and receives no whole-file line credit. No device query was issued; source-only.
Deneb USB `CMD_FLUSH` request completion pass (2026-10-20; no new OD, partial-file credit only): reread the five queued-list drain and ATL/INT/ISO PTD loops (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:961-1041`), matched them to transfer enqueue paths and PTD release helpers (`:811-955,1635-1770`), and checked the selected Poseidon unit teardown caller (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9299-9320`). This pass did not establish another flush defect; hardware DMA stop semantics and complete abort interleavings remain open. No flush or transfer was run; source-only. No whole-file line credit.
USB host-controller bus-state command contract cross-check (OD3655 retained; 2026-10-20): compared Deneb's advertised `NSDSupported` table and BeginIO dispatch for `UHCMD_USBRESUME`/`USBSUSPEND`/`USBOPER` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1540-1556`; `dev.c:545-600,610-623`) with the public command behavior and required `iouh_State`/`io_Error` outputs (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:560-583,618-669`). Deneb control-transfer admission, PTD stages and Poseidon caller pass (2026-10-20; OD3585 retained, no new OD): traced `cmdControlXFer()` through control PTD scheduling, setup/data/status completion, `FreeATL()` and `TermIO()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:811-833,1612-1651,2034-2073,2552-2771,3797-3954`; selected contract `rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:268-329`). The scheduler holds a request queued when endpoint/PTD or large-granule resources are unavailable, and once admitted copies the fixed 8-byte setup packet and owns endpoint state until `FreeATL()` clears it and replies. Data-IN completion clamps a controller-reported length to the remaining declared buffer before copying; data-OUT setup and continuation use rounded ULONG loads already covered by OD3585. Poseidon's `psdDoPipe()` sets `iouh_Length=len` and, for endpoint zero, setup `wLength` from the same length before queuing and waiting (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4705-4739,4810-4862`); no independent selected-caller mismatch established. Hardware PTD token/count semantics, controller timing, and external callers remain unverified; `uhwcmd.c` remains partial and receives no whole-file credit. No transfer or hardware was exercised; source-only.
Deneb bulk public-caller endpoint contract and zero-length reachability recheck (OD3585/OD3889/OD4160 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-20): traced Poseidon `psdAllocPipe()` endpoint setup through `psdDoPipe()` into Deneb `cmdBulkXFer()` and `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4478-4634,4705-4739`; `arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:850-875,4212-4375`). For descriptor-backed endpoints, Poseidon extracts the endpoint number from the low four address bits, direction from bit 7, and packet size from `wMaxPacketSize`; it selects `UHCMD_BULKXFER` only for bulk type. `psdDoPipe()` forwards the caller's length unchanged, including zero, confirming OD4160's in-tree trigger. The ordinary PIO OUT tail and large-area terminal-run omission remain OD3585 and OD3889. The driver rejects low-speed bulk but otherwise relies on public request/descriptor contracts; this pass established no additional selected-caller defect. No endpoint, request or hardware was exercised; Deneb `uhwcmd.c` remains partial and receives no whole-file credit. Source-only.
Deneb DEBUG ATL dump branch pass (no new OD, 2026-10-20): read `uhwDebugATLs()` and all selected call sites (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:1878-1965,4864-4919`). The helper is compiled only with `DEBUG`; its repeated volatile reads use the ISP1760 PIO data window after programming the `ISP_MEMORY` start address, consistent with the selected read-window pointer and other word-stream copies in the driver (`uhwcmd.c:371-380,2433-2447,2621-2634`; `isp1760.h:61`). The helper indexes the per-device toggle table only when the associated IOReq exists, under valid scheduler-populated endpoint fields in the examined path. DEBUG-only diagnostics and the controller's PIO read behavior remain untested; no whole-file credit. Source-only.

CAMD cluster relocation failure and report/index reconciliation (OD1497 restored, 2026-10-20): re-traced the public `SetMidiLinkAttrsA()` caller into `SetClusterForLink()`, `UnlinkMidiLink()`, `NewCluster()`, and both direction-specific `AddCluster*()` paths. CAMD cluster-iterator synchronization recheck (2026-10-20; no new OD): searched all local `NextCluster()` calls and found only the function's documented example. It holds `LockCAMD(CD_Linkages)` across traversal; `LockCAMD` obtains the global semaphore shared, while cluster list publication/removal requires the exclusive semaphore. This protects `last` and its successor for callers following the documented contract; external misuse remains outside checked-in call paths. No line credit. Source-only.

Nouveau/VMware DRM workqueue ownership recheck (OD4037 retained, 2026-10-20): reread the full `linux_workqueue.c` body and traced every direct private queue allocation/destruction found in the selected target trees. Successful `alloc_workqueue()` returns the same independently `kzalloc()`ed descriptor; only process-creation and signal-allocation failures call `kfree(wq)`. `destroy_workqueue()` flushes, sets `stopping`, signals the worker and returns without joining or freeing it; there is no later descriptor-free API. Confirmed normal per-device/per-manager pairs in TTM init/fini, Nouveau DRM init/fini including `fail_wq`, NVKM display constructor/destructor, DP MST topology init/destroy, VMware VKMS init/cleanup, and VMware/Nouveau `kthread_destroy_worker()` (which frees only its wrapper). The two system queue instances are global and not destroyed through normal use. Therefore the report's per-successful-private-queue leak is supported; the selected normal teardown paths do not reclaim the allocation, and repeated device/manager lifecycle accumulates descriptors. Worker-exit synchronization also means any eventual descriptor release must wait until the signaled worker has finished reading it. No queue, driver teardown, or worker timing was run. Source-only.

Deneb `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` contract and local-caller recheck (no new OD, 2026-10-20): reread `cmdNSDeviceQuery()` and its dispatch/`RC_DONTREPLY` path, compared the structure with `compiler/include/devices/newstyle.h`, and searched in-tree query initializers/callers. The header defines `DevQueryFormat` and `SizeAvailable` as fields reset for each query; local filesystem callers initialize both to zero, while device implementations populate them as output. Deneb's zero-only input check is consistent with that contract. `developer/debug/devtest/devtest.c:test_nsd_devicequery()` leaves the prefilled `SizeAvailable` poison value intact, but it is a trackdisk probe and does not establish a Deneb caller path. No new driver defect established; external callers and any alternate NSD specification remain outside this source-only check. No query was issued. Source-only.

Deneb active DMA AbortIO caller recheck (OD3584 confirmed, no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced `devAbortIO()` through `cmdAbortIO()` for queued requests and active ATL/INT/ISO PTDs, then followed the active ATL cleanup into `FreeATL()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/dev.c:650-690`; `uhwcmd.c:1602-1684,1778-1868`). The active ATL branch clears `ptd_IOReq` before `FreeATL()`; when that PTD is `hu_DMAPTD`, the cleanup snapshots NULL and dereferences it for `CachePostDMA()`. This confirms detailed finding OD3584. Poseidon's abort helper submits a companion abort message and waits, so its pipe teardown reaches the same selected device AbortIO vector (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4778-4801,9080-9086`). The direct Deneb DMA target is selected by the m68k USB aggregate (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/mmakefile.src:25-30`); the request must be active, ATL-backed and DMA-eligible. Non-DMA and queued/INT/ISO abort paths do not enter this exact NULL `FreeATL()` branch. No transfer, abort or hardware was run. Source-only.

NVHDMI DriverInit discovery-capacity and failure-unwind pass (2026-10-20; OD3746 retained, no new finding): traced `DriverInit()` through the common AHI `_LibInit`/`_LibExpunge` path, `ahi_hda_init`/`ahi_hda_exit`, bounded PCI discovery and all local card-array/card-data outcomes (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/NVHDMI/driver-init.c:35-136`; `Common/library.c:378-468,483-514`; `NVHDMI/hda_hidd.c:253-320,323-374,390-454`; `hdmi.c:110-160`). HDA partial-init cleanup checks each resource before releasing it; no independent cleanup defect established. No allocation failure, PCI device, controller or audio operation was exercised. RPiHDMI SoC register-table and selected-consumer pass (OD2839 retained; 2026-10-20): read both SoC table bodies and their shared type/access declarations (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/RPiHDMI/rpihdmi-bcm2712.c`, `rpihdmi-bcm283x.c`, `rpihdmi-soc.h`, `rpihdmi-hwaccess.h`), then traced all table selection and field consumption through `rpihdmi-init.c`, `rpihdmi-main.c`, DMA setup and `hdmi_mai_init/stop`. The output table remains bounded by two entries. No additional source-level table/consumer mismatch established. Credited 90 C code lines across the two SoC table bodies; struct/accessor body review was already recorded. Hardware register semantics, DT firmware contents and audio output remain unverified; no device or stream was used. Source-only.

RPiHDMI DT `reg-names` candidate recheck (2026-10-20; no finding promoted): traced `find_element_index()` against the selected Raspberry Pi OpenFirmware provider (`rpihdmi-init.c:48-75`; `arch/{arm-raspi,aarch64-raspi}/boot/devicetree.c:36-50`; `rom/openfirmware/of_init.c:132-156,174-215`). VMware MST fallback GUID generator concurrency pass (OD4242; 2026-10-20): traced the VMware copy of `get_random_u32()` through the byte-wise `guid_gen()` and topology validator, and checked the selected probe-worker and resume callers. The seed is a file-static value with non-atomic read/modify/write updates; probing takes `mgr->probe_lock`, while resume takes `mgr->lock`, so the reviewed code does not serialize both GUID-generation routes. A same-manager collision could misroute a later GUID-addressed broadcast notification; no interleaving or hardware behavior was tested. This mirrors GD5640 for Nouveau's copy. No whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Nouveau/VMware compatibility clock conversion and timeout-caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): checked the shared `jiffies.h` conversions against selected callers of `dma_fence_wait_timeout()`, `dma_resv_wait_timeout()`, timer arming, DisplayPort sideband waits, and scheduler sleeps. The selected finite reservation/fence waits are 2, 15 or 30 seconds; the delayed-delete path uses `MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT`, which `dma_fence_wait_timeout()` special-cases as an infinite wait before converting to microseconds. The selected I2C bit-bus timeout is 2,200 microseconds. Thus the 32-bit `jiffies_to_usecs()` product does not wrap for the reviewed in-tree call values. `drm_gem_dma_resv_wait()` has no in-tree caller, and the selected `EXPORT_SYMBOL` compatibility macro is empty (`include/linux/export.h:8-11`), so no external module entry path is selected here; arbitrary values remain outside the reviewed call graph. Re-read the exact-deadline loop in `timer_do_arm()` and the short-period `drm_dp_mst_wait_tx_reply()` caller; no additional wrap defect was established beyond OD4178's wall-clock basis. No timer, fence, or device operation was run; no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Nouveau delayed-work cancellation race follow-up to OD4177 (2026-10-20): traced `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` through its `del_timer()` pending-bit fast return, queued-work cancellation and `flush_work()`. Timer expiry clears pending before the delayed-work callback calls `queue_work()`, leaving a window where cancellation sees neither pending timer nor queued work and returns before the callback queues. The selected `drm_kms_helper_poll_disable()` uses this API; during suspend it sets `poll_running` false but leaves `poll_enabled` true, so late output-poll work may still probe connectors and reschedule. `drm_kms_helper_poll_fini()` also relies on the same cancellation before clearing `poll_enabled`. Expanded OD4177 with these selected delayed-work consequences; no duplicate ID added. Race timing and runtime behavior were not exercised. Source-only.

Nouveau scheduler current-record allocation failure trace (OD4243 added, 2026-10-20): followed the selected HIDD constructor's `drmOpen()` through the AROS `drm_file_alloc()` callback to `nouveau_drm_open()`. On first `current` use in an Exec task, `compat_current()` allocates and may return NULL; `nouveau_drm_open()` immediately reads `current->comm`. Added OD4243 for the conditional null dereference during Nouveau device initialization. VMware's remaining `current` fields are in optional MKS stats code not selected by the checked configuration; its `signal_pending(current)` compatibility stubs ignore their argument and do not establish the same dereference. No task record allocation or HIDD open was induced. This adds caller trace only; scheduler source was already fully credited. Source-only.

Nouveau wait-queue/completion selected-caller pass (2026-10-20; no new OD): traced six active wait-event call sites in selected Nouveau DRM users: MST sideband reply, atomic and vblank waits, PMU synchronous reply and clock-state wait (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/display/drm_dp_mst_topology.c:1252-1331`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/drm_atomic_helper.c:1897-1922`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/drm_vblank.c:1300-1323,1848-1870`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/pmu/gt215.c:75-83,115-123`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/clk/base.c:332-342`). Each checks its terminal condition before sleeping and again after wake; the traced producers update the condition before `wake_up()`/`wake_up_all()`, so no lost-wakeup path was established in these callers. Reviewed completion timeout use in atomic flip cleanup; the completion implementation preserves `complete()` tokens and `complete_all()` state as expected by the selected call. The separate `drm_file` event-read wait has no selected AROS reader; the AROS glue says its event queues are unread (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-aros/drm_drv.c:434-435`). `signal_pending()` is a constant-false compatibility stub, but no AROS signal-interruption contract or selected caller requiring `-ERESTARTSYS` was established; do not promote Linux-style interrupted-wait behavior as a standalone AROS bug without that integration contract. These checks do not cover every caller of exported waitqueue/completion helpers or device-specific scheduling. No hardware, wait, or interrupt was run. Source-only.

USB Audio full-translation-unit and finding-ledger reconciliation (2026-10-21): completed the body pass of all 4,163 physical lines of `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c` (3,330 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`), including the earlier partial regions. Crediting 3,330 lines and one path to the latest represented checkpoint of 172,836/270,754 lines and 582/598 paths yields 176,166/270,754 = 65.06% and 583/598 = 97.49%; both denominators are carried forward and the VMware source inventory is known to be incomplete, so these remain ledger proxies rather than a fresh Other Drivers census.
