PC timer VBlank `SendIO` receiver follow-up (2026-10-20; no new finding): traced the selected `arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c` request submission through `common_BeginIO()` and the `TimerProcessMicroHZ()` expiry path (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:77-128,267-321`). `SendIO()` clears `IOF_QUICK` and resets the message node type, but the embedded VBlank request is recognized specially on expiry: it is removed, VBlank processing runs, the next deadline is computed and the same request is reinserted, then processing continues without `ReplyMsg()`. The repeated request therefore is not a generic reply-port completion or stale-node reuse path; it is deliberately retained as the timer's periodic driver request. No request was submitted or timer run. Source-only.

PCIPC MSI vector caller requirement recheck (OD2987/OD2993 retained, 2026-10-21): searched the complete checked-in `HIDD_PCIDevice_ObtainVectors()` call set and read each selected PC-capable caller's request and result path. NVMe requests Min=1/Max=CPU count, obtains the negotiated queue count, but currently creates one I/O queue (`hwqcnt=1`) and queries vector index 0; AHCI, xHCI, Nouveau and VMware request exactly one vector and query only index 0. Thus the PCIPC `vectmin > table_size` behavior and zero-minimum MSI countdown still lack a selected caller trigger. xHCI releases vectors when its native-vector attribute remains invalid; Nouveau/VMware release and report ENODEV when their IRQ attribute is invalid. AHCI does not check the initialized `-1` sentinel after `GetVectorAttribs()`, but the selected PCIPC `ObtainVectors()` success paths program MSI-X table data or MSI config before returning TRUE, and the corresponding index-zero attribute read obtains that programmed value; the generic fallback `ObtainVectors()` returns FALSE, so AHCI takes INTx there. No independent selected AHCI bad-attribute path was established. No additional vector-count contract defect established; PCIPC MSI-X BAR-span/address checks, MSI count rounding/base-index behavior, destination APIC-ID assumption, and non-releasing APIC allocation remain tracked in their existing findings. No vector request or hardware interrupt was run; source-only.

MetaMake build-scope reconciliation (2026-10-21): checked the pinned parser behavior for active `#MM-` virtual targets and followed parent chains through the workbench, network, ROM USB, and m68k Deneb manifests. Corrected the prior false statements that the default network aggregate excluded PPP/Prism2, that the m68k Deneb aggregate was commented out, that PPP was an explicit-only module, and that CAMD USB-MIDI was outside the USB class aggregate. The network cards aggregate has CPU aliases for i386, x86_64, m68k, and ppc; PPP is a child of `workbench-devs-networks`; Atheros5000 is conditional on the GNU toolchain; m68k-Amiga `workbench-complete` selects the Deneb aggregate and its three variants; USB class selection includes CAMD MIDI when `kernel-usb-classes` is built on supported CPU aliases. Updated OD3580/OD3708/OD3697/OD4229/OD4234 scope text and the index/coverage rows accordingly. This is build-graph evidence only: no targets were built and no device behavior was exercised. Source-only.

Atheros5000 TKIP MIC caller/extent recheck (OD3297 retained; no new candidate, 2026-10-21): traced RX descriptor length admission and `ieee_length` initialization through the selected TKIP fragment-decrypt function table, successful-fragment accumulation, the final-fragment `UNITF_HARDMIC` gate, `TKIPDecryptFrame`, and the `rx_frames` allocation (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:1545-1561,1603-1641,218-221,659-669`; `device.h:96`; `encryption.c:1080-1103`). Confirmed the complete-frame checker is entered only for a completed fragment whose preceding per-fragment check succeeded, when software MIC checking is selected. For `ieee_length < 8`, subtracting `sizeof(mic)` wraps the UWORD; the helper reads the expected MIC from the wrapped offset, writes the eight-byte padding there, and reads `size/4+2` words from that buffer before returning a MIC mismatch. This refines OD3297’s concrete out-of-range read/write sites; it is not a separate finding. Reachability still depends on a malformed final TKIP fragment passing its per-fragment integrity check. No packet, device, or runtime memory behavior was exercised; source-only.

Atheros5000 RX-fragment slot-pressure reachability check (OD3274 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-21): searched all `rx_fragment_nos` writes and traced slot admission/release through `GetRXBuffer()` and `RXInt()` (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:1572,1621-1625,1669-1671,1737-1776`; allocation and initialization `:218-221`; array declaration `device.h:127`). A first fragment sets a slot's sequence marker; the RX path releases that slot only when a fragment without `WIFI_FRM_CONTROLF_MOREFRAGS` is processed. There is no independent expiry/reaper. Thus ten valid first fragments without their terminal fragment can hold all ten slots, after which an eleventh first fragment forces the retry loop to clear logical slot zero while its pointer has advanced one buffer past the ten-slot allocation; it returns `buffer_no == 10`, which `RXInt` later uses against the ten-entry marker array. This confirms OD3274's in-tree reachability condition and distinguishes it from the separate same-source/different-sequence reassembly issue OD3296. No packet or device was used; source-only.

NetInfo startup/expunge and usergroup caller recheck (OD1894/OD1896/OD1902/OD2344 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-21): re-read the selected first-use path from `usergroup` entry points through `ug_OpenUnit`/`OpenDevice`, `NetInfo__DevOpen`, process creation and the worker startup reply. Confirmed process-creation failure yields no worker to answer the open handshake (OD1894), while the later second-map failure is a distinct worker-side no-reply path (OD2344). Rechecked DOS base acquisition before temporary port/request allocation and absent close on those failures/worker exit (OD1896), plus the expunge hook return into generated synchronous base disposal before worker cleanup (OD1902). A suspected open-device retention on `ug_OpenUnit` buffer-allocation failure was not promoted: the device/unit is cached for later retry and `CleanupNIO` closes both units through `endpwent`/`endgrent` before deleting the shared request/port. The normal selected usergroup path uses synchronous `DoIO`; no in-tree `AbortIO` caller was found for netinfo. No allocation failure, device open, expunge or concurrent request was induced; direct external device callers and runtime scheduling remain open. Source-only.

Nouveau current-task compatibility record SMP interleaving pass (OD4244, 2026-10-21): compared the complete `task_records`/`next_pid` creation paths in both Nouveau and VMware `drm-compat/linux_sched.c`, then traced selected `current` macro callers and kthread startup. Compared the protection with Exec Forbid documentation, which explicitly says its task-switch exclusion is local to one processor on ExecSMP. The global list insertion and PID increment have no SMP lock; two first-use callers on separate CPUs can race. Added OD4244 for both PC HIDDs, separate from OD4043's persistent per-task record retention and OD4243's allocation-failure dereference. The SMP trigger remains conditional on a build selecting either HIDD and ExecSMP. No build, device or interleaving was exercised. Source-only.

Lowlevel keyboard callback-list / software-interrupt node audit (OD4245, 2026-10-21): verified that `AddKBInt` links the embedded `is_Node` into `ll_KBInterrupts` (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/addkbint.c:68-77`), then `LowLevelInputHandler` calls `Cause()` on that same node during traversal (`lowlevel_init.c:46-61`). Exec `Cause()` adds it to a priority SoftInts list and overwrites its two link fields without unlinking it from the lowlevel list (`rom/exec/cause.c:84-100`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:122-134`). `ForeachNode` follows the node’s updated `ln_Succ` (`lists.h:195-201`), and `RemKBInt` later removes using the overwritten links (`remkbint.c:38-45`). Added OD4245, the detailed report/index entries, and explicit coverage rows. No checked-in AddKBInt caller was found; affected external API use remains conditional. No callback or key event was run. Source-only.

OD3947 width/zero-size overlap recheck (2026-10-21): re-read Type I parsing, AHI frame sizing, buffer allocation and both conversion directions (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:1138-1219,1943-1953,2735-2741,2858-2964,3134-3167,3406-3412,3448-3482,3505-3550`). Updated report and index; zero-width division is no longer claimed under OD3947. The wider-width read remains conditional on an accepted mismatched descriptor and subsequent AHI allocation/playback. No descriptor, mode, buffer, or device was used; source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II capability-query error/fallback pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): read the complete wpa_driver_sana2_get_capa() body and traced its S2_GETCRYPTTYPES request, pool lifetime, fallback and capability consumption (workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:449-497; wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:2043-2054; driver_i.h:168-180). Atheros5000/Realtek8180 S2_SETKEY request and key-storage bounds pass (candidate reconciled to OD3187, 2026-10-21): traced `S2_SETKEY` dispatch into both `CmdSetKey()` handlers and `SetKey()` implementations, then checked `WIFI_KEYCOUNT`, the `KeyUnion` member sizes, and the public request-field mapping (`compiler/include/devices/sana2wireless.h:44-47`; `atheros5000/request.c:1608-1618`, `unit.c:1066-1079`, `encryption.h`; `realtek8180/request.c:1606-1616`, `unit.c:1074-1086`, `device.h`). Neither driver bounds the request key index before `unit->keys[index]`; WEP copy length is unchecked against the 13-byte member, and TKIP/CCMP fixed-size copies and receive-counter dereferences lack corresponding request-length/pointer validation. The adjacent S2_SETOPTIONS path also accepts an unchecked `S2INFO_DefaultKeyNo` into `tx_key_no`, which later indexes the same four-slot array during TX (`atheros5000/unit.c:1019-1020,2202`; `realtek8180/unit.c:1016-1017,2088`). Traced the selected supplicant key-clear caller: `wpa_clear_keys()` submits indices 4 and 5 when `CONFIG_IEEE80211W` is enabled, but the checked-in `.config` leaves that option commented. This conditional caller evidence was consolidated into OD3187; the attempted OD4250 duplicate is withdrawn below. The device targets are explicit/optional in their manifests (`realtek8180/mmakefile.src`, `atheros5000/mmakefile.src`); no build, request or device was run. Remaining command/request paths and wider unit lifecycle review remain open. Source-only.


OD4250 duplicate reconciliation (2026-10-21): compared the Atheros5000/Realtek8180 key-index and key-length pass with existing OD3187, which already covers Prism2, Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 S2_SETKEY bounds, `S2INFO_DefaultKeyNo` storage, and downstream TX indexing. Marked OD4250 withdrawn in the detailed report and removed its master-index link. No new independent bug or line credit. Source-only.


Realtek8180 FlushUnit/CMDFLUSH queue-ownership recheck (no new OD, 2026-10-21): read the complete `FlushUnit()` and traced both callers: `CMD_FLUSH` drains request ports through `EVENT_QUEUE` and passes `IOERR_ABORTED` (`request.c:480-497`), while `GoOffline()` clears the online flag first, drains through `MGMT_QUEUE`, then reports OFFLINE (`unit.c:956-964`). `FlushUnit()` also drains every opener's read and management-message ports (`unit.c:1365-1408`); selected `GetMsg()` protects each port list with the ExecSMP spinlock (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:56-71`). UnitTask serializes its own queued request servicing through `access_lock` (`unit.c:2678-2690`), while USB soft-interrupt TX completion is separate (`RetireTXSlot`, `unit.c:2419-2483`). This confirms the queued-port behavior and offline ordering. It does not establish whether the public CMD_FLUSH contract requires canceling already-submitted USB transfers held in the TX ring, so no finding is added and that contract/caller question remains open. No request or USB transfer was run; no new line credit. Source-only.


Realtek8180 rate-helper and management-duration pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): read `GetDuration()` and `AckRate()` completely and traced their three TX call sites through data and management frame construction (`unit.c:2007-2296,2298-2417,2543-2619`). The constructor initializes TX rate to 11 Mbps and management rate to 1 Mbps; `SetOptions(S2INFO_Band)` changes them only to 54/2 Mbps for 802.11g or 11/1 Mbps for 802.11b (`unit.c:132-136,1034-1048`). `AckRate()` has explicit mappings for every selected value, including management 2 Mbps to 2 Mbps; the uninitialized local result for an unsupported rate is not reached through these in-tree assignments. `GetDuration()` receives nonzero selected rates and the frame lengths remain subject to existing raw/oversize TX findings OD3275/OD3276. This closes the selected rate-helper input mapping only; external mutation of unit fields, chipset airtime semantics and remaining Realtek caller/hardware contracts remain open. No frame or device was used; no new line credit. Source-only.


Realtek8180 same-endpoint USB submission-order contract recheck (OD3266 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced the 30 TX pipe allocations for one bulk OUT endpoint and 30 RX pipe allocations for one bulk IN endpoint (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/device.h:158-159`; `usb.c:535-550`), concurrent RX submission (`usb.c:284-290`), per-slot TX dispatch (`unit.c:2030-2035,2224-2228`; `usb.c:1073-1084`) and RX slot rearm (`usb.c:751-763,1103-1114`). Poseidon forwards each pipe request to the hardware task, which issues SendIO and counts multiple requests in flight (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4742-4778,9277-9293`). The public USB hardware contract explicitly requires endpoint-scoped DATA0/DATA1 tracking and in-order queueing of multiple requests to the same endpoint (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:67-82`); its CMD_FLUSH contract also covers in-progress and queued transfers (`:140-159`). The in-tree UHCI/OHCI HIDD classes create per-pipe queue/toggle state, but I found no selected implementation connecting those HIDD methods to Poseidon's `UHCMD_BULKXFER` device-request path; treating their state as proof of a violation would be unsupported. Therefore the prior completion-order concern remains open at the host-controller backend boundary and no new Realtek defect is promoted. The detailed transfer result issue remains OD3266. No device, host controller, or transfer was run; no line credit. Source-only.

Realtek8180 receive reassembly-to-SANA-II distribution pass (OD3257/OD3258/OD3259 rechecked, no new finding, 2026-10-21): traced `RXInt()` descriptor length, fragment lookup/append/decrypt, final-fragment handling and `DistributeRXPacket()` through `CopyPacket()` and the unit RX scratch allocation (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/unit.c:1467-1609,1638-1672,1696-1868`; `device.h:145-157,211-233`). Reconfirmed OD3257's missing upper bound against the 1,552-byte data area after the descriptor; OD3258's non-SNAP branch leaves `buffer` pointing at prior `rx_buffer` contents; and OD3259's missing `ETH_MAXPACKETSIZE` distribution guard passes the computed length to the opener callback without checking posted capacity. Compared the same SNAP/non-SNAP choice and MTU guard in the selected Prism2 and Atheros5000 copies. Also followed the RX completion path: USB descriptor construction derives its pointer from the completion length (OD3255) and offline completions are dropped without rearming (OD3265). These are existing report entries, not new discoveries; this slice adds no line credit because `unit.c` was already counted as a partially reviewed path. No packet, request, device or hardware was used. Source-only.

Realtek8180 encryption translation-unit pass and OD3295 extension (2026-10-21): read all 2,126 physical lines (1,865 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`) of `workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/encryption.c`; traced WEP/TKIP/CCMP fragment wrappers, per-frame TKIP MIC helpers, replay state, RC4 CRC and AES/CCMP extent handling against `InitialiseAdapter()`'s selected function table and `RXInt()`/`TXInt()` callers (`unit.c:760-795,1467-1555,2070-2185`). Confirmed OD3295 also applies to Realtek8180: `RXInt()` permits an encrypted body length of zero and dispatches the configured cipher, while the WEP/TKIP/CCMP readers or decryptors subtract their respective overheads from an unchecked `UWORD`; the underflow can reach large copies or crypto reads. Expanded OD3295 in the detailed report and master index to include Realtek8180 and its 28-byte receive floor, while retaining Atheros5000's separate path. OD3297 remains the distinct completed-frame TKIP MIC check. Compared the body against the Prism2 copy; differences are its m68k conditional integrity implementation, not an additional selected Realtek issue in this pass. Lookup tables were read but no cryptographic test vectors, packet, key request or hardware were exercised. Source-only.

Realtek8180 EEPROM/radio power-table and caller pass (OD4251 added, 2026-10-21): traced both 14-entry EEPROM location arrays, `GetPower()`/`GetPowerPair()`, unit allocation/default channel, `SetPower()`'s CCK/OFDM indexing and channel-code branches, then initial `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` and online `S2_SETOPTIONS` callers (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/radio.c:125-136,279-323,352-429,515-528`; `unit.c:115-136,461,849-861,1024-1029`; `request.c:650-655,1557-1568`). The EEPROM loop stores entries in indices 0–13, while the public/selected channel values and RF code use channels 1–14; channel 14 consequently consumes an untouched zeroed entry and channels 1–13 are shifted. Added OD4251 to the detailed report and index, keeping invalid-channel bounds separately in OD3283. Read the EEPROM bit-serial transaction helpers; their timing and register behavior remain unverified. No EEPROM, radio, request or hardware operation was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 busy-delay helper and selected-caller pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): read both complete delay helpers and traced every in-tree caller in `eeprom.c`, `radio.c` and `unit.c` (`timer.c:44-79`; caller inventory from `rg BusyMicroDelay|BusyMilliDelay` in the selected driver). `BusyMilliDelay` multiplies only fixed caller values no greater than 500 ms by 1,000; direct microsecond callers pass fixed values no greater than 10. Rechecked the apparent reversed comparison against `rom/timer/cmptime.c:25-36`: `CmpTime(dest,src)` returns -1 when `dest > src`, so `while(CmpTime(deadline,time) < 0)` waits while the deadline remains later than the sampled current time. Its initial comparison uses the duration value before the first current-time sample; no material defect was established for the selected post-startup callers. Added a complete timer-helper row; no new finding or line credit. No delay or timer operation was run. Source-only.

Realtek8180 radio translation-unit body follow-through (OD4251 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-21): completed reading the remaining PHY and RF serial access helpers (`radio.c:557-831`) and rechecked the generation-specific USB direct-write branch against the common bit-banged path. UIKit bitmap offset/render-caller recheck (OD3006/OD2794 retained; 2026-10-21): re-read the QBitmap Get/Set and UpdateRect methods against the configured method list, generic `ScrollVPort()` and graphics display compositor selection. Confirmed `ScrollVPort()` writes signed offsets through `QBitmap__Root__Set`, then reads the cached values back into `ViewPort`; UIKit reports nonzero composition flags, so generic display setup does not create the software compositor used to validate them. The mixed signed/unsigned upper-bound comparisons therefore retain OD3006’s conditional offset-state corruption. Separately, the configured `ShowViewPorts()` implementation returns TRUE without rendering, retained as OD2794; this limits OD3006’s claim to stored ViewPort state. The current class body and caller evidence produced no additional independent candidate. No iOS HIDD or viewport operation was run. Source-only.

Generic I²C device timing-attribute reconciliation (OD4323 added, 2026-10-22): rechecked `I2CDev::Root::New/Get/Set` and the generic `I2C::PutByte/GetByte/WriteRead` delay uses (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cdeviceclass.c:200-233,326-372`; `i2cclass.c:231-321`). VideoCore GPU MemHeader failed-init unwind pass (OD4324 added, 2026-10-22): traced `VideoCoreGfx__Support__Init()` from mailbox GPU-range discovery through `InitMem()`, `InitCursor()`, `InitDMA()`, graphics.library open and `AddDisplayDriver()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_init.c:101-197`). `InitMem()` links the library-base-embedded `MemHeaderExt` into Exec's MemList (`vcgfx_memory.c:225-249`) before later operations can fail; the only shared failure cleanup frees the mailbox buffer and attribute bases and does not unlink that node. Confirmed a selected failure return is reachable from `AddDisplayDriverA()`'s `DD_NO_MEM` path (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:164-169`) and other setup errors. Exec's `AvailMem()` invokes the managed header's `mhe_Avail` (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:365-378`); this header reports `mh_Free`, while its allocation callback returns NULL (`vcgfx_memory.c:36-42,218-223`). Added OD4324 for the lingering unavailable GPU range after a post-InitMem failure. The loader's failed-library-base lifetime was not required to establish this finding and is not claimed. BCM2712 exits before GPU memory setup. No module failure, mailbox response, or memory query was induced; source-only. VC4 local source and broader HVS/display-platform review remain partial.

OD4324 Exec allocator-consequence qualification (2026-10-22): read the complete `nommu_AllocMem()` list walk and `nommu_AvailMem()` managed-header paths (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:23-83,309-378`). AR5211 regulatory noise-floor candidate caller and domain recheck (OD3824 retained, 2026-10-21): traced `ar5211CalNoiseFloor()` through the only two callers, reset and long periodic calibration (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_reset.c:475-482,734-755,985-1020`), then checked `ath_hal_getnfcheckrequired()` against the selected channel's `regDmnFlags` and the MKK table's `NEED_NFC` entries (`hal/ah_regdomain.c:528-574,2825-2832`). The loop always exits with `i == 3`; therefore `i <= N(runtime)` returns true regardless of sample outcomes. Failed samples clear `rawNoiseFloor`, including after an earlier passing sample, so the final failed attempt can leave zero while still reporting success. Refined OD3824's trigger and consequence accordingly; no duplicate added. The precise radio conditions producing above-threshold readings remain hardware-dependent. No channel or measurement was used; source-only.

AR5211 noise-floor frequency-adjustment helper caller pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced `ar5211GetNfAdjust()` through its attach-time function-pointer installation and shared `ath_hal_getChanNoise()`/`ath_hal_process_noisefloor()` consumers (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_attach.c:337`; `hal/ah_internal.h:250,331-332`; `hal/ah.c:772-851`). Public channel-noise lookup rejects a channel with no `ath_hal_checkchannel()` mapping before calling the adjustment helper; bulk processing iterates only the HAL's populated internal channel table. The adjustment table's sentinel iteration therefore receives positive, selected channel values on these in-tree paths; the apparent zero-channel overrun is not reachable through the checked callers. Values above the final threshold use the high-frequency adjustment entry. Compared the generic AR5212 path and made no independent finding. External private HAL callers and RF noise-floor calibration semantics remain open. No channel or radio was used; source-only.

AR5211 transmit-power-limit input/caller pass (no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced the apparently unclamped `AR_PHY_POWER_TX_RATE_MAX` write in `ar5211SetTxPowerLimit()` (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_reset.c:1324-1329`) through every in-tree call. The only direct device caller is `ConfigureAdapter()`, which passes the fixed `TX_POWER == 40` half-dBm value (`unit.c:53,797`), below `MAX_RATE_POWER == 63` (`hal/ah_eeprom.h:126-127`). RTL8139 TX completion scheduling-context recheck (OD3111, 2026-10-21): confirmed `RTL8139_TX_IntF` is an Exec soft interrupt installed in `rtl8139u_tx_int` and scheduled by `Cause()` from TX and timeout paths (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/unit.c:321-345,496,620,1052-1055`). `SoftIntDispatch` explicitly enables interrupts before calling each handler (`rom/exec/cause.c:176-184`). `ReplyMsg` publishes through `InternalPutMsg`/`Signal`; `Signal` documents immediate start for a higher-priority waiter and its uniprocessor path calls `Reschedule()`, whose enabled-interrupt branch invokes `KrnSchedule()` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`; `putmsg.c:81-99`; `signal.c:117-145,385-419`; `reschedule.c:55-80`). Thus the RTL8139 post-reply packet-type read can race caller reuse on a uniprocessor when the waiting reply task has higher priority, as well as on ExecSMP; no SMP-only qualification is warranted. Updated OD3111 in the detailed report and index with this Exec scheduling evidence; no new finding. No request or task switch was run. Source-only.

Keyboard pending-read lost-wakeup candidate restored (OD2389, 2026-10-21): verified the two-sided check/enqueue interleaving in `BeginIO` and `keyCallback` (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:362-379,621-646`). `Disable()` is CPU-local under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), and the initialized `kb_QueueLock` is not acquired in either path (`keyboard_intern.h:31-32`; sole code use is `InitSemaphore` at `keyboard.c:118`). If the reader checks empty, a remote callback publishes the key and sees no pending request, then the reader enqueues, the callback has already skipped `kbdSendQueuedEvents`; the key remains in the ring until a later callback. The selected input.device owns one read and waits for its reply, making the stall visible to the normal path. Restored OD2389 from the coverage-only candidate to the detailed report and index. Selected ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP manifest paths are documented in the finding. No key or cross-CPU schedule was run. Source-only.

Deneb CMD_FLUSH contract and RTIso boundary pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): compared `cmdFlush()`'s five queued request lists and three scheduled PTD pools (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:973-1041`) with the USBHardware `CMD_FLUSH` contract (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:143-160`) and Poseidon's shutdown caller (`poseidon.library.c:9290-9310`). The contract names in-progress/queued CONTROL, ISO, INT and BULK transfer requests; RTIso is a separately registered, long-lived handler with explicit `UHCMD_STOPRTISO`/`UHCMD_REMISOHANDLER` operations and is not a pending transfer IORequest. USBHub interrupt-signal assignment and OHCI registration caller pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the generic hub's `HubInterrupt` callback through `HIDD_USBDrv_AddInterrupt()` and the selected OHCI per-pipe interrupt queue (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:62-72,145-153`; `workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:453-531`). `HubData.sigInterrupt` is zero-initialized with the OOP instance and has no assignment in the checked USB stack; consequently the callback signals bit 0 and `hub_process()` waits on bit 0 (`usb.h:123`; `usbhubclass.c:628-630,684`). This is the reserved `SIGF_ABORT` bit. The same bit does deliver ordinary hub-change wakeups, and cleanup is performed via a message, not this signal. No selected in-tree producer or documented hub-task abort contract establishes a lost-cancellation consequence, so this signal overlap is not promoted as a standalone defect. It is distinct from OD2962, where OHCI `ClearPortFeature` clears the *calling task's* bit 0. No USB interrupt or abort signal was run. Source-only.

OHCI root-hub port-argument and worker error-path pass (OD2956 scope narrowed; 2026-10-21): traced all selected `USBHub` calls to `PortReset`, `GetPortStatus`, `ClearPortFeature`, and `SetPortFeature` (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:319-344,452-468,477-498,501-598`). Normal `hub_enable()`/`hub_disable()` and `hub_explore()` enumerate ports from 1 through the descriptor's `bNbrPorts`; the reset and status calls use the current loop port, so the unchecked zero/upper bounds in OHCI `PortReset` and missing lower-bound checks in `ClearPortFeature`/`SetPortFeature` are not reached by these selected worker paths. `GetPortStatus` does check both bounds. The weak/malformed descriptor fallback is at least one port, but the descriptor's advertised port count itself is trusted and bounds the same loops; descriptor validation remains a separate scope. `PortReset` remains an externally callable HIDD boundary candidate (OD2956), not a demonstrated normal hub-worker fault. Also rechecked generic `hub->children` allocation and use; its unchecked allocation and later indexed access are already OD2239, and nested-hub child disposal is already OD2469. No additional finding from this caller pass. No port method, allocation failure, malformed descriptor, or hardware was exercised; source-only.

OHCI Root construction allocation/unwind pass (OD2954/OD2955/OD2992/OD2961 rechecked; no additional finding, 2026-10-21): re-read the complete selected `OHCI::Root::New`/`Dispose` region and class initializer (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohciclass.c:59-301,335-369`) against `ohci_CreateTimer`/`ohci_DeleteTimer` and `USB::AttachDriver` (`ohcidriverclass.c:40-96`; `workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbclass.c:117-151`). OHCI RHSC interrupt-to-softint recheck (existing RHSC row retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced the complete selected handler branch from WDH/RHSC status collection through disable/ack, one-second timer submission, hub `Cause()` delivery, not-running `pendingRHSC` handling, and the timer soft-interrupt rearm (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:278-444`; `ohcihub.c:70-90,265-284`). Poseidon CAMD USB OpenPort failure-path census (OD4257 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-21): traced the generated `OpenPort` wrapper through `usbCAMDOpenPort()` and CAMD `OpenDriver()`. CAMD checks the result and unwinds with `EndReceiverProc()` only if it is NULL (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c:148-160`; `camdusbmidi.class.c:387-435`; `camdusbmidi.h:18-20`; `workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:24-56`). Poseidon custom semaphore and nested hub-scan concurrency pass (OD1602 restored/expanded, 2026-10-21): re-read `pLockSemExcl`, `pLockSemShared`, `pUnlockSem`, and the complete `psdBorrowLocksWait` transfer/reclaim path (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:492-675,735-973`) against ExecSMP `Forbid()` semantics (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). Traced nested hub concurrency: `nHubTask` signals its creator before scanning downstream devices (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:408-440`); the parent class scan waits through `psdBorrowLocksWait` while holding the PBase shared lock and device write lock, then can continue sibling scans as the child scans its downstream ports (`poseidon.library.c:6270-6295,6490-6496`). Separate CPUs can therefore mutate the common `ps_Lock.pls_ReadLocks` and wait/borrow records concurrently; ordinary `AddHead` interleaving can lose a reader node while `pls_SharedLockCount` is incremented, and `pUnlockSem` then cannot release the absent record. Restored the absent OD1602 detail and short AROS.md index entry, expanded from the earlier lock-acquisition-only note to include borrowing and this selected caller trigger. No lock, hub, device, or concurrent schedule was exercised; source-only.

USB CAMD MIDI input buffer/parser caller pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the selected `nHidTask()` endpoint completion through `psdGetPipeActual()` into `nParseMidi()` (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:487-505,736-772`). The input transfer is submitted with the fixed 1,024-byte buffer; `nParseMidi()` reads a record only while at least four bytes remain, advances exactly four bytes per record, and derives the adapter index from the low four bits of the first byte's high nibble (0–15), within the 16-entry adapter array. CAMD USB MIDI transmit ring and callback-sentinel recheck (OD4125 strengthened; OD4266 added, 2026-10-21): traced CAMD's `Transmitter()` no-data return (`workbench/libs/camd/miditodriver.c:182-220`) and the selected `GetFromCAMD()` storage/wakeup loop (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c:115-132`) through the USB task's `Wait()`/`nParseMidiOut()` consumer (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:487-507,519-533`). The no-data value `0x100` is stored into a byte slot as zero; when `ca_SysExMode` is active, the consumer treats low-bit-clear bytes as SysEx payload and emits a continuation packet after three (`:703-724`), supporting OD4266's conditional output-corruption finding. Also refined OD4125's boundary: with read=0/write=4095, one-empty-slot capacity is already full; the producer writes slot 4095, masks the next cursor with 4096, publishes 4096, and can iterate again before its final Signal to write at index 4096. If the consumer runs first, its `(write + size - read) & (size-1)` length becomes zero and does not repair the cursor. The existing report now records this sequence and the conditional task timing. The module manifest selects this optional class through `kernel-usb-classes-common` on its declared CPU aliases; the code path is not part of every default ROM. No CAMD stream, USB device, task schedule, or memory boundary was exercised. Source-only.


RTL8029 receive ring count and destination-capacity pass (OD4267 added, 2026-10-21): traced the selected `IntCode()` receive path through `PacketReceived()` and `GetPacket()` and checked the `UnitData` member extent (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:180,1131-1165,1335-1384`). The ring header supplies a 16-bit count; `PacketReceived()` passes it to `GetPacket()` without validation, and `GetPacket()` writes `(len + 1) / 2` words into `ud_RxBuffer[768]` (1,536 bytes). A corrupted or otherwise invalid count over 1,536 bytes therefore writes past the fixed destination into adjacent `UnitData` fields before the packet reaches the SANA-II callback. The configured RTL8029 receive ring and ordinary Ethernet frame range fit this buffer, so no ordinary frame is claimed as a trigger; the candidate is conditional on a bad count in the NIC ring/header. Added OD4267, recommending validation of count and next-page/status before DMA copy and ring advancement. The exact chipset count/status contract and hardware error behavior remain open. No device, packet or ring corruption was induced. Source-only.

WirelessManager SANA-II EAPOL send and selected state-machine caller pass (2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the selected `send_eapol` callback from `wpa_supplicant_eapol_send()`/`wpa_ether_send()` into `wpa_driver_sana2_send_eapol()` and the EAPOL supplicant send callbacks (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/wpas_glue.c:98-105,126-190`; `src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:507-521,1097-1104`; `src/eapol_supp/eapol_supp_sm.c:623-641,832-852`). SANA-II uses the shared request only for synchronous `DoIO`; the async read/event traffic has distinct request allocations, and the selected Amiga event loop dispatches supplicant callbacks serially. `wpa_ether_send()` propagates the `DoIO` result, but EAPOL Start/Logoff/Response callbacks ignore it; their state-machine counters/timers still advance. The state machine increments its transmission counters even if the callback reports failure; these counters are only exposed by its debug MIB output, and no selected caller relies on them. A failed individual frame can still delay/fail its protocol exchange, but this is the underlying write failure rather than a separate request-ownership defect, so no additional driver finding is promoted. This pass adds no full-file line credit; the supplicant translation unit and broader callback lifecycle remain partial. No request, frame or device was used; source-only.

Confirmed the GUI process directly mutates the supplicant configuration/selection and global singly linked timeout list while the main task reads and removes that state; no synchronization or task-message handoff is present in these paths. Added OD4269 to the detailed report and index. No GUI action, timeout interleaving, scan or network operation was run. Source-only.


WirelessManager Amiga MUI scan-list ownership pass (OD4271 added, 2026-10-21): read the complete 238-line `wpa_gui_amiga.c` body and traced scan-result delivery through `events.c:920-935` and MUI list clear/insert/destruct (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:2266-2282,3013-3017,4360-4363`). Each visible BSS allocates an SSID string and a three-pointer item with `AllocVec`/`AllocMem`, then inserts the item; every scan clears the list, but its `ListObject` has no construct/destruct hook, so default destruction frees only internal list entries, not these payloads. AHCI monitor-registration failure caller recheck (OD4063 retained, 2026-10-21; no new OD): traced the sole `ahci_RegisterPort()` caller through its lock release/reacquire and error branch (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:336-365`), then rechecked the monitor's startup signal and `NewCreateTaskA()` failure return (`:61-71,154-184`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:257-272`). Unit publication occurs before task creation; only the successfully started monitor sends `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C`, so a NULL task leaves the caller blocked before `ahci_cam_detach()` can run. This confirms OD4063's trigger and impact; it is distinct from the later-started monitor exit/stale-handle path OD4064 and the per-port worker handshake OD2559. No task creation failure, controller or attach was induced. Source-only.

AHCI port registration allocation/unwind distinction (OD4063 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): checked the `AllocPooled()` failure branch in `ahci_RegisterPort()` against its sole caller and `ahci_cam_detach()` (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:154-184,336-383`). If unit allocation fails, registration returns `ENOMEM` before assigning `ap_sim` or publishing a list node; the caller's detach checks `ap_sim` before unregistering, so that branch does not dereference or free an uninitialized unit. The distinct later `NewCreateTask()` failure remains OD4063: by then the unit is published, and the caller blocks before it can reach detach. No allocation failure or attach was induced. Source-only.

AHCI change-notification list lock and request-reuse recheck (OD2866 retained, 2026-10-21): reread the media-monitor list walk and the BeginIO insertion/completion paths (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:123-136`; `ahci_io.c:246-251,399-410,442-447`). The monitor holds only local `Forbid()` while walking `sim_IOs`; writers use `sim_Lock`. On ExecSMP, neither protects against the other CPU. Also reconfirmed that every BeginIO first inserts the request node, including `TD_REMCHANGEINT`; when a still-linked `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` request is reused, this rewrites its links and one completion-side Remove cannot restore the original list. This remains one finding for the shared list invariant and its independent race/corruption triggers. The selected NTFS, SFS, PFS3, CDVDFS, AFS and FAT callers remain as traced in OD2866. No request or interleaving was run; source-only.

E1000 `DeleteUnit()` teardown caller recheck (2026-10-21; OD2436 retained, no new OD): traced `e1000_init.c` expunge through `DeleteUnit()` and compared the parent frees with `e1000func_Schedular()` shutdown cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000_init.c:224-235`; `unit.c:578-594,1079-1111`). Expunge invokes DeleteUnit for every registered unit; DeleteUnit signals the worker, then releases request queues, PCI mapping, hardware state, and the unit without joining. The worker is responsible for closing the VBLANK request and deleting its timer/input/reply ports, but the raw `e1ku_signal_0` passed by DeleteUnit does not wake the worker's `Wait()` on the normally allocated signal bit 19 (OD2436). This confirms the existing teardown/use-after-free path. No distinct defect established in the checked teardown sequence; constructor failure/handshake paths remain under canonical OD3222 (OD2437 was later withdrawn as a duplicate), and broader timer/device behavior remain open; the current source tracker credits the full 1,195-line `unit.c` body. No unit was loaded or expunged; source-only.

Printer per-unit worker startup failure recheck (OD4287 startup-failure recheck, 2026-10-21): traced the selected module target (`workbench/devs/printer/mmakefile.src:4,13-15`), parent publication/spawn/reply-port failure branch, child `TASK_PRINTERDATA` and `WaitPort` entry, and per-unit `Expunge` (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:144-168,526-544,768-851`). A successful `CreateNewProcTags()` followed by failed parent `CreateMsgPort()` skips the only startup `PutMsg`, then `RemDevice()` invokes an Expunge path that frees the containing zero-open `PrinterUnit` without stopping/joining `pu_Process`; the child can remain blocked with stale `tc_UserData`, or dereference freed data if it starts afterward. OD1889 is the separate ordinary published-unit-before-worker-ready open race; EK9099 is the separate ExecSMP open/expunge dispatch gap. The parent `workbench` aggregate comments out its printer target edge, so the finding is limited to explicit printer-device builds. No worker, allocation failure, or expunge was run. Source-only.

BTHID GUI-release completion ordering recheck (OD3479 retained, 2026-10-21): reread both cleanup tails (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.gui.c:1786-1792`; `bthidctrl.gui.c:408-414`) and the service-release callback plus Bluetooth core caller (`bthid.class.c:294-349`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:590-604`). The callback observes each NULL pointer, then waits for the HID task and frees `nhb` before returning to the caller. Exec explicitly limits `Forbid()` to the calling CPU on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:40-57`), so it does not order that final access against the release task on another CPU. This confirms the existing conditional OD3479; the two GUI cleanup paths share one ownership/order defect. No separate candidate added. No GUI task, service release, or interleaving was run. Source-only.


RTL8029 receive ring header and count-validation recheck (OD4267 retained, 2026-10-21): followed `IntCode()` through `RingBufferNotEmpty()`, `PacketReceived()`, and `GetPacket()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:1131-1165,1335-1384,1564-1578`). `RingBufferNotEmpty()` only compares `ud_NextPage` with the controller's `CURRENT_PAGE`; it does not validate ring-page ranges or the packet header. `PacketReceived()` takes the upper 16 bits of the four-byte header as `len`, does not check header status, count against the 1,536-byte `ud_RxBuffer`, or `nextpage` against `[RX_BUFFER, BUFFER_END)`, and passes the count directly to `GetPacket()`. `GetPacket()` reads `(len + 1) / 2` words, so a count above 1,536 bytes overruns `ud_RxBuffer`; the resulting length is also used for SANA-II delivery. The configured ring spans pages `0x46..0x7f`, but this software path does not establish that the header count/page fields are valid before copying or advancing. This corroborates OD4267; ordinary Ethernet frame bounds remain within the buffer, so the finding remains conditional on malformed/corrupt ring metadata. Exact chipset status/count semantics remain open. No device or malformed header was used; source-only.

RTL8029 short receive-count and SANA-II callback recheck (OD4265/OD4267 qualified, 2026-10-21): traced `IntCode()`'s non-raw `len - (offset << 1)` argument to the selected AROSTCP `m_copy_to_mbuf()` and `sana_read()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:1131-1165`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/sana2copybuff.c:229-281`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:936-947`). For an invalid ring count below 14, unsigned `ULONG` subtraction wraps to a very large length. AROSTCP's callback exhausts the reserved mbuf chain and returns FALSE without setting `ioip_packet`; RTL8029 ignores the result and replies success. If the matching delivered frame is broadcast, `sana_read()` dereferences its still-NULL local packet pointer while applying the broadcast flag. This qualifies the prior OD4265 statement that no in-tree receive failure trigger was established and records the separate low-count consequence under OD4267; it remains conditional on invalid/corrupt controller metadata plus a packet-type match and broadcast destination. No frame, callback, or device was run. Source-only.

RTL8029 SANA-II online/configuration ordering pass (OD4297 added, 2026-10-21): traced `S2_ONLINE()` and `S2ConfigInterface()` through `GoOnline()` and `HardwareInit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:957-1018,1246-1300`). `S2_ONLINE` succeeds without `UF_CONFIGURED`; configuration then masks all interrupts through `HardwareInit()` but skips `GoOnline()` because `UF_ONLINE` remains set, leaving the software state online without the normal interrupt setup. Compared with selected Intel Pro/100 and BTPAN handlers, which return `S2ERR_BAD_STATE`/`S2WERR_NOT_CONFIGURED` before online, and traced selected AROSTCP/WirelessManager callers, which configure first. Added OD4297, conditional on direct SANA-II clients using online-before-config. No device or command sequence was run. Source-only.

RTL8029 SANA-II packet-type tracking dispatch/caller check (no finding, 2026-10-21): traced `DevBeginIO()` immediate command dispatch, `NSDSupported[]`, and AROSTCP's optional `SSF_TRACK` calls (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:294-311,526-553`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:481-505`). PC i8042 mouse setup-task affinity and pre-reset IRQ qualification (OD2331/OD2332 scope recheck, no new OD, 2026-10-21): traced `i8042_mouse_init_task()`'s `NewCreateTask(TASKTAG_PC, ...)` into the task-tag parser and Exec ETask initialization (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseps2.c:188-224`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:116-147`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:131-169`). `TASKTAG_PC` selects the task entry point and no affinity tag is supplied; under ExecSMP the new task inherits its creator's affinity mask, or defaults to the creating CPU if there is no parent ETask. The mouse class registers IRQ12 before reset, then performs the reset under `Disable()` while the controller's mouse-interrupt enable is cleared during the reset sequence (`i8042_mouseps2.c:212-224,382-435`). The driver does not establish which task/CPU invokes module initialization or whether its inherited mask includes the IRQ destination, so the pre-reset cross-CPU IRQ overlap remains a platform/startup gap rather than a new finding. No task, IRQ, or controller was run. Source-only.

PC i8042 disposal versus active IRQ callback recheck (EK9263/OD4299 added, 2026-10-21): compared the selected PC override of `krnRunIRQHandlers()` with the generic dispatcher and `KrnRemIRQHandler()` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:115-132`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:120-143`; `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-75`). The generic reader lock serializes removal, but the PC override never takes it; removal therefore does not wait for an in-progress callback on another CPU before freeing the `IntrNode`. Traced both i8042 Dispose methods through immediate superclass disposal (`i8042_kbdclass.c:335-345`; `i8042_mouseclass.c:94-102`) and added EK9263 plus driver-specific OD4299, conditional on ExecSMP cross-CPU overlap during public driver removal. No event or concurrent schedule was run; source-only.

Printer startup-port failure versus asynchronous Process lifetime recheck (OD4287 strengthened, 2026-10-21): matched the `CreateNewProcTags()` call and second `CreateMsgPort()` failure branch in `Printer_Unit()` with DOS Process defaults and Exec task cleanup (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:526-544,768-851`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:115-143,555-578`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:82-163`). `NP_Synchronous` defaults FALSE, and the printer caller does not override it; a successful process creation therefore returns asynchronously. The child waits on its own `pr_MsgPort` before initialization, while parent startup-message creation failure falls through to `RemDevice()`, whose printer-unit Expunge frees the zero-open unit. No stop/reply message or child join occurs on that branch. This confirms OD4287's stranded Process and stale `tc_UserData` lifetime condition; exact scheduling and DOS segment-unload hook effects remain untested. No worker, allocation failure or expunge was run; source-only.

Printer startup-failure branch separation recheck (OD2699/OD4287 retained as distinct, 2026-10-21): reread `pd_Init()` and the startup handshake (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:403-463,526-566,768-851`) against the selected PostScript `PRS_PREINIT` rejection already traced in the printer caller audit (`:440-458`). OD2699 is the child-side path after startup-message receipt: timer.device opens successfully, `PRS_PREINIT` rejects settings, and cleanup omits `CloseDevice(&pd->pd_TIOR)` before freeing the signal and returning failure. OD4287 is the earlier parent-side startup-reply-port allocation failure: no startup message is sent, the child remains waiting on its own port, and RemDevice frees the unit. The consequences and ordering differ; neither pass establishes runtime occurrence. No startup, device open, or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

E1000 Open ring-helper unwind and finding-boundary recheck (OD3015/OD3020/OD3023 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-21): reread the complete selected `Open`/`Close` hooks (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000_init.c:264-443`) and both TX/RX per-ring and aggregate setup/free helpers (`e1000.c:646-824,846-920`). Each aggregate setup helper frees earlier rings when a later ring fails, and each per-ring helper releases its own allocations on its internal allocation/alignment failures. Thus OD3020 is specifically the cross-stage failure where the one selected TX ring setup succeeds and the subsequent RX ring setup fails; the Open caller does not release that successful TX ring. Confirmed OD3015's count increment precedes opener allocation and no checked Close path decrements it, and OD3023's successful shared Open path reaches `request_irq()` again with the same embedded interrupt nodes while active Close has no removal call. The module manifest selects e1000 for the x86 network targets; this pass adds helper-level boundaries to the existing findings but does not change their conditions or confidence. No allocation failure, Open/Close, interrupt, or hardware operation was run; source-only.

E1000 request-port partial-allocation failure boundary recheck (OD3033 expanded; no new ID, 2026-10-21): followed all four `REQUEST_QUEUE_COUNT` allocation iterations and the common `DeleteUnit()` cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/unit.c:1006-1023,1084-1095`; queue indices in `e1000.h:113-118`). USB HID and Bluetooth HID LowLevel expunge rollback recheck (OD4302 added; OD3466 consequence corrected, 2026-10-21): compared both selected class `libExpunge()` implementations and installers with Exec `SetFunction()`'s return-and-replace semantics (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:95-125,469-481`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:110-145,509-520`; `rom/exec/setfunction.c:89-121`). In each class, if vector 5 is still owned but vector 22 has a competing replacement, the first restore removes that class's vector-5 hook; the second restore returns the competitor, which the mismatch branch puts back before returning FALSE. Thus vector 5 is left at its saved predecessor and vector 22 at the competing function; the class retains its non-NULL LowLevel base, so later installer calls skip and expunge remains refused. Corrected OD3466's prior claim that the second class hook remained installed; added OD4302 for the independent ROM USB HID class implementation. The USB HID module is selected by the `kernel-usb-classes` target (`rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:30-39`; `hid/mmakefile.src:4-10`). No competing patch or expunge was run; source-only.

BCM2711 PCI DMA size-rounding boundary recheck (2026-10-22; no new OD): read `PCIBcm2711__Hidd_PCIDriver__AllocPCIMem()` against the public `ULONG Size` contract and the selected AArch64 mapper (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/driverclass.c:243-276`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mapglobal.c:17-28`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmu.c:305-318`). `ULONG` is 32-bit; for requests above the largest page-roundable size, the 32-bit addition in `PCIMEM_ROUND()` wraps and produces zero. `krnMMUMap()` rejects zero length, so the allocator frees `raw` and returns NULL before publishing an undersized buffer. Requests at the exact aligned upper boundary retain a 4 GiB mapped length and fail through allocation if that range is unavailable; no truncation path established. The checked-in PCI DMA caller census found no near-4-GiB request. This closes only the size-rounding candidate for the BCM2711 override; other mapping and caller contracts remain as recorded. No allocation or map was run; source-only.

AHI_NextAudioID missing-prior-ID sentinel and caller recheck (OD4309 added, 2026-10-22): traced `_AHI_NextAudioID()`'s absent-ID search through the MinList sentinel and the `GetTagData`/`LibFindTagItem`/`LibNextTagItem` implementation (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:282-307`; `database.h:32-40`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:35-41`; `compiler/include/utility/tagitem.h:19-25`; `compiler/arossupport/{libgettagdata,libfindtagitem,libnexttagitem}.c`). The sentinel's flexible-array tag pointer is the database's version/name tail, not a tag list. A removed ID from the documented iterator protocol makes the search call `GetTagData` on those bytes. The initial analysis established the 64-bit overread; the pointer-width recheck below extends it to 32-bit AROS as well, where the 8-byte TagItem stride reaches beyond the database object. Neither path is bounded by the tag scanner. Whole-repository `AHI_NextAudioID` call census found the selected `_AHI_BestAudioIDA` loop (`modeinfo.c:709-724`), the AHI requester (`requester.c:1317-1324`), and AHI Preferences `GetModes()` (`AHI/support.c:863-915`) pass the previous returned ID back on the next iteration; `AddAudioModes` and `ahi.device` startup use `AHI_INVALID_ID` to repeatedly query the first item and do not carry stale IDs. Confirmed selected USB Audio `nFreeAudio` removes modes during interface teardown (`usbaudio.class.c:2081-2095`). The trigger requires removal between iterator calls and another mode keeping the database alive, separating OD4309 from OD1442. No query, removal or runtime memory access was run. Source-only.


AHI_NextAudioID sentinel-width recheck (OD4309 expanded, 2026-10-22): independently laid out `AHI_AudioDatabase`, the embedded `MinList`, sentinel `MinNode`, and `TagItem` for both pointer widths. The sentinel tag pointer starts at `ahidb_Version`; the database's initialized name contributes a nonzero pseudo-tag `"base"` at byte offset 16. On 64-bit, `TagItem` stride 16 makes the next tag read start at offset 32, beyond the 21-byte version/name payload and at-most-7-byte tail padding. On 32-bit, stride 8 makes the next read start at offset 24, beyond that payload and at-most-3-byte padding. `LibNextTagItem()` has no allocation-bound check and stops only at a control tag or NULL; neither embedded pseudo-tag is `TAG_DONE`. Expanded OD4309 from 64-bit-only to both pointer widths. Existing selected caller/removal chain remains as documented; no iteration or removal was performed. Source-only.

AHI database-retirement ownership recheck (OD1442 retained, 2026-10-22): re-read `_AHI_RemoveAudioMode()`'s final-entry branch beside `LockDatabase()`, `LockDatabaseWrite()`, `UnlockDatabase()`, `ReleaseSemaphore()` and `RemSemaphore()`. The remover holds the database write semaphore while unlinking the last node, then enters local `Forbid`, releases the semaphore (which grants/signals existing waiters), removes the public semaphore node and frees the database before `Permit()`. A waiter that already completed `FindSemaphore()` retains the object pointer; single-CPU scheduling postpones it through the free, while ExecSMP `Forbid` does not block another CPU from running the granted waiter. The AHI reader and writer lookup paths still establish users of that pointer. OD1442 remains distinct from OD4309, which requires the database to survive because other modes remain and faults during the next enumeration's missing-ID scan. No semaphore operation or interleaving was run; source-only.

USB Ethernet and Bluetooth PAN binding-release ONLINE-state and write-queue cross-check (OD4312 expanded to nine classes, 2026-10-22): checked each release callback, worker exit, cleanup, `cmdOnline`, and `cmdWrite` in ASIX, CDC Ethernet, Davicom, ethwrap, LAN78xx, MosChip, Pegasus, RNDIS, and BTPAN. All nine release paths stop the worker; cleanup disables the unit signal task without clearing `DDF_ONLINE`/`DDF_CONFIGURED`. Each checked `S2_ONLINE` returns success immediately on the stale ONLINE bit, and each `CMD_WRITE` queues its request and signals only when the unit signal task is non-NULL. Poseidon's documented release contract allows open clients to survive USB release; the Bluetooth class release likewise leaves its unit reserved. A later write can remain pending with no worker. Added this cross-driver scope to OD4312, while leaving the already documented USB read/orphan/event cases in OD3383/OD3384. No USB or Bluetooth unbind or request was exercised; source-only.

Envy24 OD2490 soft-interrupt/Stop caller and target-matrix follow-through (2026-10-22; existing finding retained): rechecked Exec `Cause()` and its dispatcher plus both selected AHI-core Stop callsites (`rom/exec/cause.c:24-28,84-122,145-190`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:719-720,1013-1014`). `Cause()` queues the embedded interrupt once and returns; the dispatcher removes it from the list before enabling interrupts and invoking the callback. `AHI_FreeAudio()` and audio-control updates invoke `AHIsub_Stop()`, whose Envy24 recording path masks/stops the device then frees its DMA buffers without draining queued work or synchronizing an active callback. OD2490 already states the necessary ExecSMP condition; its conditional concurrent-callback path is therefore not narrowed away. No line credit, audio operation, or scheduling interleaving. Source-only.

VIA Rhine private-state PCI allocation/deallocation reconciliation (OD4338 added, 2026-10-22): traced `rhineu_fe_priv` from `CreateUnit()`'s selected PCIDriver `AllocPCIMem()` through every `DeleteUnit()` call (constructor rollback and device expunge). The all-PC PCIPC class overrides `MapPCI` but inherits the generic allocator/free pair; the allocator returns a 4-KiB-aligned interior pointer with the `AllocVec` base stored immediately before it, and `FreePCIMem()` recovers that base. `DeleteUnit()` instead calls ordinary `FreeMem()` on the interior pointer, which routes the wrong extent to the system allocator and bypasses the saved-base free contract. Added OD4338, scoped to explicit VIA Rhine builds paired with PCIPC and allocator manifestation. Updated the unit inventory row; no source was changed or device/deletion path run. Source-only.

PCIPC MapPCI top-of-U64 range lead closure (2026-10-22; no finding): checked the selected x86-64 map helper's physical-address encoding (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mapglobal.c:39-79`) against the PCI HIDD `MapPCI` message length type and PCIDevice's 64-bit BAR reconstruction (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:666-691`). The MMU encodes 20 high physical bits above bit 31 (52-bit physical address ceiling); the map request length is a 32-bit `ULONG`. For a valid representable BAR, base + length + 2 MiB page-rounding slack cannot overflow 64-bit arithmetic. Replaced the ledger's unverified valid-BAR reachability note with this source-backed exclusion; invalid BARs above the processor's physical range are outside the valid-device trigger. OD2657's separate four-level noncanonical virtual-address condition remains open/conditional. No BAR or mapping was used. Source-only.

PCILinux MapPCI result and caller-selection census (2026-10-22; candidate held coverage-only): the hosted Linux PCI HIDD explicitly sets `aHidd_PCIDriver_DirectBus=FALSE` (`arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/driverclass.c:48-60`) and its `MapPCI` override returns the unmodified result of raw Linux `mmap` syscall 192 (`:123-147`; the local syscall wrappers also preserve raw `int $0x80` results in `syscall.h:17-32`). Linux syscall failures are negative errno values, so they are non-NULL pointer values; the generic PCI class instead uses `(APTR)-1` for unsupported indirect translation (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:160-178`). Repository-wide direct call census found all driver calls, but the Linux root target selects `workbench-hosted`, `workbench-unix`, `workbench-devs-tap-unix`, `workbench-devs-eth-unix`, and `kernel-hidd-pci` (`arch/all-linux/mmakefile.src`); it does not establish that the PCI BAR-mapping callers in the PC/i386 and PC/x86_64 device targets are built against PCILinux. The selected Linux target's own source also does not call `MapPCI` directly. Thus the raw-error return is a concrete backend/API mismatch, but no selected in-tree dereference of that error result is established yet; retain as coverage-only pending the Linux package/PCI caller selection trace. No mmap, PCI device, or failure was induced; source-only.

OD842 cross-platform constructor comparison (2026-10-22): compared the three selected ParallelUnit Root.New implementations after restoring the public-class candidate. PC indexes `bases[unitnum]` without a bound check (`arch/i386-pc/drivers/parallel.hidd/ParallelUnitClass.c:43,54-85`); hosted Unix indexes `unitname[unitnum]` and passes the result to `Hidd_UnixIO_OpenFile` (`arch/all-unix/hidd/parallel/ParallelUnitClass.c:46-51,65-110`). Both classes are registered with the same public `CLID_Hidd_ParallelUnit` and accept the public unit tag; their parent factories are the only checked-in callers and constrain 0–2. Native m68k's constructor returns NULL for any nonzero unit value (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/parallel/ParallelUnitClass.c:48-64`). Expanded OD842 to PC and hosted Unix; no unit object, host open, or port I/O was run. Source-only.
Parallel device CMD_READ/CMD_WRITE completion and Exec request-result pass (OD4342 added, 2026-10-22): traced active-request abort through `CMD_RESET` (`workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_init.c:483-500`), successful read/write completion (`:341-468`), and Exec `DoIO()` (`rom/exec/doio.c:57-75`). Reset writes `IOERR_ABORTED` to in-flight requests and replies them; `DoIO()` resets flags/message state only and returns `io_Error`; the parallel read/write branches set `io_Actual` but leave `io_Error` untouched. Therefore reusing a reset-aborted request can return `IOERR_ABORTED` after a later successful operation. Added OD4342 to this report and the master index. The adjacent negative-length concern was rejected: `IOStdReq.io_Length` is `ULONG`, and `-1` is the all-bits-set sentinel. No request, reset or port operation was run; source-only.

OD3221 remains the distinct stale active-pointer/reply defect. Source-only; no request or callback was run.

Printer raw-write-to-port-close caller trace (OD872 strengthened, 2026-10-22): followed the selected `workbench-fs-port` path (`workbench/fs/port/mmakefile.src:3,7-11`). A `PAR:` handler opened with `/RAW` maps `ACTION_WRITE` to `PRD_RAWWRITE` and synchronously calls `DoIO` (`port-handler.c:121-124,440-451`); `printer.device` handles that command by scheduling `pd_PWrite`'s alternating backend `SendIO` and replies the outer request immediately (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:218-241,618-626,658`). A subsequent `ACTION_END` immediately invokes `portClose`, which calls `CloseDevice` and destroys the file's IORequest/port (`port-handler.c:347-355,465-471`). Printer `pd_Close` closes both backend devices without first waiting for the outstanding alternating write (`driver.c:466-485`). This establishes a normal checked-in caller route to OD872's close-with-pending-write condition, in addition to the PostScript trailer route previously recorded. Actual backend close/completion ordering remains unverified; no raw print job or I/O was run. Source-only.

printer.device text-write tail scope correction (OD3643 expanded, 2026-10-22): reread the complete `Printer_Text_Write()` body and both selected converter paths (`workbench/devs/printer/text.c:293-352`; `workbench/printers/postscript/postscript.c:238-265,999-1029`). The earlier OD3643 wording incorrectly limited the defect to `ps_Version < 34`: bundled PostScript v44's converter appends ordinary ASCII to the same function-local buffer, while `Printer_Text_Write()` has no final flush. A short PostScript `CMD_WRITE` containing ordinary ASCII therefore sends no text but the command handler reports the full length as successful (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:609-617`). Broadened OD3643 in the detailed report and index to all converters that buffer ordinary text, explicitly including PostScript. No print request was run; source-only.

printer.device command and text-buffer lifetime pass (OD4343/OD4344 added, 2026-10-22): reread `Printer_Text_Command()` and `Printer_Text_Write()` completely (`workbench/devs/printer/text.c:1-352`) against the PostScript command table/callback (`workbench/printers/postscript/postscript.c:43-125,965-994`), the two-request `pd_PWrite()` alternation (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:218-241`), outer `CMD_WRITE` replies (`:609-626,658`), and selected parallel HIDD completion behavior. Added OD4343: each command invocation starts formatting in `pd_Stk`, then submits that buffer via `SendIO`; the next invocation reuses the same buffer but `pd_PWrite` alternates to the other IORequest and does not wait for the prior one, allowing successive commands in one text write to overwrite pending output. Added OD4344: `Printer_Text_Write` submits its function-local buffers asynchronously and can return before a pending backend request finishes; Unix partial writes and m68k one-byte writes provide selected continuation paths that retain the request pointer. Both entries are in the report and index. These are distinct from OD3643's missing final flush, which can drop a buffered tail before submission. No command, text write, backend callback or printer operation was run; source-only.

printer.device CSI parameter-index bounds pass (OD4345 added, 2026-10-22): traced `Printer_Text_Write()` and `doState()` across the full `text.c` body (`workbench/devs/printer/text.c:228-352`). `parm[4]` and `pindex` are initialized once per `Printer_Text_Write`; each new CSI only resets `parm[0]`, while the `CSI_BRACK_SEMI` promotion increments the persistent index and stores a new parameter byte (`:233-239,256-269`). This confirms OD2193: opening port zero writes `UserData[-1]`, before the four-element array. The array has no in-tree consumer, so the invalid write is established but collateral effects remain unknown. Rechecked the global `TransmitFunc` overwrite candidate and did not promote it: every CAMD port receives the same `Transmitter` function, and `ActivateXmit` receives that per-port `DriverData` userdata directly; `UserData[]` is unused. No MIDI port was opened or build run. Credited 74 code lines and one selected source path to the represented ledger, but did not recalculate its denominator or percentage; this is not a fresh full build-selected census. Source-only.

Optional ROM USB HID PS3 controller quirk pass (2026-10-22; no finding promoted): read the complete `nQuirkPS3Controller()` body (20 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) and traced its sole caller from successful HID report-descriptor parsing (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1203`). The helper gates the class `GET_REPORT` request on vendor/product `0x054c:0x0268`, checks and logs `psdDoPipe()` status, and otherwise leaves class state unchanged; its returned report buffer is not consumed in this source path. The caller continues ordinary class setup regardless of the quirk request result. No in-tree evidence establishes that the fetched report is required for subsequent behavior, so no failure-handling defect is promoted. No controller or control transfer was used. Credited 20 full-body code lines and one helper path; the Workbench package-selected HID translation unit and its broader lifecycle/caller inventory remain partial. Source-only.

Optional ROM USB HID usage-node allocator and parser-caller pass (2026-10-22; no new OD): read the complete `nAddUsage()` body (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:4487-4506`; 19 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and traced all nine call sites in the already-reviewed `nParseReport()` (`:3264-3370`). The helper rejects reversed ranges, allocates before list insertion, initializes both range fields, and returns failure without publishing a partial node. Each parser caller sets the parse result to failure when allocation or range validation fails; the parser's common tail frees all accumulated usage, designator and string nodes. No independent allocator or unwind defect established. The active `kernel-usb-classes` and `kernel-usb` rules select HID, and x86-64 PC/OpenSBI package routes include it (`hid/mmakefile.src:4-12`; `classes/mmakefile.src:40,49`). This pass remains limited to the listed helper and callers. No descriptor, allocation failure or device was used. Credited 19 full-body code lines; no aggregate denominator or whole-area percentage recalculated. Source-only.


HID singleton-root race recheck (OD1456 qualified, 2026-10-22): traced `Mouse__Root__New`'s injected cached hub through `Input__Hidd_Input__AddHardwareDriver`, and reconciled the race against module startup. Both keyboard and mouse init hooks eagerly create the cached root with `HW_AddDriver`; genmodule publishes the class in `CLASSESINIT` before calling `INITLIB` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:986-1004`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:42-62`; generated AddClass hook source `tools/genmodule/oopsupport.c:164-181`). This rules out routine concurrent first use after init, but leaves a narrow public lookup interval after class publication and before the eager constructor completes. The selected serialmouse and PC i8042 callers show the returned-root registration contract; no checked-in overlapping schedule was established. OD1456 trigger and confidence were narrowed accordingly. No input or concurrency was run. Source-only.


Clipboard device complete-body and selected-caller pass (OD4355 added; OD3642/OD3644 rechecked, 2026-10-22): read all 921 physical lines of `workbench/devs/clipboard/clipboard.c` (658 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) and the complete private unit/base header (40 code lines). VMware SVGA threaded IRQ caller/unwind reconciliation (OD4035 confirmed; OD4178 retained; no additional finding, 2026-10-22): traced `vmw_irq_install()` from driver load through vector allocation, per-vector `request_threaded_irq()` registration, and failure cleanup (`vmwgfx_drv.c:1018-1028,1127-1157`; `vmwgfx_irq.c:325-365`). `num_irq_vectors` counts only successful registrations, so the selected failure unwind frees only installed handlers before releasing the vector set. Traced normal unload and load-failure cleanup (`vmwgfx_drv.c:1130-1157,1160-1201`): both call `vmw_fence_manager_takedown()` before `vmw_irq_uninstall()`. The latter masks device interrupts, acknowledges status, then calls `free_irq()` (`vmwgfx_irq.c:297-315`); the selected compatibility `free_irq()` removes and frees its entry without cancelling or draining queued `thread_work` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm-compat/linux_irq.c:92-105`). A queued fence thread can therefore reach the freed fence manager, confirming OD4035 on normal and failed-load teardown paths. The wait deadlines continue to use the settable compatibility clock covered by OD4178. IRQ register semantics and runtime interleavings remain unverified; no IRQ or device operation was run. Source-only.


VMware SVGA IRQ-install failure caller pass (OD4356 added; OD4035 and OD4178 rechecked, 2026-10-22): traced `vmw_irq_install()` through the selected AROS PCI compatibility wrappers, PCIPC MSI allocator, and `vmw_probe()` error path (`vmwgfx_irq.c:325–365`; `drm-compat/linux_pci.c:331–383`; `drm-compat/linux_irq.c:65–78`; `vmwgfx_drv.c:1021–1027,1154–1158,1647–1675`). MSI acquisition succeeds and sets `pdev->msi_enabled`; if the first IRQ-entry `kzalloc()` fails, `request_threaded_irq()` returns `-ENOMEM`, `vmw_irq_install()` exits without freeing vectors, and `vmw_driver_load()` jumps to `out_no_irq`, bypassing `vmw_irq_uninstall()`. The selected PCIPC backend can enable one MSI vector; the established consequence is retained device MSI configuration and vector reservation after failed probe, with a later retry rejected for an MSI-only device; no installed handler is needed for this path. Added OD4356. Kept this distinct from OD4035, which concerns already queued/running thread work during teardown, and OD4178, the time-source mismatch. No PCI device, probe, or allocation failure was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau/VMware compatibility IRQ registration failure pass (OD4357 added for both selected callers; OD4035, OD4356 and OD4178 retained, 2026-10-22): traced the complete compatibility `request_threaded_irq()` and `free_irq()` bodies through Exec `AddIntServer()`/`RemIntServer()`, selected PC `KrnAddIRQHandler()`/`KrnRemIRQHandler()`, and VMware install, rollback and unload (`drm-compat/linux_irq.c:64-105`; `rom/exec/addintserver.c:64-67`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-110`; `rom/exec/remintserver.c:51-55`; `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-56`; `drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_irq.c:297-369`; `drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_drv.c:1021-1033,1154-1159,1199-1201`). If PC kernel interrupt-node allocation returns NULL, Exec stores that token but its void API cannot report failure; the compatibility wrapper still returns 0, so `vmw_irq_install()` counts the vector and driver initialization continues without an installed PC IRQ route. Later `free_irq()` passes the stored NULL token through `RemIntServer()` to the generic pre-guard dereference (EK09/EK815). Added OD4357, distinct from OD4356's compatibility-entry `kzalloc()` failure, which VMware detects and whose error path skips vector cleanup. The optional VMware target is explicitly buildable. Rechecked on 2026-11-08: the Nouveau compatibility copy has the same unchecked AddIntServer result; `nvkm_intr_install()` treats request_irq success as installed, sets `device->intr.alloc`, and its destructor later calls `free_irq()` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/core/intr.c:349-379`; `engine/device/base.c:3452-3459`). On the PC backend, a NULL KrnAddIRQHandler token is hidden the same way, and subsequent `RemIntServer()` reaches the pre-guard NULL dereference in `KrnRemIRQHandler()` (`rom/exec/remintserver.c:51-55`; `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-56`). Both optional HIDDs are affected on PC under kernel IRQ-node allocation failure. No allocation failure, IRQ, probe or teardown was induced; source-only.


Optional ROM USB HID descriptor enumeration pass (OD4358 added; 2026-10-22): read all of `nReadReports()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2062-2450`) and traced its initialization and reload callers (`:1015-1075,1210-1264`) plus `UsbHidDesc` layout (`compiler/include/devices/usb_hid.h:45-56`). The consistency check for `6 + 3*bNumDescriptors > actlen` only logs; parsing proceeds. The copy allocation uses `bLength`, but the loop follows `bNumDescriptors`, so inconsistent or short descriptors can make the loop read entry type/length fields beyond the copy. Added OD4358 to the detailed report and index. Rechecked report-object allocation/free on failed fetch or parse and the report-map/item-map construction paths; partial reports are released by `nFreeReport()` on parse failure. On report-map or item-map allocation failure, `nReadReports()` returns FALSE without draining built state, and `nAllocHid()`/`nHidTask()` failure cleanup does not call `nFreeHid()`. Added OD4359 for the resulting allocation leak. This rechecks a function already credited as full-body and adds caller/failure-path evidence without new line credit; the HID translation unit and Other Drivers scope remain incomplete. No USB descriptor or transfer was used; source-only.

Mesa 26.0.0 VC4 blit, buffer-manager, resource, screen, context, command-list and shader-program full-body passes (OD4362–OD4374 added; 2026-10-23): verified `OPT_MESAGL` defaults to 26.0.0 (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa.cfg:12-21`) and the VC4 manifest fallback selects these sources when Mesa's `Makefile.sources` is absent (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/mmakefile.src:29-78,122-124`). Read all 399, 530, 951, 424, 132, 56, 44 and 2,341 `cloc 2.06` C lines of imported `vc4_blit.c`, `vc4_bufmgr.c`, `vc4_resource.c`, `vc4_screen.c`, `vc4_context.c`, `vc4_cl.c`, `vc4_cl_dump.c` and `vc4_program.c`. Traced stencil blits through the registered context entry point, sampler-view creation and generic blitter; traced BO imports through `vc4_resource_from_handle()`, transfer mapping through registered helpers and tiling routines, screen and context lifecycle through the local HIDD bridge, command-list growth through packet emitters, debug dumps through `vc4_job_submit()`, and NIR translation through shader compilation. Added OD4362: the uncached BO path dereferences an unchecked `CALLOC_STRUCT(vc4_bo)` result before the caller's NULL check. Added OD4363: `vc4_resource_create_with_modifiers()` dereferences resource state after `vc4_resource_setup()` can return NULL; this is the registered ordinary resource-creation method. Added OD4364: tiled read mapping passes an unchecked staging `malloc()` result to the image conversion routine, which writes through the destination. Added OD4365: `vc4_screen_create()` dereferences its unchecked top-level `rzalloc()` result before the local HIDD can handle a NULL return. Added OD4366: the separately allocated BO-handle table is not destroyed when chip identification fails, so retries leak it. Added OD4367: the selected transfer-helper constructor dereferences a failed `calloc()` during VC4 screen setup. Added OD4368: context initialization restores the global shader-db debug flag only on success, so failures suppress later requested diagnostics. Added OD4369: command-list debug dumps allocate decoder state for each submission but return before freeing it (and do not free the spec on fall-through). Added OD4370: command-list growth does not check `reralloc()` before callers emit packets. Added OD4371: resource-backed constant-buffer references survive explicit unbind and context destruction. Added OD4372: NIR translation writes through the unchecked component-array allocation used for SSA definitions. Added OD4373: stencil-blit sampler-view construction uses a truthy enum instead of a texture-target comparison, constraining array views to layer zero. Added OD4374: stencil blit does not check for the registered sampler-view constructor's NULL return before the generic blitter dereferences it. Rechecked shared export and found no selected AROS caller requesting `WINSYS_HANDLE_TYPE_SHARED`; AROS lacks GEM_FLINK dispatch, and `vc4_bo_flink()` frees its BO on failure while the resource retains the pointer, so this remains an unpromoted external-API candidate.
