BWFM background-task opener-count / AROSTCP offline caller pass (OD4404 added; 2026-10-23): traced first-open `open()` through `load_firmware()` and `start_pump()`, then matched its long-lived RX/association-worker `lib_OpenCnt` pins to genmodule's generated successful device-open increment (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1250-1257`). With AROSTCP as the sole external opener and either worker pin active, the count exceeds one and the stack skips the command; BWFM's online flag remains set. BWFM is an explicitly buildable optional Raspberry Pi driver, not included by the default networks aggregate. No interface shutdown or device was run; source-only.
OD4404 AROSTCP caller/reopen recheck (2026-10-23; no new finding): confirmed both routine paths into `sana_down()`: clearing `IFF_UP` through `SIOCSIFFLAGS` (`if_sana.c:627-645`) and `sana_deinit()` during AROSTCP teardown (`:158-178`, called from `kern/amiga_main.c:510`). BWFM assigns `unit->online = FALSE` only in the `S2_OFFLINE` handler (`bwfm_dev.c:1667`); its close path decrements unit `refcount` and removes the opener but does not provide an alternate offline transition. Thus either selected caller leaves the device online when the library-count check suppresses the command, while reporting success locally. No subsequent BWFM state transition repairs that missed offline event merely because AROSTCP closes its opener; the worker tasks continue to hold the module base. Expanded OD4404's trigger/consequence and index summary. No device, ioctl, or teardown was run; source-only.


<a id="od4404-sana-unrun-teardown-qualification"></a>OD4404 AROSTCP teardown wait qualification (2026-10-31; no new finding): re-read all `sana_down()` call sites and the immediately following `sana_unrun()` path (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:158-178,593-600,627-645,875-925`). The underlying OD4404 state mismatch remains: `sana_down()` returns success without sending `S2_OFFLINE` when the background-worker references keep `lib_OpenCnt` above one, while BWFM clears `unit->online` only in its OFFLINE handler. xHCI interrupt request-list AbortIO race (OD4411 added; 2026-10-23): traced UHCMD_INTXFER enqueue through the event-task scheduler and Exec AbortIO into Poseidon's abort/wait/free path (`uhwcmd.c:1253-1295,1819-1827,1875-1888`; `xhci_hw.c:533-538`; `xhci_periodic.c:48-108`; `poseidon.library.c:4779-4802,4817-4825,4650-4679`). `ForeachNodeSafe` saves a request pointer before the scheduler body; AbortIO can concurrently unlink and reply that request. The scheduler has no common list lock, and `Disable()` is local-CPU-only on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:54-61`). Added OD4411 for the conditional stale-request/list race; distinguished it from OD2194 disconnect teardown and OD1384 cancellation cleanup. No I/O or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.


PL011BT power-capability candidate and package/caller recheck (OD3577 retained and narrowed; 2026-10-23): corrected the H:4 caller path to `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bluetooth/h4bthci/h4bthci_unit.c`, then reconciled both Raspberry Pi boot manifests, module manifests and package component lists. AArch64 has build dependencies for PL011BT and H:4, but its `PKG_RSRC` embeds `mbox.resource` and `pl011bt.resource` while `PKG_DEVS` omits H:4. ARM32 has no PL011BT/H:4 build dependency; its package includes mbox but neither PL011BT nor H:4. The separate BCM2708 convenience package includes PL011BT in `PKG_RSRC` but its parent package dependency is disabled. Re-read the H:4 worker's Claim→SetPower→Configure sequence and release-on-failure branch against PL011BT's optional mailbox acquisition, unconditional POWER_CONTROL capability and unavailable return. A repository-wide source search found no `PL011BTGetCapabilities()` caller; H:4 is the only checked-in `PL011BTSetPower()` client and is not embedded in either default Raspberry Pi package. OD3577 is retained as an exposed API capability mismatch without claiming a default-image caller trigger. The selected H:4 startup consequence requires a custom installation/package and unavailable mailbox, while any PL011BT API client can observe the false capability when mbox is unavailable. No firmware/resource failure, driver startup or hardware operation was induced; source-only.

PCI xHCI interrupt scheduler/AbortIO and endpoint-index recheck (OD4411 retained; no new finding; 2026-10-23): re-read `xhciScheduleIntTDs()` and the complete `cmdAbortIO()` search/queued-completion path. USB HID reset-chord list-walk and keyboard-device synchronization recheck (OD2603 expanded; 2026-10-23): traced `nCheckReset()`'s temporary stack node publication, list-head recovery, removal and later `Cause()` traversal (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6532-6610`) against keyboard.device BeginIO and interrupt-side `writeEvents()` (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:311-324,350-380,398-512,679-690`). The helper sets `is_Code` to NULL before KBD_ADD and walks the live list after KBD_REM/Permit; the device's Disable/Enable only protects the short mutation, while Forbid does not mask interrupts. Thus a reset-key interrupt during publication can reach the temporary node even on a single CPU. The unlocked task-context traversal also calls `Cause()`, whose selected Cause/Enable path can process softints and reschedule; a handler removal/free can invalidate the next-node read. PFS3 and VMM selected cleanup paths remove and free handler nodes. Expanded OD2603 beyond its former ExecSMP-only framing; no duplicate finding added. No keyboard event, reset chord, schedule or removal was induced. Focused helper/caller evidence only; no whole-file line credit. Source-only.

Bluetooth HID output/feature report-capacity and transport caller pass (OD3454 expanded; 2026-10-23): traced descriptor-derived output/feature bit counts through `bReadReports()`'s `nhb_MaxReportSize` calculation and `nhb_EPOutBuf` allocation (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1600-1640,1190-1204`), configured action flush (`:5665-5695`), and both `bSendReport()` transport branches (`:756-817`). For Classic HIDP, the packet buffer is fixed at `BTHID_MAXREPORT + 2` bytes; its one-byte HIDP header and optional Report ID leave 257 or 256 data bytes, respectively, and the helper silently clamps longer writes before synchronous `btDoChannel()`. The flush then clears the touched flags. HOGP uses the independent GATT path and is not included in that clamp consequence. Expanded OD3454 with Classic output/feature truncation; the existing input-field-overrun portion remains separate within that finding. No whole-file credit claimed; the BTHID translation unit remains partial. No descriptor, action, channel, or device was used; source-only.

USB PTP `nAllocVec()`/`nFreeVec()` all-callsite size and ownership recheck (no new OD; 2026-10-23): inventoried every `nAllocVec()` call in `ptp.class.c` (`:576-587,624,813,1157,1166,1197,1840,2195,2201,2453,2919,2948,2975,3062,3410,3484,4247,4249`). PIMA string allocations use a one-byte character count (`nGetPimaStr()`/`nGetPimaStrFiltered()`), and DOS paths are first converted into the 256-byte packet-local buffer; these lengths cannot wrap the allocator's four-byte header addition. `nGetPTPRsp()` allocates `pr_DataLength = response_length - 12`, so the maximum representable 32-bit PTP container payload plus the four-byte pool header stays below `ULONG_MAX`; the separate unchecked receive-capacity arithmetic remains OD4417. The only large mutable file-buffer size is `nPTPWrite()`'s growth loop, where 512-KiB increments can wrap and cycle before reaching allocation (OD4445); no independent `nAllocVec()` size-header wrap was established on a selected call path. `nFreeVec()` reads the stored pool-size header and matches the allocator for PTP-owned results; the borrowed response-buffer misuse remains OD4448. No allocation or free was run; source-only.

USB PTP object-protection helper and DOS `ACTION_SET_PROTECT` caller pass (no new OD; 2026-10-23): read `nPTPSetObjectProtection()` completely (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:2514-2566`) and traced its sole dispatcher path through `ACTION_SET_PROTECT`, `SetProtection()` packet argument conversion, and DeviceInfo operation-capability parsing (`ptp.class.c:1467-1676,3661-3680`; `rom/dos/setprotection.c:42-63`). USB PTP DOS lock/file-handle allocation and reference-drain pass (OD4428/OD4429/OD4437 rechecked; no new OD; 2026-10-23): read `nCreateLock()`, `nFreeLock()`, `nCreateFH()`, and `nFreeFH()` completely (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:2962-3108`), then reconciled every allocator/free call in `nHandleDOSPackets()` and the worker's shutdown gate (`:3327-3437,3516-3560,3598,3796-3924,4065-4102`). USB PTP MTP string-prefix probe bound recheck (no new OD; 2026-10-23): traced `psdGetStringDescriptor(pp, 0xee)` from the complete selected Poseidon implementation (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2364-2518`) and API contract (`rom/usb/docs/poseidon.doc:1721-1744`) into the PTP four-byte `MSFT` comparison (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:145-162`). Poseidon allocates from the descriptor's character count, writes at most that many converted characters, and always appends a NUL; empty results return NULL. The PTP comparison uses short-circuit `&&`, so a string shorter than four characters fails at its first mismatching character or terminator before reading a later position; a three-character `MSF` result has its terminator at index 3 within the allocation. The initial fixed-length concern is therefore not supported by this caller/producer contract. Complete producer/helper and selected-caller slice only; no descriptor or device was used; source-only.

BTHID class-default config form lifetime follow-up (OD9690 expanded; 2026-10-25): traced `libOpen()` into `bLoadClassConfig()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:86-91,526-592`) and `btGetClsCfg()` into `btFindCfgForm()`/`btNextCfgForm()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/config.c:317-376,843-859`). These APIs return form pointers after releasing their per-call shared lock; `btGetCfgChunk()` takes a lock only while locating/copying each chunk and does not hold the form alive between separate requests (`config.c:495-525`). `bLoadClassConfig()` uses `Forbid()`, which does not block an ExecSMP import on another CPU; `btReadCfg(NULL, buf)` replaces and recursively frees the configuration tree under its exclusive lock (`config.c:54-104,1296-1308`). A class open for a new service binding can overlap Preferences import while the stack runs. Expanded OD9690 to include this class-default load path. MassStorage worker final-Forbid exit-path check (2026-10-23; no new OD): `nFreeMS()` balances its first `Forbid()` at `:1866-1876`, then performs a final `Forbid()` before clearing `ncm_Task` and signaling the waiter without a source-level `Permit()` (`massstorage.class.c:1891-1898`). Traced the no-DOS branch of Poseidon's `psdSpawnSubTask()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1466-1503`) into `AddTask()` with the default `SysBase->TaskExitCode` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:303`), then through `Exec_TaskFinaliser()` to self-`RemTask()` (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:52-55`). Self-removal resets the retiring task's forbid nesting to `-1` before dispatch (`rom/exec/remtask.c:131-163`), so the unmatched final Forbid does not leave the CPU's scheduler forbidden on this task exit path; it protects the final task-pointer/signal publication until the worker exits. `psdSpawnSubTask()` also has a DOS `CreateNewProcTags()` path, whose process-return finalization is not concluded by this check. No task or teardown was run; source-only.

MassStorage worker DOS-process exit-path check (2026-10-23; no new OD): completed the DOS branch left open in the preceding final-Forbid check. `CreateNewProcTags()` installs `DosEntry` as the process task entry (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:543-550`); `DosEntry()` performs process and DOS cleanup, then returns (`:808-1005`). `AddTask()` supplies `SysBase->TaskExitCode` when no final PC is specified (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:301-306`), and Exec's default finalizer self-removes the task (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:51-55`). The self-`RemTask()` path sets the retiring task's forbid nesting to `-1` before dispatch (`rom/exec/remtask.c:130-163`), so the final unmatched `Forbid()` in `nFreeMS()` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:1891-1898`) does not establish a scheduler-forbidden leak for either the direct-task or DOS-process spawn path. Traced BWFM's `S2_ONLINE` dispatch through `try_join()` to `BWFMJoin()` and its three 200-iteration, 50-ms waits (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:880-905,1660-1664`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2493-2495,2535-2577`). NVMe AbortIO asynchronous BeginIO reachability recheck (OD4472 retained; no new OD; 2026-10-23): reread `BeginIO()`'s request publication/completion branches and `AbortIO()` in `rom/devs/nvme/nvme_io.c:230-423,430-440`, then followed submitted reads/writes through `nvme_sector_rw()` and the queue completion handler (`:124-195`; `nvme_queue_io.c:28-88,92-145`; `nvme_queue_admin.c`/`nvme_controllerclass.c` queue-task callers). A non-quick request is put on `unit->au_IOs`, its node is removed before hardware submission, and `BeginIO()` returns without replying when completion has not arrived during its bounded immediate CQ drain; the queue task later releases DMA, writes status/actual length and signals the client path. The AbortIO vector still returns zero without marking `IOERR_ABORTED`, cancelling the command slot, or changing the submitted write. Thus OD4472 applies to genuinely outstanding asynchronous read/write requests, not only a queued-before-submit request. Every checked-in NVMe parent boot edge remains commented; direct module builds are available for the configurations listed in OD4472, and no maintained direct opener was found. The finding and external/configured-client qualification remain accurate. No queue, request, abort, controller, build or hardware was exercised; source-only.

Bluetooth BTErrorLog caller and target-scope pass (2026-10-23; OD4474 retained, no new finding): read all 114 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/shellcommands/BTErrorLog.c`, tracing option parsing, Bluetooth library ownership, error-list lock selection, entry reads/printing, optional flush/removal, unlock and close. The utility calls `btRemErrorMsg()` while flushing but does not register for Bluetooth events or consume the removal-event Param1; it does not demonstrate an in-tree dereference of OD4474's freed pointer. Its source is in the direct `bluetooth-shellcommands` `%build_progs` target, but the `kernel-bluetooth` aggregate edge to that target is commented in `rom/bluetooth/mmakefile.src:6-12`; no default-package inclusion is claimed. OD4473/OD4474 therefore remain conditional on other registered subscribers using the documented object pointer. No utility, event, or flush was run; source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi timer SMP startup and shared-clock recheck (OD9393 added; 2026-10-23): corrected the prior core-0-only qualification after tracing `bcm27xx_init()` under `__AROSEXEC_SMP__`: it installs the trampoline and wakes secondary cores through PSCI or the spin-table, then waits for `cpu_Register()` (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_bcm27xx.c:309-320,339-429`; SMP is selected by the RasPi `smp` variant in `configure.in:2195-2199`). The direct `kernel-timer` target selects the AArch64 Raspberry Pi override (`arch/aarch64-raspi/timer/mmakefile.src:5-8`), and `GetSysTime()` calls its `EClockUpdate()` inside `Disable()`, which only masks the calling core (`rom/timer/getsystime.c:54-61`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/timer/ticks.c:23-57`). The standard package includes `kernel-timer` through the active `#MM` edge and `timer` in `PKG_DEVS_ARCH` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-118,217-232`). Confirmed that the CAS makes `tbp_EClockLast` monotonic, but does not serialize the subsequent non-atomic `ADDTIME()` writes to shared `tb_CurrentTime` and `tb_Elapsed`: a second core can claim a later interval before the first caller finishes adding its interval, allowing their seconds/microseconds field updates to overlap and lose or mis-normalize elapsed time. Added OD9393 for this SMP-only shared-clock accounting race. The prior inference that secondaries remain parked was false for the `smp` variant; non-SMP builds still leave them parked. The initial list-lock and rearm concerns from this pass were later confirmed and recorded as OD9394 and OD9395 after checking the target initializer and both callers. No time query, timer interrupt, SMP schedule, or hardware operation was run; source-only.


AArch64 Raspberry Pi timer SMP list-lock caller correction (OD9394 added; 2026-10-23): the earlier timer rows said secondary cores remained parked and that no cross-core trigger existed. Traced the actual `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` branch in `platform_bcm27xx.c`, which releases cores through PSCI or the spin-table, and compared the selected architecture-specific `Timer_Init()` with generic `common_init`/`timer_init`. `common_init` creates the request lists but only generic `timer_init` opens `execlock.resource` and allocates `tb_ListLock`; the AArch64 override never does. Therefore `lowlevel.c` skips its conditional locks for insertion and expiration, and `Timer_Reprogram()` likewise reads the shared MICROHZ head without a lock. Added OD9394 for AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP timer builds. Corrected the per-file rows above. `#MM kernel-timer` is an active MetaMake dependency, and the standard package lists `timer` in `PKG_DEVS_ARCH` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-118,217-232`), so the SMP package is within scope. Source-only.


AArch64 Raspberry Pi timer compare rearm caller pass (OD9395 added; 2026-10-23): traced the selected `BeginIO()` and `Timer1Tick()` callers into `Timer_Reprogram()`. Both program the same compare register; the routine reads the queue head, computes a delay, and writes the register after its optional list-lock interval. Since the arch-specific initializer leaves the lock-base field unset, concurrent rearming in RasPi SMP timer builds in the standard package and direct target builds can apply an older head snapshot after a newer short deadline. Added OD9395 for the distinct late-MICROHZ-completion consequence, qualified by SoC timer interrupt delivery; the active package dependency includes this timer device. No timer or hardware operation was run. Source-only.


AArch64 Raspberry Pi timer package-selection correction (2026-10-23): the earlier OD9393-OD9395 notes incorrectly treated `#MM kernel-timer` as disabled because it is written as a makefile comment. In MetaMake, `#MM` is an active dependency directive; `#MM-` is the disabled form. The AArch64 Raspberry Pi package target therefore depends on `kernel-timer` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-118`), and `%make_package` includes `timer.device` from `PKG_DEVS_ARCH := timer` (`:217-232`; `config/make.tmpl:3750-3768`). Corrected the three finding triggers and timer per-file rows: OD9393-OD9395 apply to the standard AArch64 Raspberry Pi `smp` package, not only direct builds. This also confirms the AArch64 Raspberry Pi VBlank producer used in GD5421 is on the selected package path. Source-only.

VirtIO BeginIO failed-submit double-unlink recheck (OD2604 retained; no separate OD, 2026-10-23): reread the complete `virtio_io.c` request dispatcher and traced both failure returns from `virtio_submit_blk_request()` (descriptor-chain exhaustion and `CachePreDMA` returning a shorter contiguous range) through `virtio_blk_rw()` into `BeginIO()` cleanup (`:76-84,266-270`; `virtio_queue.c:164-170,185-195`). The helper removes the request from `unit->au_IOs` before submit, and the outer `done` path removes it again after failure. Exec `Remove()` is only a neighbor-pointer splice and leaves the removed node's links untouched (`rom/exec/remove.c:51-62`), so the second call is harmless while those neighbors remain unchanged. The repository-wide `au_IOs` search finds no list reader; the only requests intentionally left linked are unsupported non-quick `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` requests, whose duplicate-insertion/removal corruption is already OD2604. A concurrent removal/free of a saved neighbor during the unlocked submission-failure interval is a possible extension of that existing list-lifetime condition, but I did not establish a distinct maintained caller consequence; no new finding is credited. Normal VirtIO unit publication remains blocked by OD2541. No request, descriptor exhaustion or DMA mapping was induced; source-only.

AHI HDAudio borrowed capture-buffer report/ledger reconciliation (OD3570 retained, 2026-10-23): re-read the AHI public `AHIA_RecordFunc` lifetime contract (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:401-418`), the single-slot `RecordFunc()` publication and signal (`Device/device.c:990-1003`), deferred `FillReadBuffer()` reads (`Device/devcommands.c:1020-1088`), and HDAudio's alternating two-buffer callback (`Drivers/HDAudio/interrupt.c:130-171`; `main.c:270-297`). The callback path still permits the worker to observe a later pointer/length or a reused DMA buffer if a subsequent callback occurs before it consumes the prior interval; signal-bit coalescing can also lose interval notifications. OD3570's conditional trigger and impact remain accurate. Corrected two stale HDAudio table references from nonexistent OD2147 to OD3570; no new finding or line credit. No recording or callback timing was run; source-only.

PC PIT rearm direct-caller reconciliation (OD1426/OD1427 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-23): repeated the repository-wide `Timer0Setup()` call search and read the full PC helper against its two maintained callers (`arch/all-pc/timer/beginio.c:29-35`; `timer_init.c:34-59`; helper `ticks.c:127-190`). The only direct callers are IRQ0's post-expiration rearm and `BeginIO()` after `common_BeginIO()` inserts a new head. `BeginIO()` wraps its helper call in local Disable/Enable, while the helper releases the request-list read lock before sampling/latching and programming PIT channel 0; neither operation serializes the other CPU's rearm. This preserves OD1427's stale-deadline overwrite and OD1426's related shared time-counter race; no third PC caller or independent candidate was found. The x86-64 SMP target and IRQ0 CPU routing remain as previously verified. No request or PIT operation was run; source-only.


AArch64 Raspberry Pi timer clock-update caller census (OD9393 retained; 2026-10-23): enumerated all selected callers of the AArch64 `EClockUpdate()` override: `GetSysTime()`, `GetUpTime()`, and `ReadEClock()` under local `Disable()`; `common_BeginIO()` under local `Disable()`; `Timer_Reprogram()`; and the timer interrupt path through `timer_ProcessTick()`. Deneb OD3705 per-microframe status and variant recheck (OD3705 qualified, 2026-10-23): reread the ordinary interrupt, ordinary ISO, and RTIso completion branches (`arch/m68k-amiga/usb/denebusb/uhwcmd.c:2833-2872,3053-3155,3408-3520,3590-3680`) and the selected status definitions (`isp1760.h:400-430`). AArch64 Raspberry Pi timer startup/expunge registration recheck (2026-10-23; no new OD): traced `Timer_Init()`'s `KrnAddIRQHandler`, shared `vblank_Init()`, conditional BCM2711/2712 `MicroHZVBlankInt` registration, and both registered expunge hooks against `timer.conf` and generated module lifecycle (`arch/aarch64-raspi/timer/timer_init.c:98-201`; `rom/timer/timervblank.c:30-56`; `rom/timer/timer.conf`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1506-1550`). Trackdisk retry-count loader and serialized worker consequence recheck (OD9396 retained, 2026-10-23): traced `IPrefs`' selected startup call into `ReadTDPrefs()`, the preset pair parser, the `ULONG`-to-`UBYTE` assignment, and the retry-count initialization (`workbench/c/iprefs/main.c:356-362`; `trackdiskprefs.c:18-67`; `rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:72`; `devices/trackdisk.h:110-120`). Legacy Trackdisk change-notification list synchronization and AFS caller pass (OD9397 added, 2026-10-23): traced all three listener-list sites: Add/Remove under `Forbid()` and timer-worker `ForeachNode()` walks before `Cause()` (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:395-400,456-460,522-525,768-773`). Confirmed `Forbid()` is local-CPU only on ExecSMP and `ForeachNode` reads the current node's `ln_Succ` after its body (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-201`). Followed the selected AFS caller: SendIO registration is deferred, while removal uses DoIO; DoIO enters Trackdisk's inline quick BeginIO path for TD_REMCHANGEINT, then AFS closes/deletes the request and frees the volume (`rom/exec/doio.c:56-73`; `rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:332-357,522-525`; `rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:377-399,463-471`; `rom/filesys/afs/volumes.c:267-274`). USB PTP `ACTION_INHIBIT` and format-worker serialization pass (no new OD; 2026-10-23): compared the no-op `ACTION_INHIBIT` dispatcher case (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:3213-3218`) with DOS `Inhibit()`'s documented “stop a filesystem from being used” contract and packet forwarding (`rom/dos/inhibit.c:17-38,55-60`). Traced the selected format sequence from `FormatPartition()` (`workbench/tools/InstallAROS/ia_diskio.c:674-685`) through `Inhibit(TRUE)`, the synchronous format packet, and `Inhibit(FALSE)`; `ACTION_FORMAT` runs `nPTPFormatStore()` (`ptp.class.c:3223-3228,2569-2635`). The single `nPTPTask()` receives and dispatches packets serially (`:4055-4065`), so another PTP DOS operation cannot execute concurrently inside the remote format handler; `nPTPCheckObjectInUse()` also checks existing locks before storage formatting (`:2584-2591`). This did not establish a separate format-corruption race from the no-op inhibit case. Keep the wider inhibit contract qualified/open: the no-op does not block concurrent DOS packets during an inhibit interval, and this pass did not establish a selected caller that depends on that behavior. No DOS packet, format, or device operation was run; source-only.

Legacy Trackdisk/AFS caller lifetime race recheck (OD9397 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-23): re-read the complete interrupt callback and AFS unmount teardown (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:688-697`; `rom/filesys/afs/volumes.c:267-275`). The callback dereferences the IOHandle to set flags and signal the filesystem task; unmount synchronously removes the change interrupt, closes/deletes its request port, then frees the containing Volume. `TD_REMCHANGEINT` is handled inline by the quick `DoIO()` path (`rom/exec/doio.c:56-73`; `rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:332-357,522-525`). This confirms the caller-side freeing consequence if the media worker has already selected the current listener: its `ForeachNode()` loop fetches that listener's successor after `Cause()`, while another ExecSMP CPU can run the signaled AFS task and remove/free the request (`lists.h:195-201`; `forbid.c:58-60`). The optional legacy x86-64 PC package edge remains as previously qualified. No new trigger or finding; no request, callback, media event, or SMP schedule was run; source-only.

Legacy Trackdisk worker-creation failure recheck (OD3343 expanded, 2026-10-23): read the full `TD_InitTask()`/`TD_DevTask()` handoff (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:567-702`) and traced the `NewAddTask()` failure returns (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:268-309`). In addition to the previously recorded task-data/stack/`MemList` allocation failures, `TD_InitTask()` ignores `NewAddTask()` returning NULL after `InitETask()` or `PrepareContext()` failure, then waits for `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_F`; the worker is the only sender and is never launched on those failures. Expanded OD3343 to distinguish the published-but-unusable device branch from this initialization hang. The same source review confirmed existing OD3342 and OD3731 cover timer-request allocation and boot-node ownership paths; no duplicate added. No task, allocation failure, boot operation, or interrupt was induced; source-only.

Legacy Trackdisk asynchronous change-request/AFS teardown recheck (OD9398 added, 2026-10-23): traced `SendIO()`'s nonquick flag and Trackdisk BeginIO queue path (`rom/exec/sendio.c:48-56`; `trackdisk_device.c:332-365`) against AFS's immediate return from `addChangeInt()` and later command rewrite/`DoIO(TD_REMCHANGEINT)` (`rom/filesys/afs/os_aros_support.c:377-415,390-399`). Confirmed the quick remove runs `Remove()` on the same IORequest node before the worker necessarily dequeues the asynchronous add; the message-port node may therefore still be on `td_Port`, whose `GetMsg()` path uses an ExecSMP spinlock while Trackdisk's direct Remove uses only Forbid (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:61-72`; `trackdisk_device.c:522-525`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). AFS then closes/deletes the request and port without waiting for a queued message (`os_aros_support.c:463-471`; `rom/exec/deleteiorequest.c:45-47`). Added OD9398 for the conditional cross-CPU unlink/dequeue and freed-request window. This is distinct from OD9397's listener-list traversal race. No request, volume, media event or task interleaving was run; source-only.


USB HID Wacom report-ID 12 synthetic-item dispatch pass (OD9399 added; 2026-10-23): traced the Intuos/Intuos3/Cintiq ID-12 branch through `nParseWacom()`'s shared synthetic collection, `nDetectWacom()` item construction, the default proximity mapping, `nProcessItem()` and `nFlushEvents()`. The pad branch sets only `wr_PadButtons`; each newly initialized `WacomReport` leaves `wr_InProximity` and `wr_Buttons` zero, but the common tail processes pen and pad items together. OOP attribute-base failure cleanup and selected HIDD caller pass (OD9400 added; 2026-10-23): read the complete `OOP_ObtainAttrBases()` failure branch and traced `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` allocation failures into it. After a failed entry, cleanup increments `d` once, then zeros the same later descriptor forever because the loop omits `d++`; the acquired-prefix release call is unreachable whenever another descriptor follows. Confirmed the ROM keyboard and input HIDD callers each pass three descriptors and both modules are selected by the RISC-V OpenSBI boot package. USB HID turbo-mouse saved-value range recheck (OD9401 added; OD3988 retained separately, 2026-10-23): compared the five GUI entries with the raw HIDC payload copy and both consumers of `cdc_TurboMouse`. Startup applies each nonzero config value as `1 << cdc_TurboMouse` when creating an interrupt-IN pipe; the live GUI update repeats the shift. On x86's 32-bit `int`, a persisted value of 32 or greater makes the shift count at least the operand width, which is undefined behavior; the resulting value is packed into the 16-bit `iouh_Interval` field. Added OD9401 for out-of-range persisted values, distinct from OD3988's valid-choice rate mismatch. The normal GUI range is 0..4; no runtime or controller effect is claimed. No config, device or pipe was used; source-only.


USB HID saved-string bounds and MUI caller pass (OD9402 added, 2026-10-23): traced HIDC chunk allocation/copy through `usbForceInterfaceBinding()` and `nOpenBindingCfgWindow()` to the selected GUI's `MUIA_String_Contents` fields. `cdc_HIDCtrlTitle` and `cdc_HIDCtrlRexx` are fixed 32-byte arrays copied from the binary chunk without termination checks; `psdGetCfgChunk()` allocates and copies the exact chunk. The selected MUI String constructor performs `strcmp()`/`strlen()` before clamping to `MUIA_String_MaxLen`, so a full-width non-NUL field reads beyond its array, and can pass the record boundary when its trailing numeric fields have no zero bytes. Added OD9402, distinct from Bluetooth HID OD3496. No config or GUI was used; source-only.


USB HID OD9402 field-coverage follow-up (2026-10-23): rechecked the selected GUI constructor after the initial report draft and confirmed all three fixed strings in `ClsDevCfg` are passed to MUI as string contents: `cdc_ShellCon` (128-byte field, maximum 127) plus `cdc_HIDCtrlTitle` and `cdc_HIDCtrlRexx` (32-byte fields, maximum 31) (`hid.gui.c:391-397,471-485`). Poseidon pipe and stream busy-count accounting pass (OD9413 expanded; 2026-10-23): traced `psdSendPipe()`'s one `pd_IOBusyCount` increment through `psdAbortPipe()`'s synthetic abort-message wait and `psdWaitPipe()`'s unconditional decrement (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4742-4862`; count field `poseidon_intern.h:411`). The synthetic abort message bypasses the send increment; selected clients then separately wait for the original request. Expanded the finding after reading `psdAllocPipe()` and stream cleanup: idle pipes start as `NT_FREEMSG` (`:4490-4507`), default streams allocate four pipes (`:4945-4954`), `psdCloseStream()` waits all allocated pipes regardless of node state (`:4982-4995`), and IN `psdStreamFlush()` first waits the same pipes (`:5480-5500`). Thus closing an unused OUT stream incurs four unmatched decrements and an unused IN stream eight; a pending abort also incurs the synthetic extra decrement. Selected printer and serial CP210x methods call these stream cleanup APIs (`printer.class.c:578-607,728-736`; `serialcp210x.class.c:627`). The `UWORD` count gates suspend decisions (`:3744-3757,3778-3790`). Added OD9413. The separate suspicion that Egalax explicitly waits twice on its original pipe was withdrawn: it waits once after `psdAbortPipe`, while the helper's wait targets a distinct synthetic request. No transfer, abort, stream close or suspend was run; source-only.

Poseidon stream-abort selected-package caller reconciliation (OD9413 refined; 2026-10-23): enumerated all direct `psdCloseStream()` and `psdStreamFlush()` callers in `rom/usb/classes`. MassStorage's UAS setup creates one-pipe streams, opens OUT before IN, and calls `nUasDisableStreams()` to close OUT if IN creation fails; normal worker teardown also closes both (`massstorage.class.c:1532-1543,1594-1639,1861-1878`). The failure cleanup therefore closes an idle, successfully opened OUT stream; its sole idle pipe starts `NT_FREEMSG` and still reaches `psdWaitPipe()` through `psdCloseStream()`, so the count decrements without a send. ARM and AArch64 Raspberry Pi package manifests include `USB/massstorage` (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:188`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:227`). For that explicit one-pipe UAS configuration, idle OUT close decrements once and idle IN close decrements twice (IN flush plus close); generic streams default to four pipes. Other stream callers include optional printer, CP210x, PL2303, CDC ACM, PalmPDA, and massstorage modules. No stream-open failure or teardown was induced; source-only.

USB Audio capture-buffer consumer recheck for OD3228 (2026-10-23; retained, no new finding): confirmed the sibling recording mode installs `nInReqHook`/`nInDoneHook` and sets its sample-conversion hook data to `nam_USBBuffer[0]` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2695-2735,3511-3545`). `nInReqHook()` assigns that same address on every request; `nInDoneHook()` calls the converter, whose `nRec*` routines read source samples from `hook->h_Data`. USB2OTG IRQ registration-failure consequence recheck (OD4099 retained, narrowed; 2026-10-23): followed `KrnAddIRQHandler()` through its only-in-success `ictl_enable_irq()` call and the selected ARM BCM2708 implementation (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-111`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/intr.c:32-36`; `platform_bcm2708.c:321-330,372-389`). If interrupt-node allocation fails, the legacy system IRQ line remains masked because registration returns before `ictl_enable_irq()`. Thus the controller can be initialized without its software event route as OD4099 states, but the failed registration alone does not make the BCM pending-source loop repeatedly dispatch an unhandled IRQ. No additional finding added and OD4099 does not claim a whole-system IRQ-loop lockup. No failure or interrupt was induced; source-only.

Bluetooth HID partial report-map diagnostic read recheck (OD3470 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-23): reread `bDebugMem()`/`bDebugReport()` and traced their callers from `bParseReport()` through `bReadReports()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1501-1580,1874-1937,2128-2142,2178-2188,2438-2448,2570-2592,2726-2747`). The report map is copied into a `btAllocVec(maplen)` allocation and stored with that exact logical length. On each final partial 16-byte diagnostic row, `bDebugMem()` shortens its format string and decrements `rptlen` to zero, but the call expression still evaluates all 16 `rptr[0..15]` arguments before `btAddErrorMsg()` can consume the one-to-fifteen conversions. Any parser error path invoking this logger with `maplen % 16 != 0` therefore reads beyond the report-map object; no parser rejection or log call is required for a well-formed complete map. OD3470 remains supported. This targeted helper/caller recheck adds no whole-translation-unit body credit; remaining BTHID methods, lifecycle and external Bluetooth caller contracts remain open. Bluetooth HID saved-action form-ID width and array caller pass (OD9416 added; 2026-10-23): traced array logical-range acceptance and `nhi_MapSize` allocation (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2269-2281`), sequential per-report `UWORD` list IDs (`:1683-1725`; `bthid.h:1073-1084`), GUI save iteration over every array-value list (`bthid.gui.c:2451-2462`), and the matching `bLoadItem()`/`bSaveItem()` form-key construction and load lookup (`bthid.class.c:5880-5925,5942-5972,1792-1867`). OHCI zero-length bulk transfer recheck (OD9422 added; 2026-10-23): traced public `USBDevice::BulkTransfer` forwarding through OHCI descriptor enqueue, pipe initialization and done-signal/timeout handling (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbdeviceclass.c:336-344`; `workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:639-645,1002-1086`). Zero length skips all active-TD field initialization, leaving the original dummy TD's zero flags (CC=NoError, DP=SETUP) in the active ED queue; the replacement tail is installed and the caller still waits for completion. In-tree MassStorage avoids this case (`storageclass.c:450-460`), but the public HIDD method accepts and forwards zero. OHCI public bulk zero-length caller census (OD9422 scope tightened; 2026-10-31; no new finding or LOC credit): exact repository-wide search for `HIDD_USBDevice_BulkTransfer(` found the public declaration, its dispatcher stub, and four maintained direct call sites, all in `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storageclass.c:450,455,457,460`. M68k Amiga keyboard Caps Lock event-field/caller pass (OD9423 added; 2026-10-23): traced CIA scan-code decode and event initialization into `keyboard.device`'s selected `keyCallback()` and `writeEvents()` consumer (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/keyboard/kbdclass.c:54-76`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:608-647,437-468`). Confirmed `pHidd_Kbd_Event.code` and `.flags` are separate 16-bit UWORDs (`rom/hidds/kbd/include/keyboard.h:28-37`), so OR'ing `KBD_KEYTOGGLE << 16` into `.code` truncates the value and leaves `.flags` clear; the consumer only checks `.flags` before Caps Lock qualifier handling. Amiga Gayle/PowerFlyer ATA PIO transfer-granularity and ATAPI caller pass (OD9426 added; 2026-10-23): compared the selected vector contract (`rom/devs/ata/include/hidd/ata.h:23-28`) with all four implementations in `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/gayle_ata/interface_pio.c:32-86`. The 16-bit loops process two words per iteration using `count >> 2`; 32-bit loops process two longwords using `count >> 3`. Traced both `ata_IRQPIOReadAtapi()` and `ata_IRQPIOWriteAtapi()` callers: they pass arbitrary even data-phase byte lengths, account the entire requested length, and only pad/round odd bytes (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:351-362,416-427`). For an 18-byte device phase each path transfers 16 bytes but accounts for 18; a 2-byte phase enters the post-tested assembly loop with a zero count, underflows, and performs 2^32 loop iterations before wrapping. Traced the Gayle interrupt entry to the shared ATA handler, so this short transfer stalls the interrupt callback while repeatedly moving beyond the requested buffer. The selected REQUEST SENSE call can request an 18-byte sense buffer (`lowlevel.c:1160-1171,2499-2534`). Added OD9426, scoped to the explicitly buildable optional Gayle/PowerFlyer HIDD, not the default Amiga ROM manifest; the 32-bit path is selected only when ATA 32-bit mode is enabled. This corrects the earlier even-length-only caller check. No driver build, device or transfer was used. Source-only.

OD9426 ATAPI command-packet caller extension (2026-10-23): followed `atapi_PacketSize()` into `atapi_SendPacket()` and confirmed the same Gayle vector mismatch affects the CDB itself. For a 12-byte packet device in `ATA=32bit` mode, `Unit_OutS(unit, cmd, plen)` passes 12 bytes to `ata_outsl()`, whose `count >> 3` loop executes once and outputs only eight bytes; the device's packet command is incomplete before its data phase. Added this distinct reachable trigger/consequence to OD9426. The ordinary 16-bit vector sends all twelve bytes; the CDB truncation is specific to the 32-bit option. No packet or device was used. Source-only.

ATA PIO backend comparison for OD9426 scope (2026-10-23): inspected the Efika MPC5200B backend's `ata_insw()`/`ata_outsw()` (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/ata/lowlevel_mpc5200b.c:67-103`) and its explicit `kernel-ata` archspecific file list (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/ata/mmakefile.src:7-9`). ATA PCI vector residual-length comparison for OD9426 (2026-10-23; no additional OD): checked both architecture branches in `rom/hidds/ata_pci/interface_pio.c:29-112`. Gameport queued-read trigger and sentinel-exhaustion recheck (OD2136 confirmed; 2026-10-23): followed `CMD_CLEAR`, per-open unit allocation, `GPD_READEVENT`, `fillrequest`, the callback gate and `ForeachNodeSafe` through the two-callback public sequence (`rom/devs/gameport/gameport.c:199-206,342-344,390-433,550-558,571-607,618-786`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:203-210`). `CMD_CLEAR` aligns each handle's cursor with the shared writer; the trigger predicate is under `#if 0`, so each available event sets `trigged` and completes a one-event read. After callback one replies to the first request and leaves the second pending; callback two consumes the older buffered event while the newer event remains, so `moreevents` stays true and loop exhaustion leaves `ioreq` at the tail sentinel. The empty-list cleanup then evaluates `gpUn->gpu_flags`, deriving `io_Unit` from that sentinel. The selected input.device still has one request stream; this concrete multi-open sequence is a public API trigger and requires no cross-core callback. OD1579 remains the separate one-event liveness case. No request or mouse callback was run. Source-only.

OD3492/OD3493 BTHID candidate disposition (2026-10-23): OD3492 remains withdrawn because unsigned 32-bit Logical Maximum and input values above LONG_MAX pass through implementation-defined conversions before signed range checks; no selected compiler/target result was established. OD3493 is also withdrawn pending target evidence: a signed Logical Minimum of LONG_MIN can collide with `HID_PARAM_UNDEF` and be replaced with zero on an implementation where the encoded 0x80000000 converts to LONG_MIN (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1968-1972,2143-2165,2500-2511`). Neither candidate is an active report finding or master-index entry. No descriptor or input report was processed.

Bluetooth HID OD3491 display-column caller recheck (2026-10-23): re-read the full `ItemListDisplayHook()` formatting and header path (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.gui.c:1908-1994`) plus all three input/output/feature list constructors (`:610-626,1112-1128,1142-1158`). Each list uses the same five-column `BAR,BAR,BAR,BAR,` format and the same display hook; no configured column-width limit explains or mitigates the text truncation before MUI receives it. `btSafeRawDoFmtA()`'s writer consumes up to `len` characters and then writes NUL at `buf[len-1]`, leaving at most nine visible decimal characters for each length-10 field (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:897-916`). RocketTool joystick-status caller pass (OD9429 added, 2026-10-23): enumerated every checked-in `ReadJoyPort()` call. The debug joysticks only print changed status; the LowLevel display test reports status and the misc joystick example compares/prints it; none transmits control state. `RocketTool` is the selected caller that sends a device command from the polled state: after any recognized controller type sets `nch_Buf[1..5]`, an unknown/unavailable result leaves those fields unchanged and the loop still performs `SendInit()`/`SendCommand()`. Traced m68k `ReadJoyPort()` to `llPortOpen()` potgo allocation failure (`JP_TYPE_UNKNOWN`) and invalid-port return (`JP_TYPE_NOTAVAIL`); generic LowLevel is an unconditional unavailable stub, so only the m68k implementation establishes the valid-then-failed sequence. At minimum, one failed poll retransmits the prior state. The same failure path's later `llPortClose()` releases the requested potgo mask (OD9424), so repeated failures require another reservation between polls. No device, joystick or resource contention was used. Source-only.

DRadioTool full-body and transfer-result pass (OD9432-OD9433 added, 2026-10-23): read all 290 physical lines / 237 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `rom/usb/shellapps/DRadioTool.c`, plus its local state/protocol header. UPSTool full-body and runt-reply parser pass (OD9434 added, 2026-10-23): read all 316 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `rom/usb/shellapps/UPSTool.c` and its 64-byte reply-buffer declaration. The selected setup explicitly enables `PPA_AllowRuntPackets`; Poseidon documents that such short packets can complete without `UHIOERR_RUNTPACKET` and directs callers to `psdGetPipeActual()`. `GetReply()` terminates at actual length, but status parsing checks for one remaining byte and then accesses offset five, so a short final field can be classified using zeroed, unreceived bytes. Added OD9434. No device or transfer was used.

USB shell-app release-hook cross-file reconciliation (OD9430 expanded, 2026-10-23): compared all six selected shell-app setup paths. `DRadioTool`, `PencamTool`, `PowManTool`, `RocketTool`, `SonixcamTool`, and `UPSTool` publish an app binding containing a release hook before their `Alloc*` function assigns `nch_Task`; all six hooks unconditionally call `Signal(nch->nch_Task, SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C)`. `psdAllocVec()` is backed by Poseidon's `MEMF_CLEAR` pool, and the selected removal path invokes binding release hooks. Expanded OD9430 from RocketTool to the common six-app race; file rows mark the inspected slices and do not imply complete body review for PencamTool or PowManTool. PencamTool full-body transfer, image-boundary, optional-processing and output review (OD9435-OD9441 added, 2026-10-23): read all 798 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `rom/usb/shellapps/PencamTool.c` and the local image/header structures. These findings require malformed device metadata, a short transfer, invalid command-line gamma/font dimensions, or DOS output failure as individually stated. The local source body is fully read; camera behavior, exact accepted image-format limits, disk-font rendering and filesystem failure behavior remain unverified. No camera, image, font or file operation was run; source-only.

AArch64 Broadcom PCI DMA cache-transition recheck (2026-10-24; no new OD): traced the selected BCM2711, BCM2712 and RP1 `AllocPCIMem()`/`FreePCIMem()` paths through `KrnMapGlobal()` and the AArch64 `CacheClearE` syscall implementation. Each allocator aligns the returned address and mapped extent to pages, cleans and invalidates the region with `CACRF_ClearD` before changing it from cacheable memory, and records the rounded extent for the reverse remap. The selected AArch64 syscall implements `CACRF_ClearD` with `dc civac` over the rounded cache-line span, so the apparent clean-only transition does not leave valid stale lines. Free restores the cacheable mapping only after the uncached ownership interval. This closes the source-level cache-transition concern for these allocators; noncoherent controller behavior, MMU/TLB execution, and allocation-failure cases remain untested. Source-only.

Bluetooth scan-stop command failure and event-order follow-up (OD3897 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `bBgScanStop()`, `bDiscoveryTimerCB()` and `bStopDiscovery()` through the HCI command queue and `bHandleEvent()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:564-582,713-725,1440-1470,1748-1758`; `bSubmitCmd()` at `:126-136`). The LE stop paths clear their active-state flags before submitting scan-disable, while discovery timer/stop also clear `hc_InqActive` before sending `INQUIRY_CANCEL`; all ignore queue-admission failure and completion. The timer callback advances `bStartDiscoveryPhase()` immediately after queuing cancel commands, before controller confirmation; a later Inquiry Complete event can advance it again, but `bFinishDiscovery()` guards duplicate finish publication with `BTHF_DISCOVERING`. A failed disable/cancel can therefore leave the controller scanning or in inquiry after the task reports it idle, and a successful but delayed cancel can allow discovery completion/name resolution to proceed before radio stop is confirmed. Expanded OD3897 to include this event-order consequence with the inverse state-publication path. No scan, timer, queue saturation or controller error was induced. Same root cause, not a separate OD; `hwtask.c` remains partial and gains no whole-file body credit.

OD4445 PTP size-field reachability qualification (2026-10-24): reread the size decoder at `rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:1858-1861` against the 32-bit `ULONG` field and the `nPTPWrite()` growth arithmetic. The decoder's `bufptr[3] << 24` promotes the byte to signed `int` before shifting; for values with the high bit set this exceeds signed-int range, so the language does not guarantee the intended 32-bit object size. Kept OD4445 because the unsigned growth loop definitely cycles if `poi_Size` has the stated value, but qualified end-to-end reachability as dependent on selected compiler behavior and a PTP device reporting that size. No build or device response was used; no compiler-specific result is claimed.


OD4444 large-file decoder reachability qualification (2026-10-24): rechecked the `poi_Size` assembly at `rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:1860` against OD4444's >2-GiB trigger. The top-byte `bufptr[3] << 24` is evaluated after integer promotion to signed `int`; when the high byte is at least 0x80, the shifted value exceeds signed-int range and C does not guarantee the intended ULONG bit pattern. The 32-bit range-check overflow is definite once the parsed size/cursor have those values, but selected compiler behavior and a device response are unverified; this caveat applies to OD4444 as well as OD4445. No build or device response was used.


OD4445 caller-state closure (2026-10-24): traced DOS `ACTION_FINDUPDATE` through the PTP packet dispatcher and `nCreateFH()` (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:3053-3078,3311-3333`). The PTP memory pool is created with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`:4191`), and Exec's pooled allocator clears each returned block when that flag is set (`rom/exec/memory.c:672`), so a newly created file handle has a NULL buffer and zero buffer length despite `nCreateFH()` only explicitly assigning the object pointer. `ACTION_SEEK` accepts `OFFSET_END` with zero relative offset (`ptp.class.c:3612-3637`), then `ACTION_WRITE` dispatches a writable object's request to `nPTPWrite()` when the device supports send-object (`:3646-3659`). This establishes the described caller state conditional on a reported near-4-GiB object; the `ACTION_FINDUPDATE` mode mismatch is the separate OD4431 finding. No device, file or packet was used. Android HIDD initialization rollback and input-driver ownership recheck (2026-10-24; ownership details refined 2026-10-31; no new finding): followed `agfx_init()` partial failures through `ADD2EXPUNGELIB(agfx_expunge)` and the common module init runner (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:55-69`). After UnixIO interrupt registration, failure of the protocol Hello causes expunge to remove the interrupt, close the two descriptors, and release attribute bases. Attribute-base acquisition failures unwind their partial acquisitions in `AllocAttrBases()`; UnixIO construction failure reaches expunge and frees the bases. The interrupt-registration error branch itself closes both descriptors and nulls the UnixIO field before returning, avoiding a second close. `agfx_Startup()` removes the keyboard hardware driver if mouse-driver registration fails, then disposes both temporary subsystem objects. Rechecked that `HIDD_*_AddHardwareDriver()` calls `HW_AddDriver()`, which creates, sets up and publishes a distinct driver object in the shared hub; the temporary `CLID_Hidd_Kbd`/`CLID_Hidd_Mouse` objects are not those driver instances (`rom/hidds/input/inputclass.c:307-314`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:164-209`). Their disposal only unlinks callback listeners when callbacks were installed, and these startup objects install none (`inputclass.c:240-252`). On mouse-registration failure, `HIDD_Kbd_RemHardwareDriver()` reaches `HW_RemoveDriver()`, which unlinks and disposes the published keyboard driver (`inputclass.c:358-364`; `hwclass.c:267-305`). After successful registration, `lib_OpenCnt = 1` retains the module and its installed drivers. The unchecked `AddDisplayDriverA()` result was compared against other selected driver startup paths that likewise ignore or only log the result; this pass did not establish a distinct supported consequence beyond generic registration failure, so no candidate is promoted. This narrows the earlier note that startup/failed-init cleanup remained open; native bitmap mapping and broader platform contracts remain open. Source-only.

Linux input `EVIOCGBIT` destination-width follow-up (OD9528 added; 2026-10-24): checked the local Linux UAPI encoding (`EVIOCGBIT(0, EV_MAX)`, with `EV_MAX == 0x1f`), the AROS `LONG` typedef (32-bit), and the UnixIO wrapper's direct host `ioctl()` call. Linux evdev's native `bits_to_user()` computes its output as `BITS_TO_LONGS(EV_MAX) * sizeof(long)` and caps it at the ioctl's encoded length. For a native 64-bit Linux process, the computed copy length is eight bytes, while `linuxinput_init.c` passes a four-byte `LONG param`; successful capability queries therefore overwrite four adjacent stack bytes. Added OD9528, conditional on a 64-bit Linux build with the module and a successful query. Confirmed against upstream Linux `drivers/input/evdev.c`; no host ioctl/device or runtime was used. This refines the previously open ABI question; the local 744-line manifest body credit is unchanged.

USB HID public-header wrapper caller census (2026-10-24; no new OD): searched all checked-in C/header sources for each `HIDD_USBHID_*` wrapper and `moHidd_USBHID_*` method ID declared by `workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/include/hid.h`. All calls are local to `hidclass.c`, `kbdclass.c`, and `mouseclass.c`; the shared base constructor obtains the descriptor and report buffer before parsing, while keyboard/mouse constructors use the same descriptor-length transfer path. This closes the in-tree wrapper-caller census only; external HIDD clients, descriptor conformance and controller transfer semantics remain open. No device or report was exercised; source-only.

xHCI command-timeout cleanup caller expansion (OD4127 expanded; 2026-10-24): re-read `xhciCmdSubmit()` timeout/return handling and traced both resource-owning callers. The existing Address Device path ignores Disable Slot status before freeing `dc_IN` and device DMA state (`xhci_hcd.c:1493-1513,4394-4456`). Separately, `UHA_DestroyEndpoint` registers `xhciDestroyEndpoint`; selected Poseidon `psdFreePipe()` calls `pTearDownHWEndpoint()` and therefore reaches it (`uhwcmd.c:599-601`; `poseidon.library.c:1653-1665,4669-4670`). `xhciFreeEndpointContext()` ignores Reset/Stop status, logs but does not propagate Configure Endpoint drop failure, then unconditionally releases the endpoint ring (`xhci_hcd.c:4299-4382`). Expanded OD4127 to cover both paths, conditional on the command sequence failing to establish quiescence; the controller's continued use after such failure is not runtime-demonstrated. No command timeout, pipe teardown, controller or DMA was exercised; source-only.

xHCI disconnect-time slot-disable ownership pass (OD4127 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `xhciDisconnectDevice()` from selected root-port reset/disable and physical detach callers, plus the hub-child detach caller. It aborts queued software requests, then calls `xhciFreeDeviceCtx(..., TRUE, ...)`; that routine ignores `xhciCmdSlotDisable()`'s completion and proceeds to clear the DCBAA pointer and free all endpoint rings and slot/input contexts (`xhci_hcd.c:404-436,4394-4456`; `xhci_hcport.c:284-292,394-405,778-787`; `xhcidevice.c:279-291`). Added this separate selected teardown trigger to OD4127: if Disable Slot does not establish quiescence, hardware references may outlive the freed DMA. Existing port-disconnect cleanup does not provide a second disable-success check. No physical detach, command failure, or DMA was exercised; source-only.

AHI combined Play/Record Start failure caller revalidation (OD9534 added; 2026-10-24): re-read the AHI tag accumulator and result path (`Device/audioctrl.c:959-975,1001-1021`), both selected driver Start implementations, their `AHIDB_Record` capability reports, and FreeAudio/Stop cleanup. A true Play+Record request reaches one Start call; a returned error is passed to the caller without Stop/rollback. NVHDMI reports no Record capability, nevertheless starts its output stream and sets `is_playing` before rejecting any Record flag (`NVHDMI/main.c:176-247,371-375`). HDAudio reports Record only when `adc_nid` exists; with no ADC, it allocates/stores playback resources and marks playback state before returning at the ADC check, before the output stream's later start call (`HDAudio/main.c:207-268,314-320,461-465`). Record stream allocation/setup failures similarly return before the shared start calls. Neither driver's Start path stops or releases an earlier playback stream before replacing the saved pointers on retry; later Stop/FreeAudio can only clean the currently saved stream. No selected in-tree combined Play+Record caller was found; legacy Toccata emulation is excluded from active Drivers `SUBDIRS`. Restored the historical OD1392/OD1393 behavior under OD9532, with reachability limited to public callers; OD1394/OD1395 remain unrecovered because their old IDs have no report/index entry or source description in the surviving ledger. No AHI call, stream, or failure was exercised; source-only.

AHI CMD_READ resampler buffer-boundary pass (OD9536 added; 2026-10-24): traced the selected `CMD_READ` API documentation into `ReadCmd()`, `FillReadBuffer()` and all six `devsupp.c` recording converters, then followed HDAudio's selected callback and the checked-in RecordTest consumer (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:672-692,718-769,1020-1100`; `devsupp.c:43-179`; `Drivers/HDAudio/DriverData.h:37`; `Drivers/HDAudio/interrupt.c:148-171`; `Examples/Device/RecordTest/RecordTest.c:17,53-77`). Each callback's available output count is floored independently; each converter restarts its fixed-point accumulator at zero, and partial reads reset `io_Offset` before the next callback. For 1,024 source frames at 44.1 kHz and requested 8 kHz, the exact fixed step is 361,266/65,536, so each callback yields 185 output samples rather than the 185.76 ratio and resets after consuming 1,019 whole source frames. Added OD9536 for cumulative output-rate shortfall and phase restart across non-integral buffer conversions. This pass covers this selected conversion/caller chain only; other drivers' callback timing and external CMD_READ clients remain open. No recording, driver callback or output stream was run; source-only.

AHI `CMD_READ` signed-width conversion pass (OD9538 added; 2026-10-24): traced the public read contract through `ReadCmd()` and `FillReadBuffer()` to the `AHIST_M32S`/`AHIST_S32S` dispatch and both `devsupp.c` helpers. Confirmed `WORD` is signed 16-bit, the helpers shift the promoted signed sample by 16, and the captured stream may contain negative values; the HDAudio path passes signed 16-bit stereo frames to `FeedReaders()` when `HAVE_ASMIO` selects it (`Drivers/Makefile.in:41-55`). AHI recording conversion helper sibling pass (OD9538 broadened, OD9539 added; 2026-10-24): read the complete 181-line `devsupp.c` body (124 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), compared all six converter offset updates, and traced `ReadCmd()`/`FillReadBuffer()` against the public CMD_READ double-buffering contract and the checked-in `RecordTest` request reuse. Found all six helpers multiply consumed source frames by `sizeof(struct sample *)` instead of source-frame size; on 64-bit builds the four-byte signed-stereo source frame advances by eight bytes, so a preserved offset can exceed `RecordSize`, wrap the unsigned remaining-byte calculation, and begin conversion outside the record buffer. The same pass traced signed widening in `RecM32S()`/`RecS32S()` and the default Filesave recording producer; broadened OD9538 to include its independent negative `BYTE << 8` and negative `WORD << 16` sites. `Filesave` is unconditional in the driver target list and advertises recording; HDAudio remains conditional on `HAVE_ASMIO` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Makefile.in:46-49`). No build or recording was run; source-only.

AHI DSP echo feedback-wrap candidate correction (OD139 withdrawn as an unsupported candidate, 2026-10-24): checked the documented Fixed feedback range, coefficient derivation in `effectinit.c`, `MEMF_CLEAR` delay-buffer initialization and both C/m68k recurrence bodies. The apparent signed boundary requires a delayed sample of 32767 with the exact unit feedback coefficient, so `(sample + 1) * 0x10000` reaches 2^31. At exact unit feedback, however, the normal-input coefficient is zero and the freshly allocated cleared delay buffer receives no signal; for lower representable feedback, coefficient truncation keeps the selected weighted sum below that boundary. Thus the checked-in caller path does not establish a nonzero state that reaches the suspected overflow. The historical candidate has no active detailed-report heading or `AROS.md` entry and is not retained as a finding. This is a source-level arithmetic/reachability correction; no audio or target build was run.

VMware SVGA IRQ partial-vector failure scope recheck (no new OD; 2026-10-24): reread all 370 physical lines / 246 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `vmwgfx_irq.c` and traced `vmw_irq_install()`'s loop against the AROS compatibility `pci_alloc_irq_vectors()` implementation (`drm-compat/linux_pci.c:365-372`). Envy24 AHI PCI-adapter partial-initialization cleanup recheck (no new OD; 2026-10-24): traced each false return from `ahi_pci_init()` in `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Envy24/pci_aros.c:39-62` through the AROS common `_LibInit()`/`_LibExpunge()` failure route and `DriverCleanup()` (`Common/library.c:456-500`; `driver-init.c:64-77,155-179`). This check covers the Envy24 PCI adapter's AROS failure unwind only; Envy24HT shares the implementation pattern but its own caller/driver cleanup is separately tracked. No library-open failure, PCI initialization or expunge was induced; source-only.


AHI common partial-open rollback recheck (OD1653 remains withdrawn; 2026-10-24): traced the AROS `RTF_AUTOINIT` resident path through `InitResident()` into `MakeLibrary()` (`rom/exec/initresident.c:75-95`; `rom/exec/makelibrary.c:108-110`), which allocates the entire `DRIVERBASE_SIZEOF` base with `MEMF_CLEAR` before `_LibInit()` runs. `_LibInit()` attempts both standard opens, then sends a failed-open result through `_LibExpunge()` and driver cleanup (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Common/library.c:426-468,483-514`). The failed `IntuitionBase` or `UtilityBase` pointer is used only to form the address of its first `struct Library` field; both fields are at offset zero (`compiler/include/intuition/intuitionbase.h:26-29`; `compiler/include/utility/utility.h:24-29`). Thus the null case passes NULL to Exec `CloseLibrary()`, whose selected implementation explicitly takes the no-op branch (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:64-90`). The driver-specific cleanup callbacks were already checked for their partial state; this common null-close path does not add a fault or double close. OS4-only interface-open branches are not selected by the AROS build. No library open was failed; source-only.

### AROSTCP `API_C` current body-line coverage (2026-10-24)

The selected `API_C` manifest contains 31 C translation units and 10,660 `cloc 2.06` C code lines. All 31 bodies / 10,660 lines have full-body credit (100% by file and line count). This is only the selected AROSTCP `API_C` body measure, not an overall Other Drivers or goal-completeness estimate; caller matrices, imported BSD core, configurations, and runtime/device behavior remain open. The earlier “res_send.c remains” snapshot is superseded by the OD9516 full-body pass.

PCNet32 packet-buffer Open unwind follow-up (OD9541 added; 2026-10-24): traced both selected RX/TX `AllocPCIMem()` results in `pcnet32_open()` through the common return, the device Open hook's `unit->start()` call, Close's `IFF_UP` guard, and DeleteUnit's `fe_priv` cleanup. On either allocation failure the hardware setup branch is skipped but the helper returns zero; the Open vector discards that result. If the peer allocation succeeded, its pointer is neither released on this path nor by later Close (which does not call stop for the down unit) or DeleteUnit. Added OD9541 for false successful Open and conditional packet-buffer leak. No allocation failure or lifecycle was induced; source-only.

E1000 failed-Open cleanup path correction (OD3020 strengthened; 2026-10-24): rechecked the complete `GM_UNIQUENAME(Open)` body against Exec `OpenDevice()` and `CloseDevice()`. Corrected the prior OD3020 wording: the driver's explicit `CloseDevice()` at `e1000_init.c:347-348` is only in the pre-start error branch, before any opener is added or ring setup begins. If RX setup fails after TX setup succeeds (`:382-387`), Open returns `IOERR_OPENFAIL` at `:411-413`; Exec then clears `io_Device` without invoking Close (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:109-120`). The previously linked opener and incremented `e1ku_open_count` therefore also remain, and a later `CloseDevice()` cannot reach the driver hook because the device field is NULL (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:71-85`). OD3020 now states the TX resource leak and this related failed-open state retention precisely; the retained count intersects OD3015's existing exclusive-open consequence. No Open, allocation failure, or CloseDevice call was run; source-only.

E1000 failed-Open IRQ branch reachability check (OD3020/OD3023 retained; no new OD, 2026-10-24): checked the apparent `request_irq()` failure edge after configuration (`e1000_init.c:392-402`) against its full selected implementation. `request_irq()` unconditionally calls the void `AddIntServer()` twice and returns zero (`e1000.c:626-636`); the only `free_irq()` implementation is compiled out under `#if 0` (`:638-644`). Therefore this call cannot produce the late error branch as currently written, and it does not add another reachable failed-Open trigger to OD3020. The registration/lifetime issue remains OD3023; no IRQ registration or hardware operation was run.

eaudio failed first-open rollback and ETASK partial-construction recheck (OD4069 expanded; no new ID, 2026-10-24): traced each `init_ETask()` resource acquisition and failure edge (`workbench/devs/audio/audio_commands.c:779-923`) through its nested cleanup, `init_EUnit()`'s single nullable `CreateIORequest()` (`:976-1014`), and `free_EUnit()`/`free_ETask()` (`:745-768,927-974`). Every successfully created port/request, opened AHI device, graphics library and earlier unit record has a matching cleanup on partial construction; no new partial-init leak established. Separately reconciled the first-open allocation failure through generated `set_call_devfuncs()` and Open-count handling: the hook's TRUE return increments `lib_OpenCnt` despite nonzero `io_Error`, but its in-hook `DevClose()` runs before that increment and sees zero, so it skips `FreeSLAVE()`. `_ADCMD_FREE()` signals completion and releases only matching units; it does not stop the worker. The later count increment is phantom; subsequent successful client close sees count 2 and skips shutdown, then leaves count 1, preserving the worker, ETASK units, AHI state, graphics reference and message ports. This corrects the rejected OD9542 hypothesis that a retry starts a second worker; expanded OD4069 instead, which already covers the failed-open count leak and retained worker. No allocation failure, open, or close was induced; source-only.


BTCore buffer cursor implementation pass (2026-10-24; no new finding): reconciled `core/buffer/buffer.c` and `include/btcore/buffer.h` with the optional production `BTCORE_FILES` list (`rom/bluetooth/stack/core.files`; `linklibs-btcore` edge is commented in `rom/bluetooth/stack/mmakefile.src:12-15`). Read all 265 source and 67 header lines; `cloc 2.06` counts 235 C and 44 header code lines (279 total). Reviewed reader/writer initialization, remaining-space arithmetic, all endian scalar operations, byte copies, peek/skip, cursor updates and underflow/overflow returns. Each operation validates the requested length before accessing bytes, and successful cursor advances stay within the initialized extent; no independent defect was established for initialized, caller-valid cursor/buffer arguments. The cursor structs are public and the API does not validate NULL pointers or externally corrupted `pos` fields, but no selected production caller was established that violates those preconditions, so these were not promoted as findings. This pass closes only these two implementation/interface bodies; BTCore call-site contracts, ownership and the rest of the optional library remain open. No test, buffer operation or runtime call was executed; source-only.

AR5211 included `boss.ini` table shape and reset-index pass (2026-10-24; no new OD): confirmed `ar5211_reset.c` includes this file and the default HAL option set selects AR5211 when the optional Atheros5000 target is built. Read all 352 `cloc 2.06` code lines and counted every initializer: `ar5211Modes` 35x5, `ar5211Common` 171x2, `ar5211Mode2_4` 28x3, `ar5211BB_RfGain` 64x3, and `ar5211Rf6n7` 25x3; every row matches its declared width. Traced reset's mode indices (1..4) and frequency indices (1..2) into the corresponding arrays; the EEPROM mutation indices 25/26 fit the 28-row mode table, and every `ar5211Rf6n7` mutation index (5, 6, 11..13, 17, 21) fits its 25-row table. The dynamic updates and separate-unit interleaving remain OD3825. No new local dimension/index defect was established. This does not validate silicon-specific register values or close the other included tables, external HAL clients, or hardware behavior. No build, EEPROM, reset, or hardware operation was performed; source-only.

AR5212 included `ar5212.ini` initializer and selected-index pass (2026-10-24; no new OD): rechecked the eight selected include sites (AR5212 attach, AR5111, AR5112, AR2413, AR2316, AR2317, AR2425 and AR5413). AR5416-family included INI table initializer and local-width pass (2026-10-24; no new OD): confirmed the six `.ini` data files are directly included by the default HAL-selected attach backends (`ar5416_attach.c`, `ar9160_attach.c`, `ar9280_attach.c`, and `ar9285_attach.c`); the aggregate Atheros5000 target remains optional in the network aggregate. Bluetooth HID `bReadReports()` full-body and ID-width/caller follow-up (OD9463 expanded; no new OD; 2026-10-24): read the complete function in source order (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1501-1788`; 288 physical lines) and reconciled its two callers in initial bind and configuration reload (`:1019-1023,1195-1199`). Reviewed Classic/HOGP descriptor acquisition, exact report-buffer allocation and parse-failure cleanup, report-size aggregation, report-map allocation/population, sequential per-item/action-map IDs, quick lookup-map allocation/fill, and action-config application. Expanded OD9463: the parser accepts a 65,536-entry logical map, and the `UWORD` counter wraps while assigning IDs; a later output/feature item can receive an ID already assigned to the earlier map, and `bFindItemID()` returns the earlier map first, causing the later item's action to be handled as an array. Traced this through the selected default mouse-wheel-to-Blue-LED action (`:3448-3490,5395-5426`) to establish a concrete wrong-output consequence. Rechecked startup cleanup on failed report parsing/map allocation and configuration reload: the HID worker frees the partial tree after failed initial parse; on reload it stops GUI consumers, frees/rebuilds the report tree itself, and exits through `bFreeHid()` if reconstruction fails. No separate cleanup or reload lifetime defect established. This closes the `bReadReports()` function-body slice only; BTHID's 5,973 `cloc 2.06` C code lines, wider lifecycle and external device/config contracts remain partial. No descriptor, allocation failure or device was used; source-only.

Bluetooth HOGP Report-characteristic capacity and partial channel-allocation pass (OD3961 expanded; 2026-10-24): compared the complete BTCore `build_report_list()` limit and success path with BTHID's `bOpenReportChannels()` enumeration and setup caller (`rom/bluetooth/stack/profiles/hogp/hogp_client.c:78-124,276-304`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1056-1138,1018-1034`). Confirmed both paths can silently omit input reports beyond their fixed eight-entry/channel capacity and still report successful initialization; BTHID's separate 16-entry endpoint table does not remove its eight-input-channel limit. Additionally, when one of multiple BTHID `btAllocChannel()` calls fails, the loop continues and final setup succeeds if any other channel was allocated, leaving that endpoint unserviced without an error. Confirmed BTHID returns FALSE when no channel exists despite input items, limiting both cases to partial success.
