BTCore's caller census remains limited to tests; BTHID is an explicit optional module whose parent aggregate edge is commented out. No HOGP service, endpoint, allocation failure, notification, or device was used; source-only.


speechcore renderer harmonic wave-index bound review (2026-10-24; no new OD): derived each `wave_window` sample index maximum 63 from the 10-bit `d1` mask and the two 10-bit `d2` phase fields separated by 16 bits. Reconciled parameter validation (sample frequency 5,000–28,000; rate 40–400) with `period_count = floor(frequency*75/rate/120)`, maximum 437. Since window advancement occurs only once per 9 or 11 unvoiced harmonic pairs and `Pulse` resets the window per pitch period, a conservative bound is `floor(437/9)*64+63 = 3,135 < 4,096` bytes. Noise-table access remains bounded by its 0/479 reversal and fixed 8x480 validated table. This clears the identified renderer table-index question for `SCSynthWith`-validated parameters and voice dimensions; direct internal `SCRenderFrames` callers and acoustic correctness remain outside that proof. No audio was rendered; source-only.


OHCI descriptor-pool task/interrupt caller pass (OD9545 added; 2026-10-24): traced the `ohciAllocED`/`ohciFreeED`/`ohciAllocIsoTD`/`ohciFreeIsoTD` inline head mutations through `cmdAddIsoHandler()` → `ohciInitIsochIO()` and through `ohciCompleteInt()` → `ohciHandleFinishedTDs()` → `ohciFreeEDContext()`. The public BeginIO dispatch does not wrap the task setup in a critical section; only the handler-list pop and final publication are disabled, while allocator pops and partial-failure pushes remain outside. The ISR returns descriptors to the same heads. Added OD9545 for the resulting conditional task/interrupt free-list race, with ExecSMP making local `Disable()` insufficient for cross-CPU serialization if used alone. `ohciFreeEDContext()`'s local critical section does not protect the task-side operations. This closes the allocation-failure and completion caller slice for the OHCI descriptor-pool helpers; all remaining OHCI HCD callers, external USB client timing, and hardware/controller behavior remain open. No USB request, descriptor exhaustion, or race was run; source-only.

OHCI descriptor-pool affected-build qualification for OD9545 (2026-10-24): confirmed `arch/all-pc/usb/pciusb/make.opts` defines `PCIUSB_WIP_ISO`, selecting the `UHCMD_ADDISOHANDLER` BeginIO path in the all-PC PCIUSB build. Kept the trigger conditional on that public request being invoked in task context while OHCI completion runs; ordinary control/bulk/interrupt transfer descriptors are allocated by their interrupt-side schedulers, so they do not establish another task-side allocator race. The common descriptor pools still receive interrupt-side returns. Updated OD9545's affected configuration to the checked build edge; no separate defect or runtime claim. Source-only.

OHCI RTIso shared-pool successful-pop interleaving recheck (OD9545 strengthened; 2026-10-24): confirmed the task-side `cmdAddIsoHandler()` and interrupt-side `ohciScheduleIsoTDs()` both call `ohciInitIsochIO()` and both pop the same ED and ISO-TD free-list heads without serialization (`uhwcmd.c:1483-1492`; `ohci_isoch.c:61-78,135-167`; scheduler called from `ohciCompleteInt()` at `ohci_hcd.c:1310-1339`). If the task reads a pool head and is interrupted before updating it, the ISR can read and return the same descriptor from its own initialization; both RTIso nodes can then retain that descriptor. This success path needs no allocator failure and is reachable when a task adds a real-time handler while a standard ISO request is queued. Also verified interrupt-side descriptor returns from normal ED completion and standard ISO completion (`ohci_hcd.c:147-182,740-747`; `ohci_isoch.c:570-605`), which can interleave with task cleanup pushes. Expanded OD9545's demonstrated interleaving and trigger; no USB operation or interrupt was run. Source-only.


EHCI isochronous descriptor-pool task/interrupt caller pass (OD9546 added; 2026-10-24): traced the siTD/iTD pool head helpers through task-context `cmdAddIsoHandler()` → `ehciInitIsochIO()` and its partial-failure `ehciFreeIsochIO()` cleanup, then through interrupt-context `ehciCompleteInt()` → `ehciHandleIsochTDs()` descriptor returns and the following scheduler. The RTIso-node list's short Disable/Enable regions do not cover the descriptor-pool operations; the EHCI initializer and free function do not provide their own lock. Added OD9546, distinct from OD974's single-threaded control status-TD double return and OD4341's hardware-quiescence lifecycle issue. The standard ISO scheduler also executes from completion interrupt context. This closes the selected task/interrupt caller slice for EHCI ITD/siTD pools; other EHCI QH/qTD callers, external clients and hardware timing remain open. No controller or allocation failure was exercised; source-only.

EHCI RTIso successful-pop interleaving recheck (OD9546 strengthened; 2026-10-24): verified task-side `cmdAddIsoHandler()` dispatches to `ehciInitIsochIO()` and that `ehciCompleteInt()` calls `ehciScheduleIsoTDs()` for queued standard ISO requests; both paths then invoke `ehciInitIsochIO()` and pop the same iTD or siTD pool head (`pciusb_dev.c:256-259`; `uhwcmd.c:1483-1492`; `ehci_hcd.c:1097-1144`; `ehci_isoch.c:290-323,329-379`). Neither caller serializes those pops. If the task is interrupted after reading a head and before publishing its successor, the ISR can return the same descriptor to both RTIso nodes. Confirmed all-PC PCIUSB selects this path through `arch/all-pc/usb/pciusb/make.opts`. Expanded OD9546 to this direct successful-allocation consequence and exact trigger; no controller or request was run. Source-only.


EHCI QH/qTD pool task-abort and interrupt-scheduler follow-up (no new OD; 2026-10-24): enumerated every direct QH/qTD pool helper use. Initialization reserves pool entries before interrupt registration; control/interrupt/bulk schedule builders and their allocation-failure cleanup are reached only from `ehciCompleteInt()`; finished periodic requests call `ehciFreePeriodicContext()`, which masks local interrupts; task-side `cmdAbortIO()` likewise enters with `Disable()`, routes asynchronous requests through deferred async-advance reclamation, and returns periodic QH/qTDs before re-enabling. This gives a serialized task/interrupt path on a single CPU for QH/qTD pool operations, unlike the unmasked task-side ITD/siTD RTIso initializer in OD9546. ExecSMP's `Disable()` is processor-local, so a concurrent IRQ on another CPU remains an unresolved configuration/affinity question; no independent finding is promoted without establishing the selected PCI interrupt routing contract. This closes the listed local QH/qTD call paths, not cross-CPU interrupt routing or HCD hardware quiescence. No abort or controller was run; source-only.


EHCI AbortIO/completion cross-CPU synchronization pass (OD9547 added; 2026-10-24): traced public `devAbortIO()` through `cmdAbortIO()` and both EHCI active-request branches into `ehciFreeAsyncContext()` / `ehciFreePeriodicContext()`, then compared those unlink/free/reply operations with `ehciHandleFinishedTDs()`'s active-queue walk and completion frees/replies. Reconciled the PCI HIDD's `KrnAddIRQHandler()` registration with PC IOAPIC routing: the redirection entry uses fixed physical destination mode and selects one mapped/current CPU (`acpi_ioapic.c:546-592`); Exec `Disable()` is processor-local on ExecSMP. Added OD9547 for the conditional cross-CPU abort/completion overlap. It is distinct from OD4341 (controller may still fetch descriptors after abort), OD4411 (xHCI scheduler traversal versus abort), and OD9546 (OHCI/EHCI RTIso descriptor-pool mutations). This closes the selected EHCI abort/completion source path; platform IRQ target changes, exact device timing, external AbortIO client contracts and runtime behavior remain unverified. No request, controller or SMP schedule was run; source-only.


PCIUSB multi-controller failed-init rollback pass (OD9548 added; 2026-10-24): traced PCIUSB's bus/device grouping, controller initialization loop, failure branch and `Open_Unit()` failure return (`pciusb_arospci.c:219-225,350-401`; `uhwcmd.c:249-276`). PCI xHCI OD3363 source citation and bounds recheck (2026-10-24): re-read PCI discovery and grouping (`pcixhci_arospci.c:70-76,219-253`), the complete `pciAllocUnit()` controller initialization and global map fill (`:288-355`), per-controller port cap (`xhci_controllerclass.c:137-142,319`), fixed `hu_PortMapX[MAX_ROOT_PORTS]` storage (`pcixhci.h:54,145`), and root-hub consumers (`uhwcmd.c:838-894`). PCIUSB root-port aggregation bound recheck (no new finding; 2026-10-24): reviewed the entire selected `pciAllocUnit()` mapping block (`rom/usb/pciusb/pciusb_arospci.c:423-653`) against PCIUSB's fixed 16-entry tables (`pciusb.h:54,136-149`) and root-hub consumers. PCI xHCI failed-unit unwind cross-controller follow-up (OD3369 expanded; 2026-10-24): re-read the grouped-controller initialization loop and failure path (`pcixhci_arospci.c:319-345`) against successful `xhciInit()` publication of reset/IRQ handlers and worker tasks (`xhci_hcd.c:4028-4032,4067-4077,4139-4161`). The same early return that omits teardown of the failing controller also bypasses `pciFreeUnit()` for any earlier controller whose `xhciInit()` returned TRUE in that `PCIUnit`; those prior handlers/tasks/private resources remain active after PCI ownership release. No multi-controller unit, failed start or worker schedule was exercised; source-only.


PCIUSB controller-publication caller recheck for OD3784 (expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `pciInit()` root/class lookup, per-controller publication guard, controller-node name allocation, discarded `HW_AddDriver()` result and success return (`rom/usb/pciusb/pciusb_arospci.c:212-217,254-312`) through `Open_Unit()` into internal `pciAllocUnit()` startup (`uhwcmd.c:226-276`). Expanded OD3784 to include this same observable registration gap in PCIUSB. No allocation failure, HIDD enumeration or USB unit open was induced; source-only.


PCI HIDD ownership-release semantics checked for OD3369/OD9548 (2026-10-24): read `PCIDev__Hidd_PCIDevice__Obtain()` and `PCIDev__Hidd_PCIDevice__Release()` (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:488-510,549-555`). Obtain records the owner name under `ownerLock`; Release only assigns NULL to `ss_Link.ln_Name` and does not alter PCI IO/MEM/busmaster attributes or interrupt registration. Therefore the controller ownership release in the failed-unit branches does not itself stop a previously initialized HCD or prevent another driver from obtaining that PCI function. Strengthened the retained-handler consequence in OD3369 and OD9548. PCI re-enumeration/competing-driver timing remains untested; no device was accessed. Source-only.

PC PCI no-IRQ sentinel and HDAudio caller pass (OD9549 added; 2026-10-24): traced raw `INTLine` from PCI config through the default PC driver AddInterrupt wrapper and kernel registration (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:1196-1198`; `pcidriverclass.c:279-288`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-110`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/ictl.c:19-43`). The PCI enumerator already identifies 255 as unassigned (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:190-202`), but `HW_IRQ_COUNT` admits it on i386/x86-64. Traced the selected optional HDAudio/NVHDMI subclasses treating a non-NULL token as success, HDA Setup enabling interrupts, and `HDA_IntCode` queuing stream callbacks (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/hda_hidd.c:178-184`; `NVHDMI/hda_hidd.c:178-184`; `workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:431-497`; `:166-214`). Added OD9549 with absent-line and no-alternate-route conditions; no board route, interrupt or audio stream was tested. Source-only.


PCIPC MSI-X vector-minimum contract and PCI caller census (OD2987 confirmed; no new finding, 2026-10-24): re-read `PCIPCDev__Hidd_PCIDevice__ObtainVectors()` and the public `Min`/`Max` contract (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_deviceclass.c:388-429,495-513`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:252-278`). MSI-X clamps `vectmax` to the table size and then lowers `vectmin` when that minimum is no longer attainable; it can therefore return TRUE after allocating below the documented minimum. The legacy-MSI path instead returns FALSE when `vectmin` exceeds hardware capacity (`:504-508`). Confirmed the existing OD2987 covers this separate MSI-X contract violation; made no duplicate report entry. Repository caller census (`HIDD_PCIDevice_ObtainVectors`) found AHCI, xHCI, vmwgfx and Nouveau request exactly one vector; the NVMe call requests `Min=1, Max=KrnGetCPUCount()` but currently reads only vector index 0 and configures one I/O queue (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:273-279,336-347,364-412`). Thus no checked-in caller demonstrates the lowered-minimum trigger; OD2987 remains conditional on a direct external/future client requiring more vectors than the device MSI-X table supports. Also rechecked OD2983: the selected client census does not request multiple legacy-MSI vectors and query an index above zero. No PCI device or vector allocation was run; source-only.


AHI `devcommands.c` CMD_STOP/START/FLUSH interaction and reply-lifetime recheck (OD2449/OD2450 retained; 2026-10-24): re-read `PerformIO()`, `StopCmd()`, `StartCmd()`, `FlushCmd()`, `_DevAbortIO()`, `RethinkPlayers()`, and `TermIO()` against the unit worker and Exec `ReplyMsg()` path. Confirmed that START drains `RequestQueue` only on the final nested stop release; AbortIO and FlushCmd still omit that queue (OD2450). Separately confirmed the OD2449 stale request race: FlushCmd snapshots active-list heads without the unit semaphore, while completion removes/replies under that semaphore; ReplyMsg can signal the requester after the Exec reply-port spinlock is released, and `_DevAbortIO()` reads the saved request's `io_Unit` before taking the AHI semaphore. A requester on another ExecSMP CPU can therefore reclaim the request before that read. No new candidate beyond OD2449/OD2450; no I/O, flush, schedule, or build was run. Source-only.


AHI recording fixed-point source-rate arithmetic recheck (OD2149 reconciled into report and index; 2026-10-24): traced `ReadCmd()`'s frequency-to-16.16 step through `FillReadBuffer()` and all six `Rec*` helpers, then checked the 32-bit `ULONG` definition and the Envy24HT 192 kHz recording capability. At 192 kHz source and 48 kHz requested, the 32-bit left shift wraps and produces a step of 83,186 instead of 262,144; the helpers therefore return data at roughly 151 kHz for a 48 kHz request. The coverage ledger already tracked this as OD2149; its detailed report and index entry are now restored and expanded. `AHI-Handler` sets the requested rate on its `CMD_READ` request; other caller validation and backend-specific recording behavior remain open. No recording or device was run; source-only.

AHI `CMD_READ` in-tree caller census (OD2149 trigger confirmation; 2026-10-24): searched the AHI subtree for actual request command assignments; only `AHI-Handler/main.c` and the `RecordTest` example submit `CMD_READ` (`:442,511` and `Examples/Device/RecordTest/RecordTest.c:52-60`). The handler sets `ahir_Frequency` from configured/AIFF sample-rate state; RecordTest requests a fixed 8 kHz and reuses the request with the documented continuation offset. Both provide a nonzero requested-rate path for OD2149 when the selected backend mix is above 131071 Hz; at 192 kHz, the example's 8 kHz rate also uses a wrapped step. No other maintained AHI caller was found by this source search; external direct device callers remain outside the census. No recording or build was run; source-only.

HDAudio/NVHDMI rate-selection candidate reconciliation (OD9550; 2026-10-24): traced both full _AHIsub_AllocAudio() selection loops against their converter-format programming and AHI’s CreateAudioCtrl/UpdateAudioCtrl contract. Requests below the minimum are clamped in ahiac_MixFreq; unsupported in-range requests choose the nearer table entry but leave ahiac_MixFreq unchanged; requests above the maximum leave selected_freq_index at its initialized zero. Both drivers program from selected_freq_index, while ahi.device retains the requested rate for buffer timing and software sample-rate steps. This confirms and expands the earlier ledger-only OD331 note. Added detailed candidate OD9550 to ../AROS-other-drivers.md and its link to ../AROS.md; no codec or audio playback was run. Source-only.

HDAudio/NVHDMI local manifest-to-source reconciliation (2026-10-24): verified the parent AHI aggregate selects both directories only when HAVE_ASMIO is configured (Drivers/Makefile.in:42-50); checked each local Makefile.in's six C objects, mode file and Common/Makefile.common.in mode-generation rule. Reconciled 12 C bodies, eight local headers and two mode descriptors (22 authored source files) against the coverage rows. The C bodies have full-body credit; directly reread every local header and both complete mode descriptors. cloc 2.06 counts HDAudio 2,401 code lines (2,230 C + 152 headers + 19 assembly) and NVHDMI 1,489 (1,363 C + 107 headers + 19 assembly), totaling 3,890/3,890 local source code lines fully read. This is only these two driver's local authored source bodies, not their full operational dependency or platform audit: shared HDAudio HIDD implementation, AHI core, generated gatestubs/common rules, PCI/HIDD callers, hardware/codec response behavior and runtime scheduling remain separate and open. Existing targeted findings OD2234, OD2898, OD3013, OD3574-OD3575, OD4153, OD4154 and OD9550 remain; no new candidate arose from this reconciliation. No build, hardware, codec, allocation fault or audio playback was run; source-only.

Shared HDA HIDD SetupStream reconfiguration follow-up (OD9551 added; 2026-10-24): traced HDA__Hidd_HDA__SetupStream() on an already-configured stream through HDA_FreeStreamBuffers(), BDL/sample-buffer replacement, allocation failures and the later HDA_StreamReset(). The method checks only hs_InUse and the maximum buffer count; it does not reject hs_Running or clear RUN before freeing the old DMA targets. New allocation failure exits before HDA_StreamReset, so the previous hardware descriptor programming remains active after its buffers/BDL were freed. Checked hda.conf and the public hda.h interface for a documented stopped-only precondition and found none. Repository caller census found only the HDAudio/NVHDMI wrappers, both used on newly allocated streams; no maintained reconfiguration caller was found. Added OD9551 as a public HIDD-client candidate, explicitly conditional on a repeated SetupStream call against a running stream. Existing OD2125 remains the separate zero-buffer-count setup defect. No stream or allocation failure was run; source-only.

AHI RecalcBuff/HDAudio initial-playback high-rate trace (OD9552 added; 2026-10-24): computed the exact public-tag case MixFreq=16,777,216 and PlayerFreq/MinPlayerFreq/MaxPlayerFreq=257. The current MixFreq/PlayerFreq ratio is 65,280, within the documented UWORD bound; RecalcBuff's 32-bit MixFreq<<8 wraps to zero, so both sample counts become zero and the allocated AHI mix buffer is only its 80-byte padding. UpdateAudioCtrl derives 65,280 maximum frames from MixFreq/MinPlayerFreq. For an AHIC_Play-only ControlAudio request, the tag switch leaves update false, so AHIsub_Update is skipped and HDAudio Start initializes current_frames to the maximum. The first playback callback copies 65,280 stereo frames from the 80-byte source mix buffer (16-bit path: one LONG per frame; 24-bit HiFi path: two). This confirms OD9552 as a separate buffer-overread consequence from OD9550's hardware-versus-retained-rate mismatch; no checked-in request for the unusual mix rate was found. Added report/index entries; no audio or device was run. Source-only.

Coverage-only HDA oversized-DMA label audit (OD2138 not restored as an active finding; 2026-10-24): searched the current report/index and available review files; OD2138 survives only as a label in the historical hdaclass.c coverage paragraph, with no detailed finding text. Rechecked HDA's dma_buffer_size = ahiac_MaxBuffSamples * frameSize (workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/main.c:218-225). In 24-bit stereo, ULONG multiplication wraps only once MaxBuffSamples exceeds 536,870,911; the downstream selected AHI tags can produce such a value by setting a very low MinPlayerFreq, but the API describes that tag as the minimum rate the client will use and separately requires MixFreq/PlayerFreq to fit UWORD. The precise original trigger and whether it honored those constraints cannot be recovered from the ledger wording. OD2138 is therefore left unverified and is not counted as an active detailed candidate; no separate DMA-size-overflow finding is asserted. OD9552 documents the independently reproduced RecalcBuff wrap and HDA source-buffer overread with a current player-rate ratio within the documented bound. Hardware behavior remains untested; source-only.

AHI RecalcBuff high-rate cross-backend caller census (OD9552 broadened; 2026-10-24): searched the selected AHI driver aggregate and traced each backend that sizes a mix buffer from ahiac_BuffSize but copies/converts a frame count derived from ahiac_MaxBuffSamples. Confirmed HDAudio/NVHDMI, Envy24/Envy24HT, VIA-AC97, CMI8738 and SB128 retain the max-frame copy extent through Start and read from the short mix buffer in their playback callback. Confirmed ARM/AArch64 RPiI2S uses a fixed max-sized CopyMem, RPiPWM falls back to MaxBuffSamples when the wrapped current count is zero, and RPiHDMI writes MaxBuffSamples*2 words into the mix buffer in its initial silence fill before output starts. Parent selection is HAVE_ASMIO for the native drivers (Drivers/Makefile.in:42-57) and HAVE_DMA_H plus ARM/AArch64 for the Raspberry Pi drivers (:88-94). Expanded OD9552 from the HDA example to cover these selected backend paths. The earlier coverage-only OD2138 text remains separately marked unverified because its detailed trigger is not recoverable and the inferred HDA DMA-size overflow has unresolved AHI tag-contract bounds; OD9552 itself uses a current MixFreq/PlayerFreq ratio within the documented UWORD limit. No audio, device or allocation was run; source-only.

AHI RecalcBuff high-rate trigger and Raspberry Pi PWM reachability correction (OD9552 refined; 2026-10-24): checked the cross-backend startup trace against RPiPWM's full PWM range-selection loop. The earlier MixFreq=16,777,216 example makes `samplerate * R` wrap to zero at R=1024, so the loop divides by zero before reaching the buffer conversion; that exact trigger does not support the RPiPWM inclusion. Refined OD9552 to MixFreq=16,777,217 with PlayerFreq/MinPlayerFreq/MaxPlayerFreq=257: the 32-bit `MixFreq << 8` wraps to 256, which divided by the 65,792 fixed-point denominator still yields zero BuffSamples, while MaxBuffSamples is 65,281 and the ratio remains within the UWORD bound. For this odd rate the tested R range has no zero `clk` divisor; source control flow continues to PWM conversion. The same zero-buffer result retains the HDAudio/NVHDMI/Envy24/Envy24HT/VIA-AC97/CMI8738/SB128/RPiI2S/RPiHDMI paths. Updated OD9552 trigger arithmetic and explicitly excluded the old even-rate example for RPiPWM. The separate finding remains conditional on this unusual accepted mix-rate request and successful backend start; no audio or device was run. Source-only.

Android HIDD native bitmap copy and update-rectangle caller trace (2026-10-24; no new OD): followed `ABitmap__Hidd_BitMap__UpdateRect()`'s `cmd_Update` request (`arch/all-android/hidd/androidgfx/androidgfx_bitmapclass.c:179-199`) through Java `DoCommand()`/`BitmapView.Update()` into `GetBitmap()` (`arch/all-android/bootstrap/app/src/org/aros/bootstrap/AROSBootstrap.java:257-263`; `AROSActivity.java:362-372`; `main.c:105-141`). Native copying uses the supplied rectangle to form source and destination row addresses and does not validate the bitmap bounds. `HIDD_BitMap_UpdateRect` is documented as a display refresh after drawing (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf`); the selected `workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:1139-1153` caller builds its update rectangle from a `DoHookClipRects()` callback, which intersects it with layer/ClipRect bounds before returning to `UnLockBitMapTagList()` (`rom/hyperlayers/dohookcliprects.c:111-170`; `workbench/libs/cgfx/unlockbitmaptaglist.c:111-123`); the display-show path separately supplies the full bitmap extents. These checked in-tree routes do not demonstrate an out-of-bounds rectangle reaching Android `GetBitmap()`. Android overrides that superclass method and sends its message directly, but this pass did not establish a selected maintained caller that supplies out-of-bounds coordinates to this subclass. Therefore no source-backed memory-bound finding is promoted from the missing JNI clamp alone. The Java fallback uses a whole-buffer copy; native `GetBitmap()` is selected only when `HaveNativeGraphics()` succeeds. Remaining gap: public/external HIDD callers and Android bitmap/runtime contract, plus explicit bounds behavior for direct `UpdateBitMap()` callers. No bitmap, JNI call, or out-of-range rectangle was exercised; source-only.
Bluetooth HID malformed-report diagnostic bounds pass (OD9553 added; 2026-10-24): read `bDebugMem()` and `bDebugReport()` fully and traced every active parser call to the latter in `bParseReport()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1875-1936,2134-2140,2179-2185,2438-2445,2571-2590,2727-2743`). Cross-checked descriptor ownership in `bReadReports()`: HOGP uses `btGetChannelActual()`, Classic uses the SDP descriptor length, and the parser's `nhr_ReportBuf` allocation/copy are exactly `maplen` bytes (`:1527-1532,1551-1554,1567-1580`). On parser-error logging, `bDebugMem()` reduces the remaining length for a partial final row but unconditionally evaluates 16 byte arguments; malformed map lengths not divisible by 16 therefore read up to 15 bytes beyond the buffer. Added OD9553. This closes only the two debug helpers and their parser caller trace; BTHID source and broader lifecycle remain partial. No device or malformed map was used; source-only.

BTHID `bParseReport()` source-order full-function and finding reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new OD): read the complete function body at `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1940-2788`, including short/long item decoding, report-ID transitions and collection cloning, Main-item field construction and bit-position updates, Global Push/Pop, Local usage/designator/string ranges, and all temporary-list cleanup/error exits. BTHID array signedness initialization hypothesis rechecked (2026-10-24; no new OD): the array Main-item branch does not explicitly assign `nhi_IsSigned`, while the variable branch derives it from logical bounds (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2238,2260-2282`), and `bProcessItem()` uses that flag for aligned 8-bit and generic-width array extraction (`:4270-4320`). Traced `btAllocVec()` to `AllocPooled()` and its library pool creation (`bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:95,269-300`), then Exec's `AllocPooled()` forwarding stored pool requirements (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:87-94`) and zero-fill path for `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/exec/memory.c:665-674`). Since this pool is created with `MEMF_CLEAR`, newly allocated array items begin with `nhi_IsSigned == FALSE`; the missing explicit assignment does not establish an uninitialized signedness defect. No descriptor was parsed or device used; source-only.

Filesave playback/record startup publication recheck (OD1999 retained; no duplicate; 2026-10-24): traced both `AHISub_Start()` child creation paths through AHI's `AHIC_Play`/`AHIC_Record` control caller (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Filesave/filesave-main.c:281-296,323-339`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:959-977,1007-1014`). Both assign `tc_UserData` only after `CreateNewProc()` returns while holding `Forbid()`. The selected ExecSMP `Forbid()` contract is CPU-local (`rom/exec/forbid.c:56-60`); `CreateNewProc()` publishes via `AddTask()` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:543-551`), and `AddTask()` can make the child runnable before returning (`rom/exec/addtask.c:32-35,84-88`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:33-43`). BCM GENET OD2930 task-resource rollback recheck from the Exec direct-caller census (2026-10-24; retained, no new OD): reread the service-task allocation and every failure edge in `workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/bcmgenet_unit.c:375-444`, then compared them with `BCMGENET_DeleteUnit()` (`:447-493`). The initial task/stack/MemList allocation failure explicitly frees each successful local allocation; the later request-port loop's NULL branch jumps directly to common cleanup without publishing those locals into `unit` or freeing them. Common cleanup only frees resources reachable through `unit`, confirming the existing OD2930 trigger/consequence. The successful AddTask path transfers the task/stack through `tc_MemEntry`; the AddTask failure branch explicitly frees all three. No allocation failure or device initialization was induced. This closes this task-setup rollback cross-check only; BCM GENET's broader hardware and caller contracts remain as stated in the file row.

DWMAC service-task startup/rollback cross-check from the Exec direct-caller census (2026-10-24; no new OD): reread `DWMAC_UnitTask()` and `DWMAC_CreateUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/dwmac/dwmac_unit.c:794-902,1090-1180`) against `DWMAC_DeleteUnit()` (`:1182-1222`). Prelaunch Task/stack/MemList allocation failure frees each successful local allocation; AddTask failure clears `dwu_Task`, frees all three, then deletes the unit. After successful AddTask, the creator's single-signal wait is paired with both worker outcomes: startup signals only after publishing a valid input port, while startup failure falls through cleanup, clears `dwu_Task`, and signals before returning. If startup failed, the creator sees `dwu_InputPort == NULL` and deletion does not wait for a task already exiting. Normal shutdown signals the worker and waits for its final signal before releasing unit state. No independent startup ownership or handshake defect established in these paths; this closes only the DWMAC service-task lifecycle slice. Existing OD2922/OD2923 and the file-row hardware/caller limits remain. No allocation failure, task schedule, or device was exercised; source-only.


Network-driver `AddUnitTask()` stack-failure cross-driver recheck (OD3260 expanded; 2026-10-24): compared the AROS `NewAddTask` macro and task-stack cleanup in Intel Pro/100, Broadcom4400, NvidiaNet, Realtek8180, Atheros5000, Prism2, VIA Rhine, and EtherLink III. Confirmed the existing 4-KiB stack leak in Realtek8180 and Atheros5000 and established the same omission in Prism2: `CreateUnit` stores the allocated stack in `task->tc_SPLower`, then a failed `NewAddTask` leaves `UNITF_TASKADDED` clear; `DeleteUnit` consequently frees the Task but puts the stack free inside the flag branch. Expanded OD3260 and the master index to include Prism2. The checked Intel Pro/100, Broadcom4400, NvidiaNet, Rhine and EtherLink III cleanup paths release a successfully allocated stack independently of the task-added flag, so this specific failure is not attributed to them. Prism2 has a direct build target, though its network-aggregate edge is commented out. The new Prism2 source evidence is `unit.c:319-341,394-403` and its AROS macro `:160-166`; the trigger remains task-extension allocation failure after stack allocation. No build or allocation failure was run; source-only.


Etherlink III AROS vector data-field adapter/caller reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new OD): re-read the selected `aros_device.c` BeginIO and RX/TX/DMA wrapper paths (`workbench/devs/networks/etherlink3/aros_device.c:298-310,352-419`) against every `ios2_Data` and `ios2_StatData` use in the selected `request.c` and `unit.c`. BeginIO saves the original `ios2_Data` in `ios2_StatData` and replaces it only for CMD_READ, CMD_WRITE, S2_MULTICAST, S2_BROADCAST and S2_READORPHAN; the selected unit paths consume `ios2_Data` for those commands only when invoking the wrapped buffer callbacks, which restore the saved cookie before calling the original hook. Commands whose handlers consume `ios2_StatData` (including device query/statistics operations) are not rewritten by this adapter. The AROS vector table maps Open/Close/Expunge/Reserved/BeginIO/AbortIO to slots 1–6 followed by the -1 terminator (`aros_device.c:67-83`), matching its six wrapper declarations. No independent data-field or vector mismatch established in this slice. `DevClose()` assumes a successful opener and removes/frees its opener state; failed-open callers are handled by the wrapper's error path. This closes only this adapter/caller slice; the driver’s full lifecycle, other external SANA-II clients, generated build output and controller/DMA/PC Card contracts remain open. No request or build was run; source-only.

OD3115 Exec OpenDevice-side exclusion cross-check (2026-10-24; existing finding strengthened, no new OD): inspected the full selected `rom/exec/opendevice.c` call sequence. `OpenDevice()` acquires the DeviceList read/Forbid wrapper, releases the list lock, invokes the device Open vector, and only then calls `Permit()` (`:93-123`). Exec's `Forbid()` contract explicitly limits task-switch exclusion to the local processor on EXECSMP and requires a spinlock for parallel data (`rom/exec/forbid.c:33-64`). Therefore OpenDevice's wrapper does not exclude an Open vector running on another CPU from Etherlink/Prism2/Realtek unit-list and opener-state changes; this confirms OD3115's cross-CPU premise. This is source-contract confirmation only; no SMP build or interleaving was run.


OD3115 Realtek8180 platform-selection qualification (2026-10-24; existing finding strengthened): followed the generic network dependency (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-15`) into `workbench-devs-networks-realtek8180-pc`, which selects the Realtek manifest and builds `realtek8180.device` (`workbench/devs/networks/realtek8180/mmakefile.src:4-12`). The PC configure branch sets `AROS_TARGET_ARCH=pc`; x86_64 with target variant `smp` defines `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` (`configure.in:1614-1616,1647-1671`). Therefore a Workbench build including the generic networks target on x86_64-pc-smp can select Realtek8180 and has the ExecSMP condition for OD3115. Its runtime race still requires the USB stack and matching hardware; this does not prove inclusion in a narrower board package target. No build, USB device or concurrent open/close was run; source-only.


Bluetooth shutdown-worker / module-unload lifetime pass (OD9556, 2026-10-24): traced both `bPopupTask()` and `bEventHandlerTask()` shutdown tails into their waiters and `libExpunge()`. Each worker clears its task pointer and signals the waiter before `AROS_USERFUNC_EXIT`; both waiters use the pointer clear as completion. Exec documents that `Forbid()` is processor-local on EXECSMP, while generated library expunge frees the base and returns the module segment after the expunge callback succeeds. This supports a conditional cross-CPU unload race for final close during worker shutdown. No SMP schedule, module close, or unload was run; source-only. Follow-up worker census: the separate hardware task opens `bluetooth.library` at startup and closes it before clearing `bth_Task` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2800-2804,3092-3098`), pinning the module while active; it is not included in OD9556’s unpinned popup/event-worker trigger.


Bluetooth object-removal event lifetime pass (OD9557, 2026-10-24): traced `btRemHardware()` and `btRemClass()` through `btSendEvent()` and `BENA_Param1`. Both paths free the object before passing its address as Param1; `btSendEvent()` copies that pointer into asynchronously queued notes, and the public event definitions describe the corresponding parameter as the hardware/class object. The selected preferences listener refreshes lists without dereferencing this parameter, so the stale-pointer defect is established but a checked-in crash consequence is not. Added OD9557 with that contract limitation explicit. Also checked `BEHMB_REMDEVICE`: `bFreeDevice()` unlinks and tears down the device but deliberately leaves its allocation in place for possible outstanding lock callers; it is not the same immediate-free defect. No event consumer or removal was run; source-only.


Bluetooth `bDeviceClassScan()` full control-flow pass (OD9558 added, 2026-10-24): reread the full function through all forced service/device binding and automatic device-binding branches. Confirmed `hassvcbinding` is a local `BOOL` with no initializer; its only writes set TRUE when a service binding exists or succeeds, yet it is read in the forced-device and fallback-device gates. Added OD9558. Rechecked `svcs[16]` independently against OD4349: the bounded snapshot/no-continuation finding is already tracked and is not duplicated. Rechecked `btRemClass()`'s loop: it releases tracked non-app device and service bindings and then checks `bc_UseCnt`; no separate count defect established in this pass. No class scan, binding, or build was run; source-only.


Bluetooth device-removal event / tombstone follow-up (OD9557 scope check, 2026-10-24): traced both the discovery ClearOld path (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:1333-1349`) and hardware teardown (`objects.c:128-158`) through `btFreeDevice()` and `bFreeDevice()`. `bFreeDevice()` frees nested service/name state, removes the device from its list, and deletes its lock, but intentionally leaves the `BtDevice` allocation in the Bluetooth pool (`objects.c:377-405`); therefore the immediate-free claim does not apply to `BEHMB_REMDEVICE`. The pool is later reclaimed at library expunge. OD9557 remains limited to the `BtHardware` and `BtClass` objects passed after `btFreeVec()`. No removal event was delivered; source-only.


Bluetooth hardware failed-startup ownership pass (OD9559 added, 2026-10-24): traced `btAddHardware()` through `bHWTask()`, `bQueryHCIDevice()`, the `BTCMD_ADDMSGPORT` failure branch, `bFreeCore()`, the final ready signal, and caller cleanup. Bluetooth `btAddHardware()` duplicate-check concurrency recheck (OD3721 strengthened, no separate finding, 2026-10-24): followed the unlocked `bFindHardware()` check through worker publication and the selected H4/virtual HCI `Open` vectors. The lookup ends its local `Forbid()` before `btAddHardware()` allocates/spawns; publication happens only after HCI bring-up, so overlapping adds can both pass the check even on a single CPU while the first waits. The selected H4 and virtual HCI devices each serialize and reject a second open of the same unit (`h4bthci_device.c:47-52`; `vbthci_device.c:44-50`), limiting this overlap to a redundant failed add rather than duplicate published radios in those backends. OD3721 remains the tracked issue for its stronger ExecSMP list-traversal/removal race; no separate report entry added. No add or device open was run; source-only.


OD4406 BTHID duplicate-binding consequence caller recheck (2026-10-24): followed each successful `bForceServiceBinding()` through `btSpawnSubTask(bHidTask, nhb)`, binding publication, and the worker's startup (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:257-279,904-946`). OD9556 worker-entry ownership and exit-tail pass (2026-10-24): traced `btSpawnSubTask()` from both expunge-managed workers. When DOS is available it calls `CreateNewProcTags(NP_Entry, initpc, NP_UserData, userdata, ...)` and returns the Process without opening `bluetooth.library`; otherwise it allocates a task/stack and calls `AddTask(nt, initpc, NULL)`, again without a module self-reference (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/bluetooth.library.c:978-1044`). Both worker entry functions end with `Forbid()`, clear the task pointer, signal the waiter, then return through the function epilogue (`popup.c:262-267`; `classes.c:954-959`); `AROS_USERFUNC_EXIT` is only a closing-brace macro in the generic fallback definition (`compiler/arossupport/include/asmcall.h:829-830`). No intervening handshake waits for task termination. LDDemon patches CloseLibrary/RemLibrary and calls UnLoadSeg on returned segment lists (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:569-596,626-650,893-899`). This confirms the existing OD9556 premise that signaling precedes completion of module-resident return instructions, conditional on the cross-CPU ExecSMP interleaving. No task schedule or expunge was run; source-only.


OD9560 BTHID dispatcher-to-expunge caller pass (2026-10-24): confirmed the dynamic close chain from class management. `btAddClass()` obtains and retains the class module with `OpenLibrary()` and stores its base in `bc_ClassBase` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:35-75`); `btRemClass()` releases each binding, closes that retained base at `:113-158`, and BTHID's release callback removes `nhb` from `nh_Interfaces` only after waiting for `nhb_Task` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:294-337`). The class `libExpunge()` checks only that list, while `libClose()` stops and waits for `nh_DispatcherTask` by pointer (`:93-153`). Genmodule decrements open count before the close hook and calls ExpungeLib after it when `LIBF_DELEXP` is set (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1463-1517`); LDDemon unloads the returned segment list (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:569-596,893-899`); its ExpungeLib path defers by setting that flag while still open (`:1586-1591`). `bInstallLastActionHero()` can leave the class-wide dispatcher running after its binding is released; there is no binding-list condition or join before it signals final exit. The BTHID class has an explicit build target, while its edge from the class aggregate is commented (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/mmakefile.src:5-12`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/mmakefile.src:10-13`); `btAddClass()` is the selected dynamic loader. This supports OD9560 for a class module with a pending expunge and cross-CPU final-close handoff. No load, class removal or task schedule was run; source-only.


OD9561 BTSerial service-worker/module-expunge caller pass (2026-10-24): traced binding admission, shutdown, class removal and generated deferred expunge. `btAttemptServiceBinding()` publishes a `BTSerialUnit` after `bStartUnit()` starts its worker (`btserial.class.c:125-258`); `bReleaseServiceBinding()` signals and waits only for `nsu_Task` (`:265-288`). `bSerialTask()` opens `bluetooth.library` but not its own class module, and after aborting/freeing channels, draining requests, deleting its port and closing that library, it clears `nsu_Task` and signals immediately before its function return (`:530-590,704-790`). Bluetooth `btRemClass()` invokes binding release, then closes the retained `bc_ClassBase` reference after `bc_UseCnt` reaches zero (`bluetooth/classes.c:113-158`). BTSerial `libExpunge()` frees the unit records and removes `btserial.device` when the embedded device is idle (`btserial.class.c:80-113`); generated CloseLib calls it after a last close when `LIBF_DELEXP` is pending (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1463-1517`; deferred request sets the flag at `:1586-1591`). LDDemon unloads the resulting segment list (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:569-596,893-899`). The class aggregate edge is optional/commented, but the explicit target is `rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/mmakefile.src`; `btAddClass()` loads class modules dynamically. Added OD9561 for the conditional ExecSMP interval between the worker's pointer signal and function return. No device, class removal, expunge or task schedule was run; source-only.


OD9562 BTPAN worker/module-expunge caller pass (2026-10-24): followed successful BTPAN service-binding creation into `bEthTask()` and its shutdown chain. The worker's `bAllocEth()` opens `bluetooth.library`; it does not take a `btpan.class` reference (`btpan.class.c:289-306,1000-1018`). `bReleaseServiceBinding()` signals the GUI and network task, then waits only for their task-pointer fields to clear (`:311-350`). The network worker calls `bFreeEth()`, which closes its Bluetooth library reference and clears `ncp_Task` before signaling and returning through the worker epilogue (`:944-950,1044-1092`). `btRemClass()` releases the binding and closes the retained class library reference at `bluetooth/classes.c:113-158`; when expunge was deferred, genmodule's final-close path invokes ExpungeLib after the close hook (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1463-1517`); LDDemon unloads the returned segment list (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:569-596,893-899`). BTPAN `libExpunge()` frees unit records and removes the device when its open count is idle (`btpan.class.c:81-116`) without a worker-exit join. The direct BTPAN target is buildable; its parent aggregate edge is optional (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btpan/mmakefile.src`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/mmakefile.src:10-13`). This establishes OD9562's conditional cross-CPU worker-tail/module-expunge candidate. No device, class removal, task schedule, or expunge was run; source-only.

USB MassStorage worker/object teardown recheck (no new OD; 2026-10-24): followed the cached LUN worker through `Storage::Dispose()` and the worker loop (`storageclass.c:338-371`; `storage_task.c:167-190,225-325`). Disposal deliberately moves a live unit into the cache and signals `SIGF_SINGLE`; the worker remains alive to serve a later rebind, updates `unit->msu_object` on that rebind, and only exits on `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C`. The signal sent during disposal does not join the task, but this persistent worker/cache design does not itself establish that its object data is reclaimed while used. The separate case where disposal removes pipes while the worker may still be transferring remains OD2831. The worker's startup-result and initial stack/name allocation failures are separately OD9563/OD9564. No device, disconnect, or rebind was run; source-only.


USBHub worker reply/Dispose teardown follow-up (no new OD; 2026-10-24): reread the cleanup handshake (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:204-223,650-662`). `USBHub::Dispose` waits for the worker's `evt_Cleanup` reply before freeing `children` and `proc_name`; after `ReplyMsg`, `hub_process` immediately returns and does not dereference `HubData` again. The worker does outlive the reply by its function epilogue, but the retained USB root object keeps the stack library open count nonzero (OD4051), so ordinary close cannot unload that code in this state. No separate disposed-object or module-tail consequence was established. No hub disposal or expunge was run; source-only.

AROSTCP DNS compressed-name helper label-boundary follow-up (OD9512 expanded; 2026-10-24): during the explicit full-body ledger reconciliation, rechecked all `dn_expand()` byte loads against `eomorig`. A truncated final label therefore reads one byte beyond the response end before returning an error; if the response fills the fixed answer object, that read also crosses the object boundary. xHCI RTIso local-body and interval caller recheck (OD3194 retained; no new OD; 2026-10-24): read all 378 physical lines / 293 `cloc 2.06` C lines of `rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_isoch.c` in source order. Traced `cmdAdd/Start/Stop/RemIsoHandler` through `PCIUSB_WIP_ISO` (enabled by `rom/usb/pcixhci/make.opts`), Poseidon per-speed `pep_Interval` normalization (`poseidon.library.c:8483-8583,4624-4627`), xHCI endpoint-context `xhciCalcInterval()` (`xhci_hcd.c:160-207`) and RTIso frame-step calculation (`xhci_isoch.c:232-272`). Confirmed high-/SuperSpeed Poseidon stores `1 << (bInterval-1)` microframes, while the RTIso queue interprets that normalized count as an exponent and exponentiates again; at HS `bInterval=4`, the supplied 8-microframe interval becomes a 128-microframe step. Smaller values are excluded because rounding to whole frames does not establish this distinct cadence mismatch. Reconciled the in-tree USB Audio and SonixcamTool RTIso hooks, two-request prefill, completion, Stop and Remove paths against OD1726-OD1727, OD3194-OD3196 and OD3206; no additional independent issue established. The later stop/free-versus-in-flight event-task lifetime remains OD3196/OD3206. No controller, endpoint, stream, stop, or completion was run; source-only.

OD4406 Bluetooth class-scan overlap lock/snapshot verification (retained; no new OD; 2026-10-24): re-read `bDeviceClassScan()` and `btClassScan()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:255-445`) against `bLockSemShared()` and its admission/unlock logic (`bluetooth.library.c:455-519,619-627`). The shared base lock records independent reader tasks; it does not serialize simultaneous class scans. Within each device, `bDeviceClassScan()` marks at most 16 individual services `bsv_BindingInProgress` under the device lock, drops the lock before invoking potentially blocking class methods, and later clears the snapshot markers. Separate overlapping scans can therefore reserve different batches of the same device's services. Re-traced BTHID's one-device check, worker startup/wait and late list insertion (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:224-279`); the check does not reserve the physical device across that interval. This confirms OD4406's conditional premise when HIDP and HOGP services land in separate overlapping batches; no new root cause beyond the existing duplicate-binding finding. Existing trigger qualification (concurrent scans, >16 pending services, HID bearers in different batches) remains. No binding or concurrent scan was run; source-only.

RTL8139 first-open concurrency pass (OD9568 added; 2026-10-24): traced the complete `Open()` state sequence in `workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/rtl8139_init.c:276-375` against Exec's `OpenDevice()` lock-release point (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:89-114`), `rtl8139nic_open()`'s online publication (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/rtl8139.c:577-720`), and `CmdRead()`'s offline error (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/handler.c:220-245`). The open count and `IFF_SHARED` state are changed before the start decision without serialization. In an overlap between two non-exclusive Opens, the second can increment the first-open count from one to two before either caller tests it; both then skip the `open_count == 1` start call and return success with `IFF_UP` clear. Added OD9568. This is distinct from OD3036's interrupt-visible opener-list race and OD3038's tracking-baseline lifetime. No Open, request, or device was run; source-only.


Linux input worker-start failure-to-expunge caller recheck (OD9527/OD9530 boundary; 2026-10-24): followed create_inputtask() failure through the void Init_LinuxInput_inputtask() wrapper, Init_Hidd() success, LinuxInput_Startup() registrations, and Expunge_Hidd(). On the task/stack/AddTask failure paths, eh->inputtask remains NULL; Expunge_Hidd() would pass it to Kill_LinuxInput_inputtask(), which calls Signal(NULL, SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C), and Exec Signal() dereferences the task in the ExecSMP path. However, LinuxInput_Startup() sets lib_OpenCnt to 1 as a self-open before these later teardown paths, and no checked-in path clearing that hold was established. Therefore this possible NULL-signal teardown is not promoted as an independent finding or treated as a confirmed consequence of ordinary expunge. OD9530 remains the demonstrated startup consequence: successful HIDD/driver registration with a missing event worker; OD9527 remains the separate running-worker teardown race. No task failure, Signal(NULL), open-count transition or unload was induced; source-only.


WirelessManager SANA-II backend source-order and association-lifetime recheck (OD3626/OD3946 retained; no new OD; 2026-10-24): reread the complete `driver_sana2.c` body (1,115 physical lines / 881 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) against its selected `.config` (`CONFIG_DRIVER_SANA2=y`, `CONFIG_ELOOP=eloop_amiga`) and driver table. Rechecked `wpa_driver_sana2_associate()`'s temporary 33-byte `os_zalloc()` SSID: the cloned tag list is freed after synchronous `S2_SETOPTIONS`, but the separately allocated SSID is not freed on either success or failure, confirming OD3946. Hosted parallel UnixIO callback teardown recheck (OD3508/OD4241 adjacent; no new finding; 2026-10-24): traced `SigIO_IntServer` registration through `KrnAddIRQHandler(SIGIO)` and, on Darwin, the additional `SIGALRM` timer path (`arch/all-unix/hidd/unixio/unixio_class.c:139-155,1173-1191`). UnixIO `AddInterrupt` and `RemInterrupt` bracket their interrupt-list insertion/removal with `Disable()`/`Enable()` (`:828-836,916-922`); the unit disposer removes its callback before closing the descriptor and returning through superclass disposal (`arch/all-unix/hidd/parallel/ParallelUnitClass.c:194-209`). `parallel.device` removes the unit from its own list before disposing the HIDD object (`workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_init.c:240-250`). The Unix kernel's signal mask blocks handled I/O signals during AROS interrupt work, and Darwin explicitly forwards foreign-thread ticks to the AROS host thread (`arch/all-unix/kernel/kernel.c:125-149,253-295,310-327`). In a single AROS host-thread execution this serializes the callback against disposal, so the prior evidence does not establish a callback use-after-free. `Disable()` is per-host-thread signal masking; the checked source does not establish cross-pthread exclusion on every non-Darwin host, so that host-library/signal-delivery edge remains open. No callback, removal, signal, or host device was run; source-only.


Parallel-device large-read offset recheck (OD9569 added; 2026-10-24): reread `RBF_InterruptHandler()` and `CMD_READ` queue setup, then traced the public size fields (`IOStdReq.io_Length/io_Actual` are `ULONG`) through `port.handler`'s `ACTION_READ` to `DoIO()`. The HIDD receive callback is provided by hosted Unix and transfers up to 513 bytes per call; repeated batches can carry a large request over the 65,535-byte boundary. The local `UWORD` destination index then wraps, is copied back to `io_Actual`, prevents equality with a larger requested length, and restarts writes at the beginning of the user buffer. This is a noncompletion/data-overwrite defect, not a buffer overrun. PC/m68k receive reachability was not established; no in-tree large-length caller or input stream was run.

Qualified parallel reachability to builds selecting the Unix HIDD; native PC/m68k receive paths were not established. OD11 remains the single finding for this shared offset-width defect. No large read or input was run; source-only.

AHCI OD3237 optional caller trigger correction (2026-10-24): compared the QuickPart target manifest (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`) with the AHCI disk and ATAPI `HD_SCSICMD` paths. QuickPart is optional, not default-selected. When included and used on an AHCI disk, its failed one-byte ATA IDENTIFY is followed by a one-byte SCSI INQUIRY; AHCI disk emulation reads the EVPD field past the declared CDB length. The ATAPI path rejects lengths below six before copying or decoding, so this caller does not reach the same issue on an ATAPI unit. This supersedes the earlier blanket statement that no in-tree short-CDB caller path was established, while retaining optional-build qualification. No command or device was run.

USB MIDI class partial-initialization rollback recheck (2026-10-24; no new finding): traced `libInit()`'s Utility open failure through generated `_set_libinit()` (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:58-69`) into `libExpunge()` (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:25-62`). `nh_UtilityBase` remains NULL on that failure path, and Exec `CloseLibrary()` explicitly branches on NULL without dereferencing (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:58-90`); this is not an expunge crash. AHI-Handler OD1946 partial-read-allocation teardown recheck (2026-10-24; retained, no duplicate): re-traced the three sequential non-clearing `AllocVec` calls (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:423-434`) against the only initialization/submission of `readreq` (`:437-450`) and `ACTION_END` cleanup (`:647-657`). If `readreq` succeeds while either sample buffer allocation fails, the error return leaves a non-NULL request that was neither copied from `AHIio` nor sent; `ACTION_END` nevertheless calls `AbortIO` and `WaitIO`. Exec `AbortIO` reads `io_Device` and dispatches through that field (`rom/exec/abortio.c:49-56`), confirming OD1946's invalid-request teardown consequence. No allocation failure, retry, close, or request was induced; source-only.

AHI core audio control full-body/lifecycle pass (2026-10-24; no finding added): read all 1,022 physical lines / 487 C code lines of `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c`. Traced `_AHI_AllocAudioA()` publication and its allocation-error unwind through `_AHI_FreeAudio()`, then checked the public vector tables and `_AHI_KillAudio()` (`header.c:398-417,479-498`; `audioctrl.c:457-526,702-746,793-807`). `ahib_AudioCtrl` retains only the most recently allocated control and ordinary `FreeAudio` does not clear it, so a later `KillAudio` can receive a stale pointer after a normally freed latest control. Bluetooth queued ACL transmit/disconnect ownership pass (OD3802 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `bSendACLPacket()` admission and packet copy into `hc_ACLTxQueue`, credit/request exhaustion retention, `bConnDown()` connection and L2CAP teardown, and the two later drain triggers (`bHandleDevReply()` for completed write requests and `HC_EVT_NUM_COMPLETED_PACKETS`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:140-163,1019-1121,2992-3024`; `hwtask.c:2619-2679,2722-2770`). Confirmed connection teardown does not remove queued `HCACLTx` nodes for its handle; after a write slot or credit event, `bStartACLWrite()` sends a retained node even when no matching live `BtHWConn` exists, defaulting to BR/EDR credits. This independently rechecks the source sequence already documented by OD3802; no second finding or whole-file credit was added. Bluetooth LE ACL disconnect credit-accounting and stale-ledger reconciliation (OD9579 strengthened; 2026-10-25): traced separate LE buffer-count parsing and shared-buffer fallback (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:1982-1990`), LE pool decrement plus `cn_Credits` in-flight increment (`:2633-2677`; field contract at `hwtask.h:221`), completion-event decrement/restoration (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:2992-3024`), and disconnect teardown (`:1018-1121`). Compared this handling with Bluetooth Core Specification Vol. 4, Part E §4.3: disconnection flushes outstanding controller buffers without requiring a prior Number Of Completed Packets event. The per-connection counter is therefore sufficient for teardown to restore the outstanding LE pool count, but `bConnDown()` frees it without reconciliation; completed-packet handling restores LE credits only when the live connection is found. Found and corrected an earlier ledger sentence that treated the lack of post-disconnection completion events as evidence against a credit issue; that behavior is the reason the teardown omission loses the count. Strengthened OD9579 with the explicit in-flight counter evidence; kept it separate from OD3802's stale queued-packet submission. No device, disconnect, completion event or runtime manifestation was exercised. No whole-file credit; `hwtask.c` and broader Bluetooth connection lifecycle remain partial. Source-only.

WASAPI volume capability and AHI dispatch pass (OD9570 added; 2026-10-24): traced the `AHIDB_Volume=TRUE` mode declaration (`WASAPI.s:11-18`) through AHI mode-info semantics and `ControlAudioA` set/query dispatch (`Device/modeinfo.c:612-614`; `Device/audioctrl.c:971-1000`) into `_AHIsub_HardwareControl()` and its mixer helpers. PCI generic word-write upper-half caller pass (OD9571 added; 2026-10-24): re-read the generic `WriteConfigWord` and PCIDevice forwarding bodies, confirmed `0xffff` is an `int` before the upper-half shift and traced selected PCIPC inheritance. OD9571 C shift-semantics verification (2026-10-24): checked the exact expression `0xffff << 16` against WG14 C11 committee draft N1570 §6.5.7p4. Since the left operand is signed `int` and the mathematical result does not fit that signed result type, the shift itself has undefined behavior; this is distinct from conversion of a wider unsigned value back to signed. The report now cites the clause. This confirms source-level classification only; no selected upper-half call or compiler output was established.

parallel.device native CMD_READ route through `port.handler` (OD3226 expanded, 2026-10-24): followed `decodeStartup()`'s parallel mode through its `parallel.device`/unit-0 selection (`workbench/fs/port/port-handler.c:208-224`) and the packet loop's `ACTION_READ` setup and synchronous `DoIO(CMD_READ)` (`:411-435`). A DOS read through a mounted parallel-mode port handler therefore blocks that handler task while the accepted device request waits for the receive callback that native m68k/PC HIDDs never produce. The handler target and device target are optional, and no checked-in application call to `Read(PAR:)` was found, so this is a conditional in-tree forwarding route rather than established routine use. Expanded OD3226 and its master-index summary; no handler body credit or runtime operation. Source-only.


Filesave zero-mix-rate recording caller pass (OD9572 added; 2026-10-24): traced `AHIA_MixFreq` initialization and default substitution through Filesave allocation flags and `AHIC_Record` dispatch into `RecSlave()` pacing. The zero literal is distinct from the default sentinel and survives; after a sample is loaded and the worker signals ready, its first record iteration invokes the record hook then divides by `ahiac_MixFreq` in `Delay`. The mode advertises a 5,513 Hz minimum but does not clamp in the selected allocation/start path. No AHI allocation, recording, or worker was run; no body-line credit.


`audio.device` selected OpenDevice caller census (no new finding; 2026-10-24): searched all C callers in the checkout and traced all three hits to their failure cleanup. Sound.datatype frees its request array and message port and resets its state after OpenDevice fails (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3142-3219`); Speech and Narrator both route partial acquisitions through `ReleaseAudio`, which conditionally closes only an opened device and deletes acquired requests, buffers, ports and channel-mask storage (`workbench/devs/speech/speech.c:190-232`; `workbench/devs/narrator/narrator.c:312-375`). The other `OpenDevice()` in `audio_commands.c` opens `ahi.device`, not `audio.device`, and is not counted as a caller of this device. No independent failed-open leak or stale-device cleanup was established. This closes only the in-tree OpenDevice caller slice; external clients and concurrent Open/Close remain pending. No device or failure path was run; source-only.


AHI Filesave zero-mix-rate full-path recheck (OD9572 retained; 2026-10-24): searched every selected `ahiac_MixFreq` use in AHI core and the Filesave mode. Confirmed zero is copied unchanged by `CreateAudioCtrl()`; the default sentinel substitution does not match it. `RecalcBuff()` checks its `freq` parameter (the player rate), not the mix-rate numerator, so its result is zero work rather than a zero denominator. `UpdateAudioCtrl()` divides by the defaulted player-frequency values and produces zero sample limits; it does not reject the mix rate. The successful Filesave allocator returns CANRECORD/TIMING without normalizing it. For a record-only `AHIC_Record` request, core dispatch reaches `_AHIsub_Start()` and the recording slave without invoking playback mixing; after its first record hook it evaluates the unchanged zero-rate pacing denominator. This confirms the fault's point in the selected path and keeps any simultaneous playback behavior outside the narrow OD9572 claim. No rate was supplied to the device and no recording task was run; source-only.
SD-card bus spinlock task/IRQ caller closure (OD9573 added; 2026-10-24): re-traced every `sdcb_Lock` use in the common bus body and followed initialization, `WaitCmd()` task recovery, `BusIRQEntry()` and common SDHCI `BusIRQ()` dispatch. On SMP, task-side claim/publish sections use `KrnSpinLock()` but omit the `Disable()` present in non-SMP branches; the AArch64 kernel spinlock does not mask local IRQs. The AArch64 Raspberry Pi manifest selects SDHCI implementations for BCM2711/2712 and their common callback uses the same lock; `NewCreateTask()` provides no bus-task affinity constraint. A local controller IRQ can therefore preempt an owner on the same CPU and spin forever on the lock held by the interrupted task. Narrowed scope to this AArch64 SMP SDHCI path. Earlier ARM32 SDHOST handler has a separate callback that only acknowledges controller status and does not take this lock. No hardware, IRQ, card I/O or schedule was exercised; source-only.



RTL816x PCI config-word caller pass (OD9574 added, 2026-10-24): traced `rtl_hw_start_8101()` through `rtl816x_HWStart()` and its config selection, checked RTL8101E MAC-version identification, then followed `HIDD_PCIDevice_WriteConfigWord()` through the generic PCI device forwarding method and generic driver implementation. The call at offset `0x69` rounds to dword `0x68` and selects shift zero, so it overwrites the preceding `0x68` word write. Added OD9574, scoped to RTL816x RTL8101E startup; the hardware meaning of the malformed register sequence is undocumented locally. No PCI access or hardware was run; source-only. No body-line credit.


BCM2711 PCI indexed-window SMP transaction pass (OD9575 added, 2026-10-24): traced external config reads/writes through `ReadConfigLong()`/`WriteConfigLong()` and the controller's shared `PCIE_EXT_CFG_INDEX`/`PCIE_EXT_CFG_DATA` window. ## BCM2711 PCIe HIDD selected module inventory and body pass

The `kernel-pcie-bcm2711` module manifest selects `pcie_init.c` and `driverclass.c`; the active `kernel-package-raspi-aarch64` target includes that module, and `PKG_HIDDS` includes `pcibcm2711` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:89-91,153-163,226-232`). The driver activates only when its peripheral-base and device-tree checks identify usable BCM2711 PCIe hardware. Its class configuration registers the driver/device methods and uses `pcie.h` for shared state and register definitions. These five checked-in module paths are now represented explicitly; body credit is limited to the two C translation units and the private header.

| File | Status | Remaining scope |
|---|---|---|
| `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/mmakefile.src` | Full 10-line module manifest read; `kernel-package-raspi-aarch64` selects it through `PKG_HIDDS` | Generated target build remains unverified; runtime activation is gated by BCM2711 peripheral-base and device-tree checks. |
| `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/pcibcm2711.conf` | Full 49-line class configuration read | Generated class tables and target build remain unverified. |
| `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/pcie.h` | Full 227-line private header read (107 `cloc 2.06` code lines) | Hardware register semantics and board/firmware contracts remain open. |
| `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/pcie_init.c` | Full 758-line body read (498 `cloc 2.06` C code lines); init, DT parsing, bridge setup, endpoint setup, firmware, MSI handler, and failure exits traced | Device-tree/firmware contents and hardware bring-up remain unverified. |
| `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/driverclass.c` | Full 440-line body read (284 `cloc 2.06` C code lines); config access, DMA map ownership, PCI address mapping, MSI vector lifecycle, and selected call paths traced; OD9575 | Concurrent hardware access and runtime PCI behavior remain unverified. |

TextEditor keymap conversion caller pass (OD9577 added; 2026-10-24): read the complete `MapANSI()` output-capacity/failure path and traced its direct configuration-reload caller (`rom/keymap/mapansi.c:392-429`; `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/InitConfig.c:344-389`). keymap.library failed-init resource publication follow-up (OD9578 added; 2026-10-24): traced `KeymapInit()`'s mandatory `usa` node allocation failure through generated library-init rollback and the direct resource consumer (`rom/keymap/keymap_init.c:52-62`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:64-85`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1158-1180`; `rom/exec/openresource.c:53-64`; `workbench/libs/kms/kms_library.c:107-115`; `workbench/libs/kms/openkeymap.c:60-87,134-152`). `AddResource()` publishes the embedded resource before `AddKeymap()` can fail; generic rollback invokes no resource removal, while generated `InitLib` frees the failed module base. A later `OpenResource()` can therefore return a resource node whose storage was freed, and KMS trusts and accesses its `kr_List`. Added OD9578 to the findings and master index; the previous “finding 875” ledger reference was stale and has been replaced. No failure or resource access was induced; source-only.

MapRawKey selected caller error-result census (2026-10-24; no new OD): checked selected direct callers outside the earlier console path (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2458,2515,2569`; `strgadgets.c:503`; `sysrequest_intern.c:229-247`; Zune TextEditor/BetterString helpers; AHIRecord `:1385-1424,1431-1442`; USB/Bluetooth HID GUI paths). KMS keymap short-HUNK bounds candidate recheck (OD2358 strengthened; 2026-10-24): traced `OpenKeymap()`'s `LoadSeg()` and `GetSegListInfo(GSLI_68KHUNK)` gate into `parsekeymapseg()` (`workbench/libs/kms/openkeymap.c:104-130`; `parsekeymapseg.c:132-163`) and the selected AROS HUNK loader's segment sizing (`rom/dos/internalloadseg_aos.c:174-210`). The loader allocates each segment from the HUNK-declared payload word count and does not enforce a keymap-specific minimum size; the converter skips the segment link and immediately reads fixed node fields and pointer slots, with no segment extent supplied. This corroborates OD2358 for a HUNK map declaring a short code payload, rather than relying on physical-file truncation. The converter condition excludes big-endian 32-bit builds. No HUNK file was loaded; source-only. Referenced descriptor payload/relocation bounds remain a separate open slice.

KMS converter embedded-pointer bounds follow-up (OD2358 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced each converted 68K pointer field from `COPYPTR` into fixed table loops, descriptor sizing and copy (`workbench/libs/kms/parsekeymapseg.c:79-129,151-225,272-325`). `parsekeymapseg()` receives no segment extent; it trusts the relocated name/table/descriptor pointers, uses `strlen()` on the name, and its string/dead-key sizing helpers read descriptor headers and compute copy lengths from unvalidated offsets. A short node is not required for these paths: a segment large enough for the fixed node can still carry a pointer/descriptor range beyond its declared HUNK payload. Expanded OD2358 to cover both extent cases in converter-enabled builds and updated the parser ledger row; no additional ID was split because the same missing segment/range validation at this conversion boundary is the root cause. No malformed HUNK was loaded; source-only.

USB HID/Storage failed temporary-root-object disposal configuration check (2026-10-24; no OD): both `HID_Init()` and `Storage_Init()` call `OOP_DisposeObject(usb)` after conditionally calling `HIDD_USB_AddClass()` (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid_init.c:66-71`; `classes/MassStorage/storage_init.c:71-76`). `OOP_NewObject()` may return NULL, but `OOP_DisposeObject()`'s `EnterFunc` log expands to `D()` before its explicit null return (`rom/oop/disposeobject.c:53-60`). The selected build defaults `DEBUG` to zero in `compiler/arossupport/include/debug.h:20-23,337-340`; configure's `--enable-debug=messages` adds `ADEBUG`/`MDEBUG`, not `DEBUG` (`configure.in:1059-1060,1098-1114`). Therefore the selected source configuration compiles out the pre-guard log and null disposal safely returns; no selected-build defect is established. A local build that explicitly defines `DEBUG=1` could make the log dereference NULL on temporary object-allocation failure, but that is not established by the checked-in selected build. No object allocation was induced; source-only.

AHI SSE4.1 mixer buffer-span caller recheck (no new OD; 2026-10-25): traced all four `addroutines_sse.c` fast paths against `UseFastPath()`, `Mix()`'s `samplesleft`/`cd_Samples` clipping and `AHI_SetSound()`'s inclusive first/last frame calculation (`addroutines_sse.c:29-48,66-232`; `mixer.c:713-716,836-864,1209-1226`; `sound.c:403-462,492-515`). The forward unit-step fast path is excluded at the initial `FirstOffsetI`; once selected, `index = offset - 1` is at or after the initial frame, and each vector loop reads exactly four mono frames or two interleaved stereo frames per processed group, with a scalar tail for the remainder. The final interpolation endpoint is the last selected frame. Destination stores cover exactly the processed frame count in the output representation selected by `AHIACF_STEREO`/`AHIACF_HIFI`, and `RecalcBuff()` sizes the mix buffer from that frame format (`audioctrl.c:77-99,548-567`; `mixer.c:267-425`). No SIMD-specific tail overread or output overwrite was established. `AHI_LoadSound()` retains the caller's sample pointer and declared length (`sound.c:895-918`); the implementation does not independently validate the external allocation or each `AHI_SetSound()` range, so those public caller preconditions remain outside this fast-path conclusion. Standard target flags do not define `__SSE4_1__`; execution additionally requires the Processor resource feature check (`configure.in:1364-1384`; `header.c:891-913`). No audio was mixed; source-only.


AHI AVX2 mono-to-stereo lane-order correction (OD9580 added; 2026-10-25): re-evaluated `AddLongStereo_AVX2()` using AVX2's 128-bit-lane-local `VUNPCKL`/`VUNPCKH` behavior (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/addroutines_avx.c:118-130`). For eight scaled left/right frames, the low-unpack result is frames 0,1,4,5 and the high-unpack result is 2,3,6,7; consecutive stores therefore permute the middle four frames. Confirmed this function is selected for mono M32S input and S32S output (`mixer.c:352-405`) and is reachable only after the compile-time AVX2 guard plus runtime AVX/AVX2 checks (`header.c:915-921`); the fast-path conditions and eight-sample minimum are in `addroutines_avx.c:29-48,111-130`. Other AVX2 paths were rechecked: the mono-input stereo-output path is the one that splits an eight-frame left/right vector into separately stored low/high unpacks; the interleaved-stereo path processes four frames and its one unpack result preserves frame order. Replaced the ledger's prior incorrect “no lane-order mismatch” conclusion and added OD9580 to the detailed report and master index. No AVX2 build or audio was run; source-only.


OD9580 configuration reachability qualification (2026-10-25): narrowed the reported reordering trigger to custom x86-64 standalone builds. The x86-64 standalone kernel detects XSAVE/AVX, enables OSXSAVE and XCR0 FPU/SSE/YMM state, and sizes the task context for XSAVE (`arch/x86_64-all/kernel/cpu_init.c:26-91`); the selected x86-64 context layout includes an XSAVE pointer/size (`arch/x86_64-all/include/aros/cpucontext.h:77-97`). Standard USB hub control-message/interrupt-completion ordering recheck (OD903/OD3251/OD3252 retained; no new finding; 2026-10-25): followed `nHubTask()`'s recurring EP1 submission, wait, control-port drain, and task-port completion handling (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:443-459,749-758`) against `usbDoMethod()`'s direct-call branch when the hub method is invoked by its own worker (`hub.class.c:338-350`). This confirms that nested child suspend/resume requests do not post back to and block the current hub worker. Rechecked `UCM_AttemptSuspendDevice`/`UCM_AttemptResumeDevice` (`:1429-1463`): suspend's `psdAbortPipe()` precedes `nch_Running = FALSE`; resume waits for the original EP1 message, resubmits, and marks the worker running. `psdWaitPipe()` loops on the target message's `NT_MESSAGE` state rather than treating any signal on the shared task port as completion (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4817-4825`); therefore an unrelated pipe completion signal alone does not release the wait. No additional defect established beyond OD903's incomplete xHCI root-hub abort completion and OD3251/OD3252's partial suspend/resume outcomes. `hub.class.c` already has full-body credit; this is selected caller/state-order reconciliation only. No device, pipe request or suspend/resume operation was run; source-only.

ACPI power-meter telemetry getter caller census (OD1753/OD3417 retained; no new finding; 2026-10-25): searched all checked-in C/C++ uses of `HIDD_Telemetry_GetEntryAttribs`; the only callers are SysExplorer's generic Telemetry page and Power page (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Telemetry/telemetry_window_cl.c:134-181`; `Modules/Power/power_window_cl.c:225-260,274-298`). Both initialize every output field before dispatch, use the reported telemetry count to bound indices, and skip an entry when the getter returns FALSE. The ACPI power-meter getter instead returns TRUE after an ACPI evaluation/type failure while supplying value zero (`rom/hidds/acpi/powermeter/acpipowermeter_class.c:293-327`), as already qualified in OD1753; the selected caller path establishes a displayed zero rather than an uninitialized read. Rechecked `ReadInteger`/`ReadPackageInteger` allocation cleanup: every non-NULL ACPICA result buffer reaches `FreeVec` regardless of evaluation-result type (`:31-50,58-77`); the selected native ACPICA port pairs `AcpiOsAllocate()` `AllocVec()` with `AcpiOsFree()` `FreeVec()` (`arch/all-native/acpica/acpios_aros.c:234-250`), closing the allocator-pairing question for selected native builds. No new caller defect or body credit established. No firmware method or UI query was run; source-only.

AHI AVX2 format and caller recheck (OD9580 retained; no new OD; 2026-10-25): re-read all four AVX2 routines and `SelectAddRoutine()` dispatch for 32-bit mono/stereo and interleaved stereo input (`addroutines_avx.c:66-232`; `mixer.c:313-430`). Confirmed the lane-local unpack defect is confined to `AddLongStereo_AVX2()` mono-M32S to stereo-S32S output: its eight-frame vector store order is 0,1,4,5,2,3,6,7; the mono-output reduction and interleaved-stereo paths retain their scalar frame order. `Mix()` calls the selected routine with a positive count clipped to remaining output and channel frames (`mixer.c:836-864`), while dispatch requires the `__AVX2__` build guard and AVX plus AVX2 CPU support (`header.c:915-921`). AHI OD3570 producer/consumer serialization follow-up (no new finding; 2026-10-25): confirmed `FeedReaders()` obtains `iounit->Lock`, but the interrupt-capable `RecordFunc()` replaces `RecordBuffer`/`RecordSize` and signals without acquiring that lock (`Device/devcommands.c:982-1008`; `Device/device.c:990-1003`).
