e1000 RX completion/recycling follow-up (2026-10-25; no new OD): read the complete `e1000func_clean_rx_irq()` path (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000.c:1253-1439`) and traced its invocation from `e1000func_IntHandler()` (`unit.c:368-390`), descriptor refill, packet filtering/copy and selected RX request handling (`unit.c:390-480`). Multi-descriptor and rejected/error packets are recycled; completed descriptors reuse their existing buffers through the fake refill helper, which advances RDT without allocating replacements. The cleaner consumes the descriptor buffer address as a CPU pointer; this is identity-consistent on the selected native x86 PC route because the selected PCIPC DirectBus methods return the same address for CPUtoPCI and PCItoCPU (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:129-164`; x86 PC target route in the e1000 manifest and PCIPC configuration). The generic non-DirectBus `(APTR)-1` result is outside this selected configuration and is not promoted separately. No new defect established in this slice; OD3018 remains the separate unchecked initial/refill allocation failure. Broader controller status semantics and runtime packet behavior remain source-only. No device, interrupt, packet, or allocation failure was exercised.


Nouveau/VMware DRM memory-statistics caller pass (2026-10-25; no new OD): inspected both byte-identical `drm-compat/linux_mem.c` implementations at `compat_totalram_pages()` and `si_meminfo()`. `AvailMem(MEMF_PUBLIC | MEMF_TOTAL)` and `AvailMem(MEMF_PUBLIC)` return byte counts, which callers shift by `PAGE_SHIFT`; `si_meminfo()` sets `mem_unit = PAGE_SIZE`. The result types hold page counts, and this path's unit conversion is internally consistent. Existing OD4039/OD4040 concern allocation metadata and cross-CPU cache-sync list ownership, not these statistics callers. No sysinfo request, HIDD or hardware was run; source-only.


e1000 interrupt return-convention caller pass (2026-10-25; no new OD): followed `e1000func_IntHandler()` and `e1000func_WatchdogHandler()` through both registrations in `request_irq()` (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/e1000.c:626-632`; watchdog and device callbacks in `unit.c:313-405`). The device IRQ is registered at `INTB_KERNEL + irq`; Exec's `AddIntServer()` wraps this in `krnIRQwrapper()`, whose return type is `void` and which invokes the callback without forwarding its BOOL result (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:19-24,64-67`). The device interrupt callback's final zero therefore does not suppress handling in the selected PC kernel IRQ path. The watchdog is registered on shared `INTB_VERTB`; it returns FALSE, allowing subsequent VERTB interrupt servers to run, and does not claim that interrupt. No finding established for these return values. This does not alter OD3023's distinct duplicate registration/missing removal lifetime issue. No interrupt was run; source-only.

In the `PTPF_PARTIAL` branch, both `GetPartialObject` and the full-file `GetObject` path pass the clipped DOS read length as `buflen`; the object-write preparation path passes `poi_Size` only after `nPTPWrite()` has allocated the extension buffer (`ptp.class.c:2293-2341,2428-2468,2472-2485`); the non-extending NULL-buffer case is tracked separately as OD9582. No device or transfer was used; source-only; no body-line credit changed.


PTP existing-file write buffer lifecycle pass (OD9582 added; 2026-10-25): traced `ACTION_FINDUPDATE` to `nCreateFH()` and the first `ACTION_WRITE` through `nPTPWrite()` (`ptp.class.c:3053-3078,3311-3333,2415-2504,3646-3658`). The handle allocation comes from a `MEMF_CLEAR` pool, so `pfh_Buffer` begins NULL. Only writes extending beyond `poi_Size` allocate a buffer; a partial in-range write passes NULL to `nGetPTPRspData()`, and a full in-place overwrite copies to the NULL pointer directly. No bitmap, palette, PCI device or refresh was exercised; source-only.

Bluetooth HID shared dispatcher caller-concurrency follow-up (OD9646 added; 2026-10-25): traced both `bDoAction()` action branches into `bInstallLastActionHero()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:4881-4897,5479-5500`), confirmed `bForceServiceBinding()` spawns a distinct `bHidTask` for each successful service binding (`:244-264,905-922`), and followed dispatcher creation through publication, message-port assignment, and last-close cleanup (`:96-111,6219-6350`). USB CAMD MIDI packet-budget and loader-gate recheck (OD4234 retained and qualified; 2026-10-25): re-read the complete `nParseMidiOut()` packet-emission loop and its call from the binding worker (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:467-517,519-733`), then checked the output allocation (`:854-859`), 16 adapter records/open-port bounds (`:32-48,388-436`), producer callback's 100-byte-per-activation limit and task signal (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camd/poseidonusb.c:119-132`), and the USB MIDI CAMD target edges. `goodpkt` is initialized once per output pass; after reaching 2,040 packets, each later open adapter with pending valid data still executes its `do` body once before the per-adapter loop condition is tested. Ten ports can therefore emit 2,049 four-byte packets (8,196 bytes) into the 8,192-byte allocation; the 16-port upper case emits 2,055 (8,220 bytes). The queued bytes fit the individual 4,096-byte rings, so the cross-port packet count does not require a per-ring overflow. Reconfirmed current AROS CAMD rejects this embedded bridge before calling `Init` or registering/opening ports because `MidiDeviceData.Flags` is zero (`poseidonusb.c:31-47`; `workbench/libs/camd/drivers.c:221-260`; public requirement `compiler/include/midi/camddevices.h:57-58`). Thus OD4234 remains a real source defect in the optional USB MIDI target, but its normal CAMD trigger is gated by OD4300 until that separate format flag is corrected or bypassed. The module is not a default claim: parent aggregate edges are conditional/commented in `rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:10-43` and the class CPU mapping is explicitly optional in `camdmidi/mmakefile.src:3-11`. No CAMD driver was loaded, no event was queued, and no pipe transfer was run; source-only.

BTHID report-length ID accounting and receive-buffer reuse recheck (OD9648 expanded; 2026-10-25): traced `bHandleReport()`'s Classic HIDP header strip and Report ID selection against the maximum packet-size calculation, receive-buffer allocation, first submissions and resubmissions (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:823-899,945-966,1061-1068,1127-1155,1606-1647`). The handler only tests `actual` before consuming the optional report-ID byte; it never checks that payload bytes remain for the selected report's fields. Later short packets reuse the same maximum-sized receive buffer and preserve previous trailing bytes. This sharpens OD9648's short-completion trigger; the zero-initialized first-read buffer prevents claiming stale prior-packet bytes on the first completion, but does not prevent field decoding from absent payload. BTHID class and binding config reload/error-path pass (OD3759 rechecked; no new finding; 2026-10-25): read the complete `bLoadClassConfig()`, `bCalcConfigCRC()`, and `bLoadBindingConfig()` bodies (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:526-679`) and traced calls from library open, config-change dispatch and successful service binding (`:86-92,257,460-501`). Default and per-device chunks are copied only up to the current `ClsDevCfg`/`KeymapCfg` payload sizes; `btGetCfgChunk()` returns an owned copy and the caller frees each successful result (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/config.c:494-526`). `bCalcConfigCRC()` serializes the current config form, computes over its declared byte length in 16-bit units, and frees the temporary buffer. Both reload functions return FALSE even after doing the work, but the checked in-tree callers ignore those values and use the side effects, so this is not promoted as a functional failure. The configuration-change method's `Forbid()` list walk and binding release lifetime are already covered by OD3759; no separate config-copy, CRC, or cleanup issue was established. BTHID `bSendKeyString()` sentinel event caller pass (OD9668 added; 2026-10-25): traced both `HUA_VANILLA`/`HUA_KEYSTRING` action branches through `bSendKeyString()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:6374-6390,6678-6724`), both input.device command paths, key-repeat classification and timer rescheduling (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:346-366,460-480`; `support.c:123-151`), and Intuition raw-key delivery (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2560-2600`). The trailing raw-key code `0xff` is treated as repeatable and has no matching release, so it can repeat until another non-qualifier key event cancels the timer; vanilla mapping rejects it while raw-key subscribers receive it. BWFM SDPCM receive/transmit caller recheck (2026-10-25; no new OD): traced `bwfm_rx_read()` frame-size/checksum checks and per-frame transmit-window refresh into `BWFMRxFrame()` and the RX pump, then traced `BWFMTxData()` credit wait, protected sequence allocation, packet-size cap, and SDIO error return into `tx_request()`/`TermIO()`. Etherlink III AROS Open-wrapper allocation/rollback recheck (2026-10-25; no new OD): traced `AROSDevOpen()`'s `OpenerExtra` allocation and wrapper-hook publication through `DevOpen()` and `CloseUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/etherlink3/aros_device.c:155-191`; `device.c:226-327,538-572`). If `OpenerExtra` allocation fails, `DevOpen()` is skipped and the wrapper returns `IOERR_OPENFAIL`; if the inner `Opener` allocation fails after unit admission, `DevOpen()` routes through `CloseUnit()`, which decrements the open count and releases any published opener before the wrapper frees `OpenerExtra`. On success, the wrapper stores its allocation in `read_port.mp_Node.ln_Name`, and `AROSDevClose()` frees it before `DevClose()` tears down the inner opener. No independent leak or unmatched-free path was established in these checked branches. This is a targeted wrapper/rollback pass, not additional body-line credit; SMP unit/list races remain OD3115. No allocation failure or device operation was induced; source-only.

AROSTCP resolver snapshot/serial publication race pass (OD9691 added; 2026-10-25): re-read `res_update_db()` from source-lock acquisition through array copying, lock release and serial publication (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/api/res_init.c:67-85,103-139,147-200`). OD9691 caller-serialization premise recheck (retained; 2026-10-25): verified the public selected `gethostbyname()` vector directly calls `__gethostbyname()` and its `res_search()` path without `ObtainSyscallSemaphore()` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/api/gethostnamadr.c:386-390,488-489,646-652`; no syscall-semaphore calls occur in this translation unit). The resolver state is per `SocketBase` (`api/resolv.h:36-41`) and the API allocates each open base with an owning task (`amiga_api.h:104-153,222-236`), but NetDB mutation APIs act on shared `NDB`/`DynDB` state; therefore a query on one SocketBase can overlap a writer using another task's base. Roadshow dynamic server updates hold `DynDB.dyn_Lock` only through mutation and serial increment, while the resolver samples the serial after dropping that lock; static NetDB replacement similarly increments after releasing `ndb_Lock`. This confirms OD9691's cross-task writer/query premise without claiming concurrent use of one SocketBase. No resolver query or database update was run; no full-body credit. Source-only.


AROSTCP mbuf autosize and allocation-limit follow-up (2026-10-25; no new OD): traced both `mb_autosize()` callers through `iface_make()` and `sana_ioctl(SIOCSIFMTU)` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:320-403,614-667`) into `mbinit()`, `m_alloc()` and `m_clalloc()` (`kern/uipc_mbuf.c:312-370,429-475,530-592`). The autosizer's baseline floor can exceed its one-eighth-free-RAM estimate, but the source explicitly documents that minimum as policy; it changes only the future allocation cap. No new bug established in the autosize lead; no interface or allocation was run. Source-only.

Between them, queued key processing can recognize raw key 0x78 and traverse every reset-list entry, invoking `node->is_Code` through `AROS_INTC1` without checking it (`keyboard.c:497-512`; `compiler/include/exec/interrupts.h:117-126`). The documented `Forbid()` contract does not mask interrupts and is CPU-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-66`), so it does not close that interval. BTHID initializes `cdc_EnableRH` TRUE (`bthid.class.c:555`); the class target is optional and its parent aggregate edge is commented, so keep affected scope limited to builds that install/load `bthid.class` and enable reset-handler handling (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/mmakefile.src:5-12`; dynamic load via `btAddClass()`). USB HID shared action dispatcher and terminal-action body recheck (OD3936/OD4009/OD4062/OD4290/OD4295 retained; no new OD; 2026-10-25): read `nInstallLastActionHero()`, `nDispatcherTask()`, and `nLastActionHero()` in full (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6954-7241`) and reconciled them with both `nDoAction()` message producers, configuration reload, interface release, and class `libClose()`. RTL816x post-reply unit-pointer caller recheck (OD3131 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `BeginIO()` through both dispatch modes into `handle_request()` and the deferred worker (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl816x/rtl816x_init.c:376-402`; `unit.c:716-731`; `handler.c:106-198`). When `AttemptSemaphore()` fails, `BeginIO()` clears `IOF_QUICK` and queues the request; the worker dequeues it, acquires that request's unit semaphore and calls the handler. For completed non-quick requests, the handler calls `ReplyMsg()` and then evaluates `request->ios2_Req.io_Unit` again to release the semaphore. Exec enqueues/signals the reply before returning from `ReplyMsg()` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:45-65`); `Signal()` can preempt to a waiting higher-priority reply consumer on one CPU and can schedule on another CPU under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/signal.c:372-414`). A consumer that reuses or frees the request therefore races this post-reply dereference. This confirms the RTL816x portion of OD3131; the quick inline path is not the basis for the deferred-worker trigger. No new finding and no runtime interleaving; source-only.

Bluetooth Preferences MUI ASL requester and IFF import caller pass (OD9693 added; 2026-10-25): traced the `MUIM_BtA_CfgImport` dispatch through `DoCfgImport()`, requester allocation/use/free, DOS `Read()`, and the selected FAT `ACTION_READ`/`OpRead()`/`ReadFileChunk()` path (`rom/bluetooth/prefs/ActionClass.c:965-1020,1654`; `rom/dos/read.c:59-73`; `rom/filesys/fat/packet.c:251-269`; `rom/filesys/fat/ops.c:779-798`; `rom/filesys/fat/file.c:225-237`). The optional program's IFF importer accepts declared FORM lengths below four, allocates `len+8`, copies 12 bytes, then passes unsigned `len-4` to signed `Read()`. For a file of at least 13 bytes and declared length 0–3, FAT receives the wrapped unsigned count; `want + lock->pos` can wrap below the file size, bypassing its EOF clamp before copying beyond the allocation. Added OD9693, scoped to the explicitly buildable optional Bluetooth Preferences target and FAT-backed input. The requester wrapper itself correctly handles allocation failure and frees the requester after use; this pass does not close other ASL callers or full ActionClass coverage. No file, requester, or filesystem operation was run; source-only.

Atheros5000 AR9285 attach status selected-caller qualification (OD3874; 2026-10-25): traced the sole checked-in `ath_hal_attach()` caller, `CreateUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/unit.c:128,161-164`). Bootkeyboard NULL Restore Defaults receiver discriminator (no new OD; 2026-10-25): traced the unassigned `nh_RestoreDefMI` field at the GUI notification setup (`bootkeyboard.h:52`; `bootkeyboard.class.c:1109-1115`) through both public `DoMethod()` forms. PC i8042 mouse pre-reset IRQ/parser-bound discriminator (no new OD; 2026-10-25): traced the selected keyboard-before-mouse HIDD registration order (`i8042_classinit.c:21-63`) through keyboard initialization and the mouse class constructor (`i8042_kbdclass.c:205-248`; `i8042_mouseclass.c:64-86`). Poseidon hardware-task submission/completion and shutdown recheck (OD902 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-25): traced both ordinary task-port dispatch and the optional callback dispatch (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9072-9111,9275-9326`). Ordinary requests are assigned `iouh_UserData`, submitted with `SendIO()`, then counted; HCD replies are mapped back through that pointer, replied to the original pipe message, then decremented. The abort control message instead calls `AbortIO()` on the original request and immediately replies to the synthetic abort message; it is not counted as a transfer. Shutdown sends `CMD_FLUSH`, drains device completions while polling the count, and after 30 seconds forcibly clears the count and proceeds to remove the hardware record and `CloseDevice()` with no further drain. Exec `ReplyMsg()` enqueues/signals the requester before returning (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`), so request consumers may reuse storage once reply delivery occurs; the task does not dereference the request after the reply in these shown completion branches. The forced-timeout risk for selected xHCI is already covered by OD902, which traces the direct shutdown caller and the HCD's skipped active-transfer queue; this reread does not establish an independent generic Poseidon defect. Callback-mode QuickIO is selected only when the queried HCD advertises `UHCF_QUICKIO`; no in-tree default enable was established in the previous configuration pass. No request, flush, controller or schedule was run. No whole-file credit: this is a focused recheck of an already partially represented 9,797-line library body; remaining Poseidon callers and source remain open. Source-only.

A requester left in `EasyRequestArgs()` can therefore resume into module-resident code after class removal. Console `CMD_WRITE` concurrency trigger qualification (OD4003 retained; 2026-10-25): re-read `console.device` `Open()` and `BeginIO()` alongside the two checked-in console demos. Each non-library `Open()` constructs a fresh console object (`rom/devs/console/console.c:179-223`), so independent opens do not share `pendingCSI`. The demos create separate read and write request blocks but copy the opened request's `io_Device` and `io_Unit` fields into the second block (`developer/demos/cons.c:450-459`; `cons_charmap.c:450-459`), confirming the same opened unit can be addressed through distinct requests. Neither demo establishes writes from different tasks. OD4003 is therefore scoped to a direct client that shares one opened `io_Unit` across tasks on ExecSMP and overlaps writes while a CSI is pending; this remains a source-inferred API-level concurrency candidate, not an in-tree reproduced schedule. No source lines were newly credited; no console request was issued.

Console `CMD_WRITE` direct-dispatch recheck (OD4003 retained; no new finding; 2026-10-25): verified the device vector rather than assuming writes use its command task. Exec `DoIO()` and `SendIO()` call the device's `BeginIO` vector directly (`rom/exec/doio.c:55-65`; `sendio.c:47-53`); console `BeginIO(CMD_WRITE)` calls `writeToConsole()` inline and leaves `done_quick` TRUE (`rom/devs/console/console.c:305-334,403-418`). The command-port enqueue is only in the `!done_quick` branch, which handles `CMD_READ`, so it does not serialize writes. The selected shared-unit CSI state and lack of a per-unit write lock therefore support OD4003's ExecSMP overlap; the trigger remains conditional on a direct client submitting overlapping requests with the same `io_Unit`, which the checked-in demos do not demonstrate. The `consoleTaskLock`, `copyBufferLock`, and `unitListLock` are initialized but not acquired on this write path. No new finding or body-line credit; no request or concurrent write was run. Source-only.

InstallAROS partition-name allocation and ownership pass (OD9716-OD9717 added; 2026-10-25): traced `CheckPartition()`'s name allocation and `GetPartitionAttrsTags(PT_NAME, ...)` through generic partition attribute fallback and all selected MBR/EBR/RDB/GPT getters (`workbench/tools/InstallAROS/ia_diskio.c:164-206`; `rom/partition/getpartitionattrs.c:97-105,169-179`; backend getter bodies). No translation-unit body credit.

USB HID/Bluetooth HID requester-format wrapper correction (OD9718; 2026-10-25): corrected the prior “no format-argument defect” conclusions for both `nEasyRequest()` and `bEasyRequest()`. Their `AROS_SLOWSTACKFORMAT_PRE(gadgets)` calls use the gadget labels as the format parsed to build `_data`, although the subsequent `EasyStruct` formats `body` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:7463-7484`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:6728-6750`). On the slow-stack macro branch, `PRE(format)` uses its argument for both `va_start(last)` and `GetDataStreamFromFormat(format,...)`; the correct bridge is `PRE_USING(gadgets, body)` (`compiler/include/clib/alib_protos.h:253-274`). Direct callers pass plain gadget labels but bodies with `%s`/`%ld` substitutions. `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` forwards the empty/wrong stream to `RawDoFmt()` for the body (`rom/intuition/buildeasyrequestargs.c:155-158,356-370`; `rom/exec/rawdofmt.c:83-108,276-283,300-304`). Added OD9718 for optional USB HID and Bluetooth HID targets on `AROS_SLOWSTACKFORMAT` architectures. Confidence is high for the wrong stream construction; requester behavior was not exercised. No C-body credit changed; this is a corrected helper/caller review. Source-only.

USB HID last-action dispatcher tail recheck (OD9719 added; 2026-10-25): read `nLastActionHero()`, `nLoadItem()`'s saved `VANS` restoration, `nAllocAction()`, and Poseidon's `psdGetStringChunk()` allocation/copy path (`hid.class.c:4468-4485,6615-6668,7088-7160`; `poseidon.library.c:315-378,8279-8294`). The config helper allocates `len + 1` but copies only `len` bytes; the action allocator is not clearing; and `strncpy(..., 79)` can leave the 80-byte vanilla field unterminated for a chunk of at least 79 bytes. `nLastActionHero()` subsequently applies `strcpy()` into a 128-byte local buffer and `strcat()`, establishing OD9719 as a saved-config robustness candidate. Reviewed the neighboring sound load/play/free and key-string conversion/send functions in the same tail; their selected paths did not establish an additional finding in this slice. This is a targeted tail/caller slice, not full-body credit for `hid.class.c`. No config, device, or key event was used. Source-only.

USB HID lazy dispatcher startup and shutdown pass (OD9720 added; 2026-10-25): traced `nDoAction()`'s two lazy-start call paths from per-interface HID worker contexts into `nInstallLastActionHero()`, then followed task creation, ready-signal publication, shared port/request fields and `libClose()` shutdown (`hid.class.c:710-740,1078-1090,5558-5574,6160-6178,6954-7088,7100-7440,80-100`). Startup has no shared reservation around the NULL check and publication, and each dispatcher publishes into singleton fields before entering its loop. If two callers pass the initial NULL-port check and both children start before either task pointer is published, the shared ready-task field means only the most recently recorded starter is guaranteed to receive the startup signal; the other can remain in `Wait()`. Both children can also publish singleton task/port fields, so the last-written handles are the only ones shutdown signals/joins. Added OD9720 for the conditional duplicate-worker, missed-ready-signal and shared-state race, including possible early expunge while a second worker remains. Caller/task overlap was source-inferred; no device or schedule was run. This recheck credits only the named function/caller slice, not the full `hid.class.c` body. Source-only.

SD-card selected Init/Scan/Open multi-backend lifecycle recheck (2026-10-25; existing OD3302/OD3304/OD3305/OD3315/OD3318/OD3319 retained; no new OD): reread the complete `sdcard_init.c` functions and reconciled task startup/counting and unit selection with both selected BCM backends. The generic Scan path still has the recorded allocation/task-start result gaps and task-name leak; `CommonInit`'s later backend-init failure still lacks pool rollback; Open still keeps success when `StartUnit()` fails (OD3304). Considered whether the missing lower-bound check in `Open()` can select a later bus for an earlier global unit number, and whether `sdcard_PendingBusTasks` can lose concurrent updates. The target manifests select SDHOST only on 32-bit Pi builds and both backend files on AArch64, but each runtime peripheral-base/card-presence branch registers at most one bus: SDHOST returns without registration on BCM2711/2712, while SDHCI returns without registration for earlier SoCs and chooses exactly one SDHCI window otherwise (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdcard/mmakefile.src:18-34`; `sdcard_sdhost_init.c:139-151`; `sdcard_bcm2708init.c:102-145`). Thus the multi-bus lower-bound/multiple-writer concerns have no current selected trigger and are not promoted. The single task counter is incremented before task creation and decremented either by the worker or synchronously on failed creation; no second writer overlaps that lifecycle in the selected one-bus configuration. Existing SD-card entries already credit the local bodies; this pass adds caller/selection qualification only. No card, boot, or task-start failure was induced; source-only.

AHI SSE4.1 mixer intrinsic/dispatch pass (OD9722 added; 2026-10-25): re-read `addroutines_sse.c`, its object inclusion, and `header.c`'s function-pointer installation. The source activates `MulShift16()` under `__SSE4_1__`, includes only `<smmintrin.h>`, and calls `_mm_srai_epi64()` (`addroutines_sse.c:23-27,51-58`). GCC's `smmintrin.h` does not expose that intrinsic; the GCC 14 declaration is in `avx512vlintrin.h`, while GCC documents `-mavx512vl` as enabling the AVX512VL feature (`/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/14/include/{smmintrin.h,avx512vlintrin.h}`; [GCC x86 options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/x86-Options.html)). Therefore an SSE4.1-only GCC build cannot compile this active body. `header.c` selects the pointer when `GCIT_SupportsSSE41` is true and does not check AVX512VL (`:896-912`); if a custom build makes the intrinsic available with AVX512VL, it also needs matching runtime dispatch. The standard AROS x86 configuration uses `-march=i486`, leaving this body disabled (`configure.in:1381-1382`). Added OD9722; this is limited to custom builds enabling the optional path. No build, audio mix or CPU dispatch was run; source-only.
AHI AVX2 arithmetic-shift ISA reconciliation (OD9722 expanded; 2026-10-25): checked the sibling AVX2 backend after identifying the SSE4.1 path's AVX512VL intrinsic. `addroutines_avx.c` uses `_mm256_srai_epi64()` under `__AVX2__`, and the selected dispatcher installs it after checking the AVX processor tag and CPUID leaf 7 AVX2 bit only (`addroutines_avx.c:23-27,51-58`; `header.c:104-116,915-920`). GCC's `immintrin.h` includes `avx512vlintrin.h`, where this intrinsic is declared under the AVX512VL target pragma (`/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/14/include/{immintrin.h,avx512vlintrin.h}:31-34,63,11886-11894`). This confirms the AVX2 source has a compile-target/dispatch mismatch as well as the SSE4.1 mismatch; exact compiler diagnostics and generated instruction sequence remain unverified because no build was run. Expanded OD9722 to cover both accelerated paths. Standard target flags leave both implementations disabled. Source-only.

USB HID duplicate-dispatcher shutdown consequence recheck (OD9720 strengthened and expunge claim qualified; 2026-10-25): traced the losing nInstallLastActionHero() caller through its Wait(1L << nh_ReadySignal) at hid.class.c:6954-6980, then through usbReleaseInterfaceBinding() at :283-304. The release path signals nch_Task with SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C and waits until nch_Task is NULL; the startup waiter is not waiting on that stop bit, so a lost ready signal leaves the interface task blocked and release waiting indefinitely. Narrowed the earlier module-expunge statement: libClose() joins only the currently published task, but whether expunge can proceed before another duplicate exits depends on class/module teardown ordering not established here. No hardware, action, schedule, or unload was run; source-only.

AR5312 interrupt-pending helper and StatusInt caller pass (2026-10-25; no new OD): read all 47 lines (13 `cloc 2.06` C lines) of `ar5312_interrupts.c`, then traced its method registration in `ar5312_attach()` and direct `StatusInt()` caller (`unit.c:1466-1493`). Atheros5000 RX reassembly slot lifetime recheck (OD3274/OD3296 retained; 2026-10-25): searched every `rx_fragment_nos` access and traced `RXInt()` registration and dispatch. The array is initialized to -1 only during unit construction, released when a frame without `MOREFRAGS` arrives, and opportunistically cleared only during `GetRXBuffer()`'s retry scan (`unit.c:221,367-370,1621-1625,1669-1671,1737-1766`). No age-based expiry or independent reaper exists. This confirms the documented OD3274 trigger can arise from incomplete fragments retaining the ten slots, and OD3296's same-source fragment matching can also occupy/reuse slots without sequence identity. Rechecked the retry loop against its caller: at retry index 10, `GetRXBuffer()` has advanced `buffer` one full ten-frame allocation and returns `buffer_no == 10`; `RXInt()` writes the assembled header/data through that pointer and later clears `rx_fragment_nos[10]` (`unit.c:1572-1607,1669-1671`). No separate finding beyond OD3274/OD3296. No frame or device was used; source-only.
Atheros5000 S2_SETKEY removal cross-file pass (OD9730 added; 2026-10-25): traced WirelessManager's `WPA_ALG_NONE` mapping and `wpa_clear_keys()` callers through `CmdSetKey()` to `SetKey()` and the HAL key-cache methods. Confirmed the NONE case only changes `unit->keys[index].type`; it does not reset or replace an installed hardware entry. Hardware TKIP/CCMP installs happen directly in `SetKey()`, WEP install happens in `ConfigureAdapter()`, and the only explicit cache reset in the selected unit path is during `InitialiseAdapter()`. Added OD9730 for a key-clear request that completes while hardware cache state remains. This cross-file caller pass adds no full-body path credit; further Atheros HAL and crypto callers remain partial. No request, frame, or device was used; source-only.
Atheros5000 HAL key-clear validity confirmation (OD9730 strengthened; 2026-10-25): checked all selected HAL implementations bound to `ah_setKeyCacheEntry`/`ah_resetKeyCacheEntry`. AR5211/AR5212 set the cache MAC valid bit after writing a key; AR5416 delegates key installation and reset to AR5212. The reset methods clear the key words and MAC-valid register, while the only direct reset call in the selected Atheros5000 unit source is `InitialiseAdapter()` (`unit.c:572`). `S2ENC_NONE` reaches none of these HAL operations. This confirms the finding's hardware-cache state claim for successfully installed keys; actual subsequent packet handling remains unobserved. PL2303 device-vector full-body flag-normalization hypothesis check (2026-10-25; no new OD): re-read all 489 physical lines of `rom/usb/classes/serialpl2303/dev.c` against its class worker's `nSetSerialMode()` and public `IOExtSer` flag definitions. The open path's `io_SerFlags &= ~SERF_PARTY_ON | SERF_PARTY_ODD` clears only `SERF_PARTY_ON` and preserves any existing `SERF_PARTY_ODD`; it does not set the odd bit, because `~SERF_PARTY_ON` already contains that bit. PCI ATA AddBus caller reconciliation for OD9739 (2026-10-25): traced the second direct Storage `AddBus()` caller, `ata_bus_Detect()`, against `PCIATABus__Root__New/Dispose` and the shared ATA `SetUpBus` path. After successful PCI interrupt registration, Root New sets the marker and transfers the record to the bus object; if the later mandatory PIO interface allocation fails, generic AddBus disposes the object, whose destructor unreferences the PCI device and frees the probe record, then `ata_bus_Detect()` reads `ln_Succ` and may release both again. Constructor-time interrupt-registration failure is a distinct path: PCI Root New invokes the superclass Dispose and returns NULL before setting the marker, so the probe's cleanup is still valid there. Expanded OD9739 to cover selected PC PCI ATA and optional Gayle/FastATA variants, distinguishing the constructor-failure cleanup from post-construction setup failure. No device or allocation failure was run; source-only.

ATA eject and ATAPI autosense caller pass (2026-10-25; no new OD): reread `ata_Eject()`, `atapi_Eject()`, `atapi_RequestSense()` and `atapi_DirectSCSI()` (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1112-1177,2298-2310,2474-2534`). ATA eject routes through the normal no-data command executor; ATAPI eject uses a zero-data SCSI packet, so its READ direction flag does not select a data transfer. `atapi_DirectSCSI()` zeroes output counts/status before validation and captures packet actual bytes; autosense is issued only after CHECK CONDITION and only with a non-NULL positive-length sense buffer. The helper caps REQUEST SENSE allocation length at 255 and reports the transport's actual count; the outer path propagates that count. No separate bounds, stale-result, or ownership defect was established. This pass does not close ATA device-change/eject callers, packet transport semantics, or the remaining low-level request paths. No command or device was used; source-only.

Broadcom4400 unit-body note (OD9755): traced the interrupt's `StatusInt()` to `RXInt()`, verified DMA buffers are returned eight-byte aligned by `AllocDMAMemHook()`, and followed `RXInt()`'s 30-byte RX-header skip into `AddressFilter()` and the broadcast test in `CopyFrame()`. The first four Ethernet destination bytes are loaded through `ULONG *` at base+30, which is 2 modulo 4 on PPC. This is the selected PPC cards-driver configuration; on x86 unaligned access is supported, and the report does not claim a PPC runtime fault. The direct cross-target DMA/cache sequence, full PCI setup callers, request dispatch, remaining six C bodies and local headers remain open. No device, frame, build or runtime operation was used; source-only.

A recognized packet after failed reconstruction follows the retained mode into `nParseWacom()` and dereferences the cached collection at its item-list walk (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:909-912,1031-1046,1435-1458,1801-1812,1878-1892`). FLAC bitreader callback-contract recheck (OD1977 withdrawn; 2026-10-25): revisited the earlier short-read/partial-tail cursor candidate in `bitreader_read_from_client_()`, unary reads and both active Rice block-reader branches, then traced the installed wrapper through `read_callback_()` and the public `FLAC__StreamDecoderReadCallback` contract (`bitreader.c:177-236,697-777,807-1173`; `stream_decoder.c:2790-2865`; `stream_decoder.h:467-516`). The wrapper preserves `consumed_words`/`consumed_bits` before refill; a callback may supply a short positive read, after which the bitreader recomputes available input and continues from the retained cursor. The only apparent no-progress case is zero bytes with CONTINUE, but the documented callback contract requires END_OF_STREAM iff zero bytes were read and no data remains; `read_callback_()` also consults `eof_callback` and returns false when it reports EOF. No conforming callback path establishes the claimed cursor error, so removed the stale OD1977 reference from the file row and withdraw the candidate. No report/index item existed under that ID. No stream or callback was run; no file/LOC credit changed.


FLAC decoder zero-progress callback pass (OD9770 added; 2026-10-25): traced the public `FLAC__StreamDecoderReadCallback` contract through the non-Ogg `read_callback_()` wrapper and bitreader refill/read loops (`stream_decoder.h:467-516`; `stream_decoder.c:2790-2865`; `bitreader.c:208-236,697-777,807-1173`). A client callback returning `CONTINUE` with zero bytes while the optional EOF callback is absent or false makes the wrapper return success; the bitreader receives no new bytes and immediately retries. The callback documentation reserves `END_OF_STREAM` for zero bytes when no more data remains, and does not spell out temporary nonblocking no-data semantics; report OD9770 is therefore limited to clients that use zero-byte `CONTINUE` for temporary unavailability, with medium API-reachability confidence. This is distinct from the withdrawn OD1977 cursor-corruption claim. The current stream-decoder row now names the active report candidates and marks the older IDs as historical/unmapped rather than current findings. No stream or callback was run; no source LOC credit changed. Source-only.


FLAC excessive-wasted-bits caller recheck (no separate finding; 2026-10-25): followed the subframe header and unary wasted-bit count through `bps -= u+1` into constant, verbatim, fixed and LPC sample readers (`stream_decoder.c:2453-2519`; `bitreader.c:435-455`). A count greater than the channel bit depth wraps the unsigned `bps`; it does not pass that value to a destination write. The checked reader asserts `bits <= 32` in assertion builds; without assertions, its bounded bit buffer fills and the refill eventually fails before the sample destination is assigned. The later output rescale is reached only after a successful subframe read. This malformed-header path therefore does not support the prior write-bound consequence, and it does not add a distinct finding beyond the existing signed-shift candidate for zero-width values. No frame was decoded. Source-only; no file/LOC credit.


FLAC partial metadata cleanup recheck (OD9771 restored; 2026-10-25): followed selected APPLICATION/unknown payload allocations in `read_metadata_()` and nested Vorbis Comment, CueSheet and Picture allocations through each helper return and the common cleanup (`stream_decoder.c:1494-1587,1714-1919`). Read/EOF/abort and later allocation failures return before the common cleanup; process methods propagate the failure; `finish()` frees decoder-owned state but cannot reach the stack-local partially constructed metadata block (`:667-722,1042-1120`). Non-STREAMINFO/SEEKTABLE types are parsed only when the public metadata filter enables the type; the default filter enables STREAMINFO only, while `set_metadata_respond*()` can select these types (`:760-814,1264-1278`). Revalidated the historical OD1979 candidate and restored it under current ID OD9771. No stream, callback failure, or allocation failure was exercised. No source/LOC credit changed; source-only.


FLAC output-buffer failure recovery pass (OD9772 restored; 2026-10-25): rechecked `allocate_output_()` against `read_frame_()`, `flush()`, `reset()` and the public retry contract (`stream_decoder.c:959-1010,1305-1353,2015-2020,2523-2543`; `stream_decoder.h:1371-1417`). AHIRecord FLAC finalization result handoff pass (OD9773 restored; 2026-10-25): re-read the saver’s FLAC close path and traced `FLAC__stream_encoder_finish()` through its selected write/seek/tell callbacks to `FinishFile()` and StopRecording (`AHIRecord.c:952-1001,1074-1086,1248-1255,3090-3099`; encoder finish implementation `FLAC/stream_encoder.c:1320-1385,2035-2108,2529-2633`). FLAC integer-only seek divisor recheck (OD9774 restored; 2026-10-25): traced the public seek API through metadata completion and `seek_to_absolute_sample_()` (`stream_decoder.c:1171-1234,2976-3111`; selected `FLAC__INTEGER_ONLY_LIBRARY` at `workbench/tools/AHIRecord/mmakefile.src:25`). With unknown total samples and target zero, initial sample bounds are both zero and the guard raises the upper bound to one. For a byte span at least `0xffffffff`, the integer-only formula shifts that one-sample difference right 16 bits and divides by zero. A custom length/seek callback exposes 64-bit offsets; ordinary AHIRecord recording does not use this API path. Revalidated the historical OD1980 candidate and restored it under current ID OD9774. No stream or seek was run; no source/LOC credit changed. Source-only.


FLAC application-ID filter growth pass (OD9775 restored; 2026-10-25): traced both public application-ID registration setters, initial allocation, capacity/count units, realloc helper arithmetic and subsequent ID copies (`stream_decoder.c:314-315,777-800,836-859`; `FLAC/share/alloc.h:192-199`). FLAC filename-init failure cleanup pass (OD9777 restored; 2026-10-25): followed `init_file_internal_()` `fopen("w+b")` through `init_FILE_internal_()` into `init_stream_internal_()` validation, then through failed-init `finish()`/`delete()` (`stream_encoder.c:598-610,637-700,~870,1188-1237,1270-1297,1320-1329`). PTP date parser / Utility CheckDate caller cross-reference (EK9501; no new OD; 2026-10-25): confirmed `rom/usb/classes/ptp/mmakefile.src:5-11` selects `ptp.class.c` in the `kernel-usb-classes-ptp` module. `nConvertPimaDate()` parses the remote `YYYYMMDDThhmmss` value into `ClockData`, calls `CheckDate()`, and stores the returned day count if nonzero (`ptp.class.c:1341-1423`). USB HID Report ID collection-clone caller recheck (OD3453 expanded; no new ID or body credit; 2026-10-26): re-read `nParseReport()`'s report-ID transition and collection-end paths (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2726-2761,2891-2908,3080-3097`) and traced their default-action consumer (`:3452-3461,3917-3918`). Poseidon's `MEMF_CLEAR` pool leaves the first clone's parent NULL; because the loop condition follows the replaced `nhc` pointer, the ancestor walk stops after cloning only the leaf. Closing that leaf loses the still-open outer collection; a later outer-collection Main item reaches `AddTail(&nhc->nhc_Items, ...)` with NULL, while nested Mouse/Tablet axes can also lose default mapping. This is the same root cause as Bluetooth HID OD3453, so the existing finding was expanded rather than duplicated. `nParseReport()` already has full-body credit; this caller-semantics refinement changes no represented-path/LOC totals. Both HID aggregates remain optional in the checked-in manifests; no device or report descriptor was used. Source-only.


USB HID main-GUI process-spawn branch recheck (OD3924 strengthened; no new finding or body credit; 2026-10-26): re-read `nOpenBindingCfgWindow()` and traced both `psdSpawnSubTask()` branches, including `CreateNewProcTags()` when DOS is available and the direct `AddTask()` fallback when it is not (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:641-660`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1456-1509`). Cleanup clears `nch_GUITask` (`hid.gui.c:1778-1784`), after which the parent can store the returned dead task; later open and release paths trust this field (`hid.class.c:273-306,649-660`). No process, task, GUI failure or release was run; source-only.

No allocation failure, module initialization or rollback was run; source-only.

AHIRecord FLAC bitwriter direct-buffer contract reconciliation (OD1973 historical alias consolidated into OD10990; OD2130/OD2131 retained; no new finding; 2026-10-26): re-read the complete private bitwriter declarations and all selected buffer get/release/init/free callers (`private/bitwriter.h:39-102`; `bitwriter.c:161-202,232-300`; `stream_encoder.c:986-991,2250-2260,2394-2434`; `stream_encoder_framing.c:214-224`). `write_bitbuffer_()` acquires the writer-owned buffer only after checking byte alignment, keeps the view stable through optional verification and the client write callback, then releases it before clearing the writer. ROM USB HID action-variable and feature-array branch recheck (OD3549/OD3552 retained; no new finding; 2026-10-26): re-read the complete HUA_FEATURE and HUA_VARIABLES portions of `nDoAction()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6105-6280`) against the packed `NepHidAction` layout and the GUI operation/value tables (`hid.h:130-148`; `hid.gui.c:90-112,3310-3345`). Broadcom4400 OD9755 alignment-offset recheck (2026-10-26; retained, no new finding): re-read `AllocDMAMemHook()`, the RX frame-offset calculation, `AddressFilter()`, and `CopyFrame()` (`pci.c:669-684`; `unit.c:1203-1206,1342,1423`; `broadcom4400.h:34`; `ethernet.h:36`). The allocator rounds the DMA buffer to an 8-byte boundary; adding the 30-byte hardware header yields a destination address at offset 6 mod 8, hence 2 mod 4. Both checked call paths dereference that address as `ULONG *`; `CopyFrame()` also performs the paired `UWORD *` read at offset +4, which is aligned. The misaligned 32-bit access is therefore source-established for every accepted RX frame in this driver; whether the selected PPC compiler/CPU faults or handles it remains target-dependent as stated in OD9755. No selected alignment-fix helper or bytewise access was found in these routines. OD9755 remains; this recheck adds no independent report item or LOC credit. No packet, build or hardware operation was performed; source-only.

Broadcom4400 OD9757 reply-signal scheduling recheck (2026-10-26; retained, no new finding): traced the final request reply through Exec `ReplyMsg()` and `InternalPutMsg()` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:47-65`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-108`) and re-read the Broadcom4400 unit-task priority and release order (`unit.c:42,329-330`; `request.c:242-248`). `ReplyMsg()` calls `InternalPutMsg()` before returning; for a signal reply port, `InternalPutMsg()` calls `Signal()`, whose public contract says a waiting higher-priority task begins immediately when task switches are allowed (`rom/exec/signal.c:127-131`). The unit task subsequently reads `request->ios2_Req.io_Unit` to release `access_lock`. This confirms a scheduling point can occur after the caller regains request ownership and before that field read; it does not prove every reply client or target priority triggers it. OD9757 retains its conditional trigger and high confidence in the ownership/order defect. No request, signal or scheduler was run; source-only; no body-line credit.
VC4 Gallium shared display-DMA concurrency pass (OD9785 candidate added; 2026-10-26): traced `display_blit` through the HIDD's V3D wait and direct DMA path, and the resource caller's per-layer locking. The HIDD has one shared channel/control block/busy flag; the busy check/wait/update and control-block/register programming have no DMA lock. V3D `render_lock` is released before the kick, and different destination layers have distinct layer locks. This supports the in-tree concurrency trigger; simultaneous runtime scheduling remains unverified. No concurrency, DMA, build, or hardware test was run; source-only. Mesa 26 glapi pthread-key initialization failure pass (OD9786 added; 2026-10-26): traced the selected default Mesa 26.0.0 AROS patch's one-time key creation and context/dispatch accessors (`mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff:717-805`; `mesa.cfg:19-35`) into AROS pthread key allocation and access (`compiler/pthread/pthread.h:189,199`; `pthread_key_create.c:26-58`; `pthread_setspecific.c:26-53`; `pthread_getspecific.c:26-41`). USB HID built-in keyboard key-map sentinel review (2026-10-26; no new finding): traced `usbkeymap` initialization and config copy (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:668-702,504-508`) through the page-0x07 default-action constructor (`:3707-4346`), report-item dispatch (`:4833-5132`), `HUA_KEYMAP` lookup (`:5584-5595`) and raw-key event forwarding. Unmapped entries use `0xff`, which includes the raw-key key-up bit; a down report for such a usage therefore forwards an event whose low seven-bit code is `0x7f` with the up bit set. The inspected paths do not establish a supported key at code `0x7f` or a user-visible state change from this event, so this is not promoted as a bug. Existing keymap configuration and HID report/action caller coverage remain partial; this is a targeted non-finding only. No input report or event was run; source-only.

USB HID OD9787 Store Config persistence recheck (2026-10-26; retained; no new ID or body credit): reread `nCheckForDefaultAction()` and `nSaveItem()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:4426-4455,6677-6743`) with the Control GUI's Clear/Store path (`hid.gui.c:2399-2462`) and `nLoadActionConfig()` reconstruction (`hid.class.c:2452-2532`). Store removes the previous report-form chunks before rebuilding; `nSaveItem()` returns NULL for an empty list and for all-default remaining actions, so no per-item override is written. Reload then calls `nDetectDefaultAction()` when the item form is absent and recreates the removed default suffix/list. This confirms the existing deleted-default-action persistence defect and its Save/Reload consequence. No config was changed or saved; source-only.

USB HID default-action bytewise-comparison recheck (2026-10-26; no finding): inspected `NepHidAction` layout (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.h:85-137`), `nAllocAction()` and the full `nCheckForDefaultAction()` comparison (`hid.class.c:4426-4483`), plus loaded and copied-action initialization. `psdAllocVec()` allocates from Poseidon's `MEMF_CLEAR` pool (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:124-125,315-373`); action config copies only the serialized prefix into this cleared object, and GUI Copy duplicates a fully initialized action. The comparison starts at `nha_Type`, deliberately copies `nha_IsDefault` into the generated counterpart before `memcmp()`, and therefore excludes list-node links while its compared payload/padding is zero-initialized or copied from a fully initialized action. No independent nondeterministic-padding or stale-pointer mismatch was established. OD9787's separate prefix-length omission remains confirmed. No config or GUI action was run; source-only.

USB HID analog joystick wide-range arithmetic pass (OD9792 added; 2026-10-26): traced HID variable-item parsing and report-value extraction (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2800-2825,2887-2912,4561-4575,4880-4948`) into `nDoAction()`'s `HUA_ANALOGJOY` normalization and LowLevel field packing (`:6045-6062`), then verified that `nDetectDefaultAction()` creates analog X/Y actions for gamepad items (`:4024-4038,4142-4154`). For an accepted 0..0x7fffffff logical range, multiplying a sample by 256 in signed `LONG` overflows above 0x7fffff; the intermediate is also too narrow to preserve normalized precision over most of the range. Added OD9792 as a separate USB HID issue from OD3935 (Bluetooth HID) and OD4400 (zero-range divide-by-zero). This was a targeted path review and adds no full-file/LOC credit. No descriptor, report, or device was exercised; source-only.

USB/Bluetooth HID tablet wide-range normalization pass (OD9793 added; 2026-10-26): compared the matching USB and Bluetooth default tablet-action mappings, variable-item bound representation, HUA_TABLET pressure/tilt calculations, and TABLETA tag publication (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2800-2825,2887-2912,4347-4372,5810-5838,6480-6490`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2150-2185,2228-2250,3674-3703,5136-5166,5750-5758`). Both implementations divide the scale constant by `nhi_RealMax` first; accepted positive maxima above the pressure or tilt constant yield an integer factor of zero and suppress all corresponding sample variation. Added one shared finding for the mirrored bug. Targeted path review only; no full-file/LOC credit. No tablet, descriptor, or report was used; source-only.

USB/Bluetooth HID absolute-coordinate wide-range pass (OD9794 added; 2026-10-26): traced built-in absolute mouse X/Y defaults, range parsing, clipping/stretch math, axis range storage and tablet-event publication in both HID class implementations (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2800-2825,2887-2912,3922-3950,5167-5200,5611-5626`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2145-2174,2228-2250,3244-3277,4494-4526,4935-4955`). USB/Bluetooth HID relative-delta narrowing pass (OD9795 added; 2026-10-26): traced default relative Mouse X/Y action selection, report item acceptance/dispatch, ULONG delta accumulation, flush to `InputEvent`, and the actual signed WORD coordinate declarations (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2800-2825,2887-2912,3922-3944,4880-4948,5601-5608,6432-6448`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2145-2174,2228-2250,3249-3270,4224-4277,4928-4935,5697-5713`; `compiler/include/devices/inputevent.h:22-37`). PCI xHCI RTIso start-context failure and caller pass (OD9796 added; 2026-10-26): traced the selected command dispatch, RTIso prefill, per-PTD start helper and transfer-context allocation (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_dev.c:258-272`; `uhwcmd.c:1606-1649`; `xhci_isoch.c:284-329`; `xhci_schedule.c:217-255`). `xhciInitIOTRBTransfer()` can return FALSE after endpoint acquisition or `AllocMem()` failure; `xhciStartIsochIO()` is void and returns without queueing that PTD, while `cmdStartRTIso()` ignores the result and returns `RC_OK`. With persistent failure on the initial start-helper attempt(s), no IOReq reaches `hc_IsoXFerQueue`; Poseidon's wrapper consequently reports success and increments its busy count. Traced the retry sources: the event task schedules ISO work only if the queue is nonempty (`xhci_hw.c:533-542`), and the PTD refill path otherwise runs after a completed transfer (`xhci_hcd.c:2791-2810`), so no queued initial transfer means no completion-driven retry. The selected SonixcamTool caller checks the start result then waits on the image-completion signal (`rom/usb/shellapps/SonixcamTool.c:1223-1243`); it cannot observe this masked setup failure. The xHCI module's local `make.opts` enables `PCIUSB_WIP_ISO` (the build config expects options in the same directory: `config/make.defaults.in:6-7`), and RISC-V OpenSBI selects `USBHardware/pcixhci` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:103-107`). Added OD9796, distinct from OD3174's USB Audio caller discarding an error the HCD returned. The involved translation units already had full-body credit; no LOC increment. No allocation failure, transfer or device was run; source-only.
Optional PowerPC FEC Ethernet source inventory and PHY-startup pass (OD9745/OD9798; 2026-10-26): reconciled `workbench/devs/networks/fec/mmakefile.src`'s four selected C files and `fec.conf` with `fec_handler.c`'s earlier request-queue review, then read the remaining `fec_init.c` (294 lines), `fec_unit.c` (455), `fec_hardware.c` (260), private `fec.h` (555), config and manifest. `cloc 2.06` reports 1,685 C/header code lines across the four C bodies and header. Speed/duplex similarly derive 100/full from all-bits-set timeout values, while `FEC_Start()` still sets `IFF_UP`. Added OD9798 for this false link state; exact bus behavior remains SoC/PHY-dependent. The target is optional; the Efika parent dependency is commented and this is not claimed for default images. Per-file status: `fec_handler.c` complete-body read in prior OD9745 note; `fec_hardware.c`, `fec_init.c`, `fec_unit.c` and `fec.h` now full-body read; `fec.conf` and `mmakefile.src` read. Inventory is 7 paths / 1,685 C/header code lines. This is not a runtime or hardware pass; no device, MDIO operation, or network request was used. Source-only.

OpenSBI DesignWare UART selected-caller and interrupt-path recheck (OD2110/OD839 retained; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced the boot-selected `dwuart` module (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:109-119`) through FDT port discovery, `NewUnit`, register programming, PLIC handler registration, RX interrupt dispatch and the generic serial.device callbacks. The target kernel source explicitly keeps only the boot hart running AROS until SMP bring-up (`kernel_startup.c:41-43,768-774`); generic `CMD_SETPARAMS` and `CMD_WRITE` mask local interrupts around HIDD register/state updates (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:453-494,713-811`), so a cross-hart race is not selected on this target. Reconfirmed OD839's zero-length numeric `CMD_WRITE`: serial.device forwards length zero, and DWSerUnit's do/while enters when THRE is set and reads `Outbuffer[0]` before decrementing (`serial_init.c:449-494`; `SerialUnitClass.c:287-314`). The receive ISR's 513-byte local buffer is filled by a drain-until-empty loop (`:512-539`); no fixed per-interrupt byte bound is enforced in source, but selected firmware FIFO depth and sustained arrival-versus-drain behavior are not established, so no standalone overflow finding is promoted. OD2110's generic serial read-handoff issue remains applicable to this backend when two reads are queued and a callback ends exactly at the first request boundary. No UART, serial request, interrupt, or board firmware was exercised; source-only.

RISC-V DesignWare UART serial.device error-path reconciliation (OD58/OD839/OD1887 rechecked; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced the selected `CMD_WRITE` and `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` dispatch and common cleanup in `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:449-535,713-818,861-864` against `dwuart`'s write, baud and framing methods (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:287-314,327-415,666-707`). This confirms OD58: its allocation/baud/framing error returns bypass both `Enable()` and the common `ReleaseSemaphore`, and skip non-quick completion; selected `serialtest` and Port-handler calls provide non-quick `DoIO` callers. OD839's numeric zero-length write remains the distinct HIDD do/while over-read. OD1887 remains the bounded-TEMT-poll/DLAB issue. OpenSBI's one-active-hart source state and the generic serial.device `Disable()` around these HIDD calls exclude a cross-hart SetParameters race in this target. Hardware-dependent receive-drain overflow was considered but not promoted: source lacks a per-interrupt bound, while the selected firmware FIFO and sustained input-rate relation are unknown. No serial request or UART was used; source-only.

Serial read offset full-width boundary recheck (OD9797 added; 2026-10-26; no LOC credit): re-read the complete `workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c` and traced pending numeric `CMD_READ` requests from `serial_init.c:361-444` through all receive callback backends tracked under OD2110. `IOStdReq.io_Actual`/`io_Length` are `ULONG` (`compiler/include/exec/io.h:29-39`), but `RBF_InterruptHandler()` copies `io_Actual` to a `UWORD indexDestBuf`, increments that narrowed offset per byte, and compares it against the full-width length (`serial_interrupthandlers.c:48-66`). At 65,536 bytes the offset wraps before the completion condition succeeds; later callbacks restart at buffer offset zero and the active request is not replied. Added OD9797 with the public numeric-read trigger and shared-backend scope, and added its master-index link. No request or serial input was used; source-only. The earlier 2026-10-13 full-body note saying no additional issue was established predates this exact large-length boundary review.

Legacy USB HID class initializer full-body and discovery-caller pass (2026-10-26; no new finding): read the complete 103-line `workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid_init.c` (62 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), tracing OOP attribute-base acquisition/rollback, pool creation, temporary USB-root lookup, class registration and generated expunge cleanup. USB HID discovery timing qualification (2026-10-26): refined the prior initializer note's startup order. `USB_Init()` waits for the main process's startup reply only when its initial `OpenLibrary("dos.library")` succeeds (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usb_init.c:124-169`); that process calls `UpdatePaths()` before replying (`usbprocess.c:196-218,234-241`). If DOS is not yet available, `USB_ProcessStarter()` retries opening it and only then starts the main process (`usb_init.c:51-98`), whose later directory scan still adds the `.hidd` class modules before USB enumeration begins. Thus discovery is guaranteed before the USB worker begins enumeration, but not necessarily before `USB_Init()` returns on early boot. This timing distinction does not create a separate HID-class registration finding.

Poseidon PoPo action-dispatch and standard hub-worker check (no new OD; 2026-10-26): traced `MUIM_PoPo_DisablePort`/`PowerCyclePort` notification creation through `MUIM_Application_PushMethod`, PoPo's dispatcher, and standard hub `UCM_HubDisablePort`/`PowerCyclePort` (`rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c:652-671,950-963,1515-1542`; `rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:282-319,430-510`). MUI drains pushed methods on the PoPo task before its subsequent timer/event cleanup, so the queued gadget pointer does not become stale through those same-task paths. The dispatcher disables the clicked controls before issuing the hub action and ignores the method's Boolean result; on a concurrent hub teardown it can therefore leave an action unconfirmed, but this pass did not establish a selected normal-path interleaving that both retains a valid downstream device and exposes a stopped hub worker. No standalone finding promoted. Hub binding/task shutdown lifetime remains tracked separately; no UI, hub, or task schedule was run. Source-only.

Poseidon/Trident removal-event trigger expansion (OD2852 strengthened; no new ID; 2026-10-26): censused all maintained `EHMB_REMDEVICE` send sites. In addition to `psdRemHardware()`, standard and SuperSpeed hub workers send the same event only after `psdFreeDevice()` (`hub.class.c:469-478,694-709,1050-1062`; `hubss_class.c:418-427,645-659,1015-1026`). When `pd_UseCnt` is zero, `pFreeDevice()` frees config/interface records before unlinking the retained device tombstone; `psdSendEvent()` can then lose the matching Trident notification if its per-listener event-note allocation fails. Trident's normal listener cleanup is the same for each removal source, so expanded OD2852's trigger and affected path list from controller removal to downstream disable, disconnect and hub teardown. PoPo's removal listener is not the source of the stale-interface consequence: its removal popup leaves `pog_Device` NULL. Updated the detailed report and index summary. No disconnect, allocation failure, window action, or event was run; source-only.

OD2852 Trident stale-window lifetime recheck (2026-10-26; finding refined, no LOC credit): checked for alternate cleanup after a lost `EHMB_REMDEVICE`. Trident's main device-list display hook calls `CheckDeviceValid()`, which checks only the main row's `pd` against Poseidon's live device iteration and can null that row (`rom/usb/trident/ActionClass.c:555-580`). The open per-device window has separate `IfListEntry` records holding raw interface pointers; its display hook and selected activate/unbind/config methods dereference/pass them (`rom/usb/trident/DevWinClass.c:45-54,88-106,705-719,742-783`). That child window is disposed on the normal removal event via `FreeDevEntry()`; the main-row validity check does not close it, and no independent polling close path was established. Expanded OD2852 to state that a later interface-list redraw as well as action may dereference freed records. No window, removal or redraw was run; source-only.

Poseidon-triggered HID GUI lifetime cross-check (OD3924/OD4402 retained; no new OD or body credit; 2026-10-26): followed the selected PoPo `UCM_OpenBindingCfgWindow` call through `nOpenBindingCfgWindow()` into `nGUITask()`/`nGUITaskCleanup()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:423-430,640-661`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:149-215,1722-1786`). The GUI task does not take Poseidon's base lock while it starts or runs; binding release waits on `nch_GUITask` before freeing the binding, so the callback's caller-held read lock does not itself form a lock/wait cycle. The cross-CPU child-publication/early-exit race remains OD3924, and cleanup's signal-before-final class-base access remains OD4402. No new configuration-GUI candidate was established; other GUI functions and MassStorage's corresponding callback remain outside this targeted trace. No GUI or task interleaving was run; source-only.

Poseidon binding-configuration callback lock-scope follow-up (no new OD; 2026-10-26): traced `pOpenBindingsConfigGUI()` and `pOpenClassesConfigGUI()` while they hold `psdLockReadPBase()` through class `usbDoMethod()` calls (`rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c:1212-1330`). The selected HID `UCM_OpenBindingCfgWindow` method calls `nOpenBindingCfgWindow()`, which opens `poseidon.library`, uses `Forbid()` only to check/publish `nch_GUITask`, spawns the GUI task, then returns without waiting for GUI completion (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:640-661`). Thus this selected HID configuration method does not synchronously wait for a GUI task that might need the caller-held base lock. The actual GUI task and MassStorage implementation were not traced in this pass; those remain open. DFU functional-descriptor minimum-length caller trace (OD9823 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): followed the standalone DFU interface binder through Poseidon's `psdFindDescriptor()` into descriptor creation. Configuration parsing rejects only `bLength < 2`; `pAllocDescriptor()` allocates from and copies exactly the supplied descriptor length, while `psdFindDescriptor()` filters type/interface but not length. RDB DosEnvec size follow-through in USB Mass Storage (EK9333 caller pass; 2026-10-26; no new OD or LOC credit): `AddPartitionVolume()` allocates a packet with space for the fixed `struct DosEnvec`, copies that structure from `GetPartitionAttrs()`, then passes it to `MakeDosNode()` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/partitions.c:155-157,259-260`). If an RDB PART block's oversized `DE_TABLESIZE` has already been accepted by `PartitionRDBNewHandle()`, `MakeDosNode()` computes and copies more entries than the packet contains (`rom/expansion/makedosnode.c:119-121,139-156`). This is part of EK9333's upstream table-size defect, not a separate driver finding. The packaged ARM/Raspberry Pi, AArch64/Raspberry Pi and RISC-V/OpenSBI Mass Storage callers are the selected configurations; no media or mount was used.

USB MassStorage AddVolume ownership and result follow-up (OD9833-OD9835 added; 2026-10-26): traced both branches after `MakeDosNode()` through `CreateNewProc()` and `AddBootNode()`, checked their return contracts and storage-class caller (`storage_volumes.c:436-510`; `createnewproc.c:54-73,649-672`; `addbootnode.c:134-217`; `storageclass.c:315-323`). USB Mass Storage zero-head geometry caller trace (OD9840 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced SCSI geometry synthesis from `nGetGeometry()` through `OpenRootPartition()` into the MBR partition-handle constructor. MODE SENSE page 0x04 can set `dg_Heads` to zero while marking the geometry field present; when page 0x03 supplies nonzero sectors per track, `nFakeGeometry()` is skipped. A nonzero-start MBR entry then reaches `initPartitionHandle()`'s modulo by `de_BlocksPerTrack * de_Surfaces`, which is zero. Added OD9840, scoped to the selected ARM and AArch64 Raspberry Pi USB Mass Storage packages and the exact conditional geometry/table response. Other MBR/GPT/EBR geometry and external device behavior remain open. No device or partition was used; source-only.

AHI CMD_READ sample-rate conversion math recheck (OD2149 consequence reconciled; 2026-10-26; no path/LOC credit): traced the conversion factor through `ReadCmd()`, `FillReadBuffer()`, and the S16S converters rather than treating `MultFixed()` as multiplication by the ratio. Its local definition is `(a << 16) / b` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:73`), so `FillReadBuffer()` divides available source frames by the source-frames-per-output-frame step before `RecS16S()` advances through the source (`:1034-1047`; `devsupp.c:112-132`). This count/stride pairing is correct for a valid step and does not itself overrun the current source buffer. For 192 kHz source and 48 kHz request, the intended step is 4.0; the 32-bit shift instead yields 83,186 (about 1.269), so both output count and source advance use the wrong ratio and the returned effective rate is about 151 kHz. At 96 kHz source/48 kHz request the step is 2.0 without overflow, and the reciprocal frame count is correct. Kept the finding consolidated under OD2149, which concerns the overflowed step; no second rate-count finding was added. No capture ran; source-only.

CharMap selection-copy allocation failure reconciliation (OD9843 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-read `charmapcon_get_selection()` and both consumers in `charmapcon_copy()`. `AllocMem(size)` failure returns NULL; the active-ConClip route sends NULL with positive `SGWork.NumChars` through `WriteChunkBytes()` to clipboard.device's DOS `Write()` path, and ConClip ignores the IFF write result. The fallback route frees the old `copyBuffer`, publishes NULL/zero, and consequently skips registered ConSnipHook callbacks. CharMap large-selection length propagation recheck (OD9844 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): followed the `ULONG` result of `charmapcon_calc_selection_size()` through assignment to signed `WORD SGWork.NumChars`, ConClip's `WriteChunkBytes()` call, IFFParse's nonzero-length stream path and clipboard.device's `io_Length` assignment. A 256x128 character grid admits more than 32,767 selection bytes plus line breaks under the selected window-derived geometry. CharMap blank-column copy bounds trace (OD9845 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced mouse coordinates to character-column selection, selection-size calculation, line allocation capacity, and copy-buffer construction. A same-line selection's byte count is only endpoint distance, but the source pointer is `line->text + minx` and `CopyMem` is not clipped to either `line->size` or `line->capacity`; short lines allocate only `capacity * 4` bytes for the text/attribute planes. A normal selection through blank columns can therefore read outside the allocation or copy non-text padding. Merged the older ledger-only OD53 boundary candidate into OD9845; this is separate from OD9843 allocation failure and OD9844 signed-length narrowing. No selection or copy was performed. Source-only.


CharMap multiline selection-size underflow refinement to OD9845 (2026-10-26; no new ID or body/LOC credit): confirmed `charmap_line.size` is `UWORD`, while selection column and calculated size are `ULONG` (`rom/devs/console/charmap.h:14-25`; `charmapconclass.c:1210-1225`). A multi-line selection starting beyond a nonempty first line's logical size underflows `cur->size - minx`, potentially requesting nearly 4 GiB; if allocation fails, the already detailed OD9843 path follows. Folded this case into OD9845's missing selection-bound validation. No allocation or selection was run. Source-only.

RP1 synthetic PCI HIDD full-body and selected DMA-caller recheck (2026-10-26; no new OD or path credit): re-read all 287 lines of `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/rp1/rp1_pci.c`, including config-space bounds, byte/word/long access, BAR probe and writes, address translation delegation, DMA allocation/free, and initializer failure paths. Reconciled BAR relocation with existing OD1839 and registration failure/resource rollback with OD2884; no duplicate added. Followed selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi `PKG_HIDDS`/`PKG_DEVS` inclusion into `pcixhci`, and its aligned allocator and paired free wrappers (`rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_arospci.c:473-506`; `pcixhci.h:513-561`). The wrapper passes controller-derived ring/context lengths and preserves the original base for free. For `ULONG` requests near the 32-bit rounding boundary, `PCIMEM_ROUND` yields zero; AArch64 `KrnMapGlobal` rejects zero length and the allocation is freed before return, so this does not publish an undersized DMA buffer. For a successful map, the reverse map covers the same rounded span and uses page-table levels already created during allocation; the ignored restore result did not establish a normal selected failure path. Existing OD2884 remains the registration/committed-MSI rollback candidate. External PCI method callers and physical xHCI behavior remain open. No driver, mapping, allocation, or controller was run; source-only.

CharMap OD9845 selection-source interval and allocation-layout recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): traced both mouse-derived endpoints through the same-line `MIN(minx,maxx)` source offset and `abs(maxx-minx)` copy count (`rom/devs/console/charmapconclass.c:1219-1223,1261-1268`; selection coordinates at `:1505-1533,1557-1568`). Confirmed these coordinates are bounded only by the rendered console grid, while `charmap_resize()` allocates `capacity * 4` bytes for four adjacent planes and records the logical/capacity fields separately (`rom/devs/console/charmap.c:61-112`). Therefore a nonempty short line can be selected from blank grid columns beyond both its logical size and capacity; CopyMem then reads from `text + minx` for the endpoint distance without range validation, yielding stale/adjacent-plane data and, when the source interval crosses the allocation end, an out-of-allocation read. For multi-line selection, the first-line `UWORD size` is promoted against `ULONG minx`, so `size - minx` wraps for a start column beyond the line and feeds both the allocation size and subsequent copy count. This confirms the distinct same-line out-of-bounds and multi-line size-underflow cases consolidated under OD9845. The already indexed OD9843 allocation-failure path is a possible consequence of the inflated request, not a duplicate cause. No GUI input, selection, allocation, or copy was performed; source-only.

Poseidon USB HID OD9814 worker-wakeup and GUI-poll recheck (2026-10-26; candidate strengthened, no GUI/body LOC credit): re-read one-shot control construction and action dispatch (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hidctrl.gui.c:149-170,478-495`) against `nHidTask()`'s wait/dispatch loop and `nFlushEvents()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:736-742,897-898,990-992,6352-6396`). A button press writes only `nhr_OutTouched`, signals the worker, and polls that report flag; the signal wakes `Wait()`, but the subsequent flush is globally gated by `nch_OutFeatTouched`, which this first phase leaves false. With no queued pipe message and no concurrent output action setting the global flag, the worker returns to waiting without clearing the report flag; the GUI remains in its 10-ms polling loop and never reaches its release phase. Toggle and slider actions set both levels, confirming the one-shot branch is the outlier. The candidate's trigger and consequence remain as OD9814; no issue with the release phase is claimed once the first report has actually flushed. No signal, pipe, or GUI action was run; source-only.

Potgo OD9806 in-tree overlap census refinement (2026-10-26; no new finding or body/LOC credit): compared the exact selected LowLevel and AmigaMouse masks (`arch/m68k-amiga/lowlevel/readjoyport.c:24-27,157-176`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/mouse/mouseclass.c:165-171,200-203`). AmigaMouse permanently reserves port-0 `0x0f00`; LowLevel port 0 requests that same mask and receives no bits, then calls `FreePotBits(0)`, while LowLevel port 1 uses disjoint `0xf000`. Thus the selected pair does not establish a same-mask reallocation overlap, even though it confirms cross-client ownership checks; OD9806 remains scoped to an external/direct potgo-resource client that reallocates an actually released mask during the split update. The source-defined public vectors permit allocation retention until explicit FreePotBits; no checked-in public contract specifies cross-call exclusion or an interrupt-safe lock. No potgo API call, task switch, or hardware access was run; source-only.

AHI OD1442 waiter-resume and single-CPU lifetime recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or body/LOC credit): followed `LockDatabase()`/`LockDatabaseWrite()`'s outer `Forbid` through `FindSemaphore`, `ObtainSemaphore[Shared]`, and the caller's post-lock use (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/database.c:143-194,212-214,279-309`) against Exec's queued obtain and release paths (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:120-151`; `rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:111-153,164-178`). The waiter retains the database pointer in its caller local, `ReleaseSemaphore()` removes/grants/signals the waiter, and `InternalObtainSemaphore()` resumes from `Wait()` and returns without revalidating that pointer. `_AHI_RemoveAudioMode()` then unlinks/frees the database before its outer `Permit()` allows the signaled waiter to run on a single-CPU build; that caller proceeds to traverse or update the freed database. On ExecSMP, processor-local Forbid permits the woken task to overlap the freeing CPU. This independently confirms OD1442's two scheduling cases and its distinction from OD1443's duplicate first-publication race. No request, mode removal, semaphore wait, or scheduler interleaving was run; source-only.

LowLevel StopInput ExecSMP owner/nesting race (OD9850 added; 2026-10-26; no body or LOC credit): re-read the `SetInputState()` owner/nesting transition (`workbench/libs/lowlevel/systemcontrola.c:21-65`) against Exec's explicit processor-local `Forbid()` semantics (`rom/exec/forbid.c:40-60`) and the selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP build path (`configure.in:2195-2198`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:213`; `workbench/libs/lowlevel/mmakefile.src:13-25`). Two CPUs can both observe a NULL owner from the initial `ll_InputNest == -1` state. One can publish owner A and increment the nesting value to zero; the other can then publish owner B and increment it to one. Both TRUE calls report success, but only A performs `CMD_STOP` and B overwrites the owner. B's one FALSE call decrements the count to zero without issuing `CMD_RESET`; A can no longer release ownership. Added OD9850 separately from OD9818's single-task no-op reset and failed-command state retention. This is a caller-triggered SMP interleaving established from source, not a reproduced race; no body or file-count credit because this path was already fully read. Source-only.

The source converts only NULL to the default-locale branch; an empty string remains non-NULL, is routed as a relative path from the current directory, and reaches the handler as an empty C/BSTR name. OpenLocale returns NULL on open or required IFF-read failure and does not retry the default branch. Thus the source-level API mismatch is sound, but whether a specific selected handler resolves an empty path, and whether it happens to contain a valid locale IFF, remain filesystem-dependent. The only direct checked-in GetLanguageSelection caller remains the optional LowLevel debug test (`developer/debug/test/lowlevel/lowlevel.c:381`); no selected production caller was found. Kept OD9820 conditional and specified both possible wrong results (LANG_UNKNOWN or a non-default file's language). No DOS path or locale file was opened; source-only.
