Controller HIDD consumer lifetime recheck (OD2883 expanded; 2026-10-26): read the complete `controller_notify.c` body (264 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and subsequently the complete `controllerclass.c` body (607 code lines). `ctrl_DeliverEvent()` collects consumer pointers while `Disable()` is active, enables interrupts before `ctrl_DeliverTo()`, and retains no reference or in-flight count. Consumer disposal calls `ctrl_ConsumerDetach()`, frees ring/message arrays, and reaches the OOP root disposer, which frees the object (`controllerclass.c:285-307`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-149`). Exec documents `Disable()` as CPU-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`); the hardware-driver interface documents Push methods as callable from any context (`controllersubsystem.c:60-70`). Thus a producer on one CPU can deliver through a snapshotted consumer while another CPU disposes it. Expanded OD2883, which already covered the analogous Input HIDD fanout. The constructor allocates mode-specific event storage before attaching, and this class pass established no additional candidate. Scope is conditional: the Controller HIDD module has an explicit target, but its common aggregate edge is commented and no in-tree consumer client establishing the overlap was found. This target adds 11 paths (seven C files, two headers, class definition and manifest) and 3,096 C/header code lines to the tracked inventory; `controller_notify.c` and `controllerclass.c` now receive full-body credit for 871 lines total. Controller HIDD axis normalization full-body pass (OD9852 added; 2026-10-26): read the complete `controller_controls.c` body (223 `cloc 2.06` C lines), matched descriptor and raw-report field widths in `include/controller.h`, and traced normalization callers through `ctrl_PushReport()` and `ctrl_PushValue()` in `controller_reading.c`. The bipolar path multiplies a `LONG` offset by 65,535 in signed `LONG` for all ranges through 65,535; the full signed 16-bit range therefore overflows for upper-half values before division. Its QUAD path only applies above that range threshold. The unipolar product likewise lacks a wide intermediate for larger ranges. Added OD9852, conditional on external/alternate Controller HIDD driver descriptors because no checked-in driver using this API was found and the module's aggregate edge is commented. m68k CIA LowLevel timer stop/remove contract recheck (2026-10-26; no new OD or body credit): followed the selected Amiga override's `AddTimerInt()` resource/vector registration, `StartTimerInt()` control-register programming, `StopTimerInt()` control-bit clearing, and `RemTimerInt()` through `AddICRVector()`/`RemICRVector()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/lowlevel/addtimerint.c:17-57`; `starttimerint.c:19-69`; `stoptimerint.c:16-37`; `remtimerint.c:14-37`; `arch/m68k-amiga/cia/addicrvector.c:22-56`; `remicrvector.c:20-43`). `RemICRVector()` disables the selected CIA interrupt bit and removes the matching vector; it does not clear the timer's START bit. `RemTimerInt()` itself does not call `StopTimerInt()`. This leaves a source-confirmed timer-stop/removal distinction, but no checked-in timer API caller or local API contract establishes that removing a timer interrupt must also stop the CIA counter; therefore no functional defect is promoted. Existing m68k override source/body credit is unchanged. No timer handle, CIA resource, or hardware was used; source-only.
Compositor visible-region recalculation failure and redraw caller pass (OD9867 expanded; 2026-10-26; no new body/LOC credit): traced the initial display-region `NewRegion()` result and per-node `screenregion` allocation/retry through `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()`, the compositing toggle, and the return status of `BitMapStackChanged()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:147-181,415-509,735-741,810-817,1147-1168,1243-1261`). On fresh stack nodes, visibility is set only during successful recalculation; if the initial display-region allocation fails, the recalculator returns void and leaves them unmarked. Separately, a node whose screen-region allocation fails both during construction and recalculation remains on the stack without a region or visible bit. In either case, a later redraw may skip the affected source bitmap(s), fill the remaining display region with its background, and still return compositing success without invoking the documented single-bitmap fallback. Expanded OD9867 to cover both verified allocation paths. The source body/path already had full credit in the Compositor class pass; no coverage increment applies. OD9862 remains distinct: stack-node allocation failure reaches mode selection with an empty stack and an uninitialized sync. No allocation failure, compositor, or display operation was run; source-only.

PCNet32 RX descriptor error and frame-boundary candidates recheck (OD3060/OD3079; 2026-10-26; no new finding or coverage credit): re-read the complete `PCN32_RX_Int()` descriptor path and `CopyPacket()`, including all error exits, the common `next_pkt` label, normal descriptor rearm, initial OWN setup and consumer callback. PCNet32 FCS delivery and SANA-II contract recheck (OD3078; 2026-10-26; no new finding or coverage credit): verified in the SANA-II v3.1 specification that `ios2_DataLength` excludes link header/trailer information (p. 6) and Ethernet raw format includes the 14-byte header plus payload while explicitly excluding the hardware-generated four-byte CRC (p. 57). Compared that contract with CSR4 value `0x0915` (ASTRP_RCV bit 10 clear), `CopyPacket()`'s cooked-header-only subtraction and raw full-length copy, and the per-type byte counter's use of descriptor `len`. This establishes OD3078 as a SANA-II length/data-contract mismatch for both raw and cooked read delivery, and confirms the 4-byte statistics overcount; the earlier wording that left client-visible impact dependent on policy was too weak and has been replaced. Coverage remains unchanged because source/body was already credited. No request, packet or hardware was run; source-only. Reference: [SANA-II Network Device Driver Specification](https://megaburken.net/~patrik/NDK3.2R4/SANA%2BRoadshowTCP-IP/doc/SANA-II.pdf), pp. 6, 57.

Input.device key-repeat simultaneous-signal finding promotion (OD9868, 2026-10-26): promoted the previously ledger-only OD1995 observation after rereading the complete scheduling slice in `ProcessEvents`, the `ABORT_KEYTIMER_REQUEST` macro and Exec `CheckIO`/`WaitIO` semantics. In a simultaneous command/key-timer wake, an `IND_ADDEVENT` non-qualifier key event can consume the completed timer reply and clear its signal during command-first processing, but the saved `wakeupsigs` still enters the later timer branch; that branch ignores the now-empty `GetMsg()` result and repeat state, emits the previous key as a repeat and rearms the request. Confirmed a maintained producer through HID `HUA_KEYMAP`/`nSendRawKey`; ordinary keyboard-device events are processed after the timer branch and do not establish this ordering. Reconciles the old OD1995 references as superseded by OD9868. No event or timer was run; source-only.

Keyboard.device ring-wrap trigger precision (OD34 rechecked, 2026-10-26): traced input.device `CMD_STOP` through the unchanged outstanding keyboard read, the keyboard callback reply, the stopped worker wait mask, and the resumed one-event resubmission (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:246-266,482-530`). The already-outstanding read consumes the first callback event; the worker masks that reply while stopped and submits no replacement. Exactly 128 subsequent callback writes return the ring writer to that unit's stationary read cursor, so the next read treats the full ring as empty. Tightened OD34's selected path to include this event count and lifecycle; no event burst was generated. Other openers have independent cursors. No new candidate or file-body credit; source-only.

Optional Nouveau/VMware timer init/rollback ownership pass (OD9869 expanded, 2026-10-26): traced both identical `init_timerbase()` bodies through their link-library source lists, generated HIDD module init, `_set_libinit()` rollback, `_set_libexpunge()` and Exec device/memory cleanup (`workbench/hidds/{nouveau,vmwaresvga}/{sources.drm.mak,mmakefile.src,drm-compat/linux_time.c:38-71}`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:50,64-85`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1170`; `rom/exec/{closedevice,deleteiorequest,deletemsgport}.c`). On `OpenDevice()` failure, `linux_time.c` frees the request and port without nulling its globals; rollback then calls the EXIT hook, which closes and deletes those freed allocations again. No module load or timer failure was induced; source-only.
i8042 PS/2 mouse timer-open failure ownership recheck (2026-10-26; no new OD): followed `i8042_mouse_init_task()`'s timer port/request setup through the synchronous `i8042Mouse__Root__New()` handshake and failed-object disposal (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseps2.c:179-211`; `i8042_mouseclass.c:47-89`). Although the failed `OpenDevice()` branch leaves `data->hwdata.ioTimer` pointing at the deleted request, it sets `irq=0` and signals the creator; the creator waits for that signal, sees the zero IRQ and invokes the superclass Dispose directly, bypassing `i8042Mouse__Root__Dispose()` and any subclass cleanup that might consume the stale field. The init task has already returned before the object is destroyed, and the port was deleted in the failure branch. Thus the stale field is not dereferenced on this selected failure path; no bug is promoted. The i8042 target's broader IRQ, successful-init and teardown paths remain open. No timer open failure or object operation was induced; source-only.
PC i8042 mouse IRQ-allocation/probe-failure cross-check (OD3351 revalidated, 2026-10-26; no new finding or body credit): re-read the complete mouse setup worker's IRQ-registration through completion sequence and compared it with both generic and selected-PC `KrnAddIRQHandler()` allocation returns and `KrnRemIRQHandler()` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseps2.c:211-228`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-110`; `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-56`). The IRQ API returns NULL when `krnAllocIntrNode()` cannot allocate; when the subsequent probe returns false (including a missing auxiliary port), the worker unconditionally removes that NULL token. The remover reads `h->in_nr` before its `if (h)` guard, so the worker faults before signaling its synchronous constructor. Confirmed this is the already indexed OD3351 path, distinct from the keyboard's unchecked-success OD3345 and the generic null-removal defect EK815; no duplicate report entry or LOC credit. Both conditions are conditional on IRQ-node allocation failure plus a failed mouse probe. No allocation failure, controller, or device was exercised; source-only.
i8042 PS/2 mouse packet-buffer bound and publish-order pass (2026-10-26; no new OD): compared every `mouse_data[]` access in the IRQ parser with the five-byte object buffer, the only packet-size assignments (3-byte standard and 4-byte IntelliMouse), and the controller interrupt-enable sequence (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouse.h:30-47`; `i8042_mouseps2.c:76-97,121-160,361-435`). The collected-byte counter starts clear with the class instance; only a first byte with the sync bit advances it, and a completed packet resets it to zero. The parser's maximum accessed index for the selected packet sizes is 3, within the five-byte buffer. Although the IRQ token is registered before reset sets the packet size, the selected PC i8042 initialization starts with the mouse interrupt bit clear, and `i8042_mouse_reset()` clears it before setting size 3 or 4 and reenabling the controller mouse IRQ; this ordering was separately traced against `i8042_classinit.c` keyboard initialization and the zeroed library base in the earlier 2026-10-25 pass. Thus no selected early-IRQ path with packet size zero was established. This closes only the packet-index bound/order slice; malformed controller streams beyond these checks and hardware timing remain unverified. No IRQ or packet was produced; source-only.

AHI Device combined play/record error-path caller trace (OD9842 expanded; 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): traced `AHI_ControlAudioA()` tag decoding and result propagation against the Device subdriver start order (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:959-977,1007-1021`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Device/device-main.c:140-184`). A single control request may set both `AHISF_PLAY` and `AHISF_RECORD`; Device allocates playback buffers, launches and waits for its slave, and only then rejects RECORD with `AHIE_UNKNOWN`. The dispatcher returns that error without rollback/Stop, so playback can remain active after the combined call reports failure. Expanded OD9842 and its master-index label with this distinct caller-visible consequence. No AHI control call, worker or audio operation was run; source-only.

AHI Device playback-worker persistence after combined recording rejection (OD9842 consequence strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): verified the slave signals successful AHI-device setup and then enters its playback loop before `_AHIsub_Start()` checks/rejects `AHISF_RECORD` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Device/device-playslave.c:105-150`; `device-main.c:161-184`). Rechecked `_AHI_ControlAudioA()`'s combined `playflags`, error return and absence of stop rollback (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:959-977,1007-1021`). Thus for a combined play/record request with successful slave startup, the call returns `AHIE_UNKNOWN` while the playback worker remains active until a later Stop/FreeAudio. Strengthened OD9842 consequence/confidence and its master-index description. No worker or audio request was run; source-only.
AHI Device AllocAudio/FreeAudio and partial playback-start unwind recheck (2026-10-26; no new OD): traced the selected common `AHI_AllocAudioA()` error branch and `AHI_FreeAudio()` call order against the Device subdriver hooks (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:481-521,701-748`; `Drivers/Device/device-main.c:48-98,151-184,208-231`). If DeviceData allocation fails, its `FreeAudio()` sees the NULL pointer and returns; if signal allocation fails, Exec `FreeSignal(-1)` is a no-op (`rom/exec/freesignal.c:47-58`) and DeviceData is freed. For a later Start failure after successful subdriver allocation, generic `AHI_FreeAudio()` calls `AHIsub_Stop(AHISF_PLAY|AHISF_RECORD)` before FreeAudio, and Device Stop frees both stored mix buffers even when no slave task was created. This rules out the candidate leak for the normal FreeAudio cleanup route and repeated starts (Start first calls Stop). The combined play/record return-with-live-playback case remains OD9842: it is a post-successful-start error returned to the caller, not AllocAudio rollback. AHI Device init hook's AROS library acquisition cleanup was also matched against the common generated init failure unwind; NULL `CloseLibrary()` is ignored by Exec. No new defect established. No allocation failure, AHI control, worker or library load was induced; source-only.
AHI Device acceleration-hook fallback and mixer allocation-failure caller recheck (OD4168/OD1577 retained; 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): reread all six `device-accel.c` hooks and followed their `AHIS_UNKNOWN` returns through the selected generic `AHIACF_NOMIXING`/return-code branches in `sound.c` (`SetVol`, `SetFreq`, `SetSound`, `SetEffect`, `LoadSound`, `UnloadSound`). No separate acceleration-hook bug; complete Device hook bodies and these selected caller branches were already represented, so no path or code-line credit. No allocation failure, mixer call or audio operation was run; source-only.


SM502 truecolor `SetColors()` return/caller pass (OD9870 added; 2026-10-26; prior `data->bpp` disposition refined): rechecked the only exposed mode and all direct SetColors routes. `initSM502GfxHW()` fixes 32-bit storage/24-bit depth and HIDD mode tags select TrueColor; `SM502BM::New()` skips the palette initialization branch, leaving cleared `data->bpp == 0`. No call or hardware was used; source-only.

The branch would consume a failed reply without reissuing it, but no valid selected producer trigger was established, so the former OD47 remains withdrawn rather than restoring an external-abort scenario as a driver defect. No read error, device or event was induced; source-only, no body/LOC credit.

Keyboard `KBD_READEVENT` direct-producer and shutdown recheck (OD47 remains withdrawn; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): a checkout-wide C/header search found the keyboard command only in the public command declaration, keyboard.device dispatcher, and `rom/devs/input/processevents.c`'s private worker producer. The worker creates a cleared `IOStdReq`, opens keyboard.device, supplies its persistent `InputEvent` storage and exact `sizeof(struct InputEvent)` length, submits one request, dequeues its completion, checks `io_Error`, and resubmits only after a successful event (`processevents.c:188-195,247,480-530`). For that valid request, `keyboard.device` queues the read when empty and `writeEvents()` sets `io_Error` to zero before processing (`keyboard.c:347-390,415-424`); the too-short length error is not reachable from this producer. No selected AbortIO or alternate producer exists. CMD_STOP masks the completion signals but leaves the private reads outstanding; CMD_START re-enables those signals, so this pass found no lost-request or completion-error defect in the selected producer. This closes only the direct `KBD_READEVENT` producer census and stop/start handoff slice; other keyboard commands, HIDD producers and external clients remain as recorded. No input event, device request or task transition was run; source-only.


Input.device OD9868 repeat-persistence consequence recheck (finding and index wording strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): traced the stale saved `wakeupsigs` bit through the complete key-timer branch (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:459-480`). After the canceled completion is dequeued, the branch sets `keyrepeat_state=2`, emits the unchanged `keyrepeatie`, and rearms `keytimerio` using `KeyRepeatInterval`. The initialized default is two 50-Hz ticks, or 40 ms (`input_intern.h:48-49`; `input.c:56-64`). Each later timer completion takes the same branch without checking for a matching key-down state, so the repeat can continue until a later non-qualifier raw-key command cancels it. CMD_STOP defers timer-signal handling, while CMD_START re-enables the branch for a still-pending completion. HID `IND_ADDEVENT` key-release callers are documented in the prior OD9868 producer pass. Updated the finding and index wording; no timer or key event was run. Source-only.

Prism2 software-WEP transmit caller path recheck (OD3334 retained; 2026-10-26; no new finding or body/LOC credit): re-read `InitialiseAdapter()` and its selected WEP fragment dispatch, then traced `ConfigureAdapter()`'s no-hardware-WEP flags through `EncryptWEPFragment()` to `WEPEncrypt()` (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/unit.c:597-610,768-785`; `encryption.c:587-592,1128-1150`). When `P2_REC_HASWEP` is zero, `UNITF_HARDWEP` stays clear and initialization installs `EncryptWEPFragment`; WEP configuration enables host encryption, and a transmitted WEP fragment calls `WEPEncrypt(..., FALSE)`, reaching the loop that appends `key->length` bytes after the 3-byte IV in `seed[16]`. WirelessManager's checked-in parser allows lengths up to 16 (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/wpa_supplicant/config.c:1245-1267`; `config_ssid.h:192-201`), its SANA-II backend forwards the length unchanged (`src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:351-375,415-429`), and Prism2 stores it unchanged (`unit.c:1010-1024`). This confirms the documented conditional 14..16-byte overrun route for software-WEP-capable cards; cards reporting hardware WEP use `WriteWEPFragment(..., TRUE)` and do not enter the seed-copy loop. Existing OD3187 separately captures the earlier oversized copy into the 13-byte WEP member. No card, key, association or packet was used; source-only.

Atheros5000 AR5211 calibration-scratch caller and concurrency recheck (OD4227 retained and trigger narrowed; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced the selected optional device's `GetPCICount()` → `GetUnit()` → `GetPCIUnit()` → `CreatePCIUnit()` path (`device.c:572-583`; `pci.c:100-112,136-151,211-239`) and confirmed the Prometheus implementation counts each compatible board and maps each unit index to a distinct board (`prometheus.c:49-64,82-111`). In each task, queued requests are dispatched under that unit's `access_lock` (`unit.c:2810-2865`; `request.c:176-210`), serializing that unit's `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` and `S2_SETOPTIONS` reconfiguration paths (`request.c:602-655,1537-1574`). However, separate unit tasks on separate compatible cards can enter `ConfigureAdapter()` concurrently; its per-unit lock does not protect HAL function-static storage. The AR5211 attach table selects `ar5211Reset` (`hal/ar5211/ar5211_attach.c:39-56`), whose transmit-power setup calls `ar5211SetPowerTable()` and `ar5211SetRateTable()` (`ar5211_reset.c:1375-1385`), using shared function-static arrays recorded by OD4227. OHCI root-hub OnOff superclass caller trace (OD2287 confirmed, 2026-10-26; no new OD): matched the selected `ohcihub.c` method to the generic USBHub implementation and registration callers. `OHCI::OnOff` calls `OOP_DoSuperMethod()` on both enable and disable before/after updating controller state (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcihub.c:57-94`); the USB stack invokes OnOff when registering a hub driver and when constructing a downstream hub (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbclass.c:143,329`). Its worker replies to the OnOff message (`:663-673`), while Exec `ReplyMsg()` does not queue a reply when `mn_ReplyPort` is NULL and `WaitPort(NULL)` dereferences the null port, confirming OD2287 applies to these selected OHCI caller paths. The OHCI callers ignore the returned BOOL, so the generic method's constant FALSE result is not separately promoted. No port allocation failure or hub startup was induced; source-only.


OHCI root-hub pending-RHSC cross-CPU handoff review (OD9883 added, 2026-10-26): traced both writers/readers of `running` and `pendingRHSC` across `ohcihub.c:57-94` and `ohcidriverclass.c:404-438`, the timer rearm callback (`ohcihub.c:265-284`), and the USBHub worker's scan gate (`usbhubclass.c:680-719`). The IRQ path can snapshot `running == FALSE`, then an SMP OnOff caller can set `running = TRUE` and consume `pendingRHSC == 0` before the IRQ path publishes its pending flag. The interrupt handler has already acknowledged RHSC; the timer callback reenables the interrupt but does not replay the software flag. A later hardware notification may still recover the scan, so the finding limits the consequence to a missed/deferred scan pending further hardware behavior review. The initial constructor's `pendingRHSC = 1` protects the first normal enable; the candidate requires a later off/on transition. `configure.in` selects ExecSMP for x86_64 `smp`, while the ordinary checked-in USB stack OnOff callers turn hubs on and no repeated off/on call was found. The public method remains the conditional trigger. No interleaving, hub transition or controller was run; source-only.

BTHID OD9878 report-shape and allocation-bound recheck (2026-10-26; retained, no new finding or body credit): verified the zero-count exception is explicit in the parser comment at `bthid.class.c:2175-2179` (the missing-ReportCount check is disabled because zero “seems to be a valid input”). OD1999 ExecSMP platform-scope recheck (2026-10-26; retained, no new ID or body credit): followed the child through Exec `NewAddTask()` and the selected scheduler. `NewAddTask()` inserts the task into the shared ready list through `krnSysCallReschedTask()` before returning (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:33-43,51-87`); the AArch64 scheduler selects ready tasks by CPU affinity and dispatches from that global list (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:244-269`). A second eligible CPU can therefore run the worker before the creator's post-`CreateNewProc()` assignment, while `Forbid()` is explicitly processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). The configure search found x86-64 and Raspberry Pi target branches defining `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for the `smp` variant (`configure.in:1647-1671,2195-2199`); the AHI `Device` subdriver is in the default AHI Drivers list (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Makefile.in:33-42`). AHI Device normal-stop task-state lifetime recheck (OD4305 expanded; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): followed the worker's final `Forbid(); Signal(master); dd->slavetask = NULL` sequence (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Device/device-playslave.c:211-223`) through `AHI_FreeAudio()`'s unconditional Stop-then-FreeAudio calls (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:718-727`) and the selected Device subdriver `AHIsub_FreeAudio()`, which frees `AudioCtrl->ahiac_DriverData` (`Drivers/Device/device-main.c:89-97`). The `ahi.device` process calls `FreeHardware()` on shutdown, and that caller invokes `AHI_FreeAudio()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:811-822,946`). ExecSMP `Forbid()` is CPU-local, so the waiting master can resume on another CPU after the signal, progress through FreeAudio, and release DeviceData before the worker's pointer-clear store; that store then targets freed memory. This is separate from OD4305's worker-start false-success consequence but shares its signal-before-state-clear root. Expanded OD4305's consequence, trigger and recommendation. No worker, task schedule or FreeAudio call was run; source-only.

m68k LowLevel timer remove/re-register preemption window recheck (OD9838 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no body/path credit): rechecked `RemTimerInt()` against `RemICRVector()` and the `AddTimerInt()` semaphore scope. The CIA remover reenables interrupts before returning; LowLevel then clears `is_Code` and only afterward stores `llciat_iCRBit = -1`, with no `ll_Lock` or interrupt exclusion around those writes. A preempting task can therefore pass AddTimerInt's `is_Code == NULL` gate, publish a new timer selection/vector, and have that timer bit overwritten when removal resumes. `StartTimerInt()`/`StopTimerInt()` then take the B branch for the `-1` state. This confirms the existing conditional finding; no timer task switch or hardware behavior was induced. Source-only.

USB HID Last Action Hero first-use race pass (OD9911 added; 2026-10-26): traced per-interface task creation (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:217-232,709-733`), `nDoAction()`'s lazy dispatcher call and post-wait port check (`:5556-5575,6153-6175`), and `nInstallLastActionHero()`/`nDispatcherTask()` readiness publication and cleanup (`:6954-6980,7027-7035,7077-7082`). Two interface tasks can both observe the shared dispatcher task as NULL, overwrite the one shared `nh_ReadySigTask`, and spawn workers while the readiness wait yields. The workers publish shared task/port fields without an initialization lock; only the currently stored creator receives a readiness signal. Traced final `libClose()` and confirmed it stops/waits only for the one task still stored in `nh_DispatcherTask`, so a duplicate can remain active after close returns. Added OD9911 for the conditional duplicate-dispatcher and stranded-waiter/teardown path. The module target is selected as a Poseidon HID class; occurrence requires overlapping dispatcher first use on multiple active interfaces. No USB device or task interleaving was exercised; source-only.

USB HID vanilla-action fixed-buffer recheck (no new OD or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced the selected `HUA_VANILLA` path from `nLoadItem()` and the GUI editor into `nLastActionHero()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6647-6651,7108-7116`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:3205-3209`). `nha_VanillaString` is 80 bytes (`hid.h:142`); both configuration and GUI copies use `strncpy(..., 79)`. HID action records are allocated through Poseidon's `psdAllocVec()` backed by a `MEMF_CLEAR` pool, and the extra byte for string chunks is allocated and cleared by that same helper (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:124-125,8280-8290`; HID action allocator `hid.class.c:4468-4485`). Thus a 79-byte source remains terminated at byte 79. `nLastActionHero()` wraps it in `<` and `>` in a 128-byte local buffer; at most 82 bytes including NUL are required. The selected path establishes no overflow from this field. This corroborates the prior OD9719 withdrawal; no action string or event was sent, and no whole-file credit is claimed.

USB HID dispatcher queued-action lifetime reconciliation (OD3986 retained; no new OD or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): followed both `nDoAction()` publication sites (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:5561-5574,6161-6174`) into `nLastActionHero()` (`:7089-7116` and subsequent switch cases). Each allocated `ActionMsg` owns only its message record; `am_NCH` and `am_Action` are borrowed pointers, dereferenced after dequeue. This is the same queue/reload/edit lifetime defect already documented by OD3986: `nCleanCollection()`/`nFreeReport()` release action nodes during edits or reload, and interface release tears down the binding without synchronizing the separate dispatcher. OD3986 also records the SMP-specific limits of `Forbid()` and the conditional pool-semaphore wait. The observed dispatch path adds no distinct trigger or consequence, so OD3986 remains canonical; no action or teardown was run and no whole-file credit is claimed.

USB HID sound-action allocation-failure caller pass (OD9450 extended; 2026-10-26; no new ID or file credit): followed `nLastActionHero()`'s `HUA_SOUND` branch (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:7125-7128`) through `nPlaySound()` (`:7270-7296`) and the selected sound datatype's `Sound_TRIGGER()`/`SendObjectMsg()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:2253-2288,400-420`). `nPlaySound()` ignores `DoMethodA()`'s return and itself returns TRUE; `Sound_TRIGGER()` discards the `SendObjectMsg()` result, whose allocation failure queues no command. Thus the same silent dropped-playback condition as BTHID OD9450 applies to ROM USB HID. Updated OD9450 and its master-index label to cover both implementations. The USB HID module is explicitly buildable (`rom/usb/classes/hid/mmakefile.src:4,13-15`); no allocation failure or playback was induced.

Bluetooth/USB HID failed-sound-cache cross-check (OD3476 and OD4010 retained; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): compared `bLoadSound()`/`bPlaySound()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:6508-6562`) with `nLoadSound()`/`nPlaySound()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:7243-7297`) and their dispatcher cleanup paths. Both append the filename node before `NewDTObject()`; on failure the cached node remains with a NULL handle, and later same-name plays return without retry until the corresponding dispatcher exits and frees the sound list. This is already covered separately as Bluetooth OD3476 and USB OD4010; the class-local caches and lifetimes are distinct, so no consolidation or additional issue is warranted. No sound file or playback was used; source-only.

IntelGMA initial stolen-memory header failure recheck (OD9902 retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): followed the `Enumerator()` PCI match/ownership path through BAR mapping and the first `ObtainGfxMemory(sd, 0, virtual, TRUE)` call (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_init.c:210-240,292-331`). For the stolen-memory case, `ObtainGfxMemory()` skips the system-memory allocation but still requires `AllocVec(sizeof(struct MemHeader), MEMF_CLEAR)`; a NULL header sets `success` false and returns NULL after cleanup (`intelgma_memory.c:120-183`). The caller casts that return directly into `AddTail(&sd->CardMem, ...)` without checking it, and Exec's implementation immediately stores through the supplied node (`rom/exec/addtail.c:57-65`). No intervening branch or error return handles the NULL. This confirms OD9902's conditional initialization failure path after PCI ownership and framebuffer mapping have begun. The IntelGMA target is explicitly buildable, while the monitor parent aggregate does not select it in this snapshot (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/mmakefile.src:13-26,65-67`; `workbench/devs/monitors/mmakefile.src:9-13`). No allocation failure, PCI device or display was used; source-only.

IntelGMA malformed DTD divisor boundary recheck (OD9907 retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced `G45_parse_ddc()` from its selected display-class caller (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_hiddclass.c:505-513`) through the header/checksum gate (`:223-234`) and DTD selection/refresh expression (`:299-331`). A nonzero pixel-clock field selects the DTD; header and checksum acceptance do not validate `ha + hb` or `va + vb`, both derived from descriptor bytes and used as divisors. A checksum-valid DTD with a nonzero clock and zero horizontal or vertical total therefore reaches integer division by zero. Kept distinct from Graphics/Desktop GD5979, which concerns failed/partial I2C reads leaving the stack EDID buffer uninitialized, not successful malformed-EDID content. IntelGMA remains explicitly buildable but absent from the parent monitor aggregate in this snapshot. No EDID or mode enumeration was run; source-only.

IntelGMA EDID description-allocation duplicate check (GD5983 retained; no new OD or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): while rechecking OD9907's DTD path, confirmed its adjacent `AllocVecPooled(sd->MemPool, MAX_MODE_NAME_LEN + 1)` result is passed directly to `snprintf()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_hiddclass.c:328-331`). A NULL result therefore reaches a write through a NULL destination on allocation failure. This is already covered by Graphics/Desktop GD5983, which also records the related mode-tag and LVDS description allocation paths; no duplicate OD was added. Kept OD9907 scoped to the independent zero-total divisor in a successfully read, checksum-valid EDID. No allocation failure or EDID parse was run; source-only.

ACPI button no-registration attribute-base lifecycle recheck (OD3414 retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced `ACPIButton_Init()`'s successful `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` calls for `IID_HW`, `IID_Hidd`, and `IID_HW_ACPIButton` (`rom/hidds/acpi/button/acpibutton_init.c:222-224`) through its zero-button branch (`:364-375`) and `ACPIButton_Expunge()` (`:378-391`). The branch decrements the library open count and closes Utility/ACPICA, then returns FALSE; it does not release any of the three bases. The expunge hook only logs and returns TRUE. Generated init rollback invokes registered expunge hooks on failed initialization (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:61-69`), which still leaves these references outstanding. This confirms the button portion of OD3414; no ACPI initialization or namespace walk was run; source-only.

ACPI button signal-allocation and AddDriver rollback boundary recheck (OD998 withdrawal retained; OD2607/OD2608/OD1005 unchanged; no new candidate or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): revisited `ACPIButtonServiceTask()`'s three `AllocSignal(-1)` calls and early-return cleanup (`rom/hidds/acpi/button/acpibutton_class.c:34-55`) against the selected new-task initial signal mask (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:248-251`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The task begins with the lower 16 signal bits reserved, and this service task allocates only three signals before waiting; no selected same-task allocator competes in that interval, so the prior signal-allocation-failure candidate remains withdrawn. Also followed failed `HW_AddDriver()` cleanup (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:185-214`): its DriverNode allocation occurs before object construction, and after successful construction the inherited `HW__HW__SetUpDriver()` unconditionally returns TRUE (`:418-422`); therefore this path does not establish a newly installed-handler/freed-hook overlap. Existing OD2607 (NewCreateTask failure), OD2608 (signal-index publication race), and OD1005 (ACPICA handler-install status ignored) remain distinct. No task allocation, signal allocation or firmware event was induced; source-only.

BTHID `CopyMemQuick()` fixed-size and alignment recheck (2026-10-26; no OD): retraced `bLoadClassConfig()` and the GUI reset-keymap action against `struct KeymapCfg`, the enclosing `BTHidBinding` packing, and the generic `CopyMemQuick()` contract. The class default sets `kmc_Length` to `sizeof(struct KeymapCfg) - 8`, which is exactly the 256-byte keymap array; the reset action also copies exactly 256 bytes. Thus neither call has a short-tail issue. `BTHidBinding` is under `#pragma pack(2)` and the source keymap is declared as `UBYTE[]`, so source alone still does not prove ULONG alignment of the destination field or global symbol in the selected m68k object layout. Retained the alignment question as unresolved, with no defect promoted; no copy, build or device operation was run.

BTHID report-map sizing and item-map construction follow-up (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): traced `bReadReports()`'s descriptor-derived report bit totals, byte rounding, Report ID lookup allocation, action-ID assignment, quick item-map allocation, and `bLoadActionConfig()` call against `bParseReport()` and the output/feature send callers (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1501-1790,1941-2488,5681-5689`). Existing OD3452 covers truncated-item payload reads, and OD3454 covers the fixed Classic HID output/feature capacity; no independent ordinary valid-descriptor size or allocation-path defect was established in this slice. The per-report quick-map allocation failure sets `res` false; the subsequent config loader traverses parsed reports and action mappings rather than those quick maps, so the ordering alone does not establish a dereference failure. The BTHID translation unit remains explicitly partial; this targeted recheck earns no full-body or line-count credit. No descriptor, allocation failure, channel, or device was used; source-only.
Bluetooth HID parser-failure collection ownership follow-up (OD9912 added; 2026-10-26): traced `bParseReport()` collection creation and delayed insertion through the reserved-Main parse-error path, then followed `bReadReports()` failure cleanup into `bFreeReport()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1941-1944,2386-2458,1577-1597,1377-1401`). An open collection is local to the parser and is linked into the report only at End Collection; on parse failure before that point, report cleanup walks only linked collections and cannot free the open collection, its name, or attached items. Added OD9912, scoped to a map that fails after populated collection creation but before its matching End Collection. Targeted caller/ownership slice only; no full-body or LOC credit. No map, bind, reload, or allocation failure was run; source-only.

Bluetooth HID nested collection / Report ID transition reconciliation (OD3453 retained; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): reread `bParseReport()`'s Report ID transition and collection-parent clone loop (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2030-2105`) alongside the collection construction/End Collection path (`:2380-2445`) and default-action ancestry consumers. The loop's missing cloned-parent link and resulting lost ancestor are already covered by OD3453, including the optional USB HID analogue; no separate transition defect was added. This pass also reconfirmed OD9912's distinct failure cleanup boundary: parser-local open collections are not report-list members until End Collection, so `bFreeReport()` cannot dispose of one after an earlier parse error. Targeted source pass only; no full-body or LOC credit. No descriptor or device was used; source-only.

SM502 bitmap `bpp` initialization and selected SetColors callers recheck (OD9870 retained; 2026-10-26): traced `HwInit()`'s fixed 24-bit depth/32-bit storage through pixel-format registration, bitmap construction and the SM502 SetColors override (`workbench/hidds/sm502gfx/sm502gfx_support.c:75-95; sm502gfx_hiddclass.c:97-107,206-212; sm502gfx_bitmapclass.c:44-71,194-229`). For the selected truecolor mode, OOP root allocation clears instance data and the non-palette early return leaves `bpp` zero. The override invokes the generic superclass first, so its software colormap changes before the zero-depth check returns FALSE for updates starting above index zero. Traced the checked in-tree graphics.library, display setup and pointer initialization callers; they ignore that result, consistent with the existing conditional API-result finding OD9870 (reported in ../AROS-other-drivers.md#od9870). The mode path is therefore confirmed, but no visible failure in a maintained caller was established. No new ID or LOC credit; existing bitmap body credit remains. No build, HIDD call, or palette update was run; source-only.

CAMD SysEx public-reader caller/documentation closure (no OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-26): re-read the complete `GetSysEx`, `QuerySysEx` and `SkipSysEx` bodies and searched all C/header sources in `workbench`, `rom`, `arch` and `compiler/include` for direct callers. The only matches outside the three declarations/bodies are cross-references in CAMD comments plus CAMD producer/flush references; no in-tree client invokes these APIs. The public header likewise provides no sequence contract. `GetSysEx` marks `sysex_nextis0` after consuming F7, while `SkipSysEx` checks only `lastreadstatus` and scans ring bytes until F7, so stale-ring behavior after a completed read remains a real implementation concern but cannot yet be promoted as a supported-call bug without establishing the documented external sequence contract. `QuerySysEx` performs ring-aware wrap and is bounded by reaching F7 only; no independent normal producer state was established in this pass. OD1473's wrapped-message linear reads remain separately supported. Existing full-body credits stand; no subsystem completion implied. Source-only; no MIDI data or reader call was run.

ATA OD2996 bounce-pool construction failure recheck (2026-10-26; same finding expanded; no new ID or body/LOC credit): re-read `BusTaskCode()`'s bounce-pool initialization and traced failure through `ata_exec_blk()` into Exec `AllocPooled()`. `CreatePool()` may return NULL (`rom/exec/createpool.c:55-58,89-90`); the bus task stores that unchecked at `rom/devs/ata/ata.c:1043`. For a later >4-GiB DMA buffer, `ata_exec_blk()` calls `AllocPooled(NULL, bounce_buffer_length)` (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1201-1209`). `AllocPooled()` evaluates `IsManagedMem(mhe)` without checking NULL, and the macro reads `mh_Attributes` through the argument (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:73-77`; `compiler/include/exec/memheaderext.h:57-59`). Expanded existing OD2996 to cover this Exec-side NULL dereference path as well as the already documented per-transfer allocation failure and physical-zero PRD path. The finding remains scoped to x86/x86-64 PCI ATA DMA with an above-4-GiB request after low-memory pool construction/allocation failure; target default/package selection is recorded in the ATA manifest row. No allocation failure, DMA transfer, or hardware was used; source-only.

OD2996 PC ATA target-selection precision correction (2026-10-26): the i386-PC and x86-64-PC `boot/mmakefile.src` files list `ata` in `KDEVS` and `ata_pci` in `KHIDDS` for the BSP `%make_package` rules (`i386-pc:73-78`; `x86_64-pc:66-75`). ATA bus-task startup-resource reconciliation (OD2995/OD2996/OD3681 retained; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `BusTaskCode()` startup (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:1029-1053`) and its selected caller `Hidd_ATABus_Start()` (`rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:975-1041`). OD2996 PC ATA selection correction (2026-10-26): the previous note treated the special `#MM-` / `#MM` lines as ordinary comments. They are active MetaMake dependency declarations: `kernel-link-pc-i386` and `kernel-link-pc-x86_64` both depend on the corresponding `kernel-bsp` package compression target, and each BSP `%make_package` definition includes `ata` and `ata_pci` (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:19-26,73-78`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:9-15,66-75`). PCI ATA OD3011 shared-vector dispatch recheck (2026-10-26; same finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit): reread `ata_PCI_Interrupt()`'s no-DMA branch and the complete selected handler dispatch paths. On PC, the generic kernel iterates every registered `KERNELIRQ_LIST(irq)` node and discards each handler's return value (`arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:116-139`); the PC interrupt entry calls that fanout for enabled vectors (`cpu_intr.c:500-518`). On Sam440, the UIC scans each asserted source bit and invokes `krnRunIRQHandlers()` for that vector (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/uic.c:132-156`). Confirmed OD3011's source claim that an unrelated shared-vector event reaches PCI ATA's no-DMA status test; any non-BUSY ATA status is forwarded to the ATA callback. No new issue established. The presence of a no-DMA PCI ATA controller on Sam440 and actual line-sharing remain hardware-dependent and were not verified; no IRQ or I/O was run. Source-only.

BTHID input-event conversion and requester tail slice (2026-10-26; OD3483/OD9718 retained; no new OD or LOC credit): read `bInvertString()`, `bFreeIEvents()`, `bSendKeyString()`, `bEasyRequest()` and `bEasyRequestA()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:6587-6752`). The parser links each allocated event at the head and frees the partial chain on parse/allocation failure; the standalone freer advances before releasing each fixed-size node. `bSendKeyString()` sends down/up pairs synchronously and frees the generated chain; its unchecked `InvertKeyMap()` result and zero-code event path remain OD3483. `bEasyRequest()` still uses `AROS_SLOWSTACKFORMAT_PRE(gadgets)` although `body` carries format conversions, confirming the BTHID half of OD9718; the optional slow-stack architecture condition and selected requester call strings are already documented there. These bodies are now explicitly reviewed as a targeted tail slice, but the 6,751-line BTHID translation unit and its broader method/caller/lifecycle surface remain partial. No input event, requester, build or device was used; source-only.

BTHID action configuration persistence pass (`bLoadItem()`/`bSaveItem()`; OD3459/OD3464 confirmed; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): read both complete methods (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:5880-6022`), traced action-list allocation/default initialization (`:3794-3810`), report/item load callers (`:1413,1832-1854`), GUI form replacement and save callers (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.gui.c:2407-2470`), and Bluetooth IFF chunk/string allocation helpers (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/config.c:427-455,1377-1427,1511-1562`). On load, `bLoadItem()` returns TRUE based on finding the item form even if individual action allocation or optional string allocation fails; the resulting missing action/empty field path is already covered by OD3459. On save, the GUI clears old report-form contents before rebuilding; `bSaveItem()` breaks on action-form allocation failure but returns the item form, and ignores action/string chunk add failures, while its GUI callers do not stop before disk save; this confirms OD3464's saved-action-loss path. `bGetStringChunk()` returns a separately allocated copy, so releasing the config lock before copying into the action does not leave a borrowed chunk pointer. No independent persistence issue was established. No config, allocation failure, or GUI operation was exercised; BTHID translation-unit and broader lifecycle/caller scope remain partial. Source-only.

BTHID live action-config rebuild and default-action cleanup pass (OD3459/OD3464 retained; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): read `bLoadActionConfig()` and the complete caller path from report-map construction (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1785-1865`), plus `bAddItemAction()` and `bCheckForDefaultAction()` (`:1404-1420,3752-3791`). The loader builds each item's action list from the matching saved form or falls back to generated defaults only when `bLoadItem()` returns FALSE; therefore a matching but empty/partially loaded form suppresses defaults, confirming OD3459's saved-action allocation-failure consequence. `bCheckForDefaultAction()` compares current and generated lists, marks differing/missing actions non-default, and removes/frees all temporary generated nodes; no leak or sentinel overrun was established for the inspected list shapes. The array path uses a do/while over `nhi_MapSize`; zero-sized array validation and its callers are already separately tracked under OD9878 and were not duplicated. This was a caller/function slice, not full-translation-unit credit; parser, runtime action, and lifecycle paths remain open. No config, report, allocation failure, or device was exercised; source-only.

BTHID output/feature report encode-buffer and delivery pass (OD3454/OD3471/OD3473 retained; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): traced Output/Feature actions through touched-state publication (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:5395-5465`), `bFlushEvents()` (`:5665-5695`), the report generators and `bEncodeItemBuffer()` (`:3851-3995`), and `bSendReport()` for Classic HIDP and HOGP (`:750-817`). `nhb_EPOutBuf` is sized to the largest parsed input/output/feature report plus two bytes (`:1647-1657,1200`), while each flush length is the rounded byte length of that report; report-ID/header handling is transport-specific. The accepted zero-count array do/while underflow in the encoder is already OD3471; oversized Classic report truncation is OD3454. Both transports' write errors are logged without status reaching `bFlushEvents()`, which clears touched bits before/after the send and loses the pending update; this confirms OD3473. No additional buffer-capacity or delivery defect independent of those findings was established. No report was encoded or sent; source-only. BTHID and broader device-driver coverage remain partial.

USB HID reset-marker candidate scope expansion (OD9689 expanded; 2026-10-27; no new ID or LOC credit): compared the BTHID temporary keyboard reset-list marker with `nParseKeys()` in USB `bootkeyboard.class` and `nCheckReset()` in USB `hid.class` (`rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:529-560`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6532-6584`). Both USB implementations also register a stack `Interrupt` with `is_Code == NULL`, find the list header from its predecessor, then remove the marker in a later `KBD_REMRESETHANDLER`; the selected keyboard-device reset dispatcher invokes `is_Code` without a NULL check (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:311-324,497-512`). Their reset-handler flags default TRUE (`bootkeyboard.class.c:309`; `hid.class.c:514`), and reset checks are reachable from report/event handling (`bootkeyboard.class.c:456-490`; `hid.class.c:6188,6512`). Expanded OD9689's one shared defect to all three call sites and updated the master index title. Bootkeyboard is loaded explicitly by the Sam440 boot menu; USB HID/BTHID remain separately buildable class targets, so no default aggregate claim is made. This is a function/caller/configuration expansion only; no file body or LOC credit changed. No event, reset, class load or hardware operation was run; source-only.

Generic IPMI KCS/BT transaction, timing and HIDD caller pass (2026-10-27; no new OD or body/LOC credit): read the complete new transport bodies (`rom/hidds/ipmi/ipmi_io.c`, `ipmi_kcs.c`, `ipmi_bt.c`) and traced them through `IPMI__Hidd_IPMI__SendCommand()` (`ipmi_class.c:173-225`) and the public method contract (`include/ipmi.h`). Checked request limits before stack-buffer copies, response-length caps before caller-buffer copies, KCS state/abort sequencing, BT response sequence/netfn/command checks, timer open/close fallback, timeout loops, and the per-interface semaphore. The selected workbench IPMI sensor utility's successful short Reserve-SDR response remains covered by OD2150; the transport intentionally returns its actual short response length rather than guaranteeing a command-specific payload. No independent bounds or cleanup defect was established in this pass. Transport retries can resend a request after a successful write but missing/malformed response; whether that is incorrect for a given non-idempotent IPMI command depends on command-level duplicate semantics and a concrete caller contract, so it remains an open question rather than a finding. Firmware timing, register semantics, BMC behavior and external SendCommand clients remain unverified. No port/MMIO access, timer request, command or hardware was used; source-only.

Optional PCI `nvidianet.device` wrapper adapter full-body and completion-path pass (OD9917 added; 2026-10-27): read all 224 `cloc 2.06` C code lines / 434 physical lines in `aros_device.c`. Traced `AROSDevBeginIO()`'s `ios2_Data`/`ios2_StatData` substitution through RX/TX/DMA wrappers and into `CopyFrame()`/TX workers. The local seven-body target inventory now has full reads of `startup.c`, `timer.c`, `request.c`, and `aros_device.c` (4/7 paths; 838/2,542 `cloc` C lines); `device.c`, `unit.c`, and `pci.c` remain partial pending full-body review. Adding the newly inventoried wrapper path and full-body credit advances the represented Other Drivers ledger from 1,338/1,887 to **1,339/1,888 paths**, and from 775,566/1,245,960 to **775,790/1,246,184 C/header code lines**. Nvidianet RX DMA/cache and full-body inventory update (OD9918 added; 2026-10-27): read the full 2,060 physical-line `unit.c` body (1,113 `cloc 2.06` C lines), including unit allocation and unwind, adapter initialization/link negotiation, multicast tracking, interrupt/soft-interrupt paths, RX/TX DMA rings, request completion, reset and worker lifetimes. Reconciled the RX descriptor ring with `AllocDMAMemHook()` and m68k CachePostDMA: RXInt requests post-DMA maintenance for only one descriptor at the ring base, regardless of its current slot, and writes the descriptor's INUSE ownership bit back without a pre-DMA flush (`unit.c:1289-1297,1324-1333`). OpenSBI dwuart IRQ-versus-PLIC source-count follow-up (OD2464 expanded; 2026-10-27; no body/LOC credit): traced `KrnAddIRQHandler()` against the selected controller callback and the FDT IRQ source. Generic registration accepts IDs below `HW_IRQ_COUNT` and links the handler before calling the void `ictl_enable_irq`; OpenSBI `krnPLICEnable()` separately rejects zero, missing PLIC base, and IDs greater than firmware-provided `plic_ndev`, without returning a status (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-115`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_plic.c:38-45,77-87,150-164`). The dwuart constructor accepts the first FDT interrupt cell and publishes the unit without checking either returned handle or controller range (`dwuart_init.c:130-137`; `SerialUnitClass.c:189-232`). Expanded OD2464 to distinguish NULL registration from a non-NULL but never-unmasked source in the interval `plic_ndev < irq < HW_IRQ_COUNT`. This is conditional on incompatible/malformed FDT data for the range mismatch; no device tree, allocation failure, or interrupt was exercised. Source-only; existing body/path accounting unchanged.

PC ATA `CopyMemQuick()` DMA-bounce caller recheck (OD2996 retained; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-10-27): traced `ata_exec_blk()`'s two bounce copies through its sector geometry and caller-visible DMA buffer (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1188-1247`; sector shifts set to 9 or 11 at `ata_unitclass.c:86` and `lowlevel.c:1781,1793`). Both copy lengths are whole-sector byte counts and thus multiples of ULONG; the pool-backed bounce allocation and original caller buffer remain separate. The caller buffer's ULONG alignment is not checked before `CopyMemQuick()`, but this bounce branch is only selected for above-4-GiB DMA addresses on the PC 64-bit path, whose x86-64 hardware supports unaligned scalar accesses; the source review establishes no selected runtime fault or other concrete consequence from this contract mismatch, so no separate finding is promoted. Rechecked allocation failure: the unchecked pool and per-transfer NULL paths remain covered by OD2996. No DMA, allocation failure or device was exercised; source-only.

BTHID binding-list reader/release cross-check (OD3759 expanded; 2026-10-27; no body/LOC credit): rechecked the three `nh_Interfaces` readers against the service-release path. `CopyMemQuick()` USB HID class-default keymap byte-count/endian recheck (no OD added; 2026-10-27): traced `nLoadClassConfig()` from the class open vector and config-change event (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:76,437,485-509`) against `KeymapCfg` (`hid.h:29-36`) and `AROS_LONG2BE` (`compiler/arossupport/include/macros.h:258-269`). The chunk length is first stored in big-endian representation; applying `AROS_LONG2BE()` again when passing the copy size converts that stored numeric value back to host order. The resulting copy count is 256 on both endian classes, matching `kmc_Keymap[256]`; the apparent little-endian 64-KiB overrun is not established and is not promoted. The optional HID class is selected by the RISC-V OpenSBI package (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:109-119`), but the source alignment guarantee for the global `UBYTE usbkeymap[256]` against `CopyMemQuick()`'s ULONG-alignment precondition was not established here and remains open. No copy or class load was run; no full-body or LOC credit. Source-only.

RTL8139 close-path reset-poll comparison (OD923 boundary recheck; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read the adjacent `rtl8139nic_deinitialize()` reset sequence (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/rtl8139.c:333-348`) alongside the open path covered by OD923 (`:634-643`). Both write `CmdReset`, delay, and poll up to 1,000 reads without reporting whether the bit cleared. `rtl8139nic_close()` calls the deinitializer and then removes IRQ handling and frees both DMA buffers (`:745-780`). This confirms a second unchecked reset-completion boundary during close. The source proves the cleanup continues after poll exhaustion, but the checked-in contract does not establish whether the controller can continue DMA with `CmdReset` stuck; therefore no freed-buffer/DMA consequence is added to OD923 and no separate finding is promoted. Controller reset/DMA semantics and hardware timing remain open. No device close or timeout was induced; source-only.

BTHID report-channel allocation/unwind and close-contract pass (2026-10-27; no new OD or body credit): read `bOpenReportChannels()`, `bCloseReportChannels()` and the `bAllocHid()` failure caller in full (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:1056-1260`), then matched `btAbortChannel()`/`btWaitChannel()` state checks and the library's async channel send contract (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:1152-1254`; hardware-task reply at `hwtask.c:48-57`). The HOGP Report Reference read is accepted only after a successful result with at least two bytes; channel/buffer arrays are bounded by `BTHID_MAXCHANNELS`, and endpoint bookkeeping by `BTHID_MAXREPORTEPS`. A partially created but unsubmitted channel is in a non-message state, so `btAbortChannel()` returns without queuing an abort; `btWaitChannel()` returns immediately and the channel can be freed. If a read has been submitted, close queues the abort, waits for the abort-channel reply, then waits for and removes the original channel reply before freeing the channel and its receive buffer. The allocation-failure path calls this same close helper before report/task-port teardown. No independent ownership or unwind defect established. Limits remain: fixed endpoint/channel caps can omit excess HOGP characteristics, and external profile/device expectations for those caps were not established; this pass did not audit every Bluetooth GATT discovery/configuration path. No channel or allocation failure was run; source-only.

BTHID report-size versus receive-buffer boundary reconciliation (OD3469 expanded; no new ID or body credit; 2026-10-27): compared HID parser size accumulation with channel allocation and HOGP receive completion (`bthid.class.c:1061-1069,2369,2476-2485,4160-4214`; `bluetooth/hwconn.c:3756-3770`). The parser retains descriptor-derived offsets without a 256-byte limit, while channel storage is capped at `BTHID_MAXREPORT == 256`; `bHandleReport()` supplies neither actual length nor allocated length to `bProcessItem()`. HOGP completions larger than the channel length are tagged `BTIOERR_OVERFLOW` and skipped by the BTHID worker, so that overlength route is not described as parsing truncated data. Expanded OD3469 to cover a successful short completion that fits the 256-byte channel buffer but is shorter than a descriptor-declared report over 256 bytes: decoded fields beyond the buffer can be read out of bounds. The existing stale-field case for incomplete reports within the buffer and the Classic header-plus-Report-ID zero-field-payload case remain in the same missing-length-validation root cause. No descriptor or notification was used; source-only.

BTHID large Report Size decoder-width follow-up (OD3469 expanded; same unchecked descriptor/buffer boundary; 2026-10-27): traced the global Report Size value from its `ULONG` declaration and parser assignment (`bthid.h:422`; `bthid.class.c:2534-2536`) into `bProcessItem()`'s generic decoder (`:4165-4222`). The decoder narrows `nhi_Size` to a `UWORD` loop counter; at 65,536 bits the counter becomes zero, then the pre-tested `do/while` decrements and reads using an unsigned offset that underflows. Because report sizes above the fixed channel capacity are not rejected and a successful completion can still dispatch items, this supplies an especially clear out-of-buffer trigger under OD3469's existing missing-size-validation root cause. Did not add a separate ID; no field width, packet, or device was processed. Source-only.

Nvidianet OD9931 withdrawal verification (2026-11-08; no new finding or coverage credit): traced public `OpenDevice()` replacement into `LDDemon_OpenDevice()` (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:124-128`; `rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:533-564`), then through `LDRequestObject()` and `LDReleaseObject()` (`lddemon.c:369-391,469-497`). `LDRequestObject()` obtains the named object's `ldon_SigSem`; the wrapper calls `ExecOpenDevice()` and only then releases that semaphore. Nvidianet Open versus final Close caller extension (OD3115 expanded; 2026-11-08; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `DevOpen()`/`CloseUnit()` against `GetPCIUnit()` and the public wrappers. The Open path stores the unit pointer before it increments `open_count` (`device.c:222-239`); final Close decrements the count, removes the unit at zero, then calls `DeletePCIUnit()` (`:519-528`), while `GetPCIUnit()` returns an unpinned list result and creates/publishes on a miss (`pci.c:141-156,175-194`). LDDemon serializes same-name Open/Open but its CloseDevice wrapper has no matching object semaphore (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:391,533-564,598-623`); Exec's OpenDevice/CloseDevice `Forbid()` does not serialize cross-CPU calls under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). This establishes the distinct Open/final-Close lifetime race for the explicitly buildable Nvidianet target when built on ExecSMP with a compatible PCI device. The parent network aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:49`). Expanded OD3115; no Open/Close overlap, hardware operation, or build was run; source-only.

Nvidianet startup wrapper and micro-delay full-body/caller recheck (2026-10-27; no new OD or coverage credit): reread all 12 `cloc 2.06` code lines in `startup.c` and 14 in `timer.c`; both selected bodies were already represented in the seven-file target inventory. `main()` forwards the program entry to `Main()`, while the non-AROS m68k compatibility stub returns zero; no local behavior defect was found. In `BusyMicroDelay()`, `AddTime()` turns the requested microseconds into an absolute deadline; `CmpTime()` returns -1 when its first argument is greater than the second, so `while (CmpTime(&end_time, &time) < 0)` samples `GetSysTime()` until current time reaches the deadline. Reconciled the two maintained uses in `InitialiseAdapter()` (4 µs after transceiver reset and 10 µs after powering on) and found they use small fixed intervals. No delay defect is established. No device or timing operation was run; source-only.

USB HID oversized output/feature field encoder caller extension (OD3913 expanded; 2026-10-27; no new ID or body/LOC credit): traced `nParseReport()`'s unbounded `ReportSize` into `nhi_Size`, report buffer sizing, and the output/feature item maps (`hid.class.c:2836-2841,2895,3030,2264-2317,2344-2385`). A 65,536-bit variable Output or Feature item reaches `nEncodeItemBuffer()` through `nGenerateOutReport()`/`nGenerateFeatReport()` (`:4524-4551`); narrowing `isize` to `UWORD count` yields zero, then the do/while path decrements `ioffset` from zero and writes through a far-out-of-range report index (`:4555-4599`). `HUA_OUTPUT`/`HUA_FEATURE` marks the report dirty, and the worker flush invokes generation and transfer (`:6073-6140,6352-6429`). Expanded OD3913 to cover this independent output/feature consumer alongside its existing input-decoder read. The translation unit remains partial; no descriptor, action or transfer was used, and no file/LOC credit was added. Source-only.


USB HID unterminated output-array string parser recheck (OD4115 expanded; 2026-10-27; no whole-body/LOC credit): re-read `nParseArrayString()` end-of-input handling and its output/feature action and worker flush callers (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:4649-4829,6096-6100,6133-6137,6351-6428`). In string mode, each character is written directly to the live array buffer and decrements the remaining element count. At end-of-input, the parser enters `if(!*str)` and then tests `if(*str == '"')`, which cannot be true; a missing closing quote is silently accepted. The callers still mark the output/feature report dirty, and `nFlushEvents()` submits it. Expanded OD4115 to include this unterminated-string route alongside its existing syntax-error partial-write route; no separate ID or file/LOC credit. The HID translation unit remains partial. No action, device or transfer was used; source-only.


USB HID array parser incomplete-token end-state recheck (OD4115 expanded; 2026-10-27; targeted evidence only): checked the decimal, hexadecimal and string modes at NUL termination in `nParseArrayString()` (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:4649-4829`). A lone `-` has already initialized the live value to zero and remains in decimal mode; bare `0x` has initialized it to zero and remains in hexadecimal mode; an unterminated double-quoted string has written its characters into the live array. The final end-of-string branch diagnoses only mode 3 (single-quoted character) and does not reject these incomplete modes. HUA_OUTPUT/HUA_FEATURE still mark their report dirty, and the worker flush reaches SET_REPORT as recorded in OD4115. Expanded that finding to cover silent zero substitution and incomplete string acceptance; no new ID or file/LOC credit. No parser invocation or device action was run; source-only.


USB HID Wacom detector and PS3 quirk caller pass (2026-10-27; no new OD or full-file/LOC credit): read complete `nDetectWacom()` and `nQuirkPS3Controller()` bodies and traced their startup/reload callsites (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1203,1046,1249,1819-2061`). The detector creates a synthetic report before its collection; if collection allocation fails, it leaves an empty report linked for later cleanup but does not set `nch_WacomMode` or `nch_WacomColl`, so `nParseWacom()` does not enter that parser path. If the collection exists but individual item allocation fails, those controls are omitted while the remaining list stays traversable. `nDetectWacom()` returns FALSE even after constructing the synthetic map, but both checked callers ignore the return value; no selected behavior depends on it. The PS3 quirk only logs control-transfer status and does not inspect the response buffer. No independent defect established. The 7,521-line HID translation unit remains partial; no allocation failure, transfer, or device was exercised. Source-only.


Parallel device reset ownership recheck (OD3221 confirmed; 2026-10-27; no new finding or coverage credit): reread the full `parallel_init.c` reset/flush and AbortIO paths plus both interrupt callbacks (`workbench/devs/parallel/parallel_init.c:483-540,618-653`; `parallel_interrupthandlers.c:28-75,109-175`). Confirmed reset replies active read/write requests but retains both active pointers; it falls through to flush, which drains queued requests only. A later read can therefore queue behind the stale active-read pointer, and the write callback can continue consulting/replying the stale active-write request. Existing OD3221 already records these consequences and the hosted-Unix receive path; no duplicate finding or body/LOC credit added. No I/O or callback was run; source-only.


USB MIDI generated-driver CAMD load-contract recheck (OD4300/OD4459 and gated producer candidates reconciled; 2026-10-27; no new finding or body/LOC credit): followed the class's `DEVS:Midi/<shortID>` write through the embedded `MidiDeviceData` (`Flags=0`) and CAMD's `InitCamd()` directory scan, `OpenMidiDevice()` segment scan, and `LoadDriver()` format gate (`rom/usb/classes/camdmidi/camdusbmidi.class.c:167-218`; `camd/poseidonusb.c:35-47`; `workbench/libs/camd/init.c:19-56`; `openmididevice.c:60-130`; `drivers.c:221-260`). The AROS loader closes the segment and returns before invoking `Init` when bit 0 is clear; a generated file written after CAMD's one-time scan is also not revisited during that library lifetime. This confirms OD4300 as the primary current blocker and OD4459 as a separate late-registration condition; OD4124, OD4125, OD4137, OD4234, OD4257 and OD4266 remain consequential only if the format gate is fixed/bypassed and, where relevant, the file is loaded. No USB interface, CAMD library or driver segment was loaded; source-only.


USB HID variable division boundary follow-up (OD3552 expanded; 2026-10-27; no whole-file/LOC credit): reread the `HUAT_DIVIDE` arm of `nDoAction()` and the selected GUI operation table (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6250-6255`; `hid.gui.c:104-112,3330-3338`). The branch skips only divisor zero, then evaluates signed `LONG / LONG`; `LONG_MIN / -1` has an unrepresentable quotient and is undefined. Traced a reachable state sequence through `nProcessItem()` to the action loop (`:4851-4875,4942-4949`): a signed 8-bit input can assign -1 to a global variable, a positive 32-bit input can subtract 2,147,483,647 to reach LONG_MIN without overflow, and a later signed 8-bit -1 can invoke divide. The target is signed `LONG` (`hid.h:776`); the selected local variable array is `ULONG` and is not included in this signed-division claim. Expanded existing OD3552 rather than creating a separate arithmetic-overflow entry. The optional USB HID target configuration remains required. No report or device was used; source-only.


HID variable shift signed-result and target-width recheck (OD3462 expanded; 2026-10-27; no whole-file/LOC credit): compared both `HUAT_ASL`/`HUAT_ASR` expressions with their action editors and variable types (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:5631-5637`, `bthid.h:625,845`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6304-6311`, `hid.h:554,776`). Existing OD3462's negative or >=32 shift-count UB remains. Added signed left-shift overflow for an in-range count (LONG 1 << 31), and the C implementation-defined behavior of right-shifting negative signed targets, which can differ in sign extension across targets. Qualified ROM USB local variables as unsigned: valid-count unsigned left shifts wrap and right shifts are logical; signed-result issues apply there only through global LONG targets. GUI event values can supply count 31 or invalid counts. No action or device was run; source-only.


USB HID local-variable signed-expression correction (OD3462/OD3552 scope corrected; 2026-10-27; no whole-file/LOC credit): checked `struct NepClassHid::nch_LocalVars` against `nDoAction()`'s `LONG *tarvarptr` and local-target assignment (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.h:554`; `hid.class.c:6195-6215`). Although storage is declared `ULONG`, the action arithmetic and shifts dereference it as `LONG`; a local value 1 plus `LONG_MAX`, or 1 shifted left by 31, therefore reaches signed overflow in the expression. Corrected both reports to include USB local targets and removed the former claim that these operations have defined unsigned-wrap semantics. For signed left-shift example, initial local value is representable through both corresponding types, so the overflow occurs in the signed expression itself. No action or device was used; source-only.


Rhine endian-helper cross-target recheck (OD9933 added; 2026-10-27; no new file/LOC credit): re-opened the 11 local headers already marked body-read and traced `endian.h` through the manifest-selected `unit.c` and PCI register hooks. The helper chooses native little-endian only for `__i386__`/`__x86_64__`; its `#else` swaps little-endian words/longs as though every other architecture were big-endian (`endian.h:44-70`). `MakeLELong()` initializes RX/TX descriptor fields and ring pointers (`unit.c:253-269,1364-1440`), while the selected PCI hooks use `LEWORDIN/OUT` and `LELONGIN/OUT` for controller registers (`pci.c:585-654`). Added OD9933 for explicitly built Rhine on little-endian non-x86 targets with supported hardware; parent default-image inclusion remains disabled. This corrects the earlier header-pass conclusion that no byte-order mismatch was established. The directly included local header inventory remains 11/11 body-read and all seven selected C bodies remain fully read; external PCI backend and hardware behavior remain open. No build or device was used; source-only.

Their optional target makefiles contain no x86-only architecture guard; the the active network aggregate selects Rhine, NVIDIA and Prism2 through cards, and Realtek8180 for the PC architecture (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-15,30-33,45-53`; `realtek8180/mmakefile.src:4-9`). Network endian-helper exclusion audit (OD9933 scope confirmed; 2026-10-27; no new finding or coverage credit): checked the remaining matching network helpers and target callers. Atheros5000 and Intel Pro/100 include `<aros/macros.h>` and define `BEWord`/`LEWord` and long conversions through `AROS_BE2*`/`AROS_LE2*`, with their comments explicitly documenting host-order conversion across architectures; they are not affected by OD9933. RTL8029 has the same x86-versus-other local helper text, but a repository-local search found no use of `LEWord`, `LELong`, `MakeLEWord` or `MakeLELong` outside its helper/I/O headers, so it is not included as an active defect. RTL8139's x86-specific delay implementation is separately preprocessor-guarded and is not this endian-conversion pattern. This narrows OD9933 to Rhine, NVIDIA, Prism2 and Realtek8180. No target was built or device accessed. Source-only.


USB HID config-GUI task publication race reconciliation (OD9804 expanded; 2026-10-27; no new OD or LOC credit): followed `nOpenBindingCfgWindow()` through both `psdSpawnSubTask()` branches into `CreateNewProcTags()`/`AddTask()`, then checked all early `nGUITask()` library-open failures and cleanup against interface-release/config-reload waits (`hid.class.c:640-661,273-284,1005-1019`; `hid.gui.c:148-210,1721-1785`; `poseidon.library.c:1433-1510`; `dos/createnewproc.c:531-563`; `exec/forbid.c:58-60`). The child cleanup clears `nch_GUITask` before exiting; because the parent assigns the returned task only after spawn and `Forbid()` is processor-local on ExecSMP, a remote child can clear the field before the parent overwrites it with the returned task pointer. HID release and config reload then wait on a non-NULL field after the only task has exited. Expanded the existing MassStorage OD9804 to cover this second USB-class instance of the same publication race, rather than creating a duplicate. The target remains optional and the cross-CPU failure timing is conditional. No GUI, library failure, release or reload was run; source-only.


Legacy AHI HardDiskRecord signal-allocation caller audit (OD9934 added; 2026-10-27; no AROS coverage credit): followed the `AllocSignal()` result at `workbench/devs/AHI/Examples/Low-level/HardDiskRecord/HardDiskRecord.c:540` through `signalflag`, both assembly callback `Signal()` sites in `recordfunc.a`, the main task's `Wait()`, and `FreeSignal()` cleanup. Operator precedence makes the field 1 on success, so the actual allocated task signal is not freed; the wait mask instead aliases `SIGF_CHILD`. Repeated successful recordings leak one allocatable signal each. The directory has only a legacy `smakefile` and is not selected by `workbench/devs/AHI/mmakefile.src`; OD9934 is therefore scoped to that standalone legacy example and earns no AROS manifest path/LOC coverage. No recording or signal exhaustion was run; source-only.


HDAudio/NVHDMI HWInit failure-dispatch caller recheck (OD10211 confirmed; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): followed both selected AHI subclasses' `Root_New()` calls to `HIDD_HDA_Setup()` and the shared `HDA__Hidd_HDA__Setup()`/`HDA_Shutdown()` path (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/{HDAudio,NVHDMI}/hda_hidd.c:108-134,141-184`; `workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:438-454,496-500,504-560`). The subclass sets PCI I/O, memory and bus-master command bits before BAR validation/mapping/interrupt registration. If its HWInit returns NULL, the base Setup exits before assigning `hc_MMIO`; Root_New disposes the object, but HDA_Shutdown invokes the subclass HWExit only when `hc_MMIO` is non-NULL. This confirms OD10211 for both selected subclasses. Failures after a successful HWInit do have `hc_MMIO` and use HWExit during shutdown, so this pass does not extend OD10211 to those later branches. The AHI controller enumerators release the failed wrapper claim; the PCI command-register state remains the separate defect. No controller, PCI operation or initialization failure was exercised; source-only.

Rhine RX `RXOK` versus reported-length hardware-gate follow-up (OD9938 retained as qualified; 2026-10-27; no body/LOC credit): rechecked the ring producer and consumer end to end. `CreateUnit()` allocates each RX buffer with requested size `FRAME_BUFFER_SIZE` (1518), writes the same capacity into `RH_DESC_RXCONTROL`, and rejects a DMA mapping with a different mapped length (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/unit.c:231-264`; `device.h:102`); the PCI allocation hook adds alignment slack but returns the aligned region requested by the caller (`pci.c:675-692`). `RXInt()` accepts only `RXSTATUSF_OK`, subtracts FCS from the descriptor's 15-bit length and does not test the LONG/RUNT/BUFF bits or compare against that buffer capacity (`unit.c:1026-1051`). Rechecked available VIA descriptor definitions: VT6102 documents separate LONG/RUNT/BUFF status bits, an extended length field for abnormal-size frames, and RXOK as “received packet successfully”; VT6105 calls RXOK “No Receive Errors” and LONG “length > 1518” (VIA VT6102 preliminary datasheet, descriptor table: https://people.freebsd.org/~wpaul/VIA/VT6102_021.PDF; VT6105 datasheet, Receive Descriptor 0 table: https://bitsavers.org/components/viaTechnologies/VT6105_Rhine_III_PCI_10-100_Megabit_Ethernet_200209.pdf). These documents do not establish whether the supported silicon can set RXOK alongside a length exceeding the one-buffer capacity, or how the configured unchained buffer reports that condition. Kept OD9938 conditional; no new defect is promoted or withdrawn. No packet or NIC was exercised; source-only.
