USB HID synthetic quit-action reload failure lifetime pass (OD9939 added; 2026-10-27): traced initial `nAddExtraReport()` publication of `nch_XtraQuitItem`, the configuration-reload free/reparse path, `nReadReports()` failure signaling, and `nHidTask()` shutdown (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1005-1060,1482-1542`). A successful initial report setup publishes the synthetic quit item. Reload frees that item's report tree without clearing the cached field; if descriptor/report reconstruction fails, the worker sets its exit flag and later dereferences the stale pointer to inspect `nhi_ActionList`. `nAddExtraReport()` can only replace the pointer after its needed allocations and its return is ignored. Added OD9939, distinct from OD9782's rumble-hook access to stale cached report items: this consumer is the worker's quit-action shutdown path and needs a failed reload followed by task exit, not a concurrent LowLevel call. Clearing the cached pointer before report disposal avoids this stale dereference; successful reconstruction can publish the new item. The optional ROM USB HID target is explicitly buildable but the active `kernel-usb-classes` and `kernel-usb` rules select HID, and x86-64 PC/OpenSBI package routes include it. No descriptor, reload, allocation failure or device was exercised; source-only, no body/LOC credit change.

USB HID synthetic quit-item reload replacement-failure extension (OD9939 strengthened; 2026-10-27; no new ID or body/LOC credit): rechecked the three `nAddExtraReport()` allocations against `nHidTask()`'s reload and shutdown path (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:1027-1060,1245-1250,1482-1542`). Keyboard HIDD event-layout and Linux producer pass (2026-10-27; no new OD or path/LOC credit): reconciled `pHidd_Kbd_Event`'s `kbdevt` union overlay with the selected `arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxinput/kbdclass.c` constructor and `keyboard.device:keyCallback` consumer (`rom/hidds/kbd/include/keyboard.h:28-37`; `linuxinput/kbdclass.c:100-126`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:608-640`). Linux assigns both `flags` and `code` before the synchronous callback; these occupy the complete ULONG, so the concern that `kbdevt` is uninitialized is false. Android keyboard HIDD event-layout caller closure (OD9943 impact and reachability refined 2026-11-01; no path/LOC credit): compared `PostRawKey()`'s 32-bit `kbdevt` assignment with the `pHidd_Kbd_Event` union and both keyboard.device consumption points (`arch/all-android/hidd/androidgfx/android_kbdclass.c:200-205`; `rom/hidds/kbd/include/keyboard.h:28-37`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:430-455,608-640`). Android's selected x86 and ARM targets are little-endian, so a 16-bit raw code assigned to `kbdevt` occupies `flags`, leaving `code` zero. The callback's buffered ULONG is later published through `evtData.code`; its matrix update also tests `evtData.code` for `KEYUPMASK`. Thus both down and up transitions become raw code-zero presses, set matrix bit 0, and the up transition cannot clear it because the release prefix remains in `flags`. An earlier note called this Escape; the project defines Escape as raw code `0x45`, so that label was incorrect and is removed. OD11050 precedes this path: default warning-as-error builds are expected to reject the callback pointer-to-UWORD conversion, and a build suppressing that diagnostic still passes a narrowed callback argument. OD9943's runtime event consequence is therefore conditional on OD11050 being corrected or the callback otherwise made usable. Reconciled OD9519's duplicate-down consequence with this masking event-layout bug: the Java bridge still emits the extra down, but the released-key-specific consequence is conditional on correcting OD9943. This closes only the Android producer/keyboard.device consumer layout slice; prior full-body credit is unchanged, and other Android lifecycle/platform contracts remain open. No event or build was run; source-only.


Android keyboard table-sentinel caller recheck (OD9944 added; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): checked the `UWORD KeyTable[]` entries and the `code != -1` filter in `AKbd_ReportKey()` (`arch/all-android/hidd/androidgfx/android_kbdclass.c:90-196,237-244`). The `-1` entries convert to `0xffff`; after integer promotion they do not compare equal to signed `-1`, so unsupported table entries reach `PostRawKey()`. A correctly field-initialized event would be delivered as release code `0x7f`; current `kbdevt` packing masks that consequence under OD9943. Added OD9944 as conditional on fixing OD9943, avoiding a claim that code `0x7f` is presently delivered. Existing full-body credit unchanged. No event or build was run; source-only.

## Input HIDD producer callback signature census (OD11050/GD5973/GD10578 reconciled; 2026-11-01)

Compared keyboard and mouse producer callback storage types and invocation arguments against `InputIrqCallBack_t(APTR, InputIrqData_t)` (`rom/hidds/input/include/input.h:16,33`) and the keyboard event record contract. Android keyboard stores `(APTR, UWORD)` but passes `&kEvt`, added as OD11050; Cocoa keyboard stores `(void *, UWORD)` and passes a scalar raw key, already covered by Graphics/Desktop GD5973. WinGDI stores `InputIrqCallBack_t` and calls it with `&kEvt`, but its constructor casts through `(APTR, UWORD)` before assigning that field; added GD10578 for the default warning-as-error build consequence, with no separate runtime truncation claim. Linux, X11 and m68k keyboard producers use the shared callback typedef; SDL stores a pointer-sized second argument and passes its event record. PC i8042 forwards event pointers through the common HW input push method. The inspected Android, Cocoa, SDL, X11, Linux, m68k, WinGDI and i8042 mouse callback paths likewise pass event pointers or use the shared typedef; no additional integer-width mismatch was established. No body/LOC credit changes; no compiler, HIDD event, build, or runtime operation was used.

WinGDI keyboard focus-loss candidate closure (OD9945 added; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the hook's `last_key` updates and `WM_ACTIVATE/WA_INACTIVE` synthetic-release path (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi_native.c:60,105-124,185-209`) against the selected table-to-event handler and keyboard.device matrix update (`wingdi_kbdclass.c:42-79`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:608-640`). SD-card Open false-success Exec/caller recheck (OD3304 retained; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): followed the device Open vector through Exec `OpenDevice()` and selected filesystem callers. The SD-card Open hook clears `io_Error`, increments `unit_OpenCnt`, and logs rather than propagating either a false `StartUnit()` result or the `WaitStatus()` failure swallowed inside `StartUnit()` (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_init.c:146-172`; `sdcard_bus.c:69-82`). AROS network `AddUnitTask()` failure-path comparison (2026-10-27; no new OD or path/LOC credit): inspected the AROS branch of the shared helper headers and each of the eight selected unit-start callsites in Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, Etherlink3, Intel Pro/100, NvidiaNet, Prism2, Realtek8180, and Rhine. Each AROS helper uses `NewAddTask()` with `TASKTAG_ARG1`; all eight callers check its result, mark `UNITF_TASKADDED` only on success, and route failure through `DeleteUnit()`. Stack cleanup is not uniform: Intel Pro/100 and Rhine call null-safe `FreeMem()` on the stack pointer, NvidiaNet/Broadcom4400/Etherlink3 free a non-NULL stack independently of the flag, while Atheros5000/Prism2/Realtek8180 free the stack only inside the successful-task flag branch. Deneb OD3581 remains the previously tracked instance of the ignored AddTask failure. Bodies and task helper paths were already credited; broader post-start worker lifetime, PCI/hardware behavior, and external clients remain open. Source-only; no task or device was started.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi mailbox allocation-order follow-up (OD9955 strengthened; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): traced the BCM2711 PCI HIDD's ordinary public `AllocMem()` message through `rom/exec/allocmem.c:104-116` into selected `nommu_AllocMem()` (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:20-67`). The allocator walks matching public MemHeaders in list order, skips a header when its free count is below the request, and continues to the next; AArch64 startup appends later device-tree ranges as public headers (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:375-393`). Thus the caller is not constrained to the first/low range when that range cannot satisfy the allocation. OD9955 now states the precise conditional: a device tree exposing physical memory above 4 GiB plus lower-range allocation pressure can make the selected mailbox message use an unrepresentable address. Actual device-tree layout and allocation placement remain unobserved; no mailbox or allocation was run.

NVMe read-buffer cache-line alignment caller recheck (cross-report EK8816; 2026-10-27; no OD or path/LOC credit): traced `nvme_sector_rw()` validation and data setup (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_io.c:48-122`) through PRP/SGL segment construction, `nvme_dma_release()`, and completion. The request validates LBA offset and byte length but never checks the caller `io_Data` pointer alignment; a read uses PREREAD and completion runs POSTREAD on the original segments before waking the caller. The selected Raspberry Pi 5 package includes NVMe and RP1, whose PCI driver documents noncoherent DMA. This caller evidence supports the Exec cache-line ownership finding but leaves allocation layout and concurrent adjacent writes conditional. No request or DMA was run; source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi mailbox address-width caller pass (OD9955 added; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): reconciled the AArch64 package's `mbox` and BCM2711 PCI HIDD selections (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:215,226`) with `mbox.resource`'s 32-bit mailbox register writes (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/mbox/mbox_init.c:52,69-71,195-207`) and its reply-address comparison (`:90-100`). The selected BCM2711 PCI HIDD calls `MBoxWrite()` with a normally `AllocMem()`-allocated, cache-line-aligned message and imposes no low-4-GiB requirement (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/pcie_init.c:295-323,643`). AArch64 boot parses 64-bit DT memory range tuples, may publish multiple ranges, and the kernel adds subsequent ones as `MEMF_PUBLIC` allocator headers (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:286-323`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:375-393`). This supports the conditional high-address trigger on >4-GiB systems but does not prove that this small allocation lands in such a range on a given boot. Added OD9955 for physical address truncation and broken high-address response matching. No memory placement, mailbox transaction, firmware, or build was run; source-only.

BWFM first-open list initialization SMP interleaving (OD9965 added; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): re-read `bwfm.device` Open/Close and Exec's selected `OpenDevice()` lock sequence. The driver tests `refcount == 0` and performs `NEWLIST()` outside `unit->lock`, but only links the opener and increments the count under that lock (`bwfm_dev.c:1140-1171`). Exec releases the DeviceList lock before dispatching Open (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:91-112`), and `Forbid()` is local to one CPU on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-64`). A second Open can therefore pass the zero check, resume after the first has linked its opener, and reset the live opener list. Its lost opener later reaches `Remove()` in Close, which assumes valid links (`rom/exec/remove.c:54-63`). Added OD9965 for this conditional first-open race. Scope is the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-devs-networks-bwfm` module; Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 distfile dependencies are commented out (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:25-38`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:19-29`), so no default-image inclusion is claimed. No body/LOC credit or module coverage increase; no Open, Close or SMP schedule was run. Source-only.

Serial queued-break command completion recheck (OD3661 strengthened; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): confirmed `BeginIO()` assigns `io_Error` from `HIDD_SerialUnit_SendBreak()` only on the immediate path, while the queued write-empty handler treats zero-length requests as complete after `HIDD_SerialUnit_Write(..., 0)` and never resets or assigns `io_Error` (`serial_init.c:823-843`; `serial_interrupthandlers.c:149-162,177-195`). The checked PC, Sam440, OpenSBI, m68k-Amiga and hosted Unix HIDD `SendBreak()` methods all return `SerErr_LineErr` (`PC:430-437`; `Sam440:344-348`; `OpenSBI:418-425`; `m68k:292-299`; `Unix:510-519`). Thus queued `SDCMD_BREAK` can bypass the unsupported result and complete without a break; if the caller entered with `io_Error == 0`, it appears successful. Positive `io_Length` routes the request buffer through ordinary `Write()`. A zero-length write can still send one byte on the PC, Sam440 and OpenSBI backends under the separately reported OD839, so its precise data effect is backend-dependent. OD3661 was refined with this result distinction; no request, interrupt or output was exercised. Source-only.

After the host library is loaded, a failed `libusb_init()` returns without cleanup; after successful bridge setup, unit-allocation failure also returns from Init without closing the handle. The latter additionally leaves initialized libusb/callback state, but no callback execution or retry behavior is asserted. Rhine SANA-II success-output caller qualification (OD3105 retained; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): traced the checked-in AROSTCP `S2_TRACKTYPE` setup in `sana_run()` and its `S2_ONLINE` request path in `sana_online()` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:481-509,857-870`) against Rhine's successful wire-error stores (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/request.c:721-790,1214-1252`). PCI ATA controller-class and no-bus ownership pass (OD10000 added; 2026-10-27): verified `ata_pci_controllerclass.c` is selected by `rom/hidds/ata_pci/mmakefile.src`, read its full 54-line body (40 `cloc 2.06` C lines), and traced its retained `aHW_Device` pointer through the PCI ATA probe, `PCIDeviceRef` channel reference counts, and final-bus destructor release. The probe claims a PCI device before checking channel BARs; reference counts are incremented only after an eligible channel record is allocated. No path releases ownership when no record is accepted, and the controller class has no Dispose override while its generated library config is `noexpunge`. This is one previously unrepresented selected C path; no cumulative coverage checkpoint is recomputed because the latest report-wide represented-scope denominators require reconciliation. No PCI scan, BAR, allocation failure or runtime claim was exercised; source-only.

<a id="vmware-nouveau-crtc-init-rollback-od10007"></a>
VMware/Nouveau DRM CRTC initialization rollback recheck (OD10007 added; 2026-10-27; no new path/LOC credit): re-read the complete selected `drm_crtc.c` implementation and traced the CRC init failure through mode-object unregister, CRTC list publication/counting, normal cleanup, the VMware LDU constructor unwind, and Nouveau NV04/NV50 constructors. Confirmed `drm_crtc.c` is byte-identical across the two selected copies. Under `CONFIG_DEBUG_FS`, `kstrdup("auto")` can fail after list insertion/count increment; the error branch unregisters only the ID. VMware propagates the error and frees the containing display unit without `drm_crtc_cleanup()`, leaving a dangling CRTC list node; added OD10007. Nouveau constructors ignore the init return, so their post-failure behavior remains a separate caller-path follow-up rather than being folded into the confirmed VMware sequence. The earlier coverage-table statement that no selected-path defect was established is superseded by OD10007. No allocation failure, display initialization, build, or device operation was run; source-only.


OD10007 Nouveau caller-path closure (2026-10-27; same finding, no path/LOC credit): traced the `CONFIG_DEBUG_FS` CRTC CRC-source allocation failure through both selected Nouveau display generations. NV04 `nv04_display_create()` discards the return from one or two `nv04_crtc_create()` calls and later walks `mode_config.crtc_list` to call each CRTC's save callback (`dispnv04/disp.c:247-250,297-299`); `nv04_crtc_create()` itself discards `drm_crtc_init_with_planes()`'s error before continuing (`dispnv04/crtc.c:1333-1340`). NV50 `nv50_head_create()` likewise ignores that error and returns its head; `nv50_display_create()` accepts the head and continues (`dispnv50/head.c:606-628`; `dispnv50/disp.c:3098-3128`). Thus Nouveau's affected path is confirmed as continued use of a partially published CRTC with an unregistered ID and stale list/count state, distinct in caller consequence from VMware's free-after-error dangling pointer but covered by OD10007's shared core rollback defect. The Nouveau aggregate edge remains commented, so no default-image claim is made. No allocation failure, display init, build, or device operation was run; source-only.

<a id="nouveau-nv04-flip-event-construction-failure-unwind-od10008-added-2026-10-27"></a>
Nouveau NV04 flip-event construction failure unwind trace (OD10008 added; 2026-10-27): confirmed `dispnv04/disp.c` is selected by `workbench/hidds/nouveau/sources.drm.mak:87`. `nv04_display_create()` publishes its `vzalloc()`ed private display before `nvif_event_ctor()` and returns directly on event-construction failure. The outer `nouveau_display_create()` performs only poll and mode-config cleanup on this return; the DRM load failure path skips `nouveau_display_destroy()` and eventually releases only the DRM/Nouveau device structures. Thus both separately allocated display objects lack a freeing path for this failure. Added OD10008. The adjacent NV04 CRTC-init error propagation remains covered by OD10007. No allocation/event failure, GPU probe, build, or hardware operation was induced; source-only.

A valid one-line vertical blank with a one-line sync therefore reaches the unsigned `u32` subtraction by two. Confirmed the stored result is `u16` and `HEAD_SET_RASTER_VERT_BLANK_DMI.DURATION` is 12 bits. Added OD10058 for fewer-than-two-line vertical blanking, where the claimed safe underestimate instead wraps and becomes an unrelated register value. No caller-side failure or rollback is present on this path. Added OD10059 for modesets continuing after all link-training attempts fail. The encoder atomic check reduces bpc to 6 without rejecting a still-over-capacity mode. Confirmed `nouveau_dp_train()` initializes its result to true and only clears it after attempting a candidate, so an over-capacity mode has zero link-training attempts yet reports success. These operations share queue/list and work-item state protected only by processor-local interrupt disabling; the workqueue process and GPU event context can run concurrently on different CPUs in ExecSMP. Added OD10069, limited to explicitly selected optional Nouveau HIDD builds on ExecSMP. The workqueue source already has full-body and path/LOC credit; counts are unchanged. No work item, event, GPU, interrupt or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau compatibility workqueue full concurrency/API recheck (OD10069 retained; 2026-10-27; no new finding or path/LOC credit): re-read all of `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_workqueue.c`, including worker dequeue/completion, initialization, queueing, delayed-work timer entry, flush/drain, cancel, tasklet adapters, and shared queue startup. Confirmed `Disable()` is explicitly CPU-local under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), so OD10069 covers both worker and producer accesses to `wq->items`, `work->state`, `wq->running`, and generation counters when calls overlap across CPUs. Traced additional API surfaces: threaded IRQ dispatch queues `thread_work` from interrupt context (`drm-compat/linux_irq.c:35-85`); scheduler workers use `queue_work` and flush/destroy adapters (`drm-compat/linux_sched.c:500-540`); tasklet and RCU work delegate to the same queue; delayed-work timer expiry also calls `queue_work`. This confirms selected callers share the same unsynchronized queue core, without establishing a separate root cause. `cancel_work_sync()`/`cancel_delayed_work_sync()` perform cancel then polling flush; API contract requires callers to stop concurrent requeue before cancellation, and no selected caller violating that precondition was established in this pass. `destroy_workqueue()` assumes producers are quiesced during teardown; selected teardown callers were not exhaustively re-traced here. No interrupt, cancellation race, work callback, device, or build was run; source-only.

PCIPC and PCI xHCI configuration/caller reconciliation (OD3369 confirmed; 2026-10-27; no new finding or path/LOC credit): checked PC boot manifests, the USB parent makefile, and architecture-specific HIDD routing. At this pass the x86-64 boot manifest dependency chain was read as excluding `USBHardware/pcixhci`, and the RPi/RISC-V package edges were checked. This selection interpretation was corrected on 2026-11-07: the active `#MM` metadata rules include PCI xHCI in the x86-64 USB package, with PCIPC. Consequently, x86-64 PC belongs in the affected-configuration review for xHCI findings whose code path is otherwise applicable; the correction is recorded below. Separately rechecked xHCI's selected failure chain: `xhciInit()` registers the embedded reset callback, attempts PCI interrupt registration, may start worker tasks, and has fatal-status/halt returns without full teardown; `pciAllocUnit()` then releases PCI ownership without `pciFreeUnit()` and also fails to unwind any earlier initialized controller in the same grouped unit; `Open_Unit()` closes only the timer and returns failure. This matches existing OD3369's trigger and cleanup scope. No package was built, PCI device mapped, or controller/IRQ/task exercised; source-only.

PCI xHCI worker-startup failure and interrupt caller pass (OD10070 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-27): traced both `psdSpawnSubTask()` results in `xhciInit()` through the Poseidon helper's NULL returns on `CreateNewProcTags()`, allocation, or `AddTask()` failure (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:4146-4161`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1433-1465,1481-1510`). Neither failed spawn aborts controller initialization. The completion interrupt later unconditionally signals the event task (`xhci_hcd.c:2950-2958`), and the port-change path unconditionally signals the port task (`:3378-3386`); Exec `Signal()` dereferences its task argument without a NULL check (`rom/exec/signal.c:262-270,296-306`). Added OD10070 for the conditional later interrupt-time NULL dereference after worker startup failure. The separate fatal-controller startup cleanup remains OD3369. At this pass package reconciliation checked Raspberry Pi AArch64 and RISC-V only; the 2026-11-07 correction below adds x86-64 PC through the standard USB package and PCIPC. No task-creation failure or interrupt was induced; source-only.

USB and Bluetooth HID short-item signed-shift pass (OD10155 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-28): re-read both duplicated short-item decoders and traced the decoded bounds into USB variable-item signedness and report extraction (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2660-2690,2897-2899,3161-3172,4850-4897`; `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2004-2030`). The two-byte decoder shifts a signed `BYTE` left by eight for high bytes >=0x80, and the four-byte decoder shifts the high `UBYTE` by 24 after integer promotion to signed `int`; both expressions invoke undefined behavior for the stated inputs. A compiler-dependent decoded bound can then change `nhi_IsSigned` and the logical-range filter. This is distinct from OD3557's signed-range subtraction overflow and OD9471's report-field sign extension. Added OD10155 with compiler-dependent consequence qualification. The HID translation units already have full body credit in their inventories; this targeted caller/semantics pass adds no path/LOC credit. Optional Bluetooth HID and USB HID target selection is recorded in the finding; OpenSBI packages USB HID. No descriptor, device, compiler output or build was used; source-only.


USB HID collection-name allocation caller pass (OD9461 expanded; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-28): traced USB collection construction through name helpers, nested-collection inheritance, cleanup, and the settings GUI's report-list display hook (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:3048-3065,4509-4521`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:982-995`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.gui.c:585-590,1860-1888`). A NULL top-level name alone is not asserted to crash. This is the USB counterpart of Bluetooth OD9461's same unchecked-parent-name root cause; expanded the existing finding rather than assigning a duplicate ID. Atheros GPIO interrupt pin caller reconciliation (OD9729 strengthened; 2026-10-28; no body/LOC credit): traced the AR5211/AR5212 RF-kill call from EEPROM capability setup through reset and `EnableRfKill()` into the unguarded GPIO configuration/interrupt functions. HID signed short-item promotion and consumer recheck (OD10155 retained; 2026-10-28; no body/LOC credit): verified `LONG` is signed 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-39`), so the four-byte parser's promoted `UBYTE << 24` with a high byte >= 0x80 is not representable in the signed `int` intermediate on selected AROS targets; the two-byte parser explicitly shifts signed `BYTE`. Traced parsed logical bounds into `nhi_IsSigned` in both classes, then into USB `nProcessItem()` and Bluetooth `bHandleReport()`/`bProcessItem()`. Retain OD10155 with high confidence for the undefined expressions and conditional compiler-dependent decoded bounds; no runtime/compiler output was produced. USB HID Report ID collection-clone parent-chain pass (OD10167 added; 2026-10-28; no path/LOC credit): traced `nParseReport()`'s Report ID transition, collection clone loop, subsequent `EndCollection` and Main-item error path (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2698-2761,2792-2802,3080-3097,3447`; `nReadReports():2231-2244`). Verified `newnhc->nhc_Parent` is not assigned before the loop reads the next ancestor through the clone's parent field. Poseidon creates its allocation pool with `MEMF_CLEAR`, and `psdAllocVec()` uses `AllocPooled()` (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:124-125,315-367`); Exec's pool allocation passes the pool requirements to the block allocator and clears each allocated block for `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:83-94`; `rom/exec/memory.c:1183-1185,671-674`). Thus the first clone has a NULL parent and the ancestor loop stops. HID 1.11 permits nested collections and defines Report ID as a global item, so the described ordering is valid ([USB-IF HID 1.11](https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/hid1_11.pdf), §§6.2.2.6-6.2.2.7). Added OD10167 for the resulting parser rejection and report cleanup. USB HID remains optional outside the cited OpenSBI package route. No descriptor or device was processed; source-body credit is unchanged.

PCIUSB RTIso prefill error-path recheck (2026-10-28; no new OD or coverage credit): traced `cmdStartRTIso()` queue failures across the UHCI, OHCI, and EHCI queue helpers. The dispatch can return a queue error only when the HCI cannot obtain a free PTD; the helpers otherwise return `RC_OK`. `cmdAddIsoHandler()` prepares at least two PTDs (`requested_ptds` is clamped to >=2), initializes every slot, and registers the handler only after successful initialization. Thus on initial start the first prefill call has a free PTD and the second also has a free PTD; this does not establish a partial-prefill failure for a newly registered handler. Repeated START while the handler is already running may fail to find a free PTD, but the existing stream and its queued descriptors remain present, so no separate loss or leak was established. The related UHCI/OHCI DMA mapping and ignored-start-status issue remains OD3813. No USB operation, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.

Diskimage optional CUE WAVE reader full-body and selected CDDA caller pass (OD10174 added; 2026-10-28; no default-denominator credit): read all 187 physical lines / 141 `cloc 2.06` C lines of `workbench/devs/diskimage/audio/wave.c` and traced header detection, RIFF chunk traversal, format checks, data-chunk extent, close/error cleanup, and bounded/padded read behavior. Confirmed the selected CUE target builds this body (`plugins/mmakefile.src:82-87`); its parser records the WAVE data length, rounds an audio track's final extent to 2,352-byte sectors, and `CUE_ReadCDDA()` requests complete sectors through `AUDIO_read()`. When the AIFF/WAVE data extent is not sector-aligned, the readers assign the whole stream length as `read_length` at the final partial sector rather than subtracting the offset. If later RIFF/FORM chunks provide enough bytes, the read can pass the caller's sector buffer; AIFF also swaps the oversized amount, and the subsequent `length - bytes_read` padding count can wrap. Trailing chunk bytes can also be returned as audio even when they fit within the sector buffer. Added OD10174. This reviews a second of the 438 initially unledgered workbench-device paths; the current raw-gap count is 436. No image, CDDA request, memory boundary, or build was exercised; source-only.

ATA PCI DMA exact-4-GiB endpoint false-positive recheck (2026-10-28; no new OD or coverage credit): reviewed all `DMA_Setup()` callers and the complete `atapi_SendPacket()` DMA/PIO selection. `interface_dma.c:57` compares the exclusive end (`phy_mem + tmp`) against `0xffffffff`, so a span ending with the valid final byte `0xffffffff` is rejected. Thus this boundary produces neither an invalid PRD nor an established transfer failure in the checked callers; it only rejects DMA in direct ATAPI and falls back to PIO. Existing OD2996 remains the separate unchecked allocation-failure issue. `dma_Setup()`'s 257-entry allowance matches the per-table allocated capacity, and the separately checked LBA48 request bound does not establish a hardware descriptor-count violation. OD10180 UHCI big-endian address-trigger correction (2026-10-29; finding strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit): re-evaluated the exact 16-bit generic swap against the aligned physical address and PPC `LONGOUT` backend. `AROS_SWAP_BYTES_WORD_GENERIC` first assigns its input to `UWORD`, so a valid frame-list base `0x00001000` becomes `0x0010` before the 32-bit output; the defect does not require a base above 64 KiB. Confirmed PPC `outl` uses native `stw` and adds no LE conversion. Updated OD10180 to trigger on any nonzero valid 4 KiB-aligned frame-list base, with upper-bit loss noted as an additional effect for high addresses. The UHCI initializer has one nonzero `WRITEIO32_LE` caller; its other two callers write zero. No register write or controller was run; source-only.


OD10180 PPC bus-value clarification (2026-10-29; no new finding or coverage credit): followed the narrowed `0x0010` value through `LONGOUT`/PPC `outl` to the native `stw`. For a `0x00001000` frame-list address, this stores bytes `00 00 00 10`; the little-endian UHCI register reads `0x10000000`. The report now distinguishes the source-level 16-bit truncation from the byte order observed by the controller. No bus write or hardware behavior was run. Source-only.

PCIUSB grouped-controller initializer result/unwind follow-up (OD9548 expanded; 2026-10-29; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `pciAllocUnit()`'s sequential HCI initializer loop and its online publication, then checked each HCD's failure/registration ordering and `Open_Unit()` caller. The loop overwrites `allocgood` on each iteration and does not break after FALSE; a later TRUE can therefore hide an earlier failure, while every controller record remains in the grouping and final online-marking passes. OHCI's BAR-map failure returns FALSE after allocating/storing its private record and PCI schedule buffer; the failure branch only releases PCI ownership and leaves these allocations behind. A later successful HCD can both hide that failed OHCI and cause the unit to open; the opposite order remains the existing OD9548 path, where a later FALSE also leaves earlier successful HCDs un-torn-down. Expanded OD9548 to include partial failed-HCD cleanup, overwritten failure status, and the prior-success unwind gap. This targeted trace adds no full-body credit; the PCIUSB translation unit was already fully credited. No controller, BAR failure, allocation failure, open, or USB operation was induced; source-only.

OHCI initializer failure-ladder recheck (OD9548 expanded; 2026-10-29; no new path/LOC credit): read `ohciInit()` from private-state allocation through its final success/failure returns, then traced each FALSE result through `pciAllocUnit()` and `Open_Unit()`. The private record is published before `ALLOCPCIMEM()`. If PCI DMA allocation fails, control falls through to FALSE without freeing that record; if `MAPPCI()` fails after DMA schedule allocation, the function returns directly without freeing either. The open failure branch releases PCI ownership but does not call a partial-safe OHCI cleanup routine; normal `pciFreeUnit()` would call the hardware-register teardown and is not a safe direct substitute while `hc_RegBase` is NULL. Broadened OD9548's single-controller OHCI trigger to cover both allocator failure and BAR-map failure. The `ohci_hcd.c` body already has complete source-body credit. No allocation/mapping failure, controller, or open was induced; source-only.

PCIUSB fast config-wrapper and EHCI extended-capability walk caller pass (OD2981 expanded; 2026-10-29; no body/path/LOC credit): confirmed the PCIUSB target includes `rom/usb/pciusb/make.opts`, which defines both `__OOP_NOLIBBASE__` and `__OOP_NOMETHODBASES__`; therefore `USE_FAST_PCICFG` is selected. No device, query, controller open, or capability cycle was exercised; source-only.

UHCI initializer failure-ladder and PCI DMA deallocator comparison (OD10187 added; no new path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced `uhciInit()` from private-state allocation through `init_fail`, then compared its cleanup API with `ALLOCPCIMEM`/`FREEPCIMEM`, generic `PCIDriver::AllocPCIMem`/`FreePCIMem`, `AllocVec`/`FreeVec`, and the PCIUSB caller cleanup. The ISO-array failure frees the ordinary arrays correctly but passes the PCI driver's aligned `AllocVec` view to `FreeMem()` with the requested schedule size; generic `FreePCIMem()` must recover the saved backing pointer and call `FreeVec()`. Serial private-header, shared-opener and error-path recheck (OD58/OD1372 retained; OD10188 added; 2026-10-29): read all 145 physical lines / 83 `cloc 2.06` C/header code lines of `workbench/devs/serial/serial_intern.h`, checked each `SerialUnit` field against its selected users, and traced the generic serial module manifest and `Open`/`Close` vectors. Serial mouse test full-body and asynchronous-request teardown pass (OD10190 added; 2026-10-29): read all 502 physical lines of `developer/debug/test/serial/serialmousetest.c` and traced its read loop against Exec `AbortIO`/`WaitIO`/`CloseDevice` and generic serial `CMD_READ`, `AbortIO`, and `Close`. Serial.device overlapping-read queue recheck (OD10191 added; 2026-10-29): traced generic `CMD_READ` publication through `su_ActiveRead`/`su_QReadCommandPort`, the receive interrupt's completion and successor dequeue, `AbortIO()`, and the analogous `CMD_WRITE` admission path (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:361-444,527-543,872-903`; `serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-93`). When a read remains active, the next incomplete read overwrites `su_ActiveRead` instead of being enqueued. The receive handler subsequently copies/replies the replacement and obtains any successor only from the queue; the displaced request is not reachable by completion or active/queued AbortIO. Added OD10191. The generic serial module is explicitly buildable but its parent aggregate edge is commented out; no default-image inclusion is claimed. Checked-in client traces reviewed so far retain a single outstanding read per unit, so the trigger remains a concurrent public-client condition. No request, input, abort, or build was run; source-only.


Serial.device overlapping-read in-tree caller census (OD10191 trigger narrowed; 2026-10-29; no new finding or LOC credit): repository-wide searches for literal `serial.device`, DOSDrivers `SER0`/`SER1`, and serial request submissions identified the interactive serial test, serial mouse test, PPP serial wrapper, printer backend, `port-handler`, and `AUX0`/console-handler route; Bluetooth `btserial.device` is a separate device. The interactive serial test issues `DoIO()` for each CMD_READ; `serialmousetest` owns one request and waits before the next loop iteration; PPP maintains one `SerRx` and resubmits after completion; printer `pd_PRead()` waits on the selected IORequest before submitting its next read; and `port-handler` executes CMD_READ with synchronous `DoIO()` while processing its packet loop. These checked-in paths do not establish simultaneous pending CMD_READs on one generic serial unit. OD10191 therefore remains a concurrent public-client trigger; this does not establish that all external clients obey that pattern. No request or device was run.


AHI audio-mode iterator direct-caller census (OD4309 retained; 2026-10-29; no new finding or LOC credit): repository-wide exact-symbol search for `AHI_NextAudioID()` found the device's no-mode startup checks, `modeinfo.c` and `requester.c` enumerators, AHI Preferences `GetModes()`/`AHI_BestAudioIDA()`, the AddAudioModes refresh/remove loops, and two low-level examples. Checked each loop's starting ID: all begin with `AHI_INVALID_ID`; the requester and BestAudioID initialize their local `id`, and Preferences initializes it before the loop. The existing OD4309 trigger remains: another client removes the previously returned ID between independent iterator calls, after which the absent-ID scan advances onto the MinList tail sentinel and reads it as an audio-mode node. Existing selected removal sources include USB Audio teardown and AddAudioModes; no additional caller-specific root cause was established. No mode was added/removed and no iteration was run; source-only.

AHCI callout cancellation selected-SCSI caller pass (DISK-111 scope strengthened; no OD duplication/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced the published timeout-task pointer, cancellation, timeout callback, command completion, SCSI completion callback, CCB return/reuse, and port-worker timeout scan. Confirmed a schedule window where `callout_handler` has set `co_Task = NULL` but has not called the timeout function; `callout_cancel()` cannot abort or join it, `ahci_ata_cmd_done()` sees the unchanged CCB serial and clears timeout state, and `ahci_io_complete()` returns the CCB. The delayed callback then marks the old CCB slot expired; if a new command has reused and activated that slot, the worker can time out the new command. Non-`AROS_USE_LOGRES` builds also retain a `KKASSERT(TIMEOUT_RUNNING)` that normal completion clears before the late callback. This is a selected AHCI manifestation of the existing generic cancellation-lifetime finding DISK-111, not an independent OD. Distinct from OD3175’s port-signal snapshot/clear issue. Source-only; no interleaving or I/O was run.

OD3667 generic PCI prefetch-window width and caller recheck (2026-10-29; no new ID or body/LOC credit): re-read the PCI bridge getter/setter, the config-word helpers and register-offset definitions, and searched all checked-in uses of both generated attributes. The getter reads the low words only, shifts the complete `UWORD` result, and omits the separately defined upper registers; on values with bit 15 set the promoted signed shift also exceeds `int` range. OD3670 failed-later-BAR rollback and scan-lifetime recheck (2026-10-29; no new ID or source/LOC credit): re-read both `PCIInitialize()` loops, both identical `AllocPCIResource()` implementations, and their list lifetimes. Each successful BAR allocation mutates its free list and writes the address before a subsequent BAR may fail; that failure sets `cmd = 0`, disables the current function, and breaks only the current BAR loop without restoring earlier ranges. Mediator retains the reduced lists until the complete scan ends; Prometheus retains them in the instance until disposal. Later functions in the same scan therefore see reduced capacity. Qualified the impact to a multi-BAR function with earlier fitting and later failing BARs in a constrained window; no board or BAR sizing was exercised.

Timer arithmetic macro and public request caller census (2026-10-29; no new OD or path/LOC credit): searched all maintained C/C++/assembly sources for `ADDTIME`, `SUBTIME`, `CMPTIME`, `INCTIME`, timer unit/command constants, and `struct timerequest` consumers. The PC `EClockAdd` delta is bounded below 0x20000 ticks after a single 16-bit rollover adjustment, below the approximately 1.19M-tick EClock rate; therefore one subtraction in `INCTIME` suffices for the computed delta. `CMPTIME`'s negative result for `dest > src` agrees with the timer queue completion predicates. The timer public request layout and command constants match the selected implementations and direct in-tree request setup sites found by the census; no additional source-level mismatch established. Existing OD2537/OD1426/OD1427 and architecture-specific timer findings remain unchanged. Sonixcam RTIso zero-length completion cross-controller recheck (OD3816 expanded; 2026-10-29): revisited all maintained PCIUSB/xHCI RTIso request and completion paths. Confirmed the OHCI/EHCI noncompletion finding and UHCI zero-length TD exception. Added the xHCI case: xHCI setup copies selected RTIso fields but not `rtn_IOReq.iouh_Length`; the unit is allocated from a pool created with `MEMF_CLEAR`, so that fallback remains zero. `xhciQueueIsochIO()` retains the zero length and marks the PTD buffer-valid, `xhciStartIsochIO()` declines to queue it, and refill counts it as pending; after the available active transfers complete, these zero-length entries occupy the PTD slots without producing done callbacks. Confirmed xHCI sets `UHCF_RT_ISO` under `PCIUSB_WIP_ISO` and the AArch64 Raspberry Pi package selects the device; SonixcamTool remains an optional shell-app target. OD10210 metadata-layout and end-to-end read-path recheck (2026-10-29; no new finding or file/LOC credit): compared `MDSTrack` with public `CDTrack`; their fields through `sectors` match in order and type, so `MDS_GetCDTracks()`'s cast is not an independent layout defect (`plugins/mds.c:46-55,482-487`; `include/devices/diskimage.h:208-218`). Re-traced the MODE2 track fields through all consumers: SCSI READ TOC reads `audio` to choose data/audio control (`device/scsicmd.c:195-215`); `unit.c:531-537` forwards ordinary TDRead to `MDS_Read`, which rejects `audio == TRUE` and otherwise copies 2048 bytes from `track->offset + sector_index * sector_size + sync_size` (`plugins/mds.c:407-479`); READ CDDA accepts only `audio == TRUE` and 2352-byte sectors (`:490-534`; SCSI dispatch at `scsicmd.c:257-325`). MODE2/FORM1/FORM2 nodes are linked after `MEMF_ANY` allocation with `sync_size=0`, but those switch cases assign neither `audio` nor a mode-specific sync offset or size validation (`mds.c:269-307`). Thus with 2352-byte sectors, a false audio value copies from byte zero rather than the 24-byte MODE2 header offset, while a true value misclassifies data sectors as CDDA; READ TOC can likewise label them inconsistently. This confirms OD10210's source consequence and keeps manifestation conditional on allocator contents and the optional plugin target. No MDS image or I/O was exercised; source-only.

UIF table-count width and allocation-wrap recheck (OD10211 retained; 2026-10-29; no body/LOC credit): verified `blhr_t.num` and `UIFImage.num` are `ULONG`, decoded directly from the on-disk field, while packed `blhr_data_t` is 24 bytes (`UQUAD` plus four `ULONG`s; `workbench/devs/diskimage/plugins/uif.c:115-127,151-158,210,229`). On the declared m68k-only plugin target, the 32-bit multiplication `sizeof(*data) * image->num` can wrap before allocation; the later descriptor loop still uses the full `image->num`. Separately, `Inflate()` returning `Z_STREAM_END` does not establish that `total_out == out_size`, so the short-table case remains distinct and supported. This confirms OD10211's two table-consistency paths; no finding or file/LOC credit changed. Source-only; no image, decompressor, allocation failure, or build was used.

UIF sector-total overflow consumer recheck (OD10212 retained; 2026-10-29; no body/LOC credit): followed decoded descriptor `out_size` through the 32-bit `total_blocks` accumulation and per-descriptor sector-to-byte multiplication, then through `total_bytes = total_blocks * block_size` into `UIF_Geometry()` and `UIF_Read()`'s offset check/hash selection (`workbench/devs/diskimage/plugins/uif.c:261-282,345-353,367-380`). With 2048-byte blocks, 2,097,152 sectors fit `ULONG` but represent exactly 4 GiB; the byte product wraps in 32-bit arithmetic before assignment to `UQUAD`, so geometry reports the sectors while reads see a zero total-byte limit. The descriptor-byte product can likewise wrap before the hash-offset walk. This confirms OD10212's exact threshold and consumer mismatch; no new ID or coverage credit. Optional m68k plugin only; no image or read was exercised. Source-only.

<a id="nouveau-gf100-context-generator-full-body-pass"></a>
Nouveau GF100 shared context-generator full-body and timeout-sequencing pass (OD10261 expanded; 2026-10-30): confirmed `drm/nouveau/nvkm/engine/gr/ctxgf100` is selected by `workbench/hidds/nouveau/sources.drm.mak:300`. Read the complete 1,587-line body (1,420 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), including the static register-pack tables, topology-derived alpha/beta and ROP mapping helpers, floorsweep generation, generated context buffer programming, FECS/FE power sequencing, firmware/no-firmware current-channel setup, unload/golden-save, and cleanup. Traced the shared generator callback and context-image publication through `gf100_gr_chan_new()`; its mutex serializes initial generation, and `gr->data` is retained only after the generator returns success. Rechecked OD10261: `gf100_gr_wait_idle()` has three ignored results in the generic main callback, plus the previously documented ignored no-firmware current-channel `nvkm_msec()` timeout. Expanded OD10261 with two more ignored bounded waits: `gf100_grctx_generate()` writes the FE force-on value and polls register `0x404170` before FECS reset, then writes the auto value and polls again before SCC RAM initialization (`ctxgf100.c:1444-1469`). The selected `nvkm_msec()` contract returns `-ETIMEDOUT` when its condition never breaks (`include/nvkm/subdev/timer.h:41-67`); both returns are discarded. A timeout therefore does not stop the following reset/context setup. The exact hardware consequence of a transition timeout is not established from source alone, so OD10261 retains medium confidence for malformed context-image consequences. Reviewed fixed table dimensions and the selected topology-derived indices; no additional bounded-table defect was established. Crediting this previously unrepresented selected source adds one path and 1,420 C/header code lines, advancing Other Drivers from 1,989/2,017 to **1,990/2,017 paths (98.7%)**, and from 928,032/1,259,999 to **929,452/1,259,999 C/header code lines (73.8%)**. No GPU, register, timeout, context, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

SDL event-task rollback and stack-backed interrupt recheck (GD2620 confirmed; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-traced `sdl_event_task()`'s automatic `tick_int` object through `AddIntServer(INTB_VERTB, &tick_int)` and the readiness signal (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:46-64`). `sdl_event_init()` waits for that signal before returning success (`:118-148`), and `startup.c` calls `sdl_event_expunge()` after either later `sdl_hidd_init()` or `sdl_Startup()` failure (`:275-300`). The expunge function calls `RemTask()` only (`event.c:151-155`). `NewCreateTaskA()` places the task stack in its task-owned memory list (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:23-32,246-251`), and `RemTask()` cleans that task context and frees the non-self task's memory entries (`rom/exec/remtask.c:115-128,165-180`). The VBlank interrupt list still holds the address because `RemIntServer()` is the operation that removes the node (`rom/exec/remintserver.c:58-63`); `IntServer()` later invokes the callback/data stored in each list node (`rom/exec/intservers.c:29-43`). This confirms GD2620's conditional stale stack-node/task consequence after a post-readiness SDL startup failure. The SDL source bodies and shared Exec interrupt/task files were previously credited; this pass adds only cross-area lifecycle evidence. No task, VBlank, startup failure or interrupt was run; source-only.

ATA `ATA=poll` stale-handler reply-lifetime recheck (OD9744 expanded; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced the selected PIO read/write vectors into `ata.c` command dispatch. The PIO vectors set their full byte count on successful `ata_exec_blk()` return (`lowlevel.c:1938-1993,2028-2083,2118-2173,2208-2263`); `cmd_Read32()` copies that count into `io_Actual` (`ata.c:53-99`). Read/write commands take the slow path (`isSlow()`, `:768-784`) and the bus task sends `ReplyMsg()` immediately after `HandleIO()` returns (`:1148-1157`). Since the poll path can return while `ab_HandleIRQ` remains installed (`lowlevel.c:515-553,567-571,779-785`), a later IRQ dispatched before a new command replaces the callback can invoke the stale PIO handler after reply; a read handler uses the retained `au_cmd_data` destination (`lowlevel.c:216-242`). Expanded OD9744 to include this conditional post-reply buffer mutation. The primary incomplete-transfer trigger remains conditional on a missing/delayed data-phase IRQ; no assumption that every `ATA=poll` request fails is made. No request, buffer reuse, interrupt, or device was exercised; source-only.

ACPICA cold-start resident and timer-request handoff pass (OD2621 detail restored; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the `acpica.post` and `acpica.timer` declarations and callbacks in the already credited `arch/all-native/acpica/acpios_aros.c` body. Resident sorting is descending by priority (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:105-120`), so priority 119 post setup runs before priority 49 timer setup; post setup launches the priority 127 init task (`acpios_aros.c:1121-1225`), and `TaskLaunch()` can reschedule to a higher-priority task (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:25-80,325-327`). `AcpiOsInitialize()` creates the timer request and only opens it if the timer flag is already set; the later timer resident sets that flag only after successful `OpenDevice()`. `AcpiOsSleep()`/`AcpiOsStall()` ignore `DoIO()` results, while `DoIO()` returns immediately on a null `io_Device` (`acpios_aros.c:112-133,288-310`; `rom/exec/doio.c:58-68`). Therefore delay calls in the pre-open interval, and after a failed timer open, do not delay. Restored the existing OD2621 candidate in the detailed report and index; OD9780 remains distinct for a successfully opened timer request where `Stall` waits and yields. The OSL body already has complete path/LOC credit. No ACPICA operation, timer open, firmware method, or boot was performed; source-only.

<a id="dosboot-menu-geometry-size-overflow-pass"></a>
DOSBoot menu geometry-size caller pass (OD10495 added; 2026-10-31; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `populateGadgets_PageBoot()`'s size display in the full-body-reviewed `rom/dosboot/menu.c:215-458` and traced entry through the selected `bootmenu_Init()` early-menu path (`:948-1005`; `dosboot_init.c:235`). Confirmed it uses a mounted startup `DosEnvec` only after the device opens and reports media present (`menu.c:268-294,320-342`), then computes the cylinder/head/blocks product at `IPTR` width before assigning to `UQUAD size` (`:357`). `DosEnvec` defines these members as `IPTR` and imposes no narrower value type (`compiler/include/dos/filehandler.h:29-44`); on 32-bit builds, a valid geometry above `UINT32_MAX` blocks wraps before the later scale/format path. Added OD10495 for the resulting incorrect displayed capacity. The existing body credit is unchanged; the finding is conditional on a large geometry and early-menu entry. No device, menu, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="dosboot-gadtools-open-failure-pass"></a>
DOSBoot GadTools-open failure caller pass (OD10496 added; 2026-10-31; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the early-menu call from `bootmenu_Init()` through `initScreen()`, `initWindow()`, and the selected GadTools calls (`rom/dosboot/menu.c:796-854,856-879,948-976`). Confirmed `TaggedOpenLibrary(TAGGEDOPEN_GADTOOLS)` may return NULL and does not perform its resident-init fallback because that code is disabled (`rom/exec/taggedopenlibrary.c:89-111`); `initWindow()` stores the result and immediately calls the `GetVisualInfoA()` GadTools vector without checking it. Confirmed `GetVisualInfoA()` is a GadTools vector and documents NULL only as its result for invalid screen/allocation, not as a NULL-base API (`workbench/libs/gadtools/getvisualinfoa.c:18-39`). The RISC-V OpenSBI package selects both DOSBoot and GadTools (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-120`); this is a failure-path issue, not a claim that GadTools is normally absent. The full DOSBoot body was credited earlier; no path/LOC change. No library-open failure, menu, or build was induced; source-only.

DOSBoot `TD_CHANGESTATE` media-state caller reconciliation (no new OD; 2026-10-31): traced the menu's `OpenDevice()`/`DoIO(TD_CHANGESTATE)` result test (`rom/dosboot/menu.c:320-342`) against the DOSBoot-selected RISC-V OpenSBI package backends. NVMe and VirtIO classify their nonremovable media as present with `io_Actual = 0` (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_io.c:305-309`; `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_io.c:195-199`); USB MassStorage reports zero only when `MSF_DiskPresent` is set and one otherwise (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_device.c:99-102`). The menu's `io_Actual == 0` test is consistent with these selected backends; no new media-state mismatch established. ATA/SCSI/SD and floppy implementations also use zero for present and one for absent, but are not selected by this RISC-V BSP device list. No device request or menu was run; source-only.

<a id="dosboot-menu-failure-cleanup-pass"></a>
DOSBoot failed-page retry and page-list cleanup pass (OD10497 added; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the already fully read `rom/dosboot/menu.c` failure exits and their caller. `initWindow()` leaves `newpage == -1` when gadget construction fails or `OpenWindow()` returns NULL; `initScreen()` assigns that result to `page` and continues until one of only two explicit boot-exit values is returned (`:796-854,862-875`). Confirmed `populateGadgets()` dispatches the Boot Options population even when footer gadget creation has made its gadget pointer NULL (`:513-539`); the page can therefore allocate `bootList` and `devicesList` nodes before returning failure (`:244-263,298-318`). `freeGadgets_PageBoot()` is called only in the successful-window branch (`:837-851`), so those nodes are lost on this failed attempt. The next retry receives page `-1`, so the list leak is limited to the failed Boot Options attempt; the persistent setup failure still prevents the menu call from returning. Added OD10497 to the detailed report and index. No body/path/LOC credit because `menu.c` was already fully reviewed. `bootmenu_Init()`'s result is ignored by `dosboot_init.c`, allowing a terminal menu failure return to continue normal boot preparation. No gadget/window failure or boot was induced; source-only.

Added OD10498 for returning the queried task and current effective-owner login instead of the session leader and stored login; OD10499 for substituting effective IDs for a remote task's separately maintained real IDs; and OD10500 for returning a successful group with an empty member list when the user-info allocation fails. UserGroup nobody-owner credential caller pass (OD10501 added; no path/LOC credit): traced `getcredentials(NULL)` through the security adapter, `secGetTaskExtOwner()` and its NULL-if-nobody contract. Confirmed a selected transition: `Logout QUIET` targets the current task by default, and when no owner can be restored, `secLogoutA()` sets its owner to NULL and leaves the session. The adapter maps that valid state to EINVAL, although the public UserGroup contract reserves EINVAL for an illegal task pointer. Added OD10501 for the resulting failed credential query. This is distinct from OD10498–OD10499, which concern incorrect fields after an owner record is returned. The `usergroup_security.c` body already has full credit, so this caller pass adds no path or C/header LOC credit. No logout or credentials call was run; source-only.


UserGroup nobody-owner `getgroups()` caller pass (OD10502 added; no path/LOC credit): compared the security-backed group enumeration branch with the documented `getgroups()` result/errors and legacy `getgroups(0, NULL)` behavior. `ugSecGetGroups()` obtains an extended owner before processing `ngroups`; it returns ENOENT when `secGetTaskExtOwner()` returns NULL. Confirmed that the documented NULL case includes a valid task owned by nobody and that `Logout QUIET` can select that state for the current task. Added OD10502 for returning -1/ENOENT on a valid nobody-owned current task. The precise expected group count for nobody is left unresolved because `ugSecGetGroups()` includes the primary group (`usergroup_security.c:118-133`), consistent with `cr_gid == cr_groups[0]` and `initgroups()` including basegroup (`credential.h:31`; `initgroups.c:38-41,70`). It shares the owner-state trigger with OD10501 but affects the separate `getgroups()` result contract. `usergroup_security.c` already has full-body credit; no new path or LOC credit. No logout or group query was run; source-only.

<a id="rtl8139-multicast-range-list-concurrency-pass"></a>
RTL8139 multicast RX filter and range-list synchronization pass (OD10503 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced `S2_ADDMULTICASTADDRESS`/`S2_DELMULTICASTADDRESS` through the selected unit-task request dispatch to `AddMulticastRange()`/`RemMulticastRange()`, then traced the receive IRQ into `RTL8139_RX_Process()` and `AddressFilter()`. Rejected the apparent default-mode zero multicast hash as a separate defect: adding the first software range sets `IFF_ALLMULTI` and reprograms the NIC to accept all multicast frames, after which `AddressFilter()` enforces the registered ranges (`rtl8139_init.c:367-372`; `unit.c:243,721-757,1236-1276`; `rtl8139.c:323-330,527-575`). Found OD10503 instead: the IRQ traverses the range list without the unit semaphore, while deletion uses only `Disable()` around `Remove()` and immediately frees the node (`unit.c:1279-1306`); Exec documents `Disable()` as processor-local under ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-59`). The unit worker processes requests under `rtl8139u_unit_lock` but the RX interrupt handler does not acquire it (`unit.c:512-570,857-886`). Qualified the trigger to an overlap where the worker and IRQ execute on different CPUs; the PC IOAPIC defaults to boot-CPU delivery absent a mapping (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_ioapic.c:408-430`), and the worker is created without an explicit affinity tag and inherits its creator's mask (`unit.c:1089-1096`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:126-165`). No checked-in caller proving the exact remote placement was found, so report confidence is medium for occurrence. The RTL8139 main source already has full-body credit; no path or line-count change. No multicast request, interrupt, or build was run; source-only.


NVMe sparse namespace startup-scan finding recheck (OD2840 retained and narrowed; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-traced the selected `nn` value through `NVMEBus__Root__New()`'s `UWORD ab_UnitMax` storage and the serial CNS=0 Identify Namespace loop, confirming the separate >65,535 truncation remains OD2594. Checked the NVMe Base Specification Revision 1.4c §5.15.2.3: it explicitly permits either probing each valid NSID or using the Active Namespace ID List (CNS 02h), so OD2840 is not a protocol-compliance defect. Retained it only as a conditional startup-scalability concern: a large maximum NSID and sparse active set cause sequential admin commands, but no unacceptable delay bound is established. The NVMe files already have source-body credit; no path or LOC total changes. No controller, Identify command, or build was run; source-only.

BWFM SDPCM receive-header field and TX-credit pass (2026-10-31; no OD or body/LOC credit): traced all selected inbound SDPCM paths through `bwfm_dcmd()`, `bwfm_rx_read()`, `bwfm_rx_glom()`, and `BWFMRxFrame()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:877-997,1074-1101,1200-1337,2210-2250`). The ordinary receive and control-response paths copy `sw->maxseqnr` to `bwfm_txmax`; glom processing refreshes it from each subframe, matching the TX-credit consumer's serialized `bwfm_txseq`/`bwfm_txmax` check (`:941,1098,1287,2150-2180`). The host writes `seqnr`, zero `nextlen` and zero `flowctl` only on outbound control/data frames (`:900-905,2180-2185`); inbound code does not validate or otherwise consume those three fields. The local SDPCM header declares their layout but supplies no semantic contract or resynchronization rule. Therefore this pass does not establish that omitted receive-sequence checking or ignored flow-control fields violate the selected firmware protocol; sequence continuity, flow-control semantics, and recovery after SDIO transfer failure remain explicitly open pending a protocol contract. Existing OD3590/3591 framing candidates and the earlier TX-credit analysis are unchanged. No frame, SDIO operation, firmware or build was used; source-only.

OD3036 RTL8139 affinity-condition recheck (2026-10-31; no new OD or LOC credit): re-read `CreateUnit()` and the unit-process `CreateNewProcTags()` call (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/unit.c:1089-1096`), the public `NP_Affinity` contract (`compiler/include/dos/dostags.h:91-97`), `createnewproc.c` tag defaults/dispatch (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:149,183-184,535-546`), `Exec_InitETask()` mask inheritance/current-CPU fallback (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:126-165`), and PC IOAPIC target default (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_ioapic.c:408-430`). The unit task has no explicit affinity; it inherits the creator mask, and a missing parent mask pins it to the CPU that created it. Refined OD3036 trigger: cross-CPU list overlap requires a creator mask including a CPU other than the interrupt target (or TASKAFFINITY_ANY), or a later affinity change. A single-CPU creator mask matching the IRQ CPU does not establish a remote race. No maintained caller demonstrating the required remote placement was found; retained the race as conditional with that qualification. Existing source bodies and counts unchanged; no device, affinity change or interrupt was run. Source-only.

VirtIO block I/O full-body and OD2805 arithmetic recheck (2026-10-31; OD2805 narrowed; no path/LOC credit): read the complete 291-line `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_io.c` body and traced BeginIO request publication/removal, quick and non-quick completion, read/write/format 32-/64-bit offset assembly, alignment checks, queue submission, flush/feature handling, device-query bounds, geometry output, change-interrupt behavior and AbortIO. Reconciled selected request completion with `virtio_process_used()` and queue/descriptor ownership (`virtio_queue.c:154-244,246-296`), and unit capacity/sector setup (`virtio_busclass.c:147-160,217-260`). Rechecked OD2390/OD2396, OD2604, OD2704 and OD2805 against the full BeginIO/helper path; no additional independent defect established. Corrected OD2805’s overly broad trigger: capacity mismatch requires `floor(blk_size / 512)` to be non-power-of-two (for example, 1536 gives quotient 3 while `au_SecShift` exposes 1024-byte units). A non-power-of-two value such as 520 gives quotient 1 and does not produce the stated capacity loss. VirtIO 1.2 §5.2.5 describes `blk_size` as an optimal sector-size hint and does not impose a power-of-two rule ([OASIS VirtIO 1.2](https://docs.oasis-open.org/virtio/virtio/v1.2/virtio-v1.2.html)). The selected VirtIO controller’s existing OD2541 still blocks ordinary in-tree unit publication. Existing full-body/path credit stands; no device, request, or build was run. Source-only.

DiskImage Generic write zero-progress backend reconciliation (DISK-043 strengthened; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): rechecked the already body-reviewed `workbench/devs/diskimage/plugins/generic.c:189-211` against the built-in Generic registration and write dispatch (`device/plugins.c:37-50,155-188`; `device/unit.c:530-554`). Confirmed the unit worker synchronously calls `Plugin_Write()` while processing a request and sends the reply only after the plugin returns (`unit.c:312-424`). Traced a checked-in backend: Generic opens its backing file with `Open(..., MODE_OLDFILE)` (`unit.c:538-566`); RAMFS `WriteData()` attempts `AddDataBlock()` when the current block is exhausted. If allocation fails before copying any byte, `AddDataBlock()` sets `ERROR_DISK_FULL`, `WriteData()` returns zero, `CmdWrite()` sends that count as the `ACTION_WRITE` result, and DOS `Write()` returns it unchanged (`rom/filesys/ram/filesystem.c:876-944,1280-1322`; `rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:637-665`; `rom/filesys/ram/handler.c:181-184`; `rom/dos/write.c:24-45,57-75`). Thus a writable Generic image backed by `RAM:` can hang the unit worker when a write extends a full RAMFS block and allocation fails; if bytes are written before a later allocation failure, the remaining Generic write loop also stalls. This strengthens DISK-043's existing zero-progress clause, shared with DISK-024; it is not a separate finding. The Generic body was already fully credited, so no path or C/header LOC increment. No image write, RAM exhaustion, request, or build was run; source-only.

OD3887 request-node and queued-softint lifetime recheck (strengthened; no new OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-read the USB mass-storage unit's two change-interrupt traversals (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:1415-1423,4013-4030`), `devBeginIO()` removal and completion (`dev.c:222-228,308-318`), Exec `DoIO()` (`rom/exec/doio.c:68-73`), and `Cause()`/`SoftIntDispatch` (`rom/exec/cause.c:82-122,160-188`). The worker calls `Cause(ioreq->io_Data)` and then re-reads `ioreq->ln_Succ`; removal only unlinks the request and replies, and `DoIO()` waits for that command reply without synchronizing with the separate unit-task traversal. Thus the request node itself can be freed after removal while still held as the worker's current node. The callback `Interrupt` has a separate queued lifetime: `Cause()` places it on Exec's global softint list, and `TD_REMCHANGEINT` does not cancel/drain that queue. PFS3 explicitly frees both the removal request and callback node after `DoIO()` (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/init.c:393-406`); FAT/NTFS also complete device cleanup after their removal requests. This strengthens OD3887's existing ExecSMP timing/lifetime claim; no new ID, source-body credit, or path/LOC increment. No request, callback, media change, or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.

Exec's selected `CreateIORequest()` explicitly returns NULL for a NULL reply port (`rom/exec/createiorequest.c:57-76`); `OpenAHI()` then skips `OpenDevice()` and calls `DeleteMsgPort(mp)`, whose selected implementation is NULL-tolerant (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:48-56`). A non-NULL port followed by request-allocation failure takes the same cleanup and releases the port. No leak, NULL dereference, or unacknowledged startup issue is established on these branches. These bodies were already credited; no path or C/header LOC change. No allocation failure or device open was induced; source-only.

OpenSBI PCIDT vector contract and caller census refresh (OD3521 retained conditionally; 2026-10-31; no new finding or file/LOC credit): reread the public `GetVectorAttribs` and `ObtainVectors` documentation and the complete PCIDT methods plus `PCIDT_MSIEnable`. `ObtainVectors` does not inspect the minimum or maximum tags, configures exactly one MSI message, and returns success; `GetVectorAttribs` ignores `vectorno` and returns the stored sole vector. OpenSBI PCIDT bridge-driver registration failure trace (OD10527 added; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): followed `PCIDT_InitClass()`'s one-registration-per-discovered-bridge loop through the deprecated PCI `VOID AddHardwareDriver` wrapper to generic `HW_AddDriver()`. The wrapper discards the generic method's nullable driver-object result; `HW_AddDriver()` returns NULL on driver-node allocation, driver construction, or setup failure, while `PCIDT_InitClass()` still returns TRUE after the loop. A failed construction does not advance `PCIDT__Root__New()`'s bridge selector, so successful later registrations may repeat an earlier bridge rather than cover all discovered bridges. Added OD10527 for the conditional missing/partial PCI bus registration and noted that OD1411 is the separate ignored kernel MSI-controller-registration result. This is a caller/error-propagation follow-up on already credited method bodies. No allocation failure, registration, boot, or PCI enumeration was run; source-only.

OpenSBI PCIDT MSI failure and module-lifetime recheck (OD1409/OD1411 retained; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the target page from `AllocMem()` through `PCIDT_MSIInit()` into `b->msiTarget`, then through both vector-allocation outcomes and `KrnModifyIRQA()` (`pcidt_driverclass.c:724-772`; `pcidt_access.c:363-379`). All-fail virtual allocation keeps `msiReady` false but loses the page pointer and leaves bridge MSI registers programmed; the 4 KiB page leak is direct, while no selected endpoint acquisition is enabled in that state. On controller-table exhaustion, the page and vectors remain attached to a bridge marked ready, so endpoint vector acquisition can succeed without registered fanout (OD1411). `pcidt.conf` selects `noexpunge`, and `PCIDT_Expunge()` has no successful selected module-removal route; this supports the findings' module-lifetime resource state rather than a missed normal cleanup callback. ACPI discovery sets `msiIrq` to zero and bypasses both branches. No page allocation, registration failure, endpoint, expunge or interrupt was run; source-only.

Keyboard reset-handler direct-caller census (OD14/OD2603/OD2389 retained; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): a repository-wide callsite search found every AROS `KBD_ADDRESETHANDLER`, `KBD_REMRESETHANDLER`, and `KBD_RESETHANDLERDONE` use. `input.device` installs its persistent stack-resident handler and acknowledges via a copied request on its worker task (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:141-209,578-603`); PFS3 keeps its reset request/handler until synchronous remove and free, and acknowledges after its reset signal (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/init.c:425-535`; `fs/boot.c:472-485,543-553`); optional VMM keeps its handler in the reset worker, can issue a second DONE after a later wake, and removes/frees through its reset helper (`workbench/system/VMM/pagehandler.c:582-633`; `reset_handler.c:65-150`). USB bootkeyboard, USB HID, and Bluetooth HID each add a temporary stack probe, read the list head, remove the probe, then traverse and `Cause()` the saved handler list after `Permit()` (`bootkeyboard.class.c:529-578`; `hid.class.c:6546-6602`; `bthid.class.c:5811-5868`); their captured traversal races are included in OD2603. No reset chord, worker wake, callback traversal, or build was run; source-only.

USB bootkeyboard/HID and Bluetooth's Ctrl+Alt+Delete paths manually walk/call reset handlers and reboot, rather than emitting this keyboard.device marker. This narrows reset-phase input to the PC and m68k HIDD paths for checked-in default mappings; custom/external HIDD events and hardware behavior remain unverified. No keyboard event, reset chord or build was run; source-only.

OD10520 fragment-shader allocation-failure callback reconciliation (no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): re-read the selected Mesa `i915_create_fs_state()` callback and its translator call (`src/gallium/drivers/i915/i915_state.c:569-618`; `i915_fpc_translate.c:1077-1098`). The callback's normal `NULL` return paths cover shader-object allocation failure and, when `report_compile_error` is set, a compiler error already stored in `ifs->error`; it checks that field only after `i915_translate_fragment_program()` returns. The translator calls `i915_init_compile()` without checking its result, continues into optimization/translation, and calls `i915_fini_compile()` before returning. Therefore the compile-context, error-string, and final program-buffer allocation failures described by OD10520 cannot reach the callback's cleanup/error return: they fault within the compiler path first. The registered callback assignment is `i915->base.create_fs_state = i915_create_fs_state` (`i915_state.c:1121-1123`). This confirms the selected error-propagation boundary and does not add a distinct defect or coverage credit. No allocation failure, shader compilation, GL call, GPU operation or build was run; source-only.

The complete `i915_resource_buffer.c` body is 156 physical lines / 101 C code lines. `i915_resource_destroy()` frees owned aligned buffers but leaves user buffers borrowed; transfer-map allocation failure returns NULL before publishing a transfer, and unmap releases the slab object. `i915_buffer_subdata()` and transfer-map pointer arithmetic rely on Gallium callers to supply an in-range extent; the selected utility wrappers assert that precondition, and this pass found no selected caller violating it. The selected `i915_set_constant_buffer()` temporarily wraps `cb->user_buffer`, retains the resource reference, and releases the temporary reference; allocation failure can clear the stored binding, but this void setter has no checked error return or caller-visible failure contract establishing a distinct defect. No runtime state, allocation failure, rendering, or build was exercised; source-only.

Mesa i915 resource-factory and handle caller recheck (no finding; 2026-10-31): read all 51 physical lines / 46 `cloc 2.06` C lines of the external `i915_resource.c` body. Traced screen resource creation/import and context buffer/texture map, unmap, and subdata callback installation. `resource_from_handle()` delegates non-buffer imports to `i915_texture_from_handle()`, whose generic implementation acquires the winsys buffer before validating the texture template; that ordering would require cleanup if the selected winsys returned a buffer for an unsupported template. The AROS IntelGMA provider's `IntelGMA_WS_BufferFromHandle()` always returns NULL, and `IntelGMA_WS_BufferGetHandle()` returns FALSE (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_galliumclass.c:520-539`), so that generic leak is not reachable through this selected target. No import, resource allocation, rendering operation, or build was run; source-only.
