USB Audio capture-buffer overlap build-graph and host-controller reconciliation (OD3228 retained; 2026-10-31; no new finding or path/LOC credit): confirmed `usbaudio.class` is selected by active `kernel-usb-classes-common` and `kernel-usb` build dependencies (`rom/usb/classes/audio/mmakefile.src:7-15`; `rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:10-19,35-42`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:8-15`). The checked RasPi AArch64, x86-64 PC and OpenSBI package class lists omit Audio, so package/runtime inclusion remains conditional on another package or explicit installation. Re-read the capture request/done hooks and checked their exact selected controller handoffs. xHCI copies the evolving request into each PTD, invokes the request hook per PTD, advances its stored pointer after the hook, and permits two pending PTDs; the hook resets both PTDs to `nam_USBBuffer[0]`, while event processing calls the done hook before replenishing the two-PTD target (`xhci_isoch.c:194-220,274-279`; `xhci_hcd.c:2777-2810`). OHCI and UHCI likewise invoke the hook per PTD and advance the stored request afterward; their selected paths prefill/replenish two requests, and the hook resets each destination to the same buffer (`ohci_isoch.c:213-253,322-331`; `uhci_isoch.c:237-270,341-349`). EHCI's completion path invokes the done hook before queuing/restarting the next one-packet request; the next-request hook therefore does not overwrite the completed packet before its callback (`ehci_isoch.c:250-282,391-416`). The generic PCI USB manifest selects OHCI/UHCI/EHCI, while PCI xHCI is separately selected in the RasPi AArch64 package; that package does not include USB Audio among its class list (`rom/usb/pciusb/mmakefile.src:4-18`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/mmakefile.src:4-20`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:217`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:61-65`). OD3228 remains supported for explicitly built USB Audio with xHCI, OHCI or UHCI; EHCI is excluded. No default RasPi USB Audio inclusion is claimed. This narrows configuration scope but does not change the report's existing finding. No controller, packet, callback delay, build or device was exercised; source-only.

PCI owner/removal finding caller and backend census (OD3885 rechecked; no finding-ID or path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced the selected PCI `EnumDevices()` lock interval (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-448`) against `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver()`'s exclusive `dev_lock` acquisition and owner scan/dispose (`:451-512`); in-tree PCI probe callbacks that claim with `HIDD_PCIDevice_Obtain()` during enumeration are serialized against removal. A broad call-site scan found one distinct in-tree retained-object API path: Prometheus saves callback PCI objects as `PCIBoard.aros_board` (`workbench/libs/prometheus/prometheus_init.c:45-56,85-107`) and `Prm_SetBoardAttrsTagList()` can claim/release that saved object outside enumeration (`workbench/libs/prometheus/board.c:275-298`). Removable PCI backend expunge hooks include Prometheus, Efika, Sam440 and hosted Linux (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/pci-prometheus/pci-prometheus_init.c:17-38`; `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/pci/pci_efika_init.c:17-40`; `arch/ppc-sam440/pci/pci_amcc440_init.c:17-40`; `arch/all-linux/hidd/pcilinux/pcilinux_init.c:76-105`). This confirms an in-tree-capable retained-claim/removal combination and refines OD3885; it does not establish that a normal client sequence overlaps the narrow scan-to-dispose window. No new defect or body/path/LOC credit; no enumeration, ownership operation, backend expunge or interleaving was run; source-only.
OpenDevice same-name serialization correction (OD2865, OD3113, OD3619, OD2152 and OD4264 withdrawn; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the selected public open path after noticing that `OpenDevice()` is patched by the base-ROM LDDemon resource (`rom/mmakefile.src:151`; `rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:895`). LDDemon's wrapper obtains a per-name `ldon_SigSem` before lookup/load and holds it through the saved Exec `OpenDevice()` call and the device Open vector, releasing only after that call returns (`lddemon.c:391-404,465-490,543-553`). Therefore the ordinary same-name OpenDevice calls assumed to overlap in the Rhine/Broadcom4400, PCNet32, BWFM and RTL8029 candidates are serialized. PCIUSB and PCI xHCI each enter `Open_Unit()` through their device Open callback (`pciusb_dev.c:134`; `pcixhci_dev.c:136`) and each keeps a separate unit list, so same-device first scans are serialized and the two different driver names do not share a list. Marked OD2865, OD3113, OD3619, OD2152 and OD4264 withdrawn in the detailed report. Direct calls that bypass the patched public vector were not established in-tree. Earlier dated ledger entries preserve discovery history; this correction supersedes their candidate conclusions. No device open, scan, firmware operation, or interleaving was run; source-only.

Additional LDDemon same-name Open serialization correction (OD9568, OD9923 and OD9931 withdrawn; OD3115 narrowed; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): extended the wrapper check to the RTL8139 first-start candidate, Prometheus-backed PCI network first-unit creation/reservation candidates, and Nvidianet exclusive-open candidate. All depended on overlapping calls to the same device Open vector, which the per-name semaphore prevents for ordinary public OpenDevice callers. Removed those claims from active candidate status. Re-read the LDDemon `CloseDevice()` wrapper (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:598-623`): unlike `OpenDevice()`, it does not take the per-name semaphore; it invokes the device Close vector under `Forbid()`, which remains CPU-local under ExecSMP. OD3115 is therefore narrowed to the remaining conditional new-Open versus final-Close teardown race in Prism2, Etherlink III PCI, Realtek8180 USB and the explicit Rhine PCI target. Same-name Open/Open races, duplicate initial unit creation and exclusive-open admission are withdrawn from OD3115; PC Card SMP reachability remains unestablished. No device open/close, unit teardown, or interleaving was run; source-only.
OpenDevice serialization follow-up (OD9965 withdrawn; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): the later BWFM package-selection correction established that `bwfm.device` is selected for Raspberry Pi packages, but OD9965 still assumed two ordinary same-name OpenDevice calls overlap inside its Open vector. The selected LDDemon per-name semaphore remains held through that callback (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:391-404,465-490,543-553`), so the stated first-open list-reset interleaving is unavailable through the checked public path. Marked OD9965 withdrawn; package selection alone does not sustain the race. No Open/Close or SMP schedule was run; source-only.
Prism2 Open versus final Close ordering recheck (OD3115 retained; 2026-10-31; no new OD or path/LOC credit): confirmed `workbench/devs/networks/prism2/mmakefile.src:7-10` explicitly builds `prism2.device` with `device.c` and `pci.c`, while the active cards aggregate selects `prism2` for i386, x86_64, m68k, and ppc (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-15,30-33,45-53`; `prism2/mmakefile.src:7-10`). Re-read the selected lookup, admission and teardown sequence: `DevOpen()` obtains a unit via `GetUnit()` before incrementing `open_count` (`device.c:248-260`); PCI `GetPCIUnit()` scans `pci_units`, creates on a miss, and publishes with `AddTail()` without shared synchronization (`pci.c:171-186,205-224`); `CloseUnit()` removes the opener under local `Disable()`, then decrements `open_count`, removes the unit at zero and calls `DeletePCIUnit()` (`device.c:545-573`). The concrete overlap is a cross-CPU Open that finds the unit after final Close observes the count reach zero but before `Remove()`/deletion completes; that Open can retain/use the object which Close then destroys. LDDemon's same-name Open semaphore remains held through the ordinary public Open vector (`lddemon.c:465-490,543-553`), so this recheck does not restore the withdrawn Open/Open claims. Its CloseDevice wrapper calls the close vector under `Forbid()` without that semaphore (`lddemon.c:598-623`); Exec documents `Forbid()` as processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). This supports OD3115 for an explicitly built Prism2 target on ExecSMP; it does not claim the commented network aggregate or a default-image route. No Open, Close, interrupt teardown, SMP schedule, or build was run; source-only.

PCI device-construction failure ownership cross-check (OD10528 strengthened; no new finding or path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced the selected PCIDT New method's pre-superclass interrupt masking (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_deviceclass.c:76-102`) through `OOP_DoSuperMethod()` to the generic PCI scanner's `OOP_NewObject()` call (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:71-95,153-165`). `OOP_NewObject()` returns the class New result directly and does not dispose an object when that result is NULL (`rom/oop/newobject.c:104-113`); the root New method returns NULL when its instance `AllocMem()` fails (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-131`). Thus, on the concrete PCIDT root-allocation failure path, the two configuration writes that mask MSI and INTx have occurred, no device object exists for RemoveDriver cleanup, and `InsertDevice()` returns NULL for the scanner to ignore. This independently confirms the conditional masked-and-omitted endpoint consequence in OD10528; it is not a separate finding. No allocation failure, config write, PCI scan, enumeration, or build was performed; source-only.


OD10514 IntelGMA/Mesa target-selection qualification (no new finding or path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): rechecked the build graph after confirming the state-tracker and i915 fence flow in the Mesa 26.0.0 source archive. `OPT_MESAGL` defaults to 26.0.0 (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa.cfg`), but the IntelGMA parent edge, Mesa-version edges, driver dependencies and i915 link-library dependency are commented out (`workbench/mmakefile.src:40`; `workbench/devs/monitors/mmakefile.src:9`; `workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/mmakefile.src:57-67`; `IntelGMA/i915/mmakefile.src:65-67`). The IntelGMA manifest explicitly says its glue targets Mesa 20's Gallium API and Mesa 26 changed interfaces (`IntelGMA/mmakefile.src:57-63`). Therefore OD10514 remains a source-confirmed conditional defect if the monitor/i915 path is explicitly assembled with a compatible stack, but Mesa 26.0.0 build applicability is unverified and no default/integrated build selection is claimed. Updated the report and master-index wording to carry this limitation. The Mesa source check reconfirmed `st_finish()` waits only when its flush returns a fence (`st_cb_flush.c:71-85`), i915 passes the fence output to the winsys (`i915_flush.c:39-59,75-81`), and the selected IntelGMA flush submits asynchronously without setting it (`intelgma_galliumclass.c:346-452`). No build, GL call, or GPU operation was performed; source-only.

Keyboard final-read reply lifetime and index reconciliation (OD3298 rechecked; index entry restored; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): reread `kbdSendQueuedEvents()`'s remove/reply/final flag-clear sequence (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:671-689`), the Close vector's `FreeMem(KBUnit)` path (`:237-256`), and Exec `ReplyMsg()` publication/signaling (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:60-64`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:83-106`). For a final pending request, after `ReplyMsg()` the owner can run on another ExecSMP CPU, return from its wait and close the device before the interrupt routine dereferences `ioreq->io_Unit` through `kbUn`. OD3298 remains a distinct post-reply unit-lifetime race; the stale per-unit pending flag alone remains unpromoted. Reconciled report headings against `AROS.md` and found OD3298 absent from the master index; restored its concise linked entry. Existing source bodies and path/LOC credit stand. No request, reply race, or CloseDevice call was induced; source-only.

<a id="keyboard-pending-read-empty-check-enqueue-race-od2389-recheck"></a>
Keyboard pending-read empty-check/enqueue race recheck (OD2389 retained; no new candidate or path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): replayed the two-CPU ordering against the current `KBD_READEVENT` and HIDD callback bodies. BeginIO compares the per-open read cursor with `kb_writePos` before adding the request (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:362-372`); the callback advances `kb_writePos`, then checks whether `kb_PendingQueue` is empty before invoking its drain (`:621-646`). Since both paths use only local `Disable()` and Exec explicitly states this does not exclude other CPUs (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), a callback can publish and skip the drain between the empty comparison and request insertion. The selected input.device has one persistent read outstanding (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:521-530`), so its worker can remain blocked with the event buffered until another key callback. Rechecked that `kbdSendQueuedEvents()` returns `moreevents == FALSE` when that one-event read catches the writer, explaining why no deferred retry exists after the missed trigger. OD2389 already covers the race and wider unsynchronized list mutation; no second ID is warranted. The per-unit KBUF_PENDING stale-flag behavior remains non-reportable by itself, while the post-reply lifetime race remains OD3298. No event or interleaving was run; source-only.

SANA-II `S2_DMACopyFromBuff32` NULL-result fallback audit (OD9917 expanded; no new OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-read the complete nvidianet AROS adapter and TX callback path (`workbench/devs/networks/nvidianet/aros_device.c:295-307,377-417`; `unit.c:1635-1648`), then compared all eight selected AROS SANA-II adapters and their TX workers: Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, Etherlink III, Intel Pro/100, nvidianet, Prism2, Realtek8180 and Rhine. Each adapter replaces `ios2_Data` with the request pointer for queued write commands; its DMA wrapper restores `ios2_Data` to the caller's original packet pointer before invoking the optional DMA-copy hook. Each worker explicitly treats a NULL DMA result as the ordinary TX-copy fallback and passes `request->ios2_Data` as the fallback hook's request argument. Each AROS `TXFunction()` wrapper interprets that argument as `struct IOSana2Req *` to obtain the original callback metadata. Therefore a supplied DMA hook that returns NULL makes the fallback wrapper interpret the packet pointer as the request structure. Expanded OD9917 with this distinct manifestation of the same temporary-cookie substitution root; no separate ID or file/LOC credit. The public `S2_DMACopyFromBuff32` tag is declared in `compiler/include/devices/sana2.h:51`, but no checked-in opener using it was found, so this fallback trigger is scoped to external SANA-II clients. All eight driver implementations are explicitly buildable/selected only through their respective AROS targets; no default-image inclusion is inferred. No DMA callback, packet, request or build was used; source-only.

PCI xHCI RTIso stop versus event-task completion recheck (OD3517 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-read `cmdStopRTIso()` and the full selected xHCI RTIso stop/completion path (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:1665-1695`; `xhci_isoch.c:332-360`; `xhci_hcd.c:2433-2476,2701-2830`; `xhci_hw.c:498-540`). `cmdStopRTIso()` calls `xhciStopIsochIO()` synchronously, but the stop routine only frees periodic transfer contexts and clears PTD flags under `Disable()`; it does not signal or join the separate high-priority event task. That task calls `xhciHandleFinishedTDs()` and invokes RTIso hooks inline before `xhciFreePeriodicContext()` and its request/buffer-context cleanup. `xhciFinishRequest()` removes ring back-pointers and frees the transfer context, but there is no shared cross-task lock around the completion callback and stop-side free, nor any completion acknowledgement. This supports OD3517's conditional concurrent-completion lifetime path. It does not prove that every stop interleaving reaches a callback after teardown begins; the report already scopes the issue to a completion claimed/in progress on another CPU. No controller, stream, stop request, or concurrency was run; source-only.

PCIUSB UHCI RTIso stop/completion and deferred-player recheck (OD3517 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced `cmdStopRTIso()` through `uhciStopIsochIO()` and contrasted it with the selected UHCI completion interrupt (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:1679-1715`; `uhci/uhci_isoch.c:354-495,607-630`; `uhci/uhci_hcd.c:833-860`). The stop command wraps list lookup and the backend stop call in `Disable()` on its caller, and `uhciStopIsochIO()` unlinks active descriptors and releases per-PTD bounce buffers; it does not wait for an ISR already executing on another CPU to return. The completion interrupt calls `uhciHandleIsochTDs()`, whose RTIso branches invoke the done hook inline and then mutate/requeue the PTD state. The selected USB Audio `nOutReqHook()` calls Exec `Cause()` when a player interval elapses (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2620-2647`); its queued `nam_PlayerInt` is distinct from the controller descriptors removed by stop, and the fallback/player code schedules another timer request without an in-tree stop-side `RemIntServer`/wait. This confirms the separate UHCI and deferred-softint branches already stated in OD3517; it does not establish that a particular in-tree teardown interleaving occurs. The report's ExecSMP/multi-CPU qualification remains necessary because local `Disable()` does not join remote interrupt or softint work. No request, interrupt, stream, teardown, or build was run; source-only.

USB Audio fallback timer abort versus already-queued player softint (OD3517 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): checked the fallback timer cleanup in `subLibFreeAudio()` against `rom/exec/putmsg.c:89-119`, timer `AbortIO()` (`rom/timer/abortio.c:49-87`), and `DeleteIORequest()` (`rom/exec/deleteiorequest.c:40-49`). Teardown sets the timer port to `PA_IGNORE`, calls `AbortIO()`, and waits for the timer request before freeing mode buffers (`usbaudio.class.c:3620-3640`). A cancellation completed after `PA_IGNORE` is set cannot queue a fresh callback, but `PutMsg()` adds every reply to the port list before consulting `PA_IGNORE`; for a timer reply that already selected `PA_SOFTINT`, `Cause()` has already queued/runs independently of the later port flag, and the successful AbortIO/WaitIO pair only retires the timer message. `subLibPlayerIntDummy()` does not check a teardown flag and unconditionally submits the next timer request (`:2596-2616`), while `DeleteIORequest()` only frees storage. Therefore an already queued/running softint can still access the audio control and rearm the timer after the abort/wait, consistent with OD3517. No timer completion, softint, teardown, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="pci-ata-busy-status-pio-irq-od10974"></a>ATA ordinary PIO IRQ status/caller recheck (OD10974 added; OD2998, OD3007, OD10307 retained; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): traced the selected PCI bus-master ISR and no-DMA fallback (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/ata_pci_busclass.c:34-75`), shared bus callback (`rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:27-42`), PIO read/write handlers and completion (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:203-272`), PIO command setup/return (`:705-785`), and `ATA=nodma` option plus PIO fallback (`rom/devs/ata/ata_init.c:168-172,209-213`; `lowlevel.c:1392-1397,1507-1518`). The PCI bus-master branch does not reject BSY before dispatch; a BSY/no-DRQ status latches `HFERR_BadStatus`, while `ata_IRQNoData()` leaves the handler active on BSY. The error remains if later PIO phases finish, and is returned by `ata_exec_cmd()`. Gayle and PCI-without-DMA filter BSY before invoking the callback. Added OD10974 as a low-confidence hardware-reachability candidate; the code path and sticky-error behavior are source-confirmed, but no specification or supported-device trace in this pass establishes that the PCI DMA interrupt bit can coincide with BSY during PIO. This remains explicitly conditional. No IRQ, request, controller or build was run; source-only.

<a id="pci-ata-busy-status-late-cross-unit-od10974-followup"></a>OD10974 cross-unit late-IRQ caller recheck (2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): strengthened the earlier busy-status candidate by tracing the ordinary timeout cleanup and its intended late-IRQ possibility (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:493-512`), command error return (`:779-785`), serialized bus-task reply/queue continuation (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:1138-1160`), other-unit selection (`lowlevel.c:154-172`), PIO handler installation before command issue (`:705-715`), PCI interrupt routing through the currently selected unit (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/ata_pci_busclass.c:34-75`; `rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:27-42`), and the sticky error path (`lowlevel.c:203-214,216-272`). A late completion IRQ from one timed-out unit can therefore be interpreted against the other unit selected for a queued command; the second command's BSY/no-DRQ status can latch `HFERR_BadStatus` before its own PIO phases complete. The source explicitly permits the old interrupt to arrive after timeout and continues the bus queue. Exact controller timing/inter-device behavior remains unverified, so OD10974 is medium confidence and conditional on two units sharing the channel. No device, request, IRQ, or build was run; source-only.

Nouveau/VMware DRM interruptible-wait caller closure pass (no new OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): checked all selected direct `wait_for_completion_interruptible*()` and `wait_event_interruptible*()` sites in both DRM copies and VMware command paths against `linux_sched.c`, `include/linux/sched.h`, and `include/linux/wait.h`. The compatibility stubs report no pending signals, and `wait_for_completion_interruptible()` always returns zero after its wait; however, the indefinite VMware command-buffer space wait is reached through `vmw_execbuf_cmdbuf()` from execbuf submission, while both selected AROS `drm_ioctl()` shims return `-EINVAL` (`drm-aros/drm_stubs.c:264,280`). The interruptibility mismatch is therefore retained as an API-compatibility concern, not promoted to an active bug without an in-tree trigger showing that a task-break/cancellation path is expected here. AHIRecord bundled FLAC LPC short-block/order validation recheck (no new OD or LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced frame subframe dispatch through `read_subframe_fixed_()` and `read_subframe_lpc_()` to `read_residual_partitioned_rice_()` (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/FLAC/stream_decoder.c:2049-2054,2547-2603,2603-2690,2715-2742`). Poseidon hardware-task signal-allocation candidate withdrawal (OD10979 withdrawn; 2026-10-31; no file/LOC credit): rechecked `pDeviceTask()` allocation context against the task-creation paths. `psdSpawnSubTask()` uses `AddTask()` on the no-DOS path, where `NewAddTask()` initializes a zero signal allocation mask from `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc`; on the DOS path `CreateNewProcTags()` creates the process with its fixed `SIGB_DOS` port, not an allocated user signal (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1433-1511,9140-9163`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:247-252`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:423-428`). Exec initializes `TaskSigAlloc` with the lower 16 signal bits reserved (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`), leaving the first two `AllocSignal(-1L)` calls in the new hardware task available; no in-tree code before those calls allocates a task-local signal. Thus signal exhaustion at these call sites is not reachable through the selected worker startup path, and OD10979 was withdrawn from the findings report and index rather than retained as a hypothetical API failure. Source-only; no task or signal pool was manipulated.

<a id="deneb-zero-length-bulk-ptd-reuse-recheck-od4160"></a>
Deneb zero-length bulk PTD reuse recheck (OD4160 upheld; 2026-10-31; no new body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the complete `uhwScheduleBulkPTDs()` body pass recorded above (all 5,403 physical lines / 4,357 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) against `PTDNode`, `FreeATL()`, bulk completion, the USBHardware byte-count contract, and Poseidon's selected bulk caller. A newly selected ATL slot receives `ptd_BufStart` and `ptd_BufLen` only under `if (iouh_Length)`, but its length is encoded unconditionally in `ptd_DW[0]`; `FreeATL()` clears ownership/type and frees the slot without resetting those fields. Poseidon passes zero length through to `UHCMD_BULKXFER`. Bulk IN clamps copied bytes to the remaining request, while the shared completion accounting increments `iouh_Actual` by controller `len`; for bulk OUT that establishes the documented positive-actual consequence without an equivalent copy clamp. Thus OD4160's stale-length candidate remains supported, with the trigger limited to a zero-length bulk request reusing a slot after a nonzero request. The 2026-10-20 notes above calling `uhwcmd.c` partial are historical and superseded by the 2026-10-21 complete body pass. Hardware PTD behavior remains untested; no request, transfer, or device was exercised. Source-only.

USB HID OD9783 maximum-array wire-size and exact ID-collision derivation (2026-10-31; retained, no new ID or body/LOC credit): checked parser field widths and report-size accounting to ensure the 65,536-entry logical map does not require a 65,536-element transfer. A single non-variable Output item with Report Size 1, Report Count 1, Logical Minimum 0 and Logical Maximum 65,535 yields `nhi_MapSize == 65,536` (`hid.class.c:2931-2943`) while adding only one report bit; the parser's cap is strictly `> 65535`. Encoding Logical Maximum as a four-byte item makes `data == 65535` without taking the signed two-byte shift path tracked separately by OD10155 (`:2650-2687,3165-3173`). With successful map allocation, let the array action-list ID be `k`: its values receive every UWORD ID once from `k+1` through `k` modulo 65,536; the following output item's action list also receives `k+1`, colliding with the first value ID (`:2077,2344-2385`). `nFindItemID()` searches the earlier array IDs before the later output item, and the selected output-action path stores/uses that UWORD ID (`:3496-3522,6068-6110`; `hid.class.h:157-165`; `hid.gui.c:3296-3322`). This makes the minimum report payload and exact collision concrete, conditional on successful parser/map allocation and an action configured for the later item. No descriptor, device, allocation, GUI or output report was used; source-only.

<a id="pci-ata-busy-status-pio-irq-recheck-od10974"></a>
PCI ATA late-interrupt/busy-status PIO recheck (OD10974 retained; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): reread the complete PCI bus interrupt callback and the selected generic ATA status, unit-selection, transfer-handler, timeout, bus-task and queue-continuation paths (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/ata_pci_busclass.c:34-80`; `rom/devs/ata/ata_busclass.c:27-42`; `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:154-172,203-272,493-512,705-785`; `rom/devs/ata/ata.c:1138-1160`). The bus-master path accepts `DMAF_Interrupt`, acknowledges the DMA status, reads regular status for the currently selected device, and dispatches even if that status is busy; the handler is bus-global and obtains the currently selected unit from its bus context. Timeout cleanup explicitly leaves the device free to signal later while clearing the active software handler; the serialized bus task then processes the next queued request. A later PIO request selects the other device, waits for its initial BSY to clear, installs that unit's handler, and issues its command. If the first device's shared channel IRQ arrives during the second device's busy PIO phase, the current handler sees BSY without DRQ, latches `HFERR_BadStatus`, and retains that error through later phases. No source path disproved the required late cross-device timing; this remains medium confidence for that hardware interleaving. The ATA device and PCI HIDD are separately buildable package entries (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:56-75`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:40-68`); the board-support aggregate edges are commented in this snapshot, so package inclusion is configuration/target dependent. No controller, IRQ, PIO request, package build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="pciusb-pci-obtain-lifetime-semantics-od10533"></a>
PCIUSB cached PCI object lifetime semantics recheck (OD10533 strengthened; no new OD or path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced the PCI device `Obtain()` and `Release()` implementations against `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver()` and PCIUSB's allocation, close and reopen paths (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:488-511,549-556`; `pciclass.c:489-517`; `rom/usb/pciusb/pciusb_arospci.c:326-355,709-772`; `rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:226-253,344-354`). Obtain records only an owner name under `ownerLock`; it does not acquire an OOP reference. RemoveDriver rejects a device with a non-NULL owner, but disposes each matching object after PCIUSB close has cleared ownership. PCIUSB's controller record survives that close and `hd_ScanDone` skips re-enumeration on reopen. This confirms the existing stale-object route and why it requires removal after close; it does not establish a concurrent removal path while PCIUSB still owns the controller. OD10533 remains distinct from OD3637's owner-check race. No device, ownership call, expunge, reopen or runtime operation was used; source-only.


BWFM GLOM salvage queue-offset reconciliation for OD3591 (2026-10-31; no new OD or LOC credit): re-read the control-response loop (`bwfm_init.c:910-982`), `bwfm_rx_glom()` (`:1222-1317`), `bwfm_glom_salvage()` (`:1352-1373`), queue pop (`:1322-1338`), and pump call path. Confirmed the near-end state is reachable in source: a control transaction can deaggregate a 16-frame GLOM with 32,756 bytes of accepted subframes; salvage can remove one event entry while leaving `bwfm_glom_used` unchanged and `bwfm_glom_n` at 15; a following GLOM is processed before the pump can acquire the held semaphore. A first length of 1–4 rounds to four and satisfies both `off + rl <= 32768` and `bwfm_glom_n < 16`, after which the 12-byte prefix advance points one-past/beyond the static buffer and the unsigned length subtraction admits the embedded-header read. The later source-buffer copy requires the out-of-range bytes to pass the header/channel checks. This substantiates OD3591's conditional out-of-bounds read and sharpens its caller/state trigger; no runtime frame was supplied. No path or LOC credit. Source-only.

<a id="pciusb-sibling-controller-init-result-od10981"></a>## PCIUSB sibling-controller initialization result pass (OD10981 later merged into OD9548; no new path/LOC credit)

Read `pciAllocUnit()`'s ownership, per-HCI initialization, failure branch, root-port collection and online marking in order (`rom/usb/pciusb/pciusb_arospci.c:326-438,692-699`), then followed the selected `Open_Unit()` caller (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:251-270`). Each HCI initializer overwrites `allocgood`; there is no accumulated failure or early exit. A false result followed by a true result therefore skips the cleanup branch and reaches successful open. The port-map pass iterates all controller records regardless of each initializer's result and counts their `hc_NumPorts` (`pciusb_arospci.c:424-438,466-479,484-485`). Confirmed a concrete ordering possibility in UHCI: `hc_NumPorts = 2` precedes its fallible PCI-memory allocation (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhci/uhci_hcd.c:936-957`), so an earlier UHCI failure followed by later EHCI success can publish the uninitialized UHCI's root ports. Existing source body credits are unchanged; no path/LOC credit. No device, allocation failure, request, or build was run; source-only.

BTSerial open-command caller recheck (OD3366 retained and qualified; no new finding or coverage credit; 2026-10-31): traced the selected optional `kernel-bluetooth-classes-btserial` module's `devOpen()` through Exec `OpenDevice()` and the class worker. The open vector puts the caller's IORequest on `unit_MsgPort` and immediately drains that same port with `GetMsg()` (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/dev.c:120-127`); Exec calls the vector synchronously while local task switching is forbidden (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-114,130-135`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). On a uniprocessor, the already queued request can be consumed by `devOpen()` itself, so the worker does not process the command before open returns. On ExecSMP, if the worker dequeues it first (`btserial.class.c:656-658`), `ReplyMsg()` targets the reply port supplied in the IORequest (`:694-696`; `rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`; `CreateIORequest` stores that port at `rom/exec/createiorequest.c:59-72`), while `devOpen()` waits on the unit port, allowing an indefinite wait when those ports differ. The BTSerial `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` handler is explicitly a no-op for RFCOMM, so the skipped processing does not establish a line-coding consequence for this class; retained OD3366 scopes its BTSerial consequence to the SMP wrong-port wait. No checked-in explicit `OpenDevice` call for these named serial devices was found; the trigger is a client opening a bound device. This sharpens the existing report scope only. No device open, worker schedule, or build was run; source-only.

OD3578 full-speed USB Audio cadence qualification (2026-10-31; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `subLibStart()`'s sample accumulator (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3721-3723`) and `nOutReqHook()` (`:2620-2689`) against the descriptor-derived interval/frame size. xHCI DMA preprocessing selected-platform reachability closure (no new OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): closed the `xhci_schedule.c` ledger's pending physical-address reachability question by enumerating checked-in `pcixhci` package edges and the selected Exec DMA helpers. The Raspberry Pi AArch64 boot package includes `USBHardware/pcixhci` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:217`); the OpenSBI package's xHCI module edge is commented (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:88`), though the explicit module target remains buildable (`rom/usb/pcixhci/mmakefile.src:29-47`). In the AArch64 target, `CachePreDMA()` returns `KrnVirtualToPhysical(address)` without modifying `*length` (`arch/aarch64-native/exec/cachepredma.c:20-38`), and the selected generic kernel translation returns the input pointer (`rom/kernel/virtualtophysical.c:43-48`). The generic x86 helper also returns the input pointer and leaves length unchanged (`rom/exec/cachepredma.c:62-77`). On RISC-V OpenSBI, when selected, `CachePreDMA_Zicbom()` performs cache maintenance and returns the input address without changing length (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:104-124`); its selected generic `KrnVirtualToPhysical()` is identity as well. These implementations do not justify ignoring a changed address/length as a portable API pattern, but no selected xHCI target here changes either value, so no new DMA-address mismatch is established. The existing OD2349 allocation/busy-slot findings remain separate. This resolves only selected-platform address/contiguity reachability; DMA coherency, partial-cache-line ownership, and broader controller/hardware behavior remain open. No DMA buffer, controller, build or runtime operation was used; source-only.


<a id="aarch64-partial-line-dma-cache-trace-od10983"></a> AArch64 partial-line DMA cache follow-up (OD10983; 2026-10-31; no body/LOC credit): read `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:85-155,280-289`, the AArch64 `CachePreDMA()`/`CachePostDMA()` implementations, and the public Exec DMA cache-helper contracts. The syscall rounds nonempty DMA ranges outward to 64-byte lines; `CACRF_ClearD` executes `dc civac` on each line. `CachePreDMA()` uses this clean+invalidate before transfer. For device-to-RAM transfers, `CachePostDMA()` repeats clean+invalidate after transfer. A cache line reloaded and dirtied by CPU access to neighboring bytes during DMA may still contain stale bytes from the DMA subrange; the post-DMA clean can write those bytes back over the device result. This contradicts the post-DMA helper comment that a clean line “writes back nothing,” unless callers guarantee cache-line ownership through DMA completion. The generic API describes byte ranges but does not state that adjacent cache-line bytes must remain untouched. Added OD10983 with that conditional trigger and medium caller-reachability confidence. No selected in-tree call was shown to exercise this exact overlap; no device, DMA transfer, or build was run. Source-only.


<a id="aarch64-whole-cache-sentinel-trace-od10984"></a> AArch64 whole-cache sentinel candidate correction (OD10984 withdrawn; 2026-10-31; no body/LOC credit): the initial trace stopped at the generic `CacheClearU()` call and treated its `~0` argument as the value observed by the syscall. Rechecked the selected override at `arch/aarch64-native/exec/cachecleare.c:18-30`: its `ULONG length` parameter is loaded into x1 as a 32-bit value, narrowing `~0` to `0xffffffff` before SVC. The receiver compares against exactly `0xffffffff` and executes the whole-cache set/way data operation and `ic iallu` path (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:88-106`). The prior claim that the request falls through and clears nothing was false. OD10984 was withdrawn and removed from `../AROS.md`; the source-body review adds no credit.

ATA 64-bit range arithmetic and DMA bounce-copy alignment caller recheck (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-read `cmd_Read64()`/`cmd_Write64()` in `rom/devs/ata/ata.c:118-164,230-290` and the high-address DMA bounce path in `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1190-1240`. The apparent sector-end addition overflow is not reachable from the public byte offset: the 64-bit byte offset is sector-alignment checked and shifted by `au_SectorShift` before the addition; with the 512-byte minimum sector size, the largest sector index is below 2^55, and the byte `io_Length` is at most 2^32-1, so the sum remains within UQUAD. The separate exclusive-end threshold behavior at `0x0fffffff` remains OD2999. The DMA bounce path passes caller `io_Data` through `CopyMemQuick()` without checking its documented ULONG-alignment precondition (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:24-36,52-56`); the ATA request handler itself adds no alignment check. However, the selected affected CPU paths are x86/x86-64, where unaligned scalar loads/stores are supported, and this source-only pass establishes no concrete miscopy or fault from the C alignment-contract violation, so it is not promoted to an active candidate. No full-body credit, finding, build, request or DMA transfer is claimed.

OD10983 xHCI low-address bounce alignment follow-up (2026-10-31; finding scope refined, no new ID or body/LOC credit): rechecked `xhciPrepareDMABuffer()`'s 64-bit-controller fallback (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_schedule.c:47-78`) against AArch64 allocator guarantees. For a high (>4 GiB) caller buffer and controller without `HCF_ADDR64`, the helper allocates `*dmalen` bytes using `AllocVec(..., MEMF_31BIT | MEMF_PUBLIC)`, then applies the same CachePreDMA and completion CachePostDMA to that allocation. `AllocVec()` prepends `AROS_ALIGN(sizeof(IPTR))` bytes to its AllocMem request and returns the following pointer (`rom/exec/allocvec.c:56-75`); AArch64's `AROS_WORSTALIGN` is 16 (`arch/aarch64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:34`), not 64. Thus the selected optional bounce path does not guarantee a cache-line-exclusive beginning or end, independently confirming possible partial edge lines. The actual corruption trigger still requires another CPU/task to dirty neighboring bytes in a shared edge line while DMA is active; this source pass does not establish a particular in-tree request caller doing so. PTP debug-dump length precondition recheck (OD10985; no new finding or body/LOC credit): traced all five active `dumpmem()` calls in `ptp.class.c` through their local buffer sizes and transfer lengths. <a id="ptp-findupdate-existing-file-write-null-buffer-od10992"></a>PTP existing-object MODE_READWRITE null-buffer write pass (OD10992 added; 2026-10-31; no body/LOC credit): traced DOS `MODE_READWRITE`/`ACTION_FINDUPDATE` mapping (`rom/dos/fs_driver.c:36-49`) and `Write()` packet dispatch (`rom/dos/write.c:70`) through the PTP `ACTION_FINDUPDATE`/`ACTION_FINDINPUT` open branch, `nCreateFH()`, `ACTION_WRITE`, `nPTPWrite()` and `nGetPTPRspData()` (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:3053-3078,3311-3333,3646-3659,2423-2504,930-1019`). Existing-object update opens an `ACCESS_READ` PTP handle without a data buffer; the MEMF_CLEAR pool initializes `pfh_Buffer` to NULL. For a write within `poi_Size`, `nPTPWrite()` does not enter its only allocation branch. A partial overwrite attempts to fetch old data into that NULL destination; a full overwrite skips the fetch and copies new bytes to it directly. Exec `CopyMem()` has no NULL guard (`rom/exec/copymem.c:65-103`). Added OD10992, distinct from OD10171's short-buffer source overread. The optional PTP module target is available, but its aggregate and stock class-list edges are commented (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/mmakefile.src`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:61-64`). The PTP translation unit already has full-body credit; this caller-path finding adds no path/LOC credit. No DOS operation, file, device, or build was run; source-only.

PTP FINDUPDATE lock-mode candidate disposition (OD10992 unchanged; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): compared the PTP existing-file `ACTION_FINDUPDATE` branch's `ACCESS_READ` handle creation (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:3311-3333`) with selected AROS filesystem implementations and checked-in DOS open documentation. The DOS wrapper maps `MODE_READWRITE` directly to `ACTION_FINDUPDATE` (`rom/dos/fs_driver.c:36-49`) and documents read/write access (`rom/dos/open.c:40-49`), but does not define one universal shared-versus-exclusive lock policy. NTFS chooses `EXCLUSIVE_LOCK` for every action except `ACTION_FINDINPUT` (`workbench/fs/ntfs/ops.c:185`); SMBFS history explicitly records changing `ACTION_FINDUPDATE` from exclusive to shared lock (`workbench/network/smbfs/documentation/history.doc`, smbfs 1.50). Therefore the PTP `ACCESS_READ` choice alone does not establish a separate lock-contract defect or concurrency consequence. OD10992 remains limited to the independently verified empty-buffer write path. No open, lock, DOS packet, or build was run; source-only.

USB HID keyboard modifier-count bound pass (OD10993 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): read the complete selected `kbdclass.c` body and traced the report parser/consumer sequence. `KbdData.loc_mod` has eight entries (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid.h:178`); constructor parsing increments `loc_modcnt` and only then skips storage when it exceeds eight (`kbdclass.c:154-177`). The selected `hid_get_item()` expands each variable Main item by `Report Count` (`hid.c:127-145,198-217`), allowing an over-capacity keyboard-page descriptor to leave a larger count. `USBKbd::ParseReport()` then reads each indexed location through that count (`kbdclass.c:99-119`), and the worker likewise reads indexed modifier keys (`:399-445`). The HID interface matcher selects the keyboard class for protocol 1 (`hidclass.c:380-394`); the interrupt callback dispatches reports to `ParseReport()` (`:65-82`). Added OD10993, scoped to the explicitly selected optional HID module and over-capacity descriptor; the proven effect is reading beyond the modifier array and misinterpreting adjacent instance fields, with reads beyond the instance for sufficiently large excess counts. The implementation bodies already have full-body credit; no path/LOC totals changed. No descriptor, report, device, or build was used; source-only.

USB Audio readiness handshake failure-path recheck (OD4146 retained; apparent missing-ready-signal candidate rejected; 2026-10-31; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `usbForceInterfaceBinding()`'s `psdSpawnSubTask()`/`psdBorrowLocksWait()` sequence into `nAudioTask()` and both `nAllocAudio()` exits (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:314-350,584-609,1994-2078`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:735-795`). On successful initialization, `nAllocAudio()` sets `nch_Task` and returns; on any failed initialization branch, its common cleanup calls `Forbid()`, clears `nch_Task`, and signals `nch_ReadySigTask` before returning NULL. Thus the child does not silently exit without waking the binding caller, and no separate readiness deadlock is established. The prepublished unit record still lacks rollback after the caller wakes and receives a NULL task; that retained-record issue is OD4146. No worker, library failure, binding or wait was run; source-only.

In `ParseReport()`, the same shift is reached when `hid_get_data()` reports that field set. Qualified by target integer width and field/report state; no runtime report or build was used.

USB HID AddInterrupt length-width and keyboard-copy trace (OD10997 added; OD4091 strengthened; OD2237 ledger-only note consolidated; no body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `hid->buflen` from descriptor report sizing through the public AddInterrupt message and both controller paths (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:65-82,276-318`; `workbench/devs/USB/include/usb.h:429-434,487`; OHCI `ohcidriverclass.c:453-531`; UHCI `uhciclass.c:630-652`; UHCI `hardware.c:523-590`). The 8-bit parameter truncates a 256-byte HID report to zero; UHCI computes zero TDs and dereferences `td == NULL` at `hardware.c:571`. This is the separate root cause formerly noted as OD2096 in older ledger prose; no active detailed OD2096 report exists, so added OD10997 and its index entry. For 257 bytes, the length truncates to one; UHCI's non-NAK completion path dispatches `Cause()` (`uhciclass.c:136-153`), then `HidInterrupt()` supplies the original full buffer length to `ParseReport()`. This supports OD4091's full-width destination-copy consequence with a successful short one-byte completion. Consolidated the earlier OD2237 coverage-only 257-byte trace into OD4091; it is not a separate finding. Reconciled the 256-byte case with OD4091 by making that finding's demonstrated keyboard-copy trigger 257 bytes and cross-referencing the separate zero-length UHCI setup crash. No device, descriptor, controller, transfer, or build was used; source-only.

UHCI multi-TD HID report-size candidate resolution (OD1606 not retained as a distinct defect; 2026-11-01; no body/LOC credit): rechecked `uhci_QueuedTransfer()` against the complete selected `uhci_Handler()` path (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/UHCI/hardware.c:523-590`; `uhciclass.c:121-169`). For a complete multi-TD interrupt read, only the final TD receives IOC (`hardware.c:536-571`); the handler then observes completion, invokes the callback and rearms the first TD to repeat the transfer (`uhciclass.c:139-166`). Thus merely having a HID report larger than endpoint `p_MaxTransfer` does not establish early callback or stale remainder on the successful full-length path. UHCI short/error completions may still be delivered without an actual byte count/status to `HidInterrupt`; that conditional behavior is tracked with the existing completion-status candidate and was not claimed as an OD1606-sized-report defect here. The earlier OD1606 wording in the HID inventory row is superseded by this resolution; no standalone OD1606 entry exists in the detailed report/index. No TD, short packet, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

UHCI OD2971 caller wait/error propagation refinement (duplicate OD10998 consolidated; same finding; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-11-01): followed `p_SigTask` signaling from the control-low/control-full/bulk queue scans into `ControlTransfer()` and `BulkTransfer()` (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/UHCI/uhciclass.c:194-210,238-255,283-298,761-812,828-880`). The synchronous callers wait for those scan signals; only the separate timeout signal lets the timeout branches return FALSE. A zero pipe timeout skips scheduling that timeout request, leaving the wait dependent on a completion signal that the error-only handler skipped. `p_ErrorCode` is set to zero on drained queues and has no nonzero assignment in the selected UHCI sources, so these paths do not propagate a TD failure code. Atheros5000 shared HAL rate-table initialization caller recheck (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `ar5210GetRateTable()`'s shared global table pointers into `ath_hal_setupratetable()` (`hal/ar5210/ar5210_phy.c:24-84`; `hal/ah.c:404-434`), then through the two Atheros unit consumers of `rateCodeToIndex` and ACK durations (`unit.c:2235-2240,2540-2547`). HID `nReadReports()` short-descriptor and allocation-bound pass (OD11009 added; function-level review only, no full-file body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): read the complete `nReadReports()` body (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2063-2601`) and traced both entry callers (`:1043,1245`) plus Poseidon's configuration-descriptor copy (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:2030-2045,8674-8700`). DOSBoot no-screen retry open-count boundary recheck (OD10489 retained; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): re-read `OpenBootScreenType()`, `NoBootMediaScreen()`, the retry loop, and both close callers (`rom/dosboot/bootscreen.c:18-81,144-168`; `dosboot_init.c:296-315`; `cleanup.c:53-61`). While `bm_Screen` remains NULL, the retry loop calls `NoBootMediaScreen()` again after each delay, and both after-DOS cleanup and ordinary close skip the two library closes. DOSBoot boot-block checksum index-wrap trigger recheck (OD10490 retained; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): re-read `GetBootNodeDeviceUnit()`, `dosboot_BootBlock()`, and `BootBlockCheckSum()` (`rom/dosboot/bootstrap.c:58-107,194-236`). `de_BootBlocks` and `de_SizeBlock` are `IPTR` fields with no local upper bound (`compiler/include/dos/filehandler.h:33,54`); their product is converted to a `ULONG` byte extent. The buffer must first allocate in `MEMF_CHIP`, and `DoIO(CMD_READ)` must succeed before the checksum is called. For a 65,536-byte extent, the `UWORD` index reaches 65,532, increments by four to zero, and remains below the `ULONG` size indefinitely; larger supported extents share the wrap. Thus OD10490's trigger requires both successful buffer allocation and a full successful read of the configured extent; allocation/read failure avoids the loop. No additional bound or termination path was found. No boot block, device read, large allocation, or build was used; source-only.

If the early startup menu is requested/opened and the user selects Boot Options (button or key `2`), `initWindow()` calls `populateGadgets_PageBoot()` before opening the page window, and its unconditional backup loop dereferences `devicesEnabled` at `menu.c:244-248`. Sound.datatype AHI continuous-playback caller follow-up (GD10459 retained; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the selected `COMMAND_PLAY` AHI fallback from `OpenAHI()` through `AHI_BestAudioID`, `AHI_AllocAudio`, both continuous dynamic-sample loads, play control, and failed-play/stop cleanup (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3469-3504,3892-4061`). `OpenAHI()` closes either a partial request/port or the successful device/request/port; `AHI_AllocAudio` failure does not publish a live audio control; if allocation of the doubled sample buffer fails, the path remains failed and releases the live audio control before closing AHI. The playback buffer is sized in bytes from `max(MaxPlaySamples * sourceFrequency / mixFrequency, SampleLength) * bytesPerPoint`, then doubled, and the source copy uses `SampleLength * bytesPerPoint`; for valid sample types and a successful positive-frequency AHI control, the copy extent fits the allocated half-buffer. ## BTCore L2CAP outbound-buffer lifetime and selected transport pass

Outbound L2CAP data-buffer caller census (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): enumerated all seven production calls to `bt_l2cap_channel_manager_send()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:274,346,578,2539`; `rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/sdp/sdp_client.c:239`; `rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/gatt/gatt_client.c:326,442`) plus the three host-test transports. The channel manager copies each caller payload into its local L2CAP PDU, fragments that PDU into a stack ACL buffer, and calls the transport synchronously (`stack/protocols/l2cap/channel_manager.c:720-743,67-92`). The selected `bluetooth.device` transport is `bSendACLPacket()` (`bluetooth/hwtask.c:117`), which allocates a variable-sized `HCACLTx`, copies the entire fragment before returning, and queues only that owned copy (`bluetooth/hwconn.c:140-162`); the worker later copies it again into a persistent controller-write buffer before submitting async I/O (`hwtask.c:2616-2674`). The stack-local SDP response, GATT confirmation and request buffers, SDP server reply, and SMP PDU therefore remain live for the synchronous copy; endpoint/RFCOMM writes likewise finish copying before `bReplyChannel()` returns the request. The selected in-tree transport has no deferred pointer to these caller or fragment stack buffers, and no premature input-buffer release candidate was established. The internal transport callback type does not state the synchronous-consumption requirement, so custom/out-of-tree `bt_hci_transport` implementations remain an API-contract boundary. Full bodies already have credit; no host transport test, request, ACL operation, or build was run; source-only.

BTCore L2CAP inbound reassembly callback-buffer lifetime pass (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the completed-PDU path from `bt_l2cap_reassembler_take()` through header/CID validation into `fire_event()` (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/l2cap/channel_manager.c:748-795,115-119`). The reassembled payload is owned by the manager's reusable reassembly storage, so callback data is only valid during synchronous dispatch. Checked each production data callback: classic endpoints copy to the waiting request or a newly allocated receive-queue node in `bDeliverSDU()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:222-252`); RFCOMM parses frames synchronously and its DLC callbacks route payload to the same copy path (`hwconn.c:388-419`; `stack/protocols/rfcomm/rfcomm.c:503-641`); the SDP server builds its response in server-owned state/local response storage before the outbound synchronous-copy path (`hwconn.c:574-582`; `stack/protocols/sdp/sdp_server.c:220+`); SDP client response chunks are copied into `client->result` (`stack/protocols/sdp/sdp_client.c:47-54,166-220`); GATT response handlers either copy into client-owned result fields or parse before callback return, and notification values are delivered synchronously to `bGATTNotify()`, which routes them through `bDeliverSDU()` (`stack/protocols/gatt/gatt_client.c:294-356,455-486`; `hwconn.c:758-769`); SMP parses and copies required values into manager state during `bt_smp_manager_on_pdu()` (`stack/core/security/smp_manager.c:677-721`). No selected in-tree callback retains the reassembly pointer. Public callback consumers outside these selected clients still must obey callback-scoped pointer lifetime; no new defect established. Existing bodies already have credit, so coverage totals are unchanged. No packet, host transport, device or build was exercised; source-only.

BTCore inbound HCI ACL length and reassembly-buffer ownership follow-up (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced each completed HCI read through `bHandleDevReply()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2738-2755`), `bConnHandleACL()` (`bluetooth/hwconn.c:3416-3433`), and `bt_l2cap_reassembler_feed()` (`stack/protocols/l2cap/l2cap.c:66-100`). The asynchronous read completes before `bConnHandleACL()` parses `req->iobt_Actual`; `bt_hci_parse_acl_header()` extracts the declared ACL length, and the caller's `bt_buf_reader_peek()` rejects a declaration exceeding the completed buffer before dispatch. The reassembler copies the fragment into per-connection storage before `bHandleDevReply()` resubmits that same ACL read buffer. On continuation it checks accumulated size against `BT_L2CAP_REASSEMBLY_MAX`, then checks against the L2CAP-declared total; `take()` exposes a complete PDU only after exact-length completion and resets the accumulator for the next packet. No read-buffer reuse, truncation, or trailing-length defect was established in this selected receive path. This supports the immediately preceding callback-lifetime pass and adds no body/path/LOC credit. No ACL packet, device, or build was used; source-only.

BTCore classic L2CAP asymmetric MTU caller recheck (OD3963 retained; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `start_our_configure_request()` encoding `chan->local_mtu`, incoming Configure Request storing the peer's value in `chan->remote_mtu`, and `bt_l2cap_channel_manager_send()` checking only the fixed global limit (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/l2cap/channel_manager.c:181-194,283-305,720-744`). Rechecked the selected endpoint path: `bEndpointOpen()` supplies its configured/default MTU, `bEndpointWrite()` forwards `bch_Length` unchanged, and on a successful local enqueue replies with the full requested length (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:258-280,704-720`; `hwtask.c:63-78`). The public synchronous `btDoChannel()` waits for and returns that local request result (`bluetooth/objects.c:1191-1202`). This reinforces OD3963's outbound contract failure: the peer's receive MTU is stored but is not used to bound a successful write. The reverse situation—accepting an oversized inbound Basic-mode SDU from a peer which violates the advertised local MTU—was considered; the selected local path has bounded reassembly and does not overflow its internal storage, and no separate in-tree consumer consequence was established, so it is not split into another finding. No channel, write, peer, or build was exercised; source-only. Reference: [Bluetooth Core 5.4, Vol 3 Part A §3.1 and §5.1](https://www.bluetooth.com/wp-content/uploads/Files/Specification/HTML/Core-54/out/en/host/logical-link-control-and-adaptation-protocol-specification.html).

USB Audio ordinary AHI unit-close route into OD3192 (2026-11-01; finding consolidated, no new path/LOC credit): traced the first `OpenDevice()` unit initialization and last-close path through `InitUnit()`/`ReadConfig()`, startup-message wait, unit-task `AllocHardware()`, `AHI_ControlAudio()`, `ExpungeUnit()`, `FreeHardware()`, and `_AHI_FreeAudio()` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:443-458,471-503,518-540,743-791,811-826,889-917,946-957`; `audioctrl.c:931-999,702-727`). <a id="isapnp-pointer-ordering-review-od11018"></a>
ISA PnP pointer-ordering and lock-array review (OD11018 added; no default-selected denominator or LOC credit; 2026-11-01): verified that `ComparePtr()` compares distinct `AllocVec()`-allocated card/device structures with pointer subtraction and returns the result as `int` (`rom/isapnp/devices.c:159-167`; `pnp_structs.c:43-55,105-119`). `MakeSortedArray()` passes that comparator to `qsort()`, and both public multi-lock APIs use the returned order for semaphore acquisition (`devices.c:171-201,214-258,301-345`). For valid multi-object arrays, subtraction of pointers to separate objects has undefined C behavior, and narrowing can prevent the comparator from representing the address difference consistently. Recorded OD11018 as a portability/correctness candidate: inconsistent ordering could defeat the lock-order scheme, but target-specific comparator behavior and a concrete multi-object caller are not established. The checked-in callers found each pass one device; `kernel-isapnp` is optional and commented out of the i386 PC package. Confidence is high for the C-semantics issue, medium for target-level order failure, and low for in-tree reachability. No object list, comparator, contention, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="isapnp-alternative-resource-allocation-od11020"></a>
ISA PnP alternative-resource allocation rollback pass (OD11020 added; optional-target trace, no default-selected denominator or LOC credit; 2026-11-01): followed `CreateResouces()`'s allocation loop into both callers. It appends each returned resource immediately and exits FALSE on the first failed allocation without removing the appended prefix (`rom/isapnp/pnp_iterators.c:798-825`). In `FindConfiguration()`'s alternative-group loop, failure resets `rc`, frees the iterator list, and permits iteration to continue to a later resource group; the output list is the device's persistent resource list (`rom/isapnp/pnp.c:790-829`). A later successful alternative can therefore make configuration return success with stale prefix records. `ISAPNP_ConfigureCards()` then calls `ProgramConfiguration()`, which consumes every record and advances per-type register cursors before activation (`pnp.c:1049-1084,948-1033`). Added OD11020 for the conditional mixed-configuration programming path. The simple fixed-resource failure path only returns configuration failure; the finding requires a partial alternative followed by a later successful selection. Scope is optional `kernel-isapnp`; its i386 PC package edge is commented out. No allocation failure, hardware, configuration, or build was used; source-only.


<a id="isapnp-io-range-wrap-od11021"></a>
ISA PnP I/O range exhaustion and wrap pass (OD11021 added; optional-target trace, no default-selected denominator or LOC credit; 2026-11-01): checked both initial and subsequent I/O-candidate loops. `ResourceIterator.m_Base` is `UWORD`; `ResetResourceIterator()` and `IncResourceIterator()` add the byte alignment and test only `m_Base <= MaxBase` (`rom/isapnp/pnp_iterators.c:38-49,405-424,589-650`). When an in-range candidate at `0xFFFF` conflicts, the next value wraps to zero and is still below the UWORD maximum. If zero is free in the PnP context, the iterator can accept it despite the descriptor minimum; `CreateResource()` preserves the base and `ProgramConfiguration()` writes it (`pnp_iterators.c:764-780`; `pnp.c:1011-1021`). The specification says a zero I/O base disables that range (PnP ISA 1.0a §A.3.2). If each wrapped candidate conflicts, the search can cycle rather than fail. Added OD11021 for this out-of-range assignment/nontermination root, scoped to an enabled optional `kernel-isapnp`; i386 PC package inclusion remains commented out. No card, context, configuration or build was used; source-only.


ISA PnP I/O reservation ordering and candidate-conflict recheck (OD11021 rechecked; 2026-11-01; no additional finding): reviewed `LockResource()` and `UnlockResource()` alongside the initial and subsequent I/O iterator loops. The half-open overlap predicate covers both possible interval orderings, and insertion before the first later base preserves the sorted reservation list; unlock removes the reservation by its unique candidate base. The sticky `m_InConflict` bit is intentional for backtracking: a collision marks both the existing conflicting iterator and the current iterator so both candidate choices can be revisited. Confirmed the standard describes the I/O alignment byte as the increment applied to the minimum base, while this implementation advances a 16-bit `m_Base` and checks only the wrapped value against the maximum; this preserves OD11021's stated top-of-range wrap condition. This did not establish a separate defect. Invalid/reversed descriptor ranges and the behavior of zero alignment remain unvalidated and are not promoted without stronger format-contract evidence. Optional `kernel-isapnp` remains disabled in the checked-in i386 PC package. No card, resource context, configuration, or build was exercised; source-only.

ISA PnP iterator full-body and internal-list backtracking pass (OD11022 added; optional-target trace, no default-selected denominator or LOC credit; 2026-11-01): read the complete 826-line `rom/isapnp/pnp_iterators.c` body in contiguous source-order slices (551 `cloc 2.06` C code lines). Reviewed context allocation/free, IRQ/DMA/I/O reservation and release, initial and incremental candidate selection, iterator-list construction/destruction, conflict propagation, resource materialization, and all cleanup paths. Rechecked OD11017's iterator allocation failure cleanup, OD11020's partial output-resource rollback, OD11021's 16-bit I/O candidate wrap, and the conflict ordering from the preceding pass. Added OD11022: `AllocResourceIteratorList()` greedily initializes each descriptor and aborts/frees the incomplete list when a later descriptor cannot fit; although the conflict marks the earlier iterator for backtracking, `FindConfiguration()` only enters `IncResourceIteratorList()` after list construction succeeds. A valid later choice for an earlier ranged descriptor is therefore missed; base-list failure makes `ISAPNP_ConfigureCards()` fail, while alternative-list failure skips that group. USB Audio frequency-to-index threshold recheck (OD3207 retained; OD11023 later withdrawn as duplicate; no path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): rechecked the complete `subLibGetAttr()` body in the selected USB Audio class, especially `AHIDB_Index` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3895-4078`). AHI's public GetAudioAttrs contract says `AHIDB_IndexArg` returns the index of the closest supported frequency (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:301-306`); the selected requester uses it to map its current rate into a new mode's slider (`requester.c:382-400`). The driver seeds `diff` with 100,000 and `bestfit` with zero, so when every entry is at least 100,000 Hz away, the loop never considers any entry and may return index zero even when a later entry is closer. This is the same root cause and consequence as existing OD3207; the additional caller evidence is merged into OD3207, and OD11023 is withdrawn as a duplicate. Existing Frequency/Input/Output indexed accesses remain caller-contract-bounded by their documented index counts; no USB mode or query was run. The translation unit already has full body/LOC credit; broader AHI/HCD caller and descriptor coverage remains open. Source-only.

USB Audio AHIDB_Index cross-driver and duplicate reconciliation (OD3207 strengthened; OD11023 withdrawn as duplicate; no path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): compared the `AHIDB_Index` paths in selected AHI Device and Raspberry Pi PWM drivers with USB Audio. The AHI requester consumes the returned index as a slider position (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/requester.c:382-400`); the public contract is “closest frequency” (`Device/modeinfo.c:301-306`). The Device and RPiPWM drivers explicitly clamp values outside their sorted endpoint range and choose the nearer adjacent value inside it (`Drivers/Device/device-main.c:258-278`; `Drivers/RPiPWM/rpipwm-main.c:461-480`), whereas USB Audio's fixed `100000` threshold can leave the initialized zero result even if a later table entry is nearer. No AHI device, mode, preference GUI or query was run; source-only.

USB PTP `ACTION_FH_FROM_LOCK` ownership and DOS caller recheck (2026-11-01; no new OD or body/LOC credit): followed the complete conversion branch through `nCreateFH()`/`nFreeLock()` and DOS `OpenFromLock()` (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:2999-3106,3526-3564`; `rom/dos/openfromlock.c:51-80`). On read conversion, successful handle allocation increments the shared-lock count before `nFreeLock()` consumes the source lock; allocation failure leaves the source lock in place. For write conversion, the handler temporarily clears the source exclusive bit so `nCreateFH(ACCESS_WRITE)` can acquire it, restores it on allocation failure, and after success frees the old lock then explicitly reinstates the exclusive bit held by the new handle. A device lacking SendObject returns before changing or freeing the lock. `OpenFromLock()` frees only its newly allocated DOS FileHandle on packet failure, consistent with its documented requirement that the caller still free the lock after failure; successful conversion consumes the lock. `ACTION_FREE_LOCK` inherits the worker's initialized DOSTRUE result and its DOS `UnLock()` wrapper interprets the packet result as success. No separate ownership, lock-count or error-return defect established in these paths. No DOS lock operation, allocation failure, USB device, or build was used; source-only.

Bluetooth discovery name-queue retirement recheck (OD3898 expanded; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced name-node publication in `bStartDiscoveryPhase()` through the immediate `bNextNameRequest()` dispatch, the Preferences Forget caller, and the device retirement/free path (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:613-642,1494-1527`; `rom/bluetooth/prefs/ActionClass.c:1103-1106`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/objects.c:409-450`). Bluetooth command-queue timeout and late-response source review (OD11029 queue interaction rechecked; no new OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): reread all of `rom/bluetooth/stack/core/controller/command_queue.c` (245 physical lines), its public slot/timer contract, and the checked-in queue timeout test (`stack/tests/controller/test_command_queue.c:300-335`). Event matching then uses only the outstanding opcode; the test verifies that a late same-opcode response does not double-complete when no newer command is outstanding. A late old response arriving while a later command with the same opcode is outstanding could be indistinguishable at this layer, but this source pass did not establish that a selected HCI transport/controller can deliver command responses out of order across the subsequently admitted command sequence. <a id="pc-i8042-standard-scrolllock-sequence-od11032"></a> PC i8042 standard Scroll Lock sequence and raw-key path (OD11032 added; 2026-11-01): rechecked the ordinary/E0 event construction, both table entries and lock-state dispatch. <a id="pcipc-acpi-driver-registration-failure-route-ownership-od3523"></a>PCIPC ACPI route-list registration failure follow-up (OD3523 expanded; no new ID, body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the per-host `HIDD_PCI_AddHardwareDriver` call in `PCIPC_InitClass()` through the PCI method wrapper to `HW_AddDriver()` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:619-630`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:561-565`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:180-205`). `HW_AddDriver()` can return NULL before a driver object is created when its pooled `DriverNode` allocation or `OOP_NewObject()` fails. The PCI method is void and the caller frees the outer `hbNode` regardless; `PCIPC__Root__New()` moves the nested route nodes only after superclass object creation succeeds (`pcipc_driverclass.c:69-110`). Thus that per-bridge failure leaks the route-node allocations even though the outer host-bridge allocation is freed. This is distinct from OD3523's existing PCI-base construction failure, where the entire stack-local bridge list remains unfreed; both are ownership-transfer cleanup failures, so they remain consolidated under OD3523. The selected PCI `SetUpDriver()` has no post-construction failure return, so no such branch is claimed. Existing whole-file credit stands. No allocation failure, ACPI enumeration, or module initialization was induced; source-only.

ACPI fan private/public header caller reconciliation (OD findings rechecked; no new OD or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): closed the two header caller rows for `rom/hidds/acpi/fan/{acpifan_intern.h,include/acpifan.h}`. Matched the internal `HWACPIFanData` and `ACPIFanNode` layouts, class static data, generated library base, `CSD` macro, attribute bases and `IID_HW_ACPIFan` offset use to the selected `acpifan.conf`, `acpifan_init.c`, and `acpifan_class.c`. The public `CLID_HW_ACPIFan` matches the module class ID, and the sole `Handle` attribute is the one produced by init and consumed by New/Get. Repository-wide direct-use search found no separate consumer of the public class header. Existing OD findings remain the supported init, teardown, telemetry-package and performance-state issues; no header-only mismatch established. ACPI firmware method correctness and external HIDD consumers remain open. No firmware method, device, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

ACPI discovery-node ordinary-success lifetime expansion (OD3415 expanded; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the fan discovery-list ownership through all five ACPI device initializers: fan, battery, AC-adapter, power-meter and thermal. On the normal namespace-success path each loop assigns its `HW_AddDriver()` return to the discovery node's object field, counts successful registrations and exits without removing or freeing the node. Repository-wide searches show those node lists/fields are used only by their own initializer; `HW_AddDriver()` keeps the registered driver in its separate framework-owned `DriverNode`. Each initializer retains its explicit library `lib_OpenCnt` pin on success, so the empty expunge hook cannot later drain these now-unused staging allocations. Expanded OD3415 from failure-only cleanup to include a persistent per-discovered-device node allocation on every successful module startup, in addition to the previously recorded namespace-walk and AddDriver failure leaks. This applies to the same five selected HIDDs/configurations and does not claim that the stored raw object pointer itself owns or pins the HIDD instance. The nodes are small and their count is bounded by discovered devices. No namespace scan, registration/removal, firmware, allocation failure or build was run; source-only.
