<a id="usb-hid-full-width-tablet-range-overflow-od2298"></a>
USB HID mouse tablet-range full-width boundary review (OD2298 expanded; OD3142 rechecked; no new ID or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced signed descriptor bounds through `hid_locate()` and the absolute-axis tablet event into Intuition's range divisions (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid.h:68-71`; `hid.c:271-281,407-430`; `mouseclass.c:135-158,324-341`; `compiler/include/devices/inputevent.h:196-199`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2179-2188`). Retained OD2298's exact reversed-by-one range, which yields zero. Expanded it with the ordered signed 32-bit interval `INT32_MIN..INT32_MAX`: its 2^32 cardinality is unrepresentable in the tablet's ULONG range field and the current signed expression overflows; a wrapping result can be zero before Intuition's unchecked divide. This is separate from OD3142's report-value extraction shifts; the full-width descriptor also intersects that separate extraction condition, so exact event coordinates remain compiler-dependent. Added the missing OD2298 master-index entry and explicit report anchor. Existing source bodies already have full-body credit; no path/LOC increment. No descriptor, event, build or runtime operation was used; source-only.


USB HID mouse per-report event-batch capacity pass (OD2188/OD4093 rechecked; no new OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): counted every append into the worker's fixed `10 * sizeof(struct InputEvent)` allocation against the selected report-to-event branch (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/mouseclass.c:250,324-465`; `MAX_BTN` is 16 in `hid.h:96`). A relative report contributes at most one movement event; the output switch emits transitions only for the first three button bits, with up/down mutually exclusive per bit, so at most three button events; a wheel report adds two raw-key events. Thus `IND_ADDEVENT` sees at most six entries. On the absolute/tablet branch one synchronous `IND_WRITEEVENT` uses the current slot without incrementing `iec`, after which the batch can still add at most three button and two wheel events; this also remains below ten. `input.device` derives the batch count from `io_Length / sizeof(struct InputEvent)` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:312-322`). The unchecked NULL allocation remains OD2188, distinct from capacity bounds. Buttons beyond the first three are not emitted by this switch; OD4093 specifically covers sparse Usage discovery before the supported event mappings, and this pass does not assert a general extra-button contract or add a separate finding. No event array, input request, device, build or runtime path was exercised; source-only.

USB HID mouse report-ring callback-context pass (2026-11-01; no finding or body/LOC credit): traced `HidInterrupt()` from `hidclass.c:65-84` through HID `AddInterrupt()` registration (`:310-317`) and both selected OHCI/UHCI completion paths. Their hardware interrupt handlers call `Cause()` for the registered interrupt (`ohcidriverclass.c:389-392`; `uhciclass.c:145-150`), and Exec's `Cause()` queues a soft interrupt (`rom/exec/cause.c:79-124`) before `SoftIntDispatch()` calls its code with interrupts enabled (`:140-194`). The mouse producer writes plain `head` and ring fields in `mouseclass.c:45-87`; the worker drains plain `tail` and those fields (`:294-304`). Exec's soft-interrupt node is made queueable again before its callback runs, so this pass does not by itself prove producer serialization on ExecSMP. The target-specific interrupt/softint CPU dispatch and whether a given selected OHCI/UHCI callback can overlap itself across CPUs remain open; no race finding is claimed without that link. No USB interrupt, mouse, build, or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.

USB HID mouse report-ring ExecSMP dispatch continuation (2026-11-01; candidate retained for targeted follow-up; no body/LOC credit): narrowed the previous callback-context question to x86-64 PC ExecSMP. `AddIntServer(INTB_KERNEL + irq, ...)` wraps the controller IRQ callback (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:19-21,64-67`); ACPI IOAPIC initialization routes each legacy IRQ to one configured CPU, defaulting to CPU 0 (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_ioapic.c:400-438`). This prevents simultaneous hardware delivery of that IRQ to multiple CPUs, but does not establish soft-interrupt serialization: `Cause()` enqueues on the shared `SysBase->SoftInts[]` list, sets shared `SFF_SoftInt`, and makes the node queueable again before invoking it (`rom/exec/cause.c:79-110,168-185`). The x86-64 idle dispatch loop checks the shared pending bit and calls local `core_Cause(INTB_SOFTINT, ...)` after waking (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:90-101`); therefore a second CPU can dispatch queued software work independently of the CPU that received the USB IRQ. The mouse ring producer itself has no lock around `head`, slot writes, or publication (`mouseclass.c:57-84`). This supports a plausible same-object concurrent/reentrant producer on an SMP system if another report requeues its node while the first callback runs and a second CPU services the pending soft interrupt. I have not established the timing/CPU wake condition strongly enough to promote this to a confirmed OD; keep it as a targeted synchronization candidate, distinct from OD3755's full-ring drop behavior. No USB interrupt, SMP scheduling, build, or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.

<a id="usb-hid-keyboard-report-coalescing-od11033"></a>USB HID keyboard report-state coalescing pass (OD11033 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `USBKbd::Hidd_USBHID::ParseReport()` from the shared current/previous key buffers through `Signal(kbd_task, SIGBREAKF_CTRL_F)` (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/kbdclass.c:99-120`), then through the worker's `Wait()` and transition comparison (`:357-385,405-417,485-562`). Exec stores received signals as a bitwise OR and `Wait()` returns then clears that bitmask (`rom/exec/signal.c:60-81`; `rom/exec/wait.c:129-137`), so repeated report notifications coalesce. If a press report and release report are both parsed before the worker runs, the latter leaves `prev_code` at the pressed state and `code` at the released state; the worker emits only the key-up, losing the press. Added OD11033 to the detailed report and master index. This is independent of the tentative mouse-ring SMP overlap candidate and requires no SMP configuration. The implementation body was already credited; no path or LOC increment. No keyboard report, task schedule, device, build, or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.

USB HID keyboard report coalescing startup-gate expansion (OD11033 strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the worker's readiness branch (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/kbdclass.c:357-385`). `Wait()` clears the received CTRL-F bit before `dos_not_ready` is tested; while that flag remains set, the worker only retries `OpenLibrary("dos.library")` and skips report processing even if the open succeeds in that iteration (`:361-369`). Thus a report can be dropped by the initialization gate without a second callback: on a held-key device's next unchanged report, `ParseReport()` copies the held state into both previous/current buffers, so the key-down transition is lost; if the next report is a release, only key-up is produced. Expanded OD11033's trigger to include this concrete startup route; it remains the same latest-state/notification root cause. No DOS failure, report, worker, or device was exercised; source-only.

OHCI root-hub RHSC debounce and rescan caller pass (2026-11-01; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): followed the driver's one-second RHSC mask/rearm from `ohcidriverclass.c:404-427` through `OHCI_HubInterrupt()` and the generic hub worker (`ohcihub.c:265-284`; `workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:601-717`). A controller RHSC is acknowledged and disabled, its registered hub interrupt callbacks are caused, and a one-second VBlank timer later clears/re-enables RHSC. The generic worker scans ports when signalled, but schedules its own ten-second rescan only when `hub_explore()` reports an unbound child; it does not continuously poll connected ports. Thus changes occurring while RHSC is masked rely on controller latch/reassert behavior when the RHSC status bit is cleared and the interrupt is re-enabled. Source inspection confirms the software sequence but does not establish the OHCI controller's required reassert semantics for a port-change bit that remained set through the debounce interval; retain that hardware-specific question as open, without a source finding. No controller, port event, build or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.

RTL8139 PCI mapping caller selection pass (2026-11-01; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): traced `CreateUnit()`'s complete BAR selection and cleanup paths against both module build variants and `DeleteUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/unit.c:921-1012,1153-1202`; `rtl8139/mmakefile.src:1-20`). On i386/x86-64, the selected branch reads BAR0 as an I/O port, stores that port number in `rtl8139u_BaseMem`, and explicitly avoids `HIDD_PCIDriver_MapPCI()`; matching deletion excludes `UnmapPCI()`. On other architectures, the driver maps BAR1 and, if a non-NULL unit is later deleted, calls the corresponding `UnmapPCI()`; a NULL mapping prevents device setup and flows to unit cleanup. This source does not establish the PCIPC x86-64 high-BAR mapping route for RTL8139, nor an unhandled map failure in this caller. Other architecture-specific PCI backends and their mapping lifetimes remain outside this pass. The full `unit.c` body already has ledger credit; no line was counted again. No PCI device, map, unit creation, deletion, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="usb-hid-mouse-ring-execsmp-reentrant-callback-od11037"></a>
OD11037 cross-CPU dispatch condition recheck (2026-11-01; no new ID or body/LOC credit): tightened the earlier cross-CPU timing trace to the x86-64 idle-secondary path. AP startup configures, calibrates and enables its local APIC heartbeat (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic_ia32.c:1137-1140`); the enabled heartbeat reloads its per-CPU timer (`:933-961`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/apic_heartbeat.c:41-57`). When a CPU is idle, `cpu_Dispatch()` returns from `sti; hlt; cli`, checks the shared `SFF_SoftInt`, and invokes `core_Cause()` locally (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:78-101`). Thus, if the callback is requeued during its first execution and the secondary CPU is idle, a heartbeat wake before that execution returns can dispatch the queued callback concurrently without relying on an unrelated user-mode IRQ or IRQ-affinity assumptions. The callback-duration/heartbeat timing remains a required conditional interleaving, so OD11037 remains configuration- and schedule-conditional. This supersedes the earlier note at line 28229 that left cross-CPU dispatch unresolved; no runtime schedule was run.

USB HID mouse report-ring ExecSMP dispatch recheck (OD11037 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): closed the prior callback-overlap question by tracing the selected call and dispatch chain. `HidInterrupt()` invokes `HIDD_USBHID_ParseReport()` (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:65-84`) and is installed as the HID interrupt callback (`:310-317`); OHCI/UHCI completion callbacks queue it through `Cause()` (`ohcidriverclass.c:389-392`; `uhciclass.c:145-150`). In `SoftIntDispatch()`, Exec sets `ln_Type` to `NT_INTERRUPT` before invoking the callback with interrupts enabled, so a subsequent report can requeue the same node while its first invocation is active (`rom/exec/cause.c:154-185`). The priority-list spinlock protects only enqueue/dequeue, not execution. On x86-64 SMP, `core_ExitInterrupt()` checks the shared `SFF_SoftInt` flag and dispatches queued work on any CPU returning from a user-mode interrupt (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-36`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/cpu_intr.c:530-541`); configure enables ExecSMP for the x86-64 `smp` variant (`configure.in:1644-1669`). Therefore a second CPU can dispatch a requeued callback before the first returns. `USBMouse::ParseReport()` reads plain head/tail, writes the current slot and advances head without a lock (`mouseclass.c:45-90`), while the worker drains the same ring without a lock (`:292-304`). Two overlapping producers can select the same slot and publish the same next head, dropping or mixing a report; added OD11037. The USB package edge is commented out of the default x86-64 boot package, so scope is the explicitly buildable optional OHCI/UHCI/HID modules, not default-image inclusion. The source bodies already had credit; totals do not change. No IRQ, callback, CPU schedule, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

OD11037 overlap and neighboring-candidate distinction (2026-11-01; no new OD or body/LOC credit): separated the newly confirmed concurrent-producer condition from OD3755's single-producer full-ring drop and EK10363's duplicate-enqueue race. OD11037 requires one `Cause()` to requeue the HID interrupt node after `SoftIntDispatch()` has set it to `NT_INTERRUPT`, then another CPU to dispatch that pending callback before the first invocation returns; it does not require the pair of simultaneous `Cause()` calls in EK10363. The ring overwrite can occur with spare ring capacity, unlike OD3755's full predicate. No additional root or line credit.

<a id="usb-hid-dispose-during-report-od11038"></a>
USB HID keyboard/mouse disposal during active report-processing pass (OD11038 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced hub disconnect to child disposal (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:543-546`), USBDevice recursive interface disposal (`usbdeviceclass.c:618-626`), and HID protocol-to-keyboard/mouse class selection (`classes/HID/hidclass.c:385-405`). Both subclass disposers signal Ctrl-C without joining their worker; keyboard frees `code`/`prev_code` immediately (`kbdclass.c:241-257`), and the inherited Root disposal eventually frees the object (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-149`). If detach occurs after `Wait()` has returned Ctrl-F and while the worker is processing that report, the later Ctrl-C bit does not interrupt the current branch: keyboard continues reading the freed key buffers/instance (`kbdclass.c:384-417,485-530`), and mouse continues accessing its instance ring/state (`mouseclass.c:292-304,358-433,459-465`) before the next `Wait()` checks Ctrl-C. Added OD11038 for this conditional stale-state access. This is distinct from OD2184's missed detach signal during DOS readiness and OD3754's missing release events on normal shutdown. The explicit Efika CHRP USB package selects these modules but is not an ExecSMP target; the finding is therefore scoped to explicitly built optional modules on an ExecSMP configuration such as x86-64 PC SMP (`configure.in:1644-1671`; USB aggregate edge commented at `workbench/mmakefile.src:29-30`). On a uniprocessor, the hub task starts at priority 0 then raises itself to 10 after initialization (`usbhubclass.c:190-192,618`), while the keyboard and mouse workers run at priority 20 (`kbdclass.c:231`; `mouseclass.c:216`). Exec `Signal()` reschedules the higher-priority worker before returning (`rom/exec/signal.c:390-414`), so this pass does not claim the same in-flight overlap there. Existing body credits unchanged. No disconnect, report, worker schedule, or build was exercised; source-only.

USB HID mouse event-buffer allocation counterpart (merged into OD10994; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `mouse_process()` from its unchecked ten-entry `AllocVec()` through successful `OpenDevice()`, DOS readiness, and each event construction path (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/mouseclass.c:238-260,265-292,324-355,358-455`). A tablet event, nonzero relative movement, button change, or wheel change writes `ie[iec]`; when the allocation failed and the device opened, the first such event dereferences NULL. Expanded OD10994 and its master-index entry to cover the paired keyboard and mouse workers; OD2312 remains the separate successful-allocation/OpenDevice-failure leak. Existing body/path totals are unchanged. No allocation failure, input event, device, or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="input-device-swapped-button-qualifier-state-od11039"></a>
Input-device mouse-swap qualifier-state pass (OD11039 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `IDF_SWAP_BUTTONS` from selected IPrefs source and its manifest (`workbench/c/iprefs/inputprefs.c:90-104`; `mmakefile.src:7-21`) through `AddEQTail()` (`rom/devs/input/support.c:42-82`) and the worker's `IND_WRITEEVENT` forwarding to registered handlers (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:397-416,433-434`; `support.c:94-120`). The implementation swaps the left/right button value in `ie_Code` but leaves `IEQUALIFIER_LEFTBUTTON`/`IEQUALIFIER_RBUTTON` in `ie_Qualifier` unchanged. Expanded OD11039 after tracing the selected in-tree console consumer: `console.device` registers `CDInputHandler` (`rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:200-212`), which copies events unchanged (`cdinputhandler.c:105-116`) after Intuition and forwards RAWMOUSE to `charmapconclass.c`, whose selection state depends on `IEQUALIFIER_LEFTBUTTON` (`consoletask.c:408-415`; `charmapconclass.c:1491-1504`). Input button-swap console-selection effect recheck (OD11039 strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): re-read the complete `charmapcon_handlemouse()` selection routine (`rom/devs/console/charmapconclass.c:1460-1570`) and the console event handoff. The routine ends an active selection whenever `IEQUALIFIER_LEFTBUTTON` is absent, starts a selection when that bit is present and no selection is active, and updates the range while it remains present. `CDInputHandler` is priority 0 after Intuition and copies the event unchanged to the console task; Intuition updates internal button state from the swapped code but does not normalize the qualifier on the event. Thus physical-right/logical-left events fail to start or continue character-map selection, while physical-left/logical-right events can start or continue it contrary to Intuition's logical button action. This confirms OD11039's in-tree consequence; no input event or preference change was run.

<a id="xhci-stoprtiso-event-task-refill-race-od3196"></a>
xHCI RTIso Stop versus completion-task refill recheck (OD3196 expanded; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the xHCI event task's periodic completion branch from `xhciEventTask()` into `xhciHandleFinishedTDs()` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hw.c:523-541`; `xhci_hcd.c:2701-2814`). For a completed RTIso PTD, the handler invokes any client completion hook, frees that request context, clears the PTD's active/buffer-valid flags, counts remaining pending PTDs, then replenishes up to the one-or-two-PTD target through `xhciQueueIsochIO()` and `xhciStartIsochIO()`. `cmdStopRTIso()` synchronously calls `xhciStopIsochIO()`, which frees extant contexts and clears those same flags but retains `rtn_RTIso`; it does not publish a stopped bit, take a lock shared with the event task, or join that task (`uhwcmd.c:1665-1707`; `xhci_isoch.c:332-354`). If Stop interleaves after the completed request is retired but before the event task scans pending state, the event task can observe zero pending PTDs and submit fresh work after Stop has returned. USB Audio's `subLibStop()` returns success after this Stop and does not set `nch_DenyRequests` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3780-3808`); AHI calls it for `AHIC_Play=FALSE` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/audioctrl.c:958-979,1007-1014`). Expanded existing OD3196 to cover post-Stop resubmission in addition to already-submitted TRBs continuing to access caller buffers. This is the same missing event-task/Stop synchronization root, not a new ID. No body/path/LOC credit; no transfer, device, Stop overlap or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="usb-massstorage-large-block-unaligned-iobuffer-copyquick-od11041"></a>USB MassStorage large-block emulation CopyMemQuick buffer-alignment pass (OD11041 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `nRead64()`/`nWrite64()`'s large-block fallback into both 512-byte emulation helpers (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:2659-2722,2768-2830,2902-2915,3076-3086`). A 512-byte request at offset zero is accepted by each emulation helper; for a 1,024-byte logical block it takes the one-block read/modify path and calls `CopyMemQuick()` on `io_Data + dataoffset` without checking client-buffer alignment. `IOStdReq.io_Data` is an unqualified `APTR` (`compiler/include/exec/io.h:29-42`); the generic quick-copy body treats it as `ULONG *` (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:53-58`), while the m68k helper dereferences with `move.l` (`arch/m68k-all/exec/copymemquick.S:40-50`). Added OD11041 for an odd-address buffer on alignment-sensitive targets, especially m68k 68000/010, where the copy can raise an address error. Existing OD3798 remains the distinct non-power-of-two block-size translation defect; this finding uses a power-of-two 1,024-byte block and does not depend on that conversion issue. No request, device, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="usb-massstorage-bulk-cdb-copyquick-alignment-od11042"></a>USB MassStorage Bulk CDB CopyMemQuick alignment pass (OD11042 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `HD_SCSICMD` dispatch through `nScsiDirect()` to Bulk-Only `nScsiDirectBulk()` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:1382-1384,3596-3600`; `massstorage_bulk.c:299-305`). The public command pointer is byte-typed with no alignment constraint (`compiler/include/devices/scsidisk.h:21-34`), but 16-byte-or-longer commands are copied with `CopyMemQuick()`, whose documented source and destination precondition is ULONG alignment (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:24-37,53-58`). The destination CBW is packed and its CDB array starts at offset 15 (`compiler/include/devices/usb_massstorage.h:35-50`), so alignment is not guaranteed either. Added OD11042 for the valid odd-address command case and conditional 68000/010 longword address fault; exact local stack placement is not claimed. Kept distinct from OD11041's large-block IO data copy because these are independent call sites and input buffers. The module is optional in aggregate selection; this finding applies to explicitly selected USB MassStorage Bulk-Only builds. No CDB, device, build or runtime operation was used; source-only.

HDAudio HIDD Cause() source-caller recheck (OD2898 confirmed; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): followed the direct call from the selected HDA stream interrupt (`workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:166-189`) to stream assignment in `HDA__Hidd_HDA__AllocStream()` (`:824-835`) and clearing in `HDA__Hidd_HDA__FreeStream()` (`:966-987`). OD3330 USB MassStorage immediate change-command dispatch recheck (OD3330 strengthened; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): re-read `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_device.c:663-690,705-723` against `storage_task.c:21-36,242-251`. `TD_ADDCHANGEINT` and `TD_REMCHANGEINT` are in `immediate_cmds`; `dev_BeginIO()` directly calls `HandleIO()` for them instead of putting the request on the unit task's port. Thus `DoIO(TD_REMCHANGEINT)` returns after the caller-side `Remove()` and does not join or drain the separate task's `DoChangeInt()` `ForeachNode` walk. The walk still holds only local `Forbid()`, so the cross-CPU request-unlink/free interleaving documented in OD3330 is directly supported by this dispatch split. Confirmed the affected generated device name is `usbmss.device` (`storage_device.c:784-803`) and the module's parent aggregate edge remains commented (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/mmakefile.src:1`); no default package inclusion is claimed. No device, request, media-change event, build, or SMP schedule was run; source-only.

Hosted HostDisk Cause() and change-interrupt serialization recheck (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the direct Cause() call in `eject()` (`arch/all-hosted/devs/hostdisk/hostdisk_device.c:457-480`) against `BeginIO()` forwarding (`:269-280`), `unitentry()` dequeue/dispatch (`:520-533,596-619`), and change-list add/remove (`:409-423`). All requests, including `TD_ADDCHANGEINT`, `TD_REMCHANGEINT`, and `TD_EJECT`, are queued to the per-unit worker, and both list mutation and `eject()` notification occur in that worker; a client awakened by Cause() cannot have its removal processed until the current traversal finishes. Thus no request-list traversal/removal race is established for HostDisk. The full body was already credited at row 26476; this closes the direct caller/serialization question only. Cause() can defer callback execution past queue insertion, but this pass did not establish a stale post-wakeup access for the checked filesystem interrupt handlers, so no separate HostDisk lifetime finding is added. Unix-hosted HostDisk is selected under `workbench-unix`; the shared hosted module body applies there, while host backend behavior remains separately open. No host file, device, media change, callback schedule or build was used; source-only.

OD3002 ATA change-list dispatch reachability recheck (2026-11-01; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): verified that the concurrent list operations use separate execution contexts. `CMD_NONSTD` is 9, so `TD_ADDCHANGEINT`/`TD_REMCHANGEINT` are command values 20/21 (`compiler/include/exec/io.h:53`; `devices/trackdisk.h:50-51`); both bits are set in ATA's `IMMEDIATE_COMMANDS` mask `0x803ff1e3` (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:765`). `BeginIO()` calls `HandleIO()` directly for these commands after reenabling interrupts (`:811-827`), while `cmd_TestChanged()` is invoked from the bus worker's queued command path (`:315-344`, `:1138-1160`). Thus two submitter CPUs can mutate `au_SoftList` while the bus task traverses it on the selected x86-64 ExecSMP configuration; the local `Forbid()` scopes do not serialize those CPUs. This confirms OD3002's dispatch trigger and adds no separate root cause. No media event, request, callback or SMP schedule was run; source-only.

ATA daemon request lifetime boundary recheck (2026-11-01; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): `BusTaskCode()` allocates one `DaemonReq` per successfully set-up ATAPI unit and links it into the controller's daemon list (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:1069-1078,1092-1110`); the checked ATA sources contain no `DeleteIORequest()` for that field, and `ATAUnit__Root__Dispose()` only frees `au_Drive` (`ata_unitclass.c:105-114`). Traced the selected unload path: ATA's `RemoveBus()` explicitly returns FALSE (`ata_controllerclass.c:115-123`), and `ata_expunge()` disposes a controller only when `HW_RemoveDriver()` succeeds (`ata_init.c:293-319`). A controller with an attached successful bus therefore blocks that disposal path; failed unit setup does not create the daemon request. The missing request free is not promoted as a reachable current-lifecycle leak in the selected configuration. If bus unloading is implemented, teardown will need to unlink/free the per-unit request and coordinate it with daemon shutdown. No controller removal or expunge was run; source-only.

<a id="potgo-release-reacquire-caller-topology-od9806"></a>

### Potgo release/reacquire caller topology recheck (OD9806; 2026-11-01)
 reread the complete `FreePotBits()` split update against `AllocPotBits()` and `WritePotgo()`, then traced `ReadJoyPort()` through `llPortOpen()`'s mask allocation/direct POTGO configuration and `llPortClose()`'s release. Confirmed there is no lock across the poll lifecycle. The debug joystick utility is listed in `developer/debug/test/misc/mmakefile.src:22` and loops over `ReadJoyPort()` (`joystick.c:91-113`); optional RocketTool also loops on its chosen port (`rom/usb/shellapps/RocketTool.c:230-252`) and is explicitly buildable, although its parent aggregate is commented. Separate tasks running either client against the same port can therefore provide the second acquisition/configuration during a scheduler pause inside the first release. Kept OD9806 conditional on that same-port overlap and narrow preemption window; no runtime interleaving or hardware effect is claimed.


<a id="potgo-allocator-same-port-caller-recheck-od9803"></a>

### Potgo duplicate-allocation caller recheck (OD9803; 2026-11-01)

Reread `AllocPotBits()`'s unsynchronized free-mask calculation and reservation write, then traced both repeated `ReadJoyPort()` loops to their independent command-task callers: the debug joystick executable is listed in `developer/debug/test/misc/mmakefile.src:22`; RocketTool is in the explicit shell-app build target (`rom/usb/shellapps/mmakefile.src:4-8`) but not its commented parent aggregate. Both allow the caller to select a port and request the same fixed mask for that port. Their overlap can supply a maintained caller pair, but duplicate ownership still requires a scheduler switch between the two allocator operations and overlapping hardware use before release. Kept OD9803 conditional; no task interleaving or hardware access was run, and no body/LOC credit was added.


<a id="lowlevel-cross-port-caller-topology-od10154"></a>

### LowLevel cross-port caller topology recheck (OD10154; 2026-11-01)

Rechecked the `llPollGameCtrl()` whole-byte CIA direction snapshot/restore against its callers. The debug joystick command accepts a selected port and repeats `ReadJoyPort()` (`developer/debug/test/misc/joystick.c:91-113`; target listed in `developer/debug/test/misc/mmakefile.src:22`); optional RocketTool independently selects and polls a port (`rom/usb/shellapps/RocketTool.c:230-252`; explicit shell-app build target, parent aggregate commented). Concurrently running them with opposite ports gives checked-in call paths for the two distinct `ciaddra` masks. Both paths must enter game-controller polling and the scheduler must switch during the direction transaction; the earlier statement that no maintained concurrent caller existed is superseded by this topology, while the race remains conditional and unrun. The lowlevel debug UI polls ports sequentially in one task (`developer/debug/test/lowlevel/lowlevel.c:394-397`). No body/LOC credit or runtime operation.

LowLevel `ReadJoyPort()` port and allocation-failure recheck (OD9424/OD9803/OD9806 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): reread `llPortOpen()`, `llPortClose()`, and the public vector (`arch/m68k-amiga/lowlevel/readjoyport.c:157-237`) against the Amiga init hook and every checked-in direct caller. `ReadJoyPort()` rejects every port other than 0 or 1 before indexing `llad_PortType`; `llPortOpen()` initializes `potbits` on both allocation and non-allocation branches, and on partial `AllocPotBits()` failure frees only the returned subset. The Amiga init hook checks `OpenResource("potgo.resource")` and fails LowLevel initialization on NULL, so successful vector calls have a resource base. A whole-tree C caller census found only the sequential lowlevel debug display, the repeated debug joystick command, and optional repeated RocketTool polling (the latter is buildable but not part of its parent aggregate). Thus no additional port-index, uninitialized-mask, or failed-open candidate was established; OD9803's duplicate allocation and OD9806's release/reacquire state race remain conditional on concurrent same-port task calls and scheduler interleaving. No LowLevel API call, allocation failure, task schedule, or hardware access was run; source-only.

<a id="usb2otg-directional-data-toggle-state-od11044"></a>

### USB2OTG directional DATA toggle state pass (OD11044 added; no new path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01)

OD11044 IRQ retry-path reconciliation (2026-11-01; no new finding or coverage credit): repository-wide `hu_PIDBits` search found the acknowledged-bulk recovery update in `usb2otg_intr.c:851-852`, in addition to the normal completion toggler. The ISR computes accepted full packets, advances `iouh_Actual`, and toggles the same endpoint-only PID slot on an odd accepted packet count; its retry/rearm diagnostics read that slot at `:2537-2538`, while the scheduler later reads it for a resumed request. The device address and endpoint number are used for the table index, with `iouh_Dir` absent from both update and read. This is the same OD11044 state-model defect, not an independent cause. Reconciled all production reads/updates/resets found by `rg`: scheduler setup/completion, endpoint halt-clear, successful SET_ADDRESS/device reset, and the ISR acknowledgement path; the other ISR occurrence is diagnostic-only. No path/LOC credit changes. No interrupt or transfer was run; source-only.

Reconciled the USBHardware direction and endpoint request fields with the USB2OTG scheduler's PID-state storage and every selected read/update/reset path. `hu_PIDBits` stores one two-bit state per device and endpoint number; bulk/interrupt setup, packet completion toggling, next-packet rearming and `ClearFeature(ENDPOINT_HALT)` all index without direction (`usb2otg_intern.h:355`; `usb2otg_schedule.c:472-477,479-482,521-522,914-947`; `usb2otg_core.c:395-413`). In contrast, requests carry direction independently, Poseidon populates both fields, and in-flight exclusion compares direction as well (`usbhardware.h:30-32,146-149`; `poseidon.library.c:4624-4627`; `usb2otg_schedule.c:209-220`). This establishes OD11044 for devices with same-number IN and OUT non-control endpoints after an odd packet count in either direction; endpoint-zero control sequencing is excluded. Raspberry Pi ARM and AArch64 manifests include the driver (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:149,184`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:158,217`). Also checked a possible premature reset: `TermIO()` applies the `ClearFeature(ENDPOINT_HALT)` state update only after completion and only when `io_Error == 0` (`usb2otg_core.c:314-320,388-420`), matching the USBHardware contract's successful-request condition (`rom/usb/docs/usbhardware.doc:67-73`). Failed control requests leave the host toggle state unchanged, so this is not a separate sequencing defect. Updated the detailed report, index, and scheduler inventory rows. The source body and path were already credited, so no coverage numerator changes. No device, transfer, or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="ahi-handler-unsupported-unit-range-and-null-unit-io-od1451-expanded"></a>AHI-Handler unsupported-unit range and NULL-unit I/O caller reconciliation (OD1451 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): rechecked `UNIT/K/N` parsing, `ReadArgs` numeric storage, signed `StrToLong()` handling, the `int`-to-`ULONG` `OpenDevice()` argument conversion, `_DevOpen()` acceptance branches, and AHI-Handler read/write request submission (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:307,368-380,423-450,737-758,931-950,1016-1019`; `rom/dos/readargs.c:875-889`; `rom/dos/strtolong.c:55-77`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:239-246,304-325,440-443`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:101-108`). Confirmed the handler accepts any parsed numeric unit; the device opens normal units 0–3, permits `AHI_NO_UNIT` (255) for documented low-level API use while leaving `io_Unit` NULL, and also leaves `io_Unit` NULL with success for every other unit value. The regular AUDIO file path submits queued CMD_READ/CMD_WRITE, so the trigger extends from 4–254 to 255, representable values 256 and above, and negative values converted to the 32-bit unsigned device-unit argument. Expanded OD1451 and the master index; no duplicate finding ID and no body/path/LOC credit. No device open, file I/O or build was run; source-only.

AHI device `OpenDevice()` caller census reconciliation (OD1451 scope narrowed; 2026-11-07; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): reconciled the selected AHI-device openers listed in the device-body row. `workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:367-380,423-450,737-758,931-950,1016-1019` passes its parsed `UNIT/K/N` value into `OpenDevice()` and later sends the `CMD_READ`/`CMD_WRITE` requests through the DOS `AUDIO:` path; this is the in-tree caller that turns an accepted unsupported unit into ordinary NULL-unit I/O in OD1451. Sound.datatype (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3469-3501,3892-3895`) and USB Audio (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:2009-2027`) open `AHI_NO_UNIT` to obtain `io_Device`/AHI vectors. Exhaustive use searches for their request variables show only initialization, `OpenDevice()`, `io_Device` extraction, `CloseDevice()`, and request deletion; neither submits the low-level request through `BeginIO()`/`DoIO()`. <a id="ahi-handler-od1946-dos-error-return-and-partial-allocation-state-recheck"></a>AHI-Handler OD1946 DOS error return and partial-allocation state recheck (OD1946 strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): inspected the existing full-body trace at `workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:401-435,488-530,590-640,647-673,723-770,1178-1200` and matched it to DOS `Read()`/packet dispatch (`rom/dos/read.c:59-75`) and the handler's independent `ACTION_END` path. Confirmed each first-read allocation is attempted before the combined failure check; `initialized` remains true, so a retained `buffer1` skips retry initialization, while successful later allocations can be overwritten if `buffer1` was the one that failed. A non-NULL but not-yet-copied `readreq` reaches `AbortIO` on close; Exec dispatches through its `io_Device` (`rom/exec/abortio.c:44-55`). On write, failed `buffer2` allocation leaves `data->length == 0`; a positive retry invokes `PlayAndSwap(data, 0)` and then can repeat its copy loop without reducing `length` if the zero-length request returns success. The DOS read error is returned without closing the handle, so retry and close are valid responses. Strengthened OD1946 and added its previously missing master-index link. This reconciles an existing finding and adds no new ID or coverage credit. No allocation failure, retry, close, request or build was run; source-only.

BWFM IRQ arm/clear/rearm API and selected SDIO backend recheck (2026-11-01; no new OD or body/LOC credit): traced the sole checked-in `BWFMSetRxSignal()`/`BWFMClearInt()`/`BWFMAckRx()` consumer in `workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:461-473,534-569` into the resource vectors and implementations (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/bwfm/bwfm_init.c:2678-2774`) and SDIO signal registration/IRQ/rearm (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdio/sdio_init.c:1181-1190,1490-1535`). `BWFM_USE_IRQ` is fixed to zero, so the selected BWFM device does not call the interrupt helpers at runtime; the timer/poll fallback remains the active path. PTP DOS-read result propagation check (OD4443 strengthened; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): re-read `nGetPTPRspData()` and `nPTPRead()` response handling. `nCheckPTPError()` tests `pr_IOErr` and `pr_RespCode`, but not the container type or `pr_DataLength`; `nPTPRead()` sets `dp_Res1` to the clipped requested count before transfer and advances the seek position by that count when the status check succeeds. `ACTION_READ` dispatch returns to the worker, which replies with the packet without changing `dp_Res1` (`ptp.class.c:3641-3644,3928-3946`); DOS `Read()` returns that result (`rom/dos/read.c:56-75`). Serialmouse truncated PnP-frame caller recheck (OD2297 expanded; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the begin/end-marker loop in `mouse_pnpgets()` through `mouse_DetectPNP()` into `mouse_pnpparse()` and `mouse_pnpproto()`. A frame containing only a begin and end marker returns length 2, which is treated as a PnP ID; the parser reads revision through `buf[2]`, compares the seven-byte EISA field at `buf[3..9]`, and checks `buf[10]` without validating received length. Those locations are inside the 256-byte local array but beyond the frame data, so this is an uninitialized-data false-classification path rather than an out-of-array read. <a id="keyboard-device-open-failure-caller-census-od2304"></a> Keyboard.device failed-open caller census (OD2304 scope rechecked; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): enumerated all seven checked-in `OpenDevice("keyboard.device")` sites: input.device (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:193-194`), DOSBoot's optional matrix query (`rom/dosboot/menu.c:905-911`), VMM reset-handler setup (`workbench/system/VMM/reset_handler.c:63-80`), PFS3 reset-handler setup (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/init.c:444-465`), and optional Bluetooth HID, USB boot-keyboard and USB HID reset-handler setup (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:5813-5829`; `rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:531-545`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6548-6564`). input.device treats failed Open as dead-end initialization; DOSBoot skips the matrix query; VMM frees setup allocations and returns NULL; PFS3 and the HID handlers only register after a successful open and do not loop on failed Open. No automatic retry loop was found in these callers. This supports OD2304's failed-open unit leak but narrows repeat accumulation to a later independent call or an external caller. The caller paths are not all default-image components. No open failure or device operation was induced; source-only.

<a id="pc-keyboard-numlock-raw-code-od11046"></a> PC keyboard Num Lock raw-code table recheck (OD11046 added; no new body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): compared the selected i8042 and MinGW WINGDI standard scan tables with the public raw-key definitions. Both map set-1 scan index `0x45` (`K_NumLock`) to literal `0x5A`, while `RAWKEY_NUMLOCK` is `0x6D` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/stdkeytable.h:78`; `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/stdkeytable.h:78`; `compiler/include/devices/rawkeycodes.h:129`). The i8042 parser adds the break bit to mapped make/break codes and separately toggles software state for scan `0x45` (`i8042_kbdclass.c:393-404,425-453`); WINGDI applies the shared table and release prefix before callback (`wingdi_kbdclass.c:39-75`). Therefore emitted make/break codes are `0x5A`/`0xDA`, not the public `0x6D`/`0xED`. Scoped the selected path to i386-PC and x86-64-PC manifests; WINGDI is explicitly buildable but not claimed as a default package. This is distinct from OD2336's lock LED signal-mask defect. Added OD11046; table and decoder bodies already have full-body credit, so no path or LOC denominator changes. No keyboard event or build was run; source-only.

<a id="vcgfx-copybox-horizontal-nonoverlap-od11047"></a> VCGfx failed-DMA fallback predicate recheck (OD11047 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `CopyBox()` through the DMA gate and failed-transfer branch (`vcgfx_hiddclass.c:634-663`), the no-channel return (`vcgfx_dma.c:210-211`), optional DMA initialization (`vcgfx_init.c:56-128,158-179`), the BCM2708 package manifest (`mmakefile.src:33-42`), and the graphics.library `BltBitMap()`/HIDD caller (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-215`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:642-649`). `InitDMA()` leaves the channel at -1 on setup failure, its return is ignored, and Root.New still attempts `AddDisplayDriver()`. The CopyBox alias early-return checks same buffer plus overlapping vertical ranges but omits horizontal overlap, so a same-bitmap copy with disjoint X ranges and overlapping Y ranges returns before the NEON fallback when DMA fails. The absent-channel case returns before starting DMA; timeout failure also skips the fallback, but any partial transfer is conditional and was not observed. A 16×32 32-bit copy meets the 2,048-byte threshold. The method body and caller path already have full-body credit; no path or LOC totals change. No DMA, bitmap or display operation was run; source-only.
Gameport generated-vector and lifecycle reconciliation (2026-11-01; no new OD or body/LOC credit): checked `rom/devs/gameport/gameport.conf` against `gameport.c`, `compiler/libinit/libinit.c`, and `tools/genmodule/{config.c,writestart.c}`. Keyboard reset-completion multi-worker startup reachability recheck (OD926 strengthened; 2026-11-01; no finding/path/LOC change): traced both reset-completion producers back through their task initialization. The selected VMM handler manifest includes `prepager` and `pagehandler` plus the shared `reset_handler.c`; `VM_Manager_Init()` launches the prepager and then pagehandler as separate tasks on successful startup (`workbench/system/VMM/mmakefile.src:5-22,51`; `VM_Manager_Init.c:699-714`). VCGfx failed-DMA fallback public-copy contract recheck (OD11047 retained; 2026-11-01; no new ID or body/LOC credit): followed `BltBitMap()`'s clipped positive-size Copy case through `int_bltbitmap()` and `HIDD_Gfx_CopyBox()` (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:173-197`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:626-652`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1252-1288`). ## Android keyboard callback pointer-width check (OD11050; 2026-11-01)

Compared the Android keyboard's stored callback type with the shared input-HIDD callback typedef, its selected producer call, and keyboard.device's registered consumer (`arch/all-android/hidd/androidgfx/android_keyboard.h:4`; `android_kbdclass.c:205-209`; `rom/hidds/input/include/input.h:16,33`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:202-207,608-614`). ## Generic I²C 10-bit read sequence (OD11054; no body/path/LOC credit)

Promoted the earlier OD2586 trace after rechecking the public `UWORD` address layout, `Address`'s `11110xx` branch, and both read paths in `WriteRead` (`workbench/hidds/i2c/include/i2c.h:92-134`; `workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c:149-175,330-369`). NXP UM10204 §3.1.11 specifies the 10-bit address/read sequence: a read-only request emits a read header plus the packed second byte without first issuing the write-format selection sequence; a combined write/read repeats the second address byte after the repeated-start read header. The generic bus and Sam440 bit-banged subclass are selected by the Sam440 boot manifest (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:48-49`; `arch/ppc-sam440/i2c/i2c-amcc440.conf:1-25`). A repository-wide source search found no checked-in 10-bit-address client; the checked battery-clock clients use 7-bit addresses, and the RISC-V DesignWare backend is seven-bit-only. Promoted as OD11054 with reachability explicitly conditional on a direct public client. The implementation bodies already have full-body credit; no new path/LOC credit. No I²C transaction or build was run; source-only.

MassStorage worker timer lifetime and termination-path recheck (OD9699/OD9701 rechecked; no new active finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): reread the complete `StorageTask()` startup, removal/reuse, and shutdown path (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_task.c:69-357`) against `Storage::Dispose()` and all in-tree signal senders (`storageclass.c:338-361`). Normal disposal signals `SIGF_SINGLE`; the worker cancels/waits its timer request, marks the unit removed, re-arms the timer and remains alive in its cache-wait loop. Reattachment updates `unit->msu_object` and wakes that same worker. The explicit `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C` exit path aborts/waits for the timer request and deletes its reply port and request, but does not call `CloseDevice()`. A repository search found no checked-in sender of `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C` to these worker tasks, and no selected normal unit-removal path exits the loop; therefore a timer-device open-count leak on that exit route is not promoted as an active project finding without a maintained trigger. OD9699's independent unchecked timer port/request/open results remain confirmed; OD9701's unchecked cache-record allocation remains confirmed. No signal, timer, device, worker, reattachment, allocation failure, or build was exercised; source-only.
# USB MassStorage unit-number range retention and reattachment (OD11011 strengthened; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit)

Re-read `GetUnitFromCache()` and `Storage::Dispose()` together (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storageclass.c:67-80,120-129,232-260,338-361`). New identity records reserve `sd->unitNum` and advance it by `maxLUN + 1`; the allocator is not decremented or compacted on disposal. Disposal moves each live unit into the cache record's reusable `units` list. A later reattachment of that same identity removes and republishes those objects using the cached base, while a newly encountered identity receives the allocator's later base. Therefore OD11011's `uint8_t` collision does not require seventeen simultaneously attached devices: after sixteen distinct 16-LUN identities have reserved ranges 0–255 and been detached, the seventeenth receives base 256 and publishes IDs 0–15; reattach the first identity while the seventeenth remains active to create duplicate IDs in the active list. `storage_device.c:590-607` returns the first exact unit match, confirming wrong-device resolution / inaccessible duplicate-unit behavior. Strengthened OD11011's trigger and consequence; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit. No device, attach/detach, cache reuse, Open request or build was exercised; source-only.
<a id="od11024-usb-massstorage-duplicate-identity-construction-order"></a>
# USB MassStorage duplicate-identity construction ordering (OD11024 trigger qualified; 2026-11-01; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit)

Traced device-class construction locks from `USB::NewDevice()` (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbclass.c:260-268,315-377`) and the hub worker (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:579-590,603-620,707-720`). NewDevice holds the matched USB driver's `d_Lock` across per-interface class probing and `OOP_NewObject()`; hub processing holds the same per-driver semaphore while calling `hub_explore()`. The lock is per `usb_driver` record, initialized on `AttachDriver()` (`usbclass.c:130`; `usb.h:53`). This serializes successive new-device construction on one controller, so OD11024's no-worker second-object path is established when the matching first cache record has already been published. Different controllers have distinct locks; `GetUnitFromCache()` holds `sd->Lock` for lookup, releases it, and later reacquires it for insertion (`storageclass.c:67-80,120-129`), so simultaneous identical-device constructors across controllers may both miss and append duplicate cache records. No distinct consequence from that race was established, so it is documented as an open concurrency edge rather than promoted. No USB device, construction overlap or build was exercised; source-only.

# WirelessManager SANA-II scan request and results path recheck (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01)

Traced the complete `wpa_driver_sana2_scan()` request setup and `wpa_driver_sana2_get_scan_results()` completion/cleanup path (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:159-303`) through `wpa_supplicant_trigger_scan()` and the in-tree parameter producers. The standard configured-network scan builder zeroes the structure and places configured directed SSIDs before its wildcard entry (`wpa_supplicant/scan.c:249-382`); `bgscan_simple_timeout()` also zeroes it and supplies one directed SSID (`bgscan_simple.c:41-58`). With `WPA_DRIVER_FLAGS_USER_SPACE_MLME`, `wpa_supplicant_trigger_scan()` routes to `ieee80211_sta_req_scan()` instead of this backend callback (`scan.c:185-198`); the selected SANA-II backend sets that flag when `drv->hard_mac` is false (`driver_sana2.c:498-503`). The optional D-Bus scan path directly supplies zero-initialized params; its active no-SSID request reaches SANA-II with a NULL wildcard, and its passive-with-frequency request explicitly sets one NULL wildcard (`dbus/dbus_new_handlers.c:1205-1277`). `wpa_driver_sana2_scan()` does not inspect `num_ssids`; it copies entry zero into the optional `S2INFO_SSID` filter. The public scan-parameter contract distinguishes zero entries (passive) from a NULL SSID entry (active wildcard) (`src/drivers/driver.h:201-222`), but SANA-II's `S2_GETNETWORKS` contract only defines the tag as an optional network filter, not an active/passive selector (`compiler/include/devices/sana2wireless.h:21`; selected Prism2 documentation and handler, `workbench/devs/networks/prism2/request.c:1597-1649`). An ignored passive-vs-active distinction is plausible for a hard-MAC interface, but no selected SANA-II API contract establishes that the device can or must honor passive mode; this is not promoted as a finding. Results allocation failure frees partial results and clears `drv->scanning`; successful completion destroys the request pool after copying results. The existing OD3630 pre-submit pool leak is a separate already-recorded failure path. No new OD or body/path/LOC credit; no scan, device, allocation failure or build was run; source-only.

SANA-II scan completion callback follow-up (OD3976/OD9876 rechecked; no new finding or coverage credit; 2026-11-01): traced the device-port signal handler's completed `S2_GETNETWORKS` case (`driver_sana2.c:872-874`) into `EVENT_SCAN_RESULTS`, the generic event dispatcher, and `wpa_supplicant_event_scan_results()`/`wpa_supplicant_get_scan_results()` (`wpa_supplicant/events.c:899-925`; `scan.c:639-655`). The callback consumes `ios2_DataLength`/`ios2_StatData` and deletes the request pool after copying but does not test `ios2_Req.io_Error`. This confirms the two device-specific caller cases and leaves external SANA-II implementations outside the checked set. No new OD or body/path/LOC credit; no scan, request error, device or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="sana2-scan-pool-teardown-od11057"></a>
## WirelessManager SANA-II scan-pool teardown ownership (OD11057; 2026-11-01)

Re-read `wpa_driver_sana2_scan()` and `wpa_driver_sana2_deinit()` together (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/drivers/driver_sana2.c:159-210,881-915`), then traced the only normal pool release in `wpa_driver_sana2_get_scan_results()` (`:216-313`). The scan callback creates a pool, stores it in `drv->request->ios2_Data`, submits `S2_GETNETWORKS`, and sets `drv->scanning`. Normal `EVENT_SCAN_RESULTS` processing consumes the pool and deletes it; deinit instead aborts/waits for the main request and closes/deletes the I/O request without deleting its separate `ios2_Data` pool. `wpa_supplicant_remove_iface()` calls `wpa_supplicant_deinit_iface()`, which runs `wpa_supplicant_cleanup()` and then the driver's deinitializer (`wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c:2102-2121,2204-2224`). Cleanup cancels scheduled scan timeouts, not the submitted device request (`:397-410`); the SANA-II deinitializer handles that request later. The backend only reaches this scan callback when the device advertises `S2_GETNETWORKS` (`driver_sana2.c:982-990`); soft-MAC scans use the separate user-space MLME path (`wpa_supplicant/scan.c:185-198`). This establishes a leak of the scan pool and any device result allocations made from it when interface teardown occurs before result dispatch. The already reviewed source body receives no additional path or LOC credit. No scan, interface removal, allocation failure or build was exercised; source-only.

Adjacent SANA-II teardown-allocation cross-check (OD3628 retained; no additional finding or coverage credit; 2026-11-01): the separately AllocVec-allocated `drv->event_request` is indeed aborted/waited without `FreeVec()` in the same deinitializer (`driver_sana2.c:899-905`), matching OD3628's unconditional per-teardown request leak. OD11057 is separate: it concerns the Exec pool referenced by `drv->request->ios2_Data`, and only leaks if hard-MAC scan teardown occurs before the normal scan-result callback deletes that pool. The two allocations have distinct owners, lifetimes and triggers; no duplicate report entry was added. The existing report entries OD3628 and OD11057 and the master index were checked for both IDs. No teardown, scan or build was run; source-only.

AHCI unit-list Open/Close membership reconciliation (no new OD or coverage credit; 2026-11-01): traced unit-node membership from `ahci_RegisterPort()` through `AHCI_Open()`, `AHCI_Close()`, and `ahci_UnregisterPort()` (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:160-172,192-220`; `ahci_init.c:200-253`). USB MassStorage READ CAPACITY signed-shift review (OD11058 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the SCSI READ CAPACITY(10) eight-byte response into `capacity[]` and the two output fields in `HIDD_USBStorage_ReadCapacity()` (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storageclass.c:626-633`). `uint8_t` operands undergo integer promotion to `int`; shifting a first byte >= `0x80` by 24 produces a value outside signed 32-bit `int` range before assignment to `uint32_t`, so the source expression is undefined for a valid high-capacity response. The block-size assembly at `:628` has the same issue for an unusually large logical block size. Scoped the finding to READ CAPACITY last LBAs >= 2^31 and recorded the compiler-dependent consequence without claiming observed misdecode. The class body and package paths already have full-body credit; no body/path/LOC credit changed. No device, SCSI command, I/O, or build was run; source-only.
<a id="usb-massstorage-write-chunking-buffer-length-od11059"></a>
USB MassStorage write chunking and BOT data-length pass (OD11059 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): read the complete READ/WRITE methods in `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storageclass.c:530-612`, then traced their method messages through the in-tree stubs and TrackDisk command handlers. READ advances both the data pointer and per-chunk length (`:558-563`); WRITE constructs the same 1,024-block CDB chunks but supplies `msg->buffer` and `msg->count * blocksize` on every DirectSCSI call (`:588-605`). DirectSCSI writes that supplied size to the CBW and passes it unchanged to BulkTransfer (`:431-458`). For a request over 1,024 blocks the data phase therefore exceeds the current CDB block count, and later chunks resend the original buffer. DirectSCSI ignores the data-phase Boolean result before deciding from CSW status. The TrackDisk write handler passes the sector count and reports the full byte length after a true method return (`storage_device.c:263-286,320-350`). Added OD11059 with device-side outcome bounded by BOT/device behavior. The class body already has full-body credit; no path or LOC credit changed. No device, write, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="ata-large-lba48-bounce-read-setup-failure-copyback-od11067"></a>
ATA high-address bounce-read setup-failure caller pass (OD11067 added; 2026-11-02; existing lowlevel.c body credit retained): traced the 64-bit TrackDisk read handler through `ata_ReadDMA64()`, `ata_exec_blk()`, `ata_exec_cmd()`, PCI `dma_SetupPRDSize()` and Exec pooled allocation semantics. A 32,897-sector, 512-byte LBA48 chunk is 16,843,264 bytes and requires at least 258 entries; the x86 PRD builder splits at 64 KiB, permits 257 entries, then rejects insertion of the 258th, so `ata_exec_cmd()` returns before starting DMA. The pool is `MEMF_CLEAR`; nevertheless `ata_exec_blk()` copies the complete failed read chunk from the bounce buffer to the caller. The same copy runs for post-start device/DMA errors and timeouts after `DMA_End()`, and can copy partial DMA data. `ata_ReadDMA64()` returns error with `act==0`, propagated to `io_Actual`, establishing the report's error-with-output-mutation consequence. This is distinct from OD2996's unchecked bounce allocation. The platform/large-media/high-buffer trigger remains conditional. No body/path/LOC increment, device, request or build was used; source-only.

<a id="hid-shared-report-buffer-rearm-before-deferred-parse-od11073"></a>
## HID shared DMA report buffer rearm before deferred parse (OD11073 added; 2026-11-02)

Reconciled the coverage-only OD2108 note against current detailed findings and re-read both interrupt backends and the shared HID callback. `HID::New` registers the single `hid->buffer` allocation as the DMA destination (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:276-318`); `HidInterrupt()` invalidates and parses that same storage in place (`:63-84`). OHCI's done-list handler rearms its interrupt TD with the same buffer, updates the endpoint tail, then queues the callback with `Cause()` (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:352-391`). Exec queues Cause requests for later `SoftIntDispatch`, which invokes the callback with interrupts enabled (`rom/exec/cause.c:79-124,140-194`). UHCI likewise calls `Cause()` and reactivates/requeues the first TD before leaving its handler (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/UHCI/uhciclass.c:131-169`). The selected keyboard parser reads modifier bits and copies key bytes from the report (`kbdclass.c:99-114`); the mouse parser reads X/Y/wheel/buttons before enqueuing the event (`mouseclass.c:45-85`). A subsequent periodic DMA completion can therefore overwrite fields while the deferred parser consumes them. The HID, OHCI and UHCI targets are explicitly selectable but commented out of the USB aggregate dependencies (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/mmakefile.src:3-4`; `drivers/mmakefile.src:3-4`). Promoted the timing-dependent input-coherency candidate to OD11073; kept it distinct from OD2066's failed/short-completion handling and OD2443's teardown overlap. Actual overlap depends on controller cadence and callback execution time; no hardware or runtime test was performed. Existing file-body credit is unchanged; this note adds no new file or LOC credit. Source-only.

<a id="pciusb-ohci-uhci-ehci-reset-node-expunge-follow-up-od2372-expanded-2026-11-02"></a>
PCIUSB OHCI/UHCI/EHCI reset-node expunge follow-up (OD2372 expanded; 2026-11-02; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): traced all three `AddResetCallback()` sites to `pciusb_arospci.c:pciExpunge()`. OHCI/UHCI/EHCI embed the callback node and `is_Data = hc` in each pooled `PCIController`; `Close_Unit()` calls `pciFreeUnit()`, which stops the controller and removes its PCI IRQ but leaves unit/controller records allocated. `pciExpunge()` removes the records from lists and frees each `PCIController` to the device pool without calling `RemResetCallback()`. Thus a later reset can traverse a callback node whose controller owner was freed. The target is explicitly buildable from `rom/usb/pciusb/mmakefile.src`; no package selection or in-tree expunge caller was confirmed in this pass. Folded into OD2372's existing stale reset-node owner-lifetime root. No device close, expunge, reset, build, or body/path/LOC credit; source-only.

<a id="pciusb-deferred-completion-softint-versus-close-od11075"></a>
PCIUSB deferred completion and unit-close lifetime pass (OD11075 expanded and timer-expunge trigger narrowed; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced OHCI/EHCI hardware IRQ status into `SureCause(hc_CompleteInt)`, Exec's Cause queue and later softint dispatch, then traced `Close_Unit()` through `pciFreeUnit()` and each HCD free routine. OHCI/EHCI release `hc_CPrivate` before `pciFreeUnit()` removes the hardware IRQ handler; their deferred completion callbacks dereference that private pointer and the teardown has no removal/drain/join for queued or running Cause work. The selected PCI IRQ removal ultimately calls `KrnRemIRQHandler()`, which serializes only the hardware IRQ handler chain; it does not cancel a node on Exec's separate softint list. For the unit's `PA_SOFTINT` timer reply callback, `Close_Unit()` sets the port to `PA_IGNORE` and aborts, but an already replied `NT_REPLYMSG` request is not removed by timer `AbortIO`; the callback can still reach its unconditional `SendIO()` resubmission. Corrected the prior overstatement: `hu_NakTimeoutReq` and its reply port are embedded in the retained `PCIUnit`, so ordinary close does not free that request. The resubmitted request remains on timer.device's unit wait list; final `pciExpunge()` frees the containing unit without aborting/waiting, creating a stale wait-list node if expunge occurs before the 150 ms timeout. LDDemon supplies a selected later `RemDevice()` path for idle devices. OD11075 now states the expunge-before-timeout condition. PCIUSB/timer/Exec bodies were already body-credited; no path or LOC change. No controller, interrupt, close, expunge or build was exercised; source-only.

HID OD11073 interrupt-context dispatch recheck (2026-11-02; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): verified the callback does not run synchronously from `Cause()` in the selected hard-interrupt context. `Cause()` calls `Enable()` after queueing the soft interrupt (`rom/exec/cause.c:79-124`); `Enable()` only invokes `KrnSti()` and synchronous `KrnCause()` when `!KrnIsSuper()` (`rom/exec/enable.c:89-115`). PCIUSB OD11075 close/expunge lifetime source revalidation (2026-11-02; retained; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `Close_Unit()` and timer-device state transition against `rom/timer/abortio.c:69-98`, `rom/timer/lowlevel.c:202-218,269-288`, `uhwcmd.c:342-358,2186-2187`, `pciusb_arospci.c:709-769,777-795`, and `pciusb_dev.c:159-178`. `AbortIO()` removes/replies only when `io_Message.mn_Node.ln_Type != NT_REPLYMSG`; the callback's final `SendIO()` can therefore reinsert `hu_NakTimeoutReq` after close's abort when the timer completion was already replied/queued. `Close_Unit()` closes/deletes the separately opened timer request and calls `pciFreeUnit()`, but does not abort/wait again after the callback; `pciExpunge()` later frees each `PCIUnit` without touching its embedded timer request. Timer list traversal follows the request's links/deadline, supporting the expunge-before-expiry lifetime consequence. The completion-softint subcase is separately supported by `SoftIntDispatch()` dequeue-before-callback semantics and the OHCI/EHCI callbacks' initial dereference of `hc_CPrivate`; HCI free clears/frees that state before PCI IRQ removal. LDDemon reaches `RemDevice()` for a zero-open, non-busy device, whose device expunge hook calls `pciExpunge()`. Kept the existing trigger conditions precise: request must already be replied/softint queued or executing, callback must resubmit, and expunge must precede timer expiry for the timer-list stale-node case; SMP is required for the stated cross-CPU completion race. No claim that ordinary `CloseDevice()` itself frees the PCIUnit, and no device, timer, IRQ, close, expunge, or build was exercised. Source-only.

VirtIO block range/alignment peer-driver recheck (OD2390/OD2396 retained; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): reread the complete `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_io.c` request dispatch and `virtio_blk_rw()` validation, then compared the same byte-offset/LBA boundary against `rom/devs/nvme/nvme_io.c:34-72` and `rom/devs/ahci/ahci_io.c:74-113`. VirtIO rejects a start LBA only when it is greater than `au_High` and checks transfer-length sector divisibility, but has no full-range `nblocks <= au_High - lba + 1` check; it also does not reject low offset bits before `off64 >> 9` truncates them. The selected NVMe path explicitly checks whole-transfer containment and `off64 & secmask`; AHCI rejects offsets not aligned to its sector mask before converting to an LBA. These peer paths support the distinct existing VirtIO conditions recorded in OD2390 and OD2396, rather than an inferred universal Trackdisk rule. Rechecked the VirtIO dispatch's 32/64-bit READ/WRITE/FORMAT routes and found each reaches the same helper. Normal VirtIO bus publication remains separately conditional under OD2541; no unit, request, device, or build was exercised. Source-only.

Bluetooth SMP Secure Connections confirm-order recheck (OD3807 retained and refreshed against Core v6.3; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): re-read `bt_smp_manager_start()`, Pairing Response handling, public-key/DHKey completion, Secure Connections confirm/random handlers, and `setup_sc_until_peer_random()` (`smp_manager.c:355-401,650-685,801-844`; `tests/security/test_smp_manager.c:355-400`). The public API explicitly makes the manager Central/initiator; after non-passkey DHKey completion it enters `WAIT_SC_CONFIRM` without a send, while the handler for an incoming peer confirm sends local Pairing Random. The fake port overwrites `sent[]` on each call and the helper injects the peer confirm directly after DHKey completion, so it cannot assert that the preceding local Pairing Confirm was sent. Bluetooth Core v6.3 §3.5.3 specifies that the initiating device sends Pairing Confirm first and the responding device sends its confirm after receipt (https://www.bluetooth.com/wp-content/uploads/Files/Specification/HTML/Core_v6.3/out/en/host/security-manager-specification.html). This reaffirms the scoped Just Works/Numeric Comparison finding; passkey uses a distinct local-confirm path. No test was run and no pairing/controller exchange was used; source-only.

<a id="btserial-shutdown-admission-race-od11079"></a> BTSerial worker shutdown versus request admission pass (OD11079 added; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read all 789 physical lines (671 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) of the already credited `rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/btserial.class.c` and the complete selected device dispatch in `dev.c`. `bSerialTask()` publishes `nsu_DenyRequests = TRUE`, performs its final pending/write/read queue drain at `:721-759`, then disables the unit port, deletes the worker port and clears `nsu_Task` at `:760-785`. `devBeginIO()` tests `nsu_DenyRequests` outside its `Forbid()`/`AddTail()` region for both reads and writes (`dev.c:250-281`) and does not recheck it after entering the critical section. <a id="usb-audio-control-update-flag-race-pass"></a> USB Audio control-update flag race pass (OD11085 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced all five update cases in `subLibHardwareControl()` and the consuming batch in `nAudioTask()` (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:613-760,4105-4153`), matching the shared field in `usbaudio.h:188`. USB Audio control-update callback/worker ordering recheck (OD11085 retained; 2026-11-02; no additional OD or LOC credit): reread the five `subLibHardwareControl()` setter cases and the complete consuming `nAudioTask()` flag batch (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:613-760,4105-4153`; shared field `usbaudio.h:188`). Each supported callback stores the new mode value, ORs a distinct update bit and signals the worker; the worker checks the shared word before synchronous EP0 transfers and clears the entire word only after the batch. A callback during a transfer therefore leaves its signal pending for the next `Wait()`, but its flag has been erased, so the worker wakes and performs no control transfer. Reconciled all five setters and confirmed this is one shared check/process/clear race (OD11085), not five separate findings. No device, callback, control transfer, or build was run; source-only.

BTSerial OD11079 task-port lifetime extension (2026-11-02; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): followed `devBeginIO()`'s post-enqueue signal through the complete shutdown sequence. Shutdown deletes `nsu_TaskMsgPort` and sets it NULL (`btserial.class.c:774-778`), but only clears `nsu_Task` later (`:781-783`). A caller that passed the pre-lock admission test can therefore append while `nsu_Task` is still non-NULL, then dereference the nulled task port at `dev.c:256-259` or `:277-280`; another interleaving clears `nsu_Task` first and leaves the post-drain request without a worker. Both are consequences of OD11079's same unsynchronized admission/shutdown window. No additional drain follows the read/write queue insertion. No request, task-port deletion, schedule or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.

BTSerial OD11079 message-port command extension (2026-11-02; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): traced the other `devBeginIO()` admission branch. `CMD_CLEAR`, `CMD_RESET`, `CMD_FLUSH`, `SDCMD_QUERY`, `SDCMD_SETPARAMS`, and `SDCMD_BREAK` test `nsu_DenyRequests` before `PutMsg()` (`btserial/dev.c:298-313`). Shutdown sets the port to `PA_IGNORE`, drains currently queued requests with `GetMsg()`, then exits (`btserial.class.c:760-773`). Since the admission test and enqueue are not serialized with shutdown on ExecSMP, a caller can pass the old flag value and enqueue after the final drain; there is no worker left to consume/reply, and the message-port path does not recheck the flag. This is the same OD11079 admission/shutdown root cause as the CMD_READ/CMD_WRITE path. No request, port, schedule or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.
<a id="usb-bluetooth-shutdown-admission-od11090"></a> USB Bluetooth OD11090 shutdown/admission pass (added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced all queued command families in `rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/dev.c:258-275` and the interface release/worker teardown (`bluetooth.class.c:379-408,903-961,1075-1115`). `devBeginIO()` checks `ncp_DenyRequests` before `PutMsg()`; worker shutdown sets it and drains the command port, and `nFreeBT()` disables the unit message port and performs the final drain before deleting its task port and clearing `ncp_Task`. Because ExecSMP `Forbid()` is processor-local (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`), a caller can pass the old false check and be delayed until after that final drain. It can then enqueue a request that no worker will consume or reply to. Added OD11090, scoped to the optional target and an external client overlapping interface release. No in-tree caller, device request, interface removal, USB device, schedule, or build was found/run. The class body already has full-read credit; this adds no path/LOC coverage. Source-only.

<a id="usb-hid-controller-short-completion-recheck-od2066"></a>
USB HIDD report-length versus OHCI/UHCI completion recheck (OD2066 retained; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `HID::New()`'s `hid->buflen` allocation and `HIDD_USBDrv_AddInterrupt()` registration through `HidInterrupt()` and the selected controller callbacks (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hidclass.c:65-84,271-318`; `drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:318-391,453-519`; `drivers/UHCI/uhciclass.c:131-169,622-653`). The callback receives no actual byte count; it always gives the parser the configured `hid->buflen`. OHCI calls `Cause()` for a completed interrupt TD without checking its condition code. UHCI calls for a completed TD unless its NAK bit is set; its separate terminal-error-only interrupt path is excluded because OD2971 tracks that path as dropped before queue processing. A short successful transfer can leave the rest of the reused input buffer unchanged, and a non-NAK error completion can likewise deliver stale bytes under the current length. These match OD2066's existing scope; the same-buffer rearm-before-softint race is independently OD11073. No controller, report, device or build was used; source-only.

A four-byte ID 65,535 gives max+1 = 65,536, which narrows to zero in the 16-bit `nreport`; the size loop is skipped, the multi-report branch adds only one byte, and that one-byte allocation is registered for interrupts. The callback consumes that byte as the report ID and passes its one-past pointer to the selected keyboard parser, which reads descriptor-derived fields without using the supplied length (`kbdclass.c:99-117,145-197`).
