Etherlink III AROS vector-wrapper callback and data-cookie pass (2026-11-02; no new OD or body/LOC credit): re-read the selected `aros_device.c` vector table and Open/Close/BeginIO wrappers against `device.c` Open cleanup/CloseUnit and `request.c` dispatch (`workbench/devs/networks/etherlink3/aros_device.c:48-109,142-211,258-313`; `device.c:226-319,332-359`; `request.c:145-207`). The six AROS vectors occupy the expected Open through AbortIO slots and use the common DeviceBase. Open allocates the wrapper record before `DevOpen`; on success it saves each original callback, wraps the RX/TX callbacks, conditionally wraps a non-NULL DMA-TX callback, and stores the private pointer in the opener-owned ignored read-port node name. The failure path frees the wrapper record, while `DevOpen`/`CloseUnit` unwind a partially opened unit/opener. Close frees wrapper state before `DevClose` removes/frees the opener; no selected completion path was traced here that invokes an opener callback after Close returns. BeginIO preserves the original `ios2_Data` in `ios2_StatData` and substitutes the request pointer only for CMD_READ/CMD_WRITE/S2_MULTICAST/S2_BROADCAST/S2_READORPHAN; the matching request/worker paths consume `ios2_Data` as the wrapper cookie and `ios2_StatData` as the caller buffer before restoring `ios2_Data` in RX/TX callbacks (`request.c:392-470,649-661,1119-1155`; `unit.c:1621-1633,1768-1778,2172-2182`). No additional mismatch established in this wrapper slice. This does not close full-tree SANA-II caller behavior, generated install/package output, or asynchronous close/callback quiescence; no vector call, request, close, or build was run. Source-only.


<a id="od9921-short-sana2-open-request-and-arostcp-caller-recheck"></a>
## OD9921 short SANA-II Open request and AROSTCP caller recheck (2026-11-02)

Re-read Etherlink III `DevOpen()` against the AROS vector wrapper, Exec `OpenDevice()`, `IOSana2Req` field layout, and the selected AROSTCP request constructor (`workbench/devs/networks/etherlink3/device.c:226-246`; `aros_device.c:142-179`; `compiler/include/devices/sana2.h:128-139`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:96-119`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/sana2request.h:38-60`; `if_sana.c:321-335`). The wrapper itself does not read the SANA-II tail before forwarding Open. `DevOpen()` does read and clear `ios2_BufferManagement` before comparing `mn_Length` with `sizeof(struct IOSana2Req)`, so an allocation sized only to a shorter declared request can be accessed and written past its end. Exec dispatches the device Open vector without validating this device-specific length. The selected AROSTCP caller uses `CreateIORequest(port, sizeof(*req))`, so it does not establish the short-allocation trigger. Confirmed OD9921's existing eight-driver scope and exact trigger; no new finding. Added the missing OD9921 link to `AROS.md`. No OpenDevice call or short request was used; source-only.


Etherlink III OD9917 selected AROSTCP cookie-caller recheck (2026-11-02; no new OD or LOC credit): traced AROSTCP `CreateIOSana2Req()` and its request-pool initialization/completion paths against the Etherlink III AROS cookie adapter (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/sana2request.h:38-60`; `if_sana.c:321-335,510-545,930-951`; `etherlink3/aros_device.c:299-309,351-416`). AROSTCP allocates each request at `sizeof(*req)` and deliberately initializes packet-pool requests with `ios2_Data = req`, so this selected stack client neither triggers OD9921's short-allocation case nor demonstrates a changed-cookie consequence for OD9917. The adapter still leaves the substituted request pointer in `ios2_Data` on callback-free completion (offline CMD_READ and DevAbortIO), as documented in OD9917; no selected caller contract requiring a different value after these error completions was established. Keep OD9917 scoped to clients whose data cookie must survive callback-free completion, rather than claiming impact for AROSTCP. No SANA-II request, device or build was used; source-only.

<a id="workbench-hid-report-id-protocol-boundary-od11094"></a> Workbench HID OD11094 protocol-boundary wording recheck (2026-11-02; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): checked the accepted wide Global Report ID value against USB-IF HID 1.11 §6.2.2.7 and the local one-byte interrupt consumer. The specification describes Report ID as an unsigned value, reserves ID zero, and says data reports are prefixed by a single-byte ID (`https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/hid1_11.pdf`, pp. 36–37); it does not make the descriptor's encoded item value itself the on-wire prefix. Clarified OD11094 and its index entry to call this a four-data-byte-encoded Report ID Global item with value 65,535. The source-level narrowing and callback consequence are unchanged. No descriptor, device, report, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="usb-massstorage-short-cdb-validation-od2859"></a> USB MassStorage OD2859 command-pointer and CDB-length recheck (2026-11-02; existing finding expanded; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `HD_SCSICMD` through `HandleIO()` to the complete `cmd_DirectSCSI()` entry and compared it with the public `SCSICmd` pointer/length fields (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_device.c:357-408,493-503,548-553`; `compiler/include/devices/scsidisk.h:21-31`). The debug loop evaluates `cmd->scsi_CmdLength` before the `if (cmd)` guard; for a non-NULL structure the later opcode switch reads `scsi_Command[0]` even if the CDB pointer is NULL or its declared length is zero, before the existing opcode-specific short-field accesses. Expanded OD2859 to cover those same missing pointer/minimum-length checks, retained the trigger as malformed direct `HD_SCSICMD`, and added its missing master-index entry. The selected class-generated CDB callers use 6-, 10-, or 12-byte commands and do not establish the malformed trigger. No request, CDB, device, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="nouveau-od10008-private-display-destructor-chain-recheck-2026-11-02"></a>
Nouveau OD10008 private-display destructor-chain recheck (2026-11-02; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): re-read `nv04_display_create()` and `nv04_display_destroy()` alongside `nouveau_display_create()` / `nouveau_display_destroy()` and the `nouveau_drm.c` `fail_dispctor` route (`dispnv04/disp.c:189-242`; `nouveau_display.c:642-741`; `nouveau_drm.c:675-709,723-735`). The `vzalloc()`ed `nv04_display` is published in `nouveau_display(dev)->priv` and its destructor is installed before `nvif_event_ctor()`. Event-constructor failure returns immediately; the outer `disp_create_err` path only finalizes polling and mode-config state, and `fail_dispctor` does not call `nouveau_display_destroy()`. Normal `nouveau_display_destroy()` is the only path that invokes the private destructor and frees the `nouveau_display` wrapper. Confirmed OD10008's two-object leak and kept it scoped to optional Nouveau pre-NV50 display initialization with a non-NULL channel and flip-event construction failure. No new finding or LOC credit; no event, GPU, allocation failure, display, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="nouveau-nv04-crtc-prepublication-error-unwind-od10007-expanded-2026-11-02"></a>
Nouveau NV04 CRTC pre-publication error-unwind recheck (OD10007 expanded; 2026-11-02; no new body/path/LOC credit): traced `nv04_crtc_create()` into the selected `drm_crtc_init_with_planes()` error points and its later resource setup, then into NV04 display success and generic mode-config cleanup (`dispnv04/crtc.c:1302-1349`; `drm_crtc.c:258-296`; `dispnv04/disp.c:247-250,297-306`; `drm_mode_config.c:510-554`). Mode-object registration or name allocation can fail before CRTC list publication. NV04 discards that return, creates gamma/cursor/head/event state and may return success; the outer display constructor also discards the result. The primary plane is already registered, but mode-config cleanup reaches no CRTC destructor for the unlinked `nv_crtc`, leaving its CRTC/cursor/head/event resources without their normal owner. Expanded OD10007 with this early-allocation path, distinct from the existing post-publication CONFIG_DEBUG_FS CRC failure and OD10009 cursor allocation failure. No allocation failure, display, GPU, build or device operation was run; source-only.


<a id="nouveau-od10010-nv04-pageflip-submit-completion-race-2026-11-02"></a>
Nouveau OD10010 NV04 page-flip submit/completion race recheck (2026-11-02; existing finding expanded; no new finding or LOC credit): traced the kicked NV_SW page-flip method through the NV04 FIFO interrupt handler and NVKM software event callback, which runs inline to the handler that removes and frees the queued page-flip state (`dispnv04/crtc.c:1054-1086,1119-1147`; `nvkm/engine/fifo/nv04.c:278-296,303-342,406-430`; `nvkm/engine/sw/chan.c:30-39`; `nvkm/core/event.c:172-194`; `nvkm/core/uevent.c:113-120`). Fence creation occurs only after the kick and can fail on allocation or emission (`nouveau_fence.c:404-433`). If completion wins the event lock before the submitter's failure cleanup, the latter calls `list_del()` using the already-freed state. Expanded OD10010 with this conditional completion/error race, distinct from its BO-pin tracking mismatch. No page flip, fence/allocation failure, GPU, build, or hardware operation was run; source-only.


<a id="nouveau-od10071-nv04-resume-cursor-repin-2026-11-02"></a>
<a id="nouveau-od10071-nv04-cursor-resume-pin-failure-trace-2026-11-02"></a>
Nouveau OD10071 NV04 cursor resume pin-failure trace (2026-11-02; added; no source-body/LOC credit): traced suspend unmap/unpin through resume VRAM pin/map, post-modeset cursor register restore, and TTM BO movement (`dispnv04/disp.c:85-94,145-154,175-183`; `dispnv04/cursor.c:42-65`; `nouveau_bo.c:1071-1101`). No suspend/resume, BO movement, pin failure, GPU, or build was run; source-only.


Radeon CopyBox dimension-narrowing recheck (2026-11-02; no new finding or coverage credit): re-read `ATI::Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox()` against the generated HIDD signature and `BltBitMap()` clipping/dispatch (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_class.c:253-340`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:396`; `rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-216`). The Radeon method stores the public `UWORD` width/height in signed `WORD` locals before overlap-direction adjustment. For values above `WORD_MAX`, the conversion is implementation-defined; if it yields a negative `w`, the `w - 1` adjustment no longer moves an overlapping rightward copy to its final source/destination pixel. The accelerated register path then packs the original 16-bit width field. I did not promote this to a finding: the inspected sources do not establish that this Radeon engine accepts a bitmap or transfer width above `WORD_MAX` without earlier constraints, so a supported trigger and observable result are unproven. Existing CopyBox body and path credit are unchanged; no bitmap, GPU, or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="etherlink3-opener-rx-softint-lifetime-od11097"></a> Etherlink III opener RX soft-interrupt lifetime pass (OD11097 added; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced shared opener creation/publication and close removal/free (`workbench/devs/networks/etherlink3/device.c:250-303,545-560`) against the non-DMA and DMA RX traversal sites (`unit.c:1475-1505,2002-2031`), hardware interrupt-to-`Cause()` scheduling (`unit.c:1375-1410`), and ExecSMP's documented local-only `Disable()` semantics (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`). Multiple non-owning opens are explicitly permitted after `UNITF_SHARED` is set; both insertion and removal use `Disable()`, but RX traversal uses no shared lock. Since `Cause()` queues `unit->rx_int` for deferred soft-interrupt processing and ExecSMP `Disable()` masks only the closing CPU, an RX handler on another CPU can retain and dereference the opener while `CloseUnit()` frees it. Added OD11097, conditional on the explicitly buildable, non-default-aggregate Etherlink III target, shared opens, and cross-CPU close/receive overlap. No source body or LOC credit was added; no device, packet, close, interrupt, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="radeon-bitmap-pitch-wrap-od11098"></a> Radeon bitmap pitch-width bound and register-forwarding pass (OD11098 added; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `AllocBitMap()` width/height tags through the selected GFX bitmap superclass, which stores them unchanged (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:242-255`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:915-920`), into Radeon offscreen class selection and construction (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_class.c:187-223`; `ati_bitmap.c:71-108,140,232-247`). No maximum width/pitch validation is present before the constructor marks a successful VRAM allocation framebuffer-backed. With 32-bit pixels and width 16,384, the aligned row pitch is 65,536 bytes; the `ULONG` pitch component shifted left 16 is zero modulo 2^32 (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-43`). Traced the stored word to accelerated Radeon register writes (`ati_class.c:321-322`; `ati_bitmap.c:344,409,465,563,665,1095,1248,1664`). Added OD11098 conditional on a caller-requested large offscreen bitmap and successful VRAM allocation. No new source-body or LOC credit; no bitmap, allocator, GPU, or build was exercised. Source-only.

<a id="radeon-8bit-datatype-od11099"></a> Radeon 8-bit destination datatype pass (OD11099 added; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced bitmap depth and datatype construction (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_bitmap.c:71-137`) into the register enum (`radeon_reg.h:526-527`) and accelerated same-depth CopyBox dispatch/programming (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_class.c:276-340`). The constructor has cases for 15/16/32bpp only; 8-bit maps to bytesPerPixel 1 but retains datatype zero, while the register header defines indexed 8bpp as value 2. The blit path does not reject 8-bit same-depth copies and uses the destination's control word. Added OD11099, conditional on explicitly built/loaded Radeon HIDD, successful framebuffer bitmap allocation, and an accelerated operation. No body/path/LOC credit; no GPU, bitmap, operation, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="dwuart-rx-buffer-bound-od11100"></a> OpenSBI DesignWare UART receive-buffer bound pass (OD11100 retained as a low-confidence candidate; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the RDI interrupt dispatch to `serialunit_receive_data()` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:727-732`) and its receive loop (`:512-539`). The 513-byte stack buffer is indexed without checking capacity while the UART data-ready bit remains set; index 513 (the 514th received byte) writes past it. A source-level overflow therefore requires at least 514 bytes to be drained in one callback. The selected source does not establish that the FIFO/refill timing can supply that many bytes before the loop sees data-ready clear; an earlier file-row review explicitly left sustained refill unestablished. Kept OD11100 as a low-confidence candidate rather than a confirmed supported-hardware defect. Confirmed module and OpenSBI package selection (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/mmakefile.src`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src`). No body/path/LOC credit; no UART, input stream, interrupt, or build was exercised; source-only.

OpenSBI UART RX candidate caller recheck (OD11100 retained low-confidence; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): reread `dwuart_int_handler()` and the serial.device `RBF_InterruptHandler()` callback target. RX is drained in the interrupt callback before the serial.device callback receives the stack buffer (`SerialUnitClass.c:528-539,727-732`; `workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-90`), so the consumer cannot bound the local accumulation while it is occurring. This confirms the stack overwrite if at least 514 bytes are drained in one invocation, but does not establish the required sustained refill/FIFO behavior for selected hardware. OpenSBI DesignWare UART zero-length write caller pass (OD839 confirmation; 2026-11-02; no source-body/path/LOC credit): confirmed the selected `DWSerUnit__Hidd_SerialUnit__Write()` has the same post-tested loop as the existing PC/Sam440 cases (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:287-314`). RP1 DesignWare I²C `OOP_DoMethod()` return-contract and caller recheck (OD9455 retained; no new finding or source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): followed the class overrides through the actual OOP method ABI and generic public device wrappers. `OOP_MethodFunc` returns `IPTR` (`rom/oop/include/oop.h:118-122`), while the selected RP1 class overrides `PutByte`, `GetByte`, and `WriteRead` as `void` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/hidd/i2c-dw/i2c_dw.c:51-93`). The class configuration registers these implementations for the `Hidd_I2C` interface and subclasses `CLID_Hidd_I2C` (`i2c-dw.conf:3-20`). `I2C_WriteRead()` returns the raw `OOP_DoMethod()` value (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2c.h:173-184`); generic `Hidd_I2CDevice` methods propagate it, while `ReadWord()` copies its local two-byte buffer to caller output only if that result is true (`i2cdeviceclass.c:59-66`). This confirms OD9455's invalid completion-status contract without asserting particular machine return bits. Separately, the maintained Sam440 RTC and Radeon DDC callers use `WriteRead` but do not check its result; they are not RP1 consumers. The RP1 manifest declares a directly buildable module, while its aggregate edge is commented and the Pi 5 boot package omits it (`i2c-dw/mmakefile.src:7-11`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:226`); no checked-in RP1 I²C object/client was found. Workbench USB MassStorage capacity caller pass (OD11104 added; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `HIDD_USBStorage_ReadCapacity()`'s READ CAPACITY block-address field into the class unit state, `TD_GETGEOMETRY`, block-I/O extent checks, and raw DOS-node creation/mounting (`storageclass.c:614-640`; `storage_task.c:136-140`; `storage_device.c:104-124,148-163,206-222`; `storage_volumes.c:330-358,421-445`). Also checked the raw DOS node's `DE_HIGHCYL` assignment: although it uses a block address as a cylinder index, the selected raw-node path is the removable/CDROM path, and CDFS obtains device geometry then ignores this overlarge bound when the reported cylinder count is smaller (`rom/filesys/cdfs/bcache.c:120-177`). The target is selected directly by Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 package manifests (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:182-193`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-232`), despite the disabled general USB aggregate edge. <a id="usb-massstorage-gpt-backup-od11104"></a>
OD11104 GPT-writer consequence and client trace (2026-11-02; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): followed `OpenRootPartition()`'s copied `DriveGeometry` into `WritePartitionTable()` and the selected GPT table writer (`rom/partition/openrootpartition.c:68-85`; `rom/partition/writepartitiontable.c:48-68`; `rom/partition/partitiongpt.c:512-575`). The backup location is `root->dg.dg_TotalSectors - 1`; `GPTWriteTable()` records that location in `BackupBlock` and writes the backup header there (`:482-504`). HDToolBox saves changed partition tables through `WritePartitionTable()` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/gui.c:321-344`). Because USB MassStorage supplies the last LBA instead of the sector count, the backup header is placed one block before the actual last LBA. HDToolBox is explicitly buildable; its aggregate edge is commented, so no default-image claim is made. Expanded OD11104 with this concrete GPT consequence. No body/path/LOC credit; no GPT table, disk, write, or build was used; source-only.


<a id="ahci-full-track-format-bound-od11106"></a> AHCI full-track format-length caller trace (OD11106 added; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): re-read the selected `TD_FORMAT`/`TD_FORMAT64` branches (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_io.c:326-341`), ATA identify field widths (`rom/devs/ahci/include/devices/atascsi.h:71-72`), and DOS geometry publication (`ahci_cam_aros.c:302-306`). Traced the resulting `DE_SIZEBLOCK`/`DE_BLKSPERTRACK` into Workbench Format's `cbyTrack`, `cbyTransfer` selection and exact `io_Length` submission (`workbench/system/BHFormat/main.c:338-339,593-619,665,712-728`). BHFormat selects a full cylinder when it fits the 2 MiB transfer limit and otherwise a full track; either length is at least one track. The AHCI check compares against track bytes minus one, so both request shapes are rejected before `ahci_sector_rw()` reaches the SCSI write. The Format utility's virtual dependency is commented in the parent Workbench system target, so this is scoped to an explicitly built utility; AHCI remains package-selected on PC. Existing AHCI bodies were already credited. No disk, format operation, or build was used; source-only.


<a id="ahci-format-offset-bound-od11107"></a> AHCI format absolute-offset caller trace (OD11107 added; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `TD_FORMAT`/`TD_FORMAT64` offset extraction and check (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_io.c:326-341`) against the public IO offset field, AHCI's DOS geometry publication (`ahci_cam_aros.c:302-306`), and Workbench Format's `ibyOffset = icyl * cbyCylinder`, per-transfer increment, and request assignment (`workbench/system/BHFormat/main.c:338-339,704-728`). `off64` is an absolute disk byte offset; the branch instead rejects values above one track's final byte. BHFormat's full-cylinder or full-track transfer is rejected earlier by OD11106, so this later check is not reached on that in-tree path. No in-tree shorter `TD_FORMAT` caller at a nonzero offset was found; OD11107 remains conditional on a direct client making such a request. The Format utility is explicitly buildable; no source-body/path/LOC credit. No disk, format operation, or build was used; source-only.

Confirmed both PC package device lists include AHCI (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:73`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66`). `C:Eject` makes separate SCSI attempts before its trackdisk request, so this note does not claim those attempts always fail; the advertised direct command's no-op completion remains. <a id="workbench-load-command-od11109"></a> Workbench Eject/Load behavior trace (OD11109 added; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): read the full `workbench/c/Eject.c` command body and traced `load` from command-name parsing into `SCSIEject()` and `TrackdiskEject()` (`:106-148,168-278`). `SCSIEject()` never reads `load`; its hard-coded START STOP CDBs use byte 4 values 1 then 2, and `2` sets the ATAPI eject/LOEJ bit (`rom/devs/ata/ata.h:436`; same definition in SCSI headers). The helper ignores the second and third `DoIO()` return values and reads neither `Cmd.scsi_Status` nor `Cmd.scsi_Actual`; AHCI's SCSI completion reports CHECK CONDITION in `scsi_Status` while leaving `io_Error` clear (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_scsi.c:195-216`). `main()` overwrites the first result with the trackdisk result. AHCI's `TD_EJECT` branch succeeds without operation for removable devices (OD11108, `rom/devs/ahci/ahci_io.c:283-292`). Thus `Load` can issue an eject CDB and conceal SCSI failures behind the successful trackdisk no-op. The actual media outcome depends on command/transport acceptance; no device, request, or build was used; source-only.

USB2OTG bulk-OUT packet-size invariant recheck (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): followed `iouh_MaxPktSize` from Poseidon endpoint construction to the selected OTG scheduler. USB2OTG OD1522 cache-edge concurrency qualification (2026-11-02; existing candidate refined; no body/path/LOC credit): checked both selected `CacheClearE` implementations and the caller allocator alignment. USB MassStorage optional-identity string caller recheck (OD9702 boundary; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the selected Poseidon USBDevice producer for product, manufacturer and serial strings through device-object construction and HIDD attribute reads (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbdeviceclass.c:209-260,687-698`) into MassStorage's cache-key `strcmp()` calls (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storageclass.c:48-80`). USB MassStorage internal tunnel/shutdown admission pass (OD11110 added; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the active tunnel caller from `nStartRemovableTask()`/`psdSpawnSubTask()` into `nRemovableTask()` and `nIOCmdTunnel()` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:1040-1064,3910-3966,4311-4327`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:1434-1464`). The tunnel tests `ncm_DenyRequests` under local-only `Forbid()`, then `PutMsg()`s to the unit port and waits only on the shared reply-port signal (`rom/exec/waitport.c:77-85`). Interface release sets the flag and signals the unit task (`massstorage.class.c:704-735`); worker shutdown runs `nFreeMS()`, disables the unit port and drains it (`:1861-1876`). Exec confirms `Forbid()` is processor-local on SMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`), while `InternalPutMsg()` appends regardless of `mp_Flags` and only signals when `mp_SigTask` is non-NULL (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-105`). A cross-CPU tunnel caller delayed after the false check can therefore enqueue after the final drain with no worker reply and remain in `WaitPort()`. The last-close path signals and waits for `nh_RemovableTask` (`massstorage.class.c:120-136`), but that task cannot receive the break while waiting only on `nh_IOMsgPort`, so closure also stalls. The class has an explicit module target; the parent class aggregate is commented (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/mmakefile.src:20-22`; `rom/usb/classes/mmakefile.src:36-43`). Added OD11110, scoped to the optional target and a cross-CPU interface-release interleaving. Existing full-body/path credit stands; no device, request, removal, schedule or build was run; source-only.

<a id="diskimage-expat-large-plist-buffer-growth-od11113"></a>
DiskImage Expat large-buffer arithmetic and DMG caller pass (OD11113; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `XML_GetBuffer()`'s `neededSize` and repeated signed-int capacity doubling against the `XML_CONTEXT_BYTES=1024` selected configuration, then traced the optional DMG caller from the 64-bit `koly->xml_length` field through narrowing to `ULONG`, whole-plist `AllocVec`/`Read`, and one-shot `XML_Parse`. For a positive request above 1 GiB, capacity doubling passes the signed-int range without any pre-check, so the allocation request/loop can overflow or fail to make progress instead of returning the parser's normal allocation error. This is distinct from OD10311's negative-length case and remains conditional on a very large contiguous plist allocation succeeding. WirelessManager Amiga event-loop stale timer request caller follow-up (OD3941 expanded; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read all 436 physical lines of `src/utils/eloop_amiga.c` and traced both selected SANA-II timeout-list mutation paths. The association callback can replace the authentication timeout with a fresh first-EAPOL timeout before `eloop_run()` handles a timer bit already returned by `Wait()`; the loop then invokes the new head without checking its deadline. On disconnect, the callback schedules a 100-ms recovery scan and cancels the 30-second stay-alive timeout while the timer request remains armed for the old deadline, potentially delaying the scan. These are two manifestations of the existing OD3941 stale-request/list-head defect, not a separate OD. Confirmed the build selects `CONFIG_DRIVER_SANA2=y` and `CONFIG_ELOOP=eloop_amiga` (`wpa_supplicant/.config:124,294-295`). No event, timer, device, or build was run; source-only.

Potgo START-bit TODO disposition (OD9803/OD9806 scope pass; 2026-11-02; no new finding or body/LOC credit): checked the public `resources/potgo.h`, all selected resource vectors, and repository-wide `POTGO`/`POTGOR` definitions and `AllocPotBits()` callers. <a id="potgo-failed-allocation-unowned-free-od9424"></a>OD9424 detailed-path restoration (2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): reconciled the failed-allocation branch with the later `ReadJoyPort()` close. `llPortOpen()` frees only `potres` immediately, but still returns the original requested `potbits` through `*bits`; every valid port path then calls `llPortClose()`, which frees that full mask. For the selected AmigaMouse port-0 reservation (`0x0f00`), a failed LowLevel allocation therefore reaches `FreePotBits(0x0f00)` and clears the other owner's bitmap/data. <a id="ahci-uncalibrated-hard-sleep-scale-od9920"></a>
AHCI uncalibrated hard-sleep scale and timer call-order pass (OD9920 expanded; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `rom/devs/ahci/timer.c` in full and traced every `ahci_OpenTimer()` caller plus the selected reset path. `iters_per_100ns` starts at `~0`; the first `ahci_wait_ne()` calls from `ahci_init()` precede all `ahci_OpenTimer()` calls (`ahci.c:150-161,3836-3852`; `ahci_aros.c:67,139,159`; `ahci_cam_aros.c:72`). If the reset bit remains set, each 1 µs hard sleep computes `(1000+99)/100 * 0xffffffff`, which wraps as 32-bit `ULONG` to 4,294,967,286 loop iterations. Later, `ahci_Calibrate()` can return FALSE when its measured interval reaches a whole second (`timer.c:49-56`), while `ahci_OpenTimer()` discards that result and still returns the request (`:92-98`), again leaving the sentinel. `ahci_os_hardsleep()` then sends it to `ahci_WaitNano()` without validation (`ahci_aros.c:146-149`; `timer.c:131-140`). The PC manifests list AHCI in `KDEVS` (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:73`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66`). This strengthens the existing OD9920 candidate; no new body credit because the timer implementation was already credited. No hardware, timer, or delay was exercised.


<a id="ata-controller-startup-rollback-od2573-od2574"></a>
ATA controller startup failure recheck (OD2573/OD2574 restored from existing detailed source trace; 2026-11-02; no new finding ID or body/LOC credit): a whole-file reread of `rom/devs/ata/ata_controllerclass.c` and caller reconciliation confirmed the two distinct branches already assigned to these findings. `NewCreateTask()` failure returns from subclass `Root.New` without disposing the superclass allocation; `OOP_NewObject()` returns NULL without rollback, leaking the allocated object and its root-class instance count (`ata_controllerclass.c:27-58`; `rom/oop/newobject.c:104-114`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-128`). Separately, if the worker task starts but timer setup/calibration fails, it signals the constructor before assigning `ac_Daemon`; the constructor nevertheless inserts and returns the controller, whose later Dispose signals that NULL field (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:942-963`; `ata_controllerclass.c:60-90`; `rom/exec/signal.c:262-303`). The detailed findings are OD2573 and OD2574; the temporary duplicate OD11114 entry has been removed. No allocation failure, timer failure, object lifecycle or build was run.


<a id="hosted-parallel-hidd-unixio-allocation-failure-od11115"></a>
Hosted parallel HIDD UnixIO allocation-failure cleanup (OD11115; 2026-11-02; no new path/LOC credit): traced `UXParUnit__Root__New()` from superclass allocation through UnixIO-object creation and all failure cleanup, then followed the object destructor into `RemInterrupt`/`CloseFile` (`arch/all-unix/hidd/parallel/ParallelUnitClass.c:91-153`). Root-class allocation clears all instance bytes (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-128`); the constructor leaves `unixio_int.fd` at zero until after UnixIO object creation, while the disposer treats any value except `-1` as an acquired descriptor and dispatches through `data->unixio`. Thus failure to allocate the UnixIO object reaches partial-object disposal with `unixio == NULL` and `fd == 0`. The class is selected by the hosted Unix parallel HIDD manifest and its parent factory creates these units; the same class is exposed through the public OOP unit class. Added OD11115. No allocation failure, object construction, or host operation was run; source-only.

PCNet32 generated Open/Close vector and count recheck (OD3064 detailed report restored; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the `pcnet32.conf` generated Open/Close hooks and BeginIO/AbortIO vectors against the complete Open/Close implementations and Exec `OpenDevice()` result handling. `CreateUnit()` allocates the unit with `MEMF_CLEAR`; `Open()` increments `pcnu_open_count` after the busy test even when that test sets `IOERR_UNITBUSY`, and its opener-allocation failure also occurs after increment. <a id="pcnet32-shared-close-rejected-open-od3066"></a>
PCNet32 shared-Close and rejected-exclusive-Open caller pass (OD3066 restored and expanded; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the shared admission branch (`pcnet32_init.c:200-211`), generated Open failure's direct `CloseDevice()` call (`:241-248`), the Close hook's unconditional `unit->stop()` while `IFF_UP` (`:251-271`), and the selected `pcn32_close()` teardown (`pcnet32.c:448-474`). Closing one valid shared opener while another remains removes IRQs, stops the controller, drains rings, frees the current buffers and reports offline. <a id="nouveau-r535-control-reply-status-and-ownership-review"></a>

## Nouveau R535 RM control reply/status pass (OD11121 added; 2026-11-02)

Read the complete 93-line `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/ctrl.c` body (59 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) and traced the shared control wrappers plus the no-result event-registration caller. Added OD11121: `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_wr()` passes zero expected reply bytes; the RPC receiver consumes a matching response and returns `NULL`; the control wrapper's `IS_ERR_OR_NULL` branch then returns `PTR_ERR(NULL) == 0` before examining the RM control status. The caller consequently sees success even if the RM command failed. The message receiver still propagates nonzero RPC-envelope results, so the candidate is limited to RM-level status failures inside a successful envelope. No control response, firmware failure, or GPU operation was run; source-only.

OD11145 caller and failed-oneinit lifetime follow-through (2026-11-02; no new finding or LOC credit): traced the sole `nvkm_gsp_fwsec_frts()` caller through `tu102_gsp_oneinit()` (`subdev/gsp/tu102.c:298-360`). FRTS runs after the shared GSP oneinit and WPR metadata setup; an FRTS error returns directly and aborts GSP oneinit. The selected Turing/Ampere/Ada paths use TU102 GSP oneinit; Blackwell's GH100 GSP path does not call this FRTS helper. No initialization failure or GPU operation was induced; source-only.

## Generic PCI DMA allocator public-size contract recheck (OD11159; 2026-11-03)

Re-read the generic `AllocPCIMem()`/`FreePCIMem()` methods and the PCI HIDD method declaration, then traced the allocator through selected PCIPC superclass configuration and rechecked the complete direct-call census. The request is `ULONG`, while `AllocVec` takes pointer-sized `IPTR`. On 32-bit targets, `sizeof(APTR)` and the arithmetic are also 32-bit, so the added page/alignment overhead wraps before the call; on 64-bit targets the pointer-sized terms widen the expression and this wrap is not established. A wrapped length permits successful allocation of a block smaller than the requested DMA region. OD11159 promotes this existing public-API candidate to the detailed report. PCIPC is build-selected on PC targets and inherits the allocator; the sampled in-tree DMA clients use bounded sizes, with no near-limit request established. No DMA allocation, out-of-range buffer use, device or build was run. Source-only; no new body or LOC credit.

<a id="generic-pci-interrupt-adapter-and-pcipc-inheritance-recheck-od11159-type-scope-correction-no-new-finding-or-bodyloc-credit-2026-11-03"></a>
## Generic PCI interrupt adapter and PCIPC inheritance recheck (OD11159 type-scope correction; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03)

Re-read the generic PCIDriver `AddInterrupt()`/`RemoveInterrupt()` methods and traced them through PCIDevice's `INTLine` getter/setter and the selected PCIPC class (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:279-338`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:1196-1198,1371-1375`; `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc.conf:6-8,14-30`). The inherited adapter obtains the device's byte-sized config interrupt line, stores the kernel registration token in `Interrupt.is_Node.ln_Succ`, and returns success only for a non-NULL token. `KrnAddIRQHandler()` returns NULL for an out-of-range source or allocation failure (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:77-111`); callers that mishandle failed registration are already tracked in area-specific findings, so no duplicate generic defect was added in this pass. This is targeted caller-path verification only, not a new whole-file/body credit.

This pass also revalidated OD3525: `ACPIHostBridgeCallbackA()` allocates its host-bridge node at `pcipc_driverclass.c:478` and immediately dereferences it at `:479-482` without a NULL check; this failure candidate is now restored as a detailed report entry and master-index link. It also corrected OD11159's integer-type scope against `AllocVec(IPTR byteSize, ...)` (`rom/exec/allocvec.c`): `ULONG` request-size plus allocator overhead wraps before the call on 32-bit targets, where pointer-sized types are 32-bit. On 64-bit targets the pointer-sized terms widen the expression and no wrap was established. The detailed finding and master index are now scoped to the 32-bit PCIPC/generic allocator path. No IRQ, allocation failure, PCI device, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="pcipc-multi-bridge-full-scan-and-duplicate-device-publication-od3522"></a>
## PCIPC multi-bridge full scan and duplicate device publication (OD3522 restored; 2026-11-03; no body/LOC credit)

Reconciled ACPI bridge enumeration and the generic hardware-driver registration chain with `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver()`/`InsertDevice()` (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:589-631`; `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:176-203`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:41-93,104-166`). `PCIPC_InitClass()` creates one driver instance per ACPI host bridge, while every instance starts the generic scan at bus 0 and expands through discovered secondary buses; `InsertDevice()` appends each present BDF to the shared list without checking whether that BDF is already represented. PCIPC's per-device MCFG selection is bus-based and does not limit the setup scan to its host-bridge instance. This confirms OD3522 for multiple ACPI host bridges; consequences are duplicate BDF objects and repeated enumeration callbacks. This report entry was missing despite historical ledger references and is now restored in the detailed report and master index. No multi-bridge ACPI namespace, PCI device or enumeration was exercised; source-only.

<a id="usb-hid-missing-logical-maximum-fallback-review-od11160"></a>
## USB HID missing Logical Maximum fallback review (OD11160; 2026-11-03)

Re-read the relevant `nParseReport()` Main-item construction and cleanup path and traced its caller from `nReadReports()` into the active interrupt-report item loop (`rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2216-2232,2828-2839,2897-2899,3414-3448,891-945,4833-4901`). When Logical Minimum is defined and Logical Maximum is not, the fallback computes `(1UL << nhg_ReportSize) - 1` without a width guard. For 32-bit `unsigned long` and a 32-bit field, the shift count equals the type width. The branch logs a recoverable error but leaves the parse cursor intact; the resulting variable Input item is retained, marked signed if the fallback maximum is negative, and later filtered by its stored logical range. This confirms OD11160 as a separate USB HID implementation of the same class of fallback defect as Bluetooth OD9414. Scope is limited to malformed/incomplete descriptors on 32-bit C ABIs; compiler-dependent result manifestation remains unverified. The HID class has an explicit optional module target (`rom/usb/classes/hid/mmakefile.src:4-14`). The complete `hid.class.c` body already has full-body credit, so this adds finding/caller evidence only: no path or LOC credit. No descriptor, device, report, or build was used; source-only.

USB HID logical-bound fallback branch comparison (OD11160 rechecked; no new finding or body credit; 2026-11-03): compared both the one-bound-missing and both-bounds-missing branches in `nParseReport()` and followed their LONG fields into item construction. The both-bounds-missing branch guards its `1UL << ReportSize` with `< 32` and supplies the signed 32-bit extrema for widths at least 32; the unguarded operation is specifically the `Logical Minimum defined / Logical Maximum undefined` branch, as scoped in OD11160. The array-item range cap occurs later and does not guard the earlier variable-item fallback. This confirms the finding's trigger and prevents conflating it with the adjacent protected branch. Source-only; no descriptor or build was used.

HID short-item signed-value semantics reconciliation (OD10155 restored and narrowed; 2026-11-03; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the USB and Bluetooth two-/four-byte short-item assembly at `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:2670-2689` and `rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.class.c:2014-2028`, checked the fixed 32-bit signed `LONG` declaration (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-39`), and traced USB Logical Minimum into item signedness and report filtering (`hid.class.c:3161-3172,2897-2899,4833-4897`), plus Bluetooth Logical Minimum storage/item copy/signedness (`bthid.class.c:2502,2236-2238`). A negative promoted `BYTE` shifted left by eight in the two-byte parser is undefined behavior. For the four-byte expression, the promoted `UBYTE << 24` result is within the corresponding unsigned 32-bit range but outside signed `int`; the signed conversion is implementation-defined, not a second undefined shift. Restored OD10155's detailed report and master-index entries from its source-backed ledger record, with that distinction explicit. No compiler output, descriptor, device or build was used; source-only.


<a id="efika-timer-ticks-full-body-review-od1574"></a>
## Efika timer tick arithmetic and caller recheck (OD1574 restored; 2026-11-03; no body/LOC credit)

Re-read the complete selected `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/timer/ticks.c` (156 physical lines; 99 `cloc 2.06` C lines) against its Efika timer manifest, selected slice IRQ, BeginIO, VBlank request and generic `SubTime()` macro. `EClockUpdate()` subtracts one 33 MHz second per call, then publishes the remaining tick accumulator as microseconds; a gap that leaves either accumulator at or above 66,000,000 ticks (typically about two seconds or more) can therefore leave an unnormalized fraction. The selected `TimerSetup()` path calls `SubTime()` with the shared elapsed or current clock as the source, and that macro mutates/normalizes the source without reducing the associated tick accumulator. For elapsed time, the next `EClockUpdate()` can count that excess second again. Restored OD1574's detailed report entry and master-index link because the coverage ledger cited the finding but neither artifact contained its detailed entry. OD1872 remains the separate low-word timebase-wrap issue. Full-body coverage was already credited; this follow-up adds no file or LOC credit. The Efika timer backend is selected by its architecture manifest and included in the package manifest, but current target compilation is blocked by OD9941’s shared-layout mismatch; runtime reachability is therefore latent until that is fixed. Delayed interrupt behavior and timer-request effects remain untested. Source-only.


OD1872 detail restoration (2026-11-03; no body/path/LOC credit): the Efika `ticks.c` review row already recorded that `EClockUpdate()` samples `mftbl()` into `uint32_t` and loses complete 2^32-tick cycles across a sufficiently long gap. Restored the detailed report entry and master-index link, and kept it separate from OD1574's >=66,000,000-tick accumulator-normalization condition. At 33 MHz one low-word cycle is about 130.15 seconds. The 64-bit accumulated output from `ReadEClock()` cannot recover wraps omitted before accumulation. The Efika target’s current compile blocker OD9941 prevents claiming present runtime reachability; this is latent until repaired. No hardware timing or delayed-interrupt behavior was tested; source-only.

<a id="usbmassstorage-detach-rebind-signal-coalescing-od11184"></a> USB MassStorage cached-worker detach/rebind signal-state pass (OD11184 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): rechecked `Storage::Dispose()`, cached-unit reattachment, and the worker's `SIGF_SINGLE` state machine (`storageclass.c:239-259,348-360`; `storage_task.c:173-222`). Both detach and rebind set the same signal bit, while the worker distinguishes the event by `MSF_DeviceRemoved`; Exec `Signal()` ORs bits into `tc_SigRecvd` (`rom/exec/signal.c:262-302`), so two sets before a `Wait()` consumes the bit do not preserve event count/order. In that interleaving the worker sees the flag still clear and handles the one wake as removal, despite `msu_object` already pointing to the rebound object. The removal branch cancels and consumes the current timer (`storage_task.c:212-222`); the timer rearm at `:338-341` is inside the `!(MSF_DeviceRemoved)` block (`:232-342`), so the worker does not rearm after marking the unit removed. With the rebind signal coalesced, it returns to `Wait()` without a timer or pending reconnect notification and can remain offline until another `SIGF_SINGLE` transition. This differs from OD2830's missed change-counter update. The component is included in Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 package manifests (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:188`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:227`); no detach/rebind or task schedule was run. **OD11175 caller/path refinement (2026-11-03; no new OD or body/LOC credit):** re-read the complete `res_nmkquery()` switch and included the `NS_NOTIFY_OP` completion-record branch in OD11175. After successfully encoding the question, it subtracts `RRFIXEDSZ` from unsigned `buflen` without a guard, then calls `dn_comp()` and writes the fixed RR fields. `dn_comp()` forwards that size to `ns_name_compress()`/`ns_name_pack()`, whose output bound is formed from the supplied size before copying labels (`res_comp.c:118-123`; `ns_name.c:386-397,430-464,506-513`). A small direct-call buffer can therefore underflow in either query-question sizing or optional additional-record sizing; the wrapped bound is not capped by the actual caller allocation. The selected `res_findzonecut()` caller uses ordinary QUERY and a full packet buffer; the expanded branch applies to direct API callers. No query or build was run.

Its nonempty record construction therefore demonstrates behavior of checked-in source, not a selected AROS caller. OD11171 remains scoped to direct consumers of the buildable `network-dhcp-libminires` API or future callers; no selected in-tree empty-list trigger is claimed.

<a id="gv100-family-sparse-ppc-sm-id-topology-trace-od11191"></a>
GV100-family sparse-PPC SM-ID topology trace (OD11191 added; 2026-11-03): revisiting the just-read full `gv100.c` body against generic topology population exposed that `gf100_gr_oneinit()` retains PPC masks at physical indexes while `ppc_nr[gpc]` is only a count of nonzero masks (`gf100.c:2015-2024`). Three GV100-family loops use that count as a prefix bound (`gv100.c:93-102,164-179,242-245`). The shared context generator later invokes the callback for each `gr->sm` entry (`ctxgf100.c:1303-1312`); GV100, TU102 and GA102 callbacks use the same PPC-count-bounded remapper to form TPC register addresses (`ctxgv100.c:160-168`, `ctxtu102.c:34-41`, `ctxga102.c:25-32`). Their descriptors configure three PPC slots (`gv100.c:306`, `tu102.c:123`, `ga102.c:176`), and all three context sources are selected (`sources.drm.mak:299,318,321`). OD11191 is conditional because the source does not prove that supported silicon exposes a sparse tail PPC mask. No physical topology, GPU operation, context generation or build was run; source-only.

<a id="bwfm-wifi-preferences-device-enumeration-caller-and-open-lifetime-recheck-2026-11-03"></a>

The Raspberry Pi Preferences worker probes units 0–3 and stops at the first failed open; BWFM defines a single unit and rejects out-of-range units, so the probe discovers unit 0 then terminates without a leaked `WifiDev` request/port. Unit-0 Open can start the firmware and persistent RX/control workers; the device intentionally allows a successful query-capable open when firmware loading fails, so this caller can still list the physical radio while later status/scan operations expose service failure. Atheros5000 OD11202 cross-CPU dispatch qualification (2026-11-03; no path/LOC credit): traced PCI `StatusInt` through `Cause()` to the RX/TX soft interrupts (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/pci.c:238-244`; `unit.c:1466-1489`; `rom/exec/cause.c:30-44,84-122,140-182`). Atheros5000 S2_TRACKTYPE rollback failure-path trace (OD3288 revalidated and expanded; no new ID or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `CmdTrackType()` through both global tracker setup branches, duplicate-baseline detection, baseline allocation, and `CmdUntrackType()` cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/atheros5000/request.c:742-811,842-878`). The global reference count is incremented or a node linked before either later failure, and cleanup decrements only when a per-opener baseline exists. Thus duplicate tracking and baseline allocation failure retain a phantom reference; no allocation failure/request was induced. Also confirmed `CloseUnit()` frees an opener without walking `initial_stats`, and `DeleteUnit()` frees the unit without walking `type_trackers` (`device.c:520-551`; `unit.c:474-523`); close-without-untrack and final unit destruction may therefore leak tracking allocations, but protocol expectations for mandatory untrack-before-close were not established, so this is not separately promoted here. Source-only.

Atheros5000 TX completion HAL-status trace (OD3294 revalidated and expanded; no new ID or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `TXEndInt()` and `MgmtTXEndInt()` to the selected HAL status contract and all HAL family implementations (`unit.c:2429-2457,2641-2655`; `hal/ah_desc.h:27-37,60-65`; AR5210/5211/5212/5416 `*_xmit.c` status extraction). Atheros5000 OD3288 global-tracker allocation-failure follow-up (same S2_TRACKTYPE pass; no new ID or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): rechecked the `tracker == NULL` path after `AllocMem(sizeof(TypeTracker))` fails (`request.c:766-777`). Atheros5000 OD11202 PC idle-dispatch evidence (no new finding or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): followed the shared pending state through the PC ExecSMP idle dispatchers. x86_64 and i386 `cpu_Dispatch()` check global `SysBase->SysFlags & SFF_SoftInt` after waking from `sti; hlt; cli` and invoke `core_Cause(INTB_SOFTINT, ...)` locally (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:90-100`; `arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:35-41`). Since `Cause()` queues in shared `SysBase->SoftInts` and sets the shared flag (`rom/exec/cause.c:84-108`), an idle CPU can run the callback queued by another CPU while the unpinned unit task runs elsewhere. This supports cross-CPU overlap as a possible x86 PC ExecSMP interleaving; no actual schedule was run. Updated OD11202 scope/evidence; source-only.

Atheros5000 OD11205 AROSTCP close-request ownership confirmation (no new finding or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): verified `CreateIOSana2Req(ssc)` copies the saved `ss_dev`, `ss_unit`, and `ss_bufmgnt` into the temporary close request (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/sana2request.h:37-59`); `iface_make()` stores those values from the successful OpenDevice request (`if_sana.c:375-378`). Prometheus library attribute-base teardown recheck (OD11225 added; targeted caller/path note, no source-body or LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced the two `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` calls in `LibInit()` (`workbench/libs/prometheus/prometheus_init.c:38-44`) into `DeleteLibrary()`'s conditional cleanup (`:117-135`). The first stored base corresponds to `IID_Hidd_PCIDevice`, the second to `IID_Hidd_PCIDriver`, but both cleanup branches pass `IID_Hidd_PCIDevice`. `OOP_ReleaseAttrBase()` calls `release_idbucket()`, which decrements that IID's shared bucket refcount and frees it at zero (`rom/oop/releaseattrbase.c:56-64`; `rom/oop/support.c:181-199`). Therefore successful cleanup leaks the PCI driver IID reference and releases the PCI device IID twice; a second live holder of that IID can lose its bucket early. Failed initialization with the driver IID base still zero uses only the valid PCI device release. Added OD11225. No library init/expunge or OOP reference-count operation was run; source-only.

The failure branch frees the interrupt allocation without clearing the stored handle; `PCIATABus__Root__Dispose()` then unconditionally calls `HIDD_PCIDevice_RemoveInterrupt()` and `FreeMem()` on it (`:221-235`). The PCI device wrapper routes removal to the driver's IRQ removal method (`rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:417-450`). Added OD11226 for the conditional failed-registration path. Allocation failure is kept distinct and not credited. No device or interrupt operation was run; source-only.

ISA PnP detail restoration and iterator backtracking recheck (OD11022; 2026-11-03; optional target, no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `AllocResourceIteratorList()`, `LockResource()`, `IncResourceIteratorList()`, and `FindConfiguration()` around failed list construction (`rom/isapnp/pnp_iterators.c:139-263,492-541,669-710`; `rom/isapnp/pnp.c:762-850`). A later descriptor's failed initial candidate marks an earlier iterator `m_InConflict`, but list construction destroys all iterators and returns NULL before `FindConfiguration()` can call `IncResourceIteratorList()`. Therefore a base-list conflict aborts the configuration search rather than trying the earlier descriptor's next valid base; an alternative resource-group list failure only skips that group. Restored the missing OD11022 detail linked by the index, including a length-1 ranged/fixed I/O example and the optional kernel-isapnp/i386 package scope. Full source body was already credited. No card, resource set, configuration or build was used; source-only.

<a id="ata-identify-fake-irq-busy-loop-od10307"></a>ATA IDENTIFY fake-IRQ status/handler recheck (OD10307 detailed; 2026-11-03; no path/LOC credit): traced command selection and fake-IRQ flag (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:590-599`), `ata_WaitBusyTO()` status sample, `Disable()`, and handler loop (`:440-560`), PIO-read/no-data completion (`:203-242`), and the alternate-command retry (`:1640-1675`). The fake path reads normal status once; if it sees BSY, `ata_IRQPIORead()` records missing DRQ but `ata_IRQNoData()` returns without clearing the installed handler on BSY, so the loop repeats with unchanged status while local interrupts remain disabled. This is separate from the ordinary timeout path and is conditional on a nonbusy ERR/DF alternate-status sample followed by a BSY normal-status sample. Corrected the earlier coverage wording that implied fake dispatch itself guarantees a nonbusy status. No ATA command or hardware was run; source-only.

<a id="expat-negative-parse-length-recheck-od10311"></a>Expat public parse-length validation and DMG caller recheck (OD10311 detail restored; 2026-11-03; no path/LOC credit): traced exported vectors (`workbench/devs/diskimage/expat_library/init.c:848-860`), both parsers (`xmlparse.c:1433-1605`), and DMG's `ULONG xml_length` allocation/read/parse chain (`plugins/dmg/dmg.c:285-305,322-339`). No negative check precedes the signed pointer/length operations; `XML_Parse()` can pass the negative `int` to `memcpy` when buffered leftovers are present, while `XML_ParseBuffer()` moves `bufferEnd` backward. The DMG caller's 64-bit on-disk length is narrowed to ULONG before being passed as int. No parse was executed.


<a id="expat-external-parser-shared-dtd-recheck-od10312"></a>Expat NULL-context external-parameter parser ownership recheck (OD10312 detail restored; 2026-11-03; no path/LOC credit): traced `XML_ExternalEntityParserCreate()`, `parserCreate()`, `parserInit()`, and parser cleanup (`workbench/devs/diskimage/expat_library/xmlparse.c:744-755,867-869,942-1065,1127-1134`). The shared DTD pointer is installed before `parserInit()` sets `isParamEntity` false; encoding-name pool-copy failure invokes parser free before the caller marks it as a shared parameter parser, so cleanup destroys the parent's DTD.

<a id="expat-dtd-copy-freed-element-recheck-od10313"></a>Expat DTD-copy element ownership recheck (OD10313 detail restored; 2026-11-03; no path/LOC credit): traced external child copy failure and cleanup (`workbench/devs/diskimage/expat_library/xmlparse.c:1040-1049,1127-1134,5701-5738`). `lookup()` inserts the element pointer before its default-attribute allocation; on allocation failure `dtdCopy()` frees the element but leaves its hash-table slot, then parser-free destroys the copied DTD and traverses that table. Trigger requires a copied element with default attributes and allocation failure at that array.


<a id="expat-utf16-surrogate-pair-recheck-od10314"></a>Expat UTF-16 surrogate conversion recheck (OD10314 detail restored; 2026-11-03; no path/LOC credit): traced `DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF8` and its little-/big-endian instantiations (`workbench/devs/diskimage/expat_library/xmltok.c:535-636`). DiskImage 64-bit read offset cross-plugin recheck (OD10472 expanded to DAX; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `TD_READ64`, `NSCMD_TD_READ64`, and `NSCMD_ETD_READ64` through `device/io.c:93-101` and `device/unit.c:341-349`, confirming the unit task forwards the request without clearing its high offset word in `io_Actual`. `IPF_Read()` and `DAX_Read()` both read only `io_Offset` and then set `io_Actual=0`; neither rejects nonzero high offset. Ramdrive shared reply-port WaitPort caller recheck (OD10506/OD11206 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced the two `WaitPort(&ramdrivebase->port)` sites in `Open()` and `Close()` against the unit worker's startup and exit `ReplyMsg(&unit->msg)` paths (`workbench/devs/ramdrive_device.c:147-218,231-243,492-545`). Both callers hold `ramdrivebase->sigsem` from before task creation/removal until after `GetMsg()` consumes the worker reply, serializing access to the shared reply port; the worker sends only the matching startup/exit reply to that port in these phases. No second worker, reply class or concurrent Open/Close consumer was found that could make the post-WaitPort `GetMsg()` remove an unrelated message in these paths. This does not change OD11206: the separately embedded per-unit request port is not initialized with `InitMsgPort()`/`mp_SpinLock` before concurrent `PutMsg()`/`GetMsg()` use on Exec SMP. No unit, request, worker or build was run; source-only.


FDisk shared reply-port and SMP message-lock comparison (OD10505 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `Open()`/`Close()` startup and exit handshakes and the worker reply paths (`workbench/devs/fdsk_device.c:108-179,188-206,522-545`). As in Ramdrive, the caller holds the unit-list semaphore over `WaitPort()` and the matching `GetMsg()`, serializing operations on the shared base reply port. Unlike Ramdrive's per-unit allocation, FDisk allocates each unit with `MEMF_CLEAR` before setting up `unit->port` (`:133-154`), so its embedded `mp_SpinLock` begins zeroed; the selected PC/ARM kernel `KrnSpinInit()` implementations set the lock to zero, and PC also sets owner null (`arch/all-pc/kernel/spininit.c:14-28`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/spininit.c:11-25`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/spininit.c:11-23`). The base port is in the `MakeLibrary()`-allocated cleared device base (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:100-110`), likewise giving its lock the current unlocked zero state. No FDisk counterpart to OD11206 was established. No device, message, task or build was run; source-only.

Nouveau fantog suspend/resume alarm lifecycle recheck (no new OD or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): followed `nvkm_fantog`'s private periodic alarm (`therm/fantog.c:29-70`) through shared thermal fan fini (`therm/fan.c:213-219`), device fini order, timer fini/init (`subdev/timer/base.c:152-167`), and the selected subdevice order (`include/nvkm/core/layout.h:15-27`; timer precedes therm, so fini is reverse and init is forward). The common fini removes `therm->fan->alarm`, a different member from `nvkm_fantog.alarm`; timer fini only calls the hardware alarm-disable callback and does not unlink pending alarms, while timer init calls `nvkm_timer_alarm_trigger()` before therm init. Thus a pending toggle callback can be replayed on resume before the thermal subdevice's init path restores its mode. The fan object remains allocated across suspend, and the source alone does not establish that this replay causes an incorrect output or unsafe register access; no defect is promoted. No suspend, resume, timer, GPIO or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="diskimage-selected-aros-open-startup-return-message-caller-pass-od11240"></a>DiskImage selected AROS Open/worker startup return-message caller pass (OD11240 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): reconciled `device/mmakefile.src`'s selected `init_aros` and `unit` bodies against `LibOpen()`'s `WaitPort(replyport)` handshake, `UnitProcEntry()`'s failure path, and `FreeUnit()`'s ownership (`workbench/devs/diskimage/device/init_aros.c:121-178,259-284`; `unit.c:73-120`). On early `UnitProcMain()` allocation failure, the child replies using the embedded `DeathMsg` and then reads `dm->dm_ReturnCode`; the awakened opener recognizes the non-startup message and frees that message and its containing unit. ExecSMP's `Forbid()` is processor-local, while `ReplyMsg()` publishes/signals the message, so an opener on another CPU can free it before the child's final read. Added OD11240 scoped to explicit AROS DiskImage device builds under ExecSMP and conditional worker startup allocation failure/cross-CPU scheduling. The non-AROS `init.c` is not selected by this AROS manifest. Existing full-body credits stand. No allocation failure, device, message, task schedule or build was exercised; source-only.

PTP SendObjectInfo fixed-buffer sizing recheck (OD4432 detailed finding restored; no new body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): computed the `nPTPSendObject()` fixed fields and serialized string sizes (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:1961-2024`) against `nch_OutBuf[1024]` (`ptp.h:391-393`) and one-byte PIMA string lengths (`ptp.class.c:1143-1231`). The fixed fields and date strings consume 118 bytes; two nonnull strings contribute `2*(filename_chars+keywords_chars)+6`, crossing the array when their combined character count exceeds 450. At 255 characters each, the payload is 1,144 bytes and the computed length is sent without a capacity check. Restored OD4432 with the metadata-length condition. No upload was run; no body, path, or LOC totals changed.


PTP rejected-seek cursor-state consequence recheck (OD4452 detailed finding restored with recovery qualifier; no new body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced the post-validation assignment in `ACTION_SEEK` (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:3601-3638`) through DOS `Seek()` error propagation (`rom/dos/internalseek.c:16-35`) and read/write cursor guards (`ptp.class.c:2293-2298,2415-2421`). Confirmed rejected out-of-range positions are stored, causing subsequent I/O to fail until a valid seek resets the cursor; a valid relative seek can recover, so no permanent lockout is claimed. Restored OD4452. No DOS operation was run; no body, path, or LOC totals changed.

Nouveau Falcon command/message queue timeout recheck (OD10288 confirmed; 2026-11-03): read complete `falcon/cmdq.c`, `msgq.c`, and `qmgr.c` bodies (358 C code lines), then traced all in-tree `nvkm_falcon_cmdq_send()` callers in PMU and SEC2. <a id="nouveau-r535-rpc-transport-receive-and-split-failure-review-od11270-od11271-added-2026-11-03"></a>
Nouveau R535 RPC transport receive and split-failure review (OD11270/OD11271 added; no path/LOC credit): reread the complete message queue receive, continuation assembly, notification dispatch, command queue submission, and split-RPC send/reply paths in `r535/rpc.c`. Traced the response length from queue peek into allocation, per-element copy, continuation payload subtraction, diagnostic dump, and reply dispatch. Confirmed oversized element lengths return `NULL` without consuming the queue entry (and the caller treats that as no response), mismatched continuation elements return before advancing the queue read pointer, no minimum RPC-header length check precedes parse/copy, a short continuation length underflows `len - sizeof(rpc)` passed to `memcpy`, and a continuation payload larger than the remaining aggregate reply is subtracted without checking, underflowing the remaining count and advancing the output pointer beyond capacity (OD11270). Then followed original request ownership through every split path; temporary chunks are released by `cmdq_push`, but the retained original buffer is freed only on successful final reply, leaving it allocated on chunk allocation/send/reply errors (OD11271). Existing complete-body/path coverage remains unchanged. No malformed queue element, large RPC, queue timeout, firmware, GPU, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="nouveau-r535-gsp-oneinit-and-idr-teardown-ordering-pass-od11273-added-2026-11-03"></a>
Nouveau R535 GSP oneinit and IDR teardown-ordering pass (OD11273 added; no path/LOC credit): traced all early returns in `r535_gsp_oneinit()` and its TU102/GH100 wrappers against common constructor rollback and `r535_gsp_dtor()`. Confirmed `client_id.idr` is initialized only after the final registry RPC, but the destructor always invokes `idr_destroy()`. The selected AROS `linux_idr.c` implementation initializes its mutex only in `idr_init()` and unconditionally locks it in `idr_destroy()`; the shared subdevice constructor installs the function table before later failures and rollback deletes the failed subdevice. Thus early GSP RM setup failures reach IDR destruction with an uninitialized mutex. No allocation/RPC failure, firmware, GPU, or build was induced; source-only.

<a id="nouveau-r535-gsp-radix3-table-capacity-boundary-pass-od11276-added-2026-11-03"></a>
Nouveau R535 GSP radix-3 table-capacity boundary pass (OD11276 added; no path/LOC credit): traced `.fwimage` section length through `nvkm_firmware_ctor()`'s page-rounded SGT backing and into `nvkm_gsp_radix3_sg()`. On the selected AROS compatibility layer both system and GSP pages are 4 KiB. The level-2 PTE allocation uses floor(`size / 4096`) before rounding its byte size to 4 KiB; if that floor count is a multiple of 512 but the firmware has a partial next page, the source SGT has one more page than PTE capacity and the population loop ends with that page unmapped. Added OD11276 for the conditional 2 MiB boundary case. The same layout has a hard 1 GiB ceiling (512 level-2 pages address 512 firmware pages each), but no size guard precedes the loop that writes level-2 addresses into the single 512-entry level-1 page; an image above that ceiling can overrun level 1 (OD11278). No firmware image, GPU, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="ata-pci-pio-count-unit-caller-pass"></a>
ATA PCI PIO count-unit caller pass (no new OD or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): followed all four `interface_pio.c` vector functions through `ATA_PIOInterface`, the selected PCI bus interface, and the generic ATA transfer handlers (`rom/devs/ata/include/hidd/ata.h:23-30`; `rom/hidds/ata_pci/ata_pci_busclass.c:311-327`; `rom/devs/ata/ata_bus.h:92-101`; `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:216-270,305-431,708-713,1020-1042`). The API's `count` is bytes: selected block transfers pass sector byte lengths, while ATAPI odd-length paths transfer even bytes through the word vector and handle the final byte separately. ATA sector sizes are 512 or 2048 bytes, so selected callers supply even lengths; the non-x86 word/dword loops' subtract-by-two/four behavior does not underflow for those calls. The x86 dword helper uses word transfers when bit 1 is set and dword transfers otherwise, preserving the byte count for the selected even lengths. No odd-length caller to the vector methods or independent PIO count defect established. Full helper and caller bodies already have ledger credit; totals unchanged. <a id="virtual-bluetooth-acl-fragment-reassembly-review-2026-11-03"></a>
Virtual Bluetooth ACL fragment reassembly and selected-caller pass (2026-11-03; no new finding): re-read `vbtp_HandleACL()` and `vbtp_ProcessPDU()` (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_peer.c:657-730`), the per-link reassembly fields and 1,100-byte capacity (`vbthci_intern.h:86-100`), reset/disconnect clearing (`vbthci_peer.c:108-121,1062-1072`), and the selected Bluetooth stack's queued `BTCMD_WRITEACL` buffer submission (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2616-2678`). The virtual controller advertises 1,021-byte classic and 251-byte LE ACL payload buffers; the selected stack uses those controller values as fragment limits, while this receiver maintains independent state per connection handle. A short HCI ACL request is clamped to its actual bytes before copy; every append checks the cumulative length against `VBT_RXBUFSIZE`, and an overflow resets the accumulated length before returning. Completed data is passed to L2CAP dispatch, which checks its header and declared payload extent before routing. No selected valid fragmentation or cross-link interleaving path was found that exceeds the receive buffer or mixes per-link state. The extent of malformed oversized direct `BTCMD_WRITEACL` sequences and same-link fragment interleavings remains an external-input boundary; those are not promoted here. <a id="virtual-bluetooth-event-port-shutdown-ownership-review-2026-11-03"></a>
Virtual Bluetooth event-port shutdown ownership pass (2026-11-03; no new finding): traced the selected stack registration and teardown in `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2855-2860,3044-3076` against `vbthci_QueueRequest()`/`vbt_HandleRequest()` and `vbthci_UnitTask()` (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:467-471,484-532,583-624`) plus `vbthci_CloseUnit()` (`vbthci_device.c:82-99`). The stack synchronously sends `BTCMD_REMMSGPORT`; the unit task processes it serially with event generation and clears the pointer before replying. The stack then drains/replies all queued event messages before `CloseDevice()`, which signals the worker and waits for its cleanup. Therefore the selected consumer does not free its port while the unit task can still post to it, and its queued replies return before the worker deletes its private reply port. A direct external client that closes the device without first removing its event port, or retains event messages past close, has no documented ownership contract in `bluetoothhci.h`; no in-tree caller of that form was found, so no finding is promoted. Existing full-body credit unchanged; no message, close sequence, device or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="broadcom4400-ppc-rx-alignment-handler-od9755"></a>
Broadcom4400 PPC RX alignment-handler consequence recheck (OD9755 restored/strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): followed the existing eight-byte DMA alignment plus 30-byte RX header to the `ULONG *` reads in `AddressFilter()` and `CopyFrame()` (`workbench/devs/networks/broadcom4400/pci.c:669-688`; `unit.c:1203-1206,1342,1413-1427`). The destination is 2 mod 4; the following 16-bit comparison is aligned. Confirmed the Sam440 package dependency selects EMAC (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:4-9`) and its kernel installs `alignment_handler()` for alignment exceptions. That handler emulates only floating-point instructions; other opcodes fall through `generic_handler()`, which enters its stop loop if no exception handler claims them (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/intr.c:340-356,550-644`). Thus, if the PPC compiler emits a normal word load for the misaligned `ULONG *`, this selected PPC receive path stops in the unhandled alignment exception. Strengthened the old uncertainty about target handling while retaining the compiler-output qualification because no object was built. No source body, path, or LOC credit changes; no packet or runtime operation was used.


<a id="nouveau-shared-falcon-engine-firmware-boundary-review-od11307"></a>
Nouveau shared Falcon engine full-body and firmware-length review (OD11307 added; 2026-11-03): read all 355 physical lines / 275 `cloc 2.06` C lines of `nvkm/engine/falcon.c`; reconciled the source selection in `workbench/hidds/nouveau/sources.drm.mak:269`, Falcon constructors and generation tables, interrupt callback channel-null handling, code/data limits, firmware fallback and partial-init teardown. Confirmed `nvkm_falcon_init()` copies exact `fw->size` into a `u32 *` image, then loops by four while comparing `i < code.size` and copies a complete word at each step (`falcon.c:192-203,246-259`). The selected AROS `request_firmware()` implementation allocates and reads exactly the DOS file length and returns that length unchanged (`drm-compat/linux_firmware.c:43-65`). Built-in firmware arrays and the static `.fucd`/`.fucc` path do not establish the same over-read. Callback implementations in SEC and CE guard a missing channel before dereferencing; no second independent defect was established in this file. This adds one full source-body entry and 275 C lines; aggregate represented-ledger totals are not recalculated here. No firmware, engine, GPU or build was used; source-only.

USB Bluetooth event-reply drain caller pass (2026-11-04; no new OD or path/LOC credit): traced `nBTTask()`'s `ncp_EventsPending` increments and reply-port drain through the selected Bluetooth HCI client (`rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/bluetooth.class.c:651-663,755-770,1075-1107`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:3038-3078`). On shutdown the HCI task removes the event port from the device, flushes outstanding I/O, drains its event queue with `ReplyMsg()`, and only then closes the device; those replies return to the driver's private `ncp_EventReplyPort`, where the driver removes each message and decrements the counter. Nouveau GK20A instance-memory size-width caller trace (2026-11-04; no OD added): followed selected GK20A `gk20a_instobj_new()` through `nvkm_instobj_new()` to `nvkm_memory_new()` and enumerated the in-tree `nvkm_memory_new()` call sites. The public internal wrapper takes `u64 size` (`nvkm/core/memory.c:137-160`) but forwards it to `nvkm_instobj_new(u32 size)` (`subdev/instmem/base.c:111-113`); GK20A then rounds that `u32` with `roundup(size, PAGE_SIZE)` before deriving its DMA/IOMMU page count (`subdev/instmem/gk20a.c:515-541`). GK20A FIFO/GR variable instmem-size producer check (no OD; 2026-11-04): extended the size-width trace to the selected Tegra GK20A FIFO and GR initializers. GK20A selects `nv50_fifo_chid_nr()` (fixed 128 channel IDs) and the GK104 USERD record (`size = 0x200`), so the FIFO BAR1 USERD allocation is 25,600 bytes (`engine/fifo/gk20a.c:27-31`; `nv50.c:372-374`; `gk104.c:113-119`; `fifo/base.c:307-311`). GK20A GR selects `ctxgk20a.c`: pagepool and bundle allocations are fixed at `0x8000` and `0x1800`; the attribute-buffer size is the shared formula `0x20 * (attrib_nr_max + alpha_nr_max) * tpc_total`, where the GK20A descriptor supplies fixed maxima (`ctxgk20a.c:71-88`; `ctxgf100.c:1060-1065`) and `tpc_total` is collected from the device's GPC/TPC topology (`gf100.c:2010-2014`). These selected FIFO/GR values do not establish a near-`u32` round-up trigger. The MMU descriptor/cache sizes and remaining common internal API producers still need their own bounds pass; no broad closure or new finding is claimed. No GPU or allocation was used; source-only.
GK20A MMU page-table size bound check (no OD; 2026-11-04): completed the selected MMU producer leg for the GK20A allocator trace. `nvkm_vmm_ref_hwpt()` computes its allocation as `desc->size * (1 << desc->bits)` (`subdev/mmu/vmm.c:412-428`); the descriptor fields are `u8` (`vmm.h:89-99`), and the selected GK104-derived page-table descriptors used by GK20A encode at most 17 VMA bits and 8-byte entries (`vmmgk104.c:39-60`). Thus the selected page-table allocation request is at most 1 MiB and does not approach the `u32` rounding boundary. Along with the previously traced 128-channel/0x200-byte USERD and bounded GK20A GR allocations, this closes these MMU/FIFO/GR sources of the GK20A size concern; signed firmware lengths remain below `INT_MAX`. Other `nvkm_memory_new()` generations and external/internal future callers have not been exhaustively closed. No new finding or runtime action; source-only.

SM502 PCI-enumerator and mapped-framebuffer follow-up (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/LOC credit): traced `Find_PCI_Card()`'s `tHidd_PCI_EnumDevices` callback through the selected `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices()` implementation (`workbench/hidds/sm502gfx/sm502gfx_support.c:182-259`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:395-437`). The PCI method calls the hook for every matching device and exposes no early-stop return; therefore the SM502 comment saying “Find the first device” is inaccurate, and a later matching card overwrites the stored BAR mappings. The selected Sam440 PCI path uses direct mappings; the reviewed SM502 source does not establish a user-visible failure or persistent mapping resource leak from this overwrite, so no finding is promoted. `fbsize` is declared but never populated or consumed, while scanout clears/copies use dimensions and pitch from controller registers; BAR-size versus register geometry remains an unverified hardware contract.
