Nouveau GSP-RM GR context-buffer size producer boundary (2026-11-04; no OD promoted): followed the still-open `nvkm_memory_new()` size-width caller into `r535_gr_get_ctxbufs_info()` and the shared `r535_gr_get_ctxbuf_info()` used by the R535/R570/R580 API tables (`subdev/gsp/rm/r535/gr.c:252-270`; `r570/gr.c:167-188`; `r580/gr.c:167-188`). The selected RM control structure exposes `size` as `NvU32` (`r535/nvrm/gr.h:15-20`), copied into the driver's `u32` `ctxbuf[].size` without an upper-bound check (`r535/gr.c:197-237`). For the MAIN buffer, `ALIGN(size, 0x1000) + 64 * 0x1000` is evaluated/stored as 32-bit (`:219-220`); a value close enough to `UINT32_MAX` can wrap the adjusted size before it reaches `nvkm_memory_new()` and the promoted-entry size (`:87-90,127`). This is a real arithmetic boundary, but the value comes from the integrated vendor GSP/RM internal query and this checkout does not establish a supported device/firmware returning a size near 4 GiB or the resulting behavior. No OD is promoted; keep the producer reachability question open rather than claiming a hardware trigger. No RM response, GPU, allocation or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="nouveau-framebuffer-ram-wrapper-and-bar2-full-body-review"></a>Nouveau framebuffer RAM-wrapper and GSP BAR2 failure-path full-body pass (OD10300 rechecked and expanded; 2026-11-04): read all 263 physical lines of `nvkm/subdev/fb/ram.c` (209 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), including memory-wrapper construction/destruction, multi-node VRAM allocation rollback, RAM init/teardown and RAM constructor ownership. Traced every direct `nvkm_ram_wrap()` caller and followed the selected TU102 GSP-RM BAR constructor through `r535_bar_new_()`, BAR2 init dispatch, and the memory mapping macros (`nvkm/subdev/bar/tu102.c:96-102`; `subdev/gsp/rm/r535/bar.c:100-114,165-185`; `include/nvkm/core/memory.h:68-73`; `subdev/bar/gf100.c:119-139`). Reconfirmed OD10300: the GSP BAR2 path warns but continues after wrapper/map failure and calls `nvkm_kmap()` on NULL `flushFBZero`, whose macro dereferences its argument. Reconciled the wrapper leak to the existing OD11154 report; OD10300 remains the distinct unchecked BAR2 NULL-map failure. R535 BAR is selected by `tu102_bar_new()` only when `nvkm_gsp_rm()` is active; the native path uses `gf100_bar_new_()`. The TU102 chipset table routes supported devices to this constructor (`engine/device/base.c:2340-2902`). The `ram.c` full-body/path credit already exists in the earlier shared RAM review; this recheck adds no path or LOC credit. No allocation failure, mapping, GPU operation or build was run; source-only.

<a id="nouveau-zero-page-count-vram-request-od11325"></a>Nouveau VRAM size-width and NVIF caller pass (OD11325 added; 2026-11-04; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `nvkm_ram_get()`'s `u64` request through its rounded `u32` page count, contiguous `min` selection, `nvkm_mm_head()` allocation, and returned `nvkm_vram_size()` (`subdev/fb/ram.c:148-188`; `core/mm.c:111-150`). For 16 TiB at page shift 12, the 4 KiB page count is `2^32` and narrows to zero; one byte above rounds to `2^32 + 1` and narrows to one page. With `contig=true`, the allocator accepts the zero-length or one-page node and the helper returns success. Followed the public selected UMEM request and response size (`subdev/mmu/umem.c:142-189`; `memgf100.c:69-92`; `memnv04.c:51-68`; `memnv50.c:66-89`; `nvif/mem.c:76-80`; `include/nvif/if900b.h:8-12`) and confirmed there is no earlier size bound; `nvif_mem_ctor_type()` copies the returned zero size and returns success. Added OD11325 for this oversized-request/zero-allocation result, distinct from OD10300's failed BAR2 wrapper mapping. Existing full-body/path credit for `ram.c`, `memgf100.c`, `umem.c`, `nvif/mem.c` and `core/mm.c` is unchanged. No NVIF request, allocation, GPU or build was run; source-only.

Nouveau VRAM allocator direct-caller width recheck (OD11325 scope confirmed; 2026-11-04; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated every selected `nvkm_ram_get()` call. The public `memgf100_new()` and `nv50_mem_new()` callbacks pass the NVIF `u64 size` through unchanged and can request contiguous memory; `memnv04_new()` does likewise. The other direct callers use a fixed 32 KiB GT215 link-training buffer, a `u32` NV50 instmem size, or an LTC tag size computed from detected RAM. These direct internal callers therefore do not establish the same 16 TiB rounded-page-count wrap; OD11325 remains scoped to oversized public VRAM allocation requests. Checked the outputs continue through the common memory wrapper and public size response already traced in OD11325. No request, allocation, device or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="nouveau-gsp-gr-context-size-wrap-od11326"></a>Nouveau GSP/RM GR context-size adjustment and zero-mapping recheck (OD11326 added; 2026-11-04; no new path/body/LOC credit): followed the RM `NvU32` context-buffer size through the shared R535 parser, the R570/R580 wrappers, golden-context promotion, the NV50 instance-memory allocator, and `nvkm_vmm_get_locked()`. A MAIN size of `0xffff0000` plus the 64 KiB subcontext-header adjustment wraps to zero in 32-bit arithmetic; allocation can produce a zero-sized object, and the VMM layer rejects the zero-size map with `-EINVAL`, aborting golden GR initialization. The same shared parser is selected by R535/R570/R580. The report keeps the condition on the internal RM response explicit: no vendor response or checked-in size guarantee establishes that the boundary value occurs. OD11281 already covers the control-request leak on promotion error, so that consequence is not duplicated. Existing full-body/path credit for `r535/gr.c`, `r570/gr.c`, `r580/gr.c`, `instmem/nv50.c`, `fb/ram.c`, and `mmu/vmm.c` is unchanged. No RM response, GPU, allocation, or build was exercised; source-only.


Nouveau dynamic `nvkm_memory_new()` producer-width census (MMU, fault-buffer, FIFO and GR boundary review; 2026-11-04; no new OD or path/body/LOC credit): traced the remaining dynamic allocation sizes at the MMU, fault-buffer, and FIFO call sites. MMU page-table allocations use `desc->size * (1 << desc->bits)` from the selected VMM page-format descriptors (`subdev/mmu/vmm.c:422-428`), not an external byte-size request. GV100/TU102 fault-buffer counts are masked to 20 bits and use 32-byte entries, so the largest count-derived allocation is 33,554,400 bytes (`subdev/fault/{gv100,tu102}.c` buffer-info callbacks; `subdev/fault/base.c:88-91`). FIFO USERD and runlist sizes multiply generation-specific channel counts by fixed per-entry sizes; the fixed-count families examined here use small constants, while GM200's channel count is read directly from MMIO (`engine/fifo/gm200.c:35-38`) and has no checked-in range validation before it reaches the FIFO allocations. That register-count validity contract remains open; this source pass does not establish a supported oversized value. The open GR context-size edge also remains: the internal-firmware fallback reads hardware-derived state (`gf100_gr_init_ctxctl_int()` reads `0x409804`), for which no selected supported range contract was established. No memory request, MMIO, GPU operation, or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau GR context-size path and prior GK20A attribution correction (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): followed `gf100_gr_init_ctxctl_int()`'s `0x409804` read (`engine/gr/gf100.c:1878`) through `gf100_gr_chan_bind()` (`:327-334`), where the `u32 gr->size` is passed to `nvkm_gpuobj_new()` and then used by an `int`-indexed word-copy loop. The `nvkm_gpuobj_new()` signature also accepts `u32` (`core/gpuobj.c:229`); no source-level upper bound is applied at this boundary. Corrected the preceding note's GK20A attribution: `gk20a_gr_fwif[]` has only a required firmware loader and no `nofw` fallback (`engine/gr/gk20a.c:317-345`), so that target does not reach the internal register-derived size path. The `gf100_gr_fwif[]` has a `gf100_gr_nofw` entry (`engine/gr/gf100.c:2562-2565,2614-2618`), and several GF100-family tables select that fallback; by contrast, GM200/GP100/GP102 and newer no-firmware entries return `-ENODEV` through `gm200_gr_nofw()` (`engine/gr/gm200.c:30-38`). The arithmetic/use chain is established for the internal-firmware fallback, but the checked source still does not establish a valid hardware register range or a supported device returning an oversized value. Keep the edge conditional and do not promote it to an OD without that producer contract. Relevant bodies were already credited in the Nouveau inventory; no new LOC credit. No GPU or MMIO was exercised; source-only.

GM200 FIFO channel-count register and allocation caller recheck (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): followed `gm200_fifo_chid_nr()`'s full `0x002008` read into `nvkm_fifo_oneinit()` and `gk110_fifo_chid_ctor()` (`engine/fifo/gm200.c:33-37`; `fifo/base.c:251-253`; `gk110.c:95-103`). The value is returned as signed `int` and passed to `nvkm_chid_new()` for both cgroup and channel IDs; its structure-size and data-array allocations fail closed to `-ENOMEM` for unrepresentable/oversized allocation sizes, and event-init failure propagates to FIFO oneinit (`chid.c:86-108`; `core/event.c:201-216`). USERD sizing later multiplies the channel count by the selected fixed 0x200-byte entry size (`fifo/base.c:309`; `gk104.c:115-123`), with no checked-in register-range validation. For plausible in-range counts, the source has no arithmetic wrap; for arbitrary oversized MMIO values, allocation failure or product wrap is possible, but the checkout does not define the register's supported maximum or establish such a value on a supported device. Retain the producer-range question as open and add no finding. These bodies already have full-read credit (`:32668-32673,32689-32691`); no LOC increment. No MMIO, allocation, FIFO initialization or build was exercised; source-only.


GP100 fault-buffer count-to-allocation width recheck (OD11327 added; 2026-11-04; no path/body/LOC credit): checked the previously open GP100 register-count semantics through `gp100_fault_buffer_info()`, common allocation, selected GP100 chipset constructors, NV50 instance-memory rounding, and the public fault-buffer object/map methods. Unlike the GV100/TU102 callbacks, GP100 copies the full `0x002a78` register without a mask. Since `entries` and `entry_size` are 32-bit, `0x08000001 * 32` wraps to 32 bytes; NV50 instmem backs that request with one 4 KiB page, but the user object still reports the original entry count. Added OD11327 for this conditional count/backing-size mismatch. The checked-in source does not establish the register's valid maximum or hardware behavior after the backing boundary, so those parts remain qualified. Existing full-body/path credit for `fault/gp100.c`, `fault/base.c`, `fault/user.c`, `instmem/nv50.c`, and the relevant device-table slice is unchanged. No register read, fault, mapping, GPU operation, or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau FIFO channel-count register-definition census (GM200 count range remains open; 2026-11-04; no OD or body/path/LOC credit): searched the selected Nouveau source and register headers for the `0x002008` read and named channel-count masks. `gm200_fifo_chid_nr()` returns the complete MMIO value as `int` (`nvkm/engine/fifo/gm200.c:33-38`); no in-tree symbolic field mask, documented maximum, or matching chip-specific extraction was found. Older generation `chid_nr` implementations use their own distinct reads/masks, so they do not establish the GM200/GV100/TU102 register contract. The existing constructor/allocation trace shows failure propagation for oversized allocations but cannot prove a supported register range. Retain the hardware count bound as unresolved; no larger-count finding is promoted. No register, device, allocation or build was exercised; source-only.

GP100 fault-buffer mapping-consequence refinement (OD11327 wording tightened; 2026-11-04; no new OD or path/body/LOC credit): rechecked the exposed object methods in `nvkm/subdev/fault/user.c:47-55,96-109` against `gp100_fault_buffer_info()` and the common count-times-entry-size allocation. The API returns the unbounded `buffer->entries` count while the map method reports `nvkm_memory_size(buffer->mem)`, so the proven result for a wrapping count is a count/storage-size mismatch. The inspected CPU record walker is in `gv100.c`, and was removed as evidence for GP100 boundary behavior; client/device behavior beyond the map remains unverified. <a id="sana-ii-devicequery-short-buffer-writes-od11328"></a>
SANA-II DeviceQuery short-buffer caller-boundary pass (OD11328 added; 2026-11-04; existing function-body credit unchanged): checked the SANA-II specification's `S2_DEVICEQUERY` result-size rule (section A.19: up to `SizeAvailable` bytes are copied; `SizeAvailable` includes both size fields) against all matching network-device result handlers. In 17 maintained local driver module targets, the handler clamps the initial `CopyMem()` but later writes `BPS` and, in several implementations, `MTU`/`HardwareType` unconditionally; the PPP `DeviceQuery()` also writes the full result structure without checking `SizeAvailable`; e.g. `SizeAvailable == 8` allows both size fields but does not cover the `MTU`/`BPS` offsets. The 17 bounded-copy handlers return success and report the clamped length; PPP writes all fields and reports the full structure size. Recorded OD11328 for the resulting write beyond the advertised area. Cross-checked `rtl8139`, `bcmgenet`, `dwmac`, and selected USB Ethernet classes, which reject a short buffer before those writes. The affected implementations and source lines are enumerated in the detailed finding (18 handlers total). No request, device, memory effect, or build was exercised; source-only.


Nouveau coherent-DMA tracking allocation failure candidate disposition (2026-11-04; OD11329 withdrawn; no body/path/LOC credit): confirmed `dma_alloc_attrs()` can return an untracked buffer if the later `coherent_block` allocation fails, and GH100/TU102 GSP boot flushes only listed buffers. However, the selected Nouveau target families are x86 and RISC-V; x86 cache maintenance is intentionally a no-op, and the RISC-V OpenSBI PCIDT backend explicitly states its bus-master controllers are cache coherent (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:992-1000`). No supported selected non-coherent Nouveau/PCI configuration was established. Removed OD11329 from the detailed report and index rather than retain an untriggerable cache-staleness consequence. The allocation bookkeeping omission remains an implementation difference, but this checkout does not establish an observable defect on a selected target. No allocation, firmware boot, DMA operation or build was run; source-only.


Nouveau page-allocation order caller closure (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): searched the selected Nouveau tree for `alloc_pages()`, `__get_free_pages()`, `free_pages()`, and `__free_pages()` calls. Maintained Nouveau callers use `alloc_page()`, which fixes the order at zero; no selected direct higher-order caller reaches `PAGE_SIZE << order`. Higher-order `__free_pages()` calls occur in upstream `ttm/ttm_pool.c`, but the AROS source manifest selects `drm-aros/ttm_pool_aros.c` instead. This closes the order-input question for selected callers only. The `dma_alloc_attrs()` coherent-list bookkeeping failure was reviewed and withdrawn because selected target cache coherency removes the proposed consequence; arbitrary compatibility-client size limits remain outside this caller closure. No page allocation, TTM operation, DMA operation or build was run; source-only.

Nouveau R535 EDID response-length caller reconciliation (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): traced `r535_tmds_edid_get()`'s `bufferSize <= *psize` check and `memcpy()` against the fixed 2,048-byte RM `edidBuffer` and the selected NVIF caller (`rm/r535/disp.c:1349-1381`; `rm/r535/nvrm/disp.h:341-350`; `engine/disp/uoutp.c:463-474`; `include/nvif/if0012.h:83-90`). The caller overwrites `size` with `ARRAY_SIZE(args->v0.data)` before invoking the callback, so the destination capacity is 2,048 bytes. A response `bufferSize > 2,048` would pass that capacity test only by violating the declared RM response-array bound; no valid selected caller/response path establishing such a value was found. Do not promote the apparent source overread without evidence of a supported oversized RM response. No EDID, firmware, GPU operation or build was used; source-only.

PCI message-vector backend ownership cross-check (2026-11-04; no new OD or source-body/LOC credit): compared all maintained `KrnAllocIRQ()` and PCI `ObtainVectors()` backends across PCIPC, BCM2711, BCM2712 and OpenSBI PCIDT. PCIPC's allocated APIC ranges are not freed by its release method (EK810), and the MSI post-allocation verification failure also returns without freeing the range (already recorded in the PCIPC coverage row). PCIDT omits `ReleaseVectors`, so its inherited no-op leaves the endpoint MSI configuration and bridge occupancy bit allocated (OD3520); repeated obtains can also replace the stored per-device vector (OD850). BCM2711 tracks and clears its per-device bridge bit on release. BCM2712 rolls back reservations when setup fails and clears the allocated mask on release; its selected RP1 caller and MSI-X table/global-index mismatch are already captured by OD921/OD11026. This pass found no additional ownership defect beyond those existing entries. No PCI device, IRQ, firmware, hardware, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="arostcp-sana-deinit-close-request-allocation-od11330"></a>
AROSTCP SANA-II teardown close-request failure pass (OD11330 added; 2026-11-04; no existing body/LOC credit): traced `sana_deinit()` through the selected AROSTCP build manifest and the `CreateIOSana2Req(ssc)` helper. The teardown unlinks `ssc` from `ssq` before allocating a new message port and IORequest; if either allocation fails, it logs and continues without `CloseDevice()`, abandoning the open SANA-II reference and interface state. Added OD11330 with the allocation-failure condition explicit. Normal teardown calls `sana_down()` and conditionally `sana_unrun()` first; this finding concerns the separate failure to allocate the close request. No allocation, device, or stack teardown was exercised; source-only.

AROSTCP SANA-II address-width caller check (2026-11-04; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): checked `iface_make()`'s `AddrFieldSize` conversion and subsequent `GETSTATIONADDRESS` copy (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:346-383`) against `SANA2_MAX_ADDR_BITS == 128`, the 16-byte `IOSana2Req` address arrays, and `MAXADDRSANA == 16` (`compiler/include/devices/sana2.h:16-18,133-134`; `net/if_sana.h:56,75`). The stack does not reject a nonconforming query advertising more than 128 bits, which would exceed its fixed arrays, but the maintained SANA-II network providers found by source census report standard 32- or 48-bit lengths; no selected in-tree trigger was established. Kept this as an API-contract gap rather than a finding. No request, device, or build was run; source-only.

SANA-II DeviceQuery caller census (2026-11-04; OD11328 reachability recheck; no new finding or LOC credit): separated actual `S2_DEVICEQUERY` consumers from the much larger `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` search set. AROSTCP's only direct S2 consumer, `iface_make()`, sets `SizeAvailable = sizeof(devicequery)` before `DoIO()` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:324-349`); no short-buffer path was found there. The other direct query consumer found was the diagnostic devtest, which tests `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` and passes `sizeof(NSDeviceQueryResult_t)`, a different command and result structure (`developer/debug/devtest/devtest.c:2704-2721`). WirelessManager and WiFi prefs also issue only `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY`; they do not exercise OD11328's S2 path. This confirms OD11328 as a SANA-II API boundary defect with no maintained in-tree short-buffer trigger established. No IO request, driver, device, or build was run; source-only.

AROSTCP interface-up allocation and status recovery pass (OD11331 added; 2026-11-04; targeted caller/UI trace, no additional body/LOC credit): followed `sana_up()` from the `SIOCSIFFLAGS` and `SIOCSIFADDR` callers, through `CreateIOSana2Req()` and the MiamiPanel state-message handler. It publishes GoingOnline before allocation; only the successful-allocation/S2_ONLINE-error branch publishes Offline, while the selected ioctl leaves `error` at zero. A request/message-port allocation failure therefore skips device online and leaves the panel's busy status without a recovery message. Added OD11331 with the GUI-running condition explicit. The same helper's teardown allocation failure is independently recorded as OD11330. No allocation failure, interface, GUI, or build was exercised; source-only.

AROSTCP SANA read-completion and link-event callback pass (2026-11-04; no new OD; targeted path review, no additional LOC credit): traced `sana_read()` through IPv4, ARP and IPv6 receive callbacks, then through `S2ERR_OUTOFSERVICE`, `S2_ONEVENT` ONLINE recovery, and CONNECT/DISCONNECT handling. On the normal receive path, request mbufs are reallocated before resubmission; on allocation failure, the packet/request resources are released and the sent count is reduced. Offline completion frees the reserved mbufs, reuses the request for the ONLINE notification and clears `IFF_UP`; successful event completion recycles the request before restoring receive queues. Link loss removes configured addresses through the selected `in_control(SIOCDIFADDR)` path and stops DHCP/AutoIP. No independent request-lifetime or event-state defect was established in these callbacks. This does not claim full AROSTCP protocol-stack or event concurrency closure. No SANA request, network event, device, or build was run; source-only.

AROSTCP SANA-II transmit queue and destination-resolution pass (OD11332 added; 2026-11-04; targeted body/caller review, no additional LOC credit): traced IPv4/IPv6/raw destination handling through `sana_output()`, the send-tag queue, `sana_start()` request assignment, and write completion recycling. IPv4 with `IFF_NOARP` skips `arpresolve()` without initializing local `dst_hw`, then copies the bytes into the queued destination and ultimately `ios2_DstAddr`; the selected `arpresolve()` has a defined `ENETUNREACH` branch for NOARP, while the original config-argument route was only an implementation possibility; the later OD11332 flag recheck established the selected mutable `SIOCSIFFLAGS` path on an Ethernet interface. Added OD11332 with address-based medium and consumer behavior qualified; SLIP/CSLIP/PPP defaults do not establish the same destination-address consequence. The queue respects its request pool and drains queued packets as write requests complete; no separate queue defect was established. No packet, interface, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

AROSTCP SANA copy-buffer allocator and callback pass (2026-11-04; no new OD; targeted callback/consumer review, no additional LOC credit): read both selected `ioip_alloc_mbuf()` variants (the older implementation is under `#if 0`), `m_copy_to_mbuf()` and `m_copy_from_mbuf()` in `net/sana2copybuff.c`; reconciled the active module manifest and `buffermanagement` tags. The active allocator frees and clears a partially extended reserve on allocation failure. CopyToBuff bounds the chain walk and returns failure when the driver-reported receive length exceeds the reserved chain; it detaches only after a complete copy. CopyFromBuff's missing chain-end check is DIAGNOSTIC-only, but its supported selected TX caller contract passes the packet's declared length from `sana_output()`; no maintained provider path with a larger request was established in this pass. The allocator accumulates capacity in signed `int` against ULONG MTU, but no supported in-tree SANA provider reporting a value above `INT_MAX` was established here; keep that interface boundary open rather than crediting an unsupported trigger. No buffer callback, packet, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

AROSTCP initial SANA configuration error propagation pass (OD11333 added; 2026-11-04; targeted caller trace, no additional body/LOC credit): traced `SIOCSIFADDR` through `sana_run()`, the temporary request allocation and `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` result, and into IPv4 `in_ifinit()` and IPv6 `in6_ifinit()`, both of which call the SANA ioctl and accept its zero return. Both request allocation failure (silent) and device configuration failure (logged) leave `IFF_DRV_RUNNING` clear; `sana_ioctl()` still returns its unchanged zero error, so address setup commits IPv4/IPv6 state while the following `sana_up()` guard skips bringing the interface online. Added OD11333 for the false-success/partially configured interface state. This is distinct from OD11331, where configuration is already running and the later online request allocation fails. No allocation failure, device, address setup, or build was exercised; source-only.

USB Audio AHI-open task construction and teardown recheck (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/LOC credit): traced `nAudioTask()` into `nAllocAudio()` and the `nFreeAudio()` success cleanup. Every early `nAllocAudio()` failure reaches cleanup, signals the ready waiter, and returns NULL; task shutdown calls `nFreeAudio()` only after successful construction. The early cleanup's unconditional `DeleteIORequest(NULL)`, `DeleteMsgPort(NULL)`, and `CloseLibrary(NULL)` calls are safe in the selected Exec implementations (`rom/exec/deleteiorequest.c:46-48`; `deletemsgport.c:44-55`; `closelibrary.c:65-87`), so this apparent null-cleanup defect is rejected. Successful task cleanup releases the audio modes/units, control pipe, task message port, AHI request/port and library. No separate ownership issue established in this path; descriptor negotiation, callback timing and broader class lifecycle remain open. No allocation failure, USB device, audio request or build was run; source-only.

AROSTCP IPv6 neighbor-resolution packet ownership check (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/LOC credit): traced the `AF_INET6` `sana_output()` branch into `nd6_resolve()`. Multicast and resolved-neighbor success return with the packet still owned by `sana_output()` for normal send queuing; `EAGAIN` stores the packet in the neighbor entry and the caller returns without freeing it; all other errors explicitly leave freeing to the caller and reach `sana_output()`'s single `bad:` free. No double-free or lost-packet ownership mismatch established for these return classes. No packet, route, neighbor event, or build was run; source-only.

AROSTCP SANA reply-port poll and interface shutdown pass (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/LOC credit): traced `sana_poll()`'s `GetMsg()` dispatch against every internal request constructor and the selected `amiga_main.c` signal loop. Read requests, the connect request, and command requests each set `ioip_if` before asynchronous submission; returned requests dispatch under `splnet()`. On shutdown, `sana_down()` aborts pending I/O, `sana_unrun()` waits and deletes the tracked request list plus the connect request before `sana_deinit()` deletes `SanaPort`. This pass found no separate message-port lifetime defect. OD11330 remains the distinct close-request allocation failure after list unlink. AROSTCP `splimp()` cross-task serialization check for SANA queues (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/LOC credit): traced `sana_output()`, `sana_start()`, `free_written_packet()` and `sana_down()` critical sections through `spl_n()` and its sole bootstrap caller. The selected build uses the semaphore-backed `spl_n()` implementation: raising from level zero retains `spl_semaphore`, nested calls preserve its nesting, and lowering to zero releases it (`kern/kern_synch.c:457-505`). `spl_init()` has one caller during stack startup (`amiga_main.c:382`), before normal network requests. Nouveau thermal fan-alarm teardown sequence recheck (2026-11-04; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): traced `nvkm_therm_fini()` through the selected fan and timer fini callbacks, device subdevice ordering, and final IRQ removal. `nvkm_therm_fan_fini()` cancels the fan alarm on suspend/runtime-suspend but leaves it linked for `NVKM_POWEROFF`; the selected layout orders TIMER before THERM, so reverse-order fini runs THERM first and TIMER next. Timer fini disables the hardware alarm source. `nvkm_device_fini()` then unarms the device interrupt under `device->intr.lock`; final `nvkm_device_del()` calls `nvkm_intr_dtor()`/`free_irq()` before reverse subdevice destruction frees the fan allocation. A timer IRQ already in progress is serialized by the interrupt lock and completes before unarm; no selected callback-after-fan-free path was established. The timer alarm list can retain an embedded alarm link until the timer itself is destroyed, but the checked teardown sequence removes IRQ delivery before freeing that storage. This is a source-order recheck only; no device, alarm, IRQ or power transition was exercised.

<a id="nouveau-rpc-ring-wrap-candidate-withdrawal-od11119-2026-11-04"></a>
Nouveau R535 GSP RPC ring-wrap candidate recheck (OD11119 withdrawn; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): revisited the queue layout and receive arithmetic in `rm/r535/rpc.c:34-90,193-205,261-313`. The 48-byte message-element header is counted once in `size = ALIGN(expected + GSP_MSG_HDR_SIZE, GSP_PAGE_SIZE)`; the initial copy begins at `mqe->data` and consumes bytes through the physical end of the ring, while the wrapped copy begins at the first page of the circular data ring. That wrapped span is a continuation of the same element, not a new element, so it has no second element header to skip. The explicit `info->continuation` branch applies to separate elements used when an RPC is split above the 16-page element limit; it verifies the continuation function and skips the new element's RPC header. The previous candidate misapplied that separate-element layout to physical ring wrap and is withdrawn. OD11120, the split-request error-path leak, is unaffected. No queue or firmware operation was performed.

<a id="nouveau-rpc-split-request-selected-caller-census-od11120-2026-11-04"></a>
Nouveau R535 GSP RPC split-request reachability census (OD11120 retained and qualified; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): enumerated direct `nvkm_gsp_rpc_get()` callsites and RM-control constructor uses. Fixed RPC payload constructors use selected structures; the only cumulative payload is `SET_REGISTRY`. In AROS, `NOUVEAU_REGISTRY` is read by `GetVar()` into a 256-byte local buffer before assignment to `NVreg_RegistryDwords` (`nouveau_drm.c:1530-1535,1556-1560`), so it cannot make the registry RPC exceed the roughly 65 KiB split threshold. The Linux `module_param()` declarations are no-ops in the selected AROS compatibility header; the custom AROS environment reader is the active input path. No other direct caller of the internal RPC getter was found that can construct an oversized message. OD11120's `r535_gsp_rpc_push()` failure exits do leak the original buffer once splitting has begun, but that condition is not reached by the checked-in AROS call paths at this commit; retain it only as a low-reachability future/internal-caller candidate. No RPC, firmware, allocation failure or build was exercised.

AROSTCP IPv4/IPv6 multicast membership rollback trace (OD11343 added; 2026-11-04; targeted caller and allocator review, no new body/path/LOC credit): compared `in_addmulti()` and `in6_addmulti()` with `sana_add_mcast()`/`sana_add_mcast6()` and their public/internal callers. Both successful filter-add operations precede membership-node `MALLOC`; `MALLOC` invokes the selected `bsd_malloc()` directly, and its `AllocVecPooled()` call can return NULL despite `M_WAITOK` (`sys/malloc.h:109-110`; `kern/kern_malloc.c:79-105`). Neither NULL branch sends the matching `S2_DELMULTICASTADDRESS`. IPv4 `IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP` returns `ENOBUFS` without recording the entry (`netinet/ip_output.c:965-975`); IPv6's required all-nodes/solicited-node setup ignores the NULL return (`netinet6/in6.c:580-598`). Added OD11343 for the untracked device filter and absent membership cleanup/announcement after allocation failure. No allocation failure, membership request, device or build was induced; source-only.


AROSTCP multicast-filter rollback provider verification (OD11343 expanded; 2026-11-04; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): traced an accepted stack filter-add request through the BCMGENET command handler to its stored `AddressRange` and receive-filter update (`workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/bcmgenet_handler.c:250-267`; `bcmgenet_unit.c:118-155,495-548`). Its remove command is the only path that decrements/frees that range and rebuilds the filter (`bcmgenet_unit.c:157-183`). Therefore a subsequent `in_multi`/`in6_multi` pool-allocation failure leaves driver-side range state with no corresponding stack node to trigger removal. BCMGENET is selected through the active Raspberry Pi SoC aggregate (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:42`; `workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/mmakefile.src:11-13`); the example is deployment-conditional. No filter request, allocation failure, device or build was run; source-only.

<a id="arostcp-multicast-filter-rollback-rtl8139-provider-od11343"></a>
AROSTCP multicast-filter rollback provider continuation (OD11343 expanded; 2026-11-04; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): traced `S2_ADDMULTICASTADDRESS` through the selected RTL8139 handler into `AddMulticastRange()` and `rtl8139nic_set_rxmode()`. A successful first range sets `IFF_ALLMULTI` and programs an all-ones multicast hash filter; `RemMulticastRange()` clears the flag and reprograms receive mode only when the last tracked range is removed. After the AROSTCP membership-node allocation fails, its missing remove request therefore leaves the separately buildable RTL8139 in all-multicast receive mode. This gives OD11343 a concrete receive-mode consequence in addition to BCMGENET's retained range. RTL8139 is included by the active cards aggregate for i386, x86_64, m68k and ppc Workbench builds (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:3-15,30-53`). No multicast membership, allocation failure, filter command, device or build was run; source-only.

RTL8139 multicast-range request serialization recheck (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): checked the apparent unlocked `FindMulticastRange()`/`add_count` accesses in `AddMulticastRange()` and `RemMulticastRange()` against the actual SANA-II dispatch caller. The single RTL8139 scheduler task obtains `rtl8139u_unit_lock` before `handle_request()` for every dequeued request (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/unit.c:876-886`); the handler releases it only after command dispatch and reply (`handler.c:112-210`). Both multicast commands run inside that critical section, so their list traversal, reference-count updates and first/last-range state transitions are serialized against other request-driven add/remove operations. The existing short `Disable()` brackets around list insertion/removal are not evidence of a concurrent request race on this path. No additional candidate established; no request or device was run.

AROSTCP multicast-filter rollback e1000-provider continuation (OD11343 rechecked; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced the SANA-II multicast add/remove commands in workbench/devs/networks/e1000/handler.c:757-800 through AddMulticastRange()/RemMulticastRange() in unit.c:1120-1192 and e1000func_set_multi() in e1000.c:571-627. On the first stored range, AddMulticastRange() sets IFF_ALLMULTI and calls e1000func_set_multi(), which sets E1000_RCTL_MPE; a subsequent filter-list allocation failure inside set_multi() does not roll that mode back. A stack membership allocation failure after the accepted add sends no remove, so the first-range state can remain. The corresponding final remove decrements the range count, clears IFF_ALLMULTI, and updates receive control. This confirms the already-listed e1000 provider consequence in OD11343; it does not establish a separate defect. e1000 is selected through the active network aggregate for its configured CPU group per the 2026-11-04 build-selection reconciliation. No filter request, allocation failure, device, or build was used; source-only.


Nouveau R535/R570/R580 GR context-size schema cross-check (no new OD; 2026-11-04; no body/path/LOC credit): compared the three selected RM excerpt headers `r535/nvrm/gr.h`, `r570/nvrm/gr.h`, and `r580/nvrm/gr.h` with their shared control-query callers and `r535_gr_get_ctxbuf_info()`. All three declare the returned `size` and `alignment` as `NvU32` and expose the same 25 engine slots; the R570/R580 callbacks reuse the R535 parser. The local schema provides no documented maximum or semantic validity range for MAIN context-buffer size. The driver-side `ALIGN(size, 0x1000) + 64 * 0x1000` remains a 32-bit computation before allocation and stored-size publication. This confirms the arithmetic boundary applies across the three selected RM generations, but the API excerpt and checked callers do not establish a supported provider result near `UINT32_MAX`, so no driver bug is promoted. Provider/firmware bounds remain open. No RM response, allocation, GPU or build was used; source-only.

Nouveau NV50 runlist dynamic-size arithmetic closure check (2026-11-04; no new OD or path/LOC credit): traced `nv50_runl_alloc()` allocations and per-update segment calculations in `nvkm/engine/fifo/nv50.c:254-280` to the selected generation descriptors and channel-count setup. The largest `nv50_fifo_chid_nr()` result is 128; the examined shared NV50/GF100/GK104/GM107 runlist descriptors use fixed entry sizes 4 or 8 bytes. Group/channel counts and products therefore remain far below 32-bit overflow on these selected paths. No dynamic near-U32 `nvkm_memory_new()` size input was established by this caller. This closes only the NV50 runlist size-propagation lead; other dynamic callers and RM-provided size ranges remain subject to their existing ledger notes. Source-only; no FIFO, GPU, build or runtime path was exercised.

Nouveau GSP-RM method-buffer-size caller trace (2026-11-04; no new OD; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the neighboring dynamic `nvkm_memory_new()` size input in R570/R580 GR scrubber setup. The R535 CE method-buffer-size control returns `NvU32 size` (`subdev/gsp/rm/r535/nvrm/fifo.h:126-129`), copied directly to `fifo->rm.mthdbuf_size` with no local range validation (`r535/fifo.c:571-580`). R570/R580 then compute `0x2000 + mthdbuf_size` in the `u32` expression passed to `nvkm_memory_new()` (`r570/gr.c:115-120`; `r580/gr.c:115-120`); the same response also sizes coherent per-channel method buffers and RM mappings (`r535/fifo.c:66-67,139`). A response near `UINT32_MAX` can therefore wrap the scrubber allocation expression, but checked driver sources do not establish a supported RM response near that boundary or prove a reachable device failure. No finding promoted. This is distinct from the previously recorded GR context MAIN adjustment boundary; both await vendor-RM producer bounds. No RM response, allocation, GPU or build was used; source-only.

Nouveau GM200 FIFO channel-count register consumer closure (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): followed `gm200_fifo_chid_nr()`'s full-width `nvkm_rd32(0x002008)` result through `nvkm_fifo_oneinit()` into `gk110_fifo_chid_ctor()`, both `nvkm_chid_new()` allocations, and the common FIFO destructor (`engine/fifo/gm200.c:33-36`; `base.c:247-255,305-343`; `gk110.c:95-103`; `chid.c:86-112`). The count is converted from `u32` to `int`, used for a flexible bitset and pointer-array allocation, then stored as `chid->nr`; no local positive/range/power-of-two validation exists. Downstream masked interrupt IDs pass through the runlist lookup's `id >= chid->nr` guard (`runl.c:202-223`), so the checked path does not establish a direct out-of-bounds access from a non-power-of-two count. A zero or out-of-range register value could still produce initialization failure or unusable channel capacity, but no selected-source register contract or supported GM200 state in this checkout establishes such a value; retain the previously recorded provider-range question without promoting it. Other FIFO generations use hard-coded counts or a different fixed count helper (`gm107.c:125-128`; `gk208.c:46-49`). GM200/GP100 selection is confirmed in `engine/device/base.c:1947-1973,2077-2101`. No MMIO, allocation, FIFO initialization, GPU or build was exercised; source-only.


Nouveau GSP R535 message-work teardown trace (OD11344; 2026-11-04): followed the message IRQ through `r535_gsp_intr()`/`schedule_work()` into the asynchronous AROS `system_wq`, then traced device deletion through `nvkm_intr_dtor()`/`free_irq()` and reverse subdevice destruction into `r535_gsp_dtor()`. The IRQ compatibility routine removes the interrupt server but does not drain already queued work; the GSP destructor destroys both queue mutexes and frees shared memory without `cancel_work_sync()`/`flush_work()`. Multiple selected generation descriptors use this shared destructor. Added OD11344 with the condition limited to teardown overlapping pending/running GSP message work. Source-only; no interrupt, GPU, teardown, or build was exercised. This note adds no file-body/path/LOC coverage credit.


Nouveau GSP workqueue reachability and startup-failure cross-check (OD11344 precondition confirmed; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced `nouveau_init_probe()` to `workqueue_init()` before probe creation (`drm-aros/drm_drv.c:564-572`), then checked `r535_gsp_postinit()` initializes `msgq.work` before registering the GSP interrupt (`nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/gsp.c:296-321`). Thus the asynchronous system queue and initialized work item are present on the selected GSP interrupt path. Rechecked `alloc_workqueue()`'s worker `AllocSignal(-1)` failure branch: the worker is a fresh `CreateNewProcTags()` task and `NewAddTask()` initializes a zero signal-allocation mask from `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:249-251`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`, value `0xFFFF`), leaving allocatable user signals on this selected startup path. The worker signals the creator before testing the failed allocation, but the selected startup does not establish signal exhaustion, so no additional finding is promoted. OD11344 remains limited to pending/running GSP work overlapping teardown. No worker, signal, interrupt, GPU or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau DRM output-poll delayed-work disable race trace (OD11345; 2026-11-04; no new body/path/LOC credit): traced `drm_kms_helper_poll_disable()` and Nouveau suspend/fini callers against `output_poll_execute()`, the AROS `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` implementation, and the serialized timer process. A running poll callback can rearm its delayed timer from the `repoll` path while its work state is `WORK_RUNNING`; synchronous cancellation has already attempted `del_timer()` and waits only for the work state to become idle, so it can return with the newly armed timer pending. `poll_enabled` remains true across ordinary disable. Added OD11345 for a poll callback overlapping disable and choosing to repoll. `drm_probe_helper.c`, `linux_workqueue.c` and `linux_time.c` were already body-reviewed; this targeted caller trace adds no LOC or path credit. No timer, display, suspend or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau DRM delayed-work caller census (OD11345 boundary check; 2026-11-04; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated all selected Nouveau `schedule_delayed_work`, `queue_delayed_work`, `mod_delayed_work`, `cancel_delayed_work[_sync]`, and `flush_delayed_work` call sites. The only owned delayed-work instances are DRM output polling and generic self-refresh entry. Traced self-refresh scheduling through its atomic commit worker and `drm_self_refresh_helper_cleanup()`; the entry callback does not rearm itself, and cleanup synchronously drains it before freeing its state. The output-poll callback's zero-delay `mod_delayed_work()` path is conditional on a connector status change, while its `repoll` path arms the timer from within the running callback; only the latter combines with `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` to leave a timer pending after disable (OD11345). The probe-helper body is byte-identical to the VMware SVGA DRM copy, but no in-tree VMware suspend caller was found; the reported trigger remains the selected Nouveau suspend/display-fini path. No callback, timer, suspend, or build was run; source-only.

Nouveau page-table descriptor size and input-width closure (2026-11-04; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): closed the previously open MMU descriptor-size edge against `struct nvkm_vmm_desc` and every selected generation descriptor table. The fields used in `nvkm_vmm_ref_hwpt()` are `u8 bits` and `u8 size`; the reviewed selected tables use small fixed values (typically 8- or 16-byte entries, with `bits` at most 15 in the reviewed shared chains), while NVIF page selection accepts only a shift from the fixed `vmm->func->page[]` table and checks request-size alignment before the shared allocator. Thus `1 << desc->bits` and `desc->size * pten` are bounded for the selected descriptor chains; the user-supplied mapping byte size does not feed either multiplier. The earlier note's open MMU dynamic-allocation arithmetic concern is closed for this path. This does not close the separately tracked GM200 FIFO MMIO channel-count bound or GF100 internal-firmware context-size producer range. Existing VMM and generation descriptor body credits are unchanged; no page-table allocation, NVIF request, GPU operation, or build was exercised. Source-only.

Nouveau voltage-map cycle caller expansion (OD11249 fleshed out; targeted caller trace, no new body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced the selected BIOS VMap parser into both recursive helpers and clock consumers. `nvbios_vmap_entry_parse()` reads v0x20 `link` bytes from any in-range table entry without rejecting self-links or repeated IDs (`subdev/bios/vmap.c:93-128`). The device clock constructor scans BIOS performance-state entries via `nvkm_pstate_new()`; for each referenced C-step, `nvkm_cstate_new()` calls `nvkm_volt_map_min()` before publishing the state (`subdev/clk/base.c:225-246,450-460,648-683`). Runtime `nvkm_cstate_valid()` and pstate programming also call `nvkm_volt_map()` for state IDs and voltage ceilings (`:79-105,112-138`). Thus a cyclic map referenced by a BIOS C-step can recurse during clock-state construction, as well as during runtime voltage/clock operations. The existing OD11249 remains conditional on a v0x20 cycle and the selected BIOS reference; no valid board ROM or hardware incidence is established. Existing full-body credits for the map parser, voltage base and clock base are unchanged. No BIOS, clock constructor, GPU or build was used; source-only.

Nouveau OD11324 RPC-buffer ownership recheck (no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): verified the exact allocation/consumption contract rather than inferring ownership from call-site names. R535 `ctrl_get()` returns the RPC payload backed by `r535_gsp_rpc_get()` / `r535_gsp_cmdq_get()` (`rm/r535/ctrl.c:65-85`; `rpc.c:650-665`, `:457-469`); the latter allocates the command-queue message with `kvzalloc()`. Normal `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_wr()` enters `ctrl_push()` with reply length zero, and `r535_gsp_rpc_rm_ctrl_push()` calls `nvkm_gsp_rpc_done()` to free the message (`include/nvkm/subdev/gsp.h:348-354`; `rm/r535/ctrl.c:37-62`). The promotion helper's direct returns after `ctrl_get()` at `gr.c:91-92,115-120` occur before that consuming write or any `ctrl_done()`, confirming the buffer leak on local memory/VMM/map errors. The shared helper is reached from per-channel context creation and golden-context setup in R535 (`gr.c:159,319-321`) and R570/R580 scrubber initialization (`r570/gr.c:142-145`; `r580/gr.c:142-145`); cleanup of those callers does not own the local RPC. Existing OD11324 stands, conditional on one of those resource/setup failures. No allocation failure, RPC, GPU or build was induced.

Nouveau fault-buffer pin-failure reachability recheck (OD11323 fleshed out; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): confirmed the selected GP100/GV100/TU102 fault callback routes `buffer->mem` through `nvkm_memory_bar2()` (`subdev/fault/gp100.c:52-55`; chipset selections in `engine/device/base.c:2083-2218,2309,2344-2790`). For NV50 instance-memory objects, the BAR2 accessor returns `~0ULL` when `nv50_instobj_acquire()` cannot establish/retain a BAR2 mapping (`subdev/instmem/nv50.c:121-180,297-307`); its mapping path can fail at VMM allocation/map or host `ioremap`. `nvkm_fault_oneinit_buffer()` treats that sentinel as `-EFAULT` after storing the buffer and allocating its memory, while `buffer_nr` is advanced only after the helper succeeds (`subdev/fault/base.c:72-115`). Teardown reaches the destructor, but the loop excludes this partial entry (`:127-140`; `core/subdev.c:228-240`). This confirms the pin-failure arm is a reachable selected API failure path, in addition to the direct backing-allocation failure. No GPU mapping, allocation failure, teardown, or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau OD11316 TOP-runlist consumer trace (finding fleshed out; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced failed `ga100_runl_new()` cleanup through `nvkm_runl_del()` and FIFO ownership, confirming the partial runlist is removed while FIFO-owned runqueues are later freed by `nvkm_fifo_dtor()` (`engine/fifo/runl.c:318-334`; `base.c:343-365`). `nvkm_fifo_oneinit()` propagates only a nonzero `runl_ctor` result, which `ga100_fifo_runl_ctor()` currently suppresses (`base.c:263-267`; `ga100.c:580-600`). The selected NVIF group constructor resolves the requested runlist and returns `-EINVAL` if it is absent (`ucgrp.c:97-100`); thus failed TOP runlist setup leaves a partial FIFO initialization in which clients cannot create groups on that runlist, rather than causing an unguarded null dereference. The exact unavailable engines depend on which TOP runlist failed; no all-engines-fail claim is made unless all runlist constructions fail. No TOP data, allocation failure, GPU or build was exercised; source-only.

RTL8139 OD11317 failed-slot completion-chain recheck (finding retained; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced the failed copy branch through ring admission and the later interrupt consumer. `RTL8139_TX_IntF()` programs TxAddr/TxStatus only when `tx_function()` succeeds, but replies either way and advances `tx_current` (`unit.c:381-416,418-444`). After a failed slot at the head, a later successful packet in the next slot can generate TxOK/TxErr; the completion loop still examines `tx_dirty % NUM_TX_DESC` first and stops if that failed slot's TxStatus lacks `TxStatOK|TxUnderrun|TxAborted`, leaving `tx_dirty` unchanged and never reaching the later completed descriptor (`unit.c:578-616`). On a fresh open, software initializes the counters and packet pointers but does not explicitly clear TxStatus registers in that loop (`rtl8139.c:617-624`); whether the hardware reset leaves the first slot without a completion bit remains a device-state precondition, so the report's trigger stays conditional on that status. If the slot remains incomplete, further submissions consume the four-slot software capacity and the normal queue-full retry cannot drain past the head. This confirms the persistent-head-block consequence without claiming every copy failure stalls under all prior register states. No callback, packet, register, interrupt, device or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau GM200 FIFO masked-ID error consumer recheck (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): closed the remaining software-consumer side of the raw channel-count question. `nvkm_chid_new()` sets `chid->mask = nr - 1` (`engine/fifo/chid.c:92-98`); selected GM200/GP100 FIFO error paths apply that mask to hardware PBDMA/context-switch channel IDs before looking up the channel (`engine/fifo/gf100.c:318-337`; `engine/fifo/ga100.c:198-205,237-245`; GM200/GP100 tables in `gm200.c:42-55`, `gp100.c:111-128`). If a supported register count were non-power-of-two, the mask could alias an error ID to another channel and misattribute the diagnostic/termination. The subsequent lookup checks the resulting ID against the channel table and does not establish an out-of-bounds access (`engine/fifo/runl.c:202-223`). No source in this checkout establishes the legal `0x002008` register range or whether non-power-of-two values can occur, so retain as a hardware-contract question and do not promote a bug finding. Existing FIFO body credit unchanged; no MMIO, GPU, interrupt or build was used.


Nouveau/Vulkan-Hpp OD11362 output-size contract recheck (finding expanded; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): re-read the enhanced single-result and vector overloads at `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:25875-25919`. The single-result overload always passes `sizeof(DataType)` while forwarding arbitrary `micromaps.size()` and `stride`; unlike the neighboring vector overload, it has no caller-supplied `dataSize` and no count/stride check. Verified the primary Vulkan `vkWriteMicromapsPropertiesEXT` valid-usage requirement `dataSize >= micromapCount * stride` (VUID `vkWriteMicromapsPropertiesEXT-dataSize-07576`; https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkWriteMicromapsPropertiesEXT.html). This confirms the existing multi-micromap case and adds a one-micromap trigger whenever `stride > sizeof(DataType)`; `VkDeviceSize` with stride 16 requests 16 bytes but provides 8. The driver may reject the invalid call, and an implementation that writes the requested output could exceed the local object; no unconditional overwrite is claimed. Updated OD11362 and the index. No API call or build was run; source-only.
Nouveau R570/R580 TPC-mask response ownership and GSP-init caller recheck (OD11282 confirmed; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): reread `rm/r570/gr.c:16-31` and `rm/r580/gr.c:16-31`, and traced both callers in `rm/r570/gsp.c:115-128` and `rm/r580/gsp.c:160-173`. Each `*_gr_tpc_mask()` gets a response-bearing control buffer, calls `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_push()`, and returns immediately on nonzero status before `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_done()`. GSP initialization propagates that failure, so the leak occurs during one-time GSP setup when a selected TPC query returns an RM error; repeated per-GPC failures are bounded by the 32-entry loop but each failed query can leave one response allocation outstanding. The shared push implementation leaves `*params` pointing into the received RPC for nonzero RM status with nonzero reply size (`rm/r535/ctrl.c:38-60`; R570 selects that implementation). This is the already reported OD11282 response-bearing-push ownership family. No TPC query, RM error, GPU, or build was run; source-only.

Nouveau Blackwell mode-possibility RPC reply ownership follow-up (OD11282 expanded; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced `r535_disp_imp()`'s response-bearing `NVC372_CTRL_CMD_IS_MODE_POSSIBLE` request (`rm/r535/disp.c:289-352`). When `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_push()` returns the RM status error, the function logs and returns at `:348-352` without the matching `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_done()` at `:369`; the shared R535 push implementation retains the response allocation for nonzero reply length (`rm/r535/ctrl.c:38-60`). Confirmed the display helper reaches it through `nv50_disp_imp()` (`dispnv50/disp.c:114-127`), and both checked-in Blackwell callers ignore its result (`dispnv50/coreca7d.c:180`; `headca7d.c:250`), so the mode query failure does not abort the surrounding update/start path. Nouveau Blackwell IMP request bounds and response-field cross-check (OD10018/OD11282 rechecked; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): compared `r535_disp_imp()`'s request/response indexing (`rm/r535/disp.c:290-369`) with `NVC372_CTRL_IS_MODE_POSSIBLE_PARAMS` and constants (`rm/r535/nvrm/disp.h:756-857`) and both selected callers (`dispnv50/coreca7d.c:150-181`; `headca7d.c:231-250`). Input heads are capped at the eight-element schema capacity; two windows per accepted head are bounded by the 32-entry array. Returned tile reads are capped at eight, the tile/head index is checked against the request's `numHeads`, and the resolved head index is checked against the eight-element tile result. The fixed schema lengths match those bounds; no independent selected-source array overrun established. Both selected callers still ignore `nv50_disp_imp()`'s return, as already covered by OD10018. Nouveau R535 SOR backlight response-error ownership follow-up (OD11282 expanded; no new ID or whole-body credit; 2026-11-04): audited every direct response-bearing `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_push()` call in the selected R535 RM sources and traced the shared control implementation. Most error branches call `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_done()` or flow through common cleanup; the exception in `r535_bl_ctrl()` returns `ret` at `rm/r535/disp.c:414-416` before its success-only `ctrl_done()` at `:420`. R535 registers this helper as `.bl_ctrl` (`:1920`), and `r535_sor_bl_get()` / `r535_sor_bl_set()` dispatch to it (`:425-438`). On a successful RPC envelope with nonzero RM status, `r535_gsp_rpc_rm_ctrl_push()` preserves the payload pointer for `repc > 0` while returning the translated error (`rm/r535/ctrl.c:38-60`); this helper then abandons the enclosing RPC allocation. Transport failures that null the pointer are handled by the null-safe done method and are not this trigger. Expanded OD11282 and its index summary to include this additional selected caller. The R535/R580 control bodies already have full-body ledger credit; no duplicate LOC credit. No backlight operation, RM error, GPU, or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau R570/R580 SOR backlight response-error ownership follow-up (OD11282 expanded; no new ID or whole-body credit; 2026-11-04): completed the direct response-bearing `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_push()` caller scan for R570/R580. Their `r570_bl_ctrl()` and `r580_bl_ctrl()` return immediately when push reports an error (`rm/r570/disp.c:157-159`; `rm/r580/disp.c:161-163`) and bypass `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_done()` on the following success-only path (`:163`; `:167`). Both methods are installed as `.bl_ctrl` in their generation display function tables (`rm/r570/disp.c:254`; `rm/r580/disp.c:258`), reached through the SOR callbacks in `r535/disp.c:425-446`, whose get/set dispatch uses the selected `disp->rm` API; GSP-backed GA102/TU102 constructors use this R535 SOR implementation (`engine/disp/ga102.c:148-153`; `engine/disp/tu102.c:234-239`; `rm/r535/disp.c:1866-1883`). R570 selects the R535 control API, while R580 selects R580 control. Since the push methods retain the response allocation for nonzero RM status and `repc > 0`, these add two generation instances of the already reported conditional ownership leak. The other direct response-bearing R570/R580 push callers inspected either release on error or release unconditionally; no additional leak was established in that caller set. Expanded OD11282 and the index. Existing source-body coverage is unchanged. No backlight operation, RM error, GPU, or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau R570/R580 indexed DisplayPort link-rate table bounds recheck (2026-11-04; no finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced `r570_dp_set_indexed_link_rates()` and `r580_dp_set_indexed_link_rates()` (`rm/r570/disp.c:78-95`; `rm/r580/disp.c:82-99`) through the R535 `r535_dp_rates()` selector and the selected `nouveau_dp.c` producer. The control table has eight entries (`NV0073_CTRL_DP_MAX_INDEXED_LINK_RATES` in each generation `nvrm/disp.h`); the setter checks `outp->dp.rates <= ARRAY_SIZE(linkRateTbl)`. The direct table subscript is `outp->dp.rate[i].dpcd`, but the checked-in producer supplies either indexed eDP rates with `dpcd = i` for the fixed eight-entry `DP_SUPPORTED_LINK_RATES` read, or legacy rates with `dpcd = -1`; the R535 selector returns before calling these setters when the first rate is negative. Thus selected in-tree calls have indexes 0–7, and fallback `-1` does not reach the setter. The lower NVIF method copies its arguments without independently validating each dpcd index (`engine/disp/uoutp.c:130-150`); no additional checked-in caller supplies malformed indexes, and external NVIF-client behavior remains open, so this is not promoted as a selected-source bug. No link-rate request or build was run; source-only.

Nouveau DisplayPort discovery rate-array capacity recheck (2026-11-04; no finding or body/path/LOC credit): verified `nouveau_dp_probe_dpcd()` resets `outp->dp.rate_nr` to zero before parsing (`nouveau_dp.c:68-73`). The indexed eDP parser performs at most `ARRAY_SIZE(rates)` iterations, where `rates` is `DP_MAX_SUPPORTED_RATES` (8), and inserts into the matching fixed eight-entry `outp->dp.rate[]` array; the legacy fallback runs only if no indexed rate was inserted and admits at most four entries from its fixed list (`:128-149`; `engine/disp/outp.h:47-53`). Thus neither repeated discovery nor combination of indexed and fallback lists overruns the selected array. No malformed DPCD data, AUX read, or build was used; source-only.

BWFM transmit failure-path and SDHCI retry-state refinement (OD11374 retained as conditional; 2026-11-04; no path/LOC credit): traced the SANA-II `CMD_WRITE`/`S2_MULTICAST` dispatch through `tx_request()` and `TermIO()`. A nonzero `BWFMTxData()` result sets `S2ERR_TX_FAILURE`/`S2WERR_GENERIC_ERROR`, emits TX error events, and returns to the request handler; it does not mark the unit offline, retry the same frame, roll back `bwfm_txseq`, or initiate a card/firmware reattach. In `sdio_command()`, each PIO block is copied to the FIFO only after its ready handshake; timeout/data-error branches reset the host data engine and return failure, and the next command clears pending host interrupt status before issue. This establishes host-side reset and caller behavior but not whether the Broadcom function accepts, discards, or can resynchronize an incomplete CMD53 frame. OD11374 therefore remains conditional; no stronger firmware consequence is claimed and no separate finding is added. No transfer, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

R535 GSP ELF section-size to DMA destination trace (OD11274 expanded; 2026-11-04; no path/LOC credit): followed `.fwimage`, signature and boot-image sizes from `r535_gsp_elf_section()` / `hdr->data_size` into `nvkm_gsp_mem_ctor()` and their subsequent `memcpy()` calls. `dma_alloc_coherent()` reaches the AROS `dma_alloc_attrs()` wrapper, which page-aligns the request and `page_block_alloc()` adds page/pointer overhead before passing the total to `AllocMem()` without overflow or narrowing checks. An inconsistent ELF size can therefore exceed both the source firmware extent and the allocated destination extent; when the alignment/allocator-width conversion wraps, the copy may overrun an undersized destination as well. This is the same missing ELF section-range validation root cause as OD11274, not a separate allocator finding. No firmware, allocation, copy, GPU or build was exercised; source-only.

RISC-V DesignWare UART baud-state recheck (OD1736 confirmed; 2026-11-04; no additional body/LOC credit): reread the full `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c`, sibling class/init/IO/config files, and the selected `serial.device` `SDCMD_SETPARAMS`/write callers. `SetBaudrate`'s equality guard compares `msg->baudrate` with `data->baudrate`, but only the constructor initializes that field; `set_baudrate()` programs the divisor and returns without updating it. The serial-device unit independently starts with zeroed `su_Baud`, sends the first requested rate, and caches it after the HIDD reports success. Confirmed OD1736 already captures the first same-as-HIDD-rate rejection and later rejected restoration; no duplicate finding added. OD839 already covers the shared zero-length CMD_WRITE do/while behavior, so it was not duplicated here. No serial request, UART, interrupt, or build was run.

PPP ExecSMP AbortIO queue-race recheck (OD11375 strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): re-read queue setup, all four service-side enqueue/dequeue critical sections, `AbortReq()`, `AbortIO()`, `TermIO()`, and the selected AROSTCP `sana_down()` caller. `sdu_ListLock` is initialized and consistently protects service-side `AddTail`/`RemHead`; `AbortReq()` snapshots `ln_Succ`, searches, removes and replies with no shared lock. Since ExecSMP `Disable()` is processor-local, a remote service CPU can dequeue a request after the abort scan observes its node and before the scan removes/replies it, leaving both paths to act on the same request; concurrent unsynchronized list-link traversal/removal is also established. AROSTCP calls the device abort entry for incomplete requests during interface shutdown. Refined the report's fix to make membership/removal atomic under `sdu_ListLock` and reply only after successful removal. The target remains conditional on PPP being built and used on ExecSMP; no request, schedule or build was exercised.

LinuxFB directcolor gamma-depth arithmetic pass (OD11404 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): re-read display initialization and `SetGamma()` in source order. Directcolor enables gamma; `scale_size` is `1 << max(red.length, green.length, blue.length)`, while each UBYTE step is `0x100 >> component.length`. For component widths 9–15, the step is zero, `step - 1` initializes the UBYTE index to 255, and repeated zero increments keep every cmap entry sourced from gamma table slot 255. At width 16, `scale_size` (`UWORD`) truncates 65,536 to zero, so no cmap writes occur despite success. Added OD11404 for these >8-bit scaling failures, conditional on an accepted directcolor mode and successful cmap writes. LinuxFB display body coverage was already credited; no gamma update or display operation was run. Source-only.

Bluetooth AES S-box first-use recheck and caller serialization (OD11407 added; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): reread the complete 97-line `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/aes128.c` and 12-line header, checked the 74 C / 5 header code lines with cloc 2.06, and traced both real callers (`hwtask.c:178-204`; `hwconn.c:2525-2530`). `bResolvePrivateAddr()` holds the shared base lock, but `bSMPAES()` does not; each registered hardware unit has its own `bHWTask` (`hwtask.c:2778-2797`), and the selected USB Bluetooth class creates one stack per unit (`rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/bluetooth.class.c:139-154`). On ExecSMP, multiple hardware tasks can therefore race the global lazy table's flag and writes. Qualified the previous coverage-only OD3809: concurrent writes produce identical values and do not alone establish bad output; the remaining candidate is unsynchronized publication of `aes_sbox_ready` before table visibility on weakly ordered CPUs, with incorrect AES output as the conditional consequence. Explicit SMP variant gates are in `configure.in:1669,2197`. The round/key-expansion and S-box arithmetic were source-checked; no primitive known-answer test was run, and local SMP crypto tests inject a fake AES callback. No task, adapter or AES operation was run; source-only.

USB/BTSerial setup-handshake Exec reply-port contract recheck (OD3366 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): reread `OpenDevice()`, `CreateIORequest()`/`CreateStdIO()`, `ReplyMsg()`, `PutMsg()` and `WaitPort()` (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:89-135`; `rom/exec/createiorequest.c:57-73`; `compiler/alib/createstdio.c:16-45`; `replymsg.c:50-64`; `putmsg.c:83-106`; `waitport.c:62-95`). `OpenDevice()` synchronously invokes the device Open vector and leaves the request's `mn_ReplyPort` unchanged; normal I/O-request constructors set it to the caller's port. `ReplyMsg()` therefore posts the worker's completion to that reply port (or marks the request free if it is NULL), never to the unit command port. `WaitPort(unit_MsgPort)` loops on that port's queue and waits on the current task's signal bit, while `PutMsg()` signals the port's configured worker task. This confirms OD3366's same-port self-dequeue on uniprocessor and wrong-port wait if the worker wins on ExecSMP. No OpenDevice call or task schedule was run; source-only.


BTSerial zero-length read semantics comparison (OD11406 qualified; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `bServeReads()` and compared the maintained `workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:361-438` plus `serial_support.c:23-56`. The generic serial device only calls `copyInData()` after confirming buffered input exists; with an empty input buffer, it also queues a zero-length read and waits for a later receive callback. No checked-in serial-device documentation defining zero-length `CMD_READ` completion behavior was found. Retained OD11406 for the definite BTSerial wait behavior, but reduced contract confidence to medium and classified it as an API/compatibility candidate rather than asserting a unique serial-device deviation. Serial zero-length queued-read callback recheck (OD10 confirmed; 2026-11-05; no new ID or LOC credit): traced generic `CMD_READ` admission (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:361-438`) through `RBF_InterruptHandler()` (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_interrupthandlers.c:22-92`). With an empty ring, a zero-length request is queued and marked pending. On the next receive callback, the copy loop writes `data[index]` to `io_Data[io_Actual]` before testing `indexDestBuf >= io_Length`; with `io_Length == 0`, that first write is followed by immediate reply with `io_Actual == 1`. Thus an API-valid zero-length request can receive a byte despite declaring no capacity; a NULL/zero-sized destination makes the write invalid. Confirmed this is the existing serial OD10, separate from parallel OD3224 and from BTSerial OD11406's wait-for-input behavior. Existing interrupt-handler full-body coverage and OD10 report entry stand; no request, buffer, or device was exercised. Source-only.

Serial read-until-NUL caller census and OD9 trigger qualification (2026-11-05; no new ID or body/LOC credit): searched checked-in `CMD_READ` callers and traced the special `io_Length == -1` path in `serial_init.c` into `copyInDataUntilZero()` (`serial_support.c:66-110`). When the helper sees the NUL at the ring head, it breaks before advancing `index`, assigns that same index to `su_InputFirst`, reports `io_Actual == 0`, and returns success; subsequent reads encounter the same NUL and repeat the zero-byte completion, leaving later ring bytes inaccessible through this path. The in-tree PPP reader queries available bytes and queues at least one byte (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/serial.c:221-248`); `developer/debug/test/serial/serialtest.c` uses `io_Length == -1` only for CMD_WRITE (`:102-110,240-251`) and uses positive lengths for CMD_READ (`:116-133,259-282`). Thus OD9 remains a direct-client `CMD_READ` sentinel candidate; no checked-in read caller was found in this census. No serial request or input was used; source-only.

AHI `AbortIO` queue-to-reader-list window recheck (OD11402 strengthened; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): followed `CMD_READ` from `_DevBeginIO()`'s `PutMsg()` on `unit_MsgPort` through worker `GetMsg()`/`PerformIO()` to `ReadCmd()`'s first `ReadList` insertion (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:95-109,711-758`; `device.c:916-944`). `_DevAbortIO()` takes the unit semaphore but only searches `ReadList`; before that insertion it leaves the request pending and returns zero without setting `IOERR_ABORTED` or replying (`devcommands.c:120-154`). The worker dequeues and dispatches without holding that semaphore, so the caller can win either while the message is still queued or after dequeue before `ReadCmd()` reaches the list insertion. The AHI-Handler starts a second-half prefetch before returning current read data, then aborts and waits for that prefetch in `ACTION_END` (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:442-450,498-518,647-656`). This confirms the caller can block closing until recording supplies the remaining samples when the abort falls in that interval. Retained OD11402; no additional ID or coverage credit. No request, device, schedule or build was run; source-only.

EMAC shared-open candidates restored and rechecked (OD2408/OD2461/OD2462; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the complete EMAC Open/Close logic, `EMAC_Start`/`EMAC_Stop`, the AROSTCP flags-zero opener, Exec `OpenDevice`/`Wait`, and generic `timer.device` queue insertion. USB MassStorage public BeginIO shutdown-admission caller recheck (OD3905 retained; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): re-read the complete device-vector admission and completion path (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/dev.c:197-320`) against `nFreeMS()` and the unit-worker exit sequence (`massstorage.class.c:1861-1897,1410-1430`). Every queued external command family, including ordinary and NSCMD 64-bit reads/writes, checks `ncm_DenyRequests` before `PutMsg()` and has no shared lock spanning the check/enqueue. `nFreeMS()` sets the unit port to `PA_IGNORE`, clears `mp_SigTask`, and drains the current queue once; Exec `InternalPutMsg()` appends irrespective of port action. Thus a direct device client delayed after the false check can also leave a request queued after worker exit, with no reply. This is the same root cause already recorded as OD3905 and the internal removable-monitor variant OD11110; no third finding is warranted. No request, unbind, schedule or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

USB Audio empty-rate mode selected requester follow-up (OD3172 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): traced the published zero-frequency mode through AHI's selected mode requester. `SetSelected()` calls `GetSliderAttrs()`; when `AHIDB_Frequencies` is zero, the helper sets the selected level to -1 and still queries `AHIDB_Frequency` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/requester.c:376-400,428-446`). `GetAudioAttrs()` computes `AHIDB_MaxMixFreq` by querying the last frequency at count minus one (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:491-496`), and the selected USB Audio getter indexes `nam_FreqArray[arg]` without a range check (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3930-3936`). Since the count field precedes the array, the -1 index reads that zero count under the current struct layout and returns a bogus zero rate; this is an invalid array index but not an out-of-object overwrite. Expanded OD3172 and its master-index summary. The requester hides the zero-rate slider; this check confirms an invalid query/result, not playback or a crash. No requester or USB device was used; source-only.

The sublibrary has its `AHIDB_MinMixFreq`/`AHIDB_MaxMixFreq` getter cases commented (`:3920-3930`), so AHI's generic min/max queries derive from the empty frequency list (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:491-496`). This can form an invalid native structure when passed to the Vulkan API, but its impact depends on caller misuse and the low-level API model permits caller-managed pointer validity; not promoted without stronger project-specific evidence. No C++ construction or Vulkan operation was run.

Nouveau NV50 primary-plane constructor result overwrite cross-generation recheck (OD10015 expanded; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `nv50_head_create()` and its plane factories (`dispnv50/head.c:588-607`; `base.c:27-54`; `ovly.c:27-53`; `wndw.c:929-958`). Confirmed both sides of the `GV100_DISP` branch overwrite the primary result with the overlay result before the only `ret` check. On GV100+, `nv50_wndw_new()` returns a negative `nvif_mclass()` result before assigning `*pwndw` when no supported primary window class is found; on an allocation failure inside `nv50_wndw_new_()`, the primary output can be NULL. If overlay and cursor construction then succeed, `drm_crtc_init_with_planes()` receives `&base->plane` from an unestablished pointer (`head.c:597-607`). Expanded OD10015 from pre-GV100 only to both constructor branches and updated its index entry; the existing pre-GV100 caller path remains covered. No class lookup failure, allocation failure, display initialization, GPU or build was induced; source-only.

OD888 detailed report restoration (2026-11-06; no source-body or LOC increment): restored the coverage-ledger candidate to `AROS-other-drivers.md` and `AROS.md` after rechecking `UXParUnit__Root__New()` and `Dispose` (`arch/all-unix/hidd/parallel/ParallelUnitClass.c:108-153`), UnixIO `AddInterrupt` rollback (`unixio_class.c:828-875`), and Exec `Remove()` (`rom/exec/remove.c:52-63`). The non-Darwin failed-fcntl branch removes the registered node and returns; the caller closes but retains its fd, then Dispose removes/closes again. A concurrent list insertion can be detached by the stale-node second Remove; host-fd collateral additionally requires descriptor reuse between the two closes. Darwin returns success and uses timer polling, excluding this exact rollback branch. This is distinct from OD11115, where the UnixIO object allocation itself fails and cleanup dereferences a NULL object. Confidence is high for repeated cleanup and medium for collateral effects. No fcntl failure, list/descriptor reuse, HIDD operation, or build was exercised; source-only.

UnixIO shared interrupt-list serialization and OD888 reachability check (no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-06): traced `SigIO_IntServer()` registration as a kernel IRQ callback (`arch/all-unix/hidd/unixio/unixio_class.c:139-155,1173-1190`) against `core_IRQ()` and `krnRunIRQHandlers()` (`arch/all-unix/kernel/kernel.c:125-159`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:118-139`). The UnixIO list traversal itself takes no lock; Add/Rem protect list edits with `Disable()` only (`unixio_class.c:834-836,918-922`). For Darwin SIGIO/SIGALRM delivery is forwarded to the recorded AROS host thread, and `Disable()` masks that thread's interrupt signals; the all-unix bootstrap uses one AROS kernel thread plus the Darwin UI thread, but only Darwin's UI separation is explicitly reconciled in this path. On other hosted targets, process-directed SIGIO delivery to a host-created foreign thread could bypass the AROS thread's mask, but no selected all-unix subsystem host-thread creator or exact concurrent schedule was established here. Thus do not promote a generic callback/list race. OD888's second Remove can unlink a newly appended neighbor only if the list changes between the internal rollback and the caller's Dispose; that interleaving remains possible but not established as occurring in the selected parallel-constructor failure path. No signal, callback, list mutation or host thread was run; source-only.
