Nouveau GA100 non-stall interrupt partial-registration rollback check (OD11316 adjacent-path recheck; 2026-11-06; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced `ga100_fifo_nonstall_ctor()` through `nvkm_fifo_oneinit()` and the device initialization failure/fini paths. A later vector lookup or handler registration failure can leave earlier per-runlist `nvkm_inth` registrations in place; the error propagates and device init unwinds. FIFO runlists remain allocated on that failed init, device-level interrupt delivery is unarmed during fini, and full device teardown calls `nvkm_intr_dtor()` (which frees the IRQ before subdevice destructors free runlists). Thus this check did not establish a callback into freed runlist memory. The partial registrations also make a subsequent init attempt encounter the already-populated handler state, but no supported retry path or distinct user-visible consequence beyond the failed FIFO initialization was established; no separate finding added. The existing OD11316 remains the independent suppressed runlist-construction error. No IRQ, device initialization, retry, GPU or build was run; source-only.

<a id="ahi-record-flac-bitreader-declaration-dynamic-width-reconciliation"></a>
FLAC OD2471 detailed report restoration (2026-11-06; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the signed reader shifts (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/FLAC/bitreader.c:514-522`) against the selected fixed/verbatim/LPC sample callers and escaped-residual raw-width call (`stream_decoder.c:2453-2520,2558-2562,2617-2640,2758-2772`). Negative sign extension can overflow the signed left shift; the right shift of a negative value is implementation-defined; zero width produces a width-sized shift. Kept this merged with OD2863's same-helper case and conditional on explicit decoder use; ordinary AHIRecord recording does not invoke the decoder. No stream or build was run.

This count reconciles navigation only and does not measure file-by-file source coverage; the audit remains active.

Raspberry Pi Bluetooth packaging reachability qualification (no OD or source/LOC credit; 2026-11-06): rechecked the ARM32/AArch64 Raspberry Pi package target lists against `%make_package`'s exact `PKG_FILES` construction and the `OpenDevice` path. Base `rom/exec/OpenDevice()` consults the resident device list; its documented LDDemon override can load disk modules, and the stock LDDemon searches its configured `DEVS:` device directory. Separately, `workbench/mmakefile.src` and `rom/mmakefile.src` comment out the aggregate Bluetooth stack edges, while the default Raspberry Pi packages omit `bluetooth.library` and `BTStackLoader`. Therefore omission of `h4bthci.device`/`brcmbt.fwl` from these default packages does not by itself establish a supported default Bluetooth path or a standalone package bug. The ARM32 package also lacks an explicit H:4 module build dependency, while AArch64 builds it but does not list it in the boot package; whether a full installed distribution separately builds/installs those optional modules remains open. No package or device was built or loaded; source-only.

OpenSBI RISC-V shared timer contract reconciliation (2026-11-06; no new OD or LOC credit): traced `KrnPlatformTimer` and `KrnPlatformTimerArm()` through timer.device initialization, BeginIO, `TimerInt`/`Timer0Setup`, kernel `krnTimerTick()`, and `KrnGetSystemAttr(KATTR_PlatformTimer)` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/include/aros/platformtimer.h:14-51`; timer `timer_init.c:25-103`, `ticks.c:63-110`; kernel `kernel_timer.c:248-300`, `getsystemattr.c:35-36`). Startup validates a nonzero frequency and valid IRQ before installing the device IRQ handler; the device claims VBlank only after registration succeeds. On the selected single boot hart, the two deadline writers run with interrupts disabled, and the kernel clears an expired deadline before dispatching the device handler; each arm selects the earlier of the next periodic tick and the device deadline. No additional current one-hart descriptor/arm ordering defect was established. Future SMP visibility, SBI error handling, and firmware/hardware timing are not resolved by this source pass; no timer was run.

Virtual Bluetooth Host Controller command-length matrix follow-up (2026-11-06; OD3951 retained, no new finding or LOC credit): traced `BTCMD_WRITEHCI` through `vbt_HandleRequest()` and `vbt_HandleCommand()` (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:233-417,488-497`) into the complete `vbtp_HandleCommand()` switch (`vbthci_peer.c:736-1000`). The outer parser rejects requests shorter than the three-byte header and clamps the opcode's one-byte parameter length to `iobt_Length - 3`. Checked every variable-length parameter read in the built-in command cases: handle/disconnect/auth/encryption/remote-name, classic/LE connection, class-of-device, inquiry and scan-enable accesses are guarded or use bounded defaults. The five SSP reply cases `0x040b`, `0x040c`, `0x042b`, `0x042c`, and `0x042d` still copy/read six address bytes without checking `plen`; this is the existing OD3951, not five separate defects. No other short-parameter overread was established in these two command switches. This closes the direct parser's in-tree command-length matrix; it does not validate that arbitrary external clients' `iobt_Data` allocation matches `iobt_Length`, nor cover ACL packet parsing, event-port ownership, or state-transition semantics. No command, device, or build was run; source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth inbound ACL bounds follow-up (2026-11-06; no new OD or LOC credit): traced `BTCMD_WRITEACL` length/data forwarding from `bDrainACL()` (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2635-2675`) to `vbt_HandleRequest()` and `vbtp_HandleACL()` (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_unit.c:505-518`; `vbthci_peer.c:689-733`). The outer parser requires a four-byte header and clamps the declared ACL payload length to the supplied request length before any payload read. First-fragment L2CAP length bytes are read only when at least two payload bytes are present; the reassembly append is capped by `VBT_RXBUFSIZE` (1,100 bytes), and `vbtp_ProcessPDU()` checks for the four-byte L2CAP header and declared PDU extent before dispatch. Oversized/incomplete PDUs are discarded without exceeding the fixed buffer. `ln_RxExpected` is 16-bit while the computed L2CAP total is payload length plus four, but the overflow range is beyond the 1,100-byte reassembly capacity and did not establish an out-of-bounds write; it can cause malformed/oversized input to be silently discarded. No distinct memory-safety or state-corruption finding was established in this focused bounds pass. Fragment-ordering, invalid packet-boundary flag combinations, and end-to-end reassembly behavior remain open. No ACL packet, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="virtual-bluetooth-local-cid-wrap-review-od11451"></a>
Virtual Bluetooth local-CID wrap review (OD11451 added; 2026-11-06; no file/LOC credit): traced accepted L2CAP connection allocation, disconnection cleanup, and later local-CID lookup (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_peer.c:504-514,543-566,631-637`; `vbthci_intern.h:72-100`). The counter is `UBYTE`, increments on every accepted channel, and is not reset when an individual channel closes. The connection path takes any free slot and does not check whether its computed local CID belongs to another live slot. After wrap, a duplicate can coexist with an older channel; the lookup returns the first live array match, so a request for the newer channel's CID can operate on the older channel. Added OD11451 for the conditional long-lived-link/repeated-channel-lifecycle case. No channel sequence or build was run; source-only. Remaining broader L2CAP response semantics and ACL fragment interleavings remain open.

Virtual Bluetooth configure-response correlation cross-check (no new OD; 2026-11-06): compared `vbthci_peer.c` channel transitions with the selected host L2CAP channel manager. The host stores a pending identifier when sending Configure Request and dispatches Configure Response by that identifier (`rom/bluetooth/stack/protocols/l2cap/channel_manager.c:181-195,323-349`). Responses to inbound Configure Requests echo the request identifier and report success (`:298-320`); the virtual peer's corresponding `case 0x04` also echoes the request ID and reports success (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_peer.c:583-600`). Thus normal selected in-tree negotiation does not establish an identifier/result mismatch route. The peer's `case 0x05` still ignores the response identifier/result and falls back to any configuring channel (`vbthci_peer.c:603-628`), but that remains a conditional external/malformed-peer robustness candidate and was not promoted without a selected caller trigger. No negotiation was run; source-only.

Vulkan registry publication and entry-pointer synchronization follow-up (2026-11-06; no new OD or body/LOC credit): re-read `workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_init.c:18-157` and the registry helpers in `vulkan_intern.h:114-374`, then compared all in-tree registry helper call sites. Init publishes `vulkan_global_sd` only after obtaining the Vulkan attribute base, initializes all slot `in_use` flags and the semaphore first, and expunge clears the global before releasing the base. Registration serializes slot writes; PSP flag updates serialize their writes; preferred-GPU and BDF lookups release the shared semaphore before returning entry pointers. Consumers therefore retain pointers across the lock boundary, while registration can refresh callback/data/priority fields. However, repository search finds no backend call expression for `VulkanHidd_RegisterGPU()` in this checkout (the only direct mention outside the implementation is the probe test commentary), and the Vulkan HIDD aggregate selection remains optional/commented. No in-tree concurrent registration/use trigger is established, so no additional synchronization finding is promoted. Existing OD11349/OD11399 cover the observed dispatch-selection and exclusive-lock behavior. Library lifecycle ordering with external backend modules and concurrent external registration remains open. No registry call, semaphore schedule, build, or Vulkan device was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau power-budget record-size/caller follow-up (2026-11-06; no OD or body/LOC credit): inspected `nvbios_power_budget_table()`/`header()`/`entry()` against the structure contract and sole caller `nvkm_iccsense_oneinit()` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/bios/power_budget.c:29-117`; `subdev/iccsense/base.c:215-235`). The parser accepts version 0x20/0x30 header and entry lengths without minimum-size checks; entry reads fixed fields through byte offset 13 regardless of `elen`, and header selection reads offset 9/10 regardless of `hlen`. This makes malformed logical records yield values assembled across record boundaries, while each BIOS primitive remains bounded to the image. However, the only caller stores these fields in `power_w_max`/`power_w_crit`, and repository-wide use search finds no consumers of those fields. I therefore did not claim an active hardware/control consequence or promote a bug; malformed table semantics and external users remain open. No BIOS, device, build, or power telemetry was used; source-only.

Virtual Bluetooth OD11451 protocol-range and active-channel uniqueness recheck (2026-11-06; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced the allocator state, live channel-slot selection, teardown and first-match lookup again (`vbthci_peer.c:504-514,543-566,631-637`; `vbthci_intern.h:73-100`). Each link has six channel slots, so a retained old channel plus a reused free slot is representable while later channels are repeatedly closed. `ln_NextCID` starts cleared when a link is created, increments as an 8-bit value, and is not reset by individual channel teardown. The request handler is reached on peer signaling CID 0x0001; CIDs from 0x0070 through 0x016f are within the Bluetooth Core ACL-U dynamic range, so the defect is duplicate assignment after wrap, not a range violation. The Core L2CAP specification requires distinct CIDs for simultaneously active channels on the same logical link ([Core 5.4, §2.1](https://www.bluetooth.com/wp-content/uploads/Files/Specification/HTML/Core-54/out/en/host/logical-link-control-and-adaptation-protocol-specification.html)). Rechecked the host channel manager's connection/configuration/disconnection exchange; repeated same-link channel churn is feasible in the protocol shape, but no normal in-tree workload at 256 allocations was established. OD11451 remains conditional on a long-lived virtual ACL link and repeated channel churn, with medium caller-workload confidence; no session or build was run. Source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth signaling identifier wrap review (OD11459 added; OD11451 protocol URL corrected): re-read the connection-request allocation and configure-request construction (`rom/bluetooth/hardware/vbthci/vbthci_peer.c:557-573`) and the `UBYTE ln_NextCID` declaration (`vbthci_intern.h:96-98`). After 128 successful allocations on a reset link, post-increment leaves the counter at 128; `0x80 + 128` is stored in one byte and becomes 0x00. The Bluetooth Core 5.4 L2CAP signaling command-header rule says identifier 0x00 is invalid and shall never be used in any command (section 4.1, official specification URL linked in OD11459). Added OD11459 as a separate protocol-conformance candidate from OD11451's local-CID duplicate after 256 allocations. A channel can be disconnected between requests, so the six live-channel slots do not prevent this counter history; no in-tree workload at 128 repeated allocations was established. The host's exact behavior for this malformed configure request remains unverified. No session/build; source-only.

ALSA AHI start-failure cleanup caller recheck (2026-11-06; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): traced `_AHIsub_Start()`'s `mixbuffer` ownership through all start exits (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/Alsa/alsa-main.c:188-233`) and generic `AHI_ControlAudioA()` (`Device/audioctrl.c:915-1018`). A failed `AllocVec()` stores NULL; a failed `CreateNewProc()` returns `AHIE_NOMEM` with the allocated buffer still stored. `AHI_ControlAudioA()` returns that error without an immediate compensating Stop, so the buffer remains held while the audio control remains live. On the documented eventual `AHI_FreeAudio()` lifecycle, generic teardown calls `AHIsub_Stop(PLAY|RECORD)` before `_AHIsub_FreeAudio()` (`audioctrl.c:702-733`), and ALSA Stop frees and clears the stored mix buffer even when no worker was created (`alsa-main.c:251-275`). A later retry also begins by calling Stop. Thus this pass finds delayed reclamation after a failed start but no persistent leak across normal control teardown/retry; no new report item. No process/allocation failure or audio operation was induced; source-only.


Nouveau PMU boot-range devinit selector closure (OD11335 scope widened; 2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): rechecked the exact device selectors and callback chain after the earlier GM200-only note. GM200 selects `gm200_devinit_new()` (`engine/device/base.c:1952-1953`), while GV100 selects `gv100_devinit_new()` (`:2308-2309`); GV100’s function table assigns `.post = gm200_devinit_post` (`subdev/devinit/gv100.c:66-70`). Both reach `pmu_load()`’s `post && device->pmu` gate and the same `pmu_code()` transfer loop (`subdev/devinit/gm200.c:32-49,82-103`). Updated OD11335 and the master index to name both affected devinit paths. This closes the configuration-selector slice only; the triggering malformed PMU metadata and hardware effects remain unexercised and conditional. No BIOS, PMU, GPU, build, or hardware operation was used; source-only.


Nouveau GSP FWSEC PMU descriptor extent recheck (OD11336 expanded; 2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): traced the selected type-0x85 PMU record through `nvbios_pmuEp()` into `nvkm_gsp_fwsec_init()` and its secure-boot/FRTS callers (`subdev/gsp/fwsec.c:274-286,339-356`). `nvbios_pointer()` calls `nvbios_addr(..., size=0)` (`subdev/bios/base.c:49-55`), so an offset equal to `bios->size` is accepted and points one past the buffer; offsets in the final three bytes also pass while the caller reads a 4-byte `Hdr`. Offsets greater than `bios->size` return NULL and the caller dereferences that result. Expanded OD11336 to include both the NULL and truncated-header cases; trigger still requires an invalid BIOS PMU descriptor and selected GSP FWSEC. No malformed image, GSP, GPU, or build was used; source-only.

Nouveau MXMS v2 output-device callback width recheck (OD11455 expanded; 2026-11-06; no path/LOC credit): compared all version-selected `headerlen` values in `mxms_foreach()` with the selected `mxm_match_dcb()` reads. For MXMS versions 0x0200/0x0201 the iterator sets output-device `headerlen` to 6 (`mxms.c:110-115`), while the sanitizer callback unconditionally evaluates `*(u64 *)data` before version-aware field decoding (`nv50.c:40-44`). The callback is reached by the default-enabled NV50 `MXM_SANITISE_DCB` action for type-0 output records. Thus even a valid final v2 output record can trigger an eight-byte read two bytes beyond its record and, at the end of the allocation, beyond the buffer. Expanded OD11455 to include this distinct selected width mismatch; no image or hardware was exercised.

Nouveau MXM ROM probe-to-allocation consequence recheck (OD11259 expanded; 2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): re-read `mxm_shadow_rom()` through the complete acquisition/validation caller. Expanded OD11259 to capture this same-root downstream allocation/checksum mismatch, with behavior conditional on the invalid stack value and transfer. No ROM, allocation, or I²C operation was exercised.

BTCtrl OD10333 wait-setup failure caller trace (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): re-read `WaitForDiscovery()` and the `SCAN/WAIT` caller, then traced `btAddEventHandler()` into `classes.c`. `CreateMsgPort()` failure returns immediately; event-hook allocation failure returns `NULL`, skips the wait loop, and deletes the port. In both cases the caller still prints `Discovery finished.` and leaves `rc == RETURN_OK` after successful discovery start. Confirmed that this reports false completion while the scan continues, conditional on either setup allocation failing. No allocation failure or scan was run.

BTCtrl OD10334 discovery completion lost-wakeup trace (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): traced the command's synchronous `btStartDiscovery()` call into `bSubmitCtrl()`/the hardware task start path, followed by later message-port/event-hook creation in `WaitForDiscovery()`. Confirmed `BHA_IsDiscovering` is initialized locally to TRUE and first queried only after `Wait()` wakes; `btAddEventHandler()` registers for future sends without replay, while `bFinishDiscovery()` clears the flag and sends the stop event. This establishes a narrow missed-stop interval between start return and registration that can leave `SCAN WAIT` asleep indefinitely if no other wake arrives. The timing condition's incidence was not measured; no scan was run.

BTCtrl OD10335 remote-name setup allocation trace (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): followed `DEVICE ... REMOTENAME` through both allocations and the normal command exit. `CreateMsgPort()` failure bypasses the whole request; `btAllocChannel()` returns NULL on its `btAllocVec()` failure without a corresponding error message, and BTCtrl has no `else` branch or `rc` update for either case. Bluetooth OD10336 remote-name request retirement trace (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): read the entire in-flight request selection, HCI completion, and channel reply paths. Traced BTCtrl's blocking `btDoChannel()` and both in-tree Forget callers (BTCtrl and Preferences) into `btFreeDevice()`: removal from `bth_Devices` happens before use-count handling, so the channel reference only delays destruction; it does not preserve lookup visibility. `bNameReqComplete()` searches the active list and only clears/replies the request when the result equals `hc_NameReqDev`. If the device has been retired first, the completion does neither, leaving the channel waiter and hardware name-request slot pending. No concurrent request/removal was run.

Bluetooth OD10337 BTDevLister service-list synchronization pass (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): read `ListDevices()`/`ListServices()` through the command's outer lock and compared them with SDP/GATT refresh. The lister holds only `btLockReadBase()` and walks direct service/endpoint list pointers; `btGetAttrs()` returns those internal pointers. `bClearServices()` and GATT service refresh take `btLockWriteDevice(bd)` and free unbound services/endpoints while mutating those lists. The base lock does not serialize this per-device writer, supporting the conditional stale-link/dereference candidate for `SERVICES`/`ALL`. No concurrent listing or enumeration was run.

Bluetooth OD10338 BTDevLister local-name lifetime pass (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): traced `BHA_LocalName` extraction in the hardware listing through the direct-pointer `btGetAttrs()` pack table to both selected replacement paths: `BTPRI_SETLOCALNAME` from BTCtrl and HCI local-name read completion. Both free and replace `bth_LocalName` in the hardware task without taking the base lock held by BTDevLister, so the later `Printf()` can consume the old pointer after free. AddBTHardware OD10339 enumeration result and restart-window pass (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): traced `btEnumerateHardware()`'s `BHS_READY` guard and NULL return through AddBTHardware normal, QUIET and ALL paths to `fail(errmsg)`. Normal mode only prints the failure; QUIET discards the result; neither sets `errmsg`, so `fail(NULL)` exits 0. Separately traced `btAddHardware()`'s existing-hardware return and the hardware-task late firmware reload setting `BHS_STARTING`, establishing how the not-ready guard can be reached during controller reinitialization. The command then proceeds to `btClassScan()` and, in ALL mode, next units. No firmware reload or command was run.

AddBTClasses OD10340 allocation/enumeration/load result pass (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): traced all main error paths to `fail(errmsg)`. A NULL ExAll control skips work without assigning `errmsg`; ExAll false is used only as loop termination and `IoErr()` is never checked; confirmed the DOS ExAll contract says FALSE can mean either `ERROR_NO_MORE_ENTRIES` or an error (`rom/dos/exall.c:44-47`); `btAddClass()` false prints optionally but is not accumulated. `btAddClass()` returns NULL on module-open or class-node allocation failure. AddBTClasses OD10341 REMOVE head-lifetime pass (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): traced the caller's write-lock/test, unlock, and subsequent fresh `bclist->lh_Head` read into `btRemClass()`. AddBTClasses OD10342 class-list synchronization on ExecSMP (2026-11-06; no new ID/path/LOC credit): compared the complete `AddBTClasses` duplicate-name traversal under `Forbid()` with class insertion/removal. `btAddClass()` and `btRemClass()` mutate the list using the Bluetooth base write lock; removal frees the node after unlink. Confirmed Exec's `Forbid()` documentation explicitly limits it to the calling CPU on EXECSMP and requires a spinlock for parallel shared data (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-63`). Thus the scan can race with another CPU's list mutation and read an invalid node/name or miss a new entry. No concurrent scan was run.

UHCI OD10349 public reset-port range pass (2026-11-06; no new body/LOC credit): compared `uhci_PortReset()`'s 1/2 guard with the HIDD `PortReset` wrapper. The wrapper ignores the failed return for bookkeeping and shifts `1 << (portNummer - 1)` unconditionally into an 8-bit `reset` field. Port 0 gives a negative shift; 33+ gives a count at least the 32-bit int width. Traced the selected USBHub worker's 1-based bounded loop and UHCI's two-port status method; the invalid values are external/malformed HIDD calls, and stock package inclusion remains unestablished. No HIDD method was called.

UHCI OD10350 reset status/change semantics pass (2026-11-06; no new body/LOC credit): compared the reset bit lifecycle, method override, returned status structure and selected hub consumers. `PortReset` sets the software bit irrespective of helper timeout; `GetPortStatus` places `UPS_C_PORT_RESET` in `wPortStatus`, whose same-valued bit is `UPS_RESET`, and leaves `wPortChange` untouched. UHCI implements its own PortReset separately from the generic USBHub method; the only checked-in `HIDD_USBHub_ClearPortFeature()` call is internal to that generic method and is not shown targeting the UHCI object, leaving no selected caller that clears this software bit. `UHF_C_PORT_RESET` supports clearing but no checked-in UHCI HIDD caller was found. Retain as a conditional HIDD status-contract defect, with no stock-package reachability claim. No controller or method was run.

Sam440 EMAC MAL TX cache-clear extent recheck (no new OD or LOC credit; 2026-11-06): compared `mal.c:141-154` with `TX_RING_SIZE=32`, `RX_RING_SIZE=64`, and `sizeof(mal_descriptor_t)=8` (`emac.h:129-130`; `mal.h:8-12`). The TX ring allocation reserves `32 + 32*8` requested bytes, but its `CacheClearE()` length is `64*8`; the selected PPC implementation rounds and issues `dcbf` for each cache block in that range (`arch/ppc-all/exec/cachecleare.c:26-38`). This flushes beyond the logical TX descriptor array. The checked implementation does not read/write descriptor elements through that range, and this source pass did not establish that flushing neighboring pool cache lines corrupts data or causes a functional failure. Therefore no bug finding is promoted from the length mismatch. No cache operation, DMA, hardware, or build was run; source-only.

BCM GENET OD3225 tracker-pointer lifetime recheck (2026-11-06; no source-body/path/LOC credit): traced `bcmgenet_rx_packet()` from `BCMGENET_FindTypeStats()` through the tracker counter dereferences (`bcmgenet_unit.c:60-71,859-864`) against `S2_UNTRACKTYPE`'s final-node unlink/free (`bcmgenet_handler.c:339-368`) and `BeginIO()`'s synchronous `AttemptSemaphore()` dispatch (`bcmgenet_init.c:117-135`). RX does not acquire `bgu_Lock`; the untrack path's `Disable()` does not provide cross-CPU exclusion and cannot prevent a higher-priority task from mutating while the priority-zero worker is preempted. Confirmed a concrete dangling-tracker schedule on selected Raspberry Pi ExecSMP and a conditional higher-priority single-CPU ARM32 schedule. Rechecked opener and pending-read traversal against Close/AbortIO mutations; retained those as dependent additional races, while the tracker lifetime is the primary case. BCM GENET OD3225 selected AROSTCP opener-close caller closure (2026-11-08; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): an exact source search found no in-tree `S2_UNTRACKTYPE` producer, so final-tracker removal remains an external/direct-client trigger. Traced the separate opener-list mutation from selected AROSTCP `sana_deinit()` through `sana_down()`, `sana_unrun()` and `CloseDevice()` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/net/if_sana.c:158-179,580-601,893-911`). For a last opener, offline and request draining precede Close; they do not join the BCM GENET unit task. `CloseDevice()` uses processor-local Forbid (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:60-87`), and `BCMGENET_Close()` locally disables only around unlink before freeing the opener (`bcmgenet_init.c:255-274`). The unit RX walker can still hold that opener pointer. AROSTCP sets its main task priority to 5 and restores the old priority after `deinit_all()` (`kern/amiga_main.c:264,354-358,510`); BCM GENET explicitly sets its worker to priority 0 (`bcmgenet_unit.c:404-425`). This confirms the maintained close caller and its higher-priority preemption path on single-CPU ARM32 for OD3225's opener-list lifetime branch; SMP can overlap across CPUs. It does not show every shutdown overlaps an RX packet. No interface, packet, close, or schedule was run; source-only.

DiskImage nested-open ownership correction and OD11469 (2026-11-06; no source-body/path/LOC credit): corrected the prior XAD/XPK recheck's mistaken statement that Generic is first in the selected plugin list. `InitPlugins()` priority-sorts nodes with `Enqueue()`; Generic has priority -127, so it is a last-resort handler. Its `CheckImage()` accepts arbitrary files, but `FindPlugin()` rejects a zero-byte output before scanning any handlers (`device/plugins.c:237-241,276-290`; `generic.c:63-72,94-98`). For an XAD/XPK decoder that successfully creates an empty output, nested `IPlugin_OpenImage()` therefore returns NULL without consuming the output BPTR; both wrappers then return without closing it, and `RemoveDisk()` skips `Plugin_CloseImage()` because no image exists, deleting only the temp path (`xad.c:233-260`; `xpk.c:181-202`; `device/unit.c:575-590`; `tempfile.c:89-102`). Added OD11469 with decoder reachability qualified. The old “no separate ownership defect” conclusion applies only to nonempty unsupported formats, which Generic handles; it is superseded for the zero-byte branch. No archive, extraction, handle, or build was used.

OD11103 WinGDI partial-IRQ cleanup candidate withdrawn (2026-11-06; no source/path/LOC credit): re-read the complete `GDI_Init()` allocation/cleanup nesting and MinGW `core_init()`/`KrnAllocSystemIRQ()`/`KrnFreeSystemIRQ()` implementation (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi_native.c:378-440`; `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/host_intr.c:263-296,379-413`). Core initialization marks IRQs 0 and 1 allocated and sets `Ints_Num=2`. The allocator scans from 0 but skips both reserved slots, returns only 2–255 on success, and returns -1 on failure. `GDI_Init()` reaches cleanup only after its first IRQ succeeded and stores each later successful result before attempting the next allocation; on second/third allocation failure it frees only earlier assigned fields. Therefore no path frees reserved IRQ 0, and the indexed OD11103 claim is false; removed it from `AROS.md` and corrected the source inventory rows. No IRQ allocation or host initialization was run.

The clamped semitone magnitude stays within the fixed-point routine's signed range; synthesis validates pitch before `AssignPitch()` divides by it. Prosody rejects cumulative contour storage at 128 entries and rejects each phrase whose `arr_at + n` would reach 128; `AssignPitch()` consumes at most one contour entry per marked syllable, so its `v` indexes stay within the built arrays. <a id="pci-xhci-od3369-detailed-finding-restoration"></a>
PCI xHCI OD3369 detailed-finding restoration and failed-start teardown recheck (2026-11-07; no source-body/path/LOC credit): restored the missing numbered entry and master-index link from the existing failure trace. Re-read `xhciInit()` from `AddResetCallback()` and PCI interrupt installation through fatal-status and bounded halted-start returns (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:4028-4077,4126-4133,4139-4162,4177-4240`), then followed `pciAllocUnit()` failure and `Open_Unit()` timer cleanup (`pcixhci_arospci.c:307-345`; `uhwcmd.c:251-278`). Confirmed failed Open_Unit returns through Exec as an open failure (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:109-120,133-135`), releases PCI ownership but skips `pciFreeUnit()`, including for earlier successful controllers in a grouped unit. The PCI HIDD removal path permits removal once no owner is recorded (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:489-512`); checked PCIPC and PCIDT expunge routes request this generic removal (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_init.c:54-78`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_init.c:53-75`). If backend removal and later USB device expunge occur, `pciExpunge()` frees controller/unit records without removing those registrations (`pcixhci_arospci.c:441-460`). This stale-record consequence is explicitly conditional; neither removal nor expunge was exercised. Corrected affected configuration to include x86-64 PC through the selected standard USB package and PCIPC, alongside Raspberry Pi AArch64 and RISC-V OpenSBI. Kept OD3369 distinct from OD3372's normal-close teardown and OD10070's worker-signal-before-task-publication failure. No hardware, initialization failure, expunge, interrupt, worker, or build was exercised; source-only.


PCI xHCI OD10348 route and command-result caller recheck (2026-11-07; no new finding or source-body/LOC credit): followed Poseidon's `pGetRootPort()`/`pBuildRouteString()` values into the IO request (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4500-4518,7851-7899`), then through xHCI address-zero context creation, both routed-parent and split-TT `xhciProgramHubSlot()` calls, `xhciCmdEndpointConfigure()` and the common Address Device command (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_hcd.c:1163-1222,1418-1514`; `xhci_hw.c:451-459`). Both branches discard the parent-slot setup result; command submission returns its completion code, and Address Device failure disables/frees the child slot and fails creation. This supports OD10348's conditional enumeration-failure consequence, but does not establish a successful child address with an unconfigured parent or an additional x86-specific behavior. The same source path is selected by the x86-64 PC USB package. No USB enumeration, controller command, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="pci-xhci-od11408-advertised-count-and-port-dispatch-recheck"></a>
PCI xHCI OD11408 advertised-count and root-port dispatch recheck (2026-11-07; no new finding or source-body/LOC credit): aligned the detailed report with the 2026-11-05 NULL-private-state withdrawal and re-traced the exact request limits. `pciAllocUnit()` adds to `xhciports` only when an initializer succeeds, but its later map loop walks every controller and advances `portbase` by every `hc_NumPorts` (`pcixhci_arospci.c:319-358`). The controller HIDD sets `hc_NumPorts` before that unit-open initialization (`xhci_controllerclass.c:319`; `pcixhci_arospci.c:231-249`). `cmdRootHubRequest()` uses successful-only `hu_RootHubPorts` as `numports`, rejects larger port indices, then looks up the controller in the all-controller map (`uhwcmd.c:610-620,842-848,858-889`). This establishes map-prefix displacement and healthy-port unreachability without asserting NULL private state. With every controller initialized, the independent global-to-local index bug remains: GET_STATUS, SET_FEATURE, and CLEAR_FEATURE pass `idx - 1` to local register/change-array indexing (`xhci_hcport.c:188-206,367-385,531-537`). Updated OD11408 detail, the inventory row, and master-index summary; no controller or hub request was run. Source-only.
PCI xHCI root-hub variable-descriptor bitmap recheck (OD3362; 2026-11-07; no body/path/LOC credit): compared `cmdRootHubRequest()` descriptor length and mask writes (`rom/usb/pcixhci/uhwcmd.c:956-1005`) with USB 2.0 §11.23.2.1 and Poseidon hub parsing (`rom/usb/classes/hub/hub.class.c:857-894`). With the controller class capped at 20 ports, 16–20 ports need three bytes per variable bitmap including the reserved removable bit, but xHCI emits only two; for 17–20 ports Poseidon consequently reads byte 9 of the power mask into its removable bitmap. The selected class stores that value and no downstream operational consequence was established. Restored the existing coverage-only OD3362 candidate as a detailed finding and master-index entry. The power-control-mask all-ones mismatch was observed but left as a compatibility sub-detail without a proven operational consequence. No controller or descriptor request was run; source-only.

SD-card pending-task counter concurrency and platform-selection recheck (no new OD; 2026-11-07; no body/path/LOC credit): examined the unprotected `sdcard_PendingBusTasks` increment in `FNAME_SDC(Scan)`, failure decrement, BusTask startup decrement, and boot-wait polling (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_init.c:58-96`; `sdcard_bus.c:1679-1732`; `bootwait.c:116-124`). ARM32 Raspberry Pi selects only the SDHOST controller files; AArch64 compiles both SDHOST and SDHCI initialization (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdcard/mmakefile.src`). The runtime guards make them mutually exclusive for the card slot: SDHOST returns without registering on BCM2711/2712, while SDHCI returns without registering on earlier SoCs; on BCM2711 the SDHCI fallback chooses either EMMC2 or the legacy window in the same single registration path (`sdcard_sdhost_init.c:138-145`; `sdcard_bcm2708init.c:100-154,350-353`). Thus the selected Raspberry Pi configurations register at most one bus task, so the counter's scan increment and BusTask decrement have no competing update in the current build/runtime selection. A multi-bus target would require a shared atomic/locked counter, but is not established here. No card, task, boot sequence or build was run; source-only.

SD-card OD3313 detailed-entry restoration and wrap-width recheck (2026-11-07; no body/path/LOC credit): restored the detailed finding and master-index summary from the existing timer/backend traces. Rechecked `sdcard_CurrentTime()`/`sdcard_Udelay()` (`sdcard_bcm2708time.c:18-29`) and `BCM283xWriteLong()` (`sdcard_bcm2708bus.c:91-99`) against `sdcb_Private` width (`sdcard_bus.h:109`), the BCM2711 EMMC2-to-Arasan fallback (`sdcard_bcm2708init.c:100-146,259-270`), and selected SDHOST/SDHCI delay callers. The shared helper can skip a delay when its 32-bit absolute deadline wraps; on AArch64 the Arasan deadline is 64-bit and cannot be reached by the 32-bit sample, producing a conditional nonterminating write loop. EMMC2 bypasses the inter-write helper but not shared delay calls. No source body, file or LOC credit changed. No timer, board, rollover, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="pcnet32-multi-adapter-enumeration-expunge-od11472"></a>
PCNet32 multi-adapter enumeration and expunge (OD11472; 2026-11-07): traced the PCI enumerator callback over all matching devices, PCNet32 product filtering, per-device `CreateUnit()` worker startup, singleton `pcnb_unit` replacement, and the expunge path that calls `DeleteUnit()` once. `DeleteUnit()` signals the selected worker but polls for any task with the shared name; each worker exits only on its own shutdown signal. With two successfully created adapters, the earlier worker is unreachable and unsignaled, so expunge waits indefinitely and does not complete its resource cleanup. Its stack output buffer is 512 bytes and parser capacity is 510; the selected `ReadArgs()` command-line input uses a 257-byte temporary including the maximum BCPL string, injected newline, and NUL (`rom/dos/readargs.c:205,297-304`). The parser's bounded `PUT` returns `ERROR_BUFFER_OVERFLOW` before writing past `DestLength`; `findobjects()` enters block scanning only when parsing returns nonnegative (`patternmatching.c:431-436,622-635`; `SFSfindobjects.c:503-505`). Thus the maximum command-line pattern remains within the 510-byte output budget under the parser's at-most-two-output-bytes-per-input-character encoding, and parse failure does not use the output. No independent capacity or error-path defect established. No command, disk, or build was run; source-only.

USB2OTG OD1522 ARM cache-edge recheck (2026-11-07; retained, no new OD or body/LOC credit): re-read `usb2otg_schedule.c:680-688,707-755,865-893` against both selected ARM32 and AArch64 `CacheClearE` implementations (`arch/arm-native/kernel/syscall.c:47-119`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:82-149`). The scheduler's direct-DMA branch is reachable for an aligned IN buffer when the armed segment is larger than the 16 KiB bounce capacity and has a partial tail; post-DMA maintenance covers the completed range, clipped to the armed size. Both architecture implementations round the requested range to cache-line boundaries and promote partial invalidate edges to clean+invalidate (ARM32 DCCIMVAC; AArch64 `dc civac`) while using invalidate-only for interior lines. This confirms OD1522's precise shared-edge condition and that quiescent neighboring dirty bytes are preserved by the edge operation; it does not resolve a concurrent remote-CPU write during maintenance, cache-coherency behavior on supported silicon, or establish an in-tree caller that creates the required adjacency/interleaving. Retain the existing medium-low occurrence confidence and conditional scope; no broader data-loss claim. No cache operation, transfer, concurrent schedule, hardware or build was run; source-only.

USB Bluetooth HCI event-port shutdown candidate disposition (OD11475 withdrawn; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): rechecked the apparent race between `BTCMD_REMMSGPORT`, the final `bth_EventMsgPort` drain, and event completion. The USB class worker drains completed pipe messages from `ncp_TaskMsgPort` before it dequeues synchronous unit commands (`rom/usb/classes/bluetooth/bluetooth.class.c:717-810`). The selected stack then queues `CMD_FLUSH` and waits with `DoIO()` before its final event-port drain (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:3044-3075`; `rom/exec/doio.c:62-70`). Therefore, a completion already executing with the old event-port pointer must finish and publish before the worker handles/replies to `CMD_FLUSH`, so the stack's subsequent drain catches it. A completion processed after `BTCMD_REMMSGPORT` observes the cleared pointer and routes the message to `ncp_EventReplyPort`, which `nFreeBT()` drains. No late-publication or stuck-reply trigger is established; removed OD11475 from the report and master index. No event, close, or build was run; source-only.

PCIPC root-device constructor and disposal recheck (2026-11-07; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit): traced the selected i386-PC/x86-64-PC `PCIPCDev__Root__New()` path against the generic `PCIDev__Root__New()` and the PCI-HIDD `AddHardwareDriver` initialization caller. The constructor obtains its driver instance data from the caller-supplied driver, delegates initial device construction to the superclass, and only disposes that successful object on the host-bridge ECAM discovery branch before retrying construction with the extended-config tag. If the retry fails, NULL is returned; the original object has already been disposed, so no object leak or duplicate disposal is established by this retry. The caller's temporary PCI root object is created conditionally and disposed after synchronous driver registration; the init hook returns FALSE when root creation fails. The MCFG offset/segment, config-write, and retry-failure findings remain separately tracked (OD2417, OD2949, OD3523). No PCI enumeration, object failure, firmware table, or build was run; source-only.

VirtIO OD2541 withdrawal and AddBus dispatch correction (2026-11-07; no source-body/path/LOC credit): withdrew the proposed OD2541 entry and index link after calculating the generated HIDD method-table offsets. `CLID_HW` and `CLID_Hidd_StorageController` inherit the four Root offsets (`New`, `Dispose`, `Set`, `Get`; `rom/oop/include/oop.h:139-142`), and each places its first interface method immediately after those offsets; the storage controller's intervening `I_Hidd` interface has no methods (`rom/hidds/hidd/hiddclass.conf`, `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c`, `rom/hidds/base/storage/storage.conf`). Thus `HW_AddDriver` and the receiver's `AddBus` resolve to the same table index. The generated inline call uses the `IID_HW` method base, while HIDD dispatch indexes the receiver's table directly; on the VirtIO controller, that index is the inherited storage-controller `AddBus` implementation. Its first two message fields are likewise class and tags, so this call is the controller's AddBus route, not a missing-method failure. The previous claims that no bus is attached and ordinary VirtIO open is blocked by OD2541 are incorrect and must be removed from dependent coverage prose. This makes tracked bus startup candidates including OD2364/OD2370/OD3012 reachable on selected VirtIO configurations; their failure-path triggers still require separate qualification. No dispatch, device, or build was run; source-only.

VirtIO OD2805 capacity arithmetic restoration (2026-11-07; no body/path/LOC credit): re-derived the block-size conversion from the negotiated config field through capacity division, floor-log2 shift, DOS block size, and byte-offset-to-512-sector conversion (`virtio_hw.c:266-270`; `virtio_busclass.c:152-159,217-230,251`; `virtio_io.c:48-58`). Corrected the old qualification: the capacity ratio mismatch is specifically when `floor(blk_size/512)` differs from `2^(floor(log2(blk_size))-9)`, including non-power-of-two quotients such as 3 for 1536 bytes. The OASIS VirtIO 1.2 text calls `blk_size` an optimal sector-size hint and says protocol units remain 512 bytes (§5.2.5: https://docs.oasis-open.org/virtio/virtio/v1.2/virtio-v1.2.html). Restored OD2805 and its index link, scoped to under-exported capacity; no data corruption or device response is claimed. No device or I/O was run; source-only.

VirtIO OD2842 reset-timeout restoration (2026-11-07; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `virtio_hw_reset()`'s unsigned post-decrement poll (`rom/devs/virtio/virtio_hw.c:121-138`). When status stays nonzero through the final iteration, `spin--` wraps to `ULONG_MAX`, so `if (!spin)` misses timeout and reset returns TRUE; if status clears on the last body iteration, `spin==0` can instead cause false failure. Restored OD2842 and its index link, with consequences limited to a timeout-boundary device. No reset or device was exercised; source-only.

The OASIS VirtIO 1.2 common-config contract says generation changes with device configuration and requires a changed generation after a changed device-specific value is read (§4.1.4.3: https://docs.oasis-open.org/virtio/virtio/v1.2/virtio-v1.2.html). <a id="rtl8029-concurrent-unit-lifecycle-od11482"></a>
RTL8029 per-unit open/close synchronization pass (OD11482 added; driver and Exec bodies already credited; no body/path/LOC increment; 2026-11-07): traced public `OpenDevice()` into `DevOpen()`/`OpenUnit()` and `InitializeUnit()`, then followed last-close through `CloseUnit()`/`ExpungeUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:390-420,787-903`). `OpenUnit()` reads `dd_Units[unit]`, initializes on NULL, and increments `ud_OpenCnt` without a per-unit lock; initialization publishes the slot only after hardware setup and `RunTask()` succeed. `OpenDevice()` releases the DeviceList lock before invoking the device Open vector (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-117`), and the ExecSMP `Forbid()` contract only blocks task switches on the calling CPU (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`), so the API path does not serialize calls on different CPUs. Two first opens can therefore initialize and publish distinct unit states/workers; either returned object's last close unconditionally clears the shared slot. Separately, `ExpungeUnit()` frees `ud` before clearing the slot (`driver.c:890-903`), allowing an overlapping opener that already loaded the pointer to resume and dereference freed state. The optional network-card target includes RTL8029 (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:52`; `rtl8029/mmakefile.src:4-11`); no default-image inclusion is claimed. Existing OD11222 covers failed-discovery cleanup and OD11224 covers the unchecked Prometheus ownership result; OD11482 concerns concurrent per-unit lifecycle synchronization. No in-tree pair of concurrent opens/closes was established and no task, device, board, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="netinfo-startnotify-failure-stale-map-od1909"></a>
### NetInfo `StartNotify()` failure and stale parsed map (OD1909)

Rechecked `InternalSetEnts()` in `workbench/devs/netinfo/entries.c`: it writes `nr_UserData` before calling `StartNotify()` and discards the result (`:430-440`). `StartNotify()` returns failure on path resolution, allocation, or handler-registration errors (`rom/dos/startnotify.c:67-69,91-105,157-197`). The nonzero marker suppresses retry, and only the notification handler clears it (`entries.c:478-487`). Selected `GetByNameCmd`/`GetByIDCmd` proceed to search the existing map (`entries.c:100-157`); selected `usergroup.library` lookup wrappers call those commands. Thus a post-parse registration failure followed by an external database change leaves lookups using the old parsed records. No failure was induced. The detailed finding and master-index link were restored in commits `440a9ab` and `1bfc028` after this ledger's prior references proved the detail and index entries were absent.

No shared lock or generation cutover covers both paths. The existing cap findings OD9860-OD9861 remain distinct. Controller HIDD initialization ownership recheck (OD9859 withdrawn; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): traced `ControllerHidd_InitClass()`'s `CLID_HW_Root` lookup (`controller_init.c:71-79`) through `HWRoot__Root__New()` and `HWRoot__Root__Dispose()` (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwroot.c:40-70`) and generic HIDD startup (`rom/hidds/hidd/initcode.c:43-53`). The root constructor returns the class-wide `csd->hwroot` singleton, which generic HIDD initialization creates and retains; disposing it is explicitly a no-op. The controller init local is a borrowed reference, so the failed `HW_AddDriver()` path does not leak a root object. Removed OD9859 from the active finding list and index; its old coverage entry above is historical. No initialization failure or build was run; source-only.

NVIDIA small offscreen clear boundary recheck (OD11515 retained; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): followed the VRAM-failure CPU allocation (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiabitmap.c:251-266`) into `NVBM__Hidd_BitMap__Clear()` (`:409-440`). For a 1x1 8-bit bitmap, the fallback pitch is 64 and allocates 64 bytes, while the signed `int i = width * height * bpp / 4` is zero. The do/while writes a 32-bit word, decrements `i` to -1, and continues because the signed condition remains nonzero; it consequently writes beyond the 64-byte allocation and does not terminate normally. This confirms the narrow-dimension trigger and OOB/loop consequence in OD11515; the independent row-pitch mismatch remains OD11514. No bitmap allocation or clear was performed; source-only.

NVIDIA CPU clear row-pitch/layout recheck (OD11514 retained; OD11515 remainder behavior distinguished; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): compared the offscreen fallback layout (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiabitmap.c:251-265`) with the CPU accessors (`:448-478`) and clear loop (`:409-440`). For a 65x2 8-bit offscreen bitmap, `pitch` is 128 and the allocated extent is 256 bytes, while the clear writes 32 contiguous `ULONG`s (128 bytes) from the base. The second visible row begins at offset 128 and is left untouched; the operation does not reach row 2 at its pitched address. A packed byte count with a 1-3 byte remainder also leaves those final visible bytes unwritten (tracked under OD11515), while counts below four trigger its nonterminating zero-count case. This confirms OD11514 as the distinct row-addressing error. No bitmap operation or build was run; source-only.

NVIDIA PCI BAR mapping failure recheck (OD11512 retained; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): traced both unchecked MapPCI results in `workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidia_init.c:619-648` against the selected x86-64 PCIPC override (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:230-255`) and generic PCIDriver fallback (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:163-178`). PCIPC explicitly returns NULL when the above-window global map fails; its fallback may also preserve the `(APTR)-1` failure sentinel. The framebuffer result is used as a `MemChunk *` before any validation, and the register result is used to form MMIO register pointers in `GenericInit()`/`NV4Init()` (`nvidia_init.c:102-127,336-340`). Thus neither failure representation is checked before use. The false-return cleanup at `:679-698` is reached only if chipset init returns; it does not guard the NULL-derived register accesses. OD11512 remains supported. No BAR mapping, device initialization or build was attempted; source-only.

NVIDIA cross-depth CopyBox draw-mode contract recheck (OD11513 retained; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): compared `NV__Hidd_Gfx__CopyBox()`'s branch predicates and exits (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiaclass.c:461-495,553-645`) with supported pixel-depth setup (`nvidiabitmap.c:244-256,273-295`) and generic truecolor fallback (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1131-1166`). The <=8-bit-versus-truecolor mismatch explicitly delegates, but different truecolor depths (15/16/24/32) enter the stretch engine; unlike the same-depth path, this branch neither reads `GC_DRMD` nor programs `NVSetRopSolid`, and it does not call the superclass after kicking off the stretch. The generic fallback maps each source pixel into GC foreground and calls `DRAWPIXEL`, so it preserves requested modes such as XOR. OD11513 remains supported for on-card cross-depth non-Copy requests. No graphics operation or build was run; source-only.

NVIDIA planar missing-plane advancement recheck (OD11516 retained; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): traced each relevant loop from its data source and control flow in `workbench/hidds/nvidia/planarbm.c`: native `PutImage` cases at `:273-311,322-360`, `PutImageLUT` at `:388-435`, `GetImageLUT` at `:463-510`, and color-expansion destination loops at `:551-617,631-696`. Each loop stores `*plane`, continues on NULL or `(UBYTE *)-1`, and advances `plane++` only after processing a real plane; a special plane therefore leaves the iterator at that slot for later depth iterations. The wrapped-bitmap path copies the original `BitMap.Planes[]` entries directly (`:706-804`), while the generic planar implementation explicitly recognizes the all-one sentinel (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:677-705`). OD11516 remains supported for wrapped bitmaps with a missing/sentinel plane before later allocated planes. No bitmap operation or build was run; source-only.

NVIDIA planar color-expansion mask sentinel recheck (OD11517 retained; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): traced `BlitColorExpansion()`'s same-class source branch (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/planarbm.c:543-574`) to the per-pixel `*msk` read (`:571-607`). It takes source plane zero and performs pointer arithmetic before checking whether it is NULL or the all-one sentinel; either representation therefore reaches the read for a nonempty rectangle. `SetBitMap()` copies wrapped `BitMap.Planes[]` entries without normalizing these values (`planarbm.c:706-804`), and the class's own GetPixel/GetImageLUT paths explicitly implement constant-zero/constant-one semantics for them (`:207-240,452-510`). NVIDIA planar color-expansion counter-width recheck (OD11518 qualified; 2026-11-07; no new finding or path/LOC credit): verified `WORD`/`UWORD` definitions (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:61-62`) against the public HIDD method signature (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:538`) and the local signed counters/comparisons (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/planarbm.c:524,551,571`). A width or height above 32767 forces the corresponding `WORD` counter to overflow. Qualified the finding: C signed overflow is undefined, so wrapping negative and continuing beyond the buffer is a possible manifestation, not a portable guarantee. RTL8139 startup-handshake WaitPort caller trace (no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): traced `CreateUnit()`'s `WaitPort()`/`GetMsg()` path (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/unit.c:1083-1112`) through `RTL8139_Schedular()` (`:763-844`). The creator allocates a private SyncPort and one startup message inside `RTL8139Startup`; after process creation the child writes setup status, places its task pointer in `mn_Node.ln_Name`, queues that message once, and waits on `SIGF_SINGLE`. The creator is the only SyncPort consumer, reads the message before freeing the startup structure, then signals the task pointer. The child explicitly performs no further access to the freed `sm_UD`/message after its signal wait (`:840-847`). Each setup-failure branch still reaches this handshake, so ordinary checked initialization failures do not strand the creator in WaitPort. No competing consumer, lost wakeup, or startup-storage lifetime defect was established for this caller. RTL8139 is selected through the active network-cards aggregate on supported targets (`workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:53`; `rtl8139/mmakefile.src:13-15`). No unit, task failure, message, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="rtl8029-worker-startup-timeout-od11520"></a>
RTL8029 worker startup and lifetime-port failure trace (OD11520 added; driver body already credited; no new path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): followed `OpenUnit()` → `InitializeUnit()` → `RunTask()` → failure cleanup in `ExpungeUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:787-903`). `RunTask()` returns FALSE if its 50 one-tick `FindPort()` polls do not find the worker's named port. The worker's `UnitTask()` creates that port and waits for the startup message; the worker can still be live but not yet have published its port when the 50 one-tick polls expire. Cleanup calls `KillTask()`, which signals Ctrl-C and waits on the lifetime port; if the worker later reaches its startup `WaitPort()`, that wait observes only the port signal, and the parent never queued the startup message needed to reach `MainLoop()` and the lifetime reply (`:758-767,1728-1763,890-902`). Separately, worker `CreateMsgPort()` failure makes `UnitTask()` return without any lifetime reply. Added OD11520 for the conditional first-open deadlock, distinct from OD11222's failed hardware-discovery cleanup and OD11482's ExecSMP open/close race. The driver and target selection are already in the source inventory; no body count changes. No worker, allocation failure, device open or build was run; source-only.

<a id="rtl8029-worker-create-failure-port-leak-od11521"></a>
RTL8029 worker-creation failure unwind trace (OD11521 added; driver body already credited; no new path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): traced the successful `CreateMsgPort()`/failed `CreateNewProc()` branch in `RunTask()` (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:715-754`) through `InitializeUnit()` and `ExpungeUnit()` (`:872-903`). `RunTask()` returns FALSE without deleting `ud_LifeTime`; `ExpungeUnit()` skips `KillTask()` because `ud_Task` is NULL and never deletes that port before freeing `UnitData`. Exec's `CreateMsgPort()` records the calling task as signal owner and `DeleteMsgPort()` frees the port (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:50-74`; `rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:37-57`). Added OD11521 for the repeated-open port/signal leak, separate from OD11520's wait-without-handshake deadlock. No task-creation failure or device open was induced; source-only.

Bluetooth pairing entropy and callback follow-up (OD3808 retained; 2026-11-07; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): read `hwconn.c:2224-2860` across pairing completion/reply, LE entropy collection, SMP random/key callbacks, and channel event handling. Confirmed the existing OD3808 path: `bConnRequestEntropy()` returns zero when no `LE_RAND` command can be queued, but `bStartPairing()` then starts SMP immediately; later controller-random command failures also decrement the wait count without marking entropy unavailable, while `bSMPRandom()` always returns success and uses the time/pointer/address-seeded xorshift fallback. The path can therefore reach key/nonce generation without controller-provided entropy when the command queue rejects all requests or every accepted request fails. This is the already reported finite-entropy/predictable-fallback issue, not a second finding. Pairing-state publication, user replies, and key distribution in this interval did not establish another independent issue beyond OD3713, OD3806-OD3807, and OD3808. WirelessManager SANA-II duplicate keepalive-registration candidate disposition (2026-11-07; no finding or source/path/LOC credit): compared `wpa_driver_sana2_set_associd()`'s recurring timeout registration with the second registration in the `S2EVENT_CONNECT` handler. `eloop_register_timeout()` does allow duplicate handler/context entries and `eloop_cancel_timeout()` removes all matches, so duplicate registrations would persist as parallel 30-second send/reschedule loops if both callbacks occurred. The selected Atheros5000 and Realtek8180 user-space-MLME route does call `set_associd()`, but `wpa_driver_sana2_init()` subscribes that route only to `S2EVENT_OFFLINE`; its `S2EVENT_CONNECT` notification from `S2INFO_SSID` is therefore not delivered to this event handler. The hard-MAC route does subscribe to CONNECT and schedules its timer from that event, but does not use the user-space MLME association callback that invokes `set_associd()`. The suspected duplicate does not have a selected caller path; no issue added. No association, event, timeout, or device was run; source-only.

Nouveau BIOS PLL parser selected-caller error propagation pass (2026-11-07; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated all 23 in-tree `nvbios_pll_parse()` call sites across `nvkm/subdev/{bios,clk,devinit,fb}` and `drm/nouveau/dispnv04`. The clock/devinit/framebuffer callers return or translate parser errors before using limits; NV50 RAM reclocking writes only `mpll.vco2.max_freq` before checking the parser result, then returns on error before reading the structure or executing the queued HWSQ sequence. Display callers either return `-ENOENT`/the parser error or abandon the mode calculation on failure. `nouveau_hw_fix_bad_vpll()` repeats the same parse through `nouveau_hw_get_pllvals()` and ignores that second return, but the BIOS object is unchanged between the calls and its parser result is deterministic in the inspected path; no separate failure was established. No independent caller defect found. Malformed BIOS bounds and hardware PLL programming remain source-level gaps; no BIOS, clock change, display mode, or build was exercised.

Nouveau BIOS fan-table caller and bounds disposition (2026-11-07; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced both `nvbios_fan_parse()` callers. `nvkm_therm_fan_init()` installs BIOS defaults before parsing and falls back to the thermal table when the BIT fan table is absent; `nvkm_fanpwm_create()` starts from a zeroed local structure and treats an absent table as unknown fan type. The parser reads the four-byte PWM frequency at entry offset `0x0b` without validating that the BIOS entry stride covers those bytes; `nvbios_rd32()` bounds-checks against the complete BIOS image and returns zero out of range, but a short logical entry can still make the read cross into following table bytes. No in-tree format declaration here established the minimum v1.0 entry length or that such short entries are valid, so no defect is promoted on this evidence. `fanpwm_set()` divides the timer divisor by a nonzero parsed PWM frequency; the inspected path does not establish a selected normal table value that makes the divisor zero. Table-format validation and hardware timer semantics remain open. No BIOS, fan, or PWM operation was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau power-budget parser and ICCSense consumer pass (2026-11-07; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced the sole `nvbios_power_budget_header()` / `nvbios_power_budget_entry()` caller in `nvkm_iccsense_oneinit()`. It checks the header status and capability-entry sentinel before use, checks the entry result before publishing `avg_w`/`max_w`, and treats absent/invalid budget data as optional while continuing ICCSense initialization. The entry reader uses fixed offsets through `+0xa` without checking `budget->elen >= 14`; BIOS read helpers return zero when the absolute read exceeds the image, but an undersized logical record can read into subsequent bytes. The checkout contains no table-format declaration establishing the minimum v2.0/v3.0 entry size, so the source alone does not prove that such a record is valid or expose a selected failure. The header's count/stride arithmetic is also not checked against the BIOS image extent; out-of-image reads become zero, while malformed offset wrap remains dependent on unestablished BIOS-format constraints. No finding is promoted. No BIOS or sensor was used; source-only.


Nouveau ICCSense parsed-rail ownership trace (OD11525 added; 2026-11-07): `nvbios_iccsense_parse()` allocates `iccsense->rail` with `kmalloc_array()` after a nonempty table is found (`nvkm/subdev/bios/iccsense.c:75-79`). Its sole caller `nvkm_iccsense_oneinit()` stores the returned array in stack-local `stbl`, iterates it, and has no `kfree(stbl.rail)` on success or the later per-rail `-ENOMEM` return (`nvkm/subdev/iccsense/base.c:221-243,259-294`). The ICCSense destructor frees only its own sensor/rail lists (`:131-145`), not this local table. Added OD11525 for the lost BIOS rail-array allocation on each successful nonempty parse. The optional Nouveau source manifest selects `iccsense/base.c`; supported device tables register its constructor and one-init hook. No device or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

FDisk Exec `WaitPort()` startup and unit-close caller closure (2026-11-07; no new OD or source-body/path/LOC credit): traced selected `workbench/devs/fdsk_device.c` `Open()` and final `Close()` waits (`:100-177,186-208`) through `unitentry()` startup and command loop (`:527-635`). Both API paths hold `fdskbase->sigsem` while configuring and consuming the shared reply port, so only one opener/closer can await that port at a time; each removes its reply before releasing the semaphore. Startup sends the reusable `unit->msg` to the newly created process port, whose `unitentry()` receives it and replies after establishing the unit port; final close sends the same message to that unit port, and the worker replies only after draining earlier queued commands and closing its file. The worker's selected loop has no ordinary exit other than the replied `DICMD_DIE` path, and `unitentry()` is the sole `unit->port` consumer. Thus these selected waits do not demonstrate WaitPort's concurrent-head or wrong-reply failure. CreateNewProc has no `NP_NotifyOnDeath` tag, so an abnormal worker exit before startup/close reply could strand the caller, but no ordinary such exit was established in the inspected worker. No task, request, DOS operation or build was run; source-only.


Sonixcam negative-gamma recheck (OD9438 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): reread `CreateGammaTab()` and `gammacorrection()` in SonixcamTool (`rom/usb/shellapps/SonixcamTool.c:80-100,1033-1045`) and compared them with the Pencam implementation already recorded under OD9438 (`PencamTool.c:72-92,446-458`). Both parse the `GAMMA/K` string with `atof()` without validating that gamma is nonnegative. For a negative value such as -2, the smallest table input uses `x=1`, so `255 * pow(1/256, -2)` exceeds `UWORD_MAX`; the floating-to-UWORD conversion occurs before the red clamp and has undefined behavior. Values that exceed 255 while remaining in UWORD range also narrow directly into green/blue output bytes. Expanded OD9438 to both selected shell tools and added its missing detailed report and index entries; the existing body/path/LOC credit is unchanged. Sharpen output-border bytes remain intentionally zero because `psdAllocVec()` allocates from Poseidon's `MEMF_CLEAR` pool. No gamma input, image, or build was used; source-only.

USB HID keyboard 8-bit key-count truncation recheck (2026-11-08; no body/path/LOC credit): traced a non-variable keyboard Input item through `hid_get_item()` retaining its full 32-bit `loc.count` (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/hid.c:235-244`), `USBKbd::Root::New()` narrowing it into the 8-bit `KbdData.loc_keycnt` and allocating `loc_keycnt+1` bytes (`kbdclass.c:179-191`; `hid.h:174-182`), and the first `ParseReport()` callback copying the full `loc_keycode.count` as a byte length (`kbdclass.c:99-119`). A 256-entry one-bit array produces a 32-byte descriptor-derived input buffer and fits a full-speed interrupt endpoint; it narrows to zero and later copies 256 bytes into/out of one-byte allocations. Confirmed `HID::New()` sizes the buffer from `hid_report_size()` and registers the shared interrupt callback; the selected OHCI AddInterrupt path takes the 32-byte length unchanged (`hidclass.c:276-316`; `drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:479-493`). Added OD11527 to the report and index. No descriptor, controller, or report was constructed or run; source-only.

MassStorage cross-controller identity-cache concurrency follow-up (OD11024 strengthened; 2026-11-08; no body/LOC credit): confirmed `AttachDriver()` creates one lock-bearing `usb_driver` record per host-controller object and `NewDevice()` holds that per-controller lock while constructing classes. Traced OHCI's per-controller attachment calls, then compared them with MassStorage's global cache lock, which protects lookup and insertion separately (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbclass.c:117-145,258-268,315-377`; OHCI `ohciclass.c:366`; MassStorage `storageclass.c:43-80,120-129,338-361`). Concurrent matching identities on separate controllers can both miss and append duplicate records; detach caches both unit/task sets separately, while a later exact-key scan always returns the earlier record. The later reattachment therefore cannot select the duplicate record's retained workers. Expanded OD11024 and its master-index summary; this is the same cache-key aliasing root cause, not a separate ID. Source-level interleaving only; no device, detach/rebind, schedule or build was run.
