eaudio zero-key request validation recheck (OD4083 retained; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): traced `BeginIO()` command dispatch in `workbench/devs/audio/libfunctions.c:26-120` into `audio_WRITE()`/`_CMD_WRITE()` and `audio_READ()`/`_CMD_READ()` (`audio_commands.c:599-640,1800-1857`). BeginIO resets `io_Error` and queues these commands without checking that the channel is allocated; the handlers accept equality between `ioa_AllocKey == 0` and an unallocated unit's initial `eu_allockey == 0`. Thus zero-key writes can be submitted on a free channel, and the empty-mask read maps through `writechn[0]` to channel 0 and can return success with NULL data. The source search/caller census recorded in OD4083 found selected maintained clients allocate first; the triggering direct command remains external/future-client scope, and the module is explicitly selected rather than in the active default aggregate. No audio request or playback was run; source-only.

PTP short-read caller recheck (OD4443 retained, 2026-11-08): followed the DOS `ACTION_READ` dispatch through `nPTPRead()` to `nGetPTPRspData()` and the response error check (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:2277-2355,930-1080,1264-1285,3643`). `nPTPRead()` sets `dp_Res1` to the clipped requested `len` before I/O, ignores the data-reader return and `pr_DataLength`, then advances `pfh_SeekPos` by that same `len` after `nCheckPTPError()` accepts the response. Thus a successful data container shorter than the requested range can be reported as a full read and advance the handle over bytes not supplied. This confirms OD4443's read-side consequence at the DOS caller; write-preload cases remain separately described in the finding. No device or I/O was run; source-only.

PTP DOS Read result-contract recheck (OD4443 retained, 2026-11-08): checked the public DOS `Read()` contract and packet result plumbing. `Read()` returns `dopacket3()`'s `dp_Res1` as its byte count, and documents that count as bytes actually read; `dopacket3()` initializes results then returns `dp_Res1` (`rom/dos/read.c:28-38,68-74`; `rom/dos/dopkt.c:125-145`). Combined with the PTP handler's pre-I/O assignment of requested `len` and missing comparison against `pr_DataLength`, the existing OD4443 mismatch is confirmed at the public DOS API. No packet or device was run; source-only.

USB printer OD4303 recheck (retained and qualified, 2026-11-08): re-read interface binding, worker initialization, startup notification, device Open/BeginIO, and the worker's first queue-drain iteration (`rom/usb/classes/printer/printer.class.c:183-259,480-590,770-851`; `rom/usb/classes/printer/dev.c:46-100,152-229`). The unit is linked before the worker starts, so Open can observe it during initialization; however, when initialization succeeds, `nPrinterTask()` drains the read/write queues before its first `Wait()`, so a request queued during that interval is serviced. On initialization failure, `nAllocPrinter()` clears `ncp_Task`, while the unit-removal/free block remains commented out; `devOpen()` has no live-task check and `CMD_READ`/`CMD_WRITE` are queued without a worker to consume or reply. OD4303 remains valid specifically for the failed-initialization case; transient pre-start admission alone is not a separate finding. No binding, failure, open, or request was run; source-only.


PTP response-buffer ownership recheck (OD4476 added, 2026-11-08; no source-body or LOC credit): traced the `nGetPTPRspData()` continuation-error branch to `nFreeVec(nch, buf)` (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:1049-1056`), then traced `buf` from DOS `ACTION_READ` through `nPTPRead()` to the public `Read()` caller (`:2341`; `rom/dos/read.c:68-74`). `nFreeVec()` expects a preceding size word and calls `FreePooled()` on the PTP class pool (`ptp.class.c:591-605`), whereas this read buffer belongs to the DOS caller. Poseidon's selected `psdDoPipe()` path returns synchronous transfer errors (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:4705-4730`), making the cleanup branch reachable on a failed continuation. Added OD4476 for the invalid pool free; the old-file preload caller also passes a PTP-pool buffer, but the report makes no separate claim for that case. No USB transfer or allocator operation was run; source-only.


PTP preload-buffer consequence recheck (OD4476 expanded, 2026-11-08; no source-body or LOC credit): traced the second `nGetPTPRspData()` caller in `nPTPWrite()` (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:2484-2493`). A continuation error frees its class-owned `pfh_Buffer` but the handler returns without clearing the field. `ACTION_END` later transfers any non-NULL `pfh_Buffer` into `nch_LastBuffer` (`:3590-3598`), and the next read of the same object moves that cache pointer back into a file handle and copies from it (`:2355-2393`). This confirms the stale-cache consequence as part of OD4476, alongside the public DOS `Read()` caller's invalid pool free. No transfer, close or subsequent read was run; source-only.


IntelGMA OD9910 detailed-report promotion and ownership recheck (2026-11-08; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the earlier status-slot pass before promoting it from coverage notes into the detailed report. In the non-`GALLIUM_SIMULATION` branch, `IntelGMA_WS_BatchbufferFlush()` calls `IntelGMA_StatusReserve()` while holding `BatchBufferLock`, then assigns the returned index only inside the relocation loop (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_galliumclass.c:364-410`; lock macro in `intelgma_winsys.h:30-31`). The sole `IntelGMA_StatusFree()` call is from `IntelGMA_WS_BufferIsBusy()` using a buffer's `status_index` (`:176-182,602-630`), so zero-relocation flushes cannot return their slots. Status initialization clears indices 100-1023 once (`:92-100`); exhaustion therefore leaves the next reserve loop waiting forever under the batch lock (`:149-173,369-375`). The explicit IntelGMA target compiles the local winsys, but monitor/Mesa dependency edges are commented, and repository search found no in-tree external Gallium flush caller. Promoted the conditional OD9910; no claim that a compatible client actually emits 924 relocation-free flushes. No batch or GPU operation was run; source-only.


GV100 supervisor per-head scratch-array bounds recheck (unresolved; no OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): traced the count/mask into its list consumer rather than inferring the supported head limit from register field widths. `gv100_head_cnt()` returns the low four-bit count field and a separate low eight-bit mask (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/engine/disp/gv100.c:320-325`); `nv50_disp_oneinit()` iterates set mask bits below that returned count and calls `gv100_head_new()` (`nv50.c:1601-1607`), which stores the bit index unchanged in `nvkm_head_new_()` (`head.c:54-66`). `gv100_disp_super()` then indexes its four-element local `mask` array with every stored `head->id` (`gv100.c:841-850,852-887`). Thus an instantiated head ID 4-7 would index beyond the array; the repository does not document or constrain the GV100/GA102/TU102 count/mask relationship sufficiently to establish that any selected device can report such an ID. The analogous GF119 code also uses a four-element array but its head mask is explicitly restricted to four bits (`gf119.c:1011-1025,472-476`), which does not prove the newer GV100 field has the same maximum. Retained as an unresolved bound question, not promoted to a defect without the hardware contract. No GPU/register operation or build was performed; source-only.


GV100 supervisor bounds GSP-path separation (unresolved; no OD or LOC credit; 2026-11-08): checked whether the in-tree eight-head GSP support reaches the four-slot `gv100_disp_super()` worker. GA102/TU102 use that worker only on their non-GSP path; `ga102_disp_new()`/`tu102_disp_new()` call `r535_disp_new()` when GSP RM is active (`engine/disp/ga102.c:147-155`; `tu102.c:234-241`). `r535_disp_new()` constructs a separate function table with `r535_disp_oneinit()` and does not copy the hardware table's `.super` callback (`subdev/gsp/rm/r535/disp.c:1866-1911`); that path obtains head count/mask from RM and has its own eight-bit interrupt enumeration (`:1775-1805,1560-1572`). The RM IMP schema's eight-head capacity (`r535/nvrm/disp.h:753-758,833-849`) therefore cannot establish that a head ID above 3 reaches the legacy GV100 supervisor. The legacy GA102/TU102 path and direct GV100 path still lack a checked-in maximum that resolves the four-element local array; retain the bounds question without promotion. No GPU/register operation or build was run; source-only.


Nouveau/VMware workqueue SMP synchronization trace (OD11535 added; no new body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): traced the already fully reviewed `linux_workqueue.c` producer and worker critical sections against the ExecSMP contract for `Disable()` and the multi-write `ADDTAIL`/`REMHEAD` list macros. Confirmed that the worker is a separate process and the selected IRQ shim queues threaded callbacks into the shared queue. Added conditional OD11535 for unsynchronized shared queue/list state on cross-CPU overlap in explicitly built optional Nouveau or VMware targets. No worker, interrupt, race, device, or build was run; source-only.


RTL8029 first-open board-claim caller recheck (OD11482 strengthened; driver/Prometheus/PCIDevice bodies already credited; no body/path/LOC increment; 2026-11-08): traced `FindHardware()`'s unit-index board selection and claim (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:1213-1238`). It calls `Prm_SetBoardAttrsTags(PRM_BoardOwner, dd)` and ignores its return, then returns the board MMIO base. The selected setter returns zero when `HIDD_PCIDevice_Obtain()` finds an existing owner (`workbench/libs/prometheus/board.c:275-300`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:488-510`), but RTL8029 does not use it to abort `InitializeUnit()`. Thus the board-ownership path does not serialize two concurrent first opens; both can continue hardware initialization and worker creation before racing to publish `dd_Units[unit]`. Expanded OD11482 and its index summary with this caller detail. This consequence overlaps OD11224's ownership-return defect but remains within OD11482's per-unit concurrency root cause. The separate last-close/open stale-pointer interleaving is unchanged. No board, open/close, task, or build was run; source-only.


RTL8029 Prometheus owner-claim finding promotion (OD11224 detailed; driver/helper bodies already credited; no body/path/LOC increment; 2026-11-08): restored the missing detailed report section for the existing master-index candidate. Rechecked the full claim-to-use path: `FindHardware()` ignores the setter's zero return and returns the MMIO base; `InitializeUnit()` then resets and initializes the board (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:836-884,1213-1238`). Prometheus returns zero when the PCIDevice is already owned (`workbench/libs/prometheus/board.c:275-300`; `rom/hidds/pci/pcideviceclass.c:488-510`). The source-wide caller census found that RTL8029 is the only checked-in network caller not testing the result; Intel Pro100, Etherlink3, Rhine, NvidiaNet, Broadcom4400, Atheros5000, and Prism2 all test it before continuing. Added the same-driver ExecSMP concurrent-first-open route from OD11482, while keeping the ownership-return defect and per-unit lifecycle race as separate root causes. Updated the OD11224 index link to the new detailed anchor. No board, owner conflict, device open, or build was exercised; source-only.


Generic entropy backend output-quality candidate promotion (OD11446 detailed; all source bodies already credited; no body/path/LOC increment; 2026-11-08): restored the detailed report section and fixed the master-index link for the existing coverage-only candidate. Rechecked the generic hardware stub, software collector, initialization, `GetEntropy()` and its POSIX/arc4random consumers (`rom/entropy/entropy_hw.c:15-24`; `entropy_software.c:7-14,48-95`; `entropy_init.c:21-64`; `getentropy.c:70-101`; `compiler/crt/posixc/getentropy.c:33-55,87-99`; `compiler/crt/stdc/__arc4random.c:55-79`). Nouveau logger flusher process-creation failure trace (OD11536 added; `linux_printk.c` and `linux_workqueue.c` bodies already credited; no body/path/LOC increment; 2026-11-08): followed `workqueue_init()` into `nouveau_log_init()` and traced ring allocation, the ignored `CreateNewProcTags()` result, the sticky `nlog.started` flag, `nlog_append()` signaling, severity routing, and the flusher's file-write loop (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_workqueue.c:389-400`; `linux_printk.c:350-382,387-495,498-526`). No process/allocation failure, logger operation, device, or build was induced; source-only.

PC IRQ chain SMP synchronization trace (OD11537 added, 2026-11-08; source bodies already credited; no body/path/LOC increment): compared the selected PC override with generic handler-chain code. `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c` supplies its own `KrnAddIRQHandler()` and `krnRunIRQHandlers()` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:25`); its dispatcher iterates with shared `PlatformData.kb_LastIntr` and has no SMP read lock (`addirqhandler.c:116-139`; `kernel_arch.h:48-82`). Its add path uses local `Disable()` without the generic SMP write lock (`addirqhandler.c:88-110`), while the shared generic remove path takes `kb_IntrSpinLock` in write mode under ExecSMP (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-77`). The PC IRQ entry calls the local dispatcher for enabled vectors (`cpu_intr.c:500-518`). This is the shared PC IRQ-chain synchronization root cause already reported as EK9263; the shared cursor and missing matching chain synchronization are now cross-referenced there rather than counted as an Other Drivers finding. No IRQ, mutation, build, or runtime operation was performed; source-only.

Nouveau display queue producer-quiescence recheck (OD11537 expanded, 2026-11-08; same PC IRQ-chain root cause; no source-body or LOC credit): traced `nvkm_device_del()` ordering from `nvkm_intr_dtor()`/`free_irq()` to reverse subdevice deletion (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/engine/device/base.c:3080-3098`; `core/intr.c:367-379`). The display destructor calls `destroy_workqueue()` before freeing heads and display subobjects (`engine/disp/base.c:169-215`); this workqueue implementation flushes current work, then sets `stopping`, with no IRQ-producer join (`drm-compat/linux_workqueue.c:139-147`). NV50/GF119/GV100 display IRQ handlers queue `disp->super.work` (`engine/disp/nv50.c:1501`; `gf119.c:1130`; `gv100.c:944`), and each worker dereferences the containing display and its heads (`nv50.c:1365-1430`; `gf119.c:1011+`; `gv100.c:835-925`). Because the selected PC IRQ removal does not wait for the matching active dispatch traversal, an already-running IRQ callback can queue supervisor work after the flush has observed an empty queue; reverse teardown then frees the display state the worker uses. Transferred this manifestation to EK9263 rather than retaining a duplicate Other Drivers issue. No device, IRQ, queue, teardown or build was exercised; source-only.

USB configuration descriptor failure finding restored (OD2327, 2026-11-08; `usbdeviceclass.c` and selected caller bodies already credited; no new body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `Configure()`'s first header read and retry loop (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbdeviceclass.c:531-578`) against the selected USB pool creation (`stack/usb_init.c:118-123`) and USB_UNCONFIG_NO sentinel (`stack/usb_core.h:449`). The first failed header request leaves the automatic `cd.wTotalLength` uninitialized and that value controls the pooled allocation and subsequent control request; a positive allocatable residual value plus three failed full reads proceeds through `set_config(0)`, stores the unconfigured sentinel and returns TRUE. Traced Configure's unchecked result into selected hub, HID and MassStorage construction (`usbhubclass.c:127`; `HID/hidclass.c:244-250`; `MassStorage/storageclass.c:161-173`). Restored the coverage-only candidate as OD2327, distinct from OD2324's rejected SET_CONFIGURATION after a valid descriptor and OD2328's failed interface-table allocation. No transfer, device, failure or build was induced; source-only.

VMware SVGA threaded IRQ teardown candidate restored (OD4035, 2026-11-08; irq shim, vmwgfx IRQ and driver/fence teardown bodies already credited; no body/path/LOC increment): re-traced `irq_dispatcher()` queueing `entry->thread_work`, `irq_thread_work()` dereferencing the entry, and `free_irq()` freeing it without `cancel_work_sync()`/`flush_work()` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm-compat/linux_irq.c:35-51,92-105`; compat `linux_workqueue.c:205-218`). Confirmed selected `vmw_irq_handler()` returns `IRQ_WAKE_THREAD` for fence and command-buffer events and `vmw_thread_fn()` dereferences the fence manager (`drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_irq.c:51-64,92-117`). Normal unload frees the fence manager before `vmw_irq_uninstall()` masks and removes the handlers (`vmwgfx_drv.c:1181-1201`; `vmwgfx_fence.c:146-155`; `vmwgfx_irq.c:291-315`). Restored OD4035 in the detailed report and index; no interrupt or unload was run; source-only.


PC IRQ chain duplicate reconciliation (OD11537 withdrawn, consolidated into EK9263, 2026-11-08; no new source/body/path/LOC credit): searched the Exec/Kernel report before finalizing the PC dispatch candidate and found EK9263 already covers the same all-PC add/dispatch versus generic removal lock mismatch. Expanded EK9263 with the shared `PlatformData.kb_LastIntr` cursor and traced Nouveau device/IRQ teardown through display queue flush and queued supervisor work. Marked the temporary OD11537 section withdrawn, removed its active index entry, and retained this ledger trace as the cross-scope path evidence.

USB descriptor retry zero-state contract recheck for OD2327 (2026-11-08; no body/path/LOC credit): verified the precise failure state against the allocator implementation rather than relying only on the pool creation flags. The USB stack pool requests `MEMF_CLEAR` (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usb_init.c:122`); `InternalAllocPooled()` passes pool requirements to `stdAlloc()` and clears each allocated block when `MEMF_CLEAR` is set (`rom/exec/memory.c:1038-1048,1178-1185,670-673`). Thus if the three full descriptor transfers fail, the freshly allocated `cdp` remains zeroed. `USB_UNCONFIG_NO` is explicitly zero (`workbench/devs/USB/include/usb_core.h:449`), so successful `set_config(cdp->bConfigurationValue)` sends configuration value zero and `dev->config` is stored as the unconfigured sentinel, while Configure still returns TRUE (`usbdeviceclass.c:538-578`). This confirms OD2327's false-success state. The first header still uses uninitialized `cd.wTotalLength` because its transfer result is ignored; the candidate remains conditional on a positive, allocatable residual length. No USB transfer, allocation, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

Controller HIDD queued port-message lifetime recheck for OD11532 (2026-11-08; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the port allocator, delivery, detach and dispose paths. `ctrl_MsgAlloc()` changes an embedded array element from `NT_FREEMSG` to `NT_MESSAGE`; `ctrl_DeliverTo()` queues its address to the caller's `NotifyPort` with `PutMsg()` and only a later `ReplyMsg()` (with the initialized NULL reply port) makes it reusable (`workbench/hidds/controller/controller_notify.c:57-73,93-127`; public layout/contract `workbench/hidds/controller/include/controller.h:406-411`). Consumer disposal removes future list delivery via `ctrl_ConsumerDetach()` and immediately `FreeVec()`s that array, with no port drain or wait (`controllerclass.c:285-300`; detach `controller_notify.c:248-260`). A queued message therefore remains linked in the client port after its containing array is freed; the client can later retrieve and reply to that stale message. Confirmed as distinct from the producer-snapshot/dispose race in OD2883. No port, message, consumer, disposal, or build was run; source-only.


Nouveau logger startup failure recheck for OD11536 (2026-11-08; source bodies already credited; no LOC credit): re-read `nlog_flusher()` entry and `nouveau_log_init()` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_printk.c:387-395,498-510`). Besides ignored `CreateNewProcTags()` failure, the newly-created task can fail `AllocSignal(-1)` and return before publishing `nlog.flusher`; `nlog.started` and the allocated ring remain set in both cases, preventing retry. `workqueue_init()` continues regardless of the logger initializer result, and with no flusher ordinary messages remain buffered and are not routed to serial unless their severity/configuration requires it (`linux_workqueue.c:389-400`; `linux_printk.c:350-382,513-526`). Expanded OD11536 and the master index to cover both worker-start failure branches under the same recovery defect. No process, signal, logger, allocation failure, device, or build was exercised; source-only.

Threaded IRQ NULL-primary caller recheck for OD11534 (2026-11-08; source bodies already credited; no LOC credit): rechecked both compatibility headers and enumerated actual registrations. The only in-tree `request_threaded_irq()` call is VMware `vmw_irq_install()`, which passes both non-NULL `vmw_irq_handler` and `vmw_thread_fn` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_irq.c:357`; handler definition `:92-117`). Nouveau's selected caller uses `request_irq()`, whose inline wrapper always supplies a non-NULL caller handler and a NULL thread function (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/include/linux/interrupt.h:38-43`; `nvkm/core/intr.c:358`). No current in-tree registration reaches the accepted NULL-primary state; retain OD11534 as a compatibility API defect conditional on a future/other internal caller using the documented thread-only form, not as a demonstrated current device path. No registration, interrupt, or build was exercised; source-only.

Nouveau NVIF EDID buffer-bound and caller cleanup recheck for OD10031 (2026-11-08; connector and NVIF bodies already credited; no new path/LOC credit): re-traced the full `nouveau_connector_detect()` path from both runtime-PM acquisition modes to its `out` cleanup, confirming the negative NVIF EDID return remains the only bypass in this branch (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nouveau_connector.c:572-608,675-677`). Checked the adjacent variable-length EDID boundary: `nvkm_uoutp_mthd_edid_get()` initializes the request capacity to the fixed 2048-byte data array (`nvkm/engine/disp/uoutp.c:463-474`; `include/nvif/if0012.h:83-91`), and the only checked-in `edid_get` implementation, GSP-RM `r535_tmds_edid_get()`, rejects a firmware `bufferSize` above that capacity before copying and updates the returned size (`nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/disp.c:1349-1375,1386`). The client then duplicates only the returned bounded byte count (`nvif/outp.c:444-470`); no independent size-overrun candidate established. Retained OD10031 for the PM-reference leak and conditional stale EDID on method/allocation/copy failure. No GPU, EDID, runtime-PM operation, or build was exercised; source-only.


Virtual Bluetooth phone SDP host-caller recheck for OD11453 (expanded; existing virtual Bluetooth and `hwconn.c` bodies credited; no path/LOC increment; 2026-11-08): closed the earlier external-parser uncertainty by tracing the selected AROS host enumerator: `bConnRunEnum()` searches for L2CAP UUID 0x0100, `bSDPEnumCB()` stores returned handles then advances into attribute retrieval, and the same callback calls `bParseSDPRecord()` to publish parsed records (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwconn.c:1440-1470,1788-1822,2063-2100`). Thus a connection from the selected AROS host to the simulated phone is sufficient for its in-tree parser to publish the fixed HID profile; no external peer parser assumption is needed. VUSBHCI hotplug callback startup-publication race pass (OD11538 added; `vusbhci_device.c` and `vusbhci_bridge.c` bodies already credited; no path/LOC increment; 2026-11-08): traced initialization order from `libusb_bridge_init()` callback registration through `VUSBHCI_AddNewUnit200()` and the later `usbunit200` assignment (`rom/usb/vusbhc/vusbhci_device.c:133-145`; bridge `:229-238`). `MakeLibrary()` allocates the base with `MEMF_CLEAR`, so the unit pointer begins NULL (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:109`; `vusbhci_device.h:90-95`). The child handler signals the parent before its first `libusb_handle_events()` call, while `NewCreateTask()` publishes the task and can reschedule to it before returning when its priority permits; ExecSMP may run it concurrently on another CPU (`vusbhci_device.c:35-48,104-112,503-519`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:32-47,69-80`). The callback snapshots and dereferences `usbunit200` for either event type (`vusbhci_bridge.c:30-46,156-171`); an event in this startup window can therefore reach NULL. Added OD11538, separate from OD11447 unrelated-device departure handling and OD9966 init-failure library leak. No host event, task, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

GV100 head-ID interrupt/event consumer closure (bounds candidate remains unresolved; 2026-11-08; no OD or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated the remaining direct head-ID consumers in the GV100 display path. `gv100_disp_intr()` walks all eight status bits and reads the per-head timing register for each asserted bit (`engine/disp/gv100.c:1053-1090`), then calls `nvkm_disp_vblank()`. The vblank event's `index_nr` is computed by `nvkm_disp_oneinit()` as the maximum instantiated `head->id + 1` (`engine/disp/base.c:148-165`); `nvkm_event_ntfy()` drops IDs greater than or equal to that count (`core/event.c:170-177`). This prevents an out-of-range event-list dispatch for an uninstantiated head, although the interrupt routine still accesses the hardware timing register for the asserted status bit. The independent four-slot `gv100_disp_super()` scratch-array index remains unguarded for instantiated IDs 4-7. No source-local maximum or selected-device guarantee establishes whether such an ID can be instantiated, so the scratch-array item remains a hardware-contract question and is not promoted. No interrupt, MMIO access, GPU, or build was run; source-only.

BWFM S2_ONEVENT online-level lost-completion recheck (OD3614 expanded; no new OD or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): re-traced `S2_ONEVENT` state sampling, pending-edge consumption and delayed list insertion (`workbench/devs/networks/bwfm/bwfm_dev.c:1674-1722`) against `S2_ONLINE`/`S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` publication and `report_events()` (`:1650-1664,1362-1397`). A listener can sample OFFLINE and decide to wait, then another caller can set ONLINE and run `report_events()` before the listener is linked; that dispatcher sees no listener and only latches CONNECT/DISCONNECT, not ONLINE. The first caller then queues its ONLINE mask and remains pending while ONLINE already holds, absent another matching transition. `BeginIO` dispatches requests directly (`:1904-1910`), and no per-unit lock covers this check-to-insert interval; concurrent direct SANA-II callers can therefore reach it. The selected WirelessManager sequence was previously traced and is serialized around its online/offline transitions, so that caller does not establish the race; external or independently concurrent BWFM clients remain the trigger scope. This confirms the existing conditional OD3614 lost-wake candidate rather than adding a duplicate. No request or interleaving was run; source-only.

IFFParse `AllocIFF()`/`FreeIFF()` full-body handle-lifecycle pass (2026-11-08; two selected `FUNCS` bodies, 118 physical lines / 50 `cloc 2.06` C code lines): read both complete implementations and confirmed their manifest selection. `AllocIFF()` zero-allocates the internal handle, initializes read mode, context stack and embedded default context list, then sets depth zero. `FreeIFF()` accepts NULL, purges each local item in the default context (including its configured purge hook/user data), and frees the handle with the matching allocation size. The active context stack is not unwound by `FreeIFF()` itself; the API references `CloseIFF()` and the inspected in-tree callers generally close an opened handle before freeing it. The source does not state whether freeing an open handle is supported, so this was not promoted as a defect. No independent allocation/init or ordinary teardown mismatch established. No handle or build was exercised; source-only.

BTSerial legacy parity-mask hypothesis recheck (no new OD or source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): rechecked `rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/dev.c:108-115` against the serial flag definitions and every BTSerial `io_SerFlags` use. The expression `&= ~SERF_PARTY_ON | SERF_PARTY_ODD` clears `SERF_PARTY_ON` while preserving `SERF_PARTY_ODD`; it does not clear both parity bits. Unlike CDC ACM and PL2303, the selected BTSerial worker never consumes either parity flag: its `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` branch explicitly replies without changing RFCOMM state (`btserial.class.c:694-697`), and no other `io_SerFlags` read exists in this driver. Therefore the odd-bit preservation has no demonstrated behavior consequence in BTSerial and is not an additional bug. This does not alter the separate OD3366 open-handshake wait finding or OD11079 shutdown/admission race. No device, request, or build was run; source-only.
USB serial `SERF_RAD_BOOGIE` parity-mask cross-driver recheck (no new OD or source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): compared the same `io_SerFlags &= ~SERF_PARTY_ON | SERF_PARTY_ODD` open normalization in CDC ACM, CP210x, PL2303 and Palm PDA with each selected class handler. The expression preserves `SERF_PARTY_ODD`, but CDC ACM and PL2303 subsequently force no parity/8N1 when `SERF_RAD_BOOGIE` is set (`cdcacm.class.c:673-696`; `serialpl2303.class.c:475-500`); CP210x replaces the framing configuration with `0x0800` (`serialcp210x.class.c:523-548`); Palm PDA's `nSetSerialMode()` only marks the unit configured and does not consume parity flags (`palmpda.class.c:511-514`). The maintained source search found no `SERF_RAD_BOOGIE` caller outside these open vectors. Thus the preserved odd flag has no demonstrated line-coding effect on the selected open paths, and this shared expression is not promoted to a driver bug. Existing OD3366, OD3367, and Palm PDA request-handshake findings remain separate. No device, request, or build was run; source-only.

USB2OTG recovery power-cycle execution-context recheck (2026-11-08; no new OD or body/LOC credit): traced `NakTimeoutInt()` through the device's `Cause()` wrapper and worker dispatch (`usb2otg_intr.c:875-933,3889-3905`; `usb2otg_device.c:766-797`). On ExecSMP, the wrapper sets `USB2OTG_WORK_NAKTIMEOUT` and signals `WorkerTask`, so the watchdog runs in task context. Without ExecSMP, it calls Exec `Cause()` directly; the watchdog is a software interrupt and enters with interrupts disabled. Its `hu_PortRecoverState == 10` arm can call `OpenResource()`, allocate a mailbox message and call `MBoxCall()` (`usb2otg_intr.c:569-602,3794-3810`); `MBoxCall()` obtains a semaphore and spins while polling hardware (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/mbox/mbox_init.c:34-93`). However, the only state-10 writers are the recovery-state-machine helper and debug force block, both excluded by the checked-in `USB2OTG_ENABLE_CORE_RESET_RECOVERY=0` and `USB2OTG_DEBUG_FORCE_RECOVER_TICK=0` definitions (`usb2otg_intr.c:614-653,3777-3789`; `usb2otg_intern.h:603,662`). No default-build non-SMP path into mailbox operations from the soft interrupt was established. If either local switch is enabled on non-SMP, the context needs redesign or explicit safety proof; that edited configuration is not a checked-in build selection, so no active finding is claimed. No interrupt, mailbox call, reset, or build was run; source-only.
